_childDocuments_.review: Two Acolytes down and I’m really enjoying my time with the game so far, and reading through the upcoming patch notes only fills me with more confidence. So far the weapons all have something unique to offer, combat feels weighty and chunky, the enemy design and variety (so far) is great, boss battles big and small are though but fair, the addition of the sneak button was not expected but super cool, guns actually feel like they are there for damaging enemies which is nice (I’m looking at you bloodbourne), and I absolutely love the art style/animations. Most of the negatives I have are being addressed by the upcoming patch, the only thing that bothers me is the lack of a map. I get it, it’s going for that soulsbourne style of explore and discover, but those are big huge detailed 3D environments with distinguishable landmarks to help move you in the right direction. I can’t tell you how many times I have been utterly and completely lost. I have been streaming it and me trying to figure out where the hell I’m going doesn’t make for the best viewer/player experience. Maybe the addition of a “this is the basic layout of this area” map at shrines would help? Just kind of like a “here are your points of interest” kinda thing. That way you can go “ok I’m pretty sure this is where I am and that area is where I need to go” yah know? Maybe it’s just me though haha. Other than that I can recommend this game whole heartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this game for almost 5 hours.This game is actually pretty fun for what it is. It's whacky, its fast pace and very arcadey. If you are looking for something realistic, I wouldn't recommend picking up this game. Now, there are Microtransactions but I find that King of the Battleground if done right, can net you about 1500-2000 Bucks each session, which 4 of those can get you a lower tier unlock. So to go along with that, the game IS very grindy but the story is very basic and somewhat lackluster so the grind is kinda there just to keep you playing the game.Now regarding gameplay, it is very basic but I mean so was WWE All stars and that was a great game. Same class characters shame the same moveset outside of Sigs/Fins and some moves which are unique to specific characters. Each class is better at something than others and each class feels very different to play outside of their movesets.My Recommendation, if you plan on buying this and playing on your own, It may not be really for you as its a lot more fun with your friends but I mean, dont get me wrong, its still a good solo game to play by yourself if you are looking to jump in and do a few matches cause you are bored but the real experience is with other people and the whacky stuff that can occur.Overall though, I really am loving this game through and through. I do think the AI needs a lot of work since its very easy to "Game" the AI into allowing you to win. Such as Player 2 only targeting Player 1 and Player 4 only targeting Player 3 (Obviously this does not occur when there are 4 Real players). With this happening, if you pin/sub Player 2, Player 4 nor Player 3 will bother breaking up the pin/sub but would rather opt fighting each other. Its especially easy to game Steel Cage Matches because you can just go straight for the Cash bag and have the AI grab you purposely and easily knock them down via Minigame and easily pull down the cash (This method can allow you to win cage matches in about 60 seconds if done right).Creation Suite: This is a big ooof but WWE All Stars was not very good in this department either. The Creation Suite for both Arenas and CAWS are very lackluster, very generic and do not have much depth. It's enough to make a generic/decent looking character but dont go expecting WWE2K19 levels of creation. CAW Movesets are pretty much like everyone else except being able to choose your Sig/Fin from a limited amount of moves. Battleground Arena Creation isnt all that much in depth either but can still be used to create fun little arenas to use with friends.There are a LOT of unlockables and tons of Alt Attires to unlock as well. You can also unlock unique attire, "PODS" for Entrances, Arena parts etc with Bucks earned via matches. Sadly as well, you are only allowed to have 5 Superstar Slots and from what It looks like, you have to use Bucks to buy more slots.TLDR: Does this game have its flaws? Yes but in its entirety despite Microtransactions, the game is super fun with friends and its just whacky enough that you dont really notice the basic movesets and other minor flaws regarding AI. The game is in much better shape than WWE 2K20 was and overall is fairly nice to play when you just want to have some quick fun. _childDocuments_.review: In short, even if the game is on sale, it's not great, and you can really experience all there is to it in the tutorial and by creating 1 character lol. Full review below if you care to read.While cool in concept, I was really hoping for an experience more akin to All Stars like most people have echoed in sentiment. It looks pretty good, but I can't help but not really care for the vibe of the art style. The dwarfish looking character models are a bit odd, and I don't really get what the devs were going for. When you look at the character selection screen to purchase superstars, it is represented as if you are shopping for an action figure, with superstars being in retail style packaging, very akin to Small Soldiers, yet the mini versions of the wrasslers still just end up looking like they have a type of dwarfism. No hate towards dwarfism, but it's just an odd design choice. It seems to have a good selection of superstars, but the fact that you have to grind to unlock them, in lieu of spending actual money on the typical game coins versus gold coin micro transaction model was immediately off putting. I should be able to boot the game up directly after purchase, and play as Lesnar, The Rock, Goldberg, Austin, etc. but no. It's like 5 divas available at the start. Lita, Flair, etc. just odd.I think this is actually a big missed opportunity. I loved WWE Allstars like most people who had the opportunity to play it when it came out. Super over the top, arcade style fun with legends and roster relevant to the times of when it launched. This could've been a revival of that, but instead we got a competent beat em up, soft wwe game. The weapons are funny, but lack impact. The finishers look cool, with great camera cuts and some stylish animations, but the "signature moves" that are executed with the right stick look just as impactful, if not more in some cases, The entrances leave a lot to be desired, as your chosen superstar just falls in from the sky in a box. Effects and animations all look fine, but ultimately this was just all over the place, lacking a lot of polish, and became pretty boring after about an hour. Music is cringe inducing, as it's mostly radio butt rock that is normally associated with the brand, which came as no surprise. I didn't even unlock or play as a single superstar i actually am a fan of. No Lesnar, Rock, Undertaker, Goldberg, HBK, RVD, Mankind, or Rattlesnake. Because they were all locked behind a pay wall or having to grind for hours on hours to unlock. Create a character was UNDERWHELMING as well. When you come from 2k19's robust and detailed create a character, with the ability to embroider Tiger King on the back of a king's cape while creating my 1:1 accurate Joe Exotic, to what is offered in Battle Grounds, is just sad. Create a wrestler is normally the thing that saves games in this genre with the ability to get real creative and weird with your creations. This has some very basic, and slightly inappropriate faces, body types, and every superstar is going to be over 6'  even though they look like they are around 4'.  My only created character was 7'1" . because i didn't have an option to make him a relatively normal size. I get it, this is supposed to be cRaZy, but its just boring, weird, and just a really bad attempt to save 2K's license with WWE in the wake of 2k20's dismal launch.With how broken 2K20 is and  how 2K is not willing to come down on the price of 2K19 because they know it's a superior product to both of their newer titles, forces consumers to pay MORE for an older product, if purchasing the product through conventional means. Steam has 2K19, which came out in 2018 at full retail price of $59.99. How unacceptable that is. I already own the game on PS4 so I cannot, and will not, justify repurchasing the same title for double the price that I paid for about a year ago. The game is old now and should be priced as such.. A good game, nonetheless, but when something is 2 years out of season, the price should be lower, period.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just preface this review by saying I got this game for free. A friend of mine gets the Humble Bundle, he knows I used to be a big wrestling fan so he sent this my way as a gift (that and he thought it looked ♥♥♥♥ and wanted to have a laugh watching me get mad playing an obviously crap wrestling game, cheers Andy.) Now what do I mean by used to be a wrestling fan? well I stopped watching wrestling back in 2000 or so, just after WCW and ECW went under and Vince McMahon completely eliminated all competition. In my opinion this was the worst thing that could have happened to wrestling, McMahon has single handedly destroyed a form of entertainment I grew up with and adored. The Monday night wars forced him to create compelling entertainment to compete with WCW, but ever since he had the monopoly on wrestling it's been a downhill plummet. This game pretty much accentuates the bitter feeling I have towards what the WWE has become.To start with, the game is chock full of micro transactions. You start off with a handful of wrestlers, there's a couple of legends among them such as Bret Hart and Sting and some great new talent such as Bray Wyatt, for the most part however the characters are locked behind a pay wall. Do you want to play as The Rock, Stone Cold Steve Austin, Macho Man Randy Savage or Hulk Hogan? Well you better be willing to grind your arse off or spread your wallet nice and wide for daddy Vince. This kind of practice is scummy beyond belief, especially as judging from the cartoony style of this game WWE Battlegrounds seems to be aimed at a younger audience. Imagine being a kid, it's your birthday, you have enough money to buy one, maybe two games, you're a big fan of WWE so you choose to get this, you sit down to play the game excitedly then you suddenly realise you can only play as 20% of the roster advertised in game, on top of that the game itself sucks, happy birthday kid.I hate this business practice of micro transactions, I can kind of understand it in free to play games, I play League of Legends for example but for the most part have unlocked most of what I want to get in that game for free as it 's nowhere near as tight fisted as this game in rewarding you in game currency, I spent a tenner to get a couple of skins in League, 'cause the game is free and I thoroughly enjoy it. WWE Battlegrounds on the other hand isn't even enjoyable, considering all these wrestlers are behind a pay wall, none of them have unique move sets, yes, you read that correctly, allow me to explain. The game uses a class system. There are five classes of wrestler, technician, high flyer, all rounder, power house and brawler. Each wrestler is listed under one of these classes, each one of these classes has one move set. So for example say I choose to play as Hulk Hogan vs the Boogeyman, both of these wrestlers are power houses, thus both wrestlers will have the exact same move set. This is inexcusable, it's an illusion of variety with a pay wall on top, there are essentially five wrestlers in this game and you pay for skins to make them look like famous wrestlers. How developers and publishers are able to get away with this astonishes me, it's a disgusting way for WWE to treat what few fans continue to keep them in business.Years ago when I was a kid I grew up with some trash wrestling games, the games that came out on the NES, SNES and Mega Drive were some pretty heinous turds, so much so that my only positive experience with a wrestling game as a kid was WWF Wrestlefest in the arcades, so it's safe to say the WWE has nickel and dimed it's audience for a long time. However there was this small window in time during the late 90's where AKI were busting out fantastic games like WWF No Mercy and WCW/NWO Revenge, and Yukes were giving us the legendary Smackdown series. These games were great and kind of made up for the trash games I grew up with, how then have things managed to go this downhill? Much like wrestling itself which was great through the 80's and 90's, the games industry (at least in the west) has gone down the pan and this game is a fine example of that.So then, to close this review, avoid this game at all costs, especially if you are the parent of a young wrestling fan. Instead dig out your N64 from the loft with a copy of No Mercy and relive the glory days while opening up an entire era of classic wrestling for new fans to enjoy, because while corporate asshats like Vince McMahon and modern game publishers can continue to ♥♥♥♥ up the video game and sports entertainment industries, they can't take away the glory days that came before. Let's just hope more honest content creators come along in the future so we can have nice things again, Retromania Wrestling and Fire Pro World seem to be a step in the right direction after all, so not all hope is lost just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to address it up front, NOTHING in the game is locked exclusively behind the premium currency (as far as I've seen anyway), it's just there if you're impatient or absolutely need a specific character right away. When you play through the campaign mode the game starts throwing money at you pretty fast since you get more XP and the matches pay out better, and your level up reward increases as you go along. You also have to play campaign to unlock a bunch of stuff anyway, but at default difficulty that shouldn't take very long. It took me maybe a half hour to finish the first of 7 sections.That said, this is a pretty fun arcade brawler and while a few features feel on the shallow side, it's very easy to get into and enjoy. I do wish there was a bit more variety in movesets for specific wrestlers, but since this is meant as more of a pick-up-and-play kind of thing, I can understand why it was kept relatively simple. It does feel a bit repetitive in the early going, but I imagine after unlocking all the abilites and arenas there's quite a bit more variety to be had. As it is, it's a good game to spend an hour or two with, if only to do something silly like blow up the ring with an explosive barrel and then clobber your opponents with the broken ring post.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: It's a decent game but it feels more like a mobile game with all the unlocks and currencies, lackluster custom modes,the fighting is great, but anything past that is a let down if you've ever played wrestling games before i'd rate it 2.5 out of 5 stars, slightly below average. I recommend waiting til game is on sale to purchase. Create a modes(2 out of 5 stars)- My main gripe is the CAW mode. This is one of the most lackluster CAW modes I have ever experienced (I have been playing since wwf no mercy). CAW mode is the main reason I play WWE games still, I have alot of fun creating various characters and there isn't really an ability to do that in this game. You can't even change colors of clothing items, can't even change the entrance music. The Create a battleground was interesting but without many logos or patterns what is the point of it, you have 2 customization modes with little to no customization beyond the few options given. Game play/Mechanics(3.5 out of 5 stars)- The fighting I found fun, but I didn't care much for power ups and things like that. I'd prefer it to play a bit more like wrestling game and less like a fighting game. Not many match types either, I feel this area could have been vibrant with the over the top game play(inferno matches, hell in a cell, hell you could have thrown wrestlers on a boat and had them feeding each other to sharks and it would have fit the styling of this game) But overall the matches and fighting are the best part of the game. Story(2.5 out of 5 stars)- This part actually seemed decent as well, for what I got through, but its just like reading a comic book. I feel if they actually made some cut scenes or in game visuals it could have been better. Unlocks(1 out of 5 stars)- I bought the 40.00 dollar version of the game and only had about 10 wrestlers too choose from, so this part I really hated, I buy a wrestling game why do I need to unlock every wrestler, I personally don't have the free time to grind and unlock everything. I just want a fun game that's pickup and play. This game with all the unlocks seems more like a mobile game than a console game, daily unlocks/ and 90 percent of wrestlers behind currency. I get having legends locked through story mode, or progression, but if everything is locked behind currency or pay wall then it is annoying  but that is the modern state of gaming sadly. Overall(2.5 out of 5 stars): I think this game has a lot of potential, but it is on the developers to make a decent game, they went from being to far on the simulation end and lacking improvements, too jumping the shark with a fighting game that has more in common with street fighter than professional wrestling. What I'd like too see in the future: The perfect wrestling game I feel is in between arcade and simulation, look at Smackdown Here Comes the Pain good mechanics, fast place yet realistic game play, high impact finishers, also can jump out of helicopters and do crazy unrealistic stuff if that is your cup of tea. WWF No Mercy, great game play, easy to grasp controls, you could literally remaster this on a modern graphics engine and it would sell like hot cakes. And my personal favorite WWE Day Of Reckoning 2, great game play, my favorite physics in any wrestling game, great story. These 3 all were in between arcade and simulation, have great pacing to the game play, great impact on the moves, didn't jump the shark with over the top antics(2k battlegrounds/All Stars) and weren't boringly simulation styled(wwe 2k15-2k20) and complicatedAt the end of the day all I really want too see a great wrestling game, maybe i'm too old school or stuck in the past. I'd like too see 2k succeed with the wwe license, but they haven't delivered since 2k16(for me atleast). This game could be improved pretty easily post launch, add more caw options, make that mode worth more than making goofy looking wrestlers, stop the pay to unlock bs and taking advantage of the customer for financial gain, it hurts how people view your product and led me to request a refund(first time I have ever done so on steam) after an hour of game play, add more match types to  flesh out the game and make it a unique and memorable experience. I know you guys can do it 2k. That is the end of my review, thank you for reading if you've gotten this far, I hope it  has helped you make a better decision, i'd recommend waiting til the game is on sale if you really want to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, there's a reason that I typically cover Indie and non triple A titles on Steam, which a rare exception or two. But hey, being a wrestling fan myself, and loving more arcade based experiences, I gave WWE 2K Battlegrounds a chance, knowing full well that I'd most likely be disappointed in the end result. I mean, surely it couldn't be worse that the backlash for WWE 2K20? Well, I'm here to tell you that it is worse. Oh, don't get me wrong, WWE 2K20 is the worst game. But because it was so broken in certain areas, it did at least push off people who were able to look at that and go “yeah no that doesn't seem right”. Meanwhile 2K Battlegrounds not only looks competent on the surface, it has that eye candy that can make people be drawn to it in the over the top moves and some of the expressive natures of the characters. Except when you peel back the layer of skin, you'll find an absolutely bland experience that can't hold up to any sort of scrutiny over a period of time. I'm personally convinced that this game started as a different project all together: the weird focus in the Campaign on a series of made up wrestlers that seem very one note and don't really draw anyone in in terms of design makes me think the game started as an arcade version but ended up being forced to be the WWE license later on. It explains why for some reason many of those characters have more personality then even some of the WWE superstars themselves, despite the efforts of the comic like nature of the campaign to try to “inject life in it”.But that's only the tip of the iceberg. Actual matches have as much depth as a dried out aquarium tank. Any sort of strategy goes out the window as you have very simple combos and throws that you'll be reusing a minute into the match, and not because you want to. If you hoping for a WWE All stars, run. Run far away. Go play Fire Pro Wrestling. No seriously, go play it, that's what you want. Hell you can make better models in that game then you can here anyway, because some of the characters look like they were beaten with a stick in a bad way.It's the games lack of any sort of technique when it comes to the player that drives me up the wall. The game doesn't carefully try to set you up in learning it's mechanics in a tutorial or some scenario that will make you want to keep playing: it just jams it in and hopes that it actually works. No seriously, there's a reason why those tutorials are in place: they are there to reinforce to the player how to play correctly: to reinforce that you did the moves properly. When you prompt the player that you do the combo this way: and the CPU can block and stop the combo in the “tutorial”, it leads to confusion about if the player did it correctly, when they did. The controls are clunky and feel like they have no sorta of skill for them in mind, which sucks in a game that is bout being more skillful then your competitor. Submissions are button mashing experiences without any sort of technique, pins can just happen randomly even if you finished with one punch, and frankly the game doesn't even try to use the spectical of the sport to your advantage. Hell, the UI is a problem as I sat there straining my eyes trying to tell what was going on and yet if the other character was in the right place, I couldn't. Oh, and let's talk about the AI. Ho boy. Did you want difficulty selections so you could maybe take a character like Cesaro and give you the actual challenge that you deserve? Well, like DX said famously, you can suck it. The AI is one setting, and is based on the rating it seems. Oh, and that's if the AI actually knows what it is doing. It's definitely the worse in multi man matches, as they won't even pay attention for you going for a pin, or will literally just sit there for tens of seconds watching as you fighting an opponent. This game obviously wants you to play with other humans, but considering that in order to  actually unlock wrestlers you HAVE to play the CPU, this game will put you at your limit even before things get going.There's also just confusion about how this is a WWE game .Why is the cage match using CASH to have you escape? Why not something like crowd heat, or hell, the microphone that the player has. Why can a tag team match end in a DQ seemingly when the same characters pulled out weapons earlier in the match and used them. I mean, there's no ref either, but one match in a tag team match ended because....I'm not exactly sure to be honest. It may have been a bug? God this game confused me to no end. But of course, you should expect microtransactions out of the wazoo when it comes to a 2K game, and oh boy, did they inject them here. You start off with an absolutely pitiful roster to begin with, meaning that if you wanted to just get in and play local co op with friends with at least some of your favorite wrestlers, expect to pay. Sure, they give you currency, but after 40 matches barely getting you a mid level wrestler in the early going, and only getting worse as it goes on, you'll realize that this is a war of attrition. They expect you to break down and pay for it, and jesus pay for it all over the place. What to not have a generic finisher for your made character? Pay for it.....even if the selection choices for it is sorta ridculous. Yes, I like AJ Styles, but having his finisher as one of the only selections to begin with for the technical character, what the hell were you thinking 2K? I admit, I don't know what I was expecting. This was 2K and I should know better, but even I sit here disgusted with the monteziation present, and I'm a person who thinks games are underpriced for the most part right now.  This is some of the worst I've seen for a game that's clearly trying to go for a kid audience. Don't. Not even as a joke. This game isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had another rating system, maybe a 10 star system or something.I enjoyed playing this game, but it has some quirks and problems that everyone should be aware of.The bad stuff:- Lots of locked wrestlers and costumes, i don't want to exaggerate, but i think more than half of the content is locked behind microtransactions (or extreme grinding), it's a bad business model. I don't care what people nowadays think, but i just don't think it's right to have a paid game with so much locked content. And not everyone has hours to waste grinding those blue coins. And, well, after so much grinding the fun you get is pretty much non-existent anymore.- For some reason, when you play women matches, opponents are a pain in the ass, reversing you most of the times, while in the men matches, that doesn't happen as often. Not sure about the reason.- The reversal mechanism is not that good, you barely have time to react sometimes- Gameplay tends to feel sluggish and not very smooth, and it kinda breaks the immersion you'd have in this kind of game, you know the arcade-ish feel- Slow loading screens (even installed on an NVME SSD)- If you want to upgrade power-ups, it will cost money, either the blue money that you can grind, either the yellow money that you buy with actual cash, but here's the trick, if you want to upgrade a power up, you will have to do so for each of the wrestlers you play with. You can't just upgrade the power-up and have it upgraded for everyone.You can adapt to the bad parts of it, kind of, but after i got all the achievements i got bored by it (well, i got bored before because so much content was locked behind grinding/microtransactions)If that battle pass unlocked all attires and everything else, i would've maybe considered getting it on a sale, but i am not paying 66$ for a bunch of coins that aren't even enough to unlock all content, it's plain crazy.- If i understand correctly, your coins (both the ones you grind and the ones you buy) are linked to the servers. At some point this game will be delisted because of license expiration, what will happen then? People will probably not be able to play/earn coins anymore.The good stuff:- It reminds me very much of MTV Celebrity Deathmatch, a game from 2003, and this nostalgia brought me some nice memories of happier simpler times- I really love the wacky style of everything, some moves feel like they're taken from MGR Revengeance, it simply is a fresh breath of air, and i would love a sequel- It's just minimalistic and simple, unlike the regular WWE games that have a "too technical" gameplay- Surprisingly enough game modes and features, you can even create your own wrestler, which i really didn't expect from this game, although i haven't tried it yet- Quite a big roster (but, again, a big part locked)I did enjoy the game, but the locked content was really a buzzkill that made me hate the game.I think if you have friends to play with/play online you'd enjoy this game quite a lot (the AI is pretty stupid), but i generally don't play stuff online.I would rate this maybe a 6/10It's cool and wacky, but also annoying at times.(If any dev/publisher is reading this, I and many others would really love if you added trading cards/badges for this game, just saying :p)

_childDocuments_.review: WWE Battlegrounds has made its way into my list of the most enjoyable games I've ever played.The roster itself is the most impressive one I've seen to date. As someone who absolutely loves classic WWF and WCW, I am deeply appreciative that this game features so many of my favourite legends like Ultimate Warrior, Roddy Piper, Jake the Snake and also stars like Stone Cold Steve Austin, DX Triple H, Jeff Hardy, Edge, and Brock Lesnar! There's far too many wrestlers to even mention here, in WWF, WCW and beyond. So for me personally, the roster is damn near perfect! Gameplay-wise, it's a load of fun! The combination of punchy sound design (pun-intended), super creative move-sets, mesmerizing animations and ever-hilarious stun-locks transitioning into suplex city is exactly what I need to truly have fun in a wrestling video-game. Supporting the amazing roster is also a pretty fun set of cosmetics that allow you to dress your favourite wrestlers in some of their era-specific outfits, which is super cool! Dressing Triple H in his DX gear is great fan-service in-of-itself, let alone the NWO star cosmetics, various Undertaker/Kane looks and The Rock with hair (lol)! There's o' so many options to choose from, which really adds to the fun.At the time of writing this review, I am making my way through the main story, and even that is quite fun. Fun, fun, fun. That's what I am having with this game, and it's such a needed break from all the serious RPG's and horror games I usually play. The comic system is a really great way to make a narrative more engaging for nerds like me, and it ties into the matches brilliantly. I can't wait to jump back into the expansive story with something like 100+ matches if I'm not mistaken.Overall, this game is worth every penny for me personally, but that's only because it ticks so many of the boxes I've had left un-checked for some while now; it is truly everything I have wanted to bring the fun back into gaming and appeal to my love for the WWE.2k is 2k, and I hate them all the same as EA - The excessive need to implement in-game currency and offering predatory microtransactions will never be forgotten. However, that aside, this game could certainly bring you lots of fun as it has done for me if you're willing to just play the damn game. I do respect any reservations to do so, and most certainly side with you if you choose not to support them however.Anyway, if you're:- A fan of WWE- A fan of classic WWF superstars and believe they don't receive enough recognition- Into arcadey fighting games that aren't too intricate- Wanting to relive the DX glory days with Triple H or NWO with Hulk HoganGet this for a truly entertaining experience._______________________________________________________________________Story: 8.5/10 (Purely for its vibrancy and comic theme)Gameplay: 9.5/10Graphics (not calculated in overall score): 9/10Fun Factor: 10/10Roster: 9/10Overall: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: -----------------------------------------------TL;DRIdc if you're a fan if WWE, this game actually will have limited to no functionality when they decide to pull the servers so don't get the game.------------------------------------------------I get the core audience probably only buys sports games because they're only into sports, have no standards for video games, and don't care about reviews if they can have their favorite celebrity or team in the game, but this is downright exploitative.  This was a gift from a friend some time ago so I thought I'd try it, but this is a glorified mobile game that you pay upfront for.Requires servers to be up in order to do any basic functionality for solo play.Horrible loading times because everything is server side.  Legit you own 10% of the game and the rest of it is stored on their servers.  This also means when they pull the plug, you'll only be able to play certain modes, if that.  I don't even know if you'll be able to play campaign when they do that.  If you finish a match, every single time you have to go through a screen takes 3+ seconds, including results, exp, level-ups, etc.  This means you can spend 15-30 seconds just finishing a match and if you're trying to max out a custom character (on about 90-120 / 180 of the Single-Player skill enhancement mode nodes being matches), that can add up, especially if you have to go at the same one multiple times."Special Offers" that aren't functional anymore because it's been abandoned.  Idk if these were limited-time items (I wouldn't put it past them), but that makes it so much worse if it was and not just price reduction on already available items.Special "locker" codes that expire (which most, if not all already have).Able to buy in-game currency for shortcuts.With the possible exception of loading times since mobile games have advanced far enough to not have multi-second loading times on a decent, stable connection, everything I described is pretty much what a mobile game does, but on PC.If sports fans are really this gullible, then ♥♥♥♥, maybe I should start making sports games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a glorified mobile game. The campaign is repetitive, with very little in the way of rewards. In-game currency comes far too slowly to efficiently unlock everything but the characters - some of the vanity items e.g. taunts, a piece of clothing for your CAW (Create-A-Wrestler) etc. cost more than some of the characters! Character move sets are practically the same except for signatures/finishers although there's even some overlap there. It's also littered with bugs that have been reported since launch and remain unfixed; CPU heat meter not going down after a reversal, the game not recognising some of the moves the crowd call for, the crowd calling for a submission at the start of a match etc. I don't have experience with online mode - I couldn't find any matches when I tried. Playing against a friend can be fun but again, there's so little variation that you quickly become bored. If you're looking for a successor to WWE All Stars, this isn't it. It may look like it but it's nowhere close to it in gameplay, variety or value. It feels like nothing more or less than a pathetic attempt at a cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: This is where I find issues with these big licenses in games. 2K clearly has a license for WWE and thought, "Hmm, we should try to make as much money as possible out of this so let's just make an OK game with a popular IP and monetize the hell out of it!" I hope you like using one of the wrestlers that are unlocked from the start because there's a lot locked behind paywalls. Don't worry though, they all play the exact same anyway. The game has 0 depth to the combat. The tutorial teaches you two combos, punch-punch-punch and kick-kick-kick. In case you couldn't figure those out... You have to keep up with these basic moves to build up meters before you can use your special abilities. They do look fun but it just feels tedious to keep using these basic attacks until you're allowed to use the stronger attacks. It's not like other wrestling games where you want to start with punches, then move on to body slams, then use your special. I'd say the game is eye candy but that's strictly for the animations. _childDocuments_.review: "WWE 2K Battlegrounds" is a departure from the traditional WWE 2K series, offering a more arcade-style experience compared to its simulation-focused predecessors. Here's a breakdown based on its reception:**Gameplay**: - **Arcade Style**: It's designed to be more accessible and less realistic than previous WWE 2K titles, focusing on over-the-top action and exaggerated moves.- **Controls**: Simplified controls make it easier for casual players to pick up and play, with a focus on combos and special moves.**Graphics and Presentation**: - **Cartoonish Graphics**: The game features a cartoonish art style with exaggerated character models and environments, giving it a unique visual appeal.- **Animations**: Character animations are fluid and lively, contributing to the game's arcade feel.**Modes and Content**: - **Game Modes**: Includes various modes such as Campaign, Exhibition, and Online multiplayer, offering a variety of ways to play alone or with friends.- **Customization**: Players can customize characters with different outfits and special abilities, adding depth to gameplay.**Reception**:- **Mixed Reviews**: Reception has been mixed, with praise for its accessibility and fun factor but criticism for its lack of depth compared to previous WWE 2K titles.- **Repetitiveness**: Some reviewers noted that gameplay can become repetitive over time due to the simplified mechanics and limited variety in match types.**Overall**: - **Casual Appeal**: It appeals more to casual players and fans of arcade-style games rather than hardcore wrestling simulation enthusiasts.- **Fun Factor**: Despite its shortcomings, many players find it enjoyable for quick gaming sessions and multiplayer fun.In conclusion, "WWE 2K Battlegrounds" offers a refreshing take on WWE gaming with its arcade-style approach and cartoonish presentation. While it may not satisfy everyone looking for a deep wrestling simulation experience, it provides a fun and accessible alternative with its over-the-top action and multiplayer modes.

_childDocuments_.review: So just to start off, this game is fun but still needs some work. I've always been a fan of unlocking new things by playing the game. That is why I was a fan of Smackdown vs Raw because you could unlock legends and special arenas by just playing the game and doing specific things. In this game, there really isn't anything hidden, but you do have to complete the Campaign in order to unlock everything. I feel that this makes it enjoyable. I have completed the campaign now and I actually really enjoyed it. Although the story was cheesy at times, I felt that it was still pretty enjoyable. As of right now, the campaign has been the best part for me. That is where I have had the most fun mainly because of what I said above, I love having to unlock stuff by playing the game. Now, some of the negatives are that it does get pretty repetitive since a lot of the wrestlers do pretty much the same thing. All of the superstars fall within the 5 categories (Powerhouse, Brawler, Technician, High-Flyer, and All-Rounder). All of the powerhouse wrestlers have the same moves, all of the brawlers have the same moves, and so on. I think that every superstar has a unique Finisher and maybe one more move, but that is about it. But honestly, I expected this and I feel that everyone should have expected this. The roster in this game is huge, and it will only get bigger as they release more in the future. And in games where the roster tends to be big, the fighters are not really unique. It would just be A LOT for them to make each wrestler unique. But now don't get me wrong, I do wish each wrestler was unique and was hoping for this, but it is understandable.  Now for some other things I noticed is that there are some slight bugs. During some of the fights during the campaign, the frames would drop drastically and the whole screen would freeze and stutter. This probably happened 3 or 4 times I would say and only happened when I used a weapon. Another thing is that some of the animations tend to be off. There is a reversal animation where the wrestler teleports to the persons back somehow. But this wasn't as bad the frame drops. A last bug I noticed is that I did not get any of the achievements even though I completed them all. When I go to check my achievements, the game doesn't even pop up. So I am not sure what the issue is there. When it comes to online and exhibition, I think was pretty underwhelming. If you had a group of 4 friends, then doing a 2v2 or fatal four way would be fun. But other than that the game is meh. My friend and I both bought the game, but he ended up getting refund since he didn't enjoy it much. Once you have played each mode once, its just not as fun. On top of that, you cannot play royal rumble online with a friend, you cannot team up with your friend and fight against other people, and you cannot do the gauntlet online with a friend. Its pretty limited. You can create superstars and arenas which is pretty cool. You can play through the Battleground Challenge to better your created superstar, but as I said, it will be very repetitive and it will take you some time to complete the Battleground challenge, so it will be a grind.Overall, this game is probably a 7/10 for me. I would advise people to get the regular version of the game or waiting until it is on sale. The deluxe does not really add much other than Edge and the "store" has three things that you could buy. So the golden wwe coins aren't really necessary. I am happy with the game and don't regret the purchase, but I don't think it was worth the $40.

_childDocuments_.review: and now onto the short review//intro//What is up comrades, MF Kraven here once again with another less than 10 mins review. Today I take a look at WWE 2K Battlegrounds, an over the top fast paced arcade action game starring your fav... alright you know what? I can't do a normal review on this because this game is TERRIBLE. It is a  40 dollar game with a F2P foundation. You get a handful of superstars and need to unlock the rest of the roster with in game currency or PREMIUM currency. Believe me when I say, I am an E-Drone. Sound is phenomenal and the inclusion of many of our favorite WWE theme songs are in the game even though the game does a terrible job with entrances.//Gameplay//Monotous button mashing and terrible block system make Battlegrounds a game I couldn't get invested in. _childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the kind of game I was looking for. An easy to pick up and play game that allows one to have some fun with their favorite wrestlers. I can't wait to have my kids and wife play along with me. We will have some epic matches. Do I wish there were more match types such as ladder or TLC? Yes. Could they be added later on? I sure hope so. But for what the game is and the amount of unlockable content at launch I would say it's worth money. There are micro transactions and I understand that being a bit overkill for the price that this game costs. However you don't have to pay anything extra. The micro transactions are there for those people that are impatient about unlocking everything and just want to get the wrestlers and content immediately vs actually playing the game and unlocking it. Is it a grind yes, but for me, its way more fun to unlock something by playing the game and spending the time learning how to get better at the game than just have everyone instantly because I can pay the money. I do want to make one thing clear. This game is not meant to be taken seriously. It's not a simulation game. Its meant to have fun and be silly. Just like NBA Playgrounds its an arcade game that brings back the thrill of old skool arcade classics like Wrestlemania and All Stars. Just like NBA Playgrounds was bringing back the playful silliness and easy controls of NBA Jam. It's a great game and one that anyone, no matter their age can pick up a controller and play around and have some fun with. The comments that this game is lacking content or movesets or anything like that, while warranted from a perspective of them wanting a game more like No Mercy or NWO/WCW Revenge that isn't what the studio was going for. I am definitely looking forward to playing more of this game and seeing what else the devs have in store for post launch updates.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost. Unlike WWE 2K20's release this game hasn't crashed on me constantly while playing. Thank you 2K.You shouldn't play this game with a keyboard, it's a console title so a controller is strongly recommended. The controls for this game are different from those one is used to from the WWE 2KXX games. Takes a little to adjust but it's not too hard to get a basic match running. The special moves however need to be looked into in the menu sometimes.I tried out several modes, I have alot of fun playing the game.There's Battleground challenges where you can strenghten your own character.There's Exhibition Mode (for male and female superstars seperatly) where you can play different match types.There's King of the Battleground, an online mode where you have to try to be the person that has spent the longest time inside the ring (I haven't tried online yet)There's Campaign which tells a story in comic book style about an idea Paul Heyman pitches to Vince. To create a new WWE brand with unknowns, amateurs and everyday heroes and pitting them against WWE superstars in the so called "Battlegrounds".And then there's daily challenges. 3 Challenges per day where you earn ingame currency. Which leads me to the downside of the game. The game has alot of ingame microtransactions. Some of the roster isn't unlocked (eg. Carmella, Nikki Cross, ...). You need to spend ingame currency to unlock them. I mean for legends I'd say okay, but for current roster superstars? To me a little annoying. Like I said you can earn ingame currency from daily challenges and each match you play also earns you ingame currency. But you can also buy premium currency for real money if you don't have the patience to grind for the ingame currency. A big no no for me.Alltogether however I have not been able to find a flaw beside this. It might be a little overpriced for what it is okay, but I have alot of fun playing this game. I enjoy the comic story mode. I enjoy brawling in this new arcade style WWE game.And that's the bottom line, because ... you know the rest ;)

_childDocuments_.review: So, let's sum up my morning with this game...I had characters glitch out of animations in carrying grapples, finishers, punch/kick combos and once on a turnbuckle dive. Also, sudden frame-rate drops which seem to be periodical, happening for a minute or two about every 15-30 minutes (i5 9300, GTX 1650, 16GB RAM}. Movesets are a bit shallow, with no customization options as it seems. You get moves based on your character's type and that's it. Some characters have an added unique movies, like Charlotte's Spear, but it gets old quite quickly.On the other hand, models look good and you don't have to spend a dime on unlocking (daily challenges, "story"...) despite having an option to do so. Controls are something to get used to a little bit, especially if you only played 2Kxx games until now. Story is comic-book-ish and enjoyable (SCSA and Heyman trying to bring something new to WWE). Haven't tried online, but as it seems from other reviews, you probably can't play 2v2 with just one friend and find other players online. Overall, it's been fun and can be a good party game. Don't expect 2Kxx level of customization and moveset layers. That's not what the game is meant to be, even tho I'd like to have a couple more moves at my disposal. PS: I requested (and got) a refund for above mentioned tech issues. Hopefully, a patch will be out soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Thankfully I didn't pay full price for this game.  I got it in a humble bundle sale.  I cannot imagine spending 40 dollars let alone 50 for the deluxe version.  On the surface it seems goofy and kinda fun.   Sort of a NBA Jam style WWE game.  I am totally all for that!  Then as you start playing the real nature of the game shows.It wants your money.At least with NBA Playground 2, you have the option to buy the characters instead of chancing it out in blind card packs.in WWE Battlegrounds? Sure you can play the single player to unlock a fair amount of the in game currency, however that is finite as you only get said currency once per story mode missions.  Meaning once you beat all the missions, you are only able to get the currency mostly through playing online.  Here is the problem...Most are going to be using their custom wrestlers.  You can unlock a skilltree and upgrade for each wrestler you make.  How do you upgrade? The in game currency, which more than likely you spent mostly to get characters.  OR! You have the option to pay about a dollar per 100 points or "bucks" and use that to unlock the skill tree.  About 30 dollars per custom wrestler.  That means most people are going to pay real money to upgrade their character to make them strong enough to go online....this means why bother using a wrestler you make till it is upgraded fully.  Or spending the money to do so, but most people you face will be doing the same.  In the end, it all means nothing. it counteracts each other.  Also the story mode difficulty spike is almost mind blowing in its increase.  This game acts like a free to play cell phone game.  Even the multiplayer "tournaments" have that vibe, especially how they deliver out the rewards. Of course you can always pay real money to increase your odds, but there really isn't much use in doing that.  Overall like most games of this type, it is a never ending circle, and feels very stagnant.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge disappointment:As a huge fan of fighting games this is easily one of the worst I've ever played, not to mention the ugliest. For starters, playing this game is an absolute chore. Everything is designed to waste your time. Load times are unusually long, dialogue menus take forever to give you the option to close them, intros (can be skipped) are just 15 seconds of your character standing around, and because the game requires nonstop-internet connectivity, purchasing upgrades takes 10 seconds per upgrade. There are over 40 upgrades per character, you do the math...Microtransaction city:This is a $40 game and it is RIDDLED with microtransactions. They say that everything can be purchased with in game currency which is true, but it's all priced ridiculously high. I have 14 hours in this game which got me to level 23 and 100% the campaign which comes tons of rewards. I probably got around 80k in game currency total, if that. One single outfit costs 12k. The packs which rotate each day are 12-20k. Keep in mind that I finished the campaign so from now on if I kept playing, I would have to level to get currency. You get around 300 per win and 1k per level, averaging a level up every 5-10 fights after level 20.Worst AI ever:The AI in this game is a joke. The first 2/3 of the campaign is an absolute breeze, then when you meet Ember Moon suddenly the AI gets turned up to a 10 where every move you throw will be blocked and countered. Think Shao Kahn in the old MK days. On top of this, the superstars HP gets buffed to a point where matches will take 10 minutes, especially in 3 way fights where every time you try to pin someone for the win, the other ai will get up and come punch you in the back of the head. Cheese strats are the way to win against the AI 99% of the time. They have very strict coding which is why if you're ever in invincibility frames while getting up and they have super meter you'll hear the *SHING* sound 50x back to back as they desperately try to grab you the second you get up. Once I realized this, I realized that I could simply throw them, help them up, and throw them until they were dead. They'll never counter you will full super, they always want to use it on a super move.The story:Who was this game made for? One might assume WWE fans but the entire story consists of boomer superstars going HEY BROTHER ITS ME FAMOUS WRESTLE MAN IM THE BEST KID YOU'LL NEVER BEAT ME HA IM TOO GOOD then you, a literal nobody who Steve Austin recruited (because he's trying to make the avengers of normies for WWE BATTLE ROYALE) just beat the hell out of them immediately. Imagine being a Dwayne the Rock Johnson fan, hyped to play as the Rock and then your first fight as this HACKERMAN wannabe is beating him down without any story at all. It just makes the WWE stars look even more out of touch and sadder than they already are. Literally one of the scenes in the game involves one of them crapping themselves because "nobody told me not to drink the water in Mexico." What...The art:You can see the screenshots for yourself. Whoever designed the art for this game should be tried in court for violations against the Geneva Convention. Playing this game without a blindfold is like willingly faceslamming yourself into a pile of broken glass. The worst part is that the textures are amazing so this game could've looked really good if they hadn't made everyone looks like uncanny valley dwarves.FINAL SCORE:[1/10]The one is because I was able to make Shrek in a bathrobe and KO my opponents in 3 hits due to a fully upgraded skill tree. On second thought, that just proves how P2W this game is. -0.5FINAL SCORE 2:[0.5/10]

name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain
detailed_description: Broken Porcelain brings an abundance of welcome changes to the series, introducing new gameplay and storytelling elements that breathe new life into the characters and an unprecedented level of immersion in this haunting adventure – perfect for both new and returning fans to the series. The truths buried in the Ashmann Inn will not be discovered easily - its many mysteries are intertwined and guarded by the looming threat of the stalkers, powerful hunters trapped in time and the confines of its walls. Survival will take more than just quick reactions as a strategic and resourceful approach will quickly become critical in this haunting adventure. Be smart - knowing the best time to sneak, flee or fight imminent dangers can quickly make the hunters become the hunted. Thrilling Psychological Plot. The award-winning cult classic Remothered returns in Broken Porcelain, the perfect entry point for new fans discovering the franchise as well as series veterans craving additional lore surrounding the events and characters of Tormented Fathers. Realistic Survival Horror. The Ashmann Inn is as rich in resources as it is dangers. Cautiously scour the environment for items to aid your exploration of unsettling locations that hide grave secrets of a terrifying past. Intense Stealth Gameplay. Roam among the shadows of Ashmann Inn and use everything at your disposal to distract enemies for a resourceful escape. Investigate and Escape. Challenging puzzles, expanded lore, and a haunting soundtrack by composer Luca Balboni (Remothered: Tormented Fathers, Mine, Watch Them Fall) transforms the dark and gloomy atmosphere into a terrifying experience that will haunt players well after the game is over. Captivating Characters. The roster of charismatic characters grows as fan favorites return to meet all the new additions to the cast inspired by the protagonists of horror classics. Real-Time Cinematics. In a series first, fully animated real-time cinematics will breathe new life into the characters and world of Remothered for an unprecedented level of immersion. Directed by Chris Darril.

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered: Broken Porcelain contains, without hyperbole, one of the most obtusely designed gameplay segments I have ever experienced in a video game. Now, most of the game's enemies attack by chasing you down until they can grab you and attempt to finish you off, but the game's second stalker, Mr. Ashmann, is different - Ashmann has a gun. This lets him continuously damage you and potentially even kill you as he closes in, forcing you to take cover or break line of sight as soon as he's on your trail. The scene where you're introduced to Ashmann as an enemy begins by zooming in on a fire extinguisher in his office. Your character will exclaim something to the effect of "if I use that fire extinguisher, maybe I can stand a chance." This fire extinguisher can be used to spray Ashmann and stun him at close range, which is a decent enough way to get some breathing room if he gets in too close. At this point of the game, your objective is given as "Defeat Mr. Ashmann." In the chase sequence immediately before this, the player is taught that defeating a stalker entails sneaking up on them and stabbing them with a one-use defense item, then running and hiding until the enemy's alert has lowered enough to do it again. The player has access to the entire map they've explored up to this point during their confrontation with Mr. Ashmann. However, despite being able to scour the map for screwdrivers and spades to jam into Ashmann's back to your heart's content, doing the thing the game taught you to do in the chase immediately before this one won't work. Ashmann will never stay down, no matter how many times you ambush him, because the objective to "Defeat Mr. Ashmann" is a lie. This is actually a scripted loss sequence, where continuing requires to to get caught by Ashmann after stunning him twice with the fire extinguisher. If he gets close enough to catch you BEFORE you've sprayed him twice, he'll just throw you to the side before continuing to shoot you to death. He'll still shoot at you as he approaches AFTER you've stunned him with the fire extinguisher, meaning that you're still at risk of being killed once you've failed in the specific way the game wants you to. Only once you've stunned Ashmann twice and then allowed him to grab you without getting yourself riddled with gunfire will he pistol-whip you instead, allowing you to continue the game. This is a sequence that drags itself out the longer you successfully engage the mechanics the game taught you to use to accomplish a false objective you just learned how to do the right way, and exists entirely to provide an unspoken tutorial on using the fire extinguisher.This is the only time a fire extinguisher ever appears in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game mainly focuses on Jennifer's story taking place in the '70s we also get to take control of Reed who I understand was the main protagonist of the previous episode, . There is a nice recap video when starting a new game and a text-based version is also available in the menus so I didn't have an issue with playing  not having tried its predecessor, at all.This is a bit of a mess with exploring one's real identity, brainwashing, moths, hypnosis, raping and experiments related to an important drug called Phenoxyl. At the beginning you see Jennifer as your typical rebellious teenager who serves as a maid in a hotel resort but for some reason she is attacked by Andrea, the head maid. Following your failed escape attempt you see Andrea act completely normal - and this is where you start suspecting there is some sort of hypnosis going on in the background. Things will only get messy later.The game has a lot of cutscenes which gives it a cinematic appeal though I find  a game with a lot of unnecessary cursing. A couple of playthroughs will be required to get all achievements - maxing out all your abilities and finding all collectibles can be a pain. As a decision is given to you at the end you can say we are presented with two endings.While Jennifer can use melee weapons to attack her pursuers they have to be approached stealthily. Some chapters require us to fight while others do not. The concept the game uses is a hit-and-miss. Whilst I appreciate that once you are noticed you can still flee and hide in lockers, wardrobes and closets in certain cases it's better to restart from a checkpoint. A notable area is the restaurant where you have 3 enemies and even if only one is patrolling once he gets sight of you the others are warned, too. Hats-off if you can escape all three.You can find a lot of items when opening cupboards, drawers. They are either throwables (good for generating noise and also for hurting enemies) or they are used only for diversion (you can use radios, alarm clocks and dolls for this purpose). I guess crafting is mandatory even if you play a non-open-world game nowadays. Your defensive melee weapons and the items used for diversion can be upgraded once. If you apply flour you can get a blinding effect or get an ammonia bottle for stunning etc. Your inventory is limited and the upgrades are never game changer. At the beginning there is some tutorial on the controls but crafting is not really explained so the system requires some getting used to. See crafting. Unnecessary. Using moths (this is the so-called  ability Jennifer has) can highlight important area and can stun enemies for a short time. Story-wise using  is interesting when it is required for puzzle solving. Moth keys are scattered across the mansion and finding them allows you to improve Jennifer's skills such as better health recovery, sprinting faster or using the aforementioned ability more efficiently. I needed to open a guide to find out how to upgrade my skills as the game never explains it. Special moth chests can be used for this purpose while mirrors with metronomes are used for saving the game. is an interesting game with great soundtrack and voice acting but with a messy story and mediocre gameplay. I read it is an improvement following  but this is exactly the reason why I do not intend to play that one. It is a good game for passing some time while you don't have anything better to play in your library of stealth-based games.

_childDocuments_.review: They really emphasized the 'Broken' in 'Broken Porcelain'.Story, soundtrack, and character design is absolutely fantastic and a literal 10/10, but with how buggy it is I would say it is unplayable. This game had a lot of potential but the gameplay mechanics and level design simply bogs down the rest of the game so much it is hard to recommend still. All of what I said is a 10/10 but it really makes the argument that they could've made this a novel instead because the unique aspect of the medium adds nothing to it, and in fact hinders it. The stealth is awkard and janky, the world is tiny little areas that are more cinematic than fun to navigate unlike the original, and overall it was clearly a rushed project with not enough direction outside of the story, which again is great. _childDocuments_.review: This game is about filthy girls who just won't do their chores.But more seriously it feels like a love letter to Italian 80s Giallo movies and specifically Dario Argento's Phenomena and Suspiria, which were also an inspiration for Clock Tower and Haunting Ground. So, if you like those things, you'll probably enjoy this game.My complain is a lack of synth music.edit: So I've played through it 3 times now. Initial play to just enjoy the game and 2 more times to get all the achievements. I absolutely love this game. More than 1st part. So I want to address some of negative reviews. There are a number of complains about stealth mechanics and bugs. It crashed for me just once when I was alt-tabing a bunch from full screen mode to a item location guide. That's all and that's not unusual, maybe engine's problem rather than game's. Could be that it was patched recently. About stealth: it is not Metal Gear, that's true, however I thought it was fine. Stabbing can be a bit wonky but you can play through the whole game without stabbing anyone. I think developers intended for people to explore the house and craft items rather than try to just sneak up and stab enemies. When you stun an enemy with an item stabbing works fine. Maybe it could have been communicated better - that you should stun an enemy if you want to stab it. While milking achievements I also discovered some unexpected mechanics, e.g. enemies can hurt each other and you can knock out two guys with one stun grenade so for me even getting that 50 stab achievement was fun. So don't think of this game as Metal Gear and enjoy story and atmosphere and if you come from 1st part, think of this as Aliens to Alien or Terminator 2 to Terminator - less horror, more action and plot twists.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to say that I'm just disappointed, but no, I'm actually angry at this one.Not only did the release date on this game get moved up, but it got moved up despite obviously not being ready for prime time. Yes, I didn't play the first game (which I do give credit for having the summary video), but the game is not only a technical mess, but it's a nightmare of gameplay and design decisions. It's almost like there was no direction in how to handle the game, as a loose set of features and ideas came together in what may be my worst experience since The Quiet Man. Yes. That Quiet Man.The game looks nice, and the storytelling being so off the wall adds to the horror experience. There's some good voice actors here. That's about all I'll say positively.The game is a mess. Glitches. Bugs. No kind of introduction to mechanics that obviously you need to know.  Inconsistency rule sets about how enemies are damaged, and when they hear you or not. Unclear factors about how the world works for and against you. Inconsistent rules in story that makes you question if the first draft of the script was actually the final one. Weird physics glitches where hair will float and make you think that you're now in a true ghost story. Gameplay that's frustrating in all the bad ways. For a game that is 30 dollars in total.Look, I'm not mincing words, there's too many overlooked horror and indie games as a whole for this game to even get a second glance from anyone. Do. Not. Buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered , out in 2018, managed to shake people's core through shocking plot, gasps, whilst enveloping the players in dread and grating atmosphere. You can imagine my jaw-dropping (not for the reason you'd think) when after two years of hype, anticipation via effective marketing- that Broken Porcelain was finally released to a shattered state... Are there any parts intact from criticism?You are Jennifer, a delinquent teenager serving as a maid at the Ashmann Inn as part of her rehabilitation. It's just another day of renovating and maintaining the building interiors when the staff and your colleagues start acting strange. Before you know it, a haunting whistling tune has sounded, everything goes to hell from there.Gameplay is steadily improved upon! Jennifer, being the rebel young'n- she is more agile and has the good sense of self-preservation to take cover from stalkers. She could even vault over certain railings, counters and tunnel through little vent gaps or under tables to evade the grabby pursuers. Speaking of, certain parts will pit Jen against multiple enemies at once! But worry not, the previous weapon-specific upgrade stations have been expanded; skill tree for enhancing overall attributes like stamina, QTE difficulty, "luck" and so on. There's even a real-time crafting menu for giving weapon boons to deal damage, blind or stun~ The two leads truly light up the stage whenever they're onscreen. Jen's a sensible, badass who knows how to get in-out of trouble whereas Linn is more reserved, and aspires to be a musician. Atmosphere-wise, the setting has much potential with the inn based on hotel interiors of The Shining, down to the snowy weather. Smaller in scale than the grand Felton manor, but still foreboding enough to welcome other locations too. But the winner is the score accompanying the plot. The orchestra killin' it on all counts!! Being a sequel and prequel is no easy feat. The first did this by not mentioning the timeline at all. But here, the game does a great job of losing your sense of time. You can take a stab here and there, but it was fuzzy for the most part. There's also the endearing love story of two teens' leap into adulthood and picturing lives beyond servitude. It's like a mix of an Alfred Hitchcock film, its suspense playing us like a fiddle and a typical modern day horror. Broken Porcelain's plot is probably the only tradition untainted by Chris Darril~ The first was horror in its true, pure form. This time the surface, shallow scares are less riveting but profound nonetheless because it's a treatise on the human condition. Continuing on the most prominent theme that is the frailty of memory. Lest not forget the aspect of time, which is a harsh mistress and the saying "time waits for no (wo)man" is thoroughly devastating, reminding you that once it passes, you cannot regain it back try as you might or hope... The glitches blew chunks on the enjoyment I could've had. Bearable at first but eventually I took to Twitter to post any bug footage I could find. I swear the door peeking mechanic was broken for the first week alone... Most of these have been applied insecticide but left a permanent imprint. Plagued with 90% negative reviews a few days after the launch date and now 50% mixed (thank the bugs). You wonder why Broken Porcelain was pushed forward a week in advance at the sorry state it was in. Was there a lack of communication somehow? Shortage of play-testers?? Did they all overdose on Phenoxyl?!!The game was a big oopsie from the beginning tutorial. You can be a master of the genre but . The first did nothing of the kind. Instead you'd do well to hide any chance you get because only the sweet release of death awaited.. I'd be totally okay if this game did it once but three times, what an overkill. Which leads me to the "horror" which basically amounts to a bunch of false scares or done in awfully awkward manner like the. The classical sting that accompany them will condition you to instinctively conjure an eye-roll every time. As if a pre-sequel couldn't be more obnoxious, the mainstream approach to its combat fine-tuning has rendered this game even further from its horror roots. Stealth is near sporadic, detection radius enemies have make hiding is almost impossible. The controls don't soften the blow either, with the "cover" mechanic coming and going as it pleases. You can enter the stance but only if you're facing the object directly, no angles allowed!  Who seriously thought a Beyond Two Souls inspired "Aiden" mechanic be added in? Sure it's useful for scouting ahead but it sucks the intensity by highlighting enemies and even summon swarms that the stalker has to shoo. Little did I know being a moth would be so disorienting.Don't know if it's intentional but free will is endlessly being wrestled from you. Forced walking segments, more times than I could bear. Even a normal stalker became an unavoidable showdown, where you're pitted against already uneven stealth mechanics. Boss battles- I feel I need to stress on this (OG. HAD. ONE) give or take, that's it and it's more memorable!! The pacing is scathingly questionable because it either does too much too fast, like the multiple stalkers who come at you in a line and you feel like you've experienced everything the combat has to offer.Finally, exposition. Keep in mind, the OG had healthy doses of vague mysteries culminating in a awe-filled reveal only at the end. But here, the exposition comes in phases, each time with more jargon than you can imagine and does not one but TWO big twists. I want to point out everything executed perfectly in the OG was recycled here and given fertilizer so they multiply!! Can I say I love Rosemary's return but changing her voice actress is a crime worse than death! In fact, all the dialogue suffers from some stilted or overacted intonation. Jen's a wild card, sometimes she conveys the emotions so well but few seconds later, she gets too into it and every line is delivered too (perfectly). In essence, Remothered: Broken Porcelain is aptly named given the countless bugs that infested its launch, even until now... Above all, it failed to live up to the bar set too high by its predecessor in more ways than one. Delivering a harrowing and divided experience that's more irritating than it was scary. However, should you persevere and overlook its many-many flaws, the fractured state is saved by the innovative art direction, composition and complicated plot that makes you reflect. HARD. With themes not typically discussed, much less in horror or with such artistic flair.Not forgetting the female leads, fantastically voiced and written- it was a cinch to fall in love and care for them. Lot of effort invested in streamlining the combat; not that it helped reel in their horror target audience. Held back from design choices with poor stalker encounters that manage to not only neutralize the threats but also ruin any note of immersion. It's safe to say that Broken Porcelain is the crack introduced to the Remothered series, so tread carefully at the risk of breaking more hearts.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't actually regret playing this game, but I cannot in good conscience give it a recommendation. I really wanted to learn the rest of the story and it delivers in that respect. The graphics are nice, but the atmosphere is not as nightmarish as the first game. The hotel is not that big and there is very little sense of exploration. The chapters are quite linear and you are often limited to a small area.The gameplay is not fun at all and the stealth is terrible. You are often in very frustrating situations like hiding in a restaurant with 3 stalkers. Or being chased around a small locker room and not being able to hide because the stalker saw you and you can't run away. Whenever I managed to hide in a closet, I found the mouse mini-game to be impossible, at least until I upgraded that skill (even then it was much harder than in the 1st game). Item management is extremely frustrating. You often don't see clearly what kind of item you are about to pick up because it is covered by the mouse icon. And once you pick it up you just drop something from your inventory. Anyway, I ended up almost never using any item except when absolutely required.Most of the time I found myself wishing this game would simply be a walking simulator. This is a captivating story trapped in a bad game.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: Another Remothered, using the same horrible gameplay mechanics and "improving" by replacing unique icons (hiding place, weapon, etc.) by a generic one.You click and just hope it'll do what you expect.And during the chase scenes (90% of the game), you can no longer spot the hiding places because they all have the same generic icon.That's not how "improved" a sequel should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: By offering a prequel to his horror-psychological game, Chris Darril has the merit of bringing us a little more precision on the story, while putting a final touch to Rosemary Reed's adventures. _childDocuments_.review: Remothered: Broken Porcelain has a great plot, but unfortunately, the way the story is told is a mess. The storytelling is uneven, with some moments being pretty good, but others not so much.While the graphics in the game look amazing, the lip sync, movement, shadows, and lighting inside the mouth are disastrous. The game is also a bit buggy, and the animation of the character is not present as they move or run.The game only takes six hours to complete, but I regret the time I’ve spent on it.Overall, the game has a wasted potential for a sequel due to its poorly executed storytelling, disappointing gameplay, and frustrating bugs. While the graphics are impressive, they cannot make up for the game's numerous shortcomings.In conclusion, while Remothered: Broken Porcelain has a promising plot, the game falls short due to its lackluster execution. The game's bugs, poorly executed gameplay, and uneven storytelling make it a frustrating experience, and players may ultimately regret the time they spent playing it.
