_childDocuments_.review: I want to avoid review bombing here so Ill start by saying that I love the Total War series and Warhammer breathed new life into the game. Watching my puny humans stand against Orc invasions, or Undead masses win or lose, is extremely satisfying and thematic experience. Watching a giant fire tornado tear through an army is fun. Firing rat-made artillery into a sea of elite Elvin warriors as they slaughter slave-rats is funThat being said the game is currently not getting the support it needs, 4-6 months for patch to fix the content i just bought is enough to put me off. If you're new to Total War and Creative Assembly they have a habit of releasing broken/unsupported content at full price and then maybe eventually getting around to fixing it, TW:Rome II [2013] at launch for example. This in mind I can't recommend this game or its DLC at anywhere near full price.If you're going to pick up one of the games in this trilogy i recommend TW: Warhammer II no Kislev, Demons, or Cathay but hey, mods exist and there are a lot of great ones. _childDocuments_.review: This has to be the most frustrating game in existence. No, not because of difficulty... There are so many great improvements, and yet every single one of them is ruined by some other issue. I have over 9000 hours in TWWH2. I loved that game so much. The only complaint I think I ever had, and it was only a minor thing, was sieges were a little dull.Now, sieges are simply awful. The pop up tower defense game that they have turned into is just plain terrible. I hate everything about it. It doesn't graphically look right, nor add anything interesting to the battle. They are just an annoyance that feels really out of place and makes the game look silly. This is especially annoying since the maps themselves are amazing. Why add this dumb mechanic? Who ever thought it up should be fired immediately. Then there is the level cap increase. I have no issue with this overall, but the fact that heroes often don't have enough skills to spend the points on? What the heck? You NEED a mod to make use of those points, or a skill dump... That's just pathetic. Another point of contention for me is the check boxes for notifications. I don't understand why these setting cannot be saved. Every single campaign I have uncheck a number of these that are useless and annoying. I know that sounds like a very minor thing, but its annoying. Likewise with unsaved camera setting. Modders found a way, but CA can't?Then there is balance... Or more accurately there isn't. Every unit seems wildly unbalanced in ways that continue to shock me. There are far to many units to go through to explain this in detail. But it needs a lot of work in this regard. Another issue is the new magic system. It makes no sense at all. The old system was great, why change it? Finally there is performance. Its horrible. This game runs absolutely terrible on any settings. _childDocuments_.review: Total War: Warhammer III Review: A Fun, Memorable Experience with a Daunting CampaignScore: 8.5/10Creative Assembly’s Total War: Warhammer III is a grand strategy game that successfully blends the expansive lore of Warhammer Fantasy with the deep tactical gameplay of the Total War series. It delivers a visually stunning and strategically rich experience that fans of both franchises will find deeply satisfying. However, its epic campaign, while immersive and rewarding, can be lengthy and cumbersome, making it a challenge for players to see through to the end.Gameplay and Mechanics: 9/10Total War: Warhammer III excels in offering complex and engaging gameplay. Players command vast armies, manage cities, and engage in diplomacy as they strive for dominance in a richly detailed fantasy world. The game features a diverse array of factions, each with unique units, abilities, and playstyles, ensuring that every campaign feels fresh and different. The real-time battles are thrilling, with a blend of tactical depth and visual spectacle that few other games can match.The addition of new mechanics, such as the Realm of Chaos and survival battles, adds further depth and variety to the gameplay. The strategic layer is complemented by a robust AI, which provides challenging and unpredictable opponents, keeping players on their toes.Visuals and Art Design: 9.5/10Visually, Total War: Warhammer III is a feast for the eyes. The game’s detailed unit models, stunning battlefields, and grandiose magic effects bring the Warhammer world to life in spectacular fashion. The art design captures the dark, fantastical aesthetic of Warhammer Fantasy perfectly, making every faction and environment feel distinct and atmospheric. The attention to detail, from the intricate armor of units to the sprawling cities, enhances the immersive experience.Sound and Music: 9/10The sound design in Total War: Warhammer III is top-notch. The game’s orchestral score, composed by Richard Beddow, perfectly complements the epic scale of the battles and the dark fantasy setting. Voice acting is strong across the board, with distinct and memorable performances for each faction leader. The sound effects, from the clash of swords to the roar of monsters, further enhance the immersion and bring the battlefield to life.Campaign Experience: 7/10While the campaign in Total War: Warhammer III is richly detailed and offers a deep and rewarding experience, it can also be lengthy and cumbersome. The sheer scope of the game means that campaigns can take dozens of hours to complete, which can be daunting for some players. The Realm of Chaos mechanic, while adding an interesting narrative element, can sometimes feel like a repetitive grind, interrupting the flow of the campaign.Managing an empire across multiple fronts, dealing with constant threats, and juggling diplomacy and economy can become overwhelming, especially in the late game. This complexity, while part of the game’s appeal, can also lead to fatigue, making it challenging to maintain momentum and see the campaign through to its conclusion.Conclusion:Total War: Warhammer III is a grand strategy masterpiece that offers a memorable and engaging experience. Its deep gameplay, stunning visuals, and rich lore make it a standout title in both the Total War series and the Warhammer universe. However, the lengthy and sometimes cumbersome campaign can be a significant hurdle, requiring a substantial time investment and persistence to complete. Despite these challenges, the game’s strengths far outweigh its flaws, delivering an epic and unforgettable experience for strategy enthusiasts and Warhammer fans alike. With a score of 8.5/10, Total War: Warhammer III stands as a testament to the power of combining grand strategy with fantastical storytelling, even if it demands a lot from its players.

_childDocuments_.review: I need to preface this with the simple fact that I'm not a super duper, hardcore Total War player. With that in mind, I can safely say that I would recommend this game. Like others have said, there are some issues with the game:- The survival battles are interesting, but (in my opinion) they feel like there's still some work that needs to be done on them. They just don't feel like they're at a place that a player would always rather fight than auto resolve in subsequent campaigns.- The mechanics for a few of the factions are honestly just really annoying to keep track of while also dealing with chaos portal corruption and the race to get every flavor of demonic soul.- Extra supply line cost for new armies on top of unit/lord/hero upkeep. I will die on this hill and take everyone down with me.- Technology research trees for some of the races feel incredibly underwhelming and trade is...eh.- Possibly having a "DLC" that only adds in more blood effects and having the audacity to charge money for it. They haven't done it, yet, but we all know it's going to happen.All that being said, I still enjoy the game. They recently added in support for modding, and there's some fun stuff on the workshop to play around with. As someone who only started dipping their toes into both the Warhammer Fantasy and 40k lore a few years ago (because of Total War: Warhammer 1, actually), the stories for the Legendary Lords are interesting, and the prologue was really fun to play through from a narrative perspective. I honestly wish CA would do more narrative driven micro-campaigns like the prologue/what they had in the first TW:WH game with the Beastmen, but I can see where some people might not like it.Tl;Dr - Does it have issues that CA is still hammering out? Yeah. Would I still recommend the game even knowing such issues exist? Yup. Even with the issues it's fun to control armies of fantasy races and smash them into one another.

Will Warhammer 3 require 200 GB when DLCs are released--or are some of those files pre-installed, forcing players to store files that they have not chosen to purchase yet? Either is unacceptable. That was a game they charged everyone 60 dollars with a completely unplayable multiplayer , and they never bothered to fix it, instead discontinuing support for it within a couple of years. _childDocuments_.review: Very Good.THE GOOD:It's not fair to say it like this, but it's a Total War XD, and for some reason, it still has no competition. For some reason, no one comes close in its area. If you want to feel the clash of armies in a strategic, epic, and enjoyable way, you have to buy a Total War, there's no other way. They remain unique in their kind.Very impressive graphics and the optimization in battles surprised me. I play with a 3060 laptop, and honestly, it runs quite well. Some scenarios are simply sensational, the music and overall atmosphere... very epic.Don't be scared of the DLCs; you don't have to spend 100 euros to enjoy the game. I bought the Shadow of Change because it was considered essential to fully enjoy Cathay and Kislev, and honestly, I regret paying the 15 euros because I've only made use of one of the units. I think it adds little content, and most people should stick to the base game, which already has plenty.THE BAD:I'm not a big fan of the new flag capture system; I think it only adds stress and frustration XD.It still has that childish feel that, for me, is totally unnecessary. I can understand wanting to make it kid-friendly, but for me, it would be much better with a more serious, adult, and gritty tone.Charging for the blood DLC has to stop. Paying for that seems ridiculous to me. This game (and any Total War) wouldn't make sense without blood.Despite the good optimization in battles, in the campaign, with the fast turns, it still has some epic lags, which I find very frustrating that it's still not fixed.The well-crafted animations we used to see in Shogun 2 or Rome II have disappeared. Only a few units have "special" animations.There are missing details that would easily take it from Very Good to Excellent, like being able to see your  dynamic settlements functioning normally (not just in battles), changing their appearance depending on the faction that occupies them, the weather conditions in battles as in Pharaoh, more refined animations, more developed narratives (not only the prologue), more complex economy.... Invest a bit of time and effort into the cosmetics to change the appearance of heroes, at least the Armors and Weapons. Seriously, I know there are many different heroes, but come on, you're making millions of dollars. Can't you put someone to work on that?CONCLUSION:It's a great game, to be honest, but I don't know why the developers don't want to reach Excellence. Many details are missing. The game feels like a AAA, of course, don't get me wrong, but I think that with a little more work, it could be a 9.5 or 10, but they decided to stay at 8. They could be Rockstar, but i don't know why they prefer to be Ubisoft XD. I think that big part of the problem is that CA is too accustomed to modders finishing their games, which prevents them from delivering polished products.

_childDocuments_.review: Played over 600 hours of Warhammer 1 & 2. To summarize, Warhammer III is not fun right now. That's the key word and theme of my review. It's a boring, tedious, slog that I cannot even force myself to play. It felt fresh during my first play through but the subsequent play throughs revealed what is wrong with the game currently. I don't care about the graphics, the bugs, or performance issues, I only care about the gameplay which will be the hardest for CA to fix. Problems:-- Minor settlement battles constitute 90% of all battles and they are truly the worst part of Warhammer 3. You will be attacking them almost once per turn, They are narrow extremely repetitive, time consuming, and not fun AT ALL. Only after a few hundred hours did I feel there were too many field battles in WH2 but after seeing how atrocious the minor settlement siege battles are in WH3. I would gladly take the former because at least with field battles you can innovate, have more strategic and tactical options, and have the most mobility for your units.  SOLUTION: Make minor settlement battles optional, allow you to toggle field or siege at the battle screen.--The campaign "The Great Game" rushes you to go into the Chaos Realms which are not enjoyable to go through and have zero replayability. If you don't participate you will lose, making a domination victory almost impossible to achieve beforehand. The Vortex campaign while not great either allowed for a lot more flexibility in play style which makes all the difference.SOLUTION: Have a toggle to turn off the Chaos Realms gates. OR remove The Great Game as a victory condition and make it optional so that should you complete all 4 realms and win the final battle before any other players, you get a huge bonus to help you on your way towards a domination victory.  -- In general, all factions need more units but that's easy to remedy and will come in time. The Daemon faction units and mechanics feel very similar particularly when Forsaken, Spawn of ..., and Soul Grinder (only artillery) are all shared between them further reducing variability. A big pet peeve of WH3 is having high tier units be slightly weaker versions of Legendary Lords such as Slaanesh or Tzeentch which first of all, dilute and devalue the Legendary Lords because you can just recruit weaker versions of them, but also these units use Winds of Magic which is already being all used up by your LL and heroes with none left over making their spells null if you cannot cast them. Having multiple magic users is a lot of micromanaging which at times can be a tedious pain. Visually, the unit models are cool, looking great as usual with all Warhammer games. SOLUTION: Add more units and rework/overhaul the Daemon factions.--The world map is too dense with cities, it's a large map but feels small when playing. I noticed lots of crossover during empire expansion between factions which is repetitive and boring. In WH2 Vortex you could at least pick one of the 4 continents which are VERY separated and rotate through them as starting positions so that you didn't get bored.SOLUTION: Immortal Empires.--Diplomacy is worse than in WH2, this is because the system no longer uses probability and so you need TONS of money in order to essentially buy defensive alliances, military alliances, vassals, and confederation. No longer is high military strength and good relations towards a faction enough to do any diplomacy options. Quick deal is convenient but again if you have no diplomacy options it doesn't matter. The Daemon factions always being automatically at war with new revealed factions is a never ending pain in the ass. Lastly, the super cool feature of outposts allowing you to recruit other factions troops was almost never applicable in my playthroughs. By the time I happened to get an alliance (which for the Daemon factions they have a tiny amount of feasible options) many of the AI factions only ever had one city the whole game and it usually already contained an outpost thereby preventing me from ever building one.SOLUTION: I have no idea!--The Legendary Lord skill trees are mostly lackluster and plain. And having perks specifically for tier 1 units (Nurgle) become obsolete for around 75% of the game is annoying. SOLUTION: More specific and unique abilities compared to every other LL in all of Warhammer games that can be utilized for a longer amount of time in the campaign. OR finally allow players to respec their LL, which would be a great feature.--Research options are numerous but usually weak and bare little impact on your game. I do like the increased frequency at which you complete them, it just too bad they don't feel impactful. SOLUTION: Reduce number of technologies and increase their benefits.--Unit mixing, this is on my wishlist, I would love to see CA change cities so that when you capture them you have the option to keep them the race they are such as in Heroes of Might and Magic III and Age of Wonders II. Then allow you to actually build that races building and units. This will never be implemented but it would be amazing.In conclusion, Warhammer 3 is not in a good place right now, I almost want my money back. They tried some innovation but failed. I am hopeful that they can continue to try and innovate but in more successful ways. I am looking forward to what WH3 will become and would like to see it as a complete evolution and not just a big Warhammer 2 expansion pack. Mostly, I would like the game to feel fun and not stressful!

_childDocuments_.review: While Immortal Empires certainly was a breath of fresh air for the game, there are still so many bugs and simply downgrades from game 2 that I would not recommend this game if you don't know what you are getting into. I still play it and enjoy it, but that's only because I can overlook the major issues that plague the game (and especially how incredibly slow CA has been at addressing any of them).  Just go play Total War Warhammer 2 instead, which is in a great state right now.A few specific (major and minor) negatives for Immortal Empires (The twwh3 campaign alone is awful so let's just pass over that)------------------------------------------------------------>the ui is just straight up worse than game 2. I don't even know what happened here except that they wanted to change it for the sake of changing it. The faction selection is terrible, mission panel is worse to use, etc.sound design is good for the most part, but once again projectile units sound like *** with very few exceptions. Almost like someone else did them specifically (both blackpowder and bows/crossbows)>many factions have been nerfed and a lot of their interesting mechanics removed. While I do understand the need to reduce power in some cases, the big problem here is the lack of anything interesting in its stead. Just ends up making them less exciting to play.>Bugs, bugs, oh so many bugs. Yes that's to be expected, but they could at least have done some hotfixes by now. Some of them make certain factions nigh-unplayable or remove key parts of their identity (lack of items, heroes, quests, etc.).>Hero traits ... what the hell happened here. The vast majority of them are just straight up awful, while some are very good. I don't expect all of them to be great, but at least something decent. Rn the difference in power is astonishing Ogres are especially notorious here, with some default traits providing bigger benefits than their unique faction traits in the same attribute. Cathay similarly has some very weird traits ... all the good ones are of one type (Yin), while the Yang traits are just plain useless. That's not even to speak of factions that pretty much only have useless traits.>Personal issue, but the game is generally too easy right now. The AI is way too passive even at legendary leading to extremely fast campaign burnout (by turn 50 the campaign is basically over, cause nothing can challenge you anymore).>Lack of field battles. This is especially notorious on higher difficulties due to the ai sitting in their settlements as soon as they even get a whiff of your army. Additionally, since the autoresolve is as forgiving as it is right now, you barely ever fight any field battles past turn 20. It's always siege or minor settlement battles, which are both incredibly easy to defeat (easier than field battles in most cases). This has a lot of knock-on effects, such as gunpower units being generally awful in actual battle (due to the ai behaving smarter by avoiding LoS and targeting them with archers) or ranged units in general being subpar (again due to ai perfectly microing to avoid being shot as much as possible). This leads to sieges being either a melee slog or being cheesed in the vast majority of cases.>continuing with the gunpowder issue, the obstacle detection right now is so jank, that often those type of units don't even shoot if there is virtually nothing in front of them. It was already bad in game 2, but so much worse now. You often can't even shoot larger targets stuck in your infantry, because they seemingly don't realize that 60% of those trolls are sticking out above the heads of their comrades. Add to that the fact that most ai actively targets gunpowder units (such as handgunners, ironhails, thunderers, etc.) and you'll likely get a better performance out of any bow/crossbow unit. Those can shoot above your own units, have less targetting issues and most importantly don't require 10 seconds of micro each to get into a position where they can actually shoot properly.There are many other points that irk me, but I think these are some that might give you an idea of whether or not you may enjoy the game in its current state. I do believe it will get better with time, but as it is now I can't see this being anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: You may see that this games overall reviews are a lot lower than recent reviews, and let me tell you why.I played this game on Xbox game pass on release and I was so excited because Warhammer 2 had been my favorite game during the pandemic. However, I was soon disappointed. The game was unoptimized, the campaign was a tedious and frustrating slog in which there was too little money, too few major settlements and too frequent chaos invasions which just got annoying. In the end I rage quit and uninstalled the game after losing the hour long final battle at the last wave (honestly those survival battles were a terrible idea)However, a few months later I saw immortal empires was coming out so I bought the game on steam since i already had Warhammer 1 and 2 there. Me and my brother played a coop game together and it was an entirely different experience. They got rid of all the things I did not like the lack of money and major settlements (except for the performance issues) and kept all the good thing like improved diplomacy and ally mechanics. Honestly, it's a massive improvement on both the story campaign and mortal empires and they managed to integrate the content from previous games very well. Like the devs say it really brings all the diversity of the Warhammer world to life in one chaotic and cataclysmic campaign. So in conclusion, If you already have/can afford Warhammer 1 and 2 get it, if you don't have/can't afford those games then don't get Warhammer 3 (but mortal empires might be in your price range)Have fun banishing daemons! (or leading them)

_childDocuments_.review: You can squeeze plenty of hours out of this game BUT there are a few things that you should consider before buying:- As many others, I’m not happy with the excessive increase in price of the last DLCs. This must be considered in light of the decrease in quality and quantity of the content offered. I positively reviewed the Chaos Dwarves DLC as I thought it was still worth it, but the Shadow of Change DLC is undeniably subpar. For a handful of units and some half-baked mechanics, the cost of this DLC is almost half the cost of the base game. - This situation has been aggravated by the public statement that Creative Assembly has recently released regarding this price increase controversy. The statement is half-baked as the DLC itself, but the absurd part is the vailed threat that if the community doesn’t buy the DLC, Creative Assembly will abandon the game. This statement shows that the person who signed it, is truly out of touch with the situation of the game and its community. - Over time, Creative Assembly has shown a disorganised and unprofessional way of communicating with the community despite frequent requests for a betterment. The release of this game was quite rocky, and it took ages for the company to address many issues.- This game has several bugs and there’s a list of “known issues” that comprises stuff that has been in the game for months (or more). A few of them have been easily fixed by the community, while Creative Assembly has ignored them. Warhammer Total War is also cursed with the infamous “spaghetti code”, which means that often fixing a minor thing may break something that may seem totally unrelated. So, some updates create absurd bugs that may take the fun out of some factions (see the infamous Nakai bug). Moreover, some mechanics are worse than the ones you can find in much other older Total War games (e.g., sieges). I’m not particularly bothered by most of these issues, and I think the game can still be fun despite them, BUT if you pair this situation with the previous points, you should really ponder if supporting this company is worth it. To conclude this, I enjoy this game and I’ve been playing Total War games and Warhammer since I was child. However, in good conscience, I can’t give a positive review. Even though the game may offer a positive experience for many players, you should question the company behind it. Companies aren’t your friends, but the greed here is truly palpable. It’s like having a relationship with a toxic partner, they lure you in by showing you positive things, but then you start to notice the cracks and they are nice only when they need you (or in this case, your money). This game has a huge potential but it’s so much less than what it could be, I can’t stress this enough. I’m hopeful for the future, but at the current time, something needs to change.

_childDocuments_.review: This title, including its two predecessors, is my all-time favorite game. I'm certain that it's a once-in-a-lifetime experience, as I don't think I'll ever be as invested or hyped for a game again.Let me provide a little backstory. Back in 2004-2006, my cousin and I spent all our time and money in a local paint store that sold Warhammer. We would arrive in the morning and stay until our moms would come take us home for dinner. I don't think the store owners liked us much, probably because we were broke kids who spent hours just staring at the box art, imagining epic battles. In 2009-2010, I got my first Total War game, Empire Total War. It didn't take me long to realize that Total War and Warhammer were a perfect match.Around 2013, I saw a blog post on the Total War forum or CA webpage (I can't remember exactly where) that said CA had obtained the rights to make a game for a GW IP. I was beyond excited. Then, in 2015, the first trailer dropped, and since then, I've easily spent over 300 hours listening to lore videos and prediction videos. Every single DLC announcement feels like Christmas to me. I think I've spent more time imagining what will come next for the title than actually playing the game. Without overreacting, I can say that I've thought about this game at least once every day since the first announcement.Another thing I appreciate about this game is the community. It's full of fans who are just as excited as I am, and what's unique about this community is that everyone seems really pro-DLC. People are begging CA to release more DLC and new content more often, which is a rare sight in a lot of gaming communities. But it's for good reason that people praise DLC for this game. I've bought every game and every single DLC without regrets, and I'll continue to support them until it's over. Everything they deliver is worth it in my opinion, and the game is a dream come true for Warhammer Fantasy tabletop players.If you're a fan of Warhammer fantasy and video games, Total War: Warhammer is a must-have. I feel sorry for the 40k community because there is no 40k game that can compete with this. CA, please make Total War Warhammer 40k!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I know not everyone's experience wasn't like mine, citing the glitches, crashes and performance issues. I was one of the lucky ones that suffered minimally and the worse I had was slight frame rate issues, which I solved by turning fog and lighting to low. After that, it ran quite well.I am running my game on a Geforce 1660 Super on a new PC I got, just to play this game.Playing the prologue, it is an amazing tutorial I wish was in previous TW: Warhammer titles with how it explains mechanics and the intricacies of the game, while also giving proper set up to the main campaign.I only played two factions at launch: Kislev and then Khorne. I touched upon the Legion of Chaos, but I was overwhelmed by my options in units I may recruit I chose to step away and start with a daemon faction. I played Grand Cathay and Tzeentch and Slannesh in multiplayerPersonally, the campaign was great the first time through, but going in the second time, it wasn't as fun. Though, I played Khorne afterwards, which given his faction mechanics, matters on the campaign map quite trivial. Though, expanding is punishing when I first played due to the campaign mechanics, but at the time of me writing this, they implemented some solutions to counter it.The settings are very pretty, especially the Chaos Realms where there is so much to look at and see. The snow maps are quite blinding when I played and made units, both mine and the enemy hard to see, I had to squint in order to look at the map. Thankfully, I could change the outline so it was easier to see them in that terrain, but that's like a band-aid on a severe wound, I wish they fix it in the future.Gameplay wise, The AI was an interesting challenge, I tried to exploit it sometimes, but it proved to be quite clever and smart. I had some issues with unit path finding where my units or the enemy would have very questionable routes, though it rarely happened. The overhauled sieges are fun to play through, but the "Boss fights" can be pretty tough and quite an endurance match, but they gave you the option to skip it, which is good.VERDICTPersonally, I liked what I played and had fun with the units and factions they provided. There is some sight problems I can personally get past, but I hope they get fixed soon. The main campaign in the base game is a "Play once and put down" kind of affair. I can't really see a reason fo replaying the game unless it's to try out new mechanics before the "Immortal Empires" map drops.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't an easy one to write. I've been playing the Total War series since 2002 with Medieval: Total War 1. I have bought every game on disk when they released until steam started, and then i purchased them digitally from that point onwards, and the older ones again digitally. I have bought every DLC released on launch for full retail price, because even though each game became buggier over time i still loved the franchise. I have enjoyed every game, some more than others, and some i probably won't go back to. I have several thousand hours across all of the total war games on steam, and probably another few thousand hours on the disks from the 2000's. I was dissapointed with decisions CA has made in the past such as Rome 2's infamous poor launch, 3K being abandoned early, and more recently the price increase of DLC's. But i always just let it go, moved on, or went back to play the classics. I wasn't as bothered as some when it came to the price of The Chaos Dwarf DLC race pack, as i could see the value of the content and understood that we were likely to only get maybe 1 race pack a year. I bought that DLC for full price as a pre order, played it on launch, loved it and didn't look back. A few months back, it was announced that there would be several DLC's lined up over the next 12 months, focusing on 3 races at a time. I thought this was great, as it was a quicker way to bulk up some of the leaner rostered races such as the base WH3 races, including my favourite Grand Cathay. Where things started to get rocky was when the price was leaked at being slightly more expensive than the Chaos Dwarves (in my currency). I thought that was odd, but this time they were focusing on 3 races instead of 2 like the usual lord packs, so maybe the price could be justified by some very bulky additions to the packs i thought. Fast forward a few weeks and the offical reveal and announcement happens. Each of the 3 races gets a new Legendary Lord (great, as expected), Tzeentch gets: 3 new heroes 2 new monsters 1 new infantry reskinned from a different faction (VERY POOR), Cathay gets:1 new generic Lord A war drum that buffs troops but doesn't fight (meh) 1 new Monster (not counting them as 2 as they're the same unit) 1 new war beast No new infantry/missile/cavalry (VERY POOR). Kislev gets: 1 new monster, 1 new hero1 new Missile1 new beasts.The price is one thing, but the fact that this DLC has such little content is painful. No new GL or magic for Kislev, and no infantry for Cathay and Kislev, and a poor reskin for Tzeentch. Even this wasn't enough to make me leave this negative review, but i thought maybe i'll wait for a sale for this DLC. What broke me was when i realised how little support this game receives in terms of bug fixes or even basic communication from CA. The straw that broke the camel's back for me was when CA came out and tried to convince us that the price increase was because they were struggling for money (which their PUBLIC financial records indicate the opposite), and threatened the community to abandon this game like they did with 3K if the DLC doesn't sell enough. They also expected us to pat them on the back for saying they WILL fix some game breaking bugs that have been in the game for months, that only broke when they were fixing other things months ago. This whole "only doing fixes when we have something to sell you" routine and the threats of cancellation have been enough for me to step away from this game and anything CA makes until they can prove they've made up to the community for these stacks and stacks of shambles, incompetence and talking down to and disrespecting their fanbase and customers. ENOUGH IS ENOUGH CA.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming as a basic total war and warhammer virgin, I have played this game since release. Let's see the good, the bad, and the ugly:The good: 1) Lots of replayability, a large roster of different start positions, characters, and overall different factions with considerably different strengths and weaknesses2) Lots of sandbox potential in the Immortal Empires campaign, you can try and hit victory goals, or unite your group of factions, or exterminate your enemies, or just sail around having some good fights.3) Low skill floor, meaning the game is pretty easy to pick up and play: you just grab your army, run at the enemy army, and you can generally win even battles this way. I started with Nurgle, so maybe it was a little harder if you do this way.4) High skill ceiling, there are endless variations to improvement. You can also replay your battles and try different tactics within them, see what works. Game is therefore welcoming to players of all skill levels.5) Lots of detail on models & maps, a somewhat thematic UI design. I would play a game made out of identical grains of sand so don't really take this as an endorsement that this is the most beautiful game of all time.The bad: 1) The replayability is hampered by two aspects: (a), that some factions are a puzzle rather than a strategy. If you move your army the wrong way, or don't bribe someone at the right time, you will be faced with overwhelming odds and be set back for the rest of the game. Learning the "correct" way to play campaigns hampers a single faction's replayability (looking at you, Franz!). (b), that the mid and late game is sorely lacking. Each mid game is: I survived the early game, I can cleanup my nearby enemies. Each late game is: 50 more turns of right click + auto resolve, oh look, the victory screen. We will return to this in the Ugly2) The world feels dead. People just wait for you to do your thing mostly, you do not get a sense that a rival empire is developing on the other side of the world/3) The auto resolve function is too much of a safeguard. If you don't lose any key units, you just auto-resolve and re-recruit. The game should have higher losses in regular auto resolve and less replenishment, to more accurately reflect an average fight. However, the manual battles are hampered by load times, even on SSDs. Its worse in multiplayer, where you are all waiting for the slowest player. Maybe an option for someone to idle on the campaign map would be better.4) The high skill feeling is hampered by the exploitable nature of the AI. While they keep patching things like ambush baiting etc, I never feel like a general is commanding the other forces, with a plan, they're just reacting to whatever I do. Let me predict the enemy charge, or the defensive bombardment, and have to come up with new plans.5) The detail etc is hampered by the absolute drain this puts on even good systems. The computational power is not reflective of the prettiness in the game.The Ugly:1) Nurgle, Mannfred, Malekith, Greasus, and everyone not named Sigvald.2) The End Game Crises are poorly thought out and extremely repetitive. This is because the end game itself is just a slog to finish. There should be different crises throughout the game to keep you on your toes and prevent steamrolls from setting up so easily. For example, the Wild Hunt event pops up (distinct to the End Game Wild Hunt) but you basically never see Orion become aggressive. More of those events are good, but they need to be threatening and relatively global.3) Ideas for 2) can be to have the Crises start earlier, but scale in difficulty. For example, you can set "Mid Game start" to trigger on turn 50. Now a few Crises will be between turns 50 and 100, but of lower difficulty. Then you can have the End Game Crises, and absolutely scale them up. Maybe surviving Mid Game crises will fight against the End Game, to hold the rest of the world in place.4) Wasted potential of the Chaos Wastes. Stuck in the Realms of Chaos campaign (the base game one), they had some cool ideas going for them. These could be mid-game events too, where its either one-to-two Chaos Gods opening up their realms for challengers, or a late-game crisis where the hordes of chaos descend. Add back in WH2's Warriors of Chaos crisis and this would be a very global event. 4b) Do not keep all the realms the same! The Khorne realm works well, where you go in and fight and pick up some cool weapons. I'd like this one to return with maybe a few more weapons to reflect the greater number of competitors, and then some combat strength rewards. Of course, taking Chaos Gifts should always have drawbacks for factions! It can be simple as you permanently spread that corruption, or for example, taking a gift of Khorne prevents that army from using Magic. The Slaanesh realm is the best designed, but it would need to keep a timer or sense of competition so people are encouraged to take their investments with them at different exit points. The Nurgle Realm should offer replenishment & growth, but not be as awful to walk through. Maybe your units can become Nurgle units after a while in the realm, or plagues eek out the longer the portal is open. Tzeentch realm would need a complete rework. Good luck5) The bug fixes are atrocious. They either do not work, or cause new bugs. I've seen faction leaders become unrecruitable, heroes get stuck in towns, units drop orders at a slight breeze, lack of good UI to indicate when your units cannot attack or fire, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: For update on this game please scroll to the end of review!I have put in over 1200 hrs into the Total War games series. Over 663 hours spent on Warhammer 2, so am a fan not a hater & am giving my honest opinion of this game.The campaign in Warhammer 3 forces you into a non-expansion type of play using limited armies to play 'wack a mole' with rift openings (which cause out of balance corruption in your territory).The forced claiming of 4 demon souls element was annoying & boring in equal measure.The story line is poor in my opinion. Many gamers have already stated an option to TURN OFF (or at least adjust the tempo of) the Chaos Portals & the 'soul collection' would have improved the game hugely as many players don't like the campaign & others like to play a slower, domination type, or more expansionist game...the list goes on but basically any options for going outside of a very limited & rushed linear play style have been taken away.Sadly I have found the campaign in WH3 to be restrictive, & not fun. I don't think the Campaign is fixable as it would need a complete redesign. Honestly I am sad to say Warhammer 3 is in my opinion not worth buying at the present due to its high price & would recommend Warhammer 2 to anyone new to the series.If & when a free 'Mortal Empires' upgrade becomes available I will update this review, but as for now my advice is save your money for something more fun.Update 20/03/2022After looking for a while online I  feel that CREATIVE ASSEMBLY  are sadly not replying to their customers attempts at making their views known, to my knowledge no Acknowledgement has been made about the Campaign in WH3 being poorly received by the player base, many other widely made criticisms are also not being publicly addressed.Have CREATIVE ASSEMBLY banned their staff from mentioning anything that would affect sales figures? The Wall of Silence from the developers/makers of this product is deafening & more than slightly annoying for those of us who pre-purchased this game or who have bought early at full price only to get what we feel is a sub-standard experience.Update 22/04/2022 .....I am sad to say Warhammer 3 is now uninstalled , the campaign was boring & frustrating the first time & has no replay value. As a fan I can only hope for a better game in future but will not hold my breath. Really feel let down by this game , especially after all the ads & hype from the developers. A big price tag for a deeply flawed game!!!Update 3/5/2022Warhammer 3 is not in 'Steam Stats' top 100 games when even Warhammer 2 is still clinging on...says it all really.Update 06/09/2022 I am changing this review to positive now 'Immortal Empires' has been released, this is now the game it should have been on release. Although the developers are calling it a beta, I have played around 100 hours & found it to be stable. The game is being well supported at the moment with updates & patches coming thick & fast, a refreshing change to some previous Total War offerings.Immortal Empires is all in all a fantastic game & well worth the money now.

_childDocuments_.review: I would really like to enjoy the game. The units and factions added are fine with me, and I've enjoyed the series since TW Medieval, but this one just has a lot of issues like consistent crashing and the strange way they handled sieges. They are still a regular thing, especially after manually playing a battle, which sort of just adds to their annoyance. The initial shock of the new battle system has worn off a little and I find the concept more interesting as it focuses on smaller settlements, but still in need of tweaks to make it better. The barricades are largely worthless on their own, but when you consider that they are very close in cost to building a tower, there is never really a good reason to build them in my playstyle. More time with the different factions has made me appreciate some of the mechanics added to the game, especially with the Nurgle faction once I learned how their building functioned. I still can't recommend this game over WH2, especially when fully priced or anything less than 25% off. It will hopefully grow in to a game comparable to the previous installations, but it still has a long way to go.Update 2:The latest update has fixed a large amount of the crashing issues I have been experiencing. The Immortal Empires is a step towards a hopeful fulfillment to the trilogy. Fingers crossed.

_childDocuments_.review: | Why I strongly recommend the game |WH3 feels like the end of a trilogy movie. Epic, brutal and exhilerating. Very very much recommend for veteran players of warhammer. They have outdone themselves on new mechanics and on the new factions. For starters I might recommend warhammer 2 or even 1, because these have a bit more 'basic' factions. In WH3 a lot is coming your way, and the factions are made to have a specific playstyle in mind. As a wh3 veteran with 600 hours in this is great, but it might not be ideal if you want to learn the ropes. For example, one chaos god is specifically tailored to diplomacy while another to magic and campaign mechanics.  I have never written a review but find this game so much redefines and evolves its own concept that all of the negative reviews don't do justice to the game.| Why then all the negative reviews? |The negative reviews are based on those fans that expected the same as 1 and 2 but instead got surprised and afterwards angry for the change of campaign. In WH3, you can't just go around doing what you want but really need to focus on the campaign that is thrown at you. In WH1 and WH2 the campaign was less intrusive and could pretty much be skipped. This 'conquer the world' gameplay will come back in a free DLC called Mortal Empires (ME). ME combines the maps of WH1, WH2 and WH3 together with all their factions (if you own multiple WH games). People often played Moral Empires over the campaign since the campaigns were relatively simple in structure, and ME gave more variety in battles since there were so many factions. This will be enabled but in the , late, future. Veteran players expected this to be implemented earlier. Keep in mind that balancing all 3 games means balancing out 20 or so factions. With all of the new mechanics that also need to be applied to all of the older factions, this is a huge undertaking that might take a while.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are exploring this game as a new player to Total War Warhammer I would recommend you steer clear of this franchise for now. After playing this game for years it is clear the developers have moved on to a new focus and are simply dragging out this game as a means to invest into other projects. This can be seen with the other negative reviews and the £200+ of DLC for this game.Inherently this isn't a bad thing however, due to the drive to continue to bring revenue from the franchise at the cheapest cost their new DLC updates have fundamentally broken the game. Examples of this can be seen in various game crashes, poor AI decision making, faction abilities not working correctly, and multiple quality of life game functionality that has not been implemented correctly. Fundamentally its the elements above that make the game no longer a pleasure to play and why I would not recommend anyone to buy into this franchise as it stands today. It is a huge shame to see such an amazing idea grow into a great product only to be dismantled by poor business practice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not as feature complete as Warhammer 2 is currently. Is it miles better than Warhammer 2 was at launch? Absolutely. While there were several annoyances with the campaign at launch (poor unit responsiveness, inability to prevent chaos rifts, frustrating chaos realms manuevering, bad autoresolve calculations), many of these have been improved or entirely fixed since launch. The new series features (Ally outposts allowing you to recruit allied units, better diplomacy and trade anywhere, as well as better siege battles) are great quality of life improvements over the old Warhammer 2 systems. System performance does still remain an issue (requires a large amount of graphic memory and can slow down the game loading due to this). Immortal Empires, which represents a significant chunk of game content, is not yet released. If you play these games because you want to watch entire armies get decapitated and don't care if it kills your game performance, the blood pack is also not yet released. But if you are looking for some great Total War campaigns and fantastic battles, or just more Warhammer, this is still a fantastic game that I got my money's worth out of (and I haven't even finished any of the demon campaigns yet). While I do think the vortex story was better than the Realms of Chaos story, I don't think that diminishes the improvements this game makes to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty awesome. If you like fantasy, RTS, and epic battle simulators, this will be right up your alley. Every battle is a challenge, and there is a good variety of maps to play on in most of the campaigns I've done. Even on the same maps, no two battles really feel the same because of the different unit compositions in the armies you field and face. Likewise, the progression of your lords and heroes can really turn the tide in certain situation. Most notably, there is also a TON of faction variety, especially if you own the first two games as all of their content is integrated into the third with the Immortal Empires campaign.My biggest complaint with the game is that the sandbox mode (Immortal Empires) is the supposedly superior campaign out of the main two (the other being Realms of Chaos), but the open-ended nature of it detracts from my experience as there are no meaningful objectives or rewards received for overcoming challenges. Sure, there are missions and items received for completing them, but it’s are simple stuff like "kill 5 enemy settlements" or "fight this bad guy over there who want to murder you and your family". There’s no real narrative to anything you do, and in doing all of these “basic task” missions, you receive so many items that your list of junk piles up to a point where you can't keep track of it all. Even though they make your characters stronger and there is some strategy to be had in selecting which items to use, each item individually feels like it becomes insignificant in the slew of options you have. I don't feel "good" about getting that awesome weapon for my character like I should, even if it might make them stronger. And when I finally take over all of the settlements of ogres right next to my kingdom, why can’t I parade them through the streets of my capital with their heads on spikes? I guess the main point I’m trying to make is that achieving things in the game should feel more rewarding.Disclaimer, I've never played Realms of Chaos, the supposedly more narrative campaign, so if that’s what I’m looking for I should play that. The thing is, everyone tells me it's terrible, so I haven’t had the motivation to play. Maybe I will cave in and update this review later on…I'm not even gonna talk about the DLC as everyone already has. It feels overpriced sometimes, there's no getting around it. No doubt though, it overall adds a ton to the game , especially with multiple DLCs and a ton of options to choose from if you want to be more selective rather than just get everything.Overall would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 70 hours of Total War: Warhammer 3 and I enjoyed my time with the game, however I do not recommend anyone purchase it; not until the release of the immortal empires campaign, most of the game breaking bugs are removed and sieges are actually fixed.Like many other people I did not enjoy the silly gimmick mechanics of the Chaos Realms Campaign. Each realm is just a massive chore that basically forces your legendary lord to do some tedious minigame for several turns. The rifts are also incredibly disruptive, they spawn absolutely everywhere, spread corruption, and eventually spawn enemy agents and armies; so you’re forced to recruit several agents just to close those damn rifts. The reward for winning the campaign is also very underwhelming, since every faction just receives the same legendary lord, who has an unfinished skill tree and no unique trait. The narrative of the Chaos Realms campaign is also quite lacking, it fails to live up to the prologue campaign, has no real characters and it doesn’t make any sense from a lore perspective. Honestly I don’t understand why they bothered making a narrative campaign, the Nexus in Total War: Warhammer 2 was incredibly unpopular and the last couple DLC factions did not participate in the race for the vortex, so it looked like CA had learned their lesson.Furthermore the game is a broken buggy unbalanced mess. Some of the bugs I encountered while playing are: units freezing in place, units fazing through bridges on certain maps, ai constructing towers with no cooldown, many spells and abilities not working, flying monsters getting stuck mid-charge, lot’s of flickering on some maps, and frequent crashes. There are also many problems with how armies perform on the battlefield. Units are very slow to react to orders, get stuck on other units, and have trouble navigating through cities. Units getting stuck on one another and pathfinding through siege maps was already a bit clunky in Total War: Warhammer 2, but it’s somehow way worse in this game. This affects cavalry the most, making it even weaker than it was in the previous title. Charges, charge defense, and charge reflection are also broken. Most cavalry units do little to no damage on charge (even less than in Total War: Warhammer 2) and infantry units seem to brace even when moving.There are many other problems with the game (like ugly chaos warrior reskins), but the review is getting pretty long and I haven’t even mentioned the couple of things CA did get right.With the exception of the legions of chaos (which need a complete rework) all factions have fun and unique mechanics and each feel and play very differently. I particularly like Khorne, Tzeentch and the Ogres (that being said packaging the ogres a separate DLC on launch is a scummy and toxic business practice).Minor settlement maps and the tower defense mechanics add a lot to the game making it more replayable. There are some quality of life improvements and the Ui has been improved in some areas.The game is also very pretty (with the exception of some snowy maps and accursed chaos warrior reskins) and CA’s animators and 3d artists have done an amazing job. Although I believe Total War: Warhammer 3 has the potential to become a truly excellent game, it's clearly an unfinished and rushed product with many odd and backwards design decisions. At this stage it’s basically an early access title and not worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: So Immortal Empires and mod tools dropped and numerous patches have been released since the time of my initial review.  Is this game now the greatest thing since sliced bread? No....sliced bread forever. :p  The devs have fixed numerous bugs and are continuing to update the game based on community feedback. Will they do everything the community says? Probably not, but they managed to largely redeem themselves and this game with the introduction of Immortal Empires, mod tools, and the ability to roll back your game to previous versions and finish your campaigns. Numerous bug fixes and balancing changes help as well.lol I would say the campaign was very much playable and better balanced by 2.0 and deserves a go for those getting into game 3 for the first time. Rifts are manageable now and can be prevented from spawning in your provinces at all. The actual Realms of Chaos, primarily Tzeentch and Nurgle, have been rebalanced to not make you dread playing them. You're still on the clock to clear the realm, but they aren't pure torture like before. My only real complaint is with AI factions and how they (don't)handle chaos corruption in many cases. It still needs tweaking but is actually fun now.This is the bit that everybody wanted from day 1. Creative Assembly has made it clear that there will be bugs and has so far done well handling concerns in my opinion. This mode also comes with various balancing changes and overhauls to game 1 and game 2 factions. That last part can't be understated as the two worst lords in the game, Helman Ghorst and Nakai are not just playable now; they are in fact a blast to play. I say that as a person who initially believed Ghorst should have just been yanked and replaced entirely. This mode still has weak spots though. Sieges are still a problem mechanic-wise and make you lose way too many troops. The daemon prince from the story mode should have been removed since he is even less special with Belakor's new mechanic that allows him to create more daemon princes. He was a player insert for a story mode and was fun in that regard. With IE though, daemon prince Daniel needs to go back into the chaos realms and never return. Many of the previous games' factions in somewhat odd spots regarding balancing. Many faction mechanics that worked really well in game 2 and 1 need tweaked, overhauled, or removed to account for new threats and conditions introduced for game 3.I can safely recommend game 3 by itself now and the investment for Immortal Empires, with the understanding that some bugs and subsequential patches will be a reality while things get ironed out. Overall the game runs smoothly for me and is fun to play.  If you end up with performance issues I'd check to make sure you aren't playing on a potato pc or a computer with inadequate cooling. Many of the people I'm seen with those issues just aren't in spec for components or their 3090 and *insert other high end parts here* aren't being properly cooled and thermal throttle as a result.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this. On paper it does a lot of things that I wanted out of Total War. Potentially interesting story mechanics and a unique story driven campaign. Chaos factions are interesting and well realized and the (too) few order factions are also well made.The problem is that too much of the campaign's flow is changed without adding anything to make playing it interesting. You are encouraged to turtle and wait out chaos invasions but there are no interesting management mechanics. You can't build "deep" (CIV) or engage in quirky dynasty and governance mechanics (CK3).Instead we are discouraged from engaging with the core mechanic, the battles; outside tedious rebellions and chaos incursions. You HAVE to focus on the objective and when you "win" the objective the impetus to continue playing is gone.  I like the idea of engaging and dynamic map objectives but most of the chaos objectives are just shallow and boring. After the first prince battle I just stacked an army and auto-resolved.Mods for Warhammer 2 did a much better job adding depth and engaging mechanics to governance, diplomacy, and battle tactics. CA did very little to actually try to bring any of these ideas in to Warhammer 3. I have supported CA since Warhammer 1, blindly throwing money at minor power creep DLC after DLC. But this has been some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Provided you are a fan of strategy games, Total War: Warhammer is the peak of RTS. It has challenging single player content, is equally or more fun in multiplayer, either cooperatively or against one another, and enormous replay-ability.The brilliance of the game lies three things. One the battles are large scale fantasy warfare, swords, arrows magic, monsters, artillery etc, you have any liking of these elements that alone should merit consideration as no game comes even close to having done it better. The second is the variety of races and the flavours of most feelings very unique and befitting each. Some have stronger economies, others better trading others benefit more from raiding or sacking, incentivising you into playing how that race usually operates. Lastly, It's the replayability of it. I've done some campaigns multiple times, this is because additions to the game affects everything, as the ripples of change can and often is, felt by everyone. The downside, is that the complexity of the game means there is a learning curve, it could take you as long as 20-30 hours before you really get a handle on how to play it. Even after you learn the basics of the game, each campaign has it's own challenges and unpredictable twists, meaning you are unlikely the thrive the first time you take a swing at anything. So, if you are more of a plug'n'play gamer, this may not be your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: This is based on playing the prologue and a single main campaign on Very Hard/Very Hard; no multiplayer etc.Lot of potential, but fundamentally not worth buying in its current state.In my opinion, the core mechanic of the main campaign, collecting souls in the Realm of Chaos, makes that campaign unenjoyable. It detracts from the sandbox experience I’m looking for in a total war game; I don’t want to take one of my main armies out of the picture for multiple turns at a time to ultimately play a tower-defence like minigame. It wouldn’t be such an issue if it was more viable to ignore it, as it was with the Vortex in the main campaign in Total War: Warhammer 2; but, in my experience, you’re looking at losing your campaign within about 100 turns if you don’t engage with it.The other major downside for me is the settlement battle re-work. Sieges are in an unhappy compromise between WH2 and Three Kingdoms, and in a worse state than both. Similarly to the survival battles in the Realm of Chaos, they feel, to me, more like tower defence than an actual siege. This is in contrast to Three Kingdoms, where they felt much more like a siege battle – if falling short of the hights of Medieval 2, and even to WH2, which, while those were arcady and boring due to the limited angles of attack, they at least didn’t have the player or the AI repeatedly creating towers and other defences out of thin air. The AI is also very abusable as it tries to defend too much ground at once. Major settlements are also weaker than minor ones, as they force the defender to hold at least two positions; spreading themselves too thin.   I’ve not had any major issues with performance, the new races are interesting – if in need of balancing, and the story telling when you get it is excellent. I’m also fairly confident that the game will be drastically better once the promised combined campaign is added, without the Souls/Realm of Chaos. Unfortunately, the siege rework is likely here to stay. Though I imagine it will be improved over time, with the AI less able to immediately recreate destroyed towers and barriers, it will remain, in my view, a step backwards from Three Kingdoms, and nowhere near as good as Medieval 2 or the first Rome.Save your money and time on this one, at least until its in a better place.

_childDocuments_.review: As you've probably noticed, some people have really enjoyed this game and others have not. I fall into the category of one who doesn't mind the Realm of Chaos campaign that many others despise. Yes, at times it can be annoying, but as someone who has plays the Vortex campaign in Total War Warhammer 2, I'm quite used to this type of campaign and don't need to wait for Immortal Empires to come out.Some pros to the game:- Decent Faction Selection (base game has 9 Legendary Lords from 7 different factions).- Map is very large and allows for diversity in what enemies and friends you come across.- Individual Faction Mechanics for every faction that adds some flavor to each one.- Skarbrand the Exiled punting most characters across the map.- Graphics are pretty good especially on higher settings.- Modding Community is wonderful.Cons:- Immortal Empires isn't out yet. Less sandbox-ish for now as you are kind of forced into playing the Souls Race unless you have a mod that turns it off.- Limited Units as of now for each faction, especially the Daemonic factions.- Cannot play as the Warhammer one and two races. This doesn't faze me, but I know it affects a lot of people that fancy playing the Empire for the 50th time.- Anti-Player Bias still is strong, but much better than what it was at release back in February of 2022.Conclusion:Personally, I think the game is worth it and it is only going to get better as we progress further into the year. If you are waiting for Immortal Empires, then I would hold off until later this year when the beta gets set up for that. If you really want to try out new factions like Cathay (which is new-ish to lore) and the Daemons, then I would recommend getting this game. I hope this helps you all make a good decision!

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to premise this review by saying that this is based on pre-Immortal Empires/Champions of Chaos/Blood for the Blood Gods 3 release (writing this 2 days prior) so take anything I say with that in mind if read post-release. I will also apologize in advance since this will be a long read but I will break it up so if there's something specific you want to look at feel free.Game Overall:To start off the game honestly is okay-good as it currently stands. Is the game perfect? No by no means is it perfect but it is in line with what you would expect for a Total War game's release. At launch the game was fairly buggy (not that many game breaking bugs or crash causing at least that I encountered myself or what friends of mine have encountered) but again this falls in with what's to be expected with a Total War launch. No it is by no means bug free they are there if you pay enough attention. I ran into a texture error myself due to a file corrupting during the download but that was at least fixed with a quick verify game files attempt. I have only had one crash to date (even when I had mods on) which was caused be me deciding to run multiple games at once.Narrative/Campaigns:The narrative prologue is actually pretty fun in my opinion, it's not super long and gives you an idea of how the game feels as a whole. The main game narrative is okay overall. It is fun to play through maybe once or twice but after that the structure of the mechanics involved with the campaign itself become annoying and tedious to the point where I would almost say snagging the mod that turns off the forced narrative is a must so you can play the game at your own pace. The Realms of Chaos themselves are cool to see as well as beautiful (or vile depending on the realm but it makes sense thematically) and each has their own mechanics for you to contend with, 1 of which (looking at you Tzeentch) was a nightmare to deal with early on (it has since been patched). The final battle of the scenario can be challenging depending on the Faction you are playing or the build you have but it's a nice challenge if you can handle it. My 3 biggest complaints about the campaign are for 1 it has little replay-ability, once you clear it once you will honestly have little to no desire to do so again unless you just really enjoyed it or are hunting the achievements for clearing the campaign with other Factions. The second is the spam of the portals mechanics later on in the campaign, at launch there was no way to slow these so to speak that didn't involve you spamming heroes to close them ASAP they have since added in a building to help counter them. My final big complaint is that you had to do any Realms of Chaos mechanics with your faction leader only, now I can understand this for the final battle but for the 4 realms of Chaos I don't think it should be that restrictive, it sucked having my leader fighting a big war then portals time starts and now I have to stall my war and rush a portal.The Factions:The Factions this time around are actually pretty cool and all for the most part play very unique. The Demons I will admit have a bit of overlap (each shares roughly 4 units: Soulgrinder (unique builds at least between them), chaos spawn, forsaken, and Furies) but other than a few units they each can be very fun to play though I do not feel as fleshed out as the other races at launch (granted based on their army books they are nearly done but they are getting some additions with the upcoming Champions of Chaos DLC). Kislev is very cool (no pun intended) overall with a varied roster that allows you to play in any real manner you want though you do suffer the negative of only having a few fancy capitals and almost all your other nearby settlements are minor providing economic buffs and little to no military buffs. Cathay for me was a mixed bag for me. Their units are very strong when you utilize their harmony buff and they probably have the best ranged units of the available groups at launch. However their faction mechanic of the Great Bastion sucks, the fact you have to CONSTANTLY deal with an infinitely spawning group of enemies while also dealing with the Narrative mechanics is a royal pain. Finally there is the ogres (the first DLC) which are pretty fun to play and at the moment are the only Neutral group included in the campaign.Multiplayer:I do not participate in Multiplayer battles since I personally do not find them fun or enjoyable. I have played a good bit of multiplayer campaigns though. Overall campaigns have been vastly improved for Multiplayer, in previous games you were capped at 2 players at maximum for this installment you are allowed up to 8 if you so choose which can lead to some crazy wars of diplomacy and bribery between friends and foes alike. They have added simultaneous turns which was a godsend overall in my opinion especially if you are playing beyond 2 players. You are now given options to decide who you support in a battle (if you are neutral you could side with friend or foe even utilizing that to get paid). It is a pretty fun experience overall just again having to contend with the annoying campaign mechanics makes it a bit of a pain overall and only 1 player gets the soul if you clear it even when allied, but this leads to my recommendation of just turning it off via mods.Community Complaints:This section will probably be a bit divisive since it will be a mix of my opinions and other community opinions so take it with a grain of salt. To start off I will talk about the rework to siege battles, now this was a HIGHLY requested change by the community in the previous game due to there being too many land battles when it came to minor settlements. This change for me personally felt really good, it made towns actually feel like towns versus just open fields or a single wall with a couple of small buildings behind it. The addition of the building in battle mechanics I think are cool but they can get a bit troublesome when you are the attacker. However I believe it is an improvement overall as it encourages you to actually attack (the longer you wait the more the AI builds)  instead of just AFK'ing with artillery or ranged as was the situation in previous games, now there are still ways to exploit the new sieges if you can figure them out. Now the community or at least the more vocal side of the community (I personally think a lot of people are just neutral with the changes rather than for/against) want the changes to be reverted, which I find ironic since it's basically exactly what they asked for originally. A big complaint is that the narrative campaign isn't that great, I fully agree with that it's a one and done situation for it imo. Another complaint I see a lot is about optimization, I know this can be a real back and forth topic but from what I see a lot of the time it is a mixed bag of responses here. Now from what I understand a fair amount of people were having issues, now I don't know if this was because they were going beyond their system's potential or just trying to go beyond the game engine's potential and wanting perfection where there is none to be found. Myself and the 6 other people I talk/play Warhammer (Both 2 and 3) with haven't had any issues with optimization and we each have varying set ups from lower to highest end including a few people with multi-thousand dollar rigs and heavy 4k set ups. The final big complaint from the Community is that Warhammer 2 was better this statement I half agree with. If we are talking about Warhammer 2 + Mortal Empires + All DLCs + 4 years of updates then yeah it is 100% better. If we are talking about Launch state Warhammer 2 Vs Warhammer 3 then I whole heartedly disagree. Warhammer 2's launch campaign was terribly boring and unfun, I honestly was not able to clear it even once I just gave up out of boredom I was at least able to finish Warhammer 3's 3 times before being sick of it.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it.  Just finished my first campaign with Kislev and it was overall quite fun!Good: - The artwork (especially the demon models and chaos realms maps) is absolutely gorgeous. - The Realm Of Chaos narrative campaign is a neat idea and nice story with a few flaws but overall an interesting way to play. - The campaign mechanics are really fun to work with. - Patch 1.1 did a good job of fixing the most egregious gameplay problems and overwhelming rifts. - New factions are pretty different from the other games and give you a fun new play style.- The new diplomacy mechanics are excellent (trade settlements! see where your allies are going!). - Huge new map. - Sieges are interesting, both on the campaign map and in battle. - Reinforcements take time to show up and you can move where they come inBad: - New winds of magic system is very limiting and takes away the fun of blowing up your enemies with magic. - There are many parts of the game that feel unfinished and untested. e.g. Level cap is 50 but many characters don't have that many skills (no idea how they didn't catch this in testing). - The red and black interface is terrible and hard to read, and the skill trees aren't even colored. - Landmarks are missing. - No settlement capture artwork. - Unit pathing can be frustratingly bad. Extra thought: The Workshop exists and lets you make the game into whatever you want it to be.  Don't like rifts? Mod them out! Want easier autoresolve or fewer settlement battles? Mods! Hate the interface? Mod it!
