Me not having read the reviews, and dumb, i bought the dlcs expecting accesses to every character. Nope. So to sum the entire thing up. Yes i love the game and how it functions, but i do hate how greedy the asshats running the marketing and monetization are. If i could go back in time. i would only buy the game if it was going on a 70-90 percent sale and if it never went that low then i wouldnt buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and a straight upgrade for the warhammer franchise.  I was actually pleasantly surprised about all the quality of life improvements made to the game.  I did not have any of the issues others have been reporting, if anything it runs much better than the last ones.  Turns take like 5-10 seconds for around 90 factions to make their moves.  The sieges are 10x better.  I found that to be a core weakness in past installations where city battles were literally just a wall defense, now there are multiple layers and much more strategic choices to be made.  Not to mention the battles are much bigger being able to have more than 2 armies supporting each other.  There are a bunch a fixes over the last one, especially with diplomacy and that tactical map in general, but those are best to be discovered for oneself.  Overall, I had no complaints and can't wait for the mortal empires to come out.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. The main draw is currently the amount of factions, new areas of the map, and periodic new content. However, it's still extremely buggy, and very rough in other areas. Gameplay concepts like settlement battles and refreshed sieges are still tiresome and unfun, and most campaigns drag out overly long.Old Review:I'm a long time Warhammer and Total War fan and it's honestly disappointing how half baked Warhammer 3 is. There's been a lot said about how the main campaign doesn't feel well thought out, but it's also the sheer amount of reskins, bad AI, and weird bugs.Mods fix a lot of these issues, but really, they should not for a AAA game. I do envision it will improve in time, but needless to say the road map is disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: I love Warhammer and everything it has to offer. DLC and it's prices don't bother me, because not all are essential for having fun. My only real issue I have with this game is the player bias the AI have toward players. Granted, there is a mod that apparently fixes that but on normal or even easy, I shouldn't have AI factions from across the map attacking me while avoiding their own enemies. I've seen many get destroyed just for focusing on me. Now I'm not saying I want to make this game easy, I just want to make it reasonable. I don't like steamrolling AI, but I also don't like all AI factions steamrolling me either. Beyond that, I love this game and have many hours ahead of me going to be dedicated to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: Edited review and updated to positive due to recent changes made to the game in the right direction, thanks for listening to all the feedback and keep on smashing it. Really excited to see how you move forward with this new momentum, hoping for new Wood Elf DLC in future and others still due.Old review below.Changing the sound setting of "playing sound in the background" kept crashing my campaign preventing me from playing it until I turned it off. Along with that janky mentor setting that can actually prevent you from doing anything if you cannot do what it is telling you to, resulting in an alt+f4 and loading to an earlier save. This game has the chance to be a literal masterpiece.Wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't topped off with the icing on the cake of the scummy cash grabs in place, hardly being on top of these kinds of issues people are having during a cost of living crisis. So you're asking them to fork out the money for a few lords whilst glaring issues still have the chance to botch people from actually playing properly keeping a straight face and telling people to check their privilege lmao. Clown fiesta.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a Total War fan for years and in fact Medieval 1 was what got me into video games in general. My interests in the Total War franchise has always been more with their historical releases. This is not to say that Warhammer releases are bad in general however, when I personally buy the fantasy genre in Total War, I find myself doing it to play the multiplayer over single player. I am sad to say that as it stands right now Warhammer 3 has a poor multiplayer experience than what I am looking for. I prefer army vs army battles "land battles" as they are called. Instead of this true classical experience, what I have found in its place is "Domination" which is a silly king of the hill style system in which speedy units and factions get an edge. This feels like bad move to get more 'casual' players into the multiplayer scene by promoting this arcade mode and betraying one of the many features that made me fall in love with this franchise. I think it is unfortunate and unless they fix this, I will return to the older game releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: Very bad optimization.I have a Ryzen 9 5950X, RTX 3080 Ti and 32gb ram and the game will not stay above 60fps on high at 4k and barely stay above 60fps on medium at 4k.No excuse for this, even cyberpunk 2077 performs better.EDIT: That was just the prologue performance, the actual campaign CANNOT be run above 60 fps even on low settings and anything that is medium or above stays at at around 55-40 without changing and the average fps on medium setting is 42-45 fps.Battle-wise the game stays above 60fps even at high but there is clearly issues with the campaign map and considering 70%+ of the game takes place on the campaign map it is nearly unplayable in this state which is hilarious considering the campaign map has the exact same fidelity as warhammer 2 yet that runs at 55+-60+ fps on mortal empires and 80+ on the vortex campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I play Total War because I want to paint the map. This game constantly prevents me from doing that in a very annoying and repetitive way. Whether you're talking about poor game design or actual bugs - there is always something preventing me from actually enjoying the game. I've tried letting go on my desire to dominate the world and to just play the story, but even then I find myself to be constantly annoyed by the way things are set up. No matter what faction you play, you always have to deal with high levels of tediousness. Maybe we got spoiled after TW:WH2, but IMO it's baffling how this game is nothing more than a reskin of the previous versions - and they still messed it up. Playing against or as chaos as a whole, both in the chaos realms and just as AI opponents is buggy, tiresome and just disappointing overall. The best thing about this game compared to Total War: Warhammer 2, are the actual units in the actual battles. All the chaos army rosters look really cool and their abilities are very well done. The other factions also have a very unique taste to them and I'm looking forward to playing them in the immortal empires campaign.  All in all, I can see the potential, sure, but it's quite hard to understand why they went with this campaign design. If you haven't bought TW:WH3 yet, I'd wait untill they release immortal empires. If you don't own TW:WH1 and TW:WH2 yet, my advice is to buy those two and play their mortal empires campaign, rather than buying this one. There's plenty of very good experiences in mortal empires, and as soon as you're tired of it you can always expand to TW:WH3 in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: WARHAMMER III

_childDocuments_.review:
Far beyond the world and its petty wars there exists a dimension of pure, malevolent magic: The Realm of Chaos. It is a terrible place, incomprehensible to the mortal mind. It whispers promises of power, but to behold it is to be seduced by it. To relinquish your soul to it. To become it.

The four Ruinous Powers rule over this place, ever seeking to slip their bonds and engulf the world in a tide of daemonic corruption. Nurgle, the plague god; Slaanesh, the lord of excess; Tzeentch, the changer of ways; and Khorne, the god of blood and slaughter.

On the border between the worlds, two mighty kingdoms stand sentinel: the stern warriors of Kislev and the vast empire of Grand Cathay. But each is beset by its own trials, and now both have cause to cross the threshold and send their armies into the Realm of Chaos.

The world stands on a precipice. A single push will plunge it into cataclysm. And there is one who schemes to achieve just that, an ancient figure who desires nothing less than to wield supreme power. But to succeed, he will need a champion...

name: Ready or Not
detailed_description: Be sure to join the Ready or Not Discord server to keep up with the latest updates, find recruits for your squad, and have a good time! Los Sueños - The LSPD reports a massive upsurge in violent crime across the greater Los Sueños area. Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) teams have been dispatched to respond to various scenes involving high-risk hostage situations, active bomb threats, barricaded suspects, and other criminal activities. Citizens are being advised to practice caution when traveling the city or to stay at home. It has been noted that while Los Sueños is still seen as a city where riches can be found, for many more the finer things in life are becoming less and less obtainable. “The city is sprawling with cramped high-rise apartments and decaying affordable housing, which has been exploited by the criminal underground like a malevolent parasite,” states Chief Galo Álvarez. “In a city where people are just trying to survive, lawful action from the LSPD and the LSPD SWAT team remains an integral force preventing the stretched thin social fabric in this city from snapping under this chaotic strain.” In response to the burgeoning violent crime wave inundating Los Sueños, Chief Álvarez of the LSPD has enlisted the stalwart support of David ‘Judge’ Beaumont as the Commander of the LSPD SWAT team. Shortly following this announcement, the LSPD has also confirmed active recruitment for additional talent to join this specialized tactical police unit with the mission of bringing peace back to the city. “This assignment is not for the faint of heart,” comments Commander Beaumont, “Extremists, crooked politicians, countless weapons, human trafficking, and illicit drugs and pornography… the world of policing in Los Sueños is fraught with real and harsh realities, realities that the everyday person isn’t necessarily confronted with. These are realities that you will need to navigate with your team within the proper bounds of the law or face the consequences and make matters worse.” The Los Sueños Policed Department has officially posted new details on Commander “Judge” Beaumont’s updated assignment with the LSPD SWAT team: New Expectations: Whether this is your first time in Los Sueños or not, the city has changed and so too have the tools and methods with which we conduct our work. The haunts you might have seen or heard about are re-imagined, and so have the angles with which we approach each call. Furthermore, we’ve received reports that identify at least 4 new high-risk police districts which we suspect may require future tactical intervention, plus at least 4 existing high-risk districts that underwent massive upheavals. Take Command: The role of the Commander of the LSPD SWAT is to compose their team from a large roster with unique talents, give tactical orders, meticulously plan, and carry out missions. Commanders are obligated to conduct each mission with integrity and look after their team’s mental and physical health. Officers with unaddressed deteriorating mental status may be unable to properly perform their duties or even feel compelled to quit the force. Incapacitated officers may be temporarily unavailable for missions, with the tragic prospect of death leading to a permanent loss. For SWAT Commanders in unusual circumstances based on individual choices they opt for, deadly mistakes may lead to their own permanent fatality. SWAT Team Quality Enhancement: Much anticipated improved SWAT training procedures, tactics, and experience in the LSPD has led to an overall increase in the quality and quantity of officers in our roster. Expanded tactical versatility allows our officers to take on any challenge with renewed confidence, blending coordination and independence seamlessly. There is also additional basic training now available to SWAT members to keep foundational knowledge and muscle memory in top shape. Equipment and customization: We have access to the best weapons and equipment that the LSPD can offer to fulfill our exceptionally dangerous role, including many new acquisitions. However, customization isn’t limited to the equipment we use. Through close-knit comradery while performing remarkable actions alongside the team, you’ll earn the clothes you wear, the patches on your sleeves, the artwork that may adorn your skin, and potentially even the timepiece on your wrist. Lastly, we have overhauled our headquarters' training facilities to better test our loadouts before heading out on call.

Nothing about this game is bad, but nothing about this game stands out as being particularly good.

_childDocuments_.review: There are more established games such as Rainbow Six Siege that I would rather play. When searching for a session it always shows server is full. Could not find a multiplayer match after going into a public lobby, certainly a very basic look on the menu that doesn't make me want to wait to find a match either. Basic controls, just was not fun for what it is because you've played this game before under different names. Do not recommend for the price. Game should be 19.99 for such a basic, slow, and demotivating game. Expect slow progress from an early access, but it's just not fun at all aside from not being able to get in a lobby.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: It seems like the last update fixed this issue and I'm changing my review to positive.At the moment this feels more like a SEAL Team 6 simulator than a game depicting police officers.I bought this game expecting a spiritual successor to SWAT 4, but boy was I disappointed.Main problem is enemy aggressiveness. It is only possible to restrain something like 5% of the suspects as every junkie, criminal and security guard (!) you come across is going to fight you to the bitter end. It took me few tries to understand that you absolutely have to bring lethal armament with 5+ spare mags and that shooting a fleeing suspect in the head is not only OK but a viable tactic.Otherwise everything seems to be in order. Gunplay, graphics, performance and maps are just like they ought to be and seem to get better patch by patch.I really hope the devs add options to adjust the game more to the direction of 'tactical' in stead of 'shooter' but as it is, I do not recommend this to SWAT 4 fans. :(

_childDocuments_.review: weird over emphasis on level design, lots of worthless areas to explore in the police station which you spawn completely strapped inside of. abandons painful meaningful processes to summon a prompt upon "completing" a mission to instantly teleport away to a score screen but wait I didn't secure this last dead guy I just killed along with his weapon and we can't assume you would just logically do that upon completely securing an area when accepting the vote to end mission auto prompt, goodbye easy S score. why are there scores? because the game lacks all soul beyond injected lore and level design and if there weren't scores it would feel like nothing but a husk surrounding some over elaborate level. glad to see the inclusion of obnoxious inane chatter from AI teammates reminiscing about classic burger joints after we just popped some dudes and thanks for commenting that some guy with his head entirely missing is indeed dead in some attempt at being humorous. if I am overlooking the "have some damn respect for the mission" option for the AI I apologize, i just assume this game is too poor to afford the player any choice beyond skinning and arming your men. performance seems better but is incredibly inconsistent. leave the game idle for a bit immediately after spawning into HQ, why is it 30ish fps? move the mouse less than 4 pixels, keeping the same view orientation, fps immediately more than doubles. this makes dialing in video settings pretty much impossible because no matter the setting EPIC or low its just in a constant state of flux or hugging 30fps despite just being very high. seems primed for a console release. could be so much better with properly developed mission briefings and more VO regarding the topics at hand not slapstick BS or absolute conjecture. still needs to divorce itself from masquerading as anything close to a singleplayer game with stuff like "YOU HAVE ENTERED THE GAME" and lame crap like voting to end a mission when you are the only person playing. after finishing a mission you are met with your squad's profile pictures, their names and psychological impact the mission had on them. despite your department having an epic budget for weapons and gear you only have enough for 5 total swat officers, no backups, no subs, no choice in the matter. none of these people who shouldn't even have names at this point have a bio to read about, just a stupid ugly face and a diminishing mental profile. being able to assemble a team based on various strengths and weaknesses would boost this game majorly in the quality department but no just another incredibly shallow element of the game that basically shouldn't even exist. the way this game positions itself they should be cribbing heavily from the original americas army game. make this more RPG like where you take actual tests, force the tutorial in a meaningful way where its part of becoming certified to not only join the team but lead it, imagine a mission where you followed orders, this could be a portion of the tutorial. there's a billion things this game could do to become better but it seems like they like driving wayyyyyyyyyyyy down a small handful of roads with no meaningful connection between. maybe 2.0 is what we are all actually waiting for, or the paid expansion that actually gives the game any meaning beyond farting around with friends and filling in for the dumb ai quips with "OH WOW LOOK AT THIS THING I FOUND THAT THE LEVEL DESIGNERS THOUGHT OF TO PLACE HERE WOWWWW" which feels like the entire design ethos
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good and I recommend everyone to at least one SOLO playthrough. It has great graphics, rich story, solid gunfights and every time the game makes you question your moralty. Although, I dislike that there are no character involvement in the game. The SWAT AI feels like actual NPC's, they just do their thing. Civilian AI feels like they give zero ♥♥♥♥ about the situation they are in, just some voicelines which feels overplayed. At least a couple more dialogues in the game would make it perfect. For example, the dialogue in the "Hide and seek" mission, which was great. Player doesn't feel anything when he loses a crewmember, just "ermm, now I have to unlock his ability again."Add characters, more obvious lore and the game would be perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: Post 1.0: The AI is a damn sight better, however optimization and the systems they've implemented in  campaign don't really work as intended. Wait another 6 months or year and you'll have a pretty fun game as long as development priorities don't shift. Will review after significant patching. So far the TEAM AI is better, but everything else is liable to cause a memory leak, or crash to desktop.Pre-Release: I hoped the Devs weren't lying last year with their expectations. Lies or not, the game barely has anything new from when I bought it, check back in 2 or 3 years if you want a finished game. Plenty of other options that are sadly more entertaining as tactical shooter even with half the Dev/EA time this one has had. I really hope this game gets it's stuff together and can provide either a worthwhile SP or MP experience. At the moment my feelings a they're struggling to keep Co-op and streaming interest in the game alive with silly community check in's and kind of desperate calls for streaming. Had a lot of faith in where this game could go, still have some, but by now you could've easily redesigned all of the Swat 2,3,etc maps and cobbled together a small campaign to help players identify and scale the level of tactical difficulty expected with each set of suspects, environments, and situations you'll find yourself in accordingly. This is not a spiritual succesor to SWAT at all. With rumblings of PVP being talked about i'd stay wary. Might just end up a slightly more tactical R6:S. Plenty of other games like that. If you want something fun to Solo, this really isn't it, the enemy AI requires mods to make it functional, and Team AI is no exception. Pathing is often a major issue, even on Dev built maps, and orders rarely, if ever are followed properly, usually resulting in a dead teammate when all I wanted was a gun secured. Got friends to play with? Might love the game then. If the game ever lives up to it's initial promises, even slightly, I'll change my review, but for now I'm sick of community art ♥♥♥♥ being the most consistent dev content released.
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: I've put a good chunk of hours into this game only to watch it slowly get worse. If you like moving in slow motion (you cant even properly step through a doorway like you would actually clear one) while getting head shotted through corners while your friendly ai body blocks you after every room you try to clear, then by all means. But if you plan to play solo, save your money. I regret it, especially for the price tag of 40$.
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I have followed this game on youtube, seen others playing it, having a blast. I can't say I'd recommend it for one main reason.I can't recommend this game as it feels somewhat pointless to play. There's no progression, no goal, no real punishment beyond negative points that don't even matter. You load up, lock in and just do missions... that's it.As far as gameplay QUALITY goes, the graphics are fantastic and I see nothing wrong with the mechanics of the game at all. You actually have to be tactical and play as you would approach things somewhat realistically.Overall it's a 3 out of 5 stars. It's okay, but it leaves much to be desired. Hopefully future updates will give players something to work towards, or some reason to stick around.
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: For now - Negative. I will re-purchase this after their next major update.Coming from all the others (Ground Branch, Zero Hour, Insurgency, etc) - I feel having 1-2 enemy bots per player is boring, and there's nothing but empty hallways, rooms and areas that could host them. The game is visually appealing, and that's great, but the gameplay isn't really there, nor the excitement other than the 90's bond movie music when an enemy spots you. For 30$ less, you can get Zero Hour, which may not look as pleasing, but much more content and stuff to well..shoot at. I understand they want a SWAT feel - but how many times are you going to enjoy passing through the same empty rooms to reach the same one with a single enemy in it over and over again? The bots don't even patrol around really, and with all the great visuals this game has, it does nothing for you in terms of gameplay. No reason to gain cover if there's barely any enemies, or any enemies using it to conceal themselves. Just...nothing.Furthermore - a Glock pistol should be the easiest weapon to keyframe it's animations correctly and actually reload realistically. The weapon model textures are on point, but the animations are silly. The recoil feels a little too vertically forced on the AR platform, rather than a random direction or at least a screen shake effect. Muzzle flashes are brighter than they realistically are, too. Game has a nice framework down, but it needs a lot more sprucing up. I don't see too much replayability here for the value/cost of the game. Especially when others with more content are selling for cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Ready or Not

_childDocuments_.review: ***Edit: I am positive VOID bought and paid over half of these positive reviews.***Ready or Not, this game isn't ready and was way over hyped even for early access.Problems with the game:1. Civilians are skinned the same as terrorists so there is no way to tell the difference unless they are shooting you in the face.2. Not every civilian should freak out or require tazoring to surrender.3. Commands and interact are on the same key which is very inconvenient when trying to be stealthy and yelling to get down while trying to lockpick a door.4. No intel given before mission like a preview map of the area with multiple entry points that allow a player to choose. Suggestions to add:1. Cutting power to give the nvg's an actual advantage above enemy ai.2. IR laser should be implemented to every gun.3. Add repelling to buildings.4. If I need to lockpick a door and click that option it should have me do that function instead of pulling out the lockpick and then having to click on it again to unlock the door.If everyone says these developers are as good as they say they are and care about the game I see no reason why these won't be fixed in the coming future, but as of right now, I am not having as much fun as I expected. For me, I'll be playing Zero Hour.

I'm all for difficulty, but I'd also like the game to at least pretend it's trying to be fair.Also the atmosphere here is super immersive and frankly this is an incredibly effective horror game. Copaganda it may be, but man, it's compelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be blunt. This game is not ready, pun intended. Put it back in the oven for another 6 to 8 months. I followed and tested this game from its initial alpha stage to release. I witnessed many changes from then to now. There used to be a planning stage. You could spend points to modify the operation like having a sniper watch the perimeter or use a negotiator to reduce the number of hostages. The Police HQ looked completely different. There was a Tarkov-like movement system that allowed for incremental changes to movement speed. The customization screen looked different and was pretty bad tbh. You had multiple mission types for each level like active shooter or bomb defusal. Even the gas station was completely different. The game now is just decent, when it's working. It lacks ambition and practically screams lack of clear direction and identity. The narrative push that was emphasized in trailers is completely absent here. There are virtually no cutscenes. Dynamic voicelines are largely absent. Your bland AI squadmates have zero personality. This is in stark contrast to the squadmates in SWAT 4 who spoke like actual people instead. The single player campaign is barebones and badly designed. Stress management is a bad mechanic that adds no real depth and has no business in a game like this. Why should I care about how my AI partners are feeling when there's no story or characters to speak of? There's nothing fun or compelling about having to sit out squadmates for three missions so they can go to therapy. This isn't Darkest Dungeon. It's just a layer of tedium that only exists to force you to play more non-lethally. However, given how aggressive and fearless suspect AI is, this approach feels suicidal. This is extra annoying since you can't restart missions. The devs could at least clearly explain how stress works instead of being purposely vague.AI across the board is a mess and still not as good as SWAT 3 from the 90s. Squad AI will make stupid decisions like stacking up next to an open doorway when the door is blocking their view of inside the room. They get anxious way too easily when things get too hectic for them. You can't even add AI bots in co-op which is something else SWAT 3 had.Suspects barely react to being shot repeatedly. They don't prioritize their own life. They just want to kill you by any means necessary. Suspects can get shot and still rush your location. Suspect AI feel like trained militia which feels inappropriate given the context of some missions. They'll shoot through multiple walls sometimes to hit you which is impressive. They must play a lot of CS:Source. SWAT 4 balanced this by making it so that suspects will slowly react to being ordered to drop their weapon. They'd slowly lower the weapon and either drop it fully or start aiming again to kill you. RoN just has them either drop their weapon or immediately attack upon being ordered to surrender. Don't start with the realism argument either. This is a video game. No one would send 5 SWAT officers to take on 10+ armed suspects like these games do. I don't want reality because reality is harsh and not as exciting as games make it out to be. I do want immersion though and this AI is not immersive. Also, what it realistic about having gear be unlocked through getting high ratings on specific missions? I didn't realize real SWAT officers had battlepasses.So basically if you take it slow and prioritize preserving everyone's life, you risk hostages dying, bombs detonating, and you and your team getting injured/dying which will plummet stress and make you fail the mission or get a low rating. However, if you go fast and aggressive shooting any armed suspects, you risk getting a low rating or failing for killing suspects you HAVE to arrest and plummeting stress due to all the violence. It's a lose/lose situation with this game. This leads to a dumb meta of farming easier early missions just to be able to take on later harder missions which is largely antithetical to the intended design. Old R6 games fixed this by making it so that you could restart the mission changing squads, loadouts, plans, and trying it again as many times as you want until you got the outcome you wanted and continue from then on accepting all the consequences.Regarding the technical state, this game stutters like it was bullied in high school. Performance can range wildly from 30 to 120 FPS. I've had frequent random disconnects when me or any of my friends try to host a game. The servers aren't very good either. I've had the mouse cursor get stuck on screen removing my ability to move or interact with anything forcing a full restart. My loadout would get reset to default every time we loaded back into the HQ. We'd load into missions and suddenly everyone has the cosmetic appearance as the host. Operation Rust Belt just wouldn't load for us at all.Some parts of the game just look unfinished. What is with those SWAT van loading screens? There's no sound at all and outside the windows it looks like you're either on the surface of the Sun or in a black hole. The Police HQ is so quiet which is bizarre. NPC's stand around just staring at you. There's no dialogue at all. Mirrors have no reflections. Shadows, lighting, and textures in some areas can look extremely low-res.I praise the complex and varied level design and dark subject matter of missions. It's still fairly sanitized to avoid too much controversy. Environmental storytelling is great and definitely reflects the design philosophy of SWAT 4 missions. The game still looks great and sounds mostly good. Guns don't sound that different when firing outside versus firing indoors. There could be more voice lines as well. It's a confusing game since playing the way it was intended just isn't fun. Playing like it's R6 terrorist hunt is fun, but is punished. In the end, this game is directionally confusing to me. It's lacking polish, content, and a memorable campaign. Removing mission types was a massive mistake imo. For $50, it's just not worth it. Come back after months of patches and maybe it'll be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential, but you can run the same build every time without it making a difference.  The game doesn't reward you for using flash/stinger/gas in some situations over others.  I loaded into a map in a forest with a cabin thinking I should take long-ranged sniper-type weapon since it's outside and the cabin has a lot of openings.  I had no opportunity to use my ranged gun because we were forced by the game to enter the building and immediately start fighting in close quarters.  You can't even change the build of your teammates—they are all immune to flashbangs and gas, so there is even less of an opportunity/reward for proactively planning out a full gas team when you're the only one without automatic gas immunity, or a close-quarters breach team if you will have close quarters breach teammates no matter what, or a ranged team that snipes before going in if there's no opportunities for long-ranged combat.  The game just forces you into one playstyle and does not reward creativity.  The most of a reward for creativity you’ll get is choosing between night vision goggles and a flash light if the map takes place at night time.  You would think you could get clever and use a taser/pepper spray with a riot shield?  Nope, it doesn't let you, even though you can hold a pistol in your off-hand with the riot shield.  You clear each room with whatever charge and shoot from an angle, or you can open the door with a riot shield and shoot.  These are the only two ways to play.  I wish enemies would move around more, flank you, plan ambushes, maybe set traps rather than just have people standing still in each room in most maps waiting for you to enter.  I also wish people would actually pose a greater threat after surrendering, since they rarely will do anything after putting their hands up meaning there’s very little tension.  The game just doesn’t feel tense when you go door-to-door with no threats in between.  I used to spend a ton of time planning for each individual map, telling my team to hold angles, etc, but now I just run and gun with the riot shield and haven't died since.  While the graphics are great, it feels more like slow-paced Call of Duty than an actual tactical shooter that rewards for proactive planning, creativity, patience, and attention to detail.There's also just a missing sense of progression throughout the story.  You start off equally as strong early on as you are in the end of the game, except with fewer cosmetic options.  Bullets don't feel nearly as lethal as they are in real life since after shooting someone wearing a T-Shirt 4 times, they will surrender while acting fully functional, so I'm not sure why they made a point of adding non-lethal weapons.  That’s not to mention how in single player mode, missions don't necessarily feel like they get progressively harder.  They start off harder than many of the later ones you encounter and don't seriously get difficult until the last missions in the game, which even then aren't so bad.  Multiplayer is too easy—people just run in and one-tap enemies before you can even catch up with them, often dying from recklessness early on forcing the entire team to restart, so there's no real reason to play multiplayer when the little emphasis on being tactical in single-player goes completely out the window with trigger-happy teammates.  (It’s nice that it exists though in case you want to play with a friend.)  And I wish there was more of a purpose to the planning phase, which is one giant static empty police headquarters with two points of interest (the mission board and the customization at the shooting range).  Frequent crashing which resets mission progress is also a significant issue I haven’t been able to solve after significant time trying, and the game’s modding support feels very underdeveloped—you have to manually edit your own files in your computer in order to even add a music mod to the game.    It might be worth $20 at this stage, but definitely not the $50 it's at right now.  It feels like the game is still in beta and has not earned the price of a triple-A title quite yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game get's close but it's not there and not a finished game. Pushed out the door long before it is finished.The good is that the gun's feel good and reactive. The missions are interesting and has tons of environmental story telling. However my issues are long from customization to AI, with AI being the biggest issue.My issues begin with missing a lot of typical SWAT weapons (All categories; rifles, compacts, sub machine guns, shotguns, pistols). No laser light combos. Flashlights don't blind enemies and only illuminate the area (no strobe mode for the flashlight either). Lack of customization (it feels dated by today's standards) for guns and officers. The lighting in the area also makes no difference, being able to cut lights and power and getting advantage in the dark would be so cool, but pointless anyways because of AI issues.The biggest problem with this game is the AI. Starting with the lack of self preservation, if the AI has a gun it will shoot at you, even if you get the jump barrel in back and all, the only way they will surrender is if you stun them in anyways and command them to drop their weapon (gas, taser, pepper-ball, or beanbag), otherwise you can risk their death by shooting them just enough that they surrender. Second gripe is each enemy AI seems to be a John Wick Terminator hybrid. They will whip around and shoot you through cover. If they even notice your pinky-toe you're getting blasted. Otherwise it's fun to play for a few hours, but beyond that limitations in the game dawn the realization that this quarter baked game is letting down in too many areas to really recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected this game to be WAY, WAAAAY WORSE than what was actually delivered as an Alpha EA product here. It's a great tactical and quite realistic game. There is a high level of polish and attention to detail here already (factoring in how LONG this game has been developed already that should be kind of expected though tbh). Is it perfect? No. The AI is the main detracting part of the whole here, while being unpredictable and "different" than your average AI pixel-man, they certainly perceive you through certain walls and are way more mobile, accurate and deadly than they PROBABLY should be. I am not against having a challenge, but AI literally seeing you through one door, but not another one, and instant headshoting you out of a TURN with the first round THROUGH your "heavyarmor and faceplate" is kinda BS. It's an ALPHA though so I am confident this will change, but having said that seemingly universal excuse for lacking elements in any game these days (what even is a finished game today?!), I am not entirely confident in the DEVELOPER. They certainly have provided an experience here that is certainly worth the baseline asking price, so I am very VERY content with what I bought and what is ahead, but we shouldn't forget that this game has been developed for YEARS AND YEARS already, rotating through a BUNCH of staff, a BUNCH of CONTROVERSY and at least TWO publishers. While I genuinely applaud Void Interactive for sticking to their vision and working at their own pace, there are certainly VERY MANY problems associated with the ongoing development of this title and I dread that, what we got, is going to be what we "get" in the long run and that this is in fact a build that is the cream of the crop of years of developing, leaving us to wait for several years more for something more substantial and "final". It is worth the base price. It is DEFINITELY NOT worth the ABSURD price of the supporting addition IMHO. I love the vision we have gotten here and hope the game continues to be finished up in the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my recommendation is a qualified yes, if you don't mind modding a bit. I had my eye on this for a long time, being someone who grew up playing Sierra titles including the Police Quest / SWAT series, and in particular was blown away by SWAT 4 and its sense of both tactical gameplay and immersion. Seeing that RoN seems like the spiritual successor, I finally got a computer that could run it and dove in right before and subsequent to the 1.0 release.My thinking is that the game isn't really ready. The biggest problem is that the suspect AI is way overtuned. They will 360 noscope you through walls and around corners and given that the commander mode makes deaths extremely punishing, it genuinely makes the game "not fun," and "a slog." However, there are mods that tone down the AI, and if you install those, the game becomes much more enjoyable. That aside, there are some issues that make me question whether or not it's ready for a full release. Many of the artistic assets seem AI generated and weren't given a once-over by a dev. The tone of the game veers a little bit too much into copaganda at times, and unrealistically so in my opinion. While policing is a difficult profession, the game elides the near godlike authority that police have over citizens bodies and lives. For example, if you shoot a civilian or suspect intentionally, your fellow AI teammates will immediately kill you. Full disclosure I am an attorney who has occasionally sued police in the past for excessive force, and I will tell you that I have never seen fellow officers take action to even restrain a brother or sister in blue from committing what are, frankly, crimes. There's also a bunch of posters up around HQ that just overall give an overly saccarine impression of what the police are there to do.Don't get me wrong, as I think policing is both difficult and necessary. If you have a situation like an active shooter, then you'd better hope you've got a SWAT team ready to go in and deal with it. I just think RoN's take is overall a little too simplistic and one-sided, and I think it could be much better tonally if it fell somewhere in the middle where it can recognize police are not always a force for good either. The gunplay is visceral (which, ironically, the developers of SWAT 4 noted that they wanted the gunplay to not feel good because if shots got fired, they considered that to be failure), and sometimes feels more like you're a soldier than a police officer. The environments are very detailed if lacking in interactivity. In the 1.0 update they introduced callouts from AI teammates that respond to the environment, and they help a lot with the immersion but some more voiced lines from the player character would help as well (e.g. when you're collecting evidence you bark a boilerplate line as opposed to remarking on what you're collecting.The bones of a really good game are here, but it's still got some tweaking that needs doing to it to really get it to shine. Hopefully the developers are going to continue work on it, but until then there's a strong modding community.

_childDocuments_.review: Utter garbage. This was in testing for several years and simple known bugs have still not been fixed. It still crashes if you push-to-talk during a loading screen. The AI fixes which have been implemented just aren't consistent. There is no reward for playing the game in the manner in which it's designed. _childDocuments_.review: Though there are many positives about this game, I am forced to give it a negative review due to issues that shouldn't be ignored; some issues are blaring, and others are not talked about enough in the community.The most blaring issue that you will notice right away is the optimization. To put it simply, the game is poorly optimized. My RTX 3070 struggles to run it at a consistent 45 FPS on high settings, and it's been like this since launch. I get 110 FPS in RDR2, which I would say is comparable in graphical fidelity to the game. But it gets worse - in medium and even low settings, I get lagspikes, I can't get consistent framerates above 45, all while the game looks pretty mediocre at those graphics settings. Given that the game is a tactical FPS, this takes away from the experience drastically and can be extremely frustrating at times.Another issue, less obvious, but very meaningful to me, is how the Supporters have been treated. I bought the supporter edition in May of 2020 and have been able to see quite a bit of behind-the-scenes activity since then. Though I can't get into certain things due to an NDA that all supporters had to sign, I can say that I feel like VOID has achieved what they promised. The management of the company succumbed to social pressures to avoid making RoN the experience it should have been (some of these pressures being created by scummy gaming journalist sites like Kotaku), and communication with supporters has been minimal outside of Discord. This was truly highlighted by the release of the first, and so far, only DL.C. Supporters received it for free, but it was a half-baked set of levels that unfortunately didn't live up to either the main game or it's spiritual predecessor, SWAT 4. The only communication supporters got in the months before the DLC release were screenshots of levels and promotional tidbits that did little to communicate the true points of the levels. As someone who invested in this game, I was hoping I would be given a little bit more information than that.The final thing I'm gonna say is there's blaring gameplay issues that have been present since Day One of the Public Release - just under three years ago now. Namely, the AI are all bullet sponges that act like John Wicks, except your own teammates. Room clearing is extremely frustrating when you get shot by something with an instantananous reaction time, way too much health, and the aim of a CoD player on console (auto-aim but better).Overall, if you have a NASA supercomputer and are OK with blaring gameplay issues not being solved, feel free to check it out. Otherwise, I'd recommend you to stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: SWAT 4 was one of my all time favorite game ever since its release. Been playing it a lot, usually every few months. Even played it this year too. I was a huge fan of the game, so a few years ago when I first heard about Ready Or Not, I was so hyped, and I've been following the development process. It got harder to wait for this game after each biweekly briefing.Well, the wait is over, the game is finally out. Even it's in early access, it doesn't feel like it at all: really polished, feels almost complete, well optimized. It's in better state than most fully released games in this category.I only played it for 12 hours so far, and I feel like I'm only scratching the surface, there's more to do, to find out, etc. I only managed to get A ranking on every Barricaded Suspect mission on all maps except the farm map and the classified levels, and an A and a B ranking on Raids in 2 maps. I failed all the other game modes, I still gotta learn and get more familiar with some game elements. That's how in-depth the game is. I haven't encountered any major or game-breaking bug, only a few cosmetic bugs. The game runs well, better than I expected. I play on Epic settings in 1440p, running on a PC with an i5-8600K and an RTX 2070 Super. FPS never drops below 60, except a few times, when having teammate's camera on for too long.Content wise, we have like 6 or 7 complete maps, most maps can be played in multiple game modes. Map layouts are slightly different for each game mode, and like in SWAT 4, each playthrough is unique: opponents and civilians aren't assigned to the same room over and over again, and their numbers are different with each restart too. Traps' type and locations are randomized as well. Opponents from other rooms/locations can come investigate if they hear and explosion or gunshots, they also can flee if they hurt and outnumbered. the AI is very smart, which also makes every mission unique and keeps you on your toes.I haven't found the game repetitive so far, but at some point it may get repetitive, until new maps (and maybe game modes) arrive.Also keep in mind this isn't a typical Call of Duty or Battlefield sort of game: It's kinda slow-paced, and highly tactical. You can't survive if you try to blast your way through and/or if you don't use your head and don't command your team. In the beginning, you might die, a lot. There's no progression system, as it's not a super-soldier game. Your progression is as you get better, eventually you'll be able to complete most mission without dying, and even without police and civilian casualties.Honestly, I can highly recommend this game, and I'm looking forward what the future holds for it. It's well worth it's price, and it's still in active development with a lot to come, so it's definitely a bargain to get this game right now.

I'm slapping a solid 9/10 on this bad boy – and for good reason!First things first, playing with friends is a riot. Well, unless they decide it's funny to shoot you in the back – classic move, right? The camaraderie is golden, and even the betrayal is hilarious in a twisted way. It's like a rollercoaster of emotions, and I'm loving every minute of it.Let's talk graphics – they're downright crazy! The attention to detail is insane, and every gunshot feels like it's echoing in your soul. Seriously, the devs nailed it. The visuals and sound design are on point, adding a layer of immersion that cranks up the whole experience."Ready or Not" isn't just a one-and-done kind of game. It's a grind-worthy beast. The replayability factor is off the charts. Every time you jump in, things shake up, and you've got to adapt on the fly. It keeps you on your toes, and that's what makes it so damn addictive.If you're into FPS games that make your heart race and your palms sweaty, "Ready or Not" is your jam. Trust me, it's worth the grind. This game is like a wild ride that you never want to end. Get in there, lock and load, and let the chaos begin!

_childDocuments_.review: Maps are brilliant, and there's a decent amount of customisation for weapons, equipment and tools. What I like about this game is it can go from 0 to 100 really quickly. The atmosphere and sound design is really good. The game could use some optimisation to improve framerates and the size of the game is something like 90GB which is disproportionately high for how much of the game there is. The AI is a double edged sword. For the majority of the time it is awesome. They can coordinate together, flank you, reposition, hold a corner or door, and brutally punish you quickly for mistakes. Often times, if they spot you before you spot them then you will be killed (which is enjoyable and challenging). But unfortunately, on rare occasions they can be inhumanely unfair. Sometimes turning 90 degrees, snapping onto you and one tapping you in the space of 0.2 seconds. Me and my friend also experienced a glitch only a couple of times where for the duration of a map an AI will be just shooting at your position constantly from some unknown location where the gunfire follows you wherever you go.Overall, a good game that is brutally punishing and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Limited in content, but a solid core to be built onSadly after 1.0, little has been built upon, though the team 100% deserve credit for the friendly AI orders system and behaviour. Be under no illusions, this is not a game about being a police officer. The game's 'suspects' do not behave like criminals, often offensively rushing your team to try and kill you, rather than attempting to flee. Another problem is the team size. 5 officers is simply not enough for to achieve victory in missions such as Ides Of March, where you are pit against multiple heavily armed fighters who show now self preservation and actively manoeuvre against your team. This is not the right place for 5 people or police officers really. Overall, still worth keeping an eye on Ready Or Not (I have had 77 hours of entertainment), but its not worth getting if you're looking for an experience akin to SWAT3 & 4. There are also better tactical shooters available if you're looking for a military setting instead of police.

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite tactical shooter in the market right now. Ready or not is a great game for those who want something more methodical, it's far from perfect but it's a niche cqb game. The fact that cqb tactics work here is what really attracts me to this game, also the encounters can be very dynamic not knowing what to expect and what will happen. Some of the encounters will stress you, with suspects tricking you by shooting at you and then running to another room, going silent, and waiting for you to make the mistake of chasing them and getting blasted in the next room. Some even go completely quiet, holding and angle, waiting for you to open a door exposed to the fatal funnel and getting blasted. Some fake surrender, they even drop on their knees then pull a gun on you if you drop your guard.Personally I'm not a big fan of multiplayer and coop games, and gladly this game now has a good swat AI to assist you. Not only to assist you, but you can literally clear a room with them by being their wingman or taking point and them clearing with you. They even go to their points of domination now, they pull security, they watch your six, move in different formations. I never liked the coop in this game as most players just want to shoot everyhing and run and gun, with the swat AI not only you can follow strictly the RoE you can also go very methodical. I'm glad that void thought of us single player enthusiasts by doing this. I hope more tactical shooters will have this option.My only complaint is about some of the suspects being way too suicidal and always pulling a gun on you, even when you catch them by surprise with 5 guns pointed at them, most stil feel the need to go for their gun and then get shot but Void is currently working to improve that and for now there are several mods on nexus to fix this,If you're into tactical shooters and used to play the old swat games, I'd definitely give this a go. Also if you're like me, getting old, and have no more patience to be talking over the mic all the time, the swat AI is there for you watching your six always. And trust me, the swat AI will be more tactical, more team oriented and clear a room better than 90% of the lobbies you try to play but you also need to know and learn to use them. A lot of players complain about the swat AI being weak but they give the wrong orders, forcing them to be exposed to multiple threats and angles which will eventually cause their death. My favourite part of this is that your mistake will cost you and sometimes even with the perfect tactic you'll still fail. You can't just go through a well defended threshold, with guns pointed at that threshold expecting you'll come out alive, and Ready or Not will definitely put you in your place. A lot of players complain about this but if you check most of the lobbies, you'll know exactly why most players keep dying and i'm glad that Void is not backing down.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun game but needs A LOT more content. The content it does have right now is pretty great. The guns and customization in this game is A1, the team AI is spectacular. Enemy AI is both insanely stupid and smart at the same time somehow but their stupidity will get you killed often. There's not much content but you can play each map over and over again with new gear and strats so it's not terrible. Once this game has like 5-8 more maps, more gadgets, modes, enemy types, etc etc I can fully recommend it. As for bugs, there's a few small ones but it's honestly not bad. The content you do get is great but it just needs more. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've slammed 50+ hours into this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game in less than a week, if this game ain't what I was looking for on a tactical shooter, I don't know what is.My opinion aside, what is Ready or Not?Ready or Not at this point in time IS the closest thing you can get to the real deal regarding CQB simulation on video games in my humble opinion, now this opinion of mine comes with some caveats: I do NOT have formal training or certified experience from any public or private security company, be that enforcing as a police officer, nor have I been in military service, I am but the one guy that loves tactical simulators, I have played the vast majority of them, and I have some theorical knowledge of CQB that I've learned from my own research on the internet for fun / roleplay purposes in these kind of games, and I must admit, that from all the games I have played, applying those basic concepts from the CQB professionals I've heard over the course of time really hits home with this one.From the tools down to the AI that's about to get a massive update in behaviour that will further add towards realism, this will probably be the best SWAT guy experience you'll find out there period.Down side to all this would be optimization if you have a medium performance machine, but that's not really an issue since the game is early access and will be solved in due time, and the few maps/locations you can play on, which as well, isn't big of a deal... thanks to the developers going one step further and releasing OFFICIAL COMMUNITY MODDING very early on, YES... you heard that right, official modding on a 2022 early access? sounds ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane, but it isn't. It's a gift from the gods, specially because of how easy it is to mod.Do I think it's woth it for the price? do I think it will be worth it in the future for the price? Yes on both regards.The main experience of the game is using tactics to your advantage and if you are a CQB fan like me, then you'll find plenty to test in this game, you can play with 4 AI squad mates with a wide arrange of orders, or you can team up with some buddies through match making or inviting some of your own peeps over to play, fairly simple.Nothing but good vibes for these devs, I wish I lived in a 1st world country so I could support them further, until I get more money to toss at them, I will keep the heavens packed with fresh souls that smell faintly of meth and anarchism.Good hunting operators.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much right now because it's in beta but what's there is really solid.This isn't like other shooters where you are a tank. You will die instantly if you are caught off guard and you can only take a few shots (depending on the weapon), even with the heaviest armor. Also, your injuries will impair you for the rest of the match, and when you are bleeding you can't see ♥♥♥♥ until you 'heal yourself' (by pressing F, whatever that means).The enemies will also shoot through doors or walls and you can do the same. Overall I would say the AI isn't exceptional. You can gun down a bunch of enemies in one room and their friends will just be chilling upstairs, but it's still difficult. If you aggro a group of guys they will try to hide and catch you off guard or flank you. Sometimes perps will pretend to be innocent and then try to shoot you if you look away.With good tactics I managed to clear most of the levels with a friend, but you need to be smart and use tools like the mirror gun to peek under doors, as well as flashbangs/gas/etc to breach. Some doors are also trapped which can really ♥♥♥♥ you if you don't disarm them.One thing I will say that's amazing about this game is the sound and feel of firearms and gunfights. Guns are LOUD and when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan, smoke fills the room and it can feel like complete chaos. There is a shield which is pretty useful, but you can't aim well with a sidearm while using it (you mostly need to rely on laser dots), and the shield is far from impenetrable. If it takes enough damage or you take a shotgun point blank it won't save you, and you can still get injured even if you don't die. When you shield is getting shot your camera also shakes all over the place and the glass panels break.Overall the game is really immersive, fun and intense.

I’m not saying it’s the greatest game ever made nor am I saying it’s better than [blank] any game you can compare it against, I’m saying that for me, personally, given my personal, unique preference in games, which admittedly is a very small niche genre really, that Ready or Not is hands down the best game thus far I have ever played. There. That was surprisingly difficult, and I’m not exactly sure why.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game for the listed price in its current state. It has a long way to go before I would say it is remotely worth $40.The gameplay loop for RoN in its current state is extremely stale. You walk around the map (because SWAT are not trained in running or even jogging; even when under heavy fire), try to arrest or kill the bad guys, look for extremely ambiguous and vague evidence, rescue whatever civilians are on the map, and repeat. This sounds all good and dandy until you spend 45 minutes walking around the hotel map trying to find that one civilian that ran away and is preventing you from completing the mission. Objectives placed around the map are not obvious (unless you are looking at them and get a prompt to collect them) and are very easily missed.There are not any briefings or maps to inform you of the layout of the mission you are entering. This would be extremely handy on maps like Brisa Cove that require you to find objectives in specifically named rooms that don't have the name anywhere in the mission.SWAT cannot run. This makes both chasing after fleeing enemies and traversing the level extremely tedious, monotonous and not fun. The player can lower their weapon to move barely faster, but you are still going to be outran by the other AI. On this same topic, there are not any small maps outside of the WIP restaurant level. Each level added in the updates has become larger and larger. Expect taking 30+ minutes to clear a mission because you cannot move faster than Grandma with her walker. And again, low-ready is not your sprint input.You cannot cancel any animations (switching to your secondary while reloading your primary) with another action.Armor no longer stops incoming fire as of the June update meaning that you die in 2-3 hits, no matter if you are wearing heavy armor with front, side and back steel plates.The AI (both friendly and hostile) are godawful. To start, friendly AI do not (even after the June update) have a sense of personal space and will crowd the player; blocking them in doorways and putting Dogmeat to shame. Since the update they have difficulty opening doors to clear the room behind them and will just stand there while getting beat on by an enemy with a melee weapon. They rarely react to an enemy shooting at them from cover and will allow themselves to get gunned down. On occasion they'll freeze in place and be stuck there for the remainder of the mission. Other times they will sit in one place while you direct them to do something and will not follow any commands.Enemy AI on the other hand, are a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. As of the June update, they have slightly better behavior, but are still lacking. A lot. They are still able to shoot you when their weapons are facing the ground or away from you. They track you through walls even if you are nowhere nearby. They have nearly 100% accuracy (from any range and constantly put Chris Kyle to shame) and can shoot perfectly around your armor, leaving you with a bunch of fatal wounds. They do not react to getting shot and are put to shame by GoldenEye's AI. They will take multiple headshots to drop when wearing nothing but the skin of their head. They can run which is incredibly tedious when you, the player, cannot. If the AI has a shotgun, expect to get one shot killed from any distance. If the AI has a knife, expect them to appear out of thin air and kill you faster than you can turn around because of the stun effect. Civilian AI are not as bad, but manage to be annoying. They too can run away from the player (because the player has not evolved to be able to run) and hide somewhere on the map, making you have to spend the extra time to hunt them down. A majority of the time they do not follow commands (or melee hits) to surrender and will just stand there, preventing arrest.While I have enjoyed playing the game, it has gotten to the point where I am teetering the line of uninstalling it. For a game that is $40 AND early access, it is definitely not worth the cost. My complaints could easily get fixed, or they'll stay in the game like they have for the last however many updates and not get addressed. Will update this review as things change in later updates.- Enemy AI rarely exhibit their new behaviors. They will go from roam to kill mode when they sense a disturbance in the force. They still have insane accuracy and are still able to shoot/kill you when their weapon is pointed away from you.- Armor is broken yet again and is ignored when receiving damage from enemy gunfire.- The "all" category on the weapon loadout menu adds too much clutter. I recommend removing it and having the individual weapon categories instead.- shotgun fire crashes the fast food mission- movement speed is better, but still needs a sprint function to get around the map faster.Also what is the point of having a jump input if you can't jump or climb on anything? Having sprint would be more functional than a jump- Enemy melee attack is still far better than the player's attack. Still no fighting chance at close range if you get booped- Melee range is messed up again. Missed multiple hits at close range only to get clobbered by the enemy AI- NVGs are still about as useful as wearing sunglasses at night- Cannot place door wedges occasionally- Enemy AI can open a door that is wedged- Friendly AI are useless with non-lethal weapons and will get gunned down without putting up a fight- Pepper spray, door wedges, the battering ram and M32 are unusable by AI- You are unable to mix/match equip JHP rounds if you have AP rounds equipped when using the +5 magazine on the M4. Doing so will set all your ammo to AP.- Player character resets to Alabama/Judge after every game- Enemy AI continue to track the player through walls- Enemy AI are not affected by deterrents (flashbang, CS, that grenade thing, pepper spray/ball) on occasion- Performance has taken a massive hit. I have a R7-3800X with a RTX 3090 and am getting on average around 40-50FPS on some maps.- Occasionally headshots will not one shot kill when using JHP if the person has a ballistic vest equipped- Friendly AI continue to freeze up on each map and become unresponsive to any commands or actions- Friendly AI on are unable to follow the "secure evidence" command if they just entered a door via team-specific commands. They will be unable to follow a command that involves enemies or evidence for the rest of the match- Saved loadout presets do not change when swapping team members to customize. For example, if I have "class A" on "self" and switch to "alpha", it will show "class A" instead of the correctly named preset.- loadout menu only displays Judge instead of the different operators.- Doors do not always get blown off the hinges when breached with explosives and will remain suspended in the air- Friendly AI freeze if you queue a command, cancel it, then queue another command.- Friendly AI still freeze if you command them to restrain an enemy. Fixing requires pushing the enemy to a better spot or doing it yourself. Can lead to the AI becoming stuck in a loop that is only fixable by restarting the mission.- armor still does not stop enemy rounds- jumping no longer works and inputs the default command- friendly AI cannot restrain some enemies- friendly AI freeze on half the new levels- friendly AI still do not trigger explosive traps- AI ragdoll and spin through the air occasionally when incapacitated causing the game to crash- cannot restrain some incapacitated AI- If you kill an enemy that is being restrained you will lose your weapons until you interact with another object- Numerous weapons that use the holographic sight are not zeroed. The reticle/crosshair is zeroed ~1" too high.

_childDocuments_.review: SWAT 4 does it better honestly.This game crashed on me, no joke, 6 times during loading screens before I could actually play a mission. The guns look and sound nice, and feel responsive and realistic, but actually killing enemies with them doesn't feel satisfying at all. The blood/gore effects leave much to be desired (bullet wounds look like actual paintballs hit the bodies), ragdoll physics are janky, and most of all, the suppression mechanic simply isn't fun - you can't fire back when you are suppressed. I don't mind the visual and audio effects when you are suppressed, but not allowing the player to at least panic fire blindly is an abhorrent design choice. Performance is questionable, on max settings i was getting a steady 120-144 fps, but the frame rate would plummet to 15-20 and begin to stutter when you are getting shot at or you set off a breaching charge. Seems like it simply needs some optimization.i7-9750H @ 2.60 GHz16 GB RAMRTX 2060(running the game off of an external hard drive (not that that matters, but hey)With how the game is at the moment, and considering its been, what, 4 years since the game was announced, its not worth buying in its current state. _childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game at the current state, for several reasons:1) Despite the efforts they put in the suspect AI, the SWAT AI is still very rudimentary, unable to follow proper close quarter combat tactics, going straight into a room without pieing and taking corners, unable to position itself behind cover, unable to turn to the sound of threats, etc..2) The design of the maps are trending towards becoming gigantic mazes for the sole purpose of confusing players. I appreciate the fact that the feeling of unknown makes the gameplay more exciting. However, the maps should be primarily made with practicality in mind, the layout of a facility should first and foremost serve its purpose based on the background setting, instead of having convoluted corridors and rooms for no meaningful purpose. The map designs in HITMAN series strike a good balance.3) The scenarios of the missions are unrealistic. Imagine having only a 5-man team clearing such a huge area, without any other elements providing support, securing the parameters of buildings and areas that have been cleared. The game was made with being realistic in mind, yet the scenarios are still the same as Call of Duty type of fantasy where a small team of heroes save the day.

Because the graphics are amazing (if not a little poorly optimized, but still plenty usable), the stories and situations you are placed in are eerie and unsettling (in a good way) the combat is realistic and actually feels tactical (though could use a bit more flexibility in functions) and overall for being an indy dev title, this was an amazing product. _childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface this review by stating that I really have enjoyed Ready or Not but have some valid issues I cannot look over. It might come across quite scathing but I assure you I would change this review in a heartbeat should these issues be resolved. Optimisation: (non technical complaints at bottom) Ready or not has severe optimization issues. Playing orginally on a 1650 super then upgrading to a 3080 10gb, the performance continues to get worse every update. The fps at custom medium+ results in fps of 20-150. This is crazy swings that make gameplay hard to enjoy. I understand the 3080 isnt the top anymore but it should run a game like this reasonably. During gunfights due to the realistic muzzle flash and sound design, the game turns into a 5 fps slideshow of lag and misery that results In aching ears. However you only get this exclusive experience should the game load at all. If I clock on the icon, not only does steam have to boot, but I have to hope that the game doesn't take 4.5hrs to patch. By then usually I will delete the game only for steam to break and be unable to do anything until it deletes which never occurs. Trying to delete the game from the files just causes a re-installtion to occur therefore bricking my pc for hours in a terrible combination. Then if this is avoided the game has to launch a decorative pop-up first or else it will black screen. Then I have to join a unpolished solo experience or try multiplayer which loads to 100% before freezing and not working. Then if any other application is opened through the windows key it will black screen, I then have tried to use task manager multiple times just for the game to cover the window no matter what forcing a restart. This should not be a problem for a common pc setup for a 2 yr old game that has gone out of early access.Gameplay: Even if the game loads multiplayer, (which hasn't happened for nearly a year now in part due to my apathy before 1.0), the game still has core issues. While the game is designed to be slower paced the sheer amount of rooms and low denisty of suspects can make the game forced you to breach blind. There is jsut to much ground to cover and always just one guy with meth head aim, not enough of a threat to use a flash or frag, but enough to kill a teammate. This is case specific but still can kill your desire to play when you get killed for the 10th time by some ai hiding  in a corner with a shotgun which you couldn't really do anything about. This compounds with fps drops that I mentioned earlier leading to times where you die every time to intense lag. The true problem is that this is billed as a full game now. During early access I didn't complain because the dev team deserves support. But at this point other games, like scp 5k one of my favorites, give the same tactical experience at half the price, half the storage space, and in my case double the play time in a smaller period of ownership.Overall should the optimization along be fixed I would 100% positive the game, but this is legitimately the most broken unplayable and downright disappointing game I have on steam from a technical level. It could be so good, and some others have it work fine, bit no matter what i try, it seems to be unplayable. Ps. There are youtube tutorials about how to fix crashing in this game that are made by ai and just substitute words. Also there are tutorials the legitimately crash your PC or screw it up. I presume these are just people using a situation where people like me try to play a game that they bought which continues to degrade in playibility.

_childDocuments_.review: If your interest in this game is for a realistic depiction of S.W.A.T. , Close Quarters Combat, and an enjoyable single player experience I'd tell you keep moving. This game despite having a solid dark gritty atmosphere, decent customization and cool mission locals is a slog and drag to play. Your AI teammates have next to no autonomy and you're constantly pulled out of situations to play backseat SWAT expert to make your lackeys do anything. When they do act, autonomously or not, they DO NOT behave in anyway expected by QUALIFIED SWAT OFFICERS who should have at least a baseline understanding of CQB. The entire time it feels like baby's first CQB drill and you play as the alcoholic stepfather guiding his belligerent and unfortunately very slow sons into a hell they barely can comprehend or understand. Oh and god forbid you stand in your poor little chitlin's way or else they'll hit you with "I NEED YOU TO MOVE SIR" instead of doing exactly what you told them to do. That along with the Rules of Engagement that'd make anyone in the know cringe a hole in their uni brow, the AI will violate them anytime any fire fight is initiated 9 times out of 10. So good luck getting an A without spamming flashbangs and stinger grenades. All the while you get to struggle against and all knowing and all seeing enemy that is more cracked at shooting you in the head then a 14 y/o movement kid on Warzone. In stark contrast playing multiplayer missions, which are PVE, is actual a fairly fun experience and the challenge is actually welcome once you have teammates that can think for themselves and respond to threats accordingly. TL;DR Don't buy it till they fix the A.I., unless you really wanna struggle through with friends.
