_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)You enter with a team of SWAT officers into a building. The complex is enormous, and there is a deafening silence; as you spot a hostage, you realize they are signaling to you with their hands towards a door. You open it, and there is a terrorist inside. Ready or Not is an irregular co-op FPS in which you play through dreadful situations that pays a great deal of attention to details. The title's difficulty is serious as the atmosphere lets you soak in the situation's intensity. Doors can be booby-trapped with explosives, some enemies can become Jonh Wick, quickly dispatching you, and you must also ensure the hostage's security. The result is fierce gunfights in which coordination is critical to play objectives and providing a good chance of clearing the mission!Guns have an impact and can be customized to suit the player's playstyle, they are all unlocked from the get-go, and some accessories change how you play. You can take night vision for night maps or mirror guns to see below doors on layouts with tonnes of rooms. Enemies are unpredictable; they can double back to previous rooms or create elaborate ambushes. I had fun trying different approaches until I found one that clicked with me and the mission to beat those extreme raid maps.The best part of the game is the little details found in it. Maps have cellphones ringing on desks, structures are worked so flawlessly they look real-life wise, and the title map design is so good it appears to be done by architects. In addition, the sun's light can move and make it more difficult to see what's in the next room due to the harsh sunlight! There are different modes, with raid being the most predominant. Raid missions will test you to the limit as they feature lethal enemies and require multiple runs for a clear. That extends the game's replayability and can easily net 10-20 hours of gameplay. Grabbing your friends and tackling these missions make for entertaining game sessions that are memorable and fun! I had a good laugh when one of my friends blew himself opening a door that was an explosive trap!Ready or Not sound design is spectacular as you can issue commands to hostages and enemies to give up. It integrates into the gameplay as you can use these commands to make enemies speak, revealing their location, and the direction of the audio becomes a hint as to where to watch out for. The voice acting is similar to what one might expect from a police movie.When foes engage with the players, music will play to increase combat tension. The style of music is anxious and unnerving, following a loop that keeps you on edge as you check your corners and land your shots. Once combat is over, the creepy silence sets in again, making you feel uneasy no matter what.The game looks so beautiful one could believe it had ray tracing, as the reflections on the floor have unbelievable detail. Each map is distinctive from one another with the level of graphical fidelity replicating surfaces and brightness. The visual content allows the severity and gore of the situation to be more realistic on the screen. The game was tested with an RTX 2060, 36 GB of ram, Intel Core i7-11700K - Core i7 11th Gen Rocket Lake 8-Core 3.6 GHz LGA 1200.The results were 50-60 FPS on ultra with some drops to 30 FPS at times, while the game ran at 78-90 FPS with the settings set to medium. There can be a bit of a clunky feeling to the camera when snapping your wrist for fast movement, and talking with teammates by holding the key "V" was bothersome in the middle of gunfights. As an additional note, press the "L" once the mission starts to change to team voice chat, as it is easier for your teammates to hear your voice.  is a unique game in which players must eliminate threats, arrest suspects, and prioritize saving civilian life. A tactical FPS that tries to push into a more horrific direction, it is worth the price if you have friends to play with it or plan to make new ones in-game. I recommend the title to players who enjoy realistic simulations and want to try a more tense shooter experience.9/10  AMAZINGIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator StarsDeck!

_childDocuments_.review: If i had to describe this game in one word, it would be ambitious.It tries a lot of things, accomplishes many of them but some things end up being not ideal. And thats okay.Im loving my time with this game and the overall experience. Yes there are times where i got one shot from some completely stupid angle or something else immersion breaking happens.Yet those moments are forgotten very fast because theres so much to like about this game.- Great maps: Theres a huge diversity of settings. Going from small gas station, through farm of cultists to huge villa. Additionally every map has many details that help the storytelling. Briefings only include the information thats known to control, but you can discover the details as you go. And overall theres just so many little details to appreciate. On the night club mission you can for example hear phones going off everywhere, because the incident has blown up in media and the little things like this just really add so much to the experience and immersion. - Great Sounds: Guns sound good. Shooting and getting shot at sounds good. Voice acting is pretty good for the most part and the only criticism id have here is that some npcs really talk too much which makes them repeat their lines a bit too often. Little things like walking through a room with a bunch of casings on the floor sounds like youd expect that. Explosions and flashbangs going off sounds awesome too and the effects have a good amount of punch to them. The music supports all of this perfectly with genuinly intense tracks.- Great Customization: You can change so many things about your loadout. Take more mags for your primary but less pistol mags. Or less mags and more tacticals. Many non lethal options as well. You can tailor your loadout to a specific playstyle or map. I havent even touched most of the available equipment even though i really like to adjust everything to a new mission i play and fail first. Added to functional customization comes also a lot of visual customization, that has to be unlocked via progress (or mods).Oh and you can also adjust the loadout of your teammates.- Great "teamwork" even for Solo Players: The AI has its highs and lows. I heavily recommend looking into some mods to tweak the behaviour to your liking. Sometimes your team AI is useless and doesnt react correctly to threats, sometimes the enemy AI reacts to threats (you) too well. With mods it gets a lot better though and using different tactics is really enjoyable. It gives the game a lot of replayability value.While i could put down more points, the sum of it really is that theres so many things in this game that are well thought out, many small details that add a lot of value in the greater scope. But there are also moments that break your immersion or are just frustrating. As said in the intro. This game is ambitious and i cant help but forgive many of its faults for that. Some times things dont work too well, but man if they work this really is one hell of an experience. If you like to get immersed into this type of game, there really is no substitute for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of good things to say about this game but after it took nearly 2 hours to update a 2.4GB patch I had a lot of time to think about the game in it's current state as my frustration mounted between the dismal update speeds. That being said, I'm going to have to err on the negative side and not recommend this game. Keep in mind, the patch itself only took around 10 mins roughly to load, so it wasn't an internet issue. It was the verification process that took ages because as of update 1.0 it is still a pretty buggy mess.Okay, lets start with the positives: great AI, world building, good gameplay and fun with friends. It is in every sense of the world a successor to the acclaimed SWAT 4 series and it does its job well. The maps are expertly detailed, the gunplay feels solid and impactful and the tactical aspect is pretty fantastic, as expected. The SWAT AI has seen massive improvements too with 1.0 and its pretty great how they've thought out how the AI could be helpful rather than a hindrance to the player like in former versions of the game.Now, onto the negatives. Lets talk about the fact how the developer is just really absurdly inconsistent with keeping the community informed. At times they are excellent, providing detailed overviews of whats to come in new updates with gameplay footage and explanations in laymans terms, as to help the average player understand. But then, out of the blue, they'll go radio silent for MONTHS on end. This is behaviour I'd expect from amateur game devs, not a studio that has a solid reputation and thousands of supporters. This behaviour would have flown years ago when the game first entered early access. Its been literal years and the game is still in early access, but the devs have not shown a good commitment to improving their standing and keeping their community informed. Next, what the ♥♥♥♥ is up with the enemy AI? All that work put into the friendly AI is frankly negated if the enemy can 360 blindfire and one tap your character when they are completely flashed. To put it nicely, the enemy and civvie AI in this game is a buggy mess. For all the improvements of the friendly SWAT AI, the game completely nullifies them by the lack of polish and work done on EVERY OTHER ASPECT OF AI in this game. Don't believe me? Check out the subreddit as well as Youtube; there are plenty examples of what an inconsistent mess the enemy AI has been. Frankly speaking, I am very let down by this considering the game is considered 'completed' at 1.0. This is acceptable for a game early in the development cycle NOT a game that has been in early access for several years only to be presented with a buggy mess like this. Lets also talk of the lack of polish. While the levels of the games itself are very detailed and clearly have a lot of love put into them, the fact that much of the game lacks any real polish cannot be ignored. Simply put, the game just FEELS unpolished and janky, even with years of work put into it. The sad fact is, this inherent jankiness can be ignored if there was more love put into other aspects of the gameplay, such as the AI, but both of these problems in tandem just make for an unpleasant gameplay experience. The textures of the game are inconsistent, compounding the issues of lack of polish. The overall feeling is just...not great, even with years of development. Extremely disappointing as I've been closely following the development of this game for years and was extremely excited when it touted itself as a spiritual successor to SWAT 4. That being said, even SWAT 4, a 20 year old game at the time of writing feels more polished and smooth than this game does with it's next generation graphics.All this to lead into my next point, which is that, as of 1.0, this game is a buggy, unoptimised mess. From weapons glitching through the walls to absurdly poor file optimisation, the game is just messy in every aspect. It is unbelievable that, even with a dedicated team working on this game and no other projects, they have no found a better way to get the game to update. It is absurd that a 2.4GB patch takes 2 hours because of poor file optimisation leading to slow verifying times. For 176HKD, I honestly expected a bit more. In the past year I've owned this game, I've found myself coming to it less and less because of its frankly awful load times; in the past week alone I tried launching this game TWICE for quick play sessions only to realise that the slow patch cycles paired with the buggy mess of a menu made it impossible to even join a lobby to play the game. It is precisely these issues that make the game a novelty and unpleasant for new players to actually get into. With development progressing at such a slow rate, I'd expect most of the dedicated playerbase to continue to decline until this game becomes a forgotten relic unless the developer takes strides to improvement the subpar gameplay experience as a whole.I know I've been very critical of RoN thus far, but it really isn't to say I expect a triple A experience from a developer clearly unequipped to provide one. But for ♥♥♥♥♥ sake, some communication with the community would allow for more leniency from the playerbase. The fact is VOID has neglected to do this, letting down the entire dedicated community and it is with a heavy heart I must say this game is just simply not worth buying at its current state. I was once a proud and outspoken supporter of the devs, constantly coming to their defence when people criticised them for various reasons online, but even now I am forced to say that they were right and I feel extremely let down over the years of development this game has seen so far. TL;DR: At its current state this game is undoubtedly NOT worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed this game thoroughly with some friends, and while it is a great game there are plenty of issues I have with it, especially in regards to hit detection and the a.i. Amongst the worst of the issues is the a.i. being outrageously eagle eyed in certain levels, especially greased palms, they can easily spot you and shoot you from great distance through obstacles that impede vision drastically, and in others they often can take you out through solid walls, especially in sins of the father, ive had multiple instances where i or someone with me would take multiple shots through an opaque wall by an unseen enemy with great precision. in regards to hit detection, which is in most cases fine, i am talking mainly about the beanbag shotgun, which is a weapon i use frequently as its the best non-lethal option in the game, clearly on target low distance shots are often without effect, and while i am aware the projectiles are far slower and drop far more quickly than others in this game, it is clearly not working properly, having tested this numerous occasions. Now to be more positive, this game looks great, the gunplay is excellent, and it certainly keeps you on edge, and rethinking every little decision you make, and i, as well as my friends will certainly continue to play it. There's a great deal of variation in gameplay, in atmosphere, and in tactics you'll want to use to finish the mission in a desirable outcome, it can be brutally difficult, but certainly is very satisfying to complete a mission, even if it's an easier one. I'd really like to see more weapons and tools added in the future, as they're a bit sparse, and there are no nonlethal options for secondary weapons, making the shield more of a tool to draw fire when going for s-rank. All in all great game would give a 9/10, but due to my complaints i'd rate it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Rewriting my review after the game had several major updates.Ready or Not is, without a doubt in my mind, as realistic as you can get in the market of tactical shooters today. Even putting it side by side with VR's Onward. This game is so realistic that it's sometimes scary.Gunplay: Phenomenal, very realistic in feel. The weapons feel powerful and dramatic-- even uncomfortable-- to shoot. They all function identically to their real-life counterparts. Bullet penetration is realistic: Nothing is cover in CQB. Buckshot bounces off a steel plate like it should, but a 7.62x51 round will shred Kevlar vests. Ready or Not requires patience rigorously. To the tune that real world CQB experience translates very well into the game. On that note, though, I'd heavily caution individuals with real-world LEO or military experience who have experienced any sort of traumatic events from their lines of work. This game is seriously scary.My favorite part of the game is the immersion. The firefights in this game feel like what I'd expect one in the real world to feel like: A desperate, cotton-mouthed fight to survive. The meticulous atmospheric storytelling will leave you with a thousand-yard stare. The two most recent levels at the time of writing stuck with me throughout my day after I was done with the game.If you're a tactical shooter person, this game is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Really feels like 1.0 was 3 steps forward and 10 steps back....My frame rates and overall fidelity are significantly worse in 1.0.  From a near locked frame rate at ultra 1440p on a 3060ti before the 1.0 update to stuttering constantly and medium 1440p.  AI are horrendous and worse than before if that was somehow possible. The new AI controls they've given us are janky and buggy and only work sometimes.  The QOL features they added like auto reporting suspects and civilians are very nice though.But man...  For a game that tries enforce strict ROE, the AI is no where near adequate...  Suspects are unstable at best.  Going from shady looking to headshooting you in a second or less.  They are very buggy without line of sight in this update where they'll instant hit you when you peak the corner, but if you shoot within that timeframe you'll often get hit with an ROE penalty if you didn't yell compliance even though if you do you'll die half the time.  AI team mates are still useless at best. They'll often flashbang you instead of enemies when clearing a hallway or anyroom where there is a wall near the door.  The new campaign mode is needed, but mostly useless considering how useless your AI teammates are. They'll stick themselves into line of site before a flashbang goes off and get killed. The new map and breifing are what the game was sorely needing and a great update, but the rest of the package is pretty buggy.  Lots of stuttering in the mission select screens.  I've also encountered numerous ingame bugs that are new to 1.0.   IR Laser sights refuse to toggle sometimes unless you turn off your NVGs, turn the sight on, and turn your NVGs back on.  Which is kinda useless.  Overall, it feels like a pretty rushed 1.0 that wasn't ready for release and needed a lot more ironing out before rolling it out.  THE AI NEED TO BE FIXED. That is really what 95% of my frustrations are centered around and I can live with a lot of the other issues if the AI could just  work.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome love letter to fans of Sierra's SWAT 3/4. While it IS first person shooter, you have to get the COD mindset out of your head when stepping into this. Game relies heavily, sometimes unfairly so, on law enforcement's rules of engagement and  requires the player to at least give warnings / not fire if suspect surrenders / watch for civilians, etc. RoN offers many neat and "buffy" law enforcement customization options as rewards for getting certain grades in completing missions. Your squads come with their own sets of game changing perks as well which adds more to the gun. If you're looking for slow and methodical "thinking man's" shooter, this is it. The active mod community has some neat stuff in there, too! Check them out.While I've enjoyed the game a ton and still do, there are some negatives...Your squad can be "moody". I've found that the AI will just not address suspects 10 feet away from them, not cuff them, or just leave a surrendered suspect / civilian and walk by them sometimes. I've walked back and forth to see what they'd do and sometimes they'd cuff / secure or just ...ignore them. Your squad will sometimes literally stand in the line of fire and you'll watch them eat a ton of bullets and (sadly) go down.Suspects feel like they have "wall hacks" and sometimes (not always!) I've been shot through walls.That being said, no game is perfect and if you want something different than running and gunning, this was a good time!Hope that helps! PS- congrats on the promotion, Chief Alvarez

_childDocuments_.review: Core gameplay is good, but the game performs worse than it did in early access. Yet another example of Unreal Engine 4+ not being fit for game development. Even with ini fixes to preload shaders + other assets before a level loads, the game may have a good framerate for a minute or two, then drop to 30 or less if you look in the wrong general direction. Your framerate may come back to its original high, but it will always drop intermittently. The enemy bots are tuned to have inhuman reaction time and accuracy. They track players through walls by sound from running and yelling for compliance (good, fair) with 50%+ accuracy (bad, unfair), and have no sense of self-preservation. Enemy bots only fire in full auto when the weapon allows it, and they have no differing personalities (cowardly, aggressive, evasive, etc.) that keep the game and subsequent playthroughs of levels varied which causes this 2023 game to have less replayability than SWAT 4 released 2005. A game whose ultimate mod was created by Ready or Not's development team. They've done this before, but better, in someone else's game. All of this put together makes the less-than-lethal approach to missions fans of the genre strive for unnecessarily difficult. It is still possible, but definitely not what most would call fun. Thankfully, being made in Unreal Engine has a benefit: Being able to decompile the files to adjust values in config and .uasset files to adjust variables, specifically the AILevelData.ini and BasePlayer.uasset to adjust enemy bot reaction time and accuracy, and player movement speed to reduce frustration when looking for the last piece of evidence or civilian that trailers is supposed to pick up for you. I recommend everyone to look for and edit these values yourself so when you recompile the file and put it back in it doesn't tramp-stamp your game as "modded".Some people say changing the bots and movement speed makes the game not "tactical" but the game is not advertised as a simulator, so it should focus on being a fun experience. A good compromise to please everyone is by having a standard preset for variables to have the intended difficulty, but allow the user to change whatever they want in game to play the game in a way they find fun. Having an outline for evidence isn't realistic either, but they added it into the game as an accessibility option because the majority of players found evidence-hunting not fun, so why not let people adjust the game to their liking?Overall, Ready or Not is definitely NOT. I enjoy it with a few adjustments, but I can't defend it in its current state. Definitely not worth 50 USD, wait for a sale for about 20-30 assuming it doesn't improve. I'll definitely change this to a positive review if it changes for the better.

_childDocuments_.review: Just when everyone thought 2021 was over in terms of relevant releases, Ready or Not appeared out of thin air. Well, not exactly out of thin air. People knew it was coming, and it has been under development for a while now, but Void Interactive was being rather secretive with the early access release date, throwing people off the scent with a Twitter post two days before the public EA release with the classic “it just might come out this year”. And it did.Ready or Not, or RoN like people usually refer to it, is a tactical shooter in the making, that promises to eventually become just as good as the legendary SWAT 4 from Irrational Games. Your character is a SWAT operator and your job is to arrest or kill bad guys, make sure civilians are safe and apprehend drugs, illegal weapons, destroy human trafficking schemes, and so on. The usual tactical police stuff, done brilliantly. You can either play alone with four AI-controlled teammates or cooperatively with up to four teammates, with the twist that there’s no friendly AI to offer a hand or two, meaning that heading to the mission with just one or two friends will be rather challenging. The enemy count varies per map and it’s often dependent on the environment: some will naturally have a higher civilian to bad guy ratio due to its sheer likeliness while the opposite also occurs. Currently, there are five different maps to choose from, with an extra two WIP environments, still untextured and ridden with glitches. Granted, it’s still an early access title and more maps are going to be released, along with full modding support so that the community can also help provide extra content to warrant unlimited hours of fun.As far as content is concerned, there isn’t a lot just yet, but the variety is good enough to allow different approaches to each mission so that the replay factor is nearly endless. From your average M4 rifle to a paintball gun (yup), they got you covered. The gear list is also rather extensive, with different vests, masks, cop paraphernalia like battering rams, breaching shotguns, C2 explosives, flashbangs, even a camera thing that allows you to look under doors. Who’d ever imagine that voyeurism could be used to enforce law and order!As it couldn’t be any different with an Early Access title, some things still do not work as expected, an OK thing if it gets fixed, and it probably will. The AI can be rather unpredictable sometimes, with civilians running from you, sometimes locking themselves in rooms with the enemies, or just straight up hiding from you and making your mission take a lot longer because you and your friends end up forced to play tridimensional “Where’s Wally?”. Something else that might annoy you ever so slightly is the fact that civilians and enemies don’t have a lot of different voice lines, meaning you will hear the same sentences over and over even during the very same mission. Granted, it’s probably a placeholder. On that same note, the cop’s voice is way too calm, which differs a lot from real-life operator footage telling bad guys to drop their weapons. But once again, a placeholder card probably applies.The gameplay aspect is where RoN truly shines, sporting the possible best gunplay on the market, shootouts are dynamic and challenging. The AI can be very accurate at times, making it so you and your friends got to be on the very edge, with eyes wide open. It doesn’t take much to die, just like in real life. You are not a bullet sponge, nor are the enemies or civilians. As a matter of fact, civilians are even more fragile, so be mindful of that and take extra care when breaching into a room with thugs and civvies inside. That’s where the tactical element comes into play and cohesive play rewards you, while recklessness can be punishing. There are multiple ways to approach the different situations that you will be faced with and no right answers. Go with your guts, trial and error, or develop standard operating procedures with your friends so that everyone knows what to do and what not to do to get things done the cleanest way possible. It’s easier said than done, as Ready or Not is very hard and will give you a tough time if you are not paying enough attention. The sheer unpredictability makes for very fun and engaging gameplay.It would be interesting to have a little more dynamism on certain stuff, like objective items that always spawn at a fixed location, making it so you always know where to go and how to get there efficiently without major hiccups, which is good from a speedrunning standpoint but doesn’t help when it comes to longevity, because it will get repetitive quickly. On the other hand, enemy spawn points are always random, with no mission playing the same, even if the items will always spawn at the very same location. Just like a box of chocolates, you never know what you are going to get.Visually, RoN is impressive. Powered by Unreal Engine 4, it certainly does not disappoint with textures, lighting, level design, and performance. It doesn’t take much to run, and my old faithful RTX 2070 could easily run it on epic settings in 1080p, well above 100 fps, with eventual drops here and there. As expected from any so-called next-generation title, it supports DLSS, which boosts the overall performance quite significantly, up to 40% even in sub-4K resolutions, without compromising the visual acuity, meaning no ghosting, no artifacts, as clear as it can be. A really solid implementation, even more so considering it’s still a work in progress.It’s no exaggeration to say that Ready or Not is perhaps one of the most solid early access releases ever. As much as it still has a lot of things that are not quite up to standard yet, the gameplay mechanics and the challenge are enough to keep you coming back for more. A breath of fresh new air into a genre that we haven’t seen much from, apart from Zero Hour. It was a long, painful wait, but SWAT 4’s spiritual successor is finally among us and it’s great. Why haven’t you purchased it yet?

_childDocuments_.review: So i guess i should leave a more in depth review after playing all of EA and 1.0 since the start.There seem to be 2 types of people, the fanboys and the "haters" but if you read a little of each you'll probably find the truth.1.0 is quite buggy, but not too buggy. A hotfix or two should fix most of these. The "Trailer" units never come, sometimes you cannot stop bleeding when shot so you eventually die... SWAT AI path finding sometimes goes off the rails when they use shields, the restart times are a bit ridiculous and even if you fail a mission your team still take the hit despite the fact technically it "never happened" as you go back to where you were.The main issues i see are the AI. Suspect AI are all tier 1 operators chewing coffee beans on Ritalin with training the likes we've never witnessed in real life. Or to be more specific they have aimbots and know how to wallbang. Slow and steady is the only real way to play, you cannot go aggressive generally as they know you're coming before you round the corner. The game can be very frustrating and i know its supposed to be hard but i feel that SWAT 4 had the balance perfect.The other issue is suspects do not surrender enough. To get a suspect to surrender the way i see it is they must be flashed, gassed, tasered or some sort of tactical intervention. Its VERY rare a suspect will surrender on their own accord, be it vets with a grudge or your local methhead/gas station thief. The sight of seeing 5 officers baring down on them, 2 with shields and 3 with high power rifles, will rarely deter your local cash register thief from charging at you holding his 9mm sideways doming you 4 times before you put them on their back. SWAT 4 had a great way of making suspects think twice when at barrels end of 3 trained SWAT officers.The wallhack is very prevalent when using CS GAS. Whilst GAS should be great if they are a little out of the pool, you give them a nice shooting gallery. I used it on Post Office in the main room and ended up just watching my AI and the suspect AI trading fire through this wall of smoke...I was a spectator i could see nothing.Commander mode is also...Interesting. SWAT tend to be very sensitive in Los Suenos... The mere sight of of a suspect will put them on anxious on missions end. The commander mode is not really an RTS aspect of the game its just an exercise in click-and-swap.... Every mission just move out your anxious/stressed/critical units who are upset because an arrested suspected used a profanity and put in a new one.Sort out the glaring bugs, then REALLY focus on sorting this AI out in my opinion. I am enjoying it still but the frustration level is also high.Performance wise, runs fine for me on ultra using a very much mid range rig...Id say 80 FPS. Some FPS slowdown issues (especially arresting suspect with hair!) but nothing to speak of.Lovely graphics, animations and gun models. Also good sounds. Nice atmosphere in the levels themselves before john wick the meth cook domes you from 2 rooms away because there was a crack in the door between the hinge. Id say for perspective buyers...watch some vids then choose. I have faith these issues will be looked into however.

_childDocuments_.review: ONE POT CREAMY CAJUN CHICKEN PASTAServings: 4Prep: 10 minsCook: 20 minsINGREDIENTSCajun Seasoning:2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp oregano1 tsp thyme1/2 tsp garlic powder1/2 tsp onion powder1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/4 tsp black pepper1/4 tsp saltChicken Pasta:1 Tbsp olive oil1 Tbsp butter1 lb. boneless, skinless chicken breast1 yellow onion, diced1/2 lb. penne pasta (uncooked)15 oz. fire roasted diced tomatoes2 cups chicken broth2 oz. cream cheese3 green onions, slicedINSTRUCTIONS 1: Combine the ingredients for the Cajun seasoning in a small bowl. Cut the chicken into 1/2 to 3/4-inch cubes. Place the cubed chicken in a bowl, pour the Cajun seasoning over top, and stir to coat the chicken in spices.2: Add the olive oil and butter to a large deep skillet. Heat the oil and butter over medium-high until the skillet is very hot and the butter is melted and foamy. Add the seasoned chicken to the skillet and cook for a couple minutes on each side, or just until the outside gets some color. The chicken does not need to be cooked through at this point.3: Add the diced yellow onion to the skillet and continue to sauté for about 2 minutes more, or just until the onion begins to soften. Allow the moisture from the onion to dissolve any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.4: Next, add the pasta, fire roasted diced tomatoes (with the juices), and chicken broth to the skillet. Stir just until everything is evenly combined, then place a lid on top and allow the broth to come up to a boil.5: Once boiling, turn the heat down to medium-low and let the pasta simmer for about ten minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the pasta is tender and the liquid is thick and saucy.6: Add the cream cheese to the skillet in chunks, then stir until it has melted into the sauce. Top the pasta with sliced green onions and serve.NOTES- The deep skillet I use is a 4-quart capacity.- Depending on your cookware, you may need to adjust the heat up or down to maintain a simmer in the broth. Be sure to stir often to prevent the pasta from sticking.

This issue is ongoing even before the update, and this one makes them a bit worse.- [Updated] Bugs, glitches, frame rate, and random crash issues in general. One time the game crash and restart my gaming laptop, great.- Quite troublesome glass and light reflections.- [Updated] Horrible windowed mode (mouse cursor often gets out of the screen).- Inconsistencies among props and some other details in games that affect storytelling.- Glitches/technical issues on every mission briefing dialogue and script (Tab button). - Don't have a function to stop capturing individuals (when we suddenly getting shot at).- Forcing players to complete S ranks (by also capturing all suspects alive, which is ridiculous for certain situations they try to portray in-game and it ruins a large chunk of fun for me) in order to unlock all items in the evidence locker room. In my opinion, all 3 items in each mission should be unlocked by reaching the "A rank" at least.- The way they Force-ending the missions right after teammate AIs automatically capture every piece of evidence (most of the time I didn't ask them to) without giving players a chance to explore the maps and discover more storytelling elements first. - I disagree with removing the old Wenderly Hills Hotel map (Checkin' in). Along with total redesigned maps instead of separate as a new one (old Cherryessa Farm) or separate as a different sector of the same location (old Port Hokan).- Mod users can't join the regular servers. Well for this, I kinda understand. However, this rule should NEVER apply to those who download just custom maps, regular cosmetics, and anything that doesn't affect the gameplay.---For more explanation on AI issues that affect both singleplayer and multiplayer modes, I'd highly recommend this video: [Update] and However, I have additional points to cover this up as well:- Like through smoke/gas and walls, enemy AIs can see through the glass as well, while we usually can't do the same thing for certain kinds of glasses/windows (reflection issues).- Teammate AIs are always stuck in a grate in front of the meth house (Twisted Nerve) when we try to get out from the first house and turn left to access the second house.- Teammate AIs won't move to certain positions in front of them unless we walk into those areas first (and risk of getting shot at, of course).- Teammate AIs often act or respond hideously slow in gun fights.- Teammate AIs often lose their focus and turn their backs to the exposed positions, then get themselves killed.- [Update] Teammate AIs sometimes automatically move into a further location I didn't ask them to, without any cover or preparation, of course.- Teammate AIs always secure weapons/evidence even in unsafe (yet) places and dangerous situations. I prefer playing this type of game in single player, but since savings are so messy and I can't play levels I've already unlocked I suggest playing in multiplayer since you have everything unlocked there. Seen lots of forums with people having the same problem as me, and another where if you start an ironman mode game and die, all of your save slots are deleted, not only the iron man one. _childDocuments_.review: Having participated in the alpha, my playtime is much higher than is listed here. Ready or Not is a modern take on the cult classic SWAT series, and it revives the genre in a masterful performance. Movement is deliberate and real, while shooting is satisfying and impactful. Clearing rooms of bad guys to protect and serve has never been more rewarding. If you want to earn a perfect score, you'll have to coordinate with your friends or carefully lead your team of AI officers, in actions and efforts that are timed, calculated, and often incorporate less than lethal equipment to compel suspects to surrender to avoid bloodshed.  You'll need to be smart and methodical in your clearing while also being quick on the trigger when it calls for it to bring order to chaos and survive.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes a really good attempt to act as a successor to SWAT 4, manages to actually succeed wonderfully for the most part.... only to fall apart when it comes to properly tuned AI and actually pushing updates and new maps in a timely manner (thankfully the map part is remedied by custom maps from the community). I understand the devs are minus a AI coder that dipped after the first few updates or so (as the position is currently open and is taking job offers) but atleast one of the handful of key problems (ie reaction time being confused for both itself and action time, allowing enemies to go from calm idle/taking cover to giving you a split second head ventilation installation with a shotgun/smg) could be OFFICIALLY patched in a small update that would cut down the R6 Vegas Killhouse tactics that many people resort to every time they dont stun the suspects with flashbangs/CS gas/stingers/c2 breaches to avoid getting Wick'd for daring to follow rules of engagement either with avoiding unauthorized lethal force or for using the HIGHLY ineffective less than lethal gear that dont even stagger or interupt enemies much at all.Now, the suspects' reaction/action time being counted one in the same isnt the ONLY problem that makes the AI frustrating (your Last Known Position in engine sticking on you for 5-10 seconds/map holes in AI Sight occlusion making the AI too smart even with low tier thugs but every suspect also having random chance to randomly become deaf and blind intermittently making them laughably bad being 2 sides of a bad AI coin on top of AI stat values) but when players either grin and bare with the vanilla setup or have to resort to trial and error testing of sets of AI value tweak mods for 5 months of update drought... that doesnt bode well for state of the game if a later update introduces any further problems that need prompt fixing. Couple that with the fact you currently have to pay a second purchase abit above the base game price JUST TO GET EARLY ACCESS TO THE NEW MAPS ALONGSIDE WITH TWEAKS AND CONTENT to actually play a updated/patched game to give accurate feedback on and you got a recipe for a Onion/HardDrive parody article with how oddly placed the priorities and update pipeline flow is.When the game gets updated, fixes it bipolar AI Awareness/AI behavior values, and gets back into a more steady development flow that treats the base game version as also instrumental to the game's progress: Ill gladly change my review into a shining "Highly recommended" as few games have tried to act as a successor classics and got THIS close to dethroning the classic fully. I dont want this game to fail, no AAA dev would be allowed to make this type of game but that also means getting things right is sink or swim to do.

_childDocuments_.review: To answer the game's question: not. Don't get me wrong, I'm going to play more of this. The game has awesome ideas and the execution is fun. I'm having a good time--but not a great time. There are some flaws in the game that range from annoying to discouraging--from not being able to use presets to quickly customize AI squadmates to some inputs being broken (making engagements difficult and slow) to core game design elements not matching what the game is saying it wants you to do (I'm encouraged to be nonlethal, but anything short of gov't death squad will be a game over). The drug mules and convenience store robbers have automatic weapons, do not fear death, and have skills that make me think they must have led D-Platoon before me.Then there's the QOL issues. Typos rampant, no mission restart (or even if you wanted to make me manage rosters after a mission fail, maybe I could do that from the restart screen?) so I can't quickly hop back in, SWAT AI is improved but makes some *silly* mistakes.Last night, first mission of the game, I had my AI teammates breach a room. My door guy, with his riot shield, moves in first. He walks by a doorway. His shield eats *two* shotgun blasts through that doorway, as the guy continues down the hall (as opposed to shooting at the guy that just shot at him). Then, someone appears at the end of the hall, so shield guy turns towards the hallways, *and backs sideways into the doorway where he just got shot from, peeking with his shield down the hall.* I can't engage the guy in the doorway, because shield man is now blocking it, and my team is engaging guy at the end of the hall, too, as opposed to the dude with the shotgun pointed at shield man. Shield man take a shotgun blast to the back of the head and goes down. Now, at least, I can shoot into the doorway.Point is, I'm going to keep playing this game. But I'm only doing so because I bought it back in early access, so I'm used to iterative improvements (and assume more are coming). If I was going into this game for the first time today, I would prefer to wait another six months or a year until this game is actually ready, or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this, but just barely. If you're a fan of the old Rainbow Six or Ghost Recon games before they sold out, then you will love this. It's dark, gritty, and highly realistic.However, there are some major downsides to this.The enemy AI will try to flank you and is unpredictable, which is super refreshing. However, they are straight up aim bots. I'm talking sub 1 second reaction times to seeing you and will nail you every time. There's a very limited startle effect, but it is not enough. There is no suspect fear, you can't intimidate them in any way. They also don't react to getting shot or being shot at appropriately.If the AI gets a major overhaul, then this game will be so much better.The next thing to note is the slowness of the updates. It's been almost a full year since the last major one. Most levels are missing the other mission options. In my opinion, each level needs all mission types available to enhance the re-playability factor.EDIT:I am no longer recommending this game. Still no major updates, and the performance is getting worse and worse over time (frame stutters galore). Go play Ground Branch instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Man the SWAT games were cool, right?This is trying to be that, and it may someday get to that point. Their current monetization plan, and political snafus are a huge hindrance for this game though. The content that is currently in the game is very slim, and I probably will not be returning to it in years due to this lack of features. There is another game(Ground Branch) that is trying to do what "Ready or Not" is trying to do, and they are running into the same problems. What this game currently boils down to is just average to subpar AI flailing around in a room clipping through walls, while having the reaction time of a PAYDAY 2 civilian, while you spam the same voice commands over and over again. IN THREE DIFFERENT(effectively the same) SCENARIOS PER MAP :D. You can watch the models freeze as they decide what they need to do.I had high hopes for this game, because the SWAT franchise really nailed this style of game so early on, possibly too early, and it would be wondrous to see it fleshed out in a more modern and accessible way. Unfortunantely, this ain't that yet. Again, their monetization plan really screams that they need more money to get this big of a project off the ground, or they just want more money for very close to same product plus cosmetics and a shield. Occam's razor is sharp at times like this. This game is BARELY enough content to warrant $40. Astronomically not worth the $120 mark.Skip this one for a few years, and then it may either be great, or very likely, abandoned.

_childDocuments_.review: Just before this game's announced 1.0 release, I'm delighted to say Ready or Not has evolved from a tight, tense shooter to a genuinely gorgeous, brutal, disturbing, horrifying, and intense SWAT team simulator that's as much a realistic horror experience as it is a tactical shooter.  Be warned, this is a -brutal- game with *extremely* realistic violence and some incredibly unsettling subject matter and disturbing images- in fact, every mission in this game is based on something that happened in real life, and it could be something that's actually happening right now.  I commend the developers for the level of care and taste they've treated these scenarios - never does any of the more extreme material feel exploitative, or placed for cheap shock factor, no, whatever emotions the developers were attempting to evoke out of me they got - more than once did I feel my stomach legitimately turn at what I saw in this game.  But the game is so well done, I couldn't help but come back for more.Subject matter aside, the gameplay experience feels great.  A slow-paced, methodical first-person shooter with well-researched gunplay that can be experienced solo with AI teammates or five player co-op.  Customize your officer, your kit, your weapons based on the situation you'll be going into, and prepare for intense and unforgiving encounters with permanent location-based player injury that affects aiming and/or movement, and if you aren't careful, quick and instant death.  Enemy AI is surprisingly smart and will react to your team's actions, able to set up ambushes and flanks, take cover, hide under beds and in closets, take human shields, and fake surrender.  I haven't experienced enemy AI with this level of sophistication since the first F.E.A.R. game.  Ready or Not, they're coming after you.Right now, this is by far the most content complete, polished, up-to-date tactical shooter available for PC, especially of all the Early Access tactical shooter options on Steam at the moment.  And with the recently announced 1.0 release around the corner, even more improvements and content are inbound.  On top of that, full mod support means countless ways to tweak your experience to your liking, and adds plenty of user-designed levels for you to try.  If you are able to stomach the intense and disturbing subject matter - which, again I stress, is very real and very horrifying - what you get with Ready or Not is both a highly polished tactical shooter as well as one of the scariest horror games you'll ever play.  History will see Ready or Not as one of the all-time classic greats of tactical shooters, on par with Rainbow Six and SWAT 4.  Get in on the ground floor.

There are occasional crashes, framedrops on powerful rigs, and bugged loadouts and AI.Yes, it is in alpha, but the developers seem to be preoccupied with honestly meaningless gimmicks such as coffee machines instead of fixing bugs or fleshing the game out.The friendly AI is braindead, while the enemy AI has sub 200 ms reaction times that are superhuman. The game strives to be "realistic" yet has unlimited ammo for the suspects yet the player has four magazines of ammo. There are wire traps everywhere with nonsensical locked doors, whereas in real life there ARE NO SUCH THING as "trapped doors". Such things are a videogame-only gimmick.Why are there dozens of AR style rifles but little to no SMGs or shotguns? Why does the audio cut out for full-auto firing, or when there is a lot of action going on? Audio cutting out for full-auto is 2000s era amateur hour. The reverb SHOULD BE mixed properly, and the next shot cutting out the previous shot's reverb is UNACCEPTABLE sound design in 2022.Also, this game has been in development for years. Fans of this game say it's polished, but Boundary is also in alpha but I've had ZERO crashes in that game, with a steady +80 frames with not a single hitch. There are no bugged loadouts in Boundary, whereas your gun attachments (e.g. flashlight, laser) will just vanish.I'm ragging on the sound too much, but the suspects in this game will not hear GUNFIRE and C2 explosions the room next door, muttering some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like "you hear something? yeah yeah shh". The suspects will track you through walls and sometimes shoot through them as if they have wallhacks.This game's development is seriously at a glacial pace, and yet the developers will focus their meager efforts onto stupid ♥♥♥♥ like coffee machines that make you go faster in the lobby. For some reason the fans love this stuff and will eat it up. Any voice of criticism is justified by the most braindead reasons because to them criticism === attacking their personal feelings??Oh yeah, and this early access title has an early-EARLY access version that requires you to fork up more $$$ to get the privilege of trying out the patches early. Cannot understand defending that one. Absolutely questionable behavior that leaves a bad taste even playing this game. I'm not upset about the material/content in this game, which is to be praised: it's tackling some sensitive topics that are taboo in videogames. I'm upset over bad practices of splintering/segmenting the fanbase and focusing on the wrong tasks that will improve the core gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: While I really like this game and 100% want to recommend it I am not in this review. While I have been really enjoying 1.0 there are many issues that haven't been fixed. The suspect AI is INSANE. They are way too accurate and rarely give up sometimes even when using CS gas and flashbangs. All suspects are apparently ex-navy seals with cybernetic implants that give them x-ray vision and hearing.  I have died so many times to the AI shooting me through walls with perfect accuracy. The AI straight up have X-Ray vision. The suspect AI felt way better before 1.0 and maps like the post office felt way harder now to the point where i need to download a mod which reduces suspect accuracy and reaction time. Currently without mods open maps feel nearly impossible to complete because some gangbanger will spray you down full auto from 30 meters away through a tiny crack that allowed them to see 1 pixel of you.With 1.0 the SWAT AI has been improved and it is much more enjoyable playing singleplayer now. But there are a lot of issues with their AI. Giving orders has been pretty buggy with the ai sometimes just not doing the order. Often i will tell my squad to breach and clear a door and it will say they are doing the order but they will just stand there until i give them a different order. Also when clearing big rooms my ai squad will often way overextend and will split up and be super far apart. Often after me and my squad clear a room will give an order to my squad and i will look and see that half my squad is in a completely different room because they decided to go to the other side of the map. also the feature where you can take a squad mates place in the stack is a little weird because if i tell my team to stack up on a door and i go in the spot where a teammate was going to go i have to move out of that spot wait for them to get in place and then i can actually take their spot. The AI will also often not watch different angles when following me. This happens a lot when a suspect is shooting at me from a higher level often my AI teammates who have a perfect sightline just wont shoot back at them.The levels are mostly pretty good but some of them have way too many suspects. For example the streamer level where you are supposed to be raiding a streamer who supposedly killed his mom. You go in expecting one maybe two suspects but surprise! there are a bunch of ex-military thugs with cybernetics who will rush you and shoot you through walls! some of these missions really don't make sense. There also need to be more small maps. A lot of the maps are super big often with big open areas and it just doesn't make sense that a small 5 man SWAT team is clearing it when realistically that would be a 15-20 man operation.The performance was also much worse 1.0 than before. Before 1.0 i had no issues with performance but now i will be getting 100 fps and then my game will go down to 20 fps for 20 seconds before going back up. For some reason there is lots of stuttering.Overall I still think this game is really fun but i wouldn't recommend getting it right now, at least wait for the ai to be fixed (Hopefully).  it feels like the game was released too early. It also kind of feels like the devs are going the opposite direction of what this game has been advertising itself as. I really hope the devs will take community feedback and will fix the AI and the bugs. also please more small/medium size maps the beachside house map was sooooo good i need more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. Really good. It goes above and beyond when it comes to tactical gun play simulation. I am constantly amazed at the modeling, the general feel of the weaponry, the punishing but rewarding nature of the gameplay. Maps have great variety and constantly being improved and AI is always receiving updates making them more intelligent and harder to deal with. I think this game is fantastic if you like other titles like Arma, Rainbow 6, etc. However, I have a problem with some of the principles on display in this game. I would call it, by and large, copaganda. While there are some extremely interesting and morally-simple levels like the pedophile mansion which we raid to arrest and dispose of child sex offenders, there are also details in the game which are quite distasteful. Primarily what comes to mind is the level wherein we are raiding and arresting some sort of left-wing or communist terrorist group in a convention center. Historically, left wing violence is nearly non-existent in contemporary society. Eco-terrorism could perhaps be construed as such, but only adjacently. The game notably does not address right wing violence, or white nationalism which has been on the rise in Western countries and has been named the primary threat to peace by intelligence organizations such as the FBI in recent years annual reports. Likewise, some of the dialogue about suspects or with other police also portrays the player and their allies as unabashed heroes who can do no wrong. Given the track record of militarized police departments in America, this is a gross misrepresentation of the truth and should be consciously opposed by players of the game. All that to say, this game is really great and super fun, but the politics of the studio developing it lack nuance and in fact contribute to the demonization of left-wing movements, all the while ignoring some of the most pressing issues and violent groups in America today. Please play this game, but go into every mission with a critical eye and mind about what is being shown and told to you, and who that anecdote benefits.

_childDocuments_.review: It really pains me a lot to give this game a negative review, I've been waiting for it since the first announcemente in 2017, and I've been playing it since the first open beta, I've had a lot of fun with friends in multiplayer, specially during the beta, but as of the current state of the game I gotta say this game was not ready for a full release.After more than 200 hours on this game and having completed most of the achievements except for the medal of valor (get S rank in every mission) I feel confident enough to give a review and criticize this game in full.I'll leave a list down with the good and the bad stuff of the game so you can come to your own conclussions before buying.I'll start with the GOOD STUFF:-Extremely fun to play with friends-The gunplay is probably the best there's in the FPS genre-Guns not only look and sound good, they feel really satisfying to use, I can't think of a single gun I dislike-The free lean system is the best thing they've implemented so far, it works really well for small peaks and ducking when getting shot, and it's a fun system.-Slow paced gameplay which feels like a relief, specially after the oversaturation of hyper fast shooters.-Every mission feels challenging, yet fun, specially with friends-Maps look really good (I still prefer some of the old ones, but new ones are great too)-The briefing add for the final game it's a really nice and immersive implementation-You can customize your operator-The game looks really good graphically-Character models are great-The lore is pretty interesting-Ambiental storytelling is really fun, and I still discover new stuff constantly-The suspects and civis are distributed differently on every playthrough which gives the game A LOT of replayability-I still discover new stuff that can happen or stuff the suspects can do, even after 200 hours of gameplay.-In-game mod support and a great mod community-Extremely good mods-Great community-You can still unlock most of the accessories, clothes and stuff in multiplayerTHE BAD STUFF:Friendly AI issues:-They'll obey orders only half of the time you give it to them-When you give any order that requires them to move on their own "open/move and clear", "stack up", "deploy X", etc sometimes they don't go directly to the place you send them and instead take a long path to the objective alone.-If you give the order "open and clear" or "move and clear" they will start clearing the entire map and splitting themselves until receiving a different order, this will get them all killed one by one more often than not.-The auto pick up and auto arrest thing they added to the AI will get them killed a lot and doesn't really help at all.-The way they clear rooms doesn't make sense a lot of times; they'll get into a room facing a wall and get shot in the back-They will always prioritize switching to the secondary weapon before reloading, even if they don't have any ammo on their secondary weapon, this will get them killed a lot.-If they have a shield and no ammo on their pistol they'll switch to their primary weapon and get hurt or killed.-They won't use their shields most of the times.-When "opening gas, sting or flash and clearing" they will drop the grenades in the most ineffective possible way, most of the time they won't have an effect at all.-They don't duck and they rarely take cover under fire.-They will ALWAYS start yelling at suspects and civis on sight, killing any possibility of a stealthy approach, getting YOU killed a lot.-Sometimes they aim like John Wick, sometimes they miss EVERY shot, it's incredibly inconsistent.-Their grenades are inconsistent, sometimes they'll use 2 grenades (having prepared up to 4 for each) and the "deploy grenade" or "open flash, smoke or sting" option will be greyed like if they had no more left.-They will only use 1 GRENADE per grenade launcher, they don't reload it, and the option will be greyed as well.Enemy AI Issues:-Extremely inconsistent, sometimes they one tap you on sight, sometimes they don't hit anything.-Even the lowest goon will have a "John Wick" moment and one tap kill your entire team and you with a pistol.-They'll track you throw walls once they get on alert, but they'll conveniently do things like leaving the place you're mirroring or you placed your team in a stack formation on doors even if they're not on alert-They'll shoot you throw walls-They'll see you throw smoke and shoot you like if it wasn't there-They have infinite magazines-Even the most petty criminal will fight to the very end with everything they have and pull multiple weapons on you-Every single suspect, no matter of how petty they are will ALWAYS fake surrender, sometimes pulling up to 4 weapons on you -I've got a crackhead pull 4 weapons on me on twisted nerve (a tec-9, a sawed shotgun, a pistol and a knife)-They take a stupid amount of less than lethal shots before they start complying (up to a pepper ball magazine or 4 bean bag bullets)Equipment issues:-The grenades are at their worst state, they're extremely inconsistent. -The new CS gas sucks so bad, it creates a thick smoke screen that only affects your sight, enemies will shoot throw it like if it wasn't there.-If a gas falls under a bed, cabinet, or any small surface the smoke won't come out.-Stings and flashes have a random chance of exploding on enemies feet and not affecting them AT ALL.-Grenades bounce inconsistently-Sometimes when you throw grenades into a room and they disappear and appear on your back, this is more frequent with smoke grenades-There's no short throw option for grenades.-C2 will one shot civis, but only stun suspects-Less than lethal options are too few and inconsistent-The Less than lethal shotgun is extremely lethal, one headshot is always a kill, so as a less than lethal option is not worth it.-You can't shoot between metal bars or relatively small spaces (up to a _childDocuments_.review: I like this game and up until this point it was fun playing, but as you'd expect with one update the game immediately fails to deliver. I had a stable 60 to 70 fps until now, but after the update I am experiencing not only a maximum of 40 fps (when I look at the sky. Otherwise it is around 20 to 25.) but also micro lags that obviously are extremely distracting when one tries to aim at a fast moving crack head. Well undoubtedly the game looks much nicer now after the update, but seriously I don't want EVEN BETTER graphics when that means that the game won't even run in 1080p at minimum graphic settings... So yeah its fun if you have a good pc now i guess :/update:I found a workaround on YouTube for my problem. Shoutout to Jrminate!So essentially my problem was that the graphics resolution slider would not let me actually change the resolution. It wouldnt apply no matter what. So instead you can go to your Appdata folder (AppData\Local\ReadyOrNot\Saved\Config\Windows) and in there need to open the file called "GameUserSettings.ini". In this File you should see in the very top a section called "[Scalability Groups]" under which you need to find or write yourself the line "sg.ResolutionQuality= ". Now you can adjust the value to your liking. Just mind that it needs to be within 50 to 150 I believe. After the adjustment you can simply save the file and via right click then 'properties' change the file to read only so the game won't override your change on launch again.I hope this help can help you out if you have similiar problems as I did. :)Have a nice one!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely fun at times but it’s not all there. It feels more like frustration condensed into a little jar and the game going through developmental hell doesn’t help. I like the idea, premise, art direction, some gameplay mechanics and some level design but as a whole experience it’s awful. It’s blatantly unfinished and should not have been released 1.0 of December 2023. I feel as if I can't mention anything about the good parts about the game because they’re so overshadowed by constant issues. I don’t recommend paying full price for this game let alone at 50% discount.The biggest issue and probably the biggest point of criticism is AI. It is absolutely beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you thought Escape From Tarkov scavs were bad then I would say that Ready or Not suspects are on equal footing. You are not going up against some gang-bangers in the hood. They’re clearly cracked special-forces units being deployed to Los Sueños. Those armed robbers at the gas station in the first mission? Those guys are actually undercover Spetsnaz operatives. But seriously, though. Why is it like I’m fighting an army of T-800 Terminators? Suspects are so aggressive and cheat so much. They see through walls, will shoot you through them and have laser aimbot accuracy. They also have no self-preservation. On the same first mission I went around the back on the left side and zip-tied two people outside. One civvie and a suspect. I checked under the double doors and there was no one. I ordered the team to open and clear (no grenades). I go left and there’s two doors - one directly in front and another to the right with a staff only sign. I was checking under the front door and got blasted through both the wall and door that had the staff only sign while I was using the optiwand. The suspect then opened the door and blasted me some more, retreated further back into the room they were in and grabbed a hostage. There is no reason that should have happened. It was a quiet entry with no breaching devices or explosives. If it’s because they heard me zip tie someone outside that’s just equally stupid. For a game that boasts “realism” it already fails that. I have also had issues with the mission “A Lethal Obsession” where suspects would sometimes use doors wired with explosive traps to try to get to me and either blow themselves up or kill me and the entire team stacking up outside it because they can clearly see me through walls. There are some other oddities with suspects that don’t make entire sense. They have no self-preservation and will always try to fight you rather than surrender. You’ll go to zip tie someone and they’ll pull out a knife. Some suspects will actually feign a surrender and get to their knees before pulling out a hidden pistol. I like that idea but not with how frequently it seems to happen. I can understand that for  suspects to be doing these things but it feels like it's almost all of them. I can understand terrorists doing it but not some random private security guard or generic no-name gang-banger. I want some suspects to run and hide and I want others to try and fight. Not everyone should shoot you at a moment's notice. Some suspects do try to hide and run away but it happens so little. Suspects can hide under beds and in closets but that's only available on a small handful of maps. Some maps have holes in the walls and suspects can move between them but more often than not they use them to attack you from behind rather than to try and get away. Non-compliance is also a good idea but doesn't play as I feel that it should and is more of an annoyance than anything. How many beanbags do I have to dump into a guy before they get to the ground? I have emptied entire mag-tubes while mashing the “yell for compliance” key for it to all be ignored. Some suspects just outright ignore tasers, beanbags, the pepperball guns and the pepper spray can. CS gas seems to be the only effective non-lethal option. There is no way to force someone to the ground if they ignore compliance and there really should be an option to do so. There's also plenty of dialogue that makes no sense given the context. Why are the civilians in "Neon Tomb" defending terrorists and saying they did nothing wrong when I blast them for shooting me? Terrorists in "Relapse" also sometimes act as if they are innocent and did nothing wrong when you zip tie them. It feels out of character. Los Locos members are always aggressive towards you once zip tied and some will have lines about asking for deals so they can be cut loose. That makes perfect sense for them. The terrorists should have much more aggressive and fanatical dialogue. The SWAT AI is also beyond useless. It feels like I’m constantly babysitting. They can’t do anything right and frequently ignore commands. It works okay enough if things do work. They seem to have a hard time engaging anything out of the room they are currently in and will typically ignore threats outside of it. They constantly struggle with “move and clear” commands and won't do them. This is especially apparent when stairs are involved. They’ll prioritise zip-tying people and collecting evidence instead of fighting back when getting shot. Sometimes you’ll have to issue a command a second or third time just to get them to do something. I don’t know why this is but the SWAT AI will sometimes move towards civilians and suspects backwards or diagonally to zip tie them. Commander Mode isn’t great either and it’s half-baked. It’s the de facto single player mode. You have a roster you fill out and each officer has a trait that can be unlocked after doing some missions with them. The traits don’t seem to do much and I forget they are even there. Sometimes when doing missions or failing them stress of a team member will go up and then you have to send them to therapy. That’s it, that’s Commander Mode. I feel like there should be more to it but that’s it. On top of all these issues the game’s performance isn’t optimised and it's filled with bugs. If you told me this game was made by Bethesda I’d believe you. Performance isn’t consistent and gets pretty bad on some missions. “Ides of March”, “Valley of Dolls” and “Relapse” are some examples of missions with awful performance that I have experienced.  There is also so much clipping and it really shows how unfinished the game is. NPCs have clipping with their clothes and so does the SWAT cosmetics for you and your team. As an example, gas masks don’t fit correctly on suspects faces and the headband clips through their heads. Some of the other bugs I have encountered is that sometimes the HUD bugs out and places itself in the top left corner of your screen. The phone/PDA thing that you use to manage your roster and check mission briefings can become unresponsive when opening it and won't let you select anything. Sometimes NPCs become shadow-people and have a completely black texture. Sometimes when leaning with the taser it won’t hit it’s target and that makes me think it's hitting an invisible collision mesh. I’ve had SWAT AI yell at suspects standing outside closets. I’ll shoot them with a taser to get them to comply and they’ll either rubberband or warp back inside the closet and exit it. Zip-tying downed suspects or civilians sometimes causes them to ragdoll and launch very slightly into the air. SWAT AI sometimes can’t see suspects in a room when entering and won’t engage them. Sometimes suspects in that same room will only engage the player and ignore the SWAT AI. Honestly, anything I’ve mentioned about the AI can be assumed as bugs or just ♥♥♥♥ game design. Ready or Not’s modding scene is in its infancy but there are some AI reworks and fixes for things.

_childDocuments_.review: Stack up nut to butt, get the SWAT theme playing in the background, and get your shield ready, because we finally have a true successor to SWAT 4 and other tactical shooters of Yesteryear. [Skip to the bottom for the review if the story of Void Interactive and it's trouble with cancel culture doesn't interest you.]A message about Void Interactive: _______________________To preface this, I highly recommend this game and not just because the gameplay is incredibly fun and rewarding, but also Void Interactive has put in real labor to their product and actually are interested in realizing their dream. Void Interactive is so dedicated to ensuring this game is their realized dream that they even cut ties with a publisher over conflicting views on the game.  Anyone who can pursue that level of dedication to themselves in today's climate of cancel culture is well worth the time and investment in my eyes and to support them speaks out against this climate of leftist journalists who actively target and try to shut down games that don't support their narratives like a ruthless mob. This is a very methodical shooter where the art emulates real life: Slow is smooth, fast is reckless. The difference between a dynamic entry and a deliberate entry can be the deciding factor between success and mission failure. A moment of hesitation in drawing the lines between suspect, citizen, arrest, or lethal force can result in your character having their last call over the radio. These are all very real challenges law enforcement personnel face every day, especially those involved in high risk warrant service, these are the challenges that you as a player must tackle in this SWAT successor. It is this complex and nuanced take of stepping into the boots of a law enforcement officer in this game that truly has gaming journalists rustled as leftist narrative journalists at KOTAKU consistently attack Ready or Not like a city council ready to throw an officer under the bus for following protocol and performing their job or the media (unironically because they are media) highlighting every move you make behind that badge. Void Interactive's labor of love faces consistent scrutiny every day from these video game "pundits" and it is for that reason, this game 100% deserves your support.  This is a game where many of us can finally put our foot down, hold the line, and say enough is enough when it comes to this cancel culture destroying legitimately good games, content, and honest companies that are looking to truly create immersive experiences and storytelling atmospheres of art for players to live and experience. Ready or Not, while not entirely ready yet, is almost a masterpiece in it's own right.  So please, consider supporting Void Interactive: Buy the game, even you're feeling even bolder go and get your HRT skin through the Supporter's Edition. Now that's out of the way, I'm going to summarize the review in three positives and three negatives. Keep in mind this game is a work in progress and for a work in progress it truly is a real piece of work in the best way possible. Good:- Randomization, every mission's placement of suspects and citizens is randomized for different plays each time to keep you guessing and falling into a routine of rolling dynamically through content. - Reasonable Difficulty, not even kidding, this is a very difficult game and it has a steep learning curve. Playing with friends and good communication is quintessential to success. So pick up some extra copies or get your friends playing with you. - Immersive experience, this is possibly the most immersive tactical shooter experience I've played in a very long time and while certain aspects are missing, the foundation of the game is established to build up on that with a roadmap of development ahead. Your friends and you will find yourselves stacked nut to butt, bonding over the game, frustrated with mistakes when someone ♥♥♥♥♥ up, because you are 100% going to be completely into winning. Bad:- Memorizable, once you learn a map inside and out, all you have to worry about are the different placements of AI. There's little that can be done in terms of this, unless they made a feature that would randomize the placement of furniture in a house each time you make a playthrough. - Animations, not going to lie, they can be pretty choppy at times and once more it's a work in progress.  Some of them can be down right hilarious though. - John Wick, some of the AI can be downright punishing, zeroing you before you even have a real chance to react and sprinting like they're out of the Matrix to completely teleporting from one end of the room to yours just to kill you and a friend.  While this is a rare situation as my group and I have found, it can still be an immersive shattering issue when it does occur and you get spiked after a careful deliberate entry into a room.There is so much more coming for this game and so much more on the roadmap that I'm looking forward to seeing.  I wish I could cover all of it in a single review, but I would literally be writing a novel. I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical GameplayThe core of Ready or Not lies in its slow, deliberate gameplay. Every mission feels like a real-life scenario, where breaching doors and clearing rooms requires precision and planning. The AI in this game is unpredictable, adding an intense layer of realism. Enemies can be deadly and civilians might behave unexpectedly, forcing you to constantly assess each situation. The focus on non-lethal takedowns and de-escalation adds depth, offering a unique experience compared to standard FPS games.Immersive AtmosphereVisually, the game nails the gritty, dark tone of law enforcement operations. The level design is incredibly detailed, and each map is diverse, offering everything from claustrophobic apartments to large public venues. The sound design amplifies the tension with realistic gunfire and environmental audio cues, making every breach feel nerve-wracking.Room for GrowthThere are occasional bugs and some AI behaviors that need refinement, but the frequent updates and active community engagement from the developers are promising. Features like more fleshed-out single-player content and improved animations could push the game further, but even in its current state, it offers a rich and tense experience.Co-op is a MustWhile you can play solo with AI teammates, the game truly shines in cooperative multiplayer. Communication and teamwork are key, and playing with friends elevates the experience to a whole new level of intensity. It’s incredibly satisfying to pull off a well-coordinated breach after hours of trial and error.ConclusionReady or Not is one of the best tactical shooters available, offering a level of realism and strategy that sets it apart from the rest. If you enjoy games that reward careful planning, tactical execution, and patience, this is absolutely worth checking out. Just be prepared for a game that will test your skills—and your nerves.Rating: 9/10
