_childDocuments_.review: Takes some time to get used to controlling your team if you play single, and requires a competent set of friends to play multiplayer. This game may be frustrating to some, and it is difficult. The pace is slower than most games, as this isn't your standard FPS game, if you don't go slow, smart and calculated, you and your team will die, and you will lose. Not for everyone, but the people who will like this game are REALLY going to like it. The games looks fantastic and the environment tells more story than most games do in their entirety. A solid PC is needed to run it well, and you can "beat" the game (finish all levels) in about 30 hours, however replaying for S ranks, and playing their game modes adds a lot more time and effort. Most of the negative reviews are people with lower end PC's and people who just don't like this type of think first shoot second FPS game. If you want to run around like a super hero shooting everyone go play something else. If you want a good FPS that requires thought, skill, slow and calculated movements on a more simulation level, then this is your game. Having said that, here are a few cons:Single player - Team is kinda dumb. I've watched my guys walk straight at an enemy and get shot and die a few times. Or run in to cuff someone on their own, and get killed while cuffing cause they didn't even bother checking the hall.Single player - Team can be difficult to control and sometimes requires giving an order more than once to get them to do it. Enemies - Latest update seems like the enemies are even more accurate than before to the point of defying reality and causing some frustration.General - Requires a solid PC to run well.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ready or Not" isn't just a game for me; it's a gripping experience that has evolved with each update and iteration. The initial phase with the Alpha PVP mode may have disappointed many, but with the Coop release, the tables turned, rewarding those who saw its potential.After years of anticipation since "Swat 4," a new chapter was finally unveiled with Version 1.0. The team AI has reached its zenith – smarter, more effective, and, above all, more realistic. The tight teamwork in battles is remarkable; they act tactically wise, covering corners and forming strategic formations.A significant leap forward is the addition of background stories to missions. No longer just catapulted into scenarios; instead, dialogue and 911 calls provide a captivating context, intensifying immersion. Finally, you can understand why you're in a particular building and the challenges you face.The option to send team members to therapy is not only an innovative addition but also a human aspect in the game. It shows that developers aren't solely focused on action but also address the mental strain on characters. A team consists of people, not just pixelated avatars.Overall, "Ready or Not" has proven, through its progress and profound enhancements, that it's not just a game but a journey. A journey that not only revives the nostalgia of "Swat 4" but also paves the way for a new era in the tactical shooter genre. Personally, it's more than just fun – it's an emotional rollercoaster full of intensity and teamwork.As a devoted Close-Quarters-Battle (CQB) enthusiast, I'm always on the lookout for the next adrenaline rush in the tactical shooter genre. "Ready or Not" has not only exceeded my expectations but truly blown me away. As someone impressed by the SWAT games, this title not only continues the tradition but elevates it to a new level – and that is genuinely legendary.The attention to detail in CQB moments is breathtaking. Every step in a tight corridor, every door that swings open, and every moment of tension are masterfully captured. The team AI, functioning like a well-oiled machine, makes immersing into these tactical missions an unparalleled experience. As a lover of tactical shooters, I appreciate not only the visual brilliance but also the strategic depth that "Ready or Not" provides.The decision to delve into the background of missions and infuse characters with more personality has transformed the game for me into more than just a shooter. It's an emotional journey where I'm not just fighting for survival but also forming a connection with virtual characters. The addition of the therapy option for team members shows that the developers don't neglect the human aspect – a dimension often overlooked in other games.In a gaming landscape dominated by spectacular graphics, "Ready or Not" has proven that true beauty lies in the depth of the player experience. As a CQB fan and a lover of tactical shooters, this game has not only impressed me but also touched me emotionally. It's more than just a game – it's an epic journey that captures the essence of tactical gaming and presents it in a way that deepens my passion for the genre. Bravo, Void Interactive, for a masterpiece that has conquered the hearts of tactical shooter enthusiasts like myself.A monumental thank you to Void Interactive for years of tireless dedication and commitment to perfecting "Ready or Not." Your unparalleled effort has not only given birth to a game but crafted an epic masterpiece that redefines the boundaries of the tactical shooter genre.In every line of code, in every polygon of design, one can feel the love and care poured into creating this game. It's as if you didn't just develop a game but infused a passion in the form of code and graphics. "Ready or Not" is more than a product; it's an artistic dedication that extends through every movement, every shot, and every moment of tension.The decision not to rest on laurels but consistently work towards improvement speaks of a pursuit of perfection that is not only admirable but also rare in the gaming industry. You haven't just released a game; you've continuously refined your vision to offer players an experience that not only entertains but also captivates.Every enhancement, every patch, and every update reflects your dedication that goes beyond the ordinary. _childDocuments_.review: As a 30 year law enforcement veteran I really like this game despite its current clunkiness and shortcomings.I don’t like how my AI teammates are always in the way although that might be an error on my part of leading them properly.  I’m new to the game so it’s possible I’m doing something wrong.  In fact, it’s likely a me problem and not a game problem.I really don’t like that most the maps are so apocalyptic looking.  Most of the maps look like an abandoned wasteland and that would include the police lineup room where you select your missions.  Almost nothing looks alive and lived in.  A real world inhabited (looking) map would add to the realism and immersion.For a 2022 game, with only a few acceptations, usually with mods, the graphics are cartoonish…just awful.   More lifelike graphics would greatly enhance the immersion.  I suspect that they will get better overtime given that this game is early access.I don’t like how ridiculously alert and accurate the enemy is.  It’s a bit over the top.  In SWAT callouts in real life you aren’t dealing with super alert, highly trained Navy Seals, you’re dealing with untrained, drug addled,  crackheads.  Modding greatly improves this shortcoming.I don’t like how hostile the civilians you’ve just rescued are.  In real life they’d be exceedingly thankful that you were there and saved them, but in this game they all behave like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and utter some snarky, hostile comment when you rescue them.  That’s unrealistic,    I find myself shooting the most irritating ones in the head.  Please remove their hostility and make them more thankful, like people in this situation would be in real life.I love how you’ll run into an occasional character and accidentally shoot them because they quickly reach behind them to grab their phone to record you.  Sorry, not sorry. Our decisions have consequences.I like how easy it is to mod this game.  It couldn’t be easier.  Modding greatly improves this game’s shortcomings and it couldn’t be easier to do.Overall, it’s a really fun game with some room for improvement.  It’s my current favorite game.  It’s got great bones and I can’t wait to see how things develop in future iterations.Even at full price,  I recommend it.UPDATE JULY 2024:I have quite a few more hours in this game than I did when I posted my original review.   I'm still not happy that the police station is so trashy and run down looking.   A lot of effort went into the design and layout of the police facility, truly impressive, but why can't it look like a well cared for facility?   I get that the working maps are designed to be dark and moody, but this shouldn't carry over to the police headquarters.Another pet peeve I have is how clunky getting into and out of missions can be.   If you've done ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a map and just want to try it again it's a long drawn out process while you get evaluated and graded.  Please, just give us a button to easily restart the mission without having to go back to the station.  It's a needless waste of time.Why is the new DLC buried so deep that most people have a hard time even finding it?  Why can't you play it from the singleplayer continuation tab???  I hate that you can't play it in commander mode.   Why not?Lastly, don't make map progression based on the grade you receive on your previous map.  For the singleplayer, just make all the maps available from the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: - Ready or Not started off as a promising rookie in the Tactical Shooter sub-genre. Seemingly with a glint in their eyes, it went through a long period of Early Access in an attempt to be the perfect spiritual successor and contemporary interpretation of the renown local veteran, .Unfortunately, the only thing time on the field offered to Ready or Not was jadedness. Doing the right thing turned out hard, and the benefits for so would most likely not pay off. It grew authoritarian in its dullness, abandoning its ideal vision and adopting instead a gorged caricature with a strong beating heart that pumps incompetence.The gameplay of Ready or Not (RoN) can be summed up as a hardcore PvE game where a small team of heroes will usually go against a battalion of incomprehensibly suicidal felons armed to the teeth that need to be put down at all costs. You can see some very  on the net, where players will dynamically enter a civilian building and annihilate every "bad guy" with gunshow levels of lethal weaponry to choose from.This would all be fine as a premise, if not for the fact the intended way for a game like this to be played, and the way its score system works at the highest level and difficulty, would be to have the ideal of  There's a big gaping hole in the core of RoN which makes its gameplay loop a boring failure, noticeably: Even in the event you are willing to ignore the game score rating and barge into civilian households with a full auto Armor Piercing weaponry under zero objections, the game will force you to locate and apprehend civilians in the map and other "evidence" garbage before you finish the scenario, just to rub it in that "it's a SWAT game". This also happens to be the excuse for there not being a "run" button, a match made in hell itself.RoN uses the Unreal Engine 4 (UE) to a good amount of its potential and enjoys displaying high fidelity assets in detailed environments with innumerable amounts of shades. Unfortunately, this may as well be the uniform for any self-entitled UE powered game.What RoN does with its uniformity is create a lot of visual pollution. A lot of things seem to be placed just for the sake of being placed, as if it's trying to justify having paid for those assets. Some of them are out of scale with the player size, giving you the impression the city is some sort of society composed of Elves and Dwarves; maybe the gameplay loop would have been more coherent if it were.Lights and Lasers work out terribly depending on the graphical setting, often "reflecting" or being drowned by other ambient lights. Needless to say, all these things combined makes target acquisition more difficult. It appears the game is "so realistic" it is attempting to emulate an early onset of cataracts upon the player character.The "visual storytelling" is not too subtle. It displays lots of off-screen violence, sometimes you get extremely contrasting architecture such as an entire cave system built on the backyard of a crackhouse with schizophrenic drawings on the walls. Really nails it in that we don't take the war on drugs seriously enough, and that the bad guys are so evil they'll shoot the dog!There is a lot of audio, but it often gets drowned out by the gunfire or the 20 second long screams of agony from suspects with sixteen new additional orifices paid for by the local municipality. Subtitles are full of typos and mondegreens.RoN tried to be virtuous and stand up when nobody else did when it comes to making a Tactical Shooter, and for that it quickly gained some credit. There is some gameplay and eye candy when it is in its best behavior, but a little time and experience will quickly show you its ugliness with a thoroughly broken soul.In the event you're not willing to put up with blind trial-and-error until you too start seeing there can only be degrees of guilt rather than innocence in the crowds, I'd recommend skipping this title or waiting for a hefty sale with a mod list for a first playthrough.If you kept up to here, consider checking the following:- - -

_childDocuments_.review: No doubt strategy and coordination are key in a game like this. I love how dynamic each level is, and how every playthrough is different each time due to the randomization. With this in mind, the levels can be replayed several times over, being even more intense the next time visited (although hopefully not in the sense of the AI landing deadly accuracy all in milliseconds of you turning a corner, which can happen from time to time). When you are not taken down right away the need to return action can be an adrenaline rush that could lead to stopping the death of a bystander or one of your squad mates. There are multiple levels, and each have several objectives, levels of threat, and rules of engagement accompanied; bomb threats, active shooters, barricaded suspects, and more. Even changing your gear beforehand in the Headquarters can spice up the job as you can take a less lethal or lethal approach, with appropriate equipment: stun grenades, flash bangs, riot shields, tazers, bean-bag shotguns, and more. There is a good mix of AI characters as well, all appropriately dressed for the locations they are found in. You are required to be on-guard at all times for it is possible for a suspect to pose a victim or fake a surrender and then whip out a weapon when your eyes may glance away for just a moment. Of course the AI isn't perfect, there is a tendency for the suspects to sense and shoot you through walls even without a clear line of sight, which really can pull your out of the game at that moment..luckily I've only seen this a few times.I never played Ready or Not's predecessor Swat 4, but I can see how fun it must have been. I can also see myself playing this for a while to come, as the new maps and other additions come along it is just getting better.

_childDocuments_.review: Was a big fan of games like Rainbow Six Vegas and thought this would fill that void in the gaming world. Idea is on the right track but the execution just doesn't match what it should be. Biggest problem is the AI. Your squads isn't great, but that has more to do with the poorly implemented command system that is based on clearing rooms - fine when you are entering a well defined room, horrible in open areas. But the enemy AI is what really kills the game. Sometimes they will not see you when you are directly facing them, shouting commands or even shooting at them, other times they will see you through an opaque window or tiny line of fire and start shooing (with incredibly accurate automatic fire) instantly. Death in a game like this should feel like it is a result of poor planning, but most of the time it seems totally random. All of this makes what should be a slow, methodical playstyle feel unrewarding and the game seems like a failed attempt at a "serious" shooter. None of that even gets into all the smaller problems with the game like performance issues, weapons all feeling and acting the same, poorly or non-existent item descriptions and a lack of any sort of story. I "beat" the game but you would hardly ever know that, it just returns you to the station as normal. I guess after the 10 or so hours it takes to beat each mission, it expects you to replay them, but offers nothing to improve the missions from the first time. Not worth the price they are asking and should have staying in early access awhile longer.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for some screenshots  to view all the ones I took for this game.Ready or Not (RON) takes place through a series of locations where organized crime has gotten out of hand enough to warrant the intervention of a SWAT team — that being you and your either AI-controlled or human teammates. All set in the fictional city of Los Suenos and its environs, these engagements will have you face anything from deranged preppers to terrorist groups and crime syndicates. Even though these missions are standalone from one another, some have an underlying plot that relates them to one another story-wise: these situations are all plausible and fleshed out well enough for a tactical shooter, with many indirect narration elements, dialogues and documents shedding more light on the events. Visually, RON doesn’t spare anything about realism and the brutality of true combat, with gore being abundant when needed, alongside the screams of injured suspects and blood. All maps are visually excellent also due to the recent upgrade to Unreal 5; their worldbuilding is rich in detail and immersive. If you want a realistic shooter that doesn’t cut corners in a lot of things, you’ve found it. From terrifying cartel smuggling tunnels to clubs piled with bodies after terrorist attacks, the immersion is assured. Special mention goes to the sound design, standing a notch above most other shooters.Levels differ massively in size and complexity, from wooden shacks to extensive multi-layer hotels and facilities. Aside from either killing or arresting all suspects depending on the parameters, exploring everything thoroughly is extremely important to get the higher mission ratings. Much evidence is scattered through each level, some static, some changing each time - they’re called ‘soft objectives’ and may even be mandatory to complete the mission at all. There’s no in-game map, so memorizing the operational layout during the preparation phase at your base is fundamental, even though the locations of these assets aren't always specified. Other than that, suspects and civilians may hide in closets, under beds, corners and actively roam around. Suspects and civilians aren’t only triggered by line of sight but also by noise and alerts given by others, expanding the tactical depth.Fights in RON are slow-paced, tactical and high-stakes. Despite armor, a few shots or even a single high-caliber round are all it takes for both your teammates and the enemy to hit the floor. Mainly, there are two ways to go about any map: lethal and less-lethal; the first utilizes firearms, alongside support gadgets such as flashbangs and tasers, to engage criminals in firefights, likely killing several of them. The second uses specific gear that only stuns and demoralizes the enemy, which is riskier but also more rewarding, since an alive arrest is worth many more points. You’ll have a limited amount of magazines, grenades and utilities, and you’ll have to use them smartly, alongside entering from the most strategically viable points, to get the best drop on each room full of suspects and minimize risk. Everything is paced as it is in real-life, so there’s no running, and the bulk of your armor will incrementally decrease your action speed in favor of protection. Suspects have variable degrees of expertise in a realistic way, too: some random gangsters robbing a gas station won’t be nearly as lethal as hardened cartel thugs at the Mexican border, the latter also sporting much heavier weaponry, and even laying traps. The gunplay rewards accuracy, positioning and trigger discipline, and heavily punishes impromptu gunfights without adequate cover or support. The rules of engagement differ depending on the map, and penalize you for excessive use of force. For instance, unless you’re against terrorists, you’ll always have to warn them to drop their weapon, discern between criminals and civilians, and pay attention to their behavior to make sure not to kill them if they’re surrendering. Also, you’ll need to get specific persons of interest out alive regardless, even if they’re hostile, so always having a non-lethal teammate or option is the best course of action. RON does an excellent job in portraying real life SWAT operational procedures and might take a while for newcomers to adapt to a playstyle that is “ask questions first, shoot later”.Every gun and gadget is unlocked from the start, while all unlocks depending on ratings are purely cosmetic. On one hand this is good because you’ll have all the options available to try and experiment from the start, but on the other hand it detracts from the progression experience. Still, there are achievements and many cosmetics related to getting the coveted A+ and S ratings.

Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. _childDocuments_.review: Full Launch Review (Version 1.0, 350 hours played):Since the full launch a couple of days ago I cannot recommend this game anymore. Here is why:1. Enemy and AI:Ever since the so-called "Adam" Update, VOID changed the Suspects' AI algorithms to inhumane reaction times and weapon handling skills. Being 100m away from you 2 rooms away with a wall between you? No problem for Miguel "John Wick" Sanchez aka "The Aimbot" from the Los Suenos gang.  He just turns around shooting you in the face across the map no-scope 180 through the wall! Deployables (such as CS gas, flashbangs, or C2) don't work at all. You just blasted the door in front of a suspect? No problem for Igor "Carbon Head" Coslowsky from the local arms dealing gang (or any other suspect for that matter). He just powers through it and clips you after which he wipes your entire team in 1,5 seconds. You shot a suspect without a Kevlar vest in the torso thrice? No problem for Ian "Bulletsponge" Brooks, he just eats those bullets like I eat breakfast after a good 12-hour sleep, before giving you two precise headshots, about which you can do nothing at all.It gets to an outright ridiculous point and makes the game unplayable. Here is some proof about those issues in the 1.0 release. ("The Aimbot") ("The Aimbot"/"Wallhack") ("Carbon head")So why did I recommend the game initially? As I said I have been an Early-Access supporter of this game and was one of those players, who paid 75 Euros, to help the developers. And in my opinion, Early-Access games are allowed to be a work in progress. But now the game has been fully released and the issues are still there. They haven't been fixed. During the last 12 months, I reported about 40-70 bugs in this game. And these problems I described before? They were known to the developers. I know this because I reported most of them (within those 40-70 reports). More than once. They have been very well documented within the community as well, as the following YouTube videos I linked will prove (note: the clips all discuss issues with the Early-Access version of the game): (at 2:03 SWAT throws a flash which "Carbon Head" Coslowsky eats ) (at 2:03 and following you can see Ian "Bulletsponge" Brooks in his natural environment) (4:48)So what did change with the Update? If anything, the issues got worse since the launch (as the first clips painfully demonstrated). Rather than being consistent issues throughout the entire game, the above-mentioned seems to be tied to a few specific maps now though, while it is rather fine on others (or at least bearable). It is unclear to me why this is, but I have a suspicion: Instead of giving the Suspect AI a consistent and generic behavior tree, they modified the behavior tree based on the environment of the map. Either way though: the experience sucks and this also seems to be the reason why some of the maps that were playable pre-release were taken out of the game entirely now.2. Content was removedAs already mentioned I was one of the persons who bought the supporter edition of the game instead of the Base game. With this edition, you were granted a couple of skins and cosmetics you could use. With the full release of this game, those things were removed, along with many of the maps one could play before. While I don't care much about the cosmetics this type of unreliability on the developer's end greatly bothers me. It is shady at best if not an outright breach of contract. Where is the insurance for players to be able to keep what they bought if you let this happen?So if you think about getting this game, then let me say this: Get "Ground Branch" instead. It is the better game in the Mil-Sim Genre right now. The AI is way simpler but it is playable.Early-Access Review (old review, ~300 hours played):A great game for anyone who loved Rainbow Six: Lockdown, Rainbow Six: Vegas, or SWAT 4. I have been waiting for a game like this for 10 years. Grab it and enjoy it if you are into tactical FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time, I can't YET recommend Ready Or Not, at least not at this price. Whilst I appreciate the efforts of the Void Interactive team to better their game, there are things that simply ruin mine and many other experiences with this game. The main few from my personal experience are the cracked out Suspect AI, dumb as rocks (yet equally crackshot) SWAT AI Teammates, Lack of optimisation/broken graphical options (especially since the transition to UE5), Inconsistent or hard to read mechanics such as body armour.-Suspect AI: This has been a problem for a long time and has definitely improved since I started playing in October of 2023. But STILL to this day, even with all the horse-blinders and debuffs the devs have attempted to give the AI has made certain scenarios feel completely BS. Their insane peripheral vision and unholy ability to somehow shoot perfectly accurate despite having a flashbang detonate in their face are some of the most common and annoying instances of this. And despite the devs specifically implementing specific measures to prevent it, there are still instances of Suspects spotting SWAT through windows/holes the player cannot (sometimes at ridiculous distance), in addition to the insane accuracy they carry at crazy range.-SWAT AI: MAKE THE DAMN HITBOX SMALLER, or just disable teammate clipping. For god's sake. Having to navigate around your teammates is some of the most frustrating gameplay, especially when the AI refuses to move and ESPECIALLY when their pathing won't let them walk around the player. This problem is not only annoying, but can potentially be dangerous in the wrong situation. Also I've found recently that queuing orders for teammates is temperamental AT BEST and tends to mess with other orders.Even with the release of the DLC and the transition to Unreal Engine 5, it still does not feel like a 1.0 release, but is getting there. It also feels as if VOID is committing to all these large events without actually focusing on the fundamentals of the game that ruin the rest. I and many other customers would prefer not necessarily receiving new content if the devs would focus all possible effort to making sure that the bare gameplay mechanics are nailed down and polished as best as they can be.It's a shame because despite all my issues with the game, I do enjoy it during moments that DO run smoothly and love the world, story and atmosphere that has been built up. Additionally, it does feel like a game that even in its "1.0" release relies heavily upon mods to be simply fun (which I do thank VOID for being so adamant on including). But unfortunately the previously mentioned problems always end up with me eventually uninstalling. Despite this I do find myself reinstalling from time to time simply because I do have hope that it gets better.We will be waiting.EDIT 20/11/24:I hope the next upcoming update will fix some of this. Even after fixes, I am still experiencing suicidal Suspect AI and them also having zero reaction to CS or flash grenades. Honestly, it's not surprising people play this game like COD in multiplayer when taking things smooth and tactical hardly ever pays off when the AI is dumb as hell and has no sense of self preservation. Also for the love of god, can we please put a clamp/limit on door kicks, 2-3 is fine, but when I have to kick a door 8 damn times, it feels frustrating (could argue realism, but with everything else in the game, it's just another annoyance on the pile). I keep coming back to this game because I still crave that percentage of fun and enjoyment this game gives me, but that percentage is ever decreasing at this point with the annoyances and some of VOID's practices when it comes to releases and patching. I am looking forward to the future updates, their upcoming features are nice and inject variety into the game's formulas, and that the new features for the Suspects will also be included alongside much needed AI fixes.This game is on the final stretch on it's journey to completion, in my opinion. I really hope it can reach our expectations or even blow them away. However, for now I'd still say really take a long think as to whether you want to spend full-price.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't bother buying this game untill it's finished.Graphics-wise the game is on the level of Payday 2. And for it's graphics it runs suprisingly poor; It's worse on DirectX 12 compared to DirectX11. The color palette and unnnecessary post-processing effects trying to give the game a "cinematic" feel make the game worse.  It's hard to make out enemies even on daytime maps.Movement is clunky  and slow. In this game you can't run for your life even if being shot at.Gunplay is bad. Pistols and machine pistols are not worth using as most of your enemies are wearing armor.Having a certain arbitrary set of attachments makes the difference between a gun being servicable and worthless.This makes some weapons simply worse than others and not worth using.There are 4 different flavours of an AR-15 to choose from, one of which is significantly better than the others.There is also a SCAR-16 and a G36C, but due to their low rate of fire they are not worth using.There's also a short-barreled AKM and FN-FAL which due to their recoil are simply worse than M4.You can't have a flashlight and a laser on your weapon at the same time which is mind-bogglingly stupid.Attachments cannot be used on all weapons they can in real life.Attachments' descriptions are vague and do not accurately reflect their effects on weapons in game.Magazines' descriptions show incorrect number of bullets in them.Context actions on doors are a nice idea but they're poorly implemented - more often than not you find yourself yelling rather than opening the door which is especially frustrating when you're trying to be stealthy.Local chat is bad and it should simply be removed altogether.You cannot change your loadout after you start or restart the mission if - for example - you forgot to take nightvision and IR laser instead of a flashlight - you have to go back to the lobby to change it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has extreme potential. As a firm player of the old SWAT games, i was super excited to pick this up. While the graphics are stellar, and the devs definitely care about the game, every update feels like one step forward and two steps back. Every update they talk about AI changes or new maps, but fail to fix the core problems. None of the guns in the game kill the enemy as fast as theirs kill you. (Yes i hit my shots, and they're killing me faster while i'm in full ceramic plate). For example it takes up to 4 .357 shots to the chest of a guy in a Walmart grade kevlar vest to kill. Upwards of the same amount for a semi auto shotgun chambered with slugs. Second major issue is the AI. This new update claimed to have changed how the AI work, yet i see almost no difference. Every AI, from methheads to bodyguards, is the equivalent of a navy SEAL with 8+ years of experience. They will hear nothing but your footsteps, and run full speed into the open room, snap immediately to your head, and instantly headshot you. The new update claims to have added build up to their running speed, as well as animations to mitigate the snap shooting, but i've played about 8 matches on varying maps and seen zero of these changes in effect. Fix the core mechanics before adding new maps, and you guys would have an absolutely excellent game. It's a shame I have to put the game down for now, hopefully when they fix these two absolute major issues, I can come back to a game I know has the chance to be amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Very fun WITH friends - Has a lot going for it - Misses some thingsThe game is fun and has a very solid core. It has moments of genuine horror, action and excitement. Team work with other players feels good and even the AI is acceptable (most of the time). I would only recommend it to folks who have friends that will play though. There is no rank, exp earning or leveling up. There is no campaign or narrative mode. Everything in the game is right there all guns, equipment, attachments and every mission is available right away. There is excellent environmental story story telling, as you and your team descend into the raids. Some of the maps deal with highly disturbing subject matters. I would really like to see more to the customization and the addition of a progression system. Even something simple like what the first Payday game had would be a nice touch (imo). I feel like once you've done each of the maps a few times there really isn't a whole lot there to keep me playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit November '23 (about a year later): Still not ready. Basically minor things have changed, the game is so deeply flawed, I don't see it recovering or becoming a finished product with the Devs having solved only minor issues over the past year.tl;dr: it's not ready. not at all. It looks great on those youtube shorts, content creator footage and screenshots, but really is a very, very wonky game, which is absolute barebones in many aspects, but the visual one.Edit: Lobbies are weird, sometimes laggy and not joinable without invite (friends). Enemies have literal wallhack, sometimes trying to shoot you through walls or doors, without ever seeing you.Long review:Gunplay is ok and all the tactial equipment is great. Level design is also pretty cool, especially the range of scenarios already covered.But! this is basically where the good part ends. Performance is really wonky, with framedrops, especially in more open areas. Grafics are functional but not great. Effects are neat, like flashlight cones under doors, but there are so many glitches, it takes away from the immersion, especially on darker maps, with objects and texture not having the correct lightmapping. Also: the flashlight can tank performance in some places.AI is overall pretty stupid. As soon they know you are there, most start to rush you, not giving a damn about barricading or hiding in the rooms they are in. They just straight up leave the room and walk towards you. They also have laser aim at certain ranges, which makes most firefights really short: Either you shoot them first or you are dead. It only gets interesting when there is 3 or more enemies and the engagement is mid to long range. Edit: the longer I play the worse it gets. The AI *can* sometimes suprise you, with trying to get behind you but 19/20 encounter it is soooo dumb, it can barely be called an AI.Sound is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ barebones. Yes it's directional and you can kind of tell when there is movement, but weapon sounds are overall very meh, as are environmental sounds and stuff like footsteps.Animation work is also quite barebones. This is especially anoying because it plays into the gunplay, where hit feedback is really, really bad. It often feels like only the initial hit is registered and the reaction to it are premade animations, unrelated to the point of impact. This is very apparent when playing not lethal. Another example: You shoot someone 5 times in their leg with live ammunition they don't budge a bit AND still have laserfocus aim. Overall: fun with friends, but to barebones and definitely overhyped.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game at all, but a pretty disappointing V1.0SWAT AI teammates are great but murderous, will often kill every suspect at first sign of hesitation which makes it very difficult to even make the attempt to end things non-lethally. It's also not possible to queue commands with the Z button, you have to do it via MMB for it to work.On the flip side, we're back to ADAM Update goons, who shoot through walls with hilariously obvious tracking. Get a suspect to open fire on you, swivel behind a wall, and watch as their bullets track along in a laughably linear fashion.They open fire extremely quickly, with very muted differences in behavior from suspect to suspect. None of them are skittish, frightful, suicidal or prefer barricade situations. They're ballsy and actively throw themselves into the line of fire like it's their mission to take out as many SWAT as possible before they die - From gas station goons to paid mercs alike. Guess those paychecks can still be cashed in hell.This also means that suspects, as well as being very hard to non-lethally subdue, also don't really ever do anything tricky. Hiding in closets? Flanking through rat holes? Hiding under beds? Pretty much non-existent, as they favor the Leeroy Jenkins approach.Routes through many old maps are far more restrictive, with some levels having quite a remarkable amount of cut/barricaded content. Moreover, the route from level to level doesn't really make very much sense - "The Spider" for example was clearly a prelude to, "Valley Of The Dolls" yet now they're separated by quite a number of missions, making them feel extremely disconnected despite technically being directly linked."But it's okay" I hear you, veteran player say "The levels are more flexible because they fleshed out the alternate modes - I remember Twisted Nerve and other levels had unique Raid layouts!"WRONGALTERNATE MODES HAVE BEEN REMOVED ENTIRELYYou know that thing, that we advertised the game as having? The fact that each level could be played in up to 5 different modes, with big or small differences besides the core gameplay changeup?Completely gone. It's all Barricaded Suspects with maybe one or two, "Active Shooters". Which, disappointingly, are also pretty much dumbed down to Barricaded Suspects, but you hear a gunshot or two in the distance.This has killed any energy I had going into 1.0. The fact that every level is locked into "Barricaded Suspects", besides the cut/locked off content and disappointing AI regressions, has murdered my enthusiasm.Still a good game, but if it's between Ready or Not, then I have to say V1.0 was Not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty faithful reimagining of the venerable S.W.A.T. series by my beloved childhood darling, Sierra. It sticks close to the original gameplay-wise while adding some twists, like co-op multiplayer and Ironman mode. There's a huge variety of firearms to choose from, and they’re meticulously modeled and handle in a very believable way. That said, the P90 feels surprisingly anemic and could definitely use a buff.What I like most about the game is the missions. They’re set in a near-future, semi-dystopian L.A., and some of them spiral into darker, more twisted rabbit holes than you might expect. The best part is that, being an indie game, the developers didn’t hold back—they’ve made the missions as edgy as possible without crossing the line. Some of the things you’ll see or discover might seriously ruin your day, but isn’t that what being in law enforcement is all about?On the technical side, it’s less impressive. While it looks good and runs well on a 4080, it was pretty much unplayable on a 1080. I get that the 1080 is ancient at this point, but you’d be surprised how many modern games still run fine on it. Also, some of the animations are pure jank, but honestly, that just reminded me of the original games and made them kind of endearing.Overall, it’s a solid recommendation from me, especially if you can grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: SWAT-sim lite.Good entry into tactical shooter genre. Addictive.  Opponent AI is immersive, but friendly AI (hence single player) leaves so much to be desired. Turn off the PC, get out there, get 4 friends, then you can bid farewell to the sun again until virtual terrorism is eradicated as you and your new friends learn to juggle between tactical and ethical concerns in claustrophobic battlespaces.Control is streamlined, at the cost of lacking extensive features one might expect from tactical shooters such as no sprinting (come on, don't force us to play game a certain way, let us learn ourselves via lethal mistakes), no proning.Primitive inventory system means no way to combine several equipments in ways that would be possible in real life (face shield + NVG, gas mask + NVG, etc), no way to have more than 1 grenade type.Primitive weapon customization options means that no vis + IR laser + flashlight at the same time. having only 1 button to control all of those things means that only one of them is meant to be have on at one time. _childDocuments_.review: AI are not realistic, having near perfect fully automatic accuracy at range, and their vision is not affected by visual obstructions. Yet they also seem to be unable to dynamically adjust their aim to your stances, and can be cheesed by simply leaning. Their own animations are also inconsistent, and they have rendering issues, often being invisible to you if they game thinks you shouldn't be able to see them (that anti-cheat system is very poorly made, and since many object positions don't sync well in multiplayer, it means that "invisible objects" will hide and enemy, like a blown door, and then the AI will magically appear in the middle of a hallway since they passed that door host-side).Getting an S (aka non-lethally secure all contacts in a mission, and all objectives, with no penalties) is a core mechanic of the game, yet the friendly AI programming is so simple and untested that they follow a "swap to secondary while still in combat before reloading primary" script even if their secondary has no ammo, and they'll just sit there trying to shoot someone with nothing (you can't just choose to not equip a secondary, and there are no less-lethal secondaries, as the taser is now equipment). They also don't seem to adjust where they throw grenades when entering a room, and just toss one into useless areas right in the doorway after taking 5 seconds to ready their animation. They have the same issues as enemy AI with not being visually obstructed by anything, and so they will waste all their ammo shooting at enemies through walls (less-lethal weapons do not penetrate walls, and as such achieve nothing with this).The mission type selection was removed, stripping away most of the replay-ability of the game (each location/map only has one static set of objectives now). That replay-ability has been replaced with having to repeat the same mission over and over because you failed due to the devs' incompetence. Lasers are now angled  from the barrel of the gun when canted, becoming very inaccurate at range, assuming they even draw "correctly" (often have laser jumping around, clearly trying to dynamically change its angle based on what you are looking at instead of being static like it should). Lasers also change location when you ADS, as they are "accurate" when not aiming down sights, however they sight becomes "accurate" once you do, and the laser is randomly thrown off. Lasers also do not sync in multiplayer, so pointing with them can cause much miscommunication.This is just poor development. Incorrect code. It doesn't even get into clunky UX or bad design choices yet.Some sights are also aligned incorrectly, like the 16x aims too low the further you look out. Aiming very close, it aims too high as expected, since it's above the barrel, and at medium range it hits on target, however at "long range" aka the length of that shooting range, your shots land multiple inches above your cross. That would maybe make sense if it was ranged very close, however it's a 16x scope... especially in a game where you can't zero your guns, why would a 16x scope be set to a range so close that I can't even see half the body of my target at the same time?As it is equipment and not a secondary anymore, you can no longer use the taser with a shield at the same time, forcing you to carry your empty secondary if you are going for an S while holding your shield. The taser also does not work in multiplayer, even on still, static targets. You will often desync in multiplayer and lose access to your door wedges (unless you are host), as they simply disappear (sometimes you can grab them back even though they are not visible on your client and no interaction shows up, however sometimes they are completely unable to be retrieved by you).AI commands are very clunky and restrictive, often auto-selecting your target (blue/red/gold) based on what it thinks you want to do, and removing the option to manually select a different target (for example, stack up red on a door, and then try to tell blue to do something with that door, like wedging it, mirroring it, or opening, etc. and notice how you cannot select blue, only red or gold). You also cannot tell AI to do something unless you look at it. If you ask your AI to stack on a door to open and clear it, and then you move somewhere else (as you may want to attack from multiple angles, potentially with split AI, and the AI take forever to actually position themselves), when they tell you the door is locked, you cannot remotely tell them to pick the lock, and must run all the way back so that you can look at the door when you give the order.This is very blatantly the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game practice of releasing something broken and unfinished with completely unwarranted marketing terms (like 1.0) and then having your audience find all your bugs for you. It's not ok and should not be supported. Not to mention the number of things missing from the game that were promised in development. I would refund this game if I hadn't played a large amount of the early access before this patch.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a tactical first-person shooter that brings players into intense, high-stakes scenarios as members of a SWAT team. The game’s main draw is its commitment to realism, which can make each mission feel tense and unpredictable. The environments are detailed, the AI is sharp, and the overall atmosphere is gripping, making every encounter feel like it could go wrong in a split second.One of the most talked-about aspects of the game is its dark humor, particularly when it comes to dealing with civilians. While the game’s realistic approach means you’re supposed to handle these situations carefully, the unintentional humor that arises from mishandling civilian interactions can be surprisingly funny. Whether it's accidentally flashbanging a room full of hostages or the chaotic moments when a terrified civilian bolts at the worst possible time, the game’s unpredictable nature often leads to absurd, laugh-out-loud situations.However, this humor is set against a backdrop of gruesome and realistic depictions of violence. The game doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal consequences of your actions. The gunfights are intense, with bullets having real stopping power, and the aftermath of a firefight is often messy. The realism here isn’t just for show—it makes the stakes feel incredibly high and every decision critical.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ready or Not" is an awesome tactical shooter that really pulls you in. I've played it on both Linux (Ubuntu) and Windows 10 without any problems—it runs super smoothly, though having an RTX 4090 probably helps!Playing with random people can be pretty easy if you're just trying to finish missions. But if you aim to complete them perfectly—like using non-lethal weapons and sticking to proper protocols—it becomes a real challenge that needs good teamwork and communication.The game has some intense moments. For example, storming a room and finding a hostage being used as a human shield really gets your heart racing. The missions are super interesting and sometimes tackle controversial topics, like taking down a dangerous cult, stopping an active shooter, or confronting a disturbed person live-streaming after committing crimes.Graphics are top-notch, and there's tons of customization for your character and gear. What's also great is the community. Even when playing with random players, people are usually friendly and team-oriented—not toxic at all.If you're into tactical shooters, I highly recommend "Ready or Not." I've had a ton of fun playing solo, and I'm sure it would be even better with friends!tl;dr: Funny game, even with strangers! Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: So, with a recent update changing the AI (at the least on Twisted Nerve). Its finally going in the right direction.  But without mods for AI tweaking, it finally feels like interactions with suspects are more than "Walk in, shout (optional), see gun, get shot at, shoot suspect, cuff".Like what I got to see was people using objects as cover. Their accuracy to hit being possible to deal with as a beanbag shotgun; But not a free win. Hell I had suspects try to walk  from me without drawing their gun. Someone tried to hide underneath a wire bed in vain!It just seemed to have make my flashbangs worse. 1/3 thrown flashes worked. Two into small rooms, one outside. Likely will go back to my gas mask and teargas 'nade strat just so I can rely on my throwables to disable.-----(Original Review)-----I really want to recommend it. But as it stands, the game sits in a broken state of AI. Not bug ridden, but horridly balanced. SWAT4, the game this is being a "successor" to, had more balanced AI for what was reasonable at the time. It was basic, the accuracy of the game forced you to move slowly to not hit a civvie by accident. Basic command tree for AI teammates. And a few rare sniper spots if you needed it. That was 2005, and I never felt it was unfair.Its 8 years later. Apparently that means an immersive sim should involve really unrealistic reaction speeds and accuracy to targets you are meant to subdue. There's posters to remind you, you aren't military. Bring people in alive. But the peppergun rifles don't make their aim worse so you can actually survive. And the Beanbag gun several times on mission 2, even with a full team of AI with more LTL long-guns; Cannot get one guy with no armor to drop a gun. Tried to knock the wind out of him to stun, then two shots, three, fou- Dead."Well you should use your throwables!" Guess what I had the AI do when entering the room? What do you think I do when I want to do a solo run?And that directly conflicts with the messaging police need to re-learn. Hearts and Minds, not Widows and Orphans. Even when I take anything other than one of 3 LTL primaries, I discipline my firing to be knockouts and not kills. .45 to the skull may keep myself safe; But means I failed to preserve life. The game only rewards an S rank for a perfect arrest run (that also requires to find all hidden objectives that isn't hinted at what may be important). S ranks unlocks cosmetics to help you stand out from other players. Said S rank is real hard when anything short of an AI is at 50/50 odds of dying to a new sightline.Just use SkebbZ's  mod. This isn't a kind of challenge that respects you. After that, game does start to become more fun to play. And more with friends.(Side note: Apparently the subtitles and a bunch of media is AI genned too. Is it that hard to just hire an artist? I wouldn't be surprised if the breifs are also AI voiced. Furthering the reasons why AI generated content is both a mistake and should be shamed.)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Overall, yes, this game is worth getting! BUT, I would wait until a few patches come through first. A few weeks to a month at most. let VOID have their holiday, and then cop it once they are refreshed and back to work. Anyways, onto my issues/review! Bots - the bots are currently insane. The last mission I just finished (Hospital) had 21 enemies in it. I went in with 6 AR mags, 2 sidearm mags, 2 flashbangs, and 2 breach charges. Walked out with 2 broken legs, 2 broken arms, damaged head, 2 dead teammates, and half a mag of my AR. Believe me when I say I am not bad at the game or its a "skill issue". Getting wallhacked and prefired was ridiculous, it took me multiple hours throughout today to finish.Squad AI - Majority of the time, the new Squad AI is a MAJOR improvement from pre 1.0. They are responsive, have personality, and I love when they take the initiative to cuff or bag on their own. The breach commands are simple, but complex enough to have you needing to think about your decision. On the runs they didn't work however, I have had my element blow themselves up with breach charges, (the door was not trapped looked, prior to the charge), I've had my element just walk up and Agent 47 civilians or high priority targets, I've had my element forget what colours are apparently, ect. Funny to look back on, but very frustrating in the moment. Oh, I almost forgot. You're in my spot, Sir.Map Design - Firstly, the maps are BEAUTIFUL! Especially the hotel, I spent more time getting shot because I was staring at the visuals rather than the enemies! BUT, they are a little cluttered, and sometimes offer no viable strat to bypass an enemies choke point. Visibility is an issue sometimes as well. Flashlights are nearly mandatory on almost every map, unless you really love NVG's. Voice Acting/Dialogue - Good, not great. Sometimes the VA's are a little uninspired in their dialogue during their breakdowns. The 911 call VA's are impeccable however. There are also quite a few spelling errors in the mission breakdowns/squad AI dialogue, but it's nothing game breaking, obv. One issue I do have though, is almost every 911 call's text doesn't scroll fast enough to keep up with the conversation. I personally like to read along with the audio, maybe that's just me. Also, the breakdown dialogue starts after every 911 call ends, so if you want the 911 calls first, get ready to hit play on the next one immediately lol.Weapons/Gunplay - Tight, crisp, exactly what you'd expect. It feels better than it did post 1.0, and that was already very very smooth. Not much to say here, its good!Performance - My performance has been... a mixed bag. Most maps so far I spawn in initially with 1-200 FPS, but the second I take my first steps, I struggle to hit 30. It's very inconsistent though, which is quite frustrating. I am playing on 4K with max settings, so I could easily lower my settings to alleviate the issues, but I am confident my PC is not the issue (R7 7700x, rtx4080, 32gb DDR5). I hope VOID hops on this one before Christmas break, but if not, the game is fun enough that I am just dealing with it ATM.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a worthy (Although not official) successor to the famed SWAT 3 and 4. Purely tactical, extremely tense and difficult but rewarding. This Ladies and Gentlemen is the true SWAT Tactical experience brought to life with more modern tools and approaches that we could of only dreamed of whilst playing SWAT 4.Firstly, I would like to preface that this is an early access review - the game is in it's early stages, missing content, features and general polish. However if you're interested in this game and are willing to drop the asking price, this game is absolutely worth it. Right now as of this review, I've only experienced the PvE experience, however a PvP experience is said to be featured at a later date. Biased as I may be the PvE is where this game is for me anyway.Which leads nicely onto the PvE experience. Ready or Not features multiple maps each with multiple gamemodes or situations, namely being Barricaded Suspects, Raid, Active Shooter, Bomb Threat and Hostage situation. These gamemodes are all unique in both the way the maps are laid out and the methodology required in order to take them on both effectively and more importantly - successfully. This game is  do not be dismayed when first starting out, you will fail, many times.Ready or Not features both Singleplayer with AI teammates and a Multiplayer element. The AI is pretty decent in it's current stage but does need some tweaking here and there, nothing unusual. They're fairly competent and know how to cover angles and perform room clearance without much input from the player. On the other hand is Multiplayer, up to 5 players. This game is an absolute blast with your friends, teamwork is absolutely mandatory and great communication is a gel that binds a plan together. I've not had a more fun tactical experience with my buddies for a long long time and this game certainly scratches an itch in that regard that I thought would not be scratched for a good while.Another thing that stood out to me over the course of playing was the sound design. It is absolutely  When I use a breaching charge I feel like my organs have shifted, it is pure bass. It is glorious. It reverbs and it contorts through the environment, it does exactly what it should, and the firearms behave the same, it is amazing to experience. Albeit loud but hey it's 'mersion.Whilst I could continue to sing praises about this game, there are some downsides so far that I should address. (Please bear in mind that these are most likely already going to be addressed due to the early access nature and I'm really just clutching at straws here). As of now the arsenal and gadgets at the player's disposal is quite limited - I expect this to change over the course of development. I would also like to see bots as an optional addition in Multiplayer games, maybe you don't have 5 people and could do with an extra AI or more to order around and provide assistance. Players should be able to designate AI to be ordered around in order to fill extra slots.Other than to continue listing lack of content that is almost guaranteed to be added throughout development such as more maps and things of that nature, I'm going to close it here. This game is absolutely worth the money. You may see it and think that the price is steep, well let me tell you - it's a small team that has made a AAA quality product and their attention to detail and realism is exactly what it should be. People are not exaggerating when they say it is SWAT 5. It is what we've been waiting for. It is a truly tactical joy. I cannot recommend it more.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the first 1000 people to back this game in 2019, I took a massive risk spending over $120 backing this game in it's earliest stages. Participated in various closed NDA alpha builds and held a very high expectation for Ready or Not.If the recent popularity surge isnt enough to go off of, then let me explain if I feel ready or not is worth being in the Supporter Build or just the $40 entry fee.For $40, the game is absolutely worth the money. High resolution graphical lighting and shadowing, really takes the cake over textural or powerhouse polygon count. UE4 is aged by today's standards. But ready or not really pushes the engine to the limits. The gameplay is tight. VERY tight. You will rarely get caught up on the environment, giving you a feeling of being in a tube like a real SWAT situation. Hyperfocused on every corner, door and crevice that might expose an angle for you to be ambushed. The AI has undergone massively impressive improvements. Further showing the dedication VOID has to addressing the big issues that plague every other tactical shooter.Then you have the visceral realism of the subject matter. Ready or Not has had a bunch of political controversy during its relatively short development cycle(for a team their size). Everything from calling the game a police backed murder simulator; to a towing the line glance at the real world atrocities that the media loves so much.The absolute shocking and brutal nature of the game is where the main focus SHOULD be. After adding in the Nightclub massacre map, VOID crossed a line in a very big way. And that line I argue, should be crossed further. Where the game really comes to be worth any price really; is the experience. You have active shooter scenarios, bomb threats, hostage situations.......and even worse examples of human depravity featured in this game.And yet I feel they should take it EVEN FURTHER by adding in Schools, Malls, Churches/Mosques and other real world scenarios like subways or grocery stores. And why would I say something so horrible? Why would I want to live out that experience in a video game? Because it isnt a game. It is the sad reality of the world we live in. The city of Los Suenos feels eerily similar to many of the crime ridden cities in the US at the moment. The AI have an incredibly feeling of scorn towards the police and the criminals alike. Also drawing a very realistic parallel to the real relations of officers in the US. When I say "It isnt a game". I of course have to draw the comparison to SWAT 4. A game in which I had hoped ready or not would copy exactly. And while they are close to it(very close), I feel like they could carve a path of their own by focusing on copying the real world instead. If this game was aimed out to be SWAT 5 then I would be happy enough. But the audio in this game is one of the best there is, bar none. Its so gripping that hearing the actual bullets penetrate, seeing the gory aftermath and listening to a target(intended or not) dying, is so close to the real thing that it would be considered disturbing to most.So how do I wrap this up? Disturbing, realistic, visceral. A simulation of the most atrocious and violent acts that human beings can commit. Ever wanted to hunt down child traffickers? Drug lords? Terrorists? They are all here. But the experience is so close to home, that it might actually leave you needing to reflect on how much of it is just a game.As I said, they have teased a School Shooter level before and a "Swatting" scenario as well. These type of big leaps into controversial topics are what would make this game stand above not just SWAT 4 but literally every other SWAT genre game to exist. If VOID can continue to ignore the publications and potential controversies and just jump for it, then I have no doubt the outcome would be so profound, it would shake the entire industry.As a loving supporter for over 5 years now, I have to thank VOID Interactive for maintaining their commitment to providing supporters/players with the best possible experience. An experience of real world tension, that my only request is, they turn the dial to max.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Ver.: Greatest anti-pedophile video game ever. I can go from extremely slow, methodical room clearing to John Wick-esque clearing and still get 180'd by a dude rounding the corner. Solid 8.Long Ver.: Extremely intense tactical FPS that imitates the quickness and the horrors of the situations SWAT faces. This is not a game for the faint of heart, or for the faint of the eyes. In my hours, I have mostly played solo, so you may have a different experience.+ Visuals attuned to realism. Best experienced with a mid-spec to high-spec PC.+ Storytelling is amazing. Take your time to immerse yourself in the scenario, and you will find the story from within and its many details. You will find that it is more closer to home than fiction.+ Sound quality is great. If you're scared of loud sounds, best to turn it down; you may miss some footsteps or even worse- assailants and hostages yelling. Headphones for the best experience.+ Map design feels balanced between what is reasonable expected from a tactical FPS, and realism. You will not be able to clear all the angles by yourself.+ Gun play is good. Take it as a tactical horror FPS and not like a regular arcade FPS. If you miss a shot, your enemy will make sure that is your last shot.+ Community maps and mods exist, instantly prolonging its longevity and range of enjoyment. At the time of this review, Nexusmods and mod.io are my sources of mods. If you like to have modded maps, tweaks to gameplay or different guns, RoN supports these endeavors.- Only 12 playable scenarios, ranging from long, expansive and ambitious levels to short, intimate levels. This will eventually become alleviated with more updates to the game. The quality of each levels is astonishing though, so take this point with a grain of salt.- SWAT AI doesn't feel like a team at all. No personality comparable to SWAT 4, and certainly no autonomy either. Besides following you around like a litter of puppies, you must issue them commands every time. Ease of use is granted with a single keystroke, but doesn't help the lack of a distinguishable AI here.- Enemy AI can be perceived as impossibly hard. I sure thought of that in my first couple of experiences as well, however learning how enemies work will severely tip the chances of coming out of the gunfight to you. Still doesn't take away from their incredible HS rate.- Not meant to be played solo. At the very least, play with a friend. My solo experience is complete hell-on-earth; you will run out of equipment and ammunition clearing even half the level. Maybe just skill diff., but the solo experience is not one you should try. That said, I am a solo player, and this will not stop me from enjoying the game nonetheless.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone is complaining about the AI, and rightfully so. No idea what drugs the devs are on to think 100ms reaction time from AI is acceptable. There are articles looking through the suspect AI code and, yes, it's literally 100ms if they're alerted. 200ms if they're not. The fact they can sometimes ignore CS gas and see you through it, which is essential to S rank all the missions is also so fun with their aimbot accuracy. Crazy how old women can pick you off from 70m away because they seen a pixel of your body through some boarded window. I could never fathom the reason why 9/10 suspects fake surrender to only pull out something every time you go to cuff them; the devs must have watched video compilations of the craziest criminals for their inspiration.It should be a crime for devs to make games where AI gun you down in a blink of an eye while you have to yell at them, or suffer the negative "unauthorized use of force" punishment.How fast these suspects can move in comparison to you is also insane. They can basically run around the level and come strafing across a door, with no gun collision, gunning you down so easily. They can also see you perfectly fine in complete darkness. Not sure if it's incompetency, negligence, or lack of knowledge from the devs to not have zones on the map that lower AI accuracy if they're standing in certain light levels or see a player in those zones.It makes the game a chore to play. However, mods do alleviate the frustration but at the cost of not counting the score legitimately at the end of missions.I have no idea why they don't have a difficulty scale based on how many players you have in a party, and the type of suspect they are to stop every suspect feeling like some ex-military solider.Enough with the bad talk of the game, here's some good stuff:When the optimization isn't pissing the bed, the game is fun. The level designs, briefing, weapons, uniform customization, and some audio is well done. The non-lethal weapons, pepperspray, and riotshield are underwhelming because of the reasons above but it is a fun challenge to get those nice S ranks.Regardless of the huge negative of the AI being way overtuned. I do really enjoy this game and what it offers for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: What in the world happened to this game? It was way more fun when it was in early access. I returned to it after a year or two of not playing to find that it's been gutted of maps and game modes. It used to play like a sandbox but now it's on rails, and replayability has been discarded. Performance is noticeable worse too, which is confusing to me since the game is technically released now and I didn't used to have problems with stuttering and low frame rates when I played before. Even on the same maps that look unchanged since then.A problem with the core mechanics that has been an issue for as long as I can remember and still isn't fixed: arresting armed suspects is virtually impossible without shooting them or using a flashbang. Everyone from lowly street thugs to private security are suicidal in the face of a heavily armed SWAT team; even when they are caught off-guard and held at gunpoint by the player, or have been hit with pepper balls or tasers. In short, less-lethal options are very underwhelming and not as effective as you would expect from a game about being a law enforcement officer.On the opposite end of the spectrum, and one that appears to be a new addition: your bot teammates will now turn hostile and kill you if you shoot a civilian or a detained criminal. So if you are like me and have ever wanted to clear an entire level like a psycho, that is no longer possible, cuz the developers said so. Even accidental kills will trigger this, which becomes a big concern if you're using a high caliber rifle or armor piercing ammunition. Why not just leave it the way it used to be where you get a harsh scolding over your radio and a large score penalty at the end of the mission? Is it really that important to the devs that NPCs in a video game are not unfairly killed by the player? I understand applying this kind of mechanic to public multiplayer lobbies where griefing is invariably an issue, but I am talking about singleplayer. No fun allowed.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played SWAT 3 back in 1999 I loved the dynamic gameplay of true tactical shooters.  I've been waiting for a game to replace the dynamic tactical gameplay of SWAT 3 and SWAT 4 for about 18 years and this game is the backscratcher to that itch you couldn't reach.  The devs seem to listen to their community very closely (cant want for the next FAQ/AMA) and they seem to be working their asses off to make this game the best tactical shooter ever.  There is still a long way to go, but I have backed this since day 1 so I can see a HUGE improvement going from basic alpha concept gameplay to a now fully playable game (with limited content since it is still earlier release than a full release).  I am very excited for the future of this game and the new maps/weapons/enemies/mechanics that will be introduced along the way.A few things I would like to highlight: (Content I would like to see from the devs with commentary on the current game state)The SWAT AI is great so far in how you can command them.  I love how you can command red and blue individually and the controls are simple for commanding them.  With that being said, I really would like to see AI fill spots that players are not filling in multiplayer.  For example, if you only have one friend on at the time to play with, you host the game, your friend joins in as Red Team lead.  You command any team that does not have a leader so if your friend is red team lead, they can command Red team, you would command Blue.  If your friend dies, then you can command the remaining red team member (AI) if that AI is still alive, etc.  Another thing to note is right now it seems AI does not trigger traps, which needs to be fixed and I'm sure it will be.Downed teammates, not always deceased -  Now that the carry system is in, I think it would be nice if an officer had a chance of going down/unable to continue but not be reported as deceased all the time and maybe players could receive extra points in the mission for carrying a downed officer to safety to be extracted from the scene.  I feel this would be a nice touch to the immersion. ( I am not suggesting this would revive the teammate or player in any way shape or form, just a sort of side objective to simulate the dynamic situations that could happen in a real life SWAT situation )Gore - The devs originally spoke about realistic gore, not a huge game breaking mechanic but a gore system would definitely not only add to immersion but would also add to the dark feel of the game/story.One of the things I LOVED most about SWAT 3 and SWAT 4 were introductions to a mission.  In SWAT3, one of my most fond memories is going into a mission and the loading screen had the dispatcher communicating information about the situation and I think this is a MUST in Ready or Not.  A briefing when you select the mission in the briefing room would be amazing as well, I would love to see an animated briefing with changing slides on a screen maybe explaining the situation, entry point, and targeted outcome for each map (I know it's a lot to ask, and a lot of work, but if done right could make this game look completely legit triple A quality, these small or big things added up to why the SWAT games were so good).I noticed in the new level penthouse the devs added a bit more immersive scenery with police and civilaisn/suspects down the stairs from where you start and I absolutely LOVE THAT! Please keep more of this scenery coming!Police chatter throughout the game in certain places would also be awesome for example if there are regular uniform officers at a police barricade in the street and if you get close you could hear police chatter from the police radios.Last but not least, a custom Ready or Not SDK for mods would make this game HUGE.  Another thing that made the SWAT games so successful was a semi simple way of modding the games and adding things to it WITHOUT replacing existing vanilla stuff (Unless you wanted to) such as weapons/uniform skins or models/Maps/ or even change music throughout the game (without replacing the original files) by launching the mod.  I remember the chimera mod for example for SWAT 3 which I would argue was probably one of the most popular for SWAT 3 (at least fairly early on).P.S. Add some new sidearms! P226 or variant preferably :DThanks for making this game great and continue the great work. 10/10 so far!

_childDocuments_.review:
Ready or Not is an intense, tactical, first-person shooter that depicts a modern-day world in which SWAT police units are called to defuse hostile and confronting situations.

VOID interactive has consulted with police teams globally to create rules of engagement and a scoring system that are both challenging and realistic. In order to push the bar further with realism, Ready or Not models ballistic penetration, ricochet, kevlar and plate dynamics, as well as projectile expansion and momentum.

Explore a deep and involved weapon handling and player maneuvering system, geared towards providing officers with an unprecedented level of control over their situational effectiveness. Ready or Not utilizes a simple and organic control scheme which won't have players fumbling around, forgetting dozens of key bindings.

Organize an approach, then execute the mission in real time. Officers can decide to deploy with items such as ballistic shields, door rams, tactical ladders, and much more.

Bring order to chaos online with friends through a tactical cooperative experience, lead a crack team of AI-driven swat members in a solo, story-rich campaign, or battle a rogue organization in a fierce and competitive multiplayer environment.

name: SLUDGE LIFE
detailed_description: SLUDGE LIFE is a first-person / open-world / vandalism-centric stroll through a polluted island full of cranky idiots and a vibe so thick you can taste it. Roam a tiny island stuck on a sludge covered planet as an upcoming tagger GHOST set on staking their claim amongst the graffiti elite. Traverse the corporately branded landscape, chat up other taggers, and discover secrets and idiots along the way. Will you become the king of the island and tag every open inch, infiltrate sludge-pumping corporation GLUG to find a way out, or just take it all down in flames with you? Experience the thrills of vandalism from the safety of your computer. Curiosity and free will are your only motivators - roll as you please. Find and download apps to your laptop and waste your life away playing a game in a game. Smoke Ciggy Cigs brand cigarettes. Smoke ‘em up real good. Take photos of exotic fauna and ambivalent NPCs. Dedicated fart button. A huge baby, community basketball court, and a cat with two buttholes. [no extra charge] Three distinct endings and a pretty robust credits.

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game as soon as I saw a short clip from it. Weird, SO weird.The gameplay is largely "walking simulator", with a bit of platforming. You start in this weird little island city, surrounded on all sides by... well, yeah, "Sludge". You're not really going to find out why, the game isn't that way inclined. It's much, much more about discovering the weird and wonderful people littering the various structures, from the apartments to the fast food restaurant to the building sites. Everyone has their own odd vibe, and the sense of humour here really shines. More often than not, whatever character you run into is going to say something that brings a chuckle.So where does this all go? Well, you unlock some items which allow you to move around. You can fast travel/teleport to various landmarks, you can unlock a glider so you can fly around the city. You're also collecting slugs, and spraypainting your logo all over the place, and larger pieces on billboards. BUT, this is the only real limitation of the game, it doesn't necessarily go anywhere else. You're running around, talking, laughing, tagging stuff. If you're hoping for deep narrative, this isn't it. If you want a colourful and super eclectic experience, this is a great example!
