_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a nonstop adrenaline pumping game that will dangle the exit in front of you happily right before body slamming you into the Pool of Styx with 0 shred of mercy.And every single time i walk out with a smile, pet my gigantic goodest boy, and say "Again."Game of the DECADE in my humbly correct opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Definitly one of the best, if not even the best game released in 2020 and one of the best Roguelikes I've played in a while. The key difference to other roguelike games is the story-rich runs. No other roguelike I've played so far, if you dont count Darkest Dungeon which isnt a fully fleshed roguelike, had me so invested in the story, especially because I'm a sucker for greek mythology.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews for games, but my god this is the most complete and polished "Early Access" game I've ever played. It's fun, exciting, intriguing, beautiful, and at times frustrating - what more could you ask for in a game? They say it's in development but I wouldn't have thought so if they didn't advertise that it was.Seriously, this is the best game purchase I've made in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: If you like hack'n'slash and story telling, you're gonna love it. If you prefer roguelite gameplay/metroidvania, you may not love it... at all. This is my case, I don't like hack'n'slash, I find them boring, that's my opinion but here's the thing, the gameplay of Hades is mostly hack'n'slash, if you take away the boss fights which are the very few moments of the game that I enjoy in terms of gameplay, everything is dash attack dash attack rince and repeat till the rooms are cleared.It's been 15 hours I've been playing and honestly, I don't know the patterns of most of the monsters, I'm just spamming like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥... You'ld say, ok you're not playing the game right, but this is the way to dodge the most damages and to deal the most, as well as finishing the levels the fastest...But the boss fights are nice. The story is amazing, the acting is amazing, it's really rich and awesome (I mean... Bastion y'know) the DA is amazing too.Oh and also, don't go HELL MODE, this is the worst thing ever. It has no use except making the game even more hack'n'slashy.For the roguelite side, except from the gameplay that is basically trash according to myself, there is another problems. You don't unlock things by getting further and further, you unlock things by dying over and over. That is a serious issue since you may want to die 20 times before starting to play to have all the things required to play correctly. Even if you finish the game on your first try, it'll make no sense since you won't have most of the mecanics. Why? I have no clue :'(Also monsters don't have new attacks after you finish the game the first time, like they do in other games, only bosses if you take the right options.Now my point of vue, should you buy it? It depends... do you like hack'n'slash? Then yes, otherwise buy Dead Cells, it's from a way smaller studio (French studio btw) and it is truly amazing. Or Isaac, Isaac is incredible too.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet Cerberus.Update: ......but it's still a roguelike after all, and a pretty difficult one. After about 10 escape attempts I'm now at a point where I'm not skilled enough to progress any further, and the resources I collect don't unlock anything meaningful, and the game starts becoming boring.The first few runs were still fun as hell though.Update: ......I wanted to put this game down but somehow I can't. Every day I gave it one more run, fail, and put it down again, but somehow the next day I will want to run again. This kept going for a while, and 27 escape attempts later I finally saw the final boss. Let's see how many more attempts it takes to defeat him.Update: escaped at attempt #34 after some extreme cheesing, by using the shield and the boon that regenerates health. And now the game offers ways to further increase difficulty, and looks like that is necessary for completing the story. I don't think this game is for me so my journey ends here, but it's still fun as hell.Update: did I say my journey ends here? Because it didn't, I'm still unable to put this game down. I turned on God Mode, which reduces all incoming damage by 20%, and it increases by another 2% on each death. A few more runs later I'm receiving only 50% damage, and the game's difficulty finally feels right and I'm able to escape a few more times. Meanwhile I'm constantly unlocking new renovations and advancing relationships with each run, and the game has yet to feel repetitive at all, despite being a roguelike. This feels like magic.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: It needs patience, it needs time, and it needs a little bit of understanding. Once you have those all, Hades will take you on an adventure you've not experienced before. You might find the game repetitive but that's the genre, however, the way this game revolves around that with it's narrative is too beautiful to be put to words. The hooking point for me was the first time I cleared the game (it was after I saw another friend of mine finish the game that lowkey made me jealous too, so I thought of picking up the game again) and I just finished the main quest. Never really thought I'd have had my strings pulled by the game when I bought it, but now I'm glad I did. The story is slow burn and it gets very touching, add that with their beautiful music and art and it makes the game the best title I've played till date.tl;dr Best game I've played, love it soo much, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game for circa 40 hours I can say with confidence that this game is weirdly gripping.A roguelike game is hard to make because every attempt must feel fresh from the last one, otherwise the game will be mundane and boring. Having that said, Hades nails it when it comes to replayability. You have so many objectives, especially when you unlock the fated list of minor profecies that give you an idea of what you can do and makes you wanna run out there and beat your dad's ass again and again and again. Another important aspect of this game is the soundtrack. Oh. My. God. You will not hear a soundtrack as good as this game's on any regular game you might find, the music made for this game is astonishingly fitting and so good that I listen to it even when I'm not playing. Although when I am playing, it gets my blood pumpin'.So, all in all, Hades is one of the best examples of a good roguelike that doesn't get repetitive despite the genre it is. I seriously reccomend it, as you will have a LOT to do. Gl hf!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Just play the damn game already.There's enough hype surrounding this game that you owe it to yourself to at least try it - and like so many before you you'll likely find this game is far greater than the sum of it's parts.Original review below:Hades.  What a game.If you like awesome visuals, you should play it.If you have even a passing interest in greek mythology, you should play it.If you are a fan of rogue-likes, you should play it.If you enjoy a good story, you should play it.Honestly I could sit here all day listing reasons why you should play this game, but ultimately I think if you like and enjoy games even remotely like this, you should play Hades.If you are a fan of games in general - you owe it to yourself to at least try this game.  It's a good game made well - a tight, well crafted, lean but fun game.Just play the damn game already.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: This decade could not have started with a better roguelike than Hades. This game is the new generation of roguelike that is on pair with Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon, if not better. If you have not decided yet if you want to buy the game, then please do! It will be more than worth your money for the price they're offering.Absolutely well done with the game, Supergiant Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: You know, I was super aggravated at this game - I've grown tired of the Early Access thing. Games "releasing" years before they are done, coverage that constantly talks about unfinished games, etc.But I'll be damned if this isn't a fantastic one of these. Solid action, fun progress and mechanics. Reminds me a bit of Dead Cells in the way it feels like it has just so many builds and unlockables. Once again Supergiant has knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is an extremely enjoyable rogue like, while its not the best in the genre, it delivers a completely unique experience in terms of story telling and artstyle (truly a magnificent looking game). To get it out of the way, yes this game is worth it, especially if it is on sale. If you main rogue-like games take my review with a grain of salt as i dont have many of these under my belt since its not my #1 preferred genre. Here are my pros and consPros:- Artstyle/customization. It is extremely colourfull and the game allows you to redecorate most of the underworld rooms.- Great story that actually justifies you re-running the gauntlet over and over.- Death feels great as you get permenant upgrades and god mode can be used for those going for all achievements (not me this time around).- Most characters stand out personality wise in an amusing way as well as through their abilities.- Smooth combat, never experienced a bug.Cons (For me)- Not as replayable as other rogue likes due to less ways to play than your average game of the genre. Less abilities are in the game due to a level up system. Prolly around 1/5 or less of the abilities as other rogue likes. I assume it was designed this way to avoid the players from breaking the ceiling and becoming a true God (ironic). Shame since rogue likes should allow u to make builds where you can one shot even end game areas if u get lucky enough. Maybe they wanted a more skillfull experience. - True epilogue is locked behind rng and hundreds of runs which, due to the replayability point, i felt no desire to grind for that, let alone all achievements. There are even Youtubers who say this took them 5 months to do.- Could of used more worlds and abilities, by the 7-10th run i felt like ive seen everything multiple times already.- True epilogue (which i used Youtube to see, like many others who also apparently didnt want to grind for months lol) lacks a few key character reactions people would of liked to observe. Still satisfying enough tho.Dont mind my cons too much if grinding is not an issue for you. Its a great rogue like with a great story. Grab if on sale. I will prolly prefer to pick up binding of Isaac instead to scratch my once every 3-5 months roguelike itch, but hades should still see some action every now and then.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I certainly don't regret spending my last money on it. It's fun, it's entertaining, the characters are done very nicely, both the protagonist and his voice are quite handsome and there's another literally LARGE reason to buy the game;You get to  after each time you are being forcefully taken home. Also one of the Weapons attacks gives me Xena vibes right there, heh. Some environmental things can be annoying but once you get used to the game it's nothing more than an inconvenience you either ignore or automatically get around. The soundtrack is also very nice along with the general aesthetics of the game. You'll get a lot of bang for the buck, that's for sure. As of writing this Review, I've played 4 1/2 hours straight. So yeah, recommended. Gotta go.

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant Games challenged themselves when they decided to make an action roguelite, and they succeded. The feeling of progression in Hades feels real (if a bit grindy sometimes, but then again, what roguelite isn't?)A variety of weapons, boons and trinkets makes every run feel different, and everything is actually pretty balanced which is a rarity in itself.As usual with Supergiant, the art, visual style, dialogue and MUSIC are fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: It really is everything you've heard. ...until about level 3.HADES is more than a fun as Hell (huhuh) Fight/Die/Repeat Rogue, it's a masterclass in superlative design. The visuals are distinct and fresh but also perfect for a game, with sharp lines and bold colors that keep the chaos clear and draw the eye where it needs to go. The soundtrack does more than carry it elevates the game-play. And My Olympian Gods, It's rare as rock stars for a game to  this good. HADES is a game you will actually get better at in the first hour of play, as in you will actually feel yourself get sharper, settle into its rhythm and master its elegant controls. It's not deep as much as it is nuanced. You're not memorizing some clunky dodge-and-hit whiff, you're pushing yourself to be faster, smoother, more precise.It's like this because you really are in the heroes POV. You want to get further, you want to make the first bits go faster, and the game is totally designed to make that enjoyable. Way more than any button-mashing "God of War Like," with HAADES you actually feel yourself becoming a God of War. And that's just in the first few hours.Moreover, HADES keeps its hubworld fresh. Every death is lessened by the chance to learn more story, see new scenes, pet the dog, and even make time for shopping. There are characters you love to love, hate to love and love to hate. Everything you need to whet the appetite for one more round.  REDACTEDYahtzee said it best, "at some point it gets samey and the enemies turn to HP sponges." And that point is, literally, the point where you start to feel the groove, which is absolutely garbage.It was a fun climb to level 3, after failing on level 1 a dozen times, failing level 2 a dozen times, all that empowerment vanishes when the game decides 1) The bosses get random, and 2) what the player  wants isn't , it's 5 gems of a currency for a store full of  tat, where everything costs 30 gems or more! That's right. The difficultly doesn't  come in new challenges, it comes in filler. Room after room of wasted time.Because once the game decides you're ready for a real challenge, the difficulty doesn't spike, it becomes a wall. You go from a ceaseless thrill of escalation to a painful slog. And no, it's not about it being H4RdK0R3. Binding of Isaac has more variety and depth than this. It's just spam. Where you first met three enemies, you meet twenty(!)  And every blasted one of them has a shield. The bosses go from challenging but fun to bullet-hell. The upgrades go from exciting to . Maybe it picks up again later, but I'd already given up and switched on Easy mode. Hah! Easy. Sure.The story is still there, the combat is still visceral and engaging, but the sense of progress simply vanishes along with my motivations. Turning this game from a solid recommendation to "just fine." It's fine. Hades is okay. You'll get over it. I'd give it a 👍but someone needs to counterbalance the hype.  ★☆☆So, I finally beat the @#$% and that unlocked a LOT of things. I will admit the feeling is super triumphant and I made love so hard that night I was sore the next day, but let's be real here. It's a rogue.It's super triumphant when Isaac beats Mom. When you get the keys in Rogue Legacy. Here's the question, What makes Hades stand out is the focus. It's less like a typical platform or top-down rogue because it's not about exploration, it's 100% combat; which kind of takes the risk-reward factor out and turns it into a slot-machine. A very,   slot machine, but a one-armed bandit none the less.It took me 25 hours to get my first win, right? And all the things it unlocks feel like things which would have kept me having fun back when I ready to quit in part two of this review. I'm being pretty honest that the game doesn't start until it's over. All the stuff it teases you with in the house of Hades is essentially corded off until you win . I get it. I get what they're doing there.But those 30 hours? That's 40 runs. Not (just) because I want to listen to all the wonderful voice acting. But because I breeze through the first and second levels for 20 minutes, and then I'm at the mercy of the loot boxes.It feels like Hades wants me to play it for the rest of my life, and unlike Zagreus, I've got stuff to do. There is plenty to dislike about Hades, even if it is one of the top five games of 2020. My one out of three stands. Buyer beware the beast of ballyhoo.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from Bastion, I had high expectations from the maker of a great game and oh boy, did it match my expectations and more.The mechanics by themselves are rather classic but well executed :  - The controls are sharp and responsive,  - Items (boons and upgrades) are a huge part of the gameplay and the random aspect of the roguelike genre is mitigated a bit (you can choose your path while seeing what rewards you will get) - In detail, boons change your tactics and gameplay quite a lot (as expected). All variations (and there are a lot) are nice to play with even if they ask you to change your style a bit. - Multiple weapon choices and customization allow for a large variety of strategies that fit your playstyle while the game encourages you to try all of them whith changing bonuses - Upgrades for your weapons are varied and if you feel that you're not doing well with a certain weapon, choosing some upgrades can dramatically change your experienceStorywise, I was really surprised by the depth that Hades gets to. From the small talk with characters in the hub that are always effective in cheering you up after a failed run to the one-liners of the gods of Olympus when you choose their boons that seem to be always unique, the world is full of life, happiness and personality everywhere you look.As for the the main story, it progresses (whithout surprises) depending on your runs and brings a fitting conclusion (though a bit sad) to this awesomely crafted world.P.S : Artemis is the best

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant proving yet again that they are the small team with the biggest guns, putting in the effort many won't to make a great foundation of a game and then ramp the quality up to 100 with detail upon detail of fantastic world-building and game design, and the result is another staggering accomplishment.Hades has beautiful gameplay clarity. It is incredibly direct and straightforward, yet doesn't pull any punches. Dying over and over the way rogue-likes want you to feels not only intended, but rewarding in its own way. Combat is flashy and satisfying and the upgrade progression is FUN. I don't mean what most people say when they mean fun where you're just trying to unlock every possible weapon/combination for the sake of having it all. It's actually fun, like you want to see what more the game has to offer for the sake of seeing it, even if you never use it, and boy does it offer a lot.Hours and HOURS of beautifully written and performed dialogue, all of it interesting, enveloped in actual character, and relevant to the gameplay, not just the setting. Big props to the voice actors for this game because they really laid an amazing foundation for the world of Hades. Theme-appropriate music that just nails those intense moments as well as those classic, thought-provoking, Supergiant moments.This game is wonderful, thank you Supergiant. A class-act and a love-letter to us all, reminding us that there are people out there who will make something so unnecessarily detailed and beautiful because it's what they love to do.Definitely buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades has truly redefined my understanding of what a rogue-like game can be. From the moment I started playing, I was captivated by the game’s breathtaking art style. It combines hand-drawn environments with 3D models in a way that is both striking and functional. Each area of the Underworld is visually rich and distinct, making exploration a joy. Complementing this visual splendor is the game’s exceptional soundtrack. The music is not just background noise; it’s integral to the experience, with energetic and emotionally resonant tracks that perfectly match the fast-paced action and darkly enchanting atmosphere.The game is packed with content, ensuring that there is always something new to experience. With a variety of weapons and abilities, each run feels different, and the roguelike mechanics keep the gameplay fresh and exciting. This variety is what makes me return to Hades time and time again. Its unique take on Greek mythology is another highlight. Rather than depicting Hades as a purely malevolent figure, the game provides depth and motivation to his character. The story of Zagreus’s quest to escape the Underworld and reconnect with his family is engaging and personal, offering a refreshing perspective on familiar myths.One of the most compelling aspects of Hades is how it handles death. In this game, dying is not a setback but a crucial part of the journey, unless of course you're that one person that feels the obligatory need to beat the game on its first try, in which case you'll need all the luck you can get XD! Each failure contributes to the story and progression, making every run an essential part of the overall experience. The dialogue and voice acting further enhance the game’s appeal. The interactions with the gods and other characters are engaging and memorable, thanks to exceptional voice performances and well-crafted dialogue.Returning to the House of Hades after each run is particularly satisfying. The hub area evolves with every attempt, offering new interactions and upgrades. This aspect provides a rewarding break between action-packed runs and adds a sense of continuity to the experience. The fluidity of the combat is another standout feature. The controls are responsive, and the diverse range of weapons and abilities means there’s always a new strategy to explore. Each fight feels impactful and engaging, making the gameplay deeply satisfying.Overall, Hades is a standout game that has captured my attention and kept me hooked. Its combination of stunning visuals, fantastic music, intricate storytelling, and addictive gameplay makes it a must-play. Whether you’re a fan of rogue-lites or just looking for something new, Hades offers an experience that is both deeply satisfying and endlessly replayable. It’s a game that I’m grateful to have experienced and one that I’ll remember for a long time to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Man, the way I feel about Hades makes me feel like I'm playing it wrong, but so does playing Hades.I used to think I just wasn't a fan of rougelikes and roguelites alike.(I also hate that we're now calling soulslikes, *soulslikes* although I am curious to see what a souls*lite* is like.)Having to start all the way from the beginning always sounded like a fun idea in practice, especially being able to acquire permanent upgrades and shortcuts to make you feel more powerful in your next run. The thing is most of the time you're slogging through the same handful of nearly identical (even with the standard roguelike procedural design) and a lot of the time rarely even making it back to the point where you had just failed on your last run.Upon all that, I have rarely seen a roguelike or rougelite with combat and gameplay good enough to keep you entertained for the excessive amount of hours that are asked of the player to get through one of these games in the mentioned usual only handful of areas; Hades specifically has four, only three of which you will be seeing the most throughout the majority of your play, and as it doesn't change the order of these at all, you'll obviously be seeing the first area the most. But now most of these complaints I only have for games like Hades..... and Enter The Gungeon.Recently I have come to actually really like the rogue affiliated genre. After playing and finishing Dead Cells, Returnal and -if you count it- Inscryption I can really see the appeal, and makes me more upset I can't bring myself to conquer Hades. BUT the kicker is that roguelike aspects aside, all the things surrounded that core aspect of Hades I just don't like at all or think could have been done better.Progression feels incredibly slow and once you get big upgrades to your hub world, like the ability to upgrade weapons, the excitement quickly falls flat as it takes insanely rare (even rarer than the amount you've already accrued) resources to upgrade these things. The other more common resources like what you use to upgrade general stats feels okay at first but slows down so much that it feels akin to a mobile game. And then there's the construction gems resource that never feels entirely useful and are inherently mostly cosmetic, where the cosmetic upgrades are always expensive and feel small and only effect the hub world, which kind of brings me to the next point-story and art style.I really enjoy the hand-drawn look of Hades but I can't get past the thought of it looking like fan art of some other game, I guess you could actually say this is a fanfic of Greek mythology in general, which to me isn't bad premise if it was played out better. Characters have great visual design, but in my opinion a weird smug look to them as well as some varying looking art styles in general which is a bit jarring sometimes.Getting into story, it's just boring. I appreciate a simple general goal/premise in a game but this did not have enough in between. I found myself talking to characters and paying attention only to check off the invisible percentage box in my head. I'm not extremely well versed in mythology source material, but I do enjoy it and other countless works that have been based off it. Hades fails to make any of these characters interesting other than super face value personalities and traits. They're all voiced decently and appropriately, but a ton of the dialog is so over the top seemingly just to try and give these characters, more character through voice alone a lot of the time. If you want to get to know these characters better, you can give them a nectar that ups a generic heart meter with them and unlocks a few new bits of dialog. Obtaining this item is also a slog and ever getting to any benefit from doing this seemingly dating sim inspired aspect of the game is an absolute grind. This along with other upgrade aspects always feel very far away with no discernible reward in sight. In hindsight the dating game aspect is a really neat idea that I think could have made the repetitive nature of the game a lot more tolerable.My last and biggest critique is probably a non-issue for a lot of people, but I looked into a bit of the design of the game after playing a good amount of hours on Steam and then starting over on Switch. The thing that really made me hate this game is basically an invisible score counter, if you look at it properly you start to realize when the game wants you to progress and when it doesn't. This was fine and actually pretty interesting in the first 15-20 hours and I liked being able to recognize it. After a while though it completely ruined my experience.I got so sick of beating my head against a wall and always failing miserably, run after run, to the 3rd boss (or the first two a few times which actually get harder as you go on), which I had already beat on my first try against them. I felt like the game had given me a false hope and was pushing me down the rest of the time, not letting me get to know that 4th zone that I had already gotten to explore a bit of before. The worst run was getting hugely lucky the entire time and having the most OP build yet, sure that I was going to make it past this time, but then for the first time of any of my runs, the game skipped a crucial room that would have given me enough health to pass.30 hours in I did end up finally beating the boss again, but then my switch died and I lost my progress and said f*&k it I'm done. Maybe I'll get back to it one day, but I think I feel comfortable, or uncomfortable with the time I wasted on this game. I've never really looked at a game as a waste of time before this either.Final Thoughts:That's it I really wanted to fit some positive things in there but it didn't happen. Here, I guess: combat usually felt pretty snappy and good, more skill over luck most of the time. Great weapon variety even though upgrades were too hard to obtain. A shame too because those upgrades were sick af. I also think I would have had a totally different experience if the game was only about 15 hours, or had high risk shortcuts.I don't actually think it's a bad game at all and I can see why so many people like it, but it's definitely not for me.

Considering the games we used to see in this genre there weren't many examples of games that would cover all of the following aspects: amazing gameplay loop, a decent story/narrative and good soundtracks; usually the one that was lacking was the story, but hades takes all of the above to a whole new level, Supergiant managed to make a complex way of storytelling by using the mechanic of dying over and over again and restarting from the beginning that's present in roguelikes and roguelites and also having so many lines of dialogue that it might as well never feel repetitive... and don't get me started about the soundtrack. _childDocuments_.review: I've never played one of these types of games because I'm a big fan of multiplayer games, but wow this is good. It kept popping up in my recommended so I said screw it and got it. I was surprised at how much fun I had the first time I played it. Basically, each time you try to make it to Mount Olympus you gain this in-game currency which you can then use to get new abilities and stuff to use in the next run. Each time you die, you die. You go back to the very beginning and have to do it all over again, but it's not as bad as it sounds. Using this in-game currency to upgrade and get new abilities isn't the only thing players can do after death. Players can use other currencies to befriend gods who then give you cool upgrades and abilities, as well as use the currency to upgrade the look of your home base.The story is really cool, and honestly a lot deeper than it looks. The gameplay is great, it says it recommends a controller but I've been playing mouse and keyboard with no issues. Controls are simple to pick up, and the game is very easy to learn, but tough to beat. You will get frustrated, but it's so worth the price tag. I got it on sale, but I would pay full price.  Also keep in mind that if you don't like it and you have had it for less than 2 weeks, as well as have less than 2 hours of game time, you can always get a refund (but you won't want to, trust me).Overall, fantastic game, story is good, gameplay is fun as hell, it isn't expensive, and the music is AWESOME!tldr: Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I should've written a review on this game a long time ago but after finishing my 101st run I think it's about time I gave my much needed opinion.This game is a rouge-like which if you've never heard of the genre pretty much means when you die you start from the beginning and have to do it all again. Sounds pretty tedious as a concept but Hades does such an incredible job working around this. One being the randomised chambers that almost every rouge-like has, this keeps the game refreshing and ensures every run is different but I do feel that sometimes the chambers can be fairly predictable and one wish I have for this game is just a few extra different chambers as once you clock your first 20+ hours you can start to really notice patterns of what kind of chamber you will have next. This does make the game slightly repetitive once you have "finished" it as your main goal is no longer there so going through the same chambers does become a bit tiresome but the way combat and run building works really keeps it alive.The story and the characters are what keep this game alive for me. Being based off of a real Greek mythological story the premise of Hades is you are ironically not Hades but his son Zagreus trying to escape from your father and the underworld whilst getting help from Gods upon Olympus. Your reason for escaping changes at a point but I will not spoil any of that here. The real enjoyment comes from talking to the characters. There are hundreds and hundreds of voice lines and even after more than one hundred escape attempts still every time each character has something new to say to me keeping each run interesting and worth my time. The relationships you build also gain you rewards/bonuses so there is even more to be had from interacting with the world than just some cool dialogue.Off of the story now and onto actual gameplay and another reason why this game never gets boring. A huge amount of enjoyment in this game comes from building different setups for each run as you have 6 weapons to choose from each having 4 variations, then you have the boons from the Gods which give you different power ups, you can equip charms so that you get a certain God you want first. Then you have duo boons which combine the power of two Gods to create a "super ability" that are probably the most useful boons in the game. So much fun comes from creating these different builds and finding what works for you as everyone seems to find different weapons and booms easier for themselves than they are for others making your experience more personal as there is no one way to win. Visually the game looks pretty overwhelming in trailers but when you are playing it all comes together and it's not often I lose sight of where Zagreus is. Character models in dialogue are very well drawn I do wish they had a few extra expressions as every character seems to have 3 different drawings that they cycle through. The landscapes when you reach a new area are stunning to say the least especially after your first escape the surface is such a refreshing change of colour pallet it really blows you away. Speaking of the different areas of the game the level structure works really well as every area has its own feel and vibe with its own enemies that all have unique mechanics. Unlike most rouge-likes I have played you cannot back track at all so once you decide to enter a chamber that's it even after you have cleared it you cannot go back to go up a different path. I think this really works as it makes you think about where you want to go what rewards you will get and if the difficulty is really worth throwing away a whole run for.The music, oh my god the music, is absolutely incredible from start to finish and even having characters that are completely based around music is so good for this game as the bloody music is so good. I literally have no complaints about any sounds that this game makes as they are all perfect and genuinely some of the best video game music ever I think people could play this game purely for the music and they would still have a blast.Overall I love this game to bits every time I come back to play it I cannot have a bad time and still I haven't fully completed it I still have many relationships to build and story lines to complete before I have truly finished this game the only thing holding me back is the game does become a bit repetitive after the "ending" as you have no clear goal and the very similar chambers don't help but the pure gameplay, art style and sound work make it all worth it. I cannot recommend it enough to anyone it is an amazing experience that you will not regret.Overall 92/100

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a blend of story and combat, mixed like James Bond's vodka martini. Story progress is based on how many runs you've done through the dungeons. It follows Zagreus, son of Hades on his journey to emancipate himself from his evil father. Hades is an excellent villain, with a voice that could replace Darth Vader. I was simultaneously scared and horny at his voice. There are other plotlines involving the side characters that develop alongside the main plot, and I found myself deeply invested in Achilles and Patroclus's story. Progressing these side plots will reward you with new combat mechanics. Combat is a dynamic approach. Each run you select from different Olympian boons to affect your weapon of choice. Sword, Spear, Shield, Bow, Fists, and GUN. The weapons are unique in their approach to combat. The boons are randomized, but you have a limited ability to select whom will bless you. My personal favorite is Dionysus, but none of my friends see him as anything more than a drunk, sexy party god. Hades makes use of it's roguelike element by creating procedurally generated dungeons and boons each run. Hades keeps thing interesting past the end-game with HEAT, a mechanic that alters the game in ways of your choosing. Extra enemies, higher health, hitting harder? With each HEAT you succeed with, you unlock more to alter your weapons with. If you're the kind of masochist that enjoys DS3, Enter the Gungeon, or straight of MSDB (reverse that), you will find HEAT to be a good way to challenge yourself, and really show it to your friends how much HEAT you can handle.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game. I have over 500 hours on Binding of Isaac. 50 hours on Enter the Gungeon. 140 hours on Slay the Spire. The list goes on and on... 30 hours on Bastion also. This game does something truly unique. It has compelled me in a way that none of the other roguelike games ever have.  The story for this game is absolutely outstanding. The death/reset/randomization mechanics all have logical in-universe and plot relevant explanations. I don't know that I've heard a single repeated line of dialogue in the 50 hours I've played so far. The way in which you get granular control of the buffs you're likely to receive by categorizing specific playstyles into specific deities, then allowing you to favor those deities when aiming for a specific build and then allowing you to choose the debuffs you compete with while trying to clear the game. All of this customization really shines in a way that something like binding of isaac and many others simply cannot. There are also persistent upgrades to your overall character power via weapon mods/mirror upgrades. These continue to progress well past the 'end' of the game. If you are a fan of roguelike games in any capacity, you owe it to yourself to buy this game. Hades is to roguelike games what World of Warcraft was to MMO games (back in 2004). It's absolutely revolutionary, even though I don't know that it could ever possibly be even vaguely replicated. Supergiant games has absolutely amazed me. Even the hidden upgrades/lore points/new rooms/collectibles they throw at you 40+ hours deep are fantastic. Just buy this game already.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is an amazing game. The love and quality that has been poured into dialogues, items and the whole atmosphere is really astonishing and refreshing. _childDocuments_.review: So, after 100 hours of play, I can safely say this is one my MOST FAVORITE GAMES OF ALL TIME. Easily in my Top 5 list if I ever make one. There are definitely games out there where I'm like "It was fun, but it's still missing something for me." Hades is the complete package for me.1. Good Gameplay? Check.2. Great Narrative and Characters? Check.3. Godly Art Direction? Check.3. Amazing Darren Korb OST? Check.4. Outstanding art by Jen Zee? Check.5. A Price Tag that is far too low for its own good? Maybe, but I'd pay 60 for this game, honestly.Gameplay wise, it can get button-mashy and the screen does get cluttered, but damn if it doesn't feel good. It's not the best roguelike/roguelite gameplay loop out there (Risk of Rain 2 and Dead Cells give it some competition), but it's still above the average.One thing that Hades does have over other games in its genre is its narrative. Supergiant Games have always done a great job implementing a meaningful narrative within their gameplay, and this is probably the best they've done (although it can be argued that Pyre is their most ambitious). You have an incentive to win a run, but dying isn't all that bad. You go back, talk to your underworld colleagues, pet your dog, and mindlessly spend gems of interior design and among other things.There is a LOT of dialogue in this game. Like, so much even after 100 hours I'm still getting new ones (although the amount has diminished noticeably, but, I mean, that's after like 80-100 hours). I'm pretty sure 99.9% of the dialogue is voiced, and the voice acting is great, but apparently there are some annoyances with the accents. Doesn't bother me at all, though.The fact that this game is $25 (I bought EA, so it was $20) is a steal. And, as with many games, it may not be worth that to you. Still, for what you get, it's worth it. If there was an option above recommend, I would choose that.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, as always with Supergiant Games, the art style and soundtrack are enchanting~!The gameplay reminds me of RPG games with difficulty modes set to only one save file and if your character or party dies, your save file is erased. Here though, it's the norm. You lose money and skills upon death but you keep gems, keys and gifts to level up your stats, unlock a new weapon and interact with NPCs. It's VERY grindy, fair warning.I like one feature where weapons gain a boost (atk+20%) if you haven't used it for a few runs. This is refreshing cause you'd switch up equipment every run and it'll feel totally different. Then there's the changing corridors, so a map is not really a necessity. You just keep pushing on. I've not gone very far in the game but i'm having fun. Good replay value. Concerns:- With the many deaths possible in the game (intentional and unintentional), won't that exhaust the dialogue with the NPCs greeting the hero upon revival?- Other Supergiant games had Steam trading cards and achievements... I wonder if they'll add them anytime soon. And would any of those be unlocked through previous playthrough or would we need to redo a new game for those achievements... hmmm.Theories:- The Olympians are watching Zagreus' attempts to escape the underworld like it's some kind of sport and their boons are ways to liven up the entertainment. _childDocuments_.review: Roguelike games never appealed to me as a genre. I'd never imagine I find myself writing a review praising a roguelike game but Hades is definitely an exceptional masterpiece of an exception. Here's my Hades review as a player who's unfamiliar with roguelike.What drew me to buy Hades was not only the visual presentation but the deaths in the game being requirements for story progression. With that neat mechanic and the story being the protagonist Zagreus trying to escape Hades itself with his father's elements against him in search of something precious.As I started the game, naturally I didn't last long on my first few runs but the game didn't feel unfair or cruel even to me. Slowly I feel myself getting better and farther in the game, weapons and speedy controls were easy for me to get the hang of and the flow of going through many many fights were fun and felt so good.  I was never good at fast isometric fights but it felt naturally entertaining for me in Hades. Caution your hands and controller will ache and break.As advertised, when you die (intentionally or not, beginning or end of the trip) story and events happen and progress. Pieces of the main story is slowly revealed to you everytime you return back to the Hades Household. You bond with characters by talking to them, give them gifts and help complete their story subplots. The several different sources you collected during runs and boss fights can be used for upgrading weapons, upgrading Zag's stats for faster runs, add furnitures to the house, unlock music and unlock character requests. One of the best parts of the game are definitely the characters. Not only are they gorgeously drawn, they're very compelling, funny and fascinating each in their own way (your favorite is easily guaranteed). The voice acting are definitely the greatest I've heard in a long time like listening to characters on a stage play. Dialogues are plenty, characters will say something different everytime,  some made me laugh in shock and others made me tear from endearment.With Hades you definitely need to put in hours and hours of play time but it never drags, it's so fun to play and there's a lot of stuff to do and discover. The path from start to end is four floors ( a boss per floor) and for story progression you need to climb these floors many many times. Any other game I'd say NO WAY!!! and rage quit but with Hades I never felt that. The game never intended to be frustrating or discouraging.  There's an option to make the difficulty fairly playable and an option to make it really hard for your fun. I played for 100 hours and the game hasn't felt boring to me in the slightest.My only gripe with Hades is the economy. It's not just one currency, there's seven each one with it's own value and uses. Common ones are easy to gather plenty with time but more valuable resources take longer time to get either by winning one per boss kill or trading the lesser valuable resource for the higher value ones. Boss fights, fishing and trading help to an extent, but upgrades, gifts and purchases demand loads of the most valuable resources. I either to need to grind the game for 10,0000s of the common resource to trade up to the most valuable or fight the bosses several dozen times. Gathering the resources I need is the one thing that drags and feels exhausting to me. I finished the prologue before I could gather enough resources for what I need. I wish the developers could add more features to earn more resources like Shades making personal requests in exchange for rewards.Overall, Hades is really a fun gem of a video game and I had a lot of fun with it. I'm shocked that not only did I play a roguelike game, I finished it with all achievements unlocked. I don't think it will change my mind about roguelikes for now but I appreciate that I  played an exception. It's one of my favorite games of 2020 and maybe even one of my favorites in recent times. I definitely recommend it to anyone who has the slightest interest in roguelikes, in Greek mythology or even the game itself. It's worth every penny and definitely worth the 100+ hours of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Brutal, complex, furious, and incredibly human. Hades is an intriguing blend of persistent-growth rogue-like RPG with thrilling mechanics and a deep, compelling central story about familial loss, resentment, and the quiet failures of family. But above all, it's about how to put that family back together again.I had no idea what to expect from this game other than the quality and novelty Supergiant is now known for, but wow this game hooked me and won't let go. Structured in half-hour bursts of single-minded aggression and long beats of discussion, reflection, and relationship-building, this game is deep and broad in all of the best ways.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Isometric hack and slashes are SGG's stock in trade, and this one is polished to the high heavens. Phenomenal production values - sound, art, combat, story are all stellar. With that polish, I can't believe how fresh this game feels compared to the dozens of similar games I've played over the years, and there are enough systems that each run feels fresh and your choices very meaningful. See myself putting a lot of hours into this one. Also, regarding the Epic deal, SGG never pulled back from any promises, and were with the first wave of exclusives, before we all realized how Epic would affect the market. I'm very comfortable buying this game today, knowing it's a MUCH more refined and improved version than what would have been on sale a year ago. If you played and enjoyed any of SGG's games till now, this one is a must-buy!

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of rouge-likes, moderate to hard difficulty, and deep lore then I have to recommend this game to you.Pros:The main gameplay is amazing and very easy to pickup.The story is told to you gradually and is paced almost perfectly.I personally love the art style.The sound track is one of those few video game sound tracks that I listen to in my day to day.Also, and I think this should be noted, in a lot of games like this (Risk of Rain 2 for instance) once you've beat the game or played a few times it gets kind of stale seeing the same enemies. This game fixes the problem by having the boss fights change drastically as you progress through the story. Unlocking new moves abilities and sometimes even new bosses entirely. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a real Gem...A friend bought me this game as gift from my wishlist, and I like meh at first. Then I entered the game and started my first attempts. Take note, that I am not the type of player who usually enjoys games like these, with tough boss fights, were you die often and have to try several times untill you get it right... There is also no difficulty setting to make it easier than standard... later on you can make it harder for greater rewards but not easier :PIt takes time to get used to it, it takes time to unlock all 6 weapons and discover all God Boons provided and which are good to be used in conjuction with certain weapon and ofc your playstyle. It takes time to upgrade Zagreus skills, and unlock certain upgrades which make your life easier on the field of combat or gathering certain resources... It sure as hell takes time to upgrade merely 1/6 weapons for increased effect on the field. After a few ours of gameplay though I started to feel i was getting better at it and the upgrades really felt like they made a difference... In the end though it's all about skill, personal reflexes (believe me they can and will be trainned to perfection...) and clarity of mind...Meanwhile there are several NPCs in the game with whom you get to exchange a few sentenses per escape attempt which gives you a glimpse to their story and background. There is lots of humour in the game and a bit of drama on certain occasions or characters, which adds a nice touch to the whole Underworld setting.Suprising as this may seem there is a story, you get to unlock it slowly through every attempt of escaping, you begin to gather small pieces of a large puzzle and it feels like reading a slowburn novel.The music is so awesome, i literally never get tired of hearing the music tracks in each stage of the underworld, the music of the bosses is especially tense and gives you a feeling of dread at first but also determination. There are also a few musical pieces with vocals, which are magical to hear, and in a game really violent, fast paced and relentless this pieces are like water in the desert offering a much needed break from war...I started playing out of curiosity, then out of stubborness to make my first escape attempt complete and finally i found myself loving the game, the characters, the narrative, the relationship system, I even farm resources for pure cosmetic upgrades... I am currently attempting my 3rd successfull attempt in search of answers, still gathering those pieces of the puzzle I mentioned before :), while further upgrading the weapons at my disposal to reek havoc among Hades minions...This is a 5/5 game for me, I can't find anything that I would need more of this game. It has all that you need, granted you have patience and a strong determination to see it through!

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ this game is so good. Hades had been on my wishlist for ages but I had never got around to getting it or playing it. When I finally did, I instantaneously fell in love. It was a top 3 Roguelike for me within the first hour of play and now is arguably my favorite Roguelike. This game is probably a literal 10/10 for me, I think the lowest score I could give it if I wanted to be mean is a 9/10Pros:- God-tier art, every character looks absolutely phenomenal. The level design art, Boon designs, Keepsakes, etc, everything looks fantastic. Pretty much everyone is hot as hell- Super fluid combat, regardless if you're using a fast or slow weapon. No weapon feels bad to use once you get the hang of them- Absolutely amazing music, I've added several tracks to my Spotify playlist and listen to them on the regular- Super rich stories and characters. Everything feels natural and believable, even the stuff that doesn't get a ton of focus. There's no need for prior knowledge on the Greek Gods/Titan lore either, but general knowledge does enhance the experience I think. The characters are super fun and all feel unique and the dialogue in the game is top notch.- The literal BEST ascension system I have ever seen in a game. Choose your own difficulty as you climb the ranks of making the game harder to easily farm Titan Blood, Diamonds, and Ambrosia. Or don'! Heat is completely optional (unless you want to use Erebus gates, see certain dialogue, or 100% the game) so you never HAVE to use it to farm aforementioned mats (though it is MUCH faster).- Dusa- Romance! Completely optional but fun, small little things. Male and female option available, inclusion is nice. But you don't have to do it at all! Any option that says "the character won't mind" is actually true, so you never have to worry about ruining your connection with someone (romantic or otherwise)- Voice acting is SOOOOO good for every character. I actually feel bad if I accidentally cut someone off when they're speaking because I genuinely love the voice acting so much for every character.- Side "stories" are so fun, from the prophecies to the smaller things. I think certain characters and bosses getting more expanded on the more you fight them is so cool. I won't spoil anything, but it's so fun seeing these small changes grow over time giving a little bit more life and personality to each run as you grind the story or farm for mats. There's even unique dialogue for bosses depending on your Heat, lack thereof, or switching off and on it!- F I S H I N G. God I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love fishing in video games (but not actual fishing irl or games dedicated JUST to fishing like Bass Pro games which is weird)- Customizable (to a point) House of Hades. Some stuff are just upgrades to the interior's look, but there is some stuff you can switch around- God Mode. I don't really know what this is admittedly because I haven't used it, but it's a setting that apparently makes the game easier to beat for those that just want to enjoy the story. This is in pros despite my not having used it because I've heard positive things from friends who HAVE used it.- Stat checker (once unlocked) which allows you to check various things such as weapon usage, boon usage, and run stats (W or L, what weapon was used, run time, etc). Also a small stat screen at the end of a W run showing best times for each wep, # of wins for each wep, etc.- UI is absolutely amazing, I love how they have the stuff set up. Easy to see Boon icons, their rarity, and their level at a glance or you can open the full boon menu to see exactly what was what (in case you're learning or forgot). You can also check any active Heat Modifiers and Talents active for the run as well!- Skelly the literal training dummy who is a homie and who's soul purpose in life is to give you tips and let you wail on him so you can get comfortable with a weapon's moveset (and teaches you the moves) before you jump into a runNeutral:- Variety in combat is plentiful enough for me, though I know some people will find it bland. There's a total of 6 weapons, each with 4 aspects to them (that are all pretty unique). Then there's Keepsakes, but few of these will change combat. Then there's the Boons for each God. I've seen complaints about how only "certain Gods are worth using" but I gotta say I disagree ENTIRELY with this. Are some Gods boons better than others for certain slots or on certain weapons? Sure, but everything is still fun to use. For example, I've seen some people say Zeus's boons are among some of the worst for DPS (aside from a few passive boons) but his are some of my favorite to use, the only one of his major boons I dislike is his Thunder Dash. So you've got all the boons and then there's Legendary and Duo boons, but overall you'll probably see more or less the same boons (of which there is still a lot, but it's not like Isaac with over 700 items).- Side story completion can be a bit of a hassle, though imo it is worth it (which is why I listed them in pros as well). The side stories themselves are amazing, but completing some of them is what this is about. Completion can be simple, just fight X boss Y number of times. But some are more complicated, like talk to X and Y NPCs Z number of times, but you aren't guaranteed to see Y NPC every run (or even X realistically but that's not quite the same). One prophecy has you fight a side boss (and win twice in a row) but isn't available from the get go and the boss only spawns in certain spots and even if you find it, it's not a guaranteed fight. Finding certain Boons or items to purchase is also kind of up to RNG as well, I had one Boon that required a certain Talent equipped to find and when I found this out, it took me ~20 runs to find it (even with Boon reroll) and then I proceeded to find it for 5 runs in a row... That being said, this is neutral because this is only required for people who want to finish everything/100% the game and most of this stuff will be done by just playing the game enough.Cons:- This game shares the same flaw that Gunfire Reborn shares in that the game is scaled for roughly mid level Talents. This means the first couple runs will more than likely kick your ass, especially since you're just learning attack patterns, how boons really work, etc. You can refund Darkness invested in Talents though if you want (it costs 1 key) which means if you end up not liking a talent, you can get your stuff back though which is nice.- Theseus (but just Theseus, Asterius is a homie)

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun. Think League or Diablo combat but with a Dead Cells-like gameplay loop. The feeling of progression is real, all the while still making you feel badass. Not to mention, the characters are great along with their voice acting, and the story is great. You don't even feel too bad about dying, since it 1) progresses the story, and 2) lets you hear more voice lines from the great characters. I don't think that I've ever heard a single voice line repeated in my time playing this game. All in all, great game, worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: This "review" is not for general consumption. It's specifically targeted at any of the few remaining clones of myself out there that happen to have been lucky enough, firstly, to have escaped catastrophic misadventure and, secondly, find themselves with a few spare hours to fritter away playing a new Steam game.Clones! Do not waste your money on this game! It's a one-dimensional grind-fest with some sort of derivative story bolted on that you won't be bothered to either listen to or read. You're just too old and jaded for this sort of thing. I know that your memory probably isn't as sharp as it used to be, but you should recall that you've already played several games like this during the last 40 or more years and you don't really need to play another one. Instead, why not try to make a dent in that large (and growing) pile of unread political autobiographies and engineering manuals that are probably cluttering up your house and rapidly going out of date?
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot get over how much I love this game. + Excellence and care were poured into every nook and cranny from graphics, menus, sound effects, voice overs, writing, characterization. The list goes on. For characterization, as an example, Zeus talks like the type of rich and successful uncle who I would visit and for four hours straight, all he'll be talking about is himself. It sounds right and it's consistent.+ I have "rougelite" filtered out of my steam store because I don't like repetition. But Supergiant made Hades different in that every run is the same but they put in enough "newness" to make it not feel repetitive. Bite-sized servings of story, lore, added gameplay mechanics are served through different runs making me want to know what's next.+ The combat feels great and every weapon feels like a new game in itself. I would put here my favorite but it changes every few runs. A few weeks ago it was the shield. A few days ago it was the sword. The gun I once absolutely hated and was my longest run. I was convinced it was the worst weapon selection. Then I loved it and it was my fastest run by far then hated it again. Same with the fists. Who knows what I'll like and hate next?+ Even if I lose on a run, I never feel angry or frustrated in the same way that I did in Sekiro cause that game welcomed me by stomping on my face repeatedly... which I loved in a troubled love and hate abusive relationship way. The setting of Hades doesn't take itself too seriously and even losing a run feels like I'm moving forward. I'd say it's a difficult yet chill game if that even makes sense.+ In Supergiant we trust. Loved Bastion and Transistor. I didn't like Pyre but I can't deny how polished it is. Please continue making excellent games. Please don't sell to Ubisoft/ Bethesda/ Microsoft/ EA etc. Please. ----- As a parent, the only game time I have is after the kids are asleep. For the last two weeks and counting, I've been operating on 3-4 hours of sleep a day. It's probably not sustainable and I'll address it just after this other one more last really final final run.- As I mentioned above, while some people like rougelites, I really don't so Hades is an exception. There's a point though on it's veeeeeeerrrrryy long end game content that I felt like I was scraping the bottom of the barrel for slithers of story content. It made me feel frustrated and impatient as these story beats are usually after every 30-50 minute run (plus the non timed parts). My love for this game was turning into irritation so before my love for it dissolved completely, I opted to uninstall and decided that at that point 66+ hours in, I was completely, finally, and really done.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is honestly THE best single player game I have ever played. From Sound design to game mechanics this game really takes the cake. Subtle amounts of humor and by far the best dialogue in a game I have ever been in. Despite needing to run through the game multiple times in order to achieve the final and true ending the dialogue was always fresh and new. About the final ending. Its amazing. The song with the visuals and the credits rolling down was fantastic. The first game from SuperGiant I have ever played was transistor and the sound design as well as gameplay was incredible. _childDocuments_.review: It's an addicting Rogue like set in a realm of gods.  You are the son of Hades trying to escape Hell.  Along the way you meet other gods, earn upgrades, unlock weapons, and die.  Die many times, as is apt to happen in this type of game.  This game puts a nice twist on that mechanic and actually encourages you to repeat the levels.  Each weapon you unlock has their own way of fighting and as you unlock powerups for them it can require you to adapt to a new way of playing.  My first finish was with a weapon I would never have guessed it would be with powerups I didn't know existed.  This was on try number 37.  Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like, in some time, for the designers of this game to write a book on how they worked out the mechanics and progress triggers of this game. The way the NPCs make note of what's happening game-to-game shows that a LOT of intelligent design work went into how they want you to feel as you progress towards your ultimate goal.  This is a beautiful example of a nearly perfect Roguelike:- The combat is intense but consistently fair- Progression and the development of characters is perhaps the best I've ever seen in this genre- Even after a hundred hours, there is still the feeling of "what will I find next?"- The writing and voice work deserves awards. These are characters that behave as immortals would; with all of the time in the world to become more like themselves, the writing conveys their senses of purpose as well as their trappings and exposes lore at a consistent pace that seems utterly bottomless. I think many can see a bit of themselves in each lesser and greater god they encounter.The game itself, is beautiful. The art and music are profoundly fitting for the setting. There's a muse around that I simply hung around with so that my wife could learn her song on the guitar. This game is already worth more than twice the money I've paid for it, and it doesn't even have an ending yet.This is a rare entry in the top tier of Roguelikes along with Isaac and Enter the Gungeon. I -strongly- recommend playing the absolute hell out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is my highlight of 2020.First things first:Hades is a rougelike in which you, Zagreus, son of Hades, attempt to battle out of the underworld with the help of 6 different weapons at your disposal. You choose one and begin your jouney. It can't be changed during a run. You make your way through several chambers, with randomized enemies. which offer random rewards upon succesfull completion.Maybe THE most important reward are boons, granted by olympian gods.These give one skill of yours a specific effect. (i.e. Zeus can empower your normal or special attack with extra lightning damage)So, in the end, every run is kinda unique.Inbetween runs you reside in the Palace, which functions as a hub. There you can upgrade Zagreus and the Palaces interior. It exactly hits the sweet spot that a rougelike should. It's challenging, but not too hard. The first few runs, one wouldn't get that far. But as you absorb the mechanics and start to grasp the do's and dont's, the flow pulls you in. After finishing a run, even if unsuccesful, I feel way too motivated to NOT do another. I'd argue that this is hardest thing to do in an rl. For example: In Rouge Legacy i never bothered to do any of that and still managed to beat the game.With 6 different weapons, each offer a unique playstyle, the replayability is off the charts. Especially since each weapon has 4 aspects, with each giving you a twist on how to play it a tad different.The soundtrack and voiceacting are amazing and fit very well with the overall theme. Coupled with the artwork, the aesthetics of Hades went incredibly full circle.The story is really enjoyable. Even more so if you  already have a bit of interest and maybe some knowledge about Greek mythology. The new interpretation of the gods and heroes are refreshing and show that there are still more stories to tell.I can wholeheartedly say that this is the best rougelike i have played.

The characters are absolutely fantastic and also DAAAAMN are they all HOT AF.GOTY!!!Also you can pet Cerberus so easily a 13/10EDIT : Why everyone make peepee hard

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: yet another gaming masterpiece from Supergiant, but some may be put off by Early Access. And yes, you can pet Cerberus (alas, only one of his heads).The art style of Hades is the one Supergiant fans have come to know and love - an iconic isometric style with vivid colours, detailed backgrounds, and fantastic animations. Supergiant have nailed this style and absolutely deserve all the praise they get. Character designs are incredibly memorable and distinct and really emphasise the nature of the different gods within the game. As well as graphics, Supergiant games are also known for their iconic and beautiful soundtrack, and I'm happy to say fans will not be disappointed.As is obvious, the game revolves around Greek mythology. As well as Zagreus, the playable character, we have his father Hades and (most) of the other Olympians. These gods provide our character with various powerups (more on this later) and each act just as you would expect them to - Dionysus is a lazy SOB, Poseidon is the "cool" uncle, and Hermes always sounds like he's had a  too much coffee. The voice actors completely nail their respective characters, there is an abundance of chemistry between them and Zagreus, and there are genuinely funny lines of dialogue - Supergiant obviously pays their writing team as much as their art team. The story is not  much to write home about (hehe) but the groundwork is there and Zagreus' motives are clear - I expect more of the story to come in later patches as more content is added. Combat is simple. To start with, you have a basic and special attack, a magic ability, and a dash. But that's not a bad thing - after all, the complexity in roguelikes is not the amount of different moves, but rather the upgrades you get along the way and how they interact with each other. Upgrades come in the form of boons, powers bestowed to you by the Olympians representing their own element or powers, but you can have boons from as many different Olympians as you like. On top of that are a multitude of status effects certain powers can apply to enemies, upgrades that add abilities to your weapon for that run, the ability to call a god's name and harness some of their power... the list goes on. Add that to the variety of weapons you can get, and you have a very impressive and fun system that is still being expanded upon with more gods, more weapons, and more boons. The aim is, like all roguelikes, to beat a multitude of bosses before going on to face the final boss of the run. Die once and your progress is toast - it's back to Tartarus for you. After every run, you can use the "darkness" you gain in a magic mirror of sorts to give all sorts of boosts to your character, making subsequent runs easier - all this will be quite familiar to seasoned players of roguelikes. And the game makes no assumptions of neither your competency or idiocy - there isn't really a tutorial, which works in the game's favour and allows you to get straight into the action. You learn most of the game through , which seems to happen less and less with games that hold your hand far too much. Edit: had a look on the wiki to see if there was anything I missed.  At first, I couldn't possibly understand why the game had the dreaded Early Access tag. So many studios add the tag to get away with lazy development and sluggish update turnaround. However, you won't even realise the game is Early Access - that is, until you get to the admittedly early end. Beating the game only took me 5 hours and I wouldn't say I'm that good at roguelikes or hack-and-slash games. However, I definitely wouldn't say I'm done with this game. Far from it - there's so much more to do in terms of post-game content, maxing out Zagreus and the weapons with the different aspects. Once you beat the game, there's also the ability to do runs with negative modifiers to make things harder and get extra rewards, Furthermore, with 7 major content updates in one year, it's clear that development on the game is being completed at a breakneck pace and that your early access money won't be wasted.In short, Hades is an incredibly well polished game that already contains a lot content with much more to come. Fantastic visuals, a gorgeous soundtrack, incredibly satisfying combat, and great replayability make this a strong recommendation for anyone. 9/10.

The gameplay is fast paced, the abilities, load-outs and weapons make every run feel a little different, in that way the game gets exactly what it was aiming for. The story is interesting and captivating and draws you deeper in, as you progressively get stronger and stronger. I have had an absolute blast playing this game, and I would highly recommend it.  Probably my favourite skelly-em-up.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been PC gaming for the last 30 years, and I can tell you after this much time spent in the hobby my pickiness is pretty darn high. I'm generally not a huge roguelike fan, and was pulled into the Hades game by it's graphics and buzz but was initially pleasantly surprised by the gameplay and quality of the presentation.After taking some time off from my initial playing, I jumped back in while on vacation and boy am I glad that I did. The big things I love about this game:1) Replay value - huge, and a compelling narrative reason to do so.2) Greek mythology - a fun and educational way to learn about the ancient gods; I can pretty much rattle them off and their basic info after playing this game. At the very least, makes me sound quite a bit more cultured than I probably am!3) The mixing and matching and somewhat randomness of the boons makes for a unique playthrough each time and fun learning the pairings.4) Finally, I love the concept of escaping from Hades on a regular basis, to achieve a nearly impossible goal with no hope, even when you eventually win, of retaining or deeply enjoying the victory.. It's a great metaphor for life, the concept death and rebirth of the self and the journey being the real goal of the game.It's worth your time, for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 4/5Notes: Good game, but extremely overrated IMO.The biggest issue with the game is a lack of real gameplay variety, the different weapons and boons really don't alter gameplay all that much. Combat can feel very button mashy, though this can be more or less the case depending on your weapon. The 3rd and 4th boss fights are WAY too tanky and take ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ forever to kill even if you have a fairly powerful build, if you have a weaker build it can take ages. Long boss fights aren't always a problem, however they need to be interesting to fight. These bosses dont have nearly enough mechanics to justify their length. You need to learn 2-3 attack patterns max and then beating them is fairly simple, it just takes forever.Another major issue is the reward structure and difficulty curve. For reference I played on "Hell" difficulty to start. It took me about 20 runs before i completed my first escape, and then i proceeded to go on a 4 win streak using all different weapons. The game gets significantly easier once you max out a couple key upgrades. Now you might say "oh but there's more, you have to keep beating the game to fully experience everything". And you would be right, however, the progression in this game is gated in an extremely unfun way. Far too many things in this game require grinding for no reason. For example, there are many rewards locked behind beating the game at certain "heat" levels. However, the game forces you to very slowly incrementally progress through these stages rather than just letting you choose the difficulty you think you can handle and then rewarding you appropriately. So rather than just being able to skillfully playthrough the game at 20 heat and getting all previous heat level rewards. the game forces you to play through the entire game 1 heat at a time. Extremely obnoxious design.Overall, as far as action rogue games go, personally I would much rather play Dead Cells, Enter the Gungeon, or Monolith. And I would honestly recommend all 3 of those games over this if you are more interested in gameplay over presentation. This is still overall a great game, it could just be much better IMO.

Not in the sense that it became rogue-lite, we all now that gameplay in SGG's projects is still pretty similar: you customize the abilities of your character(s), you play as them and you can make it harder with some mechanic (multiple such mechanics in Hades). So what's different about Hades?I'm certain that the early access was very useful for the game, because the instant feedback about every little bit of gameplay is leading to SGG fixing every little annoying thing and slightly adjusting the feel of gameplay if it is needed.So what i'm trying to say. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, apologies in advance, but soapbox time. This game was robbed at the Game Awards, frankly it could and maybe should have won pretty much every category it was nominated for, but particularly Best Direction. How many other nominees in that list actually direct a team they expect to keep working with, using the very best talent at their disposal to pull together gameplay, design, writing, and music in such a delightful way? A studio that doesn't force its staff to work themselves ragged, or out of their family. But no, the award ended up going to a studio that did just that. What a shame.So, as for the game itself? It's probably one of the best games I've played this year, and my personal GOTY. It's not the game I've played the most, but then I wouldn't call it's genre my favourite. However, when I do play it, I enjoy it for most of the aspects explained in my rant above, and each one on it's own is a reason to pick the game up. The game is a roguelike/roguelite isometric hack-and-slash, I think? Your goal is to escape the Underworld, and it's mostly a story about family, and I'll leave it at that because the game does the reveal better than I would. When you die in your runs, you keep most of what you earn, and use it to improve in your next run, so there's always a constant progression. The game also has a "God Mode" that makes the game progressively easier for those struggling, making it a far more accessible title than similar games in the genre.There are a few aspects I think could be better. Progression relies on spending different resources on different things, but the game is a little stingy when it comes to handing them out, especially resources for more expensive things, but I gather this is partly to incentivise you to mix up your runs. It does, however, make the late game more of a slog than I'd like.Overall, I'd argue this game is a strong contender for GOTY, as well as any other awards that are up for grabs
