_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought this game I had thought, "I will only play this once." I could not be more wrong...There is endless replay value in this game. The endless combinations of abilities and skills make it interesting depending on what weapon you are using. In other games, normally people are afraid of dying, dying in Hades is part of how the game unravels. After you respawn back in the underworld, the other characters greet you by either insulting you for dying or others may support you for your heroic attempt to ascend to the top of the underworld. The dialogue interactions in this game suck you in--I cannot get enough of the voice acting, dialogue interactions, and how the dialogue NEVER repeats (after 28 hours of play at least). Depending on who you give gifts too, you can change the dialogue and reveal more story. (I haven't even gotten to the action yet!)The gameplay mechanics are fairly simple in my opinion--depending on which abilities you have, you will use different button combinations to make the most of your abilities. Since the most recent update, the devs have added so many great things as far as more enemies and better abilities. Not too say much about the visuals except that they are so entertaining for my eyes. All of the different visuals that happening with each ability always keeps my eyes engaged on the screen. There are only 3 or 4 areas, so you happen to see the same background (which really isn't a problem for me). Overall, I bought this game when it was on sale, but I would say this game is worth buying even at full price. I can see myself putting another 40-70 hours on this game because every time I play this game I thoroughly enjoy it. Lastly, once you beat the king of the underworld on a playthrough, the game literally opens up. There is this new feature that unlocks that makes the game even more interesting and difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: My playtime on Steam may be low, but I've played well over 100 hours of this game on EGS since its launch in early access, and it's one of the best games i've ever played. _childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of Supergiant Games, and Hades increases my love for their games. I've been around since the beta and have already put 50 hours into this game. You get to meet so many unique characters and help them out in their side quests apart from the main game. I love interacting with each one of them and learning about their personalities and backstories. If you liked any of Supergiant's past games, I highly recommend playing Hades.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art style and the world building in this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is GREAT. Very fun dungeon crawler. There are 6 different weapons so there's a play style for everyone. _childDocuments_.review: Hello! It has been a while since I have posted a review but this one is worth writing about.I've been a fan of Supergiant games from the get-go because they never fail to disappoint. Each game they have come out with has a different gameplay / thus caters to different styles of gamers.  But as far as I have seen, they always deliver a flawless product. A huge fan of "Bastion" and "Transistor" -- "Hades" is amazing.. but again, it depends if this is your type of game.With that said, my comments on Hades:                 -  Story! <3  Based on Greek Mythology. You play one of the sons of Hades (Zagreus) who wants to get out of "Hell".  You defy your father and try to  leave it even if he tells you it is impossible. Along the line of your escape from "Hell" for reasons which I shall not spoil, you get to encounter other Greek mythological Gods and creatures.. who help you along the way or not.. so if you're into the mythology, that is a very big bonus.                  - Game-play! <3  It is rogue-like.  You clear a room of mobs, you go to the next room.  ;)  Along the way, random different Gods and Goddesses give you an upgrade out of 3 choices. The choice you make will customize your gameplay and what you can do throughout that run which makes it a unique experience every time. However, be prepared to die. You *will* "die" over and over and over and get sent back to Hell - But, the kicker is that you can upgrade your skills based on what you have done on each run after you "died".  That idea is philosophical to me - like in life; we make mistakes, but are rewarded by learning from them and come back better / stronger and try again.  Perseverance! ;) ! We can upgrade our character in several ways by unlocking new weapons or changing specific beneficial traits on ourselves or on the weapons over time as we collect gems and so on.       - Personal Experience! <3 * Visuals - It is beautiful - there are so many intricate artistic details that I notice every time. Breathless!* Sounds - The soundtrack by Darren Korb is always impressively done. The soundtrack is worth it.  The voice actors are well-chosen, including Darren Korb himself as the main protagonist's voice (which I can not get enough of, sorry~ just so cool!).* Performance - For my specs, this game runs smoothly in my rig. However, I am not sure but  I personally recommend a Keyboard + Mouse combo because of the accurate aiming which is very important in this game rather than a gamepad - but that is up to the weapon and it is up to you.                  ~~~~All in all: The various weapon choices and weapon upgrades make it so much fun! I went from being frustrated at first from dying to compelled to keep on playing due to how endless and very interesting their upgrading system is.. and now.. I am completely addicted since I've grasped it and feel like a boss!  Haha. There are so many things to unlock and so many combinations that *it always feels fresh*. I highly recommend it.  I truthfully have nothing bad to say about this game and it is a BONUS if you love Greek mythology.It is a masterpiece in my mind - but whether or not it is your thing is up to you!My two cents and I hope it helps! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I want everybody I know to experience this game. I have purchased this game a total of 7 times now including both on Steam and Switch and I expect that number to continue to increase as I share this absolute gift of a game with every friend that mentions it.I HATE rogue-likes I hate losing progress and doing the same thing over and over with no satisfying progression so consider that when I say that Hades is currently my FAVORITE game. If you need more reasons to buy this game I'll try and elaborate on some of my reasons for enjoying this experience so much.1. The CastYou can see the visuals and amazing soundtrack in the store videos but what you can't see is the story and characterization of these myths. Every character in this game feels wonderful to talk with! Your relationships develop as you learn more about this interpretation of Greek mythology and what is going on in the world. The design decisions for characters are clever, fitting, and meeting cast members is exciting.A run ending the violent way is always a quick sting of sadness that is quickly soothed by a new portion of dialogue to explore for the characters waiting for me at the beginning, it's almost like the game's way of putting little band-aids over your wounds and hyping you back up to try your best once more. I've never quit this game out of frustration or anger because the game feels like it wants me to succeed as much as I do.2. Rogue-Lite not Rogue-LikeThere are multiple currencies that persist throughout runs and allow you to upgrade different aspects of your character. Builds in this game are very versatile and almost everything feels wonderful and useful. I only say "almost" because a certain character has useless garbage he uses to ruin my runs! Thank you Ares, keep your trash to yourself next time.3. Skill Progression and ExpressionIf you are worried about the game being too difficult, there is a mode to reduce incoming damage and the reduction ramps up if you need it so you will always be able to experience the full story. The basic mechanics are simple and attacks flow together smoothly with most animations able to end early or buffer another attack/dash.If you are worried about the game being too easy, you are wrong. Hades has a ramping difficulty system where you can practice and crank up the Heat as you get better and better at the game. This gives you a feeling of infinite skill expression where your ceiling is as high as you can stand it.TLDR; The game's controls are very fluid and flow into one another in the way you would expect from a fast paced action game. The characters are engaging, funny, and feel like they are encouraging you to do your best. The progression system is balanced for players of all skills and give runs an additional feeling of reward even if they end badly. This is a game that the developers cared about and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant Games have a certain artsy feel to them. Incredible production values as well as very particular art direction. Bastion and Transistor are mostly beloved for their narration, visuals, music... What about gameplay? I always thought the fell a little flat. Hades... doesn't fall flat. Hades soars through the sky, like Daedalus escaping the Labyrinth of Crete. The gameplay is very finely crafted. There's a lot of fun stuff, many equally valid build options, different weapons which all play and feel unique - and to make things better, the game actually switches things around as you go as to keep things fresh, so you can't even be fully sure of how exactly the run will go. I'll leave it at that, the surprises are one of the more lovable parts of the game. Let's just say the game gives you plenty of incentives to splice things up a bit - and you'll gladly accept them, like Theseus accepted Ariadne's thread.If you watch the trailer, you'll notice the gameplay is incredibly fast-paced. Too fast you might think. But no, the actual game is EVEN FASTER - and it somehow manages to be that fast without the feeling of loss of control. You're always aware of what's going on, your actions calculated and precise, cutting through the underworld like Achilles at the battle of Troy... once you understand the workings of things, which I admit, takes some time. It's easy enough to pick up, though, so don't worry about that. It will all come naturally.So the gameplay is great, amazing even. As a roguelike + roguelite affectionado, I'll say it's up there with Dead Cells, maybe even better. But it somehow manages to spice things up even more with its incredibly charming world and characters. I mean, it's Supergiant Games' take on the greek myths, what did you expect?You play as Zagreus, a son of Hades, who wants to leave the underworld - and dies over and over trying. After every run, you get to talk to the inhabitants of the House of Hades - your fantasticly disfunctional family and their entourage - who comment on your exploits. You banter with beaten bosses, old teachers, mythological characters, all with wonderful characterisation. Same of course goes for the Pantheon of greek gods. If you thought Disney's Hercules did that well, check this out. It's a lot less silly while still being charming and humorous. Poseidon as the cheeky uncle is probably my favourite.It's easy to get lost in this exhilarating adventure, with every victory granting great satisfaction. If nothing else, grab this over the holiday season, and enter the underworld like Orpheus once did! (ok, not quite, that story went TOTALLY different)TL:DR: Incredible gameplay, amazing world. P.S. Aphrodyte is hot and Theseus makes me want to punch his face.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping I can write this review after I aced all the achievements, but I guess I just can't wait. My overall experience has been wonderful. A big RECOMMEND for almost anyone. It is hard to even pick any drawbacks -- surely you may argue you do not like things like the game mechanics and stuff, but that is not the game's fault. For what this game presents, it is a masterpiece. There are many aspects to admire for this game. Wonderful artwork and soundtracks, amazing adaptation of the Greek mythology. As a big fan of history and mythologies, Hades presents its own take of those ancient stories, and did a rather great job. The dialogue system is also surprisingly large and complicated. Quest lines and main story are seamlessly forged together, creating a coherent experience. Not to mention all dialogues have fantastic voice acting, I can never imagine any game does that until I played Hades. What is also amazing is how much you can do in this game. Some developments, if you did not straightly look up online, are so deep that it is beyond imagination. The game always introduces you new concepts and mechanics just before you are about to get tired. The game itself was not crazy hard to me. While you may experience hard battles on first encounter, they become pretty manageable as you progress. The combats are also good in my opinion, varies boons offers you cool abilities. You may feel like the god themselves if you are lucky enough to build up some powerful combinations. What is even better is there is character developments throughout the game. I particularly like this part because I feel like I grew up in a family that shares a lot of common aspects as the Hades family, and my experience makes me realize how realistic those characters grew in this game. Those designs really showed how much effort the developer has put into this game. Of course no game is perfect. The gigantic dialogue system makes a lot of the triggerings buggy, it may also feel out of place somehow because quest lines tangents with each other sometimes. It is also frustrated when you want to complete some requirements yet a lot of them are very resource demanding. The game runs are also a bit repetitive, I am not sure everyone won't get bored before they completes the game. Another small drawback is, the achievement system is very generous, which means it does not award you on some difficult achievements such as beating third stage of final boss, or other doable stuff in game. I usually hang those very hard to get achievements on my profile, but for Hades all I can find that is worth showing is epilogue. In summary, I RECOMMEND this game. It is one of my favorite game of all time, I would give 5/5 for almost any aspects you can think of.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings as I hope all is well! Below is my Steam Review for Hades, thanks for reading as I wish you well in all your gaming adventures...STORY/LORE - 7/10The story behind Hades is a decent one but definitely gets confusing the more you play. For a game called Hades, I did enjoy to a degree playing as Zagreus, his son, and having to go through various dungeons to escape Hell to find the truth about his family. It’s definitely unique but after a while and after constantly dying as you do your best to improve your stats, the story just didn’t hold up for me.I did enjoy the lore, hence why I gave it a 7/10 since anything to do with Hades and all these legendary stories of gods have always interested me. But in Hades, it did feel a bit flat, especially after you finally beat the game once, you literally have to invest a ton of hours to get the final ending that involves all the main characters. This was definitely a major turn-off for me as it’s just not worth investing hundreds of hours in just for the story through a grindfest of a game. This leads me to my next point…GAMEPLAY - 7/10Just like other Supergiant Games, the gameplay in Hades is good but definitely gets to the point where you’re just mindlessly bashing your keyboard to get through levels. It’s basically a button masher of clearing waves and waves of enemies, the same handful of bosses, and hoping you get the right random abilities, buffs, and special powers to make it all the way to kill Hades to clear it. It’s fun at first but Hades is extremely grindy and over time, starts to get very annoying with cheesy enemies and traps that will frustrate you beyond belief.This game will literally take probably a 100 if not more clears from start to finish to unlock all the weapons, abilities for these weapons, character abilities, trinkets, and much more to add more of a variety in gameplay. If you enjoy grinds like this in an action roguelike video game, you’ll undoubtedly enjoy Hades but after so many attempts and finally killing Hades once and for all, it got beyond boring. It got to the point where I just wanted to finish this game to get my “Is There No Escape?” Steam Achievement and move on already from this game.GRAPHICS - 8/10The graphics in Hades are good, cartoony, and fit the theme well. These aren’t groundbreaking graphics or anything but I thought the graphics definitely shined throughout the game. The levels are unique and look great but after you see these same main areas, over and over again, the repetitiveness definitely gets to you. The graphics do hold up but the thing is, when you’re facing constant enemies and bosses over and over again, where you have a whole bunch on the screen, it can get a bit hectic and cluttered. Way too much going on as the anxiety creeps in for losing health and/or lives just to clear encounters. This is because the majority of the time, you’ll be dashing, hitting, avoiding traps, and dodging projectiles pretty much all the time. The deeper you get into your escape run, it can get very wild, to say the least. Again, this was fun at first but once you hit your tenth, twentieth, even fiftieth attempt, it becomes just mind-numbing button mashing as there’s a lot of things going on graphically on your screen at any given time.SOUNDTRACK - 7/10Compared to other Supergiant Games in Bastion, Transistor, and Pyre, I felt the soundtrack in Hades was underwhelming. I heard two songs at most that were amazing and the rest felt rather generic and unlike the amazing soundtracks I’ve heard before in their previous video games.The music for the most part was alright while going through the game but I definitely expected more at least for boss fights and the buildup to finally facing Hades. I also felt the music was more for background noise as you grind and not anything to really chime in this is for Hades as I felt before for Bastion, Transistor, and Pyre.MULTIPLAYER - N/AThere is no multiplayer aspect at all in Hades which I felt was a shame. This would have been a perfect co-op game at least to have that as an option considering all the characters and bosses you go up against. Imagine being able to play as either Zagreus or any of the gods you with a friend?I felt that would have been a nice addition to the game considering it could have made for a fun co-op game with the ability to unlock all these characters, weapons, and abilities with a friend. If it’s going to take so many hours and attempts to get all the Steam Achievements, it would have been infinitely more fun to do it in a co-op experience right from the start. I don’t think a 1v1 PvP mode or anything would have made sense here but a fun co-op PvE experience with this system could have bumped up my final score of Hades.  FINAL SCORE - 7/10Overall, I give Hades a 7/10 for being a bit underwhelming, grindy, and a button-mashing extravaganza the deeper I got into it. Don’t get me wrong, I genuinely enjoyed playing Hades for the first time as the first 5 or so hours had me excited to see what the hype was. Unfortunately, I felt Bastion, Transistor, and even Pyre were all better games than Hades.I know a lot of gamers praise Hades beyond belief for being such a great game but to be honest, this was a letdown to me. I was expecting a lot more from Supergiant Games considering their previous successes and how much I absolutely loved their previous titles but this just didn’t do it for me. I feel once you play this game 10 or so times and constantly keep dying only to slowly improve your stats, be prepared to feel the grind and get bored. Yeah, the levels do have random events, enemies, and powerups as you play but even then, it does become a chore in the grand scheme of things. It’s okay though, I did enjoy Hades to a degree, was glad to finally play it and at least get one full clear. I am still a huge fan of anything Supergiant Games does in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest: I hate this game. It completely destroyed my nerves and any will to play it, but It’s one of the very few ones with each new furious butthurt made my desire to finish it only stronger. I did it because of the story and in the end when I finally reached the goal... it gave me another huge butthurt because - this long journey wasn’t worth it. So now you know that for me that game is a failure and 100+ wasted hours. But does it mean that it is bad? Well, not at all.First of all, if you are a fan of Dark-Souls-like games, rogue-likes, or both - this is a must-have! The game will give you tons of content and you would be able to enjoy it for 200+ hours or even more (and if the base game will seem too easy you can start with hardcore mode). You have 6 different weapons with different modifications to wield, about 30 talismans to equip, 15 skills to master, and much much more. The game is a masterpiece of a rogue-like because it has all the best aspects of this genre combined: you have both permanent and one-run progression, you have a decent randomness which makes each run unique and, which is just insane, a fully-fledged finished story with a quality voiceover. I can’t even imagine how many lines were written by the devs and how many hours actors spent in the studio. More than that, the game is a true masterpiece of an early access project and should be an example for all other developers: the team really improved the game over time, listened to the fans, and delivered the finished product. And reading all this you might ask how can I glorify the game so much, but frankly hating it. Well, firstly, despite the devs sincere attempts to make Hades their best game during early access (and, frankly, they achieved their goal), it doesn’t mean the game is perfect. Though the random makes every run different, it also can make you fail just because of a bad seed (and you also don’t have a “reset” button aka “change seed” button, so you have to wait for the mobs to kill you every time you want to reset seed). Also, the bosses and mobs are not that very diverse and even if you play on hard you will certainly get tired of them after a good amount of time. This applies to the locations and music too: they are good, but surely become repetitive after 40-50 hours of runs. But the really hurting problem is grind: you have to grind the game over and over if you want to unlock all the content, and game randomness only enhances this drawback, sometimes making you restart 3-4 times only to get the needed location\dialogue\item.To be objective, I must note that later the game tweaks random so you progress through the story faster and increases the amounts of resources, but that’s still not enough to fully unlock everything. But despite all these drawbacks, the game is still good and you get used to them after some time, so why I was so enraged in the first paragraph? Well, these were mere problems compared to the main one for me: the story. No, it’s not bad, it’s nice, and the fact that it is in the rogue-like game makes it even better. But playing the game only for it - it doesn’t worth it, because you certainly will be disappointed. And get lots of butthurts because... to reach the true ending you have to do nearly 100% in the game. And the game’s difficulty is quite high and even if you played some hardcore games before you will still have problems with Hades for the first 40-50 hours, let alone those who play games for the story only (even the “easiest difficulty” which the game calls god mode doesn’t really improve the situation). So, when you finally finish all challenges and hope to get an epic ending all you receive is... one cutscene and weak finale. Initially, I considered that the story is poorly-written but actually, it’s not, it’s on the same level as in the previous games. but if in previous games the story, gameplay, and music merged together creating an unforgettable journey, here this can’t be achieved just because of the game’s nature. So, you either enjoy the gameplay and the story is a cherry on top, or you don’t like the gameplay, and completing the story is an ordeal. So, what’s the verdict? If you like hardcore games that challenge you or a fan of rogue-likes - take it, you won't hesitate a moment. If you are just a fan of SG and ready for a hard 100+ hours semi-repetitive rogue-like - you can try it. If you value the games for their story, don’t like rogue-likes, not a fan of repetitive gameplay, or not ready for a hardcore experience - avoid it at all costs. I am, personally, not a fan of rogue-likes, but I love all previous SG games and in some reviews people, who also weren’t fans of the genre. indicated that they loved the game, so I decided to try it too. So, for me: Bastion, Transistor, Pyre - holy trinity, Hades - a great game but for a very specific audience.

_childDocuments_.review: After having heard so much about Hades, I finally decided to give it a go - and all I can say is that I wish I picked it up earlier. This game is a masterpiece. From the main menu when the incredible music comes on to the first time you die and re-emerge in the Hall of Hades, you know immediately that you're in for a ride.Hades feels very polished. The graphics are stunning; I find myself spending minutes just looking at the details in each room throughout the world whether it be Tartarus or Elysium, among others. And the action... the action feels so thrilling and rewarding. Clearing rooms and bosses with just one health left is some of the most fulfilling gameplay I've had in a long time. Fighting and gameplay just feel really good.I can't wait to continue my journey in the Underworld. I rate Hades 10/10 and recommend this game to anyone looking for a pristine action game set in a cool, engaging world.

_childDocuments_.review: I lov this game.Its the most addicting rouge lite I've played before. The plot creates a strong motivation to keep playing. The story is great. While some characters were a bit on the nose, they are very endearing overall.That said, I would recommend that you put the game down after reaching the first ending because after that point, the story slows down to a crawl. The missions become grinds for rare materials, the flaws in the combat system become painfully apparent, and the strategy is reduced to spamming dodge and attack. This gets old. There is no space for skillful combat when the tiny level is flooded with armored enemies and traps. I still find the boss fights to be challenging and fun. But the rest of the game became frustrating.I'm fairly close to the epilogue, but I won't be completing the game. It has become a time-consuming chore.This game brought some great innovation to the table with the story-line, characters, and voice acting. But it falls behind other titles in terms of combat. It is definitely worth the money. But don't expect to be hooked on this game for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 Review .Pros :Great story and story telling with astonishing amount of dialogues and quotes all voice acted.(25+hrs purely to finish main story)Smooth gameplay with no performance issues.Gameplay varies alot due to weapons,weapon aspects and boon combination.(Among the other things i dont wanna spoil)Replayability enjoyable due to the gameplay systems this game has.Very likable characters insipired by greek mythology.(Voice acting very on point aswell in my opinion.)Alot of attention to detail.I know great ost is reccuring theme for Supergiant games but this one blew me away specialy.Cons:Enemy and location variety is decent but nothing to brag about.Some minor balance issues but they are still updating the game often and working on it.To some people the amount of dialogues even tho skipable can be distracting from the gameplay.The good old one more run syndrome can have u stay up way later than u should.My overall thoughts : The game has amazing action gameplay while still maintaining storytelling better than many triple A titles .Its hard to put the game down and even in early acces i spend over 40hours on this game without even realising and while enjoying every bit of it.I should mention Hades while fairly punishing also has easy mode for people who are purely interested in story and or aint the best at this kinds of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Rewrote certain chunks of text for better readability and for better overall lookI honestly can't recommend playing this game if you find gameplay in games to be a very important aspect. Don't get me wrong, this game has an amazing story, cool characters, great lore, ton of content, beautiful stylized graphics... but gameplay itself is honestly very basic and bad, and as somebody who finds gameplay to be the most important part of games, I feel compelled to talk about it. While the combat itself is not awful, per se, it's just not good enough to make me even want to actually play this game, much less To put it simply, the base gameplay loop is just a lot of button mashing. The most prevalent strategy is to spam dash and attack. You may say "Just don't". However, in this game,  enemies are quite tanky, so it feels like you're putting yourself at a disadvantage by not using this tactic (because it helps that much). Sure, there are different weapons and playstyles, and god's gifts that add some flavor to the gameplay, but that feeling that all you're doing is button mashing never goes away. The only weapon that I found to be unique is Bow (and supposedly a Gun, but I haven't grinded to it yet) in the fact that, well, it's a bow, and you have to charge it before each shot. However it still relies heavily on button mashing.I have few issues with gameplay itself as well. There are few. Firstly, why does your character completely stops when attacking? In a game that is so fast paced, it makes combat feel rather awkward, and only facilitates supremacy of "dash and attacks mashing" tactic. This is such a small thing, that when added to other can lead to bigger frustrations. Call this a nitpick, but to me this feels like a small issue, that, like a broken immunity in a living organism, when present makes other issues worse. The other issue is that It's really hard to see anything. While the game is pretty, everything is just so flashy that most of the time you take damage, you don't even know what hit you. Adding this to whole spam thing, and you can take whole lot of damage from seemingly out of nowhere.And, if I'm being honest, the biggest issue for me is that this whole button mashing deal just makes my hands tired (and head, because it feels like you constantly have to move), which is probably my biggest issue with combat.Technically, you can unlock weapon aspects, which supposedly do add quite a bit of weapon variety (and are kind of cool, not gonna lie), but you need to do quite a bit of grinding to unlock even one for a single weapon, which brings me to another issue I have with these game.The game is very grindy, not only when it comes to stats, but also with its story. Let me explain. Everytime you die, there's always at least one NPC that has new things to say to you. Which is great in a sense that there's always something that makes your death worth it, and if you are as fascinated in ancient mythology in media as I am, you're gonna have a blast. However, the issue is that you get those story moments and character interactions in such tiny drops, that it leaves you wanting more, which combined with the gameplay issues I mentioned previously, only makes me frustrated because if I want to learn more of a story I have to engage with the systems, which makes me hesitant to even play in the first place because of the same gameplay issues. To put it simply, you can't escape the gameplay if you only care about the story. This paragraph is more of a response to some people who claim that "who cares about gameplay, if the story is good". I mean, sure, if that works for you, but why would I bother playing  if I don't want to engage in gameplay? What stops me from just watching some playthroughs on youtube, and not bothering with anything else? Just some food for thoughtsAnyway, there are few other small issues, which I just want to point out are not necessarily good, nor bad. Certain base elements that don't unlock until awhile in your game. While this specific example doesn't affect the game much, there are other similar base elements that are hidden behind play time, like, for example, character stats, which you can upgrade to become stronger and get higher chance of finishing the run. Which is not a bad thing, but they add to the overall grind, and make you feel like the game doesn't want you to be able to finish the game until you upgrade those enoughAgain, I just want to be clear, I don't think those design decisions are simply bad and need to be removed or anything, but I just want to give different perspective on why these aspects are not as simple as they might seem.The last issue I have with this game is absolute lack of accessibility options. This is bad. This game has God Mode, which increases your damage reduction by 20% when activated, and this number increases by 2% every time you die, up to 80%. This is it. This is better than nothing, of course, but where's everything else? There's no colorblindness options, no hold button to continuously attack button, or even basic text size increase. Nothing. With recent leaps in accessibility it's really hard to excuse this lack of anything in a modern game. For how much deserved criticism Last Of Us 2 got, its accessibility options are fantastic. Even Dead Cells, game sharing similar niche, recently got a fantastic update adding ton of good accessibility options. This is not even a nitpick. You know how you can fix not seeing anything while in combat? Add outlines to everything, and allow us to customize them. Accessibility options are useful even to regular players. The lack of those in this game is just puzzling.Anyway, here's my review of issues this game has, which I couldn't not mention. I probably need to add this last paragraph to all my reviews, but I don't like redundancy, so it will stay here.In case this review gets picked up by some steam algorithms or whatever, or some youtuber makes one of those dumb "reacting to negative reviews" videos, let me tell you this: The reason why any game should be suggested to criticism is because no work of human can reach perfect state, yet it does't mean we should stop trying. Any game has flaws, and the way each developers tries to perfect their product is what I find fascinating in this industry. Of course, in the recent years games have become more of a source of income, business, so to say, yet games are still an art form, and most developers do try to make a great game, which is why these sort of critiques are important, I think: To show the way these games can be improved. Frankly, I can't say that I have any authority to say that this review is anything more than just my opinion, and if it will resonate with anyone, but I still found it in me to write it, since I find the discussion itself to be most important part of these, since it generates different views from different perspectives, and damn me if those discussions aren't great to be a part of. People who are the most negative usually are the ones who care about the game the most. If I didn't care, I would drop this game and forget about it. Yet here I am.Thank you for finishing reading this reviews of somebody who just has too much free time, and sorry for having to suffer through all the rambling

_childDocuments_.review: I always felt intimidated by rogue-like games. The fact that I can die and go all the way back to the beginning after hours of progress makes me feel like I'm not making any progress in the game at all. I know there are certain standouts like Enter the Gungeon and Dead Cells, and that's the draw of the genre: mastering the game as you go along. That's just my experience with the genre and I know there are many people who are drawn to these games more than me.With that out of the way, I think Hades is my personal Game of the Year for 2020. I know Cyberpunk 2077 is coming in December but who knows, could be delayed. This game has such a level of polish and care for every single aspect of its design from gameplay to writing and more! It also just feels less consequential to me than other rogue-likes because of how every time you die, you can actually upgrade most of your stats at home so the game becomes easier the further it goes. And once you beat one run, they introduce the Pact of Punishment, a highly detailed difficulty editor that makes the game more exciting and harder with the intrigue of more rewards. I just...don't have any major flaws to talk about with this game at all!The game is just magnificent to play. Controlling Zagreus feels so fluid and badass and there are hardly times where I had difficulty with what I wanted to do in the game. No death feels like BS you couldn't do anything about since all the enemies and bosses have clearly telegraphed attacks and variety in character design that it's easy to tell them apart. Your basic moveset is already fun but there are so many added layers to the combat such as a variety of weapons with different aspects to level up, keepsakes with passive effects, and an ENORMOUS catalog of Boons from various gods that you can randomly obtain throughout your run. These all give the gameplay a huge amount of depth that increases its replayability tenfold even after you get the true ending.So the game is fun AF to play and that would have been enough of a selling point that would get the game good reception but they go LEAGUES further to make such a complete experience that I could play for a very long time. Going in, I was expecting a rogue-like with a Greek mythology set-up that was just you trying to leave the Underworld and your father Hades with the help of the gods of Olympus. I was not expecting what would probably be one of the most endearing and fantastic character casts of any game I've ever played, and there are a crapton of characters that you can progress through their separate storylines with. All of these thousands of interactions have fully voiced dialogue which is just baffling and amazing. I love Sisyphus, Achilles, Cerberus, Hades, Nyx, Megaera, Orpheus, Eurydice, Thanatos and everyone else in this game (except for Theseus). The fact that all of their lore from Greek Mythology was taken into account fully when writing these characters is so commendable! The story also gets deeper as keep beating the game and develop your relationship with Lord Hades and everyone else. I won't go further. You must see for yourself.I don't even know what genre the soundtrack fits into! I would say "orchestral rock"? Darren Korb, who is the composer for the OST, the singing voice for Orpheus, AND the voice actor for Zagreus, is so talented and so is everyone else at Supergiant Games who worked on this masterpiece. The soundtrack just takes you places in battle, story moments and more. I haven't heard anything like it before. One of the tracks even has the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DOOM main theme incorporated into it and I just find that funny.Lastly, the art of this game just speaks for itself. Look at the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game! All of the chambers you fight in throughout the game are just gorgeously hand-drawn and the character portraits are ROBUST! Ungodly perfection, I say! The visuals just have such a unique and intriguing style that is constant with Supergiant Games.I could go on and on, but I think I talked enough. This game is just perfect and outstanding in every regard! It has earned a spot alongside Hollow Knight, Breath of the Wild and Persona 5 as my favorite games of all time. This game just perfects the rogue-like genre in my eyes. Now, in the name of Hades, I invoke you buy this game and I guarantee you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Literally the best rogue-lite game I've ever played. It doesn't feel like a grueling grind or anything like that that happens with other games. Every run has something new for you, be it story or new abilities or new challenges/bosses/enemies. And the game's story DOES have an end, which you earn from beating runs enough times and talking to characters. and you still would want to play after that story is "done." It's ridiculous I got this for $20 (20% sale on release). I would have paid $60, though I'm glad Supergiant is so generous to its fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: It takes some time until Hades introduces you to all its key mechanics and starts to challenge you for real, but once it does, you're in for one of the most satisfying roguelikes to date. There's amazing variety within different runs thanks to the introduction of new enemies and bosses as you revisit each biome. It's also impressive how there are always new dialogs to find, and the voice acting is top-notch.That's, of course, not to mention Supergiant's usual breathtaking art style, soundtrack, and storytelling. Combining Pyre's branching narrative style with roguelike gameplay was such a good idea. The game is securely a good inspiration for future titles of the genre. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Bastion and enjoyed Transistor and Pyre, and also have a knack for rogue-lites like Enter the Gungeon so this game really ticked all my boxes. I'm only 8hrs in right now but I love it, it has all the great elements of a rogue-lite with a zany mythological story and crazy builds you can make with many different weapons. Devs are transparent, active and update the game often; adding loads of content while the game progresses through early access.My only complaint is that I would play this more on Nintendo Switch, so I'll probably rebuy it whenever it's finally released on that platform (there's no announcements for that yet, by the way - but Supergiant has released on Switch before, they just take their time).If you like rogue-lites this game is for you, if you liked Supergiants other games this game is for you, no need to be on the fence about it - it's a great game for 25 schmekles.

_childDocuments_.review: Undoubtedly my GoTY for 2020, and a game that was much better than I ever could've expectedTL;DR Fantastic gameplay, best story/gameplay integration in any game of its genre and a constant dripfeed of both story and gameplay content that keeps you wanting to play more even after dozens of hoursI was initially interested in this game due to the wonderful looking art style and the interesting premise. Getting into it, I knew near nothing about it aside from those two things, and man was that ever a good ideaHades is a roguelike (or more specifically a roguelite), meaning your progress in your run is erased once you die, but you get to keep some permanent unlocks between every run. I'm establishing this just because, due to the nature of a game where you keep dying and starting over, story is usually pushed to the side in favor of gameplay, but not in HadesThe story is integrated so much into the gameplay and the roguelike elements that I cannot imagine one without the other. The dialogue reacts to your exploits between each run, and every run unlocks more and more of the story, to the point where I'm 40 hours in and I'm still discovering a lot of new story contentAvoiding spoilers, the story itself is pretty good, but it would be nothing without the incredibly charming characters and dialogue. Hades takes the gods of Greek mythos and turns them into my favourite renditions of them I've seen, they're all bursting with character and have wonderful interactions with each other to the point where I can't imagine the mythological figures themselves without also thinking of their renditions from HadesThe story overall might be great, but gameplay is still where this game shines, and it REALLY shines. It's very fast paced and satisfying to do, with an insane amount of possible playstyles thanks to having 6 weapons with 4 different "aspects" each, where aspects change how the weapon is played sometimes at a fundamental levelThe game as a whole is built around player choice. You choose the weapon you want and how it plays, your rewards for almost every room, you choose which god's boons (buffs) you want, and you even get to choose exactly how difficult you want the game to be, all the while getting rewarded for itEvery run you just unlock more and more gameplay and story content, and that on top of the already amazing gameplay loop makes the game have a borderline addictive quality to it that just made me never want to put it down, I'm on over 40 hours at the time of writing and I STILL have yet to see most of what this game has to offerI could rave on and on about how good this game is and how much I love it, but I really think everyone should play it for themselves as going in as blind as possible gave me the most enjoyment out of it. The game is very cheap at only $25 while also going on sale often, and it's more worth the price than a lot of more expensive games are. If anything about what I said appeals to you, then you owe it to yourself to try it, you won't regret it

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I'm writing this review for the badge progress, but it truly is my game of the year for 2020. If I was able to vote for it in multiple categories I totally would. Jen Zee has an amazing art style, and she really impressed with Hades' art. "Best Game I Suck At"... Heck yeah! I'm terrible but it's a blast lol. "Best Soundtrack" you better believe it. Supergiant Games' Darren Korb always delivers, and Ashley Barret is a joy to hear whenever she is featured in any of their games. For me this category in particular was neck and neck with best game of the year. "Outstanding Story-Rich Game", well yeah you betcha. Talk about an evolving story with twist and turns, and then when you think it's over it's only just begun.I hope this wins, and even if it doesn't I hope you have fun playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The most beautiful, fluid and one of the best Rougelikes I have ever played, playing this gave me the same feeling I had when I played The Binding Of Isaac for the first time, which is a huge achievement.The story is okay, but if you like Greek Mythology, it's very refreshing (of similar accuracy to Apotheon - another great game).Where this game really excels is in its art and sound design, they compliment each other so well, and add onto the fluidity of the game immensely.10/10Edit: After 130 hours I have finally gotten every achievement on this game, some relationship centred achievements were a little similar but apart from that this was an absolute joy to complete. Not once in all of my hours have I ran into a bug, the game is so incredibly polished and has every nook and cranny refined that not once was my experience tainted by something unfair, unlike other popular rogue-like games.Truly a masterpiece and can only be seen as a perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so far has been one of the best experiences I've had with a rouge-like in all my time playing video games. I was hesitant at first when buying the game as I've played games like this before, mainly enter the Gungeon, and have not found it to be so enjoyable, however, after sitting and playing this game for four hours straight I can say that this is one of the best single player experiences I've had in quite some time. Below are all the things I can recommend about this game with my small time playing it so far and some reasons it's convinced me to write this.All the Great: Art Direction- The style of this game is standout to me, the vibrant colors, backgrounds, character design, and levels all feel thought out and look amazing. The great blend of 3-D models and hand draw backgrounds looks amazing and while odd to look at at first it comes to mesh together seamlessly. The characters themselves all also look amazing, staying close to depictions of their real life counter-parts and really bringing a huge sense of character and style to each and every one.Sound Design and Voice acting-All the weapons and enemies I've fought in the game thus far have sounded amazing. Weapons have a huge punch and make you feel as though you're wielding weapons of the Gods. Enemies feel like they're taking a punch and sound like they're giving one too. As for voice acting, it seems to be right on point with characters being portrayed exactly how they've been described in mythology and matching up exactly with how I feel they would sounds. Each character has a huge personality and they're portrayed greatlyWeaponry- There's a decent size arsenal in this game and they made a bow fun, that's all I feel I need to say on thatCombat- Combat flows smoothly and quickly no matter which weapon you choose on any certain attempt to escape. The foes between levels all feel different and provide a new challenge through each new location. There are certain enemies that seem to be a tad spongy at times depending on things like your boons but other than that it works great and has a superb flow to it all.The Boons-The Boon system is awesome. It adds a layer to these games which I haven't felt in many others and this one does it extremely well. They totally switch up a run through and can make each one feel like something you haven't seen before. It also make sure you don't build up a dependency on certain runes, as you're not always guaranteed to get what you desire.The "Story"-While I'm not sure whether this counts as world building or a story what I've experienced so far has been amazing with even my failed runs feeling like progression. While not wanting to go too into detail to avoid possible spoilers, its a really solid so far and I've enjoyed all that I've learned about this adaption of mythology and the depths of the underworld.Overall, I couldn't really recommend this game more. My only drawback would be is this game without any amp ups doesn't seem to be too difficult. It may just be the difficultly I've been playing in or the weapons just being my sort of thing but if you're looking for a true dungeon crawl I could possibly see you being disappointed with this game, but with the reviews that this game has and how I've felt about it so far I doubt that it would truly ruin it for you. All in all cant recommend it enough, and if you're considering it during any sales any amount off is even more reason to give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my big big brother played this game (rest in peace, Nik) and I remember him telling me casually he really enjoyed this game. I looked at it, and enjoyed the art style but I didn't feel like playing something action-y at the moment so it just went on my wishlist. After Nik passed away, I watched the game more closely and waited for the moment where I felt like committing and playing the game because I wanted to, rather than forcing myself to get into it. Finally the time came by and I was sick of turn-based crap and wanted something fast pace and something to really get the heart rate going. This game checks all the boxes and more.1. It's insanely beautiful, the music is good, sound is good, dialogue is EXTREMELY GOOD. Everything is voice-acted and 11 hours in, I have yet to hear someone say the same thing twice. It's amazing. 2. The game feels like an evolving experience even though you're repeatedly going through the dungeon, starting from square one each time. There's incentives to try different weapons, different power ups each time, and every time you die, you come back and can spend your gems to upgrade some stats for a different experience which allows you to travel further.3. There's a collectible aspect. If you ever want me to play a game more, just add collectibles. That's it. I'm not complicated. Give me an incentive to go back again and again to farm some currency and then let me buy that wallpaper that doesn't do anything besides open dialogue and change the look of my house. Also, there's this whole fate system where you need to go on your runs and unlock certain power ups from the gods in order to complete a "prophecy". And of course, when you do that, you are rewarded with more loot. More look = more house decor or power ups.4. Greek Mythology. Love it. Enough said.I really love this game and I find myself accidentally losing track of time whenever I play. I wish I had started playing sooner when my brother had told me about it, because I really want to talk to him about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've often gotten frustrated when losing lots of progress in a game, but with "Hades", each defeat doesn't really feel bad. You die, you wake up at home, pet your dog, make some witty banter with your housemates, do some interior (and exterior) improvements, get belittled by your father, stare into your mirror so you can let the darkness envelop you, struggle to sleep or even sit down, deal with family drama. . . . _childDocuments_.review: Supergiant's foray into the world of roguelikes and rogulites is a resounding success. Well balanced, addicting gameplay is coupled with a strong narrative that pushes you to complete runs over and over so you can progress the story further. The weapons are all fun to use and multifaceted each in their own way and combined with the variety of boons provided to you by Zagreus's many Olympian relatives, and the randomized levels in the rogulike aspects of the game's design ensure that every run will feel different. The characters are all well written and interesting and helping them progress in their own stories alongside your own journey is a delight. Hades deserves all the acclaim it gets and so much more and it makes me incredibly excited to see what Supergiant has in store for the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 38.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiralling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realise that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realisation, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realise that.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game, Amazing Soundtrack, Amazing Developers, Amazing Community. I wish I could nominate this game for all the categories in the Steam Awards, because honestly, it really deserves it.For anyone wanting to know what makes this game so good:Hades is a Rogue-Lite that actually doesn't make you feel bad over losing a run. It makes failure enjoyable and rewarding, albeit a bit less than success. When the game starts out, there are very few possibilities for you but that changes very fast after the first couple of attempts. The story progresses every time you die and there is a LOT of story before you even manage to escape the Underworld even a single time. Dialogues with multiple different characters inbetween and even during your escape attempts are plenty, fully voiced, and nicely written. And that's just the beginning. Every time you think you're done, there's something to take you back and make you escape the underworld once more. More dialogue, more story, more unlockables.And something to blow your mind even more, after you have actually finished the game, unlocked everything there is to unlock and there is nothing left to do on your save file, you can start a new game and see for yourself how all the growth in power you got over the playthrough doesn't matter as much as the skill you obtained by simply playing the game and escaping over and over again. (Yes, the upgrades do matter a lot, but your skill is worth more) The game also pushes you to increase the difficulty the more you play. It's optional for the story, but required for unlocking things.Before I forget to mention it: This is the most accurate depiction of greek myth I've ever seen in modern media. Sure, Supergiant Games took a few liberties with the plot, but the general depiction just feels correct. Hades himself is depicted the way he is supposed to be: stoic, highly bureaucratic and exact, and busy. He is an antagonist, but not a villain. (Looking at all the fiction depicting Hades as a purely evil being) The olympians are as much of a bickering family as they are supposed to be, with their personalities actually fitting the myths. The other denizens of the underworld are not some evil beings who want everyone to suffer. Hades is a game that has something about it for almost everyone. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the only game so good that I can't even think of a way to leave the review as nothing more than a joke. This entire game is a truly unique experience that everyone should go through. The unique artstyle is simply stunning, the story is incredibly engaing and captivating, the dialogue feels real and authentic and the voice acting for every single character absolutely nails their role. The rng factor can be a bit frustrating at times but that is more than compensated for by the insane amounts of fun that come with any half-decent combination of bonuses. The game is just the right amount of difficult and has a lot of ways to both increase and decrease how much of a struggle it is, ranging from perfect for those only interested in the story to a challenge for even the most experienced players out there. The boss fights are all vastly different and feel like actual bosses rather than just some regular enemy with inflated stats, something that not many games manage to pull off successfully. This is one of, if not the greatest roguelikes ever made and there's nobody on this planet that I wouldn't recommend this game to.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game, one of the best I've ever played. The base game is simple and easy to get the hang of, but the game gets harder as you progress. Following the play style of most dungeon crawlers, you will die, respawn, die again, and repeat. If you don't like games where you have to grind in that manner this game might not be for you, though i would still recommend trying it to find out. The story is interesting and progresses naturally as you play the game, without feeling too grindy ( except maybe the very end ). It doesn't take long to complete the "base" storyline, but even after completing the first section there's even more to the story you can progress if you choose. You can unlock weapons, aspects of weapons, abilities, and certain cosmetics as you play. Most are fairly simple to get, while other achievements and unlockables take a LOT of grinding. Each character in the game has their own story arc which makes interacting with the characters even more fun, and developing bonds with the different gods and friends you will meet is one of the best parts of the game imo. You will read some review by people who didn't like the game because of the repetitive loop; well, if you buy a roguelike expecting anything else that's your own fault. It CAN get repetitive at times, but the game never bored me even after I beat it 50 times in a row. Great game for fans of roguelikes and achievement hunters. Great characters ( not you Theseus ), the gameplay is slick and fun, the music is god-tier (pun intended), and the graphics style is one of my favorites. Highly recommend, 10/10.

I some times click through a dialogue when trying to pick up a boon and find myself missing critical plotOverall Review:Another masterpiece from SuperGiant. Well done. _childDocuments_.review: God, I love this game. Every time I tell myself I am done for the night, but then find myself on another romp through the underworld. What is Hades in its current state? Well it's sort of a Groundhogs Day in Hell as an action game. You play as Hades son who wishes to leave the underworld but continues to find himself right back at the start attempting his escape all over again. His fellow Olympian Gods have heard his plight and offer their assistance, granting him powers as he fights through Hell. Also highly recommend a controller. Game is super playable on keyboard and that is where I started, but the controller feels much more comfortable and I found my hand hurt less and my performance improved.So, let's get this out of the way, yes the game is in Early Access, but it feels polished already. There will be more updates but it kind of feels more like an expansion since what is already there feels so good. The game itself also pokes fun at the updates coming and continuously refers to "Underworld Renovations" which is pretty funny.If you liked Bastion, you'll probably like Hades. Combat feels like Bastion although turned up quite a few notches. It feels amazing to smash enemies against walls for extra damage or cleverly help them into a pit of spikes or pool of lava. Or can forget all that and just mow them down with good ol' fashion DPS. World feels completely immersive and it's easy to get sucked into the game and constantly play again and again even after destroying the final boss. After and during each run, the NPCs tailor their dialog to respond to what happened based on what other NPCs you met or conversations you had with them or even remark on how you died. The dialog and NPC system is very nice and makes the world and characters come alive. They are all very charming and can be pretty funny too. Several NPCs have some sort of storyline to them that you can expand by gifting them and continuing to talk them. Even after playing for 30+ hours I still have so much to see out of my NPC friends that I just keep playing ready to see how each progresses.Also on the point of immersion - the Gods can be so hilariously petty and fickle. True to the source material.It's also just plain fun. Throughout the game the various Olympians grant you boons of power. It's random which ones show up, and then random again which powers you are offered. Thus, each run will differ completely based on what weapon you use (currently 3 melee weapons and 2 ranged) and which Gods you get as well as their power. But say you found a combination of powers you really liked and would like to play that again? All hope is not lost. There are ways to sort of engineer the run to increase your chances of going for a specific build. After you gift each God, they return a gift that you can equip that will guarantee that God shows up in the run right after equipping it. You can change the equipped trinket in between biomes and thus use that trinket to call upon a specific combination of Gods to aid you. I really like this, since there are some weapons I found myself struggling without certain boons to power them up and compliment my playstyle.As a reference for what's currently in the game:Zeus - Lighting which can bounce across foes, good for AOE.Poseidon - Water which increases knock back, extremely good against normal enemies which can be shoved into walls.Ares - Blades and Increasing damage, cursing with a status called Doom.Artemis - Increase Critical rate/damage, lock on sniping etcAphrodite - Charm enemies, weaken them to reduce their damage outputAthena - Deflect attacks back at enemies, defensive boonsDionysus - Poison, damage over timeYou can get a boon on your normal attack, special attack, your cast (throw projectile), and your dash, as well as some just general improvements like damage reduction or increased item finding etc. Some Gods even combine their powers for example Poseidon and Zeus, you can get granted a "Duo" Boon if you have boons from the two of them that will involve lightning striking anytime the Poseidon attacks are used.The game starts out rough, and pretty hard. But as you continue to play you improve through learning the enemies and especially the boss encounters, as well as by gathering resources. Whether you die or lose, you return to a sort of hub where you can spend resources to make improvements and make the next run easier. This includes an auto-revive, better dodging, increased damage, increased power of boons, etc. Thus although there is the ultimate goal of winning a run, there are always plenty of side goals to continue on those improvements or seek out NPCs to progress their story. Really, the game is just such a good mix of fun gameplay and intriguing story that I cannot stop playing. Excited to see what content updates come next!Also, after completing the game once there is a sort of optional difficulty modifier that unlocks to incrementally make the run more challenging, which rewards you with being able to obtain some of the rarer resources from each boss again.

_childDocuments_.review: A big problem for me in past rougelike/rougelites I've played is the lack of any sense of progression. You may slowly unlock new weapons or abilities but often times theres a certain level of "git gud" you need in order to complete a run. Hades fixes this by always having something to unlock, and you do make good and visible progress in each run. In Enter the Gungeon, there are two methods of progression - unlocking new guns and unlocking elevator levels. Your entire run can be determined by how much you're lucky enough to find in order to unlock the next elevator requirement. If you lose out then you have made no progress. In Hades, you collect a few different currencies which help you progress your character build or unlocks. While there are still random encounters you can still build your character in a way that suits your play as you progress. Hades fixes the issues I had with other rougelites and is my favorite one. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put: It's a great hack-and-slash game. During every run you will find upgrades that change the way you fight drastically. These upgrades are temporary And reset every time you die, allowing you to experiment indefinitely.There are also plenty of ways to challenge yourself too. Rewards for beating different sections with certain weapons, Discovering gifts and then trying to gift every NPC in the game for more rewards, Discovering special dialogue and hidden NPCs. Characters are fun to learn about. Voice acting is good, the devs really put heart into their characters.It's a simple game to pick up but rewards you for exploring the mechanics as well as the environment.Overall, it's a fun time-killer, the replay value is high due to it being procedural generated dungeons, weapons are nice and the mechanics are fun. _childDocuments_.review: If you told me a year ago that I would end up liking a roguelite with heavy emphasis on story, I'd be sceptical. If you then  told me it would be my game of the year, I'd tell you to get out and stop messing with me. Being interrupted, especially in fast paced die-repeat-die-repeat games that the roguelite genre offers, is  something I am okay with. Let me play my damn shooty death games in peace. However, every single time I saw a new exclamation mark pop up over a character's head in Hades, it gave me just as much satisfaction as clutching out a hazardous boss fight.And in fact, I think that's actually the worst part about the game. Its story and interactions are . Every time I had to leave the house for another run around the underworld, it kind of felt like leaving the party early. I'd race through the next run just to get the chance to progress some storylines some more. That doesn't mean to say that runs are boring, but they can start to feel samey after a while, especially because - unusually for roguelites - the bosses and "floors" are fixed. You'll fight the same bosses for every world, and you'll start noticing the same rooms with the same enemies too after a while.Is that a dealbreaker? Hell no. In fact, I'm 80 hours in and just about finishing up all the stories and it is only recently nearing the point where runs are getting boring, unless I want to boost stuff into absurd difficulty. And in this game - surprisingly enough - I actually don't. Maybe I'm getting too old for cranking difficulty to 11 and testing my mettle. Maybe the game just doesn't reward that much stupidly high challenge. Or maybe the real accomplishments are, in fact, , the friends we made along the way. Masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is marvellous under many aspects and it's definitely one of the best games - if not the best altogether - that Supergiant Games have made. However, it is not devoid of flaws. Depending on your tastes and what you look for in a game, said flaws might either be a minor bother or ruin your experience completely.PROs:+ Outstanding artistic direction and character design. It's easy to make things look boring or clichéd when dealing with a renowned setting like Greek mithology, but here every single character, deity and beast have been reimagined in a way that is both faithful to the classic iconography and fresh. Music, animations and environmental design are top-notch as well, reaching a level of quality that sets a whole new standard even for a studio well-known for the polishing level of their products like Supergiant.+ Fast, rewarding and addictive gameplay with super tight controls. The main menu suggests the use of a gamepad, but I personally find myself pretty comfortable with mouse and keyboard.+ Lots of optional permanent power-ups to unlock as well as weapons aspects, skills and new boons (divinity blessing) to find in each run. There are 6 weapons in total, but they have a wide array of unlockable forms that give new abilities and bonuses.+ Metaprogressing story that unfolds while you play and keeps progressing even after clearing the game once, keeping the player eager to continue playing.+ Boons are very useful, balanced and they sinergize well with one another. Finding a combination so bad that you'd rather give up and start over is extremely hard and it never happened to me so far.CONs:- Difficulty is pretty bland during the first two areas of the game, then spikes up all of a sudden once you reach Elysium. A better progression curve would've been appreciated.- Boons are constantly re-balanced with patches, and this practically eliminates the chance to find a "gamebreaking" build. While this might be a good things for some, for some others it might completely ruin the fun to find exploitable combinations of items that might happen with luck. To be clear, this is not The Binding of Isaac, where you can just be lucky and find some ludicrously broken combo that will allow you to breeze the game. The final boss will be very hard no matter what you find around, and most of the times you just won't be able to beat it.- Some weapons are much stronger than others, the shield among all, and it might be frustrating to attempt finishing the game with weapons that are simply not the best choice just because it's needed to unlock more stuff.- The worst problem of the game is that it requires a lot of grinding to unlock weapon power-ups. Titan Blood (the currency used for weapon augmenting) is limited to a fixed amount per weapon, and in order to obtain more you have to finish the game with a set of more punitive conditions that unlock after beating one run. Until you haven't completed a run and collected all "bounties" you can't unlock more with a specific weapon (which requires more and more debuffs to be activated at the same time for each attempt), and this might lead to getting stuck for several runs without being able to increase your weapon stats. Other resources such as Darkness, Diamonds, Gems etc must also be grinded a lot, since a massive amount is required to unlock all the optional embellishments of the House.- There's little variety in the room layouts for a rogue-like. There are only 4 different areas, each consisting of 15 to 10 rooms to clear that look pretty much all the same. The final area has more chambers, most of which optional, that are also pretty small.I'm personally having a lot of fun with Hades, though I think that some of the aforementioned problems might prevent some players from having a good time with it. Consider everything that I said before buying the game, or else just wait for a sale. It's definitely a very good product nonetheless, and the creators deserve some recognition.
