_childDocuments_.review: The original was one of my favourite PNC adventure games - so I was very excited to play this. The graphics were superb and I played it on my 4K 65" TV using a Steam Controller. However, there were a number of bugs with the interface, graphical glitches and on multiple occasions I had to force quit and reload. Trying to use your inventory items against something this is moving became a frustrating experience as the menu disappeared and you had to start over. Although none of these stopped me from completing the game, it did detract from an otherwise polished experience.The plot was perhaps a little too obvious for my liking and lacked the "dark" aspects of Beneath a Steel Sky. In the opening scene of Beneath, you see a man cut in half by a gun, and I'll never forget the doctors surgery reminiscent of the popular film, Minority Report. This felt tame in comparison, clearly targeted at a younger audience - strange considering the age of people who played the original. Don't let the TellTale-esque style fool you - this is not an interactive movie, it's still very much a PNC. There are some interesting puzzles to solve and overall it kept me rapt enough to try and finish in a single sitting. Is it perfect? No. Is it wonderful to see a follow-up to a childhood favourite? Absolutely. Could it have ever lived up to my expectations? Unlikely. So all in all, I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game. The puzzles throughout all made sense, though it does have a built in hint system in the pause menu in case you get stuck or like me had a few days since you played last and don't remember what you were doing in that area. I played through it all with my kids and they had a good time playing it. They looked forward to playing it again. My 13 year old son said that he wanted it to be a couple hours longer. It took us about 9 hours to finish, so I took that as a compliment that he enjoyed it and wanted to play more of it. The people were unique and the areas were interesting. The overall story, while it is a continuation from the first game, didn't require that you played the first game. It had plenty of nods to the first game so that if you had played it over 20 years ago you'd go, oh yeah. Revolution Software has done a good job with this one. Just like the original Steel Sky and the Broken Sword games, which my kids enjoyed also, this one is a well paced adventure game that has tough enough puzzles you feel good beating them, and a story that makes you want to figure out the puzzle so that you can get to the next part. Great mix of talking, figuring out, environment searching, puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to a point-and-click adventure released in 1994 (made by the studio famous for the "Broken Sword" series; they even put their famous characters in display), that you can play for free  on Steam. It's advisable to play the earlier entry, or you'll miss a lot of context. I liked this sequel more than the original. Not only because of improved graphics and audio or for taking more than double the time to finish, but because the gameplay is more interesting and less frustrating (the original has a lot of pixel hunting, for example). The hacking puzzles, although not challenging, were interesting, giving the game more than the usual inventory-based puzzles.  The story is pretty linear, with no meaningful choices and consequences. If you're a stickler for plot holes, you'll find some, but thematically I thought that the game made some good points _ maybe inspired by the classic novel "Brave New World". Not a masterpiece by any measure, but I enjoyed playing these 2 games.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: this game didnt cut it for me. lackluster presentation, abysmal graphical fidelity, a story that still didnt hook me an hour and a half in, and very little to no gameplay.i usually love narrative games, even if they show very little in terms of gameplay and/or presentation, but the story and characters have to be amazing and carry the game forward and here, it just doesnt.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: So, yeah that was fun. It has been a while since I played a point and click style graphic adventure and I really enjoyed it. Thats not to say it didn't have its problems but certainly the game is of a high quality and was entertaining and absorbing. I finished the game in 14 hours according to Steam, I wasn't rushing anything but it honestly felt like a lot less and by the end I really felt it could have easily been twice as long, maybe this is a testament to how absorbing the whole game is that 14 hours felt like only 4 or 5, I really felt pulled into the story and the graphics and story are great.So, what could be improved? Well, some of the voice acting was a bit hit or miss, one really memorable character was the hacker "Leet" voiced by Shane Attwooll with a distinctive broad welsh accent, you can tell where this game was developed by all the regional UK accents in play. On the flip side the main character has a generic American accent and was almost instantly forgettable and rather boring to listen too.You can tell the interface was obviously designed for controller, and although navigating with a mouse is much more pleasant and realistic, using the in-game menu system could sometimes be frustrating.Most of the puzzles were fairly easy, some very clever and one or two just didn't make sense and I had to get all the hints to understand them. (The firework projector one comes to mind). The final puzzle where you twist some box puzzles could have been much better especially as it is the finale. Overall, I give 4/5 stars and I really hope they make another as this genre is one of my favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Revisit the "Beneath a steel sky"-world with todays game technology. It´s well worth it!This game got a lot of criticism for not staying true to the original game (Beneath a steel sky) and that it contained a lot of bugs, so i had my doubts for a long time whether i should buy it or not. Well, I bought it a couple of days ago - and i dont regret it.Robert Fosters encounter with the "modern" Union city mirrors a lot of todays absurdities born from the post modern world we seem to enter now adays. And its obvious that George Cecil & Co has gone through a lot of discussion on the subject.Now, down to business. The graphic is good. It´s a lot like Broken sword 5, a little improved and the art style suits the cyber punk world excellent. The voice actors are good and Robert Fosters- and Joeys voice actors have done a great job. It´s a lot of humor in the game and the conversations beteween them are often very funny. If you have played any of the Broken sword-games you know the "George Cecil humor" by now, and this game is the most funny of them all.The puzzles are the weakest ingredients in the game. They arnt very challenging. I went through the game without using any hints. The game´s got its own logic and once you get the hang of it it´s pretty easy. Most of the puzzles consist of hacking diffrent machines and the veriety isn´t that big. And the game is short. To short to my opinion considering the price. But, the story is strong and the devs continued to build from where the Beneath a steel sky ended, in a good way. And they manages to finish the story on a high note.I had little trouble with bugs. I encountered a few when there was no sound when people spoke. But thats all, and it happend only when side characters interacted with each other. So not a big problem.The final complaint i have is regarding the inhabitants of union city. They arnt well programed. They are walking aginst you when you are standing still and they feel completely like robots. This entails Union city to feel less alive.But the game as a whole is good and well worth to play if you like adventure games. And aspecially if you like Beneath a steel sky and the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful labour of love for all fans of the original, and the perfect remedy for those that miss classic point-and-click adventures (but with a beautiful modern gloss).Really couldn't have asked for a better sequel in terms of story, and the writing and performances breathe life into each and every character, just as we had seen in the original game. You'll want to exhaust dialogue trees just to hear more sass or witicisms from the Union City d-RYDs and citizens.The soundtrack is also fantastically produced, helping to carry an undercurrent of mood and drama to every scene.The game controls well too- as I played the game over a weekend all about the house I jumped between keyboard, gamepad, and touchscreen control as suited me and each felt natural to use. This is exactly the control scheme I would love to see used in future 3rd person adventures.The game is newly released at the time of writing this review so there are many bugs in the game- nothing game-breaking, but some odd graphical quirks like animations not triggering or clipping through the terrain, or dialogue options not being highlighted appropriate to whether I'd heard them or not. Nothing I encountered was game breaking, but it did make for some immersion-breaking.There was one logic puzzle in particular that I'd worked out before the game provided too much guidance (which happens often, making quite a streamlined experience where you won't generally feel lost or confused), which did cause a problem- I provided a d-RYD for someone to step onto for support when they needed help, and had the forethought to lighten its load to accommodate the weight of a person. But when this d-RYD came to their rescue, the logical conclusion of the rescure didn't happen, and I was offered no way to trigger it. After a long time of hair pulling and thinking I missed something, I found out that I had to REFILL the d-RYD, who then got the floor wet, which THEN told me to empty it, as I had already done, to carry the person. Quite frustrating, but thankfully the only occurance of such a required backpeddling.I didn't realise how much of a hunger I had for classic logic-puzzle and dialogue-tree adventure gaming I had built up until I played Beyond A Steel Sky, but having finished it I feel very satisfied. And as a fan of the original, Beneath A Steel Sky, I found the game even more rewarding and would say it is required gaming for other existing fans. If you've not played the original, it is freeware on GOG, so you have no excuse (then buy this).
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: When my brother and I were children we picked up the floppy disk version of Beneath a Steel Sky. Following our love of Sam & Max and Putt-Putt, our tiny minds were attracted to this grimier more mature adventure. We played it all the time, and loved reaching the end so that we could start again and relive the adventure with Joey.As adults we rediscovered the CD version and loved it all over again.Beyond a Steel Sky has once again reminded me of the love we had for the first game. Sure, you could play it as a standalone having never experienced BASS1, but for those of us who lived and loved the original, this sequel is a real treat and evident labour of love.Prepare to have your nostalgia glands go into overdrive, fans of BASS1! I do not want to spoil anything, so I'm just gonna say that you're in for one hell of a trip down memory lane.To that regard, if you HAVEN'T played the first game, I would recommend either getting it now and playing it first (it's free, y'all!) or watching a playthrough, or even watching a review that covers the original's characters and events, as there is a LOT of calling back to things from BASS1. Most of the major reveals do have a nod or shout out prior to their big reveal, which is helpful, but I'd still recommend jumping in with a level of familiarity.Gameplay wise, nothing challenging. A rare treat where I've not had to look up any advice on how to solve any of the puzzles, but I was challenged a few times to really think outside the box and to stretch the parameters of my thinking in order to solve a puzzle.Also, prepare to come face to face with a LOT of pop culture references. Everything from Monty Python (a staple reference course for the point-and-click genre), to the mars rover, a variety of nerdy films, the studio's earlier games, and even a Jon Ronson nod. This game was clearly made by nerds reliving the heyday of pre-millennium game devs and all the awesome junk they surrounded themselves with.Well done, Revolution! I blinkin' loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! love the story and the different characters (Even Jimmy lol). Only problem is 35 dollars for a game you can complete in a short time? I wish it was waaaaay longer. Maybe even set it to where you had to save it by zones or work your way destroying the council one by one at a time. Just ideas for a longer playtime. I did leave it running a few times (naptime is your friend). My time says 17 Hrs but Its probably 10 (or less if your using hints). Other than that BRAVO!!!  RECOMMEND RECOMMEND! RECOMMEND!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A really great modern adventure game that builds on the story of its predecessor in a really pleasing way (I recommend playing through the original before tackling this one). I enjoyed the story, the cel-shaded graphics (really gorgeous in places!), the hacking puzzles, the dialogue script and the voice acting. I also really appreciated the built-in hint system that gives you gradual hints. Sometimes a nudge is all you need to progress! Overall really enjoyed my time with this game and would recommend it to adventure fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this game, eventually I decided to recommend it.I do suggest you play beneath a steel sky first. Just so you can make more sense of it all.I enjoyed this game. The story it's trying to bring across is decent. The art style reminds me of Borderlands and it looks good in that respect considdering it's supposed to look like a comic book.the sound is goodthe music too.The puzzles should have been a bit more difficult.The animation is a bit wonky, but that could have been intentional. It reminded me of the animation sequences of old P&C adventure games.I finished the game in 11 hours and that is a bit short for 30 euros, but if it is on sale for half I'd say go for it.one last thing, the game didnt seem to register achievements..
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this because I think it's stunning. The story is so much fun, it looks absolutely beautiful, and it feels smooth and polished. Until. I got to about 4 or 5 hours into the story, and things have started getting quite buggy. I've been able to fix these things by exiting and reentering the area, or restarting the game, but in a game like this bugs can be an enormous detriment: I start questioning whether it's me not thinking of something by which to solve a puzzle, or if the game's bugged out again. Which hugely affects enjoyment. As I said, I think the good makes up for the bad, because the good is SO good. I'm even happy to have paid full price despite being a huge Broken Sword fan during the sale, but not having it in my Steam library. But there needs to be more work done before this is a perfect game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this and there is a lot to say that's probably already been said. Despite being a longtime fan of Beneath a Steel Sky, the development of Beyond a Steel Sky went right under my radar all the way up to its release. I can say that it was quite a satisfying experience and was a  rollercoaster of emotions much like the first game, and definitely feels like the direct-sequel that it is. However, that's not to say that it's perfect. I'm not sure if this has any game-overs like the Beneath a Steel Sky, as I haven't died a single time during my only playthrough. In Beneath a Steel Sky, I recall losing several times during my first playthrough and the puzzles here seemed a little too easy. So easy, in fact, that thinking a bit differently broke the sequence of some dialog and revealed other oversights. (Spoiler: )Even though this feels a bit short, wasn't much harder than a visual novel and had a few bugs, I'd definitely recommend this to fans of The first game and would recommend the two games as a whole.   Beneath a Steel Sky is free these days, so play it with SCUMMVM or on a proper MS-DOS build before playing this one. Especially the version with CD-Audio. The characters sound the same and Joey is one helluva wisecracking smartass in both. If I did have to nitpick, some of the darker tones, dark humor, gore and use of stronger language seem to be a bit nerfed compared to the first game, but I guess I don't mind that too much. This is still a masterpiece I highly recommend and meshes pretty damn well with the original, aside from trying to scroll through the inventory while trying to use an item on an NPC, just to have that NPC walk away and close the menu. That was such a pain in the ass. I finished the entire game in about thirteen hours, but apparently only one of the achievements successfully unlocked and no screenshots were taken. I'm not sure if this game has a problem with the steamAPI or if steam itself had an issue, but it looks like I'm gonna have to play this one again.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to congratulate Revolution on a worthy successor to Beneath a Steel Sky! Beyond a Steel Sky is a game I have been anticipating and following the news for since it was first announced - I was even lucky enough to be one of the Revolution "Street Team" testers to test the iPhone version of the original BASS. This sequel is a love letter to fans of the original game, there are plenty of throwbacks and notes of nostalgia, but at the same time accommodating for players new to adventure games and bringing something new to the world of Union City. I was particularly fond of the hacking system (being in the Tech industry, a certain Towers of Hanoi-like puzzle brought a smile to my face!), not to mention the dystopian 1984-like feel, where Big brother (in this case, MINOS) is watching you at all times.The only (small) criticism I can point out (at least in my play through) - I encountered a game breaking bug in a critical story part of the game, but due to the diligence of the Revolution team, this bug was fixed in the first patch so I was able to continue with no more issues.If you are a fan of 90's adventure games or just a compelling story, I would wholeheartedly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Need to preface this by saying that this is an alright game. The devs work hard on fixing the bugs and deserve your support, but if your plan is just to sit down, play an adventure game and relax there will be quite an effort on your part required.This release is a mess (And if I am going to blame anyone, I will blame the pandemic) and the bugs are ridiculous. The camera will get stuck in a wall during a conversation because it will try to change perspective and cut off your sound in the process. This game is not made with a keyboard and mouse in mind. This game is also not made with controller in mind, so dust off your Schriebman port to interface with your computer or something. Aligning the pointer with the thing you want to do is a chore, whether you are trying to go through a door (you will get stuck on walls), do an action upon a moving target (the target will run away from you faster than you can pick an option), do an action on a screen that changes angle instead of your character (the angle will change as you scroll through the inventory, moving away from the hotspot) or picking a conversation option (the joystick has to be aligned perfectly with the sentence instead of sticking to the closest approximate option).Conversations also lead you round and round until they are considered "exhausted" without adding any new information. You will hear a great variation of "Have you seen any kids around?", "Were there kidnappings lately?", "Are you sure there were no kidnappings lately?", "What of the kidnappings, tho?", "Have you seen the ludicrous display last night?", "I'm looking for kidnappers" before the option greys out, so any time a conversation comes up, there is a good possibility that there is no need to click on an option more than once (Until there suddenly is such need). Which is a waste of voice acting (The quality of which is, by the way, okay, it just doesn't work with animations really well).The story is okay, even though it is a rehash of the original. The visuals are okay if you didn't manage to break them (which is easy) and are game-y childish with a bit of Hunger Games on the side. Everything is just okay and this wouldn't have been a thumbs down if there weren't glaring quality issues. Even the 3D Broken Sword games play with less issues and those are not rose tinted glasses - I played them last year. If your plan is not to support the devs in the hopes that the game gets patched - wait on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed "Beneath a Steel Sky" as a young teenager, and this game brings back fond memories of that game. The "feeling" is still there, and all those "flashbacks" to the orginal game is so good, but it don't intrude too much for the new player.The game it self is an easy adventure game, it is perfect for playing in the evenings after a hard days work, it is realxing and easy to digest.I got this game as a reward from "PC Gamer" not from a publisher or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original game and it was great how they brought back most of the feel of it. The cell-shaded graphics felt a bit last decade, but it was still visually nice. Dialogue was pretty good and the way the story continued was done well. Pretty short game, though, with little replay value. If you're a fan of the original, or any other Revolution games, get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy followup the the seminal Sci-Fi/Cyberpunk classic, Beneath a Steel Sky. Beyond a Steel Sky builds on the world imagined in the original, with beautiful 3D renderings of Union City that was depicted in the original.Regardless of whether you've played the original (although if you haven't, I highly recommend you do; you've no excuse as it is now free), Beyond a Steel Sky is a beautifully realised adventure game that boasts the unmistakable Revolution Software shine - if you enjoy this, you will enjoy their entire catalogue of games. Impeccable visuals and a stirring score make it an absolute treat. There are plenty of nods to the original title too.With that being said however, like most new games, there are a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥; I've had a handful of crashes and weird camera angle issues in game, but I want to stress that these are few and far between - I have played this game in excess of 18 hours (I played it via Apple Arcade previously, so the playtime you see for myself against this review is not a true indicator of my playtime), and have had a two or three crashes, and a handful of scenes where the camera was a bit wrong; not impeding the actual gameplay however.I can heartily recommend Beyond a Steel Sky to anyone who enjoys adventure games. I had free access to this game on my iPhone and Mac via Apple Arcade, but purchased it again here (with the Aspiration Day pack / soundtrack) to show my support for Revolution - this is a fantastic game.On the technical side of things, I want to note that I have played this across three platforms; my gaming desktop, a 4960K @ 4.5GHz with a GTX 1080 graphics card, an iPhone 12 Pro Max, and a 2014 2GHz Quad Core i5 Mac with integrated HD4600 graphics; for anyone with a lower spec machine, this will play fine if you're willing to make some graphical sacrifices; of course you can enjoy the story, but I must say the game is well worth playing on a device with maximum eye candy switched on where possible!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game. I played the original and I was happy to see a sequel after 26 years! I just don't think it's going to hold up to the original game.It's an alright game - but that's it, not great. It had some wonderful throwback moments once in a while if you knew the original game, but those things couldn't save it. To me, the biggest issue is the setting. The original had it's own thing going but here, we end up with a really, REALLY generic 'utopia' thing and with the choice of art design, it's going to be really forgettable. I'm just glad that the top of the city kept it's old style. There were also at times where it felt like they forgot some things about the original game (Like the fact that Android Joey was named Joey - rather than the name Ken which was given to him at the end of the first game).All in all - It's alright! But nothing you'll probably ever go back to once you've finished it and more than likely just going to forget. Wait for a sale or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A nice looking game, much like an old 90s point-and-click adventure but with the freedom of a 3rd person protagonist following camera. The story seems good and with lighthearted satire, the rumblings of conspiracy in a over-controlled city is a little overdone in the gaming scene (maybe I'm just getting old) but it doesn't deter from the enjoyment. One of the game's gimmicks is a 'hacking' system where you can swap executions between conditions of certain devices which sounded interesting, but seems no more than drag and drop trial and error to advance things only in the way the game wants you to.Game play aside, sadly I must mark this as negative purely due to the excess of bugs.I don't believe I've ever played a game with so many noticeable issues in it before. Indicators of non-existent new dialogue options, a hint system of which its position of sequence seems unattached to any save file, one of the first characters you meet refusing to present a dialogue prompt, forcing you to restart from the beginning, a cleaning robot of which its actions are vital to proceed through a certain part of the game, around 4 hours in, being completely idol, disallowing you from continuing at all, forcing you to load a save file from hours prior. Having raised this on Steam discussions I received no constructive response so decided to warn others via this review instead. I've read countless posts of others having all sorts of game breaking issues, it's quite a shame.The game is enjoyable, perhaps I was just unlucky, but just be prepared to repeat hours of game play to overcome bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line:Lack of consistency and occasional bugs in solving riddles stop this from being a somewhat enjoyable experience.The solutions for some of the riddles and situations is a bit abstract and far-fetched, while more logical solutions that stare you in the face are not an option. It's not helped by the occasional bugs and leads to the player being unsure if they are just not able to grasp the answer or the game decided to not let them pass.Consistency is very important in these kind of games so that the player knows if they are just unable to solve the puzzle or they are running in circles because of a bug that's stopping the progress.Of course you could look up the solution on the internet, but I for one strive to play trough games with my own strength. Once you look one riddle up, you'll be more likely to rely on walktroughs for the rest of the game.That aside, the world building is convincing, the overall look and feel are in line and fit to the story and atmosphere rather well. The characters are somewhat likable and the humor clever and non-intrusive. The story is well rounded and conclusive, but I wouldn't mind some kind of warning to this game being a sequel to an older game; Beneath a Steel Sky.Although as someone who found this out in the middle of the playtrough, I can say it's not impossible to gather the pieces without playing the first game.A great throwback to the era of games like Broken Sword, Grim Fandango or Monkey Island series. If you enjoyed those, you might like this as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky. Latter one is free, so if you have never played it, go ahead and do that. It's not absolutely mandatory, but as this game is sequel to that, there's plenty of references to the first game.While Beyond a Steel Sky is adventure game, it's more like third person adventure game and it looks pretty good. Things have come long way from Grim Fandango (if you haven't seen it, it kind of looks like Playstation the original era game). There's still some loss of detail compared to good pixel art, but not much. It still feels like old fashioned adventure game as there's no jumping or shooting. 3D makes a difference though. Interacted things are bit more scattered around. Game is well aware that it's 3D and some puzzles take advantage of that.Puzzles start from quite simple, but more complex ones get more frequent towards the end. There are few that are bit illogical. For example in one of them same thing needs to done twice, but second time it needs to be done differently for no good reason. Hint system is pretty good though, hints start from something quite vague and go eventually to direct solution to the puzzle. I didn't feel need to look for third party walkthrough at all. Story is not very deep, but it's entertaining. There's plenty of enjoyable scenes and you might even find more jokes in the second play through as there are few multiple choice questions that you can answer only once.It's following pretty good sci-fi formula of commenting modern society through sci-fi lens. Characters are cartoony, but not entirely unbelievable. Most of them following good tradition of being obnoxious, but in a entertaining sort of way.Beyond a Steel Sky is still quite fresh release. First patch fixed several big issues, but if you enjoy bug hunting you might still find few issues. Developers and community are quite active, so I'm sure there will be patch or two.Beyond a Steel Sky is not perfect game, but positive clearly outweighs the negative. Game can be frustrating at times as adventure games usually are, but patience is rewarded with good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently playing it on Bootcamp on a Macbook Pro and the game runs perfectly 99.9% of the time. I have noticed a couple of visual glitches during play but they are so minor that it doesn't matter. It's a very funny cyberpunk game with some deep themes. I recommend it if you like this genre of adventure puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so I have very mixed feelings about this game which I will try to explain below, but unfortunately overall, at least for now my recommendation has to be a no.First of all lets get the worst part of out of the way, I encountered 2 game breaking bugs fairly early on in the game, one of which was solved after I had closed and restarted the game, the other however was not and halted all progress ( a LOT of people having this issue according to the forums), after 2 days of waiting for a patch or at least some news of an incoming patch to fix the issue I decided to start the game again and not rely on the autosave feature which fires too often and only uses 3 slots, so if like me you don't realise you have a game breaking bug early enough (i'm not the using the hint system and had spent a good amount of time looking for the "thing I missed", before eventually giving up and realsing it was due to a bug both times) then none of your autosaves will be of any use.Putting that to one side for now let me focus on the game itself.Even though the game looks and runs great, there does seem to be a general lack of polish, at least on the PC version. There were a good few time where animations were off, there were numerous dialogue options that you could choose that expanded on conversation options you hadn't chosen yet, some items seemed to randomly become uninteractable at times, NPC's can block you, joey and other NPC's in, weird camera angles during cutscenes, sounds/dialogue volume changes when you nor the sound have changed positions, and probably a few other things i've forgotten.I love the overall art style and thought all of the voice acting was great, the city looked amazing too, but unfortunately as feared, you really don't get to explore it any where near as much as you'd like.What was quite quickly evident and persisted throughout is that the tone the game is going for is a lot less gritty than the original, it feels like this is made more for the children of fans of the original than fans of the original themselves.As said above I played through the game without the hint system and never got "stuck" for more than a few minutes outside of the bugs I encountered, all of the puzzles just felt a little too easy and obvious, especially seeing as the game hand-holds you a lot by effectively locking you in to small areas until you complete the puzzle before you can move on, taking away what could/would have been a lot of the experimentation in trying to find solutions to your problems, and in designing things this way it means the solution to your problem is never far away.Quite early on you get a new tool which allows you to find and hack systems throughout the world which I thought was a really cool mechanic that could lead to some fun and inventive ways to solve puzzles, unfortunately though the mechanic never really progresses past standing in the right place to interact with multiple systems at once. The "getting inspiration" puzzle (no spoilers) was great however and felt like the hacking mechanic was really going somewhere, unfortunately though this would be the best the hacking mechanic had to offer, with it going back to more simplistic puzzles afterwards.I loved that you got to go back to linc space and the new minos, but linc space had been reduced to collecting a few items to use to get into minos and then never revisited, with minos itself being a nothing more than a couple of simple "move things around" puzzles.Despite the shift of tone to a younger audience and the overall simplicity of the puzzling I still found myself largely enjoying the game, being back with Robert and Joey (it's not a spoiler, he's on the front cover) and listening to their banter. The story itself is OK, nothing amazing to be fair, it's pretty simple and generic but I suppose that keeps it easy to understand for the seemingly younger audience this game is going for.However, and this was a big one for me, there seems to be a huge difference in the depth of the game after a certain point, without giving spoilers, all I'll say is once you get to the reflection spa. After this point everything just feels a bit rushed and weak compared to the puzzles and stuff that came before. The areas are smaller, the puzzles simpler and it unfortunately culminated in a very anti-climactic final confrontation where you have nothing to do apart from spin a couple of cube parts around. Feels there was supposed to be a good couple of hours more story and puzzling at least that didn't end up in the finished game to me.Overall it's a toughie, I really wanted to be able to recommend this game as Beneath A Steel Sky will always hold a big place in my heart in terms of favorite games, but unfortunately the bugs, combined with the focus on a younger audience, lack of general polish and the seemingly rushed nature of the last portion of the game means it's a no.When the major bugs get fixed, and if you have kids that you would love to introduce to the franchise, then definitely, all day long, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre adventure game with good graphics but with a weak storyline and repetitive puzzles. Recommended if you played the 1994 original and are an adventure game veteran. Otherwise, skip it unless you are able to ignore the story while enjoying the visuals.The game starts with a simple objective and is able to build a rather rich world that deserves exploration. However, the initial objective never matures and the  storyline becomes gradually oversimplified and often times verges on the ridiculous given the complete lack of awareness of most characters and the impact of their decisions. This is the opposite of the storyline of the 1994 Beneath a Steel Sky, which manages to be thought provoking, serious and funny at the same time. In this game, it seems that Telltale spent more time on making the 3D graphics look nice and in the voice acting (which is very good) than writing a decent script. This is a pity, given the potential of the setting of this game.The puzzles are also not a positive aspect of the game since the majority are not challenging at all and are solved exactly in the same way, using a "scanner" tool obtained in the very beginning of the game. The complexity of these puzzles is basically placing the character in a precise location in the 3D environment to be able to use said tool. This adds an artificial layer of difficulty that gets boring very fast.In short, good graphics, very good voice acting, mediocre story, mediocre puzzles, a lost opportunity to build on the 1994 Beneath a Steel Sky, which is a vastly superior game. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a steel sky is a decent game. Not going to lie. It's just not 'great' or memorable in any other way. It will entertain you, sure. But it's not a game you are going to rave about to your friends or do a deep dive in to secrets. The plot is okay, you play Robert Foster, a man on a mission to find a kidnapped child. Along the way you meet quirky characters, some better than others.  The villain of the story is rather cookie cutter sadly, both of them are. Unfortunately there were some plotholes that made me scratch my head in confusion. The humor in the game is alright. It leans a bit heavily on tropes but it did make me chuckle in a few instances. And all this is a massive waste of potential. The world is incredibly interesting but hardly any of it really gets explored. It's like only being allowed in the kiddie pool while you can see an incredible beautiful sea you coul be swimming in. You don't really explore the background of the world you inhabit and the only information you get is what you need to complete your tasks. No extra side missions, no extra info, no dress up. You get what you need and only what you need. Which is such a massive bummer.The game is also rather short for the price you pay for it. The backtracking you constantly do costs about as much as the rest of the game and is mainly there to fill the short time you'll be playing. Another bummer. You can easily finish the entire game in under 7 hours. Probably even less. WIth how easy the puzzles are, you'll be breezing through.And the bugs....dear lord, the bugs. Beyond a steel sky is beyond a broken mess. NPC's will trap you in area's to the point neither of you can move. I'm looking at you Songbird. Triggers for actions that the NPC's will have to do will just fail. NPC's that float will try to escape by hurtling themselves over railings and then get themselves stuck. Sadly, this entire game feels more like a tacked on DLC for a bigger game. Except, this is it. This is all you get. And it saddens me because Union City is a place you want to explore and learn more and more about. Good in concept, bad in execution. So in lieu of not having a 'meh' option I sadly have to go with the thumbs down.Wait for a massive steam sale with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very annoyed by the review i need to do, not to other people but mainly to Revolution Software. I was a huge fan of your work since Lure of the temptress and i finished all your games. Beyond a steel sky is not a bad game, really. But it's not a good one. You've done a great job technically and visually by providing a futurist adventure and as a former webdesigner i can applaude the UI of the game, very cool and a good improvment of adventure game interaction. Visually it's original and beautiful, i want to visit Union City!But the story is a fully classical plot with a basic philosophical outcome. Dialogs are like the ones who made in 90's but we are not in 90's anymore, humour and stories have improved and need to be more worked and when i play at this game it's like syberia 3, the sensation to follow a path already taken too much times. Sometimes dialogs are lame, simple and ludicrous. All is conventional and predictable. I don't want to talk to the few moments in story outcomes where there is bad written moves.And enigmas: most of the time boring and not well-developed. Like said by a previous review, ideas are good but lack of development and depth. Enigmas and puzzles seems they're here just because.Final negative point: Animations lack of life and sometimes they are totally bad. I know you're not a huge studios but for a 2020+ game it's not the minimal required. And sometimes they're good so lack of balance?These points can be blend in one: the lack of life and soul in the game, not like your previous games.I don't want to seem totally negative about your work but as i said i was a huge fan of Revolution Software and with the director's cut of BS1 you loose me because of the ridiculous scenarii written by a 10 yo. And with Beyond a steel sky you confirm a problem with your writing and your vision of games. You seems to be blocked on your old successes and don't understand the evolution of games and society.I'm deceived because when i played Beyond a steel sky i've always think about what this game could have been and i know you're able to do best. I'll always follow you and support your work but, please, wake up and stop the temptation to recreate your successes and just look at others games and why people loves them.Finally, for players, don't be affraid of my review, it's not a bad game, the negative recommandation is to encourage Revolution Software to reconsider their gamedesign logic. Give a chance if you're in search for nostalgia or if you're not used to play a narrative-scifi game (they're not a lot). Give a chance to Revolution Software to continue its history on a better road!

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice visuals. The graphics aren't top notch for sure and many assets look bulky, but overall it has beautiful, comic like aesthetics with its shaders and the babbles.- "Union City" is a cool dystopian futuristic city that looks alive and feels immersive. It has a weird, cheerful but oppressive atmosphere.- It has some clever, innovative puzzle mechanics like the hacking scanner, although it gets repetitive after a while.- Plenty of well written dialogues. You won't get bored of trying all the available answers.- It has great, discreet sense of humor. It isn't a comedy but has some hilarious moments.- Despite being a bit bulky visually, the characters have cool personalities and some of them feel unique. Robert and Joey are one of the most amazing pair of protagonists. - Pretty good and convincing voice acting performances. - A ton of references to the first game of the series, which was marvelous. A lot of things that you do are directly connected to it. Also, it makes a good job on explaining to you the story of "Beyond a Steel Sky", so you can understand everything even if you haven't played it.- I'm still not convinced that the 3d world is a good fit for point n' click adventures, but this is a pretty decent interpretation. Although a lot of mechanics have issues, it manages to bring back the feeling of the golden era of point n' click adventures.- It is political. The social structure of a city with the oppression covered behind the illusion of democracy and happiness, the role of the media and the politicians are direct comparisons to modern societies.- No pixel hunting. Every interactive object is clearly visibly.- Good hint system with multiple levels. Instead of telling you right away the whole solution of a puzzle, it gives you a small push in order to help you find it by yourself.The bad- Lack of puzzles diversity. The great hacking scanner mechanic is overused with a result of getting repetitive and boring after a while. It could be more creative. One or two puzzles are completely silly or the game game doesn't give you enough clues in order to understand them (like that one with the infinite Qdos). Some other puzzles are pretty worn and unimaginative like those during the final "battle"- Controls mechanics have a lot of issues. Interacting with objects may be tricky depending the angle that you look at them. Robert tends to get stuck on objects and people and his movement constantly seems glitchy. NPC's pathfinding is bad as they keep blocking you and getting into your path. There are many more small bugs here and there that often ruin the vibe you're into.- The story is simplistic and constantly feels disjoined with bad pace and escalation. It mostly forces you to solve a ton of meaningless problems that add almost nothing to the plot and decides to make a clunky twist towards the very end revealing the whole evil plan and its political background in just one lengthy conversation. It doesn't manage to build tension and it's hard for the player to create secondary thoughts without having more clues in mind during the playthrough. Also, all this "save my abducted friend" is a bit cliché.- Only few locations. Although "Union City" is cool with some imposing landscapes during the cut scenes, you end up playing at only few places, which you have to visit again and again.- It has replaced the dark, dirty atmosphere of the first game with a more colorful and cheerful one. This is not necessary a problem, but many players may not expect or want it form a successor of "Beneath a Steel Sky".
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphics and an amazing cityscape provide a backdrop to the story - with a good looking lead character and an entertaining and amusing sidekick Joey,  including a good level of humour.The puzzles are enough to make you think, and provide a challenge, but not too tough to delay things for too long. I tried the SCUMM version of this game some years age but gave up - it was too tough! This update though - perfect!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful adventure game that updates the gameplay for a more modern experience, while still keeping the atmosphere and humour of the original. Clever little hat-tips to the original can also be seen here and there in the game.Some interesting new additions are things like a universal hacking tool which turns into quite a clever little mini game as well as the ability to affect different outcomes in the story based on your actions. I'm also grateful to the publisher for setting the game at a reasonable price (with a release bonus discount no less!); games shouldn't be expensive to play! Particularly when the game itself is not very long.While you could definitely play this game and enjoy it without having played the original, I would personally recommend playing the first one before this one, as it makes the experience so much more satisfying.EDIT: I just thought I'd mention that I notice other reviews talking about performance issues and bugs. I feel as though in many cases these opinions seemed exaggerative and harsh as to how much the bugs really detract from the experience (it seems a bit nit-picky to me to be honest), and I'm just downright puzzled by the mention of performance problems.Quality control could've potentially been a bit higher standard around NPC paths and some of the subtitles, but I barely noticed any of that and the game seems reasonably well optimised to me.I have a very modest system myself (sometimes not nearly as good as the reviewers who complained about performance issues): an i5 3470 CPU, 8 GB DDR3 1600Mhz RAM and a Geforce GTX 960 2 GB graphics card.I could play the game at a reasonable frame rate of about 40-60 FPS at 1920x1080 resolution on high settings, and while I certainly wouldn't call the art direction/graphical fidelity of the game itself mind-blowing, it was enjoyable enough for me in a general sense while also being quite the nostalgia trip. Loading times between scenes were actually quite short considering how slow my RAM/HDD are.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is top notch and the game makes for fantastic commentary on utopia gone dystopia. It touches upon currently pertinent topics such as social credit, surveillance and our inability to really predict and control AI.The utopian cyberpunk aesthetic is beautiful and Union City feels well designed and alive.Unfortunately, the final third of the game feels rushed and overly relies on mini puzzles and the annoying hacking mechanic where the player has to move code segments around in physical space. I feel like the game really could have done without those gimmicks. This mechanic occasionally breaks and makes it unclear how to proceed.That being said, the game is solid and one of the better adventure games in the recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This has been sitting on my wish list for a while but not as long as games usually.I've played Beneath a Steel Sky back in the day and again later when it was released for free. For some reason I thought this would honor the old point&click adventure games. The story was OK and there were references to Beneath a Steel Sky and it helps a bit if you know the story but it is in no way a prerequisite. There weren't many twists in the plot and it sort of felt like the game spoiled the story by revealing a bit too much before it actually happened, so you kinda knew already what was going to happen next. The game is like the one friend who has already seen the film and for the love of all that's holy, can't keep his/her mouth shut. Still I wanted to return to the game to unfold the whole story. Based on the trailers, I though I wouldn't like the graphics, but I actually ended up enjoying the sort of Borderlands type of look of the game. The UI is hugely simplified version on the classic point&click style and there isn't much to choose from. The usual interactions are look and use. Main focus being on the scanner-hacking device thing that is used to do most of the "puzzles" in the game. You can use the scanner to alter the source code of tech stuff. You can for example change door locks to open on unauthorized interaction etc. There is also some item collection action but not much and there isn't much innovative use of objects: you use them as they were intended. Not very point&clicky.If the UI was simplified, so is the essence of genre: the puzzles. I can safely say that I have never encountered so blatantly obvious puzzles and if the puzzles weren't obvious enough, by checking and talking a bit you were practically told the solution. There was one "harder" scanner puzzle where you needed to transfer one action from one device to another and it involved transferring it through multiple devices to get it where it needed to go. And one where you needed to use certain actions in certain order. But by trial and error they were quite easily solvable and it was quite clear what was required. Usually the hints are subtle but in this game you were at times told EXACTLY what you need to do in order to advance. This was more like an interactive story than actual game. If this was any more obvious and simplified, the game would've had only play button to show next cut scene.If it wasn't enough that you were given overly simple "puzzles", you didn't have any choice where you could go next. First you are in this setting and you need to do this in order to advance. After that there is no need to ever in a million years to go back ever. Most times you can't, even if for some reason unbeknownst to the rest of the world you wanted to. Linear wouldn't be enough. Finnish people call this type of games with a term "putkijuoksu" which translates to "pipe run". It is used to describe the lack of possibilities to affect the path of the game and the selections or "selections" are an illusion and everything is scripted. I.E. there's a pipe, you run in it. You get to the other end. Roll the credits.For hardcore adventure game fans, probably a "no". For laid back adventure action that continues a story from the good old  days (tm), a solid 'yes'.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it.  Being able to wander around Union city and spend time with Foster again was great.  Having a full 3d city with NPCs really adds to things. The hacking system is a smart way to keep the inventory low. If you play a lot of adventures you'll probably pass through this easily. It has a fairly linear structure so it can feel a little at odds with that big city.. IT's there for scale but other than some puzzles that need you to line up hacking hotspots there's very little that makes use of it. The writing is generally really good. Characters feel like themselves and the acting is great throughout. I already felt a powerful sense of nostalgia just booting it up, so my only real complaint is it lent of references to the past a little too much . It's mostly in good fun but it does shortchange some of the new cast in a few places. The story feels smaller and more character focused than the first, but  it works; letting the animation and actors take centre stage.Despite these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it's a great game. I'm so happy to have finally gotten another game in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a worthy successor to the original overall.It follows the spirit of the story, and it is nice to see recurring characters,That said, I was personally unhappy with some of the story decisions. Not quite enough to ruin the game for me, but I do wish it had ended a chapter earlier than it did - the ending was crisper.There is an excellent puzzle mechanic based on Scratch programming, but it is massively under-used in the game - all the puzzles are simple transpositions. I would have liked some optional puzzles to challenge programming skills.The end-game "puzzles" come out of nowhere and are unrelated to any other puzzle in the game - this is jarring and felt  unnecessary - there were plenty of existing mechanics which could have been adapted (like cool programming logic puzzles?)Overall, a game I am glad I played, but with zero replayability as it is entirely linear.I would wait for it to be cheaper, or for a future patch if it extends the content.Final note - releasing without achievements, then saying they are coming in a patch? How will that work - will I get all the achievements as I have already finished the game? Will my save be interrogated to find which achievements I get?

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky has left me utterly captivated and thoroughly impressed in every aspect. It's a game that seamlessly weaves together stunning graphics, an enthralling story, exceptional voice acting, and an incredibly useful hint tool, creating an immersive experience that is nothing short of exceptional.The graphics in Beyond a Steel Sky are nothing less than breathtaking. The game's dystopian world is beautifully realized, with a richly detailed cityscape that feels alive and vibrant. The art style, a perfect blend of futuristic aesthetics and post-apocalyptic grit, adds a unique charm to the game. The attention to detail is remarkable, and it's a visual treat to explore every nook and cranny of Union City.Voice acting in Beyond a Steel Sky is of the highest quality. The characters come to life with expressive and convincing performances, making the story and dialogues feel engaging and genuine. It's a testament to the developers' commitment to delivering a top-notch narrative experience.The story itself is a true gem. It's a masterfully crafted tale that combines elements of cyberpunk, mystery, and social commentary. As Robert Foster, players are drawn into a web of intrigue, conspiracy, and ethical dilemmas that keep you hooked from beginning to end. The game's narrative is rich, thought-provoking, and emotionally resonant, making you genuinely care about the characters and the world they inhabit.One standout feature of Beyond a Steel Sky is the extremely useful hint tool. It's a perfect addition for players who appreciate a gentle nudge in the right direction without spoiling the sense of discovery. This tool ensures that you're never stuck for too long, allowing you to enjoy the game's story and puzzles without excessive frustration.The puzzles themselves are cleverly designed, offering a satisfying challenge without becoming overly obtuse. The combination of inventory-based puzzles, dialogue choices, and environmental interactions keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging.The soundtrack and ambient sound design also deserve a special mention. They create an immersive atmosphere that enhances the overall experience, drawing you deeper into the world of Union City.In conclusion, Beyond a Steel Sky is a masterclass in modern gaming. It's a triumph of storytelling, visual design, voice acting, and game mechanics. If you're a fan of adventure games or simply appreciate a well-crafted narrative experience, this is a must-play title. It's an unforgettable journey through a captivating, dystopian world that leaves a lasting impression. Beyond a Steel Sky sets a high standard for the genre, and it's a game that should not be missed by any discerning gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Quite proficient sequel, depiction of Joey was exactly the same. There weren't too many returning old faces.I encountered multiude of bugs that cut portions of dialog, few plot holes and shameless sequel baiting/teasing.Let's get gist of it.ProsPuzzles were consitent and followed repeated patterns and relied of hacking gimmick, predictable but acceptableVoice acting was fitting to character modelsNeutralsStory was vague, too many plot holes and inconsistentcies shameless sequel baiting at times. Fate of certain characters, parties and former enemies barely got any mention old faces and parties dissapeared forever and state lower class of the city, living flesh. mutations then someConsUnreal engine's camera is tied to sound, more than often camera threw me through wall, essentially muting the dialog.Implied multiple solutions and choices matter. This is a blatant lie and claim made by third rate gaming journalist sites that claim that this is like Telltale games. It's everything but telltale games. IE big mess could've been you hacking the soda machine to create a "big mess" for example. No there is only one solution and its set in stoneChoo Choo, onboard to railroad express. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, intriguing, challenging without being impossible, has a beautifully realized world full of activity, colour, and excitement. Beyond hits all the right notes, and as far as I've played, harkens back to the most beloved moments of the original without being too heavy on fanservice. And most of all: It's set in it's own universe, not one into which ours bleeds un-necessarily.  A bit rough around the edges here and there with camera positioning during some conversations, and a few other minor bugs with NPC collisions and pathfinding. The ability to break out of an automatic pathfinding routine for Foster if he collides with something on his way to carry out an action would be nice, but these can easily be fixes pushed in a patch. Overall, to paraphrase Dai from Normality, another great adventure game: Beyond A Steel Sky has "a spark, I have not seen in ages." and an earnest innocence I've deeply missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is the best game of Revolution Software since Broken Sword II: The Smoking Mirror.It is a fantastic adventure with an exciting story and superb characters! Joey and Foster are back and their verbal interaction between them is funnier than ever. There are also many other characters who are also briliantly written (and played) like, for example, a Wellbeing mantor called Alonso.Union City has changed a lot since the previous game. Forget its omnipresent dirt and rust, Union City is now shiny, clean and sterile! Though Joey had not been its saviour for a long time now as the Council with 5 departments took control of everything. It controls everything, everybody and it does not accept anything excep SMILE! So smile, you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! This is not a point/click adventure but a 3D adventure with the WSAD sytem. But hold on, this ain't also any Telltale-style graphics (pseudo)adventure with a weak gameplay. There are puzzles, there are interesting situations to solve, there is a point/click gameplay in a non-point/click game. This is how a true modern adventure should look like! Though I would not mind adding the point/click system in an update.Gameplay-wise, it is not that difficult game (Beneath a Steel Sky was neither), thogh with the coming ending things will get trickier, and thankfully you will not find here any weird combinations of items. On the other hand, the passages during the ending situations are criminally easy! Your inventory is not as important as your hacked scanner. With it you will be able to hack almost all objects connected to a new AI called MINOS and with an easy drag-drop system change their code and thus their functionality, which can result in funny situations. For example, in a bathroom you can mess around and achieve that by turning on the water tap you activate a bidet.The graphics are not bad but the textures should have had more details and overal things far away from you tend to look a bit blurry. The music is just OK. Not that it is bad at all, it just doesnt have THE character like the music in Beneath a Steel Sky had. The OST is fully orchestral and it's too serious. Also there is not that many places where you can listen to the music as it is used sporadically.There is a lot of bugs, which, I believe, will be fixed in a day one patch (or a patch in general). The buggiest thing in the game is the AI of NPC characters standing or walking around. They just walk and in case they hit something, they just still walk. Sometimes they walk so long that they will walk over the barrier in front of them - think of the horse behaviour in Oblivion or Skyrim.Playing Beneath a Steel Sky before Beyond a Steel Sky is mandatory, as this is a direct sequel and there is a lot of references!....and yes, you can die here!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting story, especially if you have played the prequel, Beneath a steel sky. I really like the artwork of the game, it is cartoony yet detailed, which gives a similar vibe as its predecessors 2D art work. The animations was clunky but that felt intentional, to also refer to the clunky animation style of Beneatth a steel sky. Even though I did enjoy the game there where several irritating bugs that made me a bit frustrated. For instance, the purple gang gang bird, Steve, can get stuck in a paper bin making it impossible to solve that puzzle unless you reload an earlier save point where he is not stuck. The most frustrating problem though is that the mouse handling gets weird with a multi monitor setup, if the mouse ends up on a different screen when the game enters a menu state everything freezes for a about a minute and then the game ends up in the background of what ever other windows are present. Also the route planning algorithms of npc:s seems somewhat broken, and they can easily walk in to each other, or you for that matter, which kind of breaks the players suspension of disbelief. But in general I liked the game.

_childDocuments_.review: BYASS is a sequel to a cult classic, that knows it. If you haven't played the original, BNASS, there'll be tons of references you'll find annoying, to the point of literally making you replay an old level and having a museum level. I  played the original, and I still found them annoying.But that isn't a killer criticism. It takes away from my experience, but it's not fatal. Another ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the voice acting for Foster, the protagonist. He never sounds like someone that's been living in the Mad Max-esque world of the Gap for years, where people survive on the scraps of technology left from the occasional super-city. He sounds, in fact, like a teacher that's trying to be friendly and cool to his students, and the limitations of the facial animation really shows when he does need to emote something.But on to the killer. The biggest criticism I have of BYASS is of the story, starting with the setting. In the original, you got to see an overview of the different levels of society in Union City - you start out in the Industrial Level at the top, proceed to a middle class commercial and residential level, and then the upper-class garden on the bottom. You also got to visit a police station, factory, surgical office and court house, all of which reinforce different parts of the society and how things have gone badly wrong. The policemen are fascistic, the factory owner is cruel and uncaring for his employees, the surgeon happily takes your testicles in payment for a new set of fingerprints, and the judge is straight-up insane.This new Union City, on the other hand...is pretty good. _childDocuments_.review: The original Beyond A Steel Sky is a game I always wanted to play because of all the praise it got but never got around to actually play. So I was excited to see there would be a new Beyond A Steel Sky game but it's not a remake, as I first believed it to be but rather a sequel to the original. I have not yet finished this game due to a game breaking bug after 9-10 hours in, which is also the reason why I'm not recommending the game just yet. My last save is from around 2 hours prior and I might play those parts again if I feel like it and perhaps change my recommendation. Beyond A Steel Sky's intro is pretty weak but that all changes once you actually enter the city. The game made me feel like I was watching some old sci-fi B-movie or sci-fi games in the early 2000's. Union City does feel a bit empty but makes up for it with its beautiful surroundings and buildings. Graphically the game just looks nice and colorful, nothing to complain there.The gameplay is pretty straightforward. Do not expect a classic point & click game in which you have to find items and combine them etc. You do have to collect items but it's all very minimal and the main feature of the game is to use your scanner to hack into electronic devices. Hacking into devices is fun and it allows you to change what the devices do for example; flushing the toilet will activate the shower...The story is nothing special either but it's interesting enough to keep playing. The writing sometimes is a bit cheesy/cringe but I guess a game like this shouldn't be too serious. Overall it's just a fun sci-fi adventure, fans of the genre should like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was announced on the same day I first completed Beneath a Steel Sky, purely by coincidence.  I had sought that game out because of how many adventure game developers cited it as a major influence in their work; particularly James Dearden, the developer of Technobabylon.I'm wondering if Beyond a Steel Sky stands on its own; it maybe does, but you are likely to enjoy it more if you first seek out and this game's predecessor.  Fortunately, it's both free and amazing.I have a feeling that a lot of players have headed into this game without an open mind - with unrealistically high expectations, with preconceived notions about 3D adventure games, with disappointment about the change in format.  I feel that a lot of the negative reviews are unfairly biased.I wasn't sure what to expect, but I am thrilled to report that Beyond a Steel Sky delivers a very solid and satisfying overall experience, sprinkled with some real moments of magic.  It also captures the essence of the original, with memorable characters and sparkling wit, but ominous undertones and high stakes.I am also happy to report that Mrs. Piermont is in the game.  That's all I really wanted, and I got it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice adventure game. Some key points (positive, negative, subjective):- gorgeous graphics- wonderful soundtrack- not fully "point and click" (some walking around required, though paths are mostly short and not intrusive)- mostly linear: contained puzzle solving, no big branching (some prefer this to openness that can be overwhelming, some don't)- some nasty bugs that will hopefully get patched including:-- dialogue that can't be heard (or read) because the camera goes off into a wall somewhere)-- a puzzle that got "stuck" and could be solved after re-starting the game (doing the correct thing before the restart simply would not trigger progress).Personally, I really enjoyed my time in Beyond A Steel Sky's world, and will gladly return if there's a successor.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a fun little game. Good story and dialog and most of the puzzles made sense.I will list the few negatives I ran into though:- FPS Controls are surprisingly bad. Apparently following some janky console control "logic" that is just stupid and prone to flaw.- Keyboard shortcuts were rather illogical. I found myself trying to exit dialogs with ESC often and it instead triggering system menu, usually when the normal skip short-cut was disabled for unknown reasons.- A few graphical artifacts appeared here and there especially with textures around the city limits.- One dialog was broken with wrong camera position and no audio or text.- The game is a little on the short side. _childDocuments_.review: I saw a sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky on steam, and I had to buy it. And I am glad I did. This sequel has been carefully crafted to be a worthy sequel, and in large it succeeds. If you like me played The original Beneath a Steel Sky, then you probably need to be told no more. This game is for you. It is lovingly and carefully designed with throwbacks, cameos, plot hooks and that little kind of inside knowledge that fans of the first game will enjoy. So please, go enjoy it, you're in for a real treat!If you haven't... a recommendation is more difficult. I appreciate the really difficult task the writers had to do to create a story both catering to the fans of the first game; and still be fully coherent to anyone not playing the original. But I'll be frank; I don't think they succeeded. There are just too many holes in this story if you didn't play the first one. So I recommend playing the wonderful Beneath a Steel Sky first. Then play Beyond a Steel Sky. I loved the hacking aspect of the game. The concept of swapping AI directives around was really well done, and I would like to see more of this idea in future games. I didn't like it when the range came into play as a game mechanic (you have to somehow move this device 10 steps to the left before the arbitrary range of your hacking tool accepts it). I hated the controls. The game controls like Assassins Creed on PC, and that's all good... if it had actually managed to reach that level of control quality. It didn't. Movement was slow and choppy. You easily get stuck the terrain forcing you to re-path, NPCs get stuck on you, you moving towards the thing you are inspecting just in front of you collide with NPC and fail, and NPCs move away from you while you are frantically scrolling through your inventory trying to show them something. This all sums up to really bad controls. You play this game despite on how you can control it, not because it feels great to play. I had serious framerate issues at times. And I don't see why I should have with my computer. This isn't crysis anno 1995, it's a standard unity engine game. The game looks awful at minimium settings, especially the faces, but the alternative was 10 FPS if I pointed my camera in the wrong direction. There were bugs. I hope those get fixed. The biggest one was that dialogue/cutscene where the camera decided that it should place itself on the other end of the city. Since that was outside of the range of audio, the audio got lost in that scene. And since the audio got lost, so did the subtitles for it. So I had a long and silly conversation with myself where many important plot points were supposedly revealed. I had to look that scene up on youtube before continuing... :/I don't think Asimov would have approved of the ending. Which is kinda my main objection to this game after finishing it. Explaining this further would be spoiling, so I shall not elaborate. But I feel this ending violated some kind of rule of science fiction storytelling.  Also: I put that  back to a safe state before clicking that , but the game didn't seem to care. I do feel cheated out of a different ending. But despite all that... this was a great game. I wasn't aware the there even was a sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky until today. To the developers - thanks for making my day a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this with saying I've played the original Beneath a Steel Sky fairly recently before playing this game, probably only about a month or so ago. To start with the good, it looks pretty good as far as translating a comic artstyle to 3d, very easy to favorably compare it to The Walking Dead and other TellTale counterparts. Visuals in general are pretty good. The music was pretty good, and I enjoyed most of the jokes in the game, very similar in tone to the original. In moving to 3d it's avoided one major pitfall of point and clicks of the past of difficult to find interactables by making a prompt pop up when hovering the camera near items. The core story is much more coherent and follows a clear logical path unlike it's predecessors fairly out of the blue weird ending.  Now for the bad, longer list. In the original game, Foster moved pretty slowly but this issue could be mostly remedied by increasing game speed, an in game option. In this game no such option exists and Fosters normal walkspeed is a brutally slow crawl while his run is at best a brisk walking speed. The actual speed of the run isn't that annoying but the fact that his run speed isn't the default and having to hold to always hold a button while moving is irritating. I encountered a small number of bugs in my playthrough including : texture popping (most noticeably with hologram signs that would regularly remain blurry for a period before eventually sharpening to the correct resolution.), issues in conversations where the camera wouldn't zoom in correctly to the characters faces and would focus on a wall or corner nearby, issues in conversations where if the previous was happening the audio could sound faded and distant, npc's walking in straight line directly into Foster during his conversations and vice versa if an npc was infront of the item I would try to interact with, animation bugs,etc. One major concern I have is how hard the game leans on it's predecessor. If I hadn't played the original it would have been confusing to understand many of the in-game terminology and plot threads. By that same token, the amount of callbacks is so large it really starts to feel absurd. At one point the game even gives you a whole area filled with nothing but callbacks to interactions and events of the first game and it just feels like blatant nostalgia pandering. All the leaning on the original starts to make the game feel more like a remake almost than a true sequel with how many recurring characters, themes, places, objects pop up (which is ironic as an in game conversation states that a remake could only improve on an old concept but wouldn't stand on it's own).  While the game adds one major gameplay change to the original in having a hacking device you acquire early on, it does painfully little with it having it only incorporated in the simplest of puzzles. The puzzles in this game are not much of an improvement from the original game either, they are all tremendously simple.  I mentioned earlier that the story follows a clear path but this is kind of to it's detriment especially at the end. The ending sequence, while having some really cool visual elements lacks the impact it should have had with it's awkwardly written arguments, embarrassingly simple puzzles that take out any real satisfaction of completing, and when the truth is finally unraveled  of what's happening in Union City, it's a fairly common scifi plot thread taken from the likes of Le Guin and others. If you aren't looking for a huge nostalgia trip of references to the first game and really loved it's humorous dialogue and setting, I absolutely can't recommend this game. It has no identity unto itself and fails to improve significantly in writing,puzzles, gameplay, or any aspect other than visuals and modern QoL features that the previous game had.

_childDocuments_.review: From the makers of the Broken Sword games, it is natural to expect a story filled with mystery, intrigue, interesting but eccentric characters and some humour.What I got was some eccentric but not very memorable characters and too much humour that wasn't even funny.  For a story about a kid being abducted and taken to some city, one would expect mystery and intrigue.  Sadly there is none.The best adventure games are the ones that keep you moving from place to place quite quickly and enabling you to make headway in unravelling the mystery.  In the hour and half I played this game, virtually all the playtime was outside the entrance to the city.  Staying in the same place for ages and ages and running around asking the same characters different things is not fun.  It was one of the most boring experiences playing an adventure game I've ever had.My recommendation - stick to Broken Sword games 1, 2 and 5.  They are classics.  They won't put you to sleep like this game will.
