The world and society in which this story takes place in was well created.  The puzzles were very much in line with the story and not out of place puzzles for puzzles sake.  They were not difficult but still fun to solve.  I very much enjoyed this game.  While there were some story plot holes and inconsistencies everything was still very cohesive.  Most games with high production values skimp on the story and characters and invest everything into graphics - this game does not.  They achieved a good balance among the various elements that make for a very fun, enjoyable, and appealing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a worthy successor. LOTS of callbacks, with an ending that goes bittersweet-preachy-downer-meh. Interesting concept, well told, with a twist that you can see coming if you pay attention to the dialogue throughout. Definitely recommend, although TBTH the 3rd person gameplay really adds nothing to the adventure-game genre xD. Keyboard controls felt totally unneccessary. The fact that is the ONLY word of caution I have for you should be a good sign about the overall quality!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original, then you will want to play the sequel, plenty of throw backs etc to wet the appetite with. If you didn't play the original, it's available free on Steam, but it's still a game worth playing, you just might not appreciate some of the nuances as much. It's been refreshing to play a good old school point and click adventure but with that modern twist, though there is a tiny part of me that would love to have seen a 2D platform version, but that's neither here nor there really. There's some replayability, without being bombarded with an infinite amount of endings and the added dev commentary is a nice touch so long as you took in the story/conversations first time around. I hope this game becomes successful enough for a third installment somewhere down the line... Oh and THANK YOU for staying away from a DLC model (for now 29/07/21). 5* 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... Just finished playing through Beyond a Steel Sky and I have to say that it was an incredible experience.I didn't pay full price but I can say that after finishing it the game is well worth it even without a discount, for a 15 to 20 hour story drive game it ticks all the boxes.Really hoping that they make a sequel and I feel that there is enough there the creators to do this.Fantastic, please make more!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: (Warning lazily formatted text block ahead!)Usually when it comes to sequels, especially sequels that are release so long after the first part, I have very low expectations.I have very little to complain about the graphics; I'm not fond of the cel-shader, but in this game it was, ahem, quite adequate.Soundwise the game also holds its own. Only thing to complain about stems from a purely audio production nerd kind of place; I noticed that some of the ADR was a bit mismatched tonally, sometimes an EQ (or perhaps a mic) was mismatched, other times the accoustics or post processing, but then again, this seems to happen with most games with lots of voice-over.The puzzles in the game range from very easy to "Oh come on!", the latter namely being the last QDos-puzzle which I will spoil for you here:  I was expecting some sort of semi-complex maths puzzle, or something.One little irritant for me was the Milo-part of the game. I had totally forgotten about Milo and why I should even care, so at the reuinion I was a bit "Meh", can't we keep mucking about in the city a little longer? :-) Maybe a flashback or dream sequence in the middle of the game to refresh why we are so adamant to get to him. Maybe I was just smitten with Orana and forgot all about kids. :-)And lastly, the hack-tool had so much more potential for fun, but that road was not taken. Sure it was fun hacking all the signs and what not, but there could have been more, like opening secret areas (there might have been, but I missed it) and getting an achievement for extracting 100+ soda cans (Yep, I tried that one), or something.This review from a guy who played Beneath A Steel Sky on the Amiga back when it was released and has that memory incorporated in his spine.Verdict:Nice game; Get it, if not for nostalgia, then just because it's a decent game, and if you haven't played Beneath a Steel Sky; Geez, go play that one first, it's a classic, and the lore will be useful in Beyond a Stel Sky.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first original game, despite it being so many years ago,  I enjoyed the first very much and to be truthful, did not expect to enjoy this as much as the 1st...  Well I was proven wrong.  I did enjoy this a lot, it took me a bit of time to get used to the way things worked, but it did bring back some memories of the first one.  The graphics were pretty good (despite seeing inside Foster at times!!!!), one part was shockingly funny,  This does get you to think what you are doing and sometimes without realising, it does drop hints on your next move sometimes.  It's a pleasant game,  If you ever played the 1st one, then I think you will LOVE this one, this is also great for the ones who have never played the first game.  I prefer point and click games and would highly recommend this game.  I thoroughly enjoyed working out each stage and interacting with the other characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, non complicated, straight forward game - similar to games like Dreamfall and Grim Fandango. The story is good, has a very straight forward and linear playthough, with a good ending. Worth playing if you enjoy chill games with puzzles, nice visuals and a good Hints system to guide you. There are occasional bugs, but nothing major or too troublesome. I would recommend this game at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I put more then 8 hours into this game. Probably like 13 or 14. All in all I enjoyed it. I've played the original about 10 times so I was familiar with some of the games terms/references I guess you could say. I wish it would have been a little more expansive to say, although the original was a point and click adventure, and this although still sort of the same did have more of explorative aesthetic to it. A full on open world Beyond A Steel Sky would be sweet though. Maybe even some sort of expansion/dlc in the future. I may have some achievements I can go back and complete, but I'll save all that for later. Maybe they can come back and kidnap the Milos kid or something and then we can have another go. lol!! A++ :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original when I was a kid and I was very dubious about returning to something lodged deeply in nostalgia, was also wary about it being a more modern 3D approach. Thankfully all my doubts were unfounded as the game is just absolutely fantastic. Great puzzles, great storytelling, just a great adventure that feels both modern but also a beautiful tribute to my point and click childhood. Also I don't think the screenshots do justice to how great the visual style of the game is, with a great comic book feel throughout. Great to see Revolution doing what they do best.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of the original, I was a little worried going into this...I needn't have been! Beyond A Steel Sky is a respectful, rich and intelligent new chapter which moves the story we started in the original along nicely.Excellent puzzles (though not tooooo challenging!) and some new mechanics, plus a continuation of things like LINCSpace give an overall cosy feeling to this dark allegory on some of the less excellent aspects of human nature, control and societal engineering.The few bugs I encountered were by no means game breaking: - NPCs have a tendency to get in the way, and can also end up playing unexpected cameos in key dialog - Camera clipping is an issue.. I kept seeing fosters disembodied teeth when the camera was too close - Some of the MINOS screens do not work great with a controller (I'm looking at you, lab control console!)Overall an excellent game - can't wait to see where the story goes next!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: For people who have played the game this one is based on (with it's pixel graphics charme) this game here brings back memories in a totally new full 3D cell shaded comic look. You meet old friends, make your way through some scenes of that big automated city again, being on the hunt once again for a yet unknown conspiracy.Puzzle design is of middle level difficulty, sometimes you have to interact with things you thought you'd already know a second time to trigger some story progess, or try every kind of interaction possible to accidentally get the one which pushes you further. But mostly fair.Technically I had to lower the graphics settings from extreme to high for my RX 580 to not let it overheat for a longer time on a level of about 70 to 80 degrees celsius, but have a bearable level of about 50 to 60 degrees celsius (It's a cel shaded environment anyhow, so you don't lose too much detail by doing it). Sometimes some NPCs tend to get stuck in some areas, so when that happens you better have a savegame ready, since you can't kick NPCs free of their miserable locations, and regular savegaming strongly recommended to avoid stuck NPC situations.Only the humour is a bit different and not necessary omnipresent, though where funny things happen they make you 'whow, what? yeah, ookay, haha!'. And the things you can interact seem not always deliver something worth for story or atmosphere. But that's criticism on high level, all in everything the game does things right.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody good little game. It feels like a solid sequel to the original while making it a bit more modern in design. Sometimes not ideal since the interaction points move with people and objects and that can make it hard to access at times but that's about the only thing I can think of as a negative.Oh and they pronounce 'aluminium' correctly! That's reason enough to buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing beneath a steel sky as a kid back in the 90's and it left me with a taste for dystopian fiction with its strong narrative and likeable characters. The sequel 20+ years in the making was worth the wait, in my opinion. Its narrative is strong and provides us with multiple interesting characters that are a pleasure to interact with. There are plenty of nods back to beneath a steel sky and good amounts of humor and dark moments making it perfectly balanced in its setting. The ending also got to me in no small way.There are a few minor technical issues such as the occasional FPS drop but then again I'm running it on near ultra on a somewhat old PC. Overall, the art style, the story, the characters and the choices are fantastic and I thoroughly recommend playing the game and its prequel if you have a love for dystopian and utopian fiction.I hope some day to return to Union city again for another adventure as it is one of the more unique settings in post apocalypse futures in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first ever fully immersive 3D game I've ever played that follows the game mechanics of classical point & click style adventure games. I was hoping for something new, but was completely gobsmacked by what this game offers. It's easy to become completely absorbed into the story, because it's both captive, well worked out and very beautiful. To finish it off, the music supports the game very well, and is constructed in such a way that it feels like you're pretty much in a directed movie: it adapts to the scene seamlessly. Music isn't even the right word, score is better. 14 hours into it (could've been faster but I don't like to rush this kind of game) and I'm still a bit mesmerized by it all. Very fat thumbs up for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, graphics are great, characters are interesting... the only thing I found was that is was really easy to complete.Normally I would get stuck somewhere in these types of games, but not this one and I found the challenges/puzzles were not very challenging.When you are higher in the city, looking down... the city does feel empty, as you don't see people moving around... nothing really, so that was a downside... no life.Other than that, I can't fault it, a nicely polished game that felt short but was fun whilst it lasted.Recommended to all.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: 26 Years later one of my favorite point and click game "Beneath A Steel Sky" got a sequel It really deserved. Robert Foster and Joey are back and they are still very iconic and funny duo. This sequal is a decent one, very interesting story and characters. Returning to Union City after all those years is a nice expierence. No stupid puzzles without any sense through the whole game. Cel shading graphic is a top notch stuff, optimilisation is great, no problems at all with amxed settings on 4k resolution. It is fully voice acted, which is great, maybe thats why game costs a little more than average point click game. Not much a choices n consequences in game though, its very linear all the way to the end. I highly recommend it to the fans of the older part. DO NOT PLAY this without playing through Beneath A Steel Sky first, its a sequel so story its very connected to the first part
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit. It's predecessor, Beneath the Steel Sky was one of those point and click games  that captured my imagination when I was younger. This definitely captures the feel of that game, while adding an extra dimension. This is put together really well, looks decent and runs well. I would recommend this mostly to fans of the original game, or fans of point and click adventures of that era. Other than that, I wouldn't say it stands out a lot, aside from the fact that there are very few games made like this these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original as a kid (and with near zero English) and wasn't even aware a sequel was made until it popped up during the Steam discovery queue. Since I've fond memories of the original and it was discounted I gave it a go.Overall it's an average game.People who actually played / liked the original will like it, but everyone else will forget it 6 months later.Graphics are decent, assuming you like cell-shading (except Foster's face, that's just atrocious).Voice acting is good, music is good (I felt some heavy Stargate vibes).Story is average. Obviously more enjoyable if you played the original, but I admit I barely remember the details of the the original's story after 2 decades.I would prefer if you could skip some dialogue or (all) cutscenes. I started a second playthrough for that one achievement (although I feel that it is fully forced to have to play through the entire game for a single achievement), but it was so slow and since I exhausted all dialogue options the first time there was literally nothing new, so I gave up. Maybe they add this in a patch later.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful movments. great look, its a simple liner game my only beef is it is too pricey for a liner game.  I would love to see them make a Open World RPG based off this world, i think that would be enjoyable, right now it is a quasi open world problem solving game that takes you back to old point and click adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic!!! I am a fan of point and click games, besides wadeyet retro-style games, there is not a lot of recent games that really evoke the old school writing and adventure feel. This game does. the story is great. it holds true to the original game with it's humor and even some puzzle solutions that are similar to the first game. The voice acting is great and visuals are as well. I hope they keep doing more games like this, I will immediately buy whatever other game they come out with. I'm still playing it so I can comment on length but I already have 9 hours and the game keeps getting better!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Got 17 hrs in on this game and am stuck as usual but I don't mind as the graphics and the crack between Foster and Joey are great. Great that there is a hint system on board to help but I ain't using it as I would rather spend an hour trying to figure out a way forward than take the easy way out. The crack between Joey and Foster stays true to first game Beneath A Steel Sky which I played way back in 90's. Love the artistic graphics as well that remind me so much of the Broken Sword series. This is a must get game if you like adventure and problem solving games.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: An adventure in the true spirit of the original. It looks beautiful and the setting, story, message is good. So it hits all the major targets. The puzzles were middle of the road. They weren't tough enough, but they were innovative.The voice acting, play time and world size were its biggest weaknesses. The voice acting being the greatest let down. Delivery just felt unconvincing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Following up a game as influential and unforgettable as Beneath a Steel Sky after over 20 years of fans ( like me) waiting was always going to be a major ask and a lot of pressure but I actually think they have done a pretty good job.It was never going to be so influential as BASS but it's pretty close.It has the same Dave Gibbons art style (Watchman, Batman Black and White etc) and it's written by Kevin Beimers ( The Bunker, Hector etc) so it has some talented people behind it.The story nicely follows on from BASS and the art style and humour is still there and the game is excellent and as long as your like stories set in a dystopian future with a point and click element , you are going to love it , I have.One thing I will add , if you are playing this on an average laptop, you will find the graphics won't be anywhere near as impressive and the frame rate will be a bit disapointing , so check the specs and to really enjoy this game , be at the upper end of the requirements as I was average 16 fps.I will add that if you haven't played the original game , it's free on GOG and you don't actually need to play it as the opening comic book style introduction , explains the story quite well.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the best point-and-click games there is. I played Beneath a Steel Sky as a kid and was totally in love with the setting and story. Seeing not a remaster, but a SEQUEL?!?! It blew my mind. This game is hilarious and there is a lot of details that you can stumble upon, miss the first playthrough and discover the second time, and ones that act as funny references (the Monty Python robot shell made me almost pee my pants from laughing). Any glitches I encountered were very minor and quickly solvable (getting stuck in some spots or some subtitle issues). Now I am crossing my fingers, toes, and eyes that they make a third game for the series soon!!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful sequel and conclusion from this LONG (26 years) awaited sequel. The complexities of humanity and morality explained in an incredibly satisfying and entertaining format. The 3D setting of this subtracts nothing at all from the original and it does an amazing job of recreating the feel, intensity and style of the 1994 Beneath A Steel Sky.I sent an email to Revolution software about 4 years ago asking if a sequel for this game would ever be made and I'm over the moon to see it come to fruition in such a beautiful way.If you're a fan of Adventure Games, Story Line or Post-apocalyptic Dystopia, give this game a go (and definitely check out the original, Beneath A Steel Sky from 1994, free on GOG and Steam.)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of Beneath a Steel Sky, this is 100% worth playing. It's not a long game, but it has a lot of references back to the original game & select characters, with all the same witty humour (and the soundtrack in one particular place as well which was a pleasant surprise) that was there in the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game which reminds me so much of the point and click golden age. I love how this game looks and feels. intuitive to play and has an interesting story laced with some light puzzle solving.the art style is brilliant and fits the game like a glove.the music was great through out, at times it blended so well you didn't really notice it but would notice its absence.If you like adventure games and wish to relive some of that point and click magic, this is the game for you.I truly hope we'll see more adventure games like this.* There's a few kinks but nothing game-breaking. it would sometimes crash but fortunately a restart of the game was all I needed to do.I only wish there was more of the story to explore and do, maybe go a bit deeper on some subjects but that is said because I loved the game so much I want more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A great game and successor to the original. The nods to the original game are well done and doesn't distract from this one. I would recommend playing the original, Beneath a Steel Sky since it's free on Steam & GOG, or watching it on youtube so those moments don't pass you by. There are bugs a plenty still, one I had to revert to an older save just to get around my problem and a few silly ones but nothing that ruins the game. You will run into people and d-RYD that block your path and are more of nuisance than anything else. Aside from that, the art style, music and voice performances are all well done and I do hope these small issues get fixed than it will be close to perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This game really came out of nowhere for me. A sequel to one of the Amiga era's more memorable point 'n click adventure games 26 years later? I didn't even know Revolution Software were still around. But I'm more than happy to continue the story of Robert Foster and Union City.The game brings the point 'n click game genre nicely into 2020 with stylized comic book like visuals in a 3D enviroment and a great story picking up where the first game left of all those years ago.The story both humorous and filled with some great social commentary is the main selling point of the game. You don't really play adventure games expecting to get knocked of your feet by the visuals or swept away by a sweeping epic musical score.The puzzles are often relativly logical and the 'hacking' mechanic brings a fresh, fun new set of challenges.After what seems like an initially quite buggy launch responsible for negative reviews the developers have been hard at work and the game is now (December 2020) in a nice stable and enjoyable state.I heartly recomend the game to any lover of the point and click genre, if you played the orginal Beneath a Steel Sky back in the day it should be a high priority buy.I hope we don't have to wait another 26 years for the next chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Good sequel for someone who played this on the Amiga in 1995. Good references to former game, and development of storyline. I think the game is equally relevant today with the increased use of algorithms and digitalisation of society. The puzzles and hacking are good - but sidequests, equipment and just walking around and being able to manipulate more in the city could have made the game better.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of Revolution and all their work, dating all the way back to Lure of the Temptress.Loved the original game in the series and took me a while to play through back in 1994. I'm pleased to see that the follow-up has the same humour and charm as its predecessor.Only 3 hours in but can definitely recommend to adventure game fans!*Edit* Finished the game and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely one of my favourites this year, great interactive story.It felt cinematic at times with the music and visuals, Great voice acting, humour and a storyline which made it difficult to put down, like a good detective story looking for clues.  I thought there would be more comic book panels like the trailer, but that is only right at the beginning introducing the story, after that it's a Borderlands style cell shaded world, which looks great.A lot of puzzles can be solved with your 'tri-corder' gadget which can swap programming between machines close to each other, and a few others are solved with another trusty piece of equipment. I'll be honest I did get stuck a couple of times, and there's an in-built help guide for that.I didn't want the game to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A nice trip to the memory lane mixed up with a great history to continue the legacy. Funny dialogs, as hard to play as you want (the hints system is great for newcommers). A bit of glitchy cameras on dialogs over the first release, but last patch I think that already fixed all of them.  I Hope that we can get a further games on this nice a funny world.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A fitting sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky.The story is interesting and engaging.  The graphics are beautiful; it was neat to see Union City rendered in 3D.  The soundtrack is much more cinematic than the original, and subtly references previous themes in moments.  The game makes enough callbacks and references to the original to please fans, without overly relying on nostalgia.The reprogramming mechanic is fun and interesting, but perhaps a bit gimmicky.  The game pace can bog down just due to the sheer amount of walking you must do in 3D.  I got stuck a few times, trying to figure out where to go next; this is a common pitfall in adventure games, though.  If you think about recent dialog and information, it does steer you in the right direction; in the end, I didn't need any hints or cheats.  I also soft locked the game once, due to a NPC movement bug; I recommend saving relatively often.I anticipated the direction of the story from nearly the beginning of the game, thinking about the themes and ending of the original.  The stories of both games complement each other as an exploration of the nature of humanity and the machines we create.  I walked away from this game with something to think about.Overall, I think this game is not as good as the original, but definitely still worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Good storytelling (if slightly heavy-handed at times), challenging puzzles, plenty of humour, and a host of memorable characters brings Union City to life like never before. Well made sequel, with oodles of things to do and places to discover, especially if you played the original (which you definitely should).Future classic!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome. The story got me hooked right from the beginning and the puzzles were logical and fun. The music and atmosphere of this game is top notch. I played it for hours at a time, which is rare for me these days, and played it all the way to the end. I whole-heartedly recommend this game to everyone who's interested in adventure games!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! I didn't know about the first game before playing this (although it became obvious in the game that there had been an earlier game), but it was still an entertaining game. The puzzles were generally not hard to solve, although there were some that were a little more difficult. They were a good level for me - I don't like it when puzzles are really tough or illogical. Graphics were good, and I liked the variety of accents within the game. Gameplay was excellent - he moved as I would expect, and responded as I'd expect to the mouse movement/keyboard presses.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: play Beneath a Steel Sky firstAt first i was not aware that this game is a sequel to some past century fossil, but museum location made it painfully obvious - references were loud, clear and meaningless. So it's obligatory to play original game. Beneath a Steel Sky (the original) is not up to classic 90xx games like Space Quest but still enjoyable. It's not as heavily censured and sugar-coated as modern games - you can actually die, kill, utterly destroy someone's life and even see naked pixelated boobs. Good stuff. But game had some plot holes and, sadly, those plot holes are fully manifested in a sequel.This game is actually better compared to original and, if references were explained, did not require fisrt game at all. Yes, story is a continuation, but it's complete and self-sufficient.Really good game. Clearly worth spent time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Though I enjoyed the game the vibe was so different from first game at some point I started having doubts if this game can be classified as "cyberpunk". And Foster had a major personality change from big cool silent type to overexcited chatty goodie two-shoes, who at times seems a bit simple to put it mildly. Puzzles and especially hacking puzzles were good, dialogs were ok with some funny interactions, story was solid but final half an hour of gameplay was incredibly boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original but was aware of it. As a fan of Telltale games I thought I'd try this and it is leagues ahead in terms of the engine and gameplay.It's not an easy adventure game, you have to think things through and do a number of tasks to reach your goal. This goes back to the difficulty levels of classic adventures.It looks really nice, runs well and the load time is very impressive. This is a well optimised game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe this game, it'd be following and taking part in a story through dialogue and problem/puzzle solving instead of outright fighting. In a way it reminded me of several games, for example: the movement system reminded me of  the problem and puzzle solving reminded me of  and the  games, and the art/visual style reminded me of  I loved the world, the mix of desolate wasteland, beautiful, clean, and sci-fi city, and bits of the older city and tech scattered about. The only criticism I have is about the animations. Especially the facial animations. They're a little jumpy and the face doesn't always seem to match the emotion in the character's voice or atmosphere. But I really enjoyed the voice acting. Also, my buddy Syber and I will never forget the name "Schnipple." Thanks. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute LOVE this game so far!  It's everything I could have hoped for, down to all the references to Beneath a Steel Sky.  Excellent voice acting and dialog, beautiful artwork and music, and a spooky dystopian aesthetic that sticks with you.Only minor complaints with slow walking speed and no option for visible mouse cursor (plays better with controller for that reason), and a couple small bugs; but otherwise wonderful!Highly recommend for any fans of scifi (especially cyberpunk)!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A more than worthy sequel, that acknowledges the technical advances between the first game and this one, and uses it to their advantage. Good story, beautiful art direction, witty dialogue and characters. Good length as well (16 hours, in my case) A few bugs here and there, but nothing game-breaking. Very recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Well where to start, as many remasters are being touted these days - this is the game as the developers envisioned in 1994 merely limited by the technology of the time.To anyone who was fond memories of Beneath a Steel Sky, Beyond will bring back a Nostalgic trip that really brings the game to life. Many different points of familiarity are present right throughout the game and it's an exciting feeling that makes it as if you never left Union City.The challenges require great thought but the point and click nature of the game makes them accessible to all players much in the same way the original did, some points in the game get caught up in the complexity of the hacking mechanic and often there are too many red herrings for the player to be able to be confident of the path they're taking - in some cases this can lead to frustrating mistakes that require backtracking through tasks and in my play through even cause various mechanics to stop working requiring a restart of the game.With that said, when players are stuck they're likely to explore the world that they've been in already which really presents the overall lack of polish in many aspects. Dialogue elements that aren't updated when the player discovers new information or hint's being given before certain dialogue has even been engaged. Whilst these aren't game breaking problems they detract from the immersion and create frustration when the player wants confidence that they're progressing.Put the very minor shortcomings to the side and this game is an exceptional breath of life back into the original, capturing very well the atmosphere and the life of the original game. A MUST play for anyone who played the original, and for those who haven't I would highly recommend picking up the original game (For Free on Steam) to play through first as the new game will feel so much more familiar.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good, fun time (for people that enjoy the point-and-click genre) but nothing more than that. I would recommend getting it when it's on sale. To give some more details: I completed it in +- 10 hours, so it's not very long. The story has a lot of promise, but the ending doesn't deliver. I was left somewhat unsatisfied, wondering about unfilled plot holes. It felt like it was building up to something that was perhaps rushed in the final act. The main character (Foster) doesn't show any real character growth . There were also some bugs left (at the time of writing) that include clipping and odd angles (and achievements don't work), but it's nothing game-breaking, and I believe there's still some upcoming patches that will hopefully fix these!  The gameplay is pretty fun but (most of the time) not very challenging. That being as it may, the characters (especially Joey) are really fun, and the world they've built (Union City) is really something creative and special. It felt a lot more alive than it did in the prequel (Beneath a Steel Sky). The hacking mechanic they made was a cool part of the gameplay and the puzzles were at least more involved than the simple "combine X with Y" that's the cornerstone of most point-and-click games. All in all, definitely recommend for a short but fun time but don't play it expecting anything groundbreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with other posts, play the first one before getting this one and it will make way more sense. (it's really old but power through it LOL)  I downloaded the first one for free yesterday and played through just so that I could get this one today.  I really love the story, it's great!  The artwork is amazing, voice acting was really good.  It's pretty linear but really enjoyable.  I only ran into a few minor bugs, but they were hardly worth a mention.  Buy this game, it's great!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I never played adventure games when I was growing up, but the Broken Sword series got me into the genre and naturally I had to try the creator's latest game Beyond a Steel Sky.The 3D world you explore, for all of it's occasional hiccups like a mysterious floating sausage or your character getting stuck on the geometry, gave me a feeling of adventure and exploration similar to what you would find in  most adventure games.  The world feels like a natural evolution of the point and click genre into 3D space.  There's still plenty of dialogue to hear and plenty of puzzles to solve as well, but it certainly felt like there was maybe a little less game as a trade off for this third dimension.  Puzzles have a helpful hint system if you ever get stuck.  Dialogue is offbeat and light (as is the art direction) to offset the grim aspects of the world.It was all over sooner than I wanted it to be, which is praise as much as it is critique.  If you like the developers other games I recommend this one.  If you're uncertain I suggest trying out some of the older (and cheaper) games first to see if this is your style.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited for this game for so long, and it was worth the wait. It was good to see some old characters like Joey and Mrs Piermont. I missed  Hobbins and seeing Lamb working in the sewage plant, but Mentor Alonso was a suitably creepy adversary. And there was even a droid channelling the Black Knight from Monty Python and the Holy Grail.But I would still like to see the original game re-imagined with modern graphics. I bet there are plenty of people who'd buy it. I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is my fourth or fifth Revolution game, and they never disappoint. The storycrafting of this company is second to none. With BASS2, they've taken their production values up a notch, using the Unreal engine and shipping on modern platforms like Apple TV, iOS and Windows 10. The game is visually enticing and the mechanics of the puzzles are fun and challenging with fewer opportunities for you to get right and truly "stuck".
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A very strong introduction lays the foundation for this game. While the story in the mid-game feels a little bit rushed - like it could do with an extra scene or two to help the story progression feel a little smoother - it returns to a very strong finale.The puzzle-solving mechanic in this game - the use of your hack-tool to mess around with the systems of Union City - feels quite unique and in a couple parts of the game allows for a lot of playing about for your own amusement. However the challenge of these puzzles can be inconsistent, ranging from quite easy to - on a couple occasions - annoyingly obtuse. When they get the challenge just right, however, it feels very satisfying.There are some minor graphical issues, such as textures clipping through each other, but visually it's very satisfying and the backdrops are vast and detailed, really immersing the player into Union City.Conversation segments can suffer from strange camera angles and you'll occasionally find that you're talking to a wall but this doesn't happen too frequently. Otherwise the branching conversations feel very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great point and click adventure game. The puzzles aren't too difficult, a welcome relief from the nonsensical puzzles of the old school PnC's. I would highly recommend playing the first game. While chronologically the game takes place much later, the story is told as if you just finished the first one. You'll want to know the characters' histories and relationships before diving in. If you disregard this and play this without having played the first, you'll think you're fine in the beginning. But the mid- and end-game are so much better having played the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I just finished the game for the first time...Let me start of with the fact that overall, Beyond a Steel Sky is a fun to play game, with a good story but also plenty of bugs, small & big.Biggest issue I encountered were a couple of UE4 Fatal Error crashes, random though, repeating the same exact steps again did not repeat the fatal error crash and allowed for the game to continue.Now, with that's out of the way, here's what I actually liked about the game...The game tells a good story that ties well into the first game, Beneath a Steel Sky (very, very old game), visually the game looks very good, apart for a few visual glitches and bugs, the combined Keyboard + Mouse controls works really well and the game controls are very easy to master, although I can't testify if that is still the case when using a controller.Voice acting was really good too, no complaints there, wasn't perfect, also glitched from time to time with lines not playing, which I understand should have been fixed in Patch #2.I also have a few negative things to point out, other than the glitches, bugs & crashes, for once, the limited number of save slots makes it a little hard sometime to come back from crashes or major glitches, apart from that, I would have appreciated a better inventory management system, for example not having to open the menu just to check what's in your inventory and the items descriptions would have been nice.Overall, I can recommend Beyond a Steel Sky if you are an hardcore adventure gamer or if you played and loved the original Beneath a Steel Sky game. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is the sequel to Revolution Software’s 1994 point-and-click adventure game Beneath a Steel Sky. However, it is still very accessible to newcomers (the opening cutscene includes a full recap of the previous game).If you've ever played any of the Broken Sword games you'll know what to expect: an engaging story with a great sense of humour, enjoyable - and logical - puzzles, quirky NPCs, a rich soundtrack, and detailed environments to explore. I did experience a few bugs while playing, but there have already been two major patches released, with another patch in the pipeline to add achievements.3D has become a bit of a taboo word in the adventure gaming community, but Beyond a Steel Sky makes good use of Unreal Engine 4; the cel/toon-shaded graphics look great (comic book artist Dave Gibbons of Watchmen fame has returned to provide art direction), and the new hacking tool adds an extra layer to the more traditional inventory-based puzzles.The voice acting sounds really good too and the banter between protagonist Foster and his robot sidekick Joey is hilarious. There have been some truly excellent games released in 2020; Beyond a Steel Sky is refreshing because it never takes itself too seriously and makes a sincere effort to make players laugh and smile.You can check out my full review on Alternative Magazine Online:
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A big improvement from the last Broken Sword. Better art and voice acting, slightly better animation.Still, pretty light on actual puzzling. The hacking tool setup is good but never exceeds the complexity of the tutorial puzzle. If anything, the game gets way simpler after about halfway.Probably worth 10 hours of your time in these lean adventure game times though.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky was an enjoyable experience, I'll admit I was disheartened when the game crashed three times but regardless I was able to complete it without any bugs that required a restart (or reverting to a much earlier save). I haven't replayed Beneath a Steel Sky since the early 2000's so my nostalgia glasses may be a bit more fogged up than others but being back in Union City was an awesome an experience, and while some may have found the hacking and crowbar use annoying I found myself more interested to see what I could screw with next. I'm not going to score it because scoring systems are for IGN gurus who hate water. it was either fun, or it wasn't and Beyond A Steel Sky was fun.With any luck we wont have to wait another decade or two for Revolution to continue Foster's story... with.any.luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if it was just on my end, but halfway through the game, the animations started getting really buggy. HOWEVER, while a little distracting, I was still able to enjoy and appreciate the plotline and general mechanics of the game. It was definitely a philosophical experience and 10/10 would recommend the existential crisis I felt afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: So beneath a steel sky is one of those games that I have had fond memories of ever since i played it. Gritty, challenging and with some really interesting world building. Beyond kind of builds upon that and adds some interesting mechanics in its own right. i quite liked the hacking in the game, and part of me wishes they had taken it further then they did. The game has some flaws, controls are a little janky at times and I found the avatar a little slow moving on occasion. I wouldn't have minded a little more challenge to the game, a lot of the puzzles were a little too obvious. Voice acting was a kind of all over the place. And the ending, was TBH a little disappointing. but despite this, the game was fun, the story engaged me right to the end and I had a lot of fun playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Carrying on from one of the best point & click adventures I have played. The good old days when games were games rather than short Movies or Multiplayer C**p. Revolution are a leader in this style! we just don't see enough these days. Gone 3D as well which adds much more ideas & fun. Recommend if your Oldskool.  More.. More.. Pleeeease.....
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beneath a Steel Sky was a masterpiece when I first played it, and the new game is just as good. It was never about crazy hard puzzles, great graphics performance or rewarding gameplay; it was all about the characters and the story. Beyond a Steel Sky stays true to this legacy, and delievers exactly what it should. That being said, if dont have the patience for story-based puzzle games, its probably not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I was 11 when I got the first one at release and it immediatly became one of my all time favorite.I 've played it so much that when I played Beneath a steel sky last week it was still fresh in my mind.So you could say I was waiting for this sequel and those 26 years were worth the wait.Where to begin ? Graphics are great and are really a faithful 3D transposition of Dave Gibbons artwork and some sceneries are real eye candies. Writing is great and dialogues are more than often funny and in the tone of the first game.Controls / Gameplay were really good and is point & click worthy.Last but not least, the story picks up 10 years after the end of the previous opus and continuity is respected. It digs into science fiction classics like Brave new world, This perfect day, 1984 and delivers a story that make you think about your condition, society and other.I really enjoyed my reunion with Foster and, hopefully, I will not have to wait 26 years for another story in Union city.Ps : Thanks for the Linux port, greatly appreciated even if it should have been tested a little more (random crashes)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: To anyone who has played Beneath A Steel Sky, this log-awaited follow up is worth the wait. Sure, the game's execution is a bit hokey in parts (there are a few glitches here and there, especially of a graphical nature) but nothing that breaks the game or stops your enjoyment of playing it; plus Revolution seem to be vigilant (pun intended) in finding these bugs and squashing them quickly.  I have only played 7 hours of the game so far and have enjoyed it all, especially the humour and sarcastic/snide remarks between Foster and Joey.  The game is also full of little easter eggs for veterans of Beneath, such as musical cues, scenery and even lines of speech taken from it.  All in all, worth every penny I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of my favorite point-and-click game of this day and age.Though, I have some issues with it. The main issue is the fact that it isn't very obvious what you needed to do and it's not clear what you can interact with. I kinda miss having the option to show every interactables in the screen.The fact that the hacking mode hide this made it confusing. I wish there's no need to go to a specific mode rather just an additional interaction, maybe with a purple icon to show that it's hackable.This game ain't perfect, it has plenty of bugs which can be infuriating at times but most of them were comestical (i.e in my gameplay, Songbird was clipping into the mirror instead of sitting).But overall, I would say it's a decent experience. I wish it was a bit longer honestly, the ending felt kinda rushed.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, very cyberpunk. Revolution makes the best adventure games. These games are very story and puzzle orientated. Broken Sword and this sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky are among the best games. I love RPGS and adventure over shooters as I love story based game, but without a doubt this game meets expectations with twists and turns and is well told and well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: So, here's the thing. If you bought this game, you've played Beneth a Steel Sky, and if you've played that game you can forgive this game its technical issues.   It's certainly a love letter to the original with a bunch of call backs, but doesn't attempt to just rely on being a sequel.  I can certainly recommend this game if you've played the original, but please stay away from this game if you haven't, you won't forgive its flaws and will probably end up hating this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Beneath A Steel Sky so I jumped at this when I could get it and it really lives up to the older game. Great design and art, lovely voice acting and a good script. The puzzles are mostly pretty good and the remote interface tool is a lot of fun, however it did all seem pretty easy and was over far too quickly. I'm not sure if it's just trying to kerb the legacy of older puzzle adventures being incomprehensible but very few of the puzzles in this presented very much challenge, and the story felt clipped in places to the point that I wonder if sections had actually been dropped in late stage development. I'd definitely recommend this, and not just to old BASS fans, but don't expect too much from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Honest review with no spoilers!  A new classic?  I think so!This is a game excels in the overall experience with a strong story, good pacing and a unknown world you can immerse yourself in.  But....Just don't go in expecting everything to be perfect.  It feels it is missing a layer of polish that more time and testing would have helped with but it's brilliance makes up for the flaws it has.  I kept looking forward to coming back to the the game to continue my adventure!  Some of the dialogue made me laugh out loud!  It is a bit buggy in places like the camera clipping into scenery, a couple of missing voice sounds on the odd bits of dialogue and a few other things.  Occasional acting/voice seemed a bit out of context (again a bit more polish). I think they were ambitious with the size of the project and I'm sure they will be patching.  Nothing broke the game in my play through and I'm sure I'm the sort of player that always does what the programmer didn't expect to do!  If the developers did have to focus anywhere to ship it on time I'm glad they focused on the fundamentals that matter.When I started the game I wasn't too sure if I would like it.  I pretty much went in blind.   The controls took a bit of getting used to but after the first section felt more natural.  After the first section I really got in to it wanting to explore and meet lots of fun characters.  It took me 15 hours to complete.  I like point and click adventures but can never ace them.  When I got stuck trial and error helped me work it out.If you liked the Broken Sword games, Monkey Island, Grim Fandango, Broken Age and other point and click adventure games I think you will enjoy this one,
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original game, and it is one of the first games I remember buying for myself to play. The new one is in 3D instead of 2.5D but maintains the humour and quirkiness of the previous game. The choice of 3D makes some interactions a bit awkward, especially when trying to interact with moving objects but other than that the puzzles are clear and fair.Overall a very enjoyable game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: While the 3rd person controls and 3D graphics are a departure from Beneath a Steel Sky the story and characters do a good job of grounding Beyond a Steel Sky withing the same world as the original game.The game engine works well, graphics are nice and crisp and the comic book style works well. There are some issues at times with close up cameras clipping through objects or obscuring characters, this tends to happen if a character is too close to a wall or other obstruction.The puzzles are with a couple exceptions straight forward and I found that I was able to work them out without impacting story progression too much. The characters are nicely animated and there are many funny moments in the game. I found the humour to be very good.It is worth playing the first game Beneath a Steel Sky as there are some minor spoilers contained in this one.But if you don't want to play old adventure games you can enjoy this one without missing out on too many funny references to the original.Recommended to fans of Graphical Adventure games.I consider this a 3rd person Adventure rather than point and click.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This is such a good game; I am very impressed. I liked Beneath a Steel Sky back in day, but this game combines all the things we loved about the old game with none of its predecessor's faults. (Yes, I liked this one better than the original; and again, I really liked the first game.)Which leads me to my first point, it's a beautiful game. They captured the mood and tone of the original and made it even better. There were many times throughout the game where I was hoping that this game would never end and that I'd be able to explore endlessly deeper into Union City. The team really delivered so many cool locations, each beautiful in their own way.The Story was compelling and the characters were awesome as well. I am partial to buddy stories. All the Puzzles made sense to me. I never had to look anything up or even use the in-game hint system. As you play, there are many hints already weaved into the Dialogue. And speaking a Dialogue, the back and forth between Foster and Joey is the real heart of the game, Funny, witty, and very touching at times. I almost feel like Joey was my Best Friend :)This is definitely the best game that I have played in many years. It's not a feeling that I experience very often. There are many good games. There are many entertaining games. Beyond a Steel Sky is "Beyond" that. I felt like I was playing a work of art and every moment brought me to a place of wonder and excitement.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It's been quite some time since I last played with Foster, heck I still remember running this from Msdos.I can't say I ever imagined a sequel to be made, but here we are.The main mechanic in the game , was extremly well implemented and with a lot of interesting applications for the genre.Game is overall really solid, good humor, graphics, tech jokes, nostalgia referances and more.I encountered a few clipping issues, (climbing behind a ladder etc.) and talking sometimes gave weird angles. But nothing to really ruin the game.Puzzles were on the easy to medium ish, nothing that you will need to bash your brain to figure out.Still I think that not getting stuck endlessly makes the story flow better overall. (for this game at any rate)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long time fan of Revolution Software, from  the Broken Sword saga to Beneath a  Steel Sky. This game does not disappoint. The writing and dialogue are amazing. The graphics are great and have come so far from the... limited technology of Broken Sword 3.  I would call this a must-play for any classic point n' click enthusiasts especially those who've played the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I only played for 15 minutes but the game looks and feels FANTASTIC! Playing maxed in 4k, rock solid. Great music and sound effects as well. I am BIG fan of the original BASS and played on the AMIGA in 1994.But this is on ANOTHER level! I can only imagine how it would feel in VR. :) FANTASTIC job Revolution!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: 5 Hours in and this is everything I expect in a point and click adventure, and probably much more. Interesting world, driving story and good humor. Graphics are above standard for the genre and the voice acting is top notch.  If you like the dying genre of point and click, don't think just buy it and enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting about 25 years for this game. loved the series use to play it as a child. game is excellent although I am bias as such a fan of the story. Would recommend it to any one well worth playing the first game as its free on gog at the moment so you can enjoy some of the subtle jokes \ and references along the way. just completed the game took about 10 hours.I encountered one bug (this games been out less than 10 days at the point of this bug so will probably be patched). got stuck on the asperiation platform part for about a hour then looked a guide and found a thing i was meant to interactive with was not displaying the option. exited and reloading solved this but on a puzzle game that could left me stuck there for days lol.I love seeing parts of my childhood redone in 3d by people that payed attention to detail to respect the original art work. Top job by the devs and artists etc
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: this was an enjoyable  comfy experience , great world building , diverse character with great voice acting . fun puzzles that you solve with "hacking". It wouldn't be a revolutions game if the character didn't narrate their thoughts to you,while hearing that lovely instrumental piece that goes with it. Robert foster is such a sweetheart ! what a great protagonist with little joey as his wise cracking partner.this a has a choices matter mechanic which i barley noticed in a good way , i played as i usually do as point and click adventure game character  good  but takes everything thats not nailed down.(for the first play through at least) and was pleasantly surprised to find out that it could be slightly different . so from what i understand this is sequel but also slight reboot? made so people who didnt play the first one can enjoy it.which is fine but make me a little confused as to whats a retcon or like a mysterious twist ? but to be fair its been many years since i played the first one either way. offer/show your mini ks to everybody ,its pretty funny. the ending is a little bittersweet but left me wanting more.ok thats the end of my thoughts Good game, glad i got it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: What a great experience! I played the original game back in 1994, being a Adventure Game junkie, "Beneath a Steel Sky" had always been one of my favorite storylines. "Beyond a Steel Sky" definitely does not dissapoint, it continues very well from the original story, and you get to relive a lot of nostalgia of the original game. Seeing everything in 3D actually makes me hope to one day play the original like this one, feeling like you are actually in Union City!The game does have quite a few bugs, which are a bit inherent of the 3D nature, getting stuck in certain movements because you are bumping into characters or things, the camera also multiple times would display from inside a wall or a character when you are having a dialog with someone, being able to speak with someone on another side of a wall, and the occasional voice being muffled as if the person was under water or far away from you. Also... there is an over reliance on the tech hacking to solve puzzles, maybe there could've been less of that.But... even with the quirks described, and most of which can be fixed in future updates... I'm am thrilled to have played this sequel, and really which there can be a remaster of the original in the pipeline... as much as I love pixels... Union City deserves to be experienced like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A funny adventure game in an interesting setting. Think Bioshock, but in post-apocalyptic cyber-future and without pseudo-philosophical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Lots of references, funny dialogue (sometimes the jokes are even rather sophisticated). Pretty art style.Among the bad things are facial animations, hacking tool range (infuriating, it should have been completely unlimited!) and poor handling of character emotions.That last bit is very weird - haven't really seen that before. Characters seem like they have the emotional memory of 5 seconds - so something happens and they react to it fairly adequately, writing and voice-acting all proper, but then literally in the next sentence they are all "back to neutral" mode, as if that funny-sad-surprising-relieving-etc. moment didn't even happen. It's like an actual AI wrote this script, which had perfect knowledge of human emotions, but no actual understanding of them.Still, overall - a good game, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Here it is the sequel of a great beneath a steel sky.Did I enjoy it ? Yes I played till the end! But... !Lets start with the Good parts:- the implementation of the point and click Interface was well done, it felt like the "show all Hotspot" button.- good graphics- interesting Story, i wanted more to konw about some characters. Except the ending felt a little bit too rushed, I dont want to spoiler...The Cons- easy Gameplay- no german voice output, but the first hadnt one either so... doesnt matterThe bad:- the puzzles where just interface puzzles in the hackingtool. I really liked the inventory puzzles before you enter the city. After that I forget I had a Inventory expect 1-2 times where you had to use one item.Noticed Bugs:- Cant enter the City Chat log, you have to use the mouse (I played with a controller).- joey was stuck, had to reload a save game.- 2-3 crashes during loading time- one hotspot of a character that was already gone- 2 hotspots for a ladder. one over and one unter the ladder, if you use the hotspot over the ladder than foster ist going against the wall.ConclusionI really liked playing foster and joey again, the story was interesting the characters and the graphics did their job.But you know its a 3D Point and click andventure when the world has not a lot of interaktiv hotspots to offer and there a no or a very few classic puzzles. Without the hacking tool it would been even a walking simulator.In German its called "schuster bleib bei deinen leisten": point and click adventure games please stay 2d, 3d dont fit you well.If you are doing a Broken Sword 6 ( I HOPE YOU DO! ) than either make more puzzles like in the opening scene or please make it 2d again!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Classic. Got to have it. Not that expensive.Considering the content (ca. 20 diff persons, 10 locations, not reaaally much detail) i don't know why it needs a whopping 15 GB though.Lots of cutscenes/video-clips. That might be it?I like it though!This 2020 version is good as a starting point for more adventures in UnionCity, Gap  together with Orana, Raquel.As DLC.  (not to expensive then I hope)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Replayed Beneath a Steel Sky before playing Beyond, and I'm really glad they kept the humour and larger than life characters intact. I had a good few laughs. Beyond is a far bigger game than Beneath, in scope and length, and I think it feels a little thinner for that. That's partly just the way games have moved in the decades between, partly due to the more systemic puzzles, and partly (in my opinion) excessive dialog options. Being able to ask every character about every topic multiple times is fine, as long as they have something unique to say, but mostly they don't.  The systemic puzzles do work really well though, logical, and not trivial to solve, I didn't need any hints but still had to think about quite a few of them. The interface was good too, unobtrusive and simple to use.Lastly, the story was very well done. It's really hard to make a sequel to a beloved franchise this far on and have it work, but it does. It's not mind blowing or anything, but it holds together, and works with the original. It feels like the sequel should.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of point and click and this is an excellent addition to my library. It has a new take on the traditional 'click  here / combine those' approach with intelligent puzzles and  good interaction (although it is still a case of wading through all of the conversation menus which can be a bit repetitive - also at times you end up having the identical conversation simply because the option still exists in the conversation menu).Artwork and interface are both excellent; voice acting a huge step up from many other games of it's ilk (all of these are typical of Revolution products).All in all a great product ; one I strongly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell you how much I love the first instalment back in the 90's... Must have been about 93, 94 I think... I love sci-fi, cyberpunk, and I love point-and-click adventure games. Especially ones with a great storyline and sense of humour. Beneath a steel sky ticked all of those boxes.  Back then I was an Amiga A500 user and back then games came in boxes... Boxes filled with cool artworks and extras ahh those were the days. Anyway I still remember this box, black with just the silver skyline in shadow on to the box.I used to look it up every now and then to see if there were any emulators I could use to play it again. I discovered a little while back that the sequel beyond a steel sky was in the making. Well I have been keeping an eye out for this to be released and now it's finally here. So the game has finally landed and after playing it for a while I can say I am not disappointed. The plot is exactly what was wanted/needed from a sequel. You start off in the GAP, and our protagonist Robert Foster is witness to a child abduction and sets on the trail of the abductors which leads him back to Union City, where he'd left his trust robot sidekick Joey many years ago to turn the city into a utopia. The gameplay feels good and I like the cartoon graphics, I think they feel nice and modern in this type of game. It's not the usual point and click type of control that I was expecting like beneath a steel sky and other games of this genre. Beyond a steel sky uses WSAD controls which isn't a bad thing at all as the game is now a 3D environment rather than the usual point and click 2D.Overall the puzzles are not too complex but are challenging enough to keep you entertained whilst managing the inevitable frustration you get from being stuck in one place. In fact, there are even hints included in the pause menu if you were to get reaaaally stuck but most players used to this type of game won't need them. For me this game is excellent and a perfect sequel to its predecessor, well worth the wait and well worth grabbing a copy. 9/10 on the vosNET scale of excellence! Check out my YouTube 2 Minute Review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original so I had to buy this, overall it's a great game and if you played the first one all those years ago you'll love this.It's not perfect however, there are some bugs in the game for sure, it's not unplayable or anything and I'm sure they will be fixed soon but my bigger gripe is that it's very short in my opinion and that's not something that can be fixed with an update.At the end of the game I felt like I should only be about half way through so that made for a disappointing ending, not sure it was worth the money I paid for such a minor distraction if I hadn’t been a fan.Other gripes would be that the MINOS hacking thing is pretty simple and a bit of a gimmick, got old quickly. Despite those bad points it was an excellent continuation and I'm generally happy enough with it, I hope they make a third and I hope revolution do a better job with it, there is certainly room for improvement.Be vigilant citizen!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very enjoyable game! I never played BASS back in the day, only the Broken Sword games (which I loved), so I didn't know what to expect. I decided to give it a shot, and I'm very glad that I did! This was an amazing experience on so many levels! Beautiful 3D cinematic graphics, clever and witty writing, generally logical puzzles. Definitely recommended!!! Hope to see more of the same. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited for a sequel all the way from the times of Amiga and was excited when i heard they were making one. Loved the first one for its atmosphere and humor.So did i like Beyond a Steel Sky? in short Yes. Did it fulfill my expectations? Well, Yes and No.Let's start with the good things i have to say about it. -The story was nice in overall and maybe i got more out of it because i played the first one.-It had a good atmosphere just like the first game, especially when you get to see the Union City. The city feels more alive with random people walking around it.-The new mechanic that the game introduced was a nice touch and i would have loved to play with it a little more with even more complex puzzles.And then to the not so great section...-The plot was nice and all. BUT! It was in my opinion a little too short and the pace of the plot felt it was picking up speed fast. In the beginning it was nice and easy, but it felt like it started going a little too fast at one point. There was some elements in the plot that did not feel right for me.-They REALLY REALLY REAAAAAALLY toned down the dark humor, grimness that the first game had. (Maybe i am the only one liked those. Dunno.)-Almost all of the puzzles were easy to solve, maybe a little too easy and predictable some times.Summary.It was a nice little adventure game and a sequel to one of my favorite adventure games. I would have liked it even more if it was a little bit longer and the plot was a little deeper. I would have loved to see even more of the Union City and more of its different areas.I got to taste of a Beneath game again and now i want more!Should you buy it?If you really like adventure games in general or want more Steel Sky then you should yeah.BE VIGILANT!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It was not bad, I enjoyed it. Few funny moments, few serious moments. The George Stobart cameo was a nice touch, pity you couldn't press a button & make him talk.A couple of the opening sequence Aussie accents were terrible, after that they were quite good. Grahams apartment has a number of bugs when talking to butler, still playable but not great.My biggest bug bear is the ending. I know it must very hard to come up with suitable puzzle for type of ending in a point & click game, but it just felt tacked on to an otherwise good closing sequence. Would have preferred a difficult time crunch ending that took multiple failures to achieve.Overall: Its no Broken Sword, but it is a solid adventure game & you could do much worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game. I can comfortably give it a 9/10, only issues were small bugs. The world was fun to explore, graphics were beautiful, and the plot was a wonderful mix of cheesy, tongue in cheek, and meaningful. There were times I got worried about the direction of the story, but the writers always found a way to keep things interesting. This game is worth whatever amount of money you end up spending on it. I got about 15 hours of playtime out of it and I plan on replaying it in the future. I will give two warnings: 1. The framerate seemed to suffer a bit near the end of the game, not sure why that would be. Mostly the game ran fine at 4K on my Vega gpu except for the last hour or so. 2. There's a chance you can run into a glitch where the camera angle gets thrown far away during a conversation and you can't hear what a person is saying. This bug should hopefully be fixed soon.I hope you enjoy this game; whether you played the first one or not! It has appeals to nostalgia for those who have, but can still inform new players clearly about the world so they feel comfortable.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a thumbs up, but just barely. The story is great and I'm sure it will be a great game once they work out the bugs, but the bugs are a big problem right now. It is not a question of if you will hit a game-stopping bug, or even when it will happen. It is a matter of how often it will happen and have you been diligent about saving your progress along the way so you can backtrack when you need to. The game has autosaves, but it only has three slots and the autosaves are time-based, not progress-based. So if you stand in the same spot long enough, you will use all three autosaves and lose your ability to go back if you haven't manually saved along the way as well. As long as you are good about saving your progress and don't mind backtracking occasionally, then the game is definitely worth playing now. But if having to do that would frustrate you, then you'd be better off waiting until they've had time to work out the kinks before you try to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A joyful revisit of Foster and Joey. Loved first game back when it came with our family computer back in 1994.I feel they hit the adventure genre very well, with a modern twist. I've missed it, as it's barely any games within this genre anymore. It tells a good story, and my memories from the first game keep coming back throughout the playthrough. The puzzles were fun, and not too hard. Loved how they utilized some certain tools creatively through the game, as well as having different results pending your choises.The controls were a tad quirky at first, but got used to it after some time. And I had to get used to the 3rd person view having the character block a lot of my screen even on an ultra wide.The graphics was ok, as I guess they target as many platforms as possible. Although I'd wish they'd have a textured variant for heavier systems.Took me about 10 hours to complete the game this time and never felt it to be too easy, however, it felt somewhat short. I guess it has the same length as the first game due to the fact I was 12 and my english was rather limited back then, so spent way more time by trial and error. There was some technical issues along the way, but not as many as I though after reading some reviews, so I guess some have been fixed. Being alt+tab'ed out while loading cause the game to crash, so had to go back a save a few times. Also, when you talk with Leet, the camera is way off, so you dont even hear the conversation at all.Anywho! I very much recommend giving it a go, even if you didnt play the first game, and especially if you're new to or want to revisit the adventure genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, if short adventure game. I'd say it rates relatively low on the puzzle complexity scale, but is shored up by the fun hacking system.The middle of the game feels.... well, like not much is happening, you're trying to find out some basic information, then all of a sudden its almost the end of the game.I completed this in about 7 hours, and was hoping it'd last another 7 at my pace.Overall, the story was solid but lacked a little oomph
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Take this review with a pinch of salt as I am biased by nostalgia.I remember playing "Beneath a Steel Sky" when it came out. It was a good adventure game with an original setting and a good sci-fi story.This game took me by surprise as I was not at all aware of its existence before the release.Going back to this universe, meeting old and new characters and remembering the old story was a blast !This game is far from perfect but it does its job well enough. Interesting story even if it sometimes it feels a bit "simple".The puzzles are not too hard but not too easy and I like the idea of hacking different objects to be able to solve them.Technically, it's OK. Graphics are colorful and "comic-like", sound and music are on par.A warning: if you never heard of the original game, there are almost no explanations during this game. The story assume that you know your history and have played "Beneath". I'm not sure that you will enjoy the game as much if you have no idea of who is Foster or Joey and what they achieved in the previous game... The should have added a recap video or something to let people get up to date imho...I enjoyed my time playing "Beyond" but as I said, Nostalgia is a powerful bias. Not sure that I would recommend this game as a stand alone if I had never played the original...
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky
