_childDocuments_.review: So we are finally back in Union City, have I waited for this? Yes. Do I enjoy the game? Yes. Do I agree with the style? Yes and no. I would much rather have played a 2D version of the game. But for being a 3D adventure game I quite enjoy it. It plays much better than their earlier Broken Sword games that were in 3D.However, the game is filled with bugs at the moment. I didn't encounter any game-breaking but one that disrupted the flow of the story. Also, there are a lot of problems with the camera showing the wrong things, characters getting stuck inside furniture or standing at the wrong place during conversations. I am sure this will be fixed in upcoming patches but it kind of felt like being a beta-tester.But, I did enjoy the game for what it is, maybe a bit short, but still a good followup to the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, okay... let's take a moment and enjoy the fact that the game is finally here!!! OMG, finally!!! I can't remember the last time I was this excited for a game.So first things first: If you have never played Beneath a Steel Sky, then you are missing out on some of the jokes, but it's really not necessary for you to have played it to enjoy this game.Basis outline of the game: This is a continuation of Robert Foster from the Gap, to "live it up" in the big city, and things have changed! Seems the child of your friends, Milo, has been abducted and taken to the city. You are of course in full pursuit and subsequently venture all over town, where your best friend Joey was once left in charge. Joey has taken good care of the city and received Legendary status among the inhabitants. But Joey "has moved on" to spread his wisdom in the vast expands of the Gap (according to the legend) and now there is a counsil of 5 running the city. I really love the story. You venture as Robert around the city, getting access to places you don't belong all in search of a missing child, and no real help. It's you against the system, haha.I've played beneath a Steel Sky sooo often and now Robert has come to life in a 3D setting. The game is fun and vibrant, not too difficult, but challenging enough at some parts to be "stuck" at, even with the hint system. Almost everything talks, and Robert has a windows box where he talks to "us" reminding me of the cartoon-ist drawing style of a comic. To me that's unique en and quite like it.So graphics are drawn, or look drawn, and character speech is great. But as much as I love it there are some points that are not so great. Some times when you need/or want to speak to a character is it impossible to get their icon on screen, and sometimes I need to walk around a character several time for it to pop up, only the have it lost again. Also when character are talking, the screen turns to a random point, or goes blank.   I don't know if it's what Foster is looking at, or if it's a random cut screen, but if your screen goes blank, you might think your pc or laptop is crashing. (I did think that because it happened two times in succession, although the second time I began to suspect it was a random screen)Right now, those two point are the only ones I have noticed, but I can live with it, because this game is great! And I quite enjoy playing it. It's been a while since I was last hooked on a game!!! I hope there is more Robert Foster action coming in the future!! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished this game yet but I'm deep into it and enjoying it a lot. There's been a few slight glitches and bugs, but nothing game breaking. If you're a fan of more traditional adventure games I think you'll like it, especially if you have fond memories of the original Beneath a Steel Sky (which is available for free if you want to give it a try).
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Huge blast playing this game. And I couldn't resist to play the previous opus first.Great artwork: sounds, graphics, storyline... everything was done to make this experience full of Joeyness.A lot of jokes, and old cliché make the game even better. (Don't want to spoil, but Lure of the Temptress poster put a smile on my face :D )Thansk again Revolution and enjoy all this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with many nostalgic throwbacks to its predecessor. Music is great and the art direction fits. Some of the hacking puzzles are far fetched and provide more logic alternatives than can be represented by the game (missing animations and sounds that makes you unsure what to do). Current state of the game features at least one game breaking bug that requires loading a previous save. I would wait a few months for patches or just adjust my expectations before going in.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. It's simple, it's joyful, it's adventorous, it's relaxing. That is the way modern adventure games should look like. Story and puzzles might be a little too simple, but storytelling is awesome just like the dialogues and characters. Graphic is just beatiful and from technical point of view it's almost AAA level. For that price it's totally worth buying game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in about 10 hours, but kept looking around in the later parts because this game does look gorgeous.It answers some questions for fans of the original game, but you don't need to have played this. this game is well made to stand on it's own. the story is good, not excellent, but good. as said, the graphics are gorgeous and the gameplay makes sense. Especially the controls are very good... didn't expect a 3D adventure to work; as some Broken Sword 3D-based games made some weird choices. The 'hacker' tool is fun and made me explore some other combinations. Hope this will be used in other games.Overall, highly recommended. It is not difficult at all, and there is an built-in hint system... just a tad short.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun game to play, but it is rough around the edges.  It has been a while since I had played an adventure game and it took a while to get into grove, but once I did the was awesome.  My only complaint is that there are times you cannot interact with object and camera angles can be very bad.  Overall, good game and will more than likely play again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only partially into the game at this point, but Beyond a Steel Sky has gone beyond my Beyond a Steel Sky expectations...for Beyond a Steel Sky. I can't wait to go beyond my current point in the game. Beyond beyond beyond beyond beyond. It's a fun word.But seriously, this is better than I predicted. Beautiful, witty, funny, and some novel gameplay aspects that I didn't expect. If you think of this game as nothing beyond a vehicle for driving Robert Fosters' sarcastic "fish out of water" type observations and witticisms directly to your PC, it will still be of significant enjoyment to you, trust me.If given the option, I'd like to immediately preorder the next sequel (hopefully they call it something like Beside a Steel Sky) even if it doesn't come out until 2046.Note: There are some minor glitches that I am sure will be worked out in a patch. I have gotten past every glitch so far by saving, exiting, and restarting the game. Also, some things look glitchy but really aren't - it just seems that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I've only been playing it for 2 hours, and I'm hooked. If you're a fan of adventure games like me, this re-thinking of the format will definitely pique your interest. Effectively, the formula blends the traditional aspect of the "click and point" genre with the "walking sim". No more side scroll mysteries to be found in this title - Revolution have done a sterling job!The humour is great, and the little throwbacks to the previous game are delightful. You won't however, have to have played the prequel to understand what is going on. The general background is told throughout in optional conversations with NPC's. The cell shaded style graphics are a nice touch as well, a massive improvement has been realised since Broken Sword 5 (of which I enjoyed the art style anyway). The protagonist is likeable, and I'm enjoying the jumble of accents although realise it might not be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I am 5 hours in. It's like a better version of the telltale games but with actual puzzles and larger environments. The hacking mechanic is fun. The presentation/graphics/sound/voice/music is all very professional. Looks great in 4k and runs well. The story is loyal to the original game.The characters are funny and entertaining to talk to. The story is intriguing and I have not been bored at all yet. I recommend this game for adventure game lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. It's certainly not without flaws, in particular some mostly minor early launch glitches, but none of them are game-breaking. There is one that cuts out some important dialogue though, but it'll take you no more than a few minutes to find and watch it on Youtube, and either way I don't expect such a bug to remain unpatched for very long.The setting is beautiful, a joy to explore, although I would have liked a few more locations and a little less reuse. The dialogue is witty and the attention to detail in the script is great, but the same can unfortunately not be said for the execution. There are many situations where the rest of the world doesn't quite keep up with your progress. This are all minor, but still takes you out of the immersion a bit.The story is where this one really shines though. This is a throwback story executed almost to perfection, and in itself a deep reflection and critique of where we might be headed as a society. Think a mix of Wall-E and Aldous Huxley's Brave New World. It does have a couple of PG feelgood segments that stands out as just plain weird in contrast to the rest of the story, but apart from being a device to drive the story forward can mostly be ignored.All-in-all a great concept executed unevenly. Some much needed polish will certainly come in the form of a patch, but not every flaw can be polished out, unfortunately. With a Director's Cut I could see this one becoming another classic however. Although judging by the game series history we might be in for bit of a wait there.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The graphic style looks great, the writing is beautiful! The whole package is so reminiscent of a broken sword game so if you enjoyed Nico’s and George’s adventures you are going to love this!Took me around 9 hours to finish my first play through which I think is decent for a point and click adventure.There is a few easter eggs too I spotted a Monty Python reference and the ‘look at all those chickens’ has to be a nod to the meme video! Highly recommend to anyone looking for a solid single player experience! *update*Still blooming awesome! get it nominated for game of the year awards

name: Lifeless Moon
detailed_description: Lifeless Moon, the spiritual successor to the popular 2014 indie title Lifeless Planet, is a 3D platformer that puts you in the center of a mysterious Moon expedition. This new adventure, inspired by classic science fiction, plays as an Apollo-era astronaut who finds themself in the aftermath of an old 1970s experiment: an oddly familiar desert town… on the moon. Explore Anomalies Secrets in the desolate moon city soon unlock mysteries on a much grander scale… Equipped with a jetpack and your sense of survival, search for the truth through landscapes one could hardly fathom. Collect Documents You’ll need perseverance and wit to uncover this mystery. Record your thoughts and find clues from the past to unravel the dark secrets residing on this celestial body. Utilize The Technology If you want to understand the forces at hand, you’ll need to use them to your advantage. Solve puzzles and work with strange technology to create a path forward. Unearth The Mystery In a land where objects materialize from nothing and time flows unexpectedly, relive the experiences and traumas of the scientists that came before you. After all, following their footsteps might be the only way to return home.

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless Moon has a very balanced blend of calmness and mystery to it and I love that about it.It goes from being peacefully scenic to super intense in a matter of seconds.The story is written in such an intriguing way that I will for sure be checking out Lifeless Planet as well. Make sure you pay attention to small details and explore the world thoroughly or you might miss out on some interesting interactions.I found myself taking a breather quite a few times simply to enjoy the scenery and the music.The sound design and voice-over are masterfully done.A brilliant game, I very much recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR if you like stories, play it. If you're looking for something else... don'tI will recommend this game, with notes (David, been there, please take this as a constructive comment, also this is my opinion, maybe I'm a weirdo). While the story is more compelling than the first one (Lifeless Planet) the story falls short and the game doesn't develop it's full potential story-wise, this results in a shorter experience (2-3h versus 5 hours on LP). All of this said, a more concise review:- Story: Really good, cool concepts but not fully exploited- Game mechanics: Underdeveloped. LP had more mechanics (robotic arm, jetpack modes, etc.), although the first person thingie is was nice to see.- Level complexity: Underdeveloped, really straighforward to the point you can navigate the environments blindfloded. LP gave a better impression of vastness and disorientation.- Music: Good as the first one, I loved seeing it a bit more present than the first one.- Graphics/textures/etc: Correct.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet as I'm taking my time, exploring every nook and cranny. I'm enjoying this so much. There is platforming, but it is much better than in Lifeless Planet. You just need to figure out the jetpack range and you're good to go. The puzzles aren't too hard. I've been stuck a couple of times, but that's just because I get lost easily and have difficulty figuring out where to go next. Fortunately, the areas are not that large, so you're bound to find what you're looking for if you just keep exploring. I definitely recommend not rushing through the game as the scenery is interesting and the secrets aren't really hidden, just require a bit of exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I regret this is a no from me. I loved lifeless planet. It was a slow burn sci-fi thriller with existential questions. It felt grouonded in some reality and you wanted to uncover the plot and what happened. This game is a barely 2 hour padded experience. The plot is mostly fed by "notes" that you have to open a menu to read. So the gameplay becomes "run a few feet and open a note". It's very poorly paced. The game starts off with the right atmosphere. I thought it would be an interesting followup to lifeless planet. But then the writer immediately plays their hand and reveals everything about the plot. The game at once over explains itself with exposition dumps and yet fails to forge any meaningful connection between the player and the rest of the cast. I'm sorry to say this is a no. I would recommend the first game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I have to go with NO for this one. I would be fine with maybe 7EUR and I would be way more lenient. For 17 I don't feel like the game is worth it. Let's go with the negatives first, that is why you are reading this.It is under 2 hours long and it feels incredibly padded. This game emphasizes the walking in the "walking sim". It's hard to combine vast areas where you should get a sense of loneliness and scale while not giving the player anything to do besides commute. The only way to break the monotony is bunnyhopping and jetpacking everywhere which makes the game kind of ridiculous.The beginning was promising - sure, a bit tropy but hey - tropes exist for a reason. But then it kind of did not go anywhere. The whole story is basically a carnival ride of a Twilight Zone episode where there is very little exposition shown but the moral in the end should make up for it somehow? Exposition is mostly dumped in logs. If I wanted to read a book, I would read a book. I wanted to play a game and instead my finger hurts from holding W for 2 hours.The game is strangely put together. It has all the components that could make it great but misses the mark on every single one:Writing - promising ideas but because the game is so short, they can't really flesh it out. Adding bunch of text to logs can't really save it. Ultimately the journey falls completely flat because nothing we went through felt meaningful. It's very straightforward and lacks depth.Music - the tracks are great but they seem to be playing in wrong places. For instance in the beginning you get big dramatic tracks but there is nothing that dramatic happening. At the beach area you get dramatic music but there is never any danger, you just do a jetpack jump two times in a row. You've done it like 100 times at that point.Level design/graphics - sure, I don't expect an AAA visuals and I like the environments but if you have to signpost everything with a green glowing area or a thread, it is odd. I don't get how it was supposed to work narratively. The surreal nature of the environments is probably the best part of this game. I feel like they could achieve so much more.If you spend the money on a bottle of rum instead of this game the experience will last much longer. Or you can buy 2 bottles of cheap vodka and you will remember nothing, which coincidentially is the same amount I will remember about this game in a week.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who loves this kind of game and Lifeless Planet in particular, I was interested in playing Lifeless Moon and I absolutely loved it. The experience is riddled with bugs and far from perfect, just like Lifeless Planet. Despite this, the atmosphere, music, and story left a deep impression on me.I will start with stuff that I didn't like. Initially, the game looked very similar to Lifeless Planet - the same barren terrains, the same model of an astronaut, the same walk/jump mechanics, the same rings, same long jumps from rock to rock where if you miss one jump, you need to start over, etc., etc. However, after some point, the game started to transform, and it was a big surprise for me how beautiful this game looks, I definitely didn't expect such visual quality from an indie game of this budget. And I spent quite a while just looking around the locations or staring at the sky.Same as Lifeless Planet, the game has a LOT of small bugs, but nothing critical. The character will occasionally jump after exiting the menu, and closing one menu sometimes causes the other to open, opening certain menus doesn't freeze the player properly, so he continues running in the same spot until you continue playing. And a lot of other small things that happen every now and then. While giving the game quite an unpolished vibe, it doesn't really affect the gameplay.Now to stuff I like. The atmosphere of hidden danger, confusion, and unease is absolutely on point. This is accompanied by great music that changes depending on the context of the current scene and makes you fret about the next thing that's coming. To me, just the combination of the visual style and the atmosphere is a more than sufficient reason to try this game out. In terms of story, I didn't like it as much as Lifeless Planet. The progression is a bit too slow and there wasn't a big plot reveal as it was in the previous game, instead the game slowly gives you all the information. But still, the whole idea of the game is very interesting and I think I will replay this game to understand the story better.Overall, if you liked the previous game, this one is definitely worth a try, Given how short it is, you can always return it if you absolutely hate it :)Otherwise, if you like mysterious scientific stories that happen in space, you might like it as well. But in such case, you should also give Lifeless Planet a go :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game was nice. Story was okay. However, it was massively too short (the story). For the amount of money for the length of play....the game should have cost at least a third of the buying price. It was over before I knew it! Lower the cost and the game would be suitable for a quick run through. OR revamp the game and make it more expansive.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless Moon is a great follow up to Lifeless Planet. It's a little shorter and a bit more surreal, but still has that eerie atmosphere and fantastic music of the first game. Games like this remind me just how much can be achieved by a solo developer or a small team. Well worth taking your time to explore as there are a few hidden secrets out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was pretty damn good.  This one, flat out sucked.  It was boring, repetitive and the notes - OMG the notes... Every few seconds stop and read a note that literally explained the in your face what is going on "action" in the game.  The graphics felt dated and there was no story worth reading or figuring out.  But what exactly do you expect from a 2 hour game.  Not worth the money at all.  Surely did not live up to expectations from the first one.  Read the negative reviews for this game and take them to heart.  This game is not good, not worth $20, not worth your time and definitely worse than the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out LM is a shorter game than LP and to me it didn't have quite the mystique or intrigue of the first game. The puzzles were fewer and seemed simpler than Lifeless Planet and there didn't seem to be as much jet-packing as in the original. Having said that I still enjoyed the game but I was hoping for a bit more. I really like this kind of game and I'd like to see more like these two from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: A low budget title with more heart than most. While it looks rough around the edges, this is more of a walking simulator than a platformer puzzler. It doesn't answer all of your questions, but the story is interesting, and weird enough to keep you thinking once you've finished the game. The sound is surprisingly good, with the music have some truly epics work to give you the chills, in a good way.It won't take you long to finish, but if you want something laid back, then go for it. It's better than the first game (Lifeless Planet) insomuch that they have learned through experience.I hope they continue to make and learn as they go. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is very similar to its predecessor, "Lifeless Planet" from the same developers. It's got all the same basic pieces down to minute details: a gripping sci-fi story, nice but obviously cheap visuals, a lot of walking, 3D platforming with a jetpack, green energy stones, round portals, and a direct connection between the mind and outside space. However, the sequel treats each of these components better than the original: the visuals have much improved at least because 10 years have passed, 3D platforming is no longer tedious and clunky, it is always clear what you are supposed to do and where to go (maybe even too much, some objectives in the journal feel a bit condescending), and the game itself is much shorter and packs more into a shorter time. I liked this one very much, but I still recommend to play "Lifeless Planet" first and "Lifeless Moon" second: the original is also well worth playing, and you will get even more enjoyment out of the sequel's improvements. Here's hoping another "Lifeless" game is not another 10 years away!
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I feel disappointed with LM. I want to like it but it didn't quite deliver for me. The first time I played LP I hadn't bought it (let's face it, these things happen) but I liked it so much that I ended buying it and playing it I think twice more. So when I saw LM was about to be launched I was full of excitement to get it and play it. But from the beginning I wasn't having fun, the notebook disturbs the flow of the gameplay every 20 seconds or so. After I finished The Biologist's chapter (an irritating and poorly executed chapter IMHO) I was tired of the story and I missed exploration. I have finished the game, it goes somewhat better after that chapter (except for the memorial, the initials and the poor, clumsy system used for... nothing?), but the overall experience has been underwhelming, frustrasting and (the worst that can be said about a game) NOT FUN. I have found LM to be a soulless, listless repetition of LP. I won't replay it not even for the missing achievements. Nevertheless I'll be there for the next one. I hope Lifeless Comet will regain the adventure, the exploration and the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good open world 1st person single-player adventure game.  The story is interesting and unfolds if you give it time - have read some reviews that it didn't make sense but have to disagree, it all fits together and a pretty good science fiction premise underlying what is going on.  Very evocative of Lifeless Moon, but much more advanced concept.The gameplay and mission goals are pretty straightforward (via the notebook).  The puzzles are pretty simple.  The graphics are well rendered and very fast - even on modest hardware it performs well at high resolution.  The inventory/notebook/object interaction/small room navigation are all just a little bit clumsy but you get used to it quickly.  Just a bit of pixel hunting - pretty obvious where to go  but the sweet spot sometimes takes a minute to find, but this is a nit overall.  Great physics - very realistic falling and floating.Overall, if you love adventure games and puzzles, add this one to your inventory!
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: "Lifeless Moon" has some fascinating ideas at its core that hint at a larger, more compelling story and world, but is limited by its small scope and basic gameplay. It's a puzzle platformer with simple puzzle and a lot of mainly just walking around looking for keys. Its main character is mostly mute, unknown, and arbitrarily inserted into a story that feels like a more interesting narrative is happening around them, rather than to them. The frame story is very fragmented with lots of little log entries and I honestly didn't really get as much as I think I was expected to. The fact the gameplay is so basic and that you can actively miss log entries is a little disappointing, considering how charming (and more polished) this developer's previous game was.It's very short, around 2.5/3 hours, very rough graphically, and slightly buggy. Music feels stock. Many times this generic music would cut out, audio lines would overlap, character would get stuck on terrain. I don't really recommend unless it's at a steep discount and you're looking for a single evening game with some mildly trippy vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: In a few words, a must play for anyone who likes the good old Science Fiction genre. It's more than just a game. It's a science fiction interactive journey through spacetime and emotions.As for the technical part, what stands out more (apart from the story) are the beautifully drawn landscapes and the captivating soundtrack. The gameplay is simple but that's how it's meant to be. It's the discoveries you make that matter, not the gameplay itself. If you have played Lifeless Planet, then you know you can expect the best. If you haven't played the Planet, then what are you doing? Go buy the bundle now!
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: A very original story which is hard to find anywhere today, with great views and a calm yet interesting pace. I do wish there were more details within gameplay, but I'm happy with the final product. Also recommend the original, Lifeless Planet, very highly (played it on my xbox years ago, me and my buddy couldn't put it down).
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: If this were a graduation project, I'd say it deserves an A grade.  But for a game that costs more than a couple of bucks, it is awful.  Bad controls (especially in point-n-click parts), bad interface, too often just impossible to understand what and where to do next (follow the cat, right... but were is it?)  Graphics is bad, Moon gravity is badly implemented, story is dump and and so is presentation. just can't believe it.  If it were just a walking simulator, it would be passable for "C" (again, if it were dirt cheap), but mixing all these extra elements without any finesse does not add up to a good game.  I bought it only because of the "Lifeless Planet" (which is no jewel either, but at least it was somewhat enjoyable in mechanics and even story/discovery), but this game totally failed my expectations.  Disappointing trash.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent experience from the Lifeless Universe. The wait was well worth following the amazing game of Lifeless Planet from 2014. Mysterious, thrilling, and emotional, the story throughout the game is right up there with the original. The visuals are absolutely breathtaking. There were times I looked up for the first time in a while and the actual star map from Goddard being used just blew my mind. The soundtrack is great as well. I greatly appreciate the care that went into this whole game and the crew showed just how much they love the universe they've created. Definitely experience this (As well as Lifeless Planet, if not done as well) when you get a chance. It's not a long game (the .9 is my Steam time played, but I Platinumed it on PS5 in about 4-5 hours), but it's a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: It's all about the feelings.This game conjures a lot of them. Mystery, awe, wonder and joy are chief among them.Music, sound effects and voice acting are spot-on.Graphics range from okay to good, visual effects are very good.Difficulty level I'd describe as "story mode". No brain-breaking puzzles or inhuman dexterity requirements to frustrate your experience.I also like the unique way in which you can balance the depth in which you experience the story. From superficial to in-depth, there's a way to play for everybody.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on Kickstarter in 2018 I think.  That was a long time ago.  I loved Lifeless Planet, so I figured this was going to be a great follow-up.  It's more of a mixed connection of emotions though.The music in the game is top-notch, and sound design is mostly spot-on.  There are times where the music makes it feel like you have a bit of a rush or sense of urgency - but that's not really true.  Voice acting is limited, but all of it is good.The story was pretty hard to follow and I feel like I have far more questions than answers at this point.The level design was another mixed feeling for me.  Some of the earlier levels were pretty cool with the platforming, and others were frustrating "go find this thing for this thing puzzle" that were as clear as mud.  In any case, I pushed through and if you liked Lifeless Planet I think you'll probably like this too.  It's just not as good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend it despite some flaws and bugs (not game breaking).The story is middling but delivered so earnestly i can forgive it,the graphics are awful but ...OMG this looks amazing. This team really knows how to set a scene.the soundtrack is so good that i hope it gets a dlc release, its got a great variety too, synthwave, atonal, orchestral... gameplay is very simple, practically a walking sim, but clips along at a decent enough and i never felt bored.voice acting is excellent.this is clearly an indie budget game, and it shows but i am astounded by whats been accomplished with so little. i would love to see what this team could accomplish with a larger one- however the contemplative style probably occludes this from happening.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive, excellent graphics and music and a story which has theright sense of exploration and the enormity of the universe (not that i can say i understand it all)Only problem was occasional janky movement As with most of this type of game its very short for its price, but I cant say i regret playing it
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless Moon is a great slow burn in that you don’t have to worry about combat or other intense encounters.  Play at your own pace, explore at your leisure, discover the clues, solve the puzzles, and advance the story until you reach the thrilling conclusion.  This is a fantastic and thought-provoking experience that you will savor while playing and excitedly tell all your friends about when done.  Don’t miss this one.Read the full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: i ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS!!! A calm, relaxed game with a beautiful atmosphere. Once you figure out your first couple of puzzles, it kind of becomes second nature to figuring the rest out. The story was intriguing and the music enhanced everything. This is short enough that it's replay-able to get 100% achievements (if that's your thing), but I apparently didn't explore quite enough to get them all the first run.Very well thought out, runs well and is an overall satisfying experience. Thank you devs. Sincerely - Fellow space dork
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Who'd a thought a space adventure such as this would have a nice mysterious plot to it. I'm intrigued. The gameplay is solid which mainly revolves around exploration that features radio transmissions, notes, and the environment tellin' the story here. The game features voice actin' so that is a nice plus. Recommended. Gameplay here:
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: - "Interact" with a strange object- Get transported to the moon- Moving around at the speed of sound! For about 10 seconds.- Find a big ring.- Find a big glowing rock.- *Light bulb appears over head*- *banging noises*- Wake up in the middle of moontown- Walk into the diner and have a chat with the ghost of christmas past- Find a giant locked chamber- Turn random valves and pull levers until it opens- Get disappointed and run off to a random cave pouting- End up in the middle of the woods- KITTY!- Wake the colossal titan!- Run away until ending up in a World War 2 aftermath reconstruction- Get kicked out by the whales- Get chased by a shadow monster- Summon the ocean so that I can have a vacation- Decide to see if the astronaut suit is waterproof- Turns out it is- Whales not happy, get kicked out again- End up in East city- Follow the flying wheelchair man across the floating buildings- Return of the titan!- Fall off the building while trying to figure out where the crouch button is- Searching for FireMan (TM)!- I don't think water is supposed to work like that- Is that the death star?- OH SHI-Then I decided to boot up steam and play this game. Never eat strange objects off the ground.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: This game just isn't doing it for me.  I really enjoyed the first game until the final third when it abandoned the sense of mystery steeped in Cold War tension in favor of LSD-infused nonsense, but this game starts with the LSD infused non-sense right from the start and really never stops sniffing its own farts.The problem isn't necessarily the story itself, but there are simply other games that have done this kind of thing better.  This game's level, audio and visual design are all simply too lacking to back up the ambition of the narrative.  It feels like the developer wrote the story and then kinda slapped everything else together to make it sort of make sense, but not really.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: first of all, i asked my mom and she said its not worth the money. kidding ofctheres minor bugs which i could live with. but what is this select chapter drop down list? you click on the drop down arrow and it directly loads chapter one without a chance to get to you last savepoint. that was gameover for me.The reason why i looked to restart the area where i was in:
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: If you played lifeless planet and you expect something similar then you will get disappointed because the vibe of the game is really different and this one is much shorter too (I finished the game in less than 3 hours)This game is an even crazier acid trip carried by the nice scenery and music. Despite providing a very unique experience, the $20 tag makes this game crazy expensive. Try to get it on a sale imho
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, definitely worth the wait. The story was succinct yet still very empathetic and emotional. David Board captured and portrayed this world very well, his Lifeless planet stuck with me ever since 2014 and I would have waited decades more just for another taste of what I first experienced. To everyone who helped make this possible, thank you. I could write so much on how this captures so many emotions that I personally relate to but I think if you play this game and take it seriously and really indulge in it you could see something most people would not care to.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Excluding the endlessly nagging journal,  is mechanically improved over its predecessor: long gone are the massive treks of absolute nothingness, asinine achievements, and (for the most part) agonizing jumps. Narrative wise, however, I definitely preferred the ambiguity and lack of exposition of . Everything here—from time continuums, to slingshot warps, to humans turned omnipotent, creationist aliens—has been done a thousand times better in countless  episodes. Even less interesting for me is science fiction that wastes most of its time plodding about boring recreations of Earth locales (but on the moon™), with only the first and final chapters tickling my imagination in some way.That's not to say it's a bad adventure, but I'd really only recommend it if you've played the first game, and crave that extra bit of inconsequential lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Hugely enjoyable to play. I'd almost forgotten the first instalment many years ago, but this one is spectacular, and with a brilliantly crafted and executed story-line. That this is a one-man effort is almost incredible. What an achievement. Yes, there are some issues and glitches, and very difficult manoeuvres, depending on what you're playing it on, most notably the somewhat shonky controller support (I have PS4 controller) and some issues with using the jetpack, but overall a very enjoyable ride. I should also mention the audio design and music - wonderful. Here's to another 7 years!
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I gave the first game a thumbs down but noted that the story of Lifeless Planet was good and the developers had future potential given a larger budget.Almost 10 years later with Lifeless Moon and it's still the same low budget style of game with so much wasted potential. The graphics are now at an Xbox 360 level, but there are some nice landscapes. The music feels disjointed and out of place at times, almost tone deaf to the game itself. The game itself feels extremely out of place in time, like it should have launched 15-20 years ago. Back then this would have been a hit, but in 2024 it really falls short. Luckily I bought it on sale, but even then I feel ripped off. At best this game should be $5 regular price, the gaming market has evolved a lot in 20 years and walking simulators have a much higher bar to reach.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, Lifeless Moon looked very interesting. I really liked the setting and the graphics. That didn't change during the playthrough and the music/sounds were okay.There were some small puzzles, but you mainly explore. The exploration takes place by running around and reading notes, but that's normal for a game like this.I liked the game and would recommend it, but not at this price.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Having read some of the reviews for both Lifeless Moon and Lifeless Planet, I almost didn't buy this game; but was able to snag a bundle discount and am really glad I did. I really enjoyed Lifeless Moon. There seemed to be a bit less platforming and jet-packing than LP, which I liked. Also, thought Lifeless Moon was more appealing visually with some very nice scenes. All in all, very nice and enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless Moon is an adventure game developed by Stage 2 Studios and published by Serenity Forge and is the sequel to Lifeless PlanetLifeless Moon is an adventure, walking simulator which offers exploration on an unknown lifeless moon. Although nothing of the story is going to be mentioned in this review, the locations of the whole game take place on a... you guessed it, lifeless moon (and others). You basically keep walking avoiding dangers, reading journals and listening to audio filesIt can get boring and yes the length of the game was fine for me and for what it was going for (I finished it in over two hours and in two whole sittings) if it had just gone over the amount of time I played it, I would have gotten bored easily, and the asking price is a bit too steep, however, Lifeless Moon's story and atmosphere are nailed perfectly in the gameThe story is well written and the planet that you traverse on is beautiful. Although this game was developed on the Unity engine, you can tell that the developers used the engine to their advantage and created a believable, beautiful, lifeless world. Even though some texture work (especially when looking up close) is a bit poor and the animations especially in the main character are pretty poor. The game's atmosphere is hit perfectly in the head. The sky boxes and music especially make the game more believableThe voice acting was pretty good for an indie budget gameI can understand the mixed responses from gamers and reviewers about Lifeless Moon and to me personally I really enjoyed playing through Lifleless Moon. True, the length of the game is short (and shorter than its predecessor) for what it is offering which is walking and walking and walking, however, it was interesting exploring the lifeless moon that was once inhabited by a civilization and what happened afterLifeless Moon will and has mixed reception but if you are reading this review, then you are dying to know my recommendation. Lifeless Moon is a game everyone should try and play and finish in one/two whole sitting/s, it is truly an indie gem which has been buried with other 'better' games, however, for the retail price it is offering, I would not recommend it at its full price and rather wait for a price drop or a saleLifeless Moon is an interesting, well made story with a few hiccups here and there but this is a true indie gem which has been burrowed away by other supposed 'better' games. Lifeless Moon, just like Lifeless Planet, will always be a favourite of mine
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game was worth the time I put into it. The atmosphere is well done and the music was fitting. Just be aware that the game-play is very easy. It's more than a walking simulator, but it is not challenging to either figure out what needs to be done (explicitly stated in the log) or to accomplish any task.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved it! If i compare Lifeless Planet and Lifeless Moon i must say that Lifeless Moon is a better game all in all. I think the music is much better,  more beautiful and more atmospheric in Lifeless Moon. The most beautiful moment in the game: When he is almost out of oxygen and talks to his friend in space. I love what you created David. Thank you, its perfect:=). Godspeed my friend, over and out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of Lifeless Planet, so when I caught wind of Lifeless Moon, I was immediately interested learning more about the lore that the developers have created.  Whereas I'd give Lifeless Planet a 9/10, this game is more like a 7/10, and here's why: [I'll try to keep this spoiler-free for anyone who cares.]The GOOD: Just like with LP, Lifeless Moon has a fantastic soundtrack that really sets the mood for the story and the level as you set out across the moon.  The story and lore is just as interesting and enjoyable to read about as it was in LP.  Each level is unique and fun to explore.  The NOT-SO-GOOD: I really can't call it 'bad' because I did enjoy this game, even for the price I paid.  Clocking in at almost 3 hours, this game does feel rather short. It ends sort of abruptly with an exposition dump from some of the other characters about what was going on.  The puzzles feel very watered down from LP.  There were some moments where I was genuinely stuck on what to do when I first played LP.  While this game doesn't hold your hand, once you figure out how to work the puzzles, it gets really easy.  I'm not sure what connection this game has to LP.  I replayed LP the week that this game dropped because it had been a long time since I revisited the previous game.  There are some things that I can recognize from LP, such as the energy sources and some structures like portals, but I have no idea how this game connects with LP.  I know the developer described this as sort of a prequel because LP takes place many, many years in the future. This game takes place in the 70's possibly before the Soviet excursion to the Lifeless Planet in 1978 (according to LP logs).  Levels feel a bit too linear.  While LP did have linear levels as well, I felt like there was this vast, open planet that I was traversing where I could probably go anywhere if I wanted.  The geography of the world ended up making natural barriers to hinder the player from exploring further.  But this game feels like a bunch of small arenas that you move around from place to place.  The only time I felt like I was on an actual large planet was the first couple of levels on 'the moon,' and the final level. Overall, the game isn't bad, and I feel thoroughly entertained with my first playthrough.  I hope to see more from this developer and this story in the future! Until then, keep exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Lifeless Planet (this game's predecessor) - I loved the eeriness, the strange vistas, the atmospheric soundtrack, and the story. So I've been looking forward to Lifeless Moon for years, and now it's out! And... Well, taken on it's own it's good, but it's very different to LP in a lot of ways. It felt a bit less involving for a start, possibly because things just appear in your notebook or are picked up without you actually doing anything (and the weird way that you enter rooms and don't move around, you just click on stuff). It also feels a lot more linear, with not much to actually puzzle out (though I actually got stuck in the Lake House because I had no idea how to get out of it and there wasn't much in the way of clues - you have to put the assembled cat photo in the holder and rearrange the items on the table and then something will happen). The story is interesting but somewhat linear, though the end felt a bit rushed and "Deus Ex Machina" to me - there's a takeaway about memories and remembering people but it seemed to me to have been thrown in right at the end and doesn't really fit with the rest (which is more about remembering places than people). If I'm honest it felt a little disappointing for something that's been in development for such a long time. That said though, it does have another excellent atmospheric Rich Douglas soundtrack (which I tracked down on Bandcamp, why is it not available as an extra here?), and it does have similar stunning vistas and the vibe is similar to Lifeless Planet - though I didn't really find anything to directly connect it to the original story other than the portals and the tendrils associated with them (and the fact that there's something from Earth in a place where it shouldn't be), and there's nothing here to actually suggest that it was supposed to be the same planet or entities as in Lifeless Planet - if there was, it wasn't obvious to me at all! So I guess it's some kind of "spiritual sequel"? (EDIT: Apparently this is indeed the intent!)Still, taken on its own Lifeless Moon is an atmospheric (though short) story and worth the experience (better on sale, perhaps) and I would recommend it, and the soundtrack is definitely worth picking up. But if you haven't played Lifeless Planet, you should definitely try that one out and I'd recommend that more.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I played, "Lifeless Planet" many years ago and felt like it was a real hidden gem. I backed the Kickstarter for "Lifeless Moon" based on the quality of the original, and I wasn't disappointed. This is a walking sim / puzzle-lite narrative game. You don't need to have played "Lifeless Planet" to enjoy this, as it tells it's own distinct story. Voice acting, writing, music and visuals are all very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Lifeless Planet.  The setting and story were right up my alley.  I thought the puzzles were pretty good and enjoyed the platforming.  It felt good.  I definitely would have backed the Kickstarter for Lifeless Moon, but news of it didn't reach me until it was over.  But I was glad it was funded and kept an eye on its progress for these years.  When I got the notification that it was finally released, I bought it immediately.Well, I've now finished it, and Lifeless Moon is fine.  There are some striking visual moments, and I'll always enjoy a space setting.  But Lifeless Moon really dropped most of the "game" aspects of Lifeless Planet.  You can't really die unless you fall in a pit.  There's no oxygen to worry about.  The jetpack is still here, but it's not used as effectively as in Lifeless Planet.  Basically, it's a walking simulator.  I have enjoyed a few walking simulators, and this one... was good.  If you liked Lifeless Planet, you'll get some enjoyment out of Lifeless Moon.  But it's definitely inferior.I'm happy the game came out, and I'm happy I played it.  But the thing is, Lifeless Planet is a game that's stuck with me, and it's something that I've contemplated replaying (And have. in fact, restarted a few times, but my gaming time is limited.  One day!).  As for Lifeless Moon, one play through was probably enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, but you get way too many notes and pop ups. It definitely detracts from the experience. Also, while it looks better than the first game, the visuals haven't exactly been upgraded that much. I'd argue that visuals are very important in a walking sim type game, but it's not that big of a deal. Artistically, it looks great, so that's good. After liking Lifeless Planet quite a bit, I expected more from Lifeless Moon, but it's not bad. I'd probably recommend getting it during a sale though.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relatively slow paced game. If you are inclined to play it quickly with little exploration of each area for content and with no wish to soak in the vibes then you may not like this too much. If you are happy to explore at a gentler pace and enjoy the mood of it, this fits the bill. Sometimes this sort of smaller game is just what I want by way of a change from larger, faster, frantic and more complex titles.I liked Lifeless planet and this is a worthy sequel in the same vein. So you have easy paced exploration with platforming and puzzles and an unfolding story. The graphics/maps, the music and voice acting, the notes and logs, all contributed to the slightly spooky atmosphere nicely.The solutions to various puzzles are simply observation and a little thought, nothing was particularly difficult and the changing scenery and action sequences kept the experience fresh.Both lifeless planet and this have a place on my replay list for when I'm in the mood for something a little more relaxed.It took me about seven hours since I'm in no hurry and it provided me with a pleasant evenings entertainment.Look forward to the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game that really needs a neutral rating. It's a fun experience, but it only lasts about 2 hours, and calling it a game is kind of generous. It's essentially 2 hours of holding W to move forward through the cutscenes until you finish the story. It's interesting and reasonably well paced, but that's basically it. There are some light puzzle elements, some basic platforming....but it's mostly just hold W. I would probably not recommend this for more than 5-10$, so maybe wait for a deep sale. How this is listed at 20$ normally I am really not sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good little game, but I have to be honest - I expected more. Lifeless Planet is one of my favorite walking sims, but this one feels like a  step backwards. It's shorter, has fewer game mechanics (the first person puzzle solving is new), and it's not as mysterious as the first one. Half way through the game you already know the mystery... Well, at least the most important part of the mystery.That being said... the story is good, atmosphere is fantastic, and I loved the music. It's an easy recommendation if you like slow paced atmospheric games. But I can't shake the feeling that with just a little more work this could have been a much better game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: Eerie, beautiful, and well driven story just like Lifeless Planet, but big improvements on removing unfun mechanics like the air refills + the jumping and traversal is more polished than Planet. I'm happy I purchased this and love this developers work. Also, the game is scored (musically) so beautifully.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review: It is a calm, fun, and inviting game to chill out and relax to. Wasn't expecting much from a 15 dollar game but the music and  style of the graphics was incredible. great but very short story that I feel like could've had a little more depth into it but still fantastic! Voice acting was absolutely gorgeous to my ears and not muffled or anything. I recommend to anyone looking for a nice calm experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

_childDocuments_.review:
During an expedition to the Moon, two astronauts find themselves in a familiar town back on Earth. They soon discover the town is the beginning of a strange and mysterious journey...

Lifeless Moon is a spiritual successor to our previous title Lifeless Planet. Featuring support for VR (but playable without!), Lifeless Moon takes players on a fantastic journey through the eyes of Apollo-era astronauts. There will be light platforming and a deeper focus on puzzles than in Lifeless Planet. The core game-play experience is one of exploration and discovery, complementing the mysterious and psychological themes of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Lifeless Moon

name: Not For Broadcast
detailed_description: Out Now on VR! About the Game Feature List: Deep and meaningful gameplay decisions 14 distinct endings Darkly-comic branching narrative Over 42 hours of full motion video (FMV) - a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ achievement Bursting with musical numbers Take control of the National Nightly News. With the nation's eyes fixed on your choices, it’s up to you to decide what gets broadcast. Choose the shots, censor any “troublesome” content, and steer the narrative as your country tumbles into totalitarianism. No pressure, right? Hand-pick the Headlines Not For Broadcast drops you into the heart of a darkly-comedic tale of televised chaos, where your every decision helps shape the fate of a nation. From ego-fueled celebrities to deceptive politicians and enigmatic advertisers - you control the public’s perception. As long as you can hold the audience’s fickle attention, it’ll be your choice whether to toe the party line or hype up the scandal. Will you make that sportsman seem like a national treasure, or an alcoholic disgrace? What about those scientists trapped in Dante’s Taint? Or that new boss at multinational giant Rymmington-Svist who seems to live a double life? Most importantly, will you help the brand-new government look benevolent, or is there something untoward about them that the public need to see? The power is in your hands to change everything, but you’ll have to decide quickly - the news goes out live! Craft the Narrative (and the Nation's Fate) You are in the driving seat of a multi-level tale about both an entire country and a single family. Being the architect of the nation’s future is a challenge, to be sure, but so is trying to hold your household together through the dark times. With multiple branching narratives, every choice you make resonates into the future. Will you help your spouse’s sibling flee the country... even if it involves breaking the law? Who are ‘Disrupt’ - concerned citizens or something more revolutionary? And how do you feel about your son spending more and more time with them? And then there’s Grandma... Can you afford her life-saving treatment, or should you and your spouse be taking advantage of one of the Government’s brand-new Transition Centres? After all, granny, there’s nothing more noble than unburdening your children! And then there’s your broadcast room - when it’s not overheating, it seems to be trying to electrocute you. Keep the plates spinning as best you can, but remember, whether it’s a newsreader who just won’t take it any more, naked streakers at the Sportsboard Final, or the ever growing threat of nuclear war... this show MUST go on. Cue the Ads Select your ads carefully to mould the public’s opinion. Why not choose to show only adverts for the companies you have shares in? Maybe that extra cash will help with the difficult decisions at home. Or maybe you’ll be selling dangerous toys to the nation’s children… With more than 50 hilarious ads to choose from there’s never a dull moment - even during the breaks. Endure the Unthinkable and Laugh in the Face of Adversity There will be smiles, there will be tears, even as the world falls apart around your ears. So grit your teeth, close your eyes and keep those cameras rolling - the people are counting on you. Long live the National Nightly News.

short_description: A new political Party has won a landslide in the General Election, and for some reason the editor at the news station you work at has done a runner. Now it’s up to you, the Janitor, to take over the editing booth in this tumultuous time - will you help the government, or stand in their way?

_childDocuments_.review: Great game ! I had a lot of fun playing the first stages, look forward to playing the next ones. Really, there were moments of pure hilarity thanks to a great script and very good actors. The game can be very hard sometimes, it demands a very good focus and to not let you distract by the good actors (for example the dance show which was hilarious but you can't just watch you need to broadcast! Or more serious moments I don't want to spoil). The underlying message could be very interesting (the supposedly righteousness of the politicians while they don't even try to hide that it is completely fake) but the way the narration is made doesn't really highlight it. Well that's not even a bad point. This game is really fun. Just one (tiny) thing - i don't really see the point of the personal story of the broadcaster (his mate Sam and her brother, and their son and...). It can take loooong minutes not fun at all to fill questionnaires, replying to questions that I don't understand how they can possibly affect the end. But let's wait til the end ! I totally trust the developers !

This one did not let me know so far. For the money I paid, I'm excited to see what the future holds for the team because as it stands I only got about 1.5 hours of play from it, but I intend to wait around for more content and play more! _childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW WAS MADE AFTER EPISODE 1I found this game while exploring the steam store, and I was immediately intrigued. I saw an opportunity for a new style of storytelling that can immerse people in ways that haven't been before. But it would only happen if the developers were able to create an interesting story to make this point and click game work. And wow they totally surpassed all of my expectations. The episodes are funny, witty, chaotic, and intriguing all at the same time. While at first the story can seem confusing, they do a great job clarifying it and do a great job keeping me at the edge of my seat. I left each level wanting more. 8.5/10, I am very excited to see where the developers take this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Because I used to work in the journalism field, I knew I wanted to play Not For Broadcast. I also knew that there was no way I would have time to immediately, so it lived on my wish list for over 2 years while I got through other things. Almost 10 hours in so far, I realize I made a huge error in depriving myself of this for more than 30 seconds. Buckle up kids, we're about to go on a trip.I was expecting the game play from the demo and the trailers. Picking the news segments, choosing where to camera, play ads, censoring politicians who get drunk and swear, all the best parts of working in a newsroom without having to have your face on it. What I was not expecting was the absolute bonkers amount of content this game has and the massive variety of branches and options, all of which is seamlessly spliced together, and all live recorded and acted. TL;DR this game is exceptionally well made, well performed, and is an absolute pleasure to play. 8.5/10The game splits between two game play modes. The first is playing the operator in the studio, pressing the buttons that determine what the media shows the public, This will swap public opinion's views on the political and cultural landscape and affect the story you experience.  This portion has several minigames of varying difficulty, representing the production of different types of segments in a daytime news show. Each game is unique in its mechanics and each comes with its own challenges. The combined effect each of these interactions gives a stunningly accurate representation of how a show of that nature is created and produced. That's not to say all of them are *fun*, as there are definitely ones that I found more tiresome than enriching (I'm looking at you Shock Tower). But they all worked together to actually feel and look like a news broadcast. It truly felt like a really talented team sat down and had meaningful discussions about how a broadcast is made. It also shows that great care was given to combine the different toys in the their toolbox into unique and interesting game play.The second play mode is a text based dialogue with response choices. While the interaction itself is just a simple choice, this is where the narrative effects of the choices you made in broadcast shape and impact the world. There are parallel story lines with members of your family, celebrities in the world, technology, and so much more. The writers had to have had an incredible time taking real headlines and stories and situations from the news and adjusting them *just* enough to be distinct, as well as the hilariously absurd and obvious names for the characters in these stories. It's also a more relaxing comedown after the more stressful active play in the broadcast segment. The ability for the team to tie the characters here into the headlines in the broadcast makes a nice overarching narrative that makes the world feel so immersive.From a design standpoint, having a high number of branches and variations is an astronomical task to coordinate and layout. But what boggles my mind is how seamless things are cut together. The filming and acting are so well done that the pieces of content tied to the choices you make is put together with no noticeable jumps or cuts or broken transitions. That's basically impossible to do when hand animating stuff; to do it with recorded media is absurd. I cannot commend NotGames enough for that.All around, this is a wonderful game in every way. If I had any critique, the musical numbers feels really long and the rhythm game with it is not super forgiving. But it also doesn't seem to impact progression very much that I've noticed, so I phone it in and pay closer attention elsewhere.Highly recommend, buy this, support this team.

_childDocuments_.review: After a shaky launch with a bug on Windows 7 OS that caused massive frame rate drops, the problem seems to be solved now. It took a few weeks, but I am not privy to the scope of the problem or the size of the team. On to the game.Not for Broadcast is a Full Motion Video (FMV) video game. Meaning you'll be seeing quite a bit of real people acting. You take control of a janitor meant to help out a friend who keeps going out to parties and such (a kind of lame plot device, but it gives you a way to feel indebted to nobody). In what amounts to a combination of minigames you'll have to balance and micromanage to get a good score, you are tasked with taking over the broadcasting desk every few days (in game time). As the story progresses you are allowed to edit what is being show to the masses, the game does a great job of showing you just how edited TV is when a stuck up movie producer/director comes in for an interview. You can tell he's a jerk beforehand but arent really allowed to hear what is being said, afterwards you can go back and review the tapes of all the screens and mute/turn up whatever you'd like. I do hope they add some more controls to go through previous broadcasts. The developers obviously have put a lot of time and effort into this game, I enjoy taking part in something created with passion.I look forward to what this game has to offer and I gladly await their next update. .

_childDocuments_.review: A tremendously unique game with a compelling blend of humor and dead-serious drama. I'm not ordinarily into FMV games but the interesting role you're placed in and choices that lead to a significant difference in outcomes is done extraordinarily well. You're bombarded with new information constantly that challenges your previous assumptions and has you questioning your alliances and choices. Even though you could try to infer real life versions of the game's parties, I thought the various fictional elements were a helpful way of encouraging the player to detach from their usual leanings and consider both sides vying for your help and to acknowledge how messy reality can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: Of course in early access, not everything will stay the same, whether this will be the visuals or some of the actors who appear. Just reached the end of the game (So far) and very excited for the release of further episodes. If you didn't read the synopsis on the steam page before scrolling down, then here's a summery:Your name is  walk into this empty studio room to clean or something, the landline phone rings, guy quits and leaves you with the baby sitting job.Personally I would walk out but, being a game all about choice, you aren't allowed to walk out, and if you decide to get fired on purpose from something you weren't even assigned to do, it's  meaning you have to start over again (Thankfully not from the very beginning but before a pivotal moment)The game also follows the usual "Sit n' Survive" games, just with a little more relatable real world stress with the need to keep viewer rates up, make sure you've got the right camera on, don't stay on the same camera for too long, mess with the signal, check whether the system's overheating , listening to multiple sounds coming from different feeds, censoring crude language to make sure parents don't sue the news for allowing their "Innocent angel" to overhear something they already use way too much  and other complicated stuff... It's almost like getting a real job, but without the effort of going out and finding one!Something that I think needs to be done for an update is the ability to skip forwards or backwards when reviewing the footage you've already edited and sent out to the gullible masses (Pretty much us) and other filmed footage, and the option to edit the size or transparency of the subtitles, they can sometimes get in the way of options.Other than that, I'm really eager for the next episodes and more of the mechanics, I just hope it won't get too cluttered.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: Not for Broadcast recreates the vision mixer/Video tape Operator role quite accurately, based off my past "media studies" course,  not in terms of the game mechanics which are innovative but the emotions of the Presenters and the crew on set during a shoot. This is also why i've only been able to play for around an hour at a time.The game recreates the "It'll be alright on the night" attitude as everything slowly falls apart around you and it's all on you to make it work! by cutting around cameras live, timing the VT's correctly and cutting to thebeat of a music video. The developers have managed to continue to deliver on Early Access promises, in the latest update "The Telethon" which is around 50 minute's long and was shot and put out during UK lockdown.If you like this format of comedy i suggest watching the movie "Living in Oblivion".Not for Broadcast is highly deserving of the Steam "Most innovative gameplay" award as there's nothing quite like it and also needs to be nominated for a BAFTA once it ends Early Access.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really interested in seeing how this story is gonna turn out (even though i already get hints of what types of endings we might get).I super dig the FMV return that's happening nowadays and the acting is really good. The writing is very on point right now and i wanna know what can happen to a broadcast station that's just 24/7 Advance propaganda or how you'll be able to integrate the resistance into it all. The gameplay is really tight but censoring needs some work with both the audio cues and visual since you can't really hear the beep while editing; otherwise I'd like to see other types of system added in the future like sound mixing if possible or other interactions with the office. I can see it being really promising and with the right notes it could be a second papers please that's a bit less subtle and more traditionally "fun" but just as engaging.Really looking foward to how this works in the long term. Keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever sat there and thought "I want to go into television" but not the boring television like antiques roadshow and homes under the hammer, you want to do exciting TV. The big news broadcasts where important breaking news is delivered, the shows and interviews that will become future memes because they are so horrendously outrageous or cringeworthy. Maybe you watched Joker and thought "Yes.. that's the type of TV I want to go into! People getting show on a talk show! How exciting!" Well first, maybe talk to someone then second play this game! Getting to bleep all the swearwords so you get the entertainment but know you're spoiling that excitement for others, watching naked protesters jiggle their privates on 3 screens whilst you only show the audience that one boring screen.. bliss!It's really funny, it's really fun, and it's really challenging. I can't wait for more!
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the devs for this game are really motivated to create a good game, and they did just that. Not For Broadcast is an immersive, challenging game with a unique story behind it. The graphics are fantastic. In this game you really do feel like you are controlling a broadcast. Multiple concepts of control and video express a comical story with only at few main characters in the early access mode. Being able to look back at your own broadcasts like you made it makes the game feel real. The old style of click-to-progress story describes in depth, what the main character does outside of broadcasting and presents tough decisions to make regarding your family. This is an outstanding game, and I am beyond excited to see what comes next in the immersive story.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game, in really it shows how different show edits can manipulate and change stories completely. The acting was great, and there were a lot of subtle jokes that were amusing. I enjoyed the multiple endings, and the rich story line. It is not action intensive, or has really any puzzles, but is focused on amusement.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: This has very quickly wormed its way into my heart and became a new favourite of mine, i first bought it when it was in early access and after playing it both on my PC and on VR i can definitely say you're getting your moneys worth with it. The classic British humour is amazing but you cannot play this game without also getting yourself sucked into its amazing story and its equally amazing characters, plus the multiple endings and DLC just make you want to play it again and again. I could not recomment Not For Broadcast more to anyone out there, it truly is a unexpected gem coming from a new studio and im excited to see what they do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game when it only had its first chapter. Since then, I've played through the game again and seen all the engaging and fun gameplay interactions. Not just in the broadcasting station, but at home as well. This game is so easy to enjoy and lose yourself in the characters and story. The gameplay itself is fun too! With most levels containing their own challenges, it's especially fun to play alongside friends!But, let me tell you something. When I hit a certain broadcast in chapter 2...I realised that this game isn't afraid to shy away from anything. And I was hit pretty hard with the truth that this game can deliver some pretty hefty blows, regardless of who you are. The character you play as in this game just so happens to have the same name as me in real life so when certain scenes happen, it  all the more powerful to me, personally. All I have to say is, if you choose to buy and play this game(which I highly recommend you do), go into it with a readiness to enjoy the story and its characters...even the ones you might not enjoy too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the game kind of surprised me. Initially, I thought I would be bored with the mechanics of the game and the content, especially if it was low effort. Boy is this anything but low effort. It's a very good game if you enjoy your decision changing the course of the game. You'll get yourself very invested into the story as you pick sides and essentially play out what the general public will see on the news. Will you be someone who shows people the truth? Or are you more concerned with those sweet sweet viewers? Don't let the simple mechanics fool you either, you slowly start to realize why people say it is impossible to multitask. I can see the difficulty of this game getting much much harder as they release more content. I bought the game for $13 and got 2.1 hours of content out of it. Even in early access form, money well spent. I look forward to new content!

_childDocuments_.review: While the basic gaming idea is similar to that of "Papers, please", the concept in which it's presented is -in my mind- really good. I love indie games that tackle serious real-life issues, and this game surely does. That said, the game is far from being complete, the current version is more like a proof of concept, a preposition of a story that I'm curious about how it will move on.Is it worth to buy it right now ? Depends highly on what you expect - if you look for a "normal" game to casually play, this may not be your best bet. But if you see games as a form of art, remember this piece - it has all the potential to be a fun game while also telling/teaching you a lot about politics, the influence of the media and the sheer crazyness this world has become. On a sidenote, I really like the absurd an semi-professional acting in some of those scenes, which reminds the player from time to time that this is (thankfully) just a game. But a game that keeps me thinking about its message, even if I'm not playing. And that's a thing a game rarely achieves. So thumbs up for this game-experiment !

_childDocuments_.review: Not for Broadcast" is a trainwreck masquerading as a game. It's a cringe-fest tailor-made for drama club dropouts who couldn't land a role in a high school play. The game is chock-full of woke nonsense, shoving endless monologues down your throat while trying to convince you that it's profound, when it's really just a tedious mess of self-important drivel. The acting is so bad, it makes low-budget 1980s pornos look like Oscar-winning performances. The entire experience feels like it was designed for someone with the IQ of a houseplant. If you're looking for a painful, eye-rolling journey through cringeworthy mediocrity, "Not for Broadcast" is the perfect punishment.
