_childDocuments_.review: "Not For Broadcast" is a truly exceptional game that immerses players in the thrilling world of television broadcasting and challenges them to make tough decisions that shape the narrative. As a fan of unique and engaging gameplay experiences, I was captivated from the moment I started playing.One of the standout features of "Not For Broadcast" is its innovative gameplay mechanics. The game brilliantly captures the essence of controlling a live television broadcast, putting you in the hot seat as the operator responsible for censoring and managing the content. The real-time decision-making adds an exciting level of tension, making every choice feel significant. It's incredibly satisfying to see the impact of your decisions unfold on the screen.The game's narrative is equally impressive. The storyline is intricately woven, filled with unexpected twists and turns that kept me engaged throughout. The satirical take on media manipulation and censorship is thought-provoking, shedding light on the power dynamics and ethical dilemmas present in the media industry. "Not For Broadcast" masterfully combines humor and social commentary, delivering a compelling and relevant narrative.Visually, the game is a treat. The attention to detail in recreating a broadcast studio is commendable. From the meticulously designed sets to the authentic-looking news segments, every aspect feels realistic and polished. The graphics are crisp, and the use of multiple camera angles enhances the immersion.Furthermore, the voice acting and audio design are top-notch. The cast delivers stellar performances, bringing the characters to life with their distinct personalities and emotions. The background music and sound effects create an immersive atmosphere, perfectly complementing the intense moments and adding depth to the overall experience.The replay value of "Not For Broadcast" is exceptional. With multiple story paths and outcomes based on your decisions, the game encourages replayability, allowing you to uncover different storylines and consequences. It's a testament to the game's depth and complexity that each playthrough feels fresh and exciting.In conclusion, "Not For Broadcast" is an outstanding game that seamlessly blends immersive gameplay, a captivating narrative, and thought-provoking themes. It's a unique experience that challenges players to think critically about the media landscape while offering an engaging and entertaining adventure. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone seeking a truly remarkable gaming experience.Rating: ★★★★★

_childDocuments_.review: NFB is so terrified of interacting with its own premise that the plot goes out of its way to be completely nonsensical while still trying to convince the player that the decisions they make do matter, resulting in the story see-sawing between humor and drama and effectively achieving neither. Add to that the poor and inconsistent execution of its main mechanics, extraordinary tedium on replay and lack of QoL features, and clear over-ambition, and Not For Broadcast falls short in basically every aspect of what it could've been.First off, credit where it is due: The FMVs work better than I thought they would. A couple of single-appearance characters are less than convincing, but that hardly detracts from the 99% of the acting that create memorable and colorful characters. There's quite a lot of actors too, and it was impressive how careful they were even about reusing extras so as to not break the illusion. That's where the game's positives end. Now, as for the negatives:- Despite the title and hints given by the game, airing footage "Not For Broadcast" almost never makes an impact and is difficult to do in the first place. Now, all games like this (the obvious comparison is "Papers, Please", which NFB even includes a nod to) tend to include a drawback to the player breaking the in-universe rules, to present risks and rewards, but NFB doesn't give you any feedback about when playing not-for-broadcast material (that is, things you weren't supposed to cut to, were supposed to cut away from, or are happening during a commercial break) will have an impact. They had to include a **loading screen hint** for the time in the first level when it *does*, because they have no other way of signalling that information to the player! And whenever you do air such content, you are punished swiftly and harshly at even the normal difficulty. *A* punishment makes sense, but making it so players can't afford to experiment on an average run is really not conducive to the mechanic IN THE NAME OF THE GAME- Because they so royally screwed up the mechanic that, once again, is the entire name of the game, they change the rules halfway through the game. The only actual "not for broadcast" material that matters will be on clearly marked tapes or cameras. The player still has the choice to play it or not, but the entire process has been dumbed down, and the penalties for playing this supposedly "not for broadcast" material are a lot more nebulous and avoidable. So all the actual feeling of risk and rebellion is taken out of the equation, again rendering the entire point of the mechanic moot. Also this happens like, twice in the entire game.- Out of I assume a terror of accidentally offending someone or saying anything meaningful, the plot has been constructed to be utterly divorced from reality, with the side effect of giving you nothing to care about. The two political factions that, broadly speaking, can be considered to be vying for your allegiance as editor of the news station, are: 1) A fascist moron who commits mass murder, orders assassinations, and has people brainwashed, but seems legitimately surprised when her supporters turn out to be fascists and is also portrayed as sincerely caring and benevolent by the game, and 2) freedom fighter black Alex Jones, who was right about everything. Because you see, the left and the right are *both* evil. Only centrism is the enlightened path, the game tells you outright.- In case those stunning choices of groups to support weren't enough player motivation, they have also given the player a family. Who do nothing. And have no impact on the story. They were extremely obviously stapled on to the actual plot in a weak attempt at pathos. In Papers, Please, keeping your family alive was the entire *point* of the game. What happened to them mattered, and effected your options later in the story. In NFB, they're just fluff.- Despite the title image for this game, the player isn't subject to anyone's controls and doesn't suffer any consequences for anything less than purposefully running a show into the ground. Not to compare to Papers, Please too much, but in that game, you could be imprisoned for hanging a picture on your wall. If you played your cards wrong, the revolution would shoot you in your booth. There were real consequences to your actions, for you. Because you were just a cog in the machine. In NFB, no one can touch you. You don't work from the shadows to help your chosen cause, or just toe the line and try to get home to your family every day. People address you, by name, on national television. You are the most important person in the country, by the end. You, and you alone, get to decide the fate of the dictator of half a continent. But it doesn't feel earned. You're just magically untouchable for the sake of the game. It's really, really shoddy writing.- There's a lot of endings, but they all come down to a few inflection points. Does the game telegraph these? No. Is it even logical what leads to what path or ending? Arguably, not always. Sometimes it's not even clear what you can do differently, and what effect it'll have. And funniest of all is that most of these inflection points have little to do with something being "not for broadcast". You don't get punished for them, but then again, we've been over how little the game has to actually punish you with.- Because of the endings being wrapped up in a couple of events, all the other levels are just filler! You CAN'T do anything differently for most of them, basically the entire second half of the game. Almost all your choices are meaningless! You just have to sit through the exact same conversations and songs and dances every time you want to do a different route. Some smaller things can get changed, especially things they can just do voiceovers on still images for, but those don't really make up for 20 minutes of nothing! Clearly a game way too ambitious for its own good.- The pacing also feels really effed up. It's weird going a week or two between levels at first, and then YEARS at the end. I get that they were trying to make a point with it, but I don't think it worked. I think that the choose-your-own-nonventure sections were dull, and again, didn't interact with the main plot, so they really could've been entirely removed from the game with nothing lost.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected Not For Broadcast to be good, given the praise it has received, and NFB managed to surpass my expectations with ease. NFB is an absolutely fantastic ride that's brimming with top notch comedy and has a brilliant character cast to offer. The amount of effort that went into making this game must've been staggering, and for what it's worth, I think the payoff is splendid.The only problem with the game that comes to mind is a certain issue that many narrative-focused experiences suffer from, the way I see it. I'm writing this review mere minutes after watching the credits, and for now I intend to walk away and let the experience settle down in my mind, but afterwards I would certainly love to revisit Not For Broadcast and discover whatever I've missed, at the very least some of the alternative endings. Trouble is, I really can't imagine that being comfortable. I've already had to partially replay a certain segment of the game, and it wasn't a great feeling. So, chances are the most pragmatic play here is to go for external sources, and that's a bit of a shame.Also, I have to admit that I went for the story mode right off the bat. The gameplay mechanics are actually surprisingly engaging: managing the broadcast was brilliant at first, and moreover, I never felt that it was becoming a bother over time. Still, zero regrets on my end. Not having to worry about the audience made it far easier to focus on whatever was happening in the studio.So, again: NFB is a positively wonderful experience that has more than earned all of its accolodes.

_childDocuments_.review: Review written when 3 levels + Lockdown was released. May update once more content is available.TL;DR - this is a game with huge potential, and I was really immersed as the role of the broadcast controller. As a gamer who dives into story-rich games, I think it's a respectable asking price given what we have now and the content that is to come. =========I went into this expecting a Five Nights At Freddy's kind of game (but without the jumpscares). I was pleasantly surprised, however, at the depth of the game, from the humour to the smooth controls and to the story that is building steadily in the background. I was hungry for more after playing the Lockdown mission only to realize that my journey has ended (until Episode 2 comes). I found myself invested in what I was putting out, replaying every section that had a grade below A, and I was strangely invested in what was happening on other cameras - I found myself going back to the Rushes after every mission and it was intriguing. This is a good game with so much promise, and I am eagerly anticipating the release of new content. Amazing work from the NotGames team!Positives:+ The acting. Not like a blockbuster movie, but I had never expected that from the get-go. Every character was quite fleshed out (for its current short runtime) and the characters were quite believable.+ The writing is fantastic. Just... wow I am pleasantly amazed at the writing and the pretty slapstick humour within+ A good learning curve, an easy game to pick up+ The Archives Room. There was no way I could watch what was really going on when it got crazy  but going back to watch the Rushes was entertaining and made me laugh a lot+ Challenge Modes. I underestimated the game modes within and I was greatly humbled.+ The "minigames" (censoring, interference, camera switching et cetera) were in good taste, and feels immersive to my role as a controller.+ The soundtrack and the songs are well-written and manages to achieve the intended atmosphere.Meh:+/- Headlines were a little strange. I get that we need to pick a picture but some headlines were not what I initially interpreted them to be. The current game runtime right now seems a little short to see the full effects of the headlines but I am anticipating to see how this will turn out.+/- I personally didn't understand the point of the text adventure that was taking place in between, except as a vehicle to obtain the achievements. Again, I believe having more content in the future will bring the story full-circle and we can see the full effects of all our choices so far but as of right now, it's a "on-the-fence" feature for me.+/- The advert cassette player was abit wonky to control. Sometimes I can't load a tape and I need to carefully align my mouse to load the tape.+/- The Archive Room doesn't contain the adverts I did not select for the broadcast. Here's to hoping that they will all be made available for viewing (perhaps once you complete the game at least once?).+/- Having both Live and Broadcast sounds playing off the same set of speakers was okay, but I was hoping that I can do a stereo setting (left speaker for Live, right speaker for Broadcast, for instance).Negatives:- - I felt that the viewer sensitivity was abit too harsh for some sections, such as having slight interference,  since it seemed a bit challenging to toggle to a greenlit screen quick enough, and away from it when it became yellow (this was during my very first attempt, however).- That being said, I felt very happy playing this so far, and I am very excited to see more content. Kudos once again!

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this is not a casual game, it starts off rather easy but the difficulty ramps up quickly, having to deal with multiple mechanics at the same time and I can imagine later versions will get more complicated.Not For Broadcast is a modern FMV game where you play as a broadcaster for a news station, having to keep the audience entertained by keeping order in the chaotic world of news and deciding what to and what not to show. In between broadcasts you have COYA sections about the protagonist dealing with family life and troubles. So far the game is around 1 to 2 hours long with decent amounts of replay value. Choices do in fact matter as what might seem like a small issue can lead to huge results. Also the game has a rank system that goes up and down depending on how interested the audience is. It's worth noting the ranking system is rather strict as even a small mistake can cause your rating to plummet. Doing something especially stupid, like playing an ad during a news section, will instantly end the game and make you replay the segment, which can be up to 10 minutes long.About the politics, the game, at least to me, seems anti-centralization, but that could change as the story progresses.EDIT: FULL RELEASEWell I was mostly right about it being anti-centralization, it does take a more middle ground than I expected. My opinion of the game is still the same as before, also there's a total of 14 endings so it's got replay value if that matters. Althoug I can imagine it'd be a pain because from what I can tell, the news broadcasts for the most part don't change all that much outside of a few key moments. For a total game length, I'd say it's about 10-ish hours long for a single playthrough

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast – A Broadcast of Chaos 📺🗣️Not For Broadcast is the political thriller we never knew we needed... until now. Picture this: you’re a janitor (yes, a janitor) suddenly thrust into the high-stakes world of news broadcasting during a political crisis. Your job? Edit and air the chaos, all while trying to stay sane. Spoiler alert: you won’t. 🧹🎥You’ll find yourself in the control room of a major news station, juggling live broadcasts, making questionable decisions (like what gets aired), and possibly altering the course of history, all from behind a desk covered in clutter. It’s like House of Cards, but with more malfunctioning equipment and less scheming politicians. 🤯📡The best part? You get to choose whether you want to help the new government stay in power or stir up some rebellion with your editorial choices. Who knew being a janitor could have such power? 💼💣The humor in this game is sharp, witty, and delightfully dark—perfect for anyone who’s ever wanted to sit in the editor’s chair and play puppet master, or in this case, propaganda guru. The ridiculousness of the situation will have you laughing and cringing at the same time. The pressure builds as you have to decide what gets aired while dealing with technical glitches, angry anchors, and the looming question: Will you save the government or expose their lies? 📰💥In short, Not For Broadcast is a satirical, wild ride that gives you power over the media (and your sanity). It’s chaotic, it’s clever, and it’ll make you wonder if maybe being a janitor wasn’t such a bad gig after all... as long as you’re behind the broadcast booth. 😜📺Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a "choices matter" fan with even a glancing interest in Soviet politics/history and/or Animal Farm and/or 1984 and/or recent U.S. decline and/or dystopian novels... well this is too juicy/fun/brilliant to miss. It's brilliantly done, especially if you have familiarity with the USSR/related cultures, imo. Unlike many of these games, I'm actually keen to do a replay right away to see how, indeed, my choices mattered. (Plus I played on easy to learn the game, but want to do a more challenging mode on replay) It's a decent time investment--about 8 hours for each play-through (ish)--and relative to the price point, I highly recommend it. It's good bang for buck, especially if you grab it during the Steam sale, as I did.  I was impressed with the acting and writing in particular, as well as the parody songs/performances. Everyone goes all in and it's engaging all the way through. The only aspect I found mildly annoying was the interference challenges... fiddling w/ that knob is tedious! Kudos to the whole team behind this, including/especially the director(s)--whatever notes you gave to the various actors were A+++ for nailing tone/satire, especially all the "celebrities." _childDocuments_.review: This was a game I really wanted to like.  The idea that you're playing as someone working in the News Room as a Communist party slowly takes over the government is very appealing.  It's even more appealing that you can choose how to react to the situation leading to several different endings.  And to be clear this game isn't a lazy cash grab, a lot of talent has been put into it, particularly the acting and it's not like there's only one talented actor, the entire cast gives an amazing performance.But I can't in good conscience recommend this game.  This is sadly an example of a game that was too ambitious and tried to do too much.  This game really needed someone higher up to pull back the developing team and force them to pick their favorite ideas and focus on them.  The game has major issues with both it's story and the game mechanics itself.Game Mechanics:The mechanics of the game have several major issues.1. The game is constantly throwing new mechanics at the player.  Even the final level of the game has a brand-new mechanic in it which is crazy.  What's even worse is that a lot of mechanics are only used once and then dropped.  Like don't get me wrong, many games have levels with a gimmick (ice level) but the issue is that the game doesn't establish a good enough flow to be breaking it up this regularly. The fact mechanics are changing constantly is made even worst by the second point.2. The game gives little to no player feedback.  The size of your audience doesn't necessarily reflect your actual score.  So you can have a green level of audience but be getting a D (A is the best) for your score.  The game doesn't ever tell you why this is but based on context clues I'm assuming your score is based on the amount of mistakes you made that level and your difficulty setting.  This is where the buzzing doesn't help, yes sometimes it will be obvious what mistakes you made but for the biggest core mechanic, editing videos, there's little to no indication on if you're doing a good job, except for the graph at the end which isn't helpful in my opinion.However the worst to suffer from this is the CYOA parts of the game.  While some major story choices will literally be spelled out to the player, others will be completely hidden.  In fact I'm convinced that unless you're using a walkthrough the game is designed to make players get a terrible ending their first time through.  Major mechanics such as public opinion on Advance (the communist party), Disrupt (the resistance) are hidden from you and you just get up arrows or down arrows.  Public opinion determines which ending you get so not having a solid number that tells you who the public likes more is very annoying and leaves you guessing based on how you've acted so far in the game.  Also I think public opinion affects the advertisers ending but I'm honestly not sure because the game doesn't make that clear.Likewise the game doesn't make it clear how you earn money.  Obviously, you can earn money through good performance at work but that's not true.  Only getting an A / B score will increase your wealth and there is no story events that will increase your wealth despite the game telling you having stock in said advertisers will increase your wealth.  This directly impacts some story choices for the player character.However the worst hidden feature is the Headliners.  The headliners that pop up at the beginning of every level DO change and have multiple outcomes but the game doesn't make this clear until the end.  And worst is that when you pick between headliners they give you the choice between two pictures and it's very unclear what the pictures are supposed to mean or what the newscasters will actually say.  So it's possible you might accidentally pick something you didn't mean but unless you replay the segment you won't know that.  This actually brings me into the third major issue with the game.3. Failing is extremely punishing!  It's very easy on normal to have your score drop from an A to an D due to a mistake, and look I like a good challenging rogue-lite like everyone but the issue here is that if you fail a segment you have to reload and watch the videos you had just seen all over again and hope you don't ♥♥♥♥ up on the same part again.  And some of these segments are 30 minutes long.  Like at times I was fiddling on my phone as I waited for the headliner section to be done so I could attempt the rest of the level again.  Halfway through the game I was ready to set it to story mode difficulty but again the game is very unclear if that's an option.  I was able to change it in the options menu but every time I quit the game it would reset back to normal and the game didn't feel that much easier so I don't know if the difficulty every actually changed.So if you want to play the game just for the story I beg you to set the difficulty to story mode, you will save yourself hours of frustration but the thing is the story itself isn't worth it in my opinion.Story Mode:To the game's credit, this isn't like your cheap telltale game.  Past choices are reference throughout the game and the game is FILLED with choices and outcomes (provided you know where to look for them).  The premise is exciting, watching the decent of a government from the eyes of a news team, there's so many things you can do with that.....and boy does the game do ALL of them.  Similar to the first bullet point of game mechanics the story suffers from over ambition and no one telling the writers to focus on something.The game's story takes place over the course of 5 years and you'll feel like the game has 5 years worth of stuff to talk about.  There's the story of the rise in power of the communist party and how they drastically change society, then there's the parody of business, the music industry, the film industry, politicians, rich people, scientist; and there's a war in there as well; plus we have the story of the PC (there name is Alex by the way) and their family, not to mention the story's of the news anchors (that's 7 people minimum, more if you count some strong supporting characters like the person who gets Alex the job).That's a lot to talk about and I haven't even gotten to the very complex themes the game wants to talk about.  The obvious issue with having all of this in the game is that there's no room to have a slow buildup or setup.  Like we don't see a slow descent as the communist party (Advanced) gains more and more power until they can only be stopped by an armed resistance; instead the party seems to get full control of the government in like 3 levels (but don't worry the time skip waves this away).Setups are constantly just not properly done.  Twice in the story they do a damasking moment, as in who is that character under the mask but neither is earned.  First off the mystery isn't properly setup since the masked figured isn't masked long enough for the audience to care, and there's nothing done to build up suspense and make the audience even ask the question "Who is under the mask?".  And second the answer is characters who we only saw once or twice prior and you can tell the writers want the audience to be like "OMG I can't believe it was them!" but more likely the audience will be like "Who are you again?".  This is made worse during the ending as each of the 12 stories the game is juggling will have their own multiple choice ending or mini character arc; which will just leave you confused as you try to remember who some of these people were.And then there are the themes which someone else can talk about because they suffer from the same setup problem.  The bottom line is because the game is so unfocused it makes for a sadly bland experience.  It would have definitely benefited from some cuts and a tighter focus but as it stands now while the game has many different endings you can find I have zero desire to sit through and rewatch that story again to experience them.

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in awhile, a piece of media just grabs hold of you, spins you around, tosses you back and forth, and doesn't let you go. This is one of those games. Humble monthly, now!I've never in my life had fits of uncontrollable laughter ina videogame. I did here twice. The story is so well presented and goofy, yet darkly serious and foreboding at times. The choices you make in the game feel weighty and change the broadcasts accordingly. The multi-tasking you must do in order to keep viewer count high and the broadcast edit watchable for your audience can be intimidating at first, but it starts to become second nature quickly. It's a dark comedy wrapped in a visual novel, dipped in a simulator sauce and baked on high til golden brown. Just fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. Plain and simple. It takes the FMV genre and twists it so much that creates something new and spectacular. Through its quirky jokes and satirical speech, it tries to touch serious matters about propaganda, politics and war.You are playing as a live TV broadcaster, and mainly try to choose the "correct" or "best" information to convey to the public. Most of the times, you face the consequences of your choices, and most of the times they are pretty brutal...The amount of content in the game is beyond belief, with up to four different (FMV) videos playing at the same time with no cuts, which can last for more than a dozen minutes.The script is amazing, the gameplay is hectic and meaningful, with implications both on the story and your performance as a broadcaster. There are also choose-your-own-adventure type of chapters where you just read the story and make your choices. And boy do your choices bite back...With 14 different endings and a lot of interesting choices and twists along the way, the game has much to offer. Maybe even too much for an FMV game.A single playthrough is about 10 hours long, but the asking price for the amount of work that was put into the game is a steal. A completionist could easily get 40 hours out of the game, but that would prove to be too much of a chore.Definitely grab it, even at full price, and when you start, give some room to the quirky humour... Serious society issues will rise through this TV satirical masterpiece.The best FMV game I have played, and most probably by far. The whole team made an excellent job: UI, OST, SFX, Acting, Story, Script, Choices, everything...10/10A must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast is a really incredibly unique and brilliant game. It is a game with real actors. You slip into the role of Alex, a man with a wife and children, who happens to broadcast a show one evening because a colleague has unfortunately fallen ill. He succeeds so well that he is hired full time. So you have to broadcast the shows: changing camera angles, censoring swear words, bringing in commercials, etc. To avoid the gameplay to become too easy and monotonous, there are always new elements: use a malfunctioning fan during a heatwave, dispense electric shocks to protect the antenna, insert emotions of the audience in the shows, etc. You also must decide what to broadcast and what to censor. All the broadcasts make up a unified story. Text passages are also introduced in between, through which you learn more about Alex and his private life.The actors are really talented, and the game is very fun. But the best thing, and I would like to emphasise this again, is definitely the incredibly good story. Not for Broadcast is set in a very special timeline. A new regime comes to power that wants to control and manipulate the masses and the media in a 1984-like (George Orwell) way. Everyone must decide for themselves which side they want to take.The game is relatively short with 5 hours of playing time. However, it is not over yet. There is still a sequel to come.I recommend this game to 100%. A refreshing, innovative gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast is a very original game concept which was executed very well. The game is still in early access so you are not getting the full experience just yet, however with more content on the horizon and the available sections hilarious and engaging I would definitely recommend this game to other players. I read some other reviews and completely agree that this game does NOT need gimmicks such as buttons breaking down or killer toys in order to be fun, the base game already introduces new mechanics at a frequent enough pace to keep the levels fresh. I think these features should be left for the challenge mode section which already exists. The game does have choice system, where you choose what makes it into the edit, what ads you play, what family choices you make - which offers some sort of replayability on top of improving your previous scores. As the game is still not complete it is hard to say whether or not these choices feel impactful later in the story. The choices are also not subtle, which is not necessarily a bad thing but the game always makes it clear to you "do you want option A or option B" or "picture A or B". Not something that annoyed me but some others seemed slightly bothered by it since its makes the choices feel shallow so I thought I would bring it up.The game is very polished, from the menu to the gameplay, everything runs well and plays well. The soundtrack is great and the game looks very nice. It touches upon political topics however approaches everything in a comedic tone. So if you want a laugh, a unique gameplay experience and a game that runs smoothly then this might be the game for you, I personally loved every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE GO INTO THIS GAME RAW. This game seriously had me reexamining my personal beliefs. Reading the wiki or looking at scripts puts into perspective how much your choices matter. One choice you make about your family changes the entire game. You start to really feel the consequences for your actions, and you really feel bad if you make the wrong choice. There are literally hundreds of alternate timelines in this game and choices at the start pave the way for your end. Even replaying this game allows you to make tiny changes to how play and you can watch the vast change in how the future pans out if you had acted differently in your first run. You get faced with crushing choices that make you think about your consequences and if what you're doing is worth it. I'm not gonna say my personal beliefs in which organizations are better, or how you should play situations, but this game had me on the pause menu for at least an hour total just thinking of the choice that I wanted to make in situations. You start to really connect with the actors and the anchors' friendships with one another. Gameplay wise, the game is simple but changes itself as you progress to make itself more difficult, but more engaging. Every day brings a new challenge, and you suffer or biinefit in other situations in the game based on how you play (Family is worse off because of wealth etc.)

_childDocuments_.review: Currently the game has around 2-3 hours of content, however, it has unique game mechanics that makes it interesting to try and makes you anticipate for more.I've played through the first episode which is available at the moment in Early Access, however, I have high hopes for this production. The work that the dev team put into it narratively (and I do not only mean the main storyline, even the micronarratives of the ads and the different segments) really shows that this game is a labor of love.Gameplaywise, I'll be waiting for the twists and implied features as I hope that the mechanics wouldn't fall back to just a game of reaction time and optimization. I hope that like the "choose-your-own-headline", there will be more mechanics that not only influence your performance rating but the story as well.Aesthetically I really like the looks of the game, the studio's controlls and layouts are intuitive. For future tweaks, I think it would be great to optimize the controls of the VHS tapes, as sometimes it needed two or three tries to place them correctly, and sometimes I encountered issues where the sound and the video of the master screen was not in sync (while the broadcast, in fact, was). I also wished for faster switches (they blacked out a milisecond longer than it was comfortable) on my main master screen as at the music and sports sections I felt that I lost some of the control over the content. However, maybe these are issues only I've encountered or only I've felt problematic.I'm invested in the narrative, and I like the family storyline also.Keep up the good work, devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst not perfect I would still highly recommend purchasing this, even in early access. The price tag is a little much for what you get, but thinking of it as an investment in the ongoing development of the game makes it more than worth it. This is certainly a project that deserves an opportunity to continue and should be supported. Positives:1) A rather endearing sense of cynical humour that hits the spot. (I'm British so maybe that helped) 2) A well observed commentary on today's growing politics and news environment. (Again, it felt particularly applicable to Britain but I get the feeling this stuff is everywhere these days.) 3) The sub plot over a strained family life is engaging and has a slowly building sense of foreboding to it, which is impressive considering it's just a few paragraphs of text and a few options. I sense it will not end well, but I don't think any of the story elements to this game will have a happy ending. (but it will be a good story)4) On the above, the general narrative and plot is intriguing. In the game as it now stands we only have hints and seeds of future events, but I already want to know more. Not just about the main plot but also the side elements such as the established host having to face a thirsty challenger after his job, Dave's flight abroad (presumably to avoid new taxes) and so many others. 5) I have the feeling that the game is setting us up for a "papers please" style choice between diligently doing you job and supporting a questionable resistance at great personal risk.  Indeed, the rapid and time pressured checking of numerous factors combined with that sort of tone makes this whole game seem like a more advanced spiritual successor to "papers please" and that is no bad thing! Particularly as this game seems to give the player more choice.6) The acting! From self aware goof to surprisingly straight the acting in this game is on point and enjoyable throughout. Serious points go to the two main hosts, the Alex Jones stand in who might just be right, our leaders from Advance and Striker and Harris who manage to play the entirely fictitious and utterly ludicrous rubber ball game with just the right blend of straight and comedy. Negatives: (I should stress the positives outweigh the negatives in my opinion) 1) Difficulty curve. I made the papers please comparison earlier and it stands. However, whilst papers please gradually introduced new elements and challenges slowly allowing the player to get to grips with it leading to the end of the game being pressured but dooable with focus, attention and calm. This game asks a little too much a little too quickly. Especially since you have to pay attention to lots of things simultaneously. Maybe I just have the uncoordinated flailing of an octopus but in places the combination of factors all at once was overwhelming and it felt like the way to do well was to repeat sections over again until you learnt what would come next, rather than react. If the difficulty curve continues in this way the game would become far too hard and frantic, to the point it might even detract from the narrative. 2)  The replay archive section needs a fast forward or time bar feature like in a youtube video. In this game you have the opportunity to re-watch the broadcast as you sent it out, and re-watch parts that did not go to air. These are interesting features and I particularly enjoyed the ability to re-watch what was edited out, as it can be illuminating. The problem is you have to sit through the whole section (that you often just watched) to get to the bit you want. This can be dull. So the ability to fast forward or jump to a timestamp of your choosing would make much better use of this feature.  Summary: If you enjoy a good narrative and don't mind some mechanical ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to enjoy said narrative, this is certainly the game for you. Funny, cynical, well acted, well observed, well written and an odd sense of foreboding all make this very enjoyable. The minor downsides only come in the mechanics / difficulty imposed by those mechanics. These are fixable and do not lessen the enjoyment mentioned above. As stated at the start of the review this is a project that deserves to go on and I would strongly encourage the reader to support this game's ongoing development.

_childDocuments_.review: lol this is absolutely brilliant!The gist of the game is that you are an operator of a TV News station. You have to control what people in their home are gonna watch and hear, switching the broadcast from 4 different cameras, beeping profanity, adjusting the signal, deciding what image to show etc..The flow alternates between broadcasting segments and home/family events, presented in the form of multi-choice textual narratives. The story unfold in a multi-layered fashion, where your decisions in the "home" segments affect your life. The kicker is that the decisions you take "in the control room" affect the political landscape of the nation, with ramifications in your everyday life.The broadcast segments will definitely test your multitasking skills and the home segments provide a nice change of pace. All the actors are very committed and it's clear that they had a lot of fun recording this. The content itself is generally politically loaded or hilarious and surreal, I know that there are a lot of interesting ideas in the indie/semi-indie scene, but I wasn't prepared on how unique, fun and original this game is. I've just barely started and can't wait to see what else there is.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. The core game play is the the most fun I've had with a niche sim in a very long time. I couldn't stop thinking about coming back home to replay all day. In the meantime, I ended up watching videos on youtube of a guy filming his being a technical director (the term in the US for what this game simulates) for his local news station (which was awesome).My point being, I'm very excited about the future of this game. I think every part about the game while you're sitting at the console is wonderful. Funny acting, commercials, skits, writing, and my god, more rhythm game cut sequences in the future please! I think that's my favorite part. However, in the hopes of offering constructive criticism to make the game even better, I must confess that I find the writing lacking in the text based intermissions between broadcasts. I found myself yelling at the screen to get on with it already until I had finally started the 3rd broadcast. I picked the option to work overtime when boseman asked me to solely in the vain hope that it would trigger another broadcast. That is a very clear indication that I care nothing for these characters as people. If I did, if the characters were developed as fleshed out people that we come to know and care about, that would be a different story. If the writing was good enough, I would even consider skipping out on a bonus broadcast just to appease my spouse. And I might do it too... I'm a real sucker for really well written empathy driven games.This game would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ legendary if that were to happen. So, please, with the money that you make from these early access sales, use some of it to research and hire a really good writer to fix these parts.To whoever wrote these parts, I'm sorry, I'm not intending to target you individually. That's what early access is for, to smooth out the rough edges. Everyone wants something truly great, and this game is so close to having it all. I'd like to end with the highest praise I can give this game, which is that it sometimes reminds me of The Day Today, with Chris Morris. Like in the first episode where he says 'sounds like sour grapes to me, Geoff', that's so Chris Morris, lol.

As soon as you hit Day 232(Episode II), everything falls off a cliff. The writing is awful, the jokes don't land, the game play becomes mundane and a chore rather than chaotic and tense. If you can get this for around 10-15 bucks just to play the first 3-4 hours, I would say go for it. but full price? _childDocuments_.review: Picked this up because I love FMV. Sadly, not one I could recommend (although I'll likely play to the end). The gameplay and concept are probably the game's strongest elements. The mix between FNAF's technological multitasking and Papers Please's governmental bureaucracy proves pretty fun - although some segments are a bit slow and some a bit overwhelming, there was never a moment where I was done with the gameplay itself. However, the FMV - the writing, acting, set design - that's where the game really ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed. I get that this is an indie project, but most of the actors feel more like youtubers doing a cameo than actors playing a role - even the lead anchorman spends most of his time doing a B- impression of David Mitchell. The humor itself is fun at times, but often obnoxiously "epic random", and the nature of the game means that several gags just go on way too long.There's massive mood swings too - the "off camera" sequences, when you're offered some choices in your day-to-day life, have no comedy in them whatsoever. You wrap up a news show where a man in a gimp suit falls out of someone's closet, and then go home to your dementia-ridden grandmother and truant son. I'm writing this review after finishing the "lockdown special", which manages to go on for entirely too long, feel dated, and unfunny - not leaving me in a great headspace.I'm only two hours into the campaign, so take this review with a grain of salt. Maybe the game really picks up near the end, and I end up loving it. Either way, only pick this up if you can handle some really, outrageously bad acting and writing - yes, that's below the standards of an FMV game.(P.S: Why is this like 60 gigabytes? Do you think they could've compressed the footage a bit more?)
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: The actors, the writing, the weird-ass gameplay...I love it.Though I haven't, obviously, played it to completion, I just have to say that the humor in this gets me. Humor is so specific to each individual, but not only did I laugh at the content of the commercials, especially, I laughed really hard at how BADLY I edited my first broadcast. Yikes. Watching it back was truly cringe inducing! I think it tickled me because I edit a lot of pretty darn elaborate videos for fun, and...well, I thought I would be better at this.I have to recommend this early because it's so unique. I haven't ever run across a game like this, and I'm happy to see the updates coming. I relish the originality as much as the snarky humor. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like NFB, I really did. Because the game borrows so strongly from bastions of satirical comedy Brass Eye and The Day Today (and due to the really innovative and exciting interface), I assumed I was in safe ideological hands and jumped in with both feet...Pretty early on you're confronted with a press conference in which a Nigel Farage-type character and a party co-leader are talking about health and education reforms, heavily taxing the rich, and cracking down on offshore accounts. All sounds pretty sensible until you realise that these characters are being played as naive, bumbling fools, and worse - that they've been amplified into picaresque caricatures that don't remotely align with left-leaning British politics. Taking away passports and closing borders...these are not the remit of the left. So the satire in this regard doesn't really work.Shortly after, you're confronted with a situation in which it's made clear your only options are to either tow the party line and be militant about completely unreasonable policies, or help some wealthy loser escape from having his own 'hard-earned money' harshly taxed.It's clear I haven't played very much of what is a truly novel and imaginative game, but, I got the sense I was going to be forced into more and more of these ideological corners, which would significantly hamper any enjoyment I could get from the game. To reiterate, the people calling for health reforms - in this fictitious version of Britain - are the bad guys. It's not offensive, it's just ♥♥♥♥.If you like neoliberalism, centrism, conservativism, libertarianism, or can just otherwise sever your political proclivities sufficiently from whatever game you're playing to be able to enjoy it, then this game is probably for you! If you are a sensitive snowflake like me and prefer to spend your escapist time with entertainment media that broadly reflects your values, then stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute masterpiece. There is so much I wanna say but a lot of it will spoil the game. I'm gonna keep this review spoiler free. To start with, this game has one of the best stories I have seen in a game in a long time. The world building, characters, and just everything story wise is perfect. There are 14 endings as well. These ending are not just slight changes from each other easy. They are completely different from each other. This game is also very easy to learn but can but is also hard to master. It is very replayable as well since you will not get to see everything on your first playthrough. I am currently at the beginning of my second playthrough and am still having a blast playing it. The are some things that will happen in the studio to make it harder, but if your not a fan of that and just wanna focus on the story and not have to worry about losing audience and other hazards, then there is a mode with that disabled (although I would not recommend it as iit takes part of the fun out of the game). Some choices in the game are very difficult to make as well. You might find yourself questioning if you made the right decision after you make it. It will also leave you wondering what would have happen if you chose differently. The soundtrack is also amazing as well. One cool thing is that every ending has different music in the credits (From what I have seen so far). The humor in this game is also really good. You're in the big seat, and everyone at home is relying on you to give the best news program they've ever seen! For your job, you can be expected to have to properly manage camera perspectives, censor words, manage the broadcast connection, as well as making sure Now, here's the catch. SINCE you're the one in the big seat, you control what everyone sees back at home,  Whatever you decide to show on the big screen will have consequences, so choose wisely! When I first tried this game when it came out, I wasn't expecting much out of it. Maybe a quick little hour-long session of fun. I've never been more glad to be wrong! _childDocuments_.review: This is fantastic.  It's kind of a "Papers Please" game, but with real-life video. The choices you make are essentially the ads you play and the 'shape' of the headlines, such as painting anti-government actions as positive/negative.   Over time more controls unlock, and it becomes a bit of a mental juggling game for different inputs.  Working to keep certain things off of cameras that are moving around in the shot while censoring swearing a few moments after it's said for example.  It's a very unique take on the game style.  And enjoyable. At the time of this review, only 3 missions are unlocked.  If they continue with this idea and flesh it out to a logical level, this is sure to be a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really unique game and well worth playing despite some room for improvement. The primary loop of choosing cameras and formatting the show is great and feels like you're a real producer, most of the time (criticism below). You choose what goes out live and there are various mini games (for lack of a better word) to keep you busy and add to the challenge of concentrating on multiple things at once. Some of the aspects can be turned off in the settings to stop them throwing random distractions your way when there's less to do on screen, but I kept them on because I initially like to play games the way the creator intended. I'll probably get rid of a few of them for a future playthrough.The Story is poignant and entertaining, you have choices and they are reflected in realistic and somewhat unpredictable ways. You might not be able to to change the immediate events happening in the studio, but everything you do will have consequences down the line. They might have localised effects on your own life, family and finances, or you can affect the lives and careers of the people in front of the camera, ultimately having an impact on worldwide events. There is a lot of whimsy and comedy thrown in to remind you to not take it too seriously and overall it's enjoyable to watch things unfold.Constructive criticism:While the acting is great at times, and with certain people, overall it feels like an amateur theatre production. This might be a very specific criticism from me, but having spent a lot of time around performing arts students, it feels like they could have done with a wider and more experienced cast. I think some of this may be due to the extremely long takes making the acting style seem like that of a theatre production (by necessity), but the casting certainly skews towards the early/mid 20s too and doesn't feel like a "real" show because of it. To a lesser extent, some of the sets, and particularly the police costumes look really under-budget. The security people have guns, but no other tactical equipment or protection and wear shirts and hats that look like kids dressup. It's hard to take the serious bits seriously when you can't tell the difference between a mall security guard and a gestapo enforcer.Secondly, they made the obvious choice to leave the gender of your character and your partner open for you to interpret how you see fit, which I commend. However the awkward use of they/them pronouns in the written portions of text can be jarring when simply reading along. Maybe another specific criticism for me as I have dyslexia, but a couple of times I found myself reading over portions of text several times to figure out if it was referring to one person, or all of the people involved. eg, Alex walked into a room full of people, which made them feel uncomfortable. Who felt uncomfortable, Alex or the people? Again, I appreciate the effort to keep the characters gender identity and sexual orientation undefined, with gender neutral names like Alex and Sam but I feel the more elegant solution would have been a simple selection at the beginning of the game to choose your gender/pronouns and that of your partner.Lastly, I think background communication should be improved for future games. There is a phone that rings for tutorial and story stuff, but I feel like the player is left wanting for more information about the clearly planned out production going on in the studio. For example a little heads up that camera 1 is going to be on the presenter, but get ready to cut away because it is going to do a wild pan off to the left to track the guest coming in. IRL there would be a plan for these things and prior knowledge of which camera is going to be doing what during a production and/or a producer constantly chattering between camera operators and the control room. They have moments in the show where the producers look to camera and say "opening on camera 1" which is super helpful and immersive, shouldn't that be happening all the time in one way or another? Some quiet behind the scenes team chatter would really help for those that want to play it more like a simulator game and make the perfect broadcast. For those into the story, it would heighten the tension and drama when unexpected things start to happen and it all breaks down, and bring you a little closer to some of the production crew you see featured on the screen. It would also help to make you feel less disconnected and isolated in your little room, and more like the world around you is alive.I think those three criticisms are minor in the face of the unique nature of the game and the clearly huge amount of effort that went into creating the live action shows in the first place. Although not perfect, the game left me wanting more, another story with a different theme, more DLCs. More than anything I would kill for a more serious broadcast simulator game with less mini-games and more focus on actually running a show and creating a good broadcast. I loved going back and watching the tapes back to see what went out and if the camera feeds and timing was right. I think the upcoming VR experience will be a gamechanger too so looking forward to that.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly didn't know what to expect when I got this game on my monthly humble bundle choice, but I was pleasantly surprised.I keep replaying this game, even though it isn't finished yet, as I just keep having fun.  You manage a news broadcast room.  Not in the sense of telling staff what to do, zooming in cameras, and so on.  Rather, your job is to edit on the fly.  The news broadcasts are live, so you need to know when to hit that censor button for those bleeps.  When to change cameras for a better shot, and what commercials to run.  Between broadcast days, you also deal with your home life based on what has been happening in the game.  By deciding on what advertisements run, when to censor, and which news reports to cut to, you control public perception of government and businesses.This is a really good game and I highly recommend this.  Get this game, play it, and love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game's mechanics and pace. However there are some issues with the content that make playing it kind of a bummer.The narrative's reliance on hacky, sometimes offensive comedy tropes weakens what could be a really groundbreaking experience. I think these tropes also hinder the game's message, so far as one can be discerned (as the game tends toward ridiculing whoever it can). In the first three game segments, we have:	1. A group of stereotypical theater kids. Included are a preening, flamboyant young man, a vapid, self-obsessed blonde, an over-eager social justice warrior type, and an intellectually disabled young man whose inability to navigate a sleeve is played for cheap laughs. 	2. A black man, recently released from prison, offering systemic critiques of the justice system while partying with strippers and a mariachi band. 	3. Government programs funding the arts and infrastructure are depicted as stupid or vaguely sinister boondoggles. I just think in 2020 this sort of writing is lazier than it needs to be. It's especially glaring in light of the narrative's strengths. The game, through its mechanics and narrative, reveals that those who work in media often have a financial incentive to portray individuals and organizations in a positive or negative light. The game's politics are often cute enough to carry the weaker segments; the recently dispossessed rich are played up as spoiled toffs with stupid accents, government critics are depicted as philanderers and police advocates hypocrites, celebrity politicians are liars and drunks. The news anchors are satisfyingly snide and self-absorbed. This is a real highlight of the experience for me. I genuinely like parts of this game so much, it's a real pain in my ass to sit through jokes that would've been stale in the 90s. ("Math's really important!" "Okay [intellectually disabled young man]. " "Math's really important!" "Yeah okay [intellectually disabled young man].") I also feel like, if I were disabled, or a person of color, I'd probably be doing more than wincing through these segments.At the end of the released Early Access segments, the devs say they read these reviews, that they read everything. To be clear, the game does have some aspects I think are thoughtful. These include gender neutral names for the protagonist and their partner, a consistently scathing take on capitalist consumerism, captains of industry (Sophia Remmington is a great Elon Musk stand-in), and sports culture, and some laugh out loud funny bits of banter among the news crew. The game also manages to spoof the stupid way the media portrays scientific endeavors. My intent isn't to cancel this game, whatever that would mean. I do think, though, the devs maybe haven't considered these angles, or if they have, dismissed them too quickly. Maybe it's too late to influence the writing- some segments clearly have already been filmed and I am excited to watch those, to be honest- but after playing through the game so far several times, I came away feeling a little icky, and I felt like I had to express why. Hopefully the devs can dig that. I am looking forward to where this is going.

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast is easily one of the best, and most promising, FMV games that I’ve experienced in quite some time. And it’s not even completed yet.IntroNot For Broadcast is a unique FMV based game to puts you in the role of a person running the National Nightly News broadcast. The game is largely a satirical parody of the news and many political topics. It’s quite humorous and is spot-on in its satirization. If this sounds like a game that you’d be interested in, do read on, it’s quite fascinating.StoryThe story to Not For Broadcast takes place in the 1980s when a radical party is sworn in as president of the country. The new party vows to take money from the rich and eliminate poverty with it but your actions in the game determine how the public views the new party and the people that show up in the game’s scenes.Currently, there’s around 3 hours worth of content to experience but this will increase drastically as the game continues its development. It’s also worth mentioning that if you get offended easily, this game probably isn’t for you because it satirizes everything you can possibly think of when it comes to politics. I personally found it quite hilarious and enjoyed it quite a lot.GameplayAt first the game seems kind of daunting, what with all the buttons and actions you have to use/take. In reality, it’s actually quite easy to learn but tough to master. The game features a pretty in-depth tutorial at the beginning of the game where your predecessor walks you through the various buttons to make it easy.Before the news begins, you must first power up the machine and then select the adverts you wish to feature in the broadcast. Once this is done, the news begins and you must use the buttons on the left to select the screen you wish to show during the broadcast. The actual broadcast runs 2 seconds slower than the one you must edit so you must make your choices fairly quickly. There are also sections where you must censor any swears that the people on the screen say. There are also sections where you will need to avoid interference in a mini-game of sorts on the right monitor. You use a dial to move the dot up and down to avoid the green sections of interference.Once the day is completed your results are tallied and you earn money based on your performance. You can then use this money to purchase upgrades and new equipment for your studio. There are also cosmetic toys to buy to spruce up your surroundings as well.There are also story elements mixed in with the gameplay as well where your choices affect your character’s personal life. These are currently done in a sort of visual novel style setup with art showing up on a nearby TV and you must read the text and make your decision from the choices given. Some choices have pretty major consequences so choose carefully.The ArchiveWhenever you finish a day’s broadcast you’re immediately taken to the archive section where you can watch the entire broadcast that you just made your way through, check out the many humorous ads that you featured in past broadcasts, and even see behind the scenes during commercial breaks.VerdictOverall, this game had me laughing out loud on numerous occasions and I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. I’m quite excited to see how the game improves over the course of its continued development and I wish the developers luck in their endeavours. If you’re a fan of FMV games as much as I am, this is definitely one to keep an eye on.

_childDocuments_.review: INTRODUCTION:Not for Broadcast is a quite splendid game about main character, Alex Winston, working as a live broadcaster for the popular news channel, "Channel One". More so for the sub-channel, National Nightly News. As you play, you will be challenged with new obstacles to keep your viewers not only entertained, but also appropriately kept from not-so-safe sights.MAIN GAME>In the main game, you will play as the broadcaster, as I mentioned before, and take part in switching cameras, keeping the language clean, and guiding the wavelengths of interference away from the news channel. You will also control what "Adverts" your viewers see, which can take a turn for the world's story. So choose wisely.STORY>The story won't be revealed here. However, if you are interested in playing a game with loads of story and "lore" if I shall lean, then this game also has that.MECHANICS>The mechanics of the game are quite splendid. Especially the update to the "Interference" mechanic, which has more uses for further updates and also is more interesting and investing gameplay-wise. If you like unique mechanics to the likes have never been seen before, then this game might perk your ears up, both literally and metaphorically.VALUE>As for the value of this game, I'd say it is truly something to behold. Although I got my version for around 17 bucks, the full 25 (as of Early Release) is still quite worth the price, especially for the upcoming updates to come (with a predicted 10 Chapters for full-release). As for the emotional value, I'd say it still hits close to home, even though it is not another Earthbound clone or narrative-driven game (at least from first-sight). CUT TO THE CHASE (OVERALL RECOMMENDATION)>Good game! I'd give it a good 9/10 for overall promising quality. For the people working on the game who might be asking "why only a 9?", do not worry. I'd give a 10 if I had all the chock-full of content promised for the future. However, we are still waiting. For consumers, I'd say buy the game if you like the demo. If you haven't played said demo, try it! And if you don't like it then, I'd still recommend wish-listing the game in case you want to change your mind!FOR THE DEVS>The devs might be wanting a bit more "spice" to take from all this. For that, I want to say there are still some more challenges I'd like to see. And maybe even wackier performances from the actors! I'm sure you plan for all of that, however, in the coming updates. Tell the development team that I love the game and that they are doing fantastic!END REVIEW>9/10Note: Hope to see more in the next update! ;)~DaPlagueDoctor (PinkiePurplez)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games I have ever played. I absolutely love anything related to TV broadcasts. In fact, if I could pick any career path, it would be live sports production This game is basically a simulator for that, except without the sports part. The game's mechanics are fun, the story is interesting and progressively gets darker as the game continues, and the bits/segments are nice. However, I'm not sure there's much replayability. Especially after playing a specific part of the game 2-3 times over, it becomes really uninteresting. Yeah, the bits can be funny, but a lot of the amusement is lost after the first watch.I really hope this game gets mod support at some point. Having the ability to make your own broadcasts, and even potentially your own mechanics, would be awesome! I would totally put time into contributing to the modding side if support were added.Overall, I think how much one may enjoy playing this game varies from person to person. If you're aspiring to be a video engineer, or think the "high-school theatre" style cheesy bits are humorous, then yeah you'll probably like this game. But I can also see how one might absolutely hate their time playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The developpers of Not for Broadcast have worked hard in order to bring us a game that is not only entertaining but also experimental in technique and in exploring the possibilities of exploring a narrative in video games.Reasons to play this game are:1)	Gameplay: You play as a broadcaster of a national news broadcast in which you have complete control over handling the techniques of the show. You can switch cameras, censor words or choose which pictures you wish to publish. Your choices in how you wish to operate is not only a question of professionalism but also a political one where they will influence the broadcasts and therefore… its viewers. But that is not all, you as an individual will also have to make decisions regarding your family and your everyday life. Personally I found these passages slightly too long but I believe they play the role of letting us remember that even anonymous people, who can subtly change a country and the perspectives of its people, are also simply people.2)	Story: The narrative of the story is incredible since you perceive the story of a political party, a country and its inhabitants and how they dwell into a dystopian government. Approaching the fiction genre of dystopia from a journalistic approach is an interesting way since it allows us to experience the news, entertainment and consequences of a dystopian society and its evolution. A brilliant reminder of how horrible life can be in a country ruled by terror and insecurity.3)	FMV: Here I wish to discuss the techniques used regarding the handling and creation of an FMV game. The filming techniques were magnificent, able to captivate each moment and every different angle offers a different perspective and interpretation regarding the matter at hand. I also notice that some passages were quite absurd and I applaud this since it can both be interpreted in a tragic and comical way. It is amusing to have absurd humour and it helps avoiding FMVs to be perceived negatively, which sometimes happen if the developers take themselves too seriously, which is not the case here. There is, however, a tragic angle which shows how it is one of the few ways to cope with the heavy dystopian content present in the narrative.I hereby recommend this game to gamers who are interested in dystopian stories, unique gameplays, FMVs or cinematic techniques.Thank you, NotGames, for this wonderful game and memory

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game for 50% on the latest Steam sales. Previously added it because Papers Please is one of my all times favourite and this game has similar mechanics. I hesitated due to the game being Early Access but the deal was too good to pass.I had a blast during the first chapter, which includes the first 3 levels of the planned 10 levels. The game premise is unique with innovative gameplay. I quickly got immersed myself in the broadcast, the editing and the mechanics. I liked the actors and the british humor, which for me is not always guaranteed. Let me expand on this.The game has a lot of acting, a lot of FMV. The actors do a hell of a job here, obviously far from movie level, but it looks professional and their commitment and motivation shows. In general their acting is better than in some low TV productions..British Humour is not really my cup of tea and often misses the mark for me. For example, I had watched some Monty Python movies and found them boring. However, there are exceptions, like the Red Dwarf TV series, and in Not for Broadcast I found the British Humour acceptable and the sketches were funny. There are multiple references to modern popular culture.You should know that the game Early access development was severely affected by the COVID19 crisis. The devs had to cancel shooting for Chapter 2 and instead released a bonus chapter (The lockdown update) which is basically made from quarantine. It is an admirable effort and in a way it shows their dedication, but the outcome was bad and it really shows when you compare to Chapter 1.The game needs plenty of polish, which is expected from a title in Early Access. In their statement they wrote, back in January 2020, that they expect at least 18 months of development before the game is complete and I think it will take them much longer given the current circumstances.In retrospective, it could have been better to wait until this game is out of Early Access as right now it just offer a few hours of gameplay, even if they are very good. I will probably revisit the title by then.In the meantime I do recommend this game as long as you do not mind the Early Access status.

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, however I had quite a few thoughts on this one. I hope the devs can read and maybe respond.I really recommend this game, even if you don't think you are interested in the genre. It's just the right amount of challenge for me, the actors are personable, funny, and similar to real life, and there are many realistic features. I also like the fact that you can replay any past broadcast you've done as if you are a viewer, and it's satisfying to pull off some great shots. I also like the political side of the game, and the amount little details are crazy (e.g. what people say off shot in the 'rushes', which are the four camera feeds you can choose from to broadcast)I'm also really thankful for the simplified life mechanics. I never likes similar 'life' games (e.g. Papers Please) because for me at least the economic part of the game is too detailed. Although it's still present in this game, you don't have to manage it down to the dollar.I saw a few other reviews complaining about the size (40gb as of this review) however it's fully justifiable due to the sheer amount of quality video in the game.One word of warning however (and the reason I have to stop playing :'( ) is the performance. I thought this game would be easy enough to run, thinking 'it's based around one scene and a few videos, I can definitely run it on my integrated graphics' (yes I read the requirements but thought to try it anyway). No. This game is actually quite detailed, and up to 6 feeds running at a time can put too much of a strain on my system (8GB, integrated UHD 620, i3-8145-U, potato amirite) so after a point I had too many crashes and game-breaking video stutters to play normally. I would have hoped to see more graphics options, however the ones already present (setting video to half res, shadows etc) were helpful to an extent. Don't think this will affect most of you with graphics cards, but I am sure there will be a few similar to me on laptops that I don't want to disappoint. I'm not blaming this on the devs, just I really wanted to try this game out. As a result I won't be refunding and am very hopeful for more to come in the future. I can't really express how much I really recommend it. Buy it now, worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a game: this is a story. You're in the story. You're controlling the story. Now you've ♥♥♥♥♥♥ everything up and ruined the world, good job, I hope you're proud of yourself.I have never felt so in control in a game like this before. Never before have I felt genuinely guilty for my choices in a game.The writing is exceptional. It achieves some impossible balance between (particularly British!) hilarity and heaviness. "It was like a rollercoaster" is a terrible cliché that doesn't even come close to it. No, one minute I was feeling great, the next I'd be feeling like the worst person to have ever been birthed, and another ten seconds later laughing at funny silly sofa selling man.I wish I hadn't played this game. I wish I hadn't played it, so I could open it up, and play it afresh, all over again, making the same silly choices I did over and over again. On the other hand, I want to go back. Make different choices. It's a feeling of genuine regret. I know, I know I could just start a new save. But I don't want to start a new save. I want to go back. To actively unmake choices I made in that first naive play-through.The gameplay itself can be a little stressful (what more could you have really expected given your job in the game!), but there is the option to enable/disable certain parts of the gameplay to make things more manageable if you so wish.There is also a lot of reading, much like those story books where you'd have to turn to different pages depending on your choices, but it really helps expand the story. There are - at time of me writing this - 9 broadcasts in the main story, a tenth broadcast which "isn't canon" but you still play through as a part of the main story, and an 11th bonus broadcast- plus the broadcast get longer and longer as the game progresses, so there is plenty of actual unique hands-on content.In my opinion, this game humbles every other entry in this genre. Deeply humbles them, too. If you're "thinking about buying it, but not sure", stop thinking, start buying. You absolutely will not regret it. I cannot put into words how much I loved this game. I always expected I was going to enjoy the game- I'm currently at university studying broadcast tech, after all- but never in a million years did I expect it to hit as hard as it did. Truly, a masterpiece.

WHAT IS THIS?!).Cons:- Mechanic in third broadcast is unclear with the shocks and it feels like the game is forcing you to get a lower score. I could just be understanding this wrong.- Story in between broadcasts focuses on a guy we have no reason to connect toThis game is great and I'm excited to see where the developers take this. You are tasked with Commercial Breaks, Dueling against signal disruptions via minigame, Bleeping swears, and showing what is currently being broad casted to the public by changing cameras on points of interest. After work is over you're given a Text Adventure esque experience in which you're given a situation in which you're given a situation that requires your input, Your choices don't have immediate effects but i imagine further down development such things will come true.Current State of Updates: For new buyers due to recent world events updates may not come as commonly or as large as one may wish, But please have patience the developers are trying there very best to push out content to make all of us happy! And as soon as things go back to a safe state production will continue as originally planned on there road map. Rating: 10/10Note: As of writing the game is rather light on content though has a fair replayability factor. I feel that this game is a worthy investment of your time and money especially when it's fully released.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done game. Choices actually matter and make a huge difference. Split second decisions have consequences that are either immediate or will have ramifications very late into the game. There is actual replay-ability because As far as choice matters games are concerned, this one is easily in the top 3. Keep in mind that every choice you make matters - even the ones that are presented in a different way compared to the broadcast room. This one is not explicitly stated in-game, perhaps intentionally. I also liked the acting and the actors as well, the story is very well written. It starts off a bit cliche, but it becomes its own thing towards the end.  It does make for a compelling tale. The game-play is a bit mixed. It starts off innocent enough, then there is a bit in the middle of the game that is so annoying it could make you just drop the game and never return.  However the game picks right back up after that hump and is mostly an enjoyable experience after that. And if the difficulty is at any point a hang-up for anyone, the difficulty is very customizable and achievements are not affected even you choose to play a game with all mechanics turned off.Overall it's a great game in terms of both story and game-play. It has flaws, but it is a game worth full price. The game is long if you go through it once, and it could be massive if you decide to replay it multiple times.
