The story is quite good so far, but doesn't go very far as the first episode ends just when things start ramping up.It's quite short as of now, but I have faith that the full game will be great and well worth the money (assuming they don't charge extra money for more episodes). I'd recommend buying if you enjoyed Papers Please and are willing to wait for more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic & unique experience that I'd highly recommend for anyone looking for something different, funny & well made.You're the man controlling what the viewers at home see when they watch the nightly news, everything depends on you - from censoring, to camera angles, and even ad breaks. There's some great comedy, both on the nose & subtle, and the game has a lot of character in general. The concept is simply brilliant, and if this sounds & looks like something that may be down your alley, I highly advise picking this up. Even in early access at full price. Can't wait for more content! 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only three hours in and I am already crowning this the best game ever made featuring FMV. I realize that's not a very high bar but this experience goes far beyond that.It is a proper game, requiring dexterity, wits, and time management but it is so much more.It is funny with a hint of subversion. It is educational in showing the general populace the very real power that media has to influence how we feel about other people or subjects.It is topical in ins politics without being overbearing or obviously partisan.This is the game I never knew I needed.I also happened to work for a CBS affiliate for a couple years and this really speaks to that time in my life.Great job by everyone involved. There are great accessibility options and a mode with no audience pressure that just lets you practice your editing skills while you passively get entertained by the seemingly endless scroll of video content so those of you who are fearful of dexterity requirements don't let that alienate you from this wonderful experience.I have a feeling when the end of the year comes around this is going to be the first GOTY candidate of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who actually works in broadcast, this game captured it very well. No other game has captured the sweating palm of fixing something live on air, the focus that comes from camera switching, and the anxiety of someone half paying attention telling you how to cover for them over the phone. A weird blend of zany jokes and serious text drama... but I still laugh a fair bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a real joy to play I must say, and I am saddened to think that their early access days will ever come to an end because I want this game to continue to grow and for content to be added ; the parallels between the events in the game and those of our current times are unmistakable, and while they up the contrast it is still in some ways subtle and almost funny. You are allowed choices, albeit not many but enough that the replay value of the game is certainly there, especially if you want to go back and get the top grades in every segment -- on top of that you are able to go back and watch your workmanship, to either nod your head in approval to your flawless transitions and how you're always right on the action seamlessly, or to cringe at just how poorly you did. They added controller inputs so you can now play with your xbox or playstation controller, and I tried it out, but I still feel more comfortable with the KB n' M, if only because it's easier to manage the signal when it goes out of whack. If you're considering this game, I recommend buying it wholeheartedly, and I know you won't be disappointed. Go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first of all, thank you to all the producers and people that took part in the making of this game.I am absolutely mind blown!The concept is really something out of the box! I have never played anything similar to this.You are basically the editor for a news channel, covering interviews in a variety of subjects. Your job consists in choosing the best cameras, bleeping out swear words, cut off images not suited for the audience, and even avoid interference to have the best image.Surrounding all this concept, you have an amazing story being developed, in which you take direct part, as you have control over the feed you pass on to the audience.Lots of choices to be made, not only "professionaly", but also at home, as the story also goes there, waiting on you to take the decisions you think are the best to choose from.The acting is really over the top! You even get empathy for all the people you see there, and all of them have an awesome own personality, which perhaps makes you take sides, and even get a liking on them like you knew them in real life.All in all, this is an early access game at this moment, and i was absolutely delighted! When i saw the first trailer, it got my curiosity, and good thing i bought this game, to give the producers some encouragement to keep on working like this. I can't wait for the next parts of this series, and will watch eagerly for more development.A big big thanks to all the people in this game, from producers, to actors, and everyone who made this game a diamond on the rough! Congratulations to everyone for making such an unique game!

_childDocuments_.review: All I gotta say is, wow. For only playing for 2.5hrs, I enjoyed it so much I'm craving more. I'm not one for purchasing early access games; I've had a lot of games that I've bought in early access only to see it abandoned or completely lost its way and changed it to a game I didn't sign up for. Not this game. Pros:-Tutorial explains everything decently well. Although its hard to concentrate on the voicemail when you also have the broadcasting sound on too, initially when you first start. You learn to turn the sound down.-If your not broadcasting there's a branching story to me looks like it has potential, but we'll have to see once this game goes through development.-Characters are absolutely hilarious; I personally loved Jeremy and Megan as they reminded me of two siblings going back and forth nagging each other. -You have control as to how you can make the audience perceive the news by choosing images during headlines. Cons:-Although I understand its early access, its TOO short for me. Maybe if I got another 2.5hrs I wouldn't mind it.-The camera placements are so out of order. From a logical stand point it makes sense; for context, there's 4 screens numbered 1-4 going from left to right in a box formation. The issue I have is that I wish I can choose what my presets are prior to starting the broadcasting. -The story that's in between has no backstory at all. You're kind of just thrown in and told "Hey, you have a wife and 2 kids." There isn't any info about yourself and how you came to becoming the editor of the studio, there's nothing about how you and your wife met, you barely know your kids at all. For a game that raves about having a branching story in the works, I wish there was a bit more meat on the bones with this.-With there only being 3 rounds and unless you 100% the segments, which is a challenge believe me, you really can't buy any of the upgrades. They gave you one opportunity to purchase them but you'd have to rack up so much more money to even purchase them.Overall: Its a fantastic game. I love the concept; its like five nights at freddies and Empire TV Tycoon made a baby. This has such a HUGE potential. I bought this while it was on sale, with that being said I'd still recommend picking it up even if it's at full price. One thing I do want to point out is that at the end of the last "round" as I like to call it, they had a video with the devs saying thank you and it felt like they care and are passionate about this project. I'm excited to see what awaits down the road for this game. I hope it won't take too long, but hey I'd rather have a polish game than a rushed EA piece of garbage game :)

_childDocuments_.review: Ooh boy. I originally left a review for this game back in early access, when it only went up to The Lockdown. Since then, the full campaign has come out and with it, a lot to say.TL;DR: Buy it. Gameplay is fun and the story is engaging.!!!THIS REVIEW WILL CONTAIN SPOILERS!!!The following observations are in no particular order. This is more of a stream of consciousness than a review so bear that in mind as well. 1. The writers really stepped up with making Advance more of a gray-area. Previously, the player was given no reason to side with Disrupt as you had seen nothing wrong and their leader was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Alex Jones. Now, the player is given a pretty tough choice on who to side with... which brings with it a whole slew of new problems. I would like to take a moment to bring up Fallout New Vegas. Yes, I know, quite odd. But in that game you are given pretty good reasons to side with and/or against the major factions. The NCR and the Legion are far from perfect, but in them you can see capacity for good. With Disrupt and Advance... their capacity for good is heavily outweighed by the bad. Advance literally has elderly death camps and has apparently taken over the entire world through nuclear war? While Advance starts off good by redistributing wealth, we are quickly shown that they have a fierce propaganda network, LITERALLY using 1984's Newspeak (cops are now "CCOs" Advance's Hitler Youth type thing is called "The Advance Go-Getters," etc...). Disrupt, on the other hand, wants to bring back the rich and is later revealed to be a puppet organization for a military coup. So the player is left with NO "good" guy to put their full support behind. It really comes off as quite odd. I don't know if this was a thematic choice (more on that later) or just lazy writing. it's just... weird. 2. The themes of this game seem to be a bit over place. At first, it clearly seems to be leaning in the direction of “don’t believe everything that you see,” and “Our worldview is controlled by just a few people.” However, later on in the game it gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy. Once the game becomes a parody of the View and Ellen (no I am not kidding, I was shocked playing the last two broadcasts,) it seems to be talking about how there is no true “good” in the world and that everything, no matter how quaint things may seem, have a seedy undertone to it. Once again, it just seems like an odd choice.3. In my earlier review, I stated that the family bits had no relation with the overall plot. I suggested that they either be removed or heavily revamped. As it stands, they still suck. So many days pass and we never even see what our family looks like. Just gender neutral names and they/them pronouns for our main character and their S.O. While there’s nothing wrong with being a they/them, the problem is that it only further detaches the player from the already faceless family. When the main character refers to Sam (their fiance) as “they” in multiple cutscenes, it just makes the player feel so far away from anything related to the family. When both of my kids died, I felt nothing simply because I don’t even know what they look like.4. This game has FOURTEEN endings. I only got one so maybe things are extremely different in the other endings. Maybe everything comes up roses or it all goes to ♥♥♥♥. Who knows. There are so many minor choices you make in the game that it is hard to tell JUST WHAT causes these branching paths.5. I remember in one of the updates there being an upgrade system that encouraged you to do well. However, that has been removed entirely and with it, money’s purpose. Since the family parts bear no relation to the plot there is little motivation to do well. Money means nothing, so why do well on broadcasts? Just seemed like an odd choice to remove it. That’s all of my thoughts for this game. Subject to change depending on the other endings but who knows. I know it comes off as negative but I really enjoyed myself and found the actual story engaging.Just buy it, it’s fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the game being in Early Access, it is an absolutely amazing game.  The developers are working very hard to make sure they are delivering an amazing story driven game, and I am absolutely loving it.  So far there's only about 2 hours of gameplay, but there are different choices in the story, so you can do multiple playthroughs.I love this game because it is unique.  It's similar to Five Nights at Freddy's, where you're stuck in an office with monitors, but different in a way that instead of a security guard at a haunted pizzeria, you're in charge of broadcasting the National Nightly News in an alternate dystopian 1980s.  It requires a lot of multitasking, and you really have to be ready for anything.  Since it's a live broadcast, anything can happen.Is this game worth it right now?  Yes, absolutely.  This game is supposed to have a ton of content when it is fully finished, and I highly suggest you buy the game right now and support the developers so they can continue making this amazing game.  Also the price is gonna be raised once the game is fully released, so take advantage of the low price while you still can!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect but, Not for Broadcast is a fun FMV game filled with heart and a love for the craft. _childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I gave this a go, and I would love to love it. Honestly I do like it, it's certainly a breath of fresh air with its unique and interesting mechanics. Unfortunately it suffers from not knowing what it's really trying to do. It wants to be political, but doesn't really know what politics it's doing. It wants to be a black comedy, but doesn't know how to balance the humour with the tone. It wants to take influence from, and then subvert Five Nights At Freddy's and Papers Please, but doesn't understand what made those games so easy to get the hang of.It wants to give the player maximum freedom and create emergent gameplay from that, but it gives the player  freedom, in a story which is quite rigid in the ways it can play out. It wants to have lots of buttons and features, but is too quick to throw them out in favour of even more new things to learn. And of course, you don't know if you're doing well. You're just doing, and hoping the mysterious gremlin behind the screens approves of your decisions, without telling you why.The characters are fantastic, and the dialogue is great. But you'll eventually find yourself only playing because you want to see the Nightly News team gossiping behind the scenes, which you'll mostly do between levels watching the tapes back separate from the game itself, since when you're actually playing it's impossible to focus on anything that isn't important in the moment.You can pick sides, but which side do you pick? You won't know because you don't know anything about anyone. You can make choices and all of them seem bad, which would be cool if this was one of those hardcore "you can't win" types, but it really doesn't come across like it's intentional. It just feels like there's too much going on and there wasn't anyone on the development team to say Basically, I think this game should have been less. Much, much less, over a longer period of time. The idea was great, and unfortunately they knew that, and couldn't restrain themselves.I would love to see what else comes from these people, as they're absolutely onto something here, and I'm a sucker for anything that tries something new. I'm glad this game exists, and I don't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just, wow.  This FMV game is well acted, hilarious at times, and overall a good time.  VERY different game than the mainstream, in a VERY good way.  You can see/hear/feel the love that went into this project.  Adjustable settings for casual play, normal play, or "My god WHAT IS HAPPENING?!!?" play. If you want to try something totally unique, fun, and intriguing, this is the game for you.  Replay-ability up the wazoo.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible, I love the tone of the story and I really really can't wait to play more!!EDIT: Now the final release is out I wanted to shower my praises for this game some more. _childDocuments_.review: This is multitask mania - you gotta cue the next tape at the right time, co-ordinate between different camera angles in an interview, avoid certain angles to prevent unsavoury content on television, mute swearwords on a two second delay, avoid interference AND NOW THERE'S AN AD CRAP and someone is throwing a tantrum off screen but you can't focus on that right now because you're trying to line up what comes after the ad...This game leaves me on the edge of my seat during each broadcast and I love it. There's some real love and effort that goes into the craft of this game, with live actors with their own story line and on-going interactions between broadcasts, as well as extra scenes that you can watch after every broadcast - like the newscaster's reaction to live interviews. _childDocuments_.review: Just to be clear: This game is very, very short right now. My time shows 9.4 hours, but 5 of those were idling, and I have  completed the game. There seems to be a lot of replayability, but it is still very short. Additionally, this is an early access game with apparently very huge ambitions in terms of the story, so be prepared that it might never get fully resolved.So far, there is little more than the tutorial.The game is very strange and has a large amount of humor mixed into it. I honestly don't love the constant humor and slapstick, but it is funny. I would have rather had a game that focuses on the very serious subject matter of an impending dictatorship, but I suppose it goes into the British way of things with the humor.The actual gameplay is incredible. It's very similar to Papers, Please in terms of the complexity of completing many tasks at once, focusing on a lot of different things, and trying to get it done well. There's a clear inspiration from Papers, Please. The game has a great bit of difficulty, but it feels like you can really get into it with skill.I'd recommend this as is. It's a good, creative, and unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: So the concept of the game is really interesting. I was really enjoying it at first, because I really liked the idea of being essentially a TV producer, and organizing segments of a live news broadcast. But it seems like the game decided to never expand on that, doing the same thing over and over again in favor of this weird dark comedy storyline about oppressive governments, media propaganda, and some of the most unfunny "lol randum" comedy I've ever seen. There was this one like 8 minute segment where I had to sit through these two idiots playing this game where they have to get this ping pong ball into a garbage can, which presented like a high school improv where everyone was just doing wacky things, all of which were meaningless slapstick while I was just switching cameras back and forth, only to end the segment, and be presented with a "choose your own text adventure" in between gameplay that was stark and solemn by comparison. By the time I was bored of the low quality, 2010 Youtube-tier "comedy" routines, I had begun to realize that the only interesting part of the game had become repetitive, just switching between cameras and censoring ultra-British swear words that I've never heard before. I stopped when the game introduced a mechanic where I have to keep tiny little baby protesters off the TV antenna by shocking them off, in between switching cameras and censoring. The storyline is about an oppressive, seemingly communist government engaging in hardcore 1984 fascism, that the writers are cutting with goofy "random" humor, and none of it flows well, or presents itself in the way that it's intending to. Big meh from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely give this game a try! Not for Broadcast has unique gameplay, incredible acting and storytelling, and choices that actually matter. (No spoilers review below)Gameplay: The gameplay is super unique and fun! Between choosing cuts between cameras, censoring swears, cutting to commercials, and many other things to keep track of and mini-games the gameplay never got boring. The difficulty can be changed but most importantly the game does a good job of slowly introducing you to new mechanics so you're not overloaded.Story: The story is incredibly entertaining and a huge part of what makes the game fun. Live editing boring footage would put anyone to sleep but this game brings a really interesting plot and a ton of humor. I was so interested in the story that I found myself sometimes messing up on mechanics trying to pay attention to the videos (don't worry, you can always go back and watch the footage after). Two highlights of the game make the story really stand out are the acting and choices. The actors are all incredible and you can tell a lot of time was put into writing the script and acting it out. Choices you make actually make a difference, with branching story lines leading to many different endings.The only con I can think of is the story cuts in between broadcasts. I know it's not the focus of the game, but it does remind me of a lot of the cheap visual novel games you see on steam with simple 3d assets as backgrounds.I bought this game in early access and the devs were always working and releasing updates even through the pandemic. You can tell they really cared about this game and it shows in the full release. This is a great example of turning an interesting idea into a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: After getting this game by my best friend Fred, i can say that this is a game that, at first glance, is confusionary, but as long as you follow what the speaker on the phone says in the first chapter, you get the hand on it.A game where basically you control the cameras, the censors and the ads of a TV studio, this game has a good story of a nation that seems on the brink of a civil war, and of a corporation with a secret to hide at all costs.The game, I can say, is good. The three levels released so far are good quality content, and the challenges seem hard at first, but then you understand what and how to do it. What caught me off guard was on level 3, but I won't spoil.This is like, a Papers Please but instead of being a checkpoint checker you are a worker on a TV station. Your choices, your editings, and your timing are essential on making the news and entertain the watchers.Kudos to you, devs. It entertained me a lot and I hope to see more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine your life as a TV news editor/censor in dystopian England. Now imagine that world with the same humor as Monty Python. The game is actually full of gameplay and it’s not just some weird interactivity so it can be excused as a game. Without mastering the controls and gameplay loop you won’t get very far at all. You sit at a desk with six monitors in front of you and it’s your job to either censor the rebels or the government. Your choices will determine who lives and dies and affect your own personal life.You start with basic controls and the game doesn’t get too crazy at first. There are four monitors that can be switched between numbers 1-4 and there are green, orange, and red LEDs under each one. The next monitor is the live camera and the last monitor is the delayed broadcast that the people see. You can adjust the volume for each of these broadcasts. On your far left are the power and switches for each board you control. These are only used at the start of each chapter to turn everything on or during certain sequences to mess up your broadcast. On the far right is usually nothing outside of an occasional thing and underneath the desk are video tapes you must load during commercial breaks. It’s important to play some and not others which affects your pay and ranking. Advance is the government tapes and Disrupt are the rebels. It’s important to play the Advance tape during the second break to get max points.Your main job will be flicking between cameras when the green LEDs light up. Certain shows will only have one fixed camera and you can’t stay on that camera for more than ten seconds or the audience will get bored. You can flick to an orange camera for a few seconds to mix things up, but flick to a red camera, and your ratings drop. Things get tricky later on when people go off script and there are multiple people talking. You also have to watch your censor meter. When people cuss you have to press space during the red segments or your ratings drop fast. Later on, you can censor the Disrupt pro-talk with blue waves or censor Advance pro-government talk with orange waves. The last meter you need to watch is your broadcast signal. This can be adjusted with the mouse wheel once it starts going out of sync. Later on, you can tune in to a Disrupt broadcast for an anti-government playthrough by following the orange waves instead of the white ones.While that’s the basic gameplay there are some other things added later like audience reactions and during songs you can flick the cameras to the beat of the song for a rating boost (which is really hard and doesn’t ever seem on the beat). You really need to focus and watch those LED colors as they’re the main thing you will watch. Sometimes you can be pro-government or anti-government by keeping the camera on certain subjects or even loading tapes from Disrupt in certain chapters. It’s up to you to censor the people’s voices or play along.The game is constantly engaging and you never get bored. This gameplay loop sounds fun, but it wouldn’t matter if the content you’re watching is boring. Thankfully, it’s utterly brilliant. The humor is very much along the lines of Monty Python. One broadcast segment has you editing a sports match of people tossing an invisible ball into a trash can. It’s hilarious. Another scene has a reporter, Patrick Banon, not realize he’s live on the air spewing anti-government remarks, his camera woman steps in for him, but Megan Wolfe (the female news anchor and one of the main characters) calls her Patrick Banon to cover everything up. She is now Patrick Banon throughout the rest of the game like no one would know. But it’s all played off like it’s half-serious. The writing is just perfect and I couldn’t stop playing the game to see more of the humor rather than find out if Advance would get overthrown or not.There are many mockeries of real-life people and events. There’s a COVID-19 pandemic segment in which killer dolls are breaking out of a facility and everyone has to stay in lockdown. There are celebrity mockeries of Chef Gordan Ramsey, Ariana Grande, Donald Trump, and some that could be a swath of other politicians or celebrities. There are so many characters, skits, and segments, even the commercials are hilarious and you can easily miss them if you don’t turn the volume up on the delayed broadcast. Of course, there are elements that are thrown in like killer dolls attacking the studio and you need to click on them before they shut things off, a heatwave that causes equipment to shut down, as well as flickering cameras, and controls that lock up. You will be very entertained during the 9-10 hours it takes to get through one playthrough.There’s also a second part of the storytelling that I can’t tell if it’s done on purpose or not. You play through a total of seven years as a broadcast editor, but the in-between segments are text-based and shown over what looks like low-budget asset flip-style graphics that you would see on a rip-off Steam game. It’s a stark contrast from the excellent writing and acting, but I think it’s done this way on purpose. You do make a few choices in these segments that affect how your family perceives you. Responding to your daughter or wife a certain way. Your success in being pro-government gives you more money and gives you an easier life which reflects in these segments. I never got attached to myself, Alex, or my family as it just felt like interludes.With that said, Not for Broadcast is an insanely well-written FMV game with a fun gameplay loop that is easy to learn, but tough to master if you want good ratings. I love the branching paths and the replay value is very high as there are entire skits that you won’t see based on your choices. Every actor is great and especially the character Jeremy Donaldson. He’s a fantastic character and is wonderful to see on screen. I love how you can rewatch the segments and mute each camera to hear what went on in the background while another shot was being broadcasted. Members arguing in the studio in the background is always fun to see. I just wish the checkpoints were closer together. This really hurts the game a bit as some chapters are up to an hour long and you must rewatch for up to 20 minutes to get back to where you failed. I also wanted to jump in at any checkpoint to replay a segment to see the alternative footage, but due to the choices needed in previous chapters, you have to replay the game again each time. For what it’s worth, this is one of the best indie games to come out in recent years and revolutionizes the FMV-style game.

I can't even finish the game because the same level keeps crashing and freezing over and over again at the last minute, forcing me to reset, do the entire level all over again, only for it to freeze again. I tried to enjoy this with all my heart, and while I can recognize its upsides, like an intriguing story with unique characters and challenging gameplay, the freezing locks all that behind a wall of bugs and errors. The way the game is designed also bugs me. It keeps giving you unique and interesting challenges that keep you on your toes, but they never stick to what you've faced before at higher difficulties, instead opting to throw a new challenge at you, force you to learn it, and then discard it to the Challenge room for the rest of the game. This makes it unsatisfying as I spent so much time learning how to do these new challenges and how to juggle them with the main game only for that new skill to be completely worthless by the end of the level. Overall, an intriguing game with lots of potential, but ultimately the bugs, freezing, and CONSTANTLY differing challenges make me feel like the game itself wants me to stop playing altogether, and I can't recommend this game because of that.

_childDocuments_.review: re-reviewing after playing when i got boredthe game can be described as "forgiving british papers please"worth the price? i would say wait for a sale.all broadcasts (the actual game) are always gonna be nearly the same, until the build up for the final (and sorta the red carpet section on second to final), which kinda killed my motivation to get all endings, but it was still fun for a while.spoilers ahead sorry lolthe game's story in episode one (first few broadcasts) is lackluster and sometimes becomes a pain when replayed over and over again, but is still fine for a few times to replay. after Jeremy's meltdown, the game kicks into high gear, with many choices, stressful and real moments, and hard choices after that, with the story and writing also getting alot better and more entertaining.the entire game is a buildup for the final episode, which is quite boring and linear (there are disrupt hacks if alan james is still alive i believe), until the third segment. the third segment is the result of solely your choices, with there being 14 different endings or so.the writing for all endings and third segments is absolutely great, with the segment of alan james and jeremy surviving being beautiful, with you being able to choose between the oppressive advance, the disruptive (sorry) disrupt, and the truth.is the ending worth 10 hours of gameplay? absolutely.i would like to mention as a side note that jeremy donaldson is one of the best characters i've ever seen, with him visibly wanting the public to know the truth, and being honest about it. it sounds alright in text form, but is vastly better when you actually see it for yourself.one thing that is either hit or miss is the very obvious british humor. i'm not british, and i did have some parts of the game (looking at you, lockdown and episode one) be quite stale or just weird. i had a better time when i understood that i'm really not gonna be understanding most of it. however, there are some parts that can be universally hilarious.as for the mechanics, they are pretty alright when used correctly. some parts aren't used correctly and it's usually in the way of being boring. the red carpet segment has only interference with a miniscule amount of editing required, which made me want to sleep during the whole segment.nonlinear, kindof replayable, great writing after episode one, and a very worth it ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This game showed a ton of promise! The first 30 minutes are incredibly engaging as you get thrown into a new job with a lot of promise and a LOT of power. unfortunately, the game seems to peak with its second level, where things are flying off the handle but still relevant enough for you to understand what's going on and follow along with the story. Soon after that, the game's flaws start showing and the pacing issues come up front and center. The game starts throwing in a bunch of new gameplay mechanics that add nothing to the experience and take away from what actually made the game so interesting. There are tons of unresolved and unadressed story threads, a lot of cringey and strange skits that go on for WAY too long, and whenever you try to mess with the broadcsasts a little bit to prevent yourself from falling comatose of sheer boredom, the game punishes you for not following its very strict and limiting formula. I'm mainly upset about how promising this game was at the beginning, but lost touch of what made it great before we even hit the 1 hour mark. Stuck in there for another hour to give it a chance and see if the experience would pick back up a little, but came to regret that choice because it didn't at all. :(

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. It is a good game, i really liked it, all the mechanics are good (Except the one with the frequencies, that was boring), but i don't really like the message this game gives. They want you to believe that they are simply in the center of the political spectrum, everyone is wrong and the neutral people are the only reasonable ones, but I actually believe that the developers are kinda right-wing or something. The left are portrayed in this cartoony fashion, and they are the baddies, they want to take all the money and give it to everyone, and that's bad! Meanwhile, the right-wing is portrayed simply as dumb and vain people, they are just a group of conspiracy nuts at first, and they want their money back, because they earned it. But as soon as the baddies (left) do something horrible that everyone can agree it's wrong (), the right-wing people become smart, and reasonable, and they are the solution to this autoritative deviants that control everything, and you have to help them, otherwise, they will kill all your family. I don't really care, i'm just roleplaying as a character in this weird world, and i think it's trying to be funny most of the time, but it kinda gives off those vibes. Left bad, right bad, but left worse. I didn't take it too seriously, otherwise, i should be kinda offended. Still, it's a good game most of the time, funny, engaging, good acting, good sets, good music, a lot of attention to detail, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really nicely put together, and manages to be funny and serious at just the right times. The Dev team are clearly passionate, (dropping multiple bonus episodes is definitely appreciated), the mechanics are great and constantly being updated with quality of life improvements, and I'm really enjoying watching the story unfold. I haven't encountered any bugs and I've played through many times, which is fab for an early access game!The only real criticism I have is plot based, and it's that between episodes 1 and 2 the antagonists seem to go from having actually fairly admirable goals and policies, albeit with controversial and highly flawed methods, to being cartoonishly evil. It's not that I can't buy that their goals were populism to disguise a hidden evil agenda, but the rapid descent between episode 1 and 2 leaves me feeling like a bit of the story is missing. This might be a result of trying to avoid alienating potential players by interrogating any specific politics too deeply, which is understandable, if a bit underwhelming for a game with politics front and centre. I won't elaborate further for fear of spoilers though!Overall I definitely recommend giving this one a go because it's an excellent game, but don't expect any great depth to the plot (as it currently stands).

Your multitasking skills are pushed to the max as you struggle to deal with the shocking and hilarious events, while trying to concentrate through your laughter, tears and splitting sides.To the Devs: Thank You for your hard work. What made this even more thrilling for me is that my RL name is featured in your content and a little dribble leaked out from laughing. Good Job !! looking forward to more. One criticism i have is that so far the power side of the control room just involves switching on the power. Perhaps balancing power for lighting, mics, cameras, transmission etc might be more interesting for players?

_childDocuments_.review: I made a large purchase right at the beginning of the Steam Sale so that I could entertain myself for the coming weeks of the lockdown. When I went through the recommendations one game that pooped up was this, Not for Broadcast. I was instantly sold just from looking at the screenshots. It reminded me of one of my favorite television series, The Newsroom and would allow me to run my own news broadcast like in the show.After installing this game I loved it from the intro sequence and completing my first broadcast I was delighted to see Andrea Valls ( Megan Wolfe ) who I recognised from Jack and Dean of All Trades and other sketches. _childDocuments_.review: I got this because I thought it would be like Papers Please. And, it sort of is. The gameplay itself is pretty good, especially when you add in a challenge or two. But, for a story heavy game, the narrative is dumb. It suffers heavily from tonal whiplash, often trying to jump from comedic to grim back to comedic in only a few minutes. And why does your choice of headline retroactively affect what has happened? And despite working in the news, why don't you know anything until two seconds before it's being broadcast live? They also refuse to name the country this is happening in despite making up other fake country names, which makes for awkward dialog with a lot of "this country" in it.And for a political game, the story sounds it was written by people who studied political theory solely on r/politicalcompassmemes and think the USSR was a 'liberal' state. The game's rather progressive socially, but it has very little subtlety with other matters, and usually just has you pick binary "good guy or bad guy" choices. It has big bad 'Advance' throw out random policies that make little sense for an authoritarian government to run. For instance, Advance run extremely progressive taxes, and I constantly get the feeling that the writers *hate* progressive taxes. Despite Advance committing actual atrocities and war crimes, it feels like all anyone cares about in the resistance movement is "I used to be rich, and now I'm not, and that's bad". They talk vaguely about freedom sometimes, but usually only in the context of "being free to be rich". I knew going in that they'd have this taxation be a plot point, but I thought they'd be more nuanced about it, rather than parroting conservative, pro-big business talking points.Advance feels like a hardcore libertarian's scaremongering tactic, warning about such evil government activities like funding the arts, allowing euthenasia, and taxing the rich. Those are Advance's three main policies, and the game portrays all of them as leading directly to fascism in a year or two. Now, to be fair, they satirize a lot of things in the game from around the political sphere, but...1: Forced neutrality is not neutral. It's a form of media bias. Ironic, huh?2: They aren't exactly being neutral when they paint one side as a literal dictatorial 'new world order' and the other as the only freedom fighters willing to stand up for what they believe in, and makes it a binary choice between them. The game paints this as freedom versus oppression, and pretty consistently spins financial equality as bad. It's like the game is saying to the player "supporting arts funding or taxation basically makes you a fascist".As another example of 2, minor spoiler: ...So, game's fun, has good representation of minorities, but the narrative has really gross and distracting undertones. Or maybe I'm just a dumb bleeding heart liberal. Take your pick.Edit: Oh right, how could I forget probably the worst message in the game? Spoilers for midgame:

Often entertaining and funny when not focused on the main plot (unless you aren't entertained by a particular segment and find yourself needing to do dull tasks for 10-15 minutes before it ends unless you fail out of it or worse miss something for the narrative you wanted to do then have to go through the whole thing again) but then, due to the style of the game, you will be punished for paying too much attention to the actors and may need to see things you missed after the gameplay segments where you can review the footage that was broadcast, play the ad videos without listening into studio talk or orders, or view the moments that weren't completely available to you. _childDocuments_.review: If the Early Access tag worries you, rest assured that this is a case of it done correctly. An FMV game on par with the classics, like Night Trap The current state of the game includes one of four promised episodes from the . There are three segments, each containing three newsroom sections and several text-based choose your own adventure style portions placed in-between. A single playthrough had taken me around two hours, but there is plenty of incentive to replay episodes, such as: branching paths that are influenced by the decisions made by the player both inside and outside of the newsroom; the opportunity to view alternate news feed that the player had missed in previous sessions, including cutting to the news presenters when they believe the camera is focused elsewhere, leading to indecent situations (at the cost or to the benefit of concurrent viewership); and aiming for a higher final ranking. The experience can also be altered by purposefully including shocking footage instead of following the planned narrative--will we introduce this CEO using a photo of their inauguration or a photo taken depicting them while brazenly drunk? How will this choice affect the viewer's perception of the representative, and will it have an impact on the station's relationship with their respective company? Aim for an increase in viewership, or go against the wishes of your superiors? Dilemmas like these are commonly presented throughout a playthrough, but the larger picture is sadly still to be seen in future updates.The development team is very responsive in discussions regarding planned content in the forums, and transparent when faced with feedback. They've even made the decision to completely re-shoot footage for future updates in order to provide the best experience possible. This is definitely a project that is worth investing in.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; unique, enjoyable mechanics combined with a surreal humour and dedicated devs mean you should absolutely give Not For Broadcast a tryNot For Broadcast may be best described as a mixture between Papers, Please and We Happy Few. As with Papers, Please, the gameplay is focused around a novel and, at first thought, potentially menial task; in the case of Not For Broadcast, managing the editing of the live National Nightly News, with each new day bringing greater complexity to the task. What starts as a simple set of instructions morphs into a chaotic management of buttons, bleepers and screens, the goal to keep the National Nightly News on air without (too much) disruption. Alone the gameplay of Not For Broadcast is interesting and fun, presenting an accessible but entirely new genre of live TV management which is refreshing to get to grips with.However, where Not For Broadcast shines, but where it is potentially striving for a particular audience, is in its theme and content. Not For Broadcast is set in a British dystopia, akin to We Happy Few's pastiche of Brave New World, focusing on a surreal world with sinister undertones, rather than the full-blown grayscale tyranny found in Papers, Please, drawing from 1984. There are differences compared with We Happy Few of course, namely that rather than Joy, the drug plying the people in latter is a political movement, Advance, whose populist policies hide potentially nefarious plans but also due to the story-focus of Not For Broadcast, the game held together by the actors playing the irate presenters or the bewildering guests. The humour of Not For Broadcast is certainly an acquired taste - think Monty Python or Shooting Stars - and would be, no doubt, confusing (or intriguing) for non-Brits but I personally found it funny, even laughing out loud on occasion.This is not to say that Not For Broadcast is perfect; some of the mechanics can be infuriating at times, such as the static slider and not all of the jokes, especially those in the commercials, land perfectly. However, without a doubt, Not For Broadcast's small flaws are carried by its unique mechanics, surrealist humour and, above all, the dedication and commitment of the NotGames team, evident in their updates and their newest Lockdown Update, to provide players with additional content in lieu of the next installment planned. Not For Broadcast is clearly a labour of love and you should absolutely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of simulation games, so when I found this one, I went into it with only the impression I got from the screenshots thinking it would be a rather simple PCR simulator. I got what I was hoping for, except in a very different way than I expected. As a side note, sharing the same name as the protagonist created a more immersive experience than I sometimes would have liked, albeit that is not to be taken negatively. places you into the role of a control room operator for a news station, assigning you various tasks ranging from mixing different video sources to playing sound effects at appropriate times. Mechanics are gradually introduced to you, scaling difficulty as the game progresses. While certain rules have to be obeyed, the game leaves a lot of room for personal choice, in more ways than one might expect at first. These features also allow for replayability, trying out new choices, perhaps to hunt down some of the many achievements.Gameplay itself is rather straightforward as the player is confined to the production control room, which makes them focus more on the many recorded segments themselves.The player will be able to follow a multi-month long story, both from a personal and from a nation-wide and global perspective, operating as a news channel CRO. The story is, however, very much dependent on player choices, creating multiple differently branching storylines that can be explored individually. The player will furthermore find themselves facing split-second decision making many times, possibly making them question their choice afterward. relies heavily on recorded, real life video segments. The surrounding environment is kept simple, yet pleasing for the liminal space the player finds themself in. Over the course of the game, a few changes can be noticed, but the main design remains steady.Similar to visual design, the sound is almost entirely composed of real life recordings, with a few sound affects added. places a surprising amount of power into the player's hands given the limited tools they have at their disposal. Able to choose between  the player can mix the news broadcast very much to their liking, with corresponding consequences. I would not call the game difficult in itself, this is however dependant on a player's own expectations.  has implemented a few ways to even encourage challenge-seeking players to give it a go, with multiple game modes to choose from.I've nominated  for the "Most Innovative Gameplay" award in the 2022 Steam Awards, which is also my reason for composing this review. It turned out to be a game hiding so much more content than visible at its surface, requiring players to observe and choose carefully to uncover every secret they can find, and it does so in a unique way with an obviously great amount of effort put into it by the developing team (during COVID-19 restrictions, nonetheless). is by all means a must try for anyone interested in simulation as well as peculiar, random, witty and sometimes even distressing story.

_childDocuments_.review: As you can probably tell by my hours on record, I was/am pretty obsessed with this game. Other than some red carpet scenes, I'm fairly sure I've seen the majority of what this game has to offer. And, with DLC coming, I'm sure my addiction to this game will return in full force.The story is great. It has a particularly British sense of humour that I haven't seen in a game before. There are several paths you can go down, including 4 finales and 14 epilogues. It's definitely replay-able, but I have to admit collecting all 14 was a bit insane of me. The four finales are probably my favourite parts (aside from the meltdown), I like comparing the differences between them. I really do think it was worth replaying at least to experience all the finales, there was one I didn't like (that being, the one that leads to the epilogues 'Wacky Fun', 'Chaos Reins', and 'Changing of the Guard'), but the rest were top tier.I love the characters and the acting is very convincing. It's emotionally compelling. I watched all the rushes as I really loved watching the characters interact when they weren't on air. They're complex, and change as the storyline continues. Even minor characters were interesting and funny. I can't imagine how long it must have taken to film all those long scenes in one shot without it going wrong, and still end up with an amazing scene.The gameplay is unique and interesting. It's easy to alter the difficulty of specific mechanics if certain aspects are too difficult. I do have to say though, that crashing was an issue, and became a bigger issue over time. I assume this was due to me unlocking so many rushes from all the different routes? Restarting the game, not playing for a few hours, and deleting old broadcasts helped when faced with repeated crashing. I also never had more than 4 profiles at a time, as I assume this could also contribute to it crashing. I did send a bug report sometimes after crashing, I haven't played since it was updated recently so I'll have to see if it has improved when I replay it.This game is so underrated. I strongly recommend it, I love it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is good enough that it has compelled me to actually do a review, since the developers have done something rare: they created a game that can be enjoyed either as a game, or a work of art. The difficulty curve is present, and manages to increase at a steady pace.But importantly and hilariously, it says the quiet part loud about media, politics, and the crap that goes on in both.

_childDocuments_.review: Not for broadcast is a great game for both its fun and stressful management of a news broadcast and its willingness to call out a government that is seen more and more in today's society. Positives: -Not for broadcast has a very engaging interactive story, I have played through about 3 times now, each time the events, some of the dialog, and the overall reaction of certain characters change depending on how you play.-Has good keybinds and fairly intuitive gameplay, takes a playthrough or so to learn but does not take long to get good at the job.-Has a very Papers-Please feel but once finished may arguably be even better then papers please was.-Has a challenge system that lets you replay broadcasts in fun variations of them.Negatives:-Has a non-intuitive system of money and money management.-Defiantly takes a lot of time to get into, broadcasts are long but do have points where you can pause them.-The music system feels clunky with it often being hard to hit the rhythm max-The conversation sections feel very repetitive in their 10/3 timing with very little forgiveness for going over that 10 second time, makes it feel like during sections that the camera shouldn't switch you have to switch it just for the game play feature.Overall I highly recommend the game, enjoy and if you can, have a peaceful night.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up on sale expecting it to be a quick and sort of interesting experience.I got far more than that. I genuinely believe this is one of the best games I've ever played. Almost certainly one of the best "short" experiences, up there with Slay the Princess and Death and Taxes. Personally, this one has to be my favourite. The moments of foreshadowing, sudden appearance of dystopian elements which are placed very far apart in time, all of it made my heart drop when it occurred. I played in the way I felt my character probably would, and only restarted a segment when I made a mistake with tape order. Otherwise, all was done with just dealing with the consequences.I'm glad I did that. It made the regime's growing control feel more like something I could have prevented, made me feel horrible yet entranced. It's honestly a very wonderful game, and I truly do think that even if you don't normally play games remotely similar to this, you'll probably still enjoy it. (Source: I primarily play sandbox and paradox interactive titles, nothing like this, and yet it still was an insane experience).I've only just gotten my first ending as I'm writing this review, but I think I'll try to get some more in the next few days. Only bought this game yesterday, and I truly think I already love it. Hopefully in the next ending, the world ends in a better state.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that I write reviews on Steam, so let it show that this game has motivated me to write this.I will always support games that push the envelope. This game does just that, and on multiple levels.The gameplay as a nightly broadcast editor is engaging, fun, and often challenging as you struggle to pick the most interesting camera angle, all while censoring expletives, keeping the signal free from interference, and putting out various other fires out while keeping the news at least somewhat coherent for the viewers.It is through this gameplay that an increasingly interesting, and topically relevant story is revealed to you, which is reflected on decisions you've made in both the at-home interlude sections, and what you've chosen to broadcast out over the airwaves to a country in political turmoil.The price of admission for this game is worth every penny, considering how novel the gameplay is. Every live news segment is shot in full motion video, and is acted out superbly, adding to the effectiveness of the story being told here.I find it easy to recommend this game to anyone looking for something new, something relevant, and something that will make you think.Well done, and cheers to the development team, Not Games.

If you don't listen to the moderators, it is not so easy to switch between the multiple cameras.Unfortunately the relationship between the text-based story and the actual director's gameplay was not quite appropriate. _childDocuments_.review: Game is unplayable for me in its current state. Runs like a slideshow. I'll be happy to give it some more playtime once they optimize it.edit: Since posting my review, the devs worked quickly to address the issues I was experiencing. Now the game runs fine for me.The game is a bit slow, in terms of pacing, in the beginning. I'd prefer to be left to my own devices sooner rather than later but instead you're forced to follow instructions in the first few missions. Gameplay is alright, though it may not be for everyone. They spent so much time and effort on the videos but you're constantly having your attention divided by small minigames that you must complete in order to keep the broadcast going. As you progress through the game you can buy modules which do these small tasks automatically for you, which is nice. There is an archive where you can watch all of the videos again after completing the mission, but why would I want to waste my time and watch them again when I could've watched them the first time?There is also a sort of "choose your own adventure" mechanic in between the missions. It is a nice touch though I wish there were more options sometimes. The choices are often binary and lack nuance.The overall story is interesting enough, but there are some places where it just goes overboard for me. I get it is supposed to be a satirical story, but it just gets absurd at some points. You're hit with some serious family drama and the plight of the average citizen then next you see some guy engaging in BDSM on national television.

_childDocuments_.review: if you liked the premise of papers please, being able to affect the story's events through small choices in gameplay, but found it too boring, difficult, and/or tedious to follow through with that, this is that game to scratch that itch. it has a super immersive world with its own politics and issues, throwing in talented and entertaining live actors. i'd just recommend playing on a low difficulty since i found the story and video to be the more intriguing part. they also crafted this in such a way that different players would form different views and opinions on certain characters. which also leaves the door open for replayability, or just wreaking havoc on the world if that's your thing! really i don't have anything bad to say about this game, pretty much if the trailer intrigues you, it's worth every dollar.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, I pirated this game. I pirated it because I'm broke as ♥♥♥♥, because I adored the concept but couldn't afford it and because I don't usually buy early access titles. It is now a nearly year since I finished the main campaign and I have come back to buy the game so I can buy the DLCs on launch. That his how much I fell in love with this title.The devs did such an amazing job keeping production going through the pandemic, I can't imagine how hard it was to make a game like this during the height of the pandemic. The extra lockdown chapter still feels very strange and out of place but I appreciate greatly that they made it just to give their fans something to chew on while production was on halt. It perfectly melds dark comedy with political commentary, showing the potential extremes of both the far-right and the far-left and taking the piss out of both. _childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wasn't expecting much going into this game, I got it from a Humble Bundle and knew nothing about it before playing short it being a bit like Papers Please, I almost gave it a miss.Let me tell you - I'm extremely glad I didn't pass this game up.It's genuinely in my top 10 gaming experiences, it ticks so many boxes and it's one of the few games I've bothered to actually play more than once, and I plan to keep going until I get all the endings and achievements.Does it have stupid but hilarious British humour? It does, in spadesA compelling story? Yup, quite a few of themActually good live action acting? YupEngaging gameplay? YupBug free? For me, yesImagine a "semi political" game like Papers Please, mechanics akin to "Please Don't Touch Anything", FMV scenes akin to old school Command and Conquer games and you're part of the way there.The humour is great if you are into British humour (as a Brit, it's semi compulsory) there were times I legitimately couldn't stop laughing, especially in "The Finale" episode. The DLC offers even more of the same humour and with a bit more flexibility to control how the humour works, which again works great.The story, I've seen some people say the central politics driven story line is quite hard to follow, not amazingly true to life and it feels difficult to pick anyone as the "winner" without feeling a bit dirty. I think that's perfect, because the world we live in isn't perfect, especially politics. It is very politics driven so if that isn't your thing then it might not be for you, but I found it compelling, and the side stories that you actively have an impact on depending on what you choose to show, or the celebrities you focus on is a great touch that keeps you involved and not just pressing buttons for the sake of it.Now the acting, it's FMV so 99% of the game is played through live action clips, if you're imagining pretty poor acting, you'll be wrong. Is it Oscar worthy? No of course not, and that's perfectly fine as that isn't what they were going for. Even some of the names have some TV roots, anyone with kids should recognise "Megan" from the game as the mother from Waffle the Wonder Dog...are you going to see AAA level names, again, no of course not. But the acting is great, and to say the majority of this game was developed and produced within Covid is another testament that shouldn't be ignored (watch their documentary)The gameplay, this might be the thing that might not be to everyone's tastes, and that's ok. It plays similar to Five Nights at Freddies in all honesty, you a fixed in place and you can turn left and right, you press buttons, listen to people on the phone and you can do various other parts from your chair. It can get a bit hectic at times remembering what to do, but if you get stressed, just switch to "Story" mode in the difficulty and enjoy the awesome story.I've seen a few comments about game breaking bugs, honestly I didn't see any issues while playing. Everything worked perfectly so I can't comment on this.I very rarely review games, good or bad, but this one deserves a hell of a lot more recognition than it currently has and I'd recommend anyone give it a try, you'll be pleasantly surprised.

I really loved watching the stories of all of the characters unfold through the broadcasts, and I was so excited to watch my efforts all come to fruition in the end. _childDocuments_.review: This game is mostly silly.  I was expecting something a little more dystopian or something taking itself a little too seriously.  It doesn't.  It's an interactive comedy.  I love the political party.  They go full communist so quickly and it's great.  I love how they show the formerly rich becoming bitter and angry after losing their wealth and how they transform into counter revolutionary terrorists, a side of the story often left out.  We often don't get to see the blood thirsty nature of the rich. Look at what chichita did in Latin America and the like over bananas.  Not that it get's very serious but it acknowledges it which is more than anyone else.  The game isn't built with Linux in mind but I'm running it with Proton.  There are pretty major frame drops which hinder the experience.  At the beginning it was as low as 7 Hz before stabilizing in the high twenties.  Usually this would be completely unacceptable.  I'd either have to boot into windows or refund the game if it wasn't worth it to me.  But you don't really do much in the game.  The video you're watching is likely 24 Hz while everything you're responsible for is on a still frame so it didn't really mater.  It's something to keep in mind for those using proton though.  There was one crash at the two and half hour mark that lead to a system freeze.  The game keeps good track of progress.  It didn't look like there was any major set backs as a result of the crash.

detailed_description: The Demon King's Castle in Ruins The human race attacking the Demon King's castle is nothing new and has happened countless times before. What makes this time different though, is that the Adventurers decided to join forces with the Imperial Army and the 'Hero of Caerleon' to lead a full onslaught in hopes of wiping out the Demons once and for all. They attacked the Demon stronghold with overwhelming numbers and succeeded in its total destruction. All of the demons in the castle were taken prisoner except for one lone skeleton named 'Skul'. Side-Scrolling Platformer Action 'Skul: The Hero Slayer' is an action-platformer that boasts rogue-like features such as everchanging and challenging maps. It will keep you on your toes, as you will never know what to expect. Tons of skulls, tons of playable characters Skul is no ordinary skeleton. In addition to his formidable fighting skills, he can gain new and exciting abilities depending on which skull he's wearing. Use up to 2 skulls at a time, each of which has its own unique attack range, speed and power. Choose combos that match your playing style and switch them in the heat of battle to bring your enemies to their knees. The power is in your hands! The Adventurers Skul has crossed paths with a party of Adventurers! They are powerful foes that hunt Demons for sport. While Skul may be small, he still packs quite a punch. So just wait and see who really is the hunter and who is the hunted....   Bosses Corrupted by Dark Quartz At the end of every chapter, go head-to-head with massive bosses corrupted with Dark Quartz and powerful beyond belief. Derived from the pain and hate of life itself, Dark Quartz taints and takes control of everything it touches.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay in  is very straightforward with attacks, skills, jumps and dodges. Survival depends almost exclusively on the players' skill as all animations are very detailed and methodical, attacks are well telegraphed and dodges can't be infinitely spammed to get out of any and all situations.On many occasions you can either find or buy  to replace your own with and gain its abilities, and you can simultaneously own up to two different heads, making the approach to each situation pleasingly varied. Additionally, each of the different heads has a pool of abilities and which one you get isn't always the same. For example, the , an ice-based transformation, can either come with the  skill, an attack where you throw three ice shards at the enemies, or it can come with the  skill which will make you impervious to damage but also immobile for a few seconds.There are more than 20 different skulls available at Early Access launch and the variety is pretty amazing, with some skulls being more common than others. After a while you'll have figured out some favorites. For me they include among others the Werewolf, the Ninja and the Harlequin, although the  Easter Eggs are also pretty neat. Note that you have little to no influence on what skulls you find and that you can only carry two at a time anyway, so it doesn't tend to get too repetitive. Each skull also has an action that activates when you switch to it and much like the skulls' skills, these aren't always the same for each skull-type.In addition to the skulls, you can carry up to six different items that give you passive effects (like 10% more damage, higher damage output while airborne but reduced damage while on the ground etc.), as well as , an item that gives you an additional skill with a cooldown that is independent of your equipped skull.Occasionally you also find caged monsters. Upon freeing them, they return to the castle, offering new upgrade possibilities.This game is tough... but also very fair. In this regard it shares a bit of the  mentality where pretty much every death you suffer was clearly your fault and you can see where you can improve and what you could have done better, as I hinted at in the Gameplay section. Nevertheless some situations can be quite overwhelming and when the screen is full of enemy attacks there aren't many spots left to evade them.Personally, I couldn't do it, I'll admit. I couldn't clear the entire game, yet. But that's where it gets interesting: I don't feel like giving up yet, either!In short,  is one of those games that isn't  difficult but instead  so. It's probably not a game you'll boot up a lot when you've had a hard day at work - although that also works due to the soundtrack and art-style - but one you'll enjoy to challenge yourself with.The story is neither groundbreaking nor complex but it's a compelling premise nonetheless: The adventurers of the Kingdom have joined forces with the Imperial Army and the dreaded  to lay the  castle to waste and kill or kidnap its inhabitants. , an unimposing skeleton, affectionately referred to by the other monsters as "Littlebone" for being the smallest, is the only one left in the castle after the attack. He discovers that the  have been defeated, the  has been captured (he promptly frees her) and the  has been captured. After further discovering that even monsters have been attacking them due to some mysterious, black stones corrupting them,  sets out to free the King and Council and defeat the Imperial Army and the Heroes.The sprites all look either cute or epic or something in between and dialogue is portrayed in JRPG-style text boxes. The enemies all have a  aesthetic that complements the setting perfectly.Having played on a preview build before the launch of Early Access, I was able to witness how much the developers have improved over time and both the way the plot is conveyed and the English localization have improved immensely.This game is absolutely gorgeous to look at. The pixel-art is beautiful, the animations fluid and the effects are used... well, ively. The game boasts vibrant colors, flashy magic, convincing destruction and very unique and sometimes surprisingly recognizable transformations for the protagonist.Since you'll die a lot in this game, you'll be hearing the track of the first area a lot. It isn't bad music but especially the start of the track does get a bit repetetive after a while. Other tracks, like the title screen music or the tutorial track, are beautiful and fit the atmosphere really well.This game is probably for you if you enjoy  like ,  or  and/or prefer short games you can jump into for single sessions like ,  or .If you're into Rogue-likes and/or Rogue-lites, or if you enjoy 2D platforming, or if you like a fair but punishing challenge, it isn't hard to find something to like in this game. Most importantly, though, if you like good pixel-art, you absolutely have to give this one a shot. There is a lot of love and passion infused in this project and it really shows.Even as someone who tends to get frustrated after a while if much of my progress is erased/reset over and over, I really can't stop enjoying this game - over and over.So yes, I definitively recommend  - at least to !

_childDocuments_.review: Skul is a challenging Rogue Lite where you play against the good guys, you can switch skulls to switch your abilities, It great pixel graphics some funny dialogue and some very likable characters.In Skul you play the antihero side. The "Heroes" attacked, destroyed the castle, Locked up the witch and defeated the skeleton guard, You play as littlebone, You are the weakest of all skeletons but somehow you survived, You are handed a legbone from one of the dying skeletons to use as a weapon, You free the Witch and find the Skeleton guard chief, He gives you his skull and you use this to defeat your first miniboss. Later you will meet up at the Demon Castle and this is where the game begins, It is up to Littlebone to save the world from these pesky heroes.I really like the characters, The Heroes all have an ego that doesn't fit on the screen and the bad guys are just very down to earth people, and from my perspective they are not that evil. I especially like Littlebone, He is just too nice, Everyone picks on him and he doesn't even seem to bother, There is not a lot of backstory in the characters, but they all make one hell of an impression. I like the dark and serious but still colorful and funny style that is added to the game. It is rather unique.The game has just 1 gamemode and it is single player only, You start in the Demon Castle every time, Here is the witch who will sell you permanent upgrades for the Dark Quartz you collect during the runs, You will unlock more NPCs, like one that gives you a free random skull to start with. You start a run by jumping off the castle, You have to clear the area from enemies and the door will open to the next area, So it is very linear, you can not go back, But it is not like that you have anything left to do there anyway.The main gimmick of the game are the skulls, You take over the abilities of the skull you wear There are a lot of them, I counted at least 20. Some enable you to fly or hit very hard, or shoot, Some are just rip offs of popular media, Like the Ghost Rider skull, The Zelda Skull and the God of War Skulls, But I like that. Next to the forementioned Quartz you enemies also drop coins and health pickups. You can spend these in the shopping areas that you encounter at times during your run. There are also chests which mostly contain coins and a upgrade, There are also treasure piles which may be impossible to reach with your current skulls.There are a lot of areas before you reach a boss, There are areas with a ton of enemies, areas where you can buy stuff, areas with just a free skull and some training dummies and areas with minibosses. The enemy rooms are different each time, Also the mini bosses differ with each run, The endboss stays the same, After you beat it you will move on to the next level with new areas and a new end boss, There are 3 levels so far. If you die you will lose everything except for the Quartz and the upgrades you bought from the Witch. You can spend the collected Quartz and start over from level 1.The graphics look very nice, It already has a great variation in enemies, Most of the animations are done very well, but it is obvious it could use a little polish in some places. The soundtrack is also nice it is joyful most of the time but during the bosses it gets a bit more tense. Overal a nice soundtrack. I love the many ways Littlebone can look, All the different skulls really add to the game, ofcourse to the gameplay, but also visually, They all look great. One thing that does not really fit is the ingame font, It is not pixelated, It feels out of place.I had absolutely no performance issues, No crashes, bugs or anything like that, The game is locked to your refresh rate, Steam Cloud save has recently been implemented and this is also working fineSince it is a rogue lite it will score high here, The skull system really helps, But I do feel more could be done to extend the lifespan of the game, There is just the one gamemode, no difficulity tweaks, no custom runs, I think more mini bosses would also be vital here.Surely we need more mini bosses and levels with bosses, unique, enemies etc, It would also be nice if we could customize what skulls will drop, Somehow I never get the ones I want, Customize the run a bit more by tweaking some settings in the castle, A Stats NPC, which gives you a nice menu with all skulls you have found and their info, total amount of runs, fastest run, enemies killed, etc, Maybe an NPC who sells you temporary upgrades back in the castleI would love to see Custom seeds so you can compete with others or improve on yourself. It also offers a static experience if people want that. Also a few more gamemodes, Daily runs, Boss Rush, Maybe a local versus or coop mode? Maybe custom challenges for each run, or each area which can help or work against you depending on if you fail or complete the challenge. Skul just released and it will probably stay in EA for a while, They do have a public roadmap with every small detail in there, It does not look very impressive so far, but I think new ideas still need to get implemented in the Roadmap. I will keep this review updated, I will edit it when I feel a lot has changed or the game leaves EA.Skul is a nice roguelite with a lot of potentional, I love the skull switching idea, And I absolutely love some of the skulls, It has nice graphics and the hard challenge should keep you busy for a while, It is obvious we are in early stages but I can see this game becoming a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Before purchasing this game, I read a decent amount of negative reviews just to know what to look out for. I went into my first play-through extremely nervous that I was going to experience some cheap combat where enemies constantly get in random hits on me and I won't be able to enjoy my experience. HOLY ♥♥♥♥ WAS I WRONGMy first hours on the game were met with nothing but pure ecstasy as I slashed my way through each stage and discovered new skulls, items, and enemies with each run. The story is short, but enough to get you decently engaged in what exactly is going on in the world you are in. The combat is an absolute blast and was neither too difficult nor too easy. One of the two main complaints for this game were 1. It's too RNG heavy2. It's very repetitive.My opinion on these complaints: Honestly, the RNG in this game is just down to personal preference, but I personally love the RNG aspect of it. It makes every run I do different and forces me to learn new play styles that I didn't even know existed. What solidified this opinion was when I was at the second stage of the game and desperately in need of finding a decent skull to upgrade. The skull I received was "Grave Digger", a new skull that was added quite recently. However, this skull was a "common", so obviously I was extremely disappointed that RNG didn't bless me with a rare or legendary. After debating whether I should restart, I figured what the hell, and gave the grave digger a go. . . .That run ended up being the VERY FIRST time I cleared the game fully. I couldn't believe it, how could I clear the game for the first time with a maxed out COMMON skull. To make sure Grave Digger wasn't just some unique case, I tested other common skulls in upgrading and was mindblown to find that most of them could compete with the upper tier skulls in terms of strength. This switched my mindset on the RNG to "man I hope I don't get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ skull" to "no matter what I get I'll just MAKE IT GOD-TIER". This revelation made me more excited to test different skulls and item builds in my future runs. Especially since the dev team showed that they planned to continue adding more skulls to the current 100+.Overall: A fantastic game to play at anytime. I personally have never been big on laptop gaming, but since this game has no need for a mouse OR internet, it was just the perfect way to enjoy an S tier game wherever I was. This game got me through an 8 hour plane flight, a 3 hour uber drive, and a 5 hour wait at the DMV, all in the same week. IF YOU LIKE RNGIF YOU LIKE ROGUELITESIF YOU LIKE CHARACTER VARIETYBUY THIS GAME
