_childDocuments_.review: After many hours in the game I'm revising my review to reflect my experience. Skul starts off challenging but quickly becomes easier as you learn to fight the various enemies and gain new permanent upgrades. Because of this the learning curve isn't steep and many casual players can jump straight in and have fun. *Skulls*The unique mechanic for the game is swapping skulls (your head) with others to gain new forms and abilities. You can have two of these at a time and switch on the fly during combat. Think of it like tagging a character out for a second one during a fight. The skulls themselves have their very own abilities that are randomly given to them each time you find them. So just because you found a Warrior skull again doesn't mean it'll be the same as the last. Mixing your duo of skulls around to suit your favourite play style is a lot of fun.*Items*The items within the game are collected either from completing treasure rooms or from shops found during your journey. Their effects range from passive ones (+30% to Physical Attack) to more unique ones (Attacks fire Shurikens from your body!). Building a strong arsenal of items along with your favourite skulls can lead to absolute chaos on the screen as you shred through enemies. *Early Access*As of writing this (Late Oct 2020) the game is still in early access but is aiming to release in December this year. The full release promises new areas explore, more enemies, bosses and an entirely new system for upgrading your skulls during runs to provide another layer of customization and power to your play. If you aren't a fan of games that are in Early Access, I understand. However I still strongly recommend you take a look at the game after its final release to make sure you aren't missing out on something you could really enjoy. The game is still young with a lot of room for growth.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game randomly on "Popular Upcoming" by chance. I watched the previews, some gameplay and decided to dive SKUL first into this. I am a huge Rogue-lite fan. I have played countless of them: Deadcells, Rogue Legacy, Wizard of Legend, Enter the Gungeon, Spelunky...you get the point. I absolutely adore the challenges and different types of gameplay that you get with each run. It took me about 10 hours to finish the story currently, while I got to the last boss 3 times total. If you love rougelites, please pick this game up. It has a lot of potential it's already hitting. Comboing skulls together and absolutely destroying a map full of enemies is really exciting. This game rewards thinking quickly very well. It's a game to pick up if you love an original story, great music and really interactive gameplay. - Lovely Pixel Art- Very Rewarding Passive Traits- Most classes (Skulls) seem viable- Music is to die for- Challenging but not pull your hair out- Player Agency- Comboing- Easy to tell what's going on- Proper character progression- There are definitely skulls that are just not that great- Rewards speed over all else- Animation locking can get pretty annoying- Wish there was a small buffer when you received damage (Passive Trait?)- Item slots are super important, I wish health items were given to you but I understand why they aren'tHere are a couple thoughts the game design itself because I love the story. Power Skulls: Minotaur, Warrior, Fighter, Yaksha and Grim Reaper. These skulls can be very strong but I feel like the animation locks really inhibit some of the game flow. It just feels SO slow when you are trying to use their abilities when you have things like the the Spearman with the dash auto-attack cancel and the Djinn that rewards 1 button mash. I-frames would be a solution to letting them hit hard but not be punished for having to stand still a little bit. Give them proper reward for being slow. Skulls I frequently avoid:Clown: Slow attack speed even though they are ranged. I like the idea of a *3* hit passive but it just feels like the animations take forever.Werewolf: Speed like this could be important in a speed run when you have 1 skill carrying everything but I figured this guy was too crazy. He moves a LOT and I would prefer some sort of Howl move to perhaps fear enemies around it.Ranger: Long wind up, doesn't feel good to use most of the time. Most power skullsSamurai: Animations a bit slow and it feels like you get locked into them. Skulls I tend to almost always pick up:Djinn: Teleport + the Fairy Tackle gives you very large vertical hit box and also lasts a deceptively long time when it comes to the Swap + Skill use.Rider: Very good mobility and feels good to use. I wish this skull would be immune to the fire mages. Motorcycle is a good concept and really love how wild it is. Ninja: Get the right items and the right skills and you can burst a lot of stuff down very quickly. I love the ninja and he is super fun.Predator: Having skills to spam really makes you feel good as long as you can control it. Immense DPS and really gives you the feeling of a dual-wielding maniac. Has a weird synergy with the Purple Ribcage where you can infinitely use the skills. This might be intentional but each press of the button is considered an independent cast, so it's almost infinite resets.Mummy: Click attack fast = destroy people. After the most recent nerf it's not as good but it gives you immunity to traps so this man is a legend. Dark Paladin: Rewards swapping and smart skill usage. Does a buttload of damage if you can get the right angle on people. Super fun to use and makes you feel really bad ass when you can pull the combos off.
_childDocuments_.name: Skul: The Hero Slayer

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Skul system is uniqueHardmode is pretty interestingSome bosses have unique mechanics that are fun.Cons:Build variety is pretty limited, if you play sword you are only looking for bleed items, hybrid classes really have no identity. Item pool seems heavily tilted toward physical items, so it puts magic dealing chars in a strange spot of hoping for re rolls being in your favor at shops. You will become very bored of the same layouts and enemies over and over. I have played up to hard mode 4, and i have already come to "hate" specific rooms. Which with proper random generation would increase replay-ability. There are people trapped in cages but there seems to be only 5 of them so even events are lacking in variety. THERE ARE NO SECRET ROOMS, you will maybe see a unique room with treasure every 10 or so runs but typically there are no secret rooms, as I've mentioned there is limited variety in layouts so this is probably why there are no secret rooms or alternative paths. Certain bosses make melee characters cry, the mage in act 4 stays airborne for 75% of the fight is very annoying, certain skuls have abilities that are impossible to use on bosses such as the gravedigger and Otello on the Boss in Act 4, all the boulders just roll off the platforms and damaging the boss becomes a game of hoping she lands on platforms long enough for the boulders to do damage. I recommend this game if you are looking for a metroidvania style game with limited rogue aspects, with minor replay-ability.
_childDocuments_.name: Skul: The Hero Slayer

_childDocuments_.review: Skul has only gotten better over time, thanks to the continuous updates that this game receives. The variance in builds is high, and the replayability is there through the gameplay loop and difficulty modifiers. Each skull (equivalent of character class) feels unique and enjoyable to play. And while it's one of the harder games I've played, it never felt unfair.Skul's approach to difficulty increase is significantly better than most. While the game becomes more challenging once you activate this mechanic, it isn't due to enemies simply statchecking your ass, but due to adding new movesets to bosses, or new enemy and stage variants. However, the game also provides you with new toys to play with, such as a new powerup system or mechanics that increase the quality of a run. While not every run will be god tier, you'll be hard pressed to find a run that can't be won with pure skill alone.And now with the seemingly final story update, it adds a new incentive to see the game through as well as some incredible boss fights near the end. The music is underrated as well.Personally, if I liked the feel of the combat a bit better, this would have become one of my new favourites in the roguelite genre, but despite that, the gameplay loop and content still makes it worth playing for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Skul: The Hero Slayer

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game with items that really impact your play-style that can lead to so many different feeling runs.The difficulty of the game is a steep learning curve but it is done well as difficulty comes through increasing variety of enemies and traps.There are two things that make me not recommend this game:1. One of the three character types "Speed" is not possible to play well unless you are able to mash one button without tiring or hurting yourself. The game would benefit greatly by an option to hold button for continuous attacks.2.Visual clarity is not this games strong suit. There is some amazing work done with the pixel art and particle effects. Too many effects. Once you stack up bonuses through items, enemies and especially bosses are incredibly hard to see. All or most of these effects should layered behind/around the enemies to allow the player to see incoming attacks and enemy projectiles. Another option would be a toggle to highlight enemy models.If these two things do not bother you, this is an easy recommend for anyone that loves rouge-like elements, varied player builds, and button mashing action with some platforming elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Skul: The Hero Slayer

_childDocuments_.review: This review is mostly against what people are saying about the game and it's "flaws". The biggest complaint I see about this game is the boss' health bars and how they are too big. The only boss I genuinely agree that this is a problem is the Chimera. Every other fight has some aspect that is either interesting, or able to be manipulated. I kind of cringe when I see people say the bosses take to long in this game because even on the final boss, it takes 3 to 5 minutes tops. That is also the FINAL boss. I enjoy fights where I have to pay attention most of the time or I could be severely punished. The chimera just kind of feels like a dps wall and the fight isn't interesting. The next problem people have with the game are the skulls you get and how broken some are compared to others. First off, this is the same mechanic as getting a bad or good gun in enter the gungeon. Similarly, some of the basic skulls can be amazing. Werewolf and Thief are godlike for commons, frozen skull and rider are the same for rares and so on. Slightly connected to this subject is bone fragments. I've put 38 hours into the game and almost have all of the legendary skulls. They are NOT hard to get. You get plenty of opportunities to get bones throughout any given run probably. While one run you may get a bunch of commons so you don't get enough bones, the next you might get 3 legendary skulls to sacrifice. This was the case in one of my runs where I upgraded two skulls to legendary and still had 113 bones remaining. It's a roguelike, there is going to be RNG. Next is the inventory and items. I would not compare the game to gungeon or isaac in terms of inventory. It is not that sort of game and there are twice as many levels in gungeon and you can potentially have a full restart while keeping your items in gungeon. The items are well balanced for a 9 item limit and they all give additional passives that can be useful in themselves. Having "the run" every run because you are good enough to get so many items every run gets boring. Having to pick and choose makes every run semi-unique due to RNG. Two last problems people say the game has are one, that the layouts get boring. I really don't get this one because this same thing happens in every roguelike I have ever played like of course you are going to remember layouts and spawns. It's a natural progression. I just do not understand this complaint. The second is that damage feels "unavoidable". The game gives you two jumps and a dash. Every normal floor enemy definitely feels avoidable. I'm so glad I can't just braindead auto through every map. If someone is really having health problems, get the vampire necklace. I could maybe see this complaint on some hitboxes in the sisters fight, but other than that, and I hate saying this, but get good.Lastly, I just wanted to say that I love this game. The variety of skulls are so cool and the mechanics of the game are so much fun to play around with. The boss fights are challenging for the most part (looking at you chimera) and are so satisfying when beaten. When you actually put together an op build with the perfect skull for the build, the gameplay just hypes me up. I'm looking forwards to any dlc this game has if any. P.S. My least favorite item is the green bone, and mummy sucks so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if I can evaluate the game properly, for I don't have too much technical knowledge. Besides all these, I think the plot and the story is also cute and is more than enoough for a game like this. However, please do not forget, these are my opinions!Lastly, I have a suggestion for the developers: It would be great if there was a mode in which we are able to use anything in order to try out different combos, different combos with characters etc. This mode can be available to the player after she/he defeats the final boss and finishes the game in normal mode. This mode probably would have caused me to play the game for another 40-50 hours...Thank you for reading!

_childDocuments_.review:
The human race attacking the Demon King's castle is nothing new and has happened countless times before. What makes this time different though, is that the Adventurers decided to join forces with the Imperial Army and the 'Hero of Caerleon' to finally succeed in the total destruction of the Demon stronghold. All of the demons in the castle were taken prisoner except for one lone skeleton named 'Skul'.

Skul is no ordinary skeleton. In addition to his formidable fighting skills, he can gain new and exciting abilities depending on which skull he's wearing.Use up to 2 skulls at a time, each of which has its own unique attack range, speed and power. So choose ones that match your playing style and switch them in the heat of battle to bring your enemies to their knees. The power is in your hands!

Skul has crossed paths with a party of Adventurers! They are powerful foes that hunt Demons for sport. But while Skul may be small, he still packs quite a punch. So just see who really is the hunter and who is the hunted...
_childDocuments_.name: Skul: The Hero Slayer

name: UFO 50
detailed_description: UFO 50 is a collection of 50 single and multiplayer games from the creators of Spelunky, Downwell, and Catacomb Kids. Explore a variety of genres, from platformers and shoot 'em ups to puzzle games, roguelites, and RPGs. Our goal is to combine a familiar 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design. 50 BRAND NEW GAMES - These are NOT minigames or microgames! Although the size of each game varies, every one is a complete experience, from its opening title screen to its ending credits. Some are small arcade-style games but there are also larger open-world adventures and a JRPG that could take many hours to beat. AN ALTERNATE UNIVERSE - According to the story of UFO 50, the games were all created by a fictional 80s video game company that was obscure but ahead of its time. Some games are sequels to other games in the collection and various characters appear in multiple titles as part of a shared continuity. AN INSTANT LIBRARY - All 50 games are available to play at the start! The concept was inspired by multicarts, retro collections, and the experience of going to a friend's house and perusing their game library. Jump in and out of games at a whim - exploring the collection is part of the fun! AUTHENTIC BUT ALSO MODERN - We carefully chose what elements to modernize. Every game shares a unique 32-color palette and we took great efforts to make them look and sound like actual 8-bit titles from the 80s. On the other hand, it was important to us that UFO 50 was fun and surprising for modern players, so we chose not to limit ourselves to the genres and design conventions of the past. VERSUS AND CO-OP PLAY - Half of the collection features local multiplayer, including co-op and versus. You can compete head-to-head in a new fighting or strategy game... or team up to beat a classic arcade game from an alternate timeline. It's great for groups! Here are some of games you'll get to play in UFO 50: CAMPANELLA 2 - The sequel to Campanella (another game in UFO 50), Campanella 2 features procedurally-generated levels where you can explore in your UFO but also hop out to enter shops and dangerous caves. You play as the intrepid treasure-hunter Isabell, but she hasn't always been a hero - by playing the entire collection you can learn more about her past. QUIBBLE RACE - In this unique sci-fi 'horse-racing' game, the goal is to win more money than your opponents, but why stop at betting? Thanks to the seedy alien underworld, you can hire thugs to tamper with the race or even sponsor your own quibble to earn extra credits. But your opponents can do the same, so the question is... how well can you anticipate their actions? Up to 3 players can compete in this turn-based game of betting and bluffing. PINGOLF - A fan favorite at gaming get-togethers like PAX, Pingolf is another fun multiplayer game that mixes golf with pinball. As you navigate 18 holes filled with bumpers, trampolines, and other crazy obstacles, a dot matrix display will light up at the bottom of the screen to cheer you on! SEASIDE DRIVE - Sometimes you'll want a break from long, open-world games and challenging strategy titles, so why not jump into a straight-forward arcade-style action game like Seaside Drive? But even in a popular genre, UFO 50 brings something new to the table - in this case, Ojiro Fumoto (the creator of Downwell) designed a stylish car-based shoot 'em up where 'drifting' across the screen is how you power-up your gun. GRIMSTONE - Yes, there is a full blown JRPG in the collection! Grimstone follows many conventions from 8-bit console RPGs, but is streamlined for a modern audience. Also, to make combat more engaging, we added a skill-based component to battles and encounters on the overworld can be strategically avoided. The story takes place in the American Wild West, where somehow the land has been swallowed up by Hell! Creating your party from the ashes of a burned-down saloon, you'll be looking for answers as to why it happened. And that's just five games! Out of 50! So come join us and enjoy this collection of 8-bit classics from another dimension! There's something for everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had much time to place since release, but from what I've seen so far this game is amazing.  I love the cute art and the sound effects.  This game feels like nostalgia even though it's brand new.  I can't wait to explore what else Derek has created for us. P.S.  Kitty put spaces in my review. Spaces stay in my review.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most interesting games to come out in a very long time. The fact that this game has managed to hold my attention for this long is a testament to it's quality. One of the very few games I would rate a 10/10, easy GOTY material. Is every game a banger? No. But pretty much all of them are at least interesting. And there are some true gems in here. If you like video games as a medium, retro games, or game design, then I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Buying UFO 50 i expected it to be just 50 arcade style games, things that would feel at home in the 80's but what UFO 50 delivers is much more then that. While the game do use the style and difficulty levels of early video games it brings with it a modern twist.Several of the games included in the pack are only one or two updates off of being worth a separate purchase (looking at you Overbold/Valbrace/Mortol) and while often these games are on the shorter side others have potentially tens of hours alone. If you enjoy old school difficulty and are interesting in a Wide range of different styles you will be sure to find something to both entertain and challenge you.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played about 15 of the games so far, and there is something to love about every single one of them. Most of these games are more individually more creative and interesting than most games I've played in recent memory. The music and graphics are wonderful. This is the most generous game I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Marvelous collection. It’s like finding an abandoned cache of 80s lost video game media and the someone patched in a lot of QOL fixes atypical for the period. So many of the games have such interesting mechanics that make you say “oh gosh that’s clever”.Haven’t even played half of what’s on offer but so excited to keep digging and finding secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The games are all pretty solid from a gameplay standpoint, but I did not get what I had hoped to out of this game. I still recommend it to anyone who likes old games and is needing to scratch an itch for something challenging. If you're looking for a game that you'll get many many hours of entertainment out of, this might not be it. Overall I'd give it a 5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty cool collection of ideas;  legitimately 50 unique games in a variety of genres styled as the releases on a fictional 1980's game console.  Recommend initially trying them all in chronological "release" order, as you can really see & feel the designs grow in complexity as time goes on in the UFOverse. While not every game is necessarily my cup of tea, the concepts are solid and without filler. The best ones here are worth the price of admission alone.  With the diverse genres included different players will gravitate to different games as their favourites.  I will say that some of the platformers are quite difficult and hitting Cherry status on all seems like quite the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is one of the most heartfelt & interesting pieces of collaborative art to have ever graced the world - none the less the videogame industry.It's a deeply loving look at a history that never was, elevating the memories of our past atop the progress of nostalgia's future.I could continue to pontificate on how perfect UFO 50 is, but I'd rather leave off with something more succinct.UFO 50 f**ks so hard & I'm so thankful for all the effort everyone put into it. It's special & precious & I cherish its existence. 🤍💜✨
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The variety and depth on offer is really impressive. The '80s design sensibilities won't be for everyone, but UFO 50 serves as a good reminder as to what has been lost in the pursuit for games with ever-increasing mass market appeal. Most of the collection does a good job of blending retro and contemporary game design, helping each game feel fresh despite having old school elements.There are a lot of multiplayer modes on offer which can be great fun with a friend. The soundtrack is also fantastic!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: get in on this now because in five years you're going to be seeing videos online with titles like "UFO 50 is a Hidden Masterpiece" and when a hundred thousand people start flocking to the game you'll get to say that you liked it before that popular person on the computer made a seven hour essay about it
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This collection gets a recommendation for me just for Avianos ALONE, what a masterpiece of a strategy game, it is very simple but contains an insane amount of strategic value, like the best of strategy games. Somehow, the lamest looking game in the collection ended up being a serious gem that i see myself playing for many more hours, it has certainly solidified Jon Perry as another indie mastermind for me, like Derek Yu with Spelunky.Aside from that very unexpected favorite, there are plenty of other great games that it would take me way too long to get into each one, so it is best experienced for yourself.The collection also hides many meta secrets that are still being uncovered, so nerds like me have a lot to tackle here.I bought this collection just to support my favorite indie game designer, not even really expecting to get more than two evenings of value from it, and ended up finding gold.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I waited 7 years for this game collection, and I'm surprised I didn't have to wait another 7. It's mind-blowing how many clever & original games can be found in UFO 50, and I've only seen half of the games so far. UFO 50 also pushes its feats further to weave a fictional continuity between every game - it's compelling to say the least, without venturing into spoilers!If you can't find enough games in UFO 50 to justify the astonishingly low $25 price tag, you might not be a fan of video games
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: So much more than just a collection of 50 small arcade games. Most games are fully worked out concepts that are really fun and creative. This entire pack brought me back to the days of playing flash games and just browsing through collections. Specifically Nitrome, with the wide variety of pixelart games made by the same developers. The games range through a wide variety of genres and concepts. So no matter what genre of games you like, there will definitely be games in here that you enjoy. At the time of writing this i have played the game for more than 10 hours and I feel like I am nowhere near discovering everything i want to do. I have beaten a few of the games, but there are several that I enjoy a lot that I still want to complete. I believe there is even an overarching secret/puzzle that I haven't even started looking for. Most games are really challenging, but in the right way, I immediately want to jump back in after every loss.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: When they say play forever, they mean it! Honestly a pretty great classica style collection for those who enjoyed the NES / SNES era of gaming, with today's style of caveats. There will be some that don't mesh with you, but you will find some bangers here if this is what you're after. If you are an achievement hunter though... you have your work cut out for you.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like numeric scores at all, but this game comes as highly recommended as I possibly can.If you've never experienced the joy of pirating all the best games for a classic console and immersing yourself in title-after-high-quality-title, this will probably *ruin* that experience: these games are empirically better than 99% of 8-bit games I've ever played. Details I like about this game: - Consistent pixel width, no subpixel motion (that I can notice)- Scanline simulation (sexy)- OST, sfx, etc all seem to come from one synthesis system, creating amazing cohesion title to title- Minor intra-title thematic references (ex. references to Campanella and Avianos in Rock On! Island)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It genuinely hurts me to say this, but... I didn't like it. Don't lynch me just yet! I love the concept of this - 50 retro throwbacks in one? And (almost) all of them actually creative, fresh and thought-out? AND it's made by highly competent devs? Hell yeah, sign me up! But then I played it... I'm sure to some extent it's just me (which is ultimately also why I decided against a negative review), but even though I'm generally a huge fan of retro and arcade gaming - hell, it makes up the overwhelming majority of what I play nowadays! - I think what I'm figuring out right now is that I don't actually like NES games.Both home computer titles from before that era and console titles from after that era click with me much more than the particular space in time that this collection aims to emulate the feel of. (Successfully so, I might add!)Point being - I'm sure it's good, but it's not for me. And should you also have some qualms with specifically NES/Famicom era gaming, you might want to do some more research before taking the plunge as well.That said, I hope this game ends up being a huge success for all involved, because I genuinely do love what it's doing.... Now you may lynch me all you like.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up in the 80s this is pure nostalgia bliss, feels like real lost media.Almost every genre you can think of, incredibly simple control scheme, the graphics and music are beautiful, and capture the feel of the era perfectly.The games are all brutally difficult and there's very little handholding, which is true to form but might turn off a few people.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It is currently 5am, I’ve been playing this all night, so sorry if my wording is insane.Don’t let the first game fool you. It is purposeful. Play on.I was initially worried about buying this because it appears to have the potential to be a ‘play for an hour and never again’ kind of game, which recently has been the case for when I revisit nes/snes/megadrive games.I caved and I’m so incredibly glad I did. Any worries of ‘motivation to play’ you have, forget them and buy this. If you are a retro game fan this is absolutely going to scratch a very particular itch. The blend of modern optimisation is incredibly well done. I skim read reviews a few days ago and the phrase ‘half baked’ kept popping up. Disregard this. People can’t seem to grasp beautiful simplicity from games in 2024. To use the word ‘simple’ even positively seems wrong because so far each game has had its own particular cleverness to it that makes playing each one so exciting, even if some may ring familiar, a uniqueness appears from it and it rarely crosses your mind the thought of ‘this feels like (game)’ Even games that didn’t quite click with me I have the need to revisit them to try and get better at them and progress if possible. The grip UFO50 has on me already is insane. Treat yourself and buy this. I can’t wait to play this with my dad who got me into gaming and introduced me to older consoles at a young age. I hope one day online multiplayer is added but with the magic of modern technology there are ways. Having official online would be fun though, with maybe global leaderboards alongside the ones already there. Those would be hilarious to look at. Overall this is YEAASSUESYSYEYSYYSEHDYSHSYSHSYSHAYESAAAA AAYAAAEAYAYAYYAYEAYAYYAYEUSYYAYAYAYYAAYAYESYAYAYESYAAYYAYAYAayeysyYwooooooWOOOOOWOOOOOOOOWOOOOOOOOOWOOOOOOO
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of the Nintendo DS game Konami Classics Series: Arcade Hits and its the best feeling of nostalgia for when I used to grind those games out in the same way, but with a refreshing twist. I've probably only played half the games so far, and plan of seeing how long it will be for all the cherries. Fantastic value if you are a variety gamer and have the patience to play all the games through. This one is a hit for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible variety of games with love poured into every one of them. If you’ve ever messed around with NES games, you might be familiar with the charm of games made with restricted resources. You aren’t spoonfed rules, you discover them through trial and error. The world isn’t completely built out and painstakingly detailed, your imagination is part of the story and tiny artistic choices communicate it to you.  UFO 50 clicks into that vibe effortlessly, while (sparingly) softening the hard edges of retro gaming. I highly recommend it, and anticipate many more hours of fun had with it. A note on bad reviews I’ve seen: the games are presented “chronologically”, so the first ones you encounter will be the most basic. Pick some at random if you must see the scope the game has to offer you within the 2 hour refund window.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This "game" is absolutely incredible. Everyone who I've seen play this immediately clicks with one of the games, finishes it in a single sitting, and has an absolute blast, and I think that UFO 50 is worth the price just for that one game alone, whatever it ends up being for you. For me, Avianos was such an absolute banger, it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun as a miniature 4x, and it has a ton of depth. Also they put an entire JRPG in this, which is worth mentioning lol
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is truly lightning in a bottle in the best possible way.It'd be hard to go over every game because the 50 or so you can play are all very distinct and engaging. There's Adventure. Racing. Side-scroller. Puzzle. Shooting. Snake. Volleyball. UFO 50 has it all and then some, presented as an adorable package of a hypothetical SNES Mini. Each game plays differently, but the main gist is that you have basic controls: two action buttons and your joystick. If you use a more modern controller plugged in, the extra two buttons are linked to those actions too, so nothing complicated. It might be the controller I'm using but sometimes I feel the turning isn't as responsive as I'd like, which is bad for making precise turns to avoid death.Difficulty may vary because there are extras you can earn on top of beating a game. There's a house gift that requires a sort of in progress goal, changing the cartridge of the game to Gold (tied to achievements) for beating the game, or changing it to Cherry Red (also achievements) for doing an above and beyond goal beating it. Like achieving a high score or winning each round without starting over. This really itches the achievement hunting itch gamers may have for clearing everything has to offer, and the games feel just long enough to justify being a fun game made with 8bit graphics. Even the total file size of UFO 50's download reflects this, being under half of a GB.There are a lot of Easter eggs, such as sprites used in other games. I recall seeing a mob snail from the side scroll game Nintek appear in a secret room in Warptank, or the use of coffee as a secret item collectible in Warptank and Campnella. It feels like reusing assets similar to 80s games, that would have wowed any kid playing an interactive gaming universe. You know, like what Nintendo did up to Super Smash Bros, or what Sony recently did with Astro Bot. Sound is also recycled in that similar tones of start up used between games. And there's a growth in sound too. The first game, Barbuta has only sound effects and lacks even a title screen where you most likely will immediately set off a trap if not paying attention. Later games have music loops or motifs that give them personality. They are chiptune but done so well fitting the 80s aesthetic and pixel work.TBH, I was wary when I read "modern game design" in the store summary. Other games that pursue making games for the modern audience tend to make things inoffensive and tone deaf. But UFO 50 just focuses on quality of life features like an easy/instant reset. I used that feature a lot when my runs in certain games weren't so perfect. These games are made with being made fun that even when I get mad not reaching the hard Cherry achievements, I come back to keep trying.So I definitely recommend picking up UFO 50. Base price of $25 for 50 games is a steal when even a fraction of them are worth hours of playtime. (And not at all like that dumpster fire Action 52 back in 1991 where they charged $200 for poorly buggy and recycled shovelware before that was even a thing. For reference, look up AVGN's review of it and Cheetahmen.)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Videogames are so cool, man. The game that sold me here was one where the d pad moved you left and the face buttons moved you right, and you had to hold one side and press the other to jump in the direction you wanted to. It was such a simple yet creative title it reminded me of my teenage years when I would go on places like gamejolt and click through page after page of games to find the real experimental and out there stuff. This game is incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Mossmouth did it again. Whatever is next is automatically on my wishlist. Just so much quality and variety spread out over 50 games. Some are short games, others longer. It is really fun to explore new games and genres you wouldn't play otherwise. Stop reading the reviews and just buy it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: What a really cool idea for a game. I'd wager many of us grew up with those bootlegged plug and plays or computer rom that claimed 50+ games in one. And they were  almost all terrible. UFO 50 showed it can be done well. Most of these games are super addictive score attack games with enough depth and variety to be fun and challenging for awhile. This game is super accurate to its concept. These games are old school NES era hard and unforgiving but also razor tight. The pig chao garden is a nice touch too. My only complaint is they took the bit too far by making alot of the puzzle games unintuitive or incoherent, but most of these are awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the first time I've played a "new retro" game and actually had it truly feel authentic.I've only now just played a bit of all 50 games on offer, and I can say I'm very excited to dive deeper. This is essentially what Action 52 should have been. There truly is something for everyone here, and regardless of genre preference (there's a few surprises), every single game here is quality while also maintaining a wonderful balance of retro and modern. If you have a love and intrigue for pure game design, this is a must buy. Everyone involved clearly worked very hard and put a lot of love into this collection, and I'm hopeful that this will usher in a new era of "the new old". Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There are 50 full games in this, each of them their own complete entry with unique ideas and mechanics. I played one game in this for hours and I'm still only halfway or so done that one specific game. Each one I've played so far is worth exploring and trying to complete at least once. There's a lot of content here and its good quality stuff. This game is an absolute steal at its asking price. This whole package is kind of mind blowing. Very recommended if you want a lot of good games that'll keep you occupied for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Nice collection of games.  To be honest, half the games are quite bad and not worth playing for more than a minute, but there are a few treasures in here.  I suppose part of the fun is the simulation of dumpster-diving to see whether a given title will be fun or trash.  And with the continuity between some of the titles, the collection provides a simulation as if you're truly playing through a singular company's game catalog.The games that are actually good are quite clever.  There's a game called "Party House" that serves as a small-scale deckbuilding game and takes a clever approach to that genre.  There's an idle/incremental game (which you can let idle while you play the other games) that mixes the idler genre with a simple dungeon-crawler.  There's a wild-west game where you rob a train, mixing action and puzzle elements.The only thing that makes me hesitant to recommend this is the price.  $25 feels very steep for what it is.  Sure, there are many games in the collection, but most of the games in here aren't even worth $0.50.  When you take all those away, and add up the value of what's left -- which is still only about $1 or $2 each for the good games due to their small scope -- $10 or $15 would be a more appropriate price for the value you're getting here.Worth it if you can pick it up in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just wow.  When a title makes you enjoy turn-based rpgs that would normally not be your cup of tea, then you know the game has achieved something. And Grimstone sure is addictive to play. Other favourites of mine are Divers and Cyber Owls. I plan on playing Night Manor close to Halloween. You are sure to find some games which you will  become your favs and the RPGs are lengthy experiences that are worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I can't imagine anyone would play all these games and not find at least 5 they absolutely adore. It's an incredibly diverse collection in terms of the genres being explored but in spite of that the familiar charm carries through in each game as you progress through this imaginary developer's chronological output. Even the games that didn't hold my interest had some great unique ideas and all of the games I passed on seem to be someone else's favourite. Also a lot of these games have a shocking amount of content considering it's basically a bargain bin 50 pack. The game somehow always manages to feel like it values the players time, everytime I open a new game I think "surely this one will be the inevitable dud or repeat" and yet it never is. UFO50 is truly a superb experience, and if you have someone to play the couch co-op multiplayer games with this is easily game of the year imo.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Basically every single game in this collection is a fully realised title, some of which would stand if released by themselves. And yet, there's 50 of them in here. I think it's safe to say that this game has it all, and the best way to play is to just embrace the variety, float from title to title, and see what sticks. Don't let the quantity of games wear you down, just select titles that look interesting, try for a few minutes and move on. Do this and before you know it, you'll be in hours deep.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a special game, a massive feat for the team and for indies in general. These are some of the most fun and creative games I've played in years and they all literally only use two buttons and a d-pad. Here's a checklist of a few things to see if you'll like the game:Do you like short and sweet arcade experiences?Do you like fun short burst multiplayer?What about drawn out strategy multiplayer?Maybe a deckbuilder or two?Got a penchant for metroidvanias?Or would you like to sink your teeth into a full JRPG?In the mood for a spooky point and click?Do you like games that are fun?It's a meme to say "there's a little something for everyone" but in this case it is 1000% true. I challenge anyone to try out a few of these games and say they didn't enjoy any of them. It won't happen. These games just ooze charm and you can tell they were all made with passion and care. I haven't even touched on the presentation, music, graphics, and meta narrative that lies underneath it all. Just believe me when I say this is a landmark game, not just indie. People will be talking about this game for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible achievement in game design! This is Mossmouth we're talking about (creators of Spelunky), so I'm sure nobody is surprised by the sheer quality and creativity on offer here. Even so, this is one of the most impressive efforts of game design I've seen in a while.UFO 50 is more than simply an assortment of retro-styled video games. It is a love letter to and reimagining of gaming and game design philosophies of the '80s. Many of the individual games are quite excellent and addictively replayable even by modern standards, sure. However, the big picture of the collection also takes players on a journey through the evolution of a fictional game studio.There are games here of just about every genre. There are quick, arcadey games and epic, thinky adventure games. Action games, puzzle games and everything in between. It's like finding a dusty console in a bin in your attic and firing it up for the first time to discover a whole library of classic games that you never knew existed.There really is something for everyone here and even if only a handful of the games really stick with you, it's still absolutely worth the pittance that Mossmouth is asking. At $0.50 (or less if you catch it on sale) per game, this is an absolute steal and several of these games could have easily sold individually for $10 or more.Highest recommendation if you have any patience and interest at all in retro games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I love video games. And as a person who loves video games, I love video games that love video games. I just finished Astro Bot last week, a game designed to celebrate the history of the PlayStation systems while also taking a look into the future of what lies ahead for the genre of 3D platforming. I think it takes a special game developer to be able to harness that feeling. To understand that concept, and feed it back to the player in a meaningful way, and that game captures that feeling almost perfectly.This game (or, collection of games) takes that celebration of PlayStation games, picks it up between its index finger and thumb before launching it 2500 feet away. Astro Bot is incredible, as a game and as a celebration of games, and yet this game is a celebration of ALL GAMES, and the experience of loving games.Inside this game are 50 games, all unique spins on concepts you’ve likely seen if you’ve ever perused the vast library of early NES or MasterSystem games. However, these games all come away as the best possible outcome of their parts: they take those concepts, apply something new to them, and make them feel new and exciting. Not only that, but the lack of information here is incredibly fun. This is the first game I’ve played where I wish I was part of a Gaming Book Club, because this game would be what eats up that time. This game facilitates that kind of gameplay.To say that this is an indie game that will be regarded as one of the greats is to do a disservice to everything that is happening here. This is a peek into a gaming legacy that never existed in the best possible way— and a box of ideas executed so well that you’ll find they grab hold of you in a way your classic Donkey Kings and Pack-Guys never did.The devs of this collection love games, and gaming history. They deserve all the awards for this. I cannot believe there are 50 of these. I cannot wait to play them all, to really sink time into them, and experience their secrets. This is such an exciting piece of media and I’m so glad I got to be here for part of it. Hope that if you have read this far, you will too.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's a variety pack of games themed after SNES/NES games (inspired by the train-wreck that was action 52 from what I've read), but on a made-up video game system instead featuring 50 actually good small games of varying genres.I've only played around 10-ish of the games so far, but I think I can safely bet that this will end up as one of the best games released this year. Most of the games I've played so far have been really well thought out and unique across the genres they are in; it reminds of me of the days around 2010 in which flash game websites were still around and providing a pool of interesting variety content which you were free to sift through. They aren't ALL amazing (to me, anyway), but not a single one so far has been bad.Update:Now much further in (tried 49 of 50 and completed more than I had before), I'd say there were only a few I thought were flawed or mediocre. Otherwise, it's 95% good or gold, with some standing out as games that I could legitimately see a high quality sequel being made for (that isn't limited by using two buttons), but I won't spoil which ones are which here. Absolutely phenomenal game/collection that's well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been abducted and brainwashed by UFO 50. I can't put this game down. 50 actually amazing games bundled in one package for $25. You might not like every game here, but if you can appreciate retro styled/inspired games I'd say you're guaranteed to find at least one you like. Or two. Or five. A lot of these games could probably make it as independent titles with how big they are. But when they're all in one collection they elevate each other so much. You can easily jump out of one game and into another, and for me that seamlessness keeps things fresh and fun. I've completed a handful of games in my 43 hours of playtime so far, and I still have 12 whole games I haven't tried yet.Not to mention the meta-narrative story and secrets woven across the collection. I've barely explored that side of UFO 50, but the fact that it's there is just another layer to what this game has to offer.For the price and the variety of full and fantastic games, UFO 50 is truly a steal. I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I got an early copy of the game for work. I've played every single game at least a little, and many of them quite a bit over the last few months, even while some were still being worked on.In short, there's not a single one I didn't enjoy at least a little bit, though some were tough to get into. Many of them I enjoyed a lot.My personal ton ten are:- 07 Velgress, the fast-paced action platfomer. I love getting into a zen state in which I see the path I must take to get as many coins as possible as I climb; when you're familiar enough with the platforms to know exactly how fast they'll decay, so you're not climbing in a panic anymore. When you're climbing calmly, you'll know you're on the road to mastering Velgress.- 10 Devilition, the tactical puzzler. Finding the perfect placements for all of your explosives is extremely satisfying.- 12 Avianos, the tactical resource war game. It's a perfect game for me. It has birds and dinosaurs and fantasy and tactical gameplay. I beat the game in one sitting because I couldn't stop playing it.- 13 Mooncat, the platformer with unusual controls. It takes some getting used to, but it's not actually very punishing since you're never sent very far back when you die. It's also just a beautiful game to see and listen to. Great vibes.- 22 Porgy, the undersea action explorer. It's just satisfying to play. It feels good to explore a little more each time, to map it all out and note things to come back to, and to grow in confidence as you take out the boss enemies. It's full of mysteries dying to be uncovered.- 28 Rail Heist, the stealth puzzle platformer. Just a strong concept overall, and extremely satisfying when you figure out a foolproof strategy to get your goods and escape unscathed.- 30 Rock On! Island, the tactical action defense game. It's not that complicated, but it takes some time to master. Heads up that you can upgrade your weapon at the base if you've got the resources!- 37 Valbrace, the dungeon exploration action RPG. You might want some grid paper on hand. Another game full of secrets and satisfying gameplay. New enemies can be rough when you first meet them, but there's always an effective strategy.- 40 Grimstone, the western jRPG. I just love jRPGs, even the clunky ones from the 80s that always require a fair bit of patience and grinding, but it's definitely not everyone's cup of tea. Still, there's a lot of game here to love if you're into it like I am.- 45 Mini & Max, the action exploration platformer. Just satisfying to play from moment to moment, with a world of stuff to explore. A clever setup with cute, compelling characters and tons of secrets.I haven't played the multiplayer games with friends yet, but I'm excited to try those out. I bet Elfazar's Hat is a blast with 2P coop.Anyway, I think there's something here for almost everyone. Take your time and give each game a shot. Every single game is packed with love.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a game where, midway through the adventure, you find some minigame inside of the game that you end up getting obsessed with? A la Gwent (Witcher 3), Tetra Master (FF9), or the arcade game in Stardew Valley? Imagine 50 of those in one package and you have UFO 50.There's truly something special here and I have so much more to go. The way it works is - each game becomes silver when played, gold when 'beaten' and cherry-colored when beaten under special conditions. Maybe it's beating without dying, maybe it's while getting the highest score, it varies game to game. So in my in my 15 current hours I have gotten silver in 5/50 gold in 2/50 and cherry in another 2/50 of the games. One of the cherry's (Barbuta) took me 7 hours to solve with all of the secrets. Then I played Mooncat, which was another joyous 2 hours. The other 5 games make up the other 8 or so hours, so they vary in length greatly. Every one of these games feels like it could have been your favorite game as a kid in the 80s and, even when I don't like the game itself, the charm built into it compels me to play more. That is to say, not every game is going to be for you, there's plenty I played and will likely not play again. But every game oozes passion and a desire to do something unique and, most importantly, fun. This collection is extremely fun and there is something for everyone. It's my 2024 GOTY. If the trailer at all is appealing to you, I can recommend it without hesitation. If it's not appealing, but you love games, it's worth checking out for the concepts, art, and music alone. I can't wait to play even more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This pitch of this game makes it sound like you're getting 50 NES-Style mini/arcade games, which for the price would actually be a pretty worthwhile value.What you get is about 30 real genuine retro-inspired full fledged video games, and 20 of the minigames you were expecting. For the price this is worth grabbing because the act of just grabbing at games at random is really fun and SOMETHING in here will click with you.Highlights for me so far:Night Manor - Retro horror point and click adventure with multiple endings. Genuinely spooky.Warptank - Puzzle game about being a tank that can only teleport to whatever surface is vertical. It's got tons of levels and is really well designed and fun.Valbrace - First person dungeon crawling mixed with Punch-out style combat. It's a blast. Get a notebook to draw your own map.Grimstone - A FULL JRPG. IVE BEEN PLAYING FOR 10 HOURS. IT'S GREAT.Fist Hell - Coop beat-em up that's really tough but fun.Overbold - Smash TV but you have upgrades between rounds and can gamble on making the next round harder to get more cash to upgrade with. _childDocuments_.review: “A collection of fifty games for an imaginary 8-bit console”, you say. “Surely you mean fifty , right?”Well, no. There are actually fifty  in here, the majority of which will take you hours to finish. Not that you’re probably going to be finishing all of them, but many are compelling enough for you to want to see the end credits roll.There’s a game or two from pretty much all imaginable genres here, ranging from seemingly simple stuff like arcade shooters, puzzle and platforming games to sprawling RPG’s, point-and-click adventures and strategy games. All of them have been modernised to remove most of the unfair janky bits you might remember from games of this era, but retaining the art style, music and level of challenge. One of the neatest things is that all of the games come with minimal instructions, leaving the discovery of gameplay mechanics, secrets and strategies to the player. UFO 50 feels like rummaging through a treasure trove of forgotten classics where you can end up playing a single game for hours on end if you find one that resonates with you.I haven’t ran into a straight-up “bad” game yet, since even the ones that aren’t from my preferred genres do play well and show a level of polish one wouldn’t expect from a collection this big. And considering the price of the whole package, you’ll easily get your money’s worth if even just five games in UFO 50 strike your fancy. Just maybe don’t play through them in chronological order…UFO 50 is one of my favorite games I’ve played so far this year, perfectly illustrating why discovery of new things, excitement and mystery are such key things in our enjoyment in video games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god! I was impressed with Zachtronic's Last Call BBS, but this blows it out of the water, no offense intended. I got goosebumps when I turned on the game the first time and saw them lined up in chronological order from like '82 to '89. I have only played 8 out of the 50 games, and I know for a fact the games are only gonna get better with fake time. The Girl Garden game I had no idea what to do. It is like renting a game at Blockbuster back in the day and having to figure the game mechanics out for yourself. I didn't know I had a nostalgia for that honestly? I hold it against modern day game developers that don't tell me everything in a tutorial. I guess I just expect tutorials because they game them to me. I've questioned why so many games today don't include maps when they used to never include them. In the 8th game that takes place in space that moves like Blaster Master/The Guardian Legend I look forward to bringing out the graph paper for the first time in 20 years or so to make my own map.The first game is great, but I will warn others that the character moves very slowly. This was likely intentional because it was the first game made for this alternate timeline gaming console. Don't rush to judgement. Old games could, and still can, kick your butt.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely incredible collection. I went into UFO 50 thinking most of the games would be simple, arcade-style experiences or interesting ideas without much fleshing out, but I couldn't have been more wrong. Every game is crafted with care and precision, and even the shorter ones left me amazed at their sheer creativity. And there's such a wide array of genres too -- it's got the usual platformers and shoot 'em ups you'd expect from an 80s throwback, but there's also puzzle games, strategy games, at least one roguelite, adventure games, multiple fully fledged RPGs, stealth games...it's such a joy to browse through the catalog and see what the next treasure will be.Even if you stick to your favorite genres, there's probably still dozens of hours of fun here. If you set out to 100% every game, it'll be more like hundreds of hours. This is the real deal. If any game in UFO 50 actually did release back in the 80s, it'd be a beloved classic to this day. And you get fifty of them. What a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought into the hype, and I regret that. "Surely if, like... 5 of these are entertaining enough it'll be worth the price?"Still looking. There's no good way to review this, since everything's all over the place. There's a weird clash of retro design with modern. EDIT: Specifically, the turn-based or more strategic games all feel made for people with a background playing complex board games, deck-builders, crafting survivor... modern genres. Had a similar problem with Across the Obelisk where the game should just have a disclaimer saying: "Play Slay the Spire for a tutorial, because we ain't pacing this for noobs."Intentionally bad controls: if you restrict movement options or make air momentum static, that's fine. When you make a vehicle always turn the same curvature regardless of speed, or make a warp tank where hitting right will reverse if you roll up a wall, let go, and repress it?Instructions. Communicating the purpose... a lot of these really fail. _childDocuments_.review: Could you put a price on finding a box containing an unreleased game system from the 8-bit era complete with a library of 50 games?  If you grew up with an NES this game will take you back to being a kid again.  That feeling of trading carts with your friends on the schoolyard, renting a game from the local video store and finding it came with no manual, receiving a game you've never heard of from your grandparents for your birthday, saving up all summer mowing lawns to buy that game with the cool fantasy themed box art.  Mossmouth aced the assignment: create a game that captures a whole era of history while also injecting modern gaming trends and innovations.  UFO50 is an instant classic and must buy for anyone interested in the 8-bit era.

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a game I had followed the development of for seven years, and the final product exceeds every high expectation I already had for it. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely outstanding. I don't believe I've ever written a proper Steam review but UFO 50 is an anomaly. Presenting itself as collection of 50 1980's titles from the now defunct developer, UFOSoft; UFO 50 is an endless stream of clever, thoughtful game design, wonderful sprite work and sound design, backed with an incredible soundtrack and fascinating meta-narrative to boot.In absence of a retro console/80's home computer, a lot of gaming experience in my 2000's youth was characterised by ROMsets. Ginormous collections of games my dad had managed to grab, all emulated on the family computer. I would spend hours scrolling through these massive lists of games, booting up whatever seemed interesting, finding all sorts of fascinating experiences from years past. I have fond memories of discovering favourites among these lists, coming back to them again and again before venturing out once more to see what else I could pick out and discover. UFO 50 has managed to recapture this experience for me, only every game (while not always in my wheelhouse) is consistently exceptional. I cannot help but adore it.I've not even dusted off all of the games in UFO 50's catalogue and this is by and large my game of the year for 2024 and potentially one of the greatest titles the medium has ever seen. I find myself stunned by the sheer scale and quality of it all. How did these developers pull this off? I could write a proper, beaming essay on UFO 50's first game chronologically, Barbuta, alone. If you have any sort of fondness for retro gaming, I'd recommend UFO 50 in a heartbeat. If you don't, I'd still give it a shot, you'd be hard-pressed to find something that you don't enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think there is ever going to be a 'perfect' moment to review this game. It is so notoriously BIG. Colossal. Monumental in size and scope. _childDocuments_.review: I've only played Night Manor so far. Just beat it tonight. I got to the "bad" ending on my own, but got stuck on the "good" ending because there's one door that *really* doesn't look like a door and I completely missed it. So I cheated and looked up a playthrough. Glad I did, though! Awesome game.I commented on this elsewhere, but I really love how they've back-ported modern game design into the retro form-factor. I grew up playing NES games. I know how difficult they could be and how painful the puzzles could be. By comparison Night Manor is extremely generous. I'm told you get a little bonus for never "dying", but there's no major consequence if you do die. You're just placed back at the start with all of your progress saved.There is one puzzle that I didn't get on my own and I somewhat resent the game design for it. There are a *ton* of objects you can inspect that have descriptions designed to tell you not to waste your time investigating them any further. But one of those objects actually has a critical clue hidden inside and you need to use a specific item on it to get that clue. Otherwise it's nice to see how far we've come in the field of game design.Some things I loved:* When the monster shows up your cursor shakes in fear and you need to fight it.* If you shoot the monster the cursor changes into a little crosshair.* There are a number of photos, dark corners, and mirrors where you will see a flash of a face or hand. Just a small touch but very cute.* The endings have a twist.* The dark theme and aesthetic. I don't feel like any 80s games had this quite so well figured out. It feels like a classic 80s horror movie turned into a NES game and given the polish that SMB3 got. Very Resident Evil inspired but running within the technical constraints of a NES-like system.If this game was available on the NES I am sure of 2 things:1. 80s parents would have assumed Night Manor was going to turn their children into satanic worshipers.2. We'd consider this one of the greatest NES games. Absolute credit to the creators here, but this is mostly down to how we stand on the shoulders of giants. Taking modern wisdom and using it within old constraints makes our progress really stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying this game immensely. I would rank it among the best indie games I've ever played. The value for money in this is enormous. Each of the 25 or so games I've played so far has been impressive. Many are based on popular formulas, such as the vertical-scrolling spaceship shooter (in the case of Star Waspir), but they combine the best ideas from classic games and add further refinements based on modern game design theory. There are also several games that exhibit notably original designs (e.g. Mortol, Party House, Mooncat), and these manage to be just as good, if not better, than those that feel more familiar.So the result is like a greatest hits compilation of 80s games, but distilled and refined to an extremely high standard, and featuring many entirely original games that feel like instant classics. Every element of each game is of high quality. In particular, I am astonished by how consistently excellent the music has been throughout.There is little to criticize and much more that I could praise. I anticipate I'll be playing this for at least another 50 hours. I'd like to congratulate Derek Yu and all involved in creating this masterpiece. It was clearly a labor of love, and I'm sure it will be loved by many for decades to come.Edit after 100 hours: I'd like to highlight Mini & Max, which is an incredible game, one of the best indie games I've ever played, and arguably worth the price of the entire package alone.

_childDocuments_.review: this isnt meant to be clown react bait but i sure feel like im going to get a bunch for saying all this.put simply, this is extremely not my thing, frankly. i only liked 8 out of the 50 games because the vast majority of them to me felt either too obtuse, too difficult, or just straight werent fun or engaging to play. if youre someone like me who doesnt exactly have the highest of attention spans for games especially when it comes to 8 bit retro games you're likely going to bounce just as hard as i have off this. the description says "we carefully chose what elements to modernize" but frankly i don't think they tried hard enough, the vast majority of these just feel like good ideas for games that are not fleshed out past the initial concept and were needlessly shoved into the limitation of "fake nes game" which ends up making them play like sh*t half the time because two buttons is nowhere near enough for what they're trying to do. if it werent so tied up in trying to be nes adjacent then this would probably be an enjoyable exploration of weird ideas for games. presentation wise its also kind of a huge ball of missed opportunity and disappointment. this came out well after last call bbs, zachtronics' final game which also went with a "this system definitely existed, heres some of the games for it look" vibe and the sheer level of comprehensiveness that title went through to make it look and feel like you were truly reviving old hardware and software was astounding. ufo 50 however doesn't really feel like it tries at all with this; in fact it feels like the whole set up of the fake system and company was completely an afterthought more than anything else that is so bafflingly slapped together that it feels as if they shouldn't have bothered.it feels...confused. it wishes to evoke being a flashcart for the aforementioned fake system vibes, but the way it approaches doing this - and in general how it starts up - gives it the vibe that this is more of an "atari 50" style approach where it is a modern piece of software compiling the historical gameography of ufo soft for future generations to experience. it doesnt seem to know if it wants to be one or the other, and as a result we have this bizarre situation where everything outside of the games also seems to somehow be within the fake system which doesnt really make much sense to me. and then you have the really clumsy menu system which feels like it wouldve been far better suited as a list with screenshots and game info being perpetually on screen off to the side so it can be more easily conveyed what the heck is going on in a game. the dusting off animation is only cute the first couple of times, when you have 50 of these games it becomes a weird brief element of tedium tbh.like visually this entire thing is bloody gorgeous but the entire encasing premise that surrounds these 50 games is disruptive to the entire concept in a way that actively bothers me just as much as i think that the way it advertises it self in the description is a little too generous and stretched from the truth. so yeah its just. tl;dr this is a bag of bizarre design choices, poor difficulty curving, false expectations and missed potential for me. you'll probably like it. but i really did not, in a lot of ways that really irk me. but hey, that's games, it aint all for everyone is it now. im curious to see what exactly theyll be changing in upcoming patches if at all and i might revisit this in future if it gets tightened up more and is less busy trying to mimic old nes games of yore slightly too hard.

_childDocuments_.review: In the current gaming landscape, the unabashedly retro UFO 50 feels like a breath of fresh air. Firing it up feels like the perfect antidote to what often feels wrong with modern game design. No need to spend hours getting through the opening cinematics and tutorial stages just to find out that it's the same thing you've already played a thousand time before. Just a few button presses and you're in. For anyone who grew up before the PlayStation era, the types of games that make up this collection should be instantly recognizable: adventure games, puzzle games, sports titles, and many more. When you launch a new one, the basic gameplay tends to be immediately obvious. Despite relying on only two buttons, many of these have a surprising amount of subtlety and depth; some even take hours to finish. UFO 50 isn't content just to rehash the tropes of those genres, but adds its own twist to whatever it does. The golf game isn't just a golf game, but also a sidescrolling sci-fi platformer. The adventure game isn't just a adventure game, but a procedurally generated open world exploration game. As such, what really makes UFO 50 stand out is not the way it is retro but the way it modernizes old tropes.Playing these games doesn't feel like they were made by someone taking their first steps towards understanding game design - rather they feel like a creative outlet for someone feeling burnt out from spending years on large game projects. These comparatively tiny games (some can be played from start to finish in as little as 15 minutes) seem to have no room in a gaming industry that favors blockbuster titles over small yet imaginative projects. In a strange way, I found that spending hours on UFO 50 didn't make me nostalgic for the glory days of NES, but I found myself missing the Flash game scene where a small game with an interesting idea could unexpectedly find itself in front of millions of players around the world. As such, I hope UFO 50 can find itself an audience large enough to inspire a cottage industry of similarly high-quality titles.

_childDocuments_.review: The mad lads at Mossmouth have done it: they've gamified the concept of playing videogames. _childDocuments_.review: Action 52 if every game was a banger.Each game has 3 main goals. A Gift (usually get halfway through a game), gold cartridge (beat the game) and cherry cartridge (100% a game, beat a high score, time trial etc).The real genius is you will boot up a game, think it's a stinker and think "okay I'll just get the gift and move on" but in doing so you will teach yourself the mechanics and actually appreciate the twist on a genre. Next thing you know you are playing 10 hours of Party House going for the cherry.It's so much more than 50 games in 1. Everything works together in ways it's hard to explain. If you love video games you owe it to yourself to buy this and rediscover why you fell in love in the first place.This should be Game of the Year.

_childDocuments_.review: The LX2 was a console in the 80's with a lineup of unusual games. The companies and programmers and designers all had complex lives and stories. In another reality. Not ours. That is the conceit of UFO 50 - you get to play the emulated games from a history that never happened, a decade not from our earth, but one parallel to it. Each game has a story, a history, none of which happened in our timeline. All the games are at least interesting, and some are quite good, even great - just as you would expect from several years of a console's life. This is a wonderbox of surprises and little joys, and if you can play along with the alternate universe notion, it is like stepping into a childhood you never had, from a world so close, yet not exactly, our own.I have greatly been enjoying, and savoring, this collection from another earth. If you are weird like me, you will too. This is worth your time, and your money.

Oddly to say, I am enjoying the experience of trying to beat some of these games unfair and outdated mechanics and I appreciate what we have now. And that is convenience.
