_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the first twenty games chronologically at the time of this review, so I haven't played them all yet, but I had to share my thoughts so far.This game has already grabbed a hold of me. This is a collection of high quality games ranging from arcade style titles that can be played repeatedly to try and get a high score, all the way up to stuff like this Zelda-like Golf RPG where you have to explore the world. There is so much variety here and lots of value for the money. So many of these arcade style games are going to be great for playing on my Steam Deck when I only have a few minutes and don't want to commit to something more substantial, and all of the longer titles exude tons of charm and have very interesting gimmicks and ideas thrown in. I have found thus far that this game really shines in the puzzle game department, EVERY SINGLE PUZZLE GAME I'VE PLAYED HAS BEEN SO COOL, especially Devilition.And one more thing I wanted to mention, this is how I personally recommend playing this game: - Play the games in chronological order (default sort) from the first game to the last game. For extra spice, pace yourself and try just a few new games at a time. (I'm doing five a day for ten days personally.)- Give each game a try, but if a game is not connecting with you don't feel like you have to stick with it and try to like it. (I'm looking at you Ninpek) You'll find they have multiple games that are the same genre and although you might not like the gimmicks or game play of one, another may be perfect for you.- Every so often, go back and give some of the games you've already tried another chance. Some of the games take a bit of time to learn because of their "classic" nature, but once you begin to understand them they really open up and become quite interesting. (I passed over Mooncat pretty quick because of how weird it was, but after giving it a second chance it's now one of my favorites.)It's also important to note if you do play them chronologically, they start out fairly primitive because they are canonically the earliest games this imaginary company released and they where still learning how to best utilize the hardware and make games approachable. Barbuta is the first game and it feels pretty clunky and hard, but don't let it discourage you. I really hope people don't download this collection, try this game first, and go well this game sucks.TLDR: There is so much to like about this awesome variety pack of old school games. Make sure to give the games a chance and you're bound to find some games you'll love!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write an in-depth review for those people on the fence about this game and not buying into the hype wholeheartedly. UFO 50 is absolutely a labor of love by it's developers, and as someone who grew up in the era these games are imitating they absolutely should appeal to me, but they do not. There is a classic trap that many "old school but new" games fall into when trying to emulate the era. That is the fallacy that old games had to have insane difficulty spikes and punishing game play.Take a look at some classic NES games for illustration of what I mean. Any Mario game will start off easier and slowly ramp up the challenge as you get deeper into the game, however the curve is balanced by not only doing that super late into the game but also by introducing new power ups and giving you alternate routes if you are clever enough to find them. Even games like Contra that are notorious for their difficulty do not punish you for not making pixel perfect jumps or exact to the second timing on your inputs. And even in the rare cases where games did expect that level of skill such as Ghost And Goblins, or Megaman, they kept the gameplay loop interesting enough that you wanted to keep trying.And sadly UFO 50 does none of that. Every single game in this series will give you one or two levels to get interested in them and then SLAM you with an insane difficulty spike. And there are also many games in this collection where the game play loop is just...bad, or boring, really really boring. Add to that the asinine control schemes of many of the titles, as well as the lack of easy to follow instructions... I just do not think this collection is the right choice for most people who are not absolutely desperate for new content from the 80s-90s era of gaming. Having said all of that there are a few games I enjoyed such as Ninpek, Mortol (both games), and Warptank. Warptank in fact easily stands up to even the best games of that era in my opinion. But at the end of the day having just a small few games that I enjoyed did not make the collection worth the price to me. I appreciate the dedication of the developers who participated in this, but at the end of the day they missed the mark on the vast majority of these games. I genuinely believe that nostalgia for their childhood is a huge factor in why so many people gave this collection positive reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a glorious homage to the games of yesteryear. It captures the feeling of finding your old console in an attic or storage unit, turning it on after years of neglect, and replaying your old childhood games. From the blowing of the cartridge to get the dust off to the look of the console and look of the cartridges as they dance on the menu select screen. It nails the feeling and invites imagination for the player to fill in the moments. From the get go the game lets you pick any of the 50 games. You will find a little of everything in the collection of games. Some even have multiplayer. The most insane part is that every game is actually quality and feels like the games you used to play. All of them are extremely polished. You will leave with at least 10 favorites. Each game more unique than the last. Each game an adventure into the unknown. Mini and max is my personal favorite. The lack of guides online for most games means we got to genuinely spread the message like the playground when we learned misingno exists. Please get this game and feel rejuvenated. Original ideas still exist and feeling them play out on retro games is the icing on the cake. Im excited to see how other developers gain inspiration from this game, to make their own version of UFO 50. I look forward to more games by Mossmouth! They got it baby!!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: You will like a majority of the games on offer here and there is so much content here you could be playing it for years and still not be done. I will say that some games are not really that good but with the amount of good quality games in the package it more than makes up for the duds. Best among them (from what I have played) would be: avianos, party house, attactics, and nintek
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A few games on here are very clever and original games you wouldn't expect to see on an NES that I genuinely appreciate. Over half of them are poorly-designed arcade games that have no continues for no other reason than because otherwise you'd beat it in 2 minutes.I think there's maybe 5 out of 50 games here I legitimately enjoy, so if you see this go on sale for $5 hey, that's a pretty good deal. $25 is a rip-off.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A must have for anyone who is or wants to get into gaming as a hobby. The games span almost every genre conceivable and are fun, unique titles on their own. 50 of 'em for this price is an absolute steal, you can easily get hundreds of hours of gameplay out of this collection. Plenty of couch co-op multiplayer games too. If you missed the boat on classic retro games, UFO 50 will give you an authentic experience of what gaming was like in the 80s-90s.Disclaimer: The game by default sorts titles by "chronological" which is the date they were "released" and mimics what games were like in that era. Don't be put off by the first few games like Barbuta or Bug Hunter, they really highlight the experimental nature of early 80s retro titles (Atari / NES) when the gaming industry was a baby, little more than a few software engineers in a basement. They are intentionally clunky, minimal in graphics and punishingly difficult as an artistic choice.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It may have taken way longer than expected, but UFO 50 was worth the wait.  Don't think of this as a minigame collection, because there is nothing "mini" about most of the titles.  They all are titles that could have been commercial releases in the 80s, or standalone indie titles today.  Whatever your genre preferences, you'll almost certainly find several games worth the price of the collection.  My own favorite, the western-themed JRPG "Grimstone", almost justifies the price on its own:  its roughly as content-rich as its inspiration, the first Final Fantasy.  And its not the only one, as the collection covers pretty much every genre you'd find during the 80s ( and several you wouldn't ).
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I tried all 50 games before posting, some longer than others.Most of the games are simple, most of them are smaller than others, but none of them feel incomplete. They're all a wide variety of genres and most of the games are completely unique from the others. Some of them are pretty straightforward, and a few of them feel borderline experimental. It's ... weird.My only complaint is most of them play very slow, even slower than an NES game would have played.I'd say for 25 bucks, you'll definitely find at least a handful you'll enjoy. I certainly enjoyed at least half of them. Works great on Steam Deck, which really feels like the best environment for a collection like this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically review a game that I haven't finished, But I'll make a exception here having finished about 20 of them and played the rest a good bit. You get what you see here. 80s arcade/NES style game design with modern controls and sensibilities.  I'd say 25 of these are great, 20 are pretty good and 5 are meh. Maybe a bit generous here but still, that is a impressive ratio. I have a pretty wide pallet in terms of games so I get a lot of value here, but even if you just like action games or shooters or you are looking for some couch co-op you are bound plenty here to justify snagging this collection. If you are looking for game design ideas or just to try out a bunch of stuff you haven't, this also maybe an idea grab.  Absolutely wonderful collection here and really, crazy how much they are asking.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: idk how it keeps happening but i think "oh i've found the best game on here" and then i boot up another one and discover its "oh ♥♥♥♥ that's a cool idea" moment. maybe not all of the games on here will click with you but there's something here for everyone, and everything made here is such a clever mixture of 80s design with modern sensibilities. absolutely cannot recommend enough
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feeling about Ufo 50. Yes you get 50 games, depending on your tastes you will find a handful of stand out games that you'll come back to again and again. Many (perhaps the majority) of games are derived from obvious classic 80's and 90's sources which reduces their appeal somewhat if you're old enough to remember the originals. Yes there are twists on the classics, but the core game-play for many of these games feels a little too familiar. Coupled with this and the deliberately awful control schemes in some of the games and I'm not sure UFO 50 is worth the sticker price. There's certainly original stand outs in here, so much so you'll wish they were separate games entirely, but of the 50 games, I can only see myself playing maybe 10 of them for more than an hour or two.The presentation of the games themselves is lovely. Jaunty music, delightful retro graphics, classic title screens, great idle cycles. Ufo 50's presentation is super polished here without question.I'm aware there's a meta-game and a lot of people are enjoying that aspect, but this seems of limited life once it's fully discovered by these bold early adopters (again, a nice riff on original cartridge style games). I understand Ufo 50 is designed so the more you put into the games, you more you'll get out. It's a bold experiment in that sense, but feels to me like it could have been Ufo 20 perhaps in terms of the games included.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is really an incredible game. I wasn't entirely sure what to expect, I assumed there'd be 50 bite-sized games and I think that would've been perfectly fine. However, it was anything but.The 50 games in UFO 50 are incredibly high quality, varied, full experiences in their own right. Everything from classic arcade style games, platformers, strategy games; the game is bursting with creativity and care. There are so many games in this that I'd buy on their own and be able to put hours and hours into.I'm not super fond of every game in the pack, but I think that's part of the beauty of it. In representing the entire history of a fictional game company's output, they also represent all the historical limitations, experimentation, and variety that comes with that.I think this game is an incredible achievement and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it but ill put some gripes i have with some of the games ive tried out of the collection in the hope maybe they could get tweakedThe Western themed RPG combat is mockingly slow, like the developers are taking a piss at anyone who enjoys turn based combat or something removing so many delays and slow enemy death animations would make it less "authentic" but definitely less of a drag to playA lot of the arcade games suffer from a modern day difficulty curve were the start is easy and picks up the pace over time, problem is most of the arcade games are pretty short (even for arcade game standards) and dying on the last stage just to get sent back to a piss easy baby level makes it feel like you are waiting for the game to actually let you playIt would be less of an issue if some of the arcade games also had their pacing smoothed out, in the drifting car game there are times were there are no enemies on the screen and most of the games have transitions between levels that cannot be skipped or sped up
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The more that I play of UFO50, the more convinced I am that this is my personal 2024 GOTY which is high praise considering Balatro also came out this year. I've only tried out 20 out of the 50 games so far and I'm having a blast. I've currently cherried (fully completed) 10 of the games and I'm slowly working my way through the other 10 and and I still have 30 games left! This game might not be for everyone, but if you enjoy old school games or pixel art, then you're likely to find at least 1 game in the collection worth your time. As an experiment, I'll try to keep this review updated with a max 3 sentence review of each individual game that I cherry below (potential spoilers):A fun little puzzle game focusing on strategically camouflaging to avoid predators, find collectibles, and return to the safety of your home. Not too difficult, but I had a pleasant hour with this oneLove child between snake and pac-man. Really addicting to shoot for high scoresI had a blast playing this one. The mechanic where you decide how difficult the next round will be by purposely increasing the number of enemies for a better monetary reward is a wonderful risk-reward system that exposed my greed many timesArena fighting game where each character has a unique movement mechanic and weapon. This one caused a bit of frustration as I felt like sometimes the CPU was essentially cheating, but I had enough fun where I've come back to play a round even after getting the cherryPoint and click horror game that is unique in the collection. I thought the puzzles were very solid and the killer/story was interesting to me. The music also really adds to the atmosphereThis is essentially the Upwell to Downwell's existence. It be ben quite chaotic as you panic jump and shoot your way up and out of the pit. Heavy "one more run" energyArcade autoscroller ninja game. When playing through the collection in chronological order originally, this was the first game that made me think there was more to UFO50 than what I thought. That being said some of the later games in the pack definintely sent Ninpek down my tier listSubmarine metroidvania. This one was tough to get into at first. The early game is absolutely brutal, but as you get upgrades to your sub this quickly climbed to be one of my favourite games in the pack so farI think this one could've used some expanding. Its essentially just a virtual horserace gambling simulator and while the quibbles are cute, I wish there was a bit more to the gameDeckbuilder roguelike focused on throwing the best party by filling out your rolodex with party guests that give you popularity and money. This is probably the most complete game in the pack and it is consistently touted as an amazing game. There is room here for this to be a standalone game as it, the random scenarios are very addictingThis is a unique spin on pong where you play as a samurai with unique hits and movement abilities that was quite fun to play. The characters have different playstyles and I enjoyed learning the best way to play each different samuraiIts a fun mario kart-lite that makes very in-universe sense. It was a nice palate cleanser, however the lack of different maps and no CC settings for varying levels of difficulty makes this one of the least fleshed out games in the packI enjoyed Kick Club, its a level by level affair where you need to use a soccer ball to destroy enemies that are personifications of non-soccer sports. I think they're a bit too stingy with the lives and the lack of a save and continue function made cherrying this game slightly frustratingMooncat is amazing. The less you know about it the better, but the music is phenomenal and the gameplay is intuitive once you get used to itA somewhat bullet hell game about escaping an evil magician's hat. I enjoyed the upgrade system and the game was fair when it came to gathering extra lives. I do feel like some of the earlier bosses and minibosses are easier than the final bosses which was a bit disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is unapologetically my favorite game I've played this year. The amount of varied gameplay, the unexpected depth from each of the 50 games, and more than anything else the awesome feeling of nostalgia that takes you back to a gaming era where half the fun is figuring out what the hell you're even supposed to be doing in a game is great. I highly recommend giving UFO 50 a try, ESPECIALLY if you fondly remember the 8-bit era.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true gaming feat. I truly cannot express how incredible of an achievement Derek and the rest of the team pulled off here!! I have 46 hours and I've only beaten 3 of the games. The depth of the experience here is insane. Not only are there 50 full games... but there is a meta narrative weaved into the mix with the fictional 'UFOSOFT' company. And you may think "oh that's cute"... but the meta narrative plays out like an in-game ARG! Using the in game terminal you can follow scavenger hunt style riddles that will truly test your knowledge of the collection, to unlock even more content!10/10 Absolutely the game of the year. You owe it to yourself to at least try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is an experience that can only be seen through experiencing the details, the challenge, and the amazing package for yourself. Get this immediately if you're a fan of one of these parallel experiences:- Playing around through a list of top 50 "sleeper hits" ROMs you found on - If you remember the /ole/ glory days of finding crazy hard indie games from communities on the web circa 2005-2015 [think TiGsource]. - Browsing period-accurate attempts to demake/remake pixel art- Enveloping yourself in one legacy company's art, lore, history [totally did this with Falcom & Ys games recently].There really is nothing like this and the team is nothing short of legendary. 8 hrs in and I have barely scraped the top of the ocean here. Some of these games are not my genre, but it's more than made up for in the *extremely* my-genre ones.  Give a large amount of games a chance before thinking about a refund, you're going to get hooked!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten 15 games in 15 hours, getting at least gold. And I think I spent over 3 of those hours on Barbuta because that was difficult to figure out. I don't think the difficulty is too high for most of these games as some people say. The games have a clear challenge that you need to complete and it is very satisfying to complete them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously a work of a passionate dev team, Derek Yu delivers again.The variety is huge and the dedication to thoughtful design is clear. Each game has been fully treated, this wasn't driven by profit and deadlines, obviously made to a high level of quality to fulfill the team's vision. I loved the concept and am a huge fan of Yu going in,  but what a fabulous and special collection this is. I know I will be playing this for years as I work on completing the cherry pie! I have still only been into around 20 games at the 11 hour mark, and have just started dabbling in coop/multiplayer with friends, and I can't wait for more.Inspiring work of concept and design, read Derek's book if you enjoy his games or design in general. I love his philosophy on difficulty, mystery and exploration. Truly refreshing. The art and music are just so stellar as well, no half baked releases here. Congrats to the whole team for a job well done. It's a 10/10 from me, buy and play this. for 25 bucks there is something for nearly everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth it. Any of these games could 100% have been a disk or cartridge from their era (and an alternate universe).  Their influences are clear though they also stand completely on their own, and the ways they've reinterpreted old game design concepts (and more modern ones, like deckbuilders, tower defense and idle games) are unique and interesting.  Any one of these would have set you back the full price of a cartridge back in the day, and it really is a steal to get the whole collection for this much.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: My first console was an NES - I grew up in the 90's, but my parents had one. It was my first real experience with video games, and oh man does this game bring me right back. The music, the graphical style, and of course the games themselves are incredible. You pay $0.50 per game in this pack (...technically less), it's an absolute steal.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you miss the experience of going to Miniclip or Orisinal and bouncing from game to game, this satisfies the itch. I know that's not the reference point here, but this has a combined voice that goes beyond the usual ROM pick-and-mix.There's authentic retro grit, there's smoother, idealized stuff, experiments, killer multiplayer games out the wazoo... Half the games aren't to my taste, but I've already played enough to justify the purpose and have barely scratched the surface.Wanna emphasize that the multiplayer games rock. If you've got local friends or someone close enough for smooth Remote Play, this is a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed. Such an awesome retro feel when it comes to the art and music. It's really cool reading all the different responses from people when asked what their favorite games are in the collection - the range of answers says something about the variety of quality games here. Currently my top played are Bug Hunter, Party House, and Devilition :)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There's a wide range of genres and they're all done pretty nicely. Some of the games are a bit rough, but if you talk to friends or look at guides there's usually enough in there to help you get through whatever it is.The music (where it exists) is catchy and liable to become an earworm. This game's had years to bake and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game has huge variety. There's something for everyone. Newer gaming concepts such as tower defenses, roguelikes, deckbuilders, but reimagined with an incredibly faithful vintage NES style. There are some shorter arcade-style games that can be played in a few minutes, as well as some fully fleshed out full-length games including a full length JRPG and a metroid type game. Even at full price this game is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is very charming when it comes to its graphics, presentation, and music but completely falls flat in terms of gameplay in more than half of the works in here. The trailers only show you less than half of the games, and mainly the stuff in the later half. Don’t fall for them. If this was 15 dollars, I’d be able to shrug it off, but even at 10 dollars more makes it hard to justify this to people.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Requested a refund. Like most of the other negative reviews here, I feel genuinely duped by the wide, seemingly unanimous praise this game appears to be getting. As someone who grew up playing the sorts of games to which this collection pays tribute, I fully expected to love it. Instead I found most of the games I tried boring and overly fixated on the worst aspects of 80s gaming--akin to renting a bunch of garbage 3rd party NES titles that you'd never heard of at Blockbuster in the early 90s. At the same time, I appreciate the creativity and passion that clearly went into making this. But people need to be warned that some of these positive reviews are *highly* misleading; this is the niche-iest of niche games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely think this is an incredible watershed achievement in the Indie gaming space, and something I hope gets the recognition it deserves. This collection of games does it all, from strange and esoteric platformer to cute mario-kart style racing game, multiple types of strategy games, and even a horror-themed point and click adventure. At times I genuinely had to remind myself that no, these actually aren't undiscovered gems, but modern games made by today's designers.This is a game collection about games, about the joy of discovering something new, about seeing these fictional designers grow and change and produce interesting software over time. Little hints of story and reoccurring themes, like how Big Bell Race is obviously a (still very fun) cheap asset flip of Campanella, and how even the words "Campanella" and "Barbuta" used as game titles hint at one of the fictional developers having Italian ancestry. This game collection is wonderful, plain and simple. Please, if you can, let yourself step into another world for a moment, and take the time to try genres and styles of game you wouldn't have played otherwise. What the team here has done is truly make a space where it feels like you can "Play Forever", where the developers have been able to create fifty odd, fun, interesting little experimental retro games while relatively unshackled to the expectations and opinions of what is expected of a modern indie title. UFO 50 is something truly valuable and special, easily worth the asking price and very much worth the wait. As i continue to play, I only become more and more impressed with what they were able to accomplish.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50, unfortunately, feels as shallow as you can imagine a retro-inspired 50-in-1 game pack made in 2024 would. I think the idea is novel, and I greatly admire the amount of love and effort put into it by both the developers and the artists. I just get a sense of "we used pixel art solely because we wanted it to feel retro and nostalgic" vibe from this.The games themselves fall fairly flat—there's not much substance here. Everything it tries to emulate, it does so pretty poorly, and the original ideas weren't interesting enough for me to want to keep playing. Games tended to either not be that fun or deep, or suffered from an insanely steep difficulty spike—which, I assume, was in an effort to emulate the brutal difficulty of NES games, but it fails at even that. As a lover of retro games, it feels to me like UFO 50 wants so badly to recapture that "tough-as-nails" feeling those old games evoked, but tried to do that in most cases by making level 1 super easy, level 2 a tiny bit tougher, and level 3 impossibly difficult. In these cases, the games were sadly not engrossing enough for me to want to try and overcome that jump in difficulty, as attainable a goal as I think it may have been; I'd simply cut my losses and moved on to something else in the pack, knowing that there were 49 other options (one of which  to be better), until I saw it as a futile effort and gave up.It feels like the problem of having a thousand TV channels and nothing to watch. Sure, there may be a diamond or two in here, but even if I had found a game I enjoyed, the package by and large still wouldn't be worth the price tag to me. I don't think there's anything here to latch onto, as much as I would have liked there to be.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass in game design. If you can push past the prickly beginning, you will find a treasure trove of incredibly well polished and cleverly designed full games spanning a huge variety of genres. Every single game in the collection is interesting to explore, and most are basically digital crack. Perhaps one of the best bang-for-your-buck games ever.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this conjured memories of a bootleg 100 games in one cartridge I used to have that was mostly full of bloatware & copy pasted games for the sake of making the number bigger. In reality, it feels like I found a dusty old box in an attic which contained a console I'd never seen before and 50 banger games. I expected to play each one for a few minutes and move on but you can spent literal hours on a single game.I've played 16 games so far, beaten 6 and cherry'd 4. My only criticism for now is the order they are presented to you by default can put some players off. I'd recommend picking randomly from the list or choosing a genre you know you'll enjoy. Also worth noting that certain games  really benefit from being played earlier than others .Overall, the amount of content packed into this more than justifies the cost of admission (especially if it happens to be on sale). Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: «God, I love video games so much».That's how UFO 50 makes me feel. It doesn't just let me enjoy the games it has on offer, it reinforces my love for gaming as a whole. Each one of the 50 games in the compilation is another complete mechanical system for me to solve and enjoy. None of the games are throwaways: each is creatively distinct, and each will be enjoyed by the right kind of video game enthusiast. The sheer variety of the games acts as a reminder of why I became enthralled by the world of video games in the first place. The completionist in me was having a great time too: UFO 50 gives you a trophy for every game you've beaten, and has a completionism challenge for every game on top of that, rewarding you with a cherry if you meet it. Also, half of the games have local multiplayer, and as I played through them, I often found myself thinking «this must be really fun to play with a friend!».The honeymoon period does eventually pass, but, as you can see from my play hours, it kept me going for quite a while. Eventually, it becomes apparent that some of the games are better than others. I definitely enjoyed the more arcade-like games like Magic Garden or Seaside Drive over the rpgs and metroidvanias. And some of the requirements for a cherry are much too tedious in comparison to others, which eventually put out the flames of completionism in me. But I had a great time while it lasted.Final score:Trophies: 40Cherries: 31
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Still have about 15 games left to try, but I've already added more than a dozen to my favourites. I love the idea of going through a pretend company's entire back catalogue, and UFO 50 executes that idea incredibly well. (About the only thing I'd want added in a sequel would be a timeline with fake documentary footage and design documents similar to Atari 50, etc)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game needs my help to convince anyone to play it, so let me just give a tip to anyone starting UFO 50: Boot up the 44th game Pilot Quest first, as it has idle game mechanics in it, so the automated processes you set up will continue to make resources while UFO 50 is open. I would recommend you start it up first so that you bank resources while you play the other games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A really interesting collection of 50 games for a console that never was. It reminds me of picking up old video game compilations as a kid, specifically the "Sonic's Ultimate Genesis Collections". I picked it up not knowing what the hell a Sonic or Genesis was but loved the seeming endless selection it offered. Good times...My only complaint really is that there’s only 6 buttons, the directional pad and an and b buttons. There is a pause button but it’s only for options and leaving/reseting the game your playing. When quite a few games would have benefited from a select button for like either a map or in game options. Just my thoughts, but overall still an outstanding package.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely legendary game. Playing through all 50 games has been so fun and also fascinating. It really gives you a good idea of the type of games you enjoy. There's a lot of instances where I got really into a type of game that I never tried before, or something I thought I wouldn't enjoy. I've seen that some of the complaints talk about difficulty, or say that they don't like the games etc, and thats fine. If you feel like you might not like them, check out someone play them on youtube first. There's a ton of really cool concepts in here and I guarantee some will stick. A few games really impressed me:Mooncat: Platformer game where the challenge is the two button controls. Feels like you are a baby learning to play videogames again, cool experience.Mini & Max: At first this game didn't seem super interesting to me, but there's a certain point you reach where you realise "woah! I can do that???". The game has sooooo much depth to it it could be an entire game on its own.Night Manor: I beat this (and 100%'d) all in one sitting because I loved it so much. It's a horror point & click game with a cool mystery and good puzzles. I also like how there are some good hints built into the dialogue to prevent it from feeling too arbitrary or to jog your memory. If you start playing the games in chronological order, the first game is Barbuta, which references how barebones and brutal early NES games were. Don't let this turn you away from the game! The others are much nicer, I promise. This game is honestly a necessary inclusion since it fits within the games lore and is a good nod to the games of the time.Get this game! It's great!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: unbelievable value for an unbelievable collection of extremely high effort, in depth games. this isn't some action 52 collection of churned out slop. each and every game is thought out, fully developed and carefully crafted with unique gameplay mechanics and assets, all of which are wrapped up and beautifully presented as a historical archive of a fictional console with bits of additional lore.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: "This game is a monumental achievement"It's been said over and over and over again by people on Youtube, Reddit, and Steam. I am happy to report that yes, yes it is. It has reminded me why I fell in love with gaming in the first place. For the price of a 12 pack, you will be getting the best gaming experience released in at least a decade.My personal favorite after 20 hours is Bug Hunter. Best strategy game since Into the Breach! I posted a getting started guide on the UFO 50 subreddit under the same username if you want some help getting started.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits the mark perfectly.It makes you a child again, roaming through a library of good games, not knowing exactly what they are or how to play them. You just go at it and discover.Not all the games in it may be of your taste but they are all well made, with a charming retro aesthetic and often with a surprising mechanical depth.Plus they are great for both quick and long game sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY.So much mystery and joy packed into one reasonably priced game. If you love discovering new games this is right up your alley. Each game I've picked up so far seems simple but has a hidden depth and is more complex then first appears.My friends and I all went WILD over Party House and were hooting and hollering when we first one. Good times.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A really fantastic collection of games that are deceptively rich and fun to play. I've only had time with the first handful of cartridges and already I'm hooked. It's a staggering amount of game for the price. Evokes strong nostalgia of a different era of video games altogether. Runs excellently on deck. Don't sleep on it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings to mind several eerie adventures from the 1980s, like the original  or the eerie . Both had a similar sense of mystery that's hard to describe, and a strong feeling of isolation in a hostile world. In this kind of games, you have to create your own maps, devise your own strategies, and no one was there to guide you through the challenges.I’ve spent a few hours playing, and I believe the absence of modern quality-of-life features doesn’t hinder the experience. Instead, the loneliness it evokes matches the sense of reward you get when uncovering the game’s secrets. I feel like I’ve just started to scratch the surface, and that feeling of discovery is both satisfying and exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Robust collection of classic style games with interesting twists. I wouldn't call all of them full games but even the short short titles provide reason to go back and replay in challenging ways to gain a Cherry. The collection has made me appreciate games I never had time for in the past. Hoping for a UFO 3D one day.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The feel of this game is like finding an old retro video game console and discovering its library.  A lot of these games combine some interesting ideas that could be their own indie title.  It's a fictional game company's games, and seeing how they evolve and develop is fascinating in a vague narrative/story.  Not all the games are bangers, but there's bound to be a couple you'll like.They're all short form games, think of it like a collection of 50 in depth mini games.  Some good 2P games in the mix as well.  UFO 50 really captures the nostalgic NES/Master System era of gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: i don't even know where to start. i have never owned a retro console, nor did i think i would enjoy a collection of retro inspired games, but man do i enjoy these. I have never been a completionist, but those cherry cartridges are calling to me. i have played plenty of AAA and indie games that don't come close to a fraction of the amount of charm this game has, and never before have i felt like i have received a love letter from a developer like this. its incredible, i love it, and i cant wait to keep coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I had honestly planned on not leaving a review until I had -at least- tried all the games once but I'm halfway through them and it's necessary. Not every game is going to click for everyone but for me each one has had a clear and concise direction and had something to love about it. Some favorites include Avianos, Mortol, and Devilition. Not only that, but the metanarrative is interesting and well planned, creating a full package that is as fun as it is interesting. I can't help but love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Probably too soon to give it a proper review, but I wanted to say I like everything about this game "collection".  It's like it's 1989 and I'm at the video store deciding which game to rent for the weekend and only being able to look at the box.  Instructions? Already missing from the last person who rented it.  Internet walkthrough? Doesn't exist.  Every game I messed around with was a lot higher quality than I expected.  I can't wait to give each game a deep dive and take my time figuring out how they each play.  I can see how anyone who didn't grow up in this era wouldn't appreciate it though.  But for us..older people...it's a no-brainer.  Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid my uncle gave me his NES and a collection of games. I spent weeks digging through and trying each game - most were bad but one of them was Mega Man 2. This is like that except most of them are Mega Man 2 and there's even a few Mega Man 3's. Big recommend, love yourself and buy this game

_childDocuments_.review: Not every game in the pack is a winner, but the fact that so many of them are is kind of staggering to me. _childDocuments_.review: My cousins got a LX system in Chinatown one summer around 1990. Not sure which edition. The only game they had was Quibble Race. After a couple of weeks, we figured out the betting mechanics. After a month, we were betting real money. Problem was, we were kids. We had no income and spent our winnings on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Anyway, long story short, my auntie caught one of my cousins stealing the tip off a table at a diner. When he explained why, he was grounded forever and I was banned from their house. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Pure fun arcade games. deceptively simple, lots to discover.  all the platformers i played had their own unique mechanics; the high score games are addicting, fast paced, and difficult; versus games like bushido ball and hyper contender have a lot of different characters to choose from with many different attacks and playstyles . Two of the games have a level editor because why not.  there's even a deckbuilding game full of cool interactions. i know i'll spend a lot of time beating every game.  with great visuals and music, this really is the complete package. UF0 50 is an overwhelming experience and something seriously worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve only beaten 5 out of the 50 games so far and I’ve already got my money’s worth. Derek Yu has yet again made an all-time classic, and some of the games here will floor you with their concept or a surprising twist on genre tropes. I strongly recommend going into this game as blind as possible as I was sadly spoiled on some of the games here, playing it in chronological order (except for Pilot Quest). The satisfaction of UFO 50 is learning how the hell some of these games work, and discovering all the hidden tricks through experimentation, like the fact that you can step on enemies in Bug Hunter or that you use detonate yourself while using the arrow move in Mortol. I do wish they designed some of the games around either having pause button or extra face buttons since the NES controller had slightly more going on than what’s available here.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Easily GOTY material for me this year: there's an insane amount of 'game' to unpack here and to call it anything short of legendary is doing it injustice. Plenty has already been said about UFO 50 on reviews, so I won't rehash that. Strong recommendation from me.In short: 50 high-quality games made with 80s 8-bit design sensibilities, but with lots of modern quality of life improvements and new genres that didn't exist back then. UFO 50 feels and plays like what we remember the NES/SMS/PC-Engine games to be like; it is the very definition of nostalgia, and in the most positive sense possible. Get it if you enjoy 8-bit games, aren't afraid of challenge, and are craving something that is simultaneously familiar and experimental. Heck, if you're on the fence, just get it and give it a try - the worst that could happen is you refund it. Just remember to try different games if the one you choose isn't doing it for you.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Quite genuinely some of the most memorable and crystalline fun I've had with any game in years, and it's that x50 games.How the devs have managed to pack in this many actually novel, unique game ideas while still maintaining a true-to-the-era vibe is crazy. Every next cart is the best thing so far. From quirky, addictive, arcade high-score hunters, to fascinating feature-complete titles I'd genuinely have paid for standalone copies of.The level of just sheer game design on display - on both a creative and technical level - is astonishing. Buy it. And then hound the devs to go hunting through more storage lockers to "find" the next console.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Vibrant beutiful game bursting with texture and flavor and a taste of home to anyone who grew up with 3rd and 4th gen gaming. As of writing this I've only given each game anywhere from 15 minutes to 2 hours but it really feels theres something for everyone in this collection and starting each new title feels like a new adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of enjoyment out of this . A good "one last try" thing and a decent variety of old style games, some with modern twists. Bit of a surprise to find an idle game and a deck builder in here. - A full on old fashioned JRPG too. - The quality and gameplay of the arcadey games is spot on. D-Pad throwbacks.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stress enough that these are fifty actual, full games.  They cover a wide variety of genres, from sports games to dungeon-crawlers, to a Civilization-esque strategy game, though the most common types are arcade-style action games and puzzlers of various complexity.  Most of the games are interesting enough to sink an hour or two into, and some of them are genuinely amazing.  I'm something like 75 hours into it, and there's a few I haven't even tried yet.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this. This whole collection is remarkable and might get you into genres of games you never thought you'd like until given such a fine treatment. Most of the games are hard and punishing, but the sheer quality and fun will keep you coming back for more.Aesthetically there's an incredible dedication to the collection's "hardware limitations", with UFO having its own selected palette, SFX, and tracker music to really sell the authenticity of its classic design. It's been worked on for several years by the team, and it shows.Support these devs and buy this game if you love a good challenge and a fun variety of genre-breaking creative entries. My personal favorite is Rakshasa: A very difficult platformer that plays off of Ghouls n' Ghosts with the gimmick of you being able to cheat death as many times as you can get away with.This collection's gotten me out of a lousy depressive slump and I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At this time of writing I have 30 gold/15 cherry/34 gifts, and I can say this is my personal goty. The sheer volume of pixel art, and original music (300 something tracks) is completely insane. The way it gamify's playing a video game is just exceptional. The garden is amazing. It made me play games I'm pretty adverse for and made me enjoy them. There's actual challenge. At the end of the day the value per dollar on this package is a no brainer. Ufo 50 is a technical achievement, and a pretty amazing project in general. Just watch out for wild buddies. They are coming.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Only played for a few hours, but there is so much to enjoy here. Every game I've tried so far has been really interesting and compelling. On the surface you might think that these are only Mario Party-esque mini-games, but the 10 or so that I've played seem to be full experiences. As someone that grew up in the era these games reference, I can tell you that the nostalgia is aesthetic only; these games feel very contemporary and modern, they are clearly standing on the shoulders of so many recent greats. Absolutely worth the admission.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to believe what the developers have achieved here. The scale of the ambition on display here is staggering; these aren't 50 mini games, these are all fully realised games with depth and charm.If these games were real and came out in the 80s then UFOsoft would be as beloved as Nintendo - these games are THAT good.Several of these games are genuinely GOTY 2024 contenders on their own. The fact that they all come together in one package is still mind-blowing even 35 hours in.I can see myself as coming back to these games for decades to come.Astonishing.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's like buying one of those "50 in one plug in consoles" at a flea market, but good.Are they all winners? No, but a lot of them are, and even the ones that I didn't enjoy add to the mystique of this fictional company's history. The amount of attention that went in to the chronology of these games and the design techniques and callbacks developed through the 50 games is legitimately insane.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's a 10/10 masterpiece, so long as you go in with the right expectations and have a love for these sort of games. An incredible collection spanning many genres and themes. I havent even played them all yet but my favorites so far are Mortol, Kick Club, Bushido Ball, Porgy, Night Manor, and Pilot Club.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal achievement. Worth more than every penny, like seriously this should cost more, why doesn't this cost more??? It does everything right and right from the beginning it sucks you into its world with so much world building just from its first game. Each game feels unique, even the sequels, and yes, this collection has sequels. Each one of these games are fully realised and as you progress through the years each one feels more and more fleshed out, as if a real company were developing their skills. And none of this is even mentioning the hidden ARG within the game that requires you to code hunt through each game and follow a trail of clues to learn more about this mysterious company. So much heart and passion went into this game it's hard to actually believe that it exists.Honestly game of the year 2024, I don't see how anything can beat this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you like UFO 50 or not is going to depend how much you enjoy retro games. If you enjoy NES, 80s arcade, or even new grounds flash games then I think you will enjoy this. Like most games from the 80s that were the inspiration for this collection, many of these games take quite a bit of trail and error to figure out. Sadly I think many players will not have the patience for most of this collection.  I find it impressive just how many fun games are here. UFO 50 is quality and quantity. The games aren't just cheap copies of classic games either. Many of them have extremely unique ideas. For example, one game I played was a mix between medieval strategy and air hockey. If you love retro games and are looking for something different, then this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave Steam reviews, but its equally as rare that I'm blown away by a game like I have been with UFO 50. Considering the price of $25 USD, the package has an insane value, with 50 games at about 50 cents per (as a reminder) fully-fledged game. Even if you don't LOVE every single one, you're bound to find a least a couple that sink their teeth into you, sometimes taking an 1-5 hours to experience everything in. There really is something for everyone here, if you're okay with the charming 8-bit aesthetic, and don't mind not jiving with 100% of the content in a given game, I think UFO 50 is well worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game, it's criminal that this game doesn't have a wider appeal than it does. Brilliant ideas executed tremendously well, a clear labour of love that has absolutely been worth the wait, at the 17 hours played at the time of writing the review, I have only played 35/50 games, and there's no way I'm not revisiting every single one I have sampled so far. Buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Really torn on this. Because there are a few great games here. But some are just complete trash. Others desperately need an instruction manual and are only difficult because they don't explain the gameplay properly to you. The worst ones are the ones that are really deep, like Lords of Diskonia, start great, and then in the last level they're just like "eff you, this game is nigh-impossible now." It's really deflating to pump hours into a game and then hit a wall you don't even wanna figure out how to climb because life is too short and the game just isn't fun anymore.I guess I recommend it? But read about the games before you play them, and don't be afraid to bounce if one gets annoying.And whoever designed that last level in Lords of Diskonia, I hope you stub your big toe everyday for the rest of your life.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is, if nothing else, a fantastic showcase of everything retro gaming has to offer, but beneath the hood it is also so much more than that.I won't spoil much, but there really is something here for everyone:- Fantastic strategy and critical thinking games- Fast paced action shooters and arcade score chasers- At least one replayable roguelike experience- Fun genre mashes that will keep providing you with unique experiences- Actually interesting lore, when you look at the history of this fictional company, and a big meta secret if you are into that sort of stuffYou can play this game as little or as long as you like, I find it unlikely you will get bored if this is your sort of thing. Congrats everyone at mossmouth for another banger.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Just an incredible achievement of game design, and it's cheap as hell for the amount of content. I think there's definitely something here for everybody, but especially if you're into retro games, enjoy a large variety of styles and genres, and like to figure things out yourself without too much handholding, then you'll likely have an excellent time exploring the library of games. I've only played about third of the games so far, with one gold cart for beating a game (Mooncat) and one cherry cart for 100% (Camouflage), so I know this is going to keep me entertained for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Really loving this game! I've been aware of and looking forward to this one for years and years. The quality of these games is honestly way higher than I really anticipated. So many unusual takes on classic formulas that end up working really well...What if a platformer only had 2 buttons (including movement!)? What if in Zelda you had a count down timer to explore the world and damage taken decreased that? What if a deck builder but you have to throw the most awesome party to attract aliens or unicorns to win? What if you battled someone for points in an arena and every playable character had wildly different jumping mechanisms? What if you only got to move 20 times in Zelda but... golf? What if pong but with ninjas and powerups? What if a JRPG but with cowboys, angels, and demons?There are lots of really fun local vs and co-op games in this collection as well.Not everything in this collection will be for you though you will immediately attach to some of these games and you can grow to enjoy nearly all of them. Don't want to take the time to master a certain game? Jump around! Lots to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I waited to write this review until after trying all 50 games contained in the title. wants you to have that experience of finding and playing one of those unlicensed multicarts for a bygone console, and it succeeds in doing so. The thing about those carts is that they're garbagey and released into the market to make a quick buck. From rip-offs of other, more fun games to total WTF finds, the only life those carts might have years later is in the novelty that such a thing exists.  totally has this going on yet I don't think this was the developers' intentions.There's possibly the gamble that, with 50 games on tap spanning multiple genres, everyone is going to find at least one that they will enjoy. I didn't have fun with any of them. Even with the ones that should have hooked me, I found boredom settling in quickly and no real interest in swinging back around to revisit them later.The game knock presentation out of the park, but it's as if too much focus was placed on the audiovisual experience and the "lore" instead of polishing the games to be approachable and a good time. There's a thread of continuity across the games that I thought was clever but, again, it's all filler.Too challenging for casual gamers. Too slow for challenge hounds. To be fair, and unlike unlicensed multicarts, none of the games here are unfinished or felt like they had been slapped together in haste.If I had to choose one of its games to highlight, it'd probably be  but you have to be really, really into tabletop dexterity games and pray regularly to RNGesus. Some people call out  (which is charming but tedious) or  (too difficult for what it intends to be) as hidden gems and I can understand how they've come to those choices. If only they were fun to play!Is it just me or does anyone else hear sampling from  in ?
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: You're walking down a corridor. The corridor has 50 doors. You assume to various tiny rooms. You open one of the doors. Inside, you discover an entire world the size of Narnia. You shut the door, intimidated.And then you remember there are 49 other doors.UFO 50 is a wildly joyous and original title that consists of a breathtakingly massive collection of games that never existed, by a company that never was, each of which winks at you and invites you in to discover its secrets.It perfectly captures the way we rosily (one might say self-deludingly) remember the games of yesteryear having made us feel. That sense of mystery, the joy of discovery, the basic core mechanic that changes the entire game and you don't realize it until you've played it for 300 hours because lol WHAT manual? You borrowed this game from your cousin and then he moved to Ohio, and the internet doesn't exist yet.The emotional arc of playing this game goes "Haha, this looks cute->Ooh, this one is fun->Wait, this game has a surprising amount of depth->Wait are they ALL this deep?"And then a chasm opens up underneath you.It's pure joy with just the right amount of artistically authentic friction.I hope this game sells a million billion zillion copies and knocks the entire industry on its ass.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this writing, I've seen 4 of the 50 games to their roll credits, and I've "Platinum Trophy'd" (This collection calls it "Cherry'd") 2 of those 4. There are many titles in this collection I want to complete yet, but even after just these 4, I've felt I've already gotten my money's worth.And yet I feel there's so much more to come.If you want quality retrogames with true pixel graphics, this is it. 50 of them.I never thought before that it was possible for a game to be TOO good. There's so much here.The game boots up to the message "Play Forever" and gosh I think you very well could.Not everyone is going to love all 50 of the titles, but everyone is going to find their money's worth in here.It's hard to wrap your head around this actually being 50 full GOOD games, but it's true.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

Still, the concept reeled me in and I’ve been telling every one about it since. There’s a surprising depth and cleverness to these titles, and you have to find it for yourself. If you have ever enjoyed retro video games of ANY genre, you should own this collection. UFO 50 will both take you back and move you forward.It will also break you, because Mossmouth doesn't go easy.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't recommend this enough, putting together a list of my top ten games on this collection would be impossible.However I can put together an easy top ten least favourite. It's easy:10: Golfaria9: Golfaria8: Golfariaetc...Whoever was responsible for that game should be sacked.Otherwise, super solid collection!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is more than the sum of its parts. And the 50 parts all seem to be very good (guessing, as I"ve only seen half at this point). They don't simply throw you into a boring UI for you to pick a game. They sell you on an alternative universe with a unique console, game design history, IP and everything. Once you realize that these games are actually GOOD, it makes it much easier to jump into the next trusting that there will be something of interest there.I don't think UFO 50 is for everybody, but as somebody who loves going into games blind and appreciates good game design, it's been a phenomenal experience so far. It's not all perfect for me personally. I think the controls for a couple games have been frustrating with the 2 button control scheme. Some games I think are too punishing initially, which makes it harder to actually get in and appreciate whats going on. But honestly I think this game is a sleeper hit. I hope more people notice it.

You should treat them well, DEREK.Barbuta- The primordial ooze that gaming was born in.Bug Hunter- Not really for me! I'd be willing to give 2p a shot.Devilition- May have been the most difficult game in the pack for me. I bled for this one.Kick Club- Do you kids remember BUBBLE BOBBLE?! Sure you do! Hits my nostalgia just right.Avianos- I *did* try the two player on this. I'll always remember the wizard army.Mooncat- You snuck a modern indie game into this pack you weasels.Bushido Ball- I love Lethal League and this is sorta that? CPU is a bastard.Block Koala- Fifty levels and one music track is cruel DEREK.Camouflage- How about some more levels for this one instead, huh?Campanella- The length of this one with no checkpoints is pretty messed up! But still fun.Golfaria- I wasn't expecting to like this one but it turned out alright!The Big Bell Race- Weakest game in the pack, I think we'll agree.Warptank- This one is a blast. Just a great little experience.Waldorf's Journey- YES. FLY FREE YOU SPECIAL BOY.Porgy- Starting you out with five seconds worth of fuel is a bold choice!Onion Delivery- The first of a few games I would classify as spite clears.Caramel Caramel- Why must you add game mechanics that make me take my eyes off the ship??Party House- The key to getting me playing deckbuilders is to hide the fact that it's a deckbuilder.Hot Foot- Really *needs* a 2p to be much fun.Divers- I don't know if the game mechanics were that special but the mood is unparalleled. Rail Heist- Without the mandatory time limit I would have liked this better!Vainger- That map is not very helpful! You guys it's not VVVVVV it's Alien Soldier. Rock On! Island- I'm not good at tower defense and this was not an ambassador. Pingolf- The punishing nature of the game is just inherent to golf, so I can't get *too* tilted.Mortol II- I'm thankful for the multiple paths that let me skip half the map, lol.Fist Hell- I'm actually pretty disappointed in this one. Didn't need to be *quite* that faithful to the old titles when stuff like Streets of Rage 4 does it so much better now.Overbold- This one took a while to beat but I can't tell if I was just playing myself.Campanella 2- Yeah I dunno how to feel about this one. Lots of work in service of platforming that's just kinda there.Hyper Contender- Donkus for president.Valbrace- I feel like I used the rapier to cheese my way to the end of this. We take those!Rakshasa- Weird weird difficulty curve where playing better makes the game easier. You know?Star Waspir- I have *no idea* how I cleared this one. I entered gamer mode.Grimstone- You need final boss music in your jrpg DEREK.Lords of Diskonia- The most needlessly cruel game in this pack. I wanna try the 2p though!Night Manor- A fantastic game, got sucked in and cleared it in one go.Elfazar's Hat- The game this is based on is right on the tip of my tongue...Pilot Quest- Well that cherry requirement can go to hell, lol.Mini & Max- So much work went into this! Needs more traversal abilities and less waiting for bugs!Combatants- People are down on this one but I thought it was... okay?Quibble Race- Could be fun with two people....Seaside Drive- HELL YEAH. Too good to be in a pack of fifty games, tbh.Campanella 3- My favorite of the trilogy!Cyber Owls- Metal Gear had more than one music track DEREK. You can afford to pay for more songs DEREK.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 3 of the 50 games so far and I'm already nearing 8 hours. Each game so far has been high quality. They take the limitations and design of those classics they are emulating but use clever modern design philosophies to remove the frustration that often came with them. Every thing is quick to navigate and don't feel like they're wasting your time even when the game itself is slow. You can easily hop in and out of games, they're low commitment to enjoy but easy to get sucked into and lose an hour or two discovering secrets or chasing high scores.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't like UFO50, you just plain don't like video games. There, I said it.This title deserves a place in the library of anyone who would consider themselves a 'gamer', from casual to hardcore.That may be the most incredibly high praise I can possibly offer any game and I mean it sincerely.Almost guaranteed, there is enough overall quality and variety here to satisfy players of all kinds.You will not enjoy every game; but you will enjoy enough of them to make it worth the money.If you truly don't, I'd wager your inner child is dead and video games in general are probably just not for you.This is an unbelievably ambitious game and a stunning display of dedication and skill from the devs.Exactly how ambitious and how stunning? That remains to be seen. I'm 20 hours in, but barely scratched the surface.This may be the best value of all time in a gaming product; even more than the Orange Box.Devs knocked it out of the park; I'm honestly blown away. STOP READING AND BUY THIS GAME AAAAAAAAAA

_childDocuments_.review: The love to old school gaming from the MSX to PC88 is out in force with these games. I've only played less than 10 of the games, adored to gold Train Heist, but "cherried" 2 of the other games and have to wait for the idle clicker to fully complete a third.An advanced version of snake, a deck builder, an idle game with a Zelda 1 overworld... I beat an optional boss just for the hell of it. All of this in 27 hours. I haven't even tried the other 40 games but for only 25 bucks this is a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The knee jerk reaction upon seeing this is to compare it to the infamous Action 52 on the Nintendo back in the day, but the games in this compilation are all amazing. With at least one or two that'll be guaranteed to become part of your regular rotation of time wasters.This isn't some shovelware pile, almost every game is a flex in game design, with incredible graphics and gameplay put together within the limitations of this fictitious games console the LX. It's a love letter to old school gaming while also showing just what new indie games could be bringing to the market. With little hidden easter eggs and secrets all through out.several of the games alone are almost worth the price of admission by themselves, most likely party house, mortol 1 and 2, and mini and max. Though there are a couple of games that I feel could have been replaced, puzzle stacking games akin to columns or tetris are strangely absent, and a 2.5d racer like outrun or pole position would have fit in comfortably, as well. Long Story short, this is an amazing game compilation, and it's garanteed to have at least one of your games of the year within it's contents.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing amount of content and passion went into this. Each game has depth and the majority are hard-as-heck. Lots of genres and world-building. I've only scratched the surface of a lot of the games, and can tell that I will come back to this for years and years. If I could only have one game in steam, I think it'd be this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I think what I appreciate most about this collection the sheer diversity of the game library as it harkens back to an older era of game design and philosophy. There's really something in the collection for everybody and while it does share Spelunky's level of difficulty at times, you feel like it's more your own fault than a broken gameAlso, if you can, go into this totally blind. Don't watch let's plays or streamers and just immerse yourself in it. Go through the library and discover the games for yourself
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is both a brilliant collection of games from an alternate reality and an incredible love letter to genuinely amazing cult hits from the 8 and 16 bit eras. If you have historical context for what's being shown in this collection, it makes it even more charming AND enjoyable. Amazing homages and takes on titles like Metal Storm, Wind Jammers, Star Tropics, Sweet Home, River City Ransom, Space Harrier, Kirby Dream Course etc etc etc the list goes on and on. These nods and inspirations are FAR from rips offs tho as they are clearly not only inspired by their sources but have inspired new and refined mechanics. Some even being completely different takes on the same idea mashed together with new genres creating something familiar, yet entirely new at the same time.  This is a collection of devs and designers flexing both their history and knowledge of game design and giving us something from another timeline crafted with love and skill.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like every game. But I liked enough of them. And I liked them enough that I would recommend this game.Rail Heist is a fantastic platformer-strategy game where you have to secure money from a train, then escape to a horse. But you only have 9 seconds to make your moves before the lawmen take their turn, with XCOM-esque Overwatch mechanics in play.Night Manor is a point-and-click adventure game where you solve puzzles while avoiding a fungus-covered killer. There's tons of spooky details, like animations that rarely play when you enter a room.Magic Garden is a cross between Pacman and Snake - rescue Oppies so they trail behind you, then drop them off at the Star Spaces. Dropping off enough gives you a 'power pellet' that lets you take out enemies, but bumping into any of them or your trail of Oppies ends your game.Waldorf's Journey is like a really atmospheric version of those "shoot the cat out of the cannon and see how far it goes" games, except you're a walrus and you have to collect seashells.Mooncat is a beautiful weird platformer with binary controls. Two inputs: Go Left, and Go Right, and everything else is a combination of those inputs in different orders or combinations.Party House is a deckbuilder where the goal is to have 4 special guest cards at once. Gain Popularity to add new Guests to your rolodex, Money to expand your house to allow more guests at once and use their abilities to manage your Trouble-causing guests so they don't get the party busted.And Porgy - well Porgy sucks but they can't all be winners.

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 feels like nothing else on steam. It captures the feeling of unboxing a new console at the holidays. It captures that feeling you might have had at the video store where you pick a game you're going to spend a weekend with based on the box art and you know it looks cool but really have no idea what you're in for. It captures what it was like living through an era when of gaming when it felt like you never knew what was coming next.  It captures that feeling of going to a friends house for the first time and finding out they have a whole shoe-box full of games you've only heard about and they are excited to play them with you.That is all to say nothing of the endlessly remarkable pixel art, unique game designs, unexpected depth, variety and replay-ability.  This is not a game you should skip or overlook. I've been playing ever chance I get and I still feel like I've barely scratched the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to finish all the games before leaving a review, but I realized that this will require at least 50 hours of gameplay, and I have my doubts about dedicating that much time to this game... My expectation with UFO50 was to feel like I was exploring real old games from a parallel dimension or something (as the game's intro indicates). What I felt was that I was playing a collection of average modern indie games. In basically everything, from the mechanics, to the gameplay twists, to the pixel art, to the audio, it's all 85% modern indie games, and only 15% old games. The devs have failed in their historical research, if they think they're representing things from back then with any fidelity. Making references to multiple famous games is not the same thing as creating a simulacrum of an ancient era.It's as if UFO50 was more of a tribute to the amateur indie scene of 2010-2019 than old 1980-1989 ganes.Regarding the games themselves, you have the formula you've come to expect from the vast majority of indies: a strong reference to old games, but with a twist on the formula. Not all games follow this pattern, but most fit it. Once the twist gets old, you're back to relying on gameplay fundamentals, and that's when you realize that most of UFO50's games are pretty shallow. Much shallower than the good games of the 1980/90s, in fact. There are some genuinely entertaining games in the collection, don't get me wrong, but even these are usually pretty shallow. The only playable shooter, for example, is fun (Seaside Drive), but after playing its 4 levels, it's not like there's much to explore. But okay, that's understandable, the guys made 50 games, so nobody expected games with depth comparable to “true” games, the real problem is that many of the games in the collection don't even manage to be entertaining on their own.Star Waspir, for example, is one of the worst shmups I've ever played, and I'm not exaggerating. Planet Zoldath is a fetch quest where you have two slots for items and have to swap them all the time in a procedural world with terrible controls, a horrible game. Paint Chase is relatively addictive, but I wonder how thirsty someone needs to be for games to really devote more than an hour to it. I'd say the same for Campanella 1, you'd have to be abstinent from games to consider dedicating a lot of time looking for secret cofees in a game with such simplistic gameplay. Golfaria is annoying. Fist Hell is a beat'n up that misses out on several of the genre's basic fundamentals. Night Manor has an uninspired story and a gimmick that just wastes your time as you try and solve the game's puzzles. Onion Delivery is simply unpleasant to play. And so on...Finally, I don't think this game will age well, many of the players who are loving the experience will at some point start to get out of the mindset that the context of the game puts you in, stop caring about collecting items and winning gold and cherry discs, and at that point UFO50 will have to sustain itself just because of the quality of its games. That's when many will begin to realize that Campanella, Mini and Max, Velgress, Magical Garden, Pilot Quest, etc., aren't as interesting as they once seemed.In my opinion, UFO50 will not stand the test of time, and I'm going to leave this review here for the next years to see if my claim will be vindicated.NOTE: this game was highly rated by critics, with a 90/100 on Metacritics, but most games are going to be 6/10, 7/10, with a few points off the curve (both up and down). It's being overrated by the critics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually so much fun.At times you will start up a game, play it for 10 minutes, frown at it and close it.At other times, there are games you will play for multiple hours, fully excited, sometimes mad, always hooked.I love what they did with this game. There are many oldschool collections, but a collection of a Fantasy Studio that never existed to begin with, all with genres and ideas that weren't there at the time, is AMAZING.There were some games I didn't enjoy to much, like "Golfaria", "Onion Delivery" or "Pingolf", all of them I played for not even 10 minutes each.But then there are some absolute gems like "Rock on! Island", "Night Manor" or "Pilot Quest" each of which I played for multiple hours and will keep on playing a lot (except maybe Night Manor, as that is more of a "do once and done" deal).I am serious, if you are at all positively attuned towards Retro Games, get this game, it REEKS of charm.
