_childDocuments_.review: This feels like an unmissable, unforgettable indie game landmark. As someone who's incredibly interested in the design of games, this feels like it's made for me, but even if I just wanted to have fun for fun's sake, I can imagine this being one of the best things I could possibly pick up. It's been in standby on my Steam Deck nearly constantly for a month now.If I did have some gripes, it's that too many of the action games have that NES-era type of design where 1–2 hits is instant death. I like hard games, but it does grind my gears a little bit when the challenge is so all-or-nothing. Then again, maybe a big part of these games' target audience do enjoy that, so I try not to hold it against it. And for all the frustration, it really does give me a sense of mastery when I start to find a flow in those punishing games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: (EDIT: Please note that the vast majority of negative reviews have maybe 2 or 3 hours of gameplay, in a collection of 50 games. There is absolute zero chance that they actually played all of the games, OR played any of them long enough to actually figure them out and learn them. So you played each game for just over a minute and think you have a good idea of what they are like? Okay, slugger.)I love this game so much.You won't like every single game here. There will be some that you love right from the start, some that you hate, some that you initially dislike or disregard and then revisit later and suddenly something clicks or you realize there is more to it than you realized, etc etc. But you will appreciate that all of them are there, even the ones that aren't necessarily your favorites. None of them are bad, all of them are at least interesting and/or have a clever touch, and i enjoyed discovering and playing every single one of them. It's also interesting how many of these games have enough similarities to certain old NES games to provide context and play upon your nostalgia, while also being completely different and/or more complex, or the way that certain games here use the history of NES games to sort of provide a framework for what they are doing. Play Combat Owls, for some example, and (depending upon which level you pick first) you may think it's a riff on the original Metal Gear... only to choose another level and think, "oh, okay; this level is NES The Punisher. I see what they're doing here. Well, let's see what games and genres the other levels are like!" You have pretty much everything here: strategy games, multi-player games sports games, arena fighters, beat 'em ups, shmups, weird melee-centric dungeon crawlers, JRPGs, platformers, etc etc. You get everything from a weird strategy game centered around praying to dinosaurs and capturing castles, to a deckbuilder where you're trying to throw the Ultimate Party without alerting the police, to a strange esoteric game about a trio of humanoid amphibians exploring the watery depths and getting into turn-based battles, to a game about betting on races between little fellas that look like the little green Dozer guys from Fraggle Rock, to.... honestly, there are so many games here that i find so interesting and impressive that i could just keep on listing my favorites for quite a while. There are so many here that deserve recognition. I even enjoy the sort of fake history and evolution of the games, and the way that the sequels iterate upon the previous entries. Just because you don't like, say, Campanella, does not mean that you will not enjoy Campanella 2, because they are different experiences. The same flying mechanics are still there, but now they are wrapped inside of a sort of riff on Blaster Master or... that one NES game whose name suddenly escapes me that alternates between shmup and side-scroller.It really is an excellent collection. I was initially afraid that maybe once i had checked out each game, the novelty would where off and it would become less interesting, or that maybe the games wouldn't have enough depth to make me continue playing. And i have actually had the exact opposite experience. The more that i play it, and the more i revisit some of the games and bounce around the selection, the more i enjoy and appreciate it, the more depth i discover in some of the games, etc etc. Seriously can't say enough about it. HUGE thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A huge, generous, beautiful love letter to the 8 bit era. The games themselves are mostly great, with a few that are worth the price of admission on their own. And even the ones I didn't care for as much can't be called filler: all 50 games are overflowing with passion and artistry. There'll never be another one (50) like it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adoring send-up of 1980s gaming dripping with quality design and attention to detail. Capitalism consumes art like an eldritch maw, so it's hard not to appreciate the fact that you just spend 7-8 hours on a game that technically cost you like $.50. Incredible that the devs of this actually managed to make 50 worthwhile games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The is an incredible collection of games many of which I would happy to buy individually. They aren't "mini games", but instead fully realized in depth games that have been fully developed many of which will take a very long time to complete. Getting all of the achievements in the batch of games would take hundreds of hours if not more.The games span many different genres. You will undoubtedly find games in the collection that you love regardless of your particular interests. Some are devilishly hard, but this isn't off putting because there are so many games. I expect to be playing games in this set on and off for years to come. I am sure I will keep circling back to it.If trapped on a desert island and could have only 1 game (actually 50) from Steam - this is it.A master class achievement. This collection would be worthwhile at 5 x the price.If you like ANY retro games from the 80's / 90's era, this game collection belongs in your library immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think we should cultivate this part of gaming culture. I know that it wasn't the intention of authors and it doesn't really matter. The collection encapsulates so many things that are wrong with today's world, it just tries to stick to every kind of brain, channel an endless stream of easy addicting fun, and switch things up, just when you start feeling bored. It hijacked my brain and broken my attention. It made me play games, that without the collection I would've dissmissed in 5 minutes. Sure, some games are more contemplative, but they are a minority and just beside them lay all the sugary raffle, that is just waiting for you to try it. All the completionist collectaphone mechanics are here to hook you more.It reminds me of fast food or some candy bar brand, with endless flavours and colorful packages, and if you don't see anything wrong with those, the point would be lost on you.Nostalgia media isn't a positive force. Referenced era of gaming wasn't something good, it spread mindless brainworms targeted at children. It didn't try enriching anybody's lives.It could've been much worse, many other games are much more intentionally predatory, but this collection, having lots of good game design and interesting ideas, tricked me into thinking it was a good time investment. I got 5/50 to 100%, calmed down, deleted profile with the progress, and now I feel better. Of course will return to it later and regret it once again.Edit. Actual subjective review after 87 hours: It is profoundly artistic, very sincere, original and I have so many problems with it…I hate the Art, the palette.. Except for cool character portraits in some games, character design is some looney toons nostalgic mumbling. Games even have readablilty problems! (e.g. Magic Garden, Rakshasa, Mini&Max)I turned off background music after a few cycles in each game. Although it is fine in playlist, for me its way too intense and in your face for constant repetition, now I have a seizure every time I hear main menu music. All sound effects seem cartoonishly annoying.The absolute worst part for me is game feel. All action controls feel clunky, unresponsive. Hit boxes are awfully awkward. The only two exceptions are games by Ojiro Fumoto, Campanella and Seaside Drive, which just feel smooth and fluent! This is completely buffles me, as I always said that Spelunkys have the BEST game feel amongst platformers! Almost none of the games rolls smoothly, animations, dialogues, screen transitions and cut-scene-likes constantly interrupt the flow. Even the starting screens of all the games and the collection's itself are unreasonably long.The game structure is almost completely a miss for me. I absolutely despise arcade-style "repeat exactly the same levels from the very beginning each time you fail". I struggle to find just any positive sides to this, except for ease of implementation and nostalgic points. 20 out of 50 games have arcade structure! Combined with the fact that I hate moment to moment game feel, it is 20 games out of the library. Other games still have this stiff rigid feeling, no room for imagination, no exploration (almost), just "complete these 99 stages and you can go".In the end I liked 4/50 games, which are Party House, Avianos, Bug Hunter and Quibble Race. None of which I want to replay, none feels like a robust game, the first two I find game-design inspiring. Overall, 23 games are in the genres I enjoy, some have interesting basis, but feel like upgraded game-jam remains. Average score: 4.08/10, favourite author: Jon Perry, with average 5.00/10.It turned out exactly as you would expect. Very artistic, way too ambitious, master of none. Mediocre rpgs, uninspired puzzles, soulless explorations and tons of arcade chaff. I was way overhyped by the suspence and Derek's image, I should've known better.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is great. It's like having an organized ROM pack of your favorite NES games... that you've never played nor heard of before. Excellent concept; every game that I've played in the collection so far is well-thought-out and beautifully executed. If you enjoy retro games (from the NES / SMS era, in particular), this one is a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid my mom saw that I liked playing video games on the computer, so as a gift she bought me a small handheld device that came with 700 games. I remember it very vividly but I remember not having a good time using that little handheld device, because those games were shovelware, quantity over quality garbage, and some were even just copy pastes of one another. I stopped touching that device not long after I got it because I had better games on the computer.A few days ago I was recommended a video on youtube about this game, and I saw it and I understood the concept that it's 50-in-1, but instead of being garbage shovelware it's actually good games? 50 of them. It sounded too good to be true but as I watched two videos on this game I liked the idea and had to try it myself.First game I launched because my friend told me it looks cool, Bushido Ball, I got hooked on it, played it for a couple hours, then a bit more, then I streamed it to a friend with Remote Play Together and we played Bushido Ball and a handful more games. Everything worked flawlessly and as we played more of the multiplayer games we came to realize every single one of these games is polished, made with love, and has a respectful amount of content. Every single one of these games we played is good fun. Of course I like some games more than others, everyone will have a preference, but I haven't played a single bad game on here.UFO 50 is a fresh take on retro style games, it's a homage to retro style games in all their genres and forms, but at the same time it does things uniquely with its own ideas that are designed really well. I haven't seen another game try to imitate one of those bootleg "x-in-1" games/consoles but do a good job at it.Well done to everyone involved in the creation of this massive project, this is truly something I never would've imagined. I'm expecting to keep playing for a while, maybe until I beat all the games, and then keep replaying this later on in life, because this has replayability through the roof.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Think this game is a bit overhyped. I kind of enjoyed it while not particularly liking any of the games. It recreates the emulator experience without resolving some of the negative elements of that.So it's initially really fun to scoot through everything and see what they're all like. But after that, feels a bit empty. While containing many interesting ideas, I feel the games are often poorly designed - needlessly frustrating and with general lack of save points/progress. It's not just the difficulty but the general lack of player friendliness.I think a good test of whether you'll like UFO50 is if you enjoy Spelunky. I don't personally and think it's the same design ethos in these games that generally puts me off.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: For you to put out a big game that deserves to be put in the S tier of any game released in 2024 is a big ask already. For you to put out 50 SMALL games, a majority of them deserving to be put in the S Tier of games released in 2024 is Impossible. To put them all in one great big bundle pack with it's own world and lore? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.UFO 50 has some blatantly fantastic games in it that really need to have expanded standalone versions available to play. If this game gets workshop mod support like Sega Mega Drive/Genesis Classics has, that's it. This game is a killer for any AAA producing company that says small games can't be as good as big games that take 5+ years to develop, tease, advertise, and release.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a collection of 50 games. That's a lot, so let's focus on what that means overall.You are  going to like every game in this collection. That's inevitable for a collection of this size. But you most likely  find at least a handful of games you'll love. Some very popular games include Party House, Mini & Max, Mortol, Warptank, and Night Manor. If you consider that the collection goes for $25, getting those five games for $5 each is more than worth the price of admission.I wanna say the claim that "these are not minigames" is  true. Out of the 50 total entries, about 20 of them are categorized as "epic play", with the rest being "quick play". There's definitely one or two games in here that feel closer to "minigame" in terms of their scope (although back in the 80's they probably would be considered more of a full game versus today). Magic Garden comes to mind as one such game, though its scoring system gives it a surprising amount of depth. On the other end of the scale you have Grimstone, a classic RPG that took me about 28 hours to do my first run.I do feel somewhat mixed about some of the "quick play" games, as they're generally in the style of short arcade games you have to beat in one go. Some of them feel addictive, like Overbold, while others feel agonizing (Caramel Caramel and Fist Hell). The difficulty of these titles is at least offset by the fact that they're a bit shorter than you might expect. Though in a sense that's a double-edged sword. I ended up playing through a few of these shorter games and wishing they were longer!The "epic play" titles were generally more my thing. These usually have you unlocking stages you can revisit at any time. Mortol even finds a clever use for this, as you can revisit past stages to try and score better to help you out in the later levels.A lot of the games in UFO 50 reward patience and perseverance. Games like Golfaria, Porgy, and Divers start you off feeling  weak (to the point where many people have understandably bounced off them), but once you take the time to figure out the mechanics and game world and collect enough upgrades, the experience will most likely become a vibe. It is up to you to decide whether or not the upfront friction is something you're willing to contend with.There's also Mooncat, which feels utterly broken at first. But once you understand what's going on it's an incredible experience....And then there's Combatants, which  feels utterly broken at first, because it is. In contrast to Mooncat, it's a miserable experience through and through, and once you learn the cheese it's still miserable, but at least doable. I 100%'d this one out of spite (and also because I wanted to get it done in case they decided to patch out the cheese to make it even ).But also keep in mind that there are also 49 games that  Combatants. And the sheer breadth of the games in this collection will probably keep you busy for a while. Many are interesting twists on old formulas, or combine multiple classics in new ways. Magic Garden is like Snake mixed with Flicky and Pac-Man. Vainger merges Metroid with Metal Storm and adds its own unique powerup system. And if you dig deep enough into each game's mechanics, you'll learn some interesting design lessons, too. Divers in particular is a neat case study in RPG minimalism.Oh, and there's a house with a little guy you can win gifts for just by dipping your toes into each game. It reminds me of Little Computer People for the C64.Overall this collection is kinda incredible and it's been a hyperfixation of mine since it came out. Perhaps you'll find a favorite game in this too!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I've only touched the first 12 games, going in "release order." It really nails the premise of finding a big pile of dusty floppies in a storage unit and booting them up to see what they are. All you get for them is a quick blurb, some "trivia" about the history of the game, and the controls - in some it really adds to the feeling that there should have been a manual you just don't have so you gotta puzzle out how the thing really works. It hasn't felt unfair about this so far though, which is great. Essentially you are getting 50 really well polished and unique game jam games with a theme. That means if you, say, try the first game "Barbuta" and decide it's not for you - that's fine! Pick a different one! You don't gotta like or even beat all these things. Don't be a silly person on the forum.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this I have played the first 27 games and beat 15 of them. The average lengths of the games are varied from arcade length quarter suckers to in depth platformers, average playtime for a win was about an hour with some games taking 15 minutes and others taking over 4 hours (4 of them for me so far, Porgy, Mortol, Golfpia and Block Koala).The variety is incredible, and games that are labeled as multiplayer experiences can be played single player with no worries of missing out on anything. The game has a sort of checkmark system with three separate goals per game. Every game has a win condition, a master clear (cherry) condition and a side condition (most are get halfway through the win condition). The side condition unlocks a fun treat that you can view within the screensaver like, CUBEWORLD-esque, garden screen. A very cute bonus and relax away from some of the more intense experiences.Every game seems handcrafted and well done within it's retro aesthetic and expanded to an even better experience beyond the conventions of a mere MSX/NES game. The first game it starts you with is a tough one, but one that many have either loved to hate or unabashedly loved. I for one am a Barbuta fan, from the seemingly unfair world all the way down to it's tightly knit experience, it's a highlight for sure.This game is a steal, everyone says the deal is 50 cents a game and it delivers experiences worth more than 2 credits a pop. Whether you like half of what is in the pack or even just 3 or 4 games, you'll find a value in this even before there's a sale. The team behind these games are crazy and there's plenty of actual secrets to be found. Cheat-codes, flavor text, hidden power-ups and opinions on loungewear.What are you readin' my opinion for? Pick up the games! LX FOREVER!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: After 16.5 hours I have finally ''tried'' all 50 games. By ''tried'' I mean I barely scratched the surface on most of them and I found at least 15-20 games that I could see myself spending dozens of hours just for the sake of fully completing it. Must buy even not on sale, at least a few games in the package will resonate with you and each of them will probably be better than some 10-20$ trash games you would get on a steam sale anyway!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I had unreasonably high expectations and was not disappointed. This new type of fantasy console collection is executed amazingly and there are so many little meta details that are woven into this launcher/wrapper presentation so perfectly that I keep finding new things to marvel at.If you like this, check out Last Call BBS and VIDEOVERSE. Locally Sourced Collection, Indiepocalypse, and others are also great game anthologies if you're still craving more.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many game collections from the NES, and while this pays homage to them, it also does something no game collection from the 80s manages: it's actually good. Some of the games are bite-sized, but even those have more depth than all of Action 52. I know; I've played through most of them (except Silver Sword).It's odd that my biggest complaints about the UFO 50 games are also my biggest praises; it captures the soul of NES-era game collections, complete with all the beauty and mess they had. You won't love every game, but that's part of the art - everything you dislike is still paying homage to the 80s, and you finally get to experience the thrill (and occasional disappointment) that used to come from new, mysterious game collections.Try several of the games before putting this down. I recommend Party House, personally - it's easy to understand, short, but extremely complicated.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a game I would have happily payed $60 for. Fifty (mayyyyyybee more?) games for the low price of $25 is a criminally great deal. And yes, what we've got here are 50 video games. Not micro games, not mini games, not game-jam games. Every game in this collection are fully fledged games that would have been a full priced cartridge in the 80's. The fact that they all have a cohesive palette and sound font is elevated even MORE by the clear iteration and evolution of the games as you play them "chronologically". There is a vast array of game genres, and even if you don't connect with a bunch of games here, there is no doubt in my mind you will become strongly hooked on several more, sinking hours into many of the offerings available. Even my 11yo child who swears she hates "simple graphic" pixel games has gotten hooked. Great games are great, regardless of resolution and fidelity, so even if you're put off by chunky pixels I defy you to sample each game here and not become enamored with several of them.Good luck; have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, its so unique and different and every game has its own identity and feels very polished. I have 7 hours at the time of this review and have only played half of the games at this point. Each one has been enjoyable to a degree and a good number of them have been super addicting.I particularly like how each game has a way to 'complete' it to get a gold cart, and each game has a few other more abstract goals to go for as well. Can't recommend enough
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Great lore and secrets, as to be expected from the developers of Spelunky 1 & 2.All of the games I've played so far have felt fun, new and addicting, while giving me memories of old NES classics.50 games, of which 25 are multiplayer games and 11 are co-op games.I haven't even scratched the surface yet, and can't wait to see all the secrets and games the game holds.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is tied with Balatro for GOTY.It's scary how good this game is. 50 fully realized unique games, each of them with beautiful graphics and modern twists that make every single one worth playing. This may be the first game of its type to ever exist, and I hope it makes as much of an impact in the history of game development as it feels like it should. It's incredibly ambitious and feels too good to be true... except that it is true. They really did it. They pulled it off! Not even to mention the bizarre ARG-esque 51st game, which ties every game together and that the internet is still piecing together an explanation for.Even though UFO 50 will take hundreds of hours to complete, no time is wasted in this game. It's all killer and no filler, as the devs have studied and condensed so many nostalgic game mechanics of our childhoods into only their most interesting and engaging components. No game feels too long or too short, it all feels "just right". It's beautiful and I never want it to end.They really meant it when they said "Play Forever"
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I would have paid 20$ for Paint Chase alone. I hope it gets a sequel.In all honesty tho, I'm stuck at the 4th out of 50 games, not because I'm at a loss, but because I just wanna keep playing that one until I beat it. Knowing there's 46 other games still waiting for me is absolutely insanity. Most charming game of 2024. Simply CLEARS.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This was a negative review but I changed my mind completely after playing a little longer. It's possible that you can wade through mid games for like 5 or 6 hours before stumbling upon really good stuff, and I made the mistake of letting my first impressions cloud me. My recommendation for maximally enjoying this game is to look in epic play and stick through some games that might seem boring or one dimensional at first.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The ingenuity and creativity on display in every single game is astounding and baffling. It's incredible something like this got made. Anyone who is a fan of video games *at all* should purchase this. It has something for everyone, and will likely broaden your own tastes for genres you didn't care to play before.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 50 games.I didn't think anything of it as I casually played through them. Most definitely, they have captured the rare nostalgia of 8-bit gaming (albeit with some modern conveniences).I just selected a game, played for 10-15 mins and moved on.But, as I slept, my mind kept coming back to the games.Like a thorn in my side, it pained me not to be playing them.I felt... I felt as If I were missing out on childhood games that I had missed playing 30 years ago.That is how excellent this collection is. Not only are the games varied and excellent, but they are an inception of nostalgia - they've implanted a soft and fuzzy feeling of the Eighties into my mind. A new memory that wasn't there before.I can't recommend this enough - just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and brilliant. It's like the Switch NES game compilation in an alternate universe. 50 retro games in one package. These aren't mini-games, they're full-on retro games.Each game is unique and interesting. Some instantly grab you and pull you in while other takes some warming up to before the "aha" moment.To make it even more interesting, there's a compelling meta-narrative where each game has it's own in-world lore. And beyond all of that are deep, unfolding secrets (similar to the developer's brilliant Spelunky series).This game is brilliant. At 50 cents a game, you can't go wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews but I have to for this title--this game is an exceptional showcase of the pure talent and ingenuity from all developers involved. Truly amazing that something like this is able to exist. Congratulations Derek Yu on having your vision with this come to fruition in such perfect fashion after seven long years.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is an amazing collection of well fleshed out and thoughtful games. Don't get the wrong idea about this game. It is not Wario ware. These are full games, some of which can take multiple hours to beat. The collection has something for everyone. From Action platformer to puzzles and deck builder. If a game gets too frustrating  then there are plenty of other titles to relax with until you are ready to pick it back up. This game is an achievement hunter's dream with a wide variety of challenges and the illusive Cherry Disk which is given out after 100% a chosen game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 has absorbed my life with its incredible gameplay - there'll be a game for everyone, but not every game is for everyone - its great variety, its challenges and sheer depth. I won't touch on highlights - the game is full of them, but it's filled with love, a meta history to explore, pretty much every genre you can imagine, and great music and visuals.What else is there to add? It's a great game that I can imagine myself playing for many more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played around 15 of the games so far, but this honestly might be in contention for my game(s?) of the year.This is like having one of those NES multi-game cartridges, but instead of 95% of the games being unplayable trash, 95% of these games are great, or masterpieces in their own right. Whether its action games, platformers, strategy games, puzzlers, shmups etc, Derek Yu and the team seem to understand what makes these genres fun, hone in on the mechanics that facilitate the fun, and then add their own fresh and innovative twists on them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so happy about the fact a game like this even exists. A collection of 50 original games and all the ones I've played so far have been fantastic. I've been having a ton of fun and I can already tell I'm gonna be putting a lot more time into this collection. Plus the concept of it being a lineup for a console that doesn't exist is so cool. If you have ever been in love with any NES or SNES era game I can't recommend this one enough. I played a lot of Genesis games as a kid and this has been giving me a similar feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: been looking up for this game since it was annouced, really wasn't expecting it to be this GOOD.I've been reccomending this to several friends but i will understand if this isn't their type of game, to remain faithful to the era these games were supposed to be released some old-fashioned aspects will turn people away, such as difficulty selection, lack of checkpoints, and always starting on level one in most of the games.but without these the experience might not be as genuine. Amazing game, will show to my dad.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it for Barbuta alone, that game is a masterpiece. You basically play as a knight, but it's not really set in medieval england or antyhing like that, it's more of a fantasy dungeon roguelike crawler with permadeath elements. The game TEACHES you about retro gaming in a really unique fun way where you go through a maze-like level, with amazing music accompanying your journey. Sound design of this game is out of this world. I love Barbuta. If Barbuta has no fans, I am no longer alive.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I like what this game is going for in terms of nostalgia.But the games need a manual... and the majority of the games I could get through before returning the game have 1 or 2 death game overs, all 1 hit deaths, and they reuse so many assets and gameplay mechanics that there's probably only 15ish games that are good and 35 games that are worst versions of the better games. But I could only get through maybe 15 and only 3 I could stomach. I would rather 15 quality titles than 35 games that are negative fun for 5 minutes and you'll never play again.Honestly, download an NES emulator and play better quality gems than this. Going to thumb it down, but I do appreciate the devs giving this a shot. But I've played singular title nes games better than this entire catalog. Again, the best versions of quality games on here can be bought for 10 cents or played for free.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person who likes to revisit the games you played as a kid, get this one.50 really well-designed and unique games with just the right amount of that nostalgic 'jank' to feel challenging, yet not unfair. Even if the influences are pretty evident sometimes, it doesn't feel like i'm playing a copy of another game someone already made.Do yourself a favor and don't spoil yourself by checking guides.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply: there are 50 games, and no bad ones. Not every game has been for me, but every one is of high quality, and almost all have a unique, inspired twist from its source material. Actually unbelievable that this (frankly insane) game collection was executed to this level of quality, and genuinely one of the best deals you can get on steam right now!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give a more complete review once I have played more.The simplest way I can put it is--if you found a turbografx or sharp x68000 in a storage unit loaded with 50 games with all kinds of genres represented but no manuals.  That's essentially the experience you're getting.Many of the different games vary a bit in difficulty but I'd describe it a bit as 50 puzzles to solve.  Every game where I feel it's difficult, it's because I a) don't have a manual and b) part of the game is figuring out and testing mechanics to find the easier path through the game.  Some games I indeed found this frustrating, as games from the 80s--especially your strategy titles, would have 50-100+ page manuals detailing all kinds of game mechanics details.To some degree, that is this game's gimmick and although this was initially a massive turn off to me.  This turned around as I see the insane attention to detail and how the reward structure exists in each game.The entire package has an insane amount of charm and nostalgia.  You will recognise many similar arcade and video games you'll played that inspired these games.  Everything has nice quirky twists and there's plenty of feel of the ol nethack 'the devs dd indeed think of that'.Definitely worth it.  Even if there's like 5 games in this you really enjoy, you'll get plenty of enjoyment out of this at the price point.Also note--there's a ton of these games you can play with friends over steam/remotely excellently.  This is a major add and thought to a package like this.--Updates on specific games:Velgress is absolutely terrible.  I hope the devs address issues and feedback that have been brought up about game's difficulty.  Many of my friends would find Velgress unfun and lacking in game design.  I've been through about half the games so about 20 of them being good and fun and I feel rewarding to the player, that is--if you follow what you're being shown and learn the game...it's reasonably possible to finish all the achievement for it as a new player within a reasonable time.  Velgress is not so and you're not even afforded the opportunity to practice the harder parts of the game so you know how to better prepare or even understand how things work.  Grind 5+ minutes to get there, lose in a second without learning anything.  That's the terrible experience that dark souls is that some have converted the grotesque idea that that is 'good' game design.  No, no it is not.Even worse is Star Waspir.  It's incredibly rough to play, with background scrolling and bullets everywhere that it's incredibly difficult to actually see what is happening.  The game, similar to Velgress is short, but needs some serious work as I'd say this one is nearly unplayable and really unfair unless you specifically are an expert I guess in this genre and don't have disabilities that make it difficult to play.  Star Waspir is the worst game so far in the 50 I've played.  It, similar to Velgress, has all the worst of the genres it mimics and none of the good.  As a raidenx clone, it has the strange property that options/side guns take damage.  This means you constantly have to collect upgrades on a playfield you cannot actually tell what is going to damage you and because the gun options are awful (you pick from 3 ships, all are terrible) between the ships, you're left with this really awkward game.  There are 2 powerups and you must spell a 3 letter word such as EGG for a score multiplier, or GGG for a gun or EEE for a TEMPORARY gun upgrade.  Naturally losing a ship means you lose all gun/options as well, so losing a ship frequently means immediate game over despite not being able to permanently upgrade the gun.  The options can shoot homing missiles and give you better angles your main gun cannot do well.  They also made the really awkward decision, despite having 2 buttons, to only allow you to rhythmically tap to spread fire or to hold for constant fire.  It hurts quite a bit to be constantly doing this and the spread shot is terrible anyway because the screen is loaded with projectiles to avoid too fast anyway.  Hopefully more patches are coming.  The rallyx/crush roller game didn't need the cherry score reduced if Velgress/Star Waspir aren't getting their difficulty and really accessibility issues fixed.  But these also require more work than simply lowering a score threshold.  If you had HP or something, both would probably be fine.  Otherwise you have so many winners in ufo50, I'd not let 2 games ruin it, but they're so significantly different than the rest of the catalog, it needs to be noted.  As I said prior, the rest of the games careful play/paying attention/solving the puzzle that is finding advantages in game mechanics, etc. will reward a player of ANY skill level and that's a reasonable achievable goal to any reasonable player.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If there have been any major releases over the past 10 years that are as consistently, unrelentingly fun as the average UFO50 game, I missed them. I honestly don't think the rest of the industry knows how to make fun games like this. Derek Yu and his friends know, and here are a bunch of them.Though I might not recommend all 50 of them, I'd recommend 6 or 7, which is more games than you usually get, and I can genuinely say that 47 of them, maybe all of them, at least brought me *joy* for a minute or so and usually far more than a minute, even though I probably wont have time to finish them, which is far more joy than you usually get.Maybe the reason UFO50 is such a breath of golden air from the before times is that the format allows games to be a little weird, to open hard, to end before they've outstayed their welcome and without trying to make themselves out to be more than they are. That is great stage for games, and it's very different to the hype-fueled spectacle oriented live service advertising and sales channels that the rest of the industry is enslaved to.My weirdest fav game here is Planet Zoldath, because I think it captures a proto-genre of figuring-out-an-alien-ecosystem, this genre really wants to be born soon and I will celebrate anything that resembles it even if it's clunky and simple, and also I guess because it's just big enough to challenge my (limited) sense of spacial recall without overwhelming it. My more normal favs are Warptank (it's flowy and cool), Mortol II (the world is freaky, and it's such a fresh, atmospheric gameplay system) and Campanella 2 (The true spiritual successor to Spelunky as far as I'm concerned).I'm eager to find out what *your* weirdest favs will turn out to be.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is 50, high quality 8-bit games for your Steam collection which have been developed by a variety of developers in the past 5 or so years.   It's weird because this game is packaged like it's one of those multi-game cartridges from the 80s that were largely garbage, but each game here is well thought out and unique from each other.There's literally every kind of old 8-bit game here - puzzlers, shooters, rpgs, questing, side scrollers, everything.  Some games, by their nature, are more in-depth than others but each one is worth the time to explore.This game isn't for everyone, though.  For the coolness that it is, UFO 50 is still a simple 2-button d-pad game and has the same amount of depth that the NES cartridges offered.  So if you don't yearn for these 'good old days' of CRT gaming then you may not care for this, which is fair.Personally, I'm pleased with this.  In the 4 or so hours I've played, I've tried about 8 or so games and more than half have some serious depth.  80s kids would love this. Probably 90s kids too.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun games in here! Just don't immediately try to beat Barbuta or Combatants and you're golden.Some I've enjoyed so far:Waldorf's JourneyMortol 1 & 2Party HouseOverboldPilot Quest (you may want to play this one first until the crystal drops a moon ingot, which lets you get the huntress to move in)Mooncat (feels great to play after you learn the goofy controls)GrimstoneMini & Max (HUGE open world which was unexpected)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: What a bizarrely wonderful idea! 50 “newly discovered” 8-bit games from a fictional long-lost console. This love letter -no, love omnibus- to the 80s reflects a deep knowledge of that era. These aren’t “remakes” of big-name hits; they’re more like “repairs” of lesser known titles. Remember Dark Castle on Macintosh but hated the controls? They fixed it….but only just enough. How about Wizardry? Karate Kid for NES? Wonder Boy? So far I’m hooked on Bug Hunt, a deceptively simple turn-based shooter with cards. My brain remembers the feeling of playing a new game on  c64, NES, master system, DOS, Amiga and longs for it again; these games made us gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: So many absolute bangers, and so much variety. Most games are waaaay more fleshed out then they have any right to be. UFO 50 does the compilation type game super well. I'm just a little over halfway into TRYING all the games because I got hooked on a few now and didn't wanna move on yet.It covers so many different genres, most games combining different genres into something new (or at least new to me), and all done quite effectively at worst and exceptionally at best. It reintroduced game types that I tend not to play due to complexity; I like complexity but too much makes me have to think and I don't play video games for that. But UFO 50 makes everything digestible.UFOSOFT have really outdone themselves here. Absolutely worth the money to revisit these "classics".
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible collection of games that celebrates the past, present, and future of game design. Many of the games combine classic and modern game mechanics in fun and inventive ways that we'll no doubt be seeing knock-offs of in the near future.I guarantee there will be a handful of games that will immediately hook you and you'll play straight to the end, but being able to quickly hop between games means you never end up feeling too bored or frustrated even with the ones that don't initially grab you.  You'll quickly sink many hours slowly progressing across a wide range of games by doing a dungeon run here, a puzzle there, another platforming level, or getting farther in the unbelievably well-made horror game.The only thing I'll caution is that many of the games intentionally lack any form of instruction, which may leave you feeling lost or frustrated. The games are 100% designed with this in mind, but if that kind of puzzling doesn't interest you then you might not want to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how to sell you on this if you aren't sold already. I'll simply say that these aren't minigames or microgames. These are FULL GAMES. You will repeatedly start a game and gradually discover that it is not *quite* like anything you've played before. And that sense of discovery is unique—I don't know what else you could find that gives you that exact feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the 50 games included in this pack, there's about 5 I'm not super into. Each of which I've seen someone online claim as their favorite. I don't know how a small team comes up with 50 unique game concepts and knocks so many out of the park, but they sure did it. Can't recommend enough, you will find a new favorite here guaranteed.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've had multiple games on emulators before. Few of the games would resonate with me and I would often quit when I got a game over. I never understand the appeal of that old school arcady design mentality until I started getting those games legally and on real hardware. Seeing your skill increase gradually as your performance improves on the 1st level is something gaming has lost these days. I never thought I would get that same experience outside of a roguelike in 2024. UFO 50 nails it and provides you with such a rich library of titles. The collection really allows players to make this selection their own. What games do YOU gravitate towards. Your journey through this library is made personal as you pick your favorites and put in the time. The sense of discover at every turn really sucks you into the narrative of this console. I can see myself pouring well over 100 trying to figure out every game. All of this for 25 bones. I don't know why they made this game like this but I'm so glad they did. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a retro compilation from another reality.  Very cool concept that I have been impatiently following for literally years.  So glad to have it in my hands.  THESE ARE NOT MINI GAMES.  These are GAMES.  You're getting 50 brand-new retro-style games for less than half the cost of a single AAA game.  VERY WORTH.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in awe that UFO 50 actually exists and with so many sub-games which are so much better than I expected them to be.  It has great games which are well within my wheelhouse -- a real-time tactics game, a sokoban game, a deck-builder -- but the in-game collectable system encouraged me to try out so many things outside the genres I usually gravitate toward and I have repeatedly found that those games are also fantastic -- a platformer-adjacent UFO piloting game, SHMUPs, even 'sports' games.  I'm repeatedly struck by how special UFO 50 is, and also left wondering if there will be anything that pulls off the same gimmick of a fictional retro game collection as well as it does, ever, in the future.  I'm 50 hours in, and I feel like I've barely scratched the surface of many games which I want to do a deep dive into!It's my 2024 game of the year, no question.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A really lovely celebration of classic and retro game design, interspersed with meta elements and modern tweaks. Some games wear their inspirations charmingly on their sleeves, while others really dive deep to create something wholly original. I think there is something for everyone in UFO 50, and even the games you may not vibe with will almost certainly be worth checking out just for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The ONLY controls are a D-pad and 2 buttons, for all 50 games. You could play this fully with a NES controller if you wanted! Or a keyboard! Or a DDR pad! But don't be fooled, some games are quite clever in their controls (button combos, press & hold, etc.) so there may be a larger moveset than you think.For the completionist, UFO 50 may be a dream or a nightmare. It's up to you. Play for fun and set your own goals. Winning any one game is an accomplishment; winning 50 will take dedication.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've barely scratched the surface of this collection, but I almost want to say each and every one of these gems of a game would be worth £18 on their own. You won't get along with all of them, but I personally have not found a single one out of the 25 I've picked up that I won't be trying again. Utterly captivating and wholly addicting, this collection is absolutely worth any price.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most audacious, imaginative, interesting, wonderful projects ever conceived. Cements Derek Yu as one of the most vital indie developers of his generation. A game design masterclass with a brilliant frame story and a metric f**k-ton of talent behind it. Makes the entire field of AAA games look like the pathetic dead-end waste of resources it is.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A great package of games. The vast majority of games are very original, it was rare that I could think of a similar game I'd played before. There's a lot of variety in genres, yet they're all well executed. Especially the strategy games are well made, with some really fun gameplay mechanics.Each game has three goals to achieve. which give little cosmetic rewards in the game selection menu. It's a nice inclusion, giving you an additional reason to play more of the games.The average quality of the games is high. The best games were so good that they could very well be sold on their own. There were a couple of games I didn't like, but it's no big deal when there are so many games included.If you'd like to play a variety of creative and mostly simple games with retro aesthetics, this is worth buying. The game is a great value even at full price, with so many complete games included.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This didn't click at all for me. I played plenty of the games available, and none of them had enough fun elements in them to play further. It is very technically impressive - it truly feels like an 80's videogame console, with really amazing pixel art and effects. As an avid old NES player, and yes, owner of an actual bloatware Action 52 cartridge - the appeal is there! It is nostalgic. It is very pretty.But it's not fun. The only game I got any fun out of was Pingolf. The game design on display here says on the store description "combining 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design". There's plenty of clever gameplay in that sense, it just isn't fun to play, basically none of it. Confusing RPG. Floaty platformer. Generic SHMUP. Streets of Rage clone. Yes I learned to play them, they just weren't fun! I feel the wrong ideas were followed in chase of that nostalgic display - would these games be of value as themselves or as part of a collection, or was it more that the developers wanted to make sure it FEELS like a game collection from 89? Would you actually WANT to play games from that era? Because whatever modern twist they added to the design, it wasn't enough.Right now it feels like a throwback bloatware collection. The appeal is purely nostalgia, the games are very shallow - as it was back then. It's sad, because I was expecting to surely find something really cool here, rummaging through this vast collection of games. The visuals and commitment to the bit is insane. I love games like these. I love Mossmouth.But UFO 50 didn't click, and there wasn't fun in it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game as a Spelunky fan wanting to see what Derek Yu was cooking up next. Game reminds me of times I'd play namco museum on my ds as a kid. Its really nostalgic, yet still pretty fresh. I haven't even played through all the games yet, and apparently there's some secrets I've yet to discover. Only critisism is that some of the games are a tad janky, but I guess you could see that as them being more authentic. Big reccomend

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bounced off these games hard because they felt like they wouldn't be much my speed. I am not used to playing NES games or any older, more brutal arcade style titles with little direction. I thought that I'd be shoveling through a pile of garbage for the few small gems that may be there. Boy was I wrong. The game is excellent. Lots of unique ideas, lots of exciting games of entirely different genres, local co-op, mysteries, beautiful art, carefully crafted music; it's truly a full package. Of these 50 games, I've tried a mere 7, beaten 2, and enjoyed several of those with the couch co-op functionality. There's still much more to see and do, and none of it has been dull thus far.I'd love to see more ambitious projects like this one and I sincerely hope that some of the games in this package get expanded upon into even bigger games, or maybe even inspire other games of a similar nature. There is a lot to love and I'm glad that I gave this a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game's existence is genuinely unbelievable. 50 is a hell of a lot of games, and even if it took a while for it to release, it is still a marvel of game development. Each game feels faithful to the NES era, but with quality of life improvements that have come with the growth of the games industry. Snappy controls and gorgeous pixel art. I have tried out a little over half of the games at this point, and  I can tell this is one for the history books. Most of the games I've tried so far have great replayability. Whether it's because of random generation or competing with friends for high scores, this is a game I can see myself playing for a long time.Do yourself a favor and buy this. It's 50 cents per game. It would be worth it if it was $60, but $25 is an outrageous deal. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I want to say something about the music. I'm extremely impressed by the amount and variety and (something that probably only musicians will notice) how there's microtonality/experiments with tuning/intonation in a lot of the tracks. While still managing to keep super catchy and powerful melodies.It's very innovative and fresh and I hope more video game composers do this. The games are very polished. They feel like full games on their own. With most of them you can clearly tell what was their direct inspirations. But they all have some interesting twist, so they don't feel generic. I'm very impressed with the amount of creativity and mastery of game design in this. If it looks like it's something you would like, you definitely will.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An essential purchase, and one of the best value games on Steam. At the time of writing, I've played for 13 hours, cleared two games and only tried four in total.Each individual game is masterfully designed to pay homage to real games from the era, but with modern game design twists that make them all much less frustrating than many of their counterparts from the "real world". Plus there's not one game here that is a straight "copy" of a real '80s title; every one of these 50 titles has some sort of hidden depth or clever mechanics to discover, and it's an absolute joy to get to know each and every one of them.The more I play it, the more it seems like an interactive work of art as much as a collection of games. Everything is deliberately designed to get you thinking about classic game design and how things have changed over time. This is so much more than just "Action 52, but good". It deserves to be required reading on game design courses -- and should be considered an essential part of every Steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: What a long wait for this one, eh?  Announced like eleventy billion years ago, this grand collection is finally here, and I've been quite excited for it.  Now, this one is kinda hard to review in the usual way...  What I want to do here is to give you a sense of what you'll really be getting here, because looking around, I've seen some complaints here and there about it, and it seems like some might be going into this not quite knowing what they'll get.The main thing to understand is that these are meant to be *true* retro-style games.  Properly emulating what games were genuinely like during the era that each one was released (mostly).  And if you didnt grow up with the NES (or similar systems from that time period of 8-bit consoles), these might seem rather strange in many ways.On Steam here, there are a lot of games that claim to be retro-styled, but in reality, that often just means the graphics... everything else about them is often very modern, and the size of the games is often quite big.  Often games like that have the sorts of mechanics in them that you really didnt see back then (often due to technical limitations, or design concepts that hadnt yet been realized), and so on.  Retro STYLE, but not truly representative of what actual retro games are like.That's not what this is.  You arent going to go into each of the 50 games and come away with like, a 20 hour experience with 80 levels and checkpoints and inventory systems and blah blah blah, for each single game.  That just aint what it was like back then, so that aint what you're going to get here.Just as an example, one of the games is called Magic Garden.  This is an arcade-style game, using the traditional "snake" mechanic of things trailing you, and having you grab things to build that up and then dropping them in marked places to get big points, avoiding enemies and such the whole way.  This all takes place on a single screen, and... that's it.  That's the game.  It gets progressively tougher as you go, and if you crash into anything bad, it's game over.  That's the extent of it.  Play to score points.  To many modern gamers, this probably sounds like it aint too much, but understand, this is seriously what a lot of games were like at that time.  This, back then, would have been released as a single, full-priced cartridge.  If you're not familiar with things from that time period, head over to Youtube and look up games such as Balloon Fight, or Clu-Clu Land.  Games of a similar scale, and indeed, they were full-priced products back then.  A game like Magic Garden, in this collection, very much takes after games like those.Similarly, you will run into elements that might seem very archaic, or things that the industry sorta left behind a long time ago.  There's one game that is soccer themed, sort of, and has you jumping around single screen levels, kicking the ball at enemies, which turn into food items when defeated.  This takes after the original Bubble Bobble, a very erratic platformer that used this exact design style (but you blew bubbles at enemies instead of launching a ball).  In a lot of modern games, you cant *really* lose.  Not truly.  You can always reload or go back to a checkpoint or whatever.  But many games werent like that back then.  In this particular game, you've got a couple of lives, it only takes one hit to kill you, and when you run out of lives, it's game over.  True game over.  No checkpoints, no reloading, no continues.  No saving the game either.  If you want to beat this game, you're going to have to do it in one sitting.  You're either good enough to do it, or you arent.  Unlike a lot of modern games, where you can pretty much always win eventually even with low skill because a real game over condition never happens.However, as you go chronologically further into the collection, the games start to get more advanced, less arcade-y.  Bigger, more expansive. Heck, there's a full-on JRPG in here.  Yet, even still, they will often use mechanics that might seem odd at first.  There's one game that is a horror-themed point and click adventure game.  A genre that isnt particularly uncommon even these days, but again, this is trying to emulate that old era, so a lot of the bells and whistles meant to smooth things out are not here.  Controls and UI and such are exactly as awkward as in old games like Shadowgate, and even that screwy room map from that game makes an appearance here (though it's just slightly less confusing than Shadowgate's map thing) as does loopy monsters just abruptly filling the screen, often leading to a quick death that comes out of nowhere.At the same time though, there are some things that are not quite accurate to that time, and typically for good reason. For instance, that JRPG has mechanics in it designed to reduce the hyper-grind that JRPGs back then were known for, because that element of those older games was just notoriously irritating to the point where, if kept in here, it could absolutely suck the enjoyment out of it.  Stuff like that.  And a bit of modern design trickles in at certain points.  Like in that garden game, enemies will very clearly telegraph where they're about to move, keeping things always feeling fair... which wasnt how things often worked back then.  Accuracy is great and all, but not if it just produces supreme irritation when it really doesnt have to.Creativity is also very high here, a lot of design concepts that are different yet familiar.  One game, Mortol, is this odd sort of puzzle platformer with a strange twist:  you need to die a lot, in specific places & ways, to progress.  But the mechanics that dont involve you drowning yourself or something all feel like they were taken right out of an old platformer, as does the general feel of the level design.  That soccer game is another example.  Plenty of games used the format it uses.  But that method of attack?  I cant think of a single thing that did anything like that.  NES games liked straightforward shooting or melee attacks.  That soccer ball sure aint that, and it makes for a much more dynamic experience here (which often was not the case back then).  Yet the game as a whole still feels accurate to the thing it's taking after.The other nice thing though is that, while accuracy is high, it does not try to unnecessarily emulate the many technical issues that often plagued older games.  NES games in particular were known for getting more than a bit loopy if there were too many sprites around at once (and that number really wasnt very high).  But that aint the case here, you can fully expect lots and lots of STUFF going on, often with big, vibrant sprites.One thing to keep in mind is that for the most part, these games are short.  Well, short by modern standards.  By retro standards, they're pretty typical.  On the NES, even many "big" games can be beaten in just a couple of hours (with RPGs typically being the exception).   However, replay value factors in here sometimes in ways that didnt really happen back then.  Some games use procedural elements for instance, which just didnt happen on consoles back then.I'm not quite sure what else to say here... it's hard to review a whole collection of stuff!  But I've loved every game I've tried so far.  That bug hunter one in particular is as addictive as caffeine.UFO 50 is clearly a love letter to an era of gaming that is long gone, yet still loved by many. As someone who grew up with and still plays old games, I'm very, very impressed to see such a high quality thing here, that truly feels authentic in ways almost no modern retro-style games manage, yet still having important differences where needed, and a level of creativity that didnt happen back then.  A very, very impressive design... and I've only gotten started with it. This game wont be for everyone, it's clearly aimed at a certain type of player.  But if it's your sort of thing, you're going to freaking love it... I know I do.

That being said, these games are fun, well made, and come at a crazy cheap price. There's something for everyone in it, and if one game isn't for you you're sure to find another that is. _childDocuments_.review: There's so much to say about this game. I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. It is such an ambitious game. There are lots of games with large scope, but it's all by the numbers. It's all logical geometric expansion. There are shockingly few games made in the last few years made with any sense of excitement, or any sense of developers pushing themselves and gaming to a new limit. UFO 50 is that game, it is the game that no one could even think of, Action 52 but good? Who could come up with such a game? Who could actually follow through with this vision, and not chicken out? And I'm not just calling out AAA developers, but even indie devs, where is the passion? Everyone is phoning it in, everyone is happy to coast doing logical, straightforward, iterative, incremental, comfortable progress. Not this game.So the games themselves. I haven't even tried all the games yet, but what I've seen is more than enough for the price of entry and then some. Every game has terrific spritework, and with lots of variety as well. Very quickly you will take for granted the consistently high standards for the visuals, unless you are constantly focusing to take it all in. Not only does the game look great, much more important is how instantly readable everything is. Clarity is sadly something neglected these days in games, even 2D sprite based games, not so here. The only thing that you can kinda tell it's made by 6 dudes making 50 games with, is that there isn't *that* much music compared to say how much amazing spritework there is. Pretty understandable and less something to knock against the game and more to make you realize what a herculean task this is. All the games control well, everything is responsive and intuitive. And, it shouldn't have to be said but it does, the game actually runs totally fine I've not had any issues with anything relating to performance. The overall length of games can be a little bit short, a couple games stand out with that, but usually within normal bounds for actual old school retro games. With Camouflage I 100%'d it fairly quickly, definitely a lot shorter than any retail puzzle game I've played but honestly it's smart, there probably wasn't much more to squeeze with its game design. I'm not usually a guy to advocate for short games... but when you have 50 yeah it's a little different lol. I haven't yet tried the JRPG, holding onto that one for later.The styling of the games is quite impressive. There are some more straight forward games you'd expect from a collection like this, like Elfazar's Hat and Fist Hell. Then you get real weird ones, like Golfaria and Waldorf's Journey. And many games that are ostensibly within a standard genre, yet with real unique distinctions and design like Night Manor and Valbrace. There's very little straightforward orthodox design, and typically that's reserved for styles of games that aren't in vogue. I cannot even tell you how happy that makes me, the developers' eyes were on the prize. No pointlessly reinventing the wheel here. Night Manor in particular, I've always wanted to enjoy point and clicks, but frankly I've never been engrossed in them besides like Snatcher. But Night Manor, there's just some very obvious streamlining the genre should have done decades ago, there's real actual danger and tension, and it makes sense. And the overall experience is engaging, and it just makes me ask, where are the point and clicks like this and why were they basically never made? When you can outshine so much of an entire genre's output... while making FORTY NINE other games, that's a success.Just to talk about a couple games: I like Bushido Ball, it's my favorite so far. Elementally fun game in the vein of Windjammers, with just a bit more extra elements to spice it up. The game is just fun, well made, and a head slapping moment of "why isn't anyone else doing this???"Rail Heist: This is the game that really got me going when I tried this collection. I tried a couple games real quick, and then hopped onto Rail Heist and wow it blew me away. Such a unique set up, turn based timed platformer heist cowboy game. The fact the developers weren't afraid of such strong binary states and logic, such as getting in front of a lawman with a loaded gun is an instant death, is what makes this game so interesting. I feel like this style of design is basically dead, nowadays everything is so 'analog' which makes everything very relative and easy to faceroll if you have any basic skill at games.Waldorf's Journey: Charming, unique, genuinely funny and oh so slightly haunting. My wife and a friend were watching me play this game with captive interest, constantly coaching me on every jump, giggling at the signs. I don't think I've seen people have this sense of wonder from just watching a game since childhood. I'd call that a success. It is a bit short, though I know I've missed some things.Then there's the frame narrative. It's a sort of creepy pasta thing or something. It seems interesting, but not exactly sure where it's going. I think I have a few ideas of how to dig deeper into it? There's a sort of haunted/demonic undertone to things... I don't like that stuff but eh IDK where it's going it might be cool. It was an obvious idea to do a loose frame narrative like this for such a collection, and I appreciate the obvious effort that went into it. I guess I'll see how it turns out.Anyway, if reading this review didn't make you want to immediately buy this game and play it you have to ask if you're even a real gamer. I like 2D games, I like retro games, but I generally just prefer 3D and more modern(ish) games. But even then, it is plainly obvious what an incredible achievement this collection is. If you aren't talking about UFO 50, you don't "get it" at all. This game is about the highest recommendation I can give for a game. It is a steal at 50 dollars, yet they're selling it for 25. Buy this if you have ever enjoyed one video game in your life for even a second.**Edit** I forgot to mention, this game is actually low key a fantastic party game. Tons of multiplayer games, easy to have quick games constantly swapping controllers. I don't think the developers intended for this, but it's a great feature.

_childDocuments_.review: Several of these games could easily have made there way into my 2024 top 10 games. The fact that they exist along side dozens of other, interconnected experiences makes ufo50 a game that I know I'll still be playing and thinking about 10 years from now. This was an absurd concept for such a small team to take on. But they did it in a way that overshot even the outrageous premise. I really didn't expect to enjoy some of the individual games to the extent that I have. As an example: mortol 1 is one of the best puzzle platformers I've ever played. I'd easily put it up against games like braid. I've replayed every level of mortol 1 several times and I'm still learning things. And that's 1/50th of UFO50. I haven't even tried all 50 games and I have 23 hours.
