_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 10 games out of the the available 50 but it really does hit you in the heart and remind you why you fell in love with video games in the first place. my personal favorite titles from what I have played is Magic Garden, a puzzle game cut in the same vein as Gomola speed on the TGFX 16 with a really nice and clean color palette. next is Kick club, which is a love letter to single screen action/puzzle games like Snow Bros and bubble bobble. Barbuta, which is a 2D side scroller action/adventure game, like a hybrid between Lode Runner and The tower of Druaga. lastly, Bushido ball, a deceptively simple 1 one 1 tennis/dodge ball hybrid, dipped in ancient Japanese flare, Almost reminds me of a Kunyu-kun sports game. there are games for every kinds of people here, (strategy games are my broccoli so i could barely play for more than a minute). UFO 50 is a definite must have for folks who grew up in the era of experimental games where video game archetypes are still in it's infancy and gaming trends have not been codified yet. 8/10 from me.Video games are fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Great, actually does what it advertised: doesn't feel like a parody or tongue-in-cheek version of old school games, but like playing very well made, very fun classic games, without the dated game design many actual 80s games. Some games that weren't too much fun in single player were a blast in local multiplayer. A couple of games in there that would be strong GOTY contenders if they had been released standalone, such as Valbrace, Party House, Devilition,  Mortol, and Magic Garden.It can feel kind of bogged down from the sheer amount of games, but they seem to almost all be well thought-out and fleshed out projects.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There's always a couple games from the collection that I am in the mood to play. Whether you want to game for 5 minutes or 5 hours there's some fun to be had.Also, going through and seeing the games advance over time in complexity, graphics, and audio is fun. I am looking forward to getting all the cherry ranks and learning more about the cryptic terminal!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFOSoft has quickly become one of my favorite developers. When their catalog is this good that they can put out a collection of 49 great-to-incredible games, they must have had die-hard fans in the 80s. Or maybe they collapsed because too many people played Combatants. Really though, UFO 49 (minus Combatants) is the greatest collection of games released. If you're a person who loves the variety that video games offer, you can't ask for a better sample platter than UFO 49. Just... skip Combatants.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: very fun. a lot of the games are just "what if we combine genre a with genre b" but with good design and polish. i feel some of the games don't really respect the players time though. they spent the time adding a terminal, why not add a password system? many games would be at least two times as fun if they had added a map. very many missed opportunities.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 20 hours in and only have 3 games gold, 1 game cherry, and barely scraped the surface of 25 titles total - half of the titular 50 you're delivered by UFOsoft. It's weird, it's hard, it's cryptic & loose in terms of "story", and it truly gives that feeling of exploration & discovery that can only come when you're dropped into foreign worlds with little to no direction. So yeah, it's a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was unsure how I felt because I sort of bounced off the first few games. Once I got further in and got to games that were more my speed I completely saw what people were talking about when they praise this game. What's nice as well is that once I was in the "classic game mindset" from playing other games, I returned to those first few I bounced off of and ended up enjoying what they had to offer! (Also the rumors are true, Mooncat is fantastic.) If you have a taste for the era these games are invoking, or even 2D indie games in general, I would highly recommend this. The games are highly varied and a lot more fleshed out than you would think in multiple ways, so there is bound to be something in here you come out loving.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a literal marvel--I don't know how they managed to make it so consistently good. I've played all 50 (beaten ~15) and very rarely did I ever find myself bored, underwhelmed, or frustrated. For every game that isn't really up your alley, there's 5 more that you'll absolutely love. This game feels like it shouldn't even exist--like someone just found a dusty cartridge and started selling its contents. Must play.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game (really 50 games) is arguably the best value you're going to find on steam. At 50 cents a game, it's a no brainer.  Unless retro style graphics make you physically ill, there's no reason not to buy this. This is what games from the 80s would have been like if they had the benefit of 40 years of reflection on what makes game design good. Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played. If you liked old NES and Genesis games that made you learn how to control the game well before you could progress, you'll like this collection. I would have payed the price of this game for the few games I've beat so far, and I still have 47 games to go. It is seriously such a cool idea, and all the different developers that worked on it did a great job. You can tell the Downwell and Spelunky guys worked on some of the games for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely believe that this might be the best game ever made. Every game is thoughtfully designed. Every detail is lovingly crafted. Gorgeous to look at, joyful to listen to, and thrilling to play. I am 40+ hours in and I have barely scratched the surface despite having played them all. Each is a fully-featured, complete experience, and several would be worthy of my $25 on their own. I have played thousands of games in my life and nothing I've seen has accomplished anything close to this. I own entire video game consoles with less notable games than this collection. What a gift.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you like video games from the bottom of your heart and have been playing for a long time or are open-minded and curious about history and towards many different gaming genres, then do yourself a favor and try this gem. I came to see it as a gift from talented developpers and a love letter to the gaming industry. This game is a collection of fictional games and every each and single game is different from the previous one, with well-thought gameplay and game design, many interesting mechanics and a lot of passion. I won't go into detailing what you'll find here but, if you enjoy discovery, challenge and thinking, you will be rewarded in many ways. This game might not be for everyone, I can understand that, but if you feel like an explorer and a challenger and aren't afraid of using your brain matter, most of the games here are brilliant, and plenty ! I've been amazed, more than once and I think it is completely worth the price. Heck, it's probably worth way more than that if I'm being honest. Good job UFOSOFT, your legacy is forerver !
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: derek and friends make good games. many such cases.edit: ignore negative reviews with short play times claiming the game is bad. it is physically impossible to have experienced this game to a degree that you can say "it's all bad" in under 3-4 hours.mooncat is worth the cost of entry alone.edit 2: goty
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: You're probably better off spending $25 on few full games rather than this monster. Even at $0.50 per game I don't see the value since a majority of the games aren't very fun or long. You've got stuff like Snake and Pong (with slight twists) mixed in with awkward SHMUPS and platformers. The games don't feel modern or retro, just cheap. What you get is basically on the tin: It's an experimental collection where you play games from a fictional developer from their first creation to their latest. There some cool ideas but the self imposed restraints limiting the games to an 80s feel really put a damper on the fun factor.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: at first I liked what it had to offer, the feeling of combing thru a fictional history of 80s gaming... then the novelty quickly wore off and I just felt like I was going through the motions with each one, it just felt like a chore, or playing games for the sake of playing them, hoping the fun would eventually come along, feel like I've wasted just under 2 hours of my life lol. I'd honestly have much preferred a collection of say 10-20 SNES style titles than 50 NES shovelware affairs, waste of money, do not buy unless you like action 52 i guess lol
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Retro gamers rejoice!Having played 30+ hours and counting, I felt like I had to delete and rewrite my previously positive review to give Mossmouth even higher praise. Night Manor is the S**T! Absolutely amazing atmosphere and cleverly well thought out puzzles. I'm daft as all hell and got stuck a few times, but eventually figured things out.Haven't played every game yet, but I also quite like Ninpek, Mortol, Velgress, Kick Club, Vainger (amazing and hard), Valbrace, Elfazar’s Hat, Rail Heist, Kick Club, Magic Garden, Party House and Pilot Quest (it gets really cool once you figure it out). It's a really varied collection, and you'll probably find yourself getting cherry on games you're not quite fond of first, like I did with Big Bell Race. Don't get me wrong, it's polished and fine, I'm just not into single screen track racing games.Overall the game is easily worth full price. If you get it cheaper, it's a hell of a deal.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Five of the hours I spent were just on one game (devilition). There's the cool idea of a game company's entire library building up over time, but even without the presentation, the collection would still be great with the quality and quantity of the games available. If I could find a game I loved from trying out just 10 of 50, then I'm certain that there will be a game you'll like too!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Several of the games in here could justify the price tag on their own. Not only is there an extremely impressive variety of games and genres in here, but most of them have more depth and nuance to them than you'd expect in a compilation of 50 games. This goes way beyond just being a compilation of 50 ideas thrown together. Mortol, Campanella, Night Manor, Caramel Caramel, Rakshasa, Star Waspir are just a few of my favorites and that's just scratching the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: just beat mooncat, felt like rewiring my brain! can’t wait to dive in to more games. little advice : don’t let Barbuta lower your expectations! keep trying different games because there are 49 other games to try too! Barbuta is fun if  you are into really REALLY retro experiences (which I don’t mind!)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like exploring a BBC Micro or early Amiga and a case of random floppies. Modern game design helps take the edge off in terms of controls and some design decisions but many games are difficult and require some time to learn and become good at. Quite a few are deeper than expected, there's a Metal Storm-esque mech metroidvania, a JRPG about cowboys, 2 fun twists on Humans/Lemmings, at least 2 excellent turn based strategy games, and an action based dungeon crawler to name a few. Everyone will have at least one favourite game out of the collection, probably from the more complex ones, but even the smaller arcade style games are fun to play though some don't entirely follow through with their ideas and feel a little too basic.There's also a meta story about a fictional developer for a fictional 8-bit system and hidden codes you input to unlock a few different things including alternate modes for some games and a hidden extra game. Even if you don't engage with this part of the package it's still worth the price of entry as the bulk of the content lies in the games that are all unlocked and presented from the start. Some of these are so good the contributing developers really need to expand those ideas. The micro point and click horror game in particular is a 10/10 worth the price of entry on its own. Similarly the Metal Storm style metroidvania needs a sequel, no questions asked.Lastly, the negative: difficulty in some games is punishing for the modern gaming mindset and might put some people off before they discover the joy of exploring and coming back to these games like you would in the '80s. It's not a knock on UFO 50 for being difficult, but a few of the games would have greatly benefited from at least a small leaflet style manual to clue the player in on a bit more information, even us older gamers can be left in the dark on a couple of small details that would have not been a frustration if explained or hinted at.Verdict: Buy it if you want an instant collection that far surpasses its value. Feels like picking up an old BBC Micro at a car boot sale and rummaging through the disks to see what's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible, the creativity on display in this game is honestly frustrating and only because it makes me question if I can even compare with my own as an artist/gamedev. There is almost 100% certainty that there is a game on here that clicks with you, and more plausibly there's multiple that are gonna click. Sure, not every game on here I think is great, but the sheer fact that most are well put together with interesting mechanics, and have art and design that imitates the third generation of consoles so well is wild.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if UFO 50 will change the way that other developers think about game development, but I hope it does. I have not played all 50 of the games in this pack yet, but every game that I've played is a small piece of art woven into the tapestry of UFO 50. Although each game has simple controls and (relatively) simple and intuitive mechanics, the process of picking a random game, not being told what to do, and discovering not just the controls, but the genre, ideas, and feels of the game is captivating. This is not a game made with anyone in mind: It's made with the experience of games in mind. If you love games (which you probably do if you're reading this review), this game is for you. You won't enjoy every game in these 50, but regardless of your tastes there will be something that hits.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it at first and then refunded it. After watching some youtube videos of people playing it I decided to give it another shot. I now have over 100 hours in and it's almost all I want to play. The desire to get golds and cherries is insatiable. I highly recommend this game(these games) and if you were thinking about giving it a second chance go for it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: MUST PLAY if you have any interest in 8bit games whatsoever. The whole package has so much soul its hard to put into words, with several game genres so there's something for everyone. There's also the joy of discovering the games one by one and trying to finish/cherry them and understand their mechanics since the instructions are minimal. It's the closest thing to finding a "9999 in 1" cartridge in a closet, along with a console forgotten to time.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The games are very minimalistic in their essence, which is all right, I guessThey are not minimalistic on its features, though, they are pretty inventive and captivating, which is goodWhat really irritates me is this: They are extremely minimalistic in the explanation of how the games work.They don't explain - or even hint - the existence of many possibilities of the gameplay. You often find yourself playing a game for 15 minutes just to find a really basic feature that was there all the time and the game expected you to either guess it or google it.I was right away hooked to this game Bug Hunter. It was not easy to get far in it, but I was very involved with it and kept trying. After 40 minutes of gameplay I found out that you can actually target and destroy energy tanks, which make them explode and kill enemies with it, and that is a VERY important feature. Took me even longer to find out that if you move from high grounds to the top of an enemy, you instakill it. There are many other examples of things that should DEFINITELY be explained, if anything, just out of respect for the player. After you actually learnt by trial and error how the game works, it gets WAY less difficult, and it makes me wonder: what's the idea? The challenge is mostly to understand the game than actually beating it? Is that what people are calling good design?I played bug hunter for like 45 minutes, but didn't want to test all other games, because that would take me much more than 2 hours and I wouldn't be able to refund it. I tested a bunch of them, though and the same trend was very apparent.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is an undeniable GOTY for 2024. It's 50 games, several of which you could easily play for 8 hours by themselves. And there's 50 of them! As a big fan of not just spelunky and downwell, but skorpulac too, a game by Eirik Suhrke, I knew UFO 50 would be wonderful. And there is, amongst the 50 games, a game with a very similar structure to spelunky 2, and another that's quite similar to downwell. UFO 50 is just the best
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Nah, sorry. While I often play and replay old games, the 8-bit era ones are always the ones I am most divided about, even though I grew up playing them and I often launch something ZX-Spectrum-like after reading another issue of Retro Gamer magazine. I own 12 gaming consoles, for god sake, including a Panic Playdate - but none of them are 8-bit ones. And there are reasons for it.I understand the effort that went into these games and I understand the joy people can get out of them if they are really into 8-bit games, specifically.But personally, after reading reviews and being told that this "will remind you why fell in love with games in the first place", by "combining a familiar 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design" I expected something else.I fell in love with games for many reasons, but junk controls, permadeath, complete lack of instructions and unforgiving difficulty were not one of them. Just because there was no choice back in the 8-bit era does not make it somehow better than it was. It wasn't.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is arguable one of the best computer game investment that I have ever made. I cannot emphasis this enough, there are FIFTY fully fleshed out good games. They might not all necasarily be the perfect game for you, but their is so much variety. I have decided to go through each game chronologically (getting the trophy and the cherry before I progress), and I am upto game 6. I can't tell you which one is my favourite because they have all have something radically fresh and interesting to offer. I really hope that in another 7 to 8 years you bring out a UFO 50 '2'. Keep up the awesome work and thank you for this proper treat.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Just to preface, I'm approximately 50 hours into UFO 50. I have played 35 of the 50 games in chronological order and fully completed 18 of them. A full completion is referred to as a 'cherry' in this game. This game is incomprehensibly ambitious and I still can't wrap my head around how this was ever made and released at such an inexpensive price point. There really are 50(!) video games in this pack, each of which could have been released for $5 and nobody would bat an eye. Of course, some are better than others but there is not a single one that I've played that could be seen as being objectively bad. As you work your way through this fictitious developer's chronology, you'll notice a marked increase in video game complexity and scope, which makes me so much more excited to try out the remaining 15 games. Many of the earlier, more simplistic games took me 1.5-2 hours for a cherry completion but the newer RPGs, puzzle games, strategy games, metroidvanias, and even an immersive sim-like are taking me upwards of 5 hours per game to cherry.One tangential complaint I have is this game's handling of achievements, it should have shipped with 100-150 achievements with 2-3 per game to meet the gift, gold, and cherry requirements. The current achievements are extremely unrewarding and frankly dull.I believe UFO 50 is a must-own for any gamer who even remotely enjoys the NES/SNES era of video games, and for those who don't, this is an excellent introduction and what may become an eventual deep dive into what made these games so iconic. Almost all of these games, if released in the 80s, would be talked about like Mario and Zelda are today. A tremendous accomplishment from Mossmouth.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game more than anything because it felt "important," like a seminal piece of indie gaming and I wanted to support it. I don't necessarily dislike games from the 8-bit era, but I don't have any great love for them. I expected to find it interesting more than fun.But it is fun! Very fun! I heard how unique and fleshed out each game was, and I'm still in disbelief. Not only does each game feel totally different, they're all full and complete games with clear care put into them. And, I repeat, they're a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This Collection is a Love Letter to Games.50!!! Very good games, in a lot of different genres, there is not a single bad one.Art, gameplay and soundtrack with so much originality and character.This is one of the greatest things to happen to gaming, I hope they do more of this in the future, but Im happy with what we got right now
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There was once a man named Vinny Vinesauce who said "This is like the best games of multiple game jams bundled together" and honestly i couldn't even begin to explain how perfect that quote is.You have this very creative game with just enough meat on its bones to try again and again without getting boring and the game is like "Cool! Now here's 49 MORE GAMES JUST LIKE THAT".
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of the year by far. This triggered so much nostalgia in me despite all of the games being new. They did an amazing job taking modern game ideas and saying, what if someone made a deckbuilder game on the NES, and much more. They even triggered my nostalgia for renting a cool looking game and bringing it home only to find out it has inexplicable and impossible to understand controls.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: "50 actual good games, no filler? Yeah right, not possible." You'd be forgiven if that's your thought. Well, after nearly 24 hours of play and having tried maybe a third of the games on offer... I can safely say I have found 0 filler games. Not only that, I have found at least 5 awesome games, and numerous other great experiences, and many others that will probably be awesome once I sink time into them. The games do seem short, the ones I've beaten have only taken 1-3 hours, but times that by 50 and there is plenty of play time. There are also several games that are worth playing over and over even after completion.Did I mention I haven't even tried 2/3rds of the collection yet?!This is a game that I'm quite confident I will happily sink hundreds of hours into!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A one-of-a-kind collection of some of the greatest retraux games you’ll ever play. You can put multiple hours, occasionally even tens of hours, into a single game, then boot yourself back to a menu with 49 games of similar depth. No long tutorials, no annoying expository cutscenes. Just boot up a game, watch a 30 second intro, and get to work figuring it out. UFO 50 is unforgettable in so many ways that can’t be articulated. It’s something everyone should own because it, without a doubt, genuinely contains something for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Ufo50 brings a lot of innovative gameplay in the form of 50 other (mostly) bite sized games. Just when you think you're hooked on Porgy's sublime underwater world and punishing loop, you discover how fun Campanella's movement and simplicity is. It's interesting trying to figure out how each game works, and if you don't like one of them, you can just move on to something else. There's truly something for everyone here!I also want to take a moment to talk about the music. Eirik Suhrke composed over 300 unique tunes, which is INSANE to think about. You can tell a lot of love was poured into the soundtrack, which is, as a composer, very important to me.Huge congrats to team Mossmouth for achieving a release of this magnitude and for making me feel like a kid again. PLAY FOREVER!!!All that being said, Ufo50 is my GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 20 hours into UFO 50 now and I've only 100%'d 2 of the games. So much of this is just pure replayable arcade fun. There are a couple stinkers that aren't for me but plenty of interesting and fun games in here. You probably won't like everything in this pack - but you're guaranteed to find several somethings in here to enjoy. This is the DEFINITIVE retro game love letter.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! I haven't even tried half of the games and I've enjoyed each one of them so far. Here are some games I like that I keep going back to:Night Manor - Horror/PuzzleSeaside Drive - Action/ArcadeBug Hunter - Strategy/PuzzleLords of Diskonia - Strategy/ActionI've heard that there is a Metroidvania, Dungeon Crawler, and RPG in this collection as well. I'm really looking forward to those, as I'm sure they'll be fantastic!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of 8-bit games, buy this collection. If not, it may be hard for you to enjoy these games. UFO 50 is a collection of 50 different, complete games, from a fictional system that never existed. You can play them in any order. Each game shows the year it was made and they get more complex as the years go on.There are many different genres to experience. Platforming, strategy, RPG, turn based tactics, RTS, sports and many more. You probably aren't going to enjoy every game in the collection, but with 50 games, you're going to find something to latch on to. These are not mini games. Each game has a beginning, middle and end. Each game also has a bonus objective that you can try to achieve. If you satisfy the requirement you get an item for the garden. The garden is a special screen that you can visit from the main menu that will display all of the items you've received. When you are on the garden screen, you will see a multi story house and a lawn. It's fun trying to unlock the item from each game.There's a lot of mystery to these games, which I enjoy. There are no manuals and you often won't know what to do, but you learn by playing and exploring, which is how it used to feel to play NES games. There is an excellent CRT filter. I like playing with the "soft" filter, which adds just enough texture to really make the games pop. I hadn't really been following this game, but it sounded interesting and I gave it a try. I have to say my initial reaction after playing for the first time was negative, because I wasn't blown away by the first games that I played. But something about this game kept me coming back for more. The more I played, the more I started to see the actual depth in each game and the full breadth of what this collection delivers. Check this game out, and enjoy playing a fictional console from the past that you wish you had growing up.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is looking like its my GOTY for 2024. Nothing else released this year has had me so hooked on every single little detail of its existence as a whole.The game has this sense of connection between the titles within, despite each game being a unique experience, and some even being direct sequels to others. Playing with friends I've found a couple of games we could play again and again for what is potentially years down the line. Multiplayer has plenty of function- half of the library has a multiplayer mode, but there's also so much to enjoy by yourself within what is literally 50 full games. Some short and sweet, but still fun for what they are. I've not even played every game in the collection and truly believe I've already gotten my moneys worth. Multiple titles within the collection are titles I could see myself paying for as standalone titles. Compiled, this is essentially 50 cents per game in a pack of 50 games. That value is insane, and everyone involved with this project should be so very proud of the creation they've spawned into our world.Today is 9/27/24, 9 days after the games release. I checked Global Achievement stats, and its displayed that NOBODY has beaten every single game in the collection. As of writing this review completion achievements are at 0.0%If that isn't a solid testament of people getting caught and hooked onto the games here, I'm not really sure what else is.P.S. Some of these titles are brutal as balls for no reason when you first play them. But once you get the hang of them its more fun that it could have been had it been easier to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It says all over the store page but it really takes playing it to get it through to people: these aren't minigames. Each of the fifty is a bonafide, full-blown video game with hours of content (in some cases at least a dozen) and surprising replay value. I can count at least ten I'd happily have paid for as standalone games, and here they all are for effectively fifty cents a pop. Really can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Yea, this one bangs. GOTY for me and an absolute recommend. I bought this to dive into right before a long flight and DAMN what a perfect steam deck title also!UFO 50 captures something really special, and is overflowing with charm from the creators packed into every pixel and sound in the games. It gave me the "Ratatouille Moment" of remembering being a kid playing the NES and SNES on a little tv at home, playing tons of random games that seemed impossible to beat and explained little to nothing to you yet you can't put it down because you know there's so much more to discover. Then going to school and hearing people talk about new techniques they discovered and secrets, intense strategies and skill to master games that have such simple mechanics but a large skill ceiling. Man, what a feeling. UFO 50 humbled me very quickly and reminded me of what it's like to just be absolutely awful at a game where the only action is jumping and moving.Nostalgia posting aside, U50 offers a GREAT bang for your buck as far as variety goes, some more fleshed out than others and some that I would legit pay 10-20$ for solo. The only thing I would say I'm not into is how difficult a few of them are, and the barrier of entry for enjoying a handful of titles is a bit intense. That only goes for a few titles though, and honestly that difficulty spike really does play into the feel of booting up a NES/SNES title back in the day and getting your ass beat by it. But yea, can't recommend this enough. What a cool game! My favorites are Party House, Camoflauge, Bushido Ball, Pilot Quest, and Min&Max.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: game rips. incentivizes players to play for score but makes it fun for the masses. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best gaming experiences of my life. I am simply taken back by the extent of polish, ingenuity and pure fun that this title oozes out. Each new game is a delight and a treasure, with the arc of "Cool art" to "Wait how do you play this" to "I feel like a genius and this game is so smart" to "Why is this tiny little experience not a full game? It has a killer soundtrack and, despite its aesthetic, many of its mechanics feel fresh. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible collection of games. Every one of them is designed with intention and creativity. This game has it's hooks in me bad! _childDocuments_.review: Very well made and precise with a great deal of depth. _childDocuments_.review: Played each game at least once, beating a few here and there. This collection has a lot to offer, there's guaranteed to be games you latch onto, and others you bounce off of. All have a difficulty that requires you explore and learn the games rather than power through them, but I think there's a lot of strength in the game design once you do learn the ropes. There's plenty to love about the collection, the dusting off of cartridges, the consistent color palette, the garden, the multiplayer - its all the little special touches and polish that really bring this collection together.I would really recommend this game to anyone who cares about design, anyone with a steam deck, or anyone nostalgic for those plug-and-play TV games, it really is a powerhouse of a collection and I found myself liking it more than I thought I would! _childDocuments_.review: I do not understand the hype for this mini-game collection nor the overwhelmingly positive reviews. The store page proclaims "These are NOT minigames or microgames" but many of them literally are and many are very shallow though some are more substantive. I get that it aims for an old Atari or NES vibe, of which many will be one-trick arcadey style games, but good lord it takes all the wrong parts of those antiquated games. For me, the thing I like about old games are the simplistic controls and straightforward game design, not the crushingly rigid game controls and harshly uncaring user experience. I've not played all the games yet and there is a smattering of the one's I've played I do like. I'm sure I'll like a few more but most are dead to me and all carry some sort of grievance(s) knocking the whole experience down.Many games are rigid to the point of being wretched. For example, at least one game has ladders you must climb but you cannot approach them while holding the climb button (up/down). No, you must stand in just the right spot then release all movement and climb buttons and then carefully only press the climb button. You also cannot jump onto the ladder or off of the ladder - you must painstakingly climb every single rung. Additionally, in this game all movement, including ladders, is excruciatingly slow. To hit every room on the "map" There's no game save or save states.There's a turn-based RPG and its in-game menu is atrocious. Would you like see how close each party member is to leveling up? That's not in the overview menu. You have to go into the stats page for each one. Can you cycle though the stats page for each character? Nope, you must back out, navigate to and select the next character. The left and right directional buttons do nothing. Also, half the screen is empty. Sure, very outdated games behaved this way but that's not what I liked about them.All games only utilize 2 buttons in addition to movement, not even a 3rd button start/pause/menu (there is a global system/pause menu). Some require mashing but there's no option to have a secondary "shoot" button set to auto-fire, for instance. One game has a built in auto-fire for its weapon but only one batch of 4 shots and you have to shoot switches so if you don't press and release quickly enough then you'll just turn the switch back off. Ugh.Many games have bizarre mechanics. These can be interesting and add to the game but they are almost never explained. Figuring out games is almost entirely trial and error. There will be lots and lots of error. They could have included "instruction manuals" for folks who aren't all that into trail and error and error and error. Every game is rife with some sort of grievance, if not several grievances. Whether this be horrible difficulty (by way of things like pixel perfect controls as opposed to any compelling gameplay design), bewildering mechanics, or just plain bad UI.One awful UI is the game menu. For some reason this mindlessly sticks to the 2 button only schtick. Want to cycle the sort options? Nope, no button for that, you must go into the system menu, never mind the 8 dead buttons on the controller (hours later I accidentally discovered if you try scrolling off the list of games you can change the sort option.. great thing to hide...). Wonder what each game even is? Well, you have to actually play it because there's no screenshot or anything when you hover over it and to even see basic info, like loosely what genre its like, you have to manually open a details popup for it, which is vapid, and you cannot cycle games from this popup. You have to cancel out, navigate to the next, and then open the tiny little vapid info popup again. Again, I get what it's going for but really they could have done something like "back of the box" info/art for each one.

_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is what happens when you ask a game developer what their "desert island game" would be.This collection is truly remarkable; there is something for literally everyone.The developers did a remarkable job creating a mood and atmosphere surrounding the IP's of this fantasy console. Each game feels distinctly unique, but holds the same kinda of familiarity between them that really sells the console as a cohesive entity.Derek Yu and his cohort of impassioned developers have done something truly artistic here. It's so refreshing and inspiring, and they pulled it off flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's not easy to understand the scope or enormity of the achievement that is UFO 50. It's a love letter to a bygone era or maybe a call to action about an era you missed. There's a indescribable joy of getting a box of games and trying them out one by one. Naturally not every game will speak to you, others might feel like they've been waiting for you to discover them your whole life and you are amazed that it took this long for you to discover it. This game is romantic, enthralling, fascinating and shows what this medium is capable of. On the off chance you've made it this far and it isn't crystal clear. You should buy this game and play it immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent collection of games. Such a wide variety of aesthetic inspirations, genres, and difficulties. And of course, the framing of this all being the software output of a fictional game company, from the faux-historical blurbs discussing which developer did what and so on, to the "sequel" and "spin-off" games, just adds so much charm.I haven't found a dud so far (have at least booted up around 20 of the games at this point), but my particular favorites right now are Camouflage, a clever stealth-puzzle game where you control a chameleon who has to strategically reach various locations in order to change colors and walk past enemies undetected, and Overbold, a Smash TV-like top-down shooter where you fight waves of enemies in an arena, acquire prize money to buy power ups, and can optionally (and should probably if you want to stand a chance at the end) add extra enemies to the fights to up your winnings- at the risk of losing, of course.Definitely going to end up being my favorite game to come out this year, and while it's too early for me to say for certain yet, I could possibly see this end up being one of my favorite games ever (a descriptor I'm picky about giving out).
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: only opened a few so farI've gotten:A weird alien horse racing management simA DOS throwback suffering platformer-explorerAnd a sweet driving-themed shmupThe presentation is absolutely delightful and I can't wait to explore all theseIt really does feel like you discovered a dusty bin full of floppies

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially worried that even if the games weren't minigames that they'd be derivative like most game comps like this. I was dead wrong. _childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game highly enough. 50 games, filled with great hits, good music, some compelling stories and loads of secrets. One of the games has an additional 50 microgames, and there's even a hidden 51st game. It's endless amounts of fun.I truly believe this game has something for everyone in it. There's a huge range of experiences, from pick up and play high score based games, platformers, puzzlers, point and click horror games, to even full-blown RPGs (plural). Now price that all at £20/$30 and you can see why it gets high recommendations.I could put recommendations in about what I like but I haven't even opened half of the games after 27 hours. Everyone will find something in this collection to enjoy, and I don't see how it can't be my game of the year.Play forever.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The most impressive game(s) I've played in a long, long time. It's made me reexamine what exactly I appreciate about gaming, largely due to the scope and presentation. Buying UFO 50 is not like buying a game, it's like buying a console with a built-in library. As a result, it comes packaged with history (even if it is made up) and an unmatched variety. I think this collection is most appealing to old school gamers who can embrace unforgiving difficulty, opaqueness, and simplicity. If you prefer a more polished experience, there are still many games in here that are very modern-sensible. Pretty much every game has some recognizable IRL counterpart, some old and some new. There are several games that, on their own, I would never really think to play more than a tiny bit of. But because they're in this collection, they have an added context that makes me want to revisit them. Partially for the completionist mindset of getting gold disks, but also because it's fun and rewarding to play through the history of a game series. For example, the in-game lore mentions that Mooncat was meant to be a sequel to Barbuda. That relationship informs you to have an exploratory approach through the games. There is so much more I could say, but I haven't even played nearly half the games on here, so I might add more to this review later.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is an anthology of games made by an incredible team of indie developers, covering dozens of genres, styles and several eras of game-making. There's a little bit of everything here, from adventure game horror to idle clickers to scrolling beat 'em ups, and with varying difficulties from laid-back fun to some of the hardest games I've played. You won't love every game equally, but you will find your own game of the year in the anthology somewhere, and the experience of rummaging through the collection for the first time and trying everything out is something no other modern release can really offer.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I dont think ive ever seen a love letter to video games quite like UFO 50. Its so immeasurably impressive that the devs were able to capture so many genres and niche little "NES throw away" title feelings. Every one of these games feels like I could dig it out of a bargain bin for 5$ and I mean that with the highest regards. Theyre fantastic, theyre clunky, theyre weird, and some (not all) would be ahead of their time. What a beautiful thing this collection is. My only note is, in true NES fashion, the games are pretty hard. Barbuta game of the year 1985-forever
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 1.5 hours of my playtime is currently just in one game. I can see myself spending a lot of time in this collection. I can't believe there actually is 50 full games in this collection. And so far each one I have played has felt like it understood what was good in older games while also modernising it enough for it to be enjoyable still. Glad Mossmouth found these 50 games in someone's storage unit.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I forgot that 8-bit games are harder than Dark Souls games.This is the legitimate equivalent to those 50-in-1 Game Boy cartridges or Plug-n-Play controllers they used to sell at toy stores.Just pick whatever game disc looks interesting/sounds interesting from the description and try it out. There's definitely something for everyone that likes playing games, and I found a few games super compelling (Golfaria and Max & Mini are phenomenal in my opinion, and there's a few more that I'm saving for later that I'm sure I'll love).But the games are all definitely more akin to NES or SNES games (leaning more towards NES), so if you know you don't really like games from that era, this may not be right for you.UPDATE: Holy **** do yourself a favor and start Pilot Quest first, it gather resources in the background while you play other games in the collection and you'll save a LOT of time if you just check in on it in-between games. Don't leave it for the end like me.

_childDocuments_.review: I havent played all the games yet but its impossible that you can get this and not find a game you love. the ones ive played are all really well made and take the best parts of those classic games and puts a modern spin on their mechanics. At 50 cents a game this is totally worth it.edit: played some more games. played Mooncat. what the ♥♥♥♥ was that. new favourite for sure
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I usually wait until I have completed games before reviewing, but I may never complete this, so after playing maybe a dozen titles I have to say that this isn't just a collection of 50 mini-games, this is a collection of 50 bangers.  Many of them are the best iteration of the game idea that I have seen, and I think it is a strong statement against the current state of the games industry when lower production value can deliver superior experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The price is wrong. This game should cost $200. maybe more? A few years ago I spent a few months building a home arcade cabinet with a raspberry Pi inside of it loaded with all my childhood nostalgic games. It was a fun build but I hardly ever play it. Most those old games don't hold up well and its mostly the memories and  nostalgia that is delivering the dopamine not the gameplay.  What a wonderful gift UFO 50 is... Instead of struggling through borderline unplayable titles from my childhood and scraping the bottom of the barrel of my mind for those last bits of nostalgia, UFO 50 just sets down a brand new fresh pot of fun games that an alternate reality me is probably nostalgic for. I did not expect to enjoy these games. I thought this would be a semi-cringe attempt to make games that look old and play bad, but these games actually are good. They are good in the way you remember those old games being, and not how they actually were.  The day I got it I played for 14 hours straight and I have only opened about 20 of the titles. There are so many of those titles I need to go back to and explore further because I honestly was just skimming the surface on them to see what the collection has to offer. These games are amazing. I am seriously considering another stand up arcade build with just UFO50 inside. Thank you devs. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just banger after banger after banger. Every game in the collection is like "oh I won't like this one", but as soon as you play enough to try and get the little trinket for the in-game terrarium collection you're hooked and knuckling down to really beat it. I boot up one game then look back at the clock and 6 hours have passed by."Overwhelmingly Positive" is well deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: So many of these games are incredible, both for single and multiplayer play. Each one is packed with novelty and creativity, and you are missing out if you don't give them a try. There are also some that could be standalone games by themselves. A few of my favorites falling into that camp are Mini and Max, Night Manor, Party House, Quibble Race, and Grimstone. This is not just some variety pack or a retro game throwback. It's something truly special that will impress you and subvert your expectations many times over.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: How do you even review an anthology like this? It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome and you'll more than likely resonate with more than a handful of the games for long enough to make it worth the asking price. I personally got hooked on Avionos until I 100%'d it. That took a few hours, which appears to be around or below  the average time it would take to complete a majority of these games, to say nothing of the games that seem like they could take dozens of hours for me to beat. Basically every game is rife with bespoke music and art that really helps sell the illusion that they're all unique products developed over several years by the same fictional studio. In some cases controls or design can feel antiquated for the benefit of authenticity. It's nothing like this package, but if you like the surprising depth and layers of the Spelunky games you will probably get a kick out of this too.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the best bang for your buck in terms of sheer variety since The Orange Box. Even if a particular game’s hook isn’t for you, you can still enjoy placing it in the timeline of the metatextual narrative to understand how UFOSoft evolved in tastes and capabilities over the years. The attention to detail is what really gets me. In Barbuta (literally game 1), they went out of their way to simulate the buzz of an old computer hitching while loading the next scene. Such attention is present in every single one of the 50 games. Extremely well done and it’s clear that the 8 years of development were well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Assuming you play each game for only 6 minutes, thats 5 hours of gameplay. Then you go back and play the 10ish games you really enjoyed, thats gotta be atleast 8 hours of gameplay right there. Im currently at 18 hours played and ive only beaten one of the twenty game i wanted to go back to. This game is well worth $25 even if you hate half the games. This feels like one of those chinese emulator machines where you can play a bunch of ripped nintendo games, except from a universe where game design was 20 years ahead. Alot of these are games really fleshed out.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I already know that this is my GOTY for 2024. Yes, it's actually that good. UFO 50 is downright insane for what it is and for such a low price point. The developers put so much love, effort, creativity, and thought into this monstrous project that I'm completely in awe.This game is an absolute must have if you love retro games and are interested in topics such as video game history, game design, ludology, art, and/or experimental storytelling. There's so much content to digest here, they obviously took much inspiration from many beloved video games released in the 80s and early 90s. I don't think there's a single game I dislike, all of them range from good to beyond amazing.If you really care about seeing all the secret then you'll likely be spending months if not years on this/these game(s).
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

And yet, the sum is greater than the parts, as each game seems to add to the universe of which they were uncovered, a sort of cohesion between them all.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game/games! Possibly the most pleasant surprise of my gaming career. I cannot recommend this game enough and hope all can bask in its glory.On a more serious note, this game has something for everyone, tower defense, shooters, metroidvanias, dungeon crawlers, and much much more. I've only played about half the games so far and found many to be a fantastic time. As long as you don't absolutely hate retro games this one is a must play, and if you do hate them you this one might just change your mind
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Keeps the best part of old-school games (not wasting your time, genuine challenge without being obnoxious for the sake of it, doing more with less) while still benefiting from modern design and smoothness. These are the games we could have gotten 20 years ago and didn't. They're here now, for like 50 cents a pop. Hell yeah. Don't start with #1; log in to Pilot Quest (which has some idle game aspects you can get started right away) and then try Ninpek, Big Bell Race, Devilition, and Bushido Ball for a nice sampler pack.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like how I remember those old Dreamgear 50-in-1 plug in plays I had as a kid in the mid 2000s feeling. They came in clutch during the post-Hurricaine Katrina fallout and despite those being not the best made games, having 50 of them to pick from still always felt so exciting. I never expected to ever get that feeling again but this game gave that to me and more. I've been excited for this game since it was annoucned 7 years ago and it's surpassing the expectations I had for it. I genuinely think this might end up being my game of the year and I've only played 6 of the 50 games so far. The team at Mossmouth really took the time they needed for this game to shine and it shows. It's something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: When I looked at this game I was concerned that the high amount of games would mean it would be a  quantity over quality situation. I bought it anyway-reviews were good and it was from the creator of spelunky. Unfortunately the developers didn't seem to make this game because they had 50 great game ideas. They came up with the gimmick first to exploit nostalgia then came up with the games after, filling it with shovelware.Take Ninpek for example. It's a simple scrolling platformer. You can jump and fire a projectile, and of course you die in one hit. That's it-no mechanics or gimmicks. That's the whole game. The collection is filled with crap like this. The excuse from defenders of this game is it's supposed to be like this because it's inspired by their boomer consoles. That doesn't make these games any more fun.While there is a ton a games here covering many genres, they are so shallow there is no reason to play them over dedicated alternatives.There is a JRPG here-but why play it over dedicated games like Sea of Stars/Chained echoes etc?Why play the crappy beat 'em up over Streets of Rage 4?Why play the Metroid clone over the many, better games in this genre on Steam?Why play the crappy platformers over the hundreds of better games on Steam?There are a few good ideas here, but you have to dig through the garbage to find them. Even then, the good games feel undercooked-but I guess that's what happens when you have to meet an arbitrary target of 50 games.If you're an aging millennial 'retro gamer' who is obsessed with collecting boomer consoles and nostalgic about shovelware you will probably love this game. If you are not a part of this group, and just want to play good games, stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: well UFO 50 does exactly that and oh boy has each game so far been exceptionally good in its own category. there will be genres here that probably wont work for you, but even I could still appreciate the work put into those games (specifically even though Block Koala isn't really for me, I still enjoyed the gameplay)in terms of length per game some have exaggerated this fact, in reality it varies between an arcade style game that's beatable within 15 minutes, to a full fledged 3-6 hour experience, to time wasters that drag on even longer!so far I went through roughly 40 games and beaten 14 of them, I'd recommend that you take your time with each game to give 'em a fair shake instead of speed running through all 50 and then playing 'the best one'Highlights: Devilition, Kick Club, Mooncat, The Big Bell Race, Waldorf's Journey, Caramel Caramel, Diverson top of the massive game collection there's a "meta secret" sprawling through the games, kinda like how Animal Well has multiple layers, UFO 50 has a 'treasure hunt layer' of sorts.

_childDocuments_.review: addicting, amazing collection of "retro" games. the difficulty of the games is offset by the ability to jump to a new one whenever you're feeling frustrated, so you're always getting new experiences and slowly getting better at all of them. at least, that's how I play it, and I've beaten 4 games already with 23 hours in the game

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is one of the best games I have ever played and potentially the best indie game to ever release. It takes all the lessons learned throughout decades of game development and applies them to the style of games that were created in gaming's infancy. There really is something in here for everyone and not in the sense that you'll like only part of a game. There is a full length game that you will like in here.You may think that because there are 50 games in the collection that there must be a sacrifice of quality for the sake of quantity. This could not be further from the truth. Each game has a remarkably unique identity with fully fleshed out ideas. From arcade-y high score games to a fully realized and surprisingly deep JRPG, the quality remains consistently best of class. One of my favorite aspects of this game is the narrative about the dev team that is created through playing their games. You see the games slowly increase in complexity, implying lessons learned by a team of passionate developers that truly want to make fun games. You see the technology get better over the years, resulting in higher graphical fidelity. The company changes names at one point. One of my favorite things is seeing the company logo change over the years. It really breaths life into this company and makes it so believable that they really existed. This is truly a must play game. If you love ANY video games, you will get value out of UFO 50.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who normally does not play Singleplayer games, I'm in love with UFO 50. It has so much passion and care put into it and so many of the games within are an absolute blast. I won't say every single game out of the 50 is a banger but certainly more of them are than I ever would have expected. More than worth the money, especially if you like to be a completionist or compete against yourself/others for times.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky guy & co made the experience of going to the arcade and jumping between 20 different cabinets in an hour, or trying out your friend's whole NES catalog in an afternoon, into a video game.In this case, though, almost every single game stands on its own as what would at least be a pretty good $5 retro-inspired indie game on Steam, with many reaching all the way up to being an absolute classic that could rank among the top 20 games of a console's library, had they actually been released in the 80s. Lots of them are really hard and rewarding to beat and complete, too. Also there are 50 of them, and half of them have a 2-player mode.At the time of writing I have 40+ hours and still haven't even opened 11 out of the 50, add another 15 or so that I've only played for a couple of minutes. It is a joy to play and browse through a collection of so many clever twists on classic games and interesting retro spins on modern game mechanics and genres.Easily one of the most enjoyable games I've played in the past decade, highly recommended if you like video games and having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Tried about 10 of the games so far and beaten 4, and I can already tell this is crazy value for money (everything I've played so far is a properly fleshed out game, and I've found quite a few I really like already). I've been into Magic Garden, Mortol and Campanella in particular. They really nailed the good things about retro games (real gameplay/design focus, no fluff, intuitive/easy to grasp controls but with a high skill ceiling) while avoiding what was often bad (there's no stiff controls, slowdown, flickering or overly punishing lives systems here). Not just cool concept for a game as they actually managed to pull it off! Love it and looking forward to playing the rest 👍
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping I'd finally have the right words for this at the 100 hour mark, but I'm still struggling. It's really good, might not be for everyone, but is ridiculously technically impressive.The developers have delivered a package that delivers 50 individual games that are all fun in their own right, but also tells a story about a company slowly developing mastery over game development over a decade.The first few games in the collection have rudimentary character controls, barely have sounds, don't have title screens, didn't have credits yet, but all innovate in their own surprising ways. Further in the collection, the games get far closer in feeling to what Rare or Capcom made for the NES, but with small callbacks to previous games in UFO 50 for anyone who's taken the time to explore them.If you're the kind of person that can appreciate the fact that this team included 2 JRPGs in two distinct styles, one where a game over requires the player to load their last save, and another where the player only drops money and is sent back to town, just to tell a story about developers getting better at their craft and ongoing experiments with save systems, you owe it to yourself to pick up this collection. Nobody at Mossmouth had to make any of these simpler games to learn. Instead, the limitations they've chosen aesthetically and mechanically help push this weird pseudo-narrative artistic interpretation of the collection as a whole. It's ridiculously cool and I don't think there's ever been anything else quite like this.Simply put, the amount of game development talent on display here is actually incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A little over 10 hours in and I'd absolutely give UFO 50 a solid 9.5/10 for an indy which is incredibly high50 games, all of them actually fleshed out and created with an insane amount of thought on gameplay loop, art style; with absolutely no space for generic titles this game pack will keep you satisfied the more you keep digging in it. WIth all sorts of different titles you will absolutely scratch that boredom itch with something Mossmouth cooked up in here.Mossmouth made absolute sure to fine tune all these new-style classic games with modern sensibility and controls so that you can experience that nostalgia D-Pad A-B style game in the modern era.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's transcendentally good.I typically review game scripts, that's like the reason I like to do reviews, but that doesn't really apply here. There's a story, it's sweet, it's light, there are POTENTIALLY interpretations to be made about the mood and subtext behind the oeuvre of the company involved, but this is less plot than it is context. It's a story in the same way Bowser At The End Of The Game provides context to what you're doing at any given time and why.The game itself, however, is the realization of a dream. In other reviews, both readers and writers have taken for granted the concept of "Action 52 But Good", we don't realize just what an insane thing that is. Not the development, of course it's insane, what a feat. But the childlike mind imagined 52 Mario 3's And Mega Man 2's inside Action 52 when there wasn't even a single Double Dragon to be found in it.As one gets older, the idea seems almost idiotic. Why would you want 52 bad games when you can have 1 good game? Because the idea of 52 good games is something so insane no one would think to ask for it.Well here it is. 50 fully realized games. They're all great in their own way. They're snack-sized sure, but they carry with them the quality of what one would consider to be a "Game". It's the dream realized. Get excited in the way that the child version of you would have been excited for Action 52. Let the dream live. It not only can come true, it undeniably has.Standouts, in my opinion, are Bushido Ball, Quibble Race, Night Manor, and Magic Garden.I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: (There is a TL:DR at the bottom)I've put 6.2 hours into this game at the time of this review. I've played about 18 of the games and have "beaten" two of them. This is a collection of games with secrets to find, easter eggs to discover, and so much to explore if you want to go in deep, but it is also just 50 fleshed out NES/FAMICOM style games here to play if that is what you want as well. While I do recommend the game for people to explore, I will say it has absolutely frustrated me so very much to the point that I almost wish that I could refund the game because it makes me very angry, but at the same time the games and game as a package is so passionately created that I want to see more of this caliber of game. (And I completely understand that it is a  thing, but that is why I am writing this review)My (very personal and probably  shared among other players) anger stems from this being an alternate reality 50 games from an NES/FAMICOM computer era, where we are just playing around with them. That's fine, but if I would have read that in the description of the game, I wouldn't have bought it. I don't  to figure out the nuances of the games by trial and error. I didn't want a "figure it out as you go" META-GAME I wanted what was in the description: "the experience of going to a friend's house and perusing their game library" but there are absolutely zero instructions or instruction books for these games.  You basically click on a disk to play a game...maybe the game has a cut scene that tells you a little about it, maybe the game has an options menu where you can see what the controls do. I understand that "figuring out" how to play a game can be part of the charm...but I know that it is not for me. "Exploring the collection is part of the fun!" Yes, I agree that it is part of the fun, if I have the instruction books to go along with the games.Although you can view the controls for a game before you open it, they will tell you what the controls do e.g. "+=move ; a=jump ; b=attack". But it doesn't explain all of the controls and this is where my frustration lies. As a kid, I would always read the instruction booklets before playing the game. I want to know the lore, I want to know how to play. This right here is what raises my blood pressure. I'm looking at you MOONCAT where every button is move, and also Block Koala where I've never enjoyed a block puzzle game and would like to know what's going on. Avianos looks like a Romance of the Three Kingdoms, but I boot the game and am immediately frustrated and not knowing how to play. This is how most games just throw you in. You get more explanation about the 5 out of the 50 games listed on the store page than anything that you can see in the game (at least initially...maybe that changes with options?) For some games...that is ok, but for others it is so very frustrating. Imagine trying to play PUNCHOUT on the NES without knowing that the "start" button allows for star punches or what the concept of star punches are.UFO 50 is an impressive package of individual games wrapped in a larger game-lore. I am truly impressed by Mossmouth and I want to encourage others to try the game, but to realize that instead of getting 50 new 8-bit games that you get to experience for the first time like when you were a kid...you get 50 games from an alternate universe where you will have to figure out without instructions that the game  originally would have come with.Maybe I'm too old to put the time and effort to put on my archaeology glasses and figure out these games, to then figure out the lore of the UFO 50 and the secrets of the terminal, etc. Maybe I'm just not in the right head-space and am getting frustrated too easily, but wanted to share for others that are curious about the game.TLDR: 50 Games, easter eggs galore, only basic instructions per game that doesn't tell you  you need to know and you're going to have to figure out a lot on your own with each game. Be ready to join a discord group or watch a video to figure some things out.

_childDocuments_.review: An embarrassing amount of riches. Multiplayer games that rival Final Fight and Towerfall, unique genre twists on dungeon crawler and SHMUPs, to even just no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, good-ass retro games.You won't love everything, but nobody loves the entire NES library. As you go further, the games grow in scale, smooth out the jank, and even weave a small tale of developers attempting to capitalize on previous successes. Achievements, unlockables, and even an ARG-esque metaplot delivered via Gameshark code sniffing, all add fantastic bowties to a minigame collection already bursting with content.How the ♥♥♥♥ is this $25?

_childDocuments_.review: Action 52 sequelt! I am over half way through this collection. It is a mixed bag. Some games are not going to hit. _childDocuments_.review: I was kinda sceptical of this game when I first heard about it (surely 50 games means most of them are very basic or not very well thought-out), but it's blown my expectations out of the water. I've been going through fairly slowly all things considered as I'm golding the games that stick out to me as I go so I'm only up to Zoldath, and most of the games so far have been super duper solid, very simple but with absolutely no extraneous features or mechanics and very fun. Velgress is my favourite so far, it's a super short but super fast and demanding little rogulike, seems like the perfect game for speedrunning, but Bug Hunter, Magic Garden, and Mortol are also fantastic in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most impressive games I've played in... well, ever.The creativity, scope, and overall quality of this collection are astounding. Many of the games are obviously inspired by other titles, but remixed in a way that makes them feel unlike anything I've played. With just over 30 hours at the time of writing this review, I have barely touched the majority of the games in UFO 50, and I like almost everything I've tried. Even the ones I've completed are tempting me to come back for more. I can see myself spending over 100 hours on this, and I'm not a completionist.There's so much here. If you have any love for retro games, I can't recommend UFO 50 highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: 28/50tl;dr Just get this game and see what games you like.Not only is this a really fun collection of 50 games of many genres, there is also a good bit of extra stuff around the collection. There are collectable gifts for giving games a good try along with gold and cherry carts for finish and 100% respectively. By the nature of the variety, don't expect to like all the games and secrets that are here. (There are tough shoot em ups here) However, all the games seem to be of quality so I promise you won't be let down by the games you do like. Well, except for one. Check below for that review, you can't miss it.Barbuta is sour in play, but if I give it more time I’m hoping to be rewarded. Though it might be more fun to share notes with peers on what you find instead of trial and error. If not, you might get tired if you don't take detailed maps. Got cherry after looking stuff up due to getting tired of combing the game for secrets.Grimstone is really fun so far. Kind of harsh, requiring some grind to get stronger, but it makes that clear and makes the strategy of grinding more in depth than you will expect. Might gold.Planet Zoldath was a game I didn't like, and yet I chose to play it and get my first gold from it. I believe that means the game is good, but not because I was having fun playing it. Bug Hunter can get real challenging, but once you figure out the key features of the game, the game get's really good. Not a favorite quite yet, but I defiantly will return to play more runs. Maybe I can get the gold then.Ninpeck was a fantastic game to gold. It was also the first game I top scored on too. It was really fun to chip away at it.Paint Chase is alright. I might come back if I feel like it, but probably not getting gold on it.Mortol is such a clever idea done fantastically. Defiantly will chip away at it more and probably get gold.Velgress is a fun rogue-like. It's a bit tough so gold is only a maybe, but I might come back to it.Devilition is satisfying. Getting a good combo put together is great. Failing to detonate some units make me sigh though. No guarantee to gold.Kick Club can be quite challenging platformer, but it was great. Will play more and maybe gold.Bushido Ballin with the gold. Might even cherry.Camouflage Is a fun puzzle game. Will gold and maybe even cherry if collectible give the cherry.Campanella is the in-lore LX system bundle game for good reason. It's tough, but super fun. It even has secrets of it own for increasing score or beating the game faster. Might gold.Goldfaria is the gold RPG we didn't know we needed. This one will take a bit, but it will be a good one to gold for sure.The Big Bell Race is super fun practice zone for Campanella flight physics. Got the gold, but will only cherry if I decide to play it again.Warptank is a great puzzle platformer that is also tough to navigate outside of the puzzles. Also has hidden secrets where you have to touch everything hoping the secrets reveal themselves. Will gold and probably cherry at the same time at my current pace.Caramel Caramel is a fine shoot-em-up with a fun mechanic. Not my kind of thing to just keep playing, but defiantly great.tl;dr👎for the secret filler,👍for the secret contents.At first, I was thinking that the Lore and Meta Secrets in the game were level 1 overall (designed be found by yourself) due to what the community has said about them. Unfortunately, with the alertness requirements worsening my game sampling (there are more games sampled than I actually played for real) and the amount of theory crafting and interpretation of said secrets, I say that they are more Level 3 overall (designed as a community game). This probably could have been better if I had started some stuff way later instead of discovering a piece way too early. Regardless, my experience became worsened by some of the filler as I am calling it. Instead of letting the secrets getting in the way of your experience, I recommend you bite the bullet and experience the key findings rather than following the threads closely to find them yourself. The fan discord has document links in the pins of #code-hunters to see the contents yourself. Trust me, it is much more fun than solving the filler stuff. Unless you find it fun to remember the past 50 games you have played instead of 5.Mini & Max was a really fun exploration game. Who knew there could be so much just in a closet to explore? Got the Gold and will likely Cherry.more reviews to come later.

_childDocuments_.review: What a massive accomplishment, and an even greater value, this game is. When we first heard 50 games, I'm sure no one expected the depth and quality that we have here. It's truly remarkable. I've only played 19 of the games so far, and I can't recall the last time I was so happy with a purchase.It's not just 50 games ranging from decent to fantastic. So many of these games are so brimming with charm and personality, that they're already carving out a place in my mind alongside full release games. I look forward to seeing speed runs of these games, and people doing guitar covers of their theme songs in their bedrooms for years to come.I keep coming back to the thought that I really look forward to whenever this game releases on the Switch, since an even greater amount of people will be able to experience its greatness, and start the conversation about it all over again.And selfishly, I hope that one day some more gems from these UFOsoft devs are uncovered. Surely these folks didn't just stop making games in the 90s after the company folded? I'm imagining a rhythm game with an off color Waldorf lookalike, or perhaps a golf themed FPS....
