_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this game a negative review.  That is because it's loaded with genres that I have zero interest in:  strategy, point-and-click, rpg, GOLF (yuck!).However, I feel the small handful of games that I do enjoy, made this worth the purchase.I recommend researching each game beforehand, so that you won't be disappointed like I initially was.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the design of games, told through a fake game company spread out through 50 unique games made just for this. Nostalgia is not the seller here, it's innovative and great design restricted to a d-pad and 2 buttons. There's a spread of a bit of everything you could want here, from platformers to strategy games to a Western JRPG to dungeon crawlers with hidden meta-gaming spread throughout. Even if one game is not your jam, there's plenty more to choose from.Personally, I've loved every single one so far. A once in a generation type of release. Couldn't recommend it more. UFO Soft is one of the best publishers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to 80s gaming, not just to the classics, but to the stranger, more experimental side of the decade. Every sub-game is weird, unique, not always good per se, but always interesting. It is a fascinating collection of games that doesn't let up on the surprises the whole way through. I've heard this took 8 years to make, and it's not hard to see why. Derek Yu and his team managed to create 50 games that, though sometimes similar to the classics, are all unique in their own way, none of which have been a complete dud and some of which have been surprisingly deep and fun.It's temping to try to review every individual game and criticize this collection for none of the games being as good as the best games of the 80s, but that would be missing the point. This collection evokes nostalgia for the era when you could buy a box of mystery games or bootleg floppies from a garage sale and have no idea what you were getting. There's a certain joy in delving into the unknown, never knowing what the next game will have in store for you. That joy is missing from the modern era of gaming where you can easily look up any game and know everything about it, but UFO 50 brings that sensation back in grand fashion, and I kind of love it for that.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It has it all!Short and Sweet Arcade Games, Mind-bending Puzzle Games, great (local) Multiplayer, some really unique RPGs and even a point and click horror adventure game... loving every minute I spend playing it.Completionists will have a hell of a time with this one, however, as each game requires you to be pretty proficient at them to "clear" it. Some can be beaten in under an hour, but others will likely require much practice and strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: While a lot of people have drawn comparisons between UFO 50 and the old "Action 52" cartridge for the Nintendo Entertainment System, there's really no comparison. UFO 50 is a package of 50 original (meaning "new", not "classic") retro-style games bundled up into one purchase with a little bit of overarching meta-story. There are all kinds of retro games; if you enjoy classic titles from the 8-bit era, then buy this now.To be clear, this is fifty games. Not a collection of minigames, and not "a couple of good games and 45 trash programs." Every single game is complete with its own title screen, mechanics, levels, and so on. Some sprites do get re-used but it's pretty sparing, at least up to the first 25 games. It's fifty real retro-style games, and while some of them can be beaten on a lunch break, the game rewards you for excelling at these titles with high scores or quick clears, and the difficulty means you'll be struggling at those challenges for a good while.The meta-plot is basically that you (or someone) find an old computer gaming system in a storage unit and you boot it up to see what games there are. Back in the real-life 8-bit era, the distinction between a "home computer" and a "game console" was not so clear, and so the "LX" computer lies somewhere between the Nintendo NES and 8-bit home computers like the Commodore 64 or the MSX.Indeed, many of the games in UFO 50 feel more like home computer games than console games. Certain titles evoke the feel of MS-DOS or even PC-98 games, while others are very clearly aping the NES or PC Engine style. However, none of the games are bone-stock reimplementations of retro game tropes. Every single title has something pretty fresh and interesting going for it, with some very clever mechanics on display.I'd like to say that the games are incredibly authentic to their retro inspirations, but the degree of authenticity varies a lot. Some games feel like they really could be NES ROMs, while others have too many colors, too many sprites, and anachronistic gameplay functions. There's also the fact that all of the LX games (games in UFO 50) are made for a wide-screen aspect ratio as befits a modern PC game.Personally speaking, the games (at least, the first 25, which I've tried) do kind of skew a little bit toward the puzzle genre, and even the action titles often have puzzle elements to them. I don't hate this, but I'm , so this makes a lot of the games extremely difficult for me. However, that doesn't apply to every game, and in most of the titles the stakes are (perhaps a bit anachronistically) pretty low, like having infinite credits or lots of checkpoints. I've managed to clear a few games already, so if I can do it, almost anyone can.If you look at it from the point of view of being a gamer in 2024 buying fifty games at once, this package is a phenomenal value. Even if you only enjoy a handful of the games, you've still paid just a few dollars for those games, and if you like them all, well, that's $0.50 a game. Are you really going to miss out on fifty games for $0.50 each? I thought not.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Shockingly jam-packed with ideas and mechanics, with surprising takes on a bunch of Nintendo-era designs and aesthetics at every turn. I don't want to say too much, as I think a big part of what's fun is discovering each game and figuring out what its deal is. I guess I just want to echo every other review and say that this is way, way more rich and varied and fun than I had any idea it would be. Oh yeah, and the multiplayer games (that I've played so far at least) have been really fun as co-op adventures, party games, and ones that you can play competitively.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like NES games? Yes? Okay, then buy this. If you don't, then don't.I've played at least a bit of almost all the games so far. Overall, the quality is insane. Each of these feel like genuine games, and each one is fairly large.  There is something for everyone.  Even the game types I'm not a fan of, have unique enough mechanics to make me excited to delve deeper into them at a later point. My favorite so far was the horror point and click. On top of that, there are secrets and hidden content that span outside of the games it seems. So there is even more than meets the eye.I'll probably add more to this review when I beat more of the games.Small standout games to me so far  -punchout + dungeon crawler combinedhorror point and clickice climbers/doodlejump/downwell type game pinball golfGOLF RPGWestern JRPGa 4x strategy gamea contra-cloneA platform/adventure game where you shrink in a house and explore it while being ant sized. an idle adventure game, that idles while you play all the other games
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 50 retro-style games of all genres, with a meta-narrative running through it and secrets to be found. Sound like a good time? It is! I am sure that everyone would find at least one game on UFO 50 that they dislike or that just don't appeal to them, maybe even a few. But for every "bad" game, there are many "good" games. I only found a couple of games that I would think are clankers, but so many have the potential to be your next gaming addiction. And for 25 bucks, that's 50 cents a game - and they are all worth more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The good:✅ 50 games and even a cheat code device, just like the old days.✅ Many different genres to choose from, so there should be something for everyone.✅ The games link together in some interesting ways I won't spoil.✅ The music is great!The bad:❌ They emulate some things a bit too faithfully.  Back in the day, Nintendo Power would rate games on their control scheme.  Yes, fixed jumps and horribly slow walk speed were common, but they were also seen as flaws even back then.  Even Mario Brothers had air control for jumps!  And NES emulators have given us speed-up buttons.❌ Some games just may not appeal to everyone.  There are a few that just aren't for me, but that only matters if you're a completionist and want to master every game, since you can have gold/cherry versions of each cart by beating it.❌ The games are Nintendo hard.  They're not very clear and they don't give any explanation and there are no manuals this time.  Others may see this point as a plus, not a minus, but back in the days of the NES some of us were buying printed strategy guides, reading Nintendo Power, or calling their tip line.  Or sending them physical letters because we wanted to know what on earth those weird spells like DIOS and BADIOS and MAPORFIC did in Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord.  And some of us read the manuals for every little clue, even the ones that made no sense because our controllers didn't have microphones in them like Japan did, so we couldn't kill that annoying enemy in Zelda the way Japanese kids did.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up, I didn't have many video games. Our household only had an NES that my dad bought on clearance sometime after the release of the SNES. Even as some of my friends started to own N64s and Playstations, we still had just that NES and about 3 games. Then, one day, one of our neighbors cleaned out their attic and found a box full of their old NES games. They had gotten rid of their NES years ago, and knew we still had one, so they gave us the whole box full of games. Suddenly, I had dozens of new games to play. None of them had their manuals or boxes, but I didn't care. I happily loaded up one game after another, learning little bits about each game, figuring out how to get a little further each time. It was one of my happiest memories related to gaming.UFO 50 immediately took me back to that memory. Playing this game, I feel like that little 7-year-old boy with that box full of NES games again. Playing through this collection is an absolute joy and I would have happily bought more that half of these games on their own. But having them together along with the meta narrative of the fictional UFOsoft just puts this game on a whole other level, and dare I say, makes it a masterpiece. UFO 50 might not click with everyone, but for those it does click with, it's something very special.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool collection of 50 new games. I've only completed one of the games, the wild west rpg Grimstone, which took me just under 16 hours. If you want a game like the early Final Fantasy and Dragon Warrior/Quest games that is fairly quick and short for an rpg I'd definitely recommend trying it out and then you can play the other 49 games after it, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Fifty 8-bit video games, each with their own genre and weird quirks, none of which hold your hand but all of which are designed in a way to help you figure things out yourself, all tied together with a fictitious timeline and publishing history, and $25 for all fifty games. If any of that appeals to you, then UFO 50 is worth checking out. Even if you don't appreciate all 50, I'm guessing you'll have a great time with at least 10 of them. My favorites are #10, #21, #26, #40, and #45.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An astonishing creation.Let's get this out of the way up front; unless you cannot stand retro-style games at all, regardless of anything else, then you should probably get UFO 50. The sheer breadth of experiences here, and the high average quality of them, basically guarantees you're going to find something here to love. Few things here are straight-up genre titles. Videogaming has been around for half a century, there are no completely new ideas left, but damn if UFO 50 doesn't do a good job of trying to convince us otherwise. On your journey through these games, you'll regularly encounter mechanical combinations you've never seen before; my favourite example may be the first-person dungeon crawler where combat is handled as a dodge-and-counter action sequence slightly like Punchout.That's the real joy here; to get 50 decent new games would be excellent. But to have them so often be fresh idea... that's the stuff, that's what sells this package. You haven't played anything quite like Mortol before, or Avianos, or Golfaria, I basically guarantee it.My favourite is probably Warptank. It's a... puzzle platform shooter?... Where you control a wall-hugging tank that navigates by teleporting to opposing surfaces. The individual levels (all found within a shape-shifting overworld full of little secrets) are action puzzles, as you try to figure out how to manoeuvre yourself through the cleverly-crafted levels, all to the lovely bouncy music. Superb.I really don't think I can praise this enough. 10/10, GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: In college I tried playing through nearly every single NES game ever released as a fun endeavor between classes. While I didn't make my way through the entire catalog (stopping around the "N"s), the late nights of difficult platforming, old-school story-telling, and crisp chiptunes are ones I'll always cherish. UFO 50 is all those glorious memories sweeping back to me in a rush, with no dumb-ass bad games to get in the way. I think the keyword of the collection is "restraint". Sure, modern game development lets you do a LOT, but that's not what UFO is about. There is a certain considered quaintness, an intentional minimalism to the modern sensibilities of today. Mooncat has some of my favorite examples; a super minimal soundtrack and clever sprite techniques all make you feel like the developer was trying desperately to save memory. UFO 50 is special. It's the collaboration of some of the greatest artists in the game development world of today. I don't think I'm being even slightly pretentious to compare this to a hypothetical collaboration of Mozart and Tchaikovsky, a painting rendered by both Van Gogh and Delacroix. Don't miss this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 might just have the coolest concept of any game I've played and it completely nails the execution.It genuinely blows my mind that this game even exists. I mean, the absolute audacity of these devs to create a package of this size and quality, and sell it for as cheap as it is. A game that is itself 50 other fully featured games, spanning all kinds of genres, and all of them made with so much care and respect for the era that they are pulled from, and for the entire medium of games on the whole.I've played 12 hours so far and only touched the first 10 games, not finished any of them yet but getting close with Mortol (Banger game btw). There are some seriously cool games in here though and I've only just begun to scratch the surface, which is very exciting!I don't expect to like every game in the collection and there's a couple already that I'm not a fan of, but I also think this is kinda the point too. For example, a game I enjoyed might be one you didn't get on with (or vice versa) and I think it's crazy that this game allows for this kinda thing. Everyone is going to have a unique experience with it, which is just so damn cool to me!So to sum up my thoughts:If you have grown up with games and have been fascinated with how they have evolved over time, you gotta play it.If you remember the days of not knowing if a game would be good or what you would even be playing when you inserted the cartridge or disc, you gotta play it.And if you just simply love playing games...you guessed it...you gotta play it!It's an insane thing they've made here, seriously, go play it!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat and a delight! 50 NES-style games with modern design sensibilities and clever ideas. The value for money here is unmatched - every one I've tried has been a banger. Shout out to Campanella (1) which seemed unfair and impossible until it became one of my favourites once I took notes on where to find all the coffee!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's 50 games by the Spelunky man. Some are INCREDIBLY, almost worth the price on their own. Some are a fun twist wrapped in a mid NES game. All are, at the very least, interesting. The premise is fun - a fake company that made 50 NES games in the 1980s. You can feel the care in every game, these are more than just "itch games". If any part of this interests you, buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I am in absolute awe at UFO 50. It's a masterpiece, an incredible labor of love, a wonderful idea that's amazingly well executed... but it's also really, really fun to play! It's one of those games that get stuck in your head and have you thinking about it all day long. I have beaten the first game (Barbuta), though I feel like I still have like half of the game left to discover. And then there's another 49 games (of which I've played a few for a while, and they're also great), plus (I'm sure) a lot of secret stuff... and I *can't wait* to discover it all. If you have even a passing interest in gaming history or, like, in videogames themselves, this is an absolute must.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: most games today are build around hooks that are "fun". which for most people means some form of metaprogression and gambling (or at least the experience of chance), lots of action feedback, replayability, guaranteed progress (collect wood) asf. this collection of games is different. its not only fun to explore but surprisingly fun to play.  through the lense of most of the games you can see the way games used to be designed (the games themselves) and in the overview screen (and some parts of the singular games), you can see how games are designed today (the metaprogression in the game). its really nice to engage with because it hits the trifecta of (a) fun games (b) narrative cohesion and (c) showing the difference between old/new design. i recommend it becuase its more than a fun game, its an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly one of the most impressive achievements in gaming in a long time. Every last game is a full experience and each of them does something unique enough to warrant playing them. If you are getting into gaming for the very first time and aren't sure even where to begin, this is probably the best place to start
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game if you like retro games. If you only enjoy 5 of the 50 games offered you'll still feel like you got value worth your money. There are certainly some games I don't enjoy, but there are many that are so good that I went back to play them a second time after beating them to try to beat the cherry challenges. Don't write this one off if you don't enjoy the first couple of games you play - try using the filters to find games you might enjoy if you prefer shorter mini games, strategic 'thinky' games, or longer form epic games.Highly recommend checking this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the OG NES, you can't go wrong with this. If you're not an old nerd, if you like, uh, Super Meat Boy, Celestia, that kind of stuff, you'll probably dig this. A lot of the games are hard, if you're like me and you're not about that life, there is still plenty here to entertain. All the genres.  I love the art and sound. This whole thing reminds me of constrained poetry, where the poem is written within a lot self imposed limitations. Would bang this game if i could.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure it's already clear in the many existing reviews that is instantly a 40 year old classic. But I still want to applaud the developers on their accomplishment and encourage others to experience this game.In my first couple hours of UFO 50, I was a bit put off by the retro trappings. The controls and "feel" of some of the early games comes can be fairly described as crude.But I tried more of the games and found some that I just keep returning to. These games are comfy and nostalgic in how they look and play, yes, but nearly every one also has some little twist of game design that _at least_ makes the experience intriguing, and in some cases, addicting! And the more I've played, the more the conceit of this alternate-universe retro console has felt incredibly fun, and I've been practically thrilled to discover some of the LX-50's secrets :) Bravo to the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool game that's made very well, one that focuses on developing NES era games like those games were developed in the 1980's, it's faithful to that, to a fault. There's a ton of creativity here, but what you're essentially buying is a collection of 50 mostly flawed games that do not come even close to representing the best of the NES and that's entirely on purpose. I don't regret buying it. For many, this will just be a curiosity, its fun unpacking all the games and giving them a go, but if you intend to beat any of them, like I did, you're not in for a fun experience, difficulty can be punishing, enemy placement can be harsh, controls can be obtuse and sometimes even awful. It represents a long bygone era of gaming, an era that's gone for a reason...  I still recommend the game, I feel the initial experience of playing these for the first time is really fun. Some of the games have a lot of mechanical depth and surprise you by just how creative they can be, that's worth it far more than actually trying to beat any of them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend IN A HEARTBEAT to anyone who considers themselves a fan of retro gaming (1980s).Would also recommend it to basically anyone who likes video games. The amount of content is staggering, and the quality of much of the content even moreso.Deserves so, SO much more love and popularity than it currently has.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is nothing short of revolutionary within the category of retro-style new games. I'd like to use this space to consider the feat of this accomplishment by Mossmouth by way of comparison, to another collection of retro-style new(er) games: the much heralded Shovel Knight series by Yacht Club Games. Shovel Knight deservedly received much critical acclaim on first release a decade ago for bringing back the essence of retro games at their best while doing one better by bringing everything learned about good game design into a very satisfying package. They went on to expand the Shovel Knight universe with several other offshoot platformers which also received acclaim, and eventually released 4 or 5 offshoots in entirely new genres: puzzle, fighting etc. But compare Yacht Club Games offering -- 10 or so games, half of which are platformers -- released over a period of a decade -- to UFO 50: one single amazing collection of 50 fully-fledged *fun* games spanning a ton of genres while adding completely new innovations and ideas. Then realize that UFO 50 also created a whole lore and "alternate reality" 1980s in which a game development company grew and matured along with their games over a ~10 year period. It makes Yacht Club Games look like child's play. It puts YCG, and similar developers on notice: UFO 50 is the new reality of the competition. UFO 50 is the new standard bearer. UFO 50 is revolutionary because it becomes clear playing it that *this* is the new gold standard if you want to make the best retro-style new games. YCF can release Mina the Hollower and it may be a great, expansive action-adventure game. But it is still just one action-adventure game. You're still just controlling one character, in one way. I don't know how many styles of game play the game may ultimately have, and many "mini-games" may be included, but again, but it clearly isn't presenting itself anyway close in terms of gameplay variety and depth to UFO 50. Don't get me wrong - I love Shovel Knight and the series. But there is a new king of retro-style games. It is here folks. UFO 50. Nothing will ever be the same.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An embarrassment of riches from a group of extremely talented developers, highly recommended. A few pointers:-- The games are ordered chronologically according to the lore, so these at the start of the list are the more 'primitive' of the collection. If you bounce off those, try some of the later ones.-- There's a filter at the bottom of the menu allowing you to narrow down on the more adventure/puzzle/arcade-orientated games as your tastes dictate-- There's no instruction manuals, but figuring out what's going on in the more obscure games is part of the fun. Some of the games will show a brief demo if you leave them hanging on the start menu.-- A few of the more approachable games, in my experience, are Party House (elegantly designed push-your-luck deckbuilder), Campanella 2 (roguelike where you swap between flying a spacecraft and on-foot sections), Pingolf (side-view arcade golf game) and Valbrace (first-person dungeon crawler with twitchy real-time combat)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played about 7 of the available 50 games but each one I've played so far I have enjoyed.UFO 50 is an awesome collection of retro-like games but designed with modern sensibilities so they're all fun to play.If you grew up on NES/SEGA or just enjoy "old-fashioned" games, this one feels like discovering a goldmine of games you never heard of but wish you did.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long wait and honestly is such a special project in the making. I'm about halfway through the library and it is SO intriguing. Some games I like more than others but there is so much care put into crafting this game. These aren't mini games, these are FULL fledged games made in a retro style of a fictional game company/console. Will continue to play, DEFINITELY recommend buying, especially at the $25 price point it is well-worth it. Especially for this dev and team.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you can deal with the most minor of NES jank and difficulty, this is one of the best games of the year, hands down. Mortol, Velgress, Vainger, Rail Heist, and Hyper Contender alone made this collection worth it for me, and Devilition, Cyber Owls, Planet Zoldath, Pilot Quest, Mooncat, Camouflage, Campenella, Night Manor, and Seaside Drive have brought it to my personal GOTY.Most of the games I'm not personally a fan of are because of lack of interest in their genres as a whole (not an RPG guy here, sorry Divers and Grimstone fans), rather than a lack of quality in those games. Literally the only complaint I have is lack of online multiplayer without the use of external programs, but considering the meta-narrative has this whole collection being made around 1989 I can't be too mad about this nitpick. 100% recommend, best $25 I've spent this year.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a modern take on the Game Center CX games that were on Nintendo DS, only with more games. If you like faux-retro indie games, or any of the games made by UFO 50's creators I can't recommend this enough.The 7-8 hours of playtime I have at time of this review were all on a Steam Deck, and so far other than one game randomly crashing it plays perfectly. In that time I've played maybe 80% of the games and only beaten one of them, there is plenty of gameplay for your money here.If you sort the games chronologically, the first game on the list is an intentional throwback to old clunky platformer maze games that were popular in the 80s (Montezuma's Revenge is my point of reference) and if you don't have nostalgia for that type of game you should definitely check out a few games later in the list, they get more complex as they go along.I still have to try out a handful of these games, but I've already found a decent number I'm going to sink some serious time into. There's also plenty of meta challenges and secrets that I've only gotten a peek at.edit: I'm now 23 hours in, I've beaten 3 games (with the cherry challenge not completed on any) and the one serious bug I found was patched. I've already hit a dollar-per-hour with this collection and nowhere near done with it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played UFO 50 for very long, but I am getting increasingly addicted.First impressions were bad. Really bad. I actually refunded the game the first time I tried it. I played the first 3 games on the list, then a handful of random ones scattered around, and found myself frustrated and/or bored with everything I played. The fact is, not all 50 games are going to be for you. This is not the kind of collection where you will obsessively 100% every single game on offer. These are very niche games, but they're also extremely varied.It was only after I saw a couple videos on UFO 50 showcasing some of the games I didn't see the first time that I decided to give it another try. Once I found a couple games that fit my personal tastes, I was hooked. I think if the aesthetic isn't a turnoff, there is guaranteed to be at least a few games in here that you will absolutely love. The problem is sticking with it long enough to find those gems. Avianos is the one that made me want to write this review. I would genuinely be happy buying this collection just for Avianos, I had that much fun with it. It has so much personality, depth, and replayability, and it's multiplayer to boot. The fact that it's just one of 50 equally unique games is astounding to me, even if they're not all to my taste. If you're a strategy and board game fanatic like me, please give Avianos a try, it's truly inspired.Part of the fun of UFO 50 is discovery. One of the most polarising aspects of the game (the most being Barbuta) is how little it explains any of the rules or mechanics of its games. There's no tutorial in any of the games that I've played, they just drop you in and you have to figure it out on your own. That's really annoying at first, but the games are designed with this in mind. They encourage you to just try things out and see what happens, and it's very intuitive. Discovering the complexities of a simple looking game is a very unique and satisfying experience. Mooncat is the most extreme example of this, another very polarising game, but highlights from my playthrough include Pingolf, Party House and Hyper Contender for this very reason. And Avianos. Avianos is incredible, please play it.Despite the fun I'm having, recommending UFO 50 is... difficult. It's simultaneously a game that needs to be played blind, but also one that's extremely frustrating to get into without knowing the games beforehand. My advice is the same as others here have said: be patient, try as many games as you can before hitting the refund button, and for the love of god don't play Barbuta first.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is my GOTY. Velgress is GOTY. Rock on! Island is GOTY. Mini & Max is GOTY. Night Manor is GOTY. Valbrace is goty. Grimstone is GOTY. Campanella 2 is GOTY. It is an absolute miracle that in a year already full of bangers, this one game has multiple games that could stand on their own as GOTY contenders in any other year.What is the nature of play? Why are we so drawn to the recreation state of games? With the limited free time that every day life provides us there seems to be little more spiritually enriching than the act of play. This collection is absolutely mind boggling, not just with its sheer breadth of great full-length experiences, but also with its connective tissue of inter-game references, and the meta-narrative of the fake studio UFOSOFT and its rise and fall.This collection has helped me learn more about myself, my taste and habits with playing games, and what I value in an interactive experience. This collection has so many strengths, least of all being its wild number of standout titles.Every game is presented in a beautiful limited 32 color palette that really harkens back to the 80s era that these games released in within the story of the game. They carry a lot of retro design with cryptic puzzles and unforgiving difficulty, but they also feel so new and modern in their super smart design and fresh ideas. With a $25 price tag, it is an absolute steal at 50¢ a game. You do have some smaller arcade style experiences but is also a 20 hour cowboy jrpg, and multiple 5-10 hour adventure games, including a zelda style golf game, and a mind bending search action game about shrinking to explore the closet your older sister locked you in. Not every game in this collection is one I like, in fact a handful of them are straight duds to me. But that’s the beauty of a collection like this, some games that call to me will be of no interest to you and vice versa.I've rated each game individually on a 5 point scale, and the total is 200.5/250, and that reaches pretty much exactly 4 out of 5. Averaging 4/5 on a package of 50 games is absolutely unbelievable, and what makes this experience a 5/5 for me is that in a package full of 50 games, no person alive is going to find equal enjoyment in every single one, and that’s fine! That is the beauty of individual taste and interests. It’s the same way you don’t buy and spend much time on games that you don’t enjoy. I’ve talked with friends and seen online circles, and the rankings for people's top games in this collection are so vastly different and I love that. I also know if I spent more time with some of my middle scoring games, there is a huge chance it would shoot way up! This is a true desert island experience because you would need to spend an untold number of hours to master every game and find all its secrets. And that is including the meta-story and terminal secrets! I won’t say much because the joy of discovery is what this game is all about. Derek Yu compared the selection menu of 50 games to an open world game and I totally agree. Poking and prodding at every corner of this masterful experience and UFOSOFT’s near decade long story of triumph and heartache is one that I know I will keep coming back to for the rest of my life. Thank you to everyone at UFOSOFT and the fantastic UFO recovery team at Mossmouth!

_childDocuments_.review: (Updated after achieving 100% completion: All 50 Gold and Cherry Disks)UFO 50 really is a package with something for everyone, especially anybody with an interest in game design or a love for old school titles (I'm both of these markets). Nearly every game offers a unique idea or a spin on a pre-existing genre and genuinely puts the modern game development scene to shame in so many instances with its well-executed ideas.Games like Warptank being a spin on Blaster Master's tank controls with gravity flips or games like Mooncat having one of the most interesting control schemes I've ever seen, there's a new idea in every experience for better or worse and I loved every minute of it.Eirik's music is also yet again nothing but bangers, but this should be expected if you're familiar with his work. The limitation of a 32-color palette across also games also lends itself insanely well to really creative color and stage design choices, its always vibrant but never eye-piercing. The only major negative I could give this game is entirely related to the type of person that may tackle it, like Spelunky/Spelunky 2 this is a game with three base levels of what someone could consider "completing a game" which are...Completing a minor objective in a game gives players an item for their virtual garden, often unlocked around midway through a game or trying out a specific mode. Completing the base game gives you a Gold Disk and if a player is really to they can go for a Cherry Disk, which is usually a difficult challenge or bonus objective to complete. Many people may get frustrated if they go for all completions in order as many of these games are old-school levels of hard, but that's the beauty of a 50-in-1 collection... you gotta figure out what methods or pace work best for you.But overall? This is an insanely polished project 8 or so years in the making, you can really tell how much heart went into every single one of these titles, especially alongside the meta-narrative story about game design and the people involved in the process of game-making as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Still cannot believe that we have been blessed with this tremendous achievement of a video game. If you are a sucker for cool game design ideas - get this immediately! all 50 games are unique and made with a philosophy where you don't have to go over lengthy tutorials, but learn while playing and discovering the mechanics in the process while playing.Those who have a huge backlog of games that stresses them out - get UFO 50! It is essentially a gamified backlog simulator that would give you a very tight and achievable experience of discovering a collection. In UFO 50 you'll have the games that you love and games that you hate, some that would appear too hard that you overcome, and some that you will beat easily, some that you'll try once and never touch again and some that you'll come back to make them your favorites.It might take a few games to get into the collection (first game, Barbuta is intentionally janky, feel free to skip it!), but once it clicks it clicks, and you will sunk hours into digging deeper and deeper and deeper into the collection. As for the actual games: I love Red Dead Redemption, but it kinda lacks compared to how Rail Heist simulates the slapstick bar fight from an old comedy western movie with cowboy sprites that have only like 10 pixels. Moon Cat is a 2D platformer with controls made like it is the first 2D platformer of its kind, completely ignoring all the genre established practices, like 40 years of Mario games didn't happen There's a lot of games that try to be bite-sized 4X strategy, but very few come close to Avianos, achieving the strategic depth with all info fit to one 384x216 pixel screen and NES two button gamepad controls.I can go on and on there, and can also name a bunch of games that I think are meh (pretty convinced that Golfaria's only reason to exist is for Derek to sound catchy in the interviews, wow, we made a Zelda where you are a golf ball, such creativity), but as I already said it is a part of the experience to discover the games and make your own opinions, and then question them and change themSo don't hesitate trying out UFO 50, which is the best game of this year, and the approach it is made with is also so hard to replicate that its central idea won't likely ever be repeated in our lifetime. An instant cult classic (better jump on our hype train now while the cult is still young)

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is not only a great game, but its also a interesting and well thought approach to the micro game genre. With so much creativity and charm oozing out of every pore that it can.UFO 50 is what happens when you take Action 52, but actually make it good. Mossmouth has done an amazing job replicating the limiting power of the NES while still holding onto the refinement of modern game design. Taking the basis of classic NES titles and refining them into addicting games worthy of time.Velgress is a good example of this. It takes the gameplay of Kid Icarus and tweaks the formula to create a faster paced game that rewards skill and decision while still holding onto the core elements of Icarus.Avianos is a tactical strategy game where you aren't just expected to overwhelm your opponents army, but also maintain your own economy in a way that no other tactics game I've seen has done.Rakshasa is a Ghost and Goblins type game that still keeps a lot of the original design elements that made Ghosts and Goblins difficult while also circumventing that challenge with a unique revival system.Night Manor is a point and click horror game that surprisingly creates and eerie atmosphere that games like Clock Tower pioneered.The List goes on, from Bushido Balls intense reflexes to Mortols extra life system. Every game has something to love and has so much thought behind every aspect. Add that with the completionist challenges, a virtual pet garden that grows the more you play each game, and the hidden lore behind the fictional UFOsoft company, and you got yourself one of the best retro indie games ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a compilation of 50 games created by the devs behind Spelunkey, Downwell, and Skorpulac among others. It's set in the fictional gaming system LX-III, a console which takes inspiration from 1980s consoles and personal computers, such as the MSX and NES. These are games that vary in scope and size, but act as solitary experiences. Some are very long, taking as long as 20 hours to beat. Each game is retro-inspired but have their own unique twist that makes each one standalone. Genres are all over the place, from platformers to puzzles to full-blown strategy and even a JRPG ala Deltarune. It's a huge labor of love that took over 7 years to finish, with tons of secrets and unlockable achievement-style rewards to keep players coming back.NO. Right from the start, you have EVERY game, as well as a quick and easy way to categorize by genre, multiplayer, and amount of time played. You don't even have to play them in order: just play whichever one you want. However, I recommend starting with Pilot Quest as soon as possible. You can read why in my short recommended games list below.Having played them all, I would say that a vast majority of them are extremely solid. Some are difficult or have odd design quirks, but for the most part it is an extremely solid list of games. There's just hit after hit, and I'm personally so excited for it that I would consider the compilation itself a solid contender for Game of the Year.The games that might not be a hit for you could be the following, which other players complained about. Doesn't mean they're bad perse, just that there's mixed opinions on them:- BARBUTA: This is an adventure game inspired by games like Citadel for the BBC Micro. Personally, it reminds me more of Spider-Man for DOS. A very simple but very slow game where you are a knight hatched from an egg attempting to explore the castle and defeat the boss. It's purposefully designed with cheap one-hit deaths, but a ton of room to find plenty of secrets the more you're willing to be patient explore. It is the most retro of retro out of every game on the list, and is the first on the list chronologically. Maybe it sets a bad taste in your mouth, maybe it doesn't, but whatever you're feeling is very much intentional.- MOONCAT: As praised as it is hated, this is an obtuse platformer where you play as a literal bean with legs and traverse to the end while avoiding obstacles. Seems straightforward, except the game uses only two buttons for every action, including movement. That means the D-pad acts as one button while the buttons on your right thumb (A, B, etc) act as the second button. The way your character controls is odd, but very clever, and I won't spoil it for you. It's an unexpected treat to play this game, and I'd say give it a proper chance before you judge it too harshly.- COMBATANTS: Definitely the most hated on the list. This is a simple RTS game similar to Pikmin where you are a blue ant building an army to destroy the red ants before they destroy you. As simple as it sounds, it's very slow, and the AI is pretty obtuse. It's also very hard, as the red ants deal more damage and take more hits to kill. It takes a lot of patience to play this game, and it's probably not for you if you're like me and get frustrated easily.It was hard to narrow it down to just a few, but here's some games you might really enjoy:- PILOT QUEST: An idle/adventure game where you're a space pilot who crash-landed on an alien planet, now on a mission to find the parts to your spaceship. A mix of Legend of Zelda 1 and Cookie Clicker, you're able to collect resources automatically, even when you switch to another game. Once in a while, you're able to spend limited resources to go out into the wild and explore, but make sure you return before the time runs out or you won't collect what you've earned. Dungeon and item locations are also randomized, so it makes for a slightly different experience each time you play. A super addicting game, and highly recommend starting this one ASAP so you don't miss out on resources.- PARTY HOUSE: The fan-favorite. This is very similar to a random card draw game where you're the host of a happenin' 80s party, and you invite guests over by clicking on the front door, which brings in a random guest from your Rolodex guest list. End the party with tons of guests and cash in Popularity resources to expand your guest list. Make your house bigger with Cash to invite more guests at one party. However, some guests can be trouble: have 3 or more people who cause trouble, and someone calls the police, ending the round early. The game ends when you invite four Star Guests, such as aliens, dinosaurs, and mermaids, all with different abilities. It's super original, easy to get into, and a blast to play with friends. This is definitely a must-play if you purchase this game.- MIN & MAX: One of the longest games on the list. This is a huge Metroidvania game in the style of Super Mario Bros. 2 meets Alice in Wonderland. Play as a little girl named Min as you shrink down in size and explore the vast world of the Closet, making friends with all sorts of little things like bugs, toys, and dust bunnies. Later on, a whole other world begins to open up, making what seems to be an 8-hour game into a 20-hour exploration game. Tons of people to meet to help with their problems, as well as new abilities to float, store items, and command enemies. Not to mention it's extremely adorable and great for kids. If you've got the time, this is a very fun and satisfying experience.- AVIANOS: A very simplistic turn-based strategy game in which you manage bird soldiers to capture and hold castles. Pray to different deities for different actions, and build up your army to rush the enemy castle. Attacks are done on-screen in a semi-automatic way with a few minor control options at the bottom to give outnumbered soldiers a fighting chance. Even if you can learn all the rules fairly quickly, the depth of this game is surprisingly pretty vast as there are tons of ways you can take the game. The story mode is unfortunately very short (3 levels), but there are many trials afterward if you want to put your skills to the test. There's also 2 player versus with a lot of home rules to mess with in the options setting.Keep in mind that there are tons of other games that fit into many more genres. I've only mentioned 7, and there's 43 other games on this list. Try them all out!This is an amazing lineup of games for all players. Even if this game is retro-inspired at heart, there are still a ton of clever modern mechanics that they use to keep a lot of games from being too frustrating. Half of the games are two-player, and is highly recommended for Steam Deck. If any of this sounds interesting, this is a must-buy, even at full price. You'll get more than your money's worth out of the amount of hours you'll be spending.

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost certainly my game of the year. Stats:* 170 hours or so* 48 games tried* 26 games completed (13 gold 13 cherry)It should be clear from my hours that it takes a lot of time to get a full taste of all the games in this collection. If you're browsing reviews, maybe steer clear of any review that doesn't have 10, 15 hours. This is just one of those games where the refund window is not enough time to know if it's for you. There's so much variety and creativity among the games that it's hard to write a single recommendation, but...here goes.Here's some people I think will really like this collection:* Speedrunners, challenge runners, and arcade score-chasers who want a bunch of fresh challenges to pick from* Anyone with 1-2 specific genre interests who is also interested to try new things* Those with nostalgia for 80s and 90s games* Game design enthusiasts looking for inspiration or just something new to nerd out over* Meta lore enjoyers who are looking for an experience full of secrets* Anyone with a friend who also loves retro gamesAlso, keep in mind that UFO 50 is very low commitment if you think you're interested! I am confident that anyone who's interested will find 5-10 games that really appeal to them, and those games alone will be worth the price. And while games themselves are full games, they're more bite-sized, so people with less time on their hands don't have to worry like they would committing to, like, a full JRPG or even the average Ubisoft game these days.Here's some reasons I think someone might not like this collection:* They aren't satisfied by games that take 2-5 hours to complete* They want complex stories in their games* They dislike difficult and/or punishing gamesThe biggest reason people will bounce off of this collection is probably the way these games reflect their inspirations. Like the classics, a lot of these games are hard, punishing, confusing, or awkward, and there's little to no handholding. There's a lot that borrow from the arcade style, where after taking a few hits you go all the way back to the start of the game. The "Controls" tab in the menu helps with some of the confusing games, but unless you're willing to sometimes treat the learning process as part of the fun, many games may leave you frustrated. A decent amount of games in the collection are forgiving, straightforward, or very tight to play, but overall the collection has more intentional rough edges than the typical modern game.I, however, love this design philosophy. In almost every case, my struggles with difficult games paid off with satisfying wins, and my confusions with games turned into rewarding moments of realization. Where classic video games were often challenging because they were poorly balanced, or mysterious because they didn't teach vital mechanics, these games have felt challenging because of their carefully crafted difficulty curves, and mysterious because they had me learn by experimenting in situations designed to teach me. Plus, the games are not too big -- games that feel too difficult don't last too long, and games where you get lost have a small number of points of interest so you find your way easier. UFO 50 takes from classic games an increased amount of friction and a decreased scope. This way, it packs more dynamic, intense experiences into smaller games. It's unusual compared to modern games, and I really appreciate the difference.Some of my favorite games are:* Barbuta, an unwieldy, secretive nonlinear platformer seemingly inspired by Maze of Galious* Bushido Ball, a 1v1 tennis-like game where each character has a unique secondary and super-move* Vainger, a Metroid clone with gravity-flipping mechanics* Mooncat, a secretive platformer using only two buttons* Rail Heist, which consists of sixteen levels of trains to rob that are guarded very creatively* Porgy, a nonlinear underwater exploration game* Valbrace, a classic dungeon crawler with combat reminiscent of Punch Out* Campanella 2, Mossmouth's new take on a 2D platformer roguelike, in a UFOThis list -- probably even just half of it -- makes the collection worth it on its own. But there's 40 other games I got to try and enjoy! There's a few I bounced off of and haven't played much at all (e.g. Divers & Rakshasa), a few that grew on me (e.g. Magic Garden & Pingolf), a few that I loved at first but mellowed on over time (e.g. Bug Hunter & Camouflage), and a few I just don't really enjoy (e.g. Devilition & Combatants). But I have things to say about all of them! And that's without mentioning all the secrets hidden among the games.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't hear about it until it hit the social media waves, great game but I don't expect everyone to be a fan of all 50 games.Story: You get a collection of games from a fictious UFOSoft company that starts from its "First game" through 50 games that span a decade. Starts from a difficult barebones exploration game all the way to strategy games, full fledged RPG's, action games, racing games... all playable on the "LX console system." Even the historic "Don't put your name in games" trope is throughout as people use aliases.Gameplay: So you get 50 games, and each game has two levels of completion. One is the "Beat the game" gold trophy and then you get a cherry "Challenge" clear. Ranging from speed runs, score runs, deathless runs, finding things that require a level of finesse and expertise to achieve. The games in the collection run the gauntlet of every genre, and different levels of depth of some of those genres. Some of the games are really good, some of the games are ok, and some you are going to hate and wish it didn't exist. Controls are simplistic with dpad and 2 buttons and some controllers will accept stick VS dpad if you prefer that. Graphics: Its the 80's era stuff, not for everyone but definitely fits the theme of the game. As you play games in "chronological" order you start to go from base sprites to some detailed shading and things as the games get more advanced in sophistication but you aren't leaving a late 8/16 bit era vibe.9/10, but some of the gems outweigh some of the turds if you are willing to try all the games.

_childDocuments_.review: Something for everyone, this collection will likely pan out to be the greatest bang for your buck value for years to come, and an essential for anyone's library the same way Team Fortress 2 was.My only issue with the game is that apparently it's intensive enough to require a dedicated GPU for it. On the one hand, getting all of the games to work properly, let alone be fun to play, is a mammoth accomplishment. I think most of the games were smartly designed and justified to exist apart from their influences. On the other hand, the fact that my computer I bought just four years ago with 16GB of RAM struggles to handle games with pixel art is insane to me. It can handle Bloodstained, but not this? Not without putting the video settings available to be low, anyway.But make no mistake - this collection is legit. Some of these are strong enough to be standalone titles and I hope that maybe without a strong enough demand from players, we could see a Campanella 4 or a Mortol 3 or a Warptank 2. _childDocuments_.review: It is incredibly generous that this is only $25. It's the easiest game of the year pick of my life, and as I play more I increasingly suspect it may be one of the best games of all time. There is a humbling wealth of game design mastery at work here.UPDATE (31 hours): By now, after many more hours, the "sampler platter" phase has dropped off and I've begun to dig into games knowing what I prefer and what I don't. I miss the feeling of taking a chance on a random game and consistently being pleasantly surprised (although truth be told, there are still games I've logged just a few minutes in), and as such I highly recommend going into UFO 50 blind, with perhaps the understanding that Barbuta is an intentional outlier among the 50 games, and some players may find it helpful to start Pilot Quest early. Most games won't give you an explicit tutorial, but figuring out how each game works is extremely rewarding - each game *demands* your engagement and rewards you proportionally. 31 hours in, and I'm nowhere near finished gilding/cherrying everything I want to, and I've barely touched the Terminal. My complaints are still few and pale in comparison to the scope and depth and care put into everything here.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a retro experience similar to that of most NES games, UFO 50 may disappoint you. Its main inspiration mainly comes from the games conceived in the 80s for microcomputers like the MSX, C64 and ZX81; where genres, conventions and standards for controls were still not set, and every company in the business was experimenting, exploring the systems and shaping the rules of gaming itself.People who grew up in a different age and context need a very open mindset to appreciate what UFO 50 has to offer, even with all its concessions to modern sensibilities. For someone like me, who grew up with a C64 and played copied games with no manual or instructions, UFO 50 is a delightful callback - I found myself drawing game maps on paper, and fiddling with odd controls with a smile on my face.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've got any nostalgia from sitting around and playing retro, cartridge based games that only used a couple of buttons, UFO 50 is the best deal on Steam right now. _childDocuments_.review: This game sounds too good to be true and somehow, it just isn't. Yes, you'll spend more time on some games than others and sure, some are better than others, but NOTHING I've played has felt like filler. Each of these games is built on a clever idea and designed with such a focus on elegant simplicity that probably about 80% my 38 hours has been spent on 5 or 6 games (and not because those are the only ones worth playing, those 5 or 6 are so fun I didn't even want to play another)The obvious influence here is the NES era, which was well before my time, but this will also appeal to kids of the Flash Games era, people who like perusing game jams, or anyone who likes to blindly explore a well curated collection of cool ideas. For the most part, these games do not have explicit tutorials or instructions. If you are a fan of learning a game through experimentation and like to microdose Aha! moments, you will love this game. If productive struggle frustrates you, you might not. -This plays flawlessly on Steam Deck-Many games contain both singleplayer and multiplayer (which are often slightly different game modes, which is to say the single player is not just a worse version of a multiplayer game)-Even the single player makes for fun 'pseudomultiplayer' as you learn a game together-I play a lot of puzzle games and while not everything in here is a puzzle game, they all scratch the "figure out what's going on" itch-Every "What's your favorite game?" thread has had a TON of variance in the responses so there is truly something for everyone hereIf you enjoy exploring clever ideas executed cleanly, $25 is beyond a bargain and I haven't even tried every game yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game collection for many reasons. I love the unified art style and the choice to lean heavily into pixel art as it really allows the artists to express themselves. You're getting tremendous value for what you purchase, each of the games are fantastic in their own right and no matter what genre you like the most, there will no doubt be quite a few that you will enjoy and some which you will treasure. The presentation is outstanding, even just with the game collection which shows off the games really puts you in the right mindset and gives you ways to sort games along with marking games as 'favourites'. The sound is spot on and really captures that retro vibe. The game looks fantastic and especially suits portable devices too such as the Steam Deck. Whether you're on a smaller-screened device or a massive monitor you will love the visuals.For me the two games that had me hooked for a while were Avianos and Party House. Going into more depth, Avianos is turn-based strategy at it's finest with some impressive real-time battles featuring your armies. The different units play into each other really well with shield units absorbing arrows, flying units being able to bombard swordsmen and each troop has their own best and worst matchups respectively. While numbers do help a lot with the armies, the composition of the army is very important as a massive shield wall could easily take down an unprepared foe. Mechanics like surprise attacks, teleporting and magic spells can easily transform the battlefield and your opposing armies. Having to choose the best deity that will not only generate resources effectively but also build up your army strength really does get you planning your moves effectively and reacting to the AI or another human player really does give this a massive amount of depth, even if there are only 20 board tiles on the map. The limited number of moves you can make in a turn really does emphasis making every single turn count.Party House starts fairly simple but becomes more complicated as the game goes on. Your objective is to build up your popularity and money in order to add VIPs to your rolladeck and expand the house to allow more guests. The constant balance of keeping troublemakers away while also trying to bring in the resources you need is a constant battle. Playing to certain guest's strengths is so crucial and often winning or losing can weigh heavy on which guests you added to your deck and which order, along with the random order of the way they enter the house. It starts simple but really ramps up and makes this challenging but manageable.Briefly touching on other games I enjoyed the most, Waldorf's Journey has a Jump King vibe as you send your walrus hurtling through the sky, frantically flapping to try and stay on a nearby platform. Buying items with collected shells gives you bonuses as well which can help, but watch out for flying obstacles and immovable walls! Onion Delivery puts you in a retro Grand Theft Auto style world where you follow the blips on your minimap, try not to hit objects or get lost and try to make it back home in one piece. Combatants is a real-time strategy life sim where you try and get your ant colony thriving and conquer against the evil red army, each mission gets slightly harder forcing you to adapt your strategy and outlast your opponent.I could easily go into more detail here but there really is a wide breath of games to sink your teeth into. There's many other games in the package including a betting simulator, platformers, shooters, sports games, metroidvanias, adventures, puzzle games and arcade-style games. Most offer a singleplayer experience while a few are playable with another player and some also support co-op gameplay too. I highly recommend this game, especially if you are a huge fan of retro gaming and high-quality pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: A compilation of 50 unique games where the DNA of 80s classics meets modern creativity. UFO 50 isn't just a collection: it's a true declaration of love for video games.Each game plunges us into the unknown, with no tutorial to guide us. Here, it's all about exploration, experimentation and figuring things out for yourself. The controls, inspired by the NES, are simple and accessible: a directional cross, two buttons. Nothing superfluous, just the essentials for immediate fun. And yet, underneath this apparent simplicity lies incredible depth: ingenious mechanics, well-hidden secrets and, sometimes, the need to draw a map or write down our discoveries in order to progress. UFO 50 is a brilliant tribute to retro games and an ode to the diversity of gameplays: action, puzzle, RPG, shoot'em up... Each title is a universe in its own right, rich in challenges and surprises. No microtransactions, no modern horrors, just pure, sincere gaming, designed to be explored, shared, replayed endlessly or even mastered as a speedrun for the most tenacious.Whether you're nostalgic for pixels or eager for new experiences, UFO 50 is a universal work that will touch you. And once you're in, it's almost impossible to get out. Ready to take up the challenge?
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is the brain child of an entire team of independent creatives at Mossmouth, the studio behind the two popular roguelite dungeon (or maybe cave?) crawlers, Spelunky and Spelunky 2. UFO 50 is hard to describe as a “game” in the word’s singular form, for it is, as the name might reveal, a collection of 50 video games made by the indie studio over the span of 9 long years. To this end, this bundle of games is nothing short of monumental, both in terms of price-to-content ratio, as well as its sheer scope for a work of independent game design. UFO 50 can also be described as quite ingenious in terms of many of the ideas that it brings to the table throughout its 50 bespoke experiences as well as for its general quality over this exhaustive number of games, both big and small.Nine years, however, is a short time to make 50 games and though amazing, UFO 50 still suffers from the occassional objectively poorly designed experience, or even downright broken game, such as the community’s most reviled “Combatants”, an RTS with abysmal level design, horrendous friendly unit AI and pathing and just a baffling blatancy to its lack of polish in these and a few other areas. This collection, telling the fictional story of short-lived 1980s gaming manufacturer “Ufosoft” is clearly inspired and arguably even somewhat of a parody of those old, bootleg shovelware cartridges for the old Nintendo Entertainment System and the like, to this end, as well as to the end of delivering a genuinely interesting story of this fictional company throughout its 50 chronologically sorted offerings, UFO 50 also delights and helps to deliver on the lofty promises those bootlegers made back in the day to every child and parent out there.However, due to its arguable overabundance of games () and due to being made by Mossmouth, of all companies, who, if you’ve ever played Spelunky or especially its sequel, have a hard time discerning between fair difficulty design and playing an RNG slot machine sometimes, some games in this collection are held back and a few of them, though mercifully not the majority, show little meaningful difference between themselves and the shovelware that inspired this collection’s existence. Some of the games in the collection also commit the cardinal sin of borrowing both the good and the bad and archaic from the retro games of old.If you’re fine with the above, can hold back your completionist urges, to not let them sully your experience and can maybe hold out a little for some of the game’s bigger flaws and bugs to potentially be ironed out with time, then I highly recommend UFO 50, even if just to witness its novelty and get inspired by some of its more bizarre and interesting ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: More than I thought I think this is more for a specific type of person. I think people who have played recent indie games and not the original games from the 80s may be disappointed or even angry at this.This really has the feeling of picking up a random game on sale or from a game bin and not really understanding anything about the game until you bring it home to play. The cover arts often did not represent the game and it was hard to understand what the game was about from the back of the box. There are 50 games, so this game gives you 50 of those experiences.I also stink at many of the early games and I don't really understand what to do in many of them. Ultimately, I am not sure how much time I can put into this and feel like many of the games may be too time consuming for me.If all this sounds great, then you are the target audience for this game.  It is definitely a lost experience in the modern era.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. The amount of content you're given for the price tag is phenomenal. You probably won't love all 50 games but there is such a variety of creative games, that there are going to be many games you will adore. The length of games will vary greatly from game to game.Its's basically a modernized beefed up NES library. I've played all the games and only fully completed a couple so far, but I've seen enough to know that I can't wait to fully dive into each one. It has rpgs, metroidvanias, racing games, rougelites, shoot em ups, puzzle games, point and click horror, and all kinds of insanely creative games with fresh inventive mechanics and ideas that are not seen elsewhere. This is an easy recommend at full price. Easy to pick up, hard to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Its 50 Top Quality NES games. I dunno what to say besides that. If you enjoy Retro games get it. You wont love all of them but they are all well made and come with the expected limitations and issues with ease of use to expect from a game of the era. There are many that are genuinely inventive and unique enough to have been sold on their own for 10 to 20 dollars if seperated from the package.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this not really knowing what to expect other than it's made by some of my favorite devs. What's crazy to me is that most of the games in here that I've played so far feel pretty simple and shallow on the surface, but then end up having some insane depth.  MoonCat stands out to me as something that perfectly shows this package, as it's super weird, has only two buttons, but has some insane depth. Those two buttons allow for a ton of different moves and it turned from one of my least favorite to most favorite in the collection. This whole package is filled with a ton of retro goodies that feels like what I remember my childhood games feeling like. Which, those games now feel awful, but this game feels great.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: fun collection of 50 different games from a fictional video game company similar to the nes. can't say i loved every single game but the ones i do are more than worth the price. you can tell the devs put a lot of time and love into this, each game is legitimately it's own game you'd have paid full price for in 1985. some of my favorite games have modern sensibilities but their recreations of 1980's platformers is very accurate. runs great on the deck.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The quality here per game is absolutely wild. You could easily put 4-5 hours in most of these, with some of them being ~10 hours to finish. And there are 50 games! All with controller support. One of the best possible buys for steam deck.The games are old school though, with a lot of emphasis on platforming, and get more complicated as "time" progresses (the first game is the fictional company's first game, with the 50th being their most recent). Lots to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

Do you like figuring things out on your own?Do you like games with a sense of humor?Do you like racing games, puzzle games, fighting games, shmups, bullet hells, RPGs, or golf games?Do you like betting on a horse and kneecapping the opponents to ensure your big payday?You might like UFO50.

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many ways an idea this ambitious could fail.  Or just be middle of the road bleh.Instead, each game feels loved, like it had a champion in the room fighting for it to be the best version of itself.  Like Spelunky and Downwell, the design choices in these games feel incredibly specific and intentional.  There isn't a throwaway in the collection, even the games I vibe with less are still clearly labors of love.It's all the spirit and bursting creativity of a game jam, with the polish of a Devolver Digital release.Easily the best game I've played released in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the greatest games I've ever playedWhen I first heard about this game I thought - interesting gimmick, wonder if there's any decent games in thereLet me tell you, the quality of these games is unbelievable - thirty plus of them I got totally invested in, and most of the rest were very well made action games that aren't my cup of tea but someone else would love - there's only two games of the fifty I'd say are actually not up to scratch, and for both of them there's lore reasons for their deficienciesI've put over a hundred hours in so far and still there's three substantial games I've yet to really sink my teeth intoHighly, highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Reading the negative reviews has actually been hilarious. This is an amazing set of games with easily a few hundred hours of content. Simplistic base that adds complexity through innovative mechanics or refined mechanics. If you consider the price and that you would enjoy at least half the games then you are already getting an incredible value.One of the reviews tried to call it 50 short demos and would be better if the games were longer, they had less than 30 minutes play time... There are several metroidvanias and RPGs in the mix that are hours of content on their own. Being so confidently ignorant is a talent if you ask me. Kids don't have the attention spam to put more than a few minutes into something and suddenly have all the answers. This is probably the best collection of retro style games ever created.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game has legitimately made waiting for anything a joy, because now I can just boot up my steam deck and play any game on UFO 50 and be sure to have a fun time. It's an amazingly addictive set of games, there's literally something for everyone in this collection, and these aren't short games; they have so much depth. There's even a whole SquareEnix-esque RPG in this thing!! If you want the best value for your buck you can't go wrong with this.One thing I will say is that, akin to classic retro games, there are a few games in this collection that are not very photosensitive-friendly; essentially, any of the shmups. If you are photosensitive, keep this in mind when selecting what games to play. There's plenty of other games in the collection that don't involve flashing effects.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say nothing more than anybody else said, but its important to emphesize. Its not for everyone,if you despise the difficulty and jank of an 8 bit era games you will find nothing of value in this package.On the other hand if you like or just even tolerate those aspects of old games you will find yourself sinking countless hours in your favourite games from the collection
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game, my game of the year for sure. I never really feel the need to leave a review for games, but this one I had to. It feels like even with all the positive praise this game is getting it still deserves tenfold more. The fact that this is 50 well crafted games for the price of only $25 is an amazing value, I have nearly 20 hours into it and have maybe only spent serious time in 1/5th of the games available and still have yet to try about 10 of them. I keep getting surprised by how each time I try a new game it is not only a fun and usually unique take on a concept that I haven't seen before, but that it is also a full fledged game sometimes being several hours long that probably could've been sold on it's own on steam for $10. And I haven't even tried the ~15 hour western themed jrpg yet. The fact that these games all tie into an overarching meta narrative on top of that with the fictional Ufosoft developer, and the progression you can see in the chronology of games going from the clunky Barbuta as game 1 to the much more polished games by the end, is just the bow that neatly ties this incredible package together. I will be enjoying many more hours of this great collection and applaud Mossmouth on the monumental achievement that is UFO 50.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this collection, I thought it would be tailored to people who enjoy either wide varieties of genres and experiences, and/or people who enjoy retro games, but honestly speaking, the quality rock-solid design between almost all of these 50 titles make it an easy recommendation for anybody! It's been a long time since I've been this enraptured with a game, and the fact that after 50 hours I still find it hard to put down is a testament to the insane value of this package. Even if not all the games are to your liking, the games have plenty of replayability and challenge, so finding and playing the ones you personally enjoy will be enough to carry you through many hours of excitement with very little of the repetitive tasks you'd normally find from a game of this length.The music is also fantastic throughout, even down to the short catchy jingles you hear during "round start" in the more arcade-style titles! From atmospheric and gentle melodies found in Night Manor and Mooncat, to the catchy tunes of Pilot Quest and Warptank, I find myself wanting to come back to the games just for the music sometimes!Finally, the art direction is charming and of a very high quality throughout all the games. Limited colour palettes and recurring sprites in various games lend themselves to the idea that these are real classic games that were just lost in time, and are sure to put a smile on your face if you've ever played anything similar!It's shocking that a game this polished and enjoyable can release with the relatively small amount of fanfare that it has (not to say it's underrated of course, but I hope more people are able to find this game and experience it all for themselves)! The team at Mossmouth did a great job on this collection, and I hope my review may convince you to give it a chance, it's truly one of a kind!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a collection of 50 single and multiplayer games from the creators of Spelunky, Downwell, and Catacomb Kids. Explore a variety of genres, from platformers and shoot 'em ups to puzzle games, roguelites, and RPGs. Our goal is to combine a familiar 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design.
