_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I wanted to recommend, but I just can't. Ever since Dragon Marked for Death was released on the Switch, it was one of the prime titles that I've considered buying the console for. I've been a long-time fan of Inti-Creates' platformer games, going all the way back to Megaman Zero. So, the idea of a co-op, RPG-based platformer from Inti-Creates seemed to hit all the right buttons.When compared to other Inti-Creates platformers, Dragon Marked for Death falls short by a impressive margin. I've had to drag myself to finish this game, to play it with a friend that I had convinced to buy this game as well. In short:There is a lack of content, padded out by time-wasting mechanics and frustrating stage design.The RPG system adds little to the game other than hitting that Skinner box feel of improvement.The stages are  in their design, and have no redeeming qualities.The music is sadly forgettable.The art and animation is good.The story is uninspired and shares a lot of the same story beats from other original Inti games.There are at most 20 different enemy types in the game, with a rotating set of 10 of them being used in every single stage. This quickly makes you feel like you're fighting the same enemies over and over again. Similarly, there's a severe lack of bosses to fight; there are at most 7 unique bosses. The problem here is that there is both a lack of variety, and uninteresting design. Enemies are extremely plain and uninspired; most will simply just charge at you in an attempt to deal contact damage. Bosses fare only slightly better than this; they're limited to 3-4 attacks with very poor telegraphs and tells. If you are coming to the game expecting the bosses to have the same combat quality as a  or  game, you will be sorely disappointed, as I have been.The stages are unforgivable. Due to the structure of the game, each stage no longer operates in a “single direction”; different missions will have you start in different locations on the same map, and will have you going left or right. The problem with this design is that the stages end up being extremely bland because you have to be able to traverse in both directions. The platform placement, the hazards, all of it is extremely amateur in comparison to the stages in other Inti games. The stages themselves are also massive, yet empty; there is so much time just simply lost to running over flat terrain, sparsely littered with enemies. Some stages have a unique gimmick to them, all of them  annoying. One stage has slippery ice sections, while another has wind constantly pushing you in a direction. There are disappearing platforms, slow elevators, and other additions that do little other than make you wait around, or retrace your steps. If you've had a similar misfortune in playing , the stage design is just as bad and annoying.The aesthetic design of the stages are also extremely “safe”. The game uses almost every stereotypical setting in the exact manner you'd expect them. Icy mountain, Saharan tomb, grassy wildlands, Japanese castle. Even some of the more unique “new” areas draw heavy inspiration from other Inti titles. There's only one new stage here, which is a shame considering the artistic talent they have.The RPG system does little to make the game more interesting. If anything, the statistical distribution of your character more or less “gear checks” you for missions; having an improper spread in the right numbers will make your playthrough incredibly annoying as you'll either “miss” enemies, get bricked by contact damage, or just deal piddly amounts of damage. This could've been replaced with a skill tree system that unlocked new abilities or effects, like the weapon-level up system in Zero, , but there's none of that here.There is a severe lack of content. This is evident in several aspects, mainly through the enemy variety and number of stages. This is made worse in how the game's missions are structured. As stated before, missions will take you back to the same 7 stages, but with a different starting area and slightly different enemy layout. You'll come to quickly memorize the map after running missions in the same area over and over again. Replayability is done through increasing the quest level to grind for better gear and levels; enemies and bosses get statistically stronger, but everything else stays the same. There is also a loot system in the game, but it's as basic as you can get.The combat on the enemy side is incredibly frustrating and annoying. This is primarily due to the inclusion of status effects in the worst way possible. You can have your controls reversed, unable to attack or dash, or slowed to a crawl. To cure these, you have to open up your inventory and use a consumable to dispel these effects. This is a action platformer, not a turn-based RPG. And these effects will  get you killed in a middle of a battle because of how debilitating they are. In addition, due to how stat scaling works with the level up system, you can very easily get one-shot by enemy attacks if they are a mere 5 levels above your level. Combine this with seeing the same batch of enemies over and over again, your patience will wear out quickly.The gameplay of each character is hit-or-miss. Empress plays like a very, very watered-down version of Zero. Basic sword swings and a projectile, but no charged moves or extended combos. Warrior plays like a traditional tanking class, but works best in a party. Bandit plays like a very basic version of Copen/Acura, but can't hover indefinitely like the latter. Witch effectively uses Magicka's casting system for spells. Most of the fun I had in DMFD came from mastering the characters, as thin as they may be.The music is extremely stereotypical and bland, and has little connecting themes between each one. Aside from the first stage theme, all the other tracks are quickly forgettable. Seth Everman's game music clichés are in full force here.The only saving grace of this game is the art. Nakayama Tooru's style is still incredibly visually distinctive. The individual character designs are still great, with the animation being incredibly fluid, despite running at effectively the same resolution as the old Zero games. And while most of the enemy designs are pretty uninspired, they animate great; breathing and bobbing with great detail.For it's current price, I would heavily recommend against it, even for enthusiasts of the genre. There are better platformers out there, like any other Inti title currently available on Steam. This would've been considered an okay title 10 years ago, but not today, and especially not from team that has made much, much better platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hear much from this game but it's an easy to miss gem.For those wanting to get into this, this game is made really well for any player's skill level. There's a lot of balancing put into place so if you're not into mega/gun volt precision type game this is one to try out. For one this game give you a lot to work with if you're not fancy to the speed life. You got healing items, gear, leveling, and various elemental teaks you can do.When it come to veterans of the game this is a master pieces. I managed to run through this game as Empress with out ever once feeling like I hit a wall or anything railroading me to level up as much as I feared. I was always able to do damage even if I was under the levels beyond 20+. I managed to run through the whole game around mid level 20 with all my points put into damage so I played as a glass-cannon that could die in one hit to anything at levels 30-40+. I should go over the positiveness and negatives.Pros:◈ In game story is really good. I can't tell you the amount of times I ask why am I fighting and who am I doing what for. The first go round really makes you question a lot on what is right and wrong(I can't tell you the amount of times I felt some type of way from just reading through it. It's rare that I get a strong feeling like that in games now)◈ Really easy to jump into at any skill level◈ Each character has their own unique ability's that give advantage or disadvantage in fights and exploration◈ The game leaves all the guide and tips in the start menu. Not once does it suddenly stop you just to tell you how to do something with your character◈ Many ways to approach this game. You are given gear, weapons, and tons of shop options along side special items to drastically change your character at will◈ When you find a good foot hold it is very addictive even without Co-op◈ You are given a nice training area for any boss you wish to fight◈ All your gold and loot is shared across other characters◈ One you made other characters on the save file of your choice you can go into the Inn and change characters on the fly without the need to go to the pause menu◈ This feels perfect for speed running.◈ You can really go whiled with how you want your character's build to be as long as you have the will power to make it◈ DLC characters comes naturally with the game so no need to worry about that◈ No matter the class just about all characters are able to run at the same speed. The only character that has a special speed skill is the Shinobi◈ Gear and armor power keeps growing even past end game◈ Is a small detail but every time you change weapons it shows on your character. Even some weapons have special max level looks that's nice to check out◈ The higher the difficulty level is the more all enemy's will change. Rather they are faster, shoot more projectiles, or get a completely new move sets it really transforms the game. This includes bosses◈ All levels are crafted well with all characters in mind so you will never be truly stuck (Unless you're me)◈ Your weapons and gear really start to shine around I be leave level 20+. This is where the points start to go high and you get extra strong passive abilities to follow (I was supper late in getting this sense by end game was the time I got my hands on one of these. This may be a con for some megaman/gun volt master who want that sweat gear and weapons. I looked like a mid-tier rookie running into satin and winning without taking damage)◈ After end game you will get a tower quest which is just going until you can't no more. Really good grind and challenge-I'm sure there's so much more I could go over but lets touch on the cons.Cons:◈ At the start of the game you are given 4 characters to pick from. The last 2 are ones you can unlock by just about finishing the game. I personally don't know where to put this sense in a way if you are keeping up with the story and everything that goes on it makes sense in a lore stand point but I don't know. I know some people after finished end game will not feel interested in running a game back over gain unless it's really worth or just that fun to do. I personally didn't mind as I had a blast with the game◈ The grind in this game for levels and power feels a bit slow and repetitive.(I personally never needed to grind but just running through the main story I noticed some repetitive areas just with different stuff layered around)◈ You will need to redo the story & quest with every new character you got. This is not a problem if you are really good and fast at the game. At best it may take a few hours 2-3 at best if you're just rushing it (You will have to be skilled or you will be spending a lot of that time grinding levels to wear gear & weapons)◈ The endgame feels empty. At best the only thing that's left in game is redoing old stages on harder difficulty beyond that I personally could cut through all of it with my damage being so high. Might feel a lot different with another build then glass cannon it is something you will have to try out◈ Even though this game has Co-op there is no one on to play with you (I head there was a server or some community out there so maybe there is people playing at set times)◈ Personally I has a speed running itch and tried my hand at blind 100% the game. Seeing how long that took me might take others double if playing casual. I managed to beat the game in about a day and a half (I'm sure I can shave off that time drastically now that I know what to expect. I'm not sure if you should call this a con but I'm putting it here for now)◈ As cool as the elemental ability are not once are they really something you will ever need to pay attention to. Never does the game give you a puzzle or does it feel amazing to use in combat. At best it's just a projectile you can optionally choose to change. (I keep forgetting about it but there is a weak/strong system with elements but never has the game really hit me with the need to think about it. It feels more like a forgettable side cosmetic that looks cool to change at first. Beyond that it is just something you use to deal with out of reach monsters)◈ From what I can see, I don't be leave there is a way to reassign and change your level points after you set them so ones they are there there is no going back to change you build◈ Putting in time to level up felt like a drag. I never really need to grind in the game I just went on but I hear a lot about how it is a huge grind at times and I felt like I understood that after endgame. It's not really required sense I'm sure you can beat ever level if you're skilled enough but a lot of gear and armor is locked behind a level wall which I know, "If your so good at the game then why do you need to wear gear any ways" but still. I wanna see all the good swords I got without needing to wait◈ (Personal Take) For me who has been playing mega games for a living my experience is more the opposite from casual community so my view may be drastically different. Some things in the game felt very easy to ignore when you can flow through the game even when I came up to the parts of the level where I can die from one hit from common enemies and boss attacks I only felt underwhelmed. It's more like, "This feels great that fight was kinda hard, wait that's it?" I'm sure a lot is do to me play as a glass cannon but it's very rare that you will be put in the situation where you can't dodge are avoid a whole cycle/attack without getting touched. You just about can avoid and dodge everything as long as you remember how it works. There where only two boss fights I felt pressured by end game boss was shockingly easy even though one hit could kill me◈ I found it hard to keep going after post game. Maybe live Co-op would fix that. I'm down to play this with anyone if they are interested-That's all I got, thanks for checking my review!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed about this one. Overall, recommended, but with criticism strong enough to avert people from buying this. If you're going to play this once and put it down, go for it and buy it. If you think there's depth here, look somewhere else. The trailer really hypes it up too much. I liked it, but for my own reasons. There are strong negatives.Positive:1. Style is on-point for any fan of Inti's MMZ and MMZX titles. It's visually appealing throughout the entire experience.2. Gameplay is solid. It's a side-scrolling hack-and-slash game, so fans of the genre will seamlessly transition into this title. It's also accessible for newer players and ramps up well in terms of actual leveling.3. Music's varied enough and SFX aren't too intrusive.4. Progression is decent. It's a bit grindy, and there were a couple of parts where being underleveled was a problem, but then after running the same, safe missions for a bit massively overleveled me. Kind of weird.5. The pace is fast and consistent. There are few places that lag or suffer from being too slow or drawn-out. The game expects you to go super fast and lets you, with a few gotchyas. The missions are timed, but the timer stops when you pause in single-player.6. Character variety is alright. Each of the four, and then extra fifth and sixth classes are different from each other, but... more on that below.Needs work:1. Character classes themselves are split between useful and useless. This game's fast, and at least the witch and oracle classes are in direct conflict with this design choice. To use any meaningful ability on either character, you must memorize cryptic button combinations that instantly fail if you get one of the sequence wrong. To use the more powerful spells, like in the trailer, you've gotta do that multiple times in a row, where you can't really afford to, since there's stuff attacking you and the timer's ticking. There's almost no incentive to choosing the oracle, witch or warrior.2. Story is weak. Even the extra expose in the full side-objectives is lacking and there's no real character arch for anyone.3. Replayability is non-existent. Your mission progress is tied to each character individually, but items carry over between them. I don't want to, and I assume others won't, either, run the same low-level missions a second, or heck third time on a different character. Why would anyone do this? Instead, have mission statuses carry over between all of the classes, I already know the story.4. Some of the missions (not levels) are incredibly poorly-designed, especially in the DLC for the bandit class. Sometimes, you're left wandering around a huge maze with arbitrary targets, sometimes you must go to point A, then find some random target in point B, but wait, point A's thing is on an invisible timeout, so better hurry! If you don't get to point B fast enough, you've gotta go back to point A, then back to B, then back to A, then forward to some random spot C, then back to A... you get it. Whoever designed stuff like this needs to rethink their approach going forward.5. Stats don't make sense. I dumped points into STR and AGI as Empress, and plowed through mostly everything, until I couldn't, then I ground. It makes no sense to get VIT until way later in the game as Empress. I'm sure it's the same for other classes with their respective stat points.6. Itemization is weak. There's a sword that's basically mandatory, but you gotta grind for it. From what I've read on the forums, it's the same for other classes. You only get two weapons and two passive item slots for rings and anklets and bracers and stuff, it just feels incredibly incomplete when compared to games in this same genre. Everything's tiered, until it's not, and there's no logic behind what can and can't be upgraded. It's a lazy Sword +1, +2, +3, etc system.7. No customization. No hats, no color-changes, no voice-changing, etc. You can do this once when you make a char, but that's it. No cosmetics exist in any way, shape or form.8. Multiplayer is so, so underutilized. There's almost no one ever on, and there's no incentive to party since drops are crap on most missions, anyway. Some missions require a fast character, and I've helped a few players already, since they chose the witch and couldn't do the mission in the specified time-limit alone. Anyway, when there are people on, the levels vary wildly, and even when you pick the biggest range and choose world-wide matchmaking, there's still going to be hardly anyone around. There's just no point to the online matchmaking, better solo it or play it with a friend. It's faster to play with others in some situations, though, and that's fine.10. Level design is... well, whatever. It's varied, with some levels being mazes, some being A to B, some being utterly crappy time-wasting garbage.It's just lazy overall. They put so much effort into the style, the forgot the story and items, character development and customization. There's no point in using suboptimal anything, anywhere, from class to item.Conclusion:Get it, as stated, if you're gonna play it once and leave it. It's a straight-forward experience you can easily do alone and it'll be enjoyable enough. If you start looking more deeply into the flaws, then just don't bother with this. It's trying to be more than it is, and until characters are fixed and matchmaking is worthwhile, items make sense and the missions are seriously reconsidered, just play this alone until you're satisfied.A great platforming hack-and-slash that's stylistic and fast, but anemic in the RPG aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the issues that reviews of this game bring up have been ironed out through a year of support since the game's launch of Switch. Notably, one of the latest updates ironed out many people's complaints about the two free unlockable characters. The game is a Megaman Zero styled game with a Castlevania-esc feel, going through instanced quests to even complete some sort of goal or, more commonly, to defeat a boss at the end of the map. Several maps (mainly ones themed around dungeons) have unique mechanics to them, too. It's a pretty enjoyable ride from start to finish, as each of the available classes FEEL like different characters, due to the number of gameplay style differences between them all. This being said, one small thing I'd warn you about ahead of time is that  obtaining the final mission requires you to do small side objectives in eight of the quests, and you'll likely just want to look up how to trigger them ahead of time, as it's very easy to miss a few of them. Also, one complaint I do have is that if you want to get the game's true ending, you'll have to get one of the endings on all of the four starting characters in order to meet the requirements. Once you know what those earlier mentioned side objectives are, this isn't too difficult to do, but it's more tedious than it needed to be.The build variety in this game is pretty good, as each available class can assign itself to one of five elements, modifying various things about the class that aren't just limited to status effects and elemental damage, as you may presume (though you do start the game as a specific element). Odds are that, with the odd exception of the witch and oracle classes, if you don't like something about a class, changing your element. your weapon (as each class can use two types), or build will help you like them much more.The story is okay - nothing award winning, but a pretty good vehicle for the gameplay. The pixel art in the game is excellent, and there are even some points in the game where they use environmental story telling incredibly well. I bring this up here because there are a number of concepts that, in my opinion, look incredible when combined with the aesthetics they chose - like how the more you see of the dragon's enemies and areas, the more occult it comes off (fitting with the game's story).The only major gripes I could say I have with the game are sort of ironic - there isn't enough of it, and despite being a multiplayer game it lacks co-op and cross-play throughout its versions (though the PC version can be modded to have split-screen co-op). The post game for Dragon Marked For Death is replaying the missions you've already obtained at higher difficulties, with an increase in enemies and several enemy variations that are limited to those higher difficulties. That being said, there are only so many times you can go through the same maps before it starts to get to you - the bosses gaining additional moves and effects does help to alleviate this somewhat, though. And, even with all this said, there ARE somewhere around 40-50 missions in this game, with some having less difficulty levels available and being shorter than others, so it isn't as if there's very little content.At the end of the day, if you like Megaman Zero games, you'll probably like this. If you liked them and thought a multiplayer version of them would be amazing, you'll probably like this game. This is one of those games out there where quickplay is dead, especially since the game lacks cross-play, so your best bet at finding online games is through DMFD's Discord server. There's an invite to it on the game's Reddit, so if you're interested, head there.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two things you need to know before buying this game:1) This game is a grind fest. You will grind, then you will grind some more... and then you will grind some more. Just when you think you're done grinding, you'll want a more powerful weapon so you'll spend a few hours farming the same boss over and over until you get the drop you want. Be prepared to grind, or you will regret it.2) This game has a relatively small playerbase. A lot of similar games have a bigger playerbase and you will have no trouble finding a multiplayer room. But with DMFD you might struggle to find a room if you just try to join public lobbies. I recommend talking to the other players in this game's community here on Steam or on Reddit or some such if you want to find a group to play with because otherwise you'll probably have trouble finding a group.Those two major issues aside, this is a really solid little action platformer. Full disclosure - I played Witch and then Oracle, but my friend recommended that I try every class, so I got them all to level 20. Very fun, and the only class I truly disliked playing as was Warrior. Too slow, but holy crap was he powerful.Onto the pros and cons...PROs~ Simple yet beautiful graphics~ Satisfying combat~ Interesting magic system~ Plenty of unique enemies~ Many unique bosses (each requiring their own strategies)~ Interesting dialogue and story~ Six unique characters, each having their own skills and styles~ Multiple possible builds per character~ Exceedingly difficult post game area to test your skills in~ Many unique buffs obtainable as drops~ Oracle is amazing - I will not be convinced otherwiseCONs~ Story is way too short~ Combat is extremely repetitive~ GRIND~ Some mechanics are significantly more difficult/tedious on keyboard (Magic)~ Requirements to unlock characters/endings are not disclosed in game (check for guides online)~ Certain quests are significantly harder than their 'Suggested Level' would suggest, causing difficulty spikes~ GRIND SOME MORE~ Drop rates for certain items feel far too low~ Crafting upgrades are unclear, too much RNG in drops for crafting materials~ Buffs usually overwrite instead of stack or refresh (Got me killed more than a few times)~ All classes that aren't Oracle feel weak, level by level.To the curious - Oracle is unlocked by defeating the final boss of the game, which can only be unlocked by collecting all of the 'flags' in story related stages. The two biggest problems here are 1) There's no clear indicator of which stages have flags; and 2) There's no clear indicator of how to obtain the flags; for both issues, you can use online guides, so it's not a huge issue at the end of the day, but it makes things difficult for anyone that doesn't want to use a guide.Not much else to say about this little gem. I'm not a fan of the price being $39.99, but I've never been a huge fan of grind games to begin with, so that's a factor for consideration. As of the writing of this review, the game is currently on sale for $19.99 so I would recommend grabbing it if the information here hasn't deterred your interest. Definitely worth $20 in my opinion. Probably not worth $40 though, but that's just my two cents. Take it for what you will.Side note: A friend of mine purchased the game for me and I'm extremely grateful for the experience. <3

_childDocuments_.review: tldr If you're looking for a Mega Man Zero/ZX like game or a metroidvania, this isn't it. Dragon Marked For Death attempts many things with varying degrees of success. From the surface level you'd think it is a Mega Man Zero like game but it's more like a "theme park" type of ARPG where you run the same dungeons over and over looking for the ever so slightly stat increase to increase the gameplay loop. However the level design is not particularly great, most of the time you will find yourself running the same flat ground holding right while nothing is happening or just fighting the same enemies over and over with the occasional shortcut some classes may be able to take.The common enemy variety is poor and most of them act very similar, either by trying to ram to do contact damage, or throwing a projectile towards you or in a arc, ocasionally having a debuff imbued in them.The boss design is also not very good,at lower levels they will throw a simple pattern at you, at higher levels the patterns become more complex or sometimes just something that you won't figure out how to dodge or it's downright impossible to depending on the class choosen, eventually doing so much damage at once that resist sudden death gear becomes mandatory to not play a one hit simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I had a huuuge review written out and Steam decided to be a jerk about it and say there was a problem, boop all gone so here's the short version dood.Good 1 - Lots of visual and gameplay references to the megaman Z, X and ZX games2 - plays super well with great variety 3 - what music there is, is good 4 - well designed bosses and monsters who gain more attacks and patterns as you do harder missions5 - six classes to play as all of which work well together in their own ways 6 - some great level design that benefits from other classes being used for speed and treasure gathering7 - online co-op with friends is a great timeBad 1 - no audio settings so limited music tends to get old real fast (some people myself included like the volume down for other things) 2 -Oracle needs a major buff in some regards as well as a fix on her dragon attacks which are genuinely actually broken and not in the good way3 - Stats on later levels mean nothing as you can happily have over 50 points more than their defence and still barely do damage to them (granted I do believe you are also meant to have a 4 man team on 80+ so that's probably actually not that bad really)End notes - Fantastic game, that I hope get's either more content or another game if not both, I'd happily spend hours and hours more playing this game and in fact still am, if you're a fan of great gameplay similar megaman X, Z and ZX albeit made it's own and improved on for all the fun times then I say buy it for sure dood.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fantastic game! Absolutely recommend if you're a fan of the Megaman Zero franchise but as well as the GBA Castlevania titles. The game's missions/levels are presented in a sort of Phantasy Star Online style in that you're often revisiting the same large sprawling stages with different objectives. What this game does that's very interesting is that depending on the quest- certain areas of said stages are sealed off and you're set to explore only certain routes of these large maps on a by-quest basis.There is quite a lot of replayability with it even- with the higher and higher difficulty versions of the quests way past the game's final level bracket (even that has a higher level version.)The characters are all fairly unique with their own respective roles and playstyles and I've found myself kind of regularly switching between them just because they're all that much fun to play as.My biggest gripe with this game is the lack of a BGM/SFX slider, the inability to turn the game's music down and listen to your own thing while grinding the same stage for the sixtieth time is pretty insufferable, I've been begging and pleading for it to be implemented hopefully in a future version of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Super well made side-scrolling, monster hunter-ish action. Moves great, like veteran Capcom Mega Man X developers must have built it. Definitely play this, the game world is way funner than Mega Man. But the online is dead, so you're on your own. _childDocuments_.review: So I'm a longterm Inti fan from the first Megaman Zero, I love the studio's character designs, spritework, and how they've stayed consistent over the years.  I like supporting them despite their games being far from perfect.  That's okay!  It's the same with Dragon Marked for Death, as this game's sprites feel a bit stiff sometimes and the world's color palette is a bit drab.  Otherwise I feel like I'm playing an Inti game with designs I instantly love, and that's what is ultimately important to me.  It feels quirkier with a stat system pulled out of an older RPG, but actually moving around feels natural and comfortable.  Sure I can feel the combat being simple, but when I think back to MMZ I pretty much jumped around, triple slashed, and charge slashed.  As long as moving is rock solid, it makes the rest fun.One quality feature that I wish I knew about is you can change your name/color/voice type after the first mission.  It would've saved me restarting a few times to find the least annoying voice, and I'll admit I wish they wouldn't make the same sound with every action input.  Having different voice actor sets at all is a pretty cool touch.I'd like to update the review as I go along, so I'll have more to say once I'm further in.  Just want to get ahead as it's already down to a Mixed rating based on the multiplayer not functioning well at launch.  It's an important feature, but review bombing does more harm than good if one wants to see the game succeed.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Devs, If you do make a "dragon marked for death 2" please do the following: -more variety in levels and music. Too many copy paste levels and tracks are not memorable. I get that the levels tie with some parts of the story but, there could at least be a slight variant or even a second part to the level.-give all characters a dodge option because half of the characters don't have one. -most importantly, Add a cloud save option for the steam port please....I lost all my progress when I got a new computer. -Work on the difficulty spike. I went from killing a kracken pretty easily to dying from a single touch just because a werewolf boss decided to breathe in my general direction. Not to mention that the bandit boss would destroy you if you didn't have the knight's shield protecting you...-For the love of god PLEASE give a better description of what ALL stats do. Hard to tell what some of the descriptions mean since it doesnt elaborate. At least include stat explanation in the tutorial. Descriptions are too vague at times for certain characters. -Team attack moves would be nice as well. Coordinated attacks are cool and I get that's the point but, what about special interactions with other class abilities? For instance:Knights shield could have a amplifying effect if you shoot projectiles from behind it giving it offensive and defensive utility. Or Shinobi get's additional air time or air dash if he dashes through the mage's wind attack? I just dont want to see this franchise die because it has something new and interesting to offer to the rogue style genre but, I can't recommend the first one because of the issues I have with it despite it having so much potential. If you're going to buy it, don't pay full price and wait for it to get marked down for $14 or $19. That's what the game feels like it's worth considering MANY other games just like it are around those price range like 30XX.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy I don't know where to begin. I love the game, played a lot, mostly solo and in duos. You can party with 4 but our distance makes the game laggy in a bad way.Gameplay is like what you see in the video, it's a side scroller, I'd compare it to megaman zero (and it's inti creates so that should be accurate). You jump and slash your way around, ranged damage is not great on most characters. The game has 4 characters you start with and 2 more you can unlock. You can level them all up independently but you carry equipment and consumables from one to another, which means you can farm female accessories on any female character and equip it on a different female character.Equipment is a little bit weird. The game tries to give you weapons for your character so you can't really farm every weapon for every other class using your strongest character. Accessories come with different limits (free for anyone, male vs female or character specific) so in a way you have the same problem.The way you go out beat stuff up might not be something some enjoy. You go to a bar and pick which quest you want to do and how hard. So you'll be seeing the exact same map a lot if you're grinding some equipment. The same map might have multiple quests which slightly change some passages or where you enter / exit, but it can get tiring if you don't like seeing the castle for the 20th time.Speaking of 20th time, I won't lie, if you want to go past "barely beating the game", there's A LOT to grind here. Getting to max level, getting a good build going, there's a lot of luck related to the drops and you only get at most 1 weapon per quest. So you end up optimizing your runs for exp or time based on your goals. It's actually the reason I haven't played in a long time, because grinding solo got boring eventually, but with a partner I can at least talk while running around.Again, I'd still totally recommend the game, even casually it's super awesome. You feel really really awesome when you perfectly avoid bosses patterns or when you make unconventional stuff work.There are a lot of details I skipped because they're less important until you play the game (elemental contracts and moveset etc)

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm walking away with a bit of mixed feelings on this one. I do enjoy it to a decent extent, but there's just so much keeping me from loving it. I'll go ahead and list a few pros and cons below just to give a brief idea of what I personally liked and dislike about it.Pros:-The art is beautiful/well done and animations are also well done/fluid-The music is quite good and fits well with each area or scene-The 6 playable characters all have a unique play style with their own gimmicks-The game has, in my opinion, quite good game feel so it is fun to play-It has a multiplayer option, and said option increases EXP earned per mission-Each class/character can have a different element, making their attacks somewhat different or have different effectsCons:-There is very little plot for something that seems to hint at being somewhat plot/adventure based-Most missions feel like side quests that have no real relevance-Mission structures are set up in a way to where the player will have to redo most of them an absurd number of times for a "full completion"-The game itself is exceptionally grindy, both in acquiring loot/drops and for leveling up-There does not feel like there is enough use out of or much importance in most characters' environmental gimmicks-Each character, with the exception of a few lines of dialogue and a few pictures, has roughly the same experience/role in the plot-Characters do not share mission completion, even though they share a save slot-Spell casting is far more complicated and time consuming than is necessary or wise-The black market, although appearing helpful, is almost completely worthless past level 30, only coming into use near level 100 for equipment that requires absurd levels of grinding-The rate for gold in this game does not seem very reasonable, especially mid to late game-Missions have time limits-Most characters' only seem to have 1 or 2 elements that seem viable for them-Changing elements requires a rare mineral that is either bought for a high price or rarely found in specific missionsCan't put the full rant I wanted here, so I'll just leave it at that and move ahead to my final thoughts.I did enjoy Dragon Marked for Death for a time, and I do recommend it, but only if you are not a completionist and you find it on sale. It can be pretty fun for maybe the first 20 hours, but anything past that just begins to be a slog. Oh, also, it's way better with friends, so, if you can, definitely get this on sale and get upwards of 3 other people to play with you. Definitely a far better experience that way.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit : Most of the issue I listed months ago about class balancing have been fixed.Supportive class have been buffed to be more useful as they don't have to recast buff that frequently anymore without spending too much stats in PIE.Oracle and Bandit have been significantly buffed so that their late game is on par with the other classes now.Witch stat buffs is still not as good but now it last twice or thrice as long (food buff duration) without much PIE stats in the first place, so it's a good incentive to pre-buff the entire party time to time before big fights now.Cleanse lv2 buff duration was significantly buffed, it lasted more than 2 recast of regen lv2 buff, which is a huge plus since you don't want to keep recasting cleanse lv2 in a boss fight way too frequently.So kudos to thumbs up.-------------------------------------------------------------------The game is good, extremely good if play with friends, but the lack luster of end game content and unbalanced class making this game cause player to lose interest rather quickly.--------------------------------------------------------------------The badsThe story is kind of weak, and the attack pattern of bosses is predictable after tons of grinding, and the end-game equipments just makes you instead of dodging hits, you'd just face tank everything regardless of what class you're playing.There aren't a lot of bosses to fight after reaching the end-game stage, and just mostly fights all returning bosses with extra attack pattern from story stages, and the additional attack patterns is just maybe 1~3 more than usual, and most of the bosses pattern pretty much fixed and aren't exactly randomized, making boss fight to become a boring grind feast after awhile.---------------------------------------------------------------------The goods, Playing this game with friends will definitely spice up the gameplay due to the targeting/hate system of this game, making boss fights slightly different and more fun due to more randomness from the attack pattern by having the boss focus it's attack on other players. (because of the targeting system, sometime causing the player that aren't being target needs a differnt approach to dodge incoming attacks).Also, playing with more players cause the bosses to have higher hp pool, in-exchange with more players to deal damage.The stage setting is great, and there are puzzles here and there for extra rewards, when players wanted to.the Music is superb, and it helps builds up the hype especially on boss fights.The gameplay itself is rewarding, especially after tons of death of fighting the same boss and finally able to learn the attack pattern and kill the said boss. This is especially true for classes like Witch and Bandit who requires more technical approach on their fighting style.The rewards of after a hard grinding to get said equipment to get stronger so you could start tackle stronger bosses is very much Monster Hunter like, people who likes grinding would definitely like this game.------------------------------------------------------------------The mixAfter the goods and bads, there will definitely some mixed.One of the mixed is that this game will require you to dies alot, and I mean ALOT...........(Think of dark souls or Megaman)This might discourage most people who don't like to dies a lot in game, but 'masochist players' who enjoys dying would definitely dig this.Difficulty of the game is weird, time to time while playing, the cause of death is extremely stupid, like dying due to paralysis / frozen states by certain mobs or bosses, or dying by dropped into poison pool without antidotes, while certain boss totally rekt you even on early stages caz it deals cause full screen (almost) undodgable moves/projectiles (looking at jinryu).--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------OverallA good game if you decide to give it a go, best if you got a few friends to play with together, will definitely able to get a good 30~60 hours of gameplay content even without trying to get into late game in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Marked For Death is a mixed bag. If you like side scrollers, looters, mission based games and don't mind assets being reused a lot in order to provide more content, you're probably going to enjoy your time, especially playing with friends. However, it's worth mentioning Dragon Marked For Death has crashes and the same alt tab black screen and resolution scaling issues as other Inti games (such as Blaster Master Zero 2 and 3), making it blurry on full screen. Fortunately, this time you can fix it by  that forces the game to run in the correct resolution, including ultrawide aspect ratios. The reason I recommend Dragon Marked For Death despite its shortcomings is there isn't anything similar on PC. We can't pick something like Odin Sphere over it and the character design and sprites are quite charming. A second game featuring more engaging missions would be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: The flaws i have with the game are vastly outweighed by the positives. If all you're looking for is great combat and bosses then i think you'll be very satisfied.Positives:Warnings:Flaws:A lot of the flaws this game have come down to little things like numbers or scaling that would take a few days to change max. Things like the stat system being kinda weird initially, and how Magic focused characters run into damage issues later because of how magic scales (still play them! all of them can solo). Or how you'll spend a significant amount of time exclusively grinding for EXP in the later parts of the game in order to wear stronger gear, which sucks extra badly because the best EXP per time missions are sadly the ones with the least fun bosses, and if you're playing solo you get significantly less exp.Still i really really love this game, 2D games with great combat and bosses, and specially good co-op sadly don't come by every day as most games seem content with just slapping a dodge roll on their game and calling it a day. So i recommend trying it, You get a very good idea of the game right from the start so you can always refund if it's not to your liking. Any confusion or doubts i recommend checking the mostly detailed in-game guide or checking out the wiki.

_childDocuments_.review: -A pretty fun game for platformer fans. Inti Create's beautiful artwork and spritework never fails to impress. -Love all the new updates and expanded movesets for all the characters. -The two new classes/chars are very welcome for variety.-Music is solid, a lot of melodic fantasy tracks. The one stands out the most for me though is the intro/theme song, which is a banger.-Characters are unique with designs that standout. There is surely a playstyle for everyone.-Currently have only played as Empress so far. I have beaten the game on Switch during its og release. From that experience, it's definitely soloable as long as you can memorize attack patterns, know how to build your character, and bring items if needed. The end game difficulties however, while doable, will likely require a party and endgame loot.-The story and lore is decent, with similarities to other Inti stuff like Gunvolt and Megaman Zero, though it won't grab you if you're accustomed to voice acting and longer triple A campaigns.-Currently playing on Xbone and PS4 controller. Both work perfectly fine. -Customization could be a whole lot better. The colors you can pick don't really show much, and element contracts could take out color unity. -More new abilities could be welcome, since aside from weapon switches and contracts, you can't gain new moves. At the very least you can switch weapons during quests. Overall, the game isn't stellar, and it's a tad overpriced at $40 unless there are plans to release more content. But, it's good for what it is. Definitely around $30 worth. It's a fun game, and definitely a fun time with friends. Definitely pick-up if you want to support Inti Creates.

_childDocuments_.review: Vanillaware ZX held back by its terrible maps.Integrating bits of Odin Sphere and Dragon's Crown into a Mega Man Z style platformer is a fresh, terrific concept.  Even if the game doesn't initially click with you, the characters are varied enough that odds are you'll find someone that satisfies your action RPG itch.  Seeing even giant bosses recoil against the Warrior gives an idea of how thoroughly their mechanics have been thought out and implemented to approach fights differently.  Aside from certain inputs feeling like they have unnecessary extra steps, the problem is the maps where all the action takes place.This is a game where all characters play the same maps, repeatedly.  You have to re-enter the same quests on increasing difficulties to grind levels and drops.  Multiple quests reuse the same maps.  There's nothing wrong with any of this so far.  The problems come in when you find out how empty and haphazardly laid out most of them are making grinding, as in most of the game, feel a lot worse.Half the maps have endless clutters of platforms that don't go anywhere, feeling a lot less satisfying or purposeful to navigate than what a lot of roguelikes generate.  With all the re-playing of the same maps, there's no sense of exploration constantly banging your head against these dead ends searching for treasure.  Just reaching these gameplay voids by slowly finding jumps you can make is a pain in itself whether or not you mess up and fall.  It can be solved by pure memorization, except they all look the same and you'll probably keep second guessing yourself into running into them again.Some of this is intentional because these areas are fun with the Shinobi, but that's because between the double jumping, gliding, and wall climbing, he has 90% of the game's platforming abilities.  In a game that's ultimately a platformer, that makes things pretty uneven.  With the Shinobi, whether seeing an object that can't be broken or needs a grappling hook, you can quicklyu shrug and move on.  Everybody else has to slowly lug their cumbersome self up somewhere awkward just to find out it's empty or something's unreachable anyway, feeling like a frustrating mess of incomplete features and bad layouts.Then there are the phoned in, blocked off sections for different quests.  Alternate sections of a map for alternate objectives makes perfect sense on paper, but whether they're closed off by a slab of stone or a white line drawn through the air, the mini-map won't show the blockades.  They also won't show your objectives so you can be left cluelessly wandering or attempt to double back before the boss to get more treasures only to find you're stuck.  A major part of the gameplay is endlessly running face first into dead ends.Between the clumsy platform cluster dead ends, the player ability dead ends, and the unmarked quest blockade dead ends, most of the game feels like a giant waste of time.  You can feel yourself aging to death as the hours get marked off the clock, which I guess is the real meaning of the subtitle.  Not helping are some of the in-game elevators being tortuously slow or making you immobile, so you can do everything right and still hear your life ticking away.  The worst part is, nearly all of this could be solved just by marking things like treasure chests and blockades on your mini-map, preferably also blotting out the quest-inaccessible parts.There's a fantastic game in Dragon Marked for Death.  It introduces a fun action RPG formula, but is unfortunately not great at exploring it because of a few missing mini-map features of all things.  Ideally there'd be better map designs in general or other cues to tell you not to bother with certain sections that aren't meant for most of the characters... but the disappointment comes from missing the much more basic steps.  Considering how grindy it is to unlock the two extra characters, this is a major, domino-ing problem.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute snore by yourself.  If you do get this game, play with some friends, maybe have 2 shows playing in the background.  Once you finish the tutorial for each character, you've pretty much seen the whole game.  There is absolutely nothing in this game that doesn't waste your time whether it's map design, navigating menus, trying to compare weapons in the shop or what you're carrying, or enemies.  If the game was released 25 years ago, it might have been good but alas, it wasn't.You grind the same ~7 levels for each character to level up and hopefully get a marginally better weapon.  The vast majority of the levels are an absolute chore to play through whether it's dealing with quicksand (like 90% quicksand, not just small areas), strong winds (same deal as quicksand), or just really awful map design.  Sometimes the map design just straight up clashes with a character's existence.  The ninja's basic attack combo makes him jut upwards and turns out the snow level has a ton of frozen spikes above you that will do 60% of your health if you touch them.  Try casting as the mage in the quicksand level and you'll find yourself stuck in the quicksand, unable to avoid enemies.  The 7 or so maps are massive and the missions essentially replay these same levels with certain sections blocked off and/or on a higher difficulty.  Basically, you can play Ice Mountain Mission 1 on like 10 different difficulties from level 5 to level 70.  The only difference in higher level Ice Mountain Mission 1 levels is that the enemies' stats are higher and you get a slightly stronger item drop.  Then you can eventually work to Ice Mountain Mission 2 (the exact same map but slightly different objective).  You'll spend the vast majority of the time trying to reach a part of the map only to realize that it's been blocked off and you just wasted a few minutes going there and need to turn around to find a different route that hopefully hasn't been blocked off.  Only one character in the 4 default characters can actually do real platforming with the other limited to a simple jump.  Lots of really bad design choices when it comes to menus and stuff (really a lot of things).  They couldn't let you look at and change your equipment in the same menu you choose missions and look at rewards.  No you have to back out, go take a few seconds to go to this other arbitrary building to do this (can't compare the reward weapon and your current weapon either).  Can't change any audio settings so you have to go to the sound mixer on your computer to lower the volume.  You can bring two weapons into a mission with you alongside several consumables.  But you need to open the menu and select them to equip/consume them rather than have a hotkey for it.You can talk to NPCs with like 5 different buttons.  Pressing a directional key near them talks to them.  Trying to sprint next to them talks to them.  ♥♥♥♥ if I know why this is a thing.  Fight some mobs near a poison mushroom and put in directional movement to do some attacks, eat the poison mushroom (because why wouldn't you eat a poison mushroom), get poisoned for like 2 minutes and lose 99% of your health.  Why not have an actual button to consume an item that's on the ground?  Idk ask them.  Negative statuses are debilitating enough that you will die from them whether it's poison doing your entire health bar (while you look around for health or an antidote) or just making you wait in place to wait them out because of how annoying them are.Expect to lose 50%+ of your health because you touched a frog.  You have a bunch of stats you want to raise but physical damage characters have to pretty much increase the same two stats or do 1 damage 80% of the time.  The mage needs you to press at a minimum 7 buttons in the correct order to cast a combat spell and can go to upwards of 20 buttons or something for a super strong spell.  You mess up ONE button press in that sequence and it cancels, locking you in place for 1-2 seconds as punishment.  It's such bad gameplay the community has created macros and scripts that will essentially play the mage for you.  Mage can't cancel casting with movement, only with the "start cast" button.  There is no defensive option for most of the characters.  Just don't touch the enemies.  Some bosses will just one shot you regardless of your level.  You'll also need to grind increasingly higher leveled missions to get more exp and weapons.  But without the already higher level weapon in these higher leveled missions, you do no damage until you get it.  There's not so much as skill involved as much as simply having higher stats than the enemy monsters which will greatly increase your damage to them and reduce their damage to you.  On top of this stat check type of game play, you'll eventually realize that missions will drop certain weapons and items and you can grind them until they drop.  This means you will eventually just ignore these basic monsters to rush to the boss and beat it over and over and over again until you get the drop you wanted, taking about 5 minutes each run.  Then you'll probably want to do that again to get a stronger version of the exact same weapon like from Greataxe+2 to Greataxe+3.  By this time, your eyes are probably drooping from how repetitive and boring it is.  But guess what, you'll need to do this with each character starting from the lowest level of that mission.Each character has like 5 different things they can do and they can "specialize" in a specific thing by changing their color.  For example, if you're the red ninja, you can dash one time.  If you're the purple ninja, you can dash two (2!!!) times.  If you're the red mage, your fire spells are strong.  If you're the blue mage, your ice spells are strong.  Truly groundbreaking stuff here.  Weapons don't really matter beyond stats.  The mage and warrior can get like one alternate attack/spell with a different type of weapon but that's about it.  If your stats aren't high enough via gear or something, you'll find yourself doing 1 damage for most of your attacks.  You can try to increase your LUCK to raise the chance of getting that weapon drop you've been grinding for but then your damage stats will suffer and it'll take 10x or longer to clear the stage.

_childDocuments_.review: Artstyle by the one and only Toru, the artist who did most of the art in Megaman Zero!I mean, its Inti. They always make good side-scrolling games. MMZ, ZX, ZXA, Gunvolt. Even Bloodstained:COTM is highly regarded. Dragon Marked for Death isn't an exception. Good art with spectacular game mechanics and multiple roles to choose from. It's just like Monster Hunter in 2D with good pixel art and superb voice cast.Gameplay wise. Although solo play can sometimes be frustrating with grinding and everything, multiplayer is pretty decent for later level progression. The multiplayer functions needs a bit of work though. Connection is good, even with worldwide matchmaking. Perhaps add a way to communicate with keyboards ontop of the current pre-made speeches. Also, it would be nice to be able to add players after finishing a quest online. Storywise, pretty standard textbook Inti story. Bittersweet ending T_T Although an in-depth story for each character would be nice. We can see in the trailer that all character has ties with their clan people (Empress-Lover, Warrior-Father/Family, Shinobi-Friend/Brother, Witch-Mentor/Teacher). Perhaps have character-specific quest to explore a bit more. Soundtrack is catchy with stage-specific themes. Boss themes are hard to remember though, due to the amount of attacking sound effects masking the music. Theme song and the "Important character" singing is pretty dope for the scenario.Replay. With multiplayer functions and up to 6 available characters to choose from, there is plenty of replays to do. You also share inventories, so you can give your second new character a start-up with superb gear from the first character. Multiplayer also help a lot to play more with others, friends and strangers. Although I do question the longevity of multiplayer, that is a question to be answered in the future.Overall, I give DMFD 8/10 with major points deducted from- Sub-par communication and interface in multiplayer lobby (Current release: May 2020)- Lack of each main character in-depth plot- Empress not having a special skill for Sword weapons (Personal rant XD)

_childDocuments_.review: I had previously reviewed this game closer to launch, but in retrospect I decided that old review was incomplete and outdated, and so I have deleted it and decided to start over the review from scratch.The first thing you should know about this game is what it is, and to get into that I'm going to have to address something very specific about it. Contrary to what the user tags say on the store page, this is not a Metroidvania. There is not one large interconnected map in which you collect new powers to unlock progress through, or even that on a smaller scale across multiple maps. If that's the kind of experience you are looking for, it's not here.So what is this exactly? It's much more akin to a combination between the Mega Man Zero series and Monster Hunter, entirely in 2D. There's a main town area in which you equip yourself with items and gear, and then when you are ready you enter into the bar which allows you to choose whether to play solo or online co-op. You choose a mission, each of which taking place in one of several different maps, and you attempt to complete the objective within a time limit. There's an RPG style level up system through which you gain EXP at the end of every mission and then if you gain enough EXP you will level up and choose what stat to allocate a skill point into.There's no true character creation feature. There's four preset starter classes and two unlockable classes. You can customize name, voice, and colors somewhat, and equipped weapons have their own unique sprites, but that's about it. Otherwise, characters of the same class will always look the same. Bandit, one of the two unlockable classes, is unlocked by completing a certain set of missions. The other, Oracle, is unlocked by reaching the ending of the game as any of the four starter characters. Each class has their own movesets, and uses DP, or Dragon Points, a bit differently. DP is typically built up by attacking enemies, and is a resource used for class specific dragon powers.Occasionally you'll be rewarded with Dragonite, which can be used to change your DP power element. This will change the color and function of your draconic body parts. This can come with changes to DP costs as well, so choose wisely. If you end up with a change to your dragon powers you do not like, you will have to earn another Dragonite to change it again.Sometimes when fighting a boss a special glowing orb will appear and begin floating over the boss arena. If you attack it enough it will heal you and grant you a time limited infinite DP bar, which allows you to use your special class specific dragon powers without having to worry about running out of DP points. This is your opportunity to deal some big damage, but don't forget that you are not invincible and can still be killed if you're not careful.The game is primarily built around co-op and is heavily mission focused. Offline solo play is doable and can still be a lot of fun, but if you want to get the most enjoyment out of this game it's recommended that you play with friends. Unlike in recent Monster Hunter games such as World and Rise, you cannot simply visit the individual locations casually and kill things at your own pace. You must be on a mission to visit any of the main gameplay locations.Every time you beat a mission, you unlock a harder version of that mission. For example, beating a level 10 mission might unlock a level 25 version of the mission. It's generally recommended that you use a character and gear suited to the level of the mission. As the difficulty increases, the time limit also decreases. There's different types of missions as well, such as "Defeat all enemies", "Defeat the boss", "Obtain a specific item", and even some special specific ones for certain missions. With some mission types the mission will clear as soon as you complete the objective. With others, you will be given an option to end the mission when you are ready via a glowing purple area you can interact with.Some gear can be simply purchased with money you collected in the stages, but this gear is generally pretty garbage and should be replaced ASAP if you want to maximize your efficiency and surviveability. Instead, you should focus on collecting necessary ingredients to craft and upgrade specific gear pieces. You can get certain ingredients from completing certain missions, and you'll also get upgrade materials from completing missions as well.Don't forget to stock up on healing items and status curing items as well. You're especially going to want to make sure you have something to take care of poison with you, as this can easily be the most dangerous status element. While poisoned, you will gradually take small chunks of damage over time. However, poison can take much longer to wear off than other status ailments, and could very easily shave almost the entirety of your health bar if left unchecked.When defeating enemies, sometimes they will drop healing items, status restore items, and even stat boosting items. You will consume any of these instantly when picking them up, gaining their effects. Beware however, not all items are good to pick up. For instance, purple mushrooms will poison you. Do not just mindlessly grab everything that drops, think about whether it's useful first.If your HP does reach 0, all hope is not lost. You have multiple tries per mission, and can revive with full health when reaching 0 so long as you haven't run out of retries. You do not lose progress from using a retry, you simply get back up on the spot and continue where you left off. However, you will fail should you run out of retries.As for the music and visuals, it's all rather high quality. The OST seems to all be full orchestrations and the visuals are high quality pixel art. You can also zoom the camera in and out unlike most other pixel art games, and the animations are all quite smooth as well. Overall high praise from me here.With all that out of the way, I do have a few nitpicks regarding this game. For instance, I would have liked to see a greater degree of character customization in the game. I'm fine with canon default presets, but in a class based game like this it's nice being able to make your character look the way you want them to and so it would have been nice to be able to choose gender and recolor the characters more extensively. It's not a deal breaker by any means and it's not even really all that big of a deal, but that's why I'm including it as a nitpick.Additionally, I would have also liked to see the individual mission areas exploreable without having to be on a mission. There's a feature like this in recent Monster Hunter games, and this would have been a fun alternative for collecting items you need for crafting at the black market, or even just for grinding experience for when you don't feel like taking on missions. Again, not really all that big of a deal but it's a bit of shame it's not here.Overall, if you're a fan of Inti's other games such as Mega Man Zero and Azure Striker Gunvolt and also into games like Monster Hunter, this is a really fun and content rich mix between these concepts and is a lot of fun to play with friends. Just don't get your hopes up if you're a huge fan of Metroidvanias because that is not the kind of experience you're getting into here. Go into this expecting Mega Man Zero as a Monster Hunter-like and you'll be getting a lot more bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: I got given it by Tem so she'd have someone to play with, and then she played it solo anyway. What a goon. >:oAnyway the game is good I think. It looks good, it runs well enough (Unless you're online with someone with a weaker connection) and the basic loop of twonking monsters and grabbing treasure chests in hope of getting better gear is a classic. There is a story but honestly it's very weak, like most other games of this style. The soundtrack is decent, though for gods know what reason  so you have to right click the speaker on windows tray to access sound mixer if you want to hear voicechat or anything else while playing.One point that definitely deserves praise is how different the characters and their builds can be. There's always an optimised route but generally most of them can go for at least two different playstyles, like having the Empress focus on doing normal melee damage or using her dragon cannon attack. One thing to note is that two classes, Witch and Oracle, are quite in-depth to learn as they require you to do specific inputs in a tight time limit while in the middle of combat.The game's difficulty might put people off though, know ahead of time that it is a hard game that expects you to grind for better gear and spend level up points efficiently. There's almost no benefit to playing single player either; everything will focus on you and if you're a DPS build, will generally kill you in 1-5 hits. Multiplayer allows for other people to take focus, heal each other AND receive higher exp for beating missions. The literal only "downside" is enemies have increased health. That's all. I would heavily recommend having a pal to help you or asking in the forums or something. It's fun as a game to dip into for a few hours at a time, but remember that if you want to make real progress, unlock all the achievements or unlock the two extra characters, you'll have to put in dozens of hours. Finding guides and such is still a pain at the moment, a bunch of information is hidden on a discord and people are still learning about the Oracle and Bandit so there's very little on them too.One last important thing you should know; this game is designed for controllers. It IS playable with keyboard (I have to because my pad died ; ;) but you have to manually bind all your keys at the main menu, and it's going to be pretty difficult to adjust. Myself I go for a WASD movement, IJKL face buttons setup with LB (Dash) on space and Start on tab. QE UO for other shoulder buttons or whatever, Numpad 2468 for right stick camera control. You can probably make it more efficient for yourself but that's what I go with as a suggestion. :x

_childDocuments_.review: My single sentence description of this game is "If Mega Man: Zero and Monster Hunter had a baby."And it is a beautiful baby.Made by the creators of Mega Man: Zero, and has a very similar playstyle and art which will bring nostalgic joy from those of you who loved MM:Zero (myself included.)In a Monster Hunter like fashion, you choose a mission from the "Mission Board" and attempt said mission, usually having a challenging boss at the end. You get loot from chests and monster drops that you can use in later missions or spend in town to exchange for gear or consumables or (now in 3.0) upgrade gear. Eventually you'll be able to challenge tougher missions or higher difficulties to get better loot.You farm a mission to get loot, so you can farm a tougher mission to get better loot, so you can farm an even tougher mission to get even better loot, so you can farm........ The MonHun formulaThere are now 6 characters to choose from with different playstyles.   The "Standard" EmpressThe "Tank" WarriorThe "Floaty Glass Cannon" Shinobi  The "High APM Glass Cannon" Witch  The "High APM plus buff management" Oracle  and the "RNG Resource Management" BanditWith some areas that can only be accessible by certain characters, make sure you have a diverse party to access all the loot.Play with friends, with online matchmaking (playerbase permitting), or even solo.Now for the cons.It does have that MonHun formula, so it also has that MonHun Grind. With some drops being in the single digit or lower percentage drop, it can get repetive.  While it does have HP scaling for more party members, it is much easier in a party. Compared to the Switch launch, going solo is much easier, but having others to divert the boss' attention allows for an easier fight overall.There are a few difficulty spikes.   The first few are just significant leaps in incoming damage (but that can be mitigated by dodging).   But the one that I'm currently attempting to break through is a huge HP increases with bosses. (A lvl 65 boss takes 7 minutes, the lvl 80 version takes 30)All in all, if you enjoyed the Mega Man: Zero or ZX series, you will have a ton of fun, even if you dont enjoy MonHun like grinds.

_childDocuments_.review: I do want to say i really do like this game and recommend anyone whos a fan of Megaman like gameplay to give it go. Each class is different, feels different and plays different, There are the standard classes you would expect from most rpgs so a variety of playstyles. Levels are visually fine but dont stand out too much, and there is one level that is absolute garbage. A tower you have to climb with constant wind pushing you around and lots of platforming.....vertically. Its a major pain to even be on those stages unless you are the shinobi as that class can double jump and climb walls.The story isnt the greatest either but serves its purpose for a premise, and im personally disappointed in what they did but it doesnt hurt anything, just couldve been better. But i will say i think the one thing that may annoy players the most is the constant status afflictions you will always get. Poision that lasts way too long (will take you from full to a fraction of health in one sitting if you dont have an antidote item) lightning status which removes ALL abilites from being used, yes that includes running.....i mean what? You get caught out in just the wrong place with that and youre dead. Then there is confusion or the wind element. It reverses the left and right controls and thats plain irritating. I dont know who started this trend in gaming but it needs to stop, its not fun or challenging its just infuriating. It seems there are lot of things in the game that is trying to prevent you from even playing as almost everything the enemies can do to you takes away youre control.Having said all that its still worth playing if none of that bothers you or will take a while to bother you like it did me. after almost 30 hrs of play time i feel i need a break from it. But there is a lot to have fun with here. Like most reviews are saying yes this game is vastly more fun with friends, but enjoyable enough solo.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Very unique game. Much more fun with friends. The spellcasting system is very fun. Who wouldn't want to make nearly 40 inputs just to cast a single max level spell?I've never found a game quite like Dragon Marked For Death and I don't think I ever will. There's some inherent magic to this game that I can't quite put my finger on. I think the major aspects are the uniqueness of multiplayer platformers and the use of RPG classes and roles in a type of game that normally wouldn't have them. Due to those factors being huge contributors to the game's feel, it works far better when you have people to play with. The online is empty, so if you want to give this game a shot I recommend getting a friend or two to play it with you.The game is very much guilty of many of the things the negative reviews will say. There's not a lot of enemy or stage variety. You'll have to replay the same quests many times over due to often insane difficulty and low item drop rates at higher levels. The systems are poorly explained and many mechanics are hard to wrap your head around. The in game tips menu helps out a lot, but can lack description in some places as well.That's not to say that all is doom and gloom though, there's certainly plenty that this game has going for it. The feeling of playing an RPG party and fulfilling your roles with a group of friends is incredibly fun. I primarily played the Witch in my time with the game, and I feel of all the characters, she plays into this the most. She's both a healer and an incredible damage dealer, but can require protection from teammates in order to operate at full power. The spellcasting system in DMFD is my favorite of all time, perhaps rivaled only by Magicka. Spells take long sequences of button presses that you have to memorize, and a single wrong input will cause the spell to fail. In return for this difficulty, the Witch's spells are devastating, with many of the 3rd level spells being essentially screen clears against regular enemies and doing huge amounts of damage to bosses. At first, these spells take far too much time and concentration to cast, so you'll only really be able to use them against bosses with the help of a Warrior's shield, but as you get used to the inputs and you begin to memorize the spell better and better, it becomes almost subconscious. The button inputs for the spells are forever ingrained in my mind, and I feel like that's the closest you can get to the feel of real magic.If you've made it this far into this review then I applaud you and leave you with some parting advice. If you do end up playing the game, definitely check out the steam guides. In particular there's a guide for the Bandit that has a link to a very important spreadsheet. It tells you what stages you need to clear in order to progress both the story and the questline to unlock the Bandit. Finally, if you decide to play the Witch, try rebinding your right joystick to the face buttons. This made some of the spellcasting inputs (namely heal and level up) far easier to input quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game by the guys who made the Mega man zero games!The game has fun game play and a rather unique take on a co-op action rpg. Each character has a unique kit, and different play styles. I highly recommend playing this game, especially if you have friends to play with, enemies do become bullet sponges as the game progresses, having a party makes the game a lot easier, turns out synergy is a good thing. Unfortunately there aren't a lot of people trying to play online.And I need to talk about the Witch, she has the coolest magic system ever, mash in inputs to make a spell. They don't make all the spells obvious—they just tell you to look at the command list. She has a great repertoire of spells she has 4 Elemental spells, Fire, Wing, Ice, and Electric, 3 support spells, levitate, heal, and illuminate. All of which (except for levitate and illuminate) can be modified. You can strengthen, condense and give your spell homing. There are 3 levels of strength which increases damage on each step, condense makes your attack hit multiple times, and homing will make the spell either land on an enemy or track an enemy. It's a great mechanic that I'd love to see in more games.Also it should be said that if you fail your input or let the meter run out you will be stunned for a second and small magic orbs will fall from you, they'll deal damage to enemies but casting a spell is always better. (if you use macros for her you're a chump, mash like a man)
