_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, it was only for the Nintendo switch. It looked interesting, but the lack of having online on my end made it less then desirable. Now that it's on steam, I picked it up to play and can sadly say I'm still playing solo. At the moment, there are not many people playing publicly like in most other games. That's not to say no one is online, for there is a discord server dedicated for the game. That aside, the gameplay has been very interesting. The game is set up to where you benefit when playing as a team, but you can still play solo without to much trouble. Enemies are plentiful, and treasure is easy to find. However, there are some issues. First of all, you see the exact same enemies form start to finish. The one time I thought I saw some new enemy group I got excited, turns out it was just another generic enemy your going to see for the rest of the game. The bosses are a little more varied and interesting. The next problem comes from multiplayer. When you choose a quest in multiplayer you are locked into that quest and only that quest. Even when you finish it, you have to back out of the room and make a new one just to play a different quest. I would like to have an option to choose the next mission after the current mission or something like that. On the bright side, this does make farming a little easier. Finally, and this is a nit pick, you cant change the mission order. I'm not entirely sure how the missions are ordered currently, but I would like the option to change it based on location or minimum level. As of the time I have completed the story with two characters. All in all, I give it a solid 7/10. A great game, but you should probably wait for a sale to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like there is an audience for this game, but I honestly can't think of who to recommend this to. Especially at the game's retail price point.It plays like a side-scroller beat em up on a 2D plane, but feels lacking in move variety outside the Witch class (She lacks baseline mobility, and has to remain stationary to use her moveset on top of that.) But has maps built like a Metroidvania, a lot of verticality and a lot of areas that require specific mobility kits (characters) to reach them. Has the equipment, stat (STR, INT, VIT), and grinding systems of an RPG but lacks an expanding moveset to keep things interesting. It is incredibly easy to get lost in the maps that are available, with little to no guidance on where to go within each one. And with each map being large vertically AND horizontally missions take a while to figure out what the goal is. Each map seems to be reused multiple times, occasionally with "invisible walls" that aren't displayed on the map preventing you from accessing areas you've visited before, not really shortening the maps just blocking certain paths from being taken around the map. And it's weird that the game reuses the maps as often as they do considering they offer each map at 5 level intervals from when you unlock it (Example: you unlock a map at level 10 and it goes from 10, 15, 20, 25... etc)I didn't find the story all that compelling past the opening personally, but it was also difficult to find what were "main missions" and what were "side missions" so it's hard to tell you for sure what to really pay attention to there. A lot of the missions boiled down to I lost thing, people, or monsters took over this place go get it back.There is co-op, but it was a little buggy with the blue-guy's movement powers. He can charge into specific walls and open up places but this:  happens a lot and they have to go back and charge more to fix it.Menuing in attrocious, be prepared to spend tons of time inside the game's various menus figuring out what specific building you need to visiting in the town in order to adjust your quick action items, where to craft items, where to obtain X material to craft said items or accessories, and unequipping items in order to upgrade them. That's right to go from +1 to +2 on an item you have to unequip it then go back into the shop.Overall I feel the game lacks the depth of the genres it is borrowing from. At the start it was entertaining, but quickly became a grind and then a chore. I wasn't able to finish the story only getting to level 26 before all the prior Cons listed outweighed my desire to see the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The people complaining got F I L T E R E D.The game's fantastic. It seems a bit shallow at first, but it opens up substantially and there're varied playstyles for each character. Also, there's a lot of information available about the game, but it is horrifyingly difficult to access; you'll have to learn for yourself how to accomplish what you want to do, or you'll need to search through the community maintained discord server. You can complete the game with minimal effort, but there's an optional post-game grind to level 100 that's pretty intense. A lot of your best-in-slot drops come from farming high-end versions of previous levels. At certain difficulty levels, levels get different enemies, bosses get more mechanics, and obviously, everything's got more health. The barrier for entry can be offputting, but pay attention to the affixes on weapons/armor (the text at the bottom of the item description box), and you'll do fine.Overall, I highly recommend the game, though 40 bucks is a bit steep. If you're a fan of grindy megaman-esque games, it's worth it. If you're on the fence, the game's often on sale for 20 bucks, which is a much easier pill to swallow.8.5/10.

Let's say you do enjoy what you see here and you want to play with someone online...1) There's really no one playing online. At the time of this post, there's 14 players online and who knows is those 14 people are even in your region2) Good luck convincing a friend to drop $40 on a game they've never heard ofOn the flipside, the character playstyles are all VERY different and I love that about this game so much, at least the main 4 you start with. The mage operates completely differently than the warrior in that there's manual spell incanting which is awesome. It also has character stat allocation, weapon acquistion and upgrading and crafting.The problem with the weapon upgrading and crafting is that it's kind of expensive to do so with no way to see what the final result of an upgrade will be (i.e. if you go from +0 to +3, you won't know what passives will be on a weapon). Also, the passives early on aren't really that interesting and there's a weird amount of trash weapons you can buy and find that you'll never want to use as the cost to upgrade the next tier of weapon would be too much instead of just waiting for a weapon to unlock with better passives. There's very much a right way to spend your money and a wrong way. The weapon variety, per weapon also doesn't exist. A light axe +3 and another light axe +3 are always the same. You're done, no reason to ever look at a different one. They will always have the same passives and stats unlike in a game like PSO, you could have two different handguns and maybe one will do more damage in the forest area while one will do more damage in the mines. Something like that would have kept the weapons a bit more interesting. You'll go a decent amount of time using the same weapon.Also, there's a weird problem about how information is delivered to the player. There's a ton of information you won't know unless you browse into the button help and tips. This is fine if you love to read to be a better player, but most people don't want to absorb walls of text in order to feel like they are playing correctly. i.e. AGI is VERY important to the warrior. Actually, I'd say it's so important that you should try to dump nearly all of your level up stats into it which common sense would not dictate.Anyway, it's fun with a friend and if were cheap. If those two conditions are met: get it. If not, pass.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I've mainly played through most of this game with friends. I've got diddly on how the 'rando' multiplayer works. As for bugs, only one stands out for me. The first time I boot the game for a session, if I alt-tab, the game screen locks so I have to relaunch. 6.5/10. Game has been described by others as "Mega Man(insert here) meets Monster Hunter". I... guess, though I hate Monster Hunter, so I'm biased. It's got some Metrovania feel to some of the levels, though you don't really get 'upgrades' to help map navigation. The best you'll get is maybe a speed or jump boost, maybe something to give you back your 'mana' for class skill spam. Everything your character or 'class' can do to get through a level they have from the start. Some classes can breeze through most of the navigation(Shinobi) only missing out on some chests or convenient back-track loops, while others have to slog through slowly(Warrior). Level navigation is much quicker with a diverse party. There's sadly not a whole lot of map variety, with each map having a few quests associated with it. It's very noticeable on certain maps you may not enjoy, like the tower map. ♥♥♥♥ the tower map.Combat wise, it's not that technical. The only class that seems 'limited' is that the Warrior is a straight up melee character. All the others have ranged options, even though there might be a 'meta' build that takes them into melee as well. As for builds themselves, there's a small amount of wiggle room, though not so much for the poor Warrior. Pick melee, magic, or 'Holy' attack tactics, and dump into the corresponding stat(s) is the go to for leveling. There are items to reset your stat investment for testing, as well as changing your character's primary element, so there are options. As for enemies, the trash mobs are basic, and can be easily dispatched before they even do anything. The game's togglable 'aggro' indicators not only show who the monsters are aiming for, but gives their location for quicker clearing. Bosses usually have a few to several attacks, with maybe the addition of a couple more or just faster/more projectiles on harder difficulties. The story is lackluster, with either translation or outright spelling errors. It's main positive is that cutscenes are either skippable, or you can toggle quick text displays. Makes the story bearable if you don't care for it, or have already seen it. There are a few different endings with set circumstances to 'unlock', so if you enjoy the story you have that to look forward to. Just don't expect much except text for the unlockable characters.All in all, game shines with more players. If you've got some friends willing to give it a try, or the genre fits your interests, give it a go.Edited for clarity.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only negative review that talks about the gameplay not the fricken portDragon Marked For Death is a unique game. You see the side scrolling platforming action, lots of stuff to beat up, loot, levels, etc. You think you're getting some sort of co-op Gunvolt Metroidvania, but you're not. The formula is MonHun, some of the worst parts of it too. You're thrust into reused, overlarge context-free levels with some vague direction, a time limit, maybe your co-op buddies are here too, and a bunch of pointless unthreatening baddies between you and the boss. The levels are exercises in complete boredom because one character is basically Copen from Gunvolt and the rest can barely manage a jump for their platforming. The enemies are tedious, unthreatening, and unrewarding, so you eventually get bored of pointlessly chopping out their "bloated enough to remind you this is an RPG, not an action game" health bars and get on with finding the boss or objective, one of the few sources of actual loot for this level.Yes, you're playing a platformer where both the platforming and content is boring filler.(EDIT: Oh geez, it gets worse the more you play. Imagine 15 minute long escort missions over these boring maps and boring enemies where the escort can only be coaxed to jump with loads of little fidgeting. Imagine a level full of almost a dozen lock-you-in monster closets that are just "The same six monsters that aren't a threat in the slightest attack you." Imagine a gimmick level that requires you to find power sources in the map to charge an elevator repeated  at least five times because there are several missions that reuse this level with PRECISELY THE SAME GIMMICK with nothing changed except what's at the top of the tower. And half the rooms in the tower are windy just to slow you down for no reason. There's NOTHING in this game that doesn't waste your time.)Then you reach, mercifully, a boss, one of about six ugly bosses reused constantly through the game. Now the bosses are MonHun too. Fat things designed to be whacked by 2-4 people all at once and designed to be fought by four different characters with different styles so you're dealing with a thing with a giant health bar that spends about a third of the fight sitting around thinking of what to do next before it hits you for nearly all your health making you down a healing item. (Don't get me wrong, the patterns are definitely no-damage possible and at least the standard Inti Creates memorize BS mostly stays out at low levels). (EDIT: Oh and it's an RPG so of course there are ailments like being unable to attack for ten seconds because you got hit once. THERE IS NOTHING IN THIS GAME THAT IS NOT TRYING TO WASTE YOUR TIME!)You do all this for sweet loot from the boss and boy howdy you'll be disappointed. A +2 stat item that goes in one of your four equipment slots, none of which change the gameplay beyond what numbers you do with the same attack combos you will be using all game.It's a MonHun loot farmer with boring overall levels, meant for co-op (Though THANKFULLY they appear to have patched solo play to be actually viable by the time for the Steam release. It was intolerable at low levels on Switch.), without anything mechanically good enough to be worth MonHun style repeat play. While there are definitely far, far worse things to grind at, I found this game to be a disappointment on every level. And though I have ripped it pretty hard, I will relent and say Inti Creates stepped outside their comfort zone here. They have attempted a mix that I don't think has been done before outside of that one PSN/XBLA Castlevania MonHun style game. Effort and creativity went into this, and I respect that, but it came out a resounding failure in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This negative review is because of the port as of the time of launch. >No resolution support past 1080. It does have Windowed/fullscreen/borderless though and monitor/display select.>There are no sound options at all. If you want to turn down the volume you have to do so in windows. >The controls are Keyboard or controller. No mouse support and it feels much better on controller in my opinion. >Japanese only voice acting which is a minor complaint for me but others might not like it.Text has multiple options.All in all this is a console game and feels like a console game which isn't the worst thing in the world, but for the price tag of $40 I would have expected better.Edit: To make it clear why this review is a negative is not because of the gameplay at all. Its because this was a very lazy port from console to PC. The lack of mouse support, even just for menus, is a major turn off for me. There are options for rebinding keys on both controller and keyboard. When rebinding controller it highlights a button and wants you to press the button you want bound. For example "Dpad up" is highlighted and you press the button you want bound to Dpad up which would probably be Dpad up. It doesn't give you an option like "Dpad up does jump". You have to cycle through all of the buttons on the controller to rebind anything and they don't tell you what any of the buttons do.  Its slightly easier to rebind the keyboard because you can select which button you want to rebind, but all it shows is what button it is on the controller, still having no idea what each button does. The default keyboard controls are just all over the place and don't really make sense for me. _childDocuments_.review: As expected of the Megaman Zero developer, the game looks great with its pixel art style. The music itself is serviceable, but the sound design for combat is pretty nice imo.The main part of the game can be played solo with all characters. Some characters might be more difficult to solo with, but still not impossible to play through the main game solo.But it is still nice if you wanna have fun with your friends.You can leave it at that because from this point you see 20~22 out of 24 bosses in the entire game.But even then, these bosses are quality encounters.Once you start transitioning to mid-game, you'll need to start learning an actual boss pattern. This is the part where you start to get good (in an unironic way) and the quality in each boss fight also went up as their level increased.Some of the boss's attacks are seemingly impossible to dodge at first, but they're all avoidable with either good positioning or evasive movements.I'd say it's the main source of enjoyment and replayability when you fight the same boss. Being able to read all of their attacks like the back of your hands then retaliate when the opportunity is presented for you.That being said, the grind from mid-game to late-game is quite excessive when you transition from early-game.These are not part of the main story so you aren't required to do them by any means. But if you want to do it, I'd heavily suggest finding at least a few ppl to grind with you. One last thing: the learning resource for this game is very difficult to find. Even vital stuff like a basic game guide can't be found on Youtube (at least in English, you can find the Japanese guides easily though), so if you're interested in learning some in-depth game info you might need to search for a discord server for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out fun but later levels demand absolute perfection from the player. Most of Inti Creates' other games allow the player to take a few hits before dying, but 1-2 shots against damage sponge bosses you're required to beat are the law of the land in Dragon Marked for Death. Many bosses have little to no windup on attacks that can cause a myriad of status effects and have absurd contact damage in a melee-focused 2d game. Multiplayer for whatever reason, give you more retries than if you played solo, and since the online is basically dead for this game, good luck making it through the endgame content unless you're a pro. Clearly this game was designed for people who could no-hit MMZ1-4.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend for the coop and gameplay even though there are some issues with this game design-wise.Game is very fun, it just leaves a lot to be desired as well. All things that can hopefully be redeemed in a sequel which I would love!Just to list the major issues off:Why is the town so needlessly large? This would have been fine if there was anything to do within it, Namely invite and see party members.Empress has the lowest skill ceiling among the characters. Witch and Oracle have so many options compared to the others its crazy that Empress really only has 2 attacks and 1 ultimate. This game is clearly inspired by Mega Man Zero but theres no input attacks on Empress? Would it have taken too long to at least make the tail hookshot have a hitbox?The difficulty spikes after level 30 missions to the point where I started needing to be 10 levels above the mission level. I imagine this is to promote more party play which is a terrible way to do it.I would have preferred not needing to beat every mission in the game to unlock the 2 characters so as to have some new challenges when I got to play the others.The story was very hit and miss, more miss than hit actually. I don't get why we are a vengeful dragonblood casually doing errands. I would have imagined these characters to be seething with rage and incapable of taking as much ♥♥♥♥ from random people as much as they do. Wordlessly to boot, there is not satisfaction of having the last word on any of the immoral characters that are properly setup to make players hate them.The changing elements feature, I did not find out about until past level 40 as empress. I also think theres no point in costing a dragonite for this.Empress has very little to do among shopping and weapon upgrades until very late in the game. Even then, everything is soo pricey that it actively discourages experimenting at all.Empress' grapple nodes are very few among the midgame, so much so that her grappling feature barely exists in the game, only at the beginning and end of the game.A lot of missions and levels are really easy to get stuck in. Sometimes it not clear what you have to do and you have to guess your way through.Some good things:I really like the asymmetric gameplay of the characters. Though I believe something could be done to improve warrior and Empress' mobility. Even a switch weapons button would have been nice to use the shortsword moves for mobility.This is the first game where I heavily relied on items to get through. Thats a cool accomplishment as I am normally the type to avoid using items for no good reason.Stil, great game. really hoping to see a sequel eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing more of the game, the stages actually aren't as bad as some people make it out to be. The stages themselves are fairly varied, have had 5 different maps and even when you're brought back to them, the encounters are scripted for each quest. Only downside is definitely enemy variety but the boss variations and additional attack patterns make up for the lack of themed enemies.Characters although quite standard can be tweaked to specialize in the abilities you like. Mage I recently found out cast elements you specialize in more efficiently and quickly. Warrior can get different shot types that give new utility.All in all, my opinion of the game just got better overtime and it's not boring playing other characters because your one character just can't do it all so theres a point to coop. I feel alot of games tend to just make your character all encompassing regardless of what class they are which is frankly boring.------------------------------------------First impression as a mage is pretty good. You have a simple spell system that you need to execute on the fly under a time limit which is quite novel to me.  The game makes you go against some basic logic while playing since the mage can't jump or run very well so I had to take contact damage to avoid an attack. Something which I don't quite feel like is good design in late game when touching something could mean you die in 1 hit.Stages are pretty well designed but the complaints about them reusing stages and enemies are quite valid. Although the stage is well thought out and is mostly accessible with 1 character. The thoughtfulness and effort in design is wasted because treasures, traps and enemies are randomized for each part of the stage.All in all great first impression.- equipment is mainly passive buffs- grinding hits you really fast. i.e you need alot of money to upgrade unless you're playing stages way above your current level

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good fun. It's a time sink with Dark Souls inspired character stat customization paired with Megaman level side-scrolling action. I guess you could call this the Salt Sanctuary of sidescrollers ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)Nevertheless, you will spend much in this game making big number go bigger. Highly recommended to play with friends to increase XP gain and to increase fun. The final smashes after hitting the small ball (Dragon Sphere) are also really flashy and clutch, making a tough fight even easier to plow through.Make sure to do thorough research on each class and the elemental contracts, while the game doesn't look like much--it definitely does not reward going into things blind. It can often feel like there's no goal, but should you do research on builds and weaponry, it'll easy to keep finding more and more to do. Some cons I would share for this particular PC port is the lack of resolution options (no 4k? Really?), and the instability of some of the quests. There's a particular endgame quest that causes frequent crashes more often than others, possibly due to story triggers present in the quest itself. The game is quick to load, however, so the frequent crashes are less of an issue and more of a nuisance. There's the nuisance of when booting the game, the sound and controller options are out of whack--make sure to start with headphones off your ears and that you enable the gamepad option so you can bind controls.Hope you found this review useful and do enjoy if you do decide purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've ever written, and probably the only one I'll ever write.I'm mostly just giving pointers into how to get the most enjoyment out of this game.First and foremost: join the Discord server for the best possible experience! You don't use Discord? I recommend you start using it. If you don't join the Discord server, you most likely won't enjoy this game.The in-game matchmaking system is less than ideal, and the Discord has an extremely active and helpful community that you can coordinate quests with in their dedicated LFG channels. Before the game had drop tables visible within the game, the community was able to create their own spreadsheet containing every weapon/accessory in the game, and the quest where it is dropped. Those tables are still actively updated to assist you in your quest for loot. There is also a list of all of the quests and objectives you need to do in order to progress the story, because this game doesn't do any hand-holding.Discord Invite Link: Now to the review:First, each mission has a baseline Quest-Level (Q.Lv), and then additional Q.Lvs you unlock by completing the previous difficulty that give you upgraded versions of old weapons, or brand new weapons with a higher level requirement. The Q.Lvs go as high as 110, currently, and the bosses get additional mechanics added at various intervals in the progression through Q.Lvs.The final quest in the main story itself has a baseline Q.Lv 30 (the "DLC" that is included in the PC version finishes with a baseline Q.Lv 50 mission, but all of the missions are typically more difficult than those in the main story). Those people saying they only finished the game in 7 hours only scratched the surface of what this game has to offer.The max player-level is 100, and it takes a considerable grind to reach that on even a single character.You get out of this game what you put in, and only playing through the main story will just have you scratch the surface. I have over 300 hours on the Switch, and there are some people with over 1k hours in the game (I know one player that has over 2k hours).I love this game so much that I bought it on Steam just to have the 3.0.0 update a few days earlier than on Switch, and, depending on how things go, I might switch over to the Steam version. I hope to see the PC get an online community as active as the one on the Switch.I hope to see you guys on Discord, and happy farming!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - If you like sidescrolling, quest based metroidvania like games, or feel like levelling up your megaman fix with rpg levelling mechanics, this is a really fun addition to your collection. It CAN get really repetitive after one playthrough, on single player. Multiplayer is personally untested as of writing this, but each stage in the game FEELS like it's made for it.I have a plethora of thoughts of criticisms and praise alike about this game, but I'll try and boil it down to a few points: Pros:   -Really fun visuals that invoke games like Megaman ZX or ZX Advent  -Gameplay that is similar to the above games, with levelling, equipment collection, and stat based builds like an metroidvania/rpg game.  -A unique set of characters and game mechanics for each that allow you to change aspects of their game play akin to   altering a character's moves in the smash brothers games for the 3DS and WiiU. When I first picked this game up, I was assuming the Bandit unlockable character would be almost identical to the shinobi, or a combination of it and the small sword using empress (as they share those weapons), and was pleasantly surprised at how different it played from either of the other classes.  -The never-ending hunt for better loot is strong in this game! Also, modifiers harken back to D&D in my brain as I'm upgrading my gear. :) Cons:-The plot is serviceable but basic, with cookie cutter dialogue that's slightly dressed up in flowery language that doesn't hide it very well. Also, dialogue doesn't change based on your characters, who are silent protagonists during story scenes.-The game reuses its resources - basic enemies, its stages, your weapons, and bosses - with a small amount of modification (colour palette swaps, slight aesthetic mods, in the case of the stages, slightly changing what rooms in the stage are accessible)-This game feels entirely built to be multiplayer, despite me playing through levels in single player. Related to this, as of yet I have had little luck finding groups/teams to play mutliplayer with, so that feeling begins to nag on you as you continue to play.*Spoilers*-One of the prerequisites to getting this games best ending is beating it with the four base characters, so that paired with the issues with its plot might get tedious for some people.Ultimately, I have to recommend this game based on how much I enjoy learning how different characters play, and how much variance there is under the different "contracts" that change their unique mechanics and elemental affinity. I have a soft spot for these sorts of games, but despite this one's flaws, the game play and it's aesthetics keep me coming back for another quest...or five....>.>

_childDocuments_.review:
Dragon MFD is a 2D side-scrolling action RPG game where up to 4 players can play together in either local multiplayer or online multiplayer. Refreshing, feel-good level designs based around intuitive 2D-action-based gameplay await!

Features:

* Play through the game as one of four Dragonkin characters!
The characters, known as the Dragonkin, have forged a pact with dragons which granted them special new powers. You can choose any one of the Princess, Warrior, Shinobi, or Witch characters to play as.

* Each playable character has different strengths and abilities!
The Princess is a well-balanced DPS character, the Warrior is a Tank class character that protects the party with his high defense, the Shinobi is DPS that places emphasis on movement on tricky attacks, and the Witch can both heal her allies and damage her emeies.

* A fascinating and immersive dark fantasy world
Carefully drawn pixel art from some of the industry's best pixelmancers paints the entire picture and brings players right into the dark fantasy setting.

* Work together with your companions to progress through stages!
In Dragon MFD, working together with your companions opens up a whole new realm of possibilities when it comes to defeating enemies and traversing stages.

* Battle against gargantuan bosses!
Absolutely gigantic bosses that are bigger than the entire screen await our heroes. Work together with your comrades to take down these larger than life baddies!

* Dozens and dozens of hours worth of gameplay!
Make no mistake, Dragon MFD is a massive game for its genre. With single stages that span 200-400 screens, over 30 main quests, and tons of side quests to tackle, players have tons of playtime to look forward to!

name: ICARUS
detailed_description: ICARUS is a PvE survival game with both Mission-based and persistent Open World modes for up to eight co-op players. Endure a savage wilderness on Icarus, an Earth-like terraformed planet now considered humanity’s greatest mistake. From their orbital station, prospectors drop to the planet surface to explore, harvest, craft and hunt while seeking their fortune. Confront and conquer a brutal PvE world determined to wear you down From toxic atmosphere to savage wildlife, apex predators to destructive storms and forest fires, Icarus is a planet with a temper. Preparation and planning are everything, whether it’s to find a source of oxygen, stalk your next meal or stockpile supplies for a long journey into the wilderness. Go at it alone, invite up to 8 Steam friends to join your game or play on dedicated servers. Immerse yourself in a deceptively familiar, yet formidable, world The First Cohort of prospectors has been granted initial mining licenses for over 64 square kilometers of hand-crafted terrain, full of hidden caves and biomes to explore. Every single tree is harvestable, every rock can be voxel mined, every creature can be hunted. Tame and ride mounts, craft advanced tech to extract resources faster and prepare yourself for harsher challenges. Master three separate tech trees: planetary tech, player talents and the orbital workshop Unlock four tiers of technology from hand-crafted to advanced composites and electronics, plus 8+ different building materials. Choose from over 100 talents as you specialize your character in exploring, building, farming, hunting, taming, fighting and more. Return to the orbital workshop to exchange exotic matter for advanced tech and items with unique properties, which may give you an advantage on your next drop. Three Game Modes: Open World, limited-time Missions, or creative Outposts However you want to experience Icarus, you can. Forge your claim in Open World, battling the elements and apex predators for survival and testing the limits of your survival instincts. Accept timed Missions to mine exotics and earn Ren as you complete tasks for the power brokers overseeing the planet. Drop down to the planet with nothing, establish a base from scratch and escape in time. Let your creative mind run wild in the Outpost regions with regenerating resources and safe environments. About the world of Icarus Icarus was once destined to be a second Earth, but when terraforming collapsed - the air turned toxic and humanity’s hopes of colonizing a new world died. Icarus became a joke, a symbol of humanity reaching for the stars and failing. The xeno-engineers salvaged what they could, released modified embryos and halted the terraforming process. Yet when they discovered the cause of the failure - exotic matter - new interest was ignited. Valuable beyond reckoning, these ‘exotics’ sparked a gold rush and fueled political tensions back on Earth. Prospectors flocked to Icarus to complete contracts to extract exotics and conduct research for various factions. Those that survive return to orbit as seasoned veterans, converting their exotics into advanced technology, and taking on ever more challenging drops. Those that get left behind... are lost forever. --- ICARUS is being made by a team of survival game veterans at RocketWerkz in beautiful Auckland, New Zealand.

_childDocuments_.review: Good day to any that read over this review,After playing this for only 10 to 11 hrs its truly hard to say yes to that I would even want to recommend any one else to really play the game. There are issues with it that just make me question like "Why? Huh? No? and Wtf?!" Moments. The game  I would have to say its a 3.5 out of 5 because several reasons.1st Why a XP debt? its already punishment enough having to respawn back at the drop pod when death happens, even then having a bedroll only works in sheltered areas. Which sure you could pickaxe a rock and use it but...you're trying to survive so what if you are in the middle of the forest or just want to camp out under the stars kinda feel. Yet the XP debt even basically makes you have earn the same exp you just lost so i'm doubling the XP that i lost to gain it back to even progress?! Why?! that just makes double work and grinding even more annoying honestly.2nd Animals lvls are 13 to 26 in the first area Huh? Now I found that it its a bit easier to see the way of sneaking and dealing damage but after moving to the second area and seeing levels at 61 to 90 i'm just like umm...i'm only 10!? Then if i used my points right i should be okay but it still just seeing that for the first time threw me for a loop its not like an RPG yet why even have levels for the animals it doesn't seem to really bother the EXP in my opinion but I could be wrong.3rd No, I don't want to lose the stuff I made if i'm coming back to the either same area or even mission. Can't we have it stored into the drop pod its really off to were you have collected enough to make bone spears and knives but missions over time to go oh...wanna take the stuff with you nope too bad. Later down the line its the same for iron and so forth. So its just like okay.4th Need water...yeah i need a canteen...its level  The entire time i was like I'll need water or something to carry water I was looking for a canteen...only to find out you cannot make anything until level 10 That helps with storing water. So this left me  I can make this hot air balloon that makes oxygen but I cannot do it for water?! I rather drown now!Other things mostly its the timers its great but then when you're playing on your own without timer I noticed the EXP is reduced greatly and the map is reallllly small I like exploring getting the fill of the land but maybe its different with friends Its just Icarus has a lot to offer but its seems like its a Gohan...It has hidden potential but its just not using it to the fullest until its really needed. Though as I stated i only spend 11 hr on it. I know i'll be jumping on more to get use to it. Also...what about a skill tree reset to allow you to replace points if you mess up. I know making another character is an option but just a thought.Recommend to friends that would like to mess around in missions sure but not really to anyone else.(EDIT)After 497 Hrs...I have to change what I stated above because that was when i was playing around in beta and thinking this company is going to be like some of the others. Make a game, wait a few months make an update do a little DLC then move on to another project.I was dead wrong and I happy to be wrong, the company has a community and they stick to it with updates every friday that could honestly be tide to DLC but are not. _childDocuments_.review: 112 hours so far. I've had Ark since alpha and I'm already well on my way to having more hours logged on Icarus. 10/10 for it's genre. Beautiful, open, rewarding. A sandbox by every definition but structured with quest elements. You can get lost in exploration and crafting, you hit a wall or maybe a good stopping point and it hits you, "Oh yeah. I'm also here for a reason" and off to the objective you go. Physics sim and weather effects are amazing. And specifically the fire animation and sounds. Hugely immersive all around. While there are no dinosaurs (that I've seen yet. Who knows what lies ahead.) I can confirm that the bears are extra dimensional in nature with their top tier parkour skills and speed that is not bound by traditional laws of physics. I stumbled upon a bear, unprepared for the encounter, I ran. I ran and ran and jumped over rocks and through some trees and even off a fairly short cliff side. I ran long enough and through enough obstacles that eventually I was like, "Surely I've lost him or he's lost interest. Let's take a look behind me." I turn around (while still moving forward) and my face is inside the bear's mouth... This was with a few points in Movement Speed and food buffs... Moral of the story? Kill them before they kill you and aim for the face. Also, the kill cam was an amazing, albeit guilt inducing, addition. Death cry + the amazing physics simulator make it feel... real lol.If you're an open world survival player, this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Stressful and punishing, yet fulfilling and rewarding.Like any game it has its flaws, but the dev team has been amazing and communicative. They are responsive to player feedback, and the weekly updates show their love and care for their game. They are clearly maintaining a careful balancing act between their own desires for the future of their game as well as giving players what they want. Sacrificing for your players keep games alive and thriving. It may have been released a bit prematurely, but the game is noticeably improving. My only fear now is that I hope the developers can keep up with the player demand and not get burnt out, and can keep introducing new content and missions. The amount of work these guys are putting into each weekly update cannot be easy.My only personal problem with this game as a whole is that my personal time is very limited, and the timing restrictions hold me back from starting some missions out of fear that I wont have time to complete them. I'm personally unsure how they can solve this problem for me without completely changing the whole point of the game.The only 2 ideas I have for this game would be to allow an option for predators in sandbox mode. I understand that there are explorations missions that last 30 days, but I fear I might forget about a character there. And I also think the number of allowed characters is way too small and needs to be increased.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are a LOT of people that seem to be having a bad experience with this game.  I think that most of the complaints are, at worst, nitpicking, and at best, not particularly relevant to the overall experience.  But it is what it is.That being said, I am having a blast so far.  I enjoyed it during the beta weekends, and I am still enjoying it now.  I'm not sure why so many people are having graphics problems, but I haven't personally had any.  I run an RTX2060S, Ryzen 7 2700, and 32gb of RAM and I am consistently getting 70-80fps with Epic settings.  I also haven't experienced any of the game breaking bugs that people are reporting.  So, I guess as far as that is concerned, it's buy at your own risk.As for the game itself, however, my opinion is that it was well worth what I paid for it.  If you're looking for something that flips the script on the survival genre, this game is probably not for you.  But if you're okay with a game that does the Survival thing really, really well and also manages to add a couple of unique aspects while it's at it, you won't be disappointed. A lot of people seem to be afraid of the "you lose everything once you leave the planet" thing.  It's not as bad in practice as it sounds.  You literally get days, if not weeks, to complete the mission.  You can get a lot done in that amount of time.  Plus, every time you complete a mission and go on to another one, you have more levels and more talents which makes starting over the next time much, much less tedious.  Eventually you are also able to bring certain things down with you that help streamline that process even more.  If all you want to do is build the base  of your dreams without a time limit, there's an option for that as well.  I haven't tried Co-Op yet, so I can't really speak to that.  From a purely hypothetical point of view, it sounds like it would be pretty fun.  Since you can't get every single talent or piece of tech even at max level you'd have to coordinate who does and gets what, which would make it slightly more interesting.  To be clear, you CAN get everything you need to complete the missions as a solo player, so there are no progression walls, as long as you're smart about what you pick.  TL;DR - I am really enjoying the game, despite all the negative reviews.  I personally think it was worth the money, but obviously mileage may vary.  It doesn't shatter the foundations of the survival genre, but what it does do, it does well.  Bottom line, if you like survival games, you'll probably like this game.  Alleged technical issues notwithstanding.

_childDocuments_.review: So it has asked me to update my review so here it is. This game is the awful. The premise is that you have to drop down onto a planet from an orbiting starship to perform different tasks. However to perform these tasks you have to research tech from the Stone Age through the space age. Remember, you're departing a star ship to start in the stone age, it's ridiculously unrealistic. _childDocuments_.review: I can sum up my 21 hours to one word.... Lazy.Icarus is a game about companies exploring a planet with life like earths, but with some subtle differences, one of them which is the games main mechanic, is its harsh weather systems that can blow your home apart with one stormy night. You are to take on prospects for companies and go to the planet to do whatever they tell you to do, kill a predator, mine a heap of resources, fix downed drop pods and gather survey information.It sounds a little interesting, a planet that needs exploring and you are tasked to do so. But it is DayZ, without the zombies, other players and ruined civilisation. If that sounds boring, that is because it is. It is forest, little caves, desert, snow and small ponds of water. This game is built around its environment by making its mechanics about surviving this environment. But the map is linear, in an open world game by locking off regions through a valley. This is suppose to be level locking, as each region makes the animals go up in level and it is such a grind.  Gameplay boils down to, land, level up character, build in biomes of your level, do mission. You gain exp to unlock more things to craft. It is just so grindy, boring and out of place. You are told you are a survival expert and thats why they chose you to go explore another planet, but your character knows f##k all. I am sure drug users in Melbourne central have more environment survival skills than your character. In the menu, you select Prospects. These details are laid out like, setting up a triangle of lasers to survey, killing an apex predator threatening wildlife or repairing downed equipment from companies. It is boring, because some are easy and some are hard which gives you more time to complete them. But they still boil down to the same of building in biomes you can, levelling up by doing small tasks and killing animals.There isn't much to talk about because there isn't much to do. It is a job to play, not fun at all. You jump into work and explore a make believe camera and not get paid at all. There is little music, the sound is bland and repetitive, graphics are not noteable at all. Sand comes during a sand storm, rain is wet, water ripples. It doesn't catch anything and you get sick of it. Landing, seeing the same rocks, the same trees, animals have the same respawn points and you leave after the mission to repeat it all over again. Worse, if your character is left on a prospect, you lose them. So you start from level 1, go back to previous missions to level up to get to the biomes you die in and blah blah... It is slow and feels like a job.I spent 21 hours trying, even a buddy helped me. We got so bored we kept betting each other on how many hyenas we can kill with a stone knife. I've spent a lot of my time playing with a video playing on the other monitor, a lot more time I spent was when I alt-tabbed to do some of my assignment and forgot I had the game open. Probably spent too much time trying to see what Dean Hall see's, or I probably sunk so many hours because lithium causes drowsiness and I might have fallen asleep. I have no idea. But I'd recommend keeping clear.

_childDocuments_.review: You've got your open world survival crafting and house building, and that's fine.You've got some half-decent stealth and surprisingly fun hunting.You've got random weather events that'll kill you and blow your house down.You've got skill trees and tech trees. And if you play solo, the devs had the foresight to provide a separate "solo" skill tree that helps buff your character to compensate for the hostile planet and lack of allies.All this makes for an pretty solid game, which probably doesn't stand out a great deal from the likes of Valheim or Conan. What I really like though is the mission structure. You (and perhaps friends) drop down on a corner of the map, with a specific set of goals (scan a region, mine some ore, exterminate a big creature, stuff like that), and up to 7 days in real life to achieve that goal and get back to your dropship. It doesn't work *quite* as well as Valheim's sort of in-story structure and guidance, but it provides you with concrete objectives to work towards, which I find very appealing as once you get to a certain point in other games, it's very easy to lose interest because there's little purpose beyond making some numbers go up. If you succeed, you get some in-game currency which you can spend on advanced gear you probably can't craft easily, like titanium harvesting tools, firearms, advanced armour and more. While you have to start from scratch each time you land on a planet, these advanced items really help take the grind out of it and give a sense of progression.Of course, you don't have to do the missions, there's an option to play on the map (which is something like 64Km sq) with no goals or time limits. Crafting doesn't seem prohibitively expensive, and while it's not as good as Valheim's (to be fair Valheim is damn close to perfection here), it's quick and straightforward.Oh, and while you always wear your environmental suit, any armour you put on is clearly put on OVER the suit, which I think is a nice touch. It looks way cooler to have some primitive hide wrapped around high-tech polymer.I cannot say you won't regret it if you purchase the €90+ edition, but the base game has a lot to like in it, and definitely represents decent value. If you pick it up in a sale, and you like this kind of game to begin with, I definitely think you'll enjoy it.Oh, and bonus points for a dev team that admitted to screwing up the release and working solidly since to improve and expand it. I have a lot of respect for that sort of honesty and effort at putting things right.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 28. December 2022I need to change my negative review of this game to a positive just because they listened to the community and implemented a open world, do whatever you want mode in Icarus and that alone pleases me to no end.HOWEVER they still tied restrictions into that like you have to do missions to unlock cave systems to other biomes which should not be in place for a completly, roam around freely mode but its just a handful of missions i guess so ill let it slide.A lot of things still hold true since the original review. Animals are no real thread except if they heavily outnumber you, level of an animal means absolutely nothing, very few new animal types to speak of (Moa and.. i think thats it?). Still with the open world update alone they won me over since icarus in a nutshell is a great game and its a lot of fun.The new mount system is a great addition to the game but the animals you have as mounts are very very annoying to keep. Everytime i open the build shed they kinda immediately run outside. If you put them on "stay", they do anything BUT stay where you want them to, if you put them in "follow" they losely follow you around. Follow works better than stay but both should get a big overhaul if you ask me. If i want a mount/pet to STAY.. then i want it to stay where it is and maybe give it a little free roam but not let it run away from me in high speed. Thats just annoying. What do i wish for, for further updates?More Animals, especially dangerous onesMore Challenging options for a open world runMore weather typesMake weather more and more dangerous the longer you play an open world sessionLet Worldbosses do... something. They dont even drop anything upon deathBetter mount systemOLD REVIEW:You heard is thousand of times and you will hear it many times again but Icarus is a love/hate game that does some things very good and some things horribly.It makes ZERO sense why you go on a planet without any equipment, not even basic stuff. Sure in the very beginning i do like that you have nothing and have to build your own stuff but the idea that you leave everything behind once you leave the planet and have to start over in the next mission is just baffling how they thought its a good idea.The first two maybe three times its not that big of a deal to "start over" but you start to wonder whats the point in crafting the best stuff if you lose it all once you leave the planet/mission.What you do keep however is your level and your overall skill tree. The level is.. just that. a level. It gates you from crafting certain things early and gates you even more with skill points. The character building with leveling is extremly small and the benefits of a unlockable skill can be as low as 1% in something (bow-damage, move speed, crit damage, carrying weight etc) which you definitly will fell/notice. just trust me on that.The balance in this game is completly forgetable. In the very first mission you can already encounter lv 70 wolf´s and you can absolutely oneshot them on level 1. There is no noticeable change in the animals stats be it damage dealt if they hit you, HP or even exp gained. so they might aswell just not write a level on the animals if a level 1 wolf has basicly the same stats and gives the same exp as a level 100 wolf does.The good things are there too like graphics are nice, combat feels overall fun to do and hunting animals for food/materials is also nice. The animal AI is pretty bad tho and with the ghille set you are basicly invisible on the map for every animal even the polar bear in the arctic. Its insane how OP the set really is.What just gets me and is killing the fun is that you feel like its completly pointless to craft higher and better gear if a longbow and bone arrow do the trick 98% of the time anyways. Why craft a shotgun or a hunting rifle if you have nothing to fear except two animals and you can sneak around these easily with the ghille suit which is obtained pretty early so its no problem to get it every time.I will keep an eye out for this game any maybe something will change with the resetting but i wont hold my breath for it thats for sure. Maybe a free roam mode with missions taken from the base with animals around and unlimited time could be a thing sometime but until then this game is for those people who either have fun doing something over and over and over again and enjoy it or just build huge projects, lose it all and burn out because of it and not playing any longer.

_childDocuments_.review: I have followed Icarus's development from the very beginning days since it was announced.  I've been excited for a game in the survival genre that featured persistent character progression for a long time. I've been active within the Icarus community () throughout trying to learn everything there is to know.Closing in on 500 hours in game (+189 in beta) should indicate that I've already experienced all there is to do by now so I feel comfortable reviewing the game for real and updating my earlier launch review which can be seen here: . I have experienced everything that is in this game. The full breadth and scope of content and progression. I have unlocked everything and have fiddled around with everything you can craft. I've helped figure out a lot of the meta speedrun tactics, including playstyles that many other's use. I've played every previous beta weekend from BW1 through BW7 and been playing on average around 60 hours every two weeks since it's official launch.  When I'm not playing, I'm active answering questions on the discord or reddit or helping icarusintel's team.  I can say with confidence that this game is positively a fun experience If you do not, you might be better suited to wait for additional content to come. I can say this based on having already seen and experienced all that there is currently and knowing the game following it well enough to know what is to come yet will only improve it. I can also confirm that it has gotten better every step of the way and the devs have impressed me by having more than shown a willingness to address the issues in a timely manner while remaining transparent throughout the entire process. Not everything they have done has been positive changes but they are quick to take in feedback and make necessary fixes. I have full confidence in them fixing issues as they arise going forward. The dev's commitment for their game is there 100%. It's refreshing to see it too. It's a rare thing in the gaming world to be so responsive and transparent with the fans.   I am super excited for what Icarus will become as it continues to evolve and grows. The scope of the game's features is only going to improve further over time as they add to it. It may not be  now, missing some elements we thought would be in it at launch [I.E. Alien creatures/biomes]. Some might even say the game isn't "done" with missing veins and such in some missions but they have a very good base skeleton or bones of the game with which they can build upon.The base structure of systems in place of which they just keep adding to and tweaking with new content and mechanics is solid. The planned stuff is really exciting too. They will continue free weekly-content and QoL updates along the way but I am less concerned with what it is like right now, after 3 months in, and more interested in what it's like in 1 years time. Admittedly the game does have some minor issues —as it stands — so I will start there. ■ Focusing on the game's performance it can slowdown when hosting. And during storms where trees often are struck by lightning and catch on fire. The game's framerates can drop drastically. The devs have yet to fix this. At times the game engine's performance issues might see random drops or hitches but overall the gameplay experience is quite smooth. ■  The overall level of difficulty also is kind of slacking. If by design it can be too easy for an experienced gamer. Some might consider the game to be too mundane or dull then because of this.■  Combat especially isn't very complex or engaging for the player. With just the second tier of crafted bow and arrows one can basically handle all the creatures currently in the game and most of them can be one-shotted and insta-killed with the kill cam's damage boost. Because the kill cam gives a large damage boost to ensure the animal actually dies when the animation zoom in happens for the auto-homing missile arrows. This Fallout-esque combat basically is not challenging for the player at all. Entire weapon types are negated by strictly better options. For example. Hardly anyone uses spears or even throws knives because shooting a bow is better and swinging a knife is faster than a spear swings which makes it strictly better. The spears not having the ability to block or negate some incoming damage means nobody uses them. Guns even are often an afterthought because bows are so good and way easier to get. Which begs the question about the new alien creatures, that eventually will come out, will they be any more fun to experience if the combat isn't fixed? You can side-step to dodge bears making them not much of a challenge besides managing your stamina. I'de like to see more character ability within combat like charged attacks, blocking/negating damage, etc.  ■ By far the most major gripe I have with the game is the  and they don't change. They should be randomized so that they actually change every mission where they would appear or which veins become active but instead once you've done a mission once you know where to go the next time and it completely negates ever needing the radar to scan for them.This is one thing that MUST change for the game to have any degree of replayability and ultimately longevity in keeping my interest levels in it. Even when new missions/new content comes out to experience eventually we will complete it and that is fine but what keeps you coming back and offers the true replayability is the general gameplay loop and the main part of it — extracting exotics — is fundamentally broken because of this one design choice to not make them randomized but static. It's simply unfun and unfulfilling to know where you gotta go everytime. No challenge of exploration. We are Prospectors? Pfft■ Missions in general are too short minded in terms of their objectives and as a result over too quickly. Not giving players any reason to stay down and tech up playing for as long as the extended timer allows for. If they gave some mission types (I.E. Exploration missions) optional objectives that you could choose to complete, it would fix this issue almost entirely.That or branching missions where you get more and more objectives in succession. ■ The graphics are on par with AAA titles and comparable to the best this gen has to offer. With full RTX Global Illumination and Ray Tracing ON, the game's lighting and textures are lifelike. The backdrops are gorgeous to where I often momentarily stare off into the night sky in awe of their beauty. If your PC can handle epic settings use them. Many players will lower their graphical settings thinking it gives better optimization though. While a stable performance without crashing the client is ultimately all one needs in any game boy does it ever look good though when you really crank up everything. You can also take some really nice screenshots with the built in photo mode tool. ■ The audio work stands out as top notch here too. Sound effects such as the pings and tings you get when voxel mining out nodes, the wind whirling around you during the storms, trees creaking and cracking and the thud when they hit the ground. It's all very well sounding and helps ground the player into the game setting and goes along way to making it believable.Review continued in here due to length restrictions;Clicking says malicious so just copy paste url into web browser. It's just googledocs Steam... increase your character limit for reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: As of right now the game has a few glaring issues, but it seems that devs are actually serious about fixing these issues. At its core the game is very fun and engaging, honestly I can recommend buying it especially at its price. However don't go in expecting a fully polished game.Full: The Bad - The game absolutely has its issues, it runs like crap, it looks like crap unless you crank every setting to max, and it while the game mechanics are good, some things really make no sense. The main issue I have is the fact that every time you complete a mission, all physical progress you've made is gone. The only thing you keep is your research and talents, all buildings and items just disappear for seemingly no reason. While not a complete deal breaker for me, its easy to see why it would be for some players. Another odd decision the devs have made is that while you can play solo, it is quite a grueling experience taking hours upon hours to complete even the most basic missions (only for your hard earned gear to disappear once you're done!). Not to mention that its impossible to unlock everything in the tech tree on your own. Luckily what I've prefaced is the bulk of the issues. I've heard of issues with bugs and connectivity but I haven't run into that personally. Any other issues I've seen really just come down to tweaking some number, most notably the death xp penalty.The Good - The game has very good core mechanics and has an engaging feel when playing. When playing, especially solo I definitely feel like a mountain man, scouting the wilderness, constantly keeping my eye out for predators trying to eat me alive. And then when I conquer those animals I use them to make better tools and equipment and slowly work my way up the tech tree and complete my mission. The game also provides interesting and unique challenges at every level and keeps you on your toes no matter how prepared you think you are. The mission objectives (a good amount of the time) also give you oppurtunity to think logically and do things the way you want to, instead of being on rails with only 1 possible way of doing things. As far as mechanics go there are definitely very interesting and unique ideas being put in place here that I think work really well, I would even say flawlessly if it weren't for the issues I described earlier. Once you complete a mission and return to the space station you are rewarded with money that you are able to use on modern equipment that you can take down with you the next time you deploy. I think this concept is really cool and really motivates me to actually go out and do all the side missions that aren't required to progress further down the mission chain. Summary: Icarus absolutely has the potential to be an incredible survival game, It just has a couple important issues that I really hope the devs can overcome. Overall in its current state I'd give the game a 7/10. It's still fun to play as of right now, but in a year or so I think this game can really be something else entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus, the survival game I scoped out since release but never purchased. I held off on this one at first due to lukewarm reviews and later due to the cost of the experience (if you include Styx and Prometheus in that equation).That said, I'm glad I did finally pick this game up and I would recommend it to fans of the genre, but in particular people, like me, who really enjoy the early portion of survival games. The mission-based part of the game (the original part that many people did not like) is basically repeatedly starting over with nothing (a bit of a rogue like experience) and as you progress you do get to bring more things down with you that you purchase with meta currency that you are earning on each mission. This gives purpose to constantly restarting and the missions also give finite objectives for each "game".I've enjoyed the mission bit enough that I haven't even started the other types of games (which you can run concurrently) including open world (more like a classic survival experience with some of the elements from the mission based game mode), and outpost (like a peaceful building option). The same character can run all 3 types of games at once from what I gather which is neat. You don't bring things between the modes but you keep your talents and research unlocks.Basically, TLDR, I think this one is a must buy if you like the start of survival games especially and if you like the idea of a rogue-like survival game :) It does everything else pretty well and the storms definitely make survival more interesting, but I'd say the biggest difference is the sort of meta game of missions and unlocks. They also seem to be really active (weekly?) in content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally love this game, and with the upcoming release of the New Frontiers DLC, now is an excellent time for me to show my own opinion on the game!A lot of the character of the game was present once it released, but just like any other game that is new, there were some issues with it. The developers have managed to release an update EVERY SINGLE WEEK, fixing bugs, adding content, and improving the game. This is pretty impressive for a studio, and something you seriously do no see in modern gaming. I can confidently say the game has improved tenfold, and with the most recent changes, I believe Icarus is one of the best survival games out there right now.As for the game itself, the flow feels a little bit like Ark: Survival Evolved, with a bit of grinding and building up a base. Originally, you could only play the game utilizing the Mission System. While I still enjoyed the game during this phase, it was slightly disheartening to have to restart everything besides my character each mission. It prevented me from recommending the game to more casual players. This downside has all been fixed now. With the addition of Open World, Outposts, and Side Missions, the only thing you don't get from playing a continuous, open world is exotics, and with the upcoming update, that should be fixed!The last thing I would like to touch on is the "RPG" elements of the game. This includes the skill tree, and the blueprint tree. The skill tree is quite expansive, and with 50 levels worth of skill points (50+ skill points) you can really cater your prospector to how you enjoy playing the game, or how you wish you improve your experience. This includes farming, grinding for materials, building, hunting, exploring, etc. This creates an awesome dynamic for you and any friends you are playing, allowing you to rely on each other for be the most efficient you can be. You may ask what you're supposed to do if you're solo... well, they have a solo tree dedicated to providing stronger buffs to allow your prospector to be more efficient if you're alone.The blueprint tree, at least to me, seems a little difficult to get through in the beginning. You won't be able to produce an amazing base right off the bat. This is when I recommend new players to complete the missions, so that there is a sense of progress. Once you've started unlocking more blueprints, you can then start completing an Outpost, or an Open World mission. There is an insane amount of content you can unlock, including decorations, structure tiers, and weapons. This only increases with their DLC, which is reasonably priced in our current video game market, supports the amazing studio, and adds some more passion to your lovely home.Thanks for reading my review! I hope to see you all on Icarus!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the entire Beta and the Full Release, I feel qualified to give my opinion...which is worth whatever you decide.  tldr; If you like the feeling you get when you first start a survival scenario, this game is for you.  If you need to race through to the end and win...it is not for you.Icarus is a misunderstood product that is better than a lot of people would lead you to believe...but...it does have some glaring issues.  Some of those issues are optimization-related, most are related to the lack of underlying systems (some of which have been fixed as of the Week 11 Patch) but IMO those systems should have shipped in Full Release.  While I am not a game developer or designer, I do find it strange that it took all of the Beta and 11 weeks of Full Release before they wrote a method for sorting inventory...and it only sorts by weight.  This game reminds me of No Man's Sky, it SUCKED when it released because it was not what we thought we were paying for...but look at it now, it's super awesome.  My money is on Icarus improving over time, and so far the devs have actively done just that (albeit a little slowly and with an emphasis on some things we don't care about as much.  I'd rather have better sorting options than another mission at this point).Icarus is wonderful, it let's me get that "I just got here and need shelter" rush every time I start a new prospect.  As long as I'm cautious and tune in to my environment, I generally don't have many issues on the surface.  It's a rare game that makes me feel like I can ignore the pain of having to get my stuff if a bear eats my face and really makes smart gameplay necessary.  Being able to slowly build up a 'locker' of equipment that I can pick and choose from depending on the mission parameters is a cool way to instill some permanence in a session-based survival game.  That being said, there needs to be some sort of plan for endgame content.  Ark has it, Conan has it...Icarus needs it.I'd recommend it, but just make sure you know what you are really paying for...

_childDocuments_.review: Like all of Dean's games this one has potential but is ultimately incredibly flawed; it's also very obviously still a beta game with bugs, missing content, horrible performance and absolutely terrible AI and enemy pathfinding.The crafting/building loop in itself is fun and engaging but everything else is like communism: good on paper but in practice it's a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Why the deletion of a character with a ticking timer?Why do you have to run back to your spaceship literally just holding W?Wny do you have to re-craft everything every mission?If your excuse for these three questions is "the lore/universe" then at least make it have some internal consistency and logic, which it does not have. It's a narrative free for all and it's obviously all just an excuse to pad out gameplay.The combat is horrible and the amount of wolves and bears I have killed in just 8 hour playtime is almost nonsensical, even for a game and listen, I understand that gamers like to abuse AI to easily kill npc's and enemies but the solution is NOT to make bears be spiderman. I got attacked by a bear while felling a tree, one of the logs apparently was a stick bomb because I could barely traverse the space while the bear just could freely walk around, over and at one point just straight through. This kind of thing happens CON-STANT-LY if you get attacked while doing some kind of resource gathering that produces items (logs, dropped items, etc); the terrain bugs and glitches out and it's incredibly frustrating. I just ALT-F4'd the last time that happened and I haven't touched the game since and I probably won't again unless things get fixed. I doubt it.Dean, I understand you have PTSD from the creating the very first "forever early access" game with DayZ mod and the first few years of standalone but jesus christ, that does not mean you now just have to spit out a 1.0 when this game is very obviously not finished. At all.TL;DR: Don't buy this game. The crafting is fun but everything else is sad mess of jank, buggy and just plain bad with the performance and optimization on the level of Ark. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:  Good graphics with good performance tooCons:  No 'craft from storage' mechanic, which makes ALL crafting in the game just an incredibly obtuse chore. You literally waste minutes looking for wood/stone/iron/nails/etc. in your various storage containers just to craft 1 item AND then you have to put all the left-over items back into the storage containers after you're done crafting. It's just a massive chore and one of the main reasons why I stopped playing the game. Instead of getting back to base and crafting for 2-3minutes then going out again to explore & kill stuff, you end up crafting for 30minutes+ and sifting through various containers looking for the stuff you need. All that time could be spent actually playing the game, instead of doing inventory management. The $30 DLC that they released recently (New Frontiers) is absolutely terrible, for two reasons: Firstly, you don't get access to the whole map, because they're 'unlocking' the full map piece-by-piece over the next few months, so you're paying $30 for 20% of a map. Secondly, you can't play on the base game's map (Olympus) together with the new map (Prometheus), so you have to choose EITHER the base game's map (which is way bigger) or the new map with the new content. I just don't fathom why a developer would not just combine the two maps? Like if you think about when most good games gets a new expansion (like Diablo 2 for instance), they don't force you to choose between the base game's map and the new map.... they allow you to play on both and they're connected, which EXPANDS the world... it's not a separate world, it's an expanded one. And yet these devs have separated the worlds and you can't even jump between them with your stuff which is doubly terrible. You can't change any of the game world's settings... so like for instance in other similar games like Conan Exiles, you can change the hunger/thirst/resource decay/health/tool durability/etc. of the world... and yet in this game you can't change anything. So the game has forced tool durability and forced hunger/thirst/oxygen, and if you're a player who doesn't like those survival mechanics, but likes open-world crafting games, then you're fxcked, because you can't change anything. The experience gain rate is also hilariously slow, plus there's diseases & injuries that you character can get and you can't change that either. No tutorial whatsoever No story or campaign. You're literally just dumped on a map, with no explanation and no story. The game has various bugs/glitches. In my 10hrs+ with the game so far, I've encountered enemies that can shoot you through walls/terrain, disappearing resources, floating enemies, etc. The character customization options are massively lacking. They shouldn't even have bothered with a character creation mechanic, if they're going to half-ass it like they did with so few options. Game has terrible regional pricing and it's for sale in ruzziaThe devs FINALLY removed their absolutely terrible 'timed' mechanic after two years, which is one of the main reasons why I didn't even CONSIDER the game until now, but the game still has some really stupid design decisions (like cons #1 and #2) which makes me not able to recommend it to anyone. If you're looking for a game that has great exploring, crafting and combat, with some survival mechanics sprinkled ontop, and which has an actual narrative story, then just get No Mans Sky on sale. I'm not touching this game again until they ATLEAST fix cons #1 and #2.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with friends. Still feels like Early Access in many places. Combat is fun as long as you don't have to go toe-to-toe with a stronger enemy. There is no block or counter mechanic so melee fells a bit lack luster compared to the complexity of a lot of other systems in the game. Optimization is also below full release. The game can be run on medium to high end PC's but the graphics will start to look rather bad when tuning down some of the options. Gameplay is fun thou and I really like the mission / rough-like type of progression in a survival game. Makes every mission feel different so far. Bioms are nice too even thou I really dislike the use of invisible walls / "out of playable area" zones. I don't think an "openworld" game should have those. I still think there is a lot of fun to be had. But i really hope the devs will keep adding to this game. I feel there are many easy ways to expand on this game to make it really good. More animal types, enemy types,  expanded melee combat... If not I think this game will become be one of those "would have had potential" open-world-early-access games that got abandoned too early by the devs. I have to give credit to the devs for fixing a lot of issues we had on launch day. So if this kind of responsiveness consists, this could be one of the better type of games in this genre.
