_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been non stop fun. Icarus keeps you on your toes with: ->*Storms keeping you on your toes for repairing the bases you make or trying to kill you.*Hostile wildlife trying to always kill you.*Illnesses you can contract from creatures or weather.*Trees falling on your head.*Fall damage.*Starving.*Running out of O2 (Oxygen)*Dehydration.*Friendly fire.*Forest fires.*Setting your own base on fire.With all of the above being said that might make people hesitant to try the game it has a lot of cool aspects such as: ->*Easy to learn hud system.*Massive Talent tree for both Blueprints (Aka Crafting) and character talents (Stat boosts... Health and gathering plus weather resistances carry weight etc)*Private session Co op with up to 8 people (No online servers to fight off griefers/pvp)*The game can also be SOLO and has a SOLO Talent tree to assist with it which is a huge help for the loner players.*Mining is piece by piece system meaning hit 1 spot and only 1 part of the rock/ore etc will break not the entire thing.*Wood cutting is like valheim but set up better (Lop a tree down it can fall and kill you) but its piece by piece harvesting. In other words smack it 1 time in a spot of it to de-branch it and smack it a few more times to split it in to wood pieces.*Building system is a mixture of a snap to free placing system in other words similar to ARK except you can clip floors into the ground. Supports for it work like Valheim. You can build it and if it has bad support either it will fall or if to much weight is on it with not enough support it will break.*There is a temp meter that can be either C or F to help you manage your heat or cold which can be vital in a some places. Yes torches give small heat.*Max level is >99< I am level 25 at the posting of this.*Benches tell ALL Recipes you can do/make what Fuel you need for the bench and what Alternate fuel you can use. (Unlike some games)*Start up gathering is simple in easy (No getting tackled and killed as soon as you spawn)*Graphics look amazing like minecraft mods stack to the point of burning up your PC amazing visuals.*So many more things I could say but ill leave the rest for you to find out.Now on to MY Opinion ratings.*Building 10/10 (Its easy to do with its usual problem placing system like any other building in survival games)*Graphics 9.8/10*Rendering speed 8.5/10 (Heavy rendering frame spikes in some places on medium settings)*Gameplay 10/10*Load times (Getting into game) 9.5/10 (somtimes loads fast, Sometimes its a little sluggish)*Character customization 5/10 (Your in a space suit. You customize a face and a small amount of your suit) (Personally id like to see at least character portion settings arms, legs etc. You looks like a stick which I understand why)*Combat 8.6/10 (The combat is solid. But it can be glitchy at times were you dont hit your target and 3rd person combat is a little bit of a mess at this moment I find myself going into 1st person just to be able to hit my targets)*Gatherings system 9.5/10 (Nothing respawns once gathered aka true survival)*Day/Night Cycle system 10/10 (Feels like a normal day and night cycle. You can rest at beds to INSTANT flip from night to day with no loading transition needed blah blah blah. Plus you get a rested buff!)*Hunting in the game for food 10/10 (Feels like skyrim with its cinematic shot whenever you land a sneak attack critical which is so satisfying)*Lighting/illumination for night time or dark areas 10/10 (I feel that the lighting for the game is pretty dang spot on with the types of lighting you can use that helps a lot in the dark. Dark is DARK in the game just a fyi)*Down time in game 9.6/10 (Meaning when you have to wait for things to craft etc nothing to do till you have finished this thing yada yada yada. Its very few and far between. Always something to do in this game)Now my over all rating of the game it self. If I could give it a rating I would say a solid 9.8/10 some things need to be worked on but aside from that its a stupid amount of fun.PS WATCH FOR BEARS.

_childDocuments_.review: : Icarus: First Cohort, developed and published by  is a session-based, open-world PvE survival and crafting game. You go down to complete missions, be it timed scans, picking up specific flora or mining exotic matter, all ending with you returning your loot to your spacecraft and starting fresh for each mission, rouge-like style but with level web upgrades that stay across all your expeditions.: It's honestly a beautiful game and I have zero complaints about it, other than the land not really screaming “alien planet”. Animals are beautiful and the design of them being skinned etc, are really well done, decently animated and all around really pleasant to look at. It just suffers from lack of character or originality. : This game needs an active soundtrack 'cause as it is, it has none and does kill a lot of atmosphere that could be there, that is instead replaced with baron quietness of the land. : I actually love the menu layout of this game, how they did character creation and lastly the level selection screen was extremely crisp.There are plenty of options for a varying range of PC's. I will also make an important note; If you are having issues with frames turn off  and if that has still not resolved your issues, turn off anti-aliasing as it has also been known to cause some issues. Once those are turned off, I personally had no issues and I read that many others frames were also fixed afterwards. : The game itself is gorgeous, however very samey from the time I have played of it. The maps seemed very bland and didn't give me any “alien planet” vibes whatsoever, It was just generic forest. Which overall is fine. Albeit uninspired. The leap to session-based play honestly intrigued me the most as it's a new concept for mashing it with the survival genre. The only game that comes to mind to relate it towards is , (I will be referencing this game again as DRG), having said that however this is where it begins to fall flat on it's face.Sessions would be a lot better if there was less distance in-between objectives, the level grind is extremely frustrating when it takes so long to traverse a pretty, but seemingly lackluster world. For the first few expeditions it has you pick up a lot of inconsequential resources solely for the exp grind to get some of your first permanent web upgrades, which conceptually is really cool, a rogue-lite style of play.However  then further falls, its building itself a very repetitive core structure whilst lacking any form of character and making it too expansive, for the at a glance, quick drop in missions like DRG.Everything is made to be and feel very slow burn which doesn't mesh well with session-based play, leaving a huge disconnect between the two ideas. This could only really be solved by going one way or the other and streamlining that, but as it is, neither side meshes well with one another and I'm left stuck in the middle with a concept of a game that is great, but executed poorly. I truly believe this can be a good game, but in it's current state, it is not. I want to recommend it, yet I cannot. It needs a lot of work to be a solid game and to live up to the concept it has made for itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most of the negative reviews I would like to start off by saying that this game has MUCH potential, and you'll most likely have fun with it if you like similar survival games. However, the bugs, "coming soon" items in the crafting menu, and lack of some elementary features makes for an unsatisfactory purchase. I can forgive a few bugs, even a couple of game breaking ones, but many of the bugs I encountered I would never expect from a full-release title. Most of the bugs I've come across are quality of life issues that are simply infuriating and are easy fixes: Can not activate floor torches (hello darkness my old friend... will update if this applies to wall torches later), unable to remove backpack from Textiles Bench let alone equip it, trees falling through the world like a seesaw (this can potentially kill you on the upswing), unable to craft anything in the player crafting menu, unable to swing tools/attack/draw bow at seemingly random moments.Fun? Absolutely. If you like similar games (Ark, Rust, etc.) you will love this game. The concept of quick, efficient basebuilding in order to complete missions on different worlds is a great innovation to the genre that I am excited to explore (and probably die over and over again in doing so but c'est la vie). Should you buy it? No. The release date for this game was clearly a money grab for holiday sales and I would advise you to check back in a few weeks for the biggest bugs to be sorted out. Thankfully the devs seem to be pretty aware of the situation the have on their hands and are working to do frequent patches/updates to fill out the rest of the game. I won't pretend to understand the ins and outs that go into the development of a game such as this, but I truly feel for the devs whom I can only assume were put under an insane deadline or possibly ran into development issues.Heyyyyyy time to throw in my two-cents. First I wanna say I admire y'all's hard work that you're clearly putting into making this game what it should be. I'm so excited to see where it goes. Here's a few things that I think would elevate the game a bit more.-color blind mode (at least for the UI/map if not the whole game. I can barely see my character's arrow on the map pleaseeeee)-nuanced pve (so far it seems like everything other than the cave things just chase and bite/scratch. perhaps a shield or domestication system w/ wolves could spice it up?)-nuanced hunting (tracks, droppings, fur tufts, bait, calls. this is already such an essential part of the game so lets make it more fun!)-maybe calm down a bit on the lightning. I'm 4 for 4 on a single lightning storm burning down my whole house lol.-more early game creatures? (admittedly I have not traveled too far yet, but I would like to see something other than the same 4 animals over and over. Although I'm disappointed with the current product as a full-release game, I'm VERY excited to see where this goes. I remember the early days of Rust (back when it was primarily a zombie game) and this game is miles above that. I wish the very best to the Devs and will be waiting on the edge of my seat for every patch and update to come.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite survival games. I logged an embarrassing amount of hours on both ARK and No Man's Sky. Most recently a bunch of Valheim and Satisfactory. This is my new addiction. There's a lot of complaints about bugs, I've experienced very few and none that were game breaking. The 'unstuck' feature usually resolves them. The building is very satisfying, although a little more complexity would be cool. The one complaint I can agree with is Tier 4 being a grind and a half. I decided to do a 30 day mission with the sole intent of getting excessive on the base. 20-30 hours and 15+ caves cleared, I was dipping my toes into tier 4. Easily double the time needed to have a full Tier 4 base. For the grind early on, that's where you need the better tools from the workshop. The first 5-6 missions were definitely tedious. Now with upgraded everything, my buddy and I can have a stone base and most tier 3 goodies in 60-90 minutes depending on the biome. The grind has become much less and we've fine tuned what we need. Graphics, sounds, weather events, combat, all very enjoyable. An amazing game I've followed since it was teased and was not even remotely let down. Must buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Played it on the free to play weekend event for the first time, but it was on my wishlist. However, I was unsure of dropping $$$ on it as there were 3 things that I was worried about making the play experience not fun. These were: 1) Unlocking gear between "missions" not being a fun way to progress. 2) Timed missions can add WAY too much stress to a survival game. 3) Wiping character progress after death (this is no longer a thing)However, I have been pleasantly surprised. I can see how the difficulty will ramp up, but so far the difficulty has been just fine. I will say the one negative thing is that the tutorial doesn't cover some basics (like that your structure needs a beam to support either going up or having a rather heavy workstation on it. Which is a mechanic I enjoy but it is not explained to you when you go through the tutorial.As you unlock new both blueprints and talents you make things much easier the next time you start a new run. Additionally, they have different modes for those who have different preferences. You don't really need to do missions (excepting the ones that will unlock blueprints you want), you can instead do either an Open World (persistent) or Outpost (persistent and all resources will respawn, but map is smaller) instead of a timed mission. Speaking of those, you really don't need to worry too much about the amount of time you're given (at least that I've experienced so far. I've been working on one mission for 8 hours, am 1/3 of the way done (after OVER preparing WAY too much) and have another 6 days and 18 hours left to go. I'm fairly sure I'll complete it before doing even 1 full 24 hours. But, its also one of the early, easy missions.I can understand those who give a negative rating because they were having a rough time, but I'm not sure how they have struggled so much...I will most likely be purchasing the game once the free weekend is over. I'm having a blast!

That game was never delivered and now I have to purchase another DLC just to get the game I was originally promised.  "Exclusive to Prometheus" is the norm for new updates. The literal definition of bait and switch.The game might get better, but I can't fundamentally support devs who rug pulled a community that supported them in early access. If you don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about that then the game might be for you. It's a bog standard survival crafting game with decent graphics and a grindy resource economy.  It takes too long to get to the stone building tier and the lighting storms can and will set your wood base on fire. You will lose everything you worked for and have to grind it again.  This is intended gameplay.  If you skip the open world and just do missions, it gets incredibly boring with half a dozen enemies set on repeat.  Give it another year to bake.  It's technically out of EA, but still for all intents and purposes still in EA. You'll likely have to buy a 3rd DLC by the time the game is in a state the devs promised when it first launched.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, I had completed an overtime work week for the UDA on Icarus.  At first, the prospect of donning a space suit, entering a capsule, and dropping to the planet with no equipment did not appeal to me.  It seemed fake.  It seemed silly; humans, capable of spaceflight, travel across the galaxy to a planet which presently appears Earthlike, only to descend and play the caveman.  I was pretty lukewarm before I dipped my toes into this kiddie pool.But after I nearly starved my first night on the planet, I changed my tune.  It had been some time since anything challenged my ability to acquire and process resources.  I knew what I was supposed to do, but I wasn't sure how I was going to realistically achieve it.  After failing to catch rabbits and find sufficient edibles, I eventually made a bow, and started to beat back the starvation.  The tiny hovel I managed to build by myself seemed like a spacious mansion.  Each piece of hard earned knowledge seemed like a precious treasure, and the richer I became, the bolder I got.  The bolder I got, the more I realized discretion is the better part of valor.You can tell any story about how the terraforming foiled colonization efforts, or whatever humdrum that's supposed to be on about; the fact of the matter is that Icarus is essentially dopamine rush for the survivalist, meant to be consumed in 12-hour chunks.The company needs to balance some things, like how certain perk trees are essentially hot garbage compared to others.  It would also be great if we ever saw anything between the threat level of a sickly wolf and a rabid bear, but sometimes you just count your blessings.10/10, would recommend to all my survivalist friends.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: To start, I can't recommend Icarus unless you've got the money burning a hole in your pocket. I had fun for the first half of my playtime but I quickly realized I needed to move on. There are some good things about the game but there's too many bad things for me to label Icarus itself as good.Icarus starts out great and the first 30 to 40 hours I really did have fun. The grind and frustration sets in once you've learned the game and have grown tired of dropping into a mission in the same location as your last base, which is entirely gone. I enjoy a grind with purpose, but the way Icarus has implemented it feels punishing for those that want to progress through the game. Coupled with a real world timer that will perma-kill (renders your character unplayable & must delete it) casting its shadow makes me feel stuck in the game. Parents/busy people beware - if a family event/work event is coming up (or something unexpected like significant other/kids get sick/work calls) or you have a trip to leave for then keep this real world timer in mind. You can abandon a mission with no harm and no foul other than your time invested in it, which can save your character...if you're able to make it back to your dropship (you can semi-abuse the respawn function to accomplish this by dying, destroying your respawn point, then dying again to be freshly dropped in by a new pod - but beware here too....dying wipes out any XP you've gained towards the next level).There are 4 separate tiers of crafting available, with some interesting items spread throughout. The issue is I found myself thinking about how much of a waste it would be to grind out to tier 4 to get the best armor and the firearm/bow you'll most likely want just to have it make the mission very simple, which means you'll complete your objective, leave the mission, and abandon your base and all items on the planet. This system and my thought process relegated me to staying mostly at tier 2 crafting (wood/bone/leather/minor iron tools) in the majority of my later missions unless the objectives specifically needed something from higher tiers.There is a sandbox mode (not a creative mode) for those that like to craft and explore without a real world time limit looming overhead. It's fun and with less pressure, the building options open up. However, any time you spend on Icarus will subject you to weather events that damage your structures and it requires you to physically be there to repair the walls and ceilings that gets damaged before they break. I wouldn't recommend large constructions because you'll not be able to keep up with the repairs required during storms and something will break. If a roof is destroyed your unbelievably expensive tier 4 crafting stations (yes, you need multiple, they have different functions) is no longer sheltered and will take damage from the storm, if it breaks there's no salvage you can reclaim to soften the blow. You can kinda cheese this by only placing the crafting stations if/when you need to use them, then picking them up and storing them in a chest or a cheaper crafting station. If the storage item gets destroyed then it just drops what it was holding and these items can be picked up.Overall - Icarus has potential to be a great game, but dev decisions haven't shaped it in a way to help. There are some distinct flaws I think are critical to improving this game, of which, I'll put just a few below:1. Allow the player to respec their talent tree. There's a button for it but it doesn't work...2. Max level is 99, blueprint points are earned up to max level. Why does my character quit learning talents at lvl 40? Have they reached the epitome of survival at lvl 40? Is my character no longer improving or learning better ways to survive after lvl 40?3. Be upfront with what the mission requirements are. Several online communities discussing Icarus are referring to it as a walking simulator. There is no good reason for me to run to an objective location JUST to find out what the objective requires for me to bring there and build. 4. The gameplay loop is too repetative, I'd suggest allowing players to accept additional missions (within the region) while they're planetside. This would encourage players to build and tech up their base. If someone knocks out a 7 day (real time) mission in 4 hours there should be a way to continue playing on that map so they can enjoy the work they've put into their base and their grind.5. Why is nighttime so freaking dark? Icarus is a MOON of another planet, there is plenty of reflected light from the planet to illuminate the surface. I grew up in the absolute middle of nowhere. It's never 100% pitch dark at night. Caves should be pitch black (and they are), I agree with that. Night should be dark, it shouldn't render your character absolutely blind.Things I like about Icarus:1. It's beautiful - A lot of gamers had graphical issues, frame stuttering, compatibilitiy issues, and overheating problems, but I did not. I ran into items glitching through the floor and I occasionally somehow launched trees into outer space but these didn't impact the performance of my game. My PC is higher end with a 3080 ti as of this review so your mileage may vary on the performance.2. The sounds of the wild are great. The ambiance is awesome3. There are a lot of cool items in the crafting tree. If you spend the enormous amount of time to farm the materials then playing around with the tier 4 firearm is a lot of fun, the bow is gorgeous, and the armor is beefy (in some ways).I'll be watching Icarus from the sidelines and reading patch notes and updates. If things change I'd be more than happy to come back and play but as of right now, I only foresee myself logging in few and far between when I'm bored of other survival craft games. I have high hopes, but low expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Update, 11/2023:     For awhile nothing seemed to get done perf wise. Seems the devs did take notice to this, that people were having issues and have been addressing this with much seriousness. I have put in quite a few hours this week pushing this game to the test and although I have found it still has some issues, it is not only playable but it shows the devs are doing their best to resolve those issues. Not only are they monitoring perf issues, but they are also making changes to the game to keep it evolving in a direction that I and many others can agree feel like a positive direction. Whether you are a new or a returning player, you should def give Icarus a try. A lot has changed, been added, and the overall experience of being scared sh!tless in the woods on an alien planet, while something is stalking you only to find out it is a baby deer still very much feels genuine and fun. Just don't feed the bears, please.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------So decided to update my review. Avoid this game. First few hours seem ok-ish, until you start noticing frequent crashes, constant low fps, and overall lack of optimization. This is not just me but plenty of people. I have ran this game with a 2070 super, 3080, and a 4080 and the performance is always the same. Starts off at about 50-60 fps, then drains itself down to 30-45 fps the moment you start going by a single base that has been built. Never bounces back even if you leave the base area. After about 20-30 mins into gameplay you will start getting down to 20-30 fps and never recover. I want to like this game, it is a beautiful and fun game to play. But the painful and sh#t show performance that the devs are "aware" of never seems to get fixed sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: I am an avid "Open World Survival Craft" Connoisseur and Icarus has pretty much surpassed all of them (excluding minecraft I think). First off this game does have issues. There's glitches where you can get stuck on a tree, texture glitches with weather, frame drops, and the biggest issue imo is my arrows don't go where I shoot them (Only happens when playing on a dedicated server or in a friends server).  But I believe this game has tons of other amazing qualities that allows me to look past these bugs.Second, I want to talk about the gameplay. Session based missions where you lose everything you craft, built, and gathered once you're done with the mission. This feature was something I was very against at first, but as I got better at this genre of game, it became one of my favorite parts. I refer to this game as "Forest speedrunning". The Forest was one of my favorite games, but I got so good at it, that it became boring. I knew the best places to build, the location of all the caves, what items they had, and how to beat it quickly. The base building in the Forest was fun and I milked some entertainment out of it, but it soon got old. Icarus was fun because it seemed to be made for someone like me that could no longer enjoy a lot of the games in this open world survival craft genre anymore. Instead of grinding for gear, loot, bases, and materials once, you get to do it a bunch of times. And it is a grind. I remember it used to take me about 4 hours to gather the materials, build a base, and make an anvil in the game (early game crafting item). Now I'm making fabricators (late game item) in under 2 hours. The improvement in my efficiency and speed at getting my mission necessary stations and items up and going was fun to experience. The early game is tough, as is any open world survival craft game, but once you get the essentials down, you can start progressing fast. Every new tier of the tech tree had me pretty much relearning the basics all over again. It's such a deep game that reaching the final items of the tech tree isn't the real challenge, its all about getting good at getting to that point and the missions do a good job of walking you through that. I want to bring up a few gripes I have with other open world survival craft games. I do love all these games, I just think its important to bring up these issues to show how Icarus corrects them.The Forest 2 and Green Hell - These games pretty much told you exactly where to go, which isn't an issue normally, but I had no incentive to build a base. It was literally just going from one part of the map to the next until I reached the end. Crafting Stations, difficulty, and hiding objective locations can incentivize me to build a base. Icarus often tells you where you need to go, but the difficulty and the need for sheltered crafting stations and storage makes building atleast a small base essential on about 90% of the missions.The Forest and RAFT - Limited replayability. The best items are found in game except for maybe the gun and a few craftables that require a blueprint. Once I know where to look, I can get it instantly. You can replay the game a few times and it'll still be fun, but once you hit 5-6 it gets old. Icarus's complex tech tree, leveling, and game knowledge makes it take so long to master the game and its still fun to get better at the process, not to mention they've released an update EVERY SINGLE WEEK for almost 2 years. There's constantly new content and the devs seem to listen to public opinion on ideas and changes. Terraria - 2D lolMinecraft - The Graphics are a part of the charm, but sometimes I need a break from blocksThis Game has become one of my favorite all time games. If you make it through the steep learning curve at the beginnning, you will love this game. If you don't like the session based missions, don't worry, one of the next big updates is combining open world mode and the mission modes so (i assume) you won't lose your base and stuff each mission. The normal, session based missions will still be available I believe. I enjoy getting better at starting from scratch but I am excited to see how different it is going into some of these missions with gear and a base already made. I feel like this game doesn't get the love it deserves. It had a rocky start no doubt, but the devs have listened to the community and have been working hard to make a game of high quality. Just know that this is a next gen game, so up to date hardware is going to create a barrier for most players.There's a youtube series on the Icarus youtube channel with live action cutscenes made for the plot of the game. In it, there's a quote "You can't fear icarus, you need to respect it". This what a lot of players like myself went through at the beginning. I spent forever grinding the first few missions because I was not confident in my ability to proceed to the more difficult missions in the Arctic and Desert Biome. Eventually I did move on to those more difficult missions and thats where I got sucked in. Icarus is no joke, especially playing alone. I reccomend using  for mission briefing and planning before a harder mission. One of my favorite parts is planning our mission with friends. I hope you guys enjoy as much as I do!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Played during a free weekend.Icarus is a relatively polished and broad co-operative Open World Survival game and whilst it doesn't bring anything new of note to the genre it covers all the usual things you have come to expect and does so very well. The upgrade path is easy to grasp and progress along it it is well paced with a sufficient variety of resources.The build system is a little limited for the moment and does not yet include any curved pieces or even angled flooring but does support complex, functionally useful and visually appealing if somewhat restrictively boxy structures. Decorations are well thought out and allow a reasonable degree of freedom in placement. To put it simply I could never build exactly what I wanted but I was also never displeased with what I could build and most importantly I rarely felt like I was fighting against the build system. Hopefully we will see an upgrade to add snap points to half pieces and the addition of equilateral triangles at some point in the development cycle.Enemy variety is slightly better than the norm for these types of games, we will always want more but there is enough that you don't always feel like you are in the same fight at least. Some effort has been made to vary enemy tactics with the addition of predictable attack patterns for certain enemy types allowing you to sometimes learn and develop useful strategies but beyond that it is the standard 'passive enemies mindlessly run away and aggressive enemies mindlessly chase you down' fare that we are all familiar with. There is unfortunately no complex behaviour either scripted or adaptive to make things more interesting. I also did not witness any inter creature behavioural relationships beyond a few rare occasions of what may have been some creature running away from another. This is definitely a part of the game that is noticeably lacking; Even some very simple Predator, Competitor, Prey relationships would go a long way toward making the world seem far more alive.Character advancement is both broad and deep, all skills are broken down to serve all of the specific wants and needs you may have allowing you to build into whatever role you most enjoy playing. You can also respec your characters Talents for a small cost to adjust to specific scenarios. Unfortunately you cannot do the same with your Tech Tree, leaving you with many wasted points in Tech as you progress through the levels and there are not enough points available in the standard game to learn everything; This ultimately restricts your characters longterm viability as it is entirely possible through a few mis-assigned points to lock that character out of certain content permanently.Character adaptability to the environment is handled primarily through crafting. The game will throw many variations of hazards at you whilst opening up the ability to craft preventative and or curative items to deal with them. This system also extends into situational buffs such as increased melee damage or carrying ability etc in a way that allows you to boost your off abilities as necessary. This system is well fleshed out however I found that by the time I unlocked the recipes, crafting stations to make them and then gathered the necessary ingredients I had essentially moved beyond needing to use them. I feel this system would be better utilised if current consumables were moved down the tech tree and significantly more powerful ones added to the higher tech levels to make those buffs available when you actually need them and warrant continued use as you progress.The game does include a taming system and the ability to use tamed creatures as mounts or even pack animals. This is a nice touch but, given the aggression of most of the creatures towards your mount when you are not around, is a feature you will likely ignore more and more as you progress. The extra speed/carry boost just isn't worth the hassle of constantly baby sitting your pet that will be targeted and killed by random creatures spawning on top of it the moment you are out of hearing range of it. There are Talents you can take to somewhat reduce the chance of aggressive creatures attacking your mount but not to any useful degree. Inter creature behavioural relationships would again be beneficial here as would expanding pet commands beyond follow, stay, or fight; The addition of a flee and some sort of return whistle or even just a flee to me when in danger command would help a lot.Questing exists in the game, though in a very limited form; This appears to be expanded in the DLC but I have not had a chance to try that yet. Mostly in the base game it is of the go here and either kill x amount of y creature or defend this area for x minutes/waves. It gives you something to do when you are feeling kind of aimless which is always appreciated but it fails to give any reason to do it beyond a rather disappointing drop of reward items you probably have no use for. This is a failing most games in the genre suffer from and this game differs only in how very easy it would be to correct. The framework is all there to provide a reason for the players actions in their sojourns from an orbital station onto this terra-formed world to identify and test the environment and it's resources. It would be a simple matter to present this story to the player, include key milestones to work toward that advance the story and even add an ultimate conclusion that serves as both meaning to play and satisfactory resolution of play. It doesn't need a hoard of dramatic characters and deep themes with surprise twists, a story treatment would be enough; But it does need something to make this feel like more than a just a game framework or very large tech demo.Multiplayer worked perfectly for me, it was easy for my friend to join and we had no random disconnects. Actions in game synced cleanly and having a co-op partner greatly added to the experience. Everything else the game has to offer such as Graphics, Movement, Sound etc are all of high quality and for me the game ran smoothly and without any major issues.All in all if I was judging this game against all of the very many others in the genre I would give it a thumbs up, I certainly enjoyed my experience, were it not for the issue of price.There is no polite way to put this so I will be blunt, the price tag of this game is delusional. This is a 25-30 USD early access indie game that they are trying to charge $120 USD for with every indication that they will continue to charge even more for each and every future update; The justification for this seems to be to pretend that the game is no longer in early access and that the ongoing patches to the game are expansions and not the very necessary feature updates they clearly are. I can only imagine this is a result of an inexperienced Chief Financial Officer who simply does not understand how to price a product in the PC Gaming market.Whilst I certainly understand the need to ensure everyone gets paid and the desire to make a profit off of your product what the CFO seems to fail to understand is the higher you price your product the more you narrow your potential market. This game is actually priced all but entirely out of the PC gaming market, you could purchase two brand new AAA games for the same price they are trying to charge for this feature incomplete early access indie game. Even if by some bizarre series of events this game managed to capture the attention and wallets of all the 'whales' in PC gaming that fraction of a percentage of the market would be insufficient to cover the cost of development. By closing their product off to the average consumer this game is all but guaranteed to fail financially.At $30 for the complete game this would be a clear winner for my co-op group and you would have had six more sales, at $120 it is a complete joke and you have nothing; Even RocketWerkz's CFO should be able to understand that math.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Icarus excited to experience a unique game-loop for the survival genre. The idea of being able to drop into a prospect, collect materials that you can spend when you complete the prospect and go back in more prepared for the next prospect is an awesome one. Unfortunately, Icarus falls short with this fantasy. The prospects seem to fall into one of two categories... 1: Run around for hours to reach some random object and interact with it, then return to your dropship and leave. 2: Collect a ridiculous amount of gold and copper in order to make the two items you need to complete the mission, run for a while to the place you gotta complete the mission, then run all the way back to the dropship. The idea of having a limited time to complete a prospect is interesting, but in practice it just ends up adding an extra step to every single mission that adds to the ever-present feeling of grinding. What's more is that the grind doesn't lead to much reward. The meta-game collection of rewards definitely help make the game a *little* less repetitive, but you can't upgrade your drop ship to allow for stations to be brought up or down from the planet - upgrades are solely items that affect the player themselves. So there is no way to skip the early game grind of setting up a boring, basic building and the same crafting stations over and over and over again.I was never very excited for the storm system, because I'm not huge on being interrupted in games like this when I have an objective in mind that I am actively working toward. I understand the concept and the potential for this system to shake things up, but it feels tacked on. Half the storms do nothing but seem to make your character run slower, and the other half will completely derail whatever you're doing or even destroy your entire base while you're miles from home trying to collect gold or copper ore. The storms are boring at their best, and more commonly frustrating.I was also wary of the limited time for prospects, because of the limited time and storm systems, other aspects like building and planting are almost entirely pointless endeavors unless you decide to disengage with character progression and play prospects that grant no rewards.  Are you doing a prospect that will take a while? Build a 3x3 stone structure and never think about storms again. Are you doing a shorter mission? Build nothing, or like a 1x2 wood structure. Either way, you'll likely spend very little time being creative in this game because nothing persists from prospect to prospect.The balance of many of these prospects are a mess. There are missions that will leave you spending tens of hours running around desperately trying to find a few more gold ore nodes so you can afford to craft the one item that is required in that prospect. The rewards for these missions are absolutely not worth the time spent, and the challenges within these missions are repetitive and bring very little joy moment-to-moment.Finally, the game is not finished. There are game-breaking bugs - bugs that will cost you to lose items that took you dozens of hours to collect and build up. At the time of writing, I would be further along if I stopped playing 30 hours ago than I am now. I lost 90% of the items I had earned in a bug that occurred three times. If you forget to put some MacGuffin item in their dropship before going to orbit, guess what? You are now unable to complete that prospect and will have to start over despite the item you needed to return orbit being in your pocket! There are so many visual bugs, back-end server issues that are constantly being updated, and balancing of enemies needs a lot of work. The game feels very much like an early-access experience with little chance of that changing in the short-term.The things that make this game stand apart from it's competitors either suck the fun out of the game, or just suck. Pass on this game for now, maybe in the future it'll be playable and the core game-loop will feel rewarding and enjoyable - but it'll be a while. tldr; game is repetitive, frustrating, broken, and feels very far from finished at the time of writing. Pass on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review 2.25.22! My original review was not to recommend this game based on numerous issues with both the functionality of the game and the QoL of the player, as well as what felt like missing content. There are also much needed changes to really make this game a more well-rounded, immersive experience, but that being said, here are my original recommendations and what has been changed so far, and why I changed my review to recommend this game!Original Recommended fixes and what's been done: 1) I don't think the farming/grinding needs to decrease, as that's part of the fun (if there's a reason for it). The time spent actually completing an objective once you're done with farming and grinding should increase to make all of it actually worth it. - This has been a constant review and update process for the developers, and so far it's been going in the right direction, although not resolved yet. With their commitment that they're still reviewing this aspect, paired with what they've updated so far, I'm comfortable waiting to see how this pans out!2)Work on bugs instead of releasing more repetitive prospects. - This started happening! So many bug fixes so far! Yes, there are still quite a few, but they don't feel so immersion-breaking or game crashing.3)Implement the quality of life changes that were recommended in the beta weekends that don't impact the gameplay or difficulty. - HUGE improvements in this area in the Week 11 and Week 12 content. This has really made the game all around MUCH more enjoyable, including some of the previous aspects that were considered to be very tedious.4) Make the tech tree items more relevant, and reduce the cost of higher tier items. - The developers have committed to improving this as well, so also looking forward to these updates! The minor changes to the cost of higher tier items helped, but they're still not viable or feasible for like 90%+ of the missions. 5) Add talent points to use in the solo branch, independent of the regular branch. - This was done in the week 12 update!6) Give the animals more AI. Add more flora and fauna diversity. - Still waiting on this as well. There were some minor improvements made here where animals will now react to sounds differently and don't get stuck on a rock or tree, and they no longer hear or see through stone walls of your shelter (unless they're right next to you outside), but I consider this as still in progress...7) Add more lore! - Still waiting patiently for this!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say it's 50/50 for me right now, but slightly leaning towards the No.On one hand, it's interesting, and there is a decent enough freedom to do certain things. On the other hand, this is Early Access/open beta, not a finished game. It essentially feels like a continuation of the beta weekends, but with some more plants, mobs, the whole map to visit, 4th tier unlocked, and the station features available. Apart from that, the basic feel and issues are pretty much the same.I think my primary pro's and cons can be summed up as follows:+ A fair bit of freedom in how you approach stuff, and how you build your hide-outs+ A rather varied skill tree, with options in how you play, though I main the resource gathering due to the 'restart restart restart'-nature of the game- The melee 'experience' is flat-out garbage. Flat ground dodging is a trick of the mind and you might as well just face-tank and hope you kill whatever it is before you get turned inside out... Or you simply exploit the terrain and hope the AI don't just run up anyway. If an enemy gets to start the attack animation and you're in range, you get hit.- I already grew slightly weary of the restart-nature during the beta weekends, and it hasn't improved for me. Whilst interesting in a way, I just don't really like how you have to restart your entire tech build-up every single new run, outside of Outpost mode, as if the planet nuked itself, and reset the environment in its entirety.A friend bought the game for me to get me to play it, and frankly? If he hadn't, I wouldn't be playing it.Near 100h playtime update:Most of it was spent gathering resources, levelling up, building outposts, and then finding out the mission was pathetic and I could've just bloody sped through it within an hour or so, even with my non-speedrun build.That pretty much sums up my experience so far. Not sure about the later missions, but the early ones? It's essentially flat-out pointless to waste time on a nice hideout, and you're better off getting some basic gear, and then just run off to do whatever menial task they came up with... at times on practically the other side of the map. Because of course it's way too much effort to land closer to the objective, or, heavens forbid, letting the player know what they have to do half-way across the map beforehand, and instead have them trundle over there to get an update that should've been in the briefing.Looks-wise, Icarus is pretty decent. Still some issues here and there, but it's fine.Story-wise, it's... not brilliant. The basic premise is that terraforming went bo-bo, air's poisonous (not devoid of oxygen, like some reviews seem to think; the planet-side life adapted to it), and stuff's all fubar. However, shiny stuff was found, so now the big megacorps are paying for scrubs to go down there and do stuff. So off you go, wearing your fancy suit that will allow you to survive planet-side, and do things like not dying from poisonous air, breathing underwater, and getting pneumonia from dampness inside caves... wait what? Gameplay-wise, the main issue I still have with the game, apart from bears with mountain climbing gear and the garbage melee combat, is the extraction mechanic.Because of course it makes sense for you to toss out any and all non-exotic gear, and do it all over again the next time around... not.I frankly really think they should rework that aspect. I'm fine with not being able to  bring back entire workbenches, a full house, and maybe a warehouse or two in ingots, as that would be rather silly.However, I genuinely do not see a reason we can't bring a small selection of normal tools and gear back with us, to bring to a next mission.We can stuff a mammoth's tusk in that pod, or stacks of exotic ores, and exotic equipment is fine, yet for 'reasons', not even a small titanium knife can go back.I might try the outpost a bit more, but frankly? I'm rather tired of the normal missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Ohhh do I wish I could recommend this game. I will be keeping an eye on this one, and will buy it again in a heartbeat if only the map timer mechanic would let me play.Gameplay is amazing, and I feel that Icarus has mastered much of what makes survival games great. Your character will be perma-killed if by lingering past the time limit...but it's a real-world timer. Tending to outside priorities directly penalizes you in-game, a strategy from addiction-inducing phone games. Every session makes you bet your precious little session time against all your game progression.Most-demanded features RocketWerkz will not add:* Persistent maps, permanent bases, or indefinite prospects on dangerous worlds.* Water bladders that don't drain faster than you dehydrate* A map timer that only ticks while someone is in a game session.* Attaching ladders to trapdoors (claimed it's too hard to do)Here are the features that have been marked as "under consideration" and neglected since the user-suggested features opened (5 months ago as of posting this)* Making buildings in stone tougher than wood* Fixing animals seeing you inside structures (they claim they "hear" you, but that's dubious)* Water bladder drains faster than you dehydrate* Not taking damage from storms while sealed in the returning pod* Talent and tech tree accessibility. Maxed-out characters only get about 20% access, and planets mostly don't have resources or need to climb the tree anyway.I'd like to think that Rocketwerkz isn't choosing to neglect their player base, but ignoring simple tunes and bugs casts doubt. These design choices alienate players that don't have the specified time window to play, even if that means they want to play longer. High stakes games are fun, being punished for outside responsibilities is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult review to write.  After 60ish hours, my overall impression is simply one of wasted potential.  Visually the game is stunning, and the survival elements are diverting.  I enjoyed hunting, building, managing oxygen. I wanted to enjoy exploring (including learning new biomes), and I thought the concept for the setting oozed potential.    However, as others have pointed out, this game is astonishingly empty.  All the systems work, but It's early early early access from a content perspective.  There's an unlock treadmill, where as you gain levels you unlock recipes which give you new survival tools and materials.  Unfortunately, all the tools feel the same - upgrading a stone knife thru bone, iron, steel, etc doesn't change the way it functions, and doesn't feel more fun to use (in any way).  Contrast that with a game like The Forest, where each new discovered tool has different animations, opens up new gameplay, can be customized, etc.  Talents are much the same - at first they seem like deep and interesting trees, but then you realize that, while they do affect gameplay, they do so in very subtle ways and a character who has invested in say 'survival' has access to the same gameplay loops, and feels  as one who's invested in 'combat', 'mining' etc.  I mentioned above that the game is beautiful, and it is.  Sadly, it's also lifeless.  There are half a dozen animal species per biome that spawn, you'll see them over and over and over.  They have very limited behaviors, they will run from you/run at you (predators will walk/run directly at you, always), they'll rest, they'll drink, they'll graze or they'll wander aimlessly.  There are no non-interactive animals - no birds, bugs, bees, flies, nothing that makes the world feel alive.  I contrast this with games like Subnautica, where marine life does it thing all around you as you explore, survive, build.  You don't immediately notice this absence, because you're probably very focused on gathering to build a shelter, but when you're on your second or third mission walking kilometers between objectives, you start to notice just how lonesome Icarus is.  You never feel like you're planning an expedition across unknown territory to get something new, necessary, rare.  As another point of comparison there, Valheim has way more resource diversity and exploration payoff than Icarus does, and Valheim has a procedural map!   Last thing I'll express as a disappointment is the storyline (or lack thereof).  So much potential!  The premise of the orbital station and the poor grunts wildcatting on the hostile surface is brilliant.  There are hints of interesting factions and concepts throughout the mission briefings.  But the missions themselves use [b}none[/b] of this material.  You never come across a failed prospector base, you never interact in a meaningful way with unique creatures (couple of bosses that you kill), and there's no mystery in the setting whatsoever.  Aliens?  Haven't seen any 60 hours in, other than cave worms and mission specific poison plants.  The map is persistent, which seems like it should be cool (learnings from one mission can be useful in the future), but within each biome (forest, desert, snow), everything is exactly.the.same.everywhere.  There's just so little variation from place to place, that there's very little payoff in travelling.  This review probably sounds angry or hyperbolic - sorry about that, I'm trying to express the prevailing emotions of playing the game, with some detail.  I wanted to love this game, and I applaud the devs for taking a risk with the concept.   It mines gameplay concepts and settings that I typically greatly enjoy.  Right now though, my take is that it's a time-waster, there's not enough payoff to the experiences.  I'm not sure if it will improve over time either - there's a great survival platform in place, but for this to become something I would enjoy playing, they need to build a game and a story on top of it, and it doesn't seem to me like they will have the customer attention time to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus is a fun game with a very large blueprint and talent tree which keeps you striving to work and improve.  The progression through these trees is good and the work required to unlock tech and talents is reasonable and fun.  I enjoy the missions but you have to build a base and crafting bench, etc. for each mission and this is fun for quite a while but it started to wear on me.  I would make a unique base for each mission to make it fun.The dialog and voice actor is not good at all, I turned the narration volume off and started ignoring the captions, they are useless and disturbing.  I'm really tired of sophisticated space outfits being run by cringe goofballs that want to make a joke out of everything.  The dialog and narration should be professional, sophisticated, and high-quality.The instability issues are real, I dealt with them but I was able to fix them with hardware changes.  The minimum-required graphics card is Nvidia GTX 1060 6GB.  I attempted to play the game with a GTX 1060 3GB and can confirm it is unplayable with this card.  I upgraded to an RTX 4070 and I was getting a complete black-screen, power-off PC crash while playing.  I upgraded my power supply from 860 watt to 1,000 watt and I haven't had that problem again.The base building and hunting is very fun, the weapons work great.  You can make massive, high-tech bases.  There is no exploration, there is nothing to find.  The world is still fun to traverse, there are mounts you can tame for faster travel.  There are multiple biomes to see with different creatures, both passive and dangerous.Icarus is a great game, I highly recommend it.  There is an update every week, they are currently on week 149.  This is very impressive, I imagine that is a lot of hard work.  Thank you for reading, feel free to ask questions.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure how I would feel about session-based survival, but the majority of timers I've seen through my progression thus far seem very forgiving for what's asked of you. You have a lot of time to explore, and most importantly, establish a presence so that you can prepare for the task ahead.Pros:- Very strong graphics, and other than the occasional blip when I run through a dense forest during extreme weather, it runs very smooth on a 3080- Amazing weather effects that can actually impact the environment and your settlement- Great sound design, the clinks and clangs of tools feel and sound great, and the atmospheric sounds are pleasant during the day, and terrifying at night- Co-op for up to 8 people; I play games with a group of roughly 10 friends and acquaintances, so finding games most of us can play together is pretty difficult- Deep tech and character progression with a lot of options, especially when factoring in multiplayer and specializing alongside friends- Satisfying destruction of resources as you gather from them- You keep all of your character progression between "prospects" (missions)Cons:- The introduction to the game is pretty rough as of this writing, it does a very poor job of setting the player up for the scanning mission- There's no "take all" hotkey that I can find, which is surprising given how common the hotkey is in games revolving around a lot of loot/resource collection and management- Inventory is restricted by both slots and weight, so unless you've played games like DayZ, it's going to be a bit of a headache to get used to early onThat's it, not a lot of cons for me at the time of writing. I will come back and update the review once I've had more time in the game. Here's my longer-winded overview on it:The truly interesting element of this game is that its progression revolves around session-based "prospects" where you complete various missions for a reward. The catch is that you're on a timer (though the timer seems rather forgiving).If you successfully complete missions, you get rewarded with special currency to progress through various equipment options to make the initial start of each prospect a little easier.You also level up while on missions and can unlock equipment, workstations, tools, weapons, etc. as well as talents that make you more effective at performing certain actions (or make you more resistant to the environmental effects of the planet).It's been a lot of fun so far, as a survival fan. Word of warning, if you don't like unfinished products then just add it to your Wishlist for now.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much wrong with this game, from simply bugs:- where you don't see a certain UI element unless you tear down and build the item again- where enemies will just jump through walls / trees- where the default language english might hold true for the speech output, but not the menus, and you have to switch to some other language and then back to english to make it workto the point where the AI must be really weird:- young animals have no instinct whatsoever, neither to attach or to run away. it must be something like a right of passing where they receive that trait- predators will only hunt players, they will eat corpses of dead animals, but they will not kill or attack them themselves- prey animals will not be frightened by predators, just by the playerand then game mechanics:- I only did four cheap missions and am level 27 already as it took such a long time to grind all the stuff.- the difficulty is absolutely unpredictable, i now thought, I'd do a short one skull mission before bed time with a 6h timer .. everything went smooth and then the last step spawned 2 bears, 8 boars and about 20 wolves .. i had multiple weapons with me, but they all eventually broke during the fight. not to mention the stamina running out. I have no idea what kind of a joke this is supposed to be, but it's disrespectful of the players time.Prepared for another go at it, then found out on reddit that this STARTING mission has been bugged for 2 years and doesn't spawn a replacement item that you need. All the while the ingame voice yells at you for getting back to the non existing device. Perfect for the blood pressure.This would also be my fundamental evaluation of the game: disrespectful of the player(s time).

_childDocuments_.review: This title carries hallmarks of a live service. It's being constantly worked on, and it's in solid state 2 years past it's release. unfortunately Tier 4 of technology tree is very disappointing and seems like Early Access. Yet I had sold hours of fun till that point. Live action short movies are very nice, for some reason you can only find them on youtube with YT links in the game.It's primary game play loop is a original idea of survival extraction game, where you drop down on the planet with mission and a goal, you need to survive and build only as much as it requires to complete the mission, rinse and repeat.There's quite a enough different missions and environments to visit.The second option is a traditional open world survival, there's three, progressively harder to survive on maps, but even on the starting map you can pick quite hostile environments.  it can be a mixed bag but overall it's good, it's focused on coop building and surviving unfortunately it's not well polished experience. There'll be technologies that don't' work right or weren't planned out well before being put into the game. There's not much happening at all in terms of narrative, but that hardly a selling point for any survival game. Developers definitely go the route of drop feature into the game hastily than perhaps fix it later or not at all.My biggest peeve with that approach is light source upgrades, you can upgrade from a torch all the way to the infinite batter flashlight but the latter one doesn't work at all and previous to that Biofuel Lantern wobbles so much it's annoying. That takes the cake RocketWerkz is the only developer that can't make working flashlight.I've had very hard time deciding if this should be positive or negative review it's rightfully mixed on steam.Well I can't get rid of bitter taste some of the issues left in my mouth, I sincerely hope I can update this to positive down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so, Icarus, this game is NOT solo friendly because there's a penalty if you die. You'll lose all your xp bar you've been working hard on because some bear just spawn close to you and try get you, EVEN THOUGH the bear doesn't see you (you're behind a wall, rock, tree, etc). I'm guessing that's the anomaly of the planet, the animals have developed some kind of wallhack thingy. I haven't finish the game yet, almost half way through the mission, and if this solo penalty stuff becoming more common because the mission become harder or some predator spawn close to you (it's like the game want me to keep dying over and over again and not enjoying the game), i won't finish this game. Ok probably i will, but not for some xp grinding to get more skill point so that i become stronger, but instead just to finish each mission (which is of course, repetitive, at least for now) to get some ingame currency so i can buy a permanent gear because all your stuff you've build on the mission will be gone. Yes, all your weapons, your armor, your workbench, your base will be gone after you complete the mission. Luckily i know about this so i'm not wasting my time getting some resources to craft a shotgun or a cool futuristic armor. BUT i'm pretty sure i'll need to make this next tier stuff on the more endgame mission. So, i guess that's kinda forgiveable.IN CONCLUSION, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME IF YOU:1.A solo player, unless you have a good amount of patient.2.Don't like a mission based survival game, perhaps you only like a survival game where you search the mission objective by yourself, example The Forest.3.Think that this game is like any other survival game where you can build anything and upgrade your stuff to next tier without fear of losing it permanently.BUY THIS GAME IF YOU:1.Have a friend to play with.2.Like a mission based survival game.3.Don't mind losing all your stuff permanently.I'll edit this review if i can finish this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! At first.. but as its progressively evolved, its become more difficult for my rig to run it. If you've got a beefy set up and you love survivalist games with creature battles and secret missions, it's a winner. I suppose the price tag is heavy, but it is a fairly detailed game. A lot of work has gone into it and continues to. I bought it back in Early Access, then got the first expansion. Then co-op, now that's where the fun begins. It's just so much more enjoyable with friends/family. But, like I mentioned; Beefy rig its a must, playing on low end setting just sucks, play can be janky and laggy, just not fun at all. The world design is beautiful, you just miss out on too much details if you have to play on lowered settings.Hunting, building, animals trying to kill you, weird creatures trying to eat/or kill you, resource hunting, upgrading tools, weapons, buildings etc. There's a lot to do. I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game in beta and then tried again at launch. The game is simply not ready. I do think it's a cool concept. I thought it would be another Valheim honestly. _childDocuments_.review: Do not buy Icarus in its current condition. Save yourself the money and buy a better survival game.Currently Icarus is a solid foundation for a good survival game. It should be in early access, because that's what the game feels like. Overall, playing the game just feels frustrating. For a hard survival game riddled with bugs that often get you killed, the death penalty is too high - especially playing solo. Missions are not clear on how to complete them and are buggy (my second mission bugged and wasted 3 hours). UI is clunky and is missing a lot of polish. Animals like bears and worms often spawn right on top of you randomly during missions too which just puts the icing on the cake. Also the wiring system is awful; it is one of the worst mechanics I have used in any video game. The talent and tech trees both do not have a respec option which really limits how you progress ESPECIALLY if you're solo. The talent tree is also very unexciting, the perks you get are only small % boosts to stats you already have.One of the biggest Icarus has right now I'd say is the lack of assets/content that fits the game. Icarus is a planet that is no where close to earth yet the wildlife consists of wolves, deer, bears, zebra, elephants, and cougars?? The assets in the game right now feel so out of place. For what is supposed to be a survival game on an alien planet, Icarus has a distinct lack of alien life to the point where you forget you aren't on Earth while playing the game. After playing Icarus for several hours, all the plants I saw were indigenous to Earth.So far Icarus has had a disappointing launch, and I will be telling my friends to stay clear of this game. However, I see that the developers have been responding to a lot of reviews. If the devs put a LOT more work into Icarus it will be a solid game. However, I think that a big portion of the game needs a LARGE overhaul - small updates, patches, and hotfixes will NOT fix this game!
_childDocuments_.name: ICARUS

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy survival crafters, this game is top notch. The game can be played in 'missions', in which you drop in and rocket out when done. It can also be played via a longer sandbox style, where you can explore; build up your base; unlock new tech, etc. I have a rather high end machine, so my experience may not be representative but I have zero hitching and have seen few bugs.     Survival crafting has been my go to genre lately. My main gauge of game is replayability. In this case, I have returned to Icarus time and time again. I play exhaustively until I burn out. The fact I keep coming back speaks volumes of the fun of the game or maybe just the sad condition of my existence. I'll stay on topic though.     I have purchased all of the DLC and the expansion. None of it disappointed. The developer appears to be very transparent and the community is great (Discord, forums). I have not spent any time with the multi-player as I lean toward solo play, so I cannot speak to that. If you enjoy survival craft games with excellent dev support, Icarus is well worth the time and investment.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great survival game to play with friends.  It will bring a lot of laughter, some scary screams, and a LOT of cussing.Two gripes we all have though is that some of the missions will mis-represent themselves.  Example:  We chose a hunting mission on the Styx map, thinking that since that was the title that was what we would be doing.  Instead while we did have to kill 15 types of animals indifferent regions, most of the mission focused on building.  Normally we don't have an issue with building in the game (we enjoy it) but at that time we REALLY just wanted to hunt, so it was frustrating.  The second gripe is the mount bug.  When you mount up, if you are in a group, you have a chance where your camera angle will change, and you will be looking WAY off to the side.  It makes riding the mount...interesting.  The best way to clear the bug is to dismount, and remove the saddle, then put the saddle back on.  A true pain if you are trying to outrun predators, or have a saddle and inventory full of stuff and have to take it off.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. There's survival elements that will really require you to keep on your toes. Having to do missions to play the game keeps the experience fun and fresh. Having an overarching progression system you can work on while working on the progression systems inside the missions makes for both short and long term gratification. Having killcams and amazing diversity in building options makes you feel like a boss. But these things don't make the game great, they make it a fun game.What makes the game great is the level of investment from the developers. I've read from other reviews that the devs were good and I was skeptical. But daily updates, being active on discord, changing the missions every week, apologizing for inconveniences, and despite knowing the backlash still bringing the game down to fix gamebreaking bugs so more people can play? Godsent. Yes it has performance issues, yes I'm very sorry your 5 digits costing monster of a pc can't run the game on full, yes there's still parts of the endgame barred behind "more to come" after a full release. But with the way the devs have been communicating, give it time. And if you don't, your loss.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: you land on an alien planet where humans tried to terraform the plant to try to inhabit it, but something went wrong and the project was abandoned. However, they discovered "exotics", a precious mineral which can make you rich if you manage to find it, extract it, and bring it back up to the space station. But exploring Icarus is no joke. You drop in on a timed mission, gather materials, build basic tools, gather more materials to build a house, crafting benches, craft better tools, better weapons, then go do what the mission says and upon completing the mission you return in your drop pod to the space station where you will be rewarded based on the difficulty of the mission. To complete each mission you will need to; Hunt, cook, fish, mine ore, chop trees, build, and above all, SURVIVE! When you return to the space station you cannot take anything that you crafted on the planet with you. As you earn more gold and reputation, u will be able to craft tools, weapons, armour, and more in the Space Station Workshop. Bringing these items on a drop with you will make things a lot easier, and you get to take them back up with you when to leave the mission. I played 142 hours in Beta and 105 hours post launch and i can say with confidence that this game is AMAZING! Game was release on Dec 3, now it's just 4 weeks later and they already have 14 updates/hotfixes. with each update having a long list of bug fixes, improvements, additional missions added, more items added to the Space Station Workshop. This is a real survival game with a learning curve. If you don't take Icarus seriously, u will die many times. As Sol the narrator said (i added a few of my own)- If u run out of Oxygen, u die- If u run out of food, u die- If u run out of water, u die- If u get caught out in a storm without shelter, u die- If you don't mind your surroundings and run into a bear, u die- If you are running away from something and aren't careful of where u going, you could accidentally run off a cliff and die- You could spend hours building a nice wooden house for yourself and party, but forget to put on a lightning rod, or u think "ah what are the chances my house will get struck by lightning?" and just like that, a storm comes in, hits your house and the entire thing goes up in flames. Say bye bye to your house coz there is no way you are putting out that fire fast enough.- If you are too focused on what you are doing and don't pay attention to the mission timer, the drop pod could leave without you, and you will LOSE YOUR CHARACTER FOREVER.(and yes, i died due to all of those reasons above. Luckily i never lost my character as i always made sure to extract before timer runs out) I also accidentally burned by friend's house down by not being careful with my torch inside the house.The game is really fun (if your computer has the minimum requirements to run it). The game looks even better if u play on Ultra settings, and i haven't even tried the Ray Tracing that is available. Extremely fun playing with a group of friends, but can be solo-able as well (it just takes  longer and u need to be more careful not to die coz there won't be anyone to revive you). _childDocuments_.review: I think this game rocks, because it fits my gaming style in many ways. It won't work for lots of other gamers and that's fair. This is quite a niche game, and hopefully people can read reviews like mine and move on if it's not a fit for them.I am a true lover of the sandbox survival base-building genre and I am happy to support any game that moves that genre forward, however imperfectly. I can chop trees and pick rocks for hours if it means I can build an awesome base and craft my way up to OPness, even if it would be way more practical to get by with less. I don't get bored easily and I mainly want a beautiful simulated world that's mine in which I can make my mark. I understand creating a massive open world in which the player has this much agency is a big challenge for game development and it's hard to have the funding to take the time necessary to not release it with growing pains. Yes, the full release is closer to an early access in its quality, but these guys did it differently. They gave us eight sessions of beta game play for preorders in which you could return the game at any time even if you had played hundreds of hours. I prefer this model to early access in which you only get two hours to refund and have to trust a promise. Those of us who did the beta know what we are getting into. While it's still a diamond in the rough, the dev team have been extremely responsive and done a ton of work along the way.My two favorite things about the approach this game is taking are the very reasons many players might hate it:First, it is effing hard. You have to shelter from violent storms, but the weather will tear your thatch or wood shack to pieces if you can't run around with your repair hammer fast enough as pieces are torn from your building parts. It has the most beautiful fire mechanic I've seen and lightning storms take every opportunity to burn down everything you've achieved. Early game, the predators will wreck you and the spawn mechanics don't play fair. When you die, and you will die, you face a massive xp debt and any diseases and wounds, of which there are many types, will persist after death. If you are the type to rage quit, don't play this. I  personally laugh at each disaster and love the challenge to overcome then. When I eventually prevail it gives it so much more meaning. So know who you are, be warned, and choose wisely.Second, in the main game, you don't get to keep anything. It is "session based", meaning each time you drop down to the world you may have days or a month, but your gear, your base, and everything you've gathered will be wiped. It's basically a survival rogue-lite. You keep your levels and the rewards can provide some small upgrades for next time. For a hardcore survival gamer like me, early game is the best part and I relish being forced to do it over and over again. You may say what's the point and that probably means this isn't for you. But I always found a server gets a bit stale once I've finished my awesome base, besides the fact that they always get laggy after that, so wipes are inevitable eventually. This tears that bandaid off, and I'm ok with that since it's really the act of building and crafting that I love the most. It reminds me of the Dada art movement in which the destruction of the art was as much a part of the art as the artwork itself. (Btw, there are some small maps in which you can keep your builds forever)I have a beast of a PC (3090, 5900x, 32GB). I can run this on epic with rtx global illumination at about 90fps and it looks gorgeous. Feedback from my friends who have played this makes it pretty clear that unless you have a 20 series card or above, performance won't be great. I think their recommended specs are pretty honest about this. That said there are some basic things people can do to help with their fps that the devs would do well to communicate better. For example turning your fov up to 100 from the default 80 can give you as much as 20fps more. Also there's a slider in the settings to turn up the vram usage to what your card can handle, which really helps with performance. I've heard people with 3080s complaining they couldn't get good performance, so better access to info like this could really help.I know this is long, but one last bit that this game struggles with is communication of the lore. It has a very involved backstory which explains why it makes perfect sense that you are running around in a space suit in a forest. They've done some really good live acted docudramas on their youtube channel that explain it. However most people aren't aware of it and just think it doesn't make sense. It would behoove RocketWerkz to convey this better. The other part of the lore and the future promise of this game is that the forest is just the beginning. It was part of a failed terraforming to make the planet earthlike, but not all of it is like that. Each season of this game promises to get more formidably alien, moving well beyond the initial stone tools in the forest into futuristic gear in hostile otherworldy environments. There are so many crazy places they can take it and I'm down for the ride.
