_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a lot of time in this game, and there are a lot of things I like about it, and a number of things I don't that inevitably wear we down to the point that I stop playing. Every so often I get back into it after they've done a few updates and added in some new stuff, but none of it is game-changing enough to keep me playing.What is done well:Crafting - there is SO much stuff to make in this game. They have done a great job with the crafting system, especially with the improvements they have made over time (such as recently adjusting the tier system to allow the higher-end benches to craft the items of the lower ones, so you no longer need to have every type of bench). The progression and depth of crafting is logical for the most part, and I appreciate a game where I have to take raw materials, refine them, and combine then to make bigger and cooler things. The methods of collecting these materials is a big part of the game, and I enjoy all of it: chopping down trees, finding caves to mine, growing crops, hunting.Weekly Updates - it is refreshing to see a development team as dedicated as these guys, and to stick to releasing something new nearly every week since launch is no small feat.The World - while the graphics aren't going to blow many people away, the world is nevertheless impressive. It's large, the biomes are well done, and overall it's immersive.The Addition of Open World - the original setup, while interesting, got old FAST: select a mission, drop into the world, and have to tediously build some basic things in order to complete the mission (or not-so-basic things in some missions, which was a useless time sink). Adding an Open World option where you could settle in, build a base, and then proceed on missions in a persistent world is the way it should have been from day one. I get they wanted to try something different, and even built up a narrative reason for it, but it was meh.What eventually gets me tired of the game - The Missions - with few exceptions, they are repetitive and boring. Far too much walking/running around to get to objectives for no reason other than to drag them out because there is a lack of content. I don't want to run 15-20 minutes across a map with nothing really going on between point A and B aside from maybe some random animal encounters that would be there anyway. After a while, you will either a) bring down Workshop items and have an easy-mode time of the mission, or b) you'll build the bare minimum necessary just to finish the mission so you can get your payment and move on.The Combat & AI - It isn't awful, but it's not good. It all feels too simplistic, boring, and annoying. Creatures are the only thing you encounter, there are no other people on the surface. They are either passive and run from you if you don't one-shot them, or they are aggressive and either die in a single hit, or they have massive health pools and you end up cheesing your way through combat. They all do the same thing: rush you head on, unrelenting (aside from the ones that spit stuff at you). The AI in this game is just not as good as I wish it would be to truly give a challenge that isn't just a healthpool vs. my weapon damage. I ended up spending most of my 800 hours avoiding combat unless I needed a specific resource because it was just annoying.Weekly Updates - far too much effort has been spent on cosmetic items, like rugs and trophies and furniture that serves no purpose aside from aesthetics. While there have been some significant improvements to certain systems within the game (such as the recent changes and expansions of how electricity systems function in the game), a whole lot of the updates have been style over substance. Many of the core issues that make me bored are the same as at release.The DLC -First of all: too many different dlc packs, and I have purchased none of the add-ons. I did buy the founders/supporters version of the original release, which includes the new alien biomes and corresponding mission sets. I have not and will not purchase the cosmetic bundles or the extra outpost maps, because I strongly disagree with any company selling nonsense like that for money. I don't care how good a game might be, those sort of purchases don't interest me in the slightest, and these ones are not priced fairly in my opinion. This is not a game that is worth $150+ to procure all content. Regarding the major DLC with new content, that is how the original release of the game should have been - I can understand having a small 'terraformed zone' that is Earth-like, but to have virtually zero "whole other alien world" content in the original release is a big miss.Now, if you can get it on sale, and you're fully prepared to be annoyed by the same things I was, you will get your money's worth. This review is more Mixed than negative, and I'm giving it a No just because I don't feel it has done enough to earn the Yes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the way the game is structured and progress toward advancement.  The scenery is fabulous and that is an understatement.  I really like the combined futuristic feel of the game coupled with the primal survivability.  As with most games there are bugs and glitches, but typically the developers have been on top of this and are constantly improving on this and other game play features that keep the game interesting as well as challenging.  It can be quite frustrating at times, but all in all it is a manageable survival type game with lots and lots of choices and items that will make playing the game fun for a long long time.  If there is a complaint or gripe I have it is that in recent weeks, profiles and server issues have cause me the loss of game currency and special exotics that I had saved up for and spent on special items that could only  be crafted before entering a game prospect.  This happened over and over until I had depleted my stored up savings to the point I was back to basic survival when going into a prospect on the planet.  The developers appear to be on top of this and have hopefully corrected the issue, but that was a lot of momentum and fun that I lost during the time this has been an issue.  All that said, I still really really enjoy this game and it is a lot of fun to play with friends in groups.  I've been playing it since the Beta, but now that it is here in complete game ready state, it has been non stop fun for me!  Highly recommend Icarus.  If you liked the game Valheim, I think you'll LOVE Icarus.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long haul for me when it comes to Icarus.More than probably any other survival-sandbox game, I have had a love/hate relationship, in equal parts, with the world of Icarus.As I recall, I pre-purchased this title back sometime in November of '21. This allowed a friend and I to take part in the Beta Weekends program that ran for several weeks prior to actual release. I am pretty sure it was released as full retail but it was arguably still in very early access condition.Since game mechanics were still being implemented it would have been defined as an alpha phase game.It was harsh, unforgiving, but strangely addictive.Many hours of hard work could be totally wiped out by a poorly placed torch, a random lightning strike, or the retro-engines of a coop buddy randomly being given a trajectory to enter the map that targeted directly at your camp.Wolves could chew through multiple layers of stone construction in as little as 60 seconds.You find yourself frequently faced with situations where you either rage-quit or simply roll over laughing hilariously at the unexpected.It's can be that kind of harsh.But fun!Since I stay pretty busy with a small cadre of gaming friends who are mostly from my generation, (I am currently approaching 62 very soon.) so after release I decided that I would keep the game and check back in every so often to see how things were going with it's development. I own server hardware from which my little band of old farts play various survival-sandbox games and such as our interests lead us. Time marches on...Now it is fast approaching Halloween for 2023 and I notice that I have around 258 hours of play under my belt from which I can form an opinion. Steam is reminding me again that I should offer up a review... so here I am.The game is quite fetching, with a lot of natural mountain splendor, open desert vistas, and frozen wastes.There are now enough play options and locations available from which to work feverishly on gathering resources while the local wildlife attempts to gnaw your ass off at every opportunity.Why does the suspiciously "alligator-esque" looking crocodile seem to find me far more appealing as a dinner entree than the pretty pony, with tusks, that also wants a piece of my sweet-meats?If you kill something, you had better dress it out in a flat-ass hurry, or hope it's small enough to throw over your shoulders and carry with you. If not, in less than 30 seconds, other denizens will come running like you rang a dinner bell.It can quickly get out of control and you find yourself needing waders to slog your way out of the corpse pile of now dead predators you unintentionally attracted.If... you survive.Players are allowed to set up camp practically anywhere.Caves are interesting, but the current mechanic is terribly janky, thoroughly breaking any semblance of believable immersion from outside weather conditions that insist on following you into the depths of the underworld in an unpredictable fashion. You can literally perish from heat stroke while suffering from frostbite inside caves that act as passageways between different biomes. The caverns seem to "want" to have their own biome but just can't manage to enforce it throughout with any dependable consistancy.Being in a cave large enough to allow you to build a completely enclosed structure is just about your only chance against those subterranean sandstorms.Beasts of burden have been added recently. A much needed addition to the game.Now, if I could just convince my buffalo that "defensive" mode means it should defend itself if attacked, not go off full-Rambo at the merest sight of a possible predator in the distance.Normally pets follow at a distance, unless they are going psycho-aggressive on a perceived intruder or if you are stopping to dress out a fresh kill. At that point they will amble over, stomp it to ensure it is dead, and then proceed to stand on the carcass in an attempt to prevent you from claiming your kill."Look fart-stain, you either get off my dinner or I am going to introduce you to my 'boom-stick' and make an entree substitution."I think you all get the idea... this title is a little gem under a considerable bit of early access crustiness.There is something to love in here, but it needs some elbow grease to make that sparkle visible.

_childDocuments_.review: 14 hours in and i think game is worth the try  if price is around 25 €.  Game is for you:  If you like grinding materials  Hunting animals' whit bows and guns. Build best base. Basic flow of  normal game:You land-Get some materials-build house-craft items-Finish the given mission-Takeoff-Upgrade in your space station-Come back with new quest-Rinse and repeat. There is 30+ missions to do. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Visuals: 8+/10 Great not much to complain no serious popping or other weird stuff. Textures are sharp and shadows look fine. Some of the weather elements are really nice. Thunderstorm that can  start fires sharp winds that can break you house and extremely cold or hot weather that can make much more interesting play session.Base building/Crafting: 7.5/10 its fine would need some work when it comes snapping or etc. Gameplay: 7/10 Game has surprisingly deep rpg system. Big negative is long grind before you get the more interesting's stuff.  You can separate you team to Crafters, hunters, builders, and miners and everyone has role that has beneficial buffs for hole team. If you dont like  timed gameplay you have outpost that is totally unlimited.No minimap and you can only do one mark to map. ?Why i need to stop and open map to see where friends are. ?Why i cant use axe and torch same time it would be really handy. ?Why stamina runs out every 100 meters. ? Guests are really simple and lot of the creating/crafting is useless/pointless if you only want to complete missions.Gameworld: 8-/10 Handmade map with some nice-looking vistas. Locations that could be found in earth. Enemy variety: 7 Normal earthbound animals like deer,wolfs,bears and bunch of others. Performance: 3/10 No good, Game is close to unplayable some times you get lots of fps drops,Visual bugs,gameplay related bugs,  game crashes time to time and player get stuck to weird places and other stuff. Story: 5/10 In short humanity tries to populate and terraform a planet ♥♥♥♥ hit the fan and now your works is to do various tasks to complete the process or something like this. I don’t think anyone plays Icarus for its story. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Total score: 6-/10. Game is for certain player base that has tolerance for repetession for games like ARK, Valhem, Rust and others similar titles. Friends in this game makes it better but same can be said about every game.

_childDocuments_.review: After getting killed by a wolf, croc, and finally a horse, I was almost ready to give up. I am very glad I didn't. It is a much more difficult survival than most, but it is also far deeper and runs very well (i7 14thgen, 4070ti, 32G Ram). Like many others I jumped right into an open world and had no idea what to do, even breathe. Do the first 'mission' and it will help you get started with a guy telling you the basics. The look reminds me of The Forest, while the gameplay is more like Ark, but much better. The stealth works great and the combat is very good. As I mentioned, it is very deep with large tech and talent trees. The game is set up for the player to leave the planet and come back doing many missions, while starting fresh each time equipment wise(other than special equipment you eventually can obtain). Your characters talents and tech progress remain however.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Don't buy this until it gets cheap. Like real cheap. And then play it for a few hours & toss it on the garbage heap.Stamina Stamina StaminaEverything you do relies on stamina, and everything sucks it out of you with massive, long lasting debuffs.While the concept is good, and the ability to co-op is great, this is a frustrating game and not worth the money I spent on it.Pros:>Unforgiving. It doesn't hold you hand. Fitting for a survival game in a hostile environment.>Skill progression is at a good pace.>Open ended. While each "scenario" has an end goal, how you achieve that goal, and how quickly is up to you.>Co-op. Nice.Cons:>Bugs. Not a finished game. No way.>Stamina. Everything you do relies on stamina, and that's fine. But everything out there will debuff your stamina by a large percentage, and usually for a long time. Hungry? Eat food. Oh dear, food poisoning. Stamina debuff. Storm event? Stamina debuff. Cave spelunking? Guaranteed pneumonia, and yep, you guessed it, stamina debuff. Nothing in the tech or trait trees that will offset the debuffs to the point that it is not infuriating. And then you have a fire, and you can't put it out because you are out of stamina...>Weather events. Too. Damn. Frequent, and too damn annoying. Lightning strikes, high winds, falling trees, anything that tries to destroy or burn down that base you worked hard to establish.>Wolves and bears destroying structures way too easy. Ever heard of a wolf tearing down a wooden wall in a minute? They do on Icarus. Plus they aggro on you when you are safely inside and cannot be seen.>Level caps at 99 (great) but skill points stop after level 40 (wut??). Now you can't unlock all the skills you want (or need) to survive. If you have no friends that play, don't bother buying. You will not survive solo. If you are a completionist, and must unlock all the skills, don't buy.>Graphics. Unless you have a 3080, graphics are crap.>Perpetual scenarios. So, you start a new scenario. You get 7 (real) days to complete it. You and your mates start on Saturday, play Sunday, have a good time. Log out & do real life stuff like work during the week. Come next Saturday, too late. Time's up. You failed. The coutdown keeps going even when no one is playing.>Borderline plagiarism. This game looks familiar? That's because it's inspired by (or ripped off) other games like Satisfactory, huge chunk of Ark, Rust, and  Valheim. Possible conyright infringements?>HOW THE HELL CAN YOU GET PNEUMONIA WHEN YOU HAVE A SEALED HELMET WITH OXYGEN PUMPED IN?? It has to be sealed because you can stay under water...Other survival games like Rust and Ark will outlive this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game finally is playable and fun after about a year of updates from the developer after launching.   Originally bears and Polar bears were just impossible to kill without dedicating your entire time to learning how and still having only a slim chance.   Now the game is actually fun and skill prevails when it comes to hunting and gathering.    Huge Time Sync, but worth while and you feel like you can actually build a base and enjoy yourself for a while while in the open world game mode.   I still don't get the point really of building up to get missions done and then leaving once again, it may be for others that this is fun, but isn't for me, too much time spent working in real life, don't have time to re-work every time i play a game, i want adventure without re-working everything every single short mission.   I'm really just hoping the open world pans out to allow for exotics and in game currency rewards in that sense.After 12 more hours and waiting until respec of skills, i still conclude this game is BS... polar bears are so ridiculously overpowered, you don't have fun playing this at all.   You can fire at the polar bear with an F'ing shotgun (after hours and hours of mining enough ore for ammo and the gun) and then after 10 shots to the face, the bear is still alive, hits you 2 swipes and you die... and then start over.   How is this fun for anyone?   Here's a thought developers:Add a difficulty control to the game for F's sake.    Early access is BS... this should have been polished before coming out and charging people $50+, and after 12 weeks you can't even have a difficulty control figured out to allow casual players, hardcore players, group, solo, and all to have an option to play the way they want.   This is not ok.   Boycotting again (2nd time) until the developers fix these stupid bears.  a 1 out of 4 rated mission should not be whooping my butt for multiple times running.

_childDocuments_.review: The people in the game are so technologically advanced that they can go to space and land on an alien planet but still they use a stone pickax and build their houses out of wood. JUST BRILLIANT... AIN'T IT!!!!It’s basically a dollar store Ark but without Dinosaurs.Both me and my wife’s boyfriend have been playing this from launch (on his account) and the game then is nothing compared to the game now. Sure it has its faults here and there but overall the experience is highly enjoyable and constant updates keep this game changing more and more for the better. No matter what anyone says, the thing that makes this game different from other survival games is the missions. In this mode of play you drop onto the planet and start from scratch. Every time. You can decide how much you want to prepare for the mission or if you want to risk going fast with little to no prep. It's got a good risk reward gameplay mechanic. But you need to be ok restarting every time. I LOVE making a new base. I realized that I always loved starting from scratch in my survival games so this game speaks to me. If you enjoyed how hard ARK was when you first loaded in then you should enjoy the mission style of this game.If you want to play on the standard survival modes there's not a lot to set it apart from other survival games though.I started playing with friends and now I play solo all the time. There's even a solo talent tree that kicks in if you are alone. So you're given advantage to play alone. It's really nice. I like logging on and playing a mission over the course of a few play sessions and then being done for a while.The other thing that makes this game unique is the meta progression of currencies you earn for doing missions which let you buy equipment to drop with. That progression which makes subsequent missions easier is a lot of fun.If you stick to the missions, you'll have a clear purpose, as every map has plenty of them. But if you prefer open world - it's a sandbox, so only you decide for how long you would be able to come up with ideas about what to do today. If you enjoy the game, and the process, take your time (mission timer is there of course). Build up and play as you see fit. If you like the missions and want to "complete" the game, go hard. Most missions can be done with rudimentary tools, etc.Open world is fun for experimenting with builds. If you liked legos as a kid, you will like building in this game. I loved the missions and the whole grind of it all, but I also have had a fun time in open world building bases in the middle of lakes, on cliff sides and wherever else looks fun. In the end this is a game you can play in your own way. It’s up to you and up to your skill and  patience. I've played everything from ARK to Minecraft to SCUM in the survival genre, and honestly this is one of the best in my opinion. If you enjoy this type of game, it seems to me that it took some of the better parts of most survival games and made them one game. Again I personally think this game is one of the better survival games to have come out in a while. If remotely interested I encourage you to try it out and I hope you get to experience it in your own way.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: ICARUS

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Very pretty game with a notable exception. The water and nature both look incredible and really let you enjoy the world while you are building and surviving. -there is plenty to look forward to while you are leveling your character and there are plenty of neat gadgets that you look forward to using.-the storm system is fun and the nights are super dark, which both allow you really spend time in your homes. I loved how comfortable the homes felt, I imagine it gets even better in later levels. -Hunting is enjoyable and not frustrating. I was worried that the rabbits would be too fast to hit, but I was headshotting wolves in no time. I love the bow. -hunger system and dehydration are handled well, though the expiration rate of food doesn't make much sense as its not tracked seperately within a stack. Cons:-Super buggy and unfinished. From having to have an 'unstuck' button in the menu to constantly seeing wood that you chop or deer that you kill clip through the floor of the world to disapear into the abyss, the game could really benefit from some TLC. I wouldn't even call it missing polish, just basic functionality.-Character models are ugly. Really doesn't match with the rest of the world because of how pretty it is. ITs not that bad, just out of place when compared with the rest of the world. -The leveling system is very slow and hard to enjoy, it would be better if there perks points where a little more easy to come by, but you have to spend the majority of two level ups of perks on getting your first articles of clothing. It takes about five to learn how to build things and you are long onto a better tier by that point. A way to fix this might be to make lower perks somehow cost less or to sperate the perk points by tier, but that might be confusing to players. -Animal spawns are sometimes right on top of you, which is frustrating when you are trying to hunt. Its basically like the game is just dumping stuff in your lap. -Servers can be buggy, which can make if so you can't play with your character until its fixed. Sure you can do offline, but you have to literally start the game over so whats the point?Bottom line:Too unfinished to justify the purchase. I would wait, the game is currently too frustrating to play. I'll keep watching for updates and pop in when the server is functional. I am certain this game will be worth the money someday, ill probably update the review when it is.

_childDocuments_.review: The game look decent enough but it does have a sort of "Let’s use some of all these Quixel assets" vibe to it - as in it looks great, detailed textures and what not but it is not that exciting in of itself, and it seems like framerate optimization was not a priority. The world seems very static - not much interaction to spot between the animal that I have seen. Like wolfs hunting deer in packs or deer traveling in groups (beyond the ever-spawning baby deer + deer couple). Likewise, animals are not interested in what the players is doing beyond either going along their path or being aggressive/scared. Now I am not saying every game must have this, but I think the game is kind of bland as is and I assume the living world is the main attraction besides the missions.The missions seem kind of copy/paste, I have not done all of them far from it. But so far none of them seem to be that interesting especially since I have experienced the need to cheese quite a few things and so the missions become the same. So far, I haven’t really spent a whole lot of time crafting more advanced gear as it seems overkill for what the missions require - often it is just easier to avoid getting spotted, complete the mission and leave. Fighting bears seems to be something you just cheese by turning 45 degrees to the side and running next to it and then waited it to turn, shoot in the head, then rinse repeat until dead. Trying to get fancy with positioning is just a death trap as they can climb straight up vertical walls. Structures don’t seem to be of much use either. Best thing is to get it stuck on environment and then it is just easy kill. Thing is I don’t feel like I am looking for creative ways of doing things because we tried that first, then saw people debating it and everyone seeming to have concluded to just cheese it.There is some lore on the website - I haven't read it. So far, I have not really been presented to anything in game. The announcing voice talks about factions/corporations or whatever they are in terms of working for them and getting on their good side. I don’t know why I would care about this because there doesn’t seem to be any sort of global political system to interact with or any representation of them in the game itself.Would I return the game? YesWould I recommend the game? NoWill I wait for future releases? NoThis seems like a game challenge that go a final spot and now has been launched as a done product but is in reality more like the first good build of an early access game - disappointing to those not already invested.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus brings some much needed innovation to the survival genre. _childDocuments_.review: Icarus, how do I really feel about this game...?  First I want to give a big shout out to the Devs, making this game couldn't have been easy and there's a lot to love about Icarus so let's get into this review which will be in The Good, the bad, and the Ugly format.THE GOOD----------The first thing you'll notice about this game is that it's beautiful.  It's immersive.  It's incredibly detailed.  When your ship touches down in the first mission, if you're at all familiar with these types of crafting games, you'll feel right at home with familiar interfaces, relatively intuitive UI designs, and some good choices for crafting, scavenging and survival.  Manage your hunger, your H20 consumption, your oxygen, find shelter during storms and manage and avoid sickness - I think these are good and immersive elements to a survival game and I think Icarus does this better than any other survival game I've played.  Navigating sickness or hunger isn't too tedious and making mistakes isn't a death sentence and it's not too frustrating.Building structures is fluid and fairly easy to master, and if you really want to get into building large interesting bases you can, with a caveat which I will get into in "The bad".  Multiplayer is solid (You can both modify the inventory of crates and storage boxes simultaneously.  This is wonderful!) and since skill points and perks are scarce it behoves you to specialise.  Combat is a bit gimmicky but it's as solid as bows and knives need to be.  Combat isn't the core of this game, although you'll be hunting often.  Weapons are few and far between, but as they're not necessary, it's not really a big issue.  THE BAD--------------------------The WORST thing about this game is the crafting grind.  Tier 2 feels fair, and you get what you put in.  Chop some trees, build a house.  Quick and painless.  But Tier 3 and 4 are hopeless mine-fests where you're just running around the map looking for caves so you can get enough copper or gold to make electronics.  You might find yourself enlisting friends to speed up the grind but that's because it's WORK.  It feels like work and I don't know why a decision was made to waste as much of the player's time as possible.  There's a mission called "Payday" where you need to build a radar and an extractor.  These are tier 4 objects so I had to empty 6 caves to get enough materials to finally get what I needed.  After using the radar to get to the extraction point, I needed to craft and fill 6 gas cans to fuel the extractor.  Gas cans don't fill immediately when you get the required materials, you have to wait for the required table to fill it - so after the hour it took to fill these things, I made the trek back to the extracting place.  I used the 6 gas cans, but 6 didn't cut it.  I needed 6 and a quarter cans.  So I had to trek all the way back and then back again.  Total wasted time:  2 hours.  Did I mention the extractor took an hour to get through all of those cans?  Nothing is instantaneous.  Everything takes an arbitrary amount of time and a lot of it is for no gameplay positive reason.THE UGLY ---------------My RTX 2070 grinds hard in this game.  All of my settings are on low or Med and I get a pretty wide range of FPS.  30 - 110 fps.  Occasionally the game just stops for a full second or two while I guess it loads another area.  Fair enough, there is a lot of stuff around.  Sometimes the game crashes.  I just get booted to the desktop.  This happens, but it's been happening since I got the game in December.  Since then there have been a number of updates, but none have addressed this.  Still, I have happily put up with these concerns for 111 hours because there's something irresistibly addictive about this game.  FINAL THOUGHTS----------This game is a great action-crafter.  It's controls are tight, it feels good, and it plays well.  It's central idea however - that you will drop onto the surface and then leave after completing objectives - appears to .  What's the point of making a big beautiful base with everything you need if you're just going to leave and it's all going to get wiped.  Some design decisions appear to be quite hostile to the player, wasting their time and even inciting the occasional rage quit.  Playing this game feels like a waste of my time and I wish that wasn't the case.  My advice to the devs would be to lighten up the crafting grind in tier 3 and 4, but also create missions that require you to reach those levels.  Stone houses are more durable than the higher tier ones and cheaper, why would you ever create concrete houses?  There's no requirement to ever craft the rifle because no mission is ever too difficult to complete with the bow.   Remove the arbitrary limit on perks at level 40.  Maybe even remove the limitation on not being able to bring stuff with you from the surface of the planet and back again.  Focus on some more mission types than "Go here, turn this on, go here, turn this on."

_childDocuments_.review: A far better game than it has any business being.  It's really quite simple and slow to progress with stupidly long missions and you have to rebuild from scratch on every single one of them, keeping only your level ups and unlocked blueprints.  There is very little overall animal diversity and bears are a complete terror, especially them white ones.  Yet somehow, I've spent 50 hours on this game over a few days and am in no way tired of it.  It's quite engaging the point of mesmerizing, though much more so with a friend.  I think I would burn out quickly were I to play much alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Find one person to play Co-op with and this is the best PvE survival game to date. Just so much love put into the progression system and the Co-op features are just so fleshed out. Maybe something has changed since the beta (which I did not play) but all the other reviews saying that this is a terrible game because every time you start a new mission you have to launch back down to the planet and rebuild, that is the best part of the game! They have short missions where you build up whatever you need to complete the mission, and they have long week/month long missions where you just tech up as much as possible and build crazy houses, there is something for everyone here. About half my time is on a solo character, and the other half is Co-op with one of my friends on another character. Solo is very hard, and if you do play a lot or majority solo, create two characters, one for co-op and one for solo.

_childDocuments_.review: FYI: played the game after the release, so take my review with a grain of salt, your mileage may vary after the major patches.TL;DR: Don't buy it yet, or keep in mind the 2 hours gameplay limit for the refund. Get familiar with the gameplay before purchasing, it's maybe not your cup of tea.Poor (or missing?) optimization, really hard to get stable 40+ fps on RX580, even FidelityFX cannot save this. Sure the graphics can look great, if you have a semi decent and current GPU, otherwise forget it, I had to crank the visuals to bottom in order to get some playable fps.There isn't a single word about the mission based gameplay, which was a surprise to me, since according to the lore, we are building "outposts", but there is not a single change from mission-to-mission basis that "improves" our situation on this exactly Earth-like planet, where we have proper modern time flora and fauna, just can't breathe the air (facepalm).  The character creation is basically unnecessary, because on the planets you cannot see your characters face at all, it wears the EVA suit and helmet all the time.Got it as a gift from a friend of mine, but the game frustrated me so badly I have deleted it after 6 hrs. Co-op and the constant updates could be the saving grace of this game, though the developers stating that this is a finished game is an obvious lie, more like an early access with minor bugs and non-existent performance optimizations.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Graphics are top notch. The beautiful landscapes are stunning. Sound design is solid. I have many times noticed a wolf stalking me just because I was listening closely.Developers are constantly adding missions, items, enemies, features, and fixing bugs. Variety of missions to keep things interesting. Immersive. Rewarding workshop system that lets you get items you can bring with you on missions, permanently making things easier on you. Cons:Lack of a clear and engaging storyline.Some missions are EXTREMELY grindy, although the devs say they are working on that. Playing solo can be very challenging. Most of the upper tier technology is not needed unless the mission explicitly calls for it. Getting upper tier technology takes way too much time to make it worth using most of the time. The framerate drops around fire and when too many things are on screen sometimes, even on very good computers. I have a top of the line machine and it chugs sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting open world survival mechanics, challenging but achievable progression that rewards careful play and especially teamwork.However, there's no reward for progressing past about mid-game. Higher levels of the tech tree just require even more grinding, without any need to actually complete those levels in order to complete missions.As other reviews mention, there are clearly beta elements still present in the game, like un-implemented skill tree paths. An interesting game for a couple dozen hours, but needs dramatically more design work to make further progression feel like it has a purpose beyond simple grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like your survival games with huge tech and talent tree's and a whole planet that wants you dead this game is for you, add in the station side gear/crafting as the icing on the cake, tis an epic game and I am loving it atm huge hermit thumbs up for this, as always playin solo, there's co op if you like people.Almost 150hrs now and I have to say, still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ epic, lol.Now at 600+ hrs and still love the game, Galileo has dropped and I found a way to completely reset your game to the 'just bought it' point so I can start all over again. I may have an addiction here but please no intervention as I think this is one of the best survival games to date. Also I have still not played with people but eww, just saying the p word is hard enough, hermit4life.Nov 30, lots of hrs, review update..A lot has changed in the game, additions and updates every weekend have made the game something else, the rl timer on missions was moved to in-game time ages ago which was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. Apart from the old ways to play ie the missions and outposts, they added in open world. In open world you can pick a map and play on it forever, build a nice big base and advance from there. They added in two nice new items recently, a mission board and a board to call down a pod to send stuff like exotics back to the station. You can dump all your gear in open world in your base, jump back to the station, take a mission and then jump back into your open world map any time. The resources can be respawned with a thumper which you build or will respawn with a meteor strike. Now once you hit max level (60) you will still level but only receive tech blueprint points. There's a shedload of other improvements and quality of life stuff like farming, mounts, fishing and other tweaks and fixes, so if you've not played since launch or never have give it a poke, damn fine game.

_childDocuments_.review: OK it's official... Deleted from my computer.  I gave it 34 hours but the game is taking more than it gives.  Huge death penalty while solo was the final straw. Terrible AI for the animals.  Added 1/1/2023  So after 19 hours I have to say there is some good stuff in here..... I think I was unprepared for how long it takes to grind up in the levels.  Not used to that much time.  Complexity is good over all but my biggest issue is the penalty for death.  As a level 18 I got attacked by a bear who for some reason can breath under water for... well it seems forever..... Not balanced... He needs to go up for air... and I lost A WHOLE LEVEL OF XP.....Yes there are console cheat codes I could use but so far I am playing the game without them.  I think they did some really amazing things here but it's not balanced.  If they think it is.... well its not.  Death penalty is too huge when solo.  It will force you to cheat and once you open up that box the game is ruined.  Player housing is the best I have seen so far.   Storms and events cause you to run to your house and make sure it makes it through the storm.  It can get hit by lighting and burn up.  Trees burn up and you can cut them down for charcoal.  I know you can't please everyone but solo deaths should not be so expensive.  Maybe a timer that scales down the longer you stay alive for deaths.  Die a lot and the penalty goes up.  I'll add to the review as the game goes on.Posting my initial thoughts.  This seems like a game in beta not a game out for a year.  The animal AI and the movement is very close to south-park.  Very crappy.  I got chased by a wolf who did not have any sort of aggro ring.  He walks underwater and never seems to need air.  It's breaking the feel of the game.  He chased me until he killed me as a new player.  Good grief.   I wish there was another choice besides a thumb up or a thumb down but since there isn't I can not recommend this game.  I will keep playing it tell the 5 hour mark and hopefully there is some saving grace here.  I will be happy to change my rating if something amazing changes.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game for a while, and was slightly naive about the early access phase. _childDocuments_.review: So almost 60 hours in. Currently on the Avalanche Expedition. Spend about 5 hours so far grinding this one out. It was fun, the lighting will make you wonder why weather effects aren't in so many more games. The woods burning down around you while bears and wolfs chase you. It is immersive, engaging and man does this game look beautiful. Runs well, no lag, I think I’ve crashed 1 time in 60 hours. While this mission is a huge skill gap and you must be leveled, this compared to what I’ve done so far is night and day.The 9 caves I had to find to get enough gold to even finish this mission, was ridiculous. This was almost the entire mission. Going cave to cave dodging weather and bears trying to scavenge enough resources to build what you need to even complete the mission. That’s not the problem, I like the grind, it was fun and if any of you have played ark, you know the grind is real.The big issue is what happens after. I just spent half a day playing non stop to accomplish…what. 600 credits to buy exotics with. Exotics that are no better than T3 or 4 crafted tools. I’m level 43 and apparently you get no skill points after 40? Are you serious dev’s? So not only do I not get to keep anything in this “session” based game, but I also can’t level up either? The lack of skill points honestly must be an oversite, because if its not, someone needs to be fired for that decision. Absolutely just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy your character ceases to become better, while still leveling.This is where you will lose players. Grinding your ass off for the stupid expensive material cost to make T4 items, that you can’t keep. This is so painful. To do all that work and have literally nothing to show for it but…lack of experience. Sick joke. This whole session-based things needs to change. Let us keep 10 or so items. Our armor, our tools. Or make exotics actually worth a damn, because even the 1000 point ones are not up to standard with crafted items. What’s the point? A good head start every mission? That tool is broken an hour into it.This is the most fun I’ve had since ark. So much potential, but things must change. I will easily hit 100 hours this week but after that, not having anything to show for it is going to make me put this game down.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr this is an early access game masquerading as a complete game with some interesting mechanics but is about as unbaked as your aunties homemade minced meat pie after a hard night of boxed white wine - get it on sale for $5 and play with some friends in a year or two when (if?) the developers get around to finishing the game.Good stuff first since it's a short list: - There's a nice big old talent tree with tons of awesome looking talents, which is one of the things I find survival games  have. If they do have them they're anemic as ♥♥♥♥, where as this game has multiple trees with really nice looking QoL perks. Sadly, you won't get to use more than 15% of it (more on that in the negatives....). - When the game doesn't run at 20-30 FPS on a 2080 TI @2k, it's beautiful. Best of luck finding a guide that helps you figure out which options decimate the engine and then praying they actually work. On the other hand, I'm genuinely impressed (technically speaking) that a company managed to find a way to make Unreal run  than Unity for an FPS. - The building and crafting is fun despite all of the various issues with both. Making bases is enjoyable, the multiple tables are nice, progression makes more or less sense (though it's stupidly expensive and grindy) - Despite being an awful grindy overall experience it's still somehow fun to play with friends, at least until you get to the end game missions and realize that you spent $27 on a running/mining simulator with combat mechanics implemented by a toddler - Some cool save-game tech; your game ('prospect') gets uploaded somewhere central any  you were playing with can resume it, at any time, and play it with or without you. This is a great approach since there's no real time limit in-game for completing things (just real-life time), so people can play at their leisure and make progress.Transitioning to the cons...: - Nothing is explained. Apparently, everyone was expected to play the two previous betas/open events and know what all the gameplay mechanics were, how the missions worked, that your character gets permanently deleted if you don't finish (or abort) a mission in X real-time days (yup!), that exotics (the end game in-game currency to buy cool unique "workshop" items) require a specific quest chain to unlock (the game now highlights these missions after some patches, at least). - Sometimes your cool unique workshop items get deleted and you lose them and have to repurchase them. No, not because you left them behind on a mission, because the game just decided to delete them. Why does this suck? Because they require in-game rare currencies (either golden dollars or purple exotic dollars) that come in small quantities from grinding missions and . - The talent trees are huge but you stop getting points at level 40. This gives you enough points to get 2 trees pretty filled out, but since you had no idea this was going to happen, you've got points spread out over random ass trees all over the place as you were having fun exploring. Naturally, though, you can respec - oh wait, the developers have never played a game with a talent tree before so that's not implemented either. Coming soon (TM), though! - The AI is about as smart a lobotomized penguin and all of the animals behave exactly the same. Prey runs and comes back to the  same spot you shot it, so hunting amounts to either 1) crit and 1-shot everything, 2) don't crit, wait for animal to pat back to you then murder it with a crit. Predator combat is either 1) bring more friends and pincushion it down with arrows, 2) crit and 1-shot everything except polar bears, 3) if it's a polar bear, crit it and glitch past it or unstuck and get teleported 15 feet away and re-engage, 4) get glitched and 1-shotted yourself when the enemy is 15 feet away and contemplate all the other things $27 could have got you (have you even tried Wendy's new breakfast sandwiches? $27 is a  of sandwiches!). - The game runs like crap and it seems to be on a completely random basis; find a guide on Youtube and pray it has an affect on your FPS. - Dropping items on the ground sometimes falls them through the planet, deleting them permanently, because this game is  early access - Crafting at later tiers is abysmal. For example, end-game benches require 40-80 gold, and on average you'll maybe get 40-80 gold ore (crafted 2:1 into ingots) from tier 2/3 mines. You need a lot of benches. This basically means all of the end-game is: run around the map decimating every mine (which have fixed amounts of ore, doesn't respawn), then hope to god you can craft the benches to make the mission materials you need at which point you then ♥♥♥♥ off back to space and lose 100% of your progress only to do it all again in the next mission. - Crafting in general is just terrible. We don't tech beyond bows for weapons or basic bone arrows for ammo as all it does is force you to play the same mission longer, re-grinding the materials you used for either item. The game is also of course very realistic - an aluminium arrow (1, mind you) naturally takes 1 copper ingot, 4 aluminum ingots, and some epoxy. Yes, 4 aluminium ingots. If you've never Googled what an "ingot" of metal is, today is the day you should, then Google "arrow head" and try to wrap your head around how they fit 4 ingots of aluminium in one arrow. - Playing without friends is a nightmare; play with friends or wait until the devs address solo play. It's just taking the already massive grind and multiplying it by the lack of friends you have. - While mining in a cave you get a permanent stamina debuff no matter what armor you are wearing, because . You also randomly develop pneumonia, which there is a later-game fix for, but no one cares because all it does is make you take 15 minutes versus 10 to grind out the mind-numbingly boring cave mining expedition. - Fun fact: 100 stones in a pile weighs far more than 100 stones in your inventory, because the stone pile is full of extra  - Dying in the beginning is awful (massive XP debuff you have to work through), dying after level 40 is 100% completely irrelevant as XP no longer matters at all.It's got potential. Somehow, despite all of that awful experienced, I almost clocked 60 hours and that was largely playing with 1-2 other people. With more I'm sure the grind would be less noticeable.This definitely feels like a come-back-in-a-few-years kind of game and see if the developers have got around to completing it. Right now it's just frustrating and unrewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm a big fan of the survival genre and enjoyed this game in general, I really cannot recommend this game. Here is why:1. The lack of lore, explanation, and logic behind game mechanics.Let me put a few examples first:  a. You landed on the planet, built something, finished the mission and returned to orbit. The next time you land at the exact same spot, the buildings you built mysteriously disappear.  b. You're wearing an environment suit and breathing from the oxygen tank, but somehow you get pneumonia inside a cave because of the air in the cave.  c. Whoever sent you to the planet can afford the cost of a drop pod, fuel, and environment suit but cannot afford a single pickaxe or knife or axe. So you have to start empty-handed.  d. There is an objective, and the drop pod tries to send you to a location ~10km away from your objective.Trust me, a random magic world with dimension warp would make more sense explaining all the mechanisms above. It feels like the devs just want those mechanisms to be in this game and did not give a ♥♥♥♥ on making them convincing. 2. 50%+ of playtime is running.By running I mean literally running. For most survival games, you EXPLORE the environment and are rarely running. In Icarus, since all missions share the same big map, I found that most of the time, I was running through the place I already knew. There is nothing to explore, no random events/resources/creatures, no need of gathering stuff, just plain running. And it feels like the whole purpose of running is to lengthen the playtime because, again, there is no lore or logic in it.3. Growth of the character feels meaningless very soon.Most of the talents are percentage increase in something. That is boring, and doesn't feel I'm progressing. Most of the talents I get are those increase moving speed. Blueprints are exciting at first, but soon you'll discover that most blueprints are useless - namely, all those from tier 3 and 4. Tier 3 and 4 blueprints require an insane amount of resources. Since you get reset every time and start bare-handed, there is no point in putting so much effort into tier 3 and 4. By the time you unlock them, you'll finish the prospect already if you choose to go straight into the mission. The workshop items are nice but the only they do is to save your first 10 minutes of resource gathering and base building. I think there should be more, like some game-changing or playstyle defining workshop items.4. It should be an EA title.Apart from the points mentioned above, there are still some important parts missing, like the ability to respec talents/blueprints, the variety of prospects, and the variety of creatures. The game feels like a game mechanism demonstrating prototype in current state. I would say that it still needs at least a year of polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews for games.I've spent a little over 30 hours in the game at the time of this review, because I really want to give this game a fair shake and I respect the fact that Dean Hall and RocketWerkz are trying to expand the Survival genre here. I understand launch difficulties and server issues that come up around them - none of my beef with this game has anything to do with that.The game is intentionally tedious and obtrusive in the worst possible ways. There are four talent trees, Survival, Construction, Combat, and Solo. The Solo tree makes no sense and forces anyone who wants to take points into it into a Solo-Only mindset, as these talents *do not work* if you are in a multiplayer game. This is a completely baffling design decision that blows my mind. The tree shouldn't exist.There's no respec functionality whatsoever, and talent points stop at level 40. If you want to try different builds, the only solution is to make another character, which seems like an absolutely bizarre design decision without any real thought put into it. Characters are not disparate enough in terms of their talent selection to warrant alt characters, so you don't get enough of a meaningful gameplay experience change by rolling a new character to try different talents that might make your life easier. If talents were so impactful that they made the player's character feel meaningfully different from others, then I could maybe see a degree of permanence being important - but there isn't, so it makes no sense in my eyes.Most missions follow a set formula. Land, spend 60% of your time in the mission teching back up to whatever level of technology and assets needed to complete the mission, 20% of your time completing the mission, and then anywhere from 10-20% of your total time in the mission is spent trudging back to your dropship. None of the mission timers we had ever felt like we were 'under the gun', with most missions giving anywhere from 3-7 RL days to complete, while the mission themselves took anywhere from 3-4 hours of playtime to complete. There isn't any way to facilitate faster travel aside from movement speed talents, so these last 10-20% of missions are actual wastes of time as you run through the landscape as fast as you can to get back to your dropship, so you can leave and go somewhere else - these trips can easily take up to 15-25 minutes, depending on how far the objectives are from your drop. There is nothing challenging about it - it is simply more tedium tacked on that doesn't respect the player's time.The missions themselves are usually cased around a biome, which is a set map that you'll complete multiple missions on. This sounds fine - except for the fact that each individual mission requires you to leave the planet at the end of it. When you return to that biome to tackle a new mission, all of your building progress is gone, but the map is the exact same otherwise. On the first winter biome, we had to build virtually the *exact same base* in the *exact same spot* no less than four times because we had multiple missions for that biome. This feels incredible repetitive, doesn't respect the player's time, isn't challenging and just feels lazy.Death is a mechanic that also makes no sense to me. In a multiplayer session, if you are killed, you drop to the ground and can be revived by a teammate. The only penalty for death in this instance is a reduction of Food / Oxygen / Water stats, which can be easily remedied. The only time you have to actually contemplate a respawn is if nobody can revive you, which in the majority of instances where you have 3 or more players, is exceedingly rare.In solo play, this is an entirely different animal. If you are killed in solo play, you *must* respawn, and take an XP penalty as well as lose all your equipment. The dropping of the equipment is fine and understandable, but the XP penalty boggles my mind. As of the time of writing this review, the XP penalty is scaled to the amount of XP you are currently into a level. So if you're 90% of the way from level 9 to level 10, the XP penalty is HIGHER than if you were just 10% of the way into a level. If this is a bug, I'm glad to be proven wrong. Even if it isn't, the penalty is staggeringly high, and massively disincentivizes solo play.There are other issues as well, many of which are covered in the other reviews plastered here. The Mixed aggregate of reviews is fair - the game itself has some good moments and the framework of the game is interesting. As it currently stands, I'd highly encourage prospective buyers to wait and see what RocketWerkz does to address everything. If you do still feel inclined to buy it, make sure you're playing with friends - as with most games, it's better when you have buddies to play with.Edit:I will say, I've given this some thought and there's a few things right off the top they could do to make things immediately better. For those of you who have upvoted and brought attention to this review, I appreciate it.Edit: 8 June, 2022I give Dean Hall and RocketWerkz credit - they are listening and trying.Most of my initial suggestions (which I had to delete to conserve space) have been addressed to a reasonable degree. The new map, Styx, looks to promise some actual continuity between missions in some context (according to their devblog, missions now can change the map in between missions). The timer change to RL time makes sense, and the hardcore mode added alleviates any remaining concerns I had on that front. I still cannot recommend the game, but I'm a lot closer to it now than I was six months ago. It's very obvious at this stage that the staff is very committed to turning this ship around, and I've kept quiet tabs on it as they've progressed. Most of what they've addressed is core functionality of the game that was just unfun - and rightfully so, that stuff needed to be addressed first. I do think if you've read the progress and see potential with the title, it's worth investing in - but you should see it as an investment, not a game really ready to sink a ton of hours into right now.I think they also realize that there's just not enough interesting and exciting enough incentives to actually play currently beyond chasing exotics for gear. What will get me back into this game is a sense of persistence. _childDocuments_.review: I played Icarus extensively during the beta. I purchased a copy for myself and a friend, and despite the many bugs, flaws, and performance issues, we had a great time, overlooking the issues in the belief that by full release, these problems would be resolved.This is far, far from the case. If anything, the panoply of immersion-breaking, fun-destroying issues has increased. The game is replete with missing features, with a sparse and non-functional end-game tech tree, skills and talents which have been marked 'Coming Soon' since the beta. Armour does not provide physical resistance despite being marked as such, the rewards for grinding up tech levels are outweighed by the tremendous costs in time and resources it takes to reach them, reducing the game to a repetitive loop of long, on-foot travel, memorising cave locations, dealing with bloated fetch quests and illogical, rapidly respawning enemies. The art style of the creatures is inconsistent - the 'boar' model added after the beta is clearly a warthog, the 'hyena' resembles a jackal, presumably so it could use the same basic skeleton as the wolf. All animals save the bear have the exact same jump animation, which they perform whenever they encounter terrain they cannot walk over. This is frequent. Animals are also cooperative, meaning that while fighting one of the ubiquitous bears, nearby wolves and pigs will rush to the bear's defense. Steam offered refunds for Cyberpunk 2077, and it was in a better state than this on release. The missions are artificially padded by enforcing incredibly long travel times, frustrating build requirements (a vast structure required to traverse a mountain from one biome to another - which is identical to the previous biome, for example), and massive 'stockpile' demands which require literally hundreds of resources to be deposited. Higher level structures are challenging and time-consuming to build, but perform worse than stone structures. Wolves will chew through concrete to get you. Some people enjoy this grinding, repetitive, and joyless process. If these things appeal to you or are what you consider a challenging, 'hardcore' experience, then by all means, purchase. For anyone else, don't be fooled by what this game could be. It is not that. There are no aliens save the annoying 'cave worms' which respawn each day to spit poison at you. They pop up through the ground and shoot little poison bullets at you while remaining otherwise immobile. At core, Icarus is designed to pad itself out, forcing you to find the most efficient ways to complete objectives within artificial and counter-intuitive constraints, which renders higher-level progress pointless. Most missions can be completed with stone/bone tools. Combined with the broken skills, talents, and useless higher-tier items, this is a job you pay for rather than a game. It could have been better. It isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of hope for this game with it having drawn inspiration from Valheim and Deep Rock Galactic. Unfortunately at present it doesn't really do much of anything better than either of them past the first 10-20 hours. It was "released" but is clearly still an early access game with missions, tech tree unlocks, and items marked as "coming soon". Talents are not balanced and a few are completely pointless. They have weekly or bi-weekly game updates where they add a couple new missions and fix a lot of existing problems. Can't tell you how many talents were broken on launch and that they've slowly fixed over time. They're actively fixing things which is acceptable for an early access game but not one marketed as released.Broken things aside, the combat is not well designed. Though knives and spears have talent trees, melee in this game is not viable and only to be used as a last resort. There are no tank / melee builds. If you are fighting more than one animal at a time, in general, you are in for a tough fight because you are not meant to take damage. You can't take a lot of hits and you can't block or parry attacks like in Valheim. You are encouraged to stealth kill animals at range with a bow or gun in a single shot. Fun at first, but it doesn't last long. So your choice of viable weapons are very limited and, additionally, the variety of enemies is extremely limited. Pretty much there's just wolves, bears, boars, and cave worms. That's it. They have different levels (e.g. level 10 wolf vs level 70 wolf) but it really doesn't make a difference. They still die in a single stealth attack. Arctic biome has Polar Bears which are noticeably tankier than the Bears in the woodlands but to the point that it's a better use of your time to just avoid them unless you've spent hours tech'ing up to rifles to kill them quickly.So limited variety of enemies and limited ways to fight them. Valheim has 10x more enemy types and the harder ones require you to work up to better quality weapons and armor where, in Icarus, you can take pretty much all enemies with a single long bow and bone arrows that you can craft within the first 5-10 minutes of a mission.Once you hit level 40, you stop getting talent points and character progression essentially stops. Once you've farmed enough money and exotics to buy the workshop items you want (out of around 50 workshop items, only about 12 are actually worthwhile), then wonder what to do next? There's no story and most of the boss fights encourage you to cheese the boss - not fun boss mechanics - unlike Valheim, and combat and mission objectives are not fun unlike Deep Rock Galactic.Some of the weather storms like lighting setting the forest on fire or high winds blowing trees over (potentially on you) are great but not very frequent compared with the less interesting storms that are not dangerous but last a long time and basically have you sheltering for far too long to be fun.Game concept has lots of potential to be great but I haven't yet seen evidence that the devs are addressing the core complaints of the players and building it towards the really enjoyable aspects of either survival or session based games like Valheim, Subnautica, or Deep Rock Galactic. Each week's patches have been fixes + 2 missions which are basically a minor twist on existing missions.If you like survival games, get it if it's on sale for < $10 or until they seriously add more content and improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Since launch I have put 10 hours into the game, on top of the 100+ that I put into the Beta Weekends that led up to the release.Is this a perfect game? Of course not. Is there such a thing? Also no. Do I think it is great value for the cost? Definitely.Lots of comments about poor optimisation and performance - I wonder what those peoples' expectations are and how realistic they are, and also what other applications they have running at the same time to impact performance.My rig is mediocre. I did recently upgrade my CPU to a Ryzen 5 5600X, but for the first few beta weekends (when the game was arguably less optimised) was running fine on my R5 1600. Graphics card is an RTX 2070, which is about similar to the 3060 Ti that they state in the 'Recommended Specifications' on the Store page. It is installed on an SSD (which I would expect to be the case of most gaming machines these days, and is the most affordable upgrade to make) and my system has only 16GB of RAM (compared to the 32GB they recommend).My settings are dialled down overall, but I have View Distance on High (was on Epic but I was trying to reduce my GPU Core utilisation below 99% to reduce heat in the humid NZ summer), Textures on High, Shadows on High, and Anti-Aliasing on High (otherwise I was getting a 'shimmer' effect on distant trees). I have turned down things like 'Post Effects' (which included things like Bloom that I do not care about), and Foliage density (which as a solo player is quite useful as it lets me see hostile creatures from further away...) and some other settings which I do not particularly care about. I am running on DX11 and have Ray Tracing turned off. I was playing in a 1080p window instead of fullscreen on my 1440p monitor, which does not bother me - and reducing the resolution is the greatest thing to improve performance overall. It looks fine at 1080 fullscreen on the larger res monitor too, but I was wanting to keep an eye on windows in the background anyway.I had two Chrome windows open with a total of 9 tabs, plus Open Hardware Monitor, and OBS Studio, and I was streaming to Twitch at 1080p60 using NVENC. <0.1% dropped frames, minimal impact on system performance.For me, I believe the game still looks amazing even with things turned down how I have them, and performs pretty smoothly, even in action like fighting multiple wolves or running from bears. Did not have FPS tracking turned on, but I'd be surprised if it dipped below 60 all that often, mostly just when loading in new areas with mission objectives (which is not often, like 3-4 times each Prospect).TL;DR, performance has been fine for me as an average rig gamer even while streaming.Gameplay-wise, this has been a great experience for me. It combines survival elements with base building aspects and offers some macro progression over the top of the session based gameplay. It is difficult to draw truly accurate comparisons, but that has not stopped others from trying, and so I would compare it to a cross between Valheim, in terms of survival and base building gameplay, and Deep Rock Galactic, in terms of its session based progression. But it is more the former than the latter, as the session durations tend to be longer (you generally have multiple _days_ of in-game time to complete your objectives) and it is very much "play at your own pace". If you want to speedrun missions for the sake of the rewards, you can - I did the same Geo-Survey mission 6 or so times today, as it is a 20-30 minute mission with a 75 credit reward, so a decent return on time spent. But if you want to just take your time and enjoy building yourself a cabin in the woods, you can do that as well - in my final Prospect of the day I spent the better part of an hour just making a little hut with some crafting stations and a nice view over the lake, even though I knew it would be gone when I launched after completing the final objective. After completing the first couple of missions (one of which is basically just an introduction to game mechanics where the objective is essentially to reach level 5), there is even a Prospect with a duration of 30 days, and no objective (though also no reward for completion) so you can just explore to your heart's content.Also for the more casual sandbox experience, there are the Outpost regions (you have 1 with the basic game version, 2 extra if you buy the Supporters DLC) which are persistent. You can play fully offline, and spend the entire game in just the Outpost, if you so wish. Or you can group up with up to 8 of your friends and all collaborate on one of the longer Prospects and have some great team experiences.I am a big fan of flexibility in games, and I think this offers a lot of that for different gameplay styles. I am sure I will tire of it eventually, but I anticipate my game time being in the hundreds of hours before that happens. And quite simply even if you only played this game for a month or so, just doing a few of the longer prospects with a bunch of friends, and then never touched it again, I would say that you'll have gotten great value for money as entertainment, and some fun memories. And maybe when the already announced DLCs come out, you play it for another few weeks to see what has changed, because I'm sure some things will have even in the base game - I believe the devs have already said they are committed to rolling out free updates with new content in addition to the extra paid modules. I believe there is a lot to look forward to, but also a lot to enjoy right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Most frustrating game I have ever played. Not a hard game by all means, its pretty simple... just frustrating. Its like someone had a lot of good ideas but in the end there is nothing to connect them.Honestly I have to say I bought it because of the advertisement. The videos were incredible and it seemed like there was a thrilling story with really good characters to be experienced...and then -No storyline, just tons of different dumb quests given to you by faceless corporations.It is clearly meant to be a multiplayer game, but doesn't let you play with strangers if you wanted to choose so.All the obvious breaks in the plot that make it hard to suspend disbelief (Looks and behaves like earth, my environmental protection suit gives me pneumonia when I am in a cave, polar bears are psychic and will detect you through objects, not a single trap in a game that relies heavily on hunting, as a spacefaring species your technological answer that you bring from a space station is---a 3D printed axe for tree cutting?!?...)Everything is an endless frustrating loop. You land on the same map, in the same location and everything you once built is gone. Everything needs to be built with your own two hands. Start from scratch with picking rocks, chopping trees with a stone axe etc. etc. etc. Crazy weather shows up like on a clock. Its not like one really bad storm once in a while to be remembered... Its a crazy storm every few minutes. Whatever you do, drop it and run back to your base and start fixing everything or else you loose it.Stamina feels like its sole purpose is to make sure you don't progress too fast.Any predator anywhere seems to have one task: slow you down.Need to built something? Sure, just stand there for 5 seconds, nothing happening...just a timer clocking off to slow you down.Landed on the planet? Conveniently not where your mission objective is, so you spend an hour to just run in between recharging stamina and fending off predators. Oh, and forget about ever having a vehicle...you can manufacture machines and concrete, but not even a bicycle.You die? No biggy... you just loose all your XP for that level...no matter if you were 1% or 99% close to the next level. Grinding to get to the next level? Better hope that no bear shows up at 98% How does that make sense??Finally the bugs: After my whole house got destroyed in one of the countless storms and I wasn't close enough to fix the timber walls immediately (as they get destroyed by any storm... as timber houses do...) I logged out in frustration. Then log back in: All the left behind contents of my destroyed things are gone.The polar bear that killed you lays down to have a nap on your bed in which you respawn...to insta kill you again and proceed to sleep there.You enter something thats marked as a zone on the map but to trigger progression in the quest you need to walk over an unmarked spot in that area.Animals will get stuck in things on the map, walk unfazed through a forest fire, clip right through your building if they got into it etc. Feels like a game from 20 years ago.Very, very disappointed.
