_childDocuments_.review: Update: I finished the whole trilogy and here are my thoughts on this game:- Utawarerumono is a visual novel series, developed by Aquaplus. Currently the main games in this series that you can find on Steam are Utawarerumono: Prelude to the fallen, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. This is the second game in the trilogy.-  Yes but I highly recommend you to finish Prelude to the fallen first because the events, the characters will have much more depth if you already knew them in Prelude to the fallen.- No. This is not an eroge. if you want Eroge, you can play the first game but keep in mind that the steam version of it doesn't have R18, because it was a port from console.- Getting the whole trilogy on sale is highly recommended.- It is highly recommended that you should finish the first game before playing this game. The story is fantastic and the world building, the character development throughout the story is awesome. You will enjoy every moment in this game, even fillers.- - Personally I think in term of story, this game is more well written than the first game.- The game has a 3D turn-based tactical strategy element, which is very refreshing compared to any traditional visual novel. The game mechanic is also improved from the first game (like new chain rings, counterattack,...) but some things like Unit rotating is removed, which is, to me, a big stepdown. Other than that, the gameplay is awesome. - You can either play as a hardcore gamer in hard mode or just enjoy the story with pretty simple turn-based gameplay.- The game's default resolution is 720p, which is a real disappointment to be honest.- Character sprites are gorgeous. the CGs are even beyond that. - I'm not gonna judge the 3D graphic because this is, mainly, a visual novel. 3D characters look really cute tho :3- This game has a very stacked cast. You can find Inori Minase, Risa Taneda , Saori Hayami and a tons of famous seiyuus in this game. You won't be disappointed by the character VAs- The BGMs are superb. Some of them are reused from the first vn, which is very nostalgic. - The OP is sung Suara, who also have sung most of Utawarerumono songs in anime and visual novel. Suara and Utawarerumono, you can't find a more perfect duo.Conclusion: Awesome game, awesome series. it's a must play. Also if you want to watch the anime, Mask of Truth's adaptation, Futari no Hakuoro is coming this July 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, it wasn't a bad experience. I gave a thumb down because for how much the game costs, I felt like I played half a game. My playtime says 34 hours, but the game really only starts in the last 15 hours or so. For a VN, the story is decent. In particular, I like the world-building and the political intrigue a lot. However, there are 2 problems with the story-telling. First, there are ways too many slice-of-life events, especially in the first half. Slice-of-life is nice to build up the bonds between the characters. However, the amount of these "let's cook together" or "let's hang out together" events is excessive at time. There was a stretch of almost 4-5 hours straight of these events. Second, the game left way too much for the sequel. I get it. Every game these days tries to set up a series. But this game goes too far. As I said, the first half is just filler after filler. Even when the game picks up in the second half, some events are left unexplained for no other reasons than to sell the sequel. I can't use an actual example from the game, so I'll make up a similar example. Let's say you meet a guy that carries around a pink cat. However, NOBODY ever thinks to ask about the pink cat. There is no reason why nobody should not be curious. They just don't ask because well, you need to buy the sequel to know. This is just plain manipulative.The gameplay is a decent grid-based TBS. Overall, gameplay is pretty easy because your team often outnumbers the enemies. The biggest problem of the gameplay is actually that it does not happen often enough. There's only 17 or so stages. Each stage is also very short. The game can use more battle stages early on. Sting is one of the developers of this game, so the gameplay has the same issue as another Sting's game, Tears to Tiara. The issue is that damage is too high. Anybody on your team or the enemies can kill someone in one-shot or be killed in one-shot easily. Random mob with their normal attack often takes off 60 to 70% of HP. Because damage is so easy to come by, none of the other stuffs like buffing or sigil matter as much. Battles become a damage race. You're trying to burst the enemies down before they do the same to you. Speed scaling is also an issue. I have a battle in which a character takes 11 turns while another moves 3 times. Not much to say about graphic. The background drawings are very nice. Character designs however are disappointing. All the girls are drawn with this "big-eye" anime style that is, quite frankly, ugly. The guys end up looking way better ironically because their eyes are normal scale. The game text goes on and on about how some characters have goddess-like beauty. All I can see are the same 8 year-old giant-eye anime face painted on top of different hairs.Overall, it's not a bad game. I plan to go and buy the sequel right after writing this review to be honest. However, I feel like the game goes too far to get you to buy the sequel. It felt manipulative at times. There's a right way to set up a sequel and a wrong way. This is the wrong way.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono. It is one of the popular Japanese franchise series developed by Aquaplus. The series is a tactics & visual-novel hybrid with an emphasis on story, nice art, and impressive soundtracks. It originated on PC back in 2002. Since then it has led to 2 anime series, with the 3rd currently in the works, and the variety of other spin-off projects. This time DMM GAMES and ShiraVN played a major role in bringing the game to Steam globally.If you're the old gamer who already played the first episode, you can feel the nostalgia, because you can meet the Utawarerumono world after a considerable time has passed from the first episode. And if you are new to this series, you will continue to have an interesting curiosity about the worldview and background of this series. FYI, it's okay to start with this episode, Mask of Deception first.The game is quite kind. For users who don't know the first episode, this game slowly explains on worldviews and terms. As a result, story progression has a rather slow pace, but this means that you can enjoy the game leisurely. Starting with your daily relationship with them, exciting events and battles await you. At least playtime is over 30 hours. This game keeps the basics of SRPG well and the visual novel part is of high quality.Depending on the view point, your evaluation or feelings may vary in this game. When we put each series into the one called Utawarerumono, this trilogy is a masterpiece. But if you look at the Mask of Deception separately, this may be somewhat lacking. The various stories with the characters and the description of the game worldview fully illustrate the appeal of this series, but the main story is rarely progressed.Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception. This is a pretty welcome series. It features nice SRPG & ADV hybrid with much more polished anime artworks and details. In Japan, the series has sold hundreds of thousands of copies. Of course, this second episode may be somewhat lacking as a standalone. Main story progress is slower and the number of battles is relatively small compared to other episodes. Nevertheless, if you remember this game and its animations, this will be a good gift for you, and new users will be a good opportunity to get to know the charm of the series. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly three years after it was first released in the west on PS4 and Vita, us PC players finally get the chance to play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the second and third games in the Utawarerumono series. It's about time honestly, as these are some games I have been wanting to play since I first watched the anime adaptation years ago.So for those unfamiliar with it, Utawarerumono is a series of visual novels with tactical RPG elements. The gameplay consists of the player going from reading various story events and dialogue to tactical, turn-based battles on a grid. As with most VNs that have gameplay elements, the focus is not on the gameplay, but rather on the story. However, with Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the gameplay is actually pretty good and doesn't feel like it was just tacked onto the experience. It may be no Disgaea, but it has a decent amount of depth to it at least, much more so than I often see with such VN hybrids. The game also provides a couple difficulty options to accommodate for both those that just want to experience the story and those that want more challenging gameplay. On normal difficulty, the battles are pretty much a breeze, but on hard difficulty, not so much.As for the actual story, well, that's something that Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth do really well. Although Mask of Deception is technically the second game in the series, it is set up in such a way as to make it easy for newcomers to enjoy. I personally have never played the first game (which is simply titled "Utawarerumono" and does not have an official English release yet) and had no problems getting into Mask of Deception. The same cannot be said for Mask of Truth though, which absolutely requires that you play Mask of Deception first, lest you be really confused as to what's going on. For those that still want to experience the first game in some form, the 2006 anime is generally considered a good adaptation. I watched it years ago and, while I may not remember much of it, I liked it enough to want to get into the games.Once you actually get into the story, you'll be met with some well-written characters, a vibrant fantasy setting that's big on world-building, and some pretty good overall pacing. The games provide a good mix of serious storytelling and more character-oriented slice of life scenes as well. In fact, I like to think of the two games as brothers. Mask of Deception is the younger brother, who is rather innocent and just wants to have fun in this fantasy world with all of its neat characters. Mask of Truth, on the other hand, is the older brother who has lost his innocence and has experienced the hardships of life. While Mask of Deception does have its serious moments, Mask of Truth is when the real story story kicks in, when everything starts coming together. It's quite the ride and there's a good reason why Mask of Truth is sitting at the #12 spot on VNDB's list of highest-rated visual novels.The art and music, as with the story, are also pretty good in both games. I ran the game at 1440p and, while that is an upscale from 720p, the art looked fine and I didn't notice any blatantly blurry assets or backgrounds. It was definitely some good news, as I'm a big fan of the fantasy aesthetic that the games go for. The music also perfectly matches this aesthetic, with a great blend of energetic battle themes and more laid-back, traditional tracks for the game's dialogue scenes. As someone that has already been listening to these soundtracks for years, it was cool to finally hear this music in-game.And of course, seeing as how these two games have never been released on PC, I should mention the quality of their port. To sum it up, it's pretty good as far as VN ports go. There's all the standard settings one would expect in a VN release, including text speed, auto-mode speed, skip options, and a voice cutoff toggle. However, both games go one step further with fullscreen, borderless, and window options, multiple resolution support, completely rebindable keyboard controls, protagonist voice toggling, and even customizable button prompts dependent on what type of controller you're using. Some of these may sound pretty standard, but with visual novels, sometimes they are hard to come by, so it's nice to see them included here.And before I wrap up this review, I should bring up the censorship question. Both games were released as 15+ titles in Japan, so there's no H-scenes like in the original 2002 PC game. This version of Mask of Truth is the exact same as the Japanese version, but this version of Mask of Deception has one CG that has been changed from the Japanese release. I'll go ahead and throw that CG up on-screen so you can see what was changed. It's a very minor change, but I know that a lot of VN fans are passionate about the subject, so it needs to be noted regardless.Overall though, both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are solid games all things considered. Great art, great music, gameplay that actually doesn't feel like a distraction from the main story, and a story that's both unique and well-written. The two games have a lot going for them and the fact that they're actually decent PC ports is also a nice bonus. It's about time we got them on PC and now it's just a wait to complete the trilogy with the release of Prelude to the Fallen, a remaster of the first game that is also slated to release on PC.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a pretty old and famous series (especially in Japan). The first game released in 2002 and was ported to consoles later. It was an adult tactical role-playing visual novel. Yes, adult, there's a lot of R18 scenes in it. However, it was not the main focus of the game. Both the writing and gameplay was pretty much excellent, leaving positive feedback from players and reviews everywhere.  Later in 2006 an anime adaptation was released, featuring great animation (for 2006) and amazing OST.  I watched the anime about 12 years ago and around that time also completed the original 2002 PC game with an english fan translation. The main point here is that even if you didn't play original game or didn't watch anime, you can still fully enjoy Utawarerumono: Mask of DeceptionRemake for the first game been already released in english under a title Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen, so it's just a matter of time when it will be available on Steam. It's already confirmed that all 3 games will be on PC. 1. Utawarerumono(2002) or (remake) Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen (will be available later on Steam)2. Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception 3. Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth - the grand finale of this series.  Okay, the most important information right off the bat.EAT THIS, WINDOWS 10!I switched to Windowed Mode and didn't got into any troubles so far.I. , i tried to play with both for awhile to check. I settled down with a gamepad, though. Any gamepad is fine, as long as it resembles something like XBox or Dualshock controllers.II. The second most concern i saw is "720p/30FPS". Oh, come on! This is a visual novel with turn-based strategy RPG gameplay, what would 60 FPS accomplish here? Better text scrolling speed? The game is perfectly fine as it is. It would be an entirely different matter if it was an action/fast-paced game, though. III. And the last one , there was only 1 problem scene, where's a small kid received some spanks. I'm sure it was done because some crazy countries may see that as "OMFG, CHILD ABUSE! TO THE COURT, COMRADES!", that's why it was changed.  Ugh, if you want to talk about the story, you need to write a book, not a 5000-letter-limit Steam review. Broadly speaking, the game is heavily story driven experience. A girl named Kuon finds you in a forest, while (you) completely blanked out and without any memories to boot. Strangely, you are speaking (and thinking) like a normal modern 20century human, so there's that.Sadly, she doesn't know who you are and where you are from. Thus starts the beginning of your adventures to obtain more information about the unknown fantasy world and yourself.  I must say the story and the characters are especially well written. Some people may be biased towards JP games due to a lot of cringe/facepalm moments, however, Utawarerumono doesn't have those. Of course, there's some traditional JP fanservice scenes, but they are hella fun & hilarious. Main character Haku is especially well done, everything he says or do follow common sense or situation he's in right now. I can't praise MC Voice actor enough for an amazing job he did, making it x10 more hilarious due to his great VA skills.  - , with gorgeous character art, backgrounds and FULL VOICEOVER. (with pretty famous VA's to boot)- During visual novel stuff you can just enjoy the story and character interactions, however, sometimes the game will ask you where you want to go and will offer some prompts.The story is quite rich and some scenes may take awhile, so you can grab a cup of tea.As for battle gameplay, in the beginning the game will ask you either about Normal or Hard difficulty, feel free to take up the Hard difficulty if you want a bit more challenge.Unlike other games, Hard difficulty will offer more enemies on each stage, thus increased your EXP and such. Leveling here is done in two ways:- When your unit attack, you will receive an EXP after attacking. This is similar to old Front Mission and Vanguard Bandits games.- When you finish a new stage, you will receive A HUGE LOAD of EXP for first time clear, up to a few levels if you don't grind.Grinding stages has it benefits, since you can acquire extra DP and use them to increase the stats of your choice. is not really complex here, with HP/ATK/DEF/SPD. There's elements in the game too, you can check menu to confirm strong/weak elements anytime in the battle, so don't fret too much, you don't need to remember it.  In order to keep the player busy and not sleeping during battle parts, the game follow the tradition of the first game from 2002. During your attack, there's an event where you need to press your action button in synch to deliver a 100% critical hit. For example, a combo attack consisting of 3 hits will do a 100% critical hit with each strike if you press the button with correct timing. Critical hits do more damage, especially true for casters.There's two types of event like that, in one you need to press button and in another you need to hold it and release at the right moment. That one with the "hold" is related to spellcaster characters mostly. would be "Rewind" which allows you to "go back in time" up to 50 last turns during your battles. Didn't get that juicy Crit? Rewind and try again.Honestly, i think 50 is way too much xD Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a briliant strategy JRPG with well written story, unique characters and fair battle system. Good job on PC port, featuring support for Windows 7 (even if not mentioned) and adapted controls for KB+M. - This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: just kidding.(I have little playtime as I have already finished both the games on PS4. Bought it again to support devs.  )Gameplay for both games is ...subjective? Hard is easy, redo function makes it childs-play. However this is a Visual Novel foremost and the "SRPG" sections are to engage you in the battle sequences, otherwise the tale of epic battles just falls flat when told in VN format. Thus, having it be easy to breeze through allows it to be engaging enough to engross you in a battle, yet doesn't require you to engage your brain and you can watch the "scene" unfold like a movie. 4/10 SRPG, but 8/10 for overall concept of it.Drawn CGs are great, 3D graphics are from the PS3 era, with weird animations and slightly-deformed models. 9/10 CGs, 5/10 3D. 8/10 overall. (math don't work like that, I know)Music 10/10 The soundtrack excites you in battle, makes whacky scenes adorable, sends dread in tense situations, but most of all: Hits. Right. In. The. Feels.Music is extremely well done, and really sets this aside from other visual novels.Mask of Deception sacrifices itself for an 10/10 sequel.  9/10 for character and world building though. 7/10 overall for this game's plot.10/10Would be a 8/10 if they had to squeeze character introductions and world building into the playtime of Mask of Truth. But with that done in Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth just has to plow through with an amazing story. 50+ hours of an amazing mix of an epic war story with slice-of-life moments, and barely any of it is spent for expanding the main cast since you've already spent 50+ hours doing that last game, leaving us with a fantastic story of Action, Drama, Romance, War, Despair and Excitement. Words can't describe how simply marvelous it is.11/10 overall experience playing both games.Highly recommended.Caution : Final moments of the saga will hook you to your screen, so ensure you have a lot of free time. Will leave a massive void in your soul after the game ends, that may take weeks to recover from.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Play this game ONLY if you are going to play the entire trilogy, because its basically a very long prologue to the third and final game. You can play the third game without it, but you will get more out of the experience if you play this one first, and you will get more out of this game if you've played the first one. Also, final important note, the Protagonist DOES get BETTER. It might seem unbelievable while playing, but it's true.Long Version: Ok, so if you've played the first game, Prelude to the Fallen, this game is going to feel familiar, but comparatively light. The game is essentially a visual novel with occasional tactical combat elements. Whereas games 1 and 3 feel nearly half and half visual novel and tactical game. This one is more like 2/3 or 3/4 visual novel with very, very little combat by comparison. The combat itself is also significantly less deep and fleshed out then it is in either the first or third games.At first this game has seemingly little connection to the first game, despite being a sequel, it clearly takes place in the same world, but in a different country across the sea from where the first game takes place. You play Haku, a man who awakens with amnesia and slowly rediscovers his past along the way, allowing him to ask the same kinds of questions we the player would ask if unfamiliar to the world. (My understanding is that this game was made with the assumption that most players wouldn't have played the first game since they were released rather far apart. [upwards of 10 years]) A small spoiler that I believe makes the game more enjoyable is this: (Skip the line below if you don't want it.)Kuon, the secondary protagonist and character who finds Haku at the beginning of the game, is the daughter of your character from the first game.Knowing this brings a lot of player to game connection improving context to the dialogue and character interactions as the game progresses. (At least in my opinion). The story follows Haku as you make friends and come under the employ of a high ranking government official who is exactly as wonderful a person as he seems. Over time the group becomes one of your employer's greatest shadow assets, and helps shape the fate of the kingdom, mostly for the better. Along the way Haku slowly regains his memories, which he learns make him a person of particular importance to this specific land and ultimately the group gets caught up in events that will change the kingdom forever, at great emotional cost to Haku and those close to him. The story ends on a bit of a cliffhanger because, as mentioned in the TLDR, it really is a giant setup for the following game.Most of the game chronicles the day to day lives of the primary cast, clearly covering the course of several months (possibly a year or more?). The group grows closer, bonds are forged, and shenanigans ensue. In terms of flavor, those familiar with anime will recognize all the the tropes they're familiar with here, for better or for worse. The game is unnecessarily cheesecakey, but for the most part they are comparatively classy about it, there's just a lot of fan service that is clearly there for that reason alone. Despite this, character interactions feel genuine, the occasional gems found in reference to the first game are almost all good, most of the primary cast is likeable. Personally I can tell there's a culture clash, because certain repeated interactions clearly considered "normal" in-universe try my patience, but overall its enjoyable. My primary problems with the game are that the combat is less complex and enjoyable than in either of the other two games, and that for the majority of the game I find Haku unlikeable, especially in comparison to your character from the first game. Who is great almost from the get go. Haku is possessed of qualities that aren't uncommon in protagonist characters both negative and positive, in fact he possesses several of the same traits as the primary character from the first game; but they are largely portrayed in a less than flattering way. For example he proudly proclaims that he is a layabout who tries to avoid work and would gladly spend his time drinking rather than being of use to society. But one of his most useful traits is his genuine cunning and in a classic "give the hard job to a lazy person" way, he often comes up with brilliant plans and solutions for the groups problems. But most of the time this is not done in a way that makes us as players look at the protagonist in a good light and even when it IS framed positively for us, he gets no credit from the rest of the cast for it. This character framing is clearly intentional, especially with hindsight from playing the third game. But having to play an unlikeable character through what felt like a very long story, was draining and dull enough that were it not for the very intense and fantastic final few chapters of the game, I might have been uninterested in picking up the third one.That being said, the trilogy as a whole is pretty fun, and the stuff you'll get because of playing this game made putting up with it worth it as the final game played on.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be alarmed by the playtime, I've finished both games on the PS Vita and bought them on PC because I just love the series so much.I found out about Utawarerumono by complete accident through a random pic of Kuon on Telegram, the name sounded somehow... familiar, so I looked into it and found the games, started playing the first one on PC and it was love at first sight, it is now my absolute favorite game series of all time.I'll make a proper review of the first game once the remake comes out on Steam, but I'll say it's absolutely necessary to play it first in order to enjoy Mask of Deception to its fullest, so either play the original 2000 game, or wait for the remake.It's a VN game with some tactical battles, the gameplay has some neat mechanics and I enjoy it quite a bit, but it's absolutely not the core here, don't come in expecting a fully-fledged strategy RPG, the focus here is on the story, and some stretches can go for dozens of hours of reading with no combat happening for a good while, so know what you're getting into beforehand. However, I was never really a big VN kind of guy, and Utawarerumono completely changed my mind, so if you don't usually play VNs, still try getting into it with an open mind, and you might be pleasantly surprised.Mask of Deception hooked me as much as the original did, the characters are instantly likeable and the world-building is top-notch. Haku is a very lovable idiot and Kuon feels like a mom.It's a slow-paced game, but in a very good way, you'll come to appreciate the "slice-of-life" like moments much more when things really start kicking into gear, the character development and interactions are just amazing.The ending to this game is one of my absolute favorite endings out of any media ever, and is one of the most brilliant sequel hooks I've ever seen. Mask of Deception, in the end, sort of feels like a MASSIVE PROLOGUE to Mask of Truth, and I admit I was slightly disappointed by the fact it has fewer battles than the original, but don't let that fool you into thinking it's not a worthwhile experience. It's still an absolutely amazing game with memorable moments on its own right, and the fact that it takes so much time to develop the world and the characters, is what makes Mask of Truth such a delightful experience. Mask of Truth wouldn't be nearly as good as it is, without Mask of Deception preparing the ground for it first.The two games should be taken in as a whole, Mask of Deception being the AMAZINGLY GOOD prologue that is only made even better by how absolutely brilliant Mask of Truth is.This is more like a 2-parter, and I'll talk more about the games in my Mask of Truth review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is resolution locked to 720p. If you have the computer specs to run an upscaler I'd recommend it. Magpie -  - 2d art comparison - 3d battle comparisonScreen shots don't do it justice. The image is very blurry without it but looks great with it imo. In game 4k vs Anime4k 3x.Took me 28.5 hours to read this at a quick pace on hard mode according to my save. Post game battles were not done.This is a sequel to Prelude of the Fallen and anyone telling you not to play it is leading you wrong. It isn't just reoccurring characters in a wink wink sort of way. Story bits aren't explained since you already know them from the first game.The story starts off pretty slow with not much going on. Mostly slice of life antics for the first 15 hours. Then it starts getting interesting and stays that way up until the end. The ending sets up the next game in a great way and makes you want to start it right away. Some don't seem to like the main character. I thought it was refreshing to see a normal person instead of a perfect JRPG hero out to save the world. He's lazy and probably has a drinking problem. But when push comes to shove he finds a way to make it work. Grows quite a bit over the game.The battle system is massively improved over the first game. The problem is there isn't a whole lot of it this time. Only 17 stages (although a few have two in one) compared to the 36 in the first. The game is much more balanced so you aren't a walking dead machine this time. BP cost scales with each use so putting all into attack is possible but it adds up. BP is also not given out as much compared to the first. Your units are still pretty powerful but the enemies this time are as well. On hard they can easily kill your units in 1-2 attacks. There are a lot more skills and customization of items. Zeal gains and uses have been tweaked for a much more fun system. I find the final battle poorly balanced around hard since without grinding you are 10-14 levels below it and it'll AOE 1-shot your units. Lowered to normal to just quickly beat the game.Overall great game. Really enjoyed the characters and their interactions. Can't wait to read the finale.For being an all ages game this is a lot more risqué than the prequel in CGs and text.

_childDocuments_.review: Personal impression about the visual novel perspective:This is my second playthrough, I played it first on the PS Vita, and decided to get it too on Steam. Don't expect much from Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, from most of its plot you'll have a tranquil, relatively shallow story with not so many successive battles, you might even spend hours with just listening to the character's interactions without a single battle, from time to time you might feel like doing some "Free Battles" just so you can get something interesting to do; in itself the game is quite slow and it can get boring at times, if you lie in bed while playing you might have the risk of falling asleep (happened to me a couple of times). The game starts to get good on the 2nd half and in overdrive at the end.Why do I recommend it after talking so bad about it, you may ask? Because the sequel is worth playing this game, enduring its slowness and from time to time boring exchanges is worth it, its the very detailed and extremely important buildup to what happens in Mask of Truth. Endure the game, try to enjoy it, try not to miss a thing since some developments in Mask of Truth are related to what happens here (same with Prelude to the Fallen, although I played the original translated by a fan a long time ago when Steam wasn't as famous as it is now and with ALL the content ;)), I might play it too too see how they changed it in the remake.On another note, if you are playing it because of the anime, then you'll definitely feel like the anime left too many important things out. Yes, this game is better than the anime of course.Personal impression about the strategy perspective:This is a very simple tactical game, this is no Fire Emblem, but it is still quite interesting to keep you enjoying the battles and immersed in the story, as sporadic as these battles might be. All battles are fun and can be hard at times (mostly because of a flaw), of course, you can power level out of those battles since you have access to the Free Battle system, that allows you to repeat previously done battles to gain BP (Bonus Points) that lets you use these points to improve the character's stats at a cost. If you are having issues with a battle, doing a couple of free battles might help you on your way out.Pros:- Lengthy story with lots of details and character development.- Fun and simple battle system.- Lovable characters from start to finish (<3 Kuon).- Plays with your nostalgia quite a bit, making it enjoyable.Cons:- Too much character development makes it feel repetitive at times.- Battle system has a flaw (won't spoil what it is; and was fixed in Mask of Truth).- It feels like the game takes too much time getting serious, and when it does... THE END.Persevere through this game and you'll be rewarded in full with Mask of Truth.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is the longest visual novel i have played yet. It is a bit shorter than it's sequel, Mask of Truth. I have finished it in 37 hours and i am glad a sequel is available, as i am writing this review i can't wait to read what is next. My first thoughts was that the game looks pretty good and that it can't be bad if the developers bothered to remaster a series that started in 2002. I can feel it being old enough since it acts differently than modern anime, its old in the good way. It is some kind of Isekai, the main character (supposedly you) loses his memories and wakes up almost naked in the cold of the snow. He would've died 3 times if it was possible if it wasn't for his luck of being saved by Kuon, the girl that gives him the name of Haku. This is where their adventure begins, adding more people to their party, making things right and protecting the ones who are dear to them. It looked boring at first, but this is how many good shows begin. At the start it gives you a feeling of disgust, then you wonder why you like it as the story gets better, and at the end you absolutely love it. The graphics are good for everything except battle maps, but they didn't decrease the quality of my experience whatsoever. The soundtrack is also very good, would be a waste if you muted it to play whatever you are listening to daily. The characters are not animated, a bit of a shame. The size is not huge compared to some other VN ports i know, good for people with not so much space like me. 9.5/10 - A great story, would watch the anime even if the same things happen in it. Very sentimental, exactly what i am aiming for in games and anime. My favorite visual novel series for now.If you want more detailed reviews on awesome games consider following , our curator page.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is the second game in the Utawarerumono Series. It is a visual novel 80% of the time and the rest are turn based RPG with tactical combat.MoD start with a young man suffering amnesia lost in a mountain and trough a series of events he came to the capital city of the country Yamato doing odd jobs as "fixer" while eventually stumbling into a political schemes and became deeply involved. it is a slow game, its purpose are to introduce players to its world and characters trough the MC's point of view. depend of your point of view, this slow, deliberate worldbuilding might feel like a slow crawl, but for me it works as a great introduction to the world. their major political powers, major figures, also your friends and the protagonist. as Phase 1 of the Mask series, Mask of Deception works very well. you will learn to love the characters, the world and become fully immersed. MoD ends with one of the best sequel hook ever created that will kick the story into high gear and a very satisfying emotional climax. the first 80% of the game are relaxed, almost slice of life-y and the end are like an accelerating rocket pushing to escape orbit.the combat itself is simple, easy and mostly non intrusive. you have a grid of squares, each unit have their own move and attack range. the attack are separated with different skills, in with each skills have a QTE input that determine your critical hit like Paper Mario / Super mario RPG. music is great, there is no english dub but the japanese voice acting is great.if you like game with detailed worldbuilding, lovable and various cast of characters but interesting underlying mystery check out the game

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but with a few flawsFirst off, the gameplay is a lot better. Improved combat systems, better character progression, better maps and, more importantly, better difficulty options. Normal is about equal to Prelude hard mode, and hard mode is actually a decent challenge in this which was nice. Aside from the final boss (which was annoying and overtuned on Hard), the game is very well balanced and fun. No more stacking attack with bonus points (which work differently) and just one shotting everythingThe problem? There isn't enough gameplay.The game has WAY TOO MUCH FILLER. The filler is much better than it was in Prelude and the writing quality is better overall (there were a bunch of scenes that got a genuine laugh out of me VS Prelude where I felt uncomfortable half the time), but it's spaced out so poorly. For most of the game you can easily go up to 5 hours without a single combat section. I like filler but I don't like it when it delays the gameplay so much. Prelude to the Fallen felt like a standard SRPG but this just felt like a raw VN. There were so few gameplay segments that by the time I unlocked my characters final strikes, I was already on the final boss so it didn't even matter.Also, the overall story is worse than Preludes. Mask of Deception basically serves as an entire games worth of worldbuilding and character development for it's sequel, and because of that nothing really happens until the very end of the game. If Prelude to the Fallen was a 9/10, this was a 7/10. Get it on sale because you need to play it before you can play Mask of Truth. Either that or watch the anime. The game is 90% VN, 10% tactics game so you'd probably get a better experience with the anime if you don't like filler or VN storytelling

_childDocuments_.review: I remember reading Utwarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen & giving it a rather mixed review, citing average gameplay & rushed, disjointed storytelling as being the biggest negatives of an otherwise enjoyable experience. My willingness to recommend that game was contingent on how much I might enjoy the sequels & whether or not I found the payoff to be worthwhile - Sadly, two thirds of the way in, I'm still waiting to make up my mind.To start with a positive, the game is absolutely stunning, to the point where I'd call it one of the best looking releases I've seen so far... In the VN portions of the title, that is. The SRPG sections are still stuck looking like early PS2 games up-ressed a bit, but that doesn't detract from the experience in any meaningful way besides being a bit jarring the first time or two. Some of the character art is a little weaker than others, but overall, the game looks spectacular & the variety in sprites really helps sell the current emotions of each individual. The OST is a small step up from the original title, with a few new tracks complimenting a strong selection of returning pieces from the original, although I didn't find it to be spectacular overall.The new cast is arguably a bit stronger overall than the original, though there's enough familiarity there for it to be a comfortable experience coming from Prelude. You could also jump straight in to Mask of Deception & not miss out on any major story points, but I'd recommend not doing that, as the commonality between setting & overall theme makes the whole experience stronger when enjoyed as a package. The world building remains excellent, even if some of my concerns from the first title continue to be an issue in this one.My biggest gripe is a carryover from the first game that I struggled to put into words until I actually sat down & thought about what it was that was annoying me so much. During the slice of life periods of the game, you're given a list of mini-stories that you need to complete before the main story itself continues, but this selection process comes in place of a naturally flowing story. You're not really choosing between which little side adventures you want to go on because you have to do them all anyway, so what you're really doing is excusing the developer for being either unable or unwilling to write one long, cohesive slice of life section, instead providing individual story chunks that can sometimes feel jarring when read in a particular order. I'm a big fan of slice of life in general, but I found that these little "choice" sections took me out of the experience on more than one occasion, which is a shame since the characters & the world itself are very impressive.As for the combat, my overwhelming feeling towards it is one of apathy. It's fine, & if you decide to go into the options menu & speed it up, it's almost completely ignorable. Playing on Normal, I didn't bother looking at any spells or even equipping any items until the last encounter of the game, partly because encounters were just mind-numbingly easy & tedious, & partly because a good 80% of the encounters you come across are just busywork with little to no meaning in the overall plot of the story.All that said, I'd still say Mask of Deception has the better story & pacing overall compared to its predecessor, so if you enjoyed that, then you're very likely to enjoy the sequel as well. None of the things I personally take issue with are new, either - If you didn't mind them in the first title, you won't mind them here either.In conclusion, as much as I enjoy the world & the characters (both of which are fantastic), there's just been too many minor issues up until this point that have culminated in an overall feeling of annoyance towards the game itself - Mostly because it feels like it's so very nearly excellent, & that's what hurts the most. If not for those immersion breaking interludes I'm sure the tone of my review would be almost fanatical in its positivity, but this sort of choice system has put me off other titles in the past, & will surely put me off titles in the years to come. There's a lot to love about Utwarerumono, & hopefully you can play it without being affected by certain elements as much as I have, but me personally? I'll be heading into the final chapter of the trilogy hoping for something to make all of it seem worthwhile in the end, despite loving so much about the core of the story & its characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen does everything its predecessor did just as well. Expanding this large world to an even bigger scale, where all characters fit perfectly. Bonds strengthened over time, memories of trifling everyday matters and good times - this is all the characters hoped for, so how dare anyone take that from them? They will not falter to this so-called fate.These fifty hours of meeting new people, being greeted by familiar faces, caring for one another, almost felt too short. Perhaps it's just me, but I wanted even more from this story. Acting as a stepping stool for the last title of the series, it set an amazing narrative to be continued.I can't praise this one enough, but the only thing I will not forget myself for not mentioning is the voice acting, especially Haku's. I have never in my life heard such great voice acting, and all that is Fujiwara Keiji's work, who unfortunately passed away last year, may he rest easy. His work will live on forever.So, just experience the unique work Utawarerumono is. Every second of it is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably never write a full review on this page, because you absolutely have to play Mask of Truth for the full experience (which in itself can be considered an issue), so I'll use this space for a fair warning for everyone getting into this franchise as a whole:The plot warnings aside, here are some key points to be aware of if you are interested in this as a game.In summary, do not eye this as an sRPG, it's more a Visual Novel than anything else.Other things to note are the 720p/30FPS lock. The game also behaves extremely strange performance-wise when you try to capture it, though this will vary depending on setup.Nevertheless, this niche franchise weaves a tale representing very strong emotional themes that isn't quite done like this in any other franchise or media that I'm aware of. If you are looking to lose yourself in a beautifully weaved adventure spanning 3 games and aren't afraid that this is basicly more an audio-visual reading experience than a game, then this franchise is for you. _childDocuments_.review: It’s primarily the tale of Haku, the aforementioned amnesiac, who awakes in an unfamiliar tent under the stewardship of Kuon. Feeling some kind of responsibility towards her new ward, she sets out to ensure he’s able to make a life for himself without her, despite having an absolute blank slate for a past. Except, it’s never really that easy; Haku’s not especially interested in finding a job and doesn’t grab on to any of the threads of purpose that Kuon often tries to provide him. He has no established trade; that vanished along with the rest of his memories, and he isn’t especially skilled in anything obvious. Then giant bugs attack. Then the pair fall in with a group of travelling guardsmen to repel them and befriend a travelling princess riding an adorable oversized bird. Subterranean slime monsters become a thing, bandits need saving from banditier bandits and there’s a near obligatory miscommunication involving public baths. Eventually, the group arrives at the massive capital of Yamato. It’s here all the heavy drinking starts.The plot proper certainly starts to slow down once the group hits the capital. Battles become a lot less frequent and big stand-alone events become less common. Instead, Mask of Deception, very gently, starts making your care about its cast of seemingly random miscreants. It does so by making you a creepy voyeur while they simply get on with the mundane activities of their lives. Haku, it turns out, will never be content with being the typical amnesia-suffering protagonist, supplied as an undisguised self-insert for the player. That kind of nonsense takes far too much effort. Instead, he’s content to coast as much as he can, easily manipulated with promises of free booze and days off.Working within the roving guards inside the capitol, he’s given a base of operations and a slowly growing collection of people to work with. Kuon, for her part, tags along under the guise of a motherly caretaker, hoarding all Haku’s earnings and proving a small allowance so he doesn’t blow it all on a grand night out. But she makes choices that belie that role, constantly accomplishing her requirements for sticking around, but then reinventing them so she doesn’t have to leave the group.It’s little personal evolutions like that which make Utawarerumono’s hard focus on character building so engaging. It’s rarely ham-fisted, always dropping little titbits of information you might initially decipher as completely throw away, only to present themselves in deeper shades of relevance later. It hides things in plain sight, rewarding the reader by letting them work things out for themselves. For example, the game never once tells you how Kuon and Haku met; he just woke up in her tent one day and that was that. But I know. And I know simply because of a series of heavy silences or guilty glances or loaded one-word replies through several tense situations. It’s brilliant writing that’s confident in both its own execution and the reader’s intelligence to put everything together without it being presented in crayon. It painstakingly builds everyone this idyllic little existence they carve for themselves, shows how they each grow within each other’s company, within responsibilities both earned and restricted. But it’s never destined to last forever. You know that. Perhaps more importantly, they know that, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I had postponed this review till the time I could complete Mask of Truth and now that I have, I can confidently say that I enjoyed Mask of Deception as much as I enjoyed Mask of Truth. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great visual novel with a surprisingly deep tactical combat system.  If you're interested in a fantasy story with adult characters, great writing, beautiful art & music, and crazy plot twists, you should play this game -- especially because it's necessary to play it before the sequel, Mask of Truth, which is easily one of the most amazing stories I've ever experienced.To break it down a little further, this game is about 80% visual novel to 20% SRPG.  There's usually an hour or two of reading that is then followed up by a battle in which you control several characters on a grid-based map.  The story is a little slow-paced at first; this game is very heavy on worldbuilding and has a ton of details about its culture, food, and history.  If you enjoy digging into a complex setting, there's a lot to enjoy here.  The character development is also very nuanced and deliberate; perhaps the worst thing about it is that it's not obvious just how well everything is done until you replay this game again after finishing Mask of Truth so that you can see exactly how all of the character arcs are set up.  The first few arcs in the game move slowly and spend a lot of time introducing you to characters and their casual lives, but after the plot really gets moving, it's a rollercoaster to the end that finishes with a series of amazing plot twists.  Do keep in mind that this is not a standalone game by any means; everything here is a prologue that leads into the events of Mask of Truth.  On top of that, this is technically the second game in the series; it's designed so that newcomers can play it without being familiar with the original, but you'll miss some cameos and references, and knowledge of the original is really necessary to enjoy the final game.As far as gameplay goes, every character is unique; there are no classes or generic units, and every character has a unique set of abilities.  The stages in the story are fairly easy; there is a Hard difficulty mode, but SRPG veterans will still find that to be on the easy side.  The game does, however, have several post-game maps that ramp up the difficulty and really show off the complexity of the battle system, and I highly recommend playing the post-game if you like the gameplay at all.I would be remiss if I didn't note that there are some technical issues.  This is a port of a PS4 game, and the port does a lot of things right; it's stable, keyboard inputs are fully remappable, and it has several different joystick button and key icon sets to choose from.  It does have one big problem, which is that the internal rendering is locked at 720.  If you're playing on a higher-resolution monitor, there are noticeable jagged edges on the font and on the 3D models in combat.  It's not game-breaking, and you can make it look better by using ReShade to tweak anti-aliasing and scaling options, but it's still annoying; hopefully the developer will address it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Deception is the start to one of my favorite stories of all time.  The journey of the lazy schemer and reluctant hero Haku, his self-proclaimed guardian Kuon, and all the other colorful characters is unforgettable.  If you're hankering for a world you can just lose yourself in for 60+ hours, you can't go wrong with this game and its sequel.  It deftly mixes comedy and drama, action and romance, slice of life hijinks and political intrigue in a way few others have managed.  Fair warning: these games are visual novels first, strategy second.  Deception only has a few battle maps, actually, so don't go into this expecting Fire Emblem with cat girls. It's more like a grand fantasy novel, where you can participate in the battles.  The pacing reminds me quite a bit of Trails in the Sky, and if you liked the first and second chapters of those games, you can expect a pretty similar pace to those two games here in Deception and its sequel Truth, with Deception taking its sweet time building up the world and its cast, and Truth really hammering out the big climactic moments.I discovered these games originally on PS4 and didn't expect much--figured it was just going to be a bargain bin anime game, but it's way more than that.  Please give these games a chance--they might surprise you like they did me.

_childDocuments_.review: While you can start with this game, you definitely should play  first. While being its own story, the game rewards players of the first game with callbacks and characters that make the experience 10x sweeter.From a technical aspect, the game is a massive step-up from the previous game, which isn’t surprising as Prelude came out 13 years before. The gameplay is more complex, making it much more enjoyable than the straightforward approach of the previous entry.The story is slow at first, choosing to develop its cast first and familiarize the player in this new area of the world. The Slice of Life sections are a treat and the stellar voice acting & OST will have you immersed. Once all the pieces are in play, the game shows you what it’s been building towards. it's not as emotional as the first game, but it perfectly sets up the stakes for the final game. The ending was once of the best cliffhangers I’ve experienced in media and had me staring at my ceiling throughout the entire credits.

If you're here searching for a decent story, I think you should play this game. Be open-minded for the first half, and just enjoy the slice-of-life ride. It's an investment for the nuances for the second half, The story just keeps getting better and better as it progresses (and you need to continue to the next game. _childDocuments_.review: So Utawarerumono, if you think this review is unbiased go somwehere else. In this review im going to talk not only about mask of deception but also mask of truth and prelude to the fallen, why you may ask? If you start with mask of deception you most likely don't know wbout utawarerumono or it's modern name prelude to the fallen, but there is no need to write review for mask of truth because entire existance of mask of truth is very big spoiler, dont look at steam page dont google anything because it's based out of quite big spoiler from mask of deception.Before I end this lengthy introduction it is time to say something quite important. You can start with mask of deception, not reccomended but works, you wont know refferences and you are going to get some spoilers about it but it's good enough, but for any reason dont go with mask of truth if you dont know 2 previous titles, even anime from 1st game will be good enough because 1 and 2 are prelude, foundation for 3rd which connects old with new, 2002 and 2014 sequel which culminated in 2016.Why utawarerumono? There are few factors which im going to write about in this review 1story2characters3musicPart 1:I'm going to talk here about 1 and 2(im going to reffer to games by numbers since its going to be lengthy anyway)So let's start with 1 it starts with your good old(well 2002 but it was old back then) amnesia start, what I love about the story is that you dont get final goal, all you have is some things happen and you end up running a nation and then what? care about it and that's all, story escalates things about his past surface and story gets quite interesting from that point.2 Here things get quite original, in this story you are not hero saving the kingdom, you are his little helper, this game is slower than 1 since you can treat it like just half of a game, just like Suga(writer of the story) made a game and higher ups told him that is two game material and they released it so(not blaming them, this game is reaaaaaaally long), this part is more about building the world, and introducing new region to the story, and laying ground for events from final part of the trilogy, it takes it's time but it's not empty, story happens it's just..well first half of the game, all spicy parts are always for 2nd half which is separate game even longer than this game(60-70 hours compared to over 80)Story is lead through two phases, first you have your good old slice of life till things start to happen and you embark on adventure or do some task important for the story, and once it's complete hero comes home and lives his daily life while you get to know more of the characters he accompanies which leads us to:part 2 charactersThis is where strength of utawarerumono comes from, imagine spending tens of hours with characters, you know their best and worst, and they are written very well. You really get to like this bunch of characters, main or companions or just episodic characters.Hakuoro, main character of 1st, it is your responsible likeble leader, nothing exceptional which doesn't mean that it's not a great character, his supporting cast is absolutely top notch you really feel life in them, even opposition is more like someone being unlucky to be on wrong side of a spear rather than villain doing evil for sake of it.Haku, which is main character of 2, here is what i absolutely praise and love. Imagine slacker always looking for chance to talk his way out of thw work and go drinking with bros, but when situation is dire he can think really quick. The point with this character is to see how he changes in span of two games, the point where he starts and where he ends. It is absolutely most heroic character i ever seen, after what happened in the story you really give him respect for his acts, he may not have power level over 9 thousand but compared to who he is, and how much he can it's quite high ratioAs for supporting cast, since this game is more about worldbuilding and character development, and Suga had 12 years to become better at writing and you have 60-70 hours game instead of 40-ish length of previous game you really get to know there characters from all of the angles and really care what happens with them, if they may be in danger you care more than "oh i like this npc, oh something happened to them, oh whatever" of quite lots of storiesPart 3 music1st and 2nd game have diffrent composers, 2 gets few of tracks adapted for new but it's 3rd game which combines both as it combines two regions and stories into grand finale.When 1st game doesn't have really great soundtrack(in 2002 it didn't even have voice acting) it catches up with songs sung during the gameSimiliar situation happens with 2nd and 3rd, while those have new composer and singer, soundtrack on itself is way more solid and songs are kept in same really high quality state.So final part without number but word:epilogueIf you are here, wow that's quite long review here and you are at this point. So bit of my personal experience with the game, part where it's about me and the game not game itself. It started quite standard, i watched anime, it was absolutely top tier, really high up my list. Year later i decided to give a try to it's source material, at first it was quite pleasant experience but soon i was completely in. Anime suddenly from 10(given quite rare from me) went to medicore and i realized how much utawareumono lost due to shortening the slice of life parts, despite knowing how it ends i went through it with pure passion about it, then it ended, instantly went for sequels. 2nd was worst out of trilogy(dont get me wrong, 1st is full story 2nd is first half 3rd is 2nd half) but i had quite a lot of fun with it, then 3rd and then it was over. This game doesn't hold back on punches to the feels, when it wants you to laugh you laugh at the top of your lungs, when it wants to be serious or sad, it conveys it really hard.  Is it worth it? Absolutely, best story i found to this day, and i'm looking for over 3 years for something that might topple it from the top.As my final words of this review my highest praise reserved only to "that one and only" story:I hope I can live long enough to find something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out as an average slice of life story in an average fantasy world with demi-humans, but is actually a . The start and middle of the game have a lighthearted tone and nothing really amazing happens. The plot starts to develop after that though. _childDocuments_.review: Now that was what called a speechless ending, Mask of Deception truly was a spectacular sequel of the original Utawarerumono (2002), it expanded the world of Utwarerumono perfectly by extremely detailed world-building, solved unanswered questions of its prequel and continued the intriguing lore of Utawarerumono universe. _childDocuments_.review: Pros-Art is bright and adorable.-Characters are cute and interesting initially.-Premise of the story is intriguing initially.-Combat is simple but fun.Cons-Your main character is a designated monkey, the butt of every joke which is the source of 75% of the humor.-The writing gets idiotically stupid to the point of offensive.-Characters quirks become tiresome and grating.-Pacing between story and combat is terrible, you'll forget there's combat after 2-3 hour blocks of story only for the combat to last 5 minutes.While I initially enjoyed this game what is essentially a visual novel must be judged on its story and the story that started fun and intriguing quickly grew grating by the 12 hour mark.To eleborate on your main character being a buttmonkey and why this gets very annoying. Every joke is at his expense. Every misunderstanding will be his fault regardless if it is or not. He rarely deserves the abuse gleefully hurled in his direction but that's whats supposed to make it funny I take it. It was funny... at first. Now its predictable and exhausting.The writing also loses several dozen IQ points around the 10 hour mark when *MILD SPOILERS* your main character who is an amnesiac illiterate whose dangerously weak compared to the fantasy world he's in is made the leader of a group of adventurers. Let that sink in. What's worse, the main female protagonist is a worldly, ultra competent, charming, beautiful traveler and apothecary.  Her being the leader should be obvious but she decides for the main character that he should be, then points out later that him not knowing anything about the world he lives in or being able to read is an embarrassment on the rest of them since he's the leader... see, cuz its funny that everything is his fault... get it? The other characters in your party have even less of a reason to be in an adventuring party but I'll stop to avoid further spoilers.In closing, a charming VN with gameplay that QUICKLY grows wearisome the more you play it unless you check in your brain at the door and chose not to think about to hard about whats going on. I couldn't do that so It overstayed its welcome for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Have been waiting for a long time because I'm not a console player. Finally Utawarerumono has come back to its origins on PC, with the two new sequels. Utawarerumono: Itsuwari no Kamen aka Mask of Deception (MoD) in English, is just a game building up the whole new world (in the future) of the 1st game, where there are more and more people with cultural things. Yes, this game is just the opening of Utawarerumono: Futari no Hakuoro aka Mask of Truth (MoT) (but actually the real meaning when we translated the name to English is "The Two White Kings"), it is definitely a significant step momentum to bring up the plot of the final game to the zenith of epic. Let me say this, Aquaplus decided to release MoD 12 years after the 1st game, so that they have to create out a new story, not really and directly related to the prequel but somehow maintain its original. A lot of guys said that MoT was much better that MoD, I also think that's true. But you really can't deny that MoD literally the 1st thing needed to build up the story in MoT, because if you do not play MoD, how can you know about who is Kuon, who really is Oshtor, what is happening now and etc... in MoT? You can even wonder why Karura and Touka appear here although they were existed only in Utawarerumono: Chiriyuku Mono he no Komoriuta (the 1st game, in english is the title 'Prelude to the Fallen')? So yeah, though MoD is not as good as the 1st game or the last game but this game also has A BUNCH OF universe-building and it's absolutely the 1st step you guys have to take and after that you can move to Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. Thanks for reading guys and hope you buy & enjoy this franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for the newer port of Prelude to the Fallen to be out before playing this game. Having done so here's my spoiler-free review:- Plot is really slow compared to Prelude to the Fallen. The concern here is not so much "there is less combat" in-between (which there is less), but more so the slice of life content seems to barely advance the plot or the personality of the characters. It is OK, but I feel it was executed better in the prior game. - Side Quests menu are not available here: You learn in the first few minutes of the game you can do "Free Battles" (i.e. revisit the battles to grind). This is OK, but in Prelude, they went the extra mile and added side quests. This added a bit of voiced content with battle, which was a nice touch. Considering the plot, they had room to add this here, but they did not.+/- Combat is similar but different from Prelude. This game does not have combo attacks. However, they gave each character more than one combat chain. + No more "healer only unit". Some characters can heal on top of an attack (In your first battle you learn this). + There is some motivation to re-do some free battles for a bit extra voiced content. I will not mention it further, or this would spoil the fun. - There is some really strong wording on some character's translated voices which I don't think matches properly with the character's personality. + Art seems better than Prelude to the fallen. +/- Item system is more shallow: There is less lore to them. Some weapons could also customize the attack pattern in Prelude. Here, items center more in "support role", which may change combat but not so much its effects. There are no specialized items for characters here.+ New ring patterns make things less dull than "press when the circle hits the dot". + Combat from each character is more unique. I can't say more without spoil, but overall the attacks feel less "DPS/Tank/Ranged" and more specialized classes.- In this game, the way you are facing does not affect damage (you can't even position where the character is facing either). In Prelude, you could. Long story short, I played this game after reading it is "35% action here and 65% action on Mask of the Truth". It is indeed the case. Hence, if you are uncertain if this is worth your time, I'd recommend you try Prelude to the Fallen first, I feel that is the better "rounded package". If you like what you see, then you can try this one hoping Mask of Truth will balance the slow pace of this one later. The plot is satisfying, it is just really slow. This game will make more sense if you play Prelude to the Fallen too, which will alleviate the slow burn.-------------Some suggestion for the devs (if they ever read this):In Prelude to the Fallen, at a few missions, you could control the more "generic unit" in the field. None of that in this game,  however. This is a visual novel first and foremost, so I did not hope for this but, it would be nice in future games if we could be given more control on training said units and/or sending them in battles in a way that may affect the visual novel as optional content (much as Prelude had). Considering the plot theme of the games, there is plenty of room for something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Very difficult to rate this game by itself, since it's really one half of a bigger package together with Mask of Truth   But like with the original Utawarerumono (and its remake Prelude to the Fallen), this is a hybrid visual novel/strategy RPG with a strong focus on story. If you're a gameplay-focused player who just wants to battle, skip these games. The plot and characters of this game are a noticeable step up from the original/Prelude, and often maintains a strong pace throughout (can lead to a night or two of continous sleepless gaming), though there are a few sections where you will find "slice of life" segments back to back which can feel a bit stale, and some of the comedy may fall a bit flat. Once again, a strong cast of characters carries this game, and the main characters are all new to this game, while a few returning faces can be encountered every now and then   The game's plot is incomplete on purpose, and is completed in Mask of Truth. So really, only buy this if you plan to play both eventually. The best way to play is to buy the series bundle and to start with Prelude (but not the "complete" bundle because that includes spoiler DLC)
