_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is another fantastic anime game. If you are interested in the series, start with the first one, Prelude of the Fallen. Both games have been fantastic. The first one is split probably 1/3 combat, 1/3 story and 1/3 relationships. This one is about 1/2 relationships and 1/4 combat + 1/4 story. Overall a very satisfying series. I will say that this one ended somewhat abruptly, but I am guessing the final will pick up where this left off.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the second of the trilogy, I think. The first game was very interesting, but had some lengths. This one also has some moments where I thought "I don't care for those secondary intrigues, let me watch the main story", but they were less numerous than in the first.Gameplay wise, I find it better, but also it is a bit lacking some things I loved in the first, i'm not sure what, but maybe a bit too few battles between the VN part?The story and characters are wonderful. I hope that the next game in the trilogy is a sequel because the plot is open and this feels like a first part of a big plot. For anyone who love good VN stories, with a bit of tactical gameplay for the battles, this is a good one. No doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Second entry in a great VN series. Mechanically this is the game that shows its age most as actually the oldest release, as its missing a number of QOL features found in the prequel and the sequel such as exp being earned by all units even if not in the battle, or healers getting exp for healing.This game is very much a title focused on setting up the second part, so its quite slow and more interested in building up and introducing the characters, much like the first entry of an arc of the Trails series. The characters are all great though, and theres alot to like here, and then it ends on a cliffhanger that makes you really want to dive into the final game.I would recommend you play Prelude first for the references to that game made in this (and even more so in Mask of Truth).If there is one main criticism to take with this series on steam, and this applies to all 3 Utaware entries, its the quality of the ports. All 3 games are optimised for 720p, all assets and internal rendering are set for that resolution, and the games are locked to 30fps. There is a dll you can find in the discussions for the mask games that will bump up the internal rendering resolution to your current window resolution, but there's nothing that can be done about the 30fps and hud elements sadly. At least since the game is 90% VN and then a Turnbased gameplay style, the 30fps doesn't hurt it too badly compared to other more action oriented gameplay styles.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second part of Utawarerumono series. In terms of "gameplay" experience, I'd say the combat system is smooth and isn't as rough as the first one. Then again, this is a visual novel with a hint of tactical rpg gameplay to it and not a pure tactical rpg. Do not expect some sort of complicated combat system. The story starts off slow and it has a lot of world building. If you like the first part of the series then you most probably would enjoy this one as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Prelude to the Fallen in my opinion but that could be because Prelude was my first ever VN so it will always hold that place of introducing me to a new genre. That being said.. GOD these games are outstanding, if you haven't played these or even haven't played a VN before just do yourself a favour and buy it. Make sure you play them in order though because the stories are back to back. Just beautiful..
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Kuon. She never gets less annoying.If you're wondering when this gets good. It is only in the last cut-scene/story segment. So you have to struggle through ~30 hours of itKuon thinks she's the main character, and maybe the author/writer does too.Nearly every scene or character interaction or action you'd expect the main character to do is taken by Kuon instead.The character you play as is the comic relief sidekick character. I found it frustrating and stressful.Everything about the story and world building feels inferior to the first game and it feels like general Japanese culture has leaked into the universe where the writers have gotten lazy.Having played the trilogy, I can say that Kuon never gets better. This is her story, not yours.I enjoyed the last 15 minutes though.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: After completing all 3 games (Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth), this was an absolutely stellar experience. I looked forward to every day I was to get back to the game and progress the story. I wish there was more but am very happy nonetheless to have had the chance to play this series. Although I’ve now completed the story, I still get to play Monochrome Mobius, so there is yet a bit more of this world to enjoy.If the “visual novel” tag tends to turn you off, then please understand this series is a “kinetic” novel. There are no choices, no routes and no self-insert character. It is primarily a narrative experience that you can simply set the dialogue to auto and enjoy watching as though reading a book or listening to an audio-book. There are tactical RPG gameplay sequences when story battles come up, but they are not difficult and largely you will simply be watching the story.I highly recommend the entire series.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Great visual novel combined with an SRPG. The SRPG's interface is not as developed as Fire Emblem's, but it's good enough. Visuals are pretty rough for a modern game though, especially the title screen UI being blurry on my 1440p screen. 3D is capped to 30fps even though it only uses low poly chibi style models and environments. Not a huge deal for me though since the story and world-building is the main reason why you would play this game in the first place. It also ended on a good part of the story, making you want to play the sequel immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a huge but very good cast and a huge cliffhanger in the end. I don't like the politics and sci-fi aspect of the first game so the adventure in a fantasy world (no isekai, no OP cheat, no gaming gimmicks) is my favorite part of Mask of Deception. Hopefully the final game still has some of that. Also, it's fortunate that we can play the whole trilogy now instead of having to wait for the third game to come out later. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Good visual novel. The story is great.Don't execpt much too much for battles since this game is more a VN tha na tactical RPG.And yet, the last battles can offer some challenge in hard difficulty.It was an unjoyable moment. The end of game litterally chills down my spine and almost made me shed a tear.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A great visual novel and quite possibly my all time favorite. One of my favorite in the Utawarerumono franchise with amazing characters while delivering a phenomenal story telling experience. _childDocuments_.review: Despite all the things I am about to say, I still recommend this game for what it is."Mask of Deception" is the awkward middle entry in the series. Playing after "Prelude to the Fallen", "Mask of Deception" establishes the base for "Mask of Truth". It is necessary in its role. It also adds new, interesting mechanics to combat, and its story is mostly wholesome and pleasant.The downsides are that the fan service aspects that refer to the first game dominate a bit too much of the story.I wouldn't play this just on its own, but rather as the first, weaker half to "Mask of Truth", which is where the series shines once again.In conclusion: This is a good game. It is great at doing what it aims to do. Sadly, it is surrounded by a prequel and a sequel that either have a more interesting story (Prelude to the Fallen), or have far superior gameplay (Mask of Truth).Unless you have a lot of money to throw around, I would probably wishlist it and wait for a sale on this one, though I still recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: To all wondering which GAME TITLE to buy, I too was confused about what game was the first and which I should buy. So I leave a few key points..There was nearly a decade long gap between the release of first game "Fallen" and release of the two sequels Mask of Deception/Truth."Fallen" The first installment has an entirely different cast of characters from another time altogether.  It made a far better third game than a first. IMO. Its combat is very basic and AoE isn't utilized very much. It also lost its mature content (which was arguably weird) but still hints at some events.If you are interested in Utawarerumono, go ahead and buy and play Mask of Deception and then Mask of Truth. Again the story is entirely set apart from the first game, the combat has more engaging features, it has more sprites and unique locations, and it's story moves MUCH further and is more creative and ambitious than the first installment.Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: There might be some minor spoilers so read on at your own risk.The second title in the Utawarerumono series, Mask of Deception continues the story albeit in another country following a new protagonist and entirely new cast. You don't need to play the first Utawarerumono game Prelude to the Fallen (henceforth Prelude) to be able to follow and enjoy the story, but it can help tie things together when some characters from the first game do appear (mostly as cameos).The feel and mood of the story is quite different from the first, so for those who have played the first and expect more of the same, that's not exactly what you will find. The best way to describe it is there's a generational shift in how the world is and the writing feels... younger.Pacing:There is considerably a lot more dialogue in this game than Prelude and at times it feels like you have to go through 1 or 2 hours of text before the next battle, so it feels a little a little slow at times but that could just be world building and character development. Things start to pick up towards the end.Combat in the game does seem more challenging compared to Prelude of the Fallen and you may find yourself using the rewind function quite often even on normal difficulty. Enemies are scaled quite evenly to your party and have more skills available to attack you with. You probably won't even need to replay battles to grind level your characters, but it can make it easier. Replaying battles do not give bonus exp at the end like Prelude does iirc, so you only get a few bonus points you can save up for boosting character stats in addition to the exp earned by characters attacking enemies of similar levels in battle.The tactical aspect of the game also evolved to include jumping spots on the map and environmental buffs to characters of certain affinities depending on weather.Items:There are no more usable/consumable items in the game compared to Prelude. However, there are a lot of equippable items (accessories) that provide buffs and multiple characters are able to perform healing with their skills, as opposed to only one in Prelude. In terms of re-watching the story, this game sadly does not include the feature of jumping to different scenes and viewing them individually after beating it, but then there are so many scenes it'd be hard to keep track in the first place. Overall I liked the game and recommend it. However it is written as part 1 of a 2 part story, so keep your save file if you intend to play the next chapter and want to reap the benefits of the time you put into this game and carry it over to the next chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: It is highly recommended that you have played the first Utawarerumono game or watched the anime adaptation of the first game before you play this second game. You'll get much more enjoyment out of it if you do. However, doing so is not mandatory, as you'll understand the story of this game just fine even without the context of the first game. Just expect some character appearances and world events to fly past your head. Now that that's out of the way, I'll briefly talk about why this game is good. Mask of Deception is basically a 30-hour long "buildup" to the climatic third game, Mask of Truth, which is widely considered to be the Muv-Luv Alternative of Utwarerumono. As such, most of Mask of Deception is simply world-building, getting to know new characters better, and slowly getting to the bigger plot. The game does this mostly through light-hearted, low-stakes slice of life/sitcom antics. While this sounds boring on paper, I enjoyed every moment of Mask of Deception. Usually, in visual novels, the sitcom stuff is usually the boring part that you have to grind through in order to get to the "good part", the plot. Well, here, I'm happy to say that every part is the good part. The sitcom and slice of life stuff are genuinely very funny, and I came to really like the characters. I was also excited to see old characters that I've come to know in the previous utawarerumono make an appearance. The world of utawarerumono also got a lot bigger and detailed with this installment. The plot really starts to heat up towards the end and launches us nicely into the third and final game of this trilogy. I highly recommend this game and the entire trilogy. It has been a very immersive and entertaining experience, and I look forward to seeing this story through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono Mask of Deception is a really well made experienceThis is the second game of a trilogy and is an alright starting point, though it would be better if people interested in this game play Prelude of the Fallen first as that is the first game.This game is very good, however I did not truly enjoy my time with it and I felt there were so many tropes used that I not only disliked, but felt repetitive and there were so many moments that I just read for the sake of reading.HOWEVER, this game truly pays off if you play the sequel (Mask of Truth) right afterwards, and if you combine the 2 experiences together, it is an unbelievably joyful experience filled with twists and turns that make the overall experience unlike any other. Playing the whole trilogy is something I recommend, playing this game as a by itself experience is not something I recommend

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game. This game cannot be really separated from its sequel Mask of Truth(Futari no Hakuoro), but I will try to review it based on this game alone as much as possible.First thing first, anyone looking to play a great Turn-Based Strategy game may be dissapointed. It's not because this is a bad Turn-Based Strategy game, it's because the game itself more focused on story aspect so play this with a Visual Novel in mind. The battle system itself is simple and quite good. I have some experience in this kind of genre so I play on Hard difficulty. Even on Hard difficulty the game is not that hard and you don't need to do any grind to beat the game.Now the story. The story overall is really good if you consider all of the game or at least just Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. I, myself will consider it a masterpiece. But, if you only look at this one game, first half of it are just slice of life things including character introductions and their relationship buildings. Many people will dislike it because too much of low tension relaxing daily life thing, but for me each of this are piece of episode on each characters relationship with other characters. Great character and relationship building like this affect on how you will feel about them in their unfolding future conflict. Now for the other half of the story. The story suddenly ramp up and hidden conflicts rain down on the story following a certain impetus. Here is all what those first half-hater waiting for. From now on it is full on action, conflict, backstabbing, conspiracy, strategy, and tragedy.And now for the pros and cons. Pros:-Great character and in game event arts. I really love the art personally.-Good 3D battle graphics. Not that cool, but good. The animation and special effect is good.-Good Turn-Based Strategy gameplay. Not that good as I feel it wasn't really the focus of the story, but good enough.-Great overall story. With all game combined, I personally consider it as masterpiece.-Each character have their own personality that build up as the story goes.-There is level system but you don't need to grind any of your character. Your usual party setup is enough to beat the game without you going out of the way to grind you characters even if you play on Hard difficulty.-Many famous Japanese Voice Actress/Actor so those who enjoy it will love it very much. Overall all VAs doing great jobs on this game.-Great English translation. If you understand Japanese you may feel "Wait, that he isn't exactly say that!", but looking on the context it is not a really wrong translation and is still in line with those characters.Cons:-Battle system gameplay may pale in comparison with many other Turn-Based Strategy games. -First-half of the story maybe too slow paced for many people. And you CANNOT choose to miss them.-If you want to raise level of all characters it will be quite hard as normal grinding reward you with really small experience points and stage first time clear bonus only applied to used characters.-Free Battle mode(play previous cleared stage) only useful to get missed achievement and grind for small exp. So, most people may not even need to play it.-The story ending give you the need to play next game as this game is not really a standalone game.Conclusion:A really great Visual Novel with Turn-Based Strategy battle system as bonus. The story is really great and it is recommended to play at least this and the next one(Mask of Truth) but it is better if you play the first one(Prelude to the Fallen) too. Even if you don't like the first-half of the story, please bear with it as it will get really good. You can set to be able skip unread story in the setting but I don't really recommend it. This game is not a standalone one so prepare to play the sequel after you finish this.If you want a great story game and don't hate Turn-Based Strategy battle system, I really sure that this game series is a really good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a review of the whole series rather than just this game. This series is considered one of the top VNs of all time so hold onto your seat or something as there's three games to all play. With the prelude, Utawarerumono mask of truth and mask of deception, it's a mature story, that gets you, it's the only rpg game I can think of where all battles are story related and all have meaning that I played. Characters even talk during battles so gameplay sections feel less like an interruption to the story but more so a continuation of it. As I see a lot of jrpg feel the need to put a battle in every 5 mins sometimes even leaving the story alone for 8 or so long battles with little to no relation to what's going on in the story. Like they're afraid players will lose attention to the game like their attention span is super low or some such, always thought that was super annoying in a lot of jrpgs. Like characters would be talking about something super important only to have random monster battle 605 pop up and bang never continue what anyone was saying, story section over, story-wise games that do this just make it feel so stunted. Like short story sections are only a reward for the gameplay sections and they're completely separate, which makes no sense why can't story-based games be a part of both. Not that I hate all games that do that, some are worse than others, it's just after so many games doing that it gets a little frustrating after playing so many. But with Utawarerumono the story never takes the backseat never gets cutoff to pad time or whatever, this allowed the story to always be at the forefront, the story exists to be told, it takes center stage at all times and never stops shining, I feel this made it feel more real, and then also more epic when you do go into battle as there's a major reason and no disconnect from said story.For Disclaimers:-First off Now this is anime styled game so obviously there's anime artwork and tropes if you're fan you'll like it as it's pretty good in that aspect, if not well you probably stumbled into a weird area in steam. I'm already corrupted from past experiences leave while you still can, it's more than likely not for you.-There's long down times within the story and it takes time to pickup were things get intense like most stories, so sticking with it will help it's a slow burning game but I for one enjoyed those times just as much as any of other times in the story. A lot of the time the mood in those are directly related to what happened before hand so even in those times it feels a bit more real as action isn't shoehorned in all the time as that makes no sense in story setting like this.-If you're here only for action or strategy in the turn based sections this probably isn't a game for you. As you might've guessed it's mostly a VN and there's peace times like E.g where characters go do normal things they'd do in their normal life. That allows you get to know them more and just have fun moments were people are not fighting for their very lives which lets the story show the more living out their lives side of the games world. To see exactly what these characters are even fight for in the first. These parts can be pretty interesting as it can show the games world's inventions and commodities, it's where a lot of world building is. Again that's not for everyone, but if you played something like a VN before this is perfect for you. -2 As I made this review after my second playthrough of the game. The only reason i'm pressing the above part is because way back for the first time a played this it was on playstation I rented it from gamefly and one of top reviews(out of the three that were there) at the time it came out(so isn't like that anymore) said something along the lines of there's no gameplay, too much talking and reading, returned it after 10mins. Besides wanting to commit toaster bath from having the pleasure of reading that "review" I realized that holds some truth for some as it just wouldn't be the game for them and that's understandable whether that constitutes giving it a bad review or not is entirely different conversation. So for me this was an eye-opening experience, for the story itself made me feel things I never had before. if I had to describe it without being too specific, it's a story about losing yourself, losing/gaining feelings, while accompanied by characters that all feel pretty real in their settings. They have their own things they get upset about, they bring others happiness in different ways, they have drinking parties to get over things, characters try to laugh at the face of their problems in their own ways. The world-building continues throughout all three games and feels accomplishing. You can tell by the name of the game as with a mask, it means hiding your identity, it means to lie, a lie can become real with enough effort, but if you live in a lie long enough can you ever go back after becoming what you lied to become?

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I watched the anime for this game in particular in 2019, finished it, and realized that this was originally a trilogy of visual novels, and I was unsure if I really wanted to dive into it because of that. I ended up by this game when it was one sale PS4 not long before the PC release. I bought it again while it was on sale a while ago, and have beaten it for the second time.I might edit this later to add in my full thoughts and copy-and-paste it after I beat Mask of Truth again, but to put it in a few sentences, I've never experienced a piece of fiction in my life that has managed to physically strangle me with the ending. This small saga as a whole is something I wholly believe is worth experiencing. If you're not sure about the visual novel aspect as I was, I would encourage you to try it anyway, but starting with Prelude to the Fallen.In all fairness, the saga as a whole is probably a 9/10, maybe a 9.5 at best, but personally, it is a masterpiece with no equal. _childDocuments_.review: It's one story told through two games in case someone who doesn't know. You also can't play just Mask of Truth without Mask of Deception and expect to understand everything, there's no point.Mask of Deception was great, but I have to admit, I had to force myself to get through some of the more less exciting parts. Some of the dialogue felt a bit boring at times, but it wasn't any deal breaker and it wasn't that common. It's more like a fantasy slice of life than anything else for the most part which is fine, in fact, it was necessary for us to get to know and love this really fantastic cast of characters and getting attached to them. The emotional impact on the second game felt absolutely huge because of that. The comedy is pretty good, the voice acting is superb, especially Haku's. Japanese voice acting is usually great in modern games anyway, but hearing Fujiwara Keiji's (Haku's voice) performance is on another level and that's the highest praise I can give. I liked the battle system, it's pretty simple and usually you don't have to think too hard, but you can still mess up and your units die pretty easily if you're not paying enough attention. The game ends with a cliffhanger which the second game picks up right after.The following can be said about both Mask of Decelption and Mask of Truth, there were some music I really disliked, but there are a lot more that I absolutely loved, they were outright beautiful and filled with emotion, so overall I was more than pleased. But what I wasn't pleased with was how it's a 720p/30 fps port. The game came out in 2020 and this is absolutely unacceptable. While it doesn't hinder the experience, this kind of lazy port is a big no-no.If you like VNs and don't mind some turn based strategy battle system, this one's a must buy, especially if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first visual novel and I'm really surprised. The world building is really good. The characters are memorable and easy to like (except for Nekone, stupid kid). This is a visual novel so don't go expecting battles all the time, it's there just to spice things up.The PC port is great. Every key is remappable and I can choose my icons whether I use keyboard or controllers. The icon options are insane, old and new xbox buttons, PS3 and PS4 buttons, keyboard. How many games much expensive do that? None in my library.I played this without playing Prelude to the Fallen due to it not being available here when I started this game. It's fine starting in this game despite what hardcore gatekeepers will say, I still loved the game and understood most part. _childDocuments_.review: As the ultimately generic Muv-Luv was a prelude to the masterpiece which was Muv-Luv: Alternative as is the Mask of deception in relation to the Mask of truth.Plotwise there is a lot of things Mask of Deception could be accused of but once you'll get to the sequel, you'll see most of them are justified in a very skillfully handled way.Suga Munemitsu like a chess player setting up a piece after piece preparing for the grand finale of the series. Slowly and steadily introduces the player to the world of Utawarerumono once again with almost overwhelming amount of lore illustrated by an enormous glossary, beautiful art style and top notch voice acting.Playing the predecessor from 2002 isn't necessary but I highly recommend it merely for the sake of full clarity of the story and appreciation of how well the author maneuvers our characters of old.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good VN game. If you like anime and deep mystery stories this is a very good choice to pick to play when you want to just chill and enjoy a story. The game doesn't have much real gameplay as there is some turn based RPG style combat situations, but they are less than 20% of the story. As writing this review the first part "Prelude to Fallen", which is a prequel to this story hasn't been released in steam yet, but you can pick this as your starting game for this amazing story. "Mask of Truth" will be the last part and will finish this story that you start here.9/10 points from me and I only take 1 point off as I would have preferred little bit more combat and for the story to not be so linear. Amazing game.ps. There is anime series for this too, so you might want to check that out. Do recommend playing the game first so you get the full enjoyment of learning the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Something to be aware of, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a VN first and foremost, and RPG-style battles are sparse and between. While game is rather long, it has only 17 + 16 battles (all battles can be replayed). All characters, including protagonist, are voiced.Storywise it's an adventure, taking place some time after first Utawarerumono game, but featuring different place and characters, so knowledge of prequel isn't really required to understand it. Main character is Haku, man with no memories of his past, or even world surrounding him. Rescued by traveller Kuon, has no choice but to tag along with her. One thing leads to another, and innitial search just for work and place to live, gets them involved in political intrigues, wars, and past best forgotten.Visually game is just lovely. Like in predecessor, CGs and character sprites are amazing quality. During battles (and some cutscenes) characters use 3D models, and while not everyone may appreciate "big head" JRPG style models, their details, design and animations are sure eye catching. Game is locked at 30 fps, but it's not a big deal IMO in a VN / turn based game. Small screen tearing may happen when watching pre-animated movies, for reasons I cannot exaplain. Battle system has been fleshed out compared to first game, it's not very complex, but perfectly functional. All mechanics are pretty well explained in lore/tutorial log, and I recommend to use it. While game seem at first to use RNG elements, that's not really the case: "random" factors (use of specials, bonus moves) seem to be predefined at start of battle, so rewinding battle will not change results.small advice: if you can't find BP menu in usual place after completing game, press esc while in battle preparation screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A great strategy RPG/Kinetic novel trilogy, probably the best made so far. Unfortunately Mask of Deception is the weakest of the three games, in story terms it really is just a lead up to the next game, Mask of Truth. All the seeds of the story of MoT are sown in this game, but Mask of Deception suffers from a lack of pacing, being very slow with a great amount of slice of life skits, character exploration/development and world building, but very little actual story development until the last act. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the Japanese style of storytelling, it lacks the usual cop-outs (anime character archetypes) which usually comes with this, and it tells a great story in an interesting archeotech world. The game element is good, being a strategy rpg similar in concept to final fantasy tactics or fire emblem.If you like this game definitely get Mask of Truth, but first go back and play the original Utawarerumono from 2002. Yes it's still good, and you will thank me when you realise you are getting the whole story.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 9/10Music: 8/10Gameplay: 7/10Completion time: 35 hoursSelected difficulty: Hard You can see this as a traditional JRPG with turn-based combat similar to Fire Emblem, focused more on the story than on combat or gameplay.Great story and 'okay' balanced combat mechanics - UI might be a bit clunky on mouse and keyboard, so I suggest using a controller for this. In gameplay, strategy plays a large role as you will often notice your units being outleveled by your enemies. However, it is possible to beat the game without having to grind Free Battle, or replaying the battles multiple times (You retain EXP and Level even if you fail and restart), and the game is quite forgiving providing these features. That way, even less experienced players in RPGs won't get stuck on any one stage for too long. Despite all of this, again I must emphasize that the combat only secondary to the story, and their story is pretty damn good. I'd certainly give it my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 90% VN and only 10% RPG so keep that in mind before you buy this. The story is pretty slow at the start of the game but after you manage to get through around 2-3 hours it actually become much better. Easy way to see if the story is interest or not, you can check out the anime adaptation which did a decent job in my opinion. The RPG part is also decent not any special and not that hard (the sequel did improve on this part) since I beat the game without a single grind in free battle. But you will still have fun with it if you are fan of game like final fantasy tatic or fire emblem.

_childDocuments_.review:
Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a grand tale that will enchant the hearts and minds of players as it takes them on an incredible journey. With a beautiful visual novel story experience, intriguing characters, fast-paced SRPG combat, world-class soundtrack, and more, the game is the perfect escape for adventure gamers!

Mask of Deception begins atop a snowy mountain where the protagonist awakens in an unfamiliar wilderness, surrounded by deadly creatures, with nothing but a hospital gown and a splitting headache. However, hes rescued by a beautiful girl named Kuon, who sports both adorable animal ears and a beastlike tail. Finding that the hapless man has no memory of anything, Kuon decides to take the amnesiac into her care, naming him Haku. As their journey takes them across the land, Haku will encounter colorful characters, build deep relationships, battle ruthless enemies, and find himself inexorably dragged into the political machinations of the mighty nation of Yamato.

name: Tesla Force
detailed_description: The Tesla Force Difference When compared to the previous game Tesla vs Lovecraft, in Tesla Force , the gameplay transcends the limits of the arena. You will have meaningful choices both inside and outside the arena, beyond simply acquiring upgrades. You can choose your path to travel, along with the challenges and rewards that come with it. You can risk it by challenging the Elite Monsters for Rare Perks , or you can play it safe and settle for lesser rewards. About the Game The cosmic horrors are awakening. It's time to call upon the heroes of science and eldritch knowledge to defend mankind from an assault from the outer reaches of reality! Endlessly replayable rogue-lite Randomly generated levels Wild array of devastating weapons Intense top-down shooting action Large selection of perks to customize your hero Over a dozen unique abominations to destroy Play as Tesla, Curie, Lovecraft or Shelley! short_description: With science as your super power, charge up your coils and zap into action! Tesla Force is a rogue-lite top-down shooter featuring endless procedural gameplay with tentacle splitting action. Play as Tesla, Curie, Lovecraft and Shelley and blast the cosmic horror back into the galactic abyss!

_childDocuments_.review: "." - Marie CurieTesla Force is a gloriously over the top, roguelite twin stick shooter and a tale of Nikola Tesla inadvertently opening a portal at the Wardenclyffe Tower and awakening the cosmic horrors while trying to provide free energy, wireless transmissions and a life of leisure to everyone. In 1916.Let me just continue with that bonkers story for a second. Before everything goes Cthulhu, a young Marie Curie pops out of a second portal in an almost Ghostbusters uniform and yells at Tesla he kind of goofed. Tesla stoically accepts that, picks up a shotgun and one of his inventions and proceeds mowing down cosmic monstrosities and closing down portals in a tutorial mission that ends with him flying off in a mech. Now if that doesn't sound like electric currents of fun and escapism at its finest, I don't know what does.After the tutorial, the game immediately throws you into the first chapter and to the map of Miskatonic county, the New England setting used by Lovecraft in many of his stories. You can choose missions here and you will have two at the beginning. Your first run will probably end quickly as a light brunch for one of the many swarms of otherworldly horrors trying to hug you. When you die, you'll spawn at the Wardenclyffe Tower and be greeted by Miss Curie again. You'll be introduced to the Doomsday Clock mechanic which ticks down whenever you're on a mission. When it ticks a full circle, Cthulhu performs a dark ritual and grants the horrors worldwide a perk and makes them stronger.This is when the procedurally generated missions kick in. There aren't a ton of map variations and missions, but there's a sufficient amount that it doesn't get stale while you close down rifts, survey hives, fix machinery, collect crystals and batteries and employ a multitude of weapons and high tech gadgetry against the cosmic horrors stalking your every move. You can't see the rewards you get after every successful mission until you upgrade the relevant ability, but you can gain a perk, a weapon or something mysterious, represented by a question mark. You’ll also sometimes get missions on a run, like killing a certain amount of enemies, rewarding extra crystals if you finish them.Whenever you fail, you'll respawn at the Tower. Experience gained and crystals collected in the run stay with you, everything else is lost. Experience unlocks upgrades, perks and abilities which you can then purchase with collected crystals and further upgrade. You can unlock weapons which you can then choose when starting a new run, research permanent upgrades, unlock 5 perk slots that you can pick and change every run and purchase starting abilities for each run. Upgraded weapons drop during runs and this is a bit of a grumble since weapons are not equally useful and it's very luck based what you will get and consequently how you'll fare on a run. It's not a big annoyance though, as runs go quickly.Combat is fast, fluid, flashy and the shooting is satisfying. Your dodge ability is a teleporter backpack. Drops from horrors include the standard health kits, weapons and their already mentioned upgraded variants, abilities, short lasting weapon buffs, including nukes, that greatly increase your speed of tentacle removal, crystals for upgrades and energy cells. Parts for your mech also randomly spawn and when you collect enough you get the ability to summon a giant robot for a limited time that makes sushi out of everything that even dares to wave something slimy at you.The game is divided into 3 chapters and each is played as a separate run, making things a bit easier. There’s a boss at the end of each run and those fights are really bombastic and fun. You can replay chapters from the beginning and all the missions will be immediately visible on the map if you restart.There are 4 playable characters. Nikola Tesla, Marie Curie, Mary Shelley and H.P. Lovecraft. A true genius level, nobel prize winning, science fiction pioneering, misanthropic force. Tesla and Curie are unlocked at the start, the other two have quests that you need to finish to unlock them. Each of them has slightly different stats and abilities, e.g. Curie can dual wield small weapons and Tesla can use energy cells to recharge abilities.Now that it’s out of Early Access, it’s polished, gleefully fun, has a good amount of replayability and a solid amount of upgrades and things to purchase. It may sometimes seem that the grind is a bit too much, but considering how short runs usually are, it’s a perfect break game. It even includes new game+ cycles.Folks at 10tons Ltd really know their twin stick shooting. As this is a spin off from 2018’s Tesla vs. Lovecraft some may complain that it’s the same game or a large expansion pack, but this one stands on it’s own and the asking price is fair. As Miss Curie would say, “Eat Science, fishsticks!”: 17 achievements, some tricky ones, like the Lucky Number and Untouchable, but permanent upgrades and good perk combinations solve everything. 100% completion is very skill based, should be ~15-20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Upfront, I really love 10tons for their minimalistic, crisp, short-leveled action twin-stick-shooter-games with high variability and extremely addictive flavor (if you’re German, I’d call them “kurz und knackig”). Actually 100%ed nearly every title from them until now. But Tesla Force, oh man, it really pains me to say this, but this is a step back. Don’t get me wrong, I don’t want to say that the game is bad, but it’s just kind of a roguelite spin-off to Tesla vs. Lovecraft. It’s got exactly the same mechanisms and gameplay, the only differences are 4 characters (2 of them are pretty useless), and instead of lots of designed levels, this time we only get 3 ‘segments’ with procedurally generated sub-levels with varying objectives (only 4 or 5). Therefore all in all the game is much, much shorter. There’s even no reason to master several cycles of these segments, because it actually doesn’t change anything, not even giving you additional cutscenes. And you can get all achievements in the first cycle as well.Final verdict, if you like 10tons and like Tesla vs. Lovecraft, go for it, because it’s at least 5 hours of additional fun, especially in coop mode. But only on a really heavy discount, because, as I said, the game is much shorter than the original. Nevertheless I’ll still give this a thumbs up, just because I love 10tons so much, but please, guys, put some more effort into your future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine someone took  (which is an  game) and slapped together a user mod to turn it into a roguelike. But never polished it and actually broke half the existing things in the process. You get to see a ton of the reused content but it all somehow feels worse.The game isn't completely awful, but it's semi-broken and simply much, much worse than Tesla vs Lovecraft. Skip this and buy the original game instead.- The map is a total mess. , can you comprehend where I am or which paths I can follow?- Perk rewards for completing levels can be white, blue, or green, and I still don't know the difference- I don't understand how "quests" are given. Are these daily like in TvL or what?- I still don't fully understand what batteries can do or how much I should care- The permanent upgrade for "+5% chance of finding loot" doesn't explain what "loot" is, does this spawn more permanent money or just more abilities etc?- Teleporting over items no longer picks them up. If you played TvL you know this is a big deal- Teleporting through enemies does not deal damage unless you have a perk for just that- Awful writing. A character you've never heard of says you must save the world before it's all gone, to which Tesla says "that sounds bad, I should go then". I'm not exaggerating- No voice acting (only subtitle text) makes garbage cutscenes. Of course it's not a story-driven game but they went for the story and implemented it this badly- One of the enemy types tends to get stuck in the open. It did work fine in TvL, too- Weapon balance seems to fly out the window when you find Jacob's Stick which is fast, strong, fully piercing, and auto-aiming- Super slow progression. You used to get a new perk every dozen seconds or so in TvL. Now you get one every several completed levels. This sucks- Perks are too weak. TvL perks could change the game dramatically (not even mentioning the rare "Epic" perks!), but these are all "+10% damage" kind- Two starting characters play the same. Unlocking the third one is far too tedious. And the fourth one I have no idea how to even unlock- Ironically having actual objectives beyond "shoot everything and survive" made things much more repetitive- You never have to clear the level, you just complete the same objectives over and over and get out, shooting some monsters on your path. Zzzzz- Tiny UI icons. I up-scaled the UI in the options but doing so makes the .- Actually at max UI scale you cannot even close the menu by clicking X at the top because it's off-screen now. WTF I just want my ability indicator bigger- When you pick up an ability you drop your current one - even if it had 0 charges left!! - and it will look identical to any fully-charged ability- If time is slowed down and you leave the mission, the whole escape animation still plays in slow-mo... painfully slowly- When you leave the mission the map zooms out to show you the whole level with pitch black background to destroy all the immersion being in a world of a sort- When tasked to destroy the statues, the first one often gets destroyed on accident because it spawns under you while you're still in mech- I could go on and on about small things but I think I wrote enough tbh

Tesla Force :/Buy Tesla vs. Lovecraft though.It's really good.Cheaper too.Doesn't feel like a shell of a game.And actually endlessly replayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a rogue-lite twin-stick shooter. It is playable solo and in co-op sessions with up to 4 players. You are also able to use steam's Remote Play Together feature - allowing you to play online with friends. They don't need to buy the game that way!The story isn't really important here but it's atmospheric. The cutscenes in combination with the music and overall feeling are great. You move your character with the left stick and aim with the right stick. Shoot with RT and that's it. You'll have a special ability later in the game, can change weapons, and go into a Mech, which is a nice way to spice things up. A level takes max. a few minutes to complete. This means a run doesn't take much longer than 30 minutes. Levels are procedurally generated. While that may be true, I wouldn't have noticed. After a few runs, you'll run into the same looking levels over and over again. Yeah, maybe a few objects are different but you won't notice. The enemies and objectives are different enough though. You also have many different weapons, abilities, perks, and more. There is a lot of content right now. Two characters are available from the start, the other two will be unlocked later. Talking about that, it is a roguelite game after all. You will need to start over and over and over again to collect crystals that allow you to unlock new (starting) perks, weapons, and more. Playing in co-op makes the game more fun. Like I said, with the RPT feature you don't need to buy more than one copy and your friends can just join without even installing the game. The latency is good enough. It worked perfectly fine in Tesla Force. Usually, the run is over if you die. If someone in co-op dies, you can revive them later. It's a nice game for in-between. It's also a pretty good mindless second-screen game but I couldn't resist listening to the music of the game and getting into this atmospheric world. Even for casuals who aren't fans of the genre, this can be a fun game. Thanks to the roguelite aspect and fast-paced gameplay, you'll fastly be in a mindset of "just one more run" and "in the next run I'll beat the boss".It's a good game for casuals, for in-between fun, and especially for people who want to play something in co-op during these hard times. The base price of 15 USD/€ is justified enough. Die-hard fans of the genre should wait for a sale since this doesn't bring something really new to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: The twin stick shooting is solid (of course, 10tons perfected that ages ago) but right now all the other aspects of the game need a lot of work and polish. The roguelite elements are very bare and lacking, balance is all over the place, and the game is exceptionally easy. Maybe wait on this, it's got some work to go.Edit: Forgot to mention, my playtime is only around 4 hours (I fell asleep with the game running ), and I have unlocked all the content and beaten the game at the highest available difficulty. I am fairly certain 10tons is working on more content, but right now this game is very short and there's not much to do. Will update this review as the game is updated.UPDATE: UPDATE. The game has had it's 1.0 release. Not much has been changed. There's 2 new characters, but they play 95% the same as the main character. Still hardly any content, and you can still waltz through the entire game on the hardest difficulty without hardly any issue. would say this one is a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this as part of the Humble Bundle Monthly subscription. I paid for the previous game early on and felt it was worth the money. For the cost of this second game, I expected a lot of new content, not just a recycled version of their last game presented in an endless mode with a couple more characters. Needs more perks, more abilities and more variety to be worth what they're asking you to pay. Buy the first game instead, it feels more cohesive.The weapons are also poorly balanced. There are two or three weapons you will use because everything else is way too weak to be viable.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely disappointed with the game during its early access, but I kept it.I just tried it again for 5.6 hours. And nothing has changed ... You have 3 possible runs, 3 "paths" ... In 30min you have literally seen everything ... No surprise, not really much "to unlock" in the long term.In 4.5 hours you have all the weapons, most of the perks and suddenly ... Your runs are all the same. So of course we can unlock XX% more HP or damage to the mob, to infinity, but we redo the same game, the same monsters (3 or 4 different) and the same backgrounds in a loop.It's almost a "shame" when you see that most of the good rogue-likes have 50 to 100 hours minimum of games, fun and surprising.Don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying i really loved the game.It's fun, very enjoyable and quite useful to just chill and unleash carnage without thinking.But, man, it's so buggy and plainly unfinished. It's out of early access (i got it while still was on it), but it totally still feels and plays like it should still be there. _childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a funny game. The scenario is so simple that it could be summarized in two short lines. The objectives are repetitive because there are only four of them. Throughout the game, you have only one mission: to be dropped on a map full of opponents to kill them all while completing certain objectives (defend a zone, fix a tower, collecting pieces all around the place, destroying statues). The bestiary is also very poor with a total of four or five different opponents excluding bosses. Boss fights certainly have something epicness but you'll soon reach a point where killing them is as effortless as breathing air. Once you complete the game for the first time, you unlock the game + which is essentially the same thing over and over and over again. I am actually and basically testing myself to see how far I can keep going in this. 'Tesla Force' does not even bother to propose an ending worthy of the name.Music is repetitive. I encountered major visual and graphical issues. When foes come by waves you can suffer from major FPS drops. The gameplay is paved with minor bugs here and there. You can play different characters (including Lovecraft himself) but it doesn't change the omnipresent and unavoidable repetitiveness of it all.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a roguelite top-down shooter game.First of all, the game isn't meant to be rushed, but I did manage to get past through the entire game in 3 hours. For a game this expensive I would've expected a lot more content, Tesla vs Lovecraft (the game I would suggest to play over this one) lasting me more than double the amount of time! There are cycles and upgrades to grind the game further, but knowing it will be the same re-used content it just makes it somewhat meh.Now in general I wouldn't have given it a negative review because I hold 10tons games close to heart, but this one was a deception to me. I really thought there would be far more content and a lot less bugs (no, not the monsters). First of all, the game is extremely RNG dependant. In one run I got a BFG and annihilated any monsters on screen all the way to the boss, in my final run I was stuck with an underpowered close-range shotgun against the final boss of the game, which I got in the level right before the boss (I was stuck with an Ion pistol before that.)As for the bugs, well maybe an oversight but half the time I don't know what stuff does. Hovering your mouse over icons should give you some explanation and having to go through 'Character menu' every time is annoying. The most OBNOXIOUS bug is the teleport that randomly starts working! Perhaps this wouldn't be an issue with good RNG, but I lost an entire run right before the boss because my teleport ability randomly stopped working for an ENTIRE MINUTE. This is unforgivable in a game that ends your 20 minutes long run when you die, especially since some monsters almost 2-3 shots you with 120 HP!Ranting done, the graphics are on par with all other similar games, so nothing to say about that. The music was alright, it's definitely not on Neon Chrome's level, but it's not bad. The sound effects were OK. The gameplay in itself is fun, but the game is too short, too repetitive, feels unpolished, is buggy, unbalanced and too RNG dependant.Overall, worth playing if you get it really cheap, or just purchase Tesla vs Lovecraft instead.

_childDocuments_.review: If there is a developer that knows how to make a twin-stick shooter, it's 10tons. Having played Crimsonland and Neon Chrome in the past, I can fairly say they've come a long way, and learned how to make rogue-lites while they were at it. Tesla Force is one of the best games of this type of I have played, let alone the best of 10tons. It's addicting, colorful, and rewarding to play, and has up to four player local/remote play coop besides.Visually set in the nebulous early 20th Century commonplace to cosmic horror, the game sees inventor Nikola Tesla, a man with vision beyond his time, activating his famous Wardenclyffe tower- only for it to open a rift for extradimensional horrors to pour into our reality. The players, as Tesla or other personages of note; Marie Curie, Mary Shelly and HP Lovecraft, must harness the destructive power of weird science and lay waste to the invaders.Tesla Force plays extremely well, with tight controls, smooth framerate even during extreme visual effects and a diverse range of weapons and perks, none of which I have used thus far feel particularly underpowered, save maybe basic starting weapons. Playing with a mouse and keyboard feels extremely natural and responsive, and the overall gamefeel, especially of enemy feedback to your attacks, is far better then Neon Chrome. One particularly nice feature is that you have a dodge ability, a teleport, which moves you in the direction of your movement, and not that of your aim- an important distinction, as I find the inverse extremely disorienting. This teleport has limited charges but they regenerate reasonably quickly and it can be upgraded through perks and unlocks. There is an onscreen indicator, a stack of chevrons, indicating both how many teleport charges you have and in what direction you will teleport. Returning from earlier 10ton titles is a health ring around your character and also a reload time indicator on your crosshair, meaning you don't necessarily have to look away from the action to your HUD, and in this game, that split-second of eye movement could make the difference.Following a brief tutorial you will arrive at Wardenclyffe Tower, a playable menu screen and your base of operations. From here you can switch your current character, activate coop play, purchase persistent upgrades using pink crystals dropped from enemies, and change which cycle of New Game + is active if you have finished a run before. Higher cycles mean meaner and more numerous enemies, but also more drops. When you're ready, you can begin a run at one of three locations. Only the city of Arkham is initially available, and completing that unlocks the Farm, and then the Caves. When I played a demo build of Tesla Force the entire game was a single run, but it's now split up into smaller runs a la Immortal Redneck. I think the game is a bit more fun this way, and it makes for quicker, tighter gameplay sessions. An additional mechanic that was not in the demo I played is the "Doomsday Clock", a running timer on your HUD that is somewhat like the difficulty timer in Risk of Rain or Kingdom Gun: Whenever the clock makes a full rotation, the enemies gain a perk, like more health, move speed or damage. Notably, finishing a stage objective does not stop the clock, only actually exiting the stage does- So you have a choice whether to farm enemies for more drops or cut your losses and immediately end a level. The Doomsday level persists between stages and only resets after a run is over.At the beginning of any stage, you'll start out in Tesla's Sparrow mech- an electrical, dual-minigun-equipped beast that reaps groups of enemies readily. However, it is only usable for a brief time barring upgrades to its duration, and taking damage will shave yet more time off that duration. However, you can use the mech again whenever you pick up its four parts in the stage. Tesla and Curie control this mech directly, while Shelly uses it as an AI-controlled ally with a brain jar bolted to the top of it. Lovecraft meanwhile foregoes the mech entirely, instead summoning a floating Aberation with a continously-damaging beam attack. To summon this creature again, he has to interact with summoning circles scattered throughout the stages.Enemies in Tesla Force are extremely numerous: Dozens on screen at one time, with more constantly spawning in as you fight. They move fast and hit hard, but thankfully most of your weapons have either a high rate of fire or wide cone of effect, or some other unique quality- The Jacob's Stick, for example, chains lightning between multiple enemies, while aptly-named BFG has a generously large splash radius. You can carry any two and more frequently drop in-game, especially if you do the "Seal the Rift" levels. Getting a multikill will drop a bonus temporary powerup, like extra shots or a smart bomb, and these powerups can send you into a vicious cycle of screen-clearing kills, obtaining more powerups, and so on. Very rarely will you kill only a single enemy at a time. Enemies drop a variety of goodies: new weapons, "energy cells" that look like batteries, crystals,  powerups, and abilities. The abilities have limited uses but you can purchase upgrades to their effectiveness and number of uses. You will also sometimes come across "shrine"-type structures that you can pay a cost in batteries, crystals or health for various benefits. These are usually worth it if you have the resources to spare.Between stages you are presented with a map of the area and a choice of stages. You can also view the current Doomsday enemy perks and your character sheet. Initially you won't be able to see the whole map of a run, until you purchase the "Radar" upgrade. At max level, you can see the entire run and can plan out your route ahead of time. A separate upgrade allows you see what a level will offer as reward- this could be a choice of new weapons or perks, with some also having a random event that presents you with a "choose-your-own-adventure" type set of options. The results of these options seem to be fixed, so you can learn their outcomes to your benefit, like interacting with the Curios in Darkest Dungeon. There are different stage types with different in-level drops, and knowing what you'll find in a level can help you plan a route. "Survey the Hive" levels offer health drops, "Destroy the Statues" yields more crystals, "Fix the Inhibitor" gives extra batteries and pauses the Doomsday Clock for a brief time, and "Seal the Rifts" results in extra weapon drops. There are also optional "Elite Monster" stages where you fight a miniboss for a large crystal payout and a guaranteed rare perk choice, and the required final boss fight as the last stage. So far my experience has been that if you're strong enough to make it to the final boss, you're strong enough to beat it. Getting there depends on your upgrades and luck with RNG, with the balance shifting towards the former as you accrue crystals- a metagame I greatly prefer. Each character has a different interaction with the abovementioned batteries: Tesla can use them to use his ability if he's otherwise out of uses for it, Curie can use it to teleport if she's out of charges for that, Shelly uses them to regenerate her shields and Lovecraft can use them to change map routes or reroll perk choices. Of the four characters, I would say Tesla and Shelly are more generally useful, the former mostly due to being the starting character with no stat weaknesses, the latter due to her shield and AI-Controlled mech summon. Curie is inherently slower and with less health, and depends on specific weapon setups for general effectiveness- she is able to dual wield pistols. Lovecraft's benefits are primarily metagame based, though he has the advantage of his floating critter being able to cross gaps, which is especially useful in the Caves region.Tesla Force is extremely fun and I highly recommend it to any arcade shooter or roguelite fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is kinda a remix of the Tesla vs Lovecraft, it re-uses a lot of the assets, but significantly changes the metagame. Instead of a chain of arenas with resetting progress, you get a repetitive RNG roguelite, where you get skills between the arenas. There are only several types of tasks you perform on the arenas, and the variety of maps is small. So as usual for 10tons roguelites the beginning is really dull. Only when you grind and unlock some new weapons and skills it starts to be fun.So, this time there are four playable heroes, and they are very distinct in their playstyle. A bunch of new guns and skills were added, and you can save currency and buy some stuff before starting the run. It allows for powerful builds accomodating your chosen character, therefore reducing the RNG nonsense. Well, and i did never get a lot of end-game guns randomly, i had to buy them to try them out. And the costs are really high. After finishing the game i saw only like half of the stuff. On the new game+4 i still did never touch last tier guns, or the mysterious tier guns, which costs a ton of currency and people say you can't unlock it anyway. I never saw two of the usables too. Oh, and they are almost useless now, because usable abilities do not recharge nor auto-unequip after you've spent them. The only point if you are making an ability-centric build with a character that can spend batteries (another currency) to have more charges. Switching them manually is more of a chore for the other three characters, and they are rarely powerful enough. You can encounter exchange shrines on the arena to transfer one currency into another or health. And you can accidentally destroy one type of the shrines, but none of the others. That would be an interesting universal mechanic, but also a punishing one, since in the endgame you cover the whole screen with projectiles. Maybe it's just a bug that one type can be destroyed.Tesla vs Lovecraft is a great game even after they've nerfed all the fun parts to death. This one is just good, and only if you force yourself through the dull slow rogue-lite beginning. It's just like Neon Chrome in this aspect.All achievements are working, but a couple of them are really pointlessly grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: I initialy gave a negative review during beta testing. I am pleased to say the  latest releases turned me from sceptical into a more enthusiastic player and re-edit significantly my initial review. Many issues have been addressed since beta testing, and few enough remains so I can recommand  this game, more especially if you are a casual gamer and haven't been playing Tesla vs Lovecraft before ( be aware that Tesla Force is quite EASIER than its predessessor,  the  few boss fights featured in the game are an anti-climax to say the least ). Out of the issues/ dev choices I still find while playing:Campaign progression:Splitting the campaign in chapters is okay but why the hell did the devs resets weaponry and perks while starting a new chapter ???Not only there is no storyline to back up  such balancing, but also it simply kills any sense of achievement and progression into the campaign. I can hardly think of any shooter having made this kind of call and for good reason:  Once you killed a boss, your reward is to keep going....naked. Meh ! Out of the ongoing issues I had since the release:UI: --PerksArt direction is schizophrenic and harbour a steampunk art and iconography on most department except character perks. Perks icons are coming straight out of an over colourful and cartoony 7+ kid game. Tesla vs Lovecraft was way more coherent in that respect. Gameplay -You cannot teleport through short crevasses, even though distance separating both sides of the rift are much shorter than your teleport jump.-Mecha teleport is a mess and does not allow you to cross a passage you would not be able to walk into, even if the narrow passage is much shorter than your teleport jump.-No logical explanation either to define when or why you fire one weapon instead of the other, neither when it is going to switch.  -To this date the “chtonian bestiary” has not much expanded and it seems fair to assess that 90% of the 3D game assets  are identical to Tesla vs Lovecraft.IF Tesla Force is as thoroughly maintained and rebalanced in the future than Tesla vs Lovecraft, I have no doubt it will keep growing on me, and outlive its predessessor in my library.

_childDocuments_.review: Great stuff!!!10tons simply are the masters of twin-stick. They manage to take a trusted and working formula and iterate on it every time with growing success, creating games that are a joy to play.All their shooting games are highly recommended, this one is going to be another high point, taking tesla vs lovecraft and making it meatier, more varied and overall much more intense. I can't wait to play the final release, but as it is right now it is already more than I had hoped for and so much fun. I escpecially like these guys with the long sticks, this is such an interesting concept for an enemy in a top down shooter, and one that I have not seen before.

_childDocuments_.review: A very repetitive game that is nevertheless good chaotic fun in small doses.The game consists of three chapters. WIthin each chapter, you have to progress through several missions that consist of a single objective each. At the end of the chapter, you fight a boss. The game purports to have 'endless replayability' and random level generation, but none of this is meaningful - there are only 4 or 5 different mission types, and the random level generation consists of assets placed in slightly different patterns around each small arena. As a result, one playthrough and you'll have seen everything the game has to offer multiple times over.There are upgrades both within each chapter, that you buy with batteries, and overall, that you buy with crystals. The drop rate for these batteries and crystals is not great at the start, until you upgrade the passive bonus that increases drop rate. Thus the starting grind is very slow, and you'll need ever increasing numbers of crystals to get the upgrades you want.All of that said - the game is still really fun. Once the drop rate is maxed, monsters will constantly be dropping bonuses ranging from frost bullets to multiple barrels to increased fire rate. It's entirely possible to saturate the entire screen with your bullets. With extra teleports you'll be zooming around the screen dodging monsters while completing your objectives. This is really fun gameplay and it's just a pity the rest of it is slightly substandard.You certainly won't be playing this for hours on end, but a quick 20min chapter every now and again might be good fun. Get this on sale or in a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: I spotted this in a bundle and didn't think twice about it because it has a Very Positive rating and I've played a number of 10tons games which have all been quality and fun, including Tesla vs. Lovecraft, the game this was based on. This one was clearly rushed or mismanaged, and is still in an unfinished state. There's very little content (I've finished 2 playthroughs in 6 hours), and unfinished bugs have started popping up. For example, after finishing the 2nd Cycle (aka the first round of new game+) the game told me I had finished the first cycle and failed to unlock the 3rd cycle. It doesn't matter much that I can no longer progress, though, because I've pretty much run out of steam on this game. There just isn't much here. I've also run into some weird menu bugs that should have been ironed out, but they don't affect anything so whatever. Just speaks to the unfinished feeling of the game. I personally really enjoy roguelikes, roguelites, etc so the repetitive quality is not the issue, it's the lack of content. I'm not complaining too much because I got the game very cheap, but it isn't worth what I paid for it, and is very far from being worth the full price. Unless the developers fix the game and add content I would recommend passing on this one. If you were interested in the look and haven't played Tesla vs. Lovecraft, definitely check that one out though. I'll be sure to update this review if anything changes for the better in the future, because I'd really like this game to be better than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2:After playing the game in its final state, I can no longer recommend Tesla Force. I feel rather disappointed at the final state of the game, and I believe it is significantly inferior to Tesla vs Lovecraft in terms of enjoyment and mechanics. This comes down to the lack of actual balance in the game. For example, in this game, there are several types of levels, one of which is Closing the Aether Rifts. This type of level was the hardest in the initial version of the game; rather than balancing it, the developers simply nerfed it so hard it is now the easier kind of level. That is roughly demonstrative, across the board, of how balance was applied to Tesla Force. I can understand why, because while Tesla Force was in early access the developers had another game release (Dysmantle) that performed substantially better - so I can't say that the lack of concern for Tesla Force is surprising, but that doesn't mean I like it. Edit 1:This is my first revision of my Tesla Force review after beating the game on the default difficulty. My biggest criticism is the fact that how good of a run you are going to have is very, very luck-based. The first half dozen games I died without making it to the first boss. The game where I finally completed a run, I got a bit of good luck with perks, beat the first boss, and then pretty much creamed everything with ease until I got to the Final BossMy main problem with this game is the lack of balance. In Tesla vs Lovecraft, the lack of balance was fine, because all of the perks and weapons only lasted for the usually under 3 minute level you were currently playing. In Tesla Force, the complete lack of balance between perks and guns is a bit of an issue. I kept a level 2 gun until a level 6 version of the same gun dropped. I kept the level 6 gun until its damage was too low and I had to pick up a level 10 version. I kept the weapons so long because the type of weapon was far more important than the level. Some of the perks are so much better its not funny. Crystal Healing FTW, take that science, crystal healing works the best! Its better than regeneration! (most of the time)This game IS in Early Access so I'll keep it recommended, but there are a few things that would HAVE to change for me to keep my recommendation once it gets a full release: 1) A bit more story to the campaign. As it is there's no story, even for a 10tons game. 2) A bit of a longer campaign. I was kinda sad when the game ended, as it is. 3) A bit more balance so that there's something between "You don't get gud enuf perks and git rekt" and "You get great perks and go around slaying all the monsters  like you're Darth Vader and they're alliance soldiers." On that note, I find it strange that people are complaining that Tesla Force is easy. I wouldn't say that's quite it. I'd say that its more accurate to say that any successful run is likely to feel easy, because you die quickly unless you get the right perks. But if you don't get the right perks, I'd honestly say that this is probably the hardest 10tons game there is.Original Review:Have been waiting for this game since it was originally scheduled to come out. So far... Compared to other 10tons games:1) Compared to the 'prequel' to this game, Tesla vs Lovecraft, its quite different. In each level of Tesla vs Lovecraft, you level up get perks and pick up weapons, and you lose those at the end of the level. You also have some permanent upgrades you can buy between levels. 2) The second game that Tesla Force seems to take inspiration from is Neon Chrome, in the sense that its a roguelite and when you die, you start at the beginning, losing most of the upgrades you've earned. (However, in Neon Chrome every few levels there was a "save level" you could choose to start from on a new run.) However, Tesla Force doesn't seem to offer as many upgrade options as Neon Chrome, and many of the upgrade options for Tesla Force seem to be non-permanent. (IE, you can buy perks at the beginning of a run, but they only last for a run, similar to the perks you pick up between levels). It also seems like (for those of you who played the alpha release during the summer a few months ago) that 10tons has altered the difficulty of some of the mission types so that some of the mission types aren't much, much harder than others, as they were during the alpha. Which is nice. Overall I'd recommend Tesla Force, though currently I'd probably recommend you try out Tesla vs Lovecraft and Neon Chrome as well, and I think I liked them a bit better. But 10tons is really good at making twin stick shooters, you should collect them all. ;)

The visual effects are really quite stunning exploding monsters for the win. The procedural element of the game is brilliant because No 2 games are the same nor the path you take to get there. Overall this is yet another 10tons twinstick shooter that is just a joy to play. I would love to see a procedural generated survival area that we can compete for High Scores. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love 10tons topdown shooter games, and been playing them since first, old Crimsonland.I was initially - slightly confused with Tesla Force because I played a lot of Tesla Vs. Lovecraft (on PS4) - but reviews helped, so I'm leaving one as well.I thought this was sort of a DLC, or an expansion - it is not, it is sort of a "reimagination".In Tesla Vs. Lovecraft, you go from level to level, and you fight always starting from scratch, looting abilities and weapons only for that one level - with few perma upgrades.This game, on the other hand, takes the concept and turns it into a roguelike!As the dev's table very nicely explain, there's procgen, you get to keep the weapons, you keep the perks, you keep the abilities. You have perma-upgrades, you collect cells so you can use them depending on your character - Tesla uses cells to activate abilities beyond their normal charge allowance, Ms. Curie uses them to teleport, when teleport is out of charges, and so on.I played for one hour, and I finished the Arkham - you may think this is short, but there are (for now, devs keep working on it) 3 different regions, and there's NG+.All in all, this game is absolutely _awesome_, even if it reuses a lot of concepts and content from Tesla Vs. Lovecraft.I never thought it would be possible to create two different games using same assets, and have them both be very playable and fun - but here's the proof!If you love top down shooters, buy it even if you own and have played Tesla Vs. Lovecraft. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: We wrote a critique of Tesla Force. Here is a select quote from the critique:"Tesla Force shows promise, but it remains to be seen whether it will reach its full potential. If you’re a fan of top-down shooters that’s looking for another one to play through, this one is worth looking into. Even at this early stage, it’s well-polished, exempting some balance issues that will almost definitely be sorted out. There’s a lack of variety at present, but that will hopefully be addressed by additional content throughout Early Access. While you never quite get to feel like an all-powerful badass, which is a bit disappointing when you consider its style of progression, there are some loadouts that allow for some really insane moments, albeit they can be a little too fleeting at times. That being said, at present, the roguelite part of the game feels underutilized and there are some issues with co-op play, so, if you’re not already a fan of top-down shooters, Tesla Force likely won’t be the one that wins you over—not yet, at least."You can find the full critique, complete with some awesome ultrawide screenshots, here:

_childDocuments_.review: Polished top down twin stick shooter. One of the best in the genre. Get a some extra controllers and your mates around for a coop blast.
