My mate and I found our first play-through challenging. But, as we progressed it became easier, due to the power-ups we had accrued. The difficulty increases were no match for the purchased upgrades.Still a whole lot of fun. Not sure we will return to this game, but gave us a couple of (LONG) nights of enjoyment. The first night we played from ~9pm - 5am and had to, reluctantly, drag ourselves off to bed!Well worth the purchase! =)We had played Crimson Land and Tesla Vs Lovecraft before this game - so maybe we were going to be used to how this game would function, hence our ease of completion.I just wish they had included some sort of randomised infinity mode, or supreme difficulty level or something that justifies some extra play throughs. We might push for all the trophies, but likely we'll move onto something else, maybe HellDivers.We did a few hours of 3 player 'couch coop' with another friend, huddled around the screen and it worked perfectly, just a little too easy.If you're a fan of the genre and you find this on sale, just buy it! _childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy Lovecraftian shooters?If you want to see Tesla Force in action, watch my video. You start off as Nikola Tesla when Lovecraftian horrors begin pouring out upon the world, and it's your job to shoot them down and prevent the world from ending. Did I mention you get a mech? Shooting is satisfying, teleporting lets you navigate effectively through enemies, and perks come pouring in. Boss fights are difficult, but normal levels are easy.Hopefully the final version will add the polish this game needs, because at this point in its development it's fairly middling compared to other shooters. Compared to other shooters, the theme and difficulty make it stand out (having a fairer, perhaps too easy, difficulty overall). But there's not much more than that yet. Still, this is the first mediocre shooter that's persuaded me to come back for more, and that's worth something.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't really recommend at the moment. Advertises "endless replayability," but it gets quite samey very quick. At this price point, there are other games that offer a more substantial amount of replayability. The Binding of Isaac, Risk of Rain 2, Hades, Enter the Gungeon, Dead Cells, and Monolith have the content/perks/concepts/mechanics that this game is lacking which make them better with replayability and keeping runs fresh. Monster variety and mechanics is lacking. There needs to be more telegraphed attacks from them instead of the main mechanic of giant hordes of the same enemy. The 5 mission types are a great idea, but it does get old quick with how many of these missions you do in a single run. Adding in more mission types would help alleviate this, such as 1 or 2 longer missions types per level or even a "dungeon crawl" type of thing to change up the monotony of the "branching" world. Hopefully the devs will listen to feedback and give this game the content it needs to compete with the other roguelites. This definitely has potential, but that's all there is right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a followup to Tesla vs Lovecraft, a game which I 100%'d happily. It uses the same engine, combat system, and a slightly modified gameplay loop. And, surprise surprise, I liked it the first time and I like it this time. This game is just TvL with Slay-the-Spire, Monster-Train, Ring-of-Pain, (etc) rouge-lite building blocks stapled to it. A map you choose a path through, with each step granting an encounter and upgrades. The Roguelite backbone is a great type of game, sometimes, but it doesn't really improve the game in this case. It honestly just felt more satisfying in TvL with well-designed waves and levels, rather than adding more randomness because "replayability" is the soup of the day.THAT SAID, the gameplay is solid and it's still pretty good, it works fairly well. I'm not upset about owning it. But if you don't own Tesla vs Lovecraft, I feel that is still the better game. If you do own it and literally just want more of that, this is fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a console ported 2D top down twin stick shooter and a sequel to the mobile app, Tesla vs Lovecraft.  This looks and feels like a copy+paste of the original game, very little seems to have changed (5 new weapons, apparently). The game looks fairly well polished for a copy+paste of a mobile app, but the console peasant nature of the game is overwhelming.  Twin stick shooters don't do well on Steam for obvious reasons... this is PC, not a console peasant gaming appliance.   That aside, it's still worth mentioning the visuals aren't the let down here, it's the boring console tier gameplay. The developer was unable to come up with decent level design or game/story flow/plot, so they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen as a substitute for adding content to the game.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning.  Developers must learn that procgen is not content.In some ways it's a shame to see so much effort going into the visuals and polish for such a shallow game, but I guess that's the crux of the console gaming experience, and it makes me glad to be a PC gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than Skeletal Avenger and Undead Horde, in my view.Still uncommitted to the full rogue-lite upgrade system, but the weapons are more fun than it those games, gives the chain-lighting fun of the tesla theme.There are some persistent upgrades, but they are not as obviously required as in the two games mentioned above. Can still get grindy to get them, but you're less reliant on them (and more reliant on which perks and weapons you get on a run).Not the most inspired game, by any means, and I still prefer Neon Chrome a Jydge to this, by a country mile. Those game had a lot more variety and customization. It felt like you were trying to figure out good enough builds and overcoming specific challenges rather than just grinding to replay the same levels on higher difficulties, as 10tons seem to have been doing since then.The game wants you to replay it at higher difficulties, which I don't find very fun at all - especially given the low variety of weapons and perks. I've beaten the game once, on the first difficult, and I feel like I've seen 80% of what is has to show. At this point, it would likely get grindier than I'm comfortable with.Still, I enjoyed it during that first run. Take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been a big fan of endless wave shooters but given that I liked 10tons Ltd roguelite games called Neon Chrome and Skeletar avenger I was ready to give Tesla force a chance and I'm glad I did.Tesla force is quite similar as how Skeletal avenger is played and progressed, you have small arenas you clear out and then select from map which area you move to next. And if you die during the run you'll be returned to hub-area where you can gain permanent upgrades or change your player character.I'm not sure is the game too easy in my opinion after beating the game or was I just very good at this game as  stats indicate that average completion of the game takes six (6) to eight (8) hours where as I managed to beat the game little under three (3) hours without a big challenge. There is however NG+ option available so I definitely want to return to this game one day and find more challenge within it.Only real negatives I had about this game was how limited story elements are in the game and unlocking new player characters requires a very precise style run to be completed (collect XXX pieces of this material during a run), where as I would have wished that new playable character unlocks upon defeating first and second chapters.If you into roguelite games with good gameplay Tesla force is a fine pick on sale.

detailed_description: In Aliens: Dark Descent , command a squad of hardened Colonial Marines to stop a terrifying Xenomorph outbreak on Planet Lethe. Lead your soldiers in real-time combat against iconic Xenomorphs, rogue operatives from the insatiable Weyland-Yutani Corporation, and a host of horrifying creatures new to the Alien franchise. You are the commander. They are your weapon. Infiltrate large open levels and annihilate enemies with your squad, dispatching orders strategically and intuitively at the touch of a button. Tread carefully, as your foes will adapt their tactics to your actions while hunting you down because death is permanent. Forge unique paths for survival, uncovering shortcuts, creating safe zones, and setting up motion trackers in a persistent world where your actions impact levels forever. Customize your squad with a selection of different classes. Level up and specialize your soldiers with unique abilities and an arsenal of weapons, armor, and perks, for high stakes missions in treacherous territory. Develop your base to research new tech and improve your squad even further. Manage your resources wisely and take calculated risks to outsmart the deadliest creature mankind has ever faced. Can you and your squad stop the outbreak before it’s too late? • Face off in a gripping original Alien story against iconic Xenomorph creatures ranging from Facehuggers to Praetorians, Alien Queens and many more, including rogue human commandos and a brand-new threat unique to this Alien storyline • Lead strategically and change squad tactics from mission to mission, carefully managing your soldiers’ health, resources, and sanity, to avoid permanent team losses and mental breakdowns • Forge unique paths for survival in a persistent world, uncovering shortcuts, creating safe zones and setting up motion trackers to stay one step ahead of these creatures • Assemble and level up squads composed of 5 starting Marines classes, with dozens of specializations, unique abilities and weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt expect much but i was pleasently suprised.The game is mix of commandos and xcom but with real time combat.Visuals and atmosphere are great and the gameplay is too.It was a bit buggy at launch but the devs seem to be hard at work on fixing them.The game has alot of potentional if the dev team does it right. The foundation is there, now the devs need to add more features and content in the future.Worth your time if you like strategy games ala xcom etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Alien franchise, you will be pleased to know that Alien Dark Ascent is a game that truly captures the essence of the movies and books. The game is set in a persistent world where you lead your soldiers in real-time to stop a new and terrifying kind of Xenomorph outbreak on Planet Lethe. The game’s immersive atmosphere is incredible, and it creates the same mood as the movies and books. The tension of knowing that there are several Xenomorphs behind you makes you feel cautious, and like the characters in the game, you feel the stress, emotion, fear, and adrenaline that the action shows.The game’s environments are detailed with incredible attention to detail, and the ambient sound makes the adventure more enjoyable. The game’s management system is interesting, and the ability to extract when everything goes wrong in the mission and then return to try a different approach makes the game less repetitive.Overall, Alien Dark Ascent is a fantastic game that will appeal to fans of the Alien franchise. The game’s immersive atmosphere, detailed environments, and interesting management system make it a must-play for anyone who loves the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Quite engaging. Nice length. Overall impressed that a smaller studio could produce something of this scale.Has some issues - notably the english voice acting is a bit sketchy at times, and there are still some annoying bugs here and there - but nothing too major, especially considering the budget price.This game, of course, now makes it abundantly clear that Aliens is a shoe-in for an X-Com-like (which this is not, as it's a real-time tactical RPG). Make it happen, Firaxis.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: To get right to the point it was becoming a magnificent game! lore friendly, phrases right out of Aliens 2, excellent USCM experience! However the game is full of bugs, the first run through I had I did not even finish the first level before coming into one of the many game breaking bugs, I could NOT complete the collection on the first level of the game, no bug fixes, everyone who has encountered it could not complete the collection, the second one just today was a terminal on the 6th level was not intractable and I had to restart my whole game again, so I looked up how much replay value there really is in this game and well.... there is none. all you get is a 11 leveled campaign with a gamble if you will even make it without encountering a bug that will force you to restart your whole adventure.Overall I am disappointed in the game for the fact it's just a campaign and even if these problems were to disappear I would still not return. Maybe if the developers of the game make it more then a campaign and add some actual replay value for the game I would gladly return, otherwise if your looking for story line, and have the will to challenge your patience with bugs this won't disappoint you and hope it will will.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but I definitely putting it on easy just till you finally figure it out.  Its X-Com but with a twist being the squad self engages in combat and periodically having to take pauses.  It might throw some people off at first, but like I said once you get a hang of it you can literally battle the aliens open as long as you have a sergeant and constantly spam the don't panic and its fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 starsThis game is a hidden gem. It has been a long time since I played a game with such good gameplay and most importantly, such good and amazing storyline. And what a story it has! An edge of my seat, anxiety inducing, thrill ride rollacoaster of a game and story.I don't want to spoil it for anyone but play the game for yourselves and find out. As for the bugs complaint. I started playing on PC in January 2024 and found only a small bug (puns intended): when looking through a CCTV camera during one mission, the Queen's model was unfinished. Yet, when I battled the Queen, her model was perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Well so far I'm not to impressed. The starting tutorial drags on. There are times when a onslaught triggers and if you didn't know it was coming you are pretty much screwed. Each time you complete a objective you get a auto save at least you have that one saving grace. I find myself always unable to preform an action due to some cool down but you don't really know what that cool down is.One stupid thing I found is that you can't pick up a sentry gun if its damaged. Really I can't take it back to the ship and fix it there; I under stand its dead weight but maybe make it so  that whomever is caring it can't do anything unless they put it down.When your moving your guys they never watch there six. But I guess that ok; your motion tracker will alert you when something is coming. The stupid hidden Xenos suck; you know they are there  and you can hear them but they won't come out unless you put yourself in danger. Only thing you can do is ready a grenade or have a shotgun blast in the processes of going off in its direction.Once your party gets a xeno in between them its hell trying to get out of that situation. Another thing that sucks is that these Xeno know when your going to shotgun them or throw a grenade. They doge out the way every time.Stress level of your characters is something you always have to be on the look out for. Running low on ammo also causes additional stress so if your in that situation its best you just retreat and come back another time.I've only see  a few bugs so far; one where a onslaught was triggered but the aliens were stuck in a corner; I had to take the APC over and break up there little pow-wow. And you can't eve-ac in the middle of a onslaught. So if your aliens are stuck in a building and you have to go break them up yourself good luck; best you put down some sentry guns or mines because hell is coming and it takes no prisoners. Well it does take prisoners; because your squad can be kidnapped. Pretty fun; but I don't see any repeat game play here. After your first run I don't think many people will play it again.Over all its' a good game. I would recommend but you probably want to wait for it to  get a discount unless your a super fan like me. And don't watch anyone play it. If you spoil it then there is really nothing to the game but going through the motions.  It's best to be carried by the unfolding story rather than just follow the icons and voices in your head.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Hard and entertaining, really polished with some minor exceptions to performance and few bugs.Detection mechanic really encourages you to stay hidden, otherwise you will be having a hard time, which will leave you with no other option than guns blazing and exterminating endless waves of xenos. But I consider that as a plus.The devs focused on so many details to make the game an authentic experience set in Aliens universe, that it makes you really engaged in it.Story is also good. It's not perfect, but it is definitely good.Both exploration and combat feel really good. Stealth system feels a bit mediocre. However judging the game by the rest of it's aspects, it would be a shame to miss this title out.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic squad tactics game. One of my GOTY. It nails the aliens IP and vibe, there was only one point in the game where the story felt a bit off and it was the whole I knew something the characters didn't which made it harder to empathise with their actions.The core gameplay is super enjoyable. The usage of the APC and the various devices you can unlock allow for super different approaches to encounters. The game is a top down squad tactics game with actually functional and good stealth gameplay. The way it ties into the enemy progression in the mission is fantastic and encourages the mechanic without it feeling painful.The campaign is also great, there isnt a huge amount of depth to it but its just the right amount for me. Require a little thinking of what you are doing each day but without making you feel like any action can cripple your campaign.Perfect length and quality level for the price too.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Good stealth action, great that the enemies where random in their patrolling enough to make you think twice.Working around the marines and their mental health / physical health was a great addition to resource constraints and encouraging the rotation of your squads and play quiet as opposed to killing everything that moves.A few game breaking bugs that where infuriating but reading the patch notes they have fixed the ones I experienced.Graphics are last gen but it sets a good atmosphere. (Game play over graphics any day!)Enough jank to enjoy but not get frustrated.Sounds is awesome, nothing like a motion detector to get the heart rate elevated. Could tone down the marine one liner repetition.Is the game good? 33 hours in 4 days. I was hooked!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Adds tense real-time combat (with pause/slow-mo) to the X-Com formula in a tense but compelling way. Expect all of the same razor-sharp margins of error and unexpected middle fingers to your careful planning along with a surprising amount of resource management that incentivizes repeat visits to persistent maps (which you will revisit a few times to complete multiple mission objectives and rest/recover in between).This resource management unfortunately becomes a problem as randomized loot drops from xenomorphs needed for special loadouts and their upgrades can sometimes make you realize too late that you've wasted one of your precious limited runs when no resources are given at all.In addition to the Infestation level that slowly ticks up (and rarely... like, INCREDIBLY rarely can be countered by a random event that I only experienced once) there will eventually be another ticking clock slamming you in the face that, if you didn't see it coming or plan in advance or grab every resource you could, can basically mean a couple dozen wasted hours of game time.It's overall a solid experience, but know what you're getting into with a game like this. It is punishing and it is occasionally obtuse. It is truly random in some of the worst ways but not game-breakingly so. And a death spiral of bad choices and bad events can screw you completely. But when it works, it's thrilling and fun -- although the story's not really much of a standout and the characters other than the lead tend to be more generic archetypes than people.Feels about as dark and brutal as the setting. 7.5/10.Also, using the same resources to save your game on the map and recover as you use to open locked doors and work a scanner and repair a robot and give yourself tactical bonuses kind of sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the story mode, it was difficult but fair. People get hurt but you can still trust your weapons and finish the game in one stint. An then I finished the game in nightmare mode, my experience is that my marines are like shooting BB at the Xenomorphs. To survive, avoid combat at all cost and managing command points carefully are the key, this is a game all about managing your teams stress and to use the special weapons efficiently in the  harder difficulties. I still love the game but I've lost interest after I've finished in the nightmare mode. If the developer can implement a level generator, this game would potentially be the best strategy game at all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent. A game that brings up the true feelings from the movies. The hardship of the Marines. And Civilians in situations that could only be described as horror out side of this world. Its well balanced and optimized from launch. It has minor hickups on Driver side but thats a small hickup. But just enough to bring the story forward with out blocking any thing. Its also the only thing i wish they had more of. Its a gem that i must urge you to buy and play. I hope to see a continue on this saga. Branch out creat. The gamers NEED MORE of this awesome game play and story. Dont change to much of this glorious game. So now go buy the game. And Enjoy. Because i enjoyed it so much i just had to make this review. Stay Safe & Stay Awesome ! This means that a little mistake sends to ashes a couple of hours of play.This means that it requires a lot of time to be played. A LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real roller coaster of emotion. One moment you are doing great and then you get your whole squad wiped because you got overconfident for a minute, really makes you think about your actions, you can't just power through the mission. Great stress and anxiety simulator. Like many have stated it is like a mix of XCOM and Dawn of War 2. First couple of hours are intimidating and you would want to quit, but if you persevere it can be rewarding. Permanent death mechanic keeps you alert.Some game bugs (no pun), still fun.EDIT AFTER BEATING THE GAME:This game is amazing. I freaking beat the whole thing. This to me personally was like "Dark Souls" of RTS games. What a challenge, and I played on Medium difficulty.Also you can see that the budget was not that big , but it doesn't matter.A challenging, solid RTS. Not for the faint of heart that's for sure.Great game overall. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A great real-time tactical experience which is pretty authentic to the alien universe. Includes the guns, sound effects and music from the Aliens film. Creates a very tense atmosphere when you can see things roaming about on your motion tracker which got ME stressed, never mind your squad of marines. This game manages to duplicate the feelings I experienced in Alien Isolation where there could be danger around every corner. I'd say it's a worthy successor to almost the best alien game of all time, Aliens v Predator 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece. A clever implementation of RTS mechanics, well written story and a billion references to original films  Everyone who loves this franchise knows how it struggles at getting good games and now this blessed piece of a game has descended on us.If you an RTS or an Alien universe enjoyer - a must play for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good. I was skeptical about the game play but it is really solid.I highly recommend this game. Story is nothing special and there are still a few bugs that can be quite detrimental. As with the studios last games (battle fleet Gothic). They make really solid game play experiences but the thing it lacks for me is a sandbox. They make a system that could function exceptionally well in a sandbox but then don't deliver the freedom of one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Aliens franchise and you wondered why they bothered making any more after the original two...like Alien Resurrection or Aliens IX "This time Ripley bumps into an Alien at whilst buying a newspaper" this you'll enjoy this game.Let's face it Aliens are as deadly as a 3am curry followed by a long lift journey with a prospective client whilst wearing light coloured trousers. The bugs in this game are equally as unpleasant and after the bowel loosening "ping" from the motion sensor your Marines are all fair game. It's ok though one of your group has an incinerator however, he put his head on backwards this morning and decides to flame a wall in the opposite direction. Then you all get eaten. YES! That's realistic and the sort of game play i am looking for! See, it's just like all the good films! The game plays ok and whilst you end up controlling the group of marines as some collective blob of old people all trying to get their pensions at the same time, it does have the same sound effects from the good films. Pulse rifles and even the little ditty that plays when you get into combat. Story line is a bit linear and you often think "Balls to that, i'm not going in there!" Also there is that moment where you have spent all time on one Marine, made him hard ass and then he gets dragged off whilst all the rest of your marines have conveniently decided to reload. It's as annoying as having your maiden aunt road for dinner and you find out she's brought some pictures to show you of her time in Ulan Bator....Play it when you have a spare minute. Probably worth the outlay but doesn't really create the neccessary tension required for these films...
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Best RTS action/horror I've played yet. There's a neat mix of starcraft 2 wings of liberty hub/no-build missions and darkest dungeon stress management. It's dark and they make you use your flashlight because there is a chance you walk into a room and get party wiped because of facehuggers. The downsides are wonky UI and there are a few game breaking bugs that made me play whole chunks of the game over. (1. deploying in the refinery to scoop up missing items resulted in running every script in the level)(2. kleptomaniac was on permanently for no reason at all so I was constantly being robbed of resources even after removing this from my klepto marine)(3. checking progress on map was often reading the wrong item amounts)...but the first play-through had zero issues, so I'm wondering if there is a recall issue on maps and commands. All of this could likely be easily fixed with a few patches and some play-testing. However, I still highly recommend for anyone looking for a challenging RTS and is a fan of the 80's chunk of the Alien(s) franchise. (I was delighted they ignored the Prometheus/Covenant incoherent lore) *my tips are: set up a choke when fighting and always keep moving.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This was surprisingly good. I played about 2 weeks after launch and did not encounter a single crash or bug at that point. Solid graphics, decent story, decent main character voice work. It's squad RTS with a pause. It will take satisfyingly long to upgrade soldiers, weapons, etc, and you'll never really feel overpowered as the hive is relentless.I feel like they captured the feel of the universe quite well with just a couple exceptions, which are mostly sound related. The guns and aliens all sound as they should, but there are little things like as you're sneaking around levels your Marines are still barking orders at full Marine volume which takes you out of the sneaking experience obviously. Also, for whatever reason they didn't use the movie sounds for the powerloaders, cryosleep chambers, and APC. That's a weird choice as surely they had license to do so and those are immediately recognizable sounds so it's weird and noticeable that they're different in game.Also, the camera is in desperate need of the ability to change the pitch. You can zoom in and out, but the angle you're looking at things is more or less always the same and I'd like to see a bit farther in front of me. Hopefully someone will mod that in at some point.Those rather small things aside though, it was quite a fun game, definitely has a number of tense moments and I feel pretty confident that I'll play through it again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: ok so, 16.5hrs in and i think i've only scratched the surface... but i'm hooked!Highlights:- Xcom style combat, but the slow-mo adds a nice twist to the gameplay- The stealth system combined with the radar ping noise really brings back the tense "eek its right there" vibes from the Aliens movies- The leveling up of the squad and the extra skills you gain are good, you can really enjoy combining the various options to combat the physical and emotional damage your squads suffer during prolonged missions- The sentry guns are fantastic and again are a really nice throwback to the excitement of the movie because, as Hudson would say "they're wall to wall in there!" and you really need that extra fire power when the horde comes for you!- Visually the game in stunning, even from the safe birds eye view angle the aesthetics are creepy as hell and really get you sucked into the vibe.I think this game is prime for DLC expansions as the playstyle is so addictive and could be transferred to other plots and stories. Especially if there was a AVP element added, it would play so well!I could go on and probably will update this later, but for now its a huge thumbs up from this fan of Aliens and the Xcom series.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a XCOM based squad game but every thing is dealt with in realtime or slo-mo.There are no turns, u move your whole squad with one click on the mouse, want to scavenge that box and weld that door, np. 2 of your squadmates each fill out 1 task with the lmb while the other 2 take cover behind that box with rmb!  This is so smooth that this feels like whole new gaming genre. I play on medium difficulty and have cleared the first map for 53%. 4% at game completion on a slowly played 6 hours. And yes u can re-send squads to earlier visited locations. All in all, a good entry for the alien franchise due to vibe, story, cutscenes and last but not least an amazing game with even better gameplay. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exceptional and I'm in love with it. In fact I wish Starship Troopers had a game like this as well. I get so invested in the characters and it can be so brutal. Everyone seems to get hung up on not being able to quick save anytime you want to. This game is generous with auto saves and you can manually save in mission. The way the save system works makes you value your decisions. It gives it weight and meaning.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid XCOM player, this game scratches that itch hard, and vastly speeds up the pace, and raw panic for you and your marines by making it an RTS.There were times of pure moment to moment crisis-management and panic with split-second decision making when I got caught out without a good fighting position during an incoming onslaught, and I LIVE FOR THAT, IT WAS GREAT.The atmosphere and graphics are top notch and fit the setting super well, everything has that Aliens feel, from the small cattle town to the dockyards and the old, Nostromo era ship, to the high tech and the new skyscraper HQ of Weyland Yutani, all of it feels authentic and looks great.This goes double for the Xenomorphs and Marines, both the sound design and looks.My only wish in this would be for the music to have been a more triumphant score on the end mission screen, it's lacklustre at best,I only have two downsides, one major and one minor.--Major--The bugs I encountered were annoying and required restarts of the game to fix, singular marines being unable to run, unable to crouch hide when pressing shift, I even had an instance of one guy bugged who was stuck pretending to be carrying a civilian, and trying and failing to operate the only elevator requiring me to restart to the beginning of the mission and wasting 1:30 hours of playtime.That said the patches have been frequent and large and have fixed a lot of issues already, so I have faith these will soon be fixed.--SPOILER WARNING----Minor--TL;DRThis Game is to Aliens, what Alien: Isolation was to Alien.I bought it and it's become one of my sleeper hits of this year.Just don't play it on ironman until most of the bugs are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst some of the gameplay does become repetitive, and some creative writing, for any fans of Aliens it's definitely a must-play. When the soundtrack kicks in, and you have to start setting up sentry guns, seeing your gunners wandering around with Smart Guns. I hope someone brings out some mods that give skins, sfx, and even levels to emulate the movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, love the gameplay mechanics and the story is captivating. I would there to be an option to replay the campaign at a new difficulty with your current marines at their max loadouts. The game can be a bit buggy, members of your team getting stuck in terrain or once knocked down, even though they are still alive will not get back up, only loading a previous save will fix this. Despite this, it was still an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved playing on a above normal difficulty through mission 6. Then I was completely stuck, with no way to continue except restarting from the beginning on a lower difficulty level.I understand locking achievements behind difficulty fixed at a specific level. But for a game that is a few hours per mission, which are set rather than procedural, it isn't really forgivable to be forced to replay them. Great game besides this ridiculous progression system. Let me switch down to story mode when I want.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Ten years ago, we got the MASTERPIECE that is ALIEN ISOLATION. Then back in 2021, we got the very good squad-based action game ALIENS: FIRETEAM ELITE. And here come's another great ALIENS game but this time, set in a strategy "RTS" format. Aliens: Dark Descent can satiate your thirst that every fan of the franchise been waiting for; a creepy strategy focused game set in the Aliens universe. It might not be the AAA game many fans were hoping for, me included, like an AVP sequel (we're so frickin' due at this point, REALLY!) but I was amazed how good the story is, the attention to detail in every location of the Lethe planet zones of interest. I don't recall when this game is set, timeline speaking but it is quite safe to say it is after Aliens/Alien3. Story is quite fleshed out for an AA game.... heck, it could surely surpass the many AAA games out there currently... even the almighty AAAA games!

_childDocuments_.review: Scaling on Random Events/Campaign events is completely ridiculous. On harder difficulties this game becomes way too much deal with. At Dead Hills, I ran into the issue of spawning a Crusher, having to Kill the Queen, while also having to deal with back-to-back onslaughts. Boss rooms need to isolated, making it so that an already difficult boss isn't made worse by random mini-bosses/drones. Squads just don't have the ammunition to deal with that, especially that early on in the game. I have tried to beat this area for a few hours with no success, I do keep getting further and further each try, but its hopeless, I run out of ammo, command points, and repair points (so no more tactical analysis) at the end of each run. I like randomness of spawning a mini-boss once you piss off the aliens enough. Its an interesting mechanic that definitely adds a lot to the mundane-ness you feel running around collecting resources and completing tasks. But it hasn't been scaled properly at higher difficulties and it makes boss-fights downright unfair if you spawn one right before or after. I'll return to this game at some point and try again, but discovering that problems with scaling exist like this hurts my opinion on this game. There are obviously features that weren't tested to the fullest on ALL difficulties. I think this game is good, despite the lackluster voice-acting and the goofy game mechanics it has been great playing this game. But I've reached a limit on how much I'm willing to put up with.Later on in the game, sure this situation wouldn't be much to deal with. But in the first area, with a squad that's all low rank, with basic weapons, skills, and traits...Its just too much. The only way to get through this area is to hope random chance doesn't perfectly align a mini-boss and a boss fight together. This problem should have been anticipated but it wasn't.Their is reason games like Elden Ring prevent other enemies from joining a boss fight. Boss fights, especially at high difficulty settings, are meant to test and break you already...by tacking on other enemies/mini-bosses it makes things completely unfair and greatly reduces the impact of player skill. I'm sure at some point I'll eventually pull off the right combo of movements, command point uses, etc. all in a strict proper order...But that is in no way what an RTS should be...Having to guess-and-check your way to the right combo of moves and prayful RNG is an absolute contradiction to the word "strategy."---EDIT---After multiple attempts I was able to finally recover my marines by running back to the APC and coming back the next day to complete the mission. While I now recommend the game after learning a little more about the mechanics, I still think there is an issue with the scaling and "boss mode" areas. I'm sure at lower difficulties it isn't much of an issue, but with higher difficulties, too much RNG is required with time, positioning of enemies, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, just one hour in and I am HOOKED!If you are an Aliens fan and cannot wait for the next Aliens movie, this game will completely scratch that itch! The prologue itself is the best part of any Aliens movie, the Aliens soundtrack and atmospheric music, lets you feel you are playing in the movie itself! This is the best prologue I ever played in any video games (movement animation is top notch too!) Some parts really also feels like playing Dead Space in 3PS with some jump scares. So true to the original Aliens movie visuals! The walls and gates of the colonies look just like in the movies, the marine armor and camo, the shuttle transport and even the USS Otago look just like the USS Sulaco in the second Aliens movie! (in fact, I highly recommend rewatching the second Aliens movie when you play this game for better and deeper immersion!)Gameplay wise, this is almost a XCOM2 reskin in a good way.No XCOM2 wannabes have ever nailed the things this game did:1. The cinematic introduction to the chiefs of each part of the base (almost exactly how it felt in XCOM2)2. The squad ready screen where they stand in front of the vehicle is almost completely XCOM23. Given a voice and face to "Commander"However, I like that they didnt go TBS with this but RTS. TBS in such a title will kill the pressure and suspense. It will kill the panic and rush that you should feel as a player as the Aliens are coming down on you. The environmental engineering is so good it feels like what XCOM2 was trying to achieve in its original alpha tech demo which didnt happen. I am just hooked!

_childDocuments_.review: -Aliens: Dark Ascent (A:DA)-Well, A:DA just consumed this past week for me because i coudln't put it down. This game has an incredibly addicting gameplay loop with just the right amount of challenge, at least on Hard difficulty. Each mission is incredibly expansive and a spooky thriller of exploration and scavenging while trying to keep your squad alive as well as maintaining their stress and resources. -RTS Survival Horror??? Count me in!The game has many clever mechanics that make each encounter with enemies unique in how you might engage them or defend against them. Use an incinerator to block off a passage to funnel xenos into your row of sentries with suppressing fire overhead to slow them and a Recon picking off high value targets all the while aliens run through your minefield on each passing corner of their approach... just to name a fewIn between each high octane onslaught there is a massive map of objectives, resources, aliens in stasis to sneak around, patrols to dodge, and personnel to rescue. Things you find (and successfully extract) during a mission are persistent throughout the campaign which means wasting your med kits or tools on one mission could lead to something dire in the next. For me this in and of itself was fun to manage as I knew if i took the risk to pack up my sentries before i left a mission i could use them later. Or if i took extra tools with me on this mission with the myriad of locked doors to open I would have an easier time navigating the complex thanks to my planning.-"Have a good day, Deputy Administrator Hayes"-Holy f***ing sh** this games voice acting is miserable. I must've heard this lifeless b**** say "HaVE a GoOd DAy, dePUtY aDmInIStraToR HaYEs" 250 times in my playthrough. Each time you go to the USS Otago expect to hear it a dozen times. Who is the dev who selected that sound bite to be stuck on repeat?? The story is cliche as all hell, but the pacing is actually quite good. Nothing was drawn out too badly or "Oopsy daisy, now we gotta go do all this extra stuff 'cus reasons." The missions have what seem to be realistic expectations that correctly follow the story and very few nonsense filler assignments that plague some other games. -Controls could use some TLC-To not be too harsh sounding, the controls are a bit quirky. Controlling the entire squad as a single entity definitely came with a learning curve for me. In a game like this where one false step could equal a restart, it felt TERRIBLE to have one jackass not standing behind cover only to alert a whole damn swarm of aliens. When interacting with a box, or a computer, or anything, the game automatically sends the best unit to perform that task (Usually closest). But this can cause problems because they are now ignoring all movement commands and enemies while SPRINTING to the task. You can shortcut a cancel order key but this cancels all orders including movement... or suppressing fire... or setting up a sentry... or reviving a squad member... Perhaps you're starting to see where that key isn't very useful a lot of the time. This simple aspect of the game makes it a bit difficult to get used to.-Conclusion-Overall this game is great. The setting of the Aliens universe is INCREDIBLE in this game. Each location you visit is just oozing detail of an alien invasion apocalypse. Even from my view of 100 feet in the air, I felt incredibly immersed in this world and was on the edge of my seat for nearly every hour of my 24.6 hr playthrough. Once i adapted to this games "quirky" controls and mechanics, I just couldn't stop. As an Aliens franchise fan I fell in love with this game but even if you're not, or perhaps are new to Aliens, give A:DA a try. Tindalos Interactive made an absolute banger and this game deserves a spot in your collection.Overall 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly amazing. It is challenging but not too hard to beat. The atmosphere and frightening feeling you get when making your way through alien infested sites is incredibly dense. I did not encouter game breaking bugs but there are some minor ones that were slightly annoying at times. Obviously a lot has been fixed since launch.Some people have critizized the save point system for being unfair. For me it's the opposite. I think it's genious that you cannot save whenever you want and have to make saving the game a tactical asset. There were enough toolboxes to find and if you leverage the fact that any kind of elevator serves as a free saving point, you're more than fine. Same with ammo boxes. Plenty to find if you use a stealthy play style (which is highly recommended anyways).There are some complaints I'd like to voice though:The game ends rather abruptly after the 10th mission (there is an 11th one but it starts seamlessly after the 10th and feels slightly cheap). I was also disappointed by the leveling of my marines stopping at level 10 and many of them did not even reach full level before the game ended. I mostly played levels through without extracting my squad in between (to avoid infestation to advance too much). This made the game fairly easy (played on hard) in the end so I finished well below the death clock (I think I still had 15 days left or so). But it also meant I didn't reach full potential of my marines because they only reached level 10 during the 10th mission without possibility to promote them in the field.So the ending does feel a bit like there should be a second part (DLC would be highly appreciated dear DEVs).Considering the moderate pricing of the game and the fact that I still put in about 100 hours of extreme fun I'd say it's still pretty good length. I would have wished for 2 or 3 more missions after mission 11 though.I you love Alien(s) or you love tactical intelligent gameplay - get this one, you won't be disappointed. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game but it has some minor issues that can make it very frustrating which I have to touch on first. One of them is the final mission. It's not hard, it's just very buggy and the fact you can be killed in a cutscene during an autosave is unforgivable. I had to reload this mission more than any other in the game and not because I'm a save scummer.Also, as an achievement hunter, there used to be nothing I hated more than collection achievements... until this game. Now there's nothing I hate more than a collection achievement that's bugged! There's also another achievement that's bugged where you have to kill 10 aliens with a single turret. There are some workarounds to get these to work, but you shouldn't have to jump through hoops to get an achievement that you've earned to pop. Especially when there are 123 datapads to collect in the game that require a full playthrough to get.That being said. I enjoyed the story and while the RTS gameplay wasn't innovative, it was still fun to play. I describe it as a mix of XCOM and Halo Wars in the Alien universe, so with a little horror thrown in for good measure. The voice acting was great and the length of the campaign was perfect for me at around 40 hours on my first run on hard mode. Definitely went under the radar for me in 2023 and I recommend this game if you can endure the buggy achievements and abysmal final mission. Honestly, I would buy DLC for this if one ever came out!

_childDocuments_.review: *EDITED* I initially gave this game a thumbs down, but after realizing I'm just not a big fan of RTS games, it's not fair I negatively review a genre I don't enjoy. What I did experience wasn't for me, so I'm leaving my comments below, but I would recommend this game if you do enjoy RTS games and to read over all the other positive reviews. This game may be for you.===============I know this game is getting great reviews, and I definitely don't speak for everyone here, but I did not see the appeal:1. Game is full of glitchy movements and weird animations.2. While I love the fact the game is challenging and has limited saves... it's pacing is horrible. Not everyone wants to sit and play a game for long periods of time before it saves. I made it to my first mission, go into the building, and then I had to stop playing due to work. When I loaded my game up... I was back at THE START of the base LOL I had to go through all the base tutorials again, then relaunch the mission. Why didn't the game save at the start of the mission, at least?3. Combat is... OK. Nothing overly exciting. Stealth around, shoot, use a few abilities, shoot more.4. The start of the game is VERY slow and the story, quite frankly, isn't that interesting. Dialogue is poorly written and just cheesy, and the serious conversations aren't that exciting.5. Controls are annoying. Edge scrolling drives me nuts, and I'm not a fan of point and click movement. WHY the devs didn't let us move with WASD... is beyond me. Especially since the game primarily consists of you moving your squad around a map/level. Point and click would make sense if we could select/deselect certain squad members, but you always move as one unit... so the constant shifting your mouse around and double clicking to run and single clicking to walk is frustrating.Basically, the game had a slow start, boring characters, nothing overly exciting about the story, and I wanted to make sure I could refund before I passed the 2 hour mark. Doesn't mean you won't enjoy this game, and maybe it gets better, but it definitely didn't grab my attention in the first TWO HOURS I played LOLI would recommend trying it. Maybe you'll like it. You can always refund like I did if you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good - but I did get bored and had to push through to the end. At first impression, it looks like the perfect culmination of Xcom and the Aliens universe. Unfortunately, the Xcom component is very shallow and you'll quickly find yourself missing Xcom's depth. To keep the player interested, the game needed to evolve more, but it really doesn't evolve at all following the prologue.There's a few bugs - some annoying, currently there is a save bug on one mission which is really annoying. The save system isn't the most favourable either, forcing you to spend game resources to save. The game is real-time, not turn-based. This is done well and helps you immerse in the Aliens atmosphere. You move the squad as a single unit, actions being carried out automatically by a random squad member. A key component is "Stress" - kind'a works well for the first few missions but quickly becomes rote resource management, annoying that if you engage a single alien, even if that is the alien walking into a firestorm of overkill, you'll stress everyone out and then start a sequence that increases the mission difficulty. Manageable - but tedious. The only expansion from the Xcom concept I really like is the ability to bug-out and return where you left off with a fresh squad - this is a great concept I wish Xcom had.

_childDocuments_.review: Like an isometric SRPG and an RTS got together in a 3some with Xcom. I havent encountered all the crashes and glitches other reviews state (maybe the patch that came just before I bought it had something to do with that.) Don't expect AAA graphics, this game isnt that, but what it does have is a very good story, excellently designed gameplay and a difficult but balanced feeling challenge. (Its not easy, even on normal.).  Gameplay involves controlling a squad of 4 marines on various drops into different combat zones in real time (this is NOT a turn based game.) , each zone has a series of missions that need to be completed.  When a squad member dies or is dragged off by an alien, or impregnated with face hugger eggs, thats it, that marine is dead,  you lose them forever.  Its challenging and you have to balance your marines to make sure you have a couple of decent teams of them.  You also must manage their mental health and wellbeing when not in mission, as their repeated encounters with aliens slowly builds up trauma and physical injuries, causing them to be less effective over time unless treated.Marines level up, have classes, skill slots, and upgrades to go along with it, including being able to customize their names, call-signs and appearances to some extent.   This game is very deep and very rewarding. Judging from the fact I am only 20% through the campaign at 13 hours in as of writing tells me the campaign is roughly going to be around 40-50 hours long. That's a lot of game for a release price under $60 CAD.  Gets a solid recommendation from me, completely exceeded my expectations.((Current main Specs:Core i5 13600k32gb DDR5nVidia RTX 4080Samsung 980 EVO 2tbSamsung 970 EVO 1tbLaptop Specs:Ryzen 9 5980HX32gb DDR4AMD Radeon 6800m 12gb2tb Samsung 980 EVO500gb SN 750 pro))

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan it's well branded and feels true to the Cameron Aliens universe. They did go a little overboard on the catch phrases. While it may look like X-Com and has a familiar base / marine upgrade mechanic the gameplay is very different. It's real time combat, and more stealth based. You control the squad and not the individual troops. It can be a challenge to move one slow wounded person where you want them without the rest trying to go there. Probably not for high stress individuals, i'm pretty mellow and i'm triggered at times with the constant tension and little control over saving the game. Be prepared for lot's of death and setbacks especially at the higher difficulty levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! How do I review this experience? So this game was a strange one. My first 3 hours I felt the game was mediocre. The acting and script was a little too cheesy & the game play seemed a little too complicated & difficult. However by 4 hours in it started growing on me. Then 6 hours in I was addicted! The story suddenly became really good. And most of all I was actually enjoying the challenge, especially once your marines get upgraded. And now that it is finished, 31 hrs in, I was actually sad it was over. The greatest crime this game commits is not allow you to continue playing it with all your marines already maxed up & all story missions open to replay, at least not that I could find yet. If so it shoots itself in the foot and should come with some DLC to play a more open game with all my upgraded marines. Now I'm in this weird situation where I want to continue playing the game but don't want to suffer through levelling up my troops from scratch again.All in All, this is probably THE BEST sequel Aliens game since Aliens vs Predator 2 all the way back in 2001! Alien Isolation still being the best original Alien game of course.DEVELOPERS: Please add DLC for us to import our maxed troops from our previous save with all chapters unlocked.

_childDocuments_.review: First, to get the bad parts out of the way:- The cutscenes look like something from 2010 in resolution, details and animation quality.- The base UI is atrocious and there are so many unnecessary clicks that I suspect that the UI designer got paid by the amount of elements they can add.- The story and characters are getting as close to being a complete ripoff of the Aliens movie as they can without being a complete carbon copy.That being said, it's still the best game of the Alien franchise that has come out in a long long time. It's atmospheric as hell and captures the spirit of the first two movies perfectly. You can tell that the devs are fans because there's an endless amount of homages, little details in the environment and equipment that perfectly emulate what the movies were about.Combat is both terrifiying and satisfying and the saving mechanic that has you welding doors to let your squad take a breather, is uniquely tense and cool.If you are a fan of James Camerons masterpiece, this game will immerse you completely and will give you the continuation of its universe that Hollywood was unable to provide.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst there are a few gripes that prevent this being a perfect game*, it absolutely nails the Aliens atmosphere. Find the right difficulty for you - easily done with a lot of customisation options - and you're in for some very tense moments as you lead your squad of marines around an infested moon. I love the realtime/turn hybrid game play, where time will slow or pause when you press space to issue special commands. A lot of management is streamlined with the way the squad controls, and things like auto-firing upon any enemy that has already detected them. *Those gripes are: The interaction between the actual view and map view not being very well intergrated, eg you can't move your view by clicking on the map, nor can you view or issue way points to move to.  Switching between squad and automated drone being very clunky.  Health bars of enemies not updating while in some kind of death animation A lack of variation in team mates voice actors, and in things they says during a mission.  The main character acting like a complete idiot serveral times during the prologue, but being fine after. Still a solid 8/10, just shame it is not a 9 or 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Alien series. The movies are my absolute favorite. The atmosphere of Alien Isolation was one of the best game experiences of all time for me. So when I got a chance to finally play the new Aliens Dark Descent Game, I was hoping for that same kind of excitement and atmosphere. With this being more of a strategy game, I wasn't sure how it was going to play out. But it somehow works. It does a good job of copying more of the Aliens movie with action and multiple characters. The game gets a little clunky at times, and maybe even poorly optimized with some laggy moments, but I honestly loved the game itself and the story. It was a little shorter than I wanted, which means I was enjoying myself and didn't want it to end. I hope they come out with an expansion or more content. It's a little short and there's not much replayability in my opinion. But it's overall an excellent story and well worth buying. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a Aliens game since AVP came out many moons ago (colonial Marines doesn't count).There are pros and cons. Since the cons are the most aggravating, I'll start there. You'll see why in a bit.Cons:MY GOD MARINE GO WITH THE SQUAD! The few times I reloaded a save was because one or two Marines would decide the path was better in a different direction. Which was also in the path of a xeno.Pathfinding needs a tiny bit of polish. I only mention it since it happened maybe twice as an issue. By then I would catch it.Sometimes the X option to cancel an order would be an entire square and unclickable unless I made the Marines sprint.Lastly, story is good up until the end. maybe its cause I want more? But the general consensus is there is much to be desired.Pros: if you've played xcom and are used to countdown mechanics, you're in for a treat. If you don't like those mechanics, you're in luck. Due to the difficulty of the game, every facet of it is customizable from the start. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND PLAYING AS EASY AS POSSIBLE FIRST GO ROUND. The devs do not shy by saying it is difficult...take your time walking.2nd, the atmosphere harkens back to AVP but from a top down perspective. Anytime that motion tracker went off I got nervous from the beginning, but by the end, just like AVP, I felt seasoned enough to take it on.Lastly, my god the attention to detail is on par. They did do their research, and injected their own spin in a way that makes sense! TAKE NOTES OTHER COMPANIES.Now get to the APC Marine! MOVE IT!

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been completing games just to try something new and I haven't been hooked on a game in a long time.. Years man. I thought that maybe I was just growing old and burnt out on games and that maybe it was just a dying hobby of mine. I found myself playing less and less games. BUT I CANT PUT THIS GAME DOWN!! I stayed up until 1:30am last night because I just wanted to keep playing. This game gets intense in all the right ways, they blend a horror atmosphere perfectly with chaos when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan and trust me it WILL hit the fan there is no way around that. I've come close to losing so many guys and having to carry unconcious/comatosed men back to the ARC (no man left behind amirite). There will be times you're running for your life as your men are terrified and screaming that hope is lost and you're stuck trying to get these men home alive... Sadly not all of these men will make it back but that's what makes this game so great! Your men will experience trauma, they will experience exhaustion, you will spend times cowering behind a welded door watching the motion sensor crowd with incoming hostiles and you know they're about to break down that door. You know you only have two magazines left and a sentry turret with 132 rounds and that it won't be enough to hold them back. This game gives you the butt puckering experience I didn't know I needed and I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ehre for it! 11/10 no regrets and I haven't beated the game and I'm stoked for coming back for another playthrough and cannot wait for the DLC this game will be bringing. _childDocuments_.review: Aliens at a foundation level is a good game, it looks incredible and captures the universes atmosphere perfectly, the environment and lighting artists did a 10/10 job on selling the scale of the maps and the alien nests, overall the game is very fun and a unique blend of XCOM / RTS style gameplay with a few caveatsThe Bad- No manual saving, it would be nice if you had two options Hardcore and Standard just for quality of life, the choice not to include this really ruins the game when there's various bugs where marines get stuck in an animation and can't be interacted with losing potentially 40 minutes of gameplay - If a manual save feature is implemented, you don't have to use it if you want a hardcore experience.- The "Stealth" in this game is probably the weakest feature mechanically overall for myself, Aliens and Humans have eyes in the back of their head and will spot you despite standing 60 meters away looking in the opposite direction, it feels rushed and lack luster, being able to crouch behind ANY surface at any point would be a nice addition or view cones similar to commandos/desperados etc- The marines only have 3 voice lines repeated on loop can be pretty annoyingThe game is good, but with bugs and lack of saves can be very tedious to play especially on the more implied stealth parts of the game for now my review is negative for the saving / bugs impeding fun

_childDocuments_.review: Game over man, game over.Alien Isolation - Atmospheric - needs more alienAlien: Fireteam Elite - Weapons, Aliens, - needs more substance more storyAliens: Dark Descent - got aliens, got weapons, got story, got atmosphere - this is an alien game that I have been looking for and want. Such a good game - they all are in their own right, but this one.... This game is like a finely aged whiskey. Sweet smelling story delivered through wonderful dialogue, data pads, and beautifully crafted atmosphere. A burning taste of combat and fear. When you play thing about where your marines are, what they see, smell, hear.... The game does it's best to present this atmosphere (turn music down real low). Feel the cold of Lethe settle into your skin, the wind blowing on the metal shutters of buildings, the creaking of rusted bolts. You sense something is watching you, but when its dark and quite you always feel that way. You tell yourself that this is different and it is, but when? Hours can pass with only a single blip on the cursory edge of your motion tracker. Suddenly multiple blips appear, traveling towards the hallway intersection 20 meters ahead. There are no side rooms nearby, no closets, the nearest junction is 45 meters behind you. Your flashlights catch a subtle flicker of motion, then black glistening skin rushes at you, a blood curdling screech bounces along the wall and fear tightens your grip on the recoiling rifle. You hear them from behind. Blips overlap on your motion tracker, you begin to scream, fire, running forward to the exit. 100 meters and closing, one of your marines cries out as acid splashes over their skin. The door opens, aliens spilling out to surround your squad, but in a last ditch effort before being over-run. Through flamethrower burst, grenade flack, and shotgun blasts the APC rolls around the corner. 100 millimetre rounds cry out in the cold air of Lethe and destroy the nightmarish horrors surrounding your squad.  A subtle feel of relief when you return to the Otago. Relief in a metal shell and fear of the next sortie. Another cold run into Lethe. to save civilians, to end a biological threat, to be food for a xenomorph. Just another day in the corp.

_childDocuments_.review: Picture a real time XCOM, but your squad moves as a singular unit, mix it with some stealth elements and a bit of survival horror, like Alien: Isolation, and you get Aliens: Dark Descent.The bulk of the game is exploring large settlements, where you'll go through all kinds of buildings and tunnels in environments that I feel perfectly capture the Aliens vibe.  The atmosphere is moody and dark, and the familiar ping of your motion tracker will constantly have you scanning your surroundings.  Each mission you partake can be broken up into multiple deployments.  This means you are able to extract your squad whenever you wish and return later.  This also allows you to revisit other areas to collect anything you may have left behind.  The missions also have multiple primary and secondary objectives, as well as hidden items you can find to help your squad, and your ship/base.  Combat is very simple, and a lot of fun.  it can be a bit tricky to get the hang of it, so thankfully the game slows down when you open your command menu for your squad.  You can also set this to pause the game when you open the menu.  Each unique ability requires a Command Point, which slowly regenerate and you have a limited amount of these, so one must really be mindful of your tactical choices.  Your squad also will get stressed out, which causes them to have negative effects in combat, and also these can affect the rest of the squad.  Each Marine will react differently, and as the stress levels build up, so do the negative effects.  There are often times where it's best to avoid combat and detection, as prolonged engagements really take a toll on your supplies, and your Marines.  When you are not on mission, you are on your ship.  This functions similar to the bunker in XCOM, where you can research new weapons and tech, upgrade and promote your Marines, and heal them when they are wounded in between missions.  The story is by no means award winning material, but it does seem to fit well into the Aliens universe style of writing.  Don't expect much in the way of the narrative, except a bunch of cliche's and predictable plot twists.  That being said, I enjoyed the story.  Mostly.Pros:Good atmosphereEasy interface and controlsFreedom to complete missions as you wishCombat is funClassic Colonial Marines armaments, Pulse Rifle, Smart Gun, Flamethrower, Shotguns and auto sentriesChallenging without being unfairCons:No manual save optionAutosave is inconsistent, and doesn't always save after an objective is completedStealth sections do exist in the game, and I found them to be rather tedious and frustratingEvery time you kill a Xeno, your squad gets hunted for a brief period of timeSome missions seem to drag on too long with poor pacingStory is mediocre, even by sci-fi standards, But i still thought it was decent enough to move the game alongIf you're a die hard Aliens fan, and felt like the last handful of games with the Colonial Marines have been a let down, I think you'll be surprised at this title.  Don't go into it thinking it's an action packed FPS.  It's quite the opposite.  It does a great job at building the tension between encounters, much like how the movie did before the Marines found the hive.  For $40, it's really hard to say no to this game.  If you're on the fence, wait for a sale.Overall, 7.5/10Not perfect by any stretch, but it delivers a pretty solid game for the price, and mixes familiar elements to make a fairly unique Aliens game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a tactical game experience that captures, in essence, the hectic last stand of the colonial marines at Hadley's Hope then this is a close as you are gonna get. The gameplay at least is a pretty faithful attempt to recreate the style of the Aliens film.It's unforgiving and can be a little tedious in places but for the most part its a good game. If you enjoyed the gameplay of XCOM then you'll enjoy this. Its a faster paced more real time, realistic, version of XCOM. The story is a lil flat so far. Also some of the characters. It suffers a lil from "modern audience" syndrome in that the colonial Marines are all but lost puppies without the direction of the company rep, who happens to be a rather unlikable character who's there to girl boss her way out of trouble at the expense of male cast members. This is where it falls flat a little as anyone who's seen the Alien and Alien's films know that a character like Ripley is not awesome at the expense of her male costars, she is just awesome in of herself. The difference between well written characters and "modern" characters. That said its not too intrusive and doesn't undermine the action of the game itself. Well worth a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim - very happy I did. I'd say it's closer to darkest dungeon than it is XCOM, with the mechanics of an RTS tactics game + the Aliens classic theme (Oh boy does it land the theme!). Each mission slowly ratchets up the amount of aliens that roam the map until you have to retreat (a la Invisible Inc) - but the neat trick is that your progress towards each mission is persistent! Along with the classic infestation level timer on the base management layer (a la XCOM), you always feel the tension of both impending doom and a strong desire to push just a bit further to get ahead of the curve.It's certainly not the best game I've played this year, but it's a unique, polished, and incredibly coherent strategy experience - and it's well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, lots of intense game play and atmosphere!I've seen a few bugs (Hints: the "Rest" button doesn't persist after you've spent the tool resource to seal a door for resting your squad so, if you miss clicking it, you have to un-weld/re-weld for another opportunity to rest, space station elevator doesn't always open to allow the squad to walk out, leaving you trapped and having to reload the game, others..).One part of the game I really DON'T LIKE is STRESS:- It's too significant in it's impact on game play, not because it particularly degrades marine performance it's just annoying to listen to the game complaining about it! (constant messages from the ARC commander to rest, marines bellyaching etc.)- It doesn't add anything to the experience because the marines (and the player) are more at the mercy of the ever increasing and stacking stress bars than, they are at the mercy of the aliens!  (in other words, it's a never-ending distraction for the player)- Having to - waste - a tool resource(s) on welding a door to overcome stress is not fun!  Especially considering that, tools aren't in great supply in the campaign maps and the (scarce) resources you pick up here and there are better spent elsewhere! (like upgraded weapons)The stress system could seriously be un-invented.  OR, at least remove the requirement to use a scarce resource for welding - safe room - doors only!Other than that, a very good game and worth the money!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid addition to the Aliens video game arsenal.  Very reminiscent of the 2nd film.  Aliens: Dark Descent is essentially a real-time version of X-COM where you build out a squad of different specialists and deploy them into mission after mission to gather resources, rescue people, discover new tech, and advance the plot.  I felt they really nailed the atmosphere, narrative, and visuals.  There were however a lot of bugs throughout my play-through... BUT a pretty major patch was just released that appears to address a lot of them.  Also, while it is a very tactical/stealth game, there were several times I felt encounters were more luck based than skill, sometimes requiring multiple reloads until the AI decided to behave as intended (such as one time where I recall an enemy sprinting across the map directly to my squad even though I had never ever been detected).  Overall, I really enjoyed it and definitely think it's worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed the game after close to 35hrs over the course of 2 weeks. Am a fan of the Alien franchise, and am always eager to try new stuff from it especially since we won't get any new movies soon - so my opinion MIGHT have a pinch of biasness.Overall - 9/10Below is the breakdown of the score: (I will try to avoid spoilers, but if any, I will add a warning)Gameplay - 9/10: Mechanics of the game is very well tuned to enable maximum enjoyment while also making it somewhat complex to make it feel deep. The tutorial is very detailed and lets you enjoy the game while learning. At the same time, the resource management on and off the field make it a bit of a management sim. This part may deter some folks because one might expect an all out RTT minus management sim. Overall, controls and mechanics become second nature very quick after the tutorial.Story - 8/10: Typical Alien story of betrayal, heroism, death, and corporate greed. Which isn't a bad thing because these are what make the Alien movies great. Score isn't higher because it does become oversimplified going closer to the end, and there is an element of deus ex machina at the end; where it feels like the writers only envisioned the beginning and middle, but just rushed the end. Hence, like 90% of the story is great, while the remaining is very mainstream-esque.I would recommend reading the optional logs found in the map. Not necessary to understand the story, but just adds depth.Graphics - 8/10: This is mostly subjective. The art style for cutscenes feels PS3/X360, including the animation. I mostly enjoyed it, but when they start showing more action heavy stuff in cutscenes, it didn't give the full punch of it. As for the in-game graphics, I would say it is what gives it a higher score. You don't need high end specs to full enjoy. I tried it on lowest settings on an RTX3050 (my laptop), and it didn't make the experience worse. The lighting on low or high settings sets a good atmosphere while playing; and the gunfights look cinematic.Sound - 10/10: Like watching a movie. In cutscenes, not much going on to fully utilize their audio arsenal since most of the story is shown through in-game. But when in-game, the gunfights have punch; the movement and interaction with the environment are realistic; and the noise from the xenos are eerie, whether in or out of sight. The music fits the Alien theme and never felt out of place, like its suddenly a generic shooter game. I have a huge phobia of facehuggers (a type of creature in the game) and the noise it makes, including the eggs gave me a proper chill down my spine.Voice actors are movie quality with some exceptions. From the protagonists, side characters, and xenos. Only issues were the repetitive voice lines from the human enemies and playable characters; and the obvious use of the same voice actors. Not immersion breaking, but definitely noticeable.Conclusion: I wouldn't fully recommend buying it full price, as I bought it only when it went on sale. (30-ish Singapore dollars) But in the end, I never felt like I was shortchanged. Plus no microtransactions! The game is a true-blue great single player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a very tight strategy/Management/XCom style game that brings some very cool new things to the table and makes all those new things shine.The main change from your classic squad strategy game is that there is no turn style combat, and instead it is replaced by real time micromanagement of a 4 marine team with different skills and perks. This is probably the best part of the game and, at first, the one that I was most scared of. It is implemented brilliantly, and even playing on a gamepad the controls were very responsive and it felt great. Missions are open ended, which means you can deploy a squad to a zone, do a couple of objectives and go back to base if you see your marines are no longer fit and then come back with a new squad the next day.Another important part of the game is the fact that combat is not the main priority of the missions (even if there are some "boss fights" here and there). Most of the time your squad of marines will be hiding from aliens and trying to achieve the mission goals as smooth as possible. Combat only occurs when the aliens see you, and the more they do the harder the fights become so it is a priority to do things silent and fast. The last part is the fact that this is,after all, an Alien franchise game, so it is full of tense moments and you need to manage the stress on your marines as they face the xenomorphs and see horrors happen.  As stress grow, they will start to be nervous, miss their shots and even freeze and usually it is a good sign that you need to go back to base.Overall a very impressive game, even if it is not for the faint hearted, and I wish some of the mechanics implemented here are brought to other strategy games in the future and become the new standard.
