_childDocuments_.review: This is it! This is the definitive game for Aliens, which was long over due. Game mechanics were designed masterfully to empower the environment, atmosphere and the enemies, letting you to delightfully interact with the play ground (which is persistent btw) and getting most out of it. You can't shoot your way out all they way, and you don't have to run&hide all the time, it's up to you (mostly) Fiction and story are both good, good enough to keep you nailed in screen. A slight negative part is the music/dynamic theme, which is quite good but could've been so much better, (at least it was done back in 1993 in X-Wing), and Aliens score (James Horner) is far too good to be looked over, which I missed in this game, especially in confrontations.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T BUY IN CURRENT STATE!!!(Final edit: The game outstays its welcome after roughly a third through the game. The game is ruined by a focus on endless enemies, and an emphasis on stealth, without providing much mechanics for it. About half the map design is good, and some of it is horrible, a complete mismatch with gameplay. You can abuse many systems because the AI is very bad. Even on hardest the game isn't hard, just tedious with endless enemies, and broken mechanics. Core game idea is good, but implemented quite badly. Atmosphere, and estetics are great, but the story is mostly just noise, with some really bad stuff at the end. Some stupid mission aswell, where you just run around with one character, going EXACTLY where they tell you, not a game at this point. Wait until they fix the numerous bugs, and would personaly get it on a sale. Since about half the content isnt worth much. Did really enjoy parts of it, especially a clutch rocket to the face...) STEALTH GAME, with some heavely punished action parts...It's a stealth game with bad, and few stealth mechanics.Imagine spending 90 procent of your time looking at a motion sensor, looking how the AI clearly knows where you are, and are just poping out new enemies that wander in your general direction.I watched one of my turrets kill 20-30 aliens just poping out of the same hole, and walk out the same door, just to get shot. And be back again in 15 sec, just to do it all again. Over, and over, and over...I still enjoy the game enough to keep playing, but its a shame how good this game could have been. Maybe they will give us more options over our campaigns in the future. But I cant recomend it, in the here and now.The game itself is a mixed bag, some good, some bad, and some really bad. There are frequent bugs, some of which ruins your "runs" by costing you the resource, without giving you the benefit. And some bugs are game-breaking (you can not proceed, and must reload) Voice-lines for example, that accompanies certain actions, play just as often for the wrong actions. Such as "Here they come!", but no one is approching. It's very frequent.You can rest in the game, by welding yourself inside a room. This cost one resource, but sometimes the prompt to rest doesnt appear, after you have spent the resource.You can't burn the eggs with the flamethrower, just let that sink in.Got another bug, where it says that all my marines are not in the elevator, and I will loose those that are not in it, if I use the elevator. Everyone was clearly in the elevator. So I reloaded an earlier checkpoint, got the same message again when I got to the elevator... Tried using using it, didn't loose anyone... Broken mess of a game.Found another bug, were my guy stopped shooting. The gun is on his back, while he just walks around. Died again to bugs, playing with limited saves is not to recomend. This is not a one time thing, had it happen to me four times. Don't play with limited saves.The characters get stuck from time too, which can kill you.And there was this one time durring a mission, when the game grabbed my hand so hard that it got me killed. It stopped me from placing turrets, unless I placed them exactly where they wanted me to, this is a problem by itself. If I hold your hand, and places your chess pieces by my hand, you are not playing chess now are you. I'm playing through you. But it gets worse, the markers that showed me where to put them, was not visable on the map, just in the "normal-view", but you turn the camera all the time, so I missed it. So I ran around for a good long while, and then when I wanted to place it, where I wanted. I couldn't and died. Had to redo about 30 min. This was the fifth mission by the way, not the tutorial.Positives:The atmosphere.The general idea of a persistent XCOM campaign in the alien universe.Most of the ideas, sadly not the ideas that you end up doing the most of.Negatives:Infinite enemies. As in you kill 150 in one "run" and they just keep coming.Spawners, that just pops out a new aliens every 15 sec.Short patrol paths.clearly keeping a minimum amount of roaming enemies, around your current position. A bit shallow. Welding should be a free action.The AI just runs straight at you, no "hunting" or flanking.And the "Alien agression" mechanic ruins the game a bit.Alien Agression mechanic:The aliens are infinite, and when they spot you they come for you in waves. And each time it triggers, the area gets more intense, for the rest of that "run".There are almost no ways of killing them without attracting the hive. So you are heavely punished for fighting the aliens. Which turns the game into a very shallow stealth game.Solution:Have a local infestation level, which is reduced when you kill the aliens, and the queen.This also effect the global infestation level. So that you can push it back, if you play well.Give each level a set amount of enemies, which you can reduce to zero.They should still roam, and track you. And if they find you they will follow, and attack you as a group, waiting for an oppertunity. To attack intelligently.Stealth should be used early until you have a better understanding about the situation, and to avoid wasting resourses/ammo. But it shouldn't be the only way to play the game, were fighting is just a way of reseting the stealth. Leading to some immersion breaking exploits of the game systems.If you decide to get the game, I strongly recomend that you adjust the difficulty as follows:-Enemy health very low (to get the accureate feel of the fire power and abilities that you use)-Enemy reaction time very slow (this will solve some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the stealth, such as being able to burn eggs, before they alert the hive. Trust me)(correction, you cant burn the eggs, even if you extend the time...)-Agression growth very slow (now you can play the game like the movies, and acctually search and destroy, without feeling like you are fighting several hundred alies, when it really should be something llike 80-150 aliens in most locations. Hadleys Hope in the movies, had between 20-30 families if I remember correctly. Not an unending horde)-Put the amount of days to finish the campaign on very limited (This will be your difficulity, and force you to make longer and harder "runs")And I know there are plenty of people that like to make games hard, and I fully agree. But you will only be frustated, and forced to just sitt and wait. They dont roam organicly, in big random patterns, they just hover around you, and infinitly respawn.This is not so much a problem in the earlier levels, yet can still be because you have next to no tools to handle it with.Dont use limited saves, too many issues and bugs at the moment.And if any developer might be reading this. You got a good idea here, just iron out the bugs, add some more campaign settings, and move a away from the stealth, and the frantic hordes. Slow down the pace, make it more methodical. Maybe more focus on ammo. Find more ways to make the game difficult, we like hard, and tense games, but this is not the way. One of the few decent alien games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: One word describes this gameALIENSRemember Alien Isolation?Remember AVP 2010?Remember ALIENS?Remember RTS games?Take Isolation's Presentation, AVP's constant feeling of dread, Aliens Colonial Marines story and shove it into a RTS formula. It came out amazinglyThis game takes has two layers that Strategic layer and the Tactical layer.Strategic Layer In the Strategic layer you customize and upgrade soldiers, you heal the wounded, you build new weapons, do research, progress the story and select missions to go on. deployments can only happen once a day and when you cycle the day you can get random little side missions that have a percent chance of failure and will also use up that next day or you could skip it.. It also allows wounded soldiers to heal and research to progress. As you go on missions the infestation level will rise increasing the threat level of the xenomorphs in the tactical level. Once you are ready to do a mission you go into the tactical level and hopefully you command your squad better than Gorman did.Tactical LayerThis is the part of the game that will keep you on the edge of your seat. Those customized soldier that you dote on and upgrade can give them nicknames. This is where they can die. This part of the game has the ever beeping motion detector which is the most iconic sound in the Aliens franchise constantly beeping telling you your knocking on deaths door and the moment that beeping gets louder and faster xenomorphs are on your squad. you have to react quickly don't freak out hit that space bar to go into slow-mo and hope you managed your limited resources well, and fight the fear. As you explore the map you will complete objectives find supplies to use in the tactical and strategic level and save people to add to you team.  The only "Safezone" in the tactical level is at the APC and even then it only has one turret. Stress, Ammo, Medical, Engineering, Tac points, and hit points these are the basic resources you need to manage to not only survive the endless xenomorphs but to do so while under threat of losing your precious marine who you have invested skills and missions to level them up, good thing you probably picked the option that allows for save scumming and not Iron man where the game save only before and after the mission. Now that you beat that mission you might have missed some objectives and now you have to go back.... sucks to be you.The Game They say this game is hard and it is. If you are not used to faster pace rts's like StarCraft, Command and Conquer, MechCommander, and Dawn of War 2 this game will be extremely hard for you. Better play on story mode. However if you love the Aliens universe and are willing to try it do it, the game will give you everything you asked for and maybe some you didn't. Good ol' quotes, the best aliens atmosphere, great sound design, amazing cut scenes that are of movie level quality and characters who are more then skin deep... hopefully not too deep.The ControlsWhile this is a RTS the controls are rather unrefined for mouse and keyboard (have not tried controller) not bad just not the best good thing you can change them. considering its a squad based RTS you would think you could control each soldier individually as well as in a group and you can but you have to fight the game to control individuals because i suspect the game would actually be too easy if you had proper control over each unit. consider this. you are in a room with two doors and xenomorphs are coming from both you would want to weld one while having the rest of the soldiers set up to defend the other you have certain skills on each soldier and you want the best ones for the job however you cannot command specific units to do things you just have to hope the right one is doing what you want.Score:   8/10Presentation 1/1: Amazing feel of the Aliens UniverseVisuals          0.5/1: Great movie level cinematic's, in-game cut-scenes look like assSounds          1/1: Beep beep beep beepCharacters   0.5/1: Not the greatest but definitely not badBugs              1/1: Very few to noneStability         1/1: Haven't crashed yetCustomization   0.5/1: there is unit customization however its rather limited and the faces aren't greatGameplay      1/1: Both Layers are excellent the fact you can customize marines really adds to the whole tense nail biting tactical levelStory              1/1: While predictable its not about the destination when it comes to Aliens movies or games its the trip to get there.Controls     0.5/1: While decent i just wish i had greater control over the individual unitsPS: I hope it gets mod support

_childDocuments_.review: The game has similarities with X-Com, but in real time and it is set in the universe of Aliens, specifically the movie Aliens 2 from the 80s. Very cool concept indeed and a must-check-out title for fans of either.It starts out very cinematic and fun, the gameplay is also very solid. The concept of commanding the whole squad at once with individual marines deciding things on their own is great and works very well. Slow-mo instead of pause is also great. That way the feeling of real time action is never lost because of extensive tactical decisionmaking on pause or too much micromanagement which is what usually happens with these type of games. Excellent design choices.I still can't recommend the game in it's current state because after playing for 10 hours or so I ran into some issues that killed the fun for me.For once I think it gets really silly when instead of xenomorphs it's suddenly dudes with shovels that start mindlessly suiciding into your fully equipped marine squad. And that they somehow pose a similar threat as actual xenomorphs while doing so. I'm sure the game will come up with a story explanation why this is happening and maybe the devs thought this was a creative original idea, but tbh it feels completely ridiculous and instantly kills any Aliens movie vibe that was going on. You get catapulted into c-tier trashmovie/videogame silly-land and ask yourself what the hell you are doing with your free time. Unfortunately the game takes a similar nosedive on the technical side. There is an UI bug that causes the game to lock up without any way to interact with it further. This forces you to ALT-F4 and lose quite some progress because you have to restart the mission from the beginning. Imho gameplay wise it's a brave and welcome decision to not allow saves during a mission to increase the tension. But if that's the case then you absolutely can't have game breaking UI bugs. This is not some early access indie-sandbox but supposedly a polished full priced game.TL/DR  This game is not bad, there are a lot of things to like and some good design choices. But at the current price in it's current state it is a bit of a disappointment, mostly due to questionable story decisions and a critical UI bug. I would recommend waiting for a sale if you are a fan of X-Com or Aliens 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Your resources are limited, death lurks everywhere and you're running out of time. They nailed what an "Aliens" tactics game should feel like!It looks great and it plays great. The level design is sometimes a bit too linear, but other times you get big open maps that reward thinking ahead and planning your advance carefully. It really pulled me in!I love how many missions are designed to be completed over multiple deployments. You're trying to "clear" as much of each map as possible in one go, which means no matter how well you do, you are encouraged to push your marines up to their limit. It ensures the game stays challenging even when you feel like you've mastered it.The only major weakpoint for me turned out to be the story and writing. It starts off very promising, but towards the end it devolves into a dissapointing run-of-the-mill hollywood heroic antics, which is a huge disservice to the dark sci-fi horror setting. Brace for the kind of brain-dead predictable game writing where the protagonists keep making incredibly stupid and irresponsible decisions and then reality itself bends to let them get away with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a pleasant surprise because it is an incredibly faithful and entertaining squad-based strategy game. It looks just like the 1986 movie and brings enough new to the table to keep things fresh. It has an interesting story, told fairly well both during and in between missions. Managing a group of Marines across the 20-30 hour campaign is satisfying as you kit them out and heal both physical and mental wounds. Combat is challenging and dynamic, rewarding careful positioning, stress management, and deployment of key abilities, although individual unit control could have elevated it further. While the stealth is a bit wishy-washy, it is still rewarding to avoid alien threats by watching the handy motion-tracker. And despite some technical blemishes, Aliens: Dark Descent is the quintessential bug hunt of 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that seemed to come out of nowhere to no particular fanfare which I bought on a whim.And I absolutely adore it.It's a masterpiece of atmosphere building and tension, which is not generally something you'd expect to find in a top-down squad based shooter. It's hard but not unfair. Your marines feel more powerful as they level up and get better gear, but because the devs nailed the difficulty curve so well I never reached the point where I felt noticeably more powerful than the challenges I faced, which is honestly a pretty rare and satisfying thing in gaming. You, the USCM, are the underdogs on Lethe. You are not the apex predators here, and that's exactly how an Aliens game should feel.There's definitely some rough edges, and some aspects that could be improved, but whilst I noticed those things during play, they never once stopped me from enjoying every second of this game. And now that I've finished it, I just want more.I'll be keeping an eye out for any further content they make for this, but it's my dearest hope that they decide to make a longer, more open sequel. They've struck upon a winning formula with this game and it would be absolutely criminal to leave at this.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the campaign I can say I enjoyed this game. I played on normal which is pretty hard. You have the option of a doomsday clock when you are setting of the campaign. This puts something like a timer on how long you have to complete the campaign. But the clock doesn't start ticking until several missions in. Still, I think I finished the game with about 10 days left (I think it started with 20). It took me 40 hours to complete but that was me being pretty cautious and reloading because things went to crap. Also I went after most of the secondary objectives.Some unique things: You don't have to complete a mission in one go. You can pull out and come back another day. Most missions took me 2 deployments, a couple 3, a few I did in one deployment. You have the option in some rooms to "rest" whereby you weld your squad into a room. This lets you save, reduce the squads stress (which is a big component of gameplay), a resupply your command points (use these for special abilities). But you have to use a "tool" to weld a door.Some hard things: On normal, it doesn't  autosave that often. I'd sometimes play 30 min or 45 min without getting a chance to save. There isn't always a good spot to "rest" and save. If you get spotted by a xeno they start to swarm you so stealth is important, but often impossible. You do fight some "people" but the xenos are the challenging part. Bugs: Mostly minor like when you kill a xeno but it's stuck mid stride. Just reduces the immersion. One time a marine got stuck in one location and couldn't move (had to reload). There was one nearly game breaking bug on mission 3 (refinery) where the game kept crashing early in the mission whenever I used the map. I tried avoid using the map but it would crash only a little farther in. I was about to throw my hands up and uninstall the game but I came across a redit post that fixed it.Please perform the following steps:Navigate to Local Disk (C:) > Users > your Windows username > AppData (*) > Local > ASF > Saved.Delete the Config folder.(*) The AppData folder is a hidden folder and to view this folder:Open File Explorer, click on the View tab > Show > click on Hidden items.3. Run Steam and click Steam (upper left) > Settings > Downloads.4. Click on the Clear Cache button from Clean Download Cache and click Confirm.5. Steam will restart automatically.6. Right click on Aliens: Dark Descent under LIBRARY > Properties.7. Click on Installed Files > Verify integrity of game files.8. Run Aliens: Dark DescentThis did not delete my game saves but I did have to redo some of the game settings. I think I ended up rebooting the computer as well.Tips:-Sniper with a silencer is handy to take out a xeno, especially the dormant types.-I didn't use stationary motion trackers early on but I used them more as the game progressed. They can be triggered to attract xenos when you're not around (put a mine nearby for good measure).-Initially I didn't think a medic had much use, but if upgrade them to resuscitate a marine that gets knocked into a coma during a mission it means you don't have a carry that marine around and they can get back to fighting. -Don't pick a map clean of ammo crates. Ammo is the one thing you can't take back to home base (tools, med kits, sentries can be carried out). So if you grab all the ammo on your initial pass through, that could make a return trip very difficult as you have limited ammo with you. Some maps you return to in separate missions as well. I would try to keep the ammo at 10-12 for early/mid mission and keep it at about 7-8 later mission.-Sentries are awesome, but don't do the "Upgrade" for them while their deployed. It's very limited and uses up a tool. Nearly every map has a few sentries in them to pick up so I usually went with one less than max capacity so I could keep some spares at the Otago in case I lost some in mission.-Tech marines are very hand for  missions as they allow you to unlock certain doors that make it easier to traverse a map. I did a couple deployments without a tech and regretted it. You don't have to have them, it just makes it easier. They can also carry drones which are useful for scouting and don't trigger dormant xenos. Possible improvements for the Devs:-Maybe give a slow-mo/pause toggle option while your looking at the command abilities. The only way to change it now is in the game settings. I kept it on slow-mo (you push the space bar and the game slows down or you can set it to pause) because xenos move fast in the game on normal speed. But sometimes I which I could pause it to issue a command action without having to go into the settings. -When looking at the map the game is in normal time. Most of the time I wish the game would pause while looking at the map. Often I had to get the **** out but couldn't really stop look at the map while I was engaged with the enemy. Again, I wish there was some kind of play/pause toggle when looking at the map.-Sometimes on a mission it will make you permanently leave an area either to move into a new map section or end the game. This would sometimes stink when you had some sentries set up but had to leave them behind because the game forced you to. This happened a bunch of times. So, I think it would be good to add a "would you like to proceed" option when leaving an area or finishing a mission. This way I could pick my sentries before I go. The game already does this proceed option when your about to do something very difficult (like fight off a xeno infinite onslaught).Regarding the DLC: It's just a few more uniforms (not particularly interesting) for the marines and the cat from the Aliens movie for the background while at home base. I got it on sale and that's the only time you should consider it.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I love this game. I've been playing it nonstop for the last few days. The gameplay, the atmosphere, it's almost perfect! Almost, however, is the keyword, and it is why I cannot recommend this game. My campaign is forever stuck at 81% complete due to a bug (One of many I've discovered while playing this game). For some reason, I was able to complete a primary objective before it was assigned to me and now my campaign will not progress further due to the game thinking I'm stuck on that one objective. (For reference, I was able to open the shutters on the spire before being given the prompt to do so). So can I recommend this game? As much as I'd like to, I'll have to say no. It's a shame, because without this essentially game-breaking bug I'd recommend it with the highest praise.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I really want to love this game but there is such a dearth of interesting things and far too many annoying design decisions.1. The world's slowest opening tutorial - It's mind boggling how all players are still forced to go through tutorials in all video games. It just makes me pine for indie videogames where their tutorials are optional or outright skippable. Like all tutorials should just be an option at the start menu under 'VR Simulation' or some in-world BS. 2. Unskippable cutscenes.- There are rendered cutscenes that you can skip but you can't skip the in-game cutscenes which just boggles the mind why they understood that you can skip one but not the other. And there's a lot of them too, I felt like there was a roadblock every other minute. 3. Technology - The tech tree feels incredibly empty, there's only 4 main weapons, maybe 3 secondary weapons, and then about 4 super weapons. Maybe the developer wanted to have a minimalist approach to weaponry & tech trees but it had me scratching my head thinking it would've been better just to not have it and instead have weapons be something that you find while exploring the world. 3 shotguns in an abandoned settlement, 2 assault rifles in a destroyed colony, 1 handgun in a prison. 4. Soldier customization - The only useful soldier class is the tekkie which isn't that good. All of the soldier upgrades feel incredibly weak and pointless to where I didn't even care about upgrading them and it felt like a hassle to upgrade them. The seargent, gunner, medic, and recon are useless and add no extra benefits over the common soldier. I really wanted to just retrain everyone to being a tekkie because then I could have flying attack drones but nope everyone is randomly assigned 2 different class branches, and then all of their subsequent upgrades are a diceroll too. Which meant that most of the upgrades I got were not upgrades I wanted. Terrible soldier skill customization. 5. Clone world - a minor gripe is how all the civilians look exactly alike. Apparently once you join the Weyland Yutani group and go to work in space you have to shave your head. Cuz you know everyone in 1979 movie definitely had a shaved head, man, woman, everyone shaved head... Except not. The marines are allowed to have hair that you can even customize but the citizens you're saving can't. IDK I hope it was a bug. 6. Humans > Aliens - This is where the game officially lost me. On the first map it's nothing but aliens which was fun and spooky and scary. On the 2nd map, it's nothing but humans, even worse is that it's humans with melee weapons. However you're a marine squad with fully automatic laser weapons but somehow the humans are able to run through your laser bullets and get 6 attacks on you with a sledgehammer while you automatic rifle their face before they finally die. I actually looked for turning down the difficulty in the menu since I had set it on hardest or 2nd hardest level but there was no option to do that and I wasn't going to restart my game. The enemies should've been androids to at least handwave why it takes 594827520 shots to kill them.

_childDocuments_.review: ps :The Shepherds Chapel Channel Youtube with Arnold Murray an Dennis Murray. OVERALL RECOMMENDATION:- Maybe worth $40. Better to get on sale- Recommended for old school players. Gets Boring fast.- Has charm despite being rushed/incomplete- Alien franchise carries the imperfect gameplayGAMEPLAY MECHANICS:- Squad-based point-and-click control (team moves as unit, not individually)- Involves strategic hide-and-seek gameplay with aliens- Uses movement tracker devices to distract aliens- Includes marine stress management system- Features turret placement for combat situationsDIFFICULTY & PROGRESSION:- Later levels become notably boring and punishingly difficult- Hidden time limit revealed in final segment that can cause game over- Odds stack against players whether they rush or take their time- Constant alien waves with numbers that only reduce during scripted eventsPROS:- Good atmosphere and level design- Well-implemented fog of war effect- Solid art style and attention to detail- Good ragdoll physics for aliens- Evokes old-school PC gaming charm- Adequate lighting effectsCONS:- Camera has noticeable lag and momentum issues- UI animations and hold-to-confirm actions slow down gameplay- Basic, repetitive alien behavior and combat- Limited resource management depth- Backtracking can be annoying- Slow menu transitions at home base- Basic RNG event card system feels incomplete- Graphics can be blurry even at high resolution- Character models are blocky with limited animations- Audio lacks environmental depth- Voice acting is repetitive and dryTECHNICAL NOTES:- Can run on lower-end PCs with reduced settings- Requires admin rights to avoid crashes- Shadow settings impact performance most- Controller precision issues; mouse recommended- Some stability issues reported

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fun. Game play is pretty good, missions are interesting, solid alien story from what I have seen. If it actually worked it would be great, so maybe in 6 months to 1 year it will be solidly playable. Don't buy this game. The game is riddled with bugs. Doors that cannot be opened even after breaking a weld, elevators that don't work that you're required to use to continue, datapads that appear but cannot be collected stopping secondary objectives, soliders getting stuck in walls (would be funny if not for the fact that to do anything objective related you need all 4 members of your squad present), your troop is four individual units with 4 individual pathing, and they can uncommonly get stuck on something causing your troop to be spread out over the entire map (can sometimes fix by madly clicking run options everywhere, sometimes they'll follow a path you didn't send them on at a walk speed forever), sometimes soldiers will just fail to do the given command but it still uses a command point, command point totals sometimes randomly change during a mission (for unknown reasons a mission that started with 5/5 command points slowly dropped to 2/2 over time with no personality trait, stress events, or unit death as possible cause), autosaves sometimes just choose not to autosave (completed two main objectives, one secondary, squad got wiped, went to autosaves and found last autosave was start of the mission 2 hours previous) and there is no way to manually save to fix it, units uncommonly switch to their secondary weapon when they still have abundant ammo for their primary with no injuries or circumstance (not carrying a person for example) to cause a need to do so and unit refuses to switch back to primary for seemingly random time interval, etc. etc. etc.I'm sure there is more that I either didn't remember or didn't think was disruptive enough to mention. The game was released in what I would call a functional state overall, but only if you have patience enough to deal with the wall of bugs and glitches that will come with playing. I didn't encounter the game-breaking bugs until after the refund period passed so I do still plan to weed through what I have, but I would warn others to wait until the majority of the reviews don't mention terrible bug problems.

_childDocuments_.review: This has many ingredients of a great game.But it falls short at delivering emotion and it is not believable.New personal you acquire has no face - is only introduced as numbers and later as names. You need to track names to know who is who. A simple portrait and maybe a background story would've done a lot for building up emotion.Things are heavily scripted and obviously so, with repeated patrols, dead aliens being respawned, taking away from an emotional experience. Leaving you with a game you don't want to experience but only optimize.For instance many events are heavily scripted and there is no threat at all until you press a button. In one case this is very obvious as you can see a horde of aliens running about outside of the map back and forth to make a stressful situation. Until you realize the situation does not change until you press a button. Only then will the aliens enter your area. This feels pretty terrible. There are many such things.In one event your marines will leave your sentries behind. You actually don't need them for the event, so you will have to load and play the event again without placing the sentries to keep them.Marines carrying people walk slower which makes things believable. But everyone of them can carry a sentry and run about with all the other equipment. When your realize the gamey things the illusion breaks.Boss aliens loose their terror, because there are masses of them.It is a shame, as many things are executed very well.So if you are more into number games and gamey games, playing the mechanics and optimizing, this might be for you. But if you look for an emotional experience look elsewhere. This is a bit like a b-movie.EDIT: Oh yes, and the bugs. Mesh rendering bugs where the face of a marine gets stretched in a cutscene. Holes in meshes.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Descent is to  what Isolation was to .It's faithful to its source material in terms of both theme and gameplay.I especially liked how this game restores the Xenomorph to an extremely threatening position.  Whilst other games in the franchise tend to make the monstrous creatures less imposing, the titular aliens in this game put your squad in constant (and very real) mortal peril.I really loved having to work with the stress mechanic. The marines are tough, but they sure as hell aren't fearless.  Fighting the aliens harms the mind just as much as it does the body.  As their stress mounts further and further, each marine will begin suffering debuffs, such as shakey hands (worsening their aim), or confusion (hampers your ability to use special commands).  If they're stressed out enough, they'll begin developing traumas, such as paranoia (stress increases when in large squads), depression (starts out with increased stress) or an assortment of phobias (stress increases when nearby certain things).You have the ability to customise your marine's appearance, and they each feel unique thanks to certain personality issues and tendencies they can have.When you inevitably get attached to certain marines, this game will not shy away from making you watch them die horribly.  They can get burned by acid, gunned down by human opposition, or torn apart by Xenomorphs.  Your squad can get facehugged, heabitten, or put into comas.  One of my marines had his arm torn off, and had to be fitted with a prosthetic once he was carried back to medbay.  You can't manually save, either, and instead the game autosaves at various points, so if something goes horribly wrong, you may simply need to accept it and move on, or surrender a considerable amount of progress.  I think this decision was one of the games biggest successes.  You need to plan carefully, act wisely, and think things through, because your actions have serious, long term consequences.The game also expands on the  universe wonderfully, and it's absolutely rich with new lore, whilst staying perfectly authentic to source material.  As a big fan of the franchise, I could tell the developers were, too.The gameplay struck a very good balance between simple and complex for me.  There was no need for micromanagement of each squad member, but this did come at the cost of some strategical options.  You can't split up, the squad moves as one at all times.  This means you're limited in positioning and manoeuvering, but there are generally workarounds to get certain marines in certain positions away from one another.Despite an array of weaponry at your disposal, none of your combat options wind up obsolete.  Skills from the early game still have many uses after you unlock late game equipment.  These tools, when combined with the ability to open up and block off paths, focus suppressive fire on certain areas, and set up defensive perimeters at your own discretion, the combat of this game is exciting and challenging.  If you're caught unprepared, it's a struggle for your life that you're likely to lose, but if you strategise and plan ahead, you can take control of the situation, and come out (relatively) unscathed.You'll be playing defence far more frequently than offense in this game, and actually, your best bet is to simply sneak around and avoid conflict as much as possible.  Your marines truly do face a dark descent through hell, and I'm all here for it!I appreciate the application of Xenotech in this game.  It gives you something to do with all the corpses, for one, and offers a grounded exploration of the use these creatures may have to Weyland Yutani.Much to my surprise, the plot and characters of this game had me engaged throughout.  While it isn't anything incredible, I felt compelled and interested in the story and wanted to progress it.If that was all, I'd give this game 5 Stars, but despite my enjoyment while playing it, and my fondness for this franchise in general, Aliens: Dark Descent has a serious problem.  It is absolutely riddled with bugs (not the space kind) and glitches that vary between comical to game breaking.  Fact is: if you play this game, you will encounter bugs.  If you're lucky, they'll cause you some mild annoyance.  If you're unlucky, they'll set you back a couple hours.  Plenty of bugfixes have been rolled out, but the game is still plagued with them.  On numerous occasions I was forced to load earlier saves due to glitches ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ me over. Sometimes something would happen, and I wouldn't be sure if it was an error or not, like strange pathfinding, AI, and inconsistent command responses.  In the end, I found myself having to use exploits and oversights to even the odds against a game that sometimes did not work.Unlike many other modern games, which are fundamentally flawed, Aliens: Dark Descent has a  chitin solid foundation, and a lot swinging in its favour.  I have confidence that after a few more rounds of thorough bughunting, this game can truly meet its potential.  I'm holding out hope that an expansion will come soon, with a set of brand new missions and challenges to overcome!

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens, Dark Descent, is a fantastic X Com style game. There are areas that are better than X Com while others are worse, but an overall fantastic game and enjoyable experience. I am currently on my second run in the new game plus. The voice acting is mostly good, with only one voice actor that is just reading his lines. He is not until later in the game, but it does come off comical in contrast.The audio is fantastic. Very reminisce of the Alien(s) movies. They did a fantastic job of it.The game play is very enjoyable. I find that my biggest dislike is the inability to control individual units, like in X Com, but it is still highly enjoyable. The skills and tools are well done and implemented.The game is not completely trouble free, but the fix is just restarting the mission before launching the mission. The game does have a couple of game breaking bugs that I ran into, but fortunately the saves to restart a mission saved me each time. Both times was dealing with a foe that did not spawn.In short, I highly recommend Aliens Dark Descent. This game is highly enjoyable, so much that I am playing through a second time straight after. There was a notification that additional and different things happen in the New Game Plus, so I am looking forward to that.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4.5/5)Alien: Dark Descent is a thrilling blend of tactical strategy and intense horror. If you love the Alien franchise and strategic gameplay, this game is a must-have.Pros:1.Deep Tactical Gameplay: Control a squad of Colonial Marines, each with unique abilities. The real-time strategy with pause lets you plan and execute your moves carefully.2.Immersive Atmosphere: Eerie lighting, haunting sound design, and detailed environments create a chilling experience. The Dev team did an amazing job at recreating the signature atmosphere of the Alien Franchise. 3.Gripping Story: A compelling narrative that keeps you hooked from start to finish.4.Replayability: Various difficulty levels and different strategic approaches ensure the game remains fun over and over again.Cons:1.Steep Learning Curve: May be challenging for newcomers to strategy games. It wasn't for me, but the devs even warn you at the beginning. Just follow the tutorials closely and you'll be fine. Alien: Dark Descent delivers a masterful mix of strategy and horror, making every encounter with Xenomorphs a nerve-wracking delight. Dive into the darkness and test your tactical skills—just remember, in space, no one can hear you scream.

The sound stage, the characters/acting, and the gameplay reminded me of that movie at many moments, and made me re-install Fireteam Elite and Isolation, because the nostalgia power was strong.It's not without flaws - at time of writing I've some 55 hours gametime, and this is because 30 hours in I got a progression softlock bug that wasn't fixed in the patches to date. _childDocuments_.review: To start, my first play-through was on medium difficulty. I meticulously explored every area of every map, picked up every single item, piece of equipment and hidden objects and had great fun doing so. My second play-through was on Nightmare and No One Can Hear Them Scream mode (a combination of the hardest difficulties) along with the "New Game +" mode, allowing my marines to attain level 15 while giving new experiences along the way. The mechanics are well thought out, generally optimised and quite true to the original Alien lore and universe (although there were no shields in the original universe!) I'm looking forward to another campaign, perhaps another NG+ play-through with different marines.Some minor downsides - nothing overwhelming or fundamentally broken:- Control over the camera is occasionally taken from the player to show a certain cutscene or event in the game - this occasionally results in damage to your team since you cannot observe the full area until control is released. Additionally, the game does not always return the camera to where the player had it originally (e.g. orientation) so if you like your camera aligned with a particular direction, you'll be adjusting it often.- There are some fairly basic bugs such as team members getting stuck in cover that necessitate a reload. While generally not a big problem, this can be frustrating when playing on Nightmare mode along with No One Can Hear Them Scream mode (where you can't save as normal).- There are the occasional moments where you are forcibly extracted and can risk losing equipment or missing hidden items (e.g. datapads) without prior notice. In my first play-through, I reloaded back two missions as I had missed a datapad that I thought was retrievable later (that area of the map had been permanently closed off following objective completion).Overall, a fantastic game with some mechanics that are extremely fun and definitely one I've thoroughly enjoyed getting all the achievements to score a Perfect Game on!

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I am not a huge fan of this franchise, but because it was an overhead tactical I had to try it. To my suprise it ended up being pretty damned good. I'll keep this as short as possible as my reviews tend to be way too long. Pros:1) Great visuals and atmosphere, the colour settings were greatly appreciated the green overlay is horrible for my eyes.2) Squad play is great and actually refreshing, very intricate compared to most tactical squad games. 3) Lighting is also fantastic, especially the heavy use of the squad flashlights which at first I thought was going to suck and be difficult to use properly but I quickly adapted and it became very helpful and massively added to the immersion.4) The story is coherent and pretty good but it feels like some elements should of been dropped earlier and perhaps missions could of been a bit shorter.5) Squad communication, small layers of banter, the little things, these things are really fun. 6) Soundscape accompanying it was also awesome.Cons:1) Not much in the way of weapon and armor customisation that have a gameplay impact. There is no weapon customisation at all and armor has no flexibility beyond different colour patterns. 2) Missions are way too long, I understand they're designed to be done over multiple deployments, coming back and going to the same place over and over in a game like this when encounters are so wildly unbalanced is frustrating, especially early on. Acid damage is extremely painful and you can quickly run out of marines over 2-3 deployments too easily. This is especially difficult with the Doom clock past mission 5. There is an upgrade to get later on to mitigate it completely, still its frustrating.3) Boss encounters are extremely meh. Especially past level 10 for your marines. Hello hello hello plasma overcharge.4) Story like I said was good but took too long to develop properly. Began to feel like a chore towards the end. 5) Facial animations are janky at times and some dialogue is just weird, its almost as if Hayes has forgotten she works for WY while whining at other people for doing it, shes also way too sure of her own plan to begin with, then it just randomly stops, thats not characters development thats a "This is gone on for too long, crap, need to cut it off" from the writers lolI hope there will be DLC expansions or something that adds more missions or context to the story or perhaps just something that adds to what we saw at the end. I know the end is a big reveal of sorts but it still deserves way more attention. Over

_childDocuments_.review: You know I thought I was going to hate this game prior it to coming out. I remember hearing there was a real time tactics/RTS being made in the Aliens universe and I thought this is going to be awful. Even after seeing what was released for it at the time and watching several convention videos showing little bits of game play I was really on the fence about this game. I only bought it because I'm a fan of the old series. Like a lot of people playing this. It took me a while to get into it but by the end of the game I actually think it's really good game. I'm glad they tried something else for a change. Being a fan of RTS and some RTT games as well it didn't take that long to understand how the mechanics work and for the most part they do so really well. You have everything Aliens shows you available to use. Plus loads more new stuff and some extra heavy weaponry that's not in any of the films to use later on. You often get the use of an APC you can deploy (with you troops if you wish inside) to different parts of the map. It will assist you in combat too if anything comes near it. The maps are fairly large too and there are usually multiple maps within one. So for instance you'll be on the surface of one and then take an elevator down or up to which takes you to another maps. They're all quite maze like a times too with lots of places, rooms and goodies to collect and explore.   The graphics are really nice looking too (although peoples faces and hair looks pretty bad, but you're not close enough to really look at their faces apart from the squad selection screen). Lots of detail has poured into the environments and even the "skyboxes" look amazing. The game has done the best out of any game to nail the look and feel of "Aliens" so far. (I just wish they used the proper pulse rifle sound and door opening sound from the film). I'm amazed they managed to make an RTT game actually scary and tense, it's quite impressive. People compare this to something like most recent XCOM games. While it takes some inspiration from it, to me it plays more like Desperados 3. It's all real time, you have abilities to use. Instead of controlling one person at a time, you control a squad that moves as one and attacks as one. Using sentry guns, the suppression skill and flares to aid you in combat at certain points is really a life saver.The game is heavily story driven and cinematic surprisingly. The story is quite interesting too, if not a little bats*** at times. There are some really cool moments in it. There are some really well done cinematics too with nice framing and epic moments. The lip sync and character animation could've been a lot better though. Of course accompanying all this is a damn pretty good musical score taking influence from all of the original 3 Alien films. I really hope they keep improving the game. Or that they add some more content. Or more story stuff. Something co-op related too would be awesome. Two players controlling their own squads and helping each other out etc..If you're a fan of the franchise, give it a chance and try it out. It's well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: The most conditional not a recommend I've ever wrote.I would recommend this game only to people who have a huge interest in the Aliens universe and like RTS, OR this is your very first 'hardcore' strategy game. Odd i know so quick TLDR; fantastic visuals, okay sounds, subdued music, interesting game play, weak story, disinterested voice acting, it is a stealth game, short game time, very clearly rushed at the end, enough bugs and weird choices to annoy veteran RTS players, easy and forgiving enough for newcomers to the genre/style.Aliens is without a doubt my favourite film and I adore it, so naturally I have an interest in the universe like the comics and weird off shoots like AVP, I despise Prometheus and Covenant. RTS are my bread and butter next RPGs so safe to say I knew what i was getting into and looking for in an hard Aliens strategy game.I'll address the difficulty first as its what most people will be curious about, I played on hard at first then restarted on nightmare after the 2nd mission because in my eyes I messed up so catastrophically bad my squad should have been wiped yet instead I walked away with minor injuries. Now the difficulty changes the Aliens health which is already iffy in an RTS as you would want smarter enemies or more numerous not spongy. There is an infestation timer that will ramp up the more days you take (THIS IS NOT THE DOOMSDAY CLOCK) which effects how many aliens roam the map and which variants compose the patrols, It can be lowered via a late game research repeatedly. A doomsday timer (difficulty also changes it) that is generous and only starts I think after mission 5 so about halfway through the game. Not all of the classes are balanced with the recon stealth sniper and sargent command point increase easily being the best followed by medics and gunners for forced hordes then the tech marine being downright useless. This is a stealth game and as such if you are detected by a xenomorph you will be hunted and the difficulty meter for that expedition will get harder, launching special xenos and hordes at certain milestones.The environment, I could gush for hours talking about how perfect the game looks down to the boxes found in some random supply closet, put simply its visually a perfect 1:1 of Aliens. The sounds are okay not great but not bad either apart from the guns all sounding the same, the smart gun uses the pulse rifles sounds as does the SAW pulse rifle. The voice acting is ooft a mixed bag, ranging from okay like the MC or awful and phoned in with the marines to pathetic whenever a movie line is used, It feels odd like they forced them at gunpoint to say "just another day in the corps".The story starts interesting and sets up some kinda worthwhile threads but falls apart in the third act, due to banking on a very weird twist and a personal connection to a character. Said threads go nowhere and will leave you with more questions than answers. The most interesting lore can be found in logs or the log could simply be a leaflet saying "join now". The game does touch the cursed Prometheus lore. The promised deep and hard choices are laughable "hmm do i deploy today or gamble for a new mechanic". Minor story spoiler ramble. The game is not long at 12 missions, each can be 100% in about an hour and a half, so don't go in expecting much management or customisation of the marines, its not X-com no matter how many reviews say "its like X-com!" its not.Accuracy wow what a bizarre modifier, each rookie marine has 50% accuracy so they hit 50% of the time and only get better, simple right? Wrong the moment they level up once their modifier changes from 50% to a range of 40% to 60% okay not the end of the world, you can always get lucky and add points into the accuracy perk or the crit one to compensate, and slap on the scope mod for some materials. Maybe the type of gun could help? Nope the smart gun aims no better than a handgun.FORCED CUTSCENES DURING FIREFIGHTS this happens far to often and will lead to some awful encounters as you will be fending off a horde and need to grenade something, but oh no here watch this door open.Inconsistent warnings before fights I personally hate the warnings but one moment you go to open a door "warning make sure to be prepared" thanks game, the next time you walk down a corridor suddenly, you are in a holdout mission or endless horde and need to shutdown an alarm. Game pick one and stick with it either no warnings or warn me.Humanoid enemies except for , are tedious and appear in the worst maps (pharos spire excluded), like stupidly tight corridors that will force an onslaught with no way to dodge patrols.Weapons are samey apart from some special abilities most all do the same damage or have slightly higher DPS.Poweloader escort sections that you can't command them where to move.Bugs and BUGS! I have encoutered 4 mission/encounter ruining bugs, Xeno queen pathfinding, door to progress not opening (fixed on reset), squad leaving stealth for the entire mission after grabbing a synth, a marine teleported back to when they first entered the powerloader and almost died.Only 2 category 2 xenos, runners having a neo dodge with decent health and being instant detection.Xenos don't climb on walls (i get it, that would be hell to balance/program), they don't flank and use vents, they will spawn out of their hidey holes the exact second you need to cross them, they are clairvoyant and one will always patrol right into the room you are in despite it never doing so for 10 mins before you got there.Welded doors are useless except for resting, as they are made out of paper and xenos always target them even during patrols which to me undermines the point of them and the importance during the films.The last mission has supplies to collect coupled with a story falling apart leads me to believe they wanted to do more but ran out of time.To reduce infestation you do a research task, instead of you know the optional queen killing which to me makes heaps more sense to slow down how fast xenos breed and infest the planet.Complaining over.Maps are great minus some cave sections and anything to do with ships or space stations due to the before mentioned tight corridors forcing fights and zero manoeuvrability.The game becomes sooooo much better with the APC to have a fifth man, its criminal how late you get it, as it opens up a lot more tactical flexibility.Now i recommend this to new comers to the genre because it does enough right, is fun and and engaging, and its not out to rip you a new one like some other harder RTSs while still providing a challenge and squad based tactics.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. But beware before purchase that there are game critical bugs risking you being unable to progress through the campaign!However, I did purchase the DLC after playing until I hit one of those bugs myself, just to support the developer team because I'm hoping that the team will fix the game stopping bugs...... and release an expansion!They have absolutely aced the Alien theme, mood, and key characteristics. I love the small unit of marines sneaking around the Weyland-Yutani outposts, hearing the pings and seeing the white dots on the radar moving. Then you get spotted by a Xenomorph, sometimes you realize it will happen before they do and stress sets in while you're thinking of how to not make this become a disaster, but sometimes it catches you totally unaware. Either way, you walk backwards in the corridor while your team is wailing away with their machine guns and automatic rifles at the crazy fast aliens.Sometimes you realize things will get hairy early, so you set up as many sentry guns you have with you, toss a couple of flares further in front of you and command a dude to setup a suppressing fire vector slowing the aliens as they burst towards you. But after a sustained period with the gun barrels running hot you realize the ammunition tickers are steadily running towards zero and a genuine Alien movie panic sets in.I thoroughly enjoy checking the map, planning the safest paths to your objectives, keeping an eye open looking for eggs lurking that you need to torch before you're spotted, using the iconic flashlights in dark rooms to find crates you can loot... the missions are swimming in suspense, making gun action incredibly frantic.The developers have crafted solid game mechanisms working together. The mission launches from your base, the exploration of the outposts, the finite resources you can carry. You have recharging command points that you might need either to burst abilities in a frantic encounter, or place mines to cover your back as you progress forward into the darkness, or use to snipe a Xenomorph that hasn't spotted you yet. During the missions your marines get experience and at your base you get to level up those with enough XP, later choosing their class, and upgrade their abilities. And those all actually changes what you can do in the next missions. Your stranded Otagu ship is a base in between the missions that actually feels alive and with a purpose for the game.As you can tell I could go on... I just haven't been this immersed in a game for a really long time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly is better than I expected. I will say there are bugs and things I would suggest in a remastered edition or a sequel/ follow up game. While close to the end and not giving spoilers the story is pretty good and making me want to know what happens next. Weapons/ classes are interesting with each one bringing their own use. You can customize you characters within reason and give them skills based on what you see fit.As for suggestionsFirst off I feel as though the hard timer that gets dropped before everything is done for comes too early by a level or 2The ability to field 5 marines is cool but it is never really brought up till you find the thing that allows it and even then it instantly goes into a cutscene of you recovering it then ending the deployment causing you to waste time on the doom counter that is in place.Customized class abilities feel like they need to be more diverse with once you unlock the class there is no reason why people would not pick stuff like silencing a sniper or being able to bring back downed Marines. Also the tech marine feels pointless at first because a perk that allows other marines to unlock doors and stuff.Also possible limits on how many of a certain weapon can be in a squad would be nice I run 3 plasma guns a smart gun and a regular pulse rifle (for the grenade launcher) and the ability to do 3 concurrent plasma overloads just destroys any threat even the boss xenos in seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the latest X-Com remakes, but set in the Aliens universe, and you've got Dark Descent.  HIGHLY recommended!Pros: - Accurately re-enacts the dark, bleak atmosphere of Aliens - most of the levels are darkly-lit, full of enemies, and a constant sense of foreboding dread.  As soon as one of your female marines yells out "LET'S ROCK!" and starts to light things up just like Vasquez, you'll feel like you're right in the middle of the movie all over again, and the whole feel is truly amazing.  Your marines are constantly saying hilarious ♥♥♥♥, you'll hear random sounds here and there, the motion tracker is always going off, etc. etc.- The storyline/campaign will run you a solid 20+ hours.  It doesn't stray much from the source material, and leaves a few questions unanswered by the end, but it still managed to be pretty compelling and kept me hooked all throughout.- Graphics are pretty impressive, even though this isn't a category of game that would ordinarily boast of graphical quality.- Gameplay is fun, as you'd expect - the controls might even be better than X-Com as your squad moves as a unit and fights automatically, so you won't feel like you have to micromanage your team too much - all you really have to worry about is special commands and healing.Cons:- The tension and intensity is constantly ratcheting upwards.  Even on story mode, I found the game incredibly difficult, and eventually resorted to using WeMod cheats, lol.  The aliens always have the upper hand, always seem to know where you are, and always have the numbers, so you'll end up having many moments where you have to decide between lifting up and carrying an unconscious marine slowly back to the APC, or just getting the hell out as fast as you can before you're all dead, to regroup and come back on a future mission.- There are definitely a few bugs - I had to replay a few levels because certain events later in the game just didn't happen (i.e. opening a bulkhead door at some point that was already opened).  Other times the scripted dialogue would quickly scroll through several events in a row without those events actually happening.- Missions can be full of a lot of fluff - each level inevitably has doors that need to be unlocked, power that needs to be restored, cameras that need to be activated, etc. etc.  Seems very fetch-quest'y. Overall, for $40 (at full price) it's hard to go wrong.  Tied for my favorite Alien game since the AVP game of the early 2000s.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does exactly what an Aliens game should do - it captures the feeling. You get the same feeling of, "Please don't make me go down that corridor," as the marines surely did in Aliens. The undertone of dread when a blip creeps ever closer to your position.The gameplay has some issues, to be sure. But the mix of X-Com squad management, Darkest Dungeon hopelessness against an alien threat, and real-time combat are well (though not perfectly) implemented. Even if you aren't a huge Xenomorph fan, you may love the small-squad shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: A Good Work-In-Progress game!!I’m enjoying being back in the Aliens universe as a strategy game! Let’s get down to the details:The squad-moves-as-one makes sense from a realistic standing but it makes it a bit tricky to achieve the angles you’re after for things like suppressing fire or sniping; often times my snipers were in the very back of the squad and would, for example, be the last one to exit the room- not exactly ideal if you’re trying to get a fix on a target which already feels painfully slow for a class that’s supposed to be a sniper.The marines can get overwhelmed very easily and not just from a “you picked a bad strategy” perspective but they often times don’t feel like they have the appropriate tools to survive. They can get killed or knocked unconscious very quickly and often times it’s easier to just leave them on the ground than pick them up and carry them unless they’re high level or you’ve got some kind of attachment to them. Same goes for your sentry guns: you absolutely need the extra firepower most of the time but you’ve got to ensure those don’t get overwhelmed either else you’re down a gun.The environments are beautiful!! It can be very hard to see at times and I’ve had to bump up the gamma a bit to be able to see. The game runs hot and I mean HOT: my 3060 is hovering around 70 when the game is just sitting there running so I think some optimisation is in order and I’ve seen similar quibbles by others with better cards than I!There are balance issues, too. Like, I get your marines aren’t super solders but they quite often seem a bit too fragile. One thing that could help is if they could execute their Command actions faster. This is from a “hey these guys have < 10% stress and no bad traits, how come it takes him so long to pull out his shotgun, aim and fire?” you can (and do!) miss quite a bit and that’s without the Xeno’s doing their weird Matrix-style dodge. Another thing that needs some attention is the banter and interaction voice-overs that I’ll detail below individually.* The constant, incessant prodding from your “commander” to “get moving”; at times it’s annoying and can reach points of highly irritating and has even been known to be triggered as I’m moving the squad: Please stop pestering me to ‘move’. I can appreciate RTS games I grew up with did similar things but for whatever reason it comes across as highly annoying .* The squad responses (“I hate this job”, etc.): it’s funny the first six times but after six hundred times it’s ridiculously obnoxious. I wish they’d have spent some extra cash to generate a deeper pool for these VO responses given you’ll be hearing these a considerable amount more than any cutscene dialogue.All told, the game is decent but needs some polish. Visually it’s quite pleasing but the balance issues and fragility of your marines (both physically and mentally) needs some tweaking given how long it takes to train up a marine to beat the bad traits out of ‘em and make ‘em worth while.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of cool concepts were attempted here unfortunately the whole thing is a buggy, oversimplified, ui/ux mess.I don't usually get excited for a game in a beloved IP because too often they lean heavily on their IP to be good games, and ending up failing to deliver. Despite being an obviously lower budget game, Dark Descent held some promise. The Previews make it look slick and we polished, but that's simply because you're not driving the action.The tutorial is an absolute dog. In reviews, there's a lot of comparisons being thrown around here, XCOM, Darkest Dungeon, etc. The game warns you it's "difficult" and it's important to pay attention to the tutorials, but it's mostly because the menus and controls don't make sense for KBM, and are extremely clunky in realtime. Menus and functions are buried under menus, under menus. This makes the stealth elements that much more frustrating. I can't tell you how many times I failed the "stealth" section of the tutorial and had to go back and skip a cinematic because guess what - the autosave sucks too. Hey - go click a stealth green hotspot over there, then press another key to "hide". it's worse than an early RTS with specialized keys and functions grouped together in nonsensical ways. Get detected? You are dead. And not insta-fail dead, but deluding you into thinking you might have a chance by firing off a few shots before getting 2-shoted and out. Once you get your squad it's no better. Your special abilities and functions are in buried in two separate menu/screens with combat actions in one, with a completely different ones than the context sensitive click on unit ones. Sprint? Sure, only until we feel like it. Want to cancel that stance/action? It's another esoteric key press. Hoping to sprint / hide in one smooth action? Nope, control is clunky and at worst detrimental to the brutal stealth mechanic. My squads in early 2000s RTS were be able to automatically adapt to their terrain. The "nearest" marine capable will perform n action leaving it impossible to maintain a strategy.Most things you'd want micro control over are automatic, so there's no sense of engagement, and those things that should be automatic, aren't. It's a confusing muddle mess with teams and units that never feel quite like they're listening or on their "A game" with pathing. Animations, voice acting, voice sync in cutscenes with laughably bad characters that can't quite decide whether they're a caricature or photo-real, failing on both counts.Having heard / seen outside of the tutorial from streams and other resources, you can tell there's a much bigger world out there other the mess fo the realtime mechanics - but hoo boy.  I am afraid to play it again lest I lose my ability to return this janky mess by running over the two hour mark.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a fascinating blend of survival horror and real-time tactics, set in the iconic Alien universe.-Engagement: Dark Descent excels in keeping me engaged. Its unique blend of stealth, resource management, and squad-based action captures the essence of the Aliens franchise.-Gameplay Style: Unlike traditional turn-based XCOM-style games, Dark Descent opts for real-time control. This intensifies the experience, making encounters with xenomorphs nerve-wracking and strategic.-Ambient Atmosphere: The game’s ambient design is outstanding. It immerses players in the eerie, claustrophobic environments reminiscent of the film.-Length: The game’s length is satisfactory, striking a balance between providing substantial content and avoiding unnecessary padding.-Graphics: Dark Descent boasts impressive visuals, enhancing the overall immersion.However, it’s worth noting that the game does have technical bugs, which can occasionally disrupt the otherwise smooth experience.If you’re a fan of the Aliens franchise, Dark Descent is definitely worth a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game. The respect and love for the franchise is evident; It has all the interesting and captivating elements from the films while still being innovative in characters, story and new lore. I in particular loved how cinematographic the game is! The cutscenes are really cool and the way the gameplay tells you the story through tasks at each level feels also organically integrated for the narrative. The variety and fun of mechanics is in my opinion great game design. Customizing your marines gear, appearance and skills made me care for them and strategically think on how to specialize my team for mission success. The game amazed me on how well it captures the essence of the Aliens film. After playing colonial marines and fireteam I must say this game is the best on the vibe-essence because it captures perfectly both the action and horror aspects. In other games I felt unstoppable with the iconic pulse Rifle but in Dark descent you have to very often hide and select optimal routes. You have to be clever instead of generic action. Every time one of my marines were abducted and carried deep into the hive or they said one of the limited but powerful lines of panic as the iconic "game over" I felt empathy. Also the stress and trauma mechanic lowering your marines performance and the possibility to cure them with therapy was a interesting addition. Horrible too was that you can read the specific wounds affecting your marines and you have vissible effects as slow moving or poor shooting, or even they can get unconscious so you should assign other to carry them back to safety.Fighting hordes with Turrets, safely exploring the map using a drone, hacking doors for shorter paths, using silenced sniper rifles to avoid calling attention... that was super satisfying capturing the Tech part of the USCM. So, to summarize my opinion: This game is fun? Yes.  Has good lore? yes. Is a generic and forgettable use of license? no. Makes you feel like a USCM commander? yes.The game off course has some flaws. In particular it had bugs which i was surprised to experience as I supposed by now they should have fixed most. Sometimes the UI commands did not work, the camera became locked or unreal ungine crashed. Anyway these bugs were not at all a problem as reloading solved all. Also some scene dialogues felt generic or obvious and I think a better more natural and deep writing could have been done. In general I really liked the voice acting and cutscene quality so those meh parts were upsetting considering the great quality of most parts visually and narratively.Oh, also the Datapads similar to the Text logs in Isolation are worth reading! They have interesting data on the main story or more personal individual stories of persons in such a horrible franchise universe.I must say as a huge fan of the alien franchise I am very biased ahaha. If the game was awful I would have tried to find something good... fortunately this is not the case. I enjoyed a lot the game. Actually, this is my first Steam review!  It was so good I had to write a review.Aliens dark descent is the best game capturing the horror, action and strategy of the second film. It has the  Sci-Fi, distopic, biology-science, philosophical and ethical deepness and quality of good Aliens stories.I recommend it a lot for old and new Alien fans. I bought it on sale and feel the price-quality was very very satisfying. I inmensely appreciate all the work put by so many people into doing this amazing game.
