_childDocuments_.review: A really well made X-Com like Aliens game, though the combat is not turn based but instead the core gameplay is real time tactics it still  very much has a lot of influence and elements from X-Com such a doom timer, a main base you upgrade stuff from between missions and other similar pieces,  alongside those it has its own original elements such as that all your marines are affected by mental stress which can cause them to perform worse in missions and even get psychological traumas overtime that need a psychologist to cope with or a special perk you get from levelling your marine.You control a set of 4 and later on 5 marines in a squad that moves together as a singular unit, though it works fairly well for the most part they should've made it so we can also have more individual control over each marine which would spare players from some occasional frustrations especially when attempting to be more sneaky because the game's squad system keeps positioning your silent sniper in awkward spot in the formation while you are attempting to silently take out a Xeno. So it would be nice if they are less glued together, something they should take in consideration for a potential sequel or maybe even an update in the future for this.When doing a mission you can EVAC any time you want, so if things are getting too out of hand such as supplies running low, marines too messed up or the game's dynamic aggression levels increased far too high for you in the mission you can get out of it and rest up your marines and prep a new team to continue the mission the following day. Any doors you opened or welded, any items you picked up, enemies you killed, progress you made will all get remembered the next time you get back there so being careless can be costly when you return for a 2nd or if needed 3rd deployment on the same mission. I managed to beat all of the missions with just 2 or 1 deployments on Normal difficulty and it was a pretty good challenge i must say, this is not an easy and forgiving game and medium strikes a good balance i feel personally but there are two more higher settings and also the ability to fully customise your difficulty, so if you perhaps don't like doom timers at all you can set it to so low it becomes basically a non-worry but perhaps you want the Xenos to be incredibly dangerous and you can then set them to very hard while setting resources to normal. There is also an ironman mode which limits you to two auto saves, while the regular mode lets you have about 10 ish auto saves, there is no manual saving per say outside of getting your marines inside a room, welding all the doors and hitting the "rest" button which heals their psychological statuses and gives other benefits alongside also saving the game.There is also stealth in the game and usually it's advised to keep yourself hidden as much as you can, however don't think you have 100% stealth the game, it's not designed in that sense and eventually some of the later missions you have to start engaging in combat some more. If you force yourself to stealth too much it can become detremential to your enjoyment, so use both stealth and combat in a smart way, just cause you got spotted doesn't mean that's it, you can still escape before more show up, hide, and distract enemies to pull them away to another part of the map. Utilising both stealth and combat together instead of soully focusing on just one is the best way to go.Visually majority of the game looks fantastic, the environments, the mood, the detail in said environments, lighting, shading, effects, weather and sound design are all stellar but the only thing lacking are the human faces and their facial animations which are very subpar. Story is fairly interesting, i wasn't expecting much out of it but i got a pretty engaging story involving alien cults which only the dark horse comics and some books explored in the past, though it feels some side characters very much didn't have enough time to really develop into anything since majority of the story is largely focused on two characters, so when some of the side characters perish you feel nothing as they were mostly just background noise often and not much else.- The aforementioned limited individual control of marines- The game is buggy, i didn't experience anything too crazy bad but i did have some lower and meidum sized problems , moments of Xenos just freezing up when they die, two times Xenos got stuck inside a welded door which made the door un-destroyable for them, i had the game once spawn an onslaught (horde) on a side of the map where they could not reach me, had a few times where a marine got stuck on a piece of the environment, one mission where you go down into some mines caused the game to randomly eat all of my RAM dipping my fps 1 but reloading the game fixed this issue, had one moment where my marines opened fire while in stealth for no apparent reason, - All missions are story missions, i was expecting there to be some non-story missions you can take on in between the story ones but there is not, all missions you jump into are story missions, those story missions have a good amount of side objectives to do and pretty large levels to explore, go through and approach in your own way, i just felt like i wanted also some non-story levels to do and complete for extra resources or other things- I wish the main base/ship had more things to upgrade and work on- There is a about 2 missions or maybe 3 that don't involve your actual squad mates but instead the main and side characters of the story and feel more like interactive story bits and not too much else, they stick out and should've not been done the way they did it honestly, would've been better if it was just a really long cut scenes rather or completely re-make those missions to involve your actual marines instead.- Performance is somewhat sketchy, not bad but not amazing it depends on the missions, some can have odd stutters, others run perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly good real-time tactics.I’m not usually into the genre, much preferring turn-based combat for strategy games,  but was pleasantly surprised by how well Dark Descent conveys the tension of any decent Alien movie, taking most of the inspiration from Cameron’s sequel. Can’t stress this enough- the atmosphere and palpable feeling of danger, waiting around every corner, would be incredible for an action game, but for a tactics game with a top-down perspective, it’s unparalleled.Add a pretty competent core gameplay, having a lot in common with the latest XCOM titles, but significantly toned down complexity-wise, and you’ve got something very enjoyable for any Aliens fan.The strategic part, with a ‘base’ for troop recovery, training, and even a certain degree of freedom on a global map, is very much an XCOM lite, with a minimal number of available weapons, upgrades, and research paths. It’s fun, but you’ll likely unlock everything moderately useful long before finishing the campaign.There’s an obvious soldier customization, although individuals seem much less personalized than they are in XCOM, which is a miss IMO. At least changing soldiers' appearance would be really nice, so losing them wouldn’t just mean losing a competent combat unit.Tactical gameplay is the core of Dark Descent, and all of its mechanics, including (annoying at first) trauma and negative traits, guide the player towards a less action-oriented walkthrough. Basically the less you encounter the enemy, the less your soldiers suffer from PTSD, and the more you save on the ammunition and medkits. The perfect approach involves lots of electronic recon, hacking and welding the doors, quick decisive squad movement when necessary, sniping the wandering alien or two, and avoiding contact at all costs.This gameplay style leads to a lot of tension and a healthy respect for the enemy, as you don’t really kill a lot of xenomorphs, thus savoring that horror core of the franchise.Sure, the game allows for a guns-blazing approach, and there are lots of options in terms of class abilities and weaponry, never mind the turrets, but overall Dark Descent doesn’t encourage this, especially on higher difficulty.The game mostly doesn’t outstay its welcome, although, by the time you’ve fully upgraded everything and found your perfect tactical approach, it’s probably going to feel repetitive, maybe affecting how you feel towards the last couple of missions.The last mission is actually the worst, and though understandable from the story point of view, it’s totally unforgivable by anyone who feels a connection to the squad members (and I don’t mean story characters).Story-wise, don’t expect miracles- if you’ve seen any piece of the Aliens side content, you already know what’s what. The plot carries the action well enough, but you won’t remember a thing after finishing the game.The soundscape is great and definitely plays a large part in how uncomfortable you’ll be most of the time, with the only nitpick being a very repetitive soldier voice-over. You are going to hear the same battle cries over and over and over again, and it gets old fast. Understandable, considering the budget nature of the game, but shortcoming nonetheless.Can’t know how someone with no prior Aliens exposure would feel about this title, but if we don’t count any crossovers, Dark Descent is possibly one of the two best videogames in the franchise, the 2nd being Aliens- Isolation.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 out of 5 Stars. Not Recommended. Absolutely suggest a Hard Pass on Aliens : Dark Decent. It's hard to over-emphasize just how much I hate this buggy, un-intuitive and poorly conceived game. Major issues ...Soft Lock Glitch : It's mission killing, random, no work-around. Restart the affected Mission if saved.Limited Save Slots : Yeah, your older saves will be overwritten. Save too much you can't restart missions.Bot Stress : Always goes up, but never goes down unless you use limited resources (Meds & Rest/Save).Resources : The entire game is one gigantic "Go For" game of consumable resource fetching ... pathetic.Difficulty : No matter what difficulty level you play, the game will increase it as you progress a mission, requiring Rest/Save & Withdrawals. It's not challenging, it's just deliberate Dev obstruction of progress.Story : Simple, trope-filled and predictable story that takes too many hours to advance between Swarms, Glitches, Gopher & Rest/Save. Anti-Player Dev-Team : To compensate for short story & poor mechanics, Dev's scripted Player failure in to some missions. Every sub-mission with Maeko will generally require multiple runs w/o cut-scene interruption. Just another example of Dev-Team's anti-Player Progress intent. Not challenging when mission rules change and opfor bots insta-spawn, insta-spot and insta-kill; it's just annoying. This Dev-Team sucks.Bot Squad : Dumb as a box of rocks. Sometimes will auto split party in to enemies & ignore attacks.*** Original Review Below ***The Developer's choice to use an isometric perspective was just bad and the bad development decisions just kept cascading from that baseline of bad. Controls and actions are awkward and often require multiple levels of menu depth. Aside from the actual glitches that were shipped with  the retail release, sometimes game progess can be stopped simply by the interaction of "squad" elements in the environment, due to poor pathing and cohesion.The never-ending resource hunt. In order to distract from a very short and simplistic story, the Dev-Team added the resource gathering sub-game to Dark Decent. Not only will you gather resources for your ship, the Otago, but you'll also need to constantly gather  sub-resources for your squad. Combined with an atrocious Inventory management system, the resource grind simply delays story-line progress.Game-play is dictated by the Dev-Team decisions and their poor scripting skills. The game deliberately punishes the player for non-stealth game-play with massive onslaughts almost guaranteed to result in a "Man down" condition. Even when the player conforms to the dev-team's preferential stealth mode the game mechanics consistently impede player progress with focused swarms that require significant idle time "hiding" to avoid. So, if you want to play fast you get hammered, but if you comply and play passive you sit and spin on your thumbs instead of playing the bloody game.The Bot Squad is too random and emo. The "squad" never operates at an optimal level, because the Dev-Team chose to add ridiculous random negative traits and assess performance penalties for any kind of contact, or even proximity to the Aliens which the squad is story-line trained to combat. Also, not only do you have to grind particular Bot Squadies to advance them, but you have to pay for each of their individual advancements with another kind of resource. again, the Dev-Team goal throughout Dark Decent seemed to have been to impede Player progress.Graphics and sounds are "meh". The isometric perspective, even when fully zoomed, features low-res modeling and VFX. The sound design is basic and nothing rises beyond that level to draw the player in to the moment. In fact, I quickly grew tired of the looped Bot soundbytes and the canned alien noises. Neither the graphics, or the sound help to immerse the Player in the story.The story is very trope laden and short. I suspect that if it were not for all the deliberate barriers to Player run-throughs the game's story could be completed in less than four hours of casual play. There just isn't much meat on the bones of the Dark Decent script. The voice acting is fair, but the rendered scenes are \unimpressive.You can find all the cut-scenes chronologically assembled for streaming and I would recommend you skip the game and just watch those story-line videos.I can't believe IGN rated Alien : Dark Decent 7/10, but ranked Alien : Isolation at just 5/10. NEVER TRUST IGN.I could go on, but you don't want to read it and I'm sick of typing about this terribad game.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent mish-mash of genres to create a creative and unique experience that feels just as tense to play as Aliens did to watch. This is a survival-horror/ real-time-strategy/ RPG-lite with an emphasis on stealth and strategic combat. For the dev's ability to coherently mash so many genres together alone, this game warrants your attention. Game runs very well at 1440p with an RTX 3080, i7 9700k and 32 GB of RAM and all settings cranked to max. While I do occasionally encounter bugs, they are minor (ammo pick-up icons that don't fade when they should, character repeating canned voice lines occasionally during a firefight, etc.). Just shy of 17 hours in (and roughly 1/3 of the way through the game based on level-count) and I have yet to encounter a bug that has hampered my enjoyment of the game. If you are in any way a fan of the franchise or have a passing interest in any of the genres this game manages to stitch together into one product, I couldn't see the game disappointing you unless 1) you are a hardcore fan and take issues with how the lore is expanded in this narrative (I personally enjoyed it), 2) find the game too stressful or difficult to enjoy (the default difficulty is harder than your average game, I'd wager, and more horror-themed than the average strategy title), or 3) you are a purist of the horror, strategy, RPG, or stealth genre and don't appreciate how this title curtails and simplifies mechanics from each genre to keep things manageable for a wider audience and easy to learn and play. This truly does feel like the Aliens analogue that Isolation was to Alien. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface comment with the following: I have made it half way through the 2nd mission at the time of writing this review. No spoilers.Very cool RTS game and faithful to "Aliens" lore. Very immersive in atmosphere and gameplay. I remember Fireteam elite that came out two years back, it didn't really keep my interest, missions felt repetitive and got boring after a while. Different kind of game, but it's all the more important when you know that game was a fastpaced shooter. This game, story gameplay and all sucks you in and keeps you meticulously checking every corner. The individual marine upgrades you can do balances well with the rest/ healing system. You can't keep taking out the same marines every time unless you want to wait 3-5 days. In this time bad things can happen to your crew, extending rest or healing periods, and not to forget the increase in "infestation" over time. This way you have to balance your troops and decide tactically which people are the right ones for the job (and so you can't take out your already leveled troops out every time). I can say a lot of great things about this game, the only negative i've experienced was with the squad AI. Sometimes they get a bit stuck when given an order to move somewhere. RTS Game: 8/10 Good implementation of squad management mechanics, abilities, and unique squad members. Gameplay somewhat unforgiving at times, but lends it self well to strategizing and making sure you engage the situation correctly. Sometimes buggy ai mapping. Overall very solid.Aliens Universe Game (so far): 10/10 Every Alien wants to kill you. *Ping*------*Ping*----*Ping*---*Ping*--*Ping*-*Ping*Ping*Ping* "Game over man! Game over!"

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a fantastic game. In the modern era of copycat/similar games this feels special. I like how the challenge is not linear, i.e. easy, medium, hard etc. There is an added layer of uncertainty, in that the longer you stay in a mission the hairier it gets. You stop and think, man, do I need to get an EVAC? I felt that the acting of the two main leads is particularly good and kept the main story rolling. I have not yet finished the game but have no doubt that the game will continue to provide fresh challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't support 32:9. You can temporarily resolve this issue with a config file fix but it comes back every time you rest (you probably rest once every 15-30 minutes or so). Restarting the game fixes the issue until you rest again.Pretty fun game but feels like it should have been baked for another 3 months in QA. Tons of bugs ranging from minor annoyances to game breaking but to name a few I've encountered:- Running out of ammo went into the negatives and then gave me infinite ammo afterwards.- Game allowed me to rest in unwelded rooms (normally, all doors would have to be welded shut)- Characters getting stuck while doing actions. Normally resolves itself with a little fidgeting but rarely permanently forcing a reload.- Game doesn't always save when it says it will- Sound levels can randomly change- Lighting can change randomly (this only happened once, assume it had something to do with the map)That said, if they fixed the above issues I'd recommend the game. _childDocuments_.review: This has been one of the best games I've played this year. It's definitely one of the most underrated games to come out in 2023. Don't sleep on this one if you like X-COM type games. Here's what I liked:1. Gameplay is tight, frantic, and frenetic. The feeling of being a small squad of USCM sorely outnumbered really comes through. 2. Voice acting is top notch. Seriously. Some of the best voice acting I've heard in a game. There was a part where Harper talks about someone I won't spoil it but you can hear the emotion in his voice. 3. Great story. I feel people often take the story for granted but when it shines it can really set a game apart from its peers. This game had a pretty decent story. It wasn't amazing and the plot was predictable BUT characters consistently behaved in believable and thematic ways. A lot of times in games (and especially in horror movies/games) characters behave really stupidly. Not here. So props to the writers. 4. The music. It was epic at times, subdued and brooding at others, and when you're playing it gets out of it's own way.Here's what I didn't like:1. Had a couple bugs that made me C2D in the beginning chapters (though this went away after I think chapter 5 or so)2. The MAP. Very confusing. I wish you could click on the map itself to order your squad to move. The orientation of the map doesn't match the orientation of the camera in-game so you'll pull up the map and there's a little trapezoid thing that shows where the camera is facing and then you have to remember the orientation when you close the map. Also if you pause the game and open the map it unpauses the game. Maybe it was intentional for the map to be a bit confusing to add to the pressure? 3. After awhile the missions can feel kinda samey. It didn't bother me too much because I enjoy this kind of gameplay loop but I can see why some would find it repetitive. Overall I think Aliens: Dark Descent is a great game and well worth the price of admission. I rarely get to finish games these days but this one had me hooked. Once I started I kept playing until I finished it. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long time fan of the Aliens franchise but not so much the majority of the games that have been released.  However, this is the first game I actually enjoyed and played all the way through.  It was challenging yet fun.  I liked the characters and the story.  The mechanics were a bit glitchy at times including a game-breaking but once (a simple reload fixed) but today a patch was released that might fix most of those glitches.  It took me roughly 35 hours to beat it... it was a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Common, but entrancing story arc in the Aliens universe.  The game started fine and got better as it went because of more story development, capable marines, and refined tactics.  Two big positives are the leadership skills and the slow motion if desired.  The base line weapons were damn near spit ball guns, so the leadership skills and slow motion were essential to utilize.  Seemed like there were good balances with respect to resources in the game- not enough to be wasteful, neither too scarce to be ridiculous.  Liked that saving in the game is tied to rest, which was tied to stress.  It did not feel tedious though.    Graphics were not over-the-top, but decent.  There was pleasantly a lot of detail in the maps.  Upgrading the marines is a bit random, but in a good way.  Soldier classes were done well with some nice perks as they leveled up.  Something I was not fond of was the frequency of random enemies.  Why is there always a bad guy around?  One sentry dead, two dead, three, four, etc.  It felt pointless because the baddies kept spawning.  There were some glitches, but nothing game breaking.  I enjoyed the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay just finished this game and all i can say is as a big Aliens fan I can without a doubt give this game an very strong 8.5/10. This game has been brutally challenging and i love it. The generous save/load system has really saved this experience in a lot of ways. Missing limbs when taking to much damage, the incredible scenery, music and graphics of each level just does an amazing job capturing the alien universe. I am so very excited for what the team/devs of this game continue to incorporate into this gem. Personally i would like to see some improvements with how you "engage/kill" the alien enemies. If there is only one alien and you kill it while there's no other aliens for miles should not trigger "being hunted" so i suggest having like a small death cry scream radius, this would be a very welcomed mechanic. By doing it this way i believe this will allow players to do the guns blazing AND stealth around approach rather than just having the game HEAVILY punish you for making to much noise and therefore giving us no choice but to take the stealth approach on almost all missions. I really enjoyed the mission where you had story characters to control, i just wish they had their own unique abilities rather than the generic stock marine abilities. An idea for future content/DLC, might i suggest "legacy missions" telling stories both past and present to help fill some gaps or explain some fan questions that were never answered. Then having control of single or few story characters at a time during those missions would definitely bring more attention to this incredible game. Yes sometimes a squad member might get stuck on things and aliens being able to insta find you while you're perfectly hiding does suck and for these small issues and many of the already reported bugs in the game im sure you've been sent. I believe these are the reasons this game is not quite a 10/10 game....yet haha Im very proud of this team for providing an amazing true to the lore experience and i look forward to the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding theme, atmosphere, gameplay and control. I'm an OG Aliens fan born in the 70s and this game blows me away. They nail the tension and survival-horror aspects of the movie 100%. Gameplay (once you get the hang of it) is intuitive and fluid. There are many 1st person Aliens games out there (going all the way back to DOOM: Aliens TC) but this is what I've always wanted. A tense, pensive, tactical squad-based game with resource management.Combat is fierce and satisfying. Setting up a killzone with sentry units and suppressive fire as a tsunami of xenos launch themselves at you is just insane. Boss battles are epic and very unforgiving. But aside from these moments, the game absolutely encourages you to stay quiet and undetected. If your marines are detected, they will stress. If they stress for too long, they'll be prone to shooting wild and/or using up more ammo. And if you run out of ammo, deep in the hive, far from extraction, game over man. Forcing the player to learn when to fight and when to stay quiet is one of the game's greatest strengths. Case in point: nervously checking your motion tracker for movement, seeing none, you enter a room and are terrified to see it is full of eggs - which are now opening. You now have two seconds to decide if you have enough time to quietly back away out of sight before a half dozen facehuggers hatch - or eff it launch a grenade to clear em out and wake the entire nest. You now have 1 second to decide. Absolute masterpeice game design.I have minor quibbles with a few things - there are still a few bugs (ha), and I think in some areas the balance can be tweaked. I'd personally love a Nightmare+ mode where saving is live (no reloading whatsoever) and the slow feature is not quite as slow. Also the squad based control is superb but occasionally I'd prefer more granular control. For instance, taking individual control of a recon unit to get into position for a snipe. It is clunky having to move 4 or 5 marines when all you want to move is 1.But these issues are very minor. The game is incredible and I cannot wait for future content.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good real-time with pause tactical combat game.  The overall campaign is reminiscent of xcom, but it plays more like somebody threw in a dash of darkest dungeon after switching from turn based to real time.  The levels are large and interesting, the classes work well together, and the game rises in difficulty well.  I think the opening level when you have a real squad of marines was the strongest part of the game but the length was just about perfect, it ended right as I was ready to be done with the more stressful and more precision requiring late missions.The game finally gets stealth right by making stealth not a thing you need to do to live but one you want to do because fighting aliens wastes resources, generates stress, and advances an internal clock that makes successive encounters rougher.  It also accepts stealth through superior firepower, if you can kill something instantly even if you do it loud it doesn't trigger a hunt until an actual live alien spots your actual team, which leads to some interesting strategies.The story is perfectly servicable.  It exists, it's aliens, it won't really make you mad.  The voice actors and everything are good, but the game isn't trying for any fancy twists or big new lore in the setting, it's just executing a standard tale quite well.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Descent presents itself as a tactical game, with squad-based missions, persistent map design, the ability to level up your marines, as well as research for various pieces of equipment and upgrades.Unfortunately, the game falls quite flat in the tactical aspect - I'd label it more as 'tacticool' as opposed to actually tactical, and this is the major reason I requested a refund. First of all, you can't really move or position individual Marines in a squad - they always move in a clump, and thus setting up things like ambushes for incoming xenos is impossible. It also makes avoiding acid splashes from dying xenos a massive annoyance, as any sergeant with two brain cells would instruct his squad to spread out to mitigate splash effects. Actions you request are generally taken by the soldier closest to that area / item / creature, so you might end up with the least effective soldier for that action (for example, suppressive fire) performing it. Attempting to specify individual actions can be tedious due to the way the game's UI is set up - you're really just meant to command the squad as a whole instead of trying to command individual Marines. I understand this from a top-down perspective - you're the deputy administrator overseeing the missions, after all. However, this doesn't make for engaging - or tactical, for that matter - gameplay. It feels as if the game's overall mechanics and design were intended for 1) people too lazy to manage 4-5 soldiers, and/or 2) consoles, since they use controllers.The motion tracker either doesn't function correctly or the devs decided to pull some BS maneuvers - pings on the tracker will show up as individual aliens before the squad is discovered. However, often times a single ping somehow magically transformed into 4-5 xenos - and yes, those pings then individually showed up on the map. It baffled me to no end, so unless this is a bug I can only assume the devs 'cheat' the spawns and enemy placement to increase difficulty.The autosaves are tedious and annoying, and reloading a game because you screwed up will often put you right before an unskippable cutscene that you have to watch - again - before attempting whatever scripted event the devs had set up. The scripted events in general are annoying, as they randomly lock / unlock doors, end missions before you can retrieve valuable equipment, force you to upgrade Marines and equipment without being able to make the choice yourself, and a host of other things. Then again, considering what I perceive as the target audience, I shouldn't be surprised.The devs also added RNG events that can randomly cripple, traumatize or otherwise negatively impact you. Some of them are also positive, where you gain random resources in exchange for losing the ability to deploy soldiers for that day. I don't think this added anything to the game, and actively detracted from it. I'm personally not a fan of purely negative RNG events that only exist to cripple your success. There's better ways to handle it (see XCOM 2's dark events, where the player's resources and capabilities allow them to choose which events they can counter and which events they can suffer through). Again, another mark against it being 'tactical'.If they had added inherent mod support many of these problems simply wouldn't exist, and I would give it a thumbs up just for that. As it stands, it's a mediocre Aliens game LARPing as a tactical game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid Alien(s) game, even in the lategame when you have everything figured out, things can go easily tits up, and with a solid plot overall.The squad control is finnicky and tends to also go tits up from time to time, and generally bugs are present here and there, but they didn't detract too much from my own experience.The sound design is rad, the enemies are rad, the missions, albeit "only" 10 (2 are kind of massive scripted sections that help propel the plot forward), they are extremely long and are supposed to be done in multiple takes (as in: you retreat a squad and let it rest up, and deploy another in their stead). My first campaign from beginning to end took 37 hours, and next to none was spent to backtracking, just slowly progressing, trudging through xeno corpses. Solid recommend, especially if you want more Colonial Marine action (in tactics form) after playing other Aliens games like Fireteam Elite.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is a EXCELLENT addition to the many aliens games through the years, mixing a solid blend of stealth and unique RTS combat goodness, well worth the cost. Details wise though, it definetly has some nasty rough edges, so lemme go over the good the bad and the ugly (aka: bad that wasnt a concious decision)Good+Combat is solid, each encounter is fun and is balanced on a knife edge. +Stealthing around the map leaving motion trackers and baiting enemies toward trapped areas is excellent+ Enemy variety is extremely good+ solid xcom style base with good upgrade varieties+ difficulty feels very well balanced. + enemy combat AI is surprisingly good, doing things such as trying to drag off downed marines. Bad-Story ranges from serviceable, to downright terrible, particularly toward the end.-Certain mini "Story" missions feel half baked and unnecessary -Final mission in particular is a colossal letdown both story and gameplaywise.Ugly-Voice acting gets extremely repeteative, and varies wildly in quality -There are some occationally nasty bugs that can ruin gameplay (such as being unable to rest and save in safe rooms)-Sometimes the "cinematic" camera will rip you away from combat to show you a story thing you ran past, which can get the squad killed. Gripes aside, having played virtually all of the other alien games out there, this is still one of the better offerings, and well worth the cost (I got it for a birthday gift, but would not be sad to have paid bucks for it)

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my mind on this game. Initially I was disappointed and irritated by the mechanics. Sometimes there was a deadly delay in orders being followed and it led to frustrations.I made myself push through and underneath is a story rich (I enjoyed it) RTS here. There is so much more that COULD be done with it. Adding deeper RPG like elements would increase immersion. Having more influence about what ship parts to repair or develop would be fun. Having a system of rank which actually makes a difference to squad cohesion etc would be awesome. That said, what is there is enough to enjoy and play through.It does require a reasonable amount of trial and error at the beginning and some of the frustrations remain but in general, I do recommend this game as a fun and engaging RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike many tv show adaptations that aren’t faithful to the source material (looking at you, Netflix, with The Witcher) this game is about as true to the movie Aliens as you can possibly get.  There are so many callbacks and references to quotes from the film that it would take you pages and pages to catalog them all.  It was very clearly made by people who are not only familiar with the source material but have an affinity for it as well.  Believe me, it shows.The cut scenes are awesome, the sound effects/sound track feel like a perfect extension of the films, and the game play lets you experience the tension just like the marines did when they entered Hadley’s Hope on LV-426.Some games are carried by the merit of the source material they are based on.  I can’t even tell you how many objectively mediocre Warhammer 40k games I’ve played that suddenly became decent just because of the subject matter.  Would Dark Descent be GOTY if it didn’t have the word “Aliens” in front of it?  No.  Would it still be a good game?  I would say so.  But the respect and love paid to the franchise in this game is so prevalent that that it makes it a worthwhile purchase for anyone who is even remotely a fan.This next paragraph is more of a feedback section directed at the developers rather than part of my review but I’m just going to leave it here:  If you’ve played any X-Com you’ll find the base building aspect of the game incredibly simplified.  I would have liked it if there was a bit more thought and decision-making whilst restoring the Otago.  Similarly, character progression is a bit of an afterthought outside of class selection. Nothing really felt meaningful while leveling up squad members other than them being able to access better guns.  However, these are pretty minor nitpicks and something that could easily be improved upon in future installments.  They absolutely nail everything else.Speaking of future installments, any future Aliens titles released by this team would be an automatic Day 1 buy from me.  Thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. It has a deeper similarity to XCOM and Resident Evil, that a lot of players seem to overlook: At first, you are a bit stressed by the monsters. But in the end, you will be the monster that stresses out the aliens. :) Every working strategy, trap, unit composition, new technology, ... it gives you joy. If you think that you have figured out a cheesy way through the game, maybe an exploit, it only makes it more fun! I think that the game is lovely paced and the difficulty is really good! If you are a bit new or feel cautious, go for an easy difficulty. :) Also: the story is pretty good. I enjoyed this very much. Full recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to how its advertised this is not an action game. You find out pretty early on that you are basically required to stay hidden as much as possible or your troops will lose sanity/morale which causes them to get negative stats. They aren't permanent, but it takes time to remove them which is annoying given the doomsday clock for the campaign. Don't get me wrong it isn't hard to manage, but I was a little disappointed that I couldn't run in guns blazing creating mountains of alien corpses in my wake like the trailers suggest. Having said that its still a pretty good game. Graphics and game play are solid and even though its not the game I went in expecting it to be it is still fun thus far. Worse case scenario you put it on easy and just enjoy the story but for most people it isn't necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: Already Finished it!TLDR: You like the Alien license? You like X-COM? Then you will love this game!Is it like X-COM? No! But it takes a lot of ideas from it and does something different to keep it fresh.The game has some jank here and there, sometimes I was going mad and had to load very old saves to bypass some softlocks, but patches will iron them out I am sure.Other than that: Absolutely nailed the atmosphere, sounds, music, feel of the movies. The gameplay loop was great and you are free to do whatever you want. The ending was a bit disapointing (kinda fits the universe)... but lots of questions never got answered. Probably setting up for DLC or sequal? Either way, it was a good time and I can't wait for more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! It’s extremely well made, with a great story and amazing graphics. it’s the whole package. Took me around 30 hours to finish the campaign, and if you’re into RTS games, this is a must for you.Having said that, it’s no walk in the park. Every session felt like work, and I needed breaks to recover. The death clock mechanic didn’t bother me much, maybe I just got lucky the way I played it since I had more than 18 days left. Had I known about this before starting the campaign, maybe I would have played it differently... Maybe I would have spent more time on the side quests to max level my marines before the death clock kicked in.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth your time and money, especially on a sale. This one gives you what you want from an X-COM style game, but you get the aesthetic of ALIENS horror, in a real-time rather than turn based set of rules. It's game play loops through waves of suspenseful exploration, into bouts of extremely high stress preparing, fighting and maybe running!Beautiful level design, interestingly you play on each level multiple times, there's set objectives and you extract at any point, able to go back in if your marines are too shook up. The squad and your marines really grow on you, their roles unique and balanced enough to want them all different specialisations.It's a decent story that has you exploring a different aspect of ALIENS lore, focused on the dark side of Weyland-Utani's experiments in the colonies, where they have a lot of power.A fun, sometimes spooky adventure in the ALIENS universe. Friends reading, buy on sale if you like ALIENS and RTS.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a MIXED review....I bought this game originally because people were saying it's like XCOM. Well... it's KIND of like XCOM. Without the punishment for failure. I'm on my first playthrough playing on Nightmare difficulty because I like to challenge myself. In this game the challenge falls short due to the fact that you're not punished on death. If your squad wipes you're met with 2 options. 1) Main Menu, 2) Load Game. There's no option 3 which I would assume would've been something like 3) Return to Outpost. This takes away any real care factor on wipe. If anything it's annoying because you have to replay 10 or so minutes of what you did up to that point.My second gripe... which wouldn't be a gripe if there was a "return to outpost" option... is that there's no save. Yes, I'm aware you can save when you weld yourself in and choose to Rest. I RARELY rest though. I typically scavenge every available room and find enough meds to deal with stress loss that way instead. So when I do have a wipe it's quite annoying replaying content I've already played. Another nuisance is that you can't tell your Marines to hold fire. If you're being hunted and would like to hide and your marines happen to spot an Alien that you're trying not to be detected by they will open fire immediately. It would be great if there was a hold fire option. Other than the few negatives that I have towards the game mostly pointing towards difficulty... The game plays really well. I haven't encountered any bugs yet that everyone seems to be mentioning. The customisation options for your marines suck compared to XCOM but at least there's some things you can choose. I would recommend this game on sale perhaps.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. The gameplay is nothing like XCOM as I previously thought. It's realtime with optional pause / slowdown for using special actions. You control your squad as a singular unit, and there's a heavy emphasis on stealth, at least if you want to make any kind of progress. Xenomorphs respawn infinitely and you can't clear the map of them, but you can make it worse by aggroing them too much and raising their agression level which spawns an overwhelming amount of patrols, onslaughts, and special mini-bosses. A recon with a silenced sniper rifle to pick off lonely patrols is a must, Customizing your recon marine with a black bandana, moustache, gray hair and nicknaming him Snake is a must (as confirmed by game's achievement). Story is nothing special, your marines don't really have anything going for them, main characters (Hayes and Harper) are written just good enough to make you give a damn about them, but the rest are meh. Also like 3 out 5 five heads of ship's departments are black women with as much personality as those other two in Helldivers 2. The ending comes quickly and is not satisfying, but the gameplay loop of sleathily exploring the map, collecting stuff and then holding ground when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan is very entertaining, enough to recommend the game.Also there are quite a few bugs. Most of them not game-breaking like marines getting stuck in supressive fire or achievements that are completely broken, but on my second playthrough with restricted saves I had to restart a whole mission 2 hours in because the marine got stuck unlocking doors and they wouldn't open during infinite onslaught. After restart I got stuck shortly after because I paused the game just as the tutorial prompting me to run to a certain place popped. So I had to forcefully kill the game, losing all progress again. It can be a mess sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a good game, that needs to be said up-front. It's a truly unique strategy game, it feels like playing an Aliens movie in the best way possible, the levels are gorgeous with the amount of detail in them and it's fun. And it's a little bit scary actually! They made a scary RTS! That's a huge accomplishment.But the bugs are the absolute worst bugs I've encountered in a game in years. These are aggravating, swear-inducing, progress-eliminating, fun-killing bugs and they're all over the place. These are not glitchy textures or weird lighting, these are bugs that made me swear in frustration.I have only had a single crash, but most of these bugs create a situation where you must reload a save which is almost as bad as a crash as far as I'm concerned.You only save the game after level-transitions, Resting in a locked room or after certain objectives. Except, I couldn't save after resting on one particular level. Some bugs you encounter are only fixed after reloading. Sometimes a marine will get stuck "interacting" with something forever. They run around and can interact with objects, but they can't shoot, be healed or use skills so they're useless until you reload. Sometimes a marine gets stuck inside of an object and they're useless for the rest of the mission. Reloading DOESN'T fix that unless it's a save from before they got stuck. The robot drone that one of your classes can get gets stuck ALL THE TIME and is not worth reloading to save.Getting spotted by an alien changes the dynamic of the game. You mostly never want to be spotted. Sometimes aliens spot you instantly. Sometimes your marines open fire on an alien before it has spotted you. Sometimes aliens spawn inside of a vent that you are walking next to and spot you instantly. Sometimes you are locked in a cutscene and an alien will wander into it, so that when you pop out of a cutscene it spots you.Oh and soft-locking because objectives won't trigger! Pick up an item and use it on an objective? Game sometimes says you never picked it up, better reload. Move into an objective room? Game's stuck on previous dialogue, will never give you a new objective.Sometimes you can do an entire 2 hour mission and not one bug comes up and you feel like you just did an entire Aliens movie and it's sick as hell. Sometimes you replay the same 20 minute segment 4 times because Sargent Rueiz can't use his arms and your previous save is from mission start.The frequency of these bugs is sometimes multiple-times per mission. It's infinitely frustrating. There is such a good game underneath all of this but it feels like I'm being trolled. Like someone took this good thing and made it worse on purpose? And It's so much more frustrating because the game IS good but these bugs muck it up!I cannot recommend anyone buys this until they've done like 3 bug-fixing patches. It IS a good game. When it works. So wait for it to work.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Aliens Dark Descent is a pleasant game. So far it is something new in the genre - a mix of real time XCOM in the Alien Universe. It plays great, its easy to get into and the atmosphere is very nice.BUT there is one thing that completely destroys the game: the lack of a proper save.In this game you pretty much have to weld your team inside a room in order to save. What that means is, you have to collect resources inside the map to be able to weld a room. You either need 1 or multiple resouces for that. Those resources are limited and are also used for other actions like quick abilities, revealing maps, etc. So not only do you have to use your resources to save a game, you have to find a proper room to do so and be clear of all threats. In almost all maps it will take quite a bit of time to aquire and find a weldable room. That means, you CAN NOT save whenever you want and not leave the game whenever you want. If you do, you have to start over from the last save which, in many cases, can set you back by a lot. The welding mechaning and letting your marines rest is awesome on its own (if it would function correctly, since in a lot of times it is bugged where you have to use double the amount of resources) but only having this mechanic to save is beyond me.Until they at least give a more friendlier save option and get rid of the incredibly annoying bugs even multiplying this annoyance, I unfortunately have to let it sit at negative since it sucks every fun out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine stepping into a squad-based tactics game that immerses you in a dark and foreboding atmosphere. Its intricate and challenging tactical gameplay never lets you rest easy, constantly demanding your utmost attention. This game bears similarities to XCOM but offers a unique twist with real-time combat, a profound emphasis on squad-level tactics, and expansive hand-crafted maps, each boasting a multitude of objectives, totaling over ten on each.As an avid enthusiast of strategy and tactics games, I've traversed numerous titles within the genre, but none have presented a challenge quite like this one. It took me a staggering three evenings of relentless effort to conquer the very first mission, set on the formidable Hard difficulty level. In this unforgiving realm, your marines wield an arsenal of versatile tools, but their physical frailty exposes them to perilous risks, including injury, dismemberment, abduction, and even permanent death. The perils don't end there; you must also contend with managing their ever-escalating stress levels. The harsh realities of injury and prolonged combat can send stress levels skyrocketing, potentially leading to lasting traumas that detrimentally affect performance in a multitude of ways.The game's horror movie-inspired lighting and spine-tingling sound effects brilliantly recreate the nail-biting tension reminiscent of the iconic Aliens film series. For players seeking a tailored experience, the game provides four distinct difficulty settings, offering a spectrum of challenges from relatively relaxed to intensely taxing. Moreover, these settings can be finely adjusted to your preference, allowing for a customized level of difficulty that suits your gaming style.Intriguingly, a substantial update graced the game just yesterday, addressing an array of pesky bugs and introducing a handful of exciting new features. What truly sets this game apart, however, is the developers' genuine engagement with the player community. They actively participate in discussions and interactions on platforms like Steam and Reddit, fostering a wholesome and collaborative relationship with the gaming community.FOLLOW ME---------------------------------------------------Youtube: Facebook: Instagram: TikTok: Twitter:
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Really addictive title, had a blast playing through. Everything is very close to the immersion of the movies and the lore. Lots of props, armors, weapons, vehicles and voice lines are recognizable to trigger many nostalgic memories.The plot is very enjoyable, sometimes vague but in the end definitely interesting.It fits right into the movies and the books. The feeling of it being plausible adds a neat atmosphere to it. Everything is inscenated through epic cutscenes and chilling soundtracks. Game can get very creepy at times too.The gameplay is super addictive, the squad mechanic functions SO GOOD, it really surprised me. Its not clunky, not chaotic and simply smooth. The marines act according and effective. There are a few situations where their pathfinding is f*cked up but its not a big problem after all. Stuff mixes between hide and seek, managing ressources carefully but also pushing and running or holding an area to defend yourself. If you get seen too often by the critters youre gonna have massive problems with later parts in the mission so you gotta be careful. Also managing wounded and sore marines after the missions.Progression is a big point here, every new unlock either in terms of new weapons, new traits or new xeno tech has direct impact and every tool is satisfying to use after all. You wanna mix your squad with every available class and tool to be suited for different situations throughout the missions.The graphics are top quality imo, as well as the environmental sounds and the soundtrack. They really took solid attention to details, even footsteps sound super satisfying. Its a joy!Performance is solid as well, sometimes dropping some frames randomly but overall stable and playable even on old hardware, big thumbs up for that.What the game made very special for me after all was the fact of possibly going game over throughout the playthrough. You got a limited amount of ingame days to finish the missions cause of lore reasons. Also the longer you spend on playing and replaying missions as more agressive the alien hordes get. The small push of "you better hurry up" added a nice amount of immersion right there and rounded everything up. You can expect roundabout 20 hours of gameplay for your first walkthrough if you take some time and play on normal. Keep in mind there are still quite a few bugs, lots of them can be sorted out by reloading a save, re entering an area via lift or simply waiting for a bit. Its a mixed bag, some arent really a problem, others definitely are and there have been a few moments where it really killed my fun. So i hope devs will invest more love into that area,Overall a lovely addition to the Alien Universe, a very unique and fresh gameplay experience combined with thrilling moments and intense action. We need more of that stuff!Definitely recommend getting into it, fair price for a great title!

_childDocuments_.review: sadly its not what you probably expect.there is little to no tactics involved, you cant properly command your squad. everything is painfully scripted and  whole endeavor becomes repetitive and boring. even very obvious things that should come up instantly during play-testing like: you cant just put your squad into apc to fend off a swarm, nope, you can only put them there if you want to move apc to another location. you cant grab additional ammo/supplies from apc, not to mention that you cant really control it. game from over 20 years ago - fallout tactics - had much better squad and vehicle control mechanics, but this one looks pretty so yeah, here we are. xcom 2 i much much better at everything this game tried to be (and a clear inspiration for dark descent) despite being released like 6 or 7 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: So heres my review.I finished the game a minute ago and was quite surprised by the quick ending. Either I didnt have a look at the campaign progress for a while or it jumped pretty hard.Overall the game was..awesome! Just the right amount of stress for me, who doesnt like horror movies and similar entertainment. I could play for 2 hours or so and then I needed a break. The Alien idea is still superb and it's well translated into the game. The story is meh, but since it is well translated, it's still pretty good. I liked how they used in game cutscenes and voice lines, the scripted scenes all work pretty well, and you never get unimmersed by anything. More like omgg let me have control again, we gonna dieee, but it never happens, you just have enough time for everything.I wish I played with a little tighter difficulty than medium. I didnt understand the game for the first fourth of the game or so, so pay hard attention to the tutorials. You need to avoid fighting at all costs. Dont be disheartened: the fights will come to you, no matter what. So just try as hard as you can to avoid them: you will fail anyway, but maybe you can limp out the missions alive, then.Dont clear the maps, it's not necessary. Watch an Alien movie before you play, and play like you're one of the marines. You just want to get out of there.. I played like other RPGs and went on a looting spree and it got me more into trouble than it helped. I doubt it's even possible to play like that on a littler harder game modes.I lost my squad about 5 times on medium difficulty, more because I got impatient than anything else. Recommended: useing the slowmotion setting for space, I played about half of the time in that mode, and it was fun.Managing the Otago and your teammembers is below standard, you never get attached or even know your crewmembers. XCOM does this way better. Voicelines are still great though.You can binge it, you can go for a session of 1-3 hours at a time, it's all possible.Buy well recommended on a sale. Maybe even on full price. But as I said, I'm generally not a fan of horror. I thought this was a turn based rpg, boy was I wrong^^Peace out

_childDocuments_.review: Bad things first:The only thing holding this game back are some pretty nasty bugs. Some objectives can get stuck and cant be completed. Since you can only save when using resources while on a mission you might even loose progress because of these bugs.If you want to complete every objective, consider turning of the time limit at the beginning of the game. This single mechanic is counterintuitive for the rest of the game.For every other aspect i can fully recommend the game, especially if you like tactical strategy games. The best comparison would be X-COM but in realtime. Controlling your squad as a single unit and the game assigning the members for different tasks based on equipment and proximity is similar brilliant to the "smart ping" feature Apex Legends introduced.

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent enough, but falls short of its potential. I've spent many hours playing XCOM 2, which this game at least somewhat has to compare itself against.First and foremost, the game severly lacks variety. Every mission plays nearly identically, and none of the unlocks with perhaps the exception of the flamethrower have the ability to alter the gameplay significantly. In XCOM 2, every loadout item counts, and appropriate use can save your bacon.The game also has a bunch of bugs that I ran into. Several times the stress meter bugged out at stress+++, eventually filling out the stress meters on my entire squad forcing me to reload. I also got soft-locked once during the tutorial. I've also had issues with ultrawide support, which would consistently break after taking refuge in a room. These are apparently not new, which suggests a lackluster post-launch support by the developers.Possibly the most annoying aspect of the game is the sound bites. Some of them are cringe-worthy on their own, but the constant repetition is infuriating. Some also don't make sense - if you send your squad to hide behind cover, they slowly walk towards it, and then have an out-of-breath quip about how they took cover.Music itself is mixed strangely at times, occasionally missing entirely giving a weird quietness to menus.The game would have benefited from an xcom-esque world map where you can choose side-missions as they pop up. Instead it's very railroad-y.I'm rambling. I guess at the end of the day I had fun, but I'm not going to replay it.

This game can be very unforgiving with unavoidable confrontations but more often than not a victorious battle feels good. Sometimes very good when things go according to plan.

_childDocuments_.review: There are also unfortunately a few game breaking bugs including softlocks during certain missions like Return to Pioneer Station. The lack of manual saves make this a HUGE sticking point........Will update review and switch to a thumbs up when the devs tone down the frequency of the marine chatter and separate the story dialogue from the marine chatter in the audio tracks so that one can be disabled without affecting the other.Overall the game is well done so far. Good challenge. Fair price. Competent mechanics. A story that harkens back to the much, MUCH earlier material of the books in the 80's and 90's before the EU lore turned into complete garbage.The atmosphere is very well done and only held back by the marine chatter constantly breaking the tension.Edit: As promised, I am switching my review to a thumbs up. Huge thanks to the devs for making a response here. It is very well appreciated and more than I expected. The new patch that dropped as of 06/22 - 06/23 has drastically reduced the frequency of the marine movement chatter, improving the overall experience and keeping it more tense.There are also a few bugs that have been fixed, but unfortunately some of the softlocks still remain. The only means with addressing those softlocks is to restart a mission before you entered the map for the first time.Overall though, I am very happy to see the devs being so rapid and engaged with the community. I am also very happy with the overall atmosphere of the game and more grounded approach to encounters between marines and xenos. The marines don't feel like spartans/doomslayers like in other games. _childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended.Let me start by saying that I'm just happy that for once a game in this day and age isn't completely broken on launch, I'm playing on ultrawide with all settings at max without issues (AMD CPU, nVidia GPU), I've so far only encountered 2 issues (and I'm on the 3rd location):Occassionally the marine pathfinding gets stuck to/from long route tasks, very easy to resolve.There's a significant fps drop if you got "hide" enabled while in cover and then start moving without disabling "hide", as if the game then keeps checking every little piece of cover to see if you're using it.For 40 euros it's a good game, I've leveled a few guys, unlocked a few upgrades, progressed through the story, stopped an abduction, lost a marine, had a marine lose a limb, found out how OP the silenced sniper is, the list goes on.I am quite anoyed with the bad traits that marines get, I feel like the in-game stress is enough of "marine management", then ontop of that after a mission they get tired and if you bring them anyway they'll get exhausted, and for trauma they need to go to the psych ward several days or suffer permanent debuffs that keep getting worse, hopefully we'll see a mod that just straight up removes in the near future or at least makes them less of a headache.Graphics-wise I'd say it's okay, the effects are pretty decent, but textures sometimes look like a 6 or 7 out of 10 quality, like the marines or the enemies if you zoom in too much.The real content-complaint I'd have is the voice acting, of the marines, of the enemies and the story folk, they all sound so B-tier and it doesn't help the squad or tactical guy tell you to "stop camping" every 30 seconds even though you're in cover to hide from a passing patrol, also hope there will be a mod to reduce the frequency and volume of those specific voicelines.I was also worried about the "End of campaign timer" that some games have these days and which I hate, I don't mind timers on like optional stuff where you get rewarded for getting there on time, but having a senseless timer just to create a false sense of urgency is just rubbing me wrong, luckily the game allows you to tone that setting down even if you want to put the rest of the difficulty at max.All in all though, the gameplay loop is solid and fun, if ♥♥♥♥ gets too hard you can always just bail, because the world and team are persistent, so you can just come back and finish the mission with a new squad or even to loot any buildings you know you left items in due to running out of space (just don't bring anything on missions, that way you can bring more back to the base).If you like Aliens and if you like RTS or you liked XCOM2, then this is a very easy recommendation, especially considering they priced the game to it's quality (not like those games that launch like trash but charge you 70 dollar).

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent, what a gem of a game into the Alien Franchise so to speak.The game itself is often referred to "XCOM" which is far from same. The only XCOM like element is the UI screen in your base of operations, otherwise, it is very much it's own game.The mechanics involve squad based stealth, management, real time action based combat, where every decision counts. You have a plethora of resources to manage, right down to your marines ammunition.Do you reload that sentry turret? Or do you pass up and keep some mags for your marines smartgun? Do you launch a grenade to kill those 2 drones entering the same room as you? Or do you let them by as you sneak around them, allowing you to save ammo, not stress your marines or alert the hive causing a hunt to be launched for your detection?The implementation of the squad based system works and as hybrid as it is, there are few games that have done it correctly. Think Dragon Age to a degree which is a more accurate reflection of the combat.If you are a fan of the Alien IP and movies, you will absolutely appreciate the art, asthetic, sounds, right down to the squelching of your marines boots going over a hive growth. They inspiration taken from the franchise is apparent with the APC being utilised as ground command vehicle, which you can use to transport your marines around a map where applicable and it can defend a location or attack on the move.Gameplay wise, there are a few bugs I have encountered, one of which is quite disruptive however, overall, absolutely would recommend and I am sure they will address those in the near future. Definitely meets the price point for the time you get out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: is singleplayer, simplified-RTS squad-based game where you control a squad of marines to uncover various location to learn its infestation, intentions, and its origins.If its not obvious enough, this game ideas and theme is heavily based on Aliens 1986. Keep in mind, this isn't  despite having "stealth" mechanics. (which will talk about that later)- A fan of Alien- Watched the movies before- Played some games related to Alien (Alien vs Predator/2/Requiem [2010/2001/PSP] and Alien: Isolation)- Played RTS and TBS games before (both complex and simple, like Company of Heroes, Halo Wars and XCOM 2)- Played stealth games before (Splinter Cell, and Metal Gear Solid)- Cracked and played its first-day release version of this game before (but will not judge the game base on this factor)- Finished the game on medium difficulty.Its what Aliens 1986 looks like, even funnier is that some parts of the story structure is also kind-of inspired by the movie too, which I don't mind tbh. For story wise, I won't spoil too much as you will only encounter 3 types of groups, and one of them obviously are the Xenomorphs themselves. The story serves good enough for this game, For gameplay, its pretty solid, fun, intense, and engaging! (Although a bit tedious, but at least the game didn't drag on too long)Controlling the squad is like any RTS game, except only controlling 1 unit (which has multiple people in it). The only thing differentiate from any ordinary RTS mechanic is that you can customize the members within the squad, like assign different roles to it, bringing certain special weapons, and giving them attributes, perks, and equipment.And by able to customize your squad member individually, your squad health are not shared together, they're separated to each individual health. This includes stress mechanic and using special weapons. Talking about stress, the game uses this mechanic to "disadvantage" your squad whenever if your squad getting into prolonged firefight or being hunted (basically caution phase like Metal Gear Solid). When being exposed to this 2 element, your squad member will gain a "debuff" whenever reaching to 1 level of stress (max at 3). Basically encourage players to treat their stress wisely by resting or extract & return to avoid consequences.For the resources management, the game provides 2 type of resources, 3 types of equipment, bunch of xenotech, and 2 types of personnel, engineer & physicist. Some of them are gain when you explore more in the field, some of them as you pass the days, and some of them when you progress your campaign. The only thing are usable on field are the equipment and xenotech, but they're only acquire on the field and can't be created.There are many interesting mechanic, but I don't want to list everything as its too long, so ill instead move to the technical and gameplay problems I faced.- Very obviously, they don't have enough time to fix the UI issues, especially when you collected an item or anything, the pop-up will not fade away when you enter the map view. I know this doesn't affect the gameplay, but its kind of annoying for blocking the view.- The available cover positions are... odd. Although I understand that putting too much cover may cause issues where player will accidentally keep taking cover, but sometime, certain places looks like it can be taken cover doesn't offer the option, which can be confusing at times.- Unable to bring ammunition back is also an odd choice, especially I only noticed it half-way through my gameplay, so I'm not sure if its a design choice to restrict only marine's pouch size on every deployment, but it certainly doesn't make sense to me. (and only makes players decision harder on whether to leave ammo box behind for next deployment or take it to be safe than sorry when running out of ammo.)- Toolkit resources are always oddly demanding. Welding door, repairing sentry/drone/powerloader, accessing certain encrypted doors, revealing all enemies, revealing entire map layout, exchange tools for command points, and "upgrading" sentry guns. Compare this to medkit (which only use-case are heals and decrease stress) and command point (which can regenerate itself and used with marine special weapons, perks, and actions) is absolutely baffling at best, even some actions can & obviously should be using command points or ammo instead are not the case.- Certain attributes and perks are very obviously and horribly useless, they're either underwhelmingly-pity benefits or straight-up disregarding any meaningful way.- Sometimes marines doesn't use their special weapon despite clearly possible without friendly-fire means.- At times, it's kind-of conflicting whether it is encourage to go-loud, shoot everything it moves, earn bunch of EXP, gains trauma or many days in medbay, or stay-quiet, spend a lot (or A BUNCH) more time "snaking" around, and earn slightly less EXP, and less time in medbay in exchange of "almost falling asleep". I know its very personal opinion, but the stealth mechanic obviously wasn't impressive to begin with, so it was probably intentionally made player feel that way.- Horrible voice line variation. Issuing squad command is literally listening to voice mail repeatedly. Its tedious and its horrible.- And more you can find on the reviews in the Steam review sectionsIn short, this game is you controlling a squad, not you being a marine in the squad. And it includes a handful amount of mechanics and variety to play combined resources management, all while trying not to get cucked by xenomorphs. Although it has its own sets of questionable issue, but it can be mostly be tolerated.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Aliens game, probably the best I've played. Voice acting is good enough, could be better. Could use more dialogue when you're directing your squad. Hearing the same lines over and over can be annoying. I've only encountered a few bugs, where a member of my squad would get stuck. The bad part is having to reload the game because it doesn't allow you to save. There are save points that can vary in time apart, so you might end up having to replay just a few minutes, or 10-15 minutes. Graphics are good and gameplay mechanics are good. Definitely captures the intensity and essence of Aliens. Having to manage health AND stress can get intense when your squad can only carry so many, but being able to weld doors to create rest areas helps with stress management. You just have to worry about tool management. Excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent is an over the top real time strategy game where you control a single Colonial Marine fireteam of four (five once upgraded) into the depths of a planet reminiscent of the movie Aliens (1986). There is many set pieces that look straight out of the movie and many references to the classic films. Featuring many features from marine customization including renaming of your marines and a class, trauma, stress, trait and leveling system. The game forces you to think and make quick decisions to survive the Xenomorph infestations on the planet Lethe where you have crash landed. Prepare to lose marines as you descent into darkness to complete various missions on many different levels. You need to get this game it's worth every single cent and does the Aliens franchise license justice!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has handed my arse back to me so many times. Even the tutorial is challenging.Its a tough game that captures the spirit of Aliens really well.Only 3 hours in, but so far you can feel the tension - the inclusion of anxiety and the effects of combat on your troops is a really good feature.Whilst many strategy games had this in terms of a triggered sudden "panic" this is much different, it creeps on the characters and you really need to balance the value of reaching an optional objective , vs the effect it's going to have on your soldier's psychological health.This is a real time strategy game with turn based features (you can optionally pause the game to pick "special moves" from a wheel - but the advantage is not as great as it sounds).So far I'm a big fan, but boy is it hard (especially if you're slightly OCD about getting everything done as efficiently as possible! This game will punish you, because you will always push your squad beyond its limits and break them.updated on 15 hours - this game is getting better and better! 9/10 would increase trauma points by 2, for an extra turret again. Updated the review since finished - The storyline is awful at the end ... jus' saying :D

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this game is not bad by any means, but I wouldn't call it the most polished game. There are numerous bugs that happen incredibly often and can cost you anywhere between a few seconds upwards of 30 minuets because the autosaves in this game are atrocious,Characters often get stuck in doorways or while running resulting in them dying which means you need to reload a save from 10 minuets ago.Enemies are sometimes just not damaged by things such as grenades or shotguns even if they are in the red.Opening boxes sometimes just don't give you what is inside of them, including ones required to continue the campaign resulting in another resetEnemies just sometimes know know exactly where your squad is after you overload or make a sound with your drone, causing them to barrel towards your troops on the other side of the map of the noise.Besides the bugs there are these two gripes of mine and that is character accuracy. Your soldiers cannot hit ****! Their accuracy ranges from anywhere between 40-60+% and you may be thinking that's not too bad but when a single Xeno Runs through 5 people raining hellfire on it only to then maul a good chunk or outright kill someone it's becomes a little irritatingAnd next is the doomsday counter. I personally didn't have much of a problem with it initially, key word being initially. I was flying through this game playing on the hardest difficulty because I have a lot of experience with games like this Xcom being the big standout as this game makes a decent attempt to replicate the feeling of having the odds stacked against you. But as I approached the final mission i realized something I am 1 day short of beating the game. Which might not sound like much but that one day means I have to go back two hours to complete the game, and that is if the last mission is possible with my squad of 5 on just one attempt. There is no way to set back the clock, even by a day which means I just loose, the worst part about it is loosing doesn't give you any unique screen or anything it's just "You loose would you like to load a save or go to the main menu" No dramatic scene of the planets surface getting glassed by nukes, just a generic "you died' screen.The Gameplay is decent, very unfair and incredibly clunky at times but it is still fun and provides a unique experience. I know i signed up for the hardest difficulty but even at the end I only lost 1 soldier, and that was souly because I sent him in as cannon fodder to quickly finish a Sidequest so to lose via the clock catching me is incredibly irritating. Another gripe I have is the lack of enemy variety. There are god knows how many xenomorph forms yet they use the same boss like 8 times, and the two minibosses after your 1st encounter with the crusher are just fodder. My final complaint is the lack of soldier individuality, your soldiers all carry the exact same gun, minus the gunner whos signature gun becomes obsolete once reaching a certain  lv. But each soldier besides maybe the technician or the sniper basically don't do much of anything especially the medic who is kinda just bad and serves to fill out the squad once you get the apc. But even then they all feel the same, the sniper being the best of them all since he can just silently snipe enemies across the map.The game has a whole lot of potential for dlc content or just a sequel, but due to the bugs and abhorrent saves i cannot recommend.Sorry for the wordy review the only way i could word every complaint or opinion would be to make a 20 minuet YouTube video

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I liked the game a lot. Definitely worth a buy.Things I liked:- Good story at start of campaign.- Very atmospheric.- Realtime gameplay was a nice change to XCOM and Xenonauts (I love turnbased).- Persistent, open maps. This made the game so immersive.- Interesting perks and skill system.- Stress mechanic. As you deal with xenos, your squad takes stress damage. When stress reaches multiples of 100, your squad takes serious performance penalties (reduced accuracy, longer reloads, fewer command action points).Things I disliked:- Late game story was meh- Most of the primary mission objectives are "the door is locked... checkout the security room" or "find the generator". This got a little tiresome after a while- The base management is okay, but I think we're missing "sort by days until available" in the barracks menu. There's a lot of manual searching to figure out what everyone is doing and when they'll be available- I (only?) had one bug in Mission 10 that meant I had to play the entire mission again. It set me back about 3 hours. I was expecting more bugs, based on the complaints here. It looks like the devs are doing a good job of patching, but it's a shame those bugs were present in the first place
