_childDocuments_.review: Having now finished the game on hard (putting me in ~1% of players at time of writing and about 5% of players who've finished the game). I would say Aliens Dark Descent is a game that punches WAYYY above it's weight class. In a few words it - has an immersive world, is built around an emotionally solid story and cast and packs some satisfying gameplay (think x-com lite).  Is it perfect? NoAre there some bugs, predictable story 'twists' occasionally janky gameplay mechanis? YesBut ultimately this is a shockingly good game for what it is - sub-AAA price indie RTT with pause. A very strong story (even if some parts were a bit predictable, spoilers WY are the baddies). The main cast were interesting, mostly free of cliches and there were a few story points (in mission 10 in particular) that were actually cinematic, they wouldn't have felt out of place in a good indie Aliens movie. Performance and graphics - only had one crash in my 50+ hours. There are a few smallish bugs, like troops getting stuck on corners of props or being permanently interacting with an objective. Easy fixes with restart but potentially devestating if you have a hardcore run, so for the time being I'd advise against that. The graphics are generally very good - AA+ standard easily. There are a few issues, textures pop in sometimes especially during cut scenes, hair doesn't look good and occasionally there appears to be some kind of memory leak after long play session. All round very solid. Gameplay - this is actually quite a hard game, much like xcom or xenonauts you're meant to suffer a bit, that's part of the immersion. Accept losses and you will have a much more enjoyable time. The mechanics are often explained well by the game but a few that become important aren't made that clear. When selecting an action for example (like using a bandage on another trooper) you can press tab on PC to rotate through the marines to select who you want to do it instead of letting the games (generally good) smart command system handle it, which might result in your slower gunner doing it instead of the medic who is faster and buffs troopers when they heal someone. The base management layer is not overly complicated but poses a few interesting decisions for you, not quite as involved as XCOM or Xenonauts but still quite fun and interacts with your in mission gameplay well. OVERALL - Aliens: Dark Descent is a rough diamond. It is easily worth the asking price and comes highly recommended if you're a fan of the Aliens universe, enjoyed XCOM or Xenonauts or have a streak for games that actually challenge you.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you know what you're getting. It does have boss encounters, and they typically break the atmospheric tension. Up to those boss fights, it's great. I kind of wish they didn't have bosses, and instead just started swarming you forcing a quick but controlled (or not) fallback.Tension is definitely there and they nailed that aspect of the Aliens universe. Overall, I really enjoyed it. I hate timed stuff, and it's a bit nebulous. For instance, you don't have to complete a mission on the first run. You can extract and go back a day later to finish it up while resetting the time-stacking difficulty within that mission. But...every 5ish (can't recall exact number) days outside missions (read every five missions) the global difficulty ramps up one tick. I don't know how hard this makes the game, so I've been running full clears in a single deployment.Overall, there's a reason it's $40 and not $60 or $70. It's a good game, and I think worthwhile if you like squad based RTS, or XCOM, because the overlay and between missions is XCOM. Combat is RTS with your squad. Or if you really like the Aliens IP. Definitely the best one to come out in a decade or so.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me wish Steam has more than just a Yes/No option for recommending. I ultimately gave this a thumbs up, but I wrestled with this decision for a  time. There's a lot to like here, but there's also so much wrong.The atmosphere of the game is great. While the characters really do need to shut up and stop quipping, the early missions have some nice buildup of tension as you slowly investigate abandoned colonies.The gameplay itself is fantastic. Exploring the map, fighting as you progress, searching for resources and surviving swarms are all fun, and the moment-to-moment gameplay of the later chapters is where this game starts to rise above it's slightly shoddy and lackluster framework and start to shine. The most common comparison is that this is a real-time X-com, and I'd agree that it does feel that way on the surface. The squad mechanics could be better implemented, and the customization is really lacking, but it gets the core feel of the X-com squad building.The level design is where the game excels. You have these massive, sprawling levels that you're encouraged to work through piece by piece. As you go through to collect resources and progress through missions, the aliens become more numerous and aggressive while your Marines become more injured and stressed. If your units get hurt too bad, you can pull them out, let them recover and drop back into the mission after a few days, or use a backup team while you wait for the main team to recover. Everything will be exactly how you left it, so each chapter has this feel of a massive expedition instead of just a little throwaway fight.The biggest problem is the sheer number of the bugs in this game.  aren't game-breaking. Often the progress bar for performing an action just doesn't appear, nor does the cancel button. Sometimes my Marines' health bars will disappear, but not all of them. Sometimes when a Marine goes down their body starts sliding across the floor and I have to chase them down to rescue them.Some bugs require a restart though. Sometimes my Marine will go down and his body will fall through the floor; this happened when one guy got facehugged and I couldn't reach him to rescue him. I'm not one to save-scum, but in these situations you're forced to. Once the camera somehow went out of bounds and it wouldn't go back through the boundary barrier. So I had to reload a save to get my camera back onto the map.Then there's Chapter 5, where you return to the space station. This entire chapter can get ♥♥♥♥♥♥. It is absolutely bugged to hell. Some narrative triggers just don't activate on this map and require a reload, which shouldn't be a major problem except for the fact that you just can't seem to safely reload saves on this mission. If you reload a save (and sometimes even if you don't) your Marines will refuse to stay in stealth afterwards. On Normal difficulty, no big deal, just mow your way through the level. On Nightmare? The stealth becomes way more difficult, and the last part of the mission will pretty much force you into getting swarmed because you won't be able to safely make it to the end.Other than the bugs, the only other major issue I have is with the Ironman mode. The saving system is good; you get 2 save files, one when you're at base and one when you rest in the field. Playing without Ironman mode will give you autosaves every few minutes which makes it too tempting to save scum, so I attest that the (horribly named) 'No One Can Hear Them Scream' mode is the best way to play the game. However, as someone who loves perma-death mechanics for pushing up the tension and risk/reward gameplay, I got blueballed so hard by the squad wipe mechanic. If your squad wipes on Ironman mode, you would think the game would send you back home and save, removing those 4 members from your roster, right? Then you can save scum to your in-field file if you wanted, or just go back into the field with a fresh team to get the dogtags. But this isn't what happens; if you wipe, the game FORCES you to save scum to reverse the process. If you lose 3 of your 5 man team, you might as well just keep pushing. Either they get a bunch of experience and complete the mission or they die and you get forced into resurrecting your team. Now it's on me to play the game fairly because the game is forcing me to save scum, and that isn't what I want in my hardcore Ironman games.Honestly? Probably not. Not as is for $40. I really love RTS games, and this is a good one at its core, but the bugs are a struggle to deal with at times.I am not exaggerating when I say that if Chapter 5 had occurred within the first 2 hours of the game, I would have refunded it on Steam.Also, the final level, Chapter 12, is god-awful game design. There's no combat, it's just a walking-sim level where you control people with infinite health and run away from an enemy that would have potentially been an interesting boss fight.If the devs fix these bugs and fix it so the Ironman mode will actually let my squad wipe, I could recommend this for $40. It has an awful script, face animations that rival the latest Mass Effect, and the most bare-boned customization possible, but the gameplay is good.Ultimately, I give this a thumbs up; it's mostly a good game, it's just currently priced too high. Get this for $20 and you'll be happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute "Gotcha" game.  Tutorial is longer than the Steam refund window. You wont even by on your first independent deployment by 2 hours. Janky movement system - marines move together as a team, and it's random who does what. Sometimes when you unlock a door, the game takes a few seconds to figure out you opened the door, so the pathfinding sends you in a completely different direction. Combat is painful at best. You have one deployment a day, and ever day adds "aggression" to the hive. You can't complete all objectives on a single deployment, so you are constantly having to return, forcing the missions to get progressively harder. Marines take stress damage ( a la Darkest Dungeon) and become more and more unhinged as you play. Ammo, meds and tools are all in scarce inventory, and you constantly have to loot what's on the map to get more. But each map has a finite supply. Marines level up extremely slowly. Even in the guides, it stresses that you need to stay for as long as possible on each mission to get a squad of max level soldiers by end game. There are a few ways to cheese this - namely calling Aliens to your APC so that it can mow them down for you. Game pulls the current Xcom 2 "gotcha" mechanic where you can completely sweep a level of enemies, then one just pops out.  All aliens are faster than you, can deal more damage than you and can take way more damage than you. Plus, your marines are just babies. 5 minutes into a mission, they are functionlessly insane, panicing, wasting ammo and meds and forgetful of their skills. Eventually you can unlock smart gunners, snipers, etc. But their skills are mostly useless. Want your sniper to use that nice rifle of his? Yeah, that is a limited skill. By the second deployment area, you only have 3 command points that sloooooooooowly regen over time. Want to use your shotgun, flamer or sniper rifle? Each of those skills takes a command point. Once they are gone, it can take about a minute to regain one. Let's play theater of the mind shall we:Marines deploy on planet. They are tired, even through they havent been in combat in a day or two. One marine is a coward, and another is paranoid. Just being in the squad they lower both your command point regen, as well as add more stress. Get to the first room, bam - you're already at 50-75% stress. SIngle alien pops up, you struggle to kill it with your now fully panic'ed team. You're being hunted, and the aliens know exactly where you are. They attack in small waves. It doesnt matter, because none of your guys can ♥♥♥♥ anything and their skills have already ended. You finally wipe them out and ONSLAUGHT. WTF...what's that? Oh hit's a horde attack mode. Okay, find a defensible position with your limping, nearly dead, panic'ed squad. Oh, what's that, a crusher has arrived. Oh, and to put more topping on this crap pizza, every night you "rest" between deployments, you will face a random event card. These cards are always aweful. First they had bad dreams, so I had to make hypersleep beds (lose all technicians for a day and everyone is tired - debuff), next day two guys get into a fight (now they are wounded and exhausted), then there was a lab accident where a doctor spilled acid on herself. I can do nothing (30% of losing the doctor), or try to save the doctor (all doctors are busy for an entire day). How the heck are you supposed to slog through this when you start every day worse off than the previous day?Game over man, game over. This review was written at 6 hours in, and I cannot fathom this getting any better.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s harsh to give this game a thumbs down because in terms of atmosphere, visual realization, and general execution it’s one of the best uses of the Aliens franchise. The design, level of detail, animations and the cut scenes are top notch. This is a very good-looking game and even the story is okay – for a video game; staying close to the source but adding some variation with the “cult” that’s pretty pulp but still works. But there are also many annoyances. First, there’s the difficulty. I don’t play a lot of strategy games, it’s not really my thing (please consider this regarding my judgement), especially not if I must multi-manage thousands of aspects. So, in theory, Aliens Dark Descent should appeal more to me with its squad moving mechanics instead of individual commands for each unit, its simple upgrade mechanics etc. Unfortunately, this wasn’t the case. Especially the “move one - move all” principle didn’t work well for me in combination with stealth actions, because somehow the marine I needed up front to perform a sniper shot or burn some eggs was always dragging behind, not in line of sight or whatever, resulting in me being detected a lot more than is advisable in this game. Because this game is difficult. Really difficult. I wish someone had warned me so that I would have played on “easy”. I’m sure I would have had a better time. But this game’s “medium” is another game’s “hardcore”. There are so many factors to make the gameplay constantly more difficult: limited tech points (for sealing doors, picking up sentry guns, hacking terminals), limited action points (for special attacks and the like), exhaustion, injuries and mental health of your marines which lower their performance (or availability), increasing hive activity from day to day and finally the nuclear countdown, so that the game gets close to impossible to play if you botched the beginning. And I did: I started slow, took several days for the first levels only to find that I soon ran out of resources, while the overall difficulty went up all the time. So, I started taking more risks, doing more in one day only to be slowed down by all the injured soldiers. Not being able to rest/save in the later parts of a level because you don’t have a stupid tech point is rather frustrating. After about 15 hours in I realized that I wouldn’t be able to finish the game like this – but I had no patience to start again (wiser and on “easy”). I just wanted to see where the story went but repeating all I’d done felt more like work than like fun.The problem is the game doesn’t have any mechanics to counter that increasing difficulty. Very close to the end you get a Xeno tech to reduce the overall hive activity, but it costs tons of resources and ultimately doesn’t help that much. Other than that, you are helpless. Now this might be in accordance with “Aliens” as an experience, but as a game it’s frustrating. It’s too late to “git gud” - you simply don’t have the time for it, you can’t grind. If your higher-level soldiers are injured, you go out with unexperienced grunts without abilities which of course stand lower chances … Again, this might be me sucking at this kind of RTS but my impression is that the game is simply not well balanced. Which brings me to the point of play testing and the one thing that really drove me up the wall. How can this game be in development for several years and no-one calls out that it’s TERRIBLY ANNOYING to have your soldiers repeat 10 phrases ALL THE TIME? Now they may be iconic phrases in the movies but if you must listen to them every few seconds it’s about as pleasant as having a face hugger on your head. Seriously, who in their right mind greenlights something like this? It kills the otherwise great atmosphere and it’s just dumb. And I just don’t get it, because the voice acting in the cut scenes is well done; they just could have recorded a 100 more lines, reduced the frequency those are uttered, and everything would have been fine. But like this? “Let’s see what’s in there.” opening the same kind of crate for the umpteenth time! “IT BURNS, IT BURNS!” in my brain. “I hate this job.”I’m not proud of it, but in the end, I used WeMod to cheat. I’ve never done that before and I advise against it because once you start cheating the tension is gone. I tried boosting my marines and then going on without cheats, but I still lacked the patience. Which brings me to another negative: the last levels are just too big. Maybe my problem wanting to discover everything, but they become real time sponges. In the end I finished the game in just under 40 hours and I will not play it again. There are some who only feel like a game is worth their money if they get dozens of hours of playtime out of it – honestly, I’d have preferred a more concise, balanced game that only takes 20 hours to finish. That might even have motivated me to try a harder difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Alien/Aliens fan.. I would like to give this game even a decent review but I am currently experiencing the first ever movement bug of this kind in all of the computer games I've ever played. Right click on the mouse button moves your squad, if you double click the right button you can move at a sprint.. The mouse worked fine in the tutorial. It was responsive to every click.. But once I got to the first mission I've lost count of how many times I'm trying to move my squad and NOTHING HAPPENS!  And the game berates you if your squad is just standing around. This adds further insult to this infuriating glitch. Right click... The squad stands still... Xenos are on patrol, I'm clicking the right mouse button  and the squad doesn't respond at all to my move commands to exit the patrol zone, so of course, the squad gets overwhelmed and slaughtered. This is the first time I've played a game at launch where the basic move commands degrade into glitch garbage.Addendum-I had to purchase another mouse in order to fix the 'glitch.' All of the issues I complained about initially have been solved by the new mouse. If you're a fan of the Alien universe and the Alien RPG published by Free League, I recommend you try this game out. As far as tactical squad based games, my favorite of all time is Fallout Tactics. But I'm sure there are others that contributors on Steam praise that qualify for better squad based games. The plot is interesting and engaging once you get beyond the third mission. There is resource management as your squad can salvage materials on each mission that you can use to upgrade your Marines individually but also universally as you can also the same materials to broaden your choice of weaponry. Your squad also has the opportunity to salvage alien samples for use in enhancing your squads strength as well as giving them new abilities...  It's a decent game, but it's not my personal favorite of squad based tactical games. Dark Descent is a solid game that immerses you in the Aliens universe, it picks up steam (pun intended)  after the first couple of missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game FEELS like Alien and Aliens.  Its dark, cramped, and somewhat stressful.  Its also awesome!  Yes, the game has XCOM elements (like the Base/ship Lab/Barracks/Workshop etc is similar, as is the general Troop Information/upgrade/customize mechanics) but thats it.  All the people calling this an XCOM-like, I dont understand.  The combat is fluid and active.  You can choose to either Slow the Combat, or pause it, when you use skills and Specials, but combat isnt turn based, nor is it grid based.  Exploration is fairly insteresting and rewarding, and there are moments where the game gets HARD.  You will fight Queens, Runners, Drones, Praetorians, Humans, and other types of Aliens Seen, and they look GREAT.  I HIGHLY recommend this game to any lover of the Alien Frandchise, and recommend it to everyone else, just because its really well done.  We FINALLY got a good Alien game!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't judge me, I've never actually seen Aliens lol. But when I saw that this game was basically Company of Heroes  squad management the game I knew I had to try it. So this review is based soly on the gameplay (though I must say the world has me interested!)It was a bit of a slow start but now that most of the scripted hand holding is over, and my marines are starting to have some levels I'm pretty hooked. Most things are very positive so I'll only highlight some of my small gripes:-The camera system is a bit clunky,  it would be nice to have some sort of semi-follow cam. I feel like I'm managing the camera half the time. -Actual combat is a bit shallow. The abilities do most of the heavy lifting as far as enjoyment is concerned. The cover system only considers desks as cover. I wish there were tiers of cover so that I could move a bit more tactically. COH did this very well.-I wish you could at the very least position individual units for those defensive moments. -More weapons and maybe attachments(i'm only 5 hours in so maybe this is a thing). -Once the xenos are in melee range, it's a bit clunky with how they interact and attack the squad. It just becomes a cluster.This game is awesome, someone else mentioned dungeon crawler. It would be sweet to see this concept iterated on. I can just see the gameplay loop of squad xcom/extraction/looter being highly addicting.

_childDocuments_.review: First: I play offline, so the shown game time is WRONG. Steam should check my achievements, with that little game time i could have never reached level 10 achievements.This game is, what the movie Alien 3 should have been, a worthy successor to the great second movie. Good story, brilliant atmosphere and lotz of stress. (and thats not a bad thing in that  other games i dont like stress but here its great...) In some ways its like x-com, but the core gameplay, the action, feels like a new genre. Basically its a tactical real time rts, where you command your 4-5 man team as one RTS unit. (so you can play this game without pause, but i dont recommand that at the beginning, or the aliens will tear you apart...) I prefer turn based games normally, but in this game rts is a MUUUCH better solution.The alien ai is good, it patrols and hunts for prey, reacts to noise, evades fire when possible, makes jump attacks, that you can evade and tries to flank your sentry turrets. The game runs very good in high detail on my old 5700 XT in 1080p, WITHOUT FSR. With FSR everything runs good on ULTRA max Detail. The sound is perfect, it delivers great atmosphere. Only downside: For me the game is too short. 40 hours is ok for 35 Euros, but i would have prefered paying more and having a longer experience. My advice: Play it on HARD from the beginning, otherwise the great horror action tactic trip is over too soon.I will definitly buy every add on that brings new story campaigns. And a second part with maybe more complex strategic elements, would be great too. A little sidenote at the end: This game is 20 years after part 3, so the marines have better technology: plasma guns, tanks that arent damaged by alien acid, motion trackers that detect non moving aliens. Even a gas that reduces the numbers of aliens on the whole planet. Otherwise you would simply have no chance, against the masses of aliens. (over 25000 if all humans are infected)  GREAT GAME for a fair price. For me the best game i played in years, but i am a big aliens fan, so thats a little subjectiv opinion. And after the two patches i had nearly no bugs at all.Update: Sadly i have many bugs in my second playthrough. But only in the olduvai mine level.  1. Once i coudnt rest, it was no hunt, it was a rest room icon and all doors where shut.2. I could rest once in another room, with no shut doors.3. I wanted to evacuate and a drone attacked when my soldiers climbed into the tank. So far so good. But when i ordered my marines to climb out and fight, they couldnt fight the drone, it was unkillable and slaughtered my marine.Played that game a lot and only TODAY so many bugs ? Maybe because i play on hard now, with limited safes ? Another patch is needed.Btw: With my new 4070 FSR 2 looks great. Not that i would need it, but it looks better AND runs cooler.Update 2: The ending feels as if you hadnt any time and money left to make it as it should be: On the one hand this great looking "giger city", on the other hand only 3 soldiers, inkl. maeko, with std. pulse rifles and immortality ??? I imagine this "walking and running level" how it could be, with 5 marines, maeko, stern and the sargeant, actually fighting their way through, like it is done in all the other missions. The boss alien could be immortal and only scared away with flame thrower and grenades for example and of course you would have to guard cassandra all the time. THIS would be the ending this great game deserves. Nevertheless, I LOVE THIS GAME, BEST GAME 2023, for me. Update 3: Seems the bugs are connected with the difficulty: in my fst. playthrough on medium nearly no bugs. In my second on hard i had a gamebreaking bug in the olduvai mine. And now, in my nightmare playthrough i cant finish pharos tower, even if its finished already. Besides, the bug, that its not always possible to end some skills (surpressing fire), is at best annoying, sometimes it kills your whole team. Some minor bugs like aliens that are dead and  still stand, or dead aliens that are shown as collectable samples on the minimap and arent collectable .... more bugfixing is needed. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 'meh' for me. The campaign mechanics are clearly heavily inspired by Starcraft II and XCOM, but they're extremely watered down to the point of being a cheap knockoff. A few examples: (1) you have a laboratory on your ship where you can research upgrades, but there are EXTREMELY limited techs and no choices to make - it's laughably shallow and linear; (2) you have a workshop where you can upgrade your weapons, but it's also ridiculously shallow: there are a whopping <10 guns in the game, they are locked by marine level, and they are just straight no-brainer upgrades with no customization; (3) there is an 'infestation level' on the planet but it steadily increases by 1 point every day and there is nothing you can do about it and no point even looking at it; (4) mission choices are completely linear so there's no choice there either, etc. etc. The combat is a much more boring and frustrating version of Warhammer 40k: Dawn of War: you don't control each individual marine but the squad as a whole, you don't get to decide which marine does what action (so your gunner might decide to deploy the sentry gun instead of shooting), and each individual marine is hardly different other than one special weapon attack they bring to the table. On top of all of that, the game is pretty buggy and there are annoying control issues that can completely wipe your squad (ex: you click on an "X" to stop a marine from performing an action but it takes 3 clicks and they get overwhelmed and die). The most annoying part is the complete lack of a manual save option and the extremely sparse autosaves, so if a bug, a control issue, or a difficult encounter wipes your squad you can lose 15-30 minutes of playtime, depending upon when the last autosave was. Overall, I really wanted to like it as I love XCOM, Warhammer 40k Dawn of War, and Starcraft II, but I was consistently frustrated and let down.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Very strange (yet still flawed) gameplay; with a cheesy story that could've been written by an AI prompt of "generic sci-fi action", and a surprising amount of polish.The game is strange in the sense that, even though you can feel the lack of budget and time pressure in certain areas of the game (story; voice acting, possibly some of the ways the mechanics work), it generally doesn't detract from the main experience.The biggest issues for me were (playing on hard difficulty):* The game can bug out quite hard at times - e.g. marines can often lock up after using the RPG and the only way I found to unlock them is to let them get hit by an enemy.* The game sort of wants to be a stealth game but also a murder party at the same time, and punishes you in different ways for going with either approach. I found that maxing out the "Aggression meter" actually makes the levels easier since you no longer have to worry about triggering Massive Onslaughts (xeno hordes) at inopportune times, making being detected far less of a pain.* It can be really, _really_ frustrating to see your entire squad fire on a single xeno for like 5 seconds straight and not hit a single shot. This is even with accuracy bonuses.* Some of the upgrade slot upgrades seemed... useless, at least for my playstyle.* The trauma mechanic is interesting, but I found that outside of the trauma that causes an increase in reload time, you can sort of just ignore them (even at max level trauma).* The AI pathing is really suspicious at times, combined with the way the game decides to spawn in xenos, can make certain areas near impossible to deal with in a stealthy manner - sometimes it's easier to trigger a detection and dash through a whole bunch of the map, then explore it leisurely once the hunt is over.* Sometimes xenos just don't respond at all to sound and the game doesn't seem to explain that this is intended. Xenos can also decide/bug out to never move, which can often force you to trigger a detection to deal with them.* Loads and loads of smaller quality of life and annoyances.I know the above is a lot of negativity, but the rest of the gameplay genuinely makes up for it. There's real potential in this formula if the devs/some other devs manage to iterate on it; map mechanics, and base/marine management even further.Highly recommend - just ignore the story even exists though tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: So now that they've fixed a lot of the major issues that were present during my first playthrough I am switching my review to positive and writing a proper review.So basically this game is an real time tactics game like Commandos except if you played as one big blob of units instead of individual units. The blob hivemind determines which unit gets sent out to do tasks that require only one of your units to perform like welding doors or setting up sentries. But otherwise it's a RTT game that is about stealthing through space facilities avoiding Alien aggro, setting up stealth kills, and when things go wrong/or as part of main story events, setting up killing floors to ensure you don't get overwhelmed by the Alien Swarm.The aliens are pretty dangerous, one drone catching your team off guard can chip away at your team health, three catching you unprepared can potentially be a unit lost. But if you play well and actually use your abilities the danger in this game isn't a few aliens, it's the swarm and attrition. If you've played Risk of Rain, there's a system in that where the difficulty timer ticks up and things get harder over time, this game has that but only during a hunt. Being detected by an alien triggers a hunt where the aliens in the level start coming to where you were detected to kill you. The hunt lasts about a minute I think and while the hunt is in process the difficulty meter ticks up. One hunt will cause it to tick up a notch by the time it ends and three notches triggers an increase in the difficulty level and a massive onslaught event that you have to set up defenses for otherwise you'll get destroyed. So put simply, you stealth in this game to avoid triggering onslaughts and keep the difficulty level down. You can survive both of those things, but you have limited resources and when those both of those things will drain you of ammo and health.Your marines also suffer from stress that rises when things go wrong, during hunts and also (if they have developed phobias) when exposed to their phobias. There are 4 stress levels for each unit and each new level reached will add some debuffs like a decrease in accuracy, them causing stress for other units, a decrease in your command point regen rate and so on. So you aren't just managing health and ammo, but also your marine's mental state. You can recover from stress by getting your guys into a room, welding off all doors in and resting, leaving the current mission (your progress saves and you can redeploy) or by popping some chill pills (but it uses up medicine that could be used for healing wounds).The game has an XCOM like overworld situation where when you leave a mission you enter a command phase where you can research guns and tech, treat marines wounds and mental states, promote and upgrade your marines and so on, and then deploy onto missions. But it's not procedural gen stuff like XCOM. There are about 10ish? hand crafted missions, your progress in them is stored when you leave and you pretty much have multiple attempts to do the mission with different squads. Leaving and coming back just gives you a chance to regroup, resupply and reset the difficulty timer. The XCOM stuff is a little undercooked to be honest, it's there, it works but it makes you wish they'd leant in a little harder into it and making a procgen game that could be replayed a bunch rather than (or in addition to) the somewhat linear not very replayable set of missions they currently have.For the most part the game works pretty well. The game is tense during stealth and chaotic outside of stealth (chaotic fun). I had a lot of fun playing it and want more, but ultimately it was only about a 30 hour game for me, which for the price is really good, but don't expect XCOM levels of replayability. As I mentioned initially, you play as a blob. This is clearly a decision aimed at making the game accessible and having it work for controllers, but it introduces a lot of frustration into the mix where you wish you could just micro each unit specifically but you can't. This means you have to fiddle about a lot to get your sniper into position to have LoS to take a shot which is REALLY annoying. Having the game auto-select a unit to do an action when that unit is one you'd rather have on standby (because they have the RPG for example) is annoying too.  There's a way to manually select who you want to do certain tasks for some things but you have to fiddle with extra button presses after selecting the thing to interact with and I actually went my entire playthrough not even knowing you could do that.There are scripted sequences where the game introduces a hard event, so like a cutscene showing a boss you're going to fight. The game usually tells you when you're about to trigger one of these events and asks you if you're sure and to prepare. The problem is sometimes you prepare and then it pulls the rug out from under you by forcing you into a new arena where your preparations (mines and sentry guns) are left behind and you can't get back to them until later. Rug pulls like this really suck.The game has a lot of small decisions like this that made me go "wait, you really decided this was a good idea? How could you be so foolish when with other parts of the game you were so smart?" Alone they're not that bad, but there's enough of them that I felt like the game could have used an editor standing behind the devs with a water bottle and for each of these things, being like "NO! BAD DEV! STOP!" and giving them a spray. The human enemies are truly awful and each time they're in the game it turns from a solid 9/10 game to a 5/10.We're pretty starved for RTT games so if you're looking for a new one to play, I'd recommend this one to you simply because there's not really any competition. But it's good enough that I'd recommend playing it even if there was a glut of them. It's one of the few good Alien™ games. This game is to Aliens what Alien Isolation is to Alien.

_childDocuments_.review: 80 Hours and finished on Medium and Hard almost one month after release.TLDR - Its a love letter to Aliens, similar to the Alien RPG combined with Another Glorious Day in the Corps. If you liked those or you just like the IP then you'll love this. I see alot of people comparing this to XCOM and it is very similar from a base management and customization perspective but not so much on the combat side. Honestly there hasn't been a game I have played like this where you control a Fireteam of 4-5 Marines in real-time and it all works decently. It has some issues, like you can't tell individual Marines where to stand in formation, nor can you modify their formation, which I think is something that should be implemented because it  would help build immersion of moving around a military unit, but also it led to some frustrations when trying to employ certain abilities at certain times. It was hardly a game breaking or overly tedious issue, but if we are talking about strategy I think it would add a dimension and provide players with the ability to construct more favorable combat situations. I read another review that compared it to Gale Force 9's Another Glorious Day in the Corps board game coupled with the stress mechanics from Free League's Alien RPG, and that hit the nail right on the head. I immediately recognized AGDITC because the Aliens (moslty) spawn from hive exits at specific points, you have communal ammo, and a broad range of weapons and equipment you can give to your small element. Free League's stress mechanics were a cool addition, but I think more dialogue choices would have been nice to really get the vibe of a Marine pulling a Hudson and going berserk until he died or ran out of ammo. I had a hard time telling which stress conditions did what as it just made my team get swarmed faster. I enjoyed the game mechanics as it was a perfect synergy of those two systems coupled with great level design, detail and appreciation for the Alien IP. Some people have been complaining about the stealth aspects of the game, and I can kinda see why, I don't mind them because it gives you a ticking clock of mission time (figuratively) before you piss the Aliens off enough to make the mission much more difficult and it also gives you a way to build team XP by repelling bug attacks. Your Marines don't get XP buy killing individual bugs (that I'm aware of), but they do get it from killing the special bugs and the wave attacks that occur at each level of agitation. The game does reward you by playing conservatively and taking a more stealthy approach, but I also played through plenty of missions with maximum bug anger and still had a great and really tense experience. Weapons and equipment were unique and lore appropriate, and on my first playthrough I just stuck with the stock Pulse Rifles and Smartguns and got through just fine. There was no artificial spike near the endgame that forced you to take harder hitting weapons, but it did make it alot easier once I did. I liked the tension that the motion tracker provided and I had my eyes glued to it every time one of my Marines gave an alert. The APC was a nice touch, though I found you could use that as a crutch as well as sentry gun spam to get by MANY situations, to include boss or special bug fights. There are also a few bugs (aside from the xenos), but those are being ironed out and they are not critical or game breaking. One thing I'm surprised nobody has mentioned was the score. I'm not sure if they ripped Futile Escape (the music that played during the hive escape in the movie) from the Aliens film score, but the combat music was essentially that or a composition of that. I loved hearing the brass and percussion once the shooting started and was just waiting for Ripley to come crashing through the wall of the hive in the APC to save me so I could yell "DRAKE! WE ARE LEAVING!".The absolute worst part of this game was the marketing. I had no idea this was even coming out until the day before it released, and I only noticed it since I was browsing through Steam and randomly saw it pop up. For all the press that Colonial Marines got this hardly got any, and I assume they took all that money they saved in marketing and threw it into making the actual game and paying the crew that put this together...I hope that is the case. Bottom line - Carter Burke did nothing wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Aliens, then it's a good reason to pick up Aliens: Dark Descent. The game does an excellent job of capturing the lore around Aliens. However, if you're looking to compare it to XCOM, note that the mechanics are different. Personally, I like the mechanics of the game. The main difference is that it takes multiple deployments to finish the level. You get to the point where the aliens become too aggressive and the nest is on to you, so you have to extract your squad. In contrast, in XCOM, I never had a problem with having enough soldiers. Although losing a couple of marines during a deployment is frustrating, it's not always avoidable in certain circumstances. If you go rushing in with guns blazing, it can make the game quite frustrating and unforgiving. It would be nice to see some DLC for the game. Overall, for a RTS "Aliens" game, I give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the first comment I've ever left. So that should tell you how strongly I feel about this game. TL;DR: I really enjoyed this game, but honestly it could have been better if they allowed you to change the squad up, and did away with tactic points, and just used the CD instead. The game-play is actually really good, but it falls short in a few places that make it easier to just sneak past everything rather than engage.  The story line is FANTASTIC though. If you're an aliens fan buy it at full price to support the devs (they deserve it for their ethic in releases a game in a released state instead of release now patch later mentality.)  If you don't like aliens but like tactics games, just buy on sale.                                                                                ---Game-play---So let me preface this by saying; one of my all time favorite games is a game called The Red Solstice. It is EXACTLY like this game, but with better game play. Oh how I wished they copied that game's squad aspect. That would have made this my favorite game of all time.For instance, in that game you can split your squad up and set up ambushes, or you can time delay like this game and give individual orders for your guys to carry out. You can't do that in this game, which REALLY hinders the "tactic" aspect of it. It basically turns it into a glorified sneak in sneak out don't get seen game, since being in combat really really hinders your marines ability to fight. So there's really no point into a shoot out, because you WILL lose, even missions that require it.  Another thing that REALLY hampers this game is the Tactic Point system. There are times where I'll have 5/5 points, and all my skills will be on CD, but the skills will be on CD, and times where I have no CP but all my skills will be ready. It kinda messes with the flow of the game, They should have gone with one or the other. (Honestly in this type of game CD is the better option) Also, the flares should be unlimited, with a 3-5 second CD. It would enhance the eeriness of the game, and help the flow of combat, especially when combat is mandatory. Also, personally, I just really want to enjoy the game, I mean the actual game, I want to see every pixel, and enjoy the work of art I'm playing. But (rightly so) the game is very dark, so there are times my marines are shooting and I have no idea what hey are shooting at until I see the neon green explosion.  I WANTED TO WATCH THE ALIEN DIE DAMN IT. buuuut since all the lights are off I missed the shoot out, and that just bugs me because I should be able to see what my marines see.Now I know I've been pretty hard on them, but that's because I can't help comparing it to The Red Solstice (which is a total clone of this game even the story is similar.) But that's not really fair to this game. Aliens has plenty of stuff going for it. The APC is fantastic, you can just send it on strafing runs to take out anything that's popping up on the motion sensor. and then follow it in, or just have it carry you to the point closest to where you're headed. It's a lot of fun to run the enemy over in in.  The gameplay is also really fluid, and fun to watch. really the only issues I have with it are what i've listed, and most of those are just quality of life improvements. Nothing game breaking just ways to improve it. It's just that I know what this game could have been, and feel a bit let down by it. But that by no means means I hate the game. I'll play it to completion, and enjoy every minute of it.If the mods are reading this, PLEASE look at what red dawn does, because game-play wise, that would have made your game  as perfect as a game can get. It would also add replay value, since it would add a ton of diversity to what you can do.                                                                   ---STORY---Aliens is one of my favorite movie universes, and that is where this game truly shines. Oh man there's been times during this game that my heart felt like it was going to burst out of my chest. the OH ♥♥♥♥ moments are truly spectacular. That's where this game really, really shines. They captured that PERFECTLY.  The story line fits the theme, and the source material and is a worthy addition to the Aliens Universe. If you like that type of stuff you will love the story. It's pretty intense, and has jump scares and plenty of "welp I'm dead" moments that this type of stuff is renowned for.    The only real issue I have is the ability to leave midway through the mission. It makes the stress meter worthless, and breaks the immersion into the game IMO, they should have shortened the missions, and forced you to stay until it was done.                                                                         ---Sound---So the sound is where this game really shines. IMO it really matches the feelings they are going for. other than that I really have no other opinions on it, it's well done, well executed, and has no reverb issues on my surround sound. Since you HAVE to put a number to make it a review I guess I'll put that here, and try to make the numbers reflect what I've said. Lets see:Game-play - 7.5/10 Story 9/10Sound 10/10Overall enjoyment: 8/10                                                                               ---Conclusion---Now I'm not saying this game is awful. It's actually really good. But it simply could have been better. that's just a fact. It's like they ALMOST made the best game ever, but stopped at the finish line and said NOPE. Which really bugs me because it's clear how much these devs LOVE this game. I mean it shipped with virtually no game breaking bugs, or CPU issues, or memory crashes, or anything that virtually every game released in the past 10 years has been a victim of because they priorities the release over doing it right. Which they did. So kudos to you guys for doing it right. As both a consumer and a gamer I truly appreciate it. Oh, and if you read my essay... er review... to this point, Thank you for reading! Feel free to leave a comment.

_childDocuments_.review: As I delved into the initial missions of this game, a singular thought relentlessly occupied my mind: Why isn't this game receiving the mega-hype it deserves? Because it's downright awesome! However, the deeper I ventured into the game's intricacies, the more it began to reveal its imperfections.First off, the game has this annoying time limit in some missions that you can't do anything about. It's frustrating!The biggest problem with the game is its story – it doesn't answer the questions it raises as you play. No answers, no clear point.On the positive side, the game mechanics are fantastic and complex. Playing it is fun and interesting. Your marines deal with physical and mental issues, they level up and get perks, and you can gear them up with attributes(buying by resources).Don't expect base-building mechanics or global map strategies, you're confined to your ship, dispatching marines to handle tasks in alien-infested locales. That's the essence of the gameplay.Stealth is the name of the game here. You have to be quiet and careful, especially on hard difficulty, or your marines will become alien food, alien host or just lose their minds.There aren't a ton of different weapons, but every gun matters. If you're smart about picking the right marines(classes and weapons) for your team, the game really shines.You can't just rely on a few top marines, your whole roster needs to work because marines need to rest, healing, and help with their mental health, and random events can mess things up. For example your top marine can lose hand, asquire mentall illnes and be wounded as hell, he will sit at base very long time =)So, the game is about cool cinematic moments, goint to one mission few times(you can't finish mission for one drop), taking care of your marines, improving them, reading an interesting codex, fighting aliens, and moving on to the next mission.It's a good game, but it has some issues with the story and those annoying time limits. And if you fun of Aliens universe - then you must try it and play for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS; tldr get it on sale if you really like Aliens. If you don't just play XCOM. PROS:- Pretty fun, and the real-time system works decent.- Decent story, but with some flaws (more on that later). - Good length, despite complaints. Any longer and it would've dragged.- Gets a little crazy with xenomorph variants, but still feels faithful to the Alien franchise.- There's a lot of optional datapads with some worldbuilding; little details like that are always appreciated. CONS:- You can't move marines individually, and it causes problems frequently. - I like the stress system, but it's way too aggressive, and just gets annoying. - Marine dialogue is cringey and nonstop. Every 15 seconds someone is saying "It's quiet... too quiet." or something similar. It's literally constant. - They don't seem to have spent a dime on any military or law enforcement consultancy. They're still calling magazines "clips" in 2024. Everything military is cliche and unrealistic. - It doesn't seem like they're going to add any new content. You get what you get. - The second half of the final mission you're invincible and it's impossible to fail, and you don't even get to use your marines. It's very unsatisfying, and then the story ends pretty abruptly and poorly. Annnddddd, its DEI as all hell. Grab a beer if you plan on reading. The MC, Hayes, is a girlboss asian woman deputy administrator of a space station. She is surrounded by incompetent, rude, fat, cowardly, and lazy white men. She saves the day and escapes her ship, then commandeers an entire military operation alongside a sergeant despite having zero military experience. By the end of the game even the sergeant is out of commission and she's running everything, and shows up in the final mission in marine gear to suddenly be an invincible badass despite admitting earlier she has no idea how to use a gun. Haye's boss? Girlboss old lesbian haircut woman. The head doctor on ship, who bravely refuses to abandon her patients? Girlboss black woman. The compassionate psychiatrist who cares for the marines? Girlboss indian woman. The extremely competent head mechanic? Girlboss black woman. Dead sheriff you find that bravely died in a last stand defending her people? Girlboss black woman. Grizzled head of security you recruit as an ally? Old black man. About 2/3rds of the NPCs you meet in missions? Black women, and usually bald, for some reason. Haye's other boss? Fat slob white man who refuses to listen her about the aliens. Catcaller in the breakroom? White man. Coward who breaks and attracts the alien? White man. Scientist who betrays everyone and lets aliens on the ship? White man. Evil scientist that kidnaps sergeant's daughter? White man. Entire cult of evil alien worshipper enemies? ALL white men with southern accents. Sergeant Harper is an okay exception to the rule, but even he has to rely on Hayes and eventually succumbs to... headaches? The other sergeant is probably the best character despite little screen time, and he dies at the end for no reason. You can't customize your marines, so they end up 50/50 male and female (very realistic for any infantry unit) and about 10% of the time a white male.At the end of the story, Hayes sacrifices most, if not all, of the marines, including two major characters, instead of just leaving the planet, because she "made a promise" to Harper and had to get his daughter out. You could argue it's because of her psychic powers' potential, but that reason isn't even fleshed out or implied. Who need good writing when can just girlboss everything?

_childDocuments_.review: I had a complete 180 on this game. Initially I found in grueling, struggling to apply myself for more an 30-60 minutes at time. Now I'm loving it and can hardly "put it down". Ultimately I think there's a balancing issue here, where the initial missions feel difficult with a weak squad, but much easier later own with higher-level marines.Aliens: Dark Descent is basically navigating a nightmare for your squad. Your marines will get tied, exhausted, stressed, develop phobias, maybe even die. Your job is to mitigate the inevitable as much as possible. This initially didn't sit well with me, as I'd like to attempt 'perfect runs' if I could. This resulted in a lot of loaded saves, which is a real problem for me due to Dark Descent's limited saving. Auto-saves occur at key objective completions, and floor changes on the map, or manually by creating welded safe rooms (which requires resource use). Save-scumming isn't really an option, and this hurt my personal requirement to play missions to perfection as I was replaying sections.This clearly isn't how the game is meant to be played however, and part of my criticism of power misbalancing is due to my own forced play-style. So when I felt like the game shifted into my favour, I likely had marines at a higher level than was initially anticipated for the mission I was on. There's also mechanics regarding 'world level' where if you need to redeploy into a mission (you can essentially leave a mission anytime - particularly helpful if things get too bad for your squad) you can, however the more days pass the higher the 'world level' gets. I'm likely not far enough along in 'world levels' for the mission I'm up to, meaning enemies aren't as difficult as they're maybe intended to be.That said, I'm having much more fun than I was. The handful of missions that caused me such grief were worth it to be in the position I am now to blast my way through waves of bugs. So if you want to play a legitimate run (only loading if your squad wipes) that's obviously an option, otherwise there is a way to play to get a sense of dominance if you so desire - just know you need to tough out the early missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing! Must play for Aliens fans!I've been a huge fan of the franchise for almost 30 years. I've played nearly every mainstream Alien/Predator/AvP game and I can confidently say that this has been my favorite, and by no small margin. I never knew I needed an Aliens tactics game in my life, but here I am playing through the campaign a 2nd time on a harder difficulty instead of playing something else like D4 because nothing is quite hitting the spot like this has.Pros: Sound Track. The score has been amazing! Incredibly immersive.Atmosphere. Fantastically dark and foreboding.Gameplay. XCOM with Xenomorphs! "Let's rock!. The Sanity/Health system was fun to work around. I thought it would be a chore at first, but having to decide if I wanted to risk taking a squad out for a second time or letting them rest was really interesting. Sending a under leveled squad in while the stronger squad rested sometimes lead to my whole force getting wiped because I wasn't anticipating the increase in difficulty so quickly, and ended up loading a much earlier save and losing half an hour +. Sometimes I risked it for the biscuit and took my main squad on 2 missions in a row just to find out the next mission was extra hard and of critical importance and now I had a bunch of rookies going into a big fight... I really enjoyed the challenge and strategy.Story. (No spoilers) The story for the most part felt like it stayed true to the franchise. There were a couple of twists that turned my head a bit, but after thinking about it didn't seem completely out of question for the universe so I just let it slide and moved on. But all in all I enjoyed the campaign, not the most unique plot ever, but I had a great time.Customization. The character customization is quite good. Not the most options for changing marines appearances but decent enough. Multiple class options, and most of them have felt impactful in their own way.Monetization. I'm honestly shocked they released this at only $39.99USD. I would have gladly spent $60-70 on this game and felt it was worth every penny. As of writing this post the only Micro transaction I've seen for the game is a cosmetic dlc for only like $4.99USD which gave an armor skin option (for the entire platoon, not just 1 character like most games these days) and a Cat to bring a little fun to home base. This Imo is how "Micro" transactions SHOULD be. Micro, fun, game wide. No complaints whatsoever. No season passes or any of that nonsense in the game (as of writing).Should they ever release a campaign dlc or expansion I'll be buying it asap.--                                                                                                                      --Cons:Bugs. I've had some mostly minor bugs, but honestly it's been surprising how few I've run into for a newly released game. I had the faces of my squad stretch and contort horrifically while they ride the elevator. But it was pretty comical.The biggest issue I had was in one of the later missions I had made my squad hide behind cover, and after the fight 1/4 members wouldn't leave the cover no matter how many times I clicked all over the screen or tried to force the other 3 members to run through them to try and dislodge them. I eventually ended up leaving them behind to die, but thankfully they got attacked before I had gone too far and after they were downed I was able to use my Medic to revive them and then they could miraculously move again. Only ever happened once so I'm not overly concerned, but figured I should mention it.--                                                                                                      --Overall I'd say I very much so recommend this game! P.S If you read this far you are quite the trooper! I appreciate your time and hope any of this wall of text was helpful to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a mashup of X-Com and Alien Isolation, Aliens Dark Descent is one of the most enjoyable sources of fear and frustration that I have played. The game perfectly encapsulates what made Alien and Aliens, great with tense horror and heart pounding action set-pieces. Navigating through the xeno infested ruins of a Weyland Yutani colony while trying not be be added to the corpses littering the place feels tense and chilling. When fights inevitably break out things quickly turn sideways as you are swarmed by an ever increasing number of monsters looking to drag you away to your doom. Add in permadeath for your marines and limited resources such as ammo and med kits and you have a game that does it's best to stack the odds against you and your team. Aliens Dark Descent is one of the best games in the franchise along side others such as Isolation and AVP 2. If you are a fan of the Aliens series or real time tactics games you will have a blast trying to snatch victory from the jaws (and inner jaws) of defeatGameplay 10/10 My only wish is that there was more of itGraphics 9/10 While the levels are beautifully designed and capture the essence of the films the human character can unintentionally look a bit horrifying Story 8/10 The story is your standard affair of xenos running wild and WY suits failing to control them. That being said the story does have some new and interesting twists and the characters seem well fleshed out and uniquePerformance 8/10 Initially the game had some nasty bugs (pun intended) but things have gotten better for the most part

_childDocuments_.review: It's barely a positive.First of all, it's a solid game.Has that XCOM feeling, but the combat and movement are all real time (with slow-mo).It makes the world look more alive, and gives the tension (you can't just think sitting still).However, there are 2 glaring negatives:1. Stealth system is a core mechanic in game, yet it's the most un-fun. I love stealth games. I loved Dishonored series, Assassin's creed, and hell, I played bunch of rogue in Skyrim, too. However, the stealth in this game is just not fun. The enemy move pattern is not predictable, and can see you from outside your vision, and the game barely gives you time to react to hide. (You might just rage-quit because of this in prologue even at lowest difficulty). Did I also mention that the game is really dark environment with black Alien? You also can't tell which obstacles really block the vision, so you are constantly guessing. Oh, and the maps are designed really poorly in terms of stealth (for thematic purpose, they look great), so hiding spots really don't exist where you want them.  I've had numerous moments where I was stuck in a corner of a map, since the enemies would just move back and forth, and there is no way out. So hell, it's time to take out the big guns, right? But that leads to second problem.2. This "hunt" time. If an Alien finds you, they will enter a hunt mode, even if you kill the Alien that spotted you right away. And once this hunt time starts, it lasts for certain amount of time, And Aliens in vicinity will constantly come towards you during that time. And the funny thing is, if you didn't finish off an Alien by the end of the hunt time (they barely have not seen you yet), they can see you, and instantly trigger another hunt time. But hey, why is it so bad that this hunt time keeps going? Oh, that's because your squad constantly gains stress during this time. And this keeps adding random debuffs to your team that synergize with each other to completely wreck you. In hard difficulty, this got annoying very quickly, especially at the nest area, where enemies spawn from every direction.I just finished the first mission "Dead Hills" in Hard difficulty, and I did not enjoy the "hard" part at all.There is a lot of other minor annoying factors in the game, that slowly drained my patience as well. (I really hate the main character, and every character in the game has 2 digit IQ. But hey, it's for PLOT)So, I'm gonna give it another go at lower difficulty.TL;DR: XCOM, but real time action + stealth. Stealth is a main feature of the game, but very stress inducing and not that fun. The game is also just rough in terms of game design. If you haven't played XCOM, I would recommend that game over this (for similar genre).

_childDocuments_.review: Undisputed best Aliens video game in perhaps 20+ years.Once you get through the 1-2 hour intro/tutorial the game really opens up and creates a truly unique innovative experience.In addition to being a live action squad game, the developers did something truly truly amazing with the levels.Instead of being forced to do a single mission per level with a pass/fail only option, you have to do several missions per map and at any time you can choose to pull your guys out via evac zones. Rest up. Rotate squad. And go back to the same level and pick up where you left off with all the weapons, ammo, weapons caches, prisoners, and progress saved from when you were last there. Pretty sure I never saw this in any other tactical game.Additionally, it expands the Alien lore into a different direction instead of playing safe by mimicking the movies.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Alien games are always hit or miss, and this one hit it on the head. Didn't think you could do horror well in a squad based tactical RTS, but i'm pleasantly surprised. A really solid game that can only be made better. Hoping this Genre and style of game takes off a bit more as it's refreshing to tactical strategy games that isn't turn based.Quality of Life Recommendations:--------------------------------------- Time it takes to swap between menus on the Otago- Not having to 'hold click' for every decision. Make it so I can shift click to make an instant decision. That way it won't be accidental, but I don't have to hold a mouse for over 30 seconds just to use all my doctors. - Please reduce the amount of times I have to hear 'Deputy Administrator Hayes' in the Otago Menus- Marine path choosing in some instances, if 3/4 marines are going down one hallway i really don't want one of my marines to split off to the other hallway especially when i'm running from a big bad.----------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but has one serious bug - Elevators often won't work, forcing you to re-load. This is a problem, bc scrambling to an elevator is often the only way to get your squad out alive.Hopefully they'll fix that, Because otherwise this is an incredibly tense real-time-tactics game with a lot of cool ideas. And it will demand a lot of you - You have to manage health, stress, ammo, equipment, and time while moving quickly and quietly to complete objectives. This is a very challenging game that will appeal to fans of both X-com series, Xenonauts, Jagged Alliance, Commandos, and similar games.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is kinda like XCOM but real time and has nearly the same experience you'll find with XCOM. Alien Drone is now at point blank range with your marine and your marine shoots? Misses 10 shots. ALIENS BABY~ The game captures the atmosphere and look of the aliens franchise. Now there are still some bugs and features that would need some work. Like for instance in the Prologue I got stuck in a cut scene when you meet up with the marines and head down the elevator and they just stay stuck standing around in the cut scene. Also the sounds of weapons in game aren't the same as the ones you'd hear in the film Aliens which is a bit of a downside.  Also the game isn't well optimized despite having a decent enough PC to handle it, the game lags or sometimes speeds up all of a sudden. Overall the game has amazing potential once they iron out these kinks. I'd wait to buy this game once they release more updates.

_childDocuments_.review: ADD is one of the best games I’ve played in a long time. Let's be clear, it’s not easy.  I started the game on Medium difficulty and was checked.  I was absolutely checked.  I was checked like a 10yr Veteran Hockey player bolting full steam at a 4yr old PeeWee team.  No chance.  This game is a seriously hot title. The RTS aspect is implemented beautifully and the team management is on par with our beloved X-Com titles.  They’ve woven in adequate voice overs and acting (if you wanna call it that), and a story that aims to please the fans of the series and overall fandom.The sound is a mixed bag.  The ambience is exceptional, absolutely exceptional.  The winds, the motion tracker, the drips and creaks.  However, there could be some passes done on Marine chatter as well as weapon overlaps.  I’ve personally experienced gunfights where I can only hear one pulse rifle, one sentry gun, or just the aliens.  That being said, it doesn’t do anything in taking away from the game.  The game is tense, visceral and worth every damn penny I spent on it.  I would buy this game 10 more times.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I have seen and played so far, this game has all the elements I've been looking for in a squad-based game. Atmosphere, customisation, unique equipment and abilities, and a challenge that demands quick thinking and a good grasp of tactics. Highly recommended. My only gripe with the game is the lack of music for the squad loadouts and return from missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Would definitely recommend against this until the Wounded bug is fixed. I mean, all those reviews talking about marines joking about falling elevator are nothing, compared to lvl 7 marines getting wounded just because they dared to step out from the vehicle. According to codex it is supposed to get wounded if the health drops below 2 points. As a matter of fact - you can get into the mission with brand-new squad, get into a single firefight, keep all armor and health and get 2-3 marines in a wounded state and shoved into medbay for days. This renders the whole combat system reduced to a joke. Once you step out of ARC (your ground vehicle) - the ground is probably full of nails and your whole squad is wearing ballet shoes. Can't explain why they get wounded out of nowhere every deployment. This will completely ruin your tactics, make upgrading marines fairly pointless (you'll be running with lvl 1 all the time, 'cause your vets will be constantly in a med bay because of the above), and generally turns a great game into a get in - get out boredom fest. If the wounded bug is fixed - this is really good. The story, the atmosphere, everything is just about it. But this wounded bug just ruins it making no real difference between head-on vs stealth. You can go heads-on, shoot anything that moves (just manage tech and medpacks), kill everything on the level, and get into medbay for a week (enough to advance to next infestation level). Or you can go all stealth, get barely detected, fight only scripted encounters and ... get your whole squad  medbay for the same week, just because.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Ive never played Xcom so i cant compare the two, though i know they are similar. The game itself is very atmospheric, it matches the alien aesthetic perfectly. The story is kinda expected for a typical aliens encounter, company bad aliens hungry. The other creatures shown are a underused plot point, but may more info on them in the future. Its not a run and gun action game, that will quickly catch up with you and get dismembered or cocooned. You have to watch your surrounding, manage your rescources, and even your marines mental status. Its no shameful to pull out instead of trying to do everything on a map. Better to be alive, then over reach and get painted in a corner. It has several difficulty setting to make it more accessible, but this game is never gonna be a cake walk. If youve played squad games before its not hard to follow, if you havent its more accessible than most. And for the 40 dollar price im more pleased than most AAA 70 dollar games
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! A really cool blend of elements from XCOM and other games. _childDocuments_.review: Was a great game from start to finish. Can't exactly say it's similar to any other game in the RTS genre i have played but it had a good balance of difficulty and reaching rewarding milestones in the game. It also gives the player enough leniency when you want to/have to go guns blazing. All in all i had a great time with the only major downside being that i don't see my self replaying this game any time soon, but for a 20+ hour game that's not a bad thing. The story although not amazing did a great job of keeping me invested in the outcome up to the very end. I do hope that we get to see more content and if possible a new story with a DLC in the future. I really do hope that we get to see more games like this in the future, and i look forward to Tindalos next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Normally I get bored easily if I'm not blowing stuff up every 30 secs. I usually go looking for combat/action. Not here. I actively try to avoid combat as much as I can! not because it's boring or bad (the combat), but because I'm so immersed in the game and what my mission is, that (as the Colonial Marines actually would) I try my best to do the missions as cleanly as possible, without getting marines wounded (or worse) and without spending all my squads resources on pointless encounters that aren't mission critical.I don't claim to know what type of people would like/love this game, all I can say, is I like it!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Legitimately worth a play if you are into tactical RTS style games. You'll have a blast!Lacks in replay-ability unless you are an achievement hunter or just want to "do better" because of a linear, non-dynamic campaign. That aside, it is an absolutely phenomenal tactical RTS and I didn't think I would love it as much as I did. There are legitimate jump scares where you just go dang....I'm done for, and slowly accept your fate.... or manage your command points and barely scrape by? Great game, and glad to pay homage to a slightly forgotten franchise. I hope the developers look into furthering the story of this game through DLC and perhaps add a more dynamic element where you simply take back land/settlements taken by the aliens/humanoids and reinforce it before you can figure out how to stop them. Could include more research elements (not just xeno based), resource management as it is already implemented would work perfectly for it, and maybe settlement upgrades that include predetermined sentry placement, sandbags/defence areas, greater "daily resource intake", and "cannon fodder" militia for defense. A "play how you wish" style campaign DLC would be amazing. But that may be wishful thinking.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I have never wanted a game to get just a bit more post launch support more than i want this game to get it. It is so close to being perfect, but there are a few things that really drag it down. the biggest problem probably being cutsences railroading you into boss fights, or bad tactical positions. Sometimes you are given a pop up warning you about the upcoming danger sometimes you are not. The iron man mode also provides 2 slots instead of one and doesn't auto save very often so instead of uping tension by making all your choices irrevocable it just makes save scumming time consuming but no less effective. The railroading, the iron man save system and the sound mixing on your ship are my 3 biggest problems. wish steam had a mixed option, still worth getting  if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A real love letter to Aliens, and a fantastic tactical rts. The tone, the [excellent] soundscape and music, various plot points: all combine to stress you/your avatars out, and it's beautiful. Controller controls are a little "clicky" - lotta buttons to push sometimes to do a thing - but... that can actually be part of the fun when a horde is on the way & you're out of meds & low on ammo. One of the fast ones are about to pounce on your dude in slow motion, and music and enemy screeches are telling you you're doomed, but you've got to do a comlicated dance of rb/lb, rtx5, a, x, frickin w idk. It's fun. But outside of combat, controls and navigation are exactly what they should be & pretty intuitive. If you like tactics: it's good! Other than some liberties taken with the canon, you're just a squad of grunts sneaking or running around a bunch of xenos, cultists, and other things. Basic weapons w/ limited unlocks, but it takes a while to unlock most things so most of the time you're struggling against barely manageable odds, which is proper. If you want story, there is one. 'Lotta themes & story beats from the movie(s) and (imo, as a fan) the perfect amount of playful fan service. The plot itself serves to crank up the pressure & stakes, and informs why characters do what they do, which is great! In a game where I didn't expect a story, to have a well-written story & competent-to-great voice acting is wonderful.The game is crazy polished. The animation & art direction is pitch perfect, the sound is amazing and the gameplay challenging. What's not to like?ps: unless you really need to, don't select the "pause" option. Keep the action slo-mo. The action & animations were designed for it, but above all, slow motion lets the game do its playing-as-a-squad-of-Aliens-marines thing: with individual marines shooting, cursing, screaming, on fire maybe; all while dozens/100s of screeching, spitting, deadly things race toward you.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overally really good and I had great time playing it. Pretty unique experience, cool idea that works in this setting very nicely. Managing big team of marines, who have different classes, feats, and through campaing they earn experience, new weapons, devices, skills (and traumas) felt very satisfying.I have found stress mechanics quite innovative, also being able to return to base and get back to action with a new squad felt like something "fresh" (although I am not that much of a gamer, so "results may vary").There are some cons:-I had problems with characters models in some menus. The game was lagging a bit.-Unability to control each of the marines individually (other than using skills) is limiting your strategy.-Plot is ok, but ending and main concept is... well, a bit cliched. I found nice that it is not only fighting Xenomorphs.-Stealth is a good strategy - unless it is not.-It could have some added campaigns or "skirmishes" for enhanced replayability.Wishlist:-Multiplayer, maybe with some kind of gamemaster mode and custom maps would make play this ALL THE TIME.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game that captures the essence of Aliens perfectly.Unfortunately, I've encountered a bug in the Atmospheric Processor level in which a terminal I need to unlock a door is not responding - my Marine goes to the terminal, starts the animation, and then nothing happens. The action cannot be cancelled, and if I try to quit out, the game crashes and has to be force closed. When I reload, the same bug occurs and I cannot progress. I've tried reloading, leaving the level and returning, and returning to base and restarting the mission, all with no joy. Requested a refund which was declined. Caveat emptor.
