_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, unexpected and has some original twists to usual squad tactics games.The different aliens are well introduced and lead to some interesting cinematic moments.Some minor criticism:- it is difficult to get into and understand all the mechanisms. I only found out about the silencer for scouts halfway through for instance.- the daily events are often punitive, and bad luck at the start sets you up for failure.- on higher difficulties, you basically play the game in slow mode.Defo recommended for any tactics fan looking for something different
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Too much stealth. The game sold me on shooting aliens, but turns out it's a bare-bones stealth walk or let's sit and wait simulator. The most optimal way to play is to avoid as much confrontation with aliens as possible. I wanted to play as Corporal Hicks, but the game keeps forcing me to play as Newt.Another immersion breaking aspect is that aliens are terrifying not because of their nature (or their numbers), but because of how pathetically weak your marines are.Last but not least, beware that you cannot save at will, something which I find simply retarded in this day and age. You have a choice between two auto save systems, neither of which respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: 6,8 out of 10Game Visuals and Artwork 7Game Sound and Music  7Core Loop And Gameplay 8Character Design and story 7Technical Aspect/Friendly user interface 5 Longevity And Replayability  6Fun and Overall Feeling 8Game Visuals and Artwork: 7It has some stunning cinematics. And others kinda look like they are 10years old. But it works. The overall visuals are there, and get the job done above avrage. Game Sound and Music  : 7Great weapon sounds, great alien noises. The motion tracker sound can get a bit redundant after some hours though. Great voice acting. Even though the dialogue can get a bit cringy at times. Lacking some thought-out sound effects for the in-between mission menus.Core Loop And Gameplay: 8You do missions with your selected marines, which you then upgrade in between missions. The actual gameplay is exciting and tense. I really enjoyed it. The objectives change a lot so it never feels repetitive. Would have preferred a better upgrade system for my marines, and a more fleshed-out base system. It’s just missing that 3 steps extra and this game would have gone from great to amazing. Side note: Great saving system!Character Design and story: 7Surprisingly well-written story. Had me interested from start to finish. The dialogue can sometimes make your eyes roll a bit but all in all, one of the better stories for an Alien game. Left me wanting more. You can customize your marines, which is nice, too bad most of the options looked awful though. Lacks a bit here. Technical Aspect/Friendly user interface: 5It lacks here, especially in between missions. The menus for upgrading your marines and ‘healing them’ are pretty awful. The interface for each marine is alright but really could have used some polish. And I really got the feeling that this part of the game wasn’t polished enough.Longevity And Replayability: 6The game lasted around 30 hours for the full campaign, which is alright. They don’t drag out the game with unnecessary grinding, which I appreciate. There is a new game+ mode, but I didn’t feel like trying it since the core loop would be pretty much the same. If this game had a DLC, I would play it.Fun and Overall Feeling: 8I had a great time. Those tense moments in slow motion where you are getting swarmed made my sweat pump. The stealth when you are low on ammo and just want to get out of the mission. Some really great game design here. It falls short with the in-between missions systems lacking depth and feeling very unpolished. A different take on the Alien genre that I would love to see more of :)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this enough, it's right up there with RDR2 and Days Gone for addiction.The top down team strategy is a totally different play style to everything else I own, reminds me of Syndicate on the Amiga 500 in 1993 (30 years ago!)It's crazy hard & that makes it feel like being a character in the original movie... scary ♥♥♥♥!It can be a little buggy at times but the devs are working on it and keep the subreddit up to date so you know it's being fixed.

I am worried about how much difficulty will ramp up, as only done the 1st mission (which seemed balanced on medium).I'd put Fireteam as the best Multiplayer Aliens game though. But between Fireteam and Descent, I'd take this.Aliens versus Predator on the Xbox wasn't a bad little single player RTS game, and this has its feel in places.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has many good features, but it also has some problems with the enemy AI. The enemy AI are ridiculously stupid, especially in detecting and path finding. For example, they cannot detect your squad through dead bodies and they do not react when their teammates die next to them. At most of time, they also avoid going through the fire area to attack your squad, even if they are hivemind.Hopefully the developers can patch this or keep these stupid AI in lower difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: As an Alien, and Aliens movie-lover this game has blown me away. The atmosphere is just so perfect. It has no pretentious level-up system, no big talent-trees and it is just so fitting. My marines all have their own negative perk to start with. It suits the atmosphere of the movies so well. While playing missions, I feel constantly on my nerves. The sound of an alien approaching on the scanner takes me back to the 1978 film. And it scares the hell out of me sometimes when I get caught off guard. The stress system I think is very well designed. It keeps you constantly debating whether to press on, or maybe take some rest. This game is unique, I don't know of any other games that have similar gameplay. The fact that a game like xcom is turnbased, where this game isn't makes it even more scary. No minutes of carefully debating your every move. No, you have to move, NOW, make a mistake and it can always turn out to be fatal (I played on hard immediately, since I figured an Alien game should be hard, right?), but making no decision is often even worse. The lore, the story, the maps, the characters, the sometimes clunky gameplay, it all feels like you are stuck in a very bad place just like the people on the movies. I hope SOOOOOO much this game will get a sequel or prequel or whatever quel because I haveenjoyed it throughout! Some minuses: Replayability is not that high. It is more like a great experience, but after you had that experience, and know the plot, there is not much need to play again, for me at least. I have played the game two times and it cost me 98 hours so far (in the 2nd playthrough now). That is all I can think of actually lol. Highly recommend you play the game on hard from the get-go. If you are like me, and only experience it once or twice, make it the perfect Alien experience by challenging yourself. Keep frosty, soldier. Salute!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is  a really hard game on a number of levels. First you control a group  they move  as a group if a marine has a sniper rifle but in on the edge of a group they may have no shot and by the time they have shot you are in trouble. Second the aliens are quick  and you are going to take damage. Third traits can be brutal , Bad aim, slow, coward etc. Stress is a major problem. So you spend most the time avoiding the aliens and  creeping forward and running away as the Sh*t hit the fan fast in this game . No manual saves which suck especially when you are learning the game.  The atmosphere is great, the alien music adds to the tension.the feeling is pure Aliens. It is just tough  and hard to move forward as the difficulty cranks up . All in all a good game but it is frustrating. There are still a few bugs but generally fairly stable . Buy on sale and if you rage quit it doesn't matter.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Not as polished as I would like, but it captures the feeling of the Aliens (1986) movie. I found myself yelling "Marines! We are leaving!" far more often than I thought I would, which is a glowing endorsement to me. I prefer the squad-based playstyle over something like XCOM and I found the classes unique enough to warrant bringing one of each along. The story is engaging without leaning too heavily on the nostalgia factor. I just wish there were more missions and that it used the Aliens soundtrack more than it does. I hope that we get a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing strategic a squad based game. Really awesome once I got used to it. If you are playing because you are a fan of the Aliens movies (1 and 2), this will not disappoint. Totally new story here, but hits the vibe and atmosphere of Aliens (2) really well. Super intense the whole way through, missions get better along the way, and the game play and story stay interesting. It is really difficult at times, but very rewarding. As many reviewers have stated, this is a good companion to Alien: Isolation. Tons of action, and a Dark Descent for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of the Aliens and xcom, this is the game for you. It really helps capture the Aliens feel with tension and danger from the aliens by keeping stealth at its core forcing you to weigh the risk of engaging the aliens yet and alerting the hive or if its better to creep through and potentially be attacked from all around. Another bonus to this game are the developers. If you look through the patchnotes or the reddit page you'll see these guys are active and listening to the community, even though the game is still fresh, we have seen some large updates addressing some of the concerns raised by the community and you can tell they are clearly fans of the Aliens universe and able to have fun in what they do. The only things I would say this game needs is more options to add replayability such as customisation in a similar manner to the marine customisation of XCOM with new armour designs, colours and voice lines, a way to randomise levels to help and/ or a way to add modding/ workshop support to contribute to these features. TLDRGameplayTense and rewarding, if you like xcom and the old starcraft 2 campaigns you'll enjoy this. Though they are similar they are not the same, this game is very challenging if you're not prepared. StoryEnjoyable in its delivery, the plot follows what you would expect of an aliens movie. Voice Lines"Double time"SummaryFor fans of the originals, this is Aliens as Alien Isolation is to Alien. Its tense, fun and challenging with a good atmosphere. "Stay Frosty"
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Captures the aesthetic and atmosphere of the movie. Simple controls, yet many things to think about. Good variety of tasks and missions. Decent cut scenes, also can be skipped. Visuals are good. Some base and inventory management.Rename and customise your marines. Lacks voice options, but the voice acting is of a decent quality. You get an APC
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Alien games of all time. Yes, the graphics and voice-acting are a little average, but the actual core game itself is astounding. It somehow captures the tension of the first film as your marines creep around, trying not to trigger an encounter, and then brings all the fun and action of the sequel in combat as you blast away, and try not to get your squad disembowelled. Is it perfect? No. But it *is* delightful, terrifying, challenging, and an all-round great time.Edit: After finishing the game, I can firmly say that this is one of the best Alien games of all time. Below Isolation, but a strong second. Worth every cent, even if there's no sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game that captures the terror of the zenomorphs balanced well with the kick ass nature of the colonial marines. _childDocuments_.review: It's a squad based Aliens game with some light base and unit management a la XCOM. Leveling marines, managing time in the med bay, unlocking new weapons and researching ♥♥♥♥, that kind of thing. The interesting wrinkle is that you control the squad as one unit. Think of it more as a single "character" that you move around the map, with each person in it giving you some different abilities. Smart gun for base of fire, medic for medic ♥♥♥♥, sergeant for leadership bonuses, that kind of idea.The core gameplay loop is about navigating the map to complete objectives while managing your squad - stress, ammo, medkits, command points used for calling in special abilities, etc. As you're messing around on the map the alien hive gets more and more agitated, which increases the number of enemies on the map and the frequency and severity of special events. So you really don't want to just grind your way through if you can avoid it, some finesse is useful.Additionally, you can retreat from the map whenever and come back with a new crew. Are your people panicking, shooting at shadows, and cut to ribbons? Plus the hive is on full alert and just spitting new aliens out non stop? Screw, it, get back to the dropship and get the hell out. Come back with a squad full of four fresh marines and reset the hive agitation. The catch is that this will cost you a full day and each day that goes by increases the global infestation level. It's absolutely a tool you'll use, but you can't use it all the time or you'll get hopelessly behind.The story is pretty decent, but kinda boilerplate. Jerks set loose some eggs, people are trapped, Weyland-Yutani are the corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ we all love and remember. It's not going to win any writing awards - BG3 it ain't - but it's totally serviceable as a means for putting your marines on different maps to squash bugs. But most importantly they absolutely NAIL the ambiance. The music is spot on, the map design is great, the banter between the marines is solid, and most importantly the sound is PERFECT. From the click of the motion detector to the high pitched chitter of a pulse rifle to the screech of the aliens they got the sound right.It's a good game in and of itself, and if you have any fondness for Aliens at all it knocks it out of the park.Don't get me wrong, it's not a perfect game, but I have yet to have any major complaints. The worst I have are some spots here and there where things are a bit rough around the edges. Some of the character models move funky in cut scenes. Like a month ago one of my auto-saves somehow got corrupted and I get an annoying warning about it every time I start the game, and I can't figure out how to kill that save and save myself a button click.Oh, and it's $40. This game would be a solid recommendation at full modern gaming MSRP but they aren't going for that.The gameplay is unique and fun and they knock it out of the park with an IP that gets run into the dirt a lot.  Just buy it.

Thoughts so far is that it's an absolutely incredible, nerve racking, and immersive game. Perfect pairing for XCOM 2 and Alien fans. A bit buggy here and there but the devs have shown they take constructive feedback and plan on fixing known bugs. I do wish the tutorials covered more gameplay mechanics such as specialists abilities and how to rotate the sentry turret when you place it down but that’s what Aliens: Dark Descent content creators excel in helping with right now. A real shame too, hopefully going forward they do their job and play their game and not just test mechanics. Either way I am never playing this again.) Here are my thoughts so far about the game, I am on hiatus from finishing this because I was not having fun and I was getting more and more just pissed at the game and if I finish it with this mindset my review will be jaded and not as accurate as I would like it to be. Second the more limited save mode that I am currently playing can still be save scummed super easily by simply reloading to your last rest room, it is very tedious but also very easy to do which is another reason why having no manual saves is a totally bad decision because it doesn't even give xcoms ironman mode's effect of saving every action making your choices truly meaningful.2. Bugs: this game is absolutely riddled with bugs from many game breaking bugs that progress lock you, and at best force you to fully restart the mission or at worst fully restart the campaign. _childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a squad based real time strategy game that can be described as a cross between "Colonial Marines" with "XCom". What sets this game apart from other representatives of the franchise is that "Dark Descent" first and foremost strives to be a faithful adaption of  J. Cameron's 1986 Aliens movie, rather than just another representative of a gaming genre in an Aliens dress up.As such, it assembles aspects from a whole slew of genres under its umbrella: horror, stealth, tactics, resource management as well as frantic action! And it works! Despite presenting itself from a top down perspective, the dense atmosphere had me sucked in very quickly, and I'm glad to say that the subtle hammering of the motion tracker has lost none of its potency when it comes to creating tension.As for the Xenomorphs, they are handled very close to their movie counterparts.A single Alien is hardly a threat to a squad of Marines with Pulse Rifles, but a whole bunch of them can overpower you very quickly, if you are not prepared for their onslaught.In order to be able to stem the tide, the game provides you with all the beloved toys from the USCMC arsenal: Pulse Rifles, Grenades, Flame Throwers, Shotguns, Smartguns and, of course, everyone's favorite: the Sentry Gun!In other words: fans of the movie will feel right at home.With all that firepower at your disposal, one would think that you could simply shoot your way through every mission. Well, you could in "theory", but it is a really bad idea.As a matter of fact, you want to avoid combat as much as possible, and the reason for that is due to limited resources and the implementation of two mechanics: "stress damage" and "the hunt".Whenever an Alien spots you, it will alert others to your presence. Make enough noise, and the whole hive will awaken.Getting chased relentlessly will take a toll on your squad's stress level until your soldiers reach their breaking point and go nuts.While the game offers ways to mitigate stress and the negative effects that accompany it, you always want to pick your fights carefully; even as your soldiers level up and become stronger and more resilient.In short: Dark Desscent is probably the best and most authentic "Aliens" experience out there, so if you liked the movie at all, you really should check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: The headline for this review is that this game is a bold, innovative, and clever strategy game with a excellent license and look that, while rough at points, is overall a solid game any strategy or tactical game player should at least try.In more detail the positives of this game shine very very bright. The environments are intricately crafted and sprawling with clever design choices to relay important information to the player quickly. Mainly its the UI which is clean and streamlined while readable (something I've noticed has been going to the wayside over the years) and the very clever idea of making objects that you cam interact with have a bright green or red light to separate them from the muted colors of the environment. As for the atmosphere that comes with that environment its a easy 9/10. I may be a wimp as xenomorphs make me scared really easily (literally had to drop alien isolation because of it) but I genuinely believe the tension caused by the game mechanics and resource scarcity, especially in the early game, will put most folks on edge and hyper alert for any potential threat. It also helps that even in a small fight the aliens can do some very serious damage to your guys both physically and mentally as they are tough, fast, and I think smart.See, in terms of gameplay it is a lot like a real time xcom. You have classes that determine the weapon type they carry and abilitys they user. you got a home base with a admittedly b tier management mechanic, and you got a world to deploy onto. BUT the thing that makes a massive difference is 1) the game being real time with pause or slow down, meaning more dynamic interactions and situations and 2) the context. You know from the jump that you are not saving this world. It feels like a brutal fight for survival and your just doing your best to save a few dozen people. The aliens are tough and oppressive. Not only do the basic drones take a pounding but they are fast and will surprise you. They will dodge out of the line of fire, they rush into melee within seconds of contact, and they will make sure to do as much damage as they can be that by attacking all out for the kill, targeting your weaker units to be dragged off in the chaos of the attack, or breaking apart welds and turrets costing you valuable resources. Combat is inevitable and when it happens it is quick and decisive but it hurts. Even outside of combat however they prove a terrifying threat as they hide in vents and go into stasis to ambush you or patrol the abandoned halls of whatever hell hole your in.Theres a lot more positives I  could go into but for the sake a brevity lets skip to a quick few negatives. The most glaring one off the bat is the tutorial which while needed at first is slow and honestly should have a option to skip on replay. Next would be the constant voice lines confirming orders which has actually already been fixed supposedly (the devs listen!). The third one is very arguable but ive heard it alot and can see why which is the barebones base managment. I'm kinda meh about it as I think its fine because im here for the ground action. Don't get me wrong I loved coming home in xcom to all my new goodies and looking at my guys doing stuff but with 90% of my game taking place in the field i think the effort was better spent there. Lastly is human enemys, they have an interesting moment here or there and some of their relationships with aliens are intriguing but i personally feel like the time taken to make peer to peer combat possible could have been better used creating some different aliens. I imagine theres likely a reason why that wasnt done and i still think they are a additions that adds something to the game and they arnt a constant but just wish it was something different.In the end the game is a 8 or 9 out of 10, It is refreshing to see a developer take a risk like this on a non indie level with such a respected IP. There is flaws but the positives shine so bright and theres so many that you really cant argue with results of the care these devs have put in. Patches seem to be catering to the complaints of players as well so that bodes well. The game is so good as a matter of fact that it has convinced me to follow the devs output overall just to see what else they will do.

_childDocuments_.review: In the same way that Alien: Isolation is the perfect game adaptation of Alien, this is the perfect game adaptation of Aliens. On top of that it does a lot of new things for tactics games that the genre desperately needs rather than being stuck with XCOM imitators (either original action-point 90s X-com or the Firaxis games) as the only way to do things.Mechanically, things like squad progression and abilities and upgrades are best in genre. Almost everything works towards maintaining the atmosphere and ambience and theme of the game. It is stressful and intense but gives you a mountain of tools to manage this. Each lovingly hand-crafted level is fascinating to explore and spend time in, and the mix of scripted setpieces and emergent moments due to the mechanical framework is a real breath of fresh air. It looks and feels great, and even the characters and storyline are compelling - although I think the plot falls apart at the end and the final level is a real let down that ditches almost everything that makes the game good, although it's mercifully short. Even so, I'd recommend this to anyone who likes tactics games and especially has a tolerance for the vaunted 'friction' in games. In some ways this feels like the tactical strategy version of Pathologic 2, where the effect on the mental state of the player is as important a part of the design as the nuts and bolts of playing the game.I've played it through twice now (with a bit of a break between playthroughs) and I enjoyed it even more on my second run. A very special game and I am eager to see what the developers do next, especially as their previous game (Battlefleet Gothic Armada 2) was also excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: **Aliens: Dark Descent** is 50% off right now - and it's actually really quite good! The story is solid; the gameplay is tense... and kind of really stressful, especially with the motion track beeping away. I usually avoid these real-time action-stealth titles, but I like the way the control scheme works in *Dark Descent*; I suppose, in modern parlance it is almost an idler. You control the whole squad (fireteam, really), with each soldier reacting automatically, or acting individually on your specific orders, such as searching a body, or taking a special action like providing overwatch.There's also a light "base building" and squad upgrade system between missions, a la *XCOM: Chimera Squad*. The missions themselves appear to be fairly linear... which I must admit is almost a blessing in this age of procedurally generated open world aimlessness! Hopefully the story keeps up its flow and tension as the game continues.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good RTS X-com like strategy game. Your squad members have little quirks to mix up game play, sound design is fairly good in the sound effects dept. but man could it use something for the mission debriefing even if it was just the same song regardless of how well the mission went the silence is some how more immersion breaking than if it just played a random song from your local radio station. My only real game play complaint is this game not worthy of an iron man mode, I haven't come across game breaking bugs but scripted segments really ♥♥♥♥ you over not matter how careful you were. Also the Aliens have a fun habit of getting in between you and the goal so your basically required to kill them and raise the alarm. A good game but there are some sharp edges you should look out for.

_childDocuments_.review: Near perfect game. I'll start with the good. Then the bad. And give some final opinions. First. The Game play, atmosphere and overall plot are excellent. Your rewarded for being careful, quick thinking, and using the different Marine types to their fullest. The random selection of Marines for voice acted bits also makes it feel more alive. Well normally squad based RTS games usually suck from personal experience I'd say this one not only doesn't suck I'd highly recommend it. It has a sorta X-COM in real time feel if that makes any sense. Now the bad. Well the overall Story is good and serves it's purpose.. It's also a tad cliche and predictable especially for anyone familiar with the Aliens Franchise. "Oh yes the Scientist gets greedy and betrays everyone. Oh yes.. The Franchise always known for Weyland-Yutani having scummy people that back stab, and the Scientists always causing a crisis. The Corporation being one dimensional and the worst at risk analysis. That's been done to death. And unfortunately they gotta continue that trend in this game's story. I mean at this point Weyland-Yutani not being the big bad or the cause would actually be refreshing in the Franchise. Well the Gameplay is solid. The Pathing for your marines, the Drones, and the survivors when you rescue them.. Can cause some headache. The Tekker class can get a drone that follows it around, with upgrades the Drone can actually be a combat aid being a decent bit of supplemental firepower. Problem is. I seen this with your Marines, The Drone, and yes when you rescue a survivor they can sometimes get caught on the environment and require 3 or 4 move orders to get them unstuck. This isn't too big a problem if you catch it right away. But the Drone is small, and black.. In environments that are usually dark and black.. You'd be surprised how hard it can be to see the Drone in the heat of gameplay. Thank god for it's distinct rotor noises.  The biggest flaw however.. Is there simply just isn't enough game to the game. Which sucks. It's an awesome game. Just wish there was more levels Or hell maybe some expansions that give additional campaigns would be awesome. That said.. Yes even though I spent more time talking about the flaws I give it a thumbs up. There isn't really much to say of what is good. And the flaws need a little elaboration to explain. I am not pointing out flaws to ♥♥♥♥ on the dev's work. Far from it. I love what the devs made flaws aside and wish for them to improve either the game from patching etc or future projects learn a lil from what I pointed out.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the concept of the game. Honestly I liked just about everything about the game except two major issue's which I feel are so egregious they ruin the whole experience.The first problem is the event order. You fight an Alien Queen in the very first mission. That's right the big bad of the alien universe you fight at the beginning of the game. What a waste. They could have done so much more with it. Having several missions leading up to going deeper and deeper into more caves/tunnels would have been such a great experience, but instead they go here's an elevator, go down one floor and you fight a queen... on the first level. Makes all the missions afterwards disappointing because there's no where to go from there. but down.The second issue is what ruins the entire game for me. While the game leads you to believe there's a lot of action and alien shooting going on in reality it's pretty sparse. The game you bought isn't a shoot aliens game, but more of a hide and seek simulator. The game puts all your mission incursions on timers with some ridiculous stress system so if you're fighting aliens even if they aren't around in combat with you the marines build up stress which gives huge stat penalties and eventually just kills the marine. The only way to combat this is to NOT fight enemies ever. You just play hide and seek and run around doing missions while not attacking anything and you win. You can avoid 90% of enemies if you know what you're doing and the game is designed for you to play like this.Personally I like the framework of the game, but I would have liked to see the game be more focused on combating enemies at ALL times and less hide and seek. It wouldn't even be that much of a change because you're already limited in mission by health and ammo. I want to go in with my marines and shoot some damn aliens. Not run and hide like some wimp.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes every difficulty mechanic invented in the last 20 years and throws it all together, making the game full of cheap tricks and undermining it's own mechanics. The designers didn't learn from game history.- The tutorial is too hard. The first stealth section reveals the first unfair difficulty: off-screen enemies can see you but you can't see them. You have to navigate the level by constantly toggling between the map screen so you can see the enemies and the 3D level where you can actually issue move orders. Get used to toggling between those 2 because you'll be doing that every 15 seconds for however many hours this game takes.- Infinite enemies when you have finite ammunition. This was unfair when Call of Duty was called out for it 10 years ago. - Incredibly limited saves that require a resource used for 5 other vital tasks. Literally worse idea than Resident Evil 1 requiring type writer ribbons to save 20 years ago. I've had to leave this game running for hours on end in the pause menu because I have a life and work but this game insists I'm not allowed to save when I want to.- Campaign gets harder the more time you take, completely undermining the 'persistent levels' that can be done in multiple deployments- Soldiers take far too long to get into action. Spend days to heal wounds then spend days in therapy to heal trauma, then spend days waiting until the random events ease up, allowing you to deploy again- The game breaks it's own rules every 30 minutes. Use motion trackers to attract enemies, but not enemies running around this room. Enemies running around so fast they are quantum particles everywhere at once to see all but nowhere for the bullets to hit.- For a stealth game, this game forces the player to break stealth far too often. Cut scenes several times a level break stealth into instant combat. Enemies in narrow corridors that don't move, can't be distracted, and spot you the moment you open a door that you have to go through.- The difficult sections of the game are so poorly telegraphed that they had to literally have a warning popup that a difficult part is ahead. "But they designed this game to be hard" is the game excuse that is posted in main menu. No, they used cheap difficulty tricks so they could avoid learning their own systems. Bizarrely enough the game becomes far too easy in sections. If you have time to setup defenses (not where the game tells you to, because the game will set you up to fail with the cheap trick 'they spawned behind you') you can setup infinite mines, making the encounter trivial. You just have to sit there for a half hour spamming mines. Boring. Also fails to learn from history as that is the exact flaw with Baldur's Gate 2 with bounty hunter traps 20 years ago.It's a shame that the difficulty is so bonkers because the rest of the game is decent. Fun additions to the Aliens lore. Interesting character arcs, especially in the tutorial. Love the cult idea. I'm going to try to finish this game for the story but I'm hating the gameplay that gets in the way of the fun. I'm stubborn but not happy.Edit:Finished the game out of stubbornness. Opinion of game not changed: do not recommend. The stealth and encounter mechanics are unfairly difficult.Gripes:- Game continues to undermine it's own features. Always do a mission in 1 deployment regardless of what the game tells you. The incurable kleptomaniac flaw and doom clock punish using multiple deployments.-- The Doom Clock deserves its own mention for bad design: A hard turn limit is put on the campaign when there's an unknown number of missions ahead and random events that prevent deployment. I don't trust you game, so I'm save-scumming to complete every mission in the least deplyments. Not fun but it's the behaviour the game incentivizes.- Game continues to set player up for failure: "Let's lure some super deadly xenomorphs to kill these pathetic mercs and then we'll sneak into the same area. What could go wrong?" Of course, seeing that as a terrible idea, I refuse to do it, instead easily killing the mercs without having to open the vents for the xenomorphs. The xenomorphs show up immediately anyway.- Game wastes your resources by surprise. Ending a deployment wrecks any sentry guns left behind. That is fair until a surprise ending of a deployment gives no chance to recover the guns. The game surprise-ends deployments repeatedly without warning, including in the middle of the mission. Opening a random unmarked door can force end a deployment and waste resources.- Bugs or intentionally cruel difficulty? I can't tell anymore.-- Uncurable, unlocatable kleptomaniac flaw steals precious resources with every deployment. Encourages doing entire missions in 1 deployment.-- All soldiers always finish a mission wounded, despite actual health at mission end. Once again encourages doing entire missions in 1 deployment to decrease down time due to healing.-- Spawned xenomorphs sometimes refuse to move or be lured by motion trackers. Had to lure with grenade sniping.-- Resting option randomly disappears in closed rooms forcing a tool lost for break weld then reweld. Rest option is present once in giant rooms with many open doors. Mission 11 had this weirdness repeatedly. I think it's alt-tab related.Good parts of the game (because it's not all bad):- Story gets keeps getting better as it goes along. Clever ways of utilising the Alien franchise's common tropes.- Types of action scenes are varied and fun. I wish the missions were entirely the dangerous encounter spikes.- Ordering a squad instead of individual marines was an excellent idea. The reduced micro more than made up for the few times more micro would have been better. I hope more games do the same.- Art design for varied levels and soldiers is pretty good. Would be excellent if they allowed for more dramatic colouring for marines. In X-Com-like games like this I like to colour units by class for easy recognition.- Risk-reward for research upgrades is satisfying. The research upgrades are pretty good too (except the face-hugger one, but that's still a remarkable success rate)To any devs determined enough to read this: look at Sniper Elite 4 for a positive example. It is a stealth game with some set-piece action, real-time exploration, traps, alarms, and large maps. It managed to have fair difficulty mechanics without ever resorting to infinite enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: My PC specMotherboard: ASRock Fatal1ty B450 Gaming K4Ram: 32GB (2666MHz)GPU: Asus GeForce RTX 3080 TUF Gaming OC V2 10GBCPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 3,7GHzA fantastic game that captures the Alien feeling perfectly.First off the game has some bugs. At the time this review is written there is a rare bug that makes your squad instantly shoot at enemies when they see them, when you are not defected yet (In stealth mode). This can accrue when you have a “survivor” in your squad or after the “onslaught” event. To fix this you can…1. Load a save before you started the mission. 2. Extract from the mission & deploy again. Hopefully it’s fixed soon because it can be really frustrating & ruin a mission. The game also has some minor bugs like enemy models standing up when they are dead instead of laying down. It’s only visually though, your squads treat it as if it’s dead..The game runs just fine on my PC but sometimes after a long session the game can start dropping frames. Restarting the game fixes this. However, sadly you can’t just save & restart the game. To manually save you have to create a “safe zone” by using up resources, if you are not playing on “No one can hear them scream” mode (Ironman mode, only 2 saves) the game also autosaves.People compare Aliens: Dark Descent to Xcom & I can see why. It’s however very different in my opinion & telling someone that it’s like Xcom could give them false expectations. It’s like you would say that Escape from Tarkov is like a battlefield game. Instead of controlling each marine you control the squad as one entity. When you give an action order it’s most of the time the closest marine that performs the action unless a specific class is needed. For example, a Tecker for hacking or a Medic for giving first aid. The system works well most of the time but can be a bit frustrating when you want to use an ability with a specific marine but they don’t have a line of sight so you have to find just the right spot so they can see.There’s not that many weapons & the customisation for appearance is very basic but it has an interesting Trauma system. During a mission stress is built up & with time they build up traumas that give some kind of negative effect. I love this mechanic because it reminds me of the second Alien movie & the classic line “It’s game over man it’s game over!”.The story is good, it’s cheesy as hell but in a “Aliens” kind of way. I liked it & it had some really nice story parts.I highly recommend this game & really hope they will release dlc or even make a second game.

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked/ enjoyed about Aliens Dark Descent was:-Top down approach as opposed to generic 1st or 3rd person COD shooter-New original story-Staying close to source material-Game play very responsive-The first half of the  campaign is structured to allow casual players to take extra time if needed to learn the mechanics and finish the game even on hard difficulty.-Graphics/ visuals were adequate for what they were trying to do in cut scenes. Some of the things I did NOT like so much in the game was:-Sometimes Story specific Tasks are not very clear later on in the story for example the first time you enter this room with multiple entry points because you have to survive a defend against massive ONSLAUGHT on Pioneer Station when squad functions are disabled until you figure out what you're supposed to do like placing three sentry guns in specific locations. -Sometimes I find the 360 degree camera rotation can be a bit disorienting at times when you suddenly have to move your to a general direction and you have to pull up your map to make sure the marines are moving in the intended direction. -Have to switch back and forth between the top down view and map screen to click on a point in order to move the squad in what ever location on the map. Other thoughts:-Often hitting the escape key and clicking the load button for many a common practice when you are unfortunate enough walk too close to the wrong vent or get hopelessly swarmed by xenomorphs in a narrow corridor.-Somehow xenomorphs are not alerted to your presence when AI squad members start shouting random things out loud when a command is given or not even when you are not detected or being hunted. -I think the basic story telling of each mission chapter was told with great respect to the source material and lore of the Aliens franchise. -I'd give it a rating of about 8 out of 10. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent. It feels like a natural extension of the old game Aliens vs Predator: Extinction, for the Marine campaign, and it plays fantastically. You play as constantly overwhelmed marines, can customize and level them up, and even though the enemy variety isn't the largest (it never was canonically), it doesn't ever feel like a walk in the park. You constantly run the risk of being overwhelmed even on the easier difficulties if you're not smart. It's a fun challenge and definitely priced correctly at $40 or so USD. There's limited replayability, as the missions are simply the missions, but it's worth the playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up really enjoying this, even though I'm usually pretty bad at real-time strategy like this! The game has a good blend of biding your time/hiding like a terrified grunt and demolishing bugs like a can of RAID.Other people have given better reviews than me, so I'll say instead that I felt like this was totally worth buying at full price. My only real complaints were that the difficulty (on normal) felt very all-or-nothing: either my squad would walk away from a fight with a few nicks and scratches, or they would all be ripped apart. There were only a few casualties my squad could walk away from. ...And the scripted story sections (which were largely stealth focused) were interesting from a cinematic standpoint, but were like pulling teeth. All I wanted was to get past them and get back to the main gameplay draw, which really stung when I found out the last level of the game was another scripted segment. We'd been fighting through a mine and then...oh, I guess it's just...over. It wasn't a particularly bombastic finale, the character deaths were either for people I didn't care about at all dying suddenly, or not given enough focus. There just wasn't enough drama there to chew on, and there really needed to be something that felt more like a finale for the squads you were actually playing with during gameplay proper - I didn't even realize it was the last level; it had been a pretty easy run.I won't say the game felt too short, but I WILL say I'm dying for more, an expansion pack or a sequel or something with similar mechanics. I got the plasma rifle just in time for the last level, for crying out loud - I didn't even get to use the special attack! :(I feel like this sort of gameplay would probably map really well onto a left 4 dead style zombie apocalypse setting, as a side thought.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Aliens (Alien 2): The Movie: The Game. The original space marines and the original scary bugs. With the blessing of 20th Century Studios. Myself having gone through all the movies and most of the books, I think this script is material for a proper Aliens episode, or rather a 40-ish hours Aliens TV-series (honestly, this story is better than some of the books').A bit scary game, but more about tension and pressure. Definitely not a game for chilling out.The gameplay is initially a stealth, Commandos-like tactics game, but it escalates quickly into more of a bullet hell/tower defense. There is no tactical pause as such, more like "tactical slo-mo", which I enjoy even more. The game may be hard if you are a tactics fan. The game may feel easy if you are a survival/tower defense fan. It really depends.My point is that this game is really, really fun. To give an idea of what an acid-spilling party this game feels like, many of the ending missions will finish with a balance of 120+ alien kills, give or take. To put this into context, in Riftbreaker you may end a mission with 300+ kills, and an enemy wave in Age of Darkness, let's say a few thousand kills.The graphics are really the best I've seen in a game of this genre, to the point that the game animations look better than many of the cinematics. It's Unreal Engine, though, so the performance starts suffering when there's more than 30 enemies on screen, and there's not much you can do about it. The bottleneck in games like this is usually single-thread CPU performance.As I write this, the developers have added "New Game+" mode for the xenomorph-cide freaks out there who want to keep massacring, so the developers keep supporting.All in all I recommend this game a lot, unless you are looking for something chill, or you are against crimes against extraterrestrial species. It is really not that difficult.As alternatives to this game, if you didn't have enough carnage, I am going to recommend Riftbreaker and Age of Darkness, but especially Riftbreaker.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the first Aliens game to really capture the spirit and atmosphere of the movie. What Isolation was to Alien, Dark Descent is to Aliens.It has a few rough edges -- for some reason, beards would not stop looking like they were added by the  MSPaint spraycan and some of the voice acting can be a little lacklustre -- but I didn't notice anything game breaking. The priority system does a good job of making it feel like you're commanding a cohesive unit, and the way the visibility and motion tracking system work together to raise the tension at the right times is great for the overall feel.The ability and necessity to pull out of missions and come back after a rest gives the whole thing a nice bit of risk as well -- push a little harder even though your marines are getting stressed or extract, rest up, and come back fresh knowing that you're one day closer to being nuked into oblivion?My one main complaint is the repetitiveness of the voice barks. Clicking between rooms on the Otago always nets the exact same voice line, and as you'll be doing this a lot it wears out its welcome quickly. Same with commands on missions -- hearing "THEY'RE HEADED OUR WAY" or "LET'S SEE WHAT'S INSIDE" for the billionth time did start to grate by the end of the game.Overall though, a great Aliens game and worth picking up :)

_childDocuments_.review: When this game was initially announced it looked "ok" to me, not great, maybe worth checking out eventually on a steam sale. This week when the final launch trailer released I checked it out and was underwhelmed by it. However, as the week went on I began to see reviews coming in from some of my favorite channels (Worth a Buy and Mandalore gaming). The reviews were glowing and I decided to give it a shot. I am so happy that I did, this is easily one of my favorite tactical strategy games of all time and the youtube trailers absolutely do not do this game justice at all.There is a lot of tactical strategy like XCOM, Fallout 2, Jagged Alliance and the Aliens TTRPG. This game obviously takes a great deal of its inspiration from Aliens 1986, but it makes every Alien encounter feel extremely tense and dangerous. The Aliens in this are fast and ruthless, especially on the higher difficulties. Even if you have a lot of firepower if just one slips past your front line and lands a hit there is a very high chance your Marine will become injured and receive a minor injury. A decent chance they receive a major injury that will have consequences on their combat effectiveness for the rest of the deployment or a slight possibility of something absolutely catastrophic happening (a limb being severed such as an arm or leg, being struck unconscious from a concussion, comas, hemorrhaging etc.)Had a really desperate encounter where my squad had to infiltrate a hive, and things went from going smoothly to hectic very quickly. Long story short it was a very tense game of cat and mouse with combat sprinkled throughout leaving 2 of my marines incapacitated and having to carry both of them back to the ship for extraction. When carrying another marine you can only use a side arm such as a pistol, needless to say not very effective against the universes most lethal apex predator. Thats when I knew this was one of my favorite Alien games of all time.  Swapping between moments of tense anxiety to combat has a really great flow and makes the pacing for every play through feel different In addition the developers did an excellent job crating the environments. The worlds feel alive and lived in and you can really see their attention to detail and you just know they have a deep respect for this universe. Lots of environmental story telling and interesting design. My cons with this game are minor. Some of the animations are a bit stiff and customization options are a bit on the weaker side which is a shame. It would have been great if the visual fidelity was a bit higher for the individual marines I want to be that much more invested with my squad, that way when something goes horribly wrong (like a squad mate getting abducted and being dragged off to the hive), I would feel it that much more. This is a small developer studio and they really punched above their weight overall. I understand some of these things are likely due to budget constraints. But compared to the recent AAA game industry landscape where every release has to have a foreward apology letter, this is a breath of fresh air. Let me close by saying I have been a huge Aliens fan since I was like 12 years old. I grew up playing Alien 3 on the genesis and SNES and played pretty much every one since then. From Alien Trilogy on psx to the AvP series. Next to Isolation so far my impressions of this currently has it sitting at my #2 favorite in the series.

If you have a super ultrawide monitor, be aware, this game will probaly not run right for you!A little more in deapth: I have only 61 minutes played of the game, at the time of writing this, and more than half of that has been trying to get it to run on my super ultrawide monitor. After a good amount of research, browsing various forums, youtube and where else i could think of to search, I still havent managed to get i to run right, no matter what i do the game is very zoomed in to the point where early on in the tutorial i cannot see and click the point i am supposed to go to. Some people claim to have a fix/workaround, involving some editing of files, to get it to run on a super UW monitor, those fixes didnt work for me (some claim it did for them, some claim it was somewhat fixed but reverted later) and im now sitting idle hoping they will patch in support for my monitor. The game looks good, fun and i hear positive things about it. But since it wont work for me, i cannot recommend this to someone who has a super UW monitor like me (i use a samsung G9), and would like to add that i think its very disappointing that the devs havent got super UW support implemented. _childDocuments_.review: A very interesting and unexpected mix of various game mechanics which all work very well together and are fun as hell. Bugs and glitches are rare and are mostly related to marines getting stuck in level scenery. I would love to see a map editor get released, there's great potential here to make all sorts of fun, memorable and replayable levels. This is Alien games done right.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I love Aliens and it's early days... but I think the Squad control is good.. the atmosphere is excellent.. and so far its been respectful to the source material. This is interesting in the way it fuses RTS with Squad combat. Some video game reviewers wanted more micro management, but I like this variation. It feels like an innovation in this game. _childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, but it's fun. It could use a lot more polish in some areas, but excels in atmosphere and nostalgia  generation, as a decades-long fan of the Alien franchise.The AI is pretty rudimentary and could use some work - marines will, rarely, get stuck while walking and be unable to unstick themselves, requiring manual intervention. The game is a little slow to start as far as fun goes - unlocking initial stuff felt like a slog, but is worth waiting for.Skills usage needs some work - if two marines have the same skill, I'm unable to choose which to use - the game chooses the closest marine, who inevitably gets interrupted if it's a close-quarters fight. That means it's almost impossible to deploy the flamethrower in close-quarters high-action moments, which is not how it should work.Hoping for more content added - it's kind of "minimum viable" so far from what I can see, but it IS viable. Reiterating: the warm-up is slow but it's worth the push, especially if you like the IP.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is an amazing game but not really playable in its current state due to bugs and balancing.This game really feels like an alien movie. Its creepy, stylish, movie-esque cutscenes, aliens are very powerful, and stuff goes downhill very fast. One wrong move can doom the entire mission. Autosaves only happen very rarely, meaning mistakes will set you back quite a bit. This makes the game a very tense experience.Because of this it is unbelievably frustrating if a marine gets stuck outside of a door for no reason and gets spotted, triggering a huge wave of aliens killing your squad and setting you back 10 minutes due to no fault of your own. Or you click a button to get command points back and nothing happens, so you click it again and suddenly it happens twice meaning you are now out of resources to repair your sentry gun, resulting in death. Or you set down a marine you are carrying and for some reason during this animation you cannot make any other orders, causing your squad to die.. the list goes on.Then, the balancing. I have no issue with hard games, but for hard games to be good they have to be skill based. That is not the case here. This game is incredibly unforgiving. Things spiral out of control very fast with no means for the player to stop it. I play on medium but I still just had to replay a save for multiple hours just to barely make it out during the FIRST MISSION. And the issue is, it does not feel like my fault. I snuck in undetected, I had full health, good tactics, used everything at my disposal. Then, there was a bossfight, that causes you to be detected, that causes you to be hunted, that causes a huge wave of enemies to swarm you, that causes you to be hunted MORE, that causes another boss to spawn... One one hand, this makes it feel like an alien movie. On the other hand, it feels like the player has no input on this. These are things happening TO YOU, not because of your actions. Even worse, after I finally made it out it did not feel like a success. I tried the same exact thing over and over until by sheer luck it randomly worked.These are all fixable things. Don't trigger detected state during or after a bossfight. Make xenomorph spawns less random. Give us some ability to autosave outside of a shelter, maybe once a mission. A little bit more hiding places here and there. But it needs to be fixed.Also, for some reason the game is incredibly unoptimized. Why is my 3090 sounding like a jet fighter barely making 70 FPS during the after action report screen?
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A true experience for the Alien franchise and USCM fans. It's fun, it's got the lingo, and you can't help but grin as you fight of hordes of Xenos while the looming light of the red flare lights up your surroundings.Not without it's flaws, some bugs (no pun) and some spelling errors, but nothing that drew me out of the game or experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Lt. Gorman simulator Accidentally waking up the hive, with one marine getting his arm ripped off, and now your squad has to carry him back to the elevator while your motion tracker is lighting up and you can hear the aliens getting closer.Easily the most tense tactical game I've played in a while, excellent use of lighting and game systems really ratchets up the tension. Avoiding combat is often more important than combat itself as you really do have a limited number of recruits and losing marines hurts. Combat is pretty lethal and if you don't manage to have a plan/engagement point you're gonna get hurt. Only real complaint I have is some bugs, but the devs are squashing them out pretty regularly

_childDocuments_.review: It's like XCOM cross AVP Extinction (Marine campaign). You control a single squad of marines in large, open colonies (legit Hadley's Hope style from Aliens). Weld doors, place motion trackers, sentry turrets and avoid attention as best you can. The more you shoot, the more the alien hive knows your location and the swarms become more and more intense. Basically the moment it goes to ♥♥♥♥, you should take off and nuke the site from orbit - really cool mechanic.Edit: Just finished the campaign - took about 25 hours. Last mission was eh, but the rest of the campaign was exceptional. In my top 3 Aliens games of all times, the fact that an RTS can be this tense and match the movies so well is FANTASTIC. Buy if you're an Aliens fan :)

My marines open fire on aliens the moment they see them despite not currently being hunted.5. a side mission where you make a decision to execute 3 separate survivors depending on what info you find about them is bugged where no matter what option you choose your ship gets sabotaged from picking the *wrong* survivor AND you can't complete the quest.6. _childDocuments_.review: Don't play this game if you do not like "mobile game" mechanics added to it. I did have fun for some aspects of it but the developers really have a hard-on for making playing this game difficult for you. Between the quickly on-setting tired/exhaust (cannot use dude for 4 in-game days)mechanic. The stupid personality traits that come with your marine are always debuffs (Had one with -1xp every mission when most missions you may get at most 3xp, and another that immediately got exhausted after one deploy)as if a personality is never a positive thing. Gotta waste a level perk to get rid of it. Overall it feels very punishing to play, like I never once felt I had gotten a good thing.Never have I ever played a game that presented me with unacceptable options for in-between day mechanics, always negative and insanely punishing. Once a day event told me my most valuable marine and expensive marine(hours poured into this one) was to suddenly a cultist leader and that she needed to be removed from my crew FOREVER or I leave her on the crew and some unstoppable event with negative affects would happen down the line because I wanted to keep my trooper, who oh I don't know, WAS WITH ME FROM THE VERY BEGINNING OF THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GAME AND CRASHED WITH THE SHIP WITH THE REST OF THE MARINES!! Ridiculous. And the fact that the shotgun and sniper rifle are special weapons instead of primary or secondary weapons is ridiculous. You only get 3 command points to use for specials to start, and I was at lvl 10 and I had only 6 command points to use by that point with a bunch of investments of resources. Balancing with the rest of the items used for specials that number dwindles quickly. Face hugger nests are invulnerable to flamethrower damage(which is stupid cuz I can flame a whole room with fire and none die, wonderful), and shooting them with normal weapons attracts attention. Making the sniper rifle with the "noise cancel perk" the ONLY option for stealth kills. Yeah, I only had to get a dude to lvl3 in recon(which took time) and then buy the sniper for him to use(which took even longer) only problem now is that it is a special weapon and requires command points to use which means at most I can take out 6 of the 8-10 that are often huddled together making me wait until one more CP recharges to be used again. Only to have a xeno drone spawn on me, ruining my effort for a stealth approach and making everything a waste of time. Its too punishing, play elden ring.*More to add. They had done an update is the only useful correction was the ability for the face huggers to be destroyed with flame.  Tried to play again because I paid for it but now I cannot save unless I leave the mission. Stupid thing even says "game saved" yet never saves, its frustrating making progress and no way of saving it. Would refund if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play every game on hard, but I'm too old for endless retries, so I play this one on story and I'm still losing my squad occasionally (and definitely NOT because I'm sloppy... no-oh!!).Anyway, I really dig it and I hope there will be DLC or another part soon.Having been a longtime Alien-franchise admirer, I must say that some of the story beats are a bit too far-out for me, but don't count that as criticism, it's my taste.A few bugs here and there have usually been squashed by reloading and I never mind redoing a sequence, so all is good. The many updates they've already pushed out are proof that they care and I thank the devs for that (and the clever update notifications and wording of the updates).If you like Alien and don't mind letting others do the shooting while you tell them where to go, this game should be your cup of tea!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good RTS squad game in a great setting. You set up your squad like in xcom games but the gameplay is real time.In your squad, everyone starts as a rookie and can become any of the other classes: sergeant, gunner, medic, sniper and tecker. are the backbone of your team, increasing command points and bravery, both extremely important since one resource is used for skills and the other to reduce stress gain (which induces debuffs).  are the only class with access to the iconic smart gun and are all around good damage dealers. Medics increase both the health points of your teams and the healing capabilities.  are broken (as is tradition in these games) during stealth/undetected phases thanks to their silenced sniper upgrade.Finally  have a cool drone that can explore/weld and do some extra defense/shooting, but are the class you try once and replace with an extra gunner or sergeant, since their distinctive class attribute (being able to open tech doors) is a common attribute available to all other classes., pretty to look at and fun to explore and fight in. There is a lot to enjoy in the environment and design. Especially with the flashlight mechanic, that invites you to aim around to better see what is around you.Has multiple ; easy, normal, hard and nightmare and custom. Includes a pseudo-ironman mode where you are limited to one pre game save and one in mission save triggered after resting in safe areas. . This setting affects how the game behaves while you are selecting your skills to use. You can freely choose one or the other at any time, but . With tactical pause you will have unlimited time to react to any enemy sighting and, for example, take your sniper shots to instantly avoid triggering an encounter. Meanwhile with slow motion you can be punished for your positioning and timing mistakes.Likewise for tough combat situations where with slow motion you will be hard pressed to make the right choices and may be even hit or interrupted for not being fast enough or choosing the wrong target.It’s strange that this setting is an option and not part of the difficulty selection with how much it can affect the actual difficulty of the game.I personally think the slow motion mode fits the Aliens setting better, since it adds an additional stress factor to combat that is not there with tactical pause., nothing amazing but it's good enough to support the gameplay. Of course it has a lot of recurring alien themes, like the comically evil Weyland-Yutani corporate drones.At the time I played through the campaign the game was in a good state but there were a lot of weird bugs, besides the Xenomorphs. Things I had happen; pathing issues, both marines and enemies getting stuck on something, an objective being impossible to complete for missing some kind of trigger forcing a reload, ammo counters disappearing for sentries, skills getting stuck in use (can be a benefit if it happens with something like reprimand, but still annoying), and a bunch of other minor things. Something else that wasn't a bug but was really irritating was being locked out of using my sentry turrets unless in a specific location during a specific story mission. Which led to me getting overrun during an onslaught I was unable to properly prepare for.Overall all things I expect to get fixed, but that you should keep in mind going into this game close to release.Overall .

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful atmosphere, decent management, and TONS OF XENOMORPHS. I honestly loved the game. You do not control your squad individually and it feels a bit awkward at first. Ngl, I was hoping something closer to Partisans 1941 or Commandos in terms of gameplay but I am not disappointed. You can apply different tactics and try different soldier builds to maximize squad efficiency.  Still, it is better to watch a few gameplay videos first to see if it is for your taste. There's enough tactical depth for a horror/strategy game if you ask me. Aliens: Dark Descent really keeps you on your toes. It is a must for fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The one game in the Alien franchise least likely to give you a fear induced aneurysm or make you soil your pants. (Disclaimer: Least likely does NOT indicate 0% chance. It's still the Alien franchise.)Okay, introductionary joke done, down to the nitty gritty: this game is a pretty damn good stealth based small unit strategy, with an eye on picking your approach and battles and managing your ressources. Your squads health and sanity are ressources. I'd say it runs well, is challenging but not completely unfair - the moments where the game decides to spawn a drone from the hive entrance you are currently passing by can be a bit nerve wracking, but mostly, if you play it smart, you got a good chance at victory. Knowing when to pack it in and run away to try another day is also part of that.The story fits the universe, the visuals are on point, the Aliens are bastard coated bastards with bastard filling, your marines run out of ammo, sanity and health just before you make a fatal missclick, and you are going to sometimes just need a break. But it is good.Also, big one, there is no manual saving, apart from deliberately creating a shelter and resting, since that triggers the autosave, so, save scumming, while possible, is a bit harder. The autosave in general however is pretty decent, once you know the limitations and how to manage your squads ressources.I enjoyed it, even though sometimes I wished I could have deployed more marines or given some of them specific tasks, but then again, that would have circumvented parts of the story, even though you can see some of the twists coming from lightyears away.Anyway, Weyland-Yutani, building better worlds, inquire about our job openings.I liked this game, quite a bit, I can't play its First Person cousins at all, I like the Alien franchise, I hate the Alien franchise (in the good way).
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: On the first playthrough I thought that this was a solid real time tactics game which is an interesting spin on games like XCOM. It is truly like XCOM, just in real time making it its own beast. It really heightens tension knowing the game never really stops besides the slowdown from using special actions. However, on my next playthrough on Nightmare I started to really see the strengths of the game. It elevates it to a much stronger status that forces you to use all the tools you have. Never get detected by using suppressed snipes, suppress fire on chokes, pre-prep sentries when you make a mistake, flame choke points. It just all comes together on Nightmare which if you only played this game on normal I highly advise going back and playing the highest difficulty.It feels like it is the way the game was initially designed. Aside from a few instances I felt I got robbed, all the times missions went to hell I knew what went wrong and how I can re-address it. It does have its faults however, I apparently played this after the game has had a buggy launch. Most of the bugs I experienced were minor but annoying such as- Enemies on different planes yet still appearing. Thankfully I discovered the flamethrower seems to hit all planes in its line of fire so this can remedy it.- Marines randomly no longer talk until another cinematic happens.- Cutscenes failing to load, leading to the game just being stuck on a door opening sequence.Nothing too crazy, and most reloads solve the problem. I thankfully never encountered the cutscene fail on the games Ironman mode because honestly I would have been furious.There are some features I wish were in the game. The squads move as a unit, which probably makes this game better on controller, but I really wish I could assign marines to specific actions. The amount of times my sniper would take initiative to do something to us then be discovered, or walking in a doorway where I need that snipe immediately and he's the last one in. So I have to do this weird wiggle dance just to get the shot which is quite annoying. If I could at least set the formation so he is always on point that would have been great. Also, the game uses proximity as priority, so if a Xeno is on top of me and I want to use the shotgun but they are very close, the wrong marine may shoot because the game thinks it has a better angle. I really wish I could command THAT marine to use that specific ability.Even though the game's atmosphere is great, marines are far too chatty, especially when undetected. And although I appreciate the references, I think I heard all the random dialog they could say when I was about 60% through the game. Honestly, just a handful more lines would have done wonders. However, that gun truly is indeed a freakin’ lawnmower.This game has a great foundation and I hope it can get a sequel to expand on its systems. It is fantastic, but it feels it lacks variety in options in the missions as well as abilities and weapons you have even though the ones given all have purpose. I wish there were hard choices to make between 2 really good options but most of the time there is usually an obvious answer.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The cringy/juvenile plot and dialogue gets a pass because the gameplay is solid and fun.But the numerous bugs, some of which can potentially cost a mission, are a hard Not recommend.Bugs I've experienced:- A elevator suddenly not working and the crew waiting forever for it to start... which by the way, for anyone experiencing that, it's caused because the droid can get stuck on  wall instead of taking a corner and will stay there until you notice and go all the way back for it... which hilariously can also happen to the alien queen...- Giving an order to the crew and the only want who wants to take on the order is the one carrying an injured crewmember on his shoulder... so he cannot undertake the order, and no one else does, either, because the guy insists on being the one to do it... despite not being able to...- Giving an order to move while a crewmember is busy doing something should result in two things:A) He moves while carrying the order. Like for example shooting the shotgun.B) He carries the order and then moves. Like for example setting up a mine or opening a box.Whatever the case, they start walking or running to the position the squad moved at, following the issued movement command and speed.However, on certain occasions, mostly when shooting a bazooka or healing a crewmember, a member of the squad may just stay still after he finishes, and will only move again after you click to move again a few times. Should you fail to notice, this being a real time strategy game, the poor soul may have triggered the "alien alarm" or be overrun by enemies. A few seconds make a huge difference in this game.- Sometimes when a crewmember was downed, their body floated along the ground unnaturally until finishing the last movement order, on one such occasion I tried to carry him to safety and despite the mechanics seemingly okay, the body was floating three five meters in front of the guy carrying him, instead of over his shoulder. A minute later I ran a bug I previoulsy mentioned: I couldn't open a door because the only one offering to press a button was the one with his hands busy, so I put down the body... which suddenly teleported all the way back to when I had picked him up and messed up the mission. In fact, I returned for him and I couldn't even pick the body anymore. I was left with the choice of either restarting a whole mission or killing a valued member of the crew.Fun game until that stuff happens. The core ideas and elements of the gameplay are pretty good (albeit easily cheeseable at least on hard difficulty).

_childDocuments_.review: This is an Aliens game I didn't know I needed. It's not perfect, but the devs have put in a lot of effort and this FEELS like it's in-universe. It's right up there with Alien Isolation as far as being true to the style. I'd recommend it to everyone that is a fan of the genre. It's a RTS, but with slo-mo and pause features. The squad mechanic is unique to me, but it works great for the most part. A little more polish and it's a top ten game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Aliens movie and/or love the XCOM games, you will love this game. I really liked the intensity and thrill of the ride. It felt like being in the Alien movie. Constant stress, wanting to push marines the extra mile, but fearing they will break, running out of ammo, incoming hordes, sentry guns placed before a horde attack. All of the makes the game fun, with a good variety of missions that press the narrative forward. The atmosphere and the story makes it great. Also the tactical side of the "base building" with limited funds and time, make the experience feel right.. But be warned, it is not a relaxing casual game. It is hard AF and you will reload a lot, even on medium difficulty.  One of my favorite games recently. Just sad it is over (after 30+ hours), but can't quite let it so, so started a game + run right after it finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic experience. The strategy is straight forward, but there is depth to it. You can't just run and gun a level, or you will die. Take you time, and play like an actual marine squad (even though you are technically playing as a fire team - There is 4 marines to a team, 3 teams to a squad + 1 squad leader, 4 squads to a platoon...Hoorah).  Anyway, you do feel the intensity of the mission seeing that there is just so many things you need to accomplish. Resources are also tough to come by. How it is explained in game for being limited as much as it is works out fine, and a level of dread to the way you approach each mission. If you have been sitting on this one in the Wishlist, time to just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Protocol has to be the most un-fun "Repeat it until you can beat it" mission that I've played since Superman 64.Telling me to "Prepare or face certain death" is a joke when the cut-scene throws you in front of doors that lock behind you (making any of your preparation void), and then it throws you in the middle of a room surrounded by instant-kill enemies.Literally having to repeat-repeat-repeat play the same ~5 minute long session until you can complete it, is not fun, nor is it "challenging." I'm fine with losing marines when I make a mistake or get overwhelmed, it happens.Ripping the control away from me and removing all of my choices and then going "Aww, you should have prepared better," Is awful game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Squad based Aliens top down shooterThe story, atmosphere, characters, setting and sound are all serviceable. In fact I would say the atmosphere is excellent you really do feel all alone surrounded by monsters. The big problem with this game is the gameplay and the mechanics especially around control of the squad. There is no individual control, they move as a group. This is horrible when you’re using line of sight weapons but can’t move the person into the right position. Add in the fact that there is a distinct delay between orders being issued and them being carried out, a big problem when the aliens jump around like crazy and dodge all your shots. The squad progression and customization is extremely weak and feels like a late addition. The weapon selection is also poor. Plus they could only afford three voice actors and about six lines so be prepared for hearing the same lines over and over again. The game also likes to yank control away from you at the worst possible times, or forces you into untenable positions. This isn’t a deal breaker but they can be frustrating.   All that being said there is a good amount of content here but it does all feel very samey after a while. Overall the game lacks a certain amount of polish and is a little buggy even several months later. I’d recommend this one only when on sale.
