_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a game that I wish I could recommend more than I do. I’m generally a fan of puzzle games so I thought this might be very much up my alley. Don’t let the isometric viewpoint and the stealth inspired level design fool you, this is a pure puzzle game. You have to navigate your characters past sentries while using switches to lock or unlock doors and use one character’s powers to restore broken elements in the level to open them up for traversal. So far, so standard. The interesting twist of Timelie is that it lets you rewind and fast-forward through time, so you can look ahead and plan routes around enemies, sync up your movements with their patrols and if you mess up you can easily go back and try a different tactic. I really like the way the mechanic allows you to iterate on your puzzle solutions very quickly and without much of a fuss. It’s a neat solution to the typical stealth problem of having to hide somewhere and wait in order to learn enemy patrol routes.The first couple of chapters were all fairly enjoyable. I liked how the game taught me its mechanics and how it explored those mechanics with its level progression. The addition of a second character in the form of a cat that allows you to distract enemies, and who can crawl through small vents to hide from them indefinitely was really cool. Both character’s mechanics complement the others nicely. And I especially love the way the game introduces the cat by first using her as an NPC before giving you control over her.What eventually soured me on the game a bit however were the last two chapters. Chapter 4 felt like the developers just grouped together the most frustrating levels that relied on a ton of trial-and-error and a bunch of almost frame-perfect timing between movements and actions and called it a day. It just felt needlessly annoying, so forgive me if I didn’t go out and download the DLC levels that promised even more of that frustration. Seriously, that’s how that DLC is advertised. It prioritized frustration by making the levels longer and harder to beat and thinks that this somehow counts as meaningful content.When chapter 5 started, I enjoyed how it recontextualized levels from earlier in the game and tasked you with maneuvering through them a second time on an alternate route while your former selves are also present in the level. I appreciate the concept of the game recording your own solutions and playing them back again later for you to find an alternate route, at least in theory. In practice however this turned into a frustrating mess because there’s no 100% guarantee that you’ll even be able to make it through a level, given that the game can’t make sure that the path you took last time doesn’t interfere with the possible solutions you have to employ the second time around. This only really works if there is precisely one solution to any given puzzle, so the designer can anticipate your movements. It also robs the puzzles of a degree of predictability which, given the time manipulation mechanic, should be part of the core engagement of the game and it reduces every puzzle into a quick-fire trial-and-error session where you’re constantly doing course-corrections. It’s unfortunate that the game falls apart toward the end like this. In more ways than one. Because even though the game makes it appear that you’re trying to escape from something here, there’s no narrative to be found anywhere. You could replace all the characters with random shapes in a blank void and nothing about it would change. Well, I say that, but that’s not entirely correct. The game does try to tug at your heart strings at the end when the cat dies, I guess, spoiler alert. I’m not sure it actually dies, but it has this sequence where the cat “sacrifices” herself to open up the final door and the girl mourns over the cat and tries to turn back time to get her back. But truthfully, I felt that the game really didn’t earn this moment, which is why I’m so nonchalant about spoiling it. To me it just seemed like a cheap way to elicit an emotional reaction from the audience. Sure, I like cats and I found her design and mannerisms cute in this game. But it just feels cheap and manipulative for a game to introduce something that a large portion of the audience is probably going to have a visceral emotional reaction to and then using that as an easy way to create emotional drama. Also, I’m not sure what that post-credit scene is supposed to represent where we get to see the girl wake up in her room and then get greeted by what looks like a prison guard, that just seemed like a total non sequitur.And while I personally didn’t go for all the relics, which rely on you figuring out ways to solve certain levels with some kind of unspecified alternate goal, like not getting seen at all or not killing enemies, I looked up the secret ending you get for doing so and it’s just a short sequence in the hallway outside of the girl’s room where she notices a boy who is probably implied to be the cat given their identical hair color. I have no clue what the developers aimed at here, it just seems like tacked on bullshit that makes it appear as if the game had a broader point to make or an actual story to tell when it doesn’t. I don’t often call things “pretentious”, but Timelie is pretentious. It pretends to be something it isn’t. Because what it is is a simple puzzle game. One that I enjoyed the first couple of chapters of but couldn’t in good conscience recommend because of the severe dip in quality as well as the quite frankly unjustifiable price tag. Yeah, you get free DLC with 30 additional levels that are apparently so frustrating that they take twice as long to solve than the regular ones. But that’s just that, more of the same and not in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling all puzzle detectives! Ever wanted to rewind time like a superhero or a cat? Timelie is a charming puzzler that lets you do just that! Here's why it's a blast in 2024:Timey-Whimey Fun•	Outsmart tricky robots and explore strange places by rewinding time! It's like having your own personal rewind button (way cooler than memorizing!).•	Your Fuzzy Friend: Team up with a mysterious cat companion who helps you on your timey-whimey adventures. Who says cats aren't secretly time-traveling geniuses?•	A Relaxing Puzzle Journey: The game is full of clever challenges, but it's more about having fun than feeling stressed. Perfect for unwinding after a long dayA Few Things to Keep in Mind:•	The Story is Shorter: The game focuses more on the puzzles than a long, dramatic plot. But hey, sometimes a shorter adventure is purrfect for a weekend!•	A Quicker Time Trip: You can solve Timelie in a couple of days, so if you're looking for a super long adventure, this might be a shorter trip.Overall, Timelie is a delightful puzzle game with a unique time mechanic and a charming cat sidekick. It's a great choice for puzzle fans or anyone looking for a relaxing and fun adventure in 2024

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is not a long game, but the time you spend with it is in my opinion incredibly well spent. This is one of those games whose cure to detail shows in the little, unsaid things that aren't fully and constantly in evidence. There are glimpses of a plot or possible world-building information here and there in a few levels, and it's easy to find a common plot denominator from which you can deduce what's going on. But even then you could even just go in it blind and taking it without emotion, as a simple puzzle-game, and the game would still fully be worth playing: the concept of it is very interesting, and done with the right presentation for this kind of genre: you need to escape from those that chase you, getting to safety before things get out of control and you will remain forever trapped or caught.I don't want to spoil too much in this review, but I can say without reservation that it's a joy to watch the consequences and final result of your actions. It shouldn't take too long to become familiar with what might happen, even if the game might still surprise you, both with the puzzles themselves, and with the full extent of the efforts that you put into it.I hope Urnique Studio will expand more on this world, but even if they don't, I'm curious and looking forward to what other games they will develop nesxt.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept, bad execution:Cons: * Gameplay doesn't affect story at all. * Story doesn't affect gameplay at all. * Playing back your gameplay at the end of a level should happen at double speed. It's way too slow and I end up always skipping it rather than enjoying it because of that. * No rewards/benefits to finishing a level normally (no fanfare). * No rewards/benefits to finishing a chapter (the only story you get is before the last level). * No introduction to secret objectives (too bad if you missed some because you didn't realise they existed! Replay the chapter!) * No explanation to what the current level's secret objective is until after you've already completed the secret objective (some of them are wierd, like complete the level without using X abililty or without being spotted). * The chapter items you collect don't add to/affect the story or affect the gameplay at  all. * Selecting UI stuff with the mouse will often cause your character to start walking away. * Switching characters will cancel the original character's movement if you just made them do something. * Clicking on a door switch will only work if you're already standing in front of it. Clicking it when you're not standing in front of it will cause you to walk to behind the wall it's on. * You get nerfed half way through the game where they (in a cutscene) take away your companion character for no reason. * You can fail objectives on later levels by playing "wrong" on earlier levels with NO indication that an earlier level will affect a later level. * Reusing levels is interesting, but having to replay entire chapter(s) in order to complete objectives in later levels sucks. (It sucks so bad it gets TWO bullet points!) * The ending is one of those "oh you did this? Well psych! it doesn't matter anymore!" WHICH SUCKS. * The secret ending is really not worth the extra effort.I did quit and just look up the ending if you're wondering about the low time score. Because I didn't want to have to play through everything for the perfect ending and wanted to see if the game got any better.

_childDocuments_.review: A well done though short stealth puzzle game that I can recommend to anyone who enjoys puzzles or stealth.  Although there isn't a lot that's unique here, the puzzle difficulty hitting a sweet spot and the game's polish are the main appeals of the game.To be clear about what is or isn't unique here: This is not the first stealth puzzle game to allow pausing, not the first puzzle game that allows for a single player to control more than one character, not the first to elicit player's feelings by the end of the game, nor the first to completely lack dialog.It is slightly unique in how actions can be initiated during progression of time, the final chapter does have some unique interactive elements, and the final level requires you to think like a cat.I kind of don't understand the ending, but I don't need to, because the game's story nor does satisfaction of playing rely on that. Its a solid puzzle that can take an hour or less per chapter, for several chapters, all driven by a girl who can stop time and works together with a cat to escape robots.  I don't know that I personally can call it a GOTY or GOAT stealth puzzler because of how many games I have played, but I can certainly understand why some others people might say that.

It's kinda like other puzzle games mechanics undo button, the only difference is that the plot recognizes you can do this. There is very few interactions with the enemy, and there are only one enemy type so you wont get any variation in enemy behavior either.If what you are looking for is a game with time manipulation mechanics and puzzles I would recommend Braid and The Sexy Brutale, the later of the 2 even have stealth mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Good stealthy puzzle game where your character has the superpower of planning. You try to reach the goal while avoiding obstacles, but you plan out your moves in advance. In other games if you mess up, the game calls you an idiot and tosses you back to the start of the level, but here you just go back in time and try out a different strategy, which is great.Story/music/art is decent - for gameplay, it builds on itself a lot. It'll introduce a simple puzzle that requires a new way of solving it, and then incorporate that method into future, more complicated levels - but again, you don't ever feel like you're losing progress because if you get caught, you can just go back in time and try a different strategy. You're never thrown back to the start of the level.One minor issue I had was about relics, which you get by completing levels under certain challenge conditions. I didn't figure out where to see all the relics and the challenge conditions, until I got them all by following a guide. They're not in the pause menu, they're in the chapter select screen I believe. Another thing is that when you're going back thru the levels to get relics after beating the game for the first time, it's slow to transition from one level to another because there's so many loading screens and wait times.Overall, I do heartily recommend the game for puzzle fans. It's gentle and it's difficult, and the reward for collecting all relics is neat. Also, if you play through the game and like the mechanics, there's DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: A stealth puzzle game in which you must guide a girl and her cat companion through a surreal dream world that resembles pieces of a building, floating in an endless void and populated by robotic guards. The game features no spoken dialogue and is deliberately vague on plot details, leaving it up to the player to figure out the story (but who needs story when there's a cat that sits on your head?).In each level, the girl and/or the cat must navigate through a series of rooms and corridors to the exit. The girl can operate keypads to open and close doors, as well as collect gems that let her repair holes in the floor; meanwhile, the cat can fit through tiny crawlspaces and meow loudly to lure robots away from their posts. Some robots simply follow a basic patrol pattern while others take more complicated routes, but should one of them spot you, it will chase after you until either it reaches you and attacks or it loses track of you. You'll have to keep on your toes to guide the characters safely through each level.This is done by visually planning out the characters' routes beforehand, then watching them do it for real once successful, similarly to . What sets this game apart, though, is the timeline bar that lets you freely rewind or fast forward through time. This lets you alter the characters' routes and actions at any point, making it easy to correct mistakes, experiment with different paths, or sync the characters' movements to solve the levels faster. Some levels feature a collectible that can be obtained by speedrunning the level or not using a certain ability, encouraging you to rewind and try different tactics. Other levels force you to get the characters to the exit within a strict time limit, either via a robot shutting the only door to the exit after a while, or because the entire level is slowly vanishing from existence. Plus, if you find the base game to be too easy, there's always the free Hell Loop DLC to give yourself a real challenge.Time is infinite, yet we only have a limited amount of it to spend. Our choices in the past will inevitably affect our options in the future.  has built a game around these concepts, and pulled it off brilliantly.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game about time manipulation, I wish I could fast forward through a lot of it. This is a game that steam makes me wish had a middle ground between yes and no on the recommendation.There's a few reasons that I ultimately decide to say no on this one. First, when you complete a level, the game insists that you watch your solution from start to finish. You can skip these replays individually, though there needs to be an option to disable them by default. There's is in fact a "story" here, though it's impossibly vague so don't expect too much. Finally, some levels have secret objectives and give you no indication whatsoever until after the level has been completed. This means you'll be playing through them a couple times if you're unprepared. I ended up using a guide to see what levels had objectives, and what their conditions were before attempting to solve them on my own. The gameplay was entertaining, but no so good that I want to repeat levels more than once.If you're a puzzle fan, you'll get some value out of this (especially the free, hell loop DLC). _childDocuments_.review: I think this is a perfectly fine game if you know what you're getting but can also lead to disappointment if you're expecting something different. Since Steam doesn't allow a mixed recommendation & the rating is high enough that a single negative recommendation wouldn't really affect it, this is submitted as negative.The game's description talks about time manipulation, but that's more window dressing than gameplay. Gameplay-wise, this is a sequenced move game, where the goal is to time your planned moves on the grid to the enemies' in order to metaphorically get keys, flip switches, and avoid getting caught.  Think any of the Go games — Hitman Go, Lara Croft Go, Deus Ex Go — and you'll get the idea.If you know this and you like these types of games, then it's a perfectly fine example of them. The additional twist of multiple characters that you have to control simultaneously adds a new challenge, though it is also occasionally annoying. If you're expecting a game with the time-manipulation to be more involved in the gameplay, you'll probably be disappointed.The closest I've come to actual time manipulation are the occasional objects that touching will reset the level back to the beginning, only with some of the metaphorical keys having already been used. ["Metaphorical keys": there are glowing white cubes that let you visually reverse time on parts of the map, restoring damage & allowing you to progress past a previously inaccessible route. Despite the graphical trappings, they're effectively just a variation on keys & locked doors.]At this point someone is going to bring up the rewind functionality that lets you move backwards in the move sequence — and you're going to use it a lot. Since any action automatically unpauses the game, you'll need to rewind a lot in order to get the two characters to act simultaneously. [e.g. Enter a move for character #1, which automatically unpauses time. Rewind back to when you entered the move, which also serves to pause time. Swap to character #2 & enter their move. Time again unpauses only both characters now move.] But rewind is 100% ordinary in these sort of sequenced move games. It's just normally not as noticeable.(Maybe there's something more further into the game. Don't know and it hasn't grabbed me enough to care at this point.)Graphics are ok. Something closer to the game's concept/store art would have been more pleasing.As others have said, this would have been a great mobile game, as these types of games fit well into a play style of picking it up, playing a level or two, and then putting it down.A good sequenced move game with some fresh ideas [having to move simultaneously more than one character] but the time manipulation feels more like theming than a gameplay element.

_childDocuments_.review: The time manipulation is really fun to play around with, and the game makes great use of this concept. A couple of them bring back a really interesting concept regarding time-loops, but these might be really difficult to solve on your own without knowing the trick. _childDocuments_.review: Timelie is an isometric puzzle game that consists of manipulation of time, surrounding objects, and enemies in order to escape the various chambers.The visuals and character design are simplistic in a good way. The puzzles are well thought out. I liked solving them. They become difficult as you progress further. There is an intro chapter, four main chapters, and the fifth chapter, which is quite small. Each chapter comprises various chambers or levels.A couple of puzzles may become frustrating as you have to be perfect by 1/10th of a second. I had to refer to an online guide to get through them.There are no voice-overs, no text. The story is told using simple cutscenes and some vague symbols. I didn’t get it that much, to be honest. The ending was a bit emotional. The music is quite excellent, and the sound design also serves its purpose.You are accompanied by a cat that helps you solve the puzzles. Cute touch.The movement is grid-based. I played with a gamepad without any problem. The gameplay felt smooth. There is only one enemy type: aggressive robots. You’ll play hide and seek with them throughout the game.There are secret relic challenges in 15 chambers. You have to complete some chambers a certain way to get these relics. No worries. There is a chapter select option. And you can select any chamber you wish to play again. You may need to refer to a guide (for some of the challenges). After getting all the relics, you will unlock a small secret cutscene after the end credits.The achievements are chapter completion and challenge-related. Make sure to watch the credits till the end after completing all the challenges. It may take around 8 to 9 hours if you are going for all the achievements.After finishing the main game, you may revisit the chapter select option and access the extra DLC levels called “Hell Loop." This DLC is free to add to the library. The DLC has 30 levels with no story. I’ve played 3-4 levels and didn’t bother going further. Because the difficulty is quite absurd with these levels. They require so much trial and error with so many variables. I didn’t like it. Totally time-wasting and rage-inducing. I’m glad that it was not required for 100% game completion. Otherwise, it would have ruined my experience.Overall, I have enjoyed my time, with some frustrating moments here and there. If you are into challenging puzzle games, you may get this on sale.My verdict: 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a game that I had pleasant time with. Usually I am not a fan of stealth games or strategy games because I find them either too anxiety inducing or boring, but that wasn't the case for this game. I found myself enjoying this game pretty early in and as I started becoming excited about what was in the next room instead of stressed over being caught. I’ve never enjoyed playing a stealth game before but this one won me over with it’s cute characters, nice gameplay, and beautiful visuals. I specifically loved the magic effects of this game, they were very pretty. It sounds kind of funny to say that a stealth strategy game is relaxing and a comfort game for me, but I think that’s why it’s great. It’s a very cute and comfy game with a cool futuristic aesthetic.I only have one or two critiques of the game. While I felt like the animation on the models of all the characters were very expressive and well done, that was not the case for facial expressions. The main character’s face didn’t have any emoting or blinking throughout the game. It was incredibly unnerving in a way that I don’t think was intentional (especially during the cut scenes). I would be very grateful if either the developers coded or a fan moded blinking and/or expression animations onto the main character. Also, the ending (including the secret one) felt a little anticlimactic and disappointing in comparison to the rest of the game to me. Overall, while it can be a little grindy for those who want the secret ending, it was a well designed game that was very pretty.

_childDocuments_.review: charming little iso stealth puzzle game!timelie (rhymes with lime pie)'s selling points are its polished, beautiful artstyle; simple-yet-moving story with everything shown, not told; and a gimmick of controlling two characters simultaneously, dragging a playhead around on a timeline (timelie?) to synchronise their movements.its greatest weakness is that it's an iso stealth puzzle game, the market for which is... slightly oversaturated; however, its twist on this concept keeps it interesting and fun.of course, not every game mechanic is introduced at once, and it starts off rather uninspiring in the first chapter, which might cause some players to abandon it; i was tempted. but past its weak beginning, it's excellent! most puzzles do a good job of introducing a new challenge that's satisfying to solve, with a few forgivable blips scattered onto an otherwise smooth difficulty curve. no one section or mechanic overstayed its welcome, and the puzzles feel nonlinear, with a few different solutions in the best ones, and some crazy interplay when your previous solutions are remembered in new levels.timelie isn't a must-play paragon of puzzle games, and it could've explored more thoroughly the mind-bending, accumulating puzzles in the final act. its mechanic isn't particularly new, as braid, thinking with time machine, and others have explored similar concepts. however, it confidently stands on its own beside those, and is certainly worth a shot if you're into that genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie deftly leverages time manipulation to create puzzles with precision. The ability to rewind and fast forward freely gives the player time to think and experiment, making it possible to tackle challenges without the frustration of losing progress. In fact, failure doesn't even feel like a factor at all, which is genuinely refreshing. I did get stuck at times, but I appreciated the simple gesture of not having it rubbed it in my face with "You Died" or punitive load screens.There's a small dose of bittersweet story to enjoy as well, but the intricacy and novelty of the puzzles are what set it apart. Don't miss this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle mechanics are original and well thought-out, but the controls are clumsy, and you often cannot zoom out enough to see the whole puzzle board. The puzzles aren't too hard, though; I could solve them all rather quickly, though I reached the ending with only 6 of the 15 relics. Others are more about timing each step one by one, which will challenge your patience more than your intellect.The graphics are beautiful and the soundtrack haunting, but the story is more puzzling than the game itself, even if you get to the "secret" ending, which requires that you collect all the relics. _childDocuments_.review: This game is  very aesthetically and mechanically pleasing.  Visually, pretty much everything in the game is clearly discernible, and the contrast between the dull colored environment and the bright colors of the characters and interact-able objects made a nice combination of  appealing visuals and aspects of the level that are vitally important, such as our protagonist, enemies, and mechanisms. The  timeline is an interesting mechanic, although sometimes it felt tedious to handle. Visually, pretty much everything in the game is clearly discernible, and the contrast between the dull colored environment and the bright colors of the characters and interact-able objects made a nice combination of appealing visuals and aspects of the level that are vitally important, such as our protagonist, enemies, and mechanisms. Mechanically the puzzles have a good difficultly curve, and throughout the game I felt challenged without feeling stuck, and the game does a good job of introducing mechanics before taking things to a higher level. The timeline is an interesting mechanic, although sometimes it felt tedious to handle. For example, there are times when I needed to move at a very specific time to avoid multiple sight lines that needed precise placement of the timeline. _childDocuments_.review: Imma be honest: The cat is adorable and probably composed like 50% of my enjoyment of this game. Hits me right in my weak spot, ooof.Focusing on the rest though:Cool game overall. The general idea is to sneak past robot sentries and proceed from one level to the next. You have the ability to control time -- using future knowledge to modify and fine-tune your past actions -- and you also have a cat companion who can fit through small vents and meow to distract nearby sentries temporarily.The difficulty is about average, though there is a bit of extra challenge in the side-achievements for completing certain levels under tougher constraints (speedrun, no meows, no kills, etc). The soundtrack is very fitting - it's atmospheric, immersive, and easy on the ears. No Last Eternity in particular is a fantastic theme song.At first, I was bummed that the base game was so short (38 levels). By the time the game starts to hit its stride, it's over. But there is a free DLC (Hell Loop) that offers 35 additional levels -- most of which are harder than the hardest level in the base game. So if you want more, the option is there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty good! You play as some girl who likes cats and can see the future, who is trying to escape some sort of facility by making bridges, being stealthy, and extracting the life from the robots that kill her when given the chance. Though lore wise there is not much to go off of, when it comes to the mechanics I can say I enjoyed it. Always liked these sorts of puzzle games, and this one puts some innovation into its work through the single-player cooperative style, and the ways in which the player can choose to solve the puzzles. That being said, it is not the most ground breaking. Visually, though the art is unique, there was not a lot of emphasis placed on making it look well polished, as the character animations can be off at times with clipping. Good games do not need good graphics, though. Wishing to have a casual puzzle game, this was the perfect go to for me. There were some levels that were far harder than others, but most were pretty easy to solve, and fun to do.  Still think this game shines through with its game-play, though. Not everything needs to have a whole universe attached to it to make it interesting. Each level was unique and fun, and some made you sit and think for a second as to how to solve. Would recommend, it was a very nice game for a one time play through, and something different from the usual indie-puzzle stuff I buy. If there is a second one, I will purchase.

The addition of the cat added some nice coordination requirements, and some of the levels have an evolution mechanic which has you use the same level but some some changes which was interesting. For me the story was a bit abstract and I wasn't sure what was going on leading me to care more about the cat than the main character. Overall I thought the game was challenging but not frustrating and there are level achievements if you are looking for more challenge. If you like puzzle games and gameplay is more important than story this is worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game that provides a nice challenge with some unique gameplay. But if you stick with it, it's a very rewarding game that feels good every time you finish a level, especially towards the end of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Very elegantly designed; despite having only a small handful of moves at your disposal the puzzles are varied and engaging. The game looks and sounds great too.The story was a bit opaque, which made it a bit hard to engage there. But it's not very intrusive, so it's fine to just kind of nod at it vaguely and carry on playing.There's a cool system to push you to try for harder solutions to puzzles, such as total stealth or beating a specific time limit. Unfortunately it's a little hard to tell which levels have which requirements, which I think adds a layer of obfuscation that doesn't benefit the game. If it were more clear how to hunt the relics I'd have been more inclined to go see how many I could get, since the ones I did find were fun to try for.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable puzzle game. Being able to rewind time and choose very precise actions for your character is great. Once you have found a solution to a level, the game shows you your decisions in real time, and it is very satisfying to see it all come together. Nice music, great level design, highly recommended game.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: In the wide world of puzzle video games, Timelie stands out as being truly one of the greats. The mechanics are a wonderful mix of discrete locations with a continuous temporal mechanic that makes puzzles feel both deliberate and cheesy, in the best possible way. Tie all of this in with an end-game twist reminiscent of The Pedestrian, and we've been given a true hidden gem in the puzzle game genre.Timelie is not, however, without its shortcomings. The cutscenes are frequent, slow, usually uninteresting, and annoying, though easily skippable. Gameplay can feel slow as well, particularly before I got better with the controls. These problems overall were particularly pronounced in the beginning of the game, but got significantly better over time as puzzles got harder.Despite these shortcomings, by the time I completed Timelie, I couldn't help but be in awe of the game we were given, and I believe it is absolutely worth full price despite only taking me ~5 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This review concerns the base game and does not include the "Hell Loop - DLC Puzzle Pack"."Timelie" can be summarized as "short, but sweet". This puzzle game consists of you navigating one-to-two characters towards the end of each level, while avoiding getting caught by enemy sentries roaming in each level. The key mechanic is the ability to control time, letting you undo actions that lead to failure and observe enemy sentry movement patterns as time progresses. There is just enough challenge in each level to prevent you from blasting through them with ease yet not too hair-pulling difficulty in most levels. Extra challenge lies in "relics" that are awarded in some levels after completing certain actions. These relics add an additional layer of difficulty and feel great when you find the right combination of actions to get them. Performance-wise, the game performs well on both Mac and PC. The soundtrack provides effective atmospheric tunes that enhance the overall experience. The art style is simple yet effective. Character models and animations look great. This game will satisfy a lot of people from different preferences for games.Not all games are perfect, and there are some issues with "Timelie". There are some levels that are mentally taxing and do require you to explore a multitude of options to find a correct solution. These usually amount to trial and error, repeating actions with minuscule changes until you find an optimal pattern. It's not often, but there are such moments. Some quality of life improvements are missing, such as the ability to chapter select from within the menu and some cut scenes not being skippable. The lack of indicators in the chapter select to see if a level already has its relic obtained is a confusing UX issue, but this will only apply to achievement hunters. A bar at the bottom of the screen akin to a YouTube progress bar lets you skip chunks of time, but sometimes the bar will think you clicked on it when you actually clicked on the environment, skipping time in large chunks with no way back to your original timestamp. Furthermore, with the addition of two controllable characters, sometimes it is not obvious which character you are controlling. While there is a story in this game, it's mostly up to interpretation - take that however you will.Despite some negative points here and there, this is a great package all around. A comfortable distraction at worst, and a fun brain-scratcher at best.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as puzzle games go Timelie is one of the better ones. It has a neat atmosphere, very interesting mechanics for puzzles, and some impressive music.The gameplay is simple: press buttons and stand on pressure plates to open doors, avoid enemies, use some limited abilities to influence the way you play, and move back and forth time to try and retry approaches in an attempt to reach the exit of each level. The usage of time as a mechanic is done extremely well, it forced me to think ahead, observe patterns, and plan in a way I had not done before. And when I figured out that some of the puzzles utilized previous mission’s results to influence your current mission I found that absolutely fascinating. The game really got interesting when it gave you not only the main character to control but a cat as well, meaning you had to get both to the end using different paths and utilizing their unique abilities to solve puzzles. It all works really well and I found the game to be a little challenging at times, especially if you are going for the secret ending, but overall I found that I really enjoyed how the game played. Of note, I attempted to play the second harder run of the game and found that ♥♥♥♥ to be absolutely grating, if you are really into this game I think that it is cool that they offer a massive challenge but it was not for me. But yeah, it was really fun, it was a very unique approach to puzzles and I can’t think of many games that top it. As for the story, it is minimalistic; no text, no voice acting, just visuals. It was not really clear what is happening, but the emotions built are pretty solid. I am a real sucker for cats and building a bond with the stray cat in the game was cute to see. If you came for a story I think you will likely be disappointed, but personally, I thought it was an interesting experience to try and interpret.The sound design for this game is pretty good in my opinion. The in-game sound effects are limited, but what they have is good. As for the music I found it to be pretty good overall, a lot of it is ambient, but I thought it was all well composed. Best of all though was the song at the end credits, I thought it was phenomenal and went ahead and picked it up. If you are not interested in the game I at least suggest that you look it up, No Last Eternity by Pongsathorn Posayanonth and Aun Jessada (it has both an English and a Thai version, both are good though I prefer the English because I like the lyrics as well). Overall I never felt like running my own music which is always a great sign, so I was very happy with the soundtrack.Graphically this game is very simple, it reminds me of Pokémon games in the way that it is styled (specifically the main character). What had the most effort put into it though was the environments, and overall I think that they are done wonderfully. I do feel that the game was not as colorful as it could have been so it generally feels pretty muted, but I did find that it made some of the neon colors really pop, so perhaps it was for the best. The atmosphere the game has though is really good, it is always hard to describe a visual feel but this one feels really good, it is just dark enough, it has a unique sci-fi feel, and it feels strong emotionally. Overall it is not a masterpiece, but it is visually appealing nonetheless.I liked Timelie a lot, I think it is easily one of the best and most unique puzzle games I have ever played. It was a bit challenging and I did have to get some help on getting the bonuses to get the secret ending, but I think this game is well-balanced in its base game difficulty. I did not have any really big complaints, I think this is a wonderful game and was really happy to have played it. So if you are a fan of puzzle games I think that this is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: A polished puzzle game in the guise of a stealth game.  Plot your path through the level...but don't worry if you get caught, because you can just rewind time to where you made your mistake and replot your path from that point without having to redo the entire level.It reminds me a bit of when Dr. Strange did the whole 14 million futures thing.  You get to pick the one that works!There are hints of a storyline here and there.  Where is this mystery place?  Is it physical or metaphorical?  What do those runes mean?  Whats the deal with that cat?  And wait...I just collected the 15 relics by completing special objectives during the missions...but what does that ending MEAN?All in all, it gave me about 8 hours of playing total.  It is worth noting that if you get into the game the dev also made some free DLC with difficult levels that you may enjoy too!All in all, I enjoyed it.  Difficult enough to be a challenge and engrossing, but the time rewind feature keeps it casual.  Definitely worth a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic little puzzle game. Though short, this is now in my "Top 10 Puzzlers" of all-time, next to "The Sexy Brutale" and heavy-weight "The Talos Principle", to give an idea of how much I enjoyed it.Solving a puzzle here feels like cheating on a Stealth-Action game; the main mechanics is that you can rewind or forward time at will, so you can time narrow escapes perfectly. Once you solve a level, you can then watch the action unfold in real time, and it looks really cool, with all those impressive moves you carefully built. This might sound repetitive (there is a lot of trial and error for your timings if you want to solve a level in a time-efficient way), but the well thought-out interface makes it very easy to advance or rewind a few frames at a time until you get it just right.Also, the puzzles had a perfect difficulty level for me -- they had me thinking hard at times, and every so often I needed a new idea, but I never had to look up solutions of anything. The story is only hinted at, but has a few well done dramatic moments.Finally, I thought the last few puzzles to be brilliant -- they caught me off-guard, but adapting to the new challenges made up for great playing moments, the kind you want to tell other people about.Score: 88/100.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: GoodClear Time: 5~ Hours100% Time: 5~ HoursSummary: An absolutely fine and interesting puzzle game. While I personally wasn't a fan of it's mechanics nor interested in the weak story there is no denying that this is a perfectly fine brain teaser of a game that will keep you engaged through it's entire length. It's also great for low IQ brainlets like me, where the final few levels are complicated enough they make you feel good enough to get that rush of dopamine that helps you stop feeling sorry for yourself for 15 seconds.Very similar to Lara Croft GO and Hitman GO. A top down isometric puzzle game where you start at point A, have to hit buttons and avoid patrols to reach point B. What's unique about this game is it's "timeline" feature which is basically a glorified restart/skip feature. A timeline appear on the bottom of the screen each level and as you go through the level it advances. If at any point you make a mistake, instead of having to restart the level you can just rewind the timeline to a point before you made the mistake rather than having to wait for a loading screen and retry. You can also advance time: click where you want to go and instead of waiting for your character to move you can just advance the timeline until they're there.From Chapter 2+ you also have to control a cat, you can distract in a radius but otherwise controls the same as the main character.The timeline feature is astoundingly fantastic. It totally eliminates the need for loading screens and it really shows the developer values your time. Did you make it to the end of the level only to realise you can't complete it because of a button you hit at the start? Just rewind to the start (which takes about a second, if that) and try again. Even if the puzzles aren't fantastic (which overall they're generally pretty good anyway) the timeline feature makes doing each puzzle totally hassle free. You'll never ever feel like you're wasting time because you can skip to any point in the puzzle. There is never a need to wait, reload or die. It's utterly fantastic and one of the best features in a puzzle game, or game in general.There are quite a few things I didn't like, but none of them compare to how much I liked the timeline feature which is why I give this a thumbs up. First, the story is almost nonexistant, yet the game does focus way too much time on unskippable cutscenes which don't really serve any purpose. The ending goes for like 10 minutes and you have to sit through entirely arbitrary story. Second, controlling two character basically the entire game was frustrating: there is never a clear indication of which character you have selected at any given time and I spent a good 40% of each level rewinding because I moved the wrong character. The puzzle mechanics themselves i'm not a particularly big fan of (not that they're bad!! It's totally subjective) but they're done well enough in this game.Last, some levels have "relics", which you get by beating a certain challenge on levels that have them. You don't know if a level has a relic until you beat it: if the relic is dim you need to rewind the level until it's light > see what you did that turned it off > don't do that. The challenges themselves aren't hard to do but some later levels have relics that require you to do specific things in EARLIER levels that don't have relics. Like, you need to have the cat stand in a certain position in level 3-? so that in 5-? you can meet the relic requirement. These relics are rare but they really suck. Having to go back and do previous levels to meet the requirement (which it never tells you what they are) is pretty poor design.Make the currently selected character way more prominent and obvious. Get rid of the relics that require multiple levels, or at least tell the player that a certain level has consequences for a later level. Let me skip cutscenes please.It's ironic that for a game that really loves making you use time efficiently, it absurdly wastes your time in anything that isn't gameplay related. I also really didn't like controlling two separate character to solve puzzles, I mean I can barely control myself in real life. I also can't believe that that it took a developer this long to have such an amazing feature in the timeline. It's really just such a simple idea...Super easy. Get all the relics (there is level select at any point in the game) and then beat the game, you'll get your 100%!!

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie. It's a time-looping puzzle game where you need to progress through a series of levels by sneaking past enemies as a girl or a cat (or both!), all while controlling time like a media player. Did you catch that? If you mess up, you can immediately rewind and try something new. It makes the gameplay very fluid even during difficult puzzles. It's one of the better sets of controls I've seen for a puzzle game.My only complaint is that the game is a bit short; I would have loved to play a few more of the end-game levels where you traverse backwards through the levels you just completed, dodging all the obstacles from the first round in addition to your past self. Cause we wouldn't want to mess up the timeline now, would we?Seriously, try this game out. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a somewhat short puzzler involving time manipulation that does a pretty good job at combining different things you learn and using them more as levels go on. The levels are relatively interesting and the only real gripes I had were the vagueness of the story and needing some direction of which previous levels affected the ones in the finale. Besides that, it was definitely worth the playthrough and the steins;gate reference did not go unnoticed.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Very well-crafted puzzles in a wonderful futuristic gameplay environment. Use your time wisely to manipulate events to meet your needs in the timeline. Though the ending is very strange, that's probably the only downside. Be warned that the story might elicit some tears in the end. Also, completing all the achievements (called relics) is a nice bonus challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle part is very solid and quite enjoyable. Also, the graphics are highly polished, which made me buy the game because I anticipated a good overall game. However, I struggled with several issues that made the game much less enjoyable, which is a real shame:- The controls feels extremely sluggish, as if you are walking through knee-deep mud. I did play with gamepad, though.- The intro and outro scenes of each level can't be nicely skipped (you have to hold a button, but not too early!) and do not really add much to the experience, even more contributing to the first issue.- The game led me to believe that there would be some kind of story arc to be resolved, but in the end, there was nothing but unconnected pieces. Even other players seem hardly be able to make any sense of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Very innovative, no consequences for failure (you just rewind), and excellent puzzles. Story is not really the focus (one could probably piece together the base concepts of what's going on, but it's really not about that). Music is great, relaxing and moving. There's extra challenges you can go for, which is very neat! The art style is charming and informative. The controls are all they need to be, in my experience.Overall, you will probably not play this for a deep story, but if you want a very good puzzle game with some new takes on things, I can wholeheartedly recommend you pick this up.P.S: There is also now a free DLC of harder levels, which is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a stealth puzzle point and click game where the puzzles are engaging although at points infuriating when you can't quite get the timings right for what you want to do but that is part of the fun. _childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic concept with a great execution, the levels are fun with a solid challenge. The game looks beautiful, the music is lovely, and it does not overstay its welcome in the slightest. The way the game interacts with its own main mechanics and story is also fantastically done. The only complaint I really have is that I wish you could speed up the 'real' portion of the levels, rather than just skipping it, but that's a minor complaint at best. Strongly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Quite the interesting direction they went with the time manipulation puzzle concept with great execution. With every puzzle you have a time bar at the bottom that acts as your reset and undo which allows you to move the playhead to any point to see how things occur or will occur in the allotted time.The character goes where you click and as she moves the playhead slowly moves to the right. Once they reach the destination the game will pause automatically so you never have to worry about losing crucial time. The game gives you the feeling of having to time things perfectly and in some puzzles it comes close, however, with the freedom you have to manipulate time it removes that unneeded pressure.Later on you will be accompanied by a cat that you will also have to guide through the puzzles with the girl. You are free to interchange between the two and help them help each other reach the exits. This part is where it really shines. They share the same time bar but yet have their own as well. For instance you can make a path for the girl and once you see everything will work up to that point you can rewind that used time back to a specific point you need to then guide the cat across that same time so you can be as efficient as possible.She has a power that allows her to repair broken bridges  with the cat's ability is to meow to catch the attention of the robots to steer them away from a blocked path or door.The puzzles themselves are challenging enough to make you not overthink while at the same time it's not a cakewalk either. Even the challenges that do add an extra level of difficulty aren't hair pulling hard either (this is left for the free DLC which is optional, even warns you about this and how it's not needed to completed the main story).Puzzle genre is one of my favorites and one thing they did which I have never seen done before that I can remember but absolutely love is that  Again even doing this they were still able to keep the challenge without it being overly difficult or too easy.I would love a sequel or at least another puzzle game with this same concept, it has been a long while that I came across a puzzle game where I felt satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a puzzle game where you play as a little girl and her cat as she navigates time puzzles in her dream. The objective of every puzzle is to reach the exit while ensuring the cat and the girl do not get caught by any robot.Gameplay-wise, mouse and keyboard. A to reverse time and D to fast-forward time. Mouse to click on the points you wish to move to. What's interesting is that each character moves individually on their on layer, you can control each characters movement to move individually at their own time, while simultaneously moving them all at once. Think of it as a video editing software where you set the sound, speech, subtitles and other effects to occur at different timings of the video. Conclusion, do try Timelie. The puzzles are reminescent of Lara Craft: GO.1. Interesting PuzzlesThe ones where you have to deal with yourself are somewhat interesting. Not in the actual puzzle but in the concept of preventing a time paradox.1. ShortIt's over in 5 hours.2. LoreThere really isn't any lore to "glue" the player to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A young girl embraces her inner cat lady and gains the power to control space and time.  The main game takes 3-5 hs to complete and a bit more if you want to unlock the "secret" ending but mostly due to how obscure certain achievements are. I haven't gone through the DLC yet but that supposedly ads 10h more so the price is rather fair.. Storywise the game is rather open to interpretation, with some hints here and there to set the tone. Graphically it is minimalist almost to a fault. It manages to be easy on the eye which is a pro for a puzzle game. The puzzles, which is the important part, range between quite easy to normal with a couple of them pushing you a bit more. Overall a good choice if you like puzzles and are fine with shorter games.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a friend gift this to me and was unsure what to expect. _childDocuments_.review: Soft Recommendation for this one. Enjoyable, compact game about moving a girl (and then cat!!) to avoid getting bonked by robots or vaporized into nothingness.All your movement is based on a timeli(n)e which essentially boils down the gameplay to how efficiently you maneuver your characters on a frame by frame basis. That may sound tedious to some but there's a certain level of satisfaction in weaving around multiple, densely packed cones of sight.The game starts out fairly basic. You move the girl, she has some time powers, that's it. Then they introduce a second character, the cat, which can distract robots by meowing loud. Then they tighten up the puzzles so you really have to time each action down to the wire. And then finally, they further utilize the fact that this is a game about time, which I won't elaborate on since it might spoil first playthroughs but seriously, it should be obvious about what you'll pull in a time game. Definitely attempt all the 'secret' challenges for certain levels, gives the game a nice bite of... challenge (also lets you 100% the game as well).Personally thought the game could have ramped up the difficulty earlier, and they should have expanded further on the late-game stuff. But hey, engaging 5+ hour TAS-lite simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Love the concept, visual vibes, and soundtrack.It was worth a short ride, and it's even more fun when I play with my friends as we tried to solve the puzzle together (but jus to be clear, this is a single-player game).First, the concept of "time control" power might have been used in some other games, Life is Strange being one of the famous title, but I personally love the way it is implemented into "media player"-like scroller. The movement are based on point/grid system, which I only found out later  it has to be that way instead of a "ASWD free movement".At the end of each stage, after "simulating" the movement and help the girl reaches the finish line, we have the option to review our gameplay in a perfect manner (although behind the scene it might took hours to solve it lol). I think this part is particularly interesting since it gives off the vibe that we're actually watching pseudo-cutscene instead of our own point-and-click gameplay.The puzzle is entertaining and I must warn you it relies on mili-to-nanoseconds timing for some higher levels. There is a lot of "trial-and-error" needed as you try lots of combination, and even split-second matters here. They say there is always be only 1 solution for each phase, although I haven't tried to find any other ways, I can see some truth in those words. The stages in each chapter has 1 "core gameplay"; in chapter 2 it's impossible to solve all puzzles without the help of the cat and ventilation, in chapter 3 it's all about timing and reading enemy's pattern, and in chapter 4 it's about . The earlier stages serves as an introduction some sort, and by understanding the core I mentioned before, we can solve the later stages.And the thing I love most is the "Easter Egg" of this game, which relates to its level design. That is simply mindblowing and conceptual!The game has 4 chapter + 1 final chapter, with an average of 10+ stages per chapter. I'm aware that puzzle-solving game has low repetitive value, so you might want to enjoy all your progress to the fullest while you're at it. I bought this at 50% discounted price, so IMO it's still worth it for a unique gameplay, level design, and good graphic and music that the developer put their efforts into.There isn't any "Story Rich" tag in this game, and I think we'll just have to accept the game as it is. Warning first if you're looking for a good story: . It did indeed confuse me first because there aren't hints to at least tell us if this game might be an analogy of something, all the way to the ending I'm still only interpreting the story pretty straightforwardly from what's happening right in front of my eyes. In the ending we finally got like, 5 seconds to get a gist of the story, but the rest is up for player's interpretation. And then, the  came, and within that 10 seconds, we are given a clearer hint to finally understand and wraps the story completely (putting aside of the open interpretation for the why and the how).Without the Secret Ending, I'm probably only feel like 80% satisfied, but watching the Secret Ending made up for the rest of 20%. That's how I'd describe it.Memorable original ending song, great puzzle and level design, fresh mechanism, and top-notch visuals (although not something new). Do not expect anything story-rich except for the open ending + secret ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a time-manipulated strategy puzzle game and I wanted to try this because it looked interesting. I thought it was going to be a mind-blowing experience from a gameplay standpoint. To be frank, I was indeed a little disappointed by the first few stages as they were too easy. I mean, how difficult could it be if we were able to undo a mistake instantly and redo it differently right? Despite that, I continued playing as I did not want to waste the bucks spent (it was on sale). The more I progressed, the more I felt cheated. Why? For thinking, even for a second, that this game was easy. Timelie is a hardcore brain-twister that will challenge you to think out of the box and into the fire, or be tempted to look at gameplay walkthroughs for hints on how to beat it, or both. After the first few stages, it becomes apparent (if not already) that a lot of passion and effort has been put into the game. From the model designs to the visual style of the game. There is a vision from the creators and it feels so fully realized here. There is a hint of a story from the puzzles as the creators have kept things ambiguous, but really, you are not playing this for the story, or even for the main storyline. You are playing this for the Hell Loop DLC! Yes. That free DLC which, in my opinion, should have been the main gameplay and the storyline mode be a bonus DLC instead. Here's why. I spent about 7-8 hours to finish the main storyline, according to Steam. As of this writing, I have also completed the DLC and that duration has reached 23 hours. 15-16 hours is the difference. Twice the time I spent on the main storyline. If you thought the main storyline was hard (yes it gets pretty hard), the DLC will make you question the existence of life itself. Then, you will only have a gesture of a word: Tenet.Because this is a thoroughly excellent game, I am a little bugged by some of its flaws. Let's talk about that.1) There is an unskippable animation for almost everything, and it adds up to quite a bit of accumulated waste of time. Things like doors opening, the camera zooming in to something and then zooming back out, etc. It is extremely cumbersome since some stages might require you to visit the main menu frequently, and you only get to the menu after a few animations. There are even animations for when you select a chapter in the menu. All unnecessary. The design is great and all, and maybe it adds "immersion" for some, but really, all I want for Christmas is to solve some puzzles. Let's get on with it.2) Because of the issue mentioned above, there are also long, unskippable "running along a long pathway" segments during the game that only shows the character progressing to the lobby after every chapter, and literally nothing else. I'm not sure what symbolic elements are present here, but we should not have to sit through this every time we complete a chapter because it is way too long and boring. Fortunately, all these animations can be skipped if you have seen them once. The menu animations can't be skipped though.3) Many stages require you to switch between a girl and a cat character. Every time you do this, the camera will center on the character you switch to. Personally, I wish there was an option to disable this camera movement and allow free cam instead. I always zoom out to the fullest because I like to see the whole map while strategizing, like looking at a chess board while planning for moves. However, the camera moves every time I switch characters, shifting part of the map out of frame and I have to reset it every time. It can get frustrating at times, but this is quite minor. I doubt it would affect many as much as it did me. 4) There is not much of a story in the main storyline. As mentioned earlier, the creators have chosen to keep things ambiguous. However, there is no identifiable plot either, save for some "plot twists" that just happens. I believe it is supposed to be some sort of a sad story at the end, but there was nothing that happened during the gameplay for me to care one way or another, except for the slight attachment I got from spending hours playing those characters. 5) No Steam achievements for the Hell Loop DLC. Like, seriously, why? I feel more accomplished playing the DLC than the main gameplay, but there are no achievements to prove that I was there. I think this is a tragic missed opportunity for a game this well thought out. Timelie is a truly well-designed game, able to surprise you and then demolish your hopes later on. The concept is simple, but not easy to play. When you do get to the end (especially if completely on your own without looking up for hints), there will be a sense of satisfaction that is hard to deny. Highly recommended for anybody who is looking for a challenge, and the DLC is not only worth the price of admission alone but essential playing as well. If the creators at Urnique Studio do develop a sequel to this, I would gladly torture my brain all over again.Note: I have read some comments that commented on some stages "cracking" or some bugs. I personally have not experienced any such glitches. The entire game worked smoothly for me. No issues whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic stealth puzzle game with time manipulation. Very fun challenge and satisfying gameplay when you solve very tough puzzles!The story....umm...so yeah the story is very vague. You get hints of it, but there is no dialogue or subtitles throughout the entire game. You're just a girl who awakens in some weird abstract world that has robot sentries. She gets the ability to manipulate time and preform precognition (like Katana Zero!). She befriends a cat along her journey through this world and they work together to escape.The controls are simple. You move in a grid and control time like on a media player. You use this to see the robot patrol routes and how to get past them. The girl runs very slow, so if a robot sees you, you aren't outrunning them. So you have to get a good lead on them if you wanna trick them. As the game progresses you'll obtain a special ability on some levels. If the girl picks up a power-up, she can repair certain broken parts of the world that were not traversable.  She can activate keypads to open doors as well. You will also control the cat on levels as well. They can move a little faster than the girl, but still not faster than robots. They can, however, go through vents and small spaces. They can also meow which will distract the sentries and force them to investigate the noise. It is super satisfying to see your plan work out perfectly when solving the puzzles. You can switch between both the girl and cat while moving the timeline and play out their actions. Click on them to make them stand in place and go forward and backwards until you find the solution!I don't have many gripes with this game. The controls may be a lil confusing at first, but since you control time...you have all the time in the world to get used to it (sorry couldn't resist). The lack of story may shut some gamers off, but I think the gameplay makes up for it. Lastly, sometimes it's unclear how far enemies can see you. Sometimes you'll think you're out of their sight, but they catch you, and vice versa. Not a serious issue but something I wanted to point out.Final verdict? If you love puzzle games that will test your brain muscles, this game is perfect. I finished in about 6-8 hours, but if you're really good, you can probably beat it in 4. If you found the game too short and easy, there is a DLC campaign with harder puzzles to solve. I personally recommend not looking up guides when playing this, it is a lot more satisfying to figure out the answer yourself (I only looked up one because I was pressed for time one session). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was completely different from any puzzle game i've played before.The gameplay was fluid, the graphics smooth and also mysterious in a sense. Puzzles were super unique and can be very tricky (I got stuck at 1-2 puzzles for around 20+ mins). Gameplay was relatively short at around 5 hours for me but can vary depending on how long you take to solve puzzles.Most importantly, this puzzle game surprisingly had a deep storyline. The ending to me was very surprising but at the same time got me thinking a lot about the actual story of what happened. It reminded me of games like Limbo or Little Nightmares where you have little to no information about the story, where you need to find out the story. _childDocuments_.review: One of those short indie games that provides an unforgettable experience. Timelie starts out simple, and gradually introduces a myriad of time manipulation and stealth related puzzle mechanics. As these mechanics combined in ways that required me to start thinking more creatively to solve each level, Timelie turned into one of my all time favourite puzzle games.The soundtrack is wonderfully crafted too. Just like the puzzle mechanics, it starts out simple, soothing and contemplative but evolves as you progress through the game. One gameplay mechanic in particular  has its own theme that is delightfully suspenseful.

_childDocuments_.review: I was incredibly surprised by how much i was moved by this game. The soundtrack is beautiful and is worth it to hear the music alone. There's no dialogue in this game, everything is communicated through the movement of the characters and the occasional laugh/meow/grunt. As a puzzle game, the mechanics are well thought out and it always feels like they try to improve on what is built on. Now I see some people say that the game is like a tablet puzzle game, and in some ways that's true but I feel the way its said discredits the game. In no way does this game feel like its rushed, cash grabby, or feel like very little thought is put into it. Its very obvious that the devs put their love and soul into this game.The story is a little vague but if you put on your thinking cap for 2 seconds, you'll get the gist of it. Despite me being able to beat this in 5 hours I felt pretty connected to the characters. I had some laughs  Overall I'd say this worthy of your time and money, and I can't to see what's next from the devs.

However, in this case, I'm all for a game that is more quality over quantity.The game's difficulty is on the lower end of the puzzle game scale.  However, the game does VERY clever things with time travel that I've not seen before, even in something like Braid.I feel that if the game had a score system, or more challenge relics, it might have allowed for a little more replay, which despite my norm, I think I would have invested in.The short answer? _childDocuments_.review: A small-child-scary-world puzzle game. I's very short. I'm no superb puzzler but I beat the game in 4 hours. That said, I don't have high hopes a sequel will ever come out. _childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent.  It is a rock-solid puzzle game. It's well-designed, well-polished, and a great way to kill about 8-10 hours.At its core, Timelie is a rather simple multi-stage puzzle game. Each stage is a small area where you must navigate from point A to point B, while avoiding being captured by robots - which mostly involves avoiding detection (though not always.)  To aid you in this task, you, the player, are given the -like power to fast-forward time (to observe enemy patrol patterns, for example, or to simply wait for the right moment) and rewind time (to undo a mistake.)  You can rewind all the way to the start of the stage. (In theory, there's a time limit, but I've never even come close to hitting it.) Later stages introduce a cat who can distract the robots by meowing, and later still you gain the means to destroy some of the robots.At the end of each stage you are treated to a nice cinematic (no UI elements except the mouse cursor) showing your character(s) making their way through the stage using your final solution.  One of my favorite things to do is time things exactly right so I was  out of sight at all times, à la .Where Timelie stands out, however, is the interdependency of these stages.  There are a number of stages, for example, which take place in the same area but at different times.  The specific path and sequence of actions you choose during earlier stages -- destroy this robot or evade, repair that bridge or go around -- will affect the state of the area for later stages, which can make those stages easier or more difficult.Of the 25 or so gameplay stages, 15 of them have a "relic" (achievement) that you can obtain by completing the level with a secret restriction, such as not using the cat's meow to distract any robots, or completing the stage without destroying any robots.  While playing these stages, you can see the artifact (it looks like a purple bug zapper) at the exit; failing the relic's requirement will cause the artifact to turn grey, giving a clue as to the requirement.You can replay any past stage at any time -- and unless you're  lucky, you'll need to do this for a few stages in order to get all of the relics (and thus 100% completion.)

name: Fallout 76
detailed_description: Fallout 76: Skyline Valley Expand southward to Skyline Valley – a brand-new region of Appalachia. Investigate the cause of the electric storm circling overhead and unveil the mystery around Vault 63 and its dwellers, including a shocking new Ghoul type – The Lost. Explore a brand-new region in Appalachia – Skyline Valley adds the rolling hills of Shenandoah to the southwest area of the map. Uncover a new Storyline – Discover the location of Vault 63 and meet its cabal of Ghoul dwellers. Act as the enigmatic overseer’s gun for hire as you uncover mysteries that could change -- or break -- the Wasteland Encounter a new enemy type – Meet a new type of supercharged Ghoul with electrifying weapons and armor and expose their origin. Chase storms in a new Public Event – Dangerous Pastimes brings together thrill-seekers to gather electrical energy from the skies but beware The Lost and other electrified creatures attracted by the storm. Summon a new Region Boss – Help to defend Skyline Valley from the very things created to keep it safe, a trio of robot titans: the Storm Goliaths. Digital Deluxe Edition The Skyline Valley Deluxe Edition includes access to the Fallout 76 base game, as well as the Lost Treasures bundle. Featured DLC The Lost Treasures Bundle includes the following bonus in-game C.A.M.P. items and cosmetics: Weather Control Station (Skyline Valley): Give your C.A.M.P an electrical red glow! V63 Power Armor & Jetpack Paint: Become a Vault 63 champion with this shiny new Power Armor and Jetpack skin. Vault 63 Door Display: Bring a piece of Vault 63 to your C.A.M.P. Moe the Mole Plushie: Moe the Mole really digs safety. V63 Chassis Display Frame: Showcase your Power Armor in Vault 63 style! Lightning Rod Pose: Harness the power of lightning with this pose. Fallout 76 base game required, sold separately. About the Game Bethesda Game Studios, the award-winning creators of Skyrim and Fallout 4, welcome you to Fallout 76. Twenty-five years after the bombs fell, you and your fellow Vault Dwellers—chosen from the nation’s best and brightest – emerge into post-nuclear America on Reclamation Day, 2102. Play solo or join together as you explore, quest, build, and triumph against the wasteland’s greatest threats. Explore a vast wasteland, devastated by nuclear war, in this open-world multiplayer addition to the Fallout story. Experience the largest, most dynamic world ever created in the legendary Fallout universe. Immersive Questlines and Engaging Characters Uncover the secrets of West Virginia by playing through an immersive main quest, starting from the moment you leave Vault 76. Befriend or betray new neighbors who have come to rebuild, and experience Appalachia through the eyes of its residents. Seasons Progress through each season and unlock free rewards like consumables, C.A.M.P. items and more by completing limited-time challenges. Multiplayer Roleplaying Create your character with the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system and forge your own path and reputation in a new and untamed wasteland with hundreds of locations. Whether you journey alone or with friends, a new and unique Fallout adventure awaits. Mountain Splendorland The story lives and breathes through the world of Fallout 76, which brings to life six distinct West Virginia regions. From the forests of Appalachia to the noxious crimson expanses of the Cranberry Bog, each area offers its own risks and rewards. A New American Dream Use the all-new Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform (C.A.M.P.) to build and craft anywhere in the world. Your C.A.M.P. will provide much-needed shelter, supplies, and safety. You can even set up shop to trade goods with other survivors. Fallout Worlds Play unique adventures in Appalachia with Fallout Worlds, which is an evolving set of features that give players the capability to play Fallout 76 in unique ways with customizable settings.

_childDocuments_.review: After 2 years of a rough start, Bethesda finally redeems itself by making Fallout 76 a better game than left it for dead. Been playing with my friend for 5 hours and so far it's enjoyable, tons of interesting quests, and loots for your character to equip, it's a solid Fallout game now.Pros:-1. Beautiful vast open world. Todd Howard is not even joking 16 times the detail? Hell yeah it is! Also 4 times much bigger than Fallout 4's map2. Beautiful graphics. I would say 4 times better than Fallout 4, the lighting, textures, and particles are just outstanding.3. Interesting quests. Rather than boring kill 10 of this thing, collect 30 of this thing, the quests actually have stories behind them.4. Beautiful retro-futuristic design. The game takes place years before any Fallout games so most of the pre-war era buildings and properties are still intact.5. Smoother combat mechanics. Personally, it felt much better than Fallout 4's combat.6. Pre-Fallout 4 styled dialogue choices. (I am yet to discover more of this so I will update it soon enough)7. Events. There are events around the world that you can participate in to make things more interesting.8. Weapons and armor mods. I am a sucker for upgrades so I want this to be in the review because I love it so much9. The cosmetic skins. Cool looking skins that you can obtain by playing the game and also a free battle pass!Meh:-1. The VATS system. It's just aimbot with RNG, it's meh to me.2. Server. Can you place two Asian players on an Asian server please? Delays are immersion-breaking.Cons:-1. Bugs. some of the bugs from the game launch are still here, and hopefully they'll fix them as soon as possible2. Optimization. The game does not run that smoothly, sometimes my FPS will drop from 50-40FPS. (Maybe it's my PC? I have a mid-range PC and above the recommended specifications of the game in case you are wondering)3. Some downgrades from Fallout 4 and other Fallout games. For example you can't sell junks and it's pretty hard to obtain caps in this game? (I will update this)i give Fallout 76 a 7 Nuka Cola Quantum
