_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game off and on since the Beta. Let me tell you, those first few months were . But underneath all that, I could tell there was a fun game.Here we are, years later, and  has matured. Though I personally loved the nearly-empty wasteland at launch, the Wastelanders update added human NPCs back to the game, and people flocked in. The game is full of players who really love Fallout, and you'll always find someone willing to help you out. There's tons of stuff to do, lots of lore to learn, and plenty of weird physics typical of Bethesda games.Downside is that it can feel like a grind to keep up with the SCORE board, and you're constantly being reminded of the microtransactions, But that's how they keep the servers paid, so I can't complain too much. You can earn enough of the currency to buy things once in a while just from regular play, and there's no "pay to win" here. The only real advantage is extra storage space for people who subscribe to Fallout 1st. That's pretty much it, everything else is purely cosmetic.If you've played previous Fallout games, it's absolutely worth grabbing  and taking it for a spin.

_childDocuments_.review: Continuing the tradition of getting slightly worse with every release [for both fallout and elder scrolls], 76 is the most watered down Bethesda game yet. The ability score system is once again neutered a little farther from what it was in Fallout 4, a weird perk system based off of cards has taken the place of the old system and some various other things veterans will notice. Gameplay is surprisingly similar to Fallout 4, if you had good frames on it, you'll have good frames in 76, which is surprising considering how vast the world is. You can see a drag...I mean scorch beast attacking other players nearly half way across the map, complete with its little bombing runs and your frames don't seem to dip.Quests don't have anywhere near the effort that 4 or skyrim had for the most part. MaIn missions will have some umph but the side missions are largely forgetable. The world does have some love in it though, if you enjoy picking up little pieces of lore as you go along, the misc info you'll snag or read along your journey is classic bethesda. Whoever they brought back to do the computer terminals knows his stuff.Overall, if its on sale for 15~, you'll get your moneys worth. It's basically a diluted DLC  for fallout 4 which you can play with your friends. It's basically a co-op game meant to be played over discord.Although its weird as hell they still haven't put in a text chat.

_childDocuments_.review: As 2020 nears to a close, and Fallout76 has been on Steam for nearly a year now, this is probably as good a time as any to review the current state of the game...which has plenty of sour points, but also some good.It is perhaps best described as being a browned banana. It looks rough, is kind of aged, but is still edible and will sate your hunger. After about 3 years of release, the game is currently in a playable state. It has NPCs, a decent number of random encounters, plenty of quests, and I even found myself enjoying the game. However I have been killed by literally invisible/immortal enemies whom I could not see/hit, yet whose health bars would appear as I could audibly hear them growling/snarling as they beat me to death. My game has de-sync'd from the server and I was forced to restart the entire game (this seems more likely to occur if you play for 3+ hours). I've (somewhat) struggled to actually earn bottlecaps ingame since vendors charge like 1000+ for a item, yet will only buy a weapon for like 5 caps, forcing me to spend absurd amounts of time trying to grind the basic currency which is used for fast-travel and buying blueprints. Economy is broken to the point where the only reliable way to earn money is to set up player-run vendors, and HOPE that someone stops by and buys your crap. And I have seen enemies freeze entirely, or outright refuse to drop loot because they died mid-animation (this happens mostly with ghouls).Yet I have put up with it all, because at the end of the day...it's somehow still fun. As a game that feels like it should have been singleplayer (in nearly 60 hours I have only done 1 event with other players, and was 1-shot killed by another level 200 player after getting an accidental 5 cap bounty on my head for touching someone's stuff), I have enjoyed wandering the wasteland of Fallout76. The variety in areas/biomes, and the stranger monsters such as the Wendigo or Scorthbeast have been a fresh breath to the formula. Plus being able to build and relocate my own homebase nearly anywhere in the world is pretty neat, and seeing some of the other creative builds by players has been cool too. If anything this game is STILL buggier than Cyberpunk2077 (which is saying something), yet keeps me coming back again and again.If I could sum it all up, it would essentially be that Fallout76 is just the typical Bethesda experience. A buggy open-world mess of a game that somehow you will find yourself loving if you go into it without taking things too seriously. Punch super-mutants while naked in a drug-fuel induced rage, dress like a cowboy and pop heads with a single-action revolver, or dress like a serial killer and launch a mini-nuke at some poor player's house. Just have fun for fun's sake, and ignore the Atom Shop, because you earn enough atoms ingame that you can honestly "buy" the cash-shop items without spending a actual cent (although I will guiltily admit I did spend $10 to get some cosmetic items, because I am a cheeky boi who likes to look fancy).

_childDocuments_.review: For the new player, the game will have some value with the content they have created over  the 4+ years that the game has been out but it will quickly become stale as the same weekly events will be repeated over and over with nothing new being added to the game. The recent trend from the Devs is removing content or taking away parts of the game or items and not doing anything to make the game rewarding or fun. When certain parts of the game become broken because of a patch that takes them 3 months to release, they do nothing to fix what is broken for another 3 months. This process has been repeated over and over again for at least the last 3 years.  It doesnt appear that Bethesda cares much for this Title or the Fallout Universe with the way that this game has been handled which is a shame. The Fallout 76 Community is truly amazing and unique. The Community Managers with Bethesda are also equally amazing and very very good people. If they had the backing of a good product, I have no doubt they would be able to create a better name and even stronger Community with Fallout 76.  Unfortunately, management is more interested in monetization of items focused on the Cosmetics and "Builders" of the game who've already invested heaps of money for items that should be rewards or gained through gameplay.  Focus on monetization and not capitalizing on the games enormous potential or even optimizing and fixing bugs within the game that have existed since day one (fast travel bug, terrible social menu, in game communications) and not putting any effort into more content has made the game bland and more of a Camp Building simulator. Streamers and Players create more content than the Devs to be honest. Testament to how amazing the community really is and how starved they are for something more. If you're a gamer that enjoys variety, I would recommend Fallout 76 since you're likely to work through the content then move to another title. If you're interested in a game to make your "main" than I would say move along and find something else. This will end up being a disappointment as you see the wasted potential and lack of development of the game by Bethesda.

_childDocuments_.review: When the game works it is legitimately the best of the three Bethesda Fallouts. It has a complex relationship with politics and class struggle, superb environmental storytelling, and a suite of quality of life improvements over 3 and 4. Subsequent updates have added funny, engaging, and thoughtful character writing on top of this.But lately I catch myself spending more time on insufferable MMO-like loot treadmills, groaning at eye-rollingly tone deaf cash shop items (what better addition to a franchise built on a critique of American jingoism than the ability to literally wear the American flag?) or just straight up waiting entire, actual minutes for crafting menus to load. At times borderline unplayable, thoroughly soulless, cravenly opportunistic. Run while you still can.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are lots of questions about this game in your mind. I had them too until free weekend. I tried it and bought the game. The reason behind it is not very simple. Let's read what I think.Not even close to be a masterpiece. Not good for pvp yet. Not a good survival game nor a good role-playing game. What is it then? It is the mixture of everything above.  I knew that this game's release was too harsh on players who bought it at that point. Yes, they are right and still lot's of bugs, exploits and unbalanced mechanism of player interactions. I would like to rate this game in four categories such as single-player, multi-player, technical, and overall. Singleplayer:I wouldn't recommend Fallout 76 to any player who wants to play Fallout series as single-player game. Why? Because quests are so simple, too repeating game play. You have to pay for single-player experience or private server experience with friends as co-op. Except your base and your quest line, everything on map belongs to server and it will reset everything else, once you logged out from the server or quit the game. Only plus of this game for single-player experience is that you usually feel alone and you encounter different events during your game play as other Fallout games.Rate: 4/10Multiplayer:I wouldn't recommend Fallout 76 to any player who wants to play Fallout series as multi-player game too. It's not a good game for competitive online gaming genre. There is no balance between players until you have the same level which is nearly impossible until end-game. Pvp is really bad in this game and seems it's not possible to be fixed. Best way to play this game as multi-player game is to play with your friends but still higher level player can come and kill you easily. There is no strong reward for killing someone in this game and it takes time to reach someone so it's not as easy as in GTA V.Rate: 3/10Technical: Same textures, animations, items, etc. from Fallout 4 are there. Server system is okay. You can find other players to interact more often than other survival, crafting games but there is a reason to find them or interact with them? I found many reasons to interact them but in this game I couldn't make any friends but enemies. I don't know what is the reason under this kind of an act but players prefer not interacting with you.There are lots of bugs and some exploits in this game which made selling items through vendors to other players banned. You can't sell any item with vending machines because of one exploit right now. I hope they will fix it as other bugs which still occurs. Rate: 5/10Overall:This is where I can recommend this game to people. It may not be a good single-player game nor multi-player game but it's a good mixture of it so if you buy this game expect some experience between. You will mostly play it co-op with your friends or single-player themed Fallout and see other players around. You can get killed time to time or kill other players for your own purposes and continue playing it alone or co-op.I can only recommend this game if you can play a game not less than 2 hours when you sit in front of it. Most of your playing time can be undone because of quitting the game. Anything that you do on map except your camping area and quest lines, will be the products that you gained from map, anything else will be undone. So it's better to play longer hours to get those products from what you built. Grinding is there and it's there because of this punishing system.Rate: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : Wish I played it sooner !Played every Fallout, but avoided this one at launch as the online aspect wasn't really my thing. Here I am years later now checking it out and wishing I had done so sooner. Fantastic Fallout game that I play just like a "normal" Fallout game, I keep passive mode on so that other online players cannot kill me or ruin my experience, and keeping my camp small or hardly using it at all, and using others camps instead, however I have yet to meet anyone who is trolling, so far my experience has been fantastic solo and with others, whether that be joining a casual team for the intelligence boost or going solo and running into others during events, the online aspect is fun !At first I kinda hated not being able to save (game auto saves) just in case I missed a speech/barter/intelligence check but quickly got over it as with any Fallout game there is always another way to finish your quest or complete the next step.Keeping with "any Fallout game" this game includes far much more lore IMO then Fallout 4, which is my least favorite of the series. I love to read the terminal lore, holo tapes etc, I like to take my time and enjoy these aspect of the game, and Fallout 76 delivered on that. The world is beautiful and full, lots to craft, cook, loot, and learn. The NPC's you will meet are full of life and usually have a lot to say, either it be "you look sick you should rest" to "I am going to enjoy killing you" which is always a fun treat to hear on your adventures. The radio stations are typical Fallout which is just what we all love, to have the best in classical music roaring while your beheading someone in VATS.Fantastic game, that can easily be played like a normal Fallout game.

_childDocuments_.review: I not going to go on and on about the bugs. I love Fallout 4 despite the major problems with it to this day. Fallout 76 isn't a bad game, but it's a pretty horrible grind fest unless you play with other people all of the time. It's really geared towards melee builds because the grind to keep up ammunition requires capturing and maintaining control of key nodes. Assuming you pay to play in your own instance, you can keep control of these nodes relatively easy, but you'e constantly being nagged to defend them instead of playing the content. If you play in a shared instance, forget it, players hundreds of levels higher than you will take it over. To level, you will play the same areas and events over and over. If you play with other players, the events are not much of a problem, but if you play solo, some of the events can easily expire before you are able to complete them unless you know exactly what to do for that event before starting it.The incremental upgrades when leveling don't do much to make you feel like you're gaining any kind of power over the wasteland; going from level 1 to 50 takes a long time and you are still relatively weak. Weapon and armor upgrades just don't feel special and most of the really good epic weapons have been nerfed or aren't even available any longer. Fallout 76 is a game I wanted to like, despite the bugs and glitchy game-play, but just felt like it was a big disappointment. I started playing when it first came out, but abandoned it after a few months due to bugs. Today it is nowhere near as buggy, but after putting 60 more hours in when it was moved to Steam (I probably played 60 more pre-Steam), I wished I never wasted any time on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for full price on day one because I have loved every Fallout game released since their inception, and despite repeated updates over the past two years remain desperately unhappy with my purchase. You won't see it above with my play stats, but I sunk a couple hundred hours into it prior to its arrival on the Steam platform, and have a couple level 60+ characters.This LOOKS like a fallout game, and there have been a couple things added to make it FEEL more like a Fallout game, but in its bones this game is a hard miss. It's clunky, grindy, super RNG, and feels like a half-hearted DLC for Fallout 4 (which for the kids in the back is a full 5 years old)TL/DR: This is a clunky inventory simulator with badly cobbled together systems, all of which punish a player for exploring wrong but fail to reward any sort of "correct exploration". I'm not even sure it's worth $10, and I'm pissed I spent $60. * It was originally designed with no NPCs in the world, and despite their addition since, the world still feels lifeless* The inventory management system is every bit as bad as it has been since Fallout 3, compounded by now also having a storage cap in your base* The base building, while it sounds like a good idea, is every bit as clunky as it was in Fallout 4, compounded by most of the interesting things to build WITH being random recipe drops with little guidance on if anywhere improves drop chances (grindy)* Weapon modification has been vastly expanded, but most mods are learned by trashing weapons which are largely random world drops (so you gotta farm rare spawns to get mods for rare spawns) (grindy)* High level play really requires you seek out good high level weapons with very specific perks, the drops of which and the perks on which are largely RNG (grindy)* While the Perks cards idea is neat, the implementation with the SPECIAL system is trash. If you don't pre-plan online, you'll have no idea in game which perks are available to you. If you don't luck out very early on with perk cards related to your chosen playstyle, you won't get the cards you need to play the way you want until way later than they are useful. In fact, you're liable to spend SPECIAL points badly in order to use good perks just so you can use something. _childDocuments_.review: Much improved over where it started and absolutely worth playing if you're a fan of the Fallout or Elder Scrolls series of Bethesda games. Similar to No Man's Sky this game has had a huge turnaround from being ridiculed to being an absolute blast to play. You can play it alone or with friends. While I personally think it would be a waste, you can even play it if you're not interested in the multiplayer elements, as a single player game, with some caveats (such as other people running around and the public events). But for those worried about griefing or being bullied by other players, my friends and I never had any issues with that. The community always seemed pretty nice. The one issue I would have with the online aspect is that sometimes it could be hard to complete a specific quest because other players in the area would affect it, such as killing everything in the area before you. But even that was a rather minor issue.A lot of Bethesda mainstays were missing at launch but are all there now. The NPCs, the quests, storylines, branching dialogues and choices, all the RPG choices with skills and traits, etc. are there similar to other modern Fallouts or Skyrim. I played a lot of it with a friend of mine and we had a great time. The public events could be quite fun. There's a lot of depth to this game now, as Bethesda fans have come to expect. The world is vast and there's a lot to explore and secrets to find.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so now that I've put in nearly 200 hours into the Steam version with the Wastelanders and the seasons update (along with around 150 hours on the  version before the Wastelanders update) I felt like I had to update my review.This game is in a much better state than it was at launch and it seems to keep getting better with each major update. Its a really fun addition to the Fallout franchise, its got everything you'd expect in a Bethesda Fallout game and its packed with content if you're just starting out now.There are a few frustrating things about the game, mainly the stash limit as you'll constantly be battling your weight limit, trying to decide on what to keep and what to trash (1st membership fixes this somewhat with unlimited junk storage, but thats £11 a month...eh). The graphics will bug out a lot, and since its running on a server and always online you'll get the occasional hitch and server slow down when trying to build a camp or pick up an item. All of those above can be annoying, but if you're willing to put up with it there's a really great game here. The Legendary Run update is really fun for casual play as it helps unlock items and caps as you just do daily and weekly tasks, which does a lot to help alleviate the grind. Public groups are now in the game, making teaming up with other players a lot easier and it comes with bonuses too.Im not a hardcore player, so these new additions are great as you kind of hit a wall around level 50 in terms of casual progression, and things seem a lot tougher.Overall, I honestly think its now a game worth picking up even if you're a solo player like me, and with the planned future content it seems it'll only get better!Old Review:Fallout 76 isn't an amazing game, but its far from terrible. I'd recommend getting it on a sale rather than full price.Put simply if you like Fallout 4 but think multiplayer elements sound good, then you'll like 76. Its much better now than it was at release and I'm hoping Wastelanders makes it even better, if not then I'll revisit this review.Side note: If you have performance issues but switching to fullscreen isn't fixing them, go to Documents>MyGames>Fallout 76> Fallout76Prefs and change iPresentInterval=1 to 0This will turn off Vsync and hopefully fix your performance, which can also make the frame pacing terrible so cap it in the Nvidia control panel to your taste. I was getting a cap of 40fps with my 2070 and switching that fixed my issues completely.

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel like I should preface this, I played both the original release launch and now the current NPC released update. I got this game for free as a gift from a friend who really wanted to play with me and I was hooked...But I feel extremely ripped off, getting the game, FOR FREE. I want you all to know that.This game is still the absolute buggiest multiplayer AAA mess I think I really have ever seen and all the positive ratings absolutely confuse me because I had the patience to try this game over and over, only to constantly feel like I was always getting robbed. NPC's are not even remotely polished either, considering I've wasted hundreds of resources of caps and ammo and junk to have the NPC not want to do the thing it's programmed to do, like talk to another NPC. One or twice, its a bethesda game... over 5 or so times? No, that doesn't get to slide.The quests are still an awful mess with some improvement here and there, but overall it is still just horrible. I've tried one where I needed to get a certain bug part... only for all the spawns to suddenly NOT want to give me said bugs anymore EVEN IN THE AREA HIGHLIGHTED THAT THE GAME WANTS YOU TO GO. NPC's are going to often bug out and not do anything, or crash your game and force you to restart everything with all your resources lost to the wind. Because that's fair. Once or twice is a given, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ten is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disaster.The servers are still a jittering mess, constantly jumping frames even on the most stable of computers. You could have a titan and the game would run like garbage. The optimization is a joke in this game, no matter WHAT you do. Your frames will stutter, you will crash for no good reason, and even freezing just the same. There's no way to tell when it will happen, it just happens. It just, works!Areas constantly DO NOT REMAIN CONSISTENT considering I had to fight a legendary 72 beast as a level 45 character while being surrounded by level 22 beasts. Because that's just how it should work right? The quests will also give you the same treatment, not letting you know what you're walking into. They're about as consistent as the customizing your CAMP (which, for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ life of me, why is the part highlighting green if it still can't be placed?)Weapons are also horribly inconsistent as well, tip of advice, carry a flamer everywhere considering its the only thing that actually keeps you safe. Other guns will vary on how they work for you, or you could just go running around and tapping things in VATS which doesn't remain consistent either. I found myself carrying around a level 25 flamer because it was doing more damage for me than a minigun or 50 cal (that WAS at my level). THAT'S NOT TO MENTION YOU CAN LITERALLY BUY CAPS FOR CASH THROUGH A THIRD PARTY SELLER! HOW FANTASTIC IS THAT RIGHT!? Literally its $7 for 25,000 caps, let that sink in everyone! You can buy the strongest currency in the game and just undermine everyone else, paying to win essentially.This game is a joke still, save every bit of your money and just walk away before you get sucked into this cult like enjoyment of grinding away that will ultimately mean nothing because level 1 timmy can just buy a years worth of caps for $7. This game is a blood pressure raiser and it's really nothing else at the moment. And don't let everyone try to fool you into thinking "ITS A BRAND NEW BETHESDA, THEY FIXED IT!"They didn't. It's still buggy and it's still a horrendous mess that has only had a few minor and major fixes out of the bazillion other issues.=============================UPDATE 2022:It's still a bit of a garbage game lmao, you're better off getting it on a really good sale. Don't pay full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my very first public review, and it's mostly due to my love for the Fallout franchise.I started playing F76 on , reached around level 65 and had a fairly good time. When it came to Steam, I started fresh and worked my way up from scratch enjoying the new NPCs, Locations, Quests and so on. Still had a great time. By far the best perk of this game is its community. For a wasteland focused, post-apocalyptic world it is the most friendly PVP/PVE environment I have ever witnessed which is something I enjoy. With the new updates of quick-teams, new quests and random events it adds an element to the game that will take your hours away and spend it with friends or strangers, killing waves and waves of monsters.Once I reached level 100 I expected the achievement to pop, bringing me one step closer to 100% the game. It did not. Apparently this is quite the common bug with the game across platforms, so I realised that my old character has to be refreshed and leveled up to 100 to get the achievement (hopefully, as the char originated on  and there are bugs crossing chars over to platforms as well).As long as there were quests to be done (which I have done all) this game can distract you enough to have fun, and explore the huge map that is Appalachia, as long as you are willing to accept some very frustrating bugs (which there are plenty of) as well as very poor optimisation and slow updates. As a massive Fallout fan I 100% every Fallout game to date, this one was no exception until it bugged out and didn't give the achievement as it is meant to, for reaching level 100. I know its a trivial issue to many who may not care about it, but IMO if you spend hundreds of hours in a game that is mostly broken and hated by majority of the gaming community, you should have at least a stupid virtual trophy to show for it.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost if you are a competitive CoD, Fortnite, WoW, League of Legends toxic player please keep moving on.if you need your Bethesda fix but are dissapointed with Starfield this game will definitely give you that.  I have played 3 separate times.  Before human NPCs and couldn't get into it.  Right after human NPC's were added and it felt better but still kind of lifeless and now this time it feels like Fallout. Levels 1-50 is like playing FO3 or FO4.  Very much just progressing to "max" item level and figuring out your playstyleLevels 50-100ish - Learning the specific MMO currencies and systems like Scrip, Treasury Notes, Events, Expeditions.  Choosing your first few legendary perks. Or farming and stabiilizing flux early and often for higher end mods.  Or using multiple camp slots as fast travel points. With the tv show coming out there is definitely an influx of the toxic WoW and CoD players but hopefully they will figure it out.  I say it twice because in 200+ hours the only three bad experiences I have had with other players are post Amazon show and I hope it stays wholesome and inviting!

_childDocuments_.review: UP-UPDATE: Been having fun the past week playing this with a new character speccing into damage with rifles. Guess I must've specced wrong to begin with, damage bonuses are a must. Playing with fallout with friends, despite its typical clunkiness, minor bugs, and grind, has been pretty fun. Dailies offer a good challenge with different mutations for that day, with enemies that drop the ammo of the gun you're using given that it's not something expensive like a fat man. There's plenty of quests: Main, side, events, dailies. Set up a workshop and build defenses to collect resources over time. Set up your CAMP at a good location to do the same thing, or to just have a good fast travel location. Set out to explore, collect junk to scrap, use to craft weapons and armor, and then use those to shoot your way through the game as you progress. Level up to unlock perk cards, combine duplicates to max them out, or scrap them to points to use towards upgrading your legendary account-wide perk cards. (One of those legendary perk cards give you max lockpicking and hacking, very useful. Another, exploding enemies on death and so on.) Farm for legendaries, apply legendary mods to a weapon. Plenty of stuff to shoot. It's fallout, online, and the best we're gonna get for now, and it's not too bad.UPDATE: The game is good with the addition of Fallout Worlds, custom worlds that have world settings to change. One of them being damage scaling. The game is much more fun when played with a few friends with the damage dealt cranked up to 200% to avoid bullet sponges. However to get Fallout Worlds you need to have Fallout 1st, a subscription.While it is a fun being able to play fallout with friends, the game itself is sub-par. Quests are pretty boring, having to find plans and grind resources is a chore, and the best thing to do with your friends is to wander Appalachia doing what you can together.You'd think the quest system would work well with friends/teams, letting everyone progress together as they do the quests together, but unfortunately completing quests is independent to each player. If you want to play with your friends in a mission separate from Appalachia, you can only join your team leader's instance, where your solo mission progress is disabled. Your team leader can't join you, and you can't join other team members' "solo" quests.This all goes without saying that the movement and combat is janky, as much as you would expect from a Fallout game. I got used to it, except the part where the enemy scaling is ridiculous as you dump all your ammo from your level 45 guns into level 45 cannon fodder. Not to mention, when you do manage to finally kill a sentry bot or an assaultron, you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for loot.With that being said, it was still fun playing a fallout game with friends when we could. However the game itself is lackluster and a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: The game became pay to win and still isn't addressing launch day bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Do I like this game? Yes.Can I in good conscience recommend it to others? No.Bethesda regularly adds content updates, on the surface this may sound great, but this will usually introduce a boatload of bugs, many of which will not be addressed for a very long time. One example is a recent update fixed a bug where gunfire would ring out constantly, even after an encounter ends, this bug had existed since around 2020! 4 years to implement a minor fix like this a little concerning. The same update made a newly added weapon completely useless in VATS mode, a major component of the gameplay for many players. Its like Bethesda Austin, the office in charge of the development is void of quality and version control.Another annoying aspect is that attempts by Devs to 'balance' the game consist of nerfing what works, instead of buffing what doesn't, imagine grinding hours out with the RNG to attain the weapon build you're happy with, to log in one day and find you now do 40% less of the damage you did the day before, leaving your build worthless and the weapon you spent maybe 60hrs of grind attaining, nothing more than scrap. Would this scenario make you happy with the game or make you throw the towel in? The above reasons (amongst other things) probably lend to why the game has such a high attrition rate of players, it gets frustrating to play, leaving you thinking your time has been wasted and that the devs don't have a clue what they are doing.To summarise, would I ask my friends to give it a go? No, I'd be embarrassed to, they have standards this game doesn't meet and this game, while containing many enjoyable aspects, its an endless cycle of game broken, game not so broken.I personally believe the only way to fix the rotation of problems in this game would be a complete overhaul of the studio, the engine and the entire game, which will never happen.

_childDocuments_.review: To say I am currently addicted to this game is an understatement. Is it a perfect experience? No. Is it a fun experience? Definitely. I played Fallout 76 at launch and while I mostly enjoyed the game back then simply because the gameplay is basically fallout 4, it was missing The Wastelanders expansion has breathed a whole heap of life into the game, both literally and figuratively, while the game is still lacking any real endgame content, the direction it seems to be going leaves me excited to see what comes next. The perk system is varied enough that you can make multiple characters and find a fun, unique and rewarding experience with the myriad different playstyles and weapons at your disposal. If you enjoy looting, Crafting/base building, (A carbon copy of Fallout 4s settlement building on a smaller scale for those of you who have played Fallout 4, for those who haven't, you can find plans for hundreds of different buildable items, both weaponry and armour as well as base items, things like keypad locked doors, different structural materials and furniture, as well as a really cool and unique power system) then this game has plenty of it.Would I recommend this for people looking for an exact Fallout 4 experience? No, unfortunately you won't get the story or the well crafted missions you see in previous Bethesda singleplayer games, but for anyone looking for a fun pve survival game to play with your friends, then you could find dozens, maybe even hundreds of hours of enjoyment in this game. As for any negatives I have, the real issues are bugs and glitches, things can go wrong and you may be forced to join a different server to correct them, other things are a bit more of an issue, like graphical glitches and performance. Theres also the obvious ingame store, generally I don't have an issue with ingame stores aslong as they are selling cosmetics. That is what the Atomic shop is and the fact you can earn atoms through completing challenges ingame means I am cool with this aspect of the game. All of the content that matters is available to everyone that owns the base game. I should also point out that I am a Fallout 1st member, after receiving the game for free on steam for having a linked bethesda account and with how little I initially spent on the game, I didn't mind spending the money for Fallout 1st, if I'm being honest, I didn't like the sound of it when I heard it first announced and I was skeptical of its value when I first purchased it, but now I don't think I could play without it, this is a bad thing, it really does enhance alot of aspects of the game (the scrap box with unlimited scrap storage and the tent being the 2 main features that it seems it may be hard to live without, however I have 2 friends playing with me who are not using Fallout 1st and are equally as addicted as me. At the end of the day, this game is great fun, it holds my attention and I find I enjoy every minute I spend in the game, is it perfect? No, but what game truly is? If you're interested, just give it a go, maybe wait for a sale and grab it cheaper along with a month of Fallout 1st.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a couple of hundred hours in the non-Wastelanders version - only just recently converted to Steam.Be warned, I'm one of those people who actually liked the game at launch. Well, ok, not at launch - but a few weeks after launch, when they introduced the ability to run it at a proper frame rate and other PC specific fixes.I never quite understood the amount of criticism the game received from professional reviewers. The game had issues, for sure - and it was never polished, and it's still a little quirky to be honest.I'll try not to get into the anti-Beth vitriol - as there's really nothing to do about that. I trust people who're genuinely curious will remain open-minded and have their own reasons to check this game out.Anyway, this is essentially Fallout 4 with multiplayer. It's 99% consensual multiplayer, by the way - as the world is very large and you're not forced to do any kind of interaction. Personally, I've never had another player attack me in a few hundred hours of playing this game - and I can count on one hand the amount of times I've actually interacted with anyone.I'm not a very social player when it comes to strangers - but I don't mind seeing other people running around.In terms of exploration and distinct content, this is head and shoulders above all the other Fallouts - and, yes, that includes FO1 and FO2.The world is 4 times larger than Fallout 4 afterall.The mechanics are relatively straightforward - and if you've ever played a cooperative multiplayer game, you should have a pretty good idea of how Fallout would work in such a setting.For Wastelanders, the NPC interaction seems much improved over Fallout 4 - but that's based on only a short time I've played it, and what certain popular streamers are saying about it. It has genuine SPECIAL checks all over the place, and apparently you can make quite meaningful choices.I find that delightful - but I was never against a desolate and lonely Fallout experience, because I think it fits well with the setting and formula. So, for NPC interaction - I could really take it or leave it. But what's there seems better than one would expect from a free expansion-sized update.But be aware that this IS a multiplayer game - and that means online infrastructure and always online. It also means the occasional bug related to lag or similar issues. Though it's quite rare - and seems improved from last time I played.If you're emotionally invested against other people - even seeing them - then be aware that you CAN play on private servers, but they charge you for that. I personally don't like that, because that wasn't at all the gist I got from their original talk of private servers in a 100% free update kind of game.But, as I said, you don't have to interact with other people - and once you go beyond the starter areas, it's relatively rare to even see another person. As I said, the world is huge for this type of game and there are only 24 players on a given server when it's full.What I particularly like about Fallout 76 is that most of the story is a lot more mature - and you'll come across countless audio logs that tell quite a sobering tale of nuclear aftermath and such. The world is also divided into 6 very distinct biomes - which was never the case with past Fallouts.So, we're talking a LOT more variety than any previous game in that way.So, for an exploration junkie - this is really a dream if you can get past the above mentioned issues.If you're looking for some kind of looter shooter - where you go on a treadmill for eternal progression, this game isn't really that - though it actually does a decent job of trying considering what it really is.The game is terrific for what it is - and it's the most polished it's ever been at the moment. But it's not perfect by a long shot.I'd probably rate it around 8/10 - as a reasonably objective score. For personal reasons, it's closer to 9/10 - but that's because I'm a great fit for the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I currently have just under 80 hours in this game and I can confidently say that I cannot possibly recommend it to anyone in good faith. They say Fallout 76 has been fixed, that it is good now but that is only a half truth. The actual truth, for me at least, is that this is the buggiest and most unpolished game I have ever played. I have encountered roughly 7 or so bugs that I would consider at least mildly game-breaking as they all required me to restart the game to fix them. From getting stuck into terrain multiple times, to a broken quest and strange UI disappearances, I had to basically restart the game every 10 hours or so if you do the math. That is without mentioning the copious amounts of smaller and inconsequential bugs as well as the horribly broken lighting system in the game. The gameplay itself doesn't fare much better either in my opinion. The survival elements have been heavily trivialized to the point they may as well not exist anymore. Ammo is way too plentyful with enemies magically spawning loads of whatever ammo is utilized by the weapon you used to kill them with, you cannot make this up. Gunplay feels horrible by virtue of the fact that anemies dash and zip around the field faster than Usain Bolt on coke. Speaking of enemies, their AI is horrendous as well. Guns break and become irrelevant fast so you'll spend a lot of time making sure you can actually do decent damage to the bullet sponges in this game. Both of the main stories are just boring slogfests that make Fallout 4's story look like Shakespeare in his prime. Boring premise, boring characters and boring quests. The vast majority of the quests in this game are a variation of fetching, killing or interacting with some automated AI system. I've done a few really good ones such as the Nuka Shine quest but sadly, most the other quests in the game don't even come close.It would be disingenuous to say I have not had some fun with the game because I did, but the longer I played the less fun I had until I just gave up altogether. In my opinion Fallout 76 doesn't just fail as a Fallout game, it even fails as a Bethesda game as well as a live service one, since you know, live service games require actual expansions not scraps of new content here and there which is what 76 gets.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not "good now", anyone who tries to convince you otherwise is a consumer of dogslop. Anything taken for granted in previous FO games from mechanics to cosmetics will be taken away and sold back to you in an effort to nickle and dime you. There is no rhyme or reason to balancing weapons/ammo types, even more damning is if you complain about this other players will berate you for not using the meta legendary assault rifle chambered in .45 as if every other weapon exists in the game for no reason at all.Tedium is the name of the game, as you will be made to server hop to access another pool of the legendary shop (which sports an abysmally small selection) to get the items you want. Even though you're paying for the price of a full game, better pay some more in a subscription so you get more inventory space! State of the game can only be attributed to the people playing it. When I first started, someone was kind enough to drop a  level 25 Fixer for me to make use of. When I outgrew its use, it figured I'd pass it on by posting it on my shop for a exorbitantly small amount of caps, well within what someone making their way through their starter levels can afford. Ofc when a lvl 500 buys it, I find it being sold on their shop for.... 40,000 caps.Can I even blame Bestheda for this? _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Big open world with tons of content in the shape of quests, events and the sort- The game has seasonal events every now and then with unique, limited rewards that can range from weapons, outfits and the sort- C.A.M.P. building system similar to Fallout 4's settlement building system that allows for almost infinite base variations- Decent variety of weapons, armor and outfits, allowing thorough customizability and many build possibilities- One of the nicest communities I've seen in a online RPGCons:- Game can become very repetitive after a certain level- Server latency can be very high depending on the amount of players in the server (the game allows for a maximum of 24 per server), leading to low performance and sync problems- At the time of this review, the game still features some balancing issues despite the frequency of hotfixes and updates in general- Fallout 1st (to sum it up, it's a subscription that gives the player exclusive rewards and quality of life "services". Considering Fallout 76 is already a paid game and what the subscription offers, in my point of view Fallout 1st is another cash grab attempt by Bethesda, which is unfortunately working very well)Conclusion: If you don't mind the grind, Fallout 76 can become a pretty enjoyable experience. At least for a while. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played this at launch when it was a disaster, I come back a few years later hoping it has changed. It has, most good, but still some very bad mechanics are holding this game hostage. Mainly, the game deliberately limits how much time you can play, while actually feeling like you have accomplished something.Just spent an hour doing public events and expeditions? Now go spend 30 minutes figuring out how to manage all the legendary items you just got. You can't sell them all for scrip, because of a daily limit, so you sell them to a vendor for 1/3 what they are worth. You could try and sell them at your base vendor, but that will quickly fill your inventory space and leave you with no room for things you actually need. Then you have all these treasury notes to spend on gold, to get some of the best blueprints/items..... But you can only get 400 a day + 300 a week, and damn near all the blueprints for the good items cost a MINIMUM of 750. Some of us do enjoy the grind, but not even getting 1 of the gear pieces you need a day is brutal. NOT TO MENTION THE VENDOR RESET ON THESE IS BASED ON YOUR FIRST SALE TO THEM. 20 hours later you can sell to them again. Which is not displayed anywhere in game, so you need to make a mental note of when you made the first transaction.  Forgot when you made that sale? Tough ♥♥♥♥, better check back every hour to find out if it reset. I wont bother talking about how they built the inventory system to deliberately drive you towards the 13$ (US) a month subscription to avoid spending 30-40 minutes managing your inventory.This game has some really great qualities, AND an amazing player base. Some of the best experiences I have had are people giving me cool things. But that was quickly made clear it was only happening because people have no space to keep these things, and have hit their daily limit on vendors.I want to play this game as much as I want, not as much as I am allowed.With all of this said I can't recommend a game that limits that amount of fun you can have. If you do spend money on this game, just know you will at a certain point be forced into paying a monthly/annual fee as well as limiting the amount of time you spend playing before you are encumbered for 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excited, and did get some beta in on this game, and it was absolutely disappointing. Empty, boring, broken-ass closeup graphics with mega motion blur and poor FOV/depth of field, it made me sick to play for even a few hours.As recently as a few weeks ago I've made fun of people on forums / discord for playing it, booing it on ads, commenting snarky remarks under their sponsored ads, etc.But I did long for the days of New Vegas or Fallout 4, decided I might replay one of them when suddenly the free weekend came around. I thought I'd at least give it a try, see if the NPCs make the difference, how the graphics look now, and try it with my fiancee instead of alone.This game now, on the whole, is fixed in my eyes. If you told me a few years ago "hey, you can play FO4 on a new map with a friend or two" I would jump for joy, and i know that many fallout fans would say the same. I let the vile internet effect seep into my brain and poison me against something that I honestly genuinely knew I could probably like. I made a mistake. Don't jump on the "this game is garbage" bandwagon like I had (commenting on trailers that you'll never play it, etc) - it's boring. it's not original, and it actually comes across as ignorant to feel like you're important enough to warrant thinking anyone cares about your negative opinion. it's also HELLA IGNORANT to act like something is beneath you even TRYING it, especially if you call yourself a fan. before i tried this game i think i was way too jaded, heard bad hype, and didn't want to give in to the "ohhh we fixed it, don't worry!" vibe. By trying, in error, to not conform to the people who were saying it was good, I was bandwagoning with the even lamer side of "People are saying this is good so with 0 recent frame of reference I am going to argue that it is bad." It makes me slightly embarassed to think of now, because I know for a fact that I tend to do that with TV/Movies/Games yet I didn't even stop to think that I might be making the same mistake again.it's not fallout 300,000. the graphics look like brushed up fo4 graphics, the FOV default is nightmarishly low to begin with which is why i spent the first 4 hours feeling like my eyes were broken - set it to 90. turn the depth of field down ALMOST all the way. now you're just playing fallout 4, with new characters (loveable npcs really do make all the difference) new areas, less scrounging for ammo and more shooting guys who MIGHT ACTUALLY kill you.Things can change. People, and studios because of it, are inherently flawed. What they did, though, was not go "HEY ♥♥♥♥ YOU" and never fix it - they listened, and slowly they fixed it. Bethesda is now like any other AAA studio and super in it for the moolah, but you've gotta give Todd some credit, he did the dirty and didn't love the response he got but in the end they jumped on and improved the things that didn't work, and polished the things that did.The CAMP system is really cool, I love that you can't REALLY get into too much PVP unless you agree to it - and your stash is always safe, only you can access it. Worst case scenario some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decide to blow up your camp while you're off running around, it's a learning experience for placing more turrets next time, or for just leaving your camp completely open to the public - if you don't store much in other containers / don't have anything actively mining you're not up to lose too much.So far in about 20 hours I've met 4-5 other people, all of whom gave me gifts, showed me where the good stuff on the level was / cap stashes / got me to follow them to large events where they mowed down all the baddies for us. Not one real person (aside from when I had a 10 cap bounty on me for government supply theft) has shot at me, or even moved toward me in a threatening manner. Most people make liberal use of the in-game emotes, with less voice chat as far as I've seen - which is honestly my preference so I'm into it!If you're THINKING about trying the game, because you loved Fallout 3 / 4 / NV - I recommend giving it the benefit of the doubt. If you think you hate it but have never played it, and are just bandwagoning because of word of mouth - rethink your stance. Maybe being "non-mainstream" is just as mainstream, but kinda boring and tiresome?

_childDocuments_.review: First, hear me out:I love this game, I'm a sucker for everything Fallout ever since Fallout 3, and there's some real fun to be had in this game, I for one have almost 1000 hours of play time at the time of writing this review, but there are some things that you should know if you haven't followed the (mess of a) progress this game have had through it's time.FIRST: The negative stuffBugs, a lot of bugs, from not being able to simply fast travel at first try due to someone (or even you) having a mutation that's supposed to just heal you outside of battle to people (read: jerks) being able to buy stuff that you're actually not selling, this game is riddled with bugs, to the point that I wonder if Bethesda's team actually know what they're doing when they try to fix something and inevitably brake 5 other very unrelated things... It gets messy real quick. Most of the (worst) bugs have been fixed by now, but it's pretty common to read of new "features" (let's call it that) being "added" to the game every other week.The game does NOT run very well on anything other than Windows 10 OS, I suffered quite of problems (namely stutter issues) when I had a Windows 7 install and then I moved to Linux, only to find that, after a few weeks of perfectly good gameplay, the issues started there too. I think this is quite intentional by Bethesda since they were aquired by Microsoft, which in by itself is well known of employing some really shady mob tactics to get it's products into more computers. There's nothing in this game that should technically require Windows 10 or any of its features, and it even says on the "recommended" system requirements that it fully supports 7, 8 and 10 equally. Well I can say that it does run fairly smooth on Windows 10 but not on any of the others (Linux w/proton included), so consider yourself warned.NOW, the GOOD stuffThe community - this game has one of the nicest communities you'll find in a game, especially with this low of a reputation. Servers are usually filled with people that are very noob friendly and will go out of their way to help you on your low level tasks. I had some really good social experiences just by finding strangers and commenting on their camp.Trading -this is where F76 really shines in my opinion, when you're done with the main Wastelanders, Enclave and Brotherhood questlines, you'll be fairly high leveled to start some trading with other high leveled players, there are quite a lot of trading forums with a reputation system like Reddit's Market76 and the trading discord server. You're bound to have some really good experiences.The guns - the last good point in this game is, in my opinion, the guns. The vast majority of weapons have a very good feeling and are very fun to use, the gunplay is most excellent for a game that is considered more of a RPG nature.So, if you're willing to accept its flaws, F76 can be quite rewarding and fun to play, but its good moments are not enough for me to recommend new players to get into. Only venture into this game if you, like me, really, and I mean really, like Fallout.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin.  Remember Fallout 4?  Remember not liking the bugs, crashes, rendering issues, object clipping, etc?  Well get ready for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is..........Fallout 76.  I don't even know where to begin.  The tutorial seemed legit, walking through the vault and collecting my items.  I was thinking to myself, "Oh boy, this isn't as bad as everyone makes it out to be."  I was so wrong.  The second I step out into the wasteland i was bombarded with a long distance rendering bug that left the terrain in sheets instead of a 3D render.  After that cleared up, i began to walk out into the wasteland.  The first thing i noticed was the graphics.  My god, from a distance the grass and plants look beautiful, almost too good.  Then you get up close and realise that its just a flat surface rendered in 3D.  But graphics aren't a problem, because the game is fun, right?  W R O N G.  First death, i didn't even attack the NPC and his dogs were after me, but he was cool as a cucumber sitting in his chair.  It took me 2 attempts to kill the unbelievably overpowered dogs before he decided to shoot me with his shotgun.  So, after another attempt i finally kill him, and take his gun.  Oh boy, a new gun, with high damage!  Lets equip it!  W R O N G.  Because for whatever reason, Bethesda decided that the good guns need to be level locked, so new players can't use nice guns early on.  but i had hope, and ventured on with the shotgun in my inventory.  Farther we push into the wasteland, until we come to a farm.  In this farm were some scorchers.  Oh boy, easy loot!  I was slaying, i had killed 2 without a single scratch, when suddenly, one comes out of nowhere and decides to attack me.  No problem, i'll just fight back!  W R O N G.  I dumped at least 20 bullets straight into the damn thing, and it did no damage.  On a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level 2 scorcher!  And so, of course, i ran, suffering immeasurable damage in the process.  Once out of sight, i heal up, and continue onward.  I come across a player base.  Oh boy, a low level player, maybe we can be a team!  W R O N G.  He took one look at me and one tapped me.  Ah, that's ok, i'll just continue in the other direction when i respawn.  respawned back at the vault, and again, i'm plagued with graphical bugs (not on my end, i checked my systems and they were all fine). In addition, when you press ESC to go to the menu, it takes you straight to the map, where you have to press the Z key just to access the menu.  This is such a poor design feature, why not just make it with a normal function?  And the atom shop, if you like this game, don't even bother with the atomic shop.  Bethesda wants you to pay for overpriced aesthetic items that don't have any practical use other than making you a visible target.  In a short conclusion, this game is not, NOT worth your time or money.  If this game was like $10 or $15, we might be talking, but this is low even by Bethesda standards.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many people, I bought this game on release as the idea of having a legit mulitplayer fallout game seemed awesome. We all know what happened next over the next year and a half. No need to go into much detail, (just watch the internet historian vid) but pretty much a lot was missing, a lot of controversy happened, and the game was broken. Now we have Wastelanders which brings NPCs, new questline and a bunch of new content. I'll briefly go over the pros and cons of this update and give my overall opinion on this game.Pros:- World is now populated with NPCs each with dialogue and backstories- Dialogue has skill checks and interesting options. (Maybe even better than FO4)- Main questline has interesting choices and faction options- New content is appreciated and gives you incentives to take part in daily quests and nuking new areas.Cons:- Not too many sidequests, making the game feel empty after the main quest is finished- Endgame is lacking. Again once main quest is finished the endgame is mainly daily quests and events. - Most quests are just fetch or radiant. (This is more of a complaint with Beth RPGs in general, but is more prevalent here than before)- Bugs bugs bugs. I mean c'mon it's Bethesda. Still no excuse for a triple A game.These are just a few things off the top of my head. My biggest complaint with this game is the endgame. Whilst many people would probably be happy with the daily quests and events. I would have liked to have seen more story-based sidequests and NPC interaction. The new dialogue system is a promising sign of what this game could move towards. Despite all of this though. After installing this game again on my steam account, and spending the better part of a week in lockdown playing this game. I have had a lot of fun playing this game. Whether it's playing through the main story, nuking areas with friends and farming loot, or building my character into a sneaky beaky sniper. I can safely say this game is certainly on the right track.This update is a step in the right direction. There's still a lot missing and a lot that needs to be fixed. However I'd still recommend giving this game a go. Even moreso if you have people to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Bethesda game.  It's using an engine that's 30 years old and was passed off to a team that did their best having never built with it before.  Every game that came before this one sits underneath a coat of paint and primer, leaving the bugs and code from those past games sitting and waiting to rear their ugly heads.  This game was fun when it came out for a certain type of player.  Was it your traditional Fallout game?  Absolutely not.  Could you have fun if you had people to play with?  For sure.  Now with years of updates  and the introduction of NPC's you can actually talk to that are robots it's much closer.The community is mostly helpful and friendly.  You'll find people that you can team up with but with a lack of any form of in game chat beyond team or area voice it can be difficult without joining an online community through discord to find lasting in game friendships.  If you like Fallout, want to be able to play something with others, and take it for what it is and not what you want it to be you will have a good time. Just find a community to join that's interested first or you find the game a bit lacking.  This was a game designed to be played with friends but the story and missions are mostly done in the traditional single player fallout format.  This means that there is little substance in the parts that matter most to Fallout players with a larger emphasis on group events.  This leaves the game in an awkward middle ground where it doesn't do either side justice.  It's an average game that is fun with other people but leaves that squarely in your hands to deal with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so after coming back from 2018, there is WAY more content in this game than there was originally, and is a massive improvement over what the game initially was, especially when compared to it at launch. It feels like Fallout 4 with all of the mods everyone wanted.HOWEVER: this game is only worth $9 on sale.YOU STILL HAVE TO PAY FOR INVENTORY SPACE. This is the single stupidest decision I have ever seen in this game series. Your inventory space is artificially shrunk to get you to buy more, literally infinite, space. Items were added for various crafting mechanics, but they added so much and artificially increased the amount of materials so far that you almost need to pay for the infinite inventory space, or you just aren't going to be able to craft anything. I guess that was too much of an ask for a Fallout game that's done it many times before. And don't tell me it's a "resource issue" for servers, because they literally are offering infinite space to stash stuff as a paid option.IT IS STILL PAY TO WIN. You're now joining the game with people who are level 600+, so good luck getting a shot in quicker than they can with their AOE cannon bought straight from the Store. I'm sitting in events afk because I can't get a shot in, and they encourage it. It's the most mind numbing gameplay I've seen in a while - And this is what they call "balanced gameplay"? But hey, you can buy the weapons from the store too! and they work in pvp. THERE ARE LIMITS ON EVERYTHING. Selling items? There is a GLOBAL cap limit for ALL vendors - every vendor shares the same amount of caps, and when one runs out, they all do. And this goes for every currency in the game. Vendors sold out? might as well stop playing because you aren't making any money, your inventory space is limited, and you can't carry or store anymore. Dumbest decision I've seen in any game; BUY OR YOU'LL MISS OUT!!! The game also heavily relies on FOMO. They rotate shop items every week, and from what I've seen, doesn't bring them back regularly. Apparently they also used to have a board game mechanic for "seasonal" events, which is now gone. I guess having a fun mechanic in the game with rewarding items was too much? Now it's just "level up, collect items from a list, repeat." - they really know how to make it monotonous.THEY HAVE FOUND A WAY TO MONETIZE LITERALLY EVERY ITEM IN THE GAME.It sucks that I'm not joking about any of this. You pay for inventory space. You pay for weapons.You pay for armor.You pay for resources.You pay for TEMPORARY carry weight.You pay for TEMPORARY buffs.You pay for literally junk items.And that's before getting into the skins that were straight ripped from people modding, and from what I've seen, without any credit given.THE GAME HAS BROKEN MECHANICS EVERYWHERE. This game comes with all the bugs of previous fallout games as well, this far into it's release - except now you cant get mods to fix it - and we know they aren't paying developers to fix it, skins and cosmetics are just too profitable.The conclusion:This game still reeks of being an EXTREMELY LAZY PAY-TO-WIN MONEY GRAB, poor planning, and poor mission design, but it is currently only $9 - and only $9 is actually worth it due to the game being Fallout at it's core - at least until you get frustrated with having to pay for parts of the game just to make it enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been interested since 76s' release, but the bad press kept me away. Only the combination of quarantine fatigue and it going on sale inspired me to hop in and check it out. And I am not as disappointed as I was expecting to be.On the surface, it feels a LOT like Fallout 4. Inventory management and Player UI is very familiar to anyone who has played a Bethesda game in the past. The C.A.M.P system can be frustrating to get started, as the building interface is straight from Fallout 4. But once you have a structure in place, being able to have a Base of Operations that is entirely your own is amazing in a multiplayer environment (the added benefit of being able to pay a few caps to move base when you're exploring a far away zone is wonderful).Combat is comfortable and familiar. For obvious Reasons, VATS no longer slows time letting you target, but makes up for it by becoming a simple auto-aiming mechanic. I pretty much keep it on Torsos for quick-kills on enemies who get too close.Leveling up has been adjusted the most from the standard single-player system. each level you gain allows you to put a single point into one of your traits. Doing this gives you space to socket perk cards. Once you have a perk card, it's yours. They can be upgraded for higher benefit (at a cost to how much space in that trait they take up), and you can swap them out on the fly. So if you are using a shotgun and have shotgun damage perks, suddenly finding a much better automatic rifle, you can just swap out the perk cards.The World, while not the size of a traditional MMO, is LARGE. To make up for this, server sizes are a maximum of eight, and running into other players is a mix of extreme luck, or willingness to be where they are. As of this review I've only run across one other player (who dropped some stimpacks, waved and ran off). I do see invitations to join groups for various events/missions, though for the moment I am content exploring on my own.On top of that, there's always somewhere to explore. The appalachian wasteland is just as lovingly detailed as any other fallout game. Aside from main quests, the chances of stumbling across a side quest, or even a new daily quest, is fairly strong. Enemies near you are always your level (as long as you're not in A later-game area), so keeping level-matched weapons ensured you have at least a fighting chance.While I would never go back to a monthly subscription service. that lack of getting content behind payments allows me to enjoy this game. There's definitely much more to it that I have yet to experience, such as finding Nuclear silos codes, but for what I have done, I could not fault this game for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly... It's still boring. Fallout 76 released in 2018 to much criticism for being boring, lacking interactivity, and having little to no story. There was also a controversial in-game store that really sent players over the edge when it came to Bethesda's handling of the game. 5 years later and I finally purchased the game at the ripe price of $9.99 and decided to give it a go. Well, although many people say the game has improved I don't really see it. The story is lackluster. Essentially you are a vault dweller whose goal is to re-habituate the Appalachian region (West Virginia in Fallout 76). Much of the story is communicated through holotapes that you are sent here and to across the map to retrieve. After the 6th request to go find a holo-tape I gave up on the game. There was really no charm that Fallout typically possesses that sucked me in.The gameplay was overall what you can expect from a Fallout series. VATS exists and is useful, but you really do not need it. There's a lot of aim assist and I found myself easily landing headshots on enemies at distances that would make any military marksman jealous. Melee weapons seem to be stronger than guns and more useful since you do not need to scavenge for ammo. Sneaking around was nice but on many occasions I had enemies one floor above me detect my presence and come flying down a hole in the ground to put an end to my journey. Perks and buffs never made me feel more powerful, I just needed an upgraded weapon to do that. Multiplayer was pretty meh. If friends can join on the journey then it's sure to be a blast. However, most of the time I never encountered any other players as they were always on the other side of the map from where I spawned. All in all, I recommend you look elsewhere for a post-apocalyptic survival game (there are plenty others on Steam).

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is overshadowed by painful, time-consuming inventory management. You can only store a small fraction of what you are expected to loot. You can regularly find piles of legendary weapons/armor dumped on the ground after events because people just can't store their rewards.When you aren't having your gameplay sidetracked by hours of managing inventory, you are likely encountering very serious bugs. The inability to trade, getting stuck getting in/out of your power armor. The UI doesn't even work consistently... honestly there is a lot of very basic things that consistently don't work.If you can get around those issues you will likely encounter very bad game-play balancing and scaling. I decided to use automatic rifles for my build and they were never able to keep up with anything else while also eating through significantly larger amounts of ammo. With 3 different maxed-out skills you can take 30-60 shots to kill moderate difficulty enemies and you'll get maybe 10 bullets in loot for it. If you use a shotgun with no skills you can kill the same enemy with maybe 10 shots and you'll get 20 shells in loot. I remember running totally out of ammo at one point, picking up a random sledge hammer, and immediately going "oh wow, this is WAY better".The multiplayer elements in this game do not provide any meaningful interaction. The most someone will interact with you under normal circumstances is maybe emote at you. There is no text chat, and generally no way to communicate outside of voicechat for local and group. No one uses it. Under abnormal circumstances you will sometimes encounter people who are dead set on griefing/harassing/mic spaming. You often will be competing for resources/mobs when you encounter other players and will generally have your experience diminished in the process.Oh and the building is broken. Snap points refusing to snap, stuff refusing to be placed when it's shown as placable. Walls not rotating and facing correctly, invisible clipping issues preventing placement of objects. It's the worst building I've had to deal with since FO4. I think they actually made it work less.I honestly think the story of FO76 is sad. It's a game that has a lot of squandered potential that was crippled by bad monetization and mismanagement. It's come a long way, but it's still just not a fun experience. It's a frustrating chaotic mess with frustratingly limited inventory, frustratingly abundant and heavy items, and riddled with frustrating bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Fallout 76

_childDocuments_.review: Only 3 hours in, but I just don't want to waste any more of my time. It's like any other Bethesda RPG but with multiplayer and without a modding scene to fix the stuff that's broken, and random disconnects to spice it up. 4 years after release and there's still game breaking bugs (for example, I tried to cook some food at the same time as a friend, this broke my UI, had to restart to fix). Speaking of the UI, it's like they took the FO4 UI and made it worse. It's even less intuitive with absolutely random key selections like it was designed by someone who has never used a keyboard to game in their life, and for a bunch of it, there isn't even tooltips, like how to select different types within the categories in the camp building menu. They make sure to inject the shop into the options as well, though, making it hard to find what you can actually build, but pretty clear what the priorities are for the game. No fixes, all of the whale milking.There's NPCs and such now, but even the starting vault you spawn in as a new character feels more dead than any game they've made before. The story so far is awful, and to make that even worse, you need to do EVERYTHING solo despite your buddies being in the team with you and being able to hang out, but needing to do the same conversation multiple times because the game doesn't allow you to complete stuff together feels really bad. Why allow people to team but not do quests together? Might as well play fallout 3/4/NV side by side streaming what you're doing to them. Unless you get this on a deep, deep sale have a very high tolerance to bugs, pass this one, just play one of the ones they kind of finished and grab some mods from a third party instead of their awful in-game mod shops.

I want to be able to repair a gun with a duplicate weapon or through a vendor like in NV. Not to mention I was blowing through healing items like bullets in a minigun regardless of who I was battling. All in all, it was fun, but I don't know if it's worth continuing.

_childDocuments_.review: Played free in the 2020 anniversary weekend to see if F76 had been fixed.  Partly, yes, the bugs and glitches were far better than in the first year or so from launch.  But they are still there.  The game overall is a pale rendition of the Fallout experience, and this is immediately apparent in the opening tutorial where you can barely pick up anything from the vault and leave into the world basically naked.  Over the four days I've played Ive hit level 31 and I'm not much better off than I was then.  I've run out of Ammo, run out of Stimpaks, got no caps and no real way to get more.  Even though I have two power armour frames, im weak and only have basic metal armour underneath.  I'm quitting on Roses questline because looking ahead its just grinding ♥♥♥♥ uphill and I'm not in any shape to get through it.  Weapon degradation is ravenous, and this game is more about eating and repairing your stuff than it is about getting some badass weapons and armour together, because there isnt any better armour to get. Find power armour, well done its level locked twenty levels above you and all you can have is the bare frame. Every mission accomplished is replaced with more fetch quests spread far far across the map and running the world takes forever unless you dump everything and dont stop to gather or interact...fun.   The lag during combat is mystifying, and seems to only affect me, with the enemies always able to land their shots.  A pretty game, fun at times, but overall not worth the time or money.  Fallout 4 is still much much better, and Fallout 3 better yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally got around to playing and almost 40 hours into it I'm not so impressed. Sure, it's a new environment with the Fallout feel, the familiar gun play from Fallout 4, and there's lots of quests to complete and locations to explore. But I think I'm playing it from a perspective different from what the developers intended, that of the Lone Wanderer, the Courier, or the Sole Survivor. I play solo and I'm disappointed to find no available companion NPCs, which means I often end up over-encumbered, keep building CAMPs in random spots, and am running all over the map trying to complete underwhelming quests.One part of me wants to keep playing because it's Fallout and maybe I just haven't gotten to the better stuff yet. Another part of me is considering throwing in the towel and hoping for something better with Fallout 5, which I would cautiously research before getting. I feel that the point of the Fallout series is to have a fairly personal RPG experience in that post apocalyptic environment, and Fallout 76 isn't delivering well on that point to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, I really did.  Fair warning:  I'm not a big MMO fan, yet here we are. On top of that, it is pretty buggy and even a lot of the MMO elements don't work very well (join a party?  OK, but you won't hear any of the quest dialog...).  If you love MMOs, there are probably better ones out there.  If you love Fallout, play Fallout 4 or New Vegas again.

_childDocuments_.review: My life was over and this game saved me!!!I know I haven't played this as much as some of you, but this is my story.I basically was living in a dream state of being in a coma.I felt my life was content, when I was with my ex. We grew strong together, we became an unstoppable gaming force.We played, elder scrolls online. Together, we became legendary. Then on one gloomy night, the rain pouring from the gutters. I hear every splash of water upon the concrete outside of my window. She looks me dead in the eyes and says "You're not good enough for me." I can't even utter any words of repentance. I surely thought she still liked me, but maybe she disliked that our internet was slow. I mean it would buffer while watching netflix sometimes. But as my mind cleared she was gone.. I must had zoned out. I instantly call my internet provider to increase my internet speeds. "YES I WILL TAKE GIGABLAST INTERNET!" I shout. It's only twice as much as I was paying, but 5 times as fast! Surely she will love me again.WRONG!! It wasn't the internet speed, turns out it was my feet. See when I don't wear socks, my feet really start to smell horrid. Imagine a rotting fish stuffed full of two month old chicken alfredo (Not from olive garden). and multiply the stench of that times 4. And that's what my feet smell like, with just THIRTY minutes of not wearing socks. I was lost in despair. Not idea how to repair myself, my life or my smelly feet. I seeked a game to just ease my mind..I found this gem. I sat down, prepared a glass of water and a plate of chicken nuggets (Tyson brand). I ate a couple chicken nuggets dipped into honey bbq sauce and I opened the game on my PC.It loads. WOW!! I then shut down my PC, walk outside and the world has color again. It helped me realize how much beauty there truly is in this world.Thank you Fallout76!And thank you for listening to my story.
