_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 was created to answer the question of what a Fallout style game would be like if played with others.If all those stories you told your friends of the things that happened to you could now be experienced together.Well Fallout 76 answered that question, and it said it could be done, and with time and effort from both sides it has developed into a unique and ultimately worthwhile addition to the Fallout franchise.🔸 Fallout 76 is not Fallout 5, or a conventional MMO, (and it has not been advertised as it)🔹 Yes Fallout 76 had a bumpy start, and some issue still exist,It had bugs, it had limited ‘NPCs’ (too many would make it a different game)🔸 Have Bethesda addressed these, yes … mostly, and they keep doing so.🔹 They fixed most of the animations,🔸 They added quality of life improvements,🔹 They steadily increased storage space,🔸 They have added/amended, locations, events, game modes, enemies, NPC’s …Fallout 76 is not like previous games in a sense you are not a hero that can take anything they want, buy anything they don't have or join/lead factions with military level backup.You are in a world where things are scarce, settlements are few and the currency is less.You are rebuilding Appalachia.This makes FO76 a unique version of a Fallout game and out of the comfort zone for most of the negative review players.As additions to the game keep getting added the overworld keeps changing.New factions have settlements & outposts, and although loads of people wanted more NPC’s, the introduction of more takes locations that were once exclusively occupied by enemies and makes them ‘relatively’ safe. It’s only a few locations, but ones I used to visit often, and with rumors and radio signals from others Appalachia could become a little more crowded, and IMO this takes away from FO76's unique feel.They added more concentrated enemy locations, Bandit (Blood Egels) camps that are always fun to swipe out.🔸 Fallout 76 has a map 4x the size of Fallout 4,🔹 Fallout 76 has 16x the detail as Fallout 4,🔸 Fallout 76 runs smoother on the same PC than Fallout 4.🔹 Your in a world with at most 23 other players, it's not a MMO,🔸 Your death does not mean loss of progression,🔹 Your progression is not dependent on others or the server,🔸 Loot in containers or on enemies is instanced,🔹 Loot in the outerworld in first come first serve, 🔸 You can play it Solo (99% of my 500h are solo) (recent with Public teams, and its fun)🔹 Joining a team can be fun & beneficial, even when not fighting together,🔸 Yes there is a survival mechanic, but it is light,🔹 Yes you can build, and do so anywhere, and then move it if you wish,🔸 Yes you can launch Nukes, (with some effort)🔹 Yes there is a Vault 76 story, now with Settler & Raider stories,🔸 Yes they have added skill checks, (it’s on light side, for more info or reward)🔹 Yes there are NPC’s. The wastelanders expansion doesn't just add them to the new missions, but integrates them into the previous one and adds additional options for completion.🔸 Yes there is a PVP, although this comes into play so little unless you're doing the battle royal events.🔹 Yes you can team up with friends or others on the server.This offers a few additional abilities such as being able to build at allies camps, and free fast travel to them or their camp..But mostly it makes use of a lot of Charisma perk cards that have team bonuses and allows you to share perk card effects.With public teams you can set up an open invite to anyone and gain increased bonuses after playing with them for a while, giving more reason to team up than just adding an additional gun to the fight.Most circumstances don’t require teams to complete (or at least from my perspective and playstyle) but there are public events and big private events where teams become far better at handling and provide a great source for those stories you once told each other when playing solo.More of these kinds of events have been added, some with side/optional objectives where teams are even better suited to get the best rewards from.🔸 Yes you have a limited personal Item stores (Stash)This gets stick from some ‘players’ and doesn't need it.The cap has increased to double its starting (800) that is more than enough for late game play, as long as you don’t hoard stuff you don’t need.Inventory management is easy and a small part of the game.Knowing where to go for larger amounts of specific scrap, food, chems, water .. is something that will make your survival much easier (or you could randomly mouch about and be lucky). 🔹  FYI anyone that claims it is obviously doesn't play the game.The closest/only you can get is to buy atoms (that you can easy earn by just playing the game),To get repair kits (that fix your gear to 100%)  ignoring a huge part of the game to manage scrap (that with perks are cheaper and take gear to 200%)Keep in mind you can only get Improved repair kits from in game that take gear to 200%Any impression that you would/could use a kit in PVP is ridiculous.🔹 Enemy level scaling;FO76 does not have this, and that could be for the best as it's a bit of a double edged sword. Yes you will get better gear, and always have a good fight on your hands, but game progression through levels is negated (disregarding perks and items with buffs). And trying to resupply ammo, meds or items would become and infinite battle with no easy areas.I didn’t know if I would enjoy 76, elements of it were outside what I would normally buy/enjoy, but I went in with an open mind after seeing what it was going to be like, you know the E3 presentation and the Beta!I know this is not review material but it had to be said because there is a lot of misinformation out there from people that have played too little (if any) of the game they are crying about.In my honest opinion, Bethesda has done a good job here.Fine FO76  had a slow, bumpy start but it's growing into its own game that nothing else can match, and for the first of its kind it has done a brilliant job.I enjoy this game, this is why I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is still buggy and glitchy, barely worth getting at a discount, only get if its free or on a major discount.So after five years i finally decided to take a crack at fallout 76. I got it during the last black friday/cybe monday sale for 8 bucks or so. And after looking into other peoples reviews i kept hearing the same thing, "the community is the best part" and i 100% agree. The community is very kind to new comers, it isnt toxic, it isnt filled with griefers. Just nice people wanting to share the loot and help ease you into the game. But after that the game falls apart.As of right now over 5 years since launch the game is still glitchy and buggy. Although im sure its better since release it isnt at a acceptable state, especially for a company the size of Bethesda. For me personally at around 65 hours or so ive encountered tons of issues such as:Not launching or being able to sign in nearly every time the first timeMajor to minor visual bugs, such as "ghosting" where ill see the outlines of trees or building clippingHaving my character get stuck in the gun aiming animation, unable to heal, use vats, bring up the pipboy, or reloadClipping and falling through the world occasionally when using the cannibal perkGetting stuck in doors or other movable objects in the worldAnd encountering an insanely broke main story quest where im forced to fast travel away and back over and over and over again to try and fix broke npc path finding. So youd think after 5 YEARS they would have fixed these things right? Major issues that heavily impact players during the most basic day to day issues or even a major quest in the main story. Cyberpunk fixed itself, no mans sky fixed itself but not fallout 76. Other then glitches and bugs, the game is basic MMO stuff. Grinding materials, overly long quests sending you back and forth a hundred times, Basic ten minutes enemy waves as events, cosmetic grind etc. If your into that stuff youll more then likley have a good time but im finally hitting the wall and finally getting fed up with the game.I think if the best thing people can say about a game is that "Its fun with Friends!" or " The game has a great community!" then you as a company have failed. ANY game is fun with friends no matter how boring or bugged or simple it is. Having your community have to help and pander to newbies to keep them coming back isnt a good thing, but bethesda doesnt care. They wouldnt be going to reviews telling people they are wrong and showing how insecure they are about the garbage they put out. They would have made it up to their fans not gave them the middle finger and refused to give refunds, or leak personal information, or give a few bucks worth of in game currency to collector editon buyers, or put out such a ♥♥♥♥ game for a cash grab. _childDocuments_.review: Alright I've seen enough (My game time may appear low for steam, but trust me I've played on and off since 2018.) Fallout 76 hasn't changed with the addition of NPC's. Claimed locations for these NPC's still have corpses from the vanilla game everywhere with a few small exceptions. The NPCs now offer the exact same quests you would get anyway from the Vanilla game, but with a few extra steps, granted NPC's are fully voiced. The dialogue choices are a nice touch and do give some insight that they've tried to write some decent characters, but the choices are just an illusion that give you extra items if you have the right amount of stats. It's still the Fallout 4 style of dialogue, "Yes, I'll do it, or sarcastic yes.The world hasn't changed other than new buildings plopped down and the npcs just dotted around the map.Robot Venders are still the main source of trade in the game, I haven't checked yet to see if there are human traders in the main outposts, but there was a woman running a bar who sold drinks, so maybe that's the case.Glitches that have existed since the games release are still there, Enemies are still jank as hell and hard to hit, often requiring VATS to not waste ammunition, and melee is still as broken as ever. Enemies will launch themselves through the floor after dying, preventing you from looting them, and some new assets are completely hollow with no collision.I'll give this update it's fair shake when I have a few days off soon, but as far as I can tell, this is an update that is a year too late. This game is trash and adding NPC's is not going to fix the underlying problems with the aging and patchworked engine. Bethesda really needs to step up their game and make some hardcore changes to the way they do things. Otherwise, bigger titles like Elder Scrolls 6 and Starfield are just going to end up with the same exact stigma.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played since launch, only played a few hours at that time for obvious reasons. Just got done playing my first sitting revisiting Fallout 76. I played through Fallout 3, but no other FO games. I loved 3. Looking forward to trying out 1, 2 and, Tactics that I got for free with the steam promo.  I went for just over 8 hours today.Did the game crash? Yes, twice. Once at the end of character creator. At the end of character creator you are prompted to take a photo of yourself. There is a box with some options, one option is "show character - ON/OFF". When I toggled this, game crash (I never toggled it the 2nd or 3rd time). It also crashed one more time randomly when I was sitting in a chair.Were there bugs? Yes, in a certain building near where you fight Mr. Farmbots for a low-level event. I could hear enemies walking around and sounded like they were wading through water, but alas, no enemies, and no water. (Oddly I recall this same thing from like 2 years ago or whatever when I played for like an hour back then) I jumped onto a counter in the vault, having fun popping balloons, knocking over bottles, generally just wanted to wreck the place before I left and well, got stuck in a kitchen sink and had to remake my character for the 3rd time because it doesn't save until after you leave the vault. I tried to get out of the sink for like 20 minutes. Jumping, crouching, trying everything I could, was completely stuck in the sink. Also a dead feral dog that just kept twitching for eternity after I bashed it's mutant brains into a pulp. I felt bad. It was funny. SO, 8 hours, 2 crashes and a few minor bugs/glitches. Besides that, the game seems pretty awesome. Some people will argue that the graphics are "bad" or "trash" or "garbage" whatever gamer adjective you prefer. But tbh I thought the game looks pretty awesome. It's not the Unreal4 engine, but it's not crap, at all. The fog I thought was especially cool. I don't mind the bloom and all that, I like 'god rays'. I will say that night could be darker, it's not dark-dark. I like my nights pitch black tho. If you ever played SCUM then you know what I'm talking about, PITCH BLACK.   The building mechanic takes some getting use to for me, the keybindings are kind of weird compared to other games (I build in Ark-like, Conan Exiles). The camera was a bit obscured in the build mode, couldn't seem to fully see if wtf I was placing was going to fit right, and you can't seem to align things to the ground, it has to be flat. Boo. Materials seem plentiful. I was surprised at all I could build/craft by the time I set up my camp. (Coming from games where you harvest rocks/iron etc with a pick ax for a good while before you can build a decent amount of stuff) The 'pay-with-real-money' Atom Shop is kind of in your face, but it's all cosmetic so not too annoying. You will probably end up there on accident. I got a free emote.I wish the factions were more than just "settlers" and "raiders". Just the names feel kind of shallow and very "not-badass" Other than a few minor frustration outlined above, I had a great time. The fallout universe is here. It's beautiful, sad, bleak, death and turmoil abound. I enjoyed the holo tapes I found in the first town, they felt chilling and set the tone for me. The NPCs seem interesting, they are voiced and voiced well. There are other players and teams around doing their thing, interact with them, or don't. There's no raiding in the game it seems. You can't get at other players stuff...(EXCEPT SOME STUFF...I did jack some guys purified water out of his refiner things and took all the Tatu fruit in his garden. THANKS FLIPGUY123!!!). You can use their crafting benches too. Every base I came across was wide open. Very contrast to games where you have to worry about protecting all your crap with secret walls and deception tactics.Your stash box is linked with every other stash box. I guess it's cool, for me it's a bit immersion breaking but it's cool, it's whatever.Although I enjoyed the VATS in Fallout 3, I can understand how that system would be problematic in an online game, since it would pause the game to work in the single player FO3. I have a melee build going and had a good time smacking mutated opossums across the screen with a wooden sword-like board. Some robot enemies exploded into badass mushroom clouds. I enjoy the station animations and the cooking mechanic, crafting recipes on the campfire/stove is fun to me. I made opossum bacon. Follow me for more great opossum recipes. If you love fallout, you'll probably be okay with the current $40 price. There's a good chance you'll dump a ton of hours into it and get your moneys worth. _childDocuments_.review: With the release of the Fallout show, 76 and previous Fallout titles felt like they've just came out for the first time with newer members of the community giving all love and support for the franchise that had been here for years.Having pre-ordered the Tricentennial Edition on PS4 back in November 2018, Fallout 76's launch wasn't too great with the numerous bugs, lack of fixes and the horrible 30-FPS cap but despite this, I completed every main quest and reached to level 150+.Although it was bombarded with negative reviews, the 15+ players you randomly met all at the same time in-game, the amount of group photos taken, then coming to the nuked locations and helped fend off the Scorchbeast Queen was something to remember.Now again about the Fallout show, because of it, 76 is thriving and the great things that I've experienced back then is something you can still experience now - Seeing new players exploring Appalachia and gathering for public events is very wholesome to see.Although there isn't any cross-progression between Playstation and PC, I didn't mind starting fresh to see what's been renewed and upon expecting that, Bethesda delivered.It will always have that start where getting exp and going up in levels will be somewhat slow but it is still enjoyable  I am only level 79 after putting in 65+ hours within two weeks at the time of this review, I hope to go higher than my original character as the build making and the grind to get good gear hasn't bored me.If you are new, definitely pick this game up if you'd like to try a multiplayer version of Fallout 4 or if you've never tried out this franchise.And for the players who have played it in the past but didn't like it, please pick it up again because it is good in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is the best come back story of 2020 thus far. I despise Bethesda, but I can't hate what ended up becoming pretty darn good.The NPCs and dialogue are not Fallout 4 style. This actually has much more depth, more consequences (many of the story areas are instanced for you and you alone) and more dialogue options. The amount of dialogue that is locked behind skills and stats is insane. Reminds me so much of Fallout New Vegas.They didn't stop at just adding NPCs and quests. You can also have an NPC ally join you at your CAMP (home). There you are able to do quests for them. Once you are done with their quests, you can send them off and find more allies to gain and do quests for. I really enjoy having an ally at my camp.I have yet to experience the reputation system, but I will try and remember to update this once I get that far. I am nearly 10 hours in with a new character and have hardly scratched the surface of the new content. I know Bethesda went way over budget for this update, and it really shows.Performance? Well, I run Ultra 1440p at a solid 90fps. It never dips below that. Ever. I am also running, lag free, on a private server. The near 10 hours was from launch day. No problems. No bugs. Nothing. Just A LOT of fun. It did crash at character creation, but smooth sailing after that so I can't knock it muchI went from being pretty meh about the game, to changing my mind within a couple hours. I had an amazing time and did not want to log off. Keep doing what you are doing Bethesda, you can actually get this on a much better track. Please don't screw this up. Please.

_childDocuments_.review: Beside it's own launcher i have nearly 500 hours of playtime on steam. Got over 500 lvl on my belt and maxed, grinded every repu or playstyle combinations. Played single and with full private server of friends, did pvp and end-game alike. First of all let me tell you, you will either love this game or hate this. There're very few people who holds middle ground at this. And a tip from veteran, don't ever post anything slightly negative on forums, reddit or community tab, because that's when this "nicest community" will show it's bloody fangs. Don't do it, seriously. Fallout 76 has problems. But first let me state positive ones, because it's easy to list. +World design is amazing, a huge map with different vibes worthy to exploring fully for sure. Post-apocalyptic feeling that fallout gives still there and survival elements are kinda fine too. Due to being online you can see lot's of amazing camps and making one for yourself. Hell even better, you can meet up with people. People who play Fallout, people with same culture you have. +They're still updating game, fixing and breaking at the same time. I guess it's a positive too?For negative sides,-It feels like developers are somewhat clueless, despite of getting huge amount of feedback and ideas their implements are amateurish at best. I forget how many time i facepalmed after reading patch notes. Maybe because of this every content patch they also added terrible amount of exploits and bugs too. This process was so long and repetitive that people started to clap Bethesda for fixing problems, instead of thinking "we payed for a full game, so it's normal to have a full and smooth one" tons of critical exploits, cheats and dupes are still exists and will get fixed-added every single major patch without question. For example, you can farm best weapon for your build for 2 years without a luck or buy from a duper within minutes. You can farm reputation for a month or two or get maxed within a week with exploit. You can grind "season" for 10 weeks every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ day or you can use exp exploit to get it done. Simple as that.-Terrible legendary system, Let me explain simply enough. You need a "X" weapon for your builds. There's 1-3 star level of legendaries so you need to found a 3 star legendary monster, their levels are not consistent for half of the map so you need to find over lvl50 monster, you can get 1-3 star item in there but you need 3 star. Tired yet? No? Okay now hard part, there are rumoured over 400-ish weapon armor types out there. You just need to find your weapon type in there. So you need weapon, not armor. But it's not the end, considering that you slain a 3 star monster and got a 3 star specific weapon that 3 star means 3 talent of your weapon. There are many weapon talents and you need to get at least 2 of them right. Yeah. It's pretty hard. -Lack of end-game, you got simply two bosses. Plus because of that horrible loots system you will loot worthless pipes and poles most of time.-Events are lacking and repetitive.-Perk system is grindy and loathsome (did you find a locked safe? good now open your menu, go perk system, remove three card, put your three lockpicking after finding them in tens of perks open the safe, loot crappy things, now again put your old perks instead of lockpicking ones. They don't have a loadout system yet.-Due to "economy" and "server load" you got limited stash box, but if you pay them monthly you will get unlimited scrap box. -Limits, there's daily caps limits, gold bullion limits, legendary scraps limits and maybe few other i forget. Their excuses are "player should consume moderately and have fun" that's also can be translated as "log-in every single day like a slave or get your reward within a few years" Yes, that's it i guess... For me i'm a huge fallout fan and got every single game of theirs. It took 500-700 hours for me to finally exhaust every single piece of fallout love i stored since fallout tactics. Probably never gonna install again, never going to buy any of their products too. But hey! That was a fun ride. See you later vaulters.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the game that cemented my decision to never pre-order again. At launch, this game was under baked, over hyped, and lacked purpose or direction. It felt like a lazy attempt to cash in on the Fallout 4 assets while attempting to draw out monetization with yet another live service. I played for three months before writing the game off as repetitive and lacking any meaningful endgame content.Returning to the game a few years later and some changes have been made. Endgame has been expanded, though not nearly enough to keep your attention if you like variety. The dailies and weeklies provide some entertainment but finding people to run the instanced dungeon of the day is difficult if you aren't around just as the day changes over. The S.C.O.R.E board has some value, but feels like a slog in the middle. The events are fun the first few times, but get repetitive grinding them out every hour. All this topped off by the shadow of Fallout First looming in the background, reminding players that this game was launched with promises of no non-cosmetic items in the Atoms Shop, and that all mechanics would be kept as 'earnable in game'. All in all, this game was disappointing. As a single player, the game can lean much more heavily on the story to draw and keep players attention, but as a multiplayer, the mechanics are revealed to be clunky and the mechanics for things like crafting and fiddly micromanagement that comes at the endgame grind are painfully simple. The takeaway. Don't pre-order your games. Ever. None of the speciality items will live up to the hype and you will end up paying 70 dollars for a game that will cost 40 dollars less than a year later.

_childDocuments_.review: Like other players, I am a big fan of the fallout series but sadly cannot recommend this game at its current state. Upon launch on steam, I had to troubleshoot for hours on how to get it to run properly. When I finally got it working and started playing I ran into a myriad of issues in-game such as frequent crashes, server disconnects, and severe in-game bugs. When contacting customer support I was either just completely ignored, or sent a link to a help page with generic troubleshooting steps such as restarting my wifi and making sure my P.C was updated.Honestly, the new wastelander’s quest wasn’t that good. It didn’t have the most critical aspects of a fallout quest: consequences, meaningful choices, and memorable characters. Yes, you got to choose which side you got to complete the quest with, the settlers or raiders, and in the end, you got to choose whether you kept the loot or shared it with the settlers, raiders, or both. Your choice would affect your reputation with both factions. But this choice was an illusion, in the end, the most logical choice was to keep the loot for yourself and take the hit to your reputation with the factions as you could always regain reputation through the meaningless and repetitive daily quests. Your choices had no overall real consequencesOther than the quests the game has you take part in repetitive daily quests and events, all for the purpose of getting special armor or weapons. The game lets you complete these dailys only once a day to keep you logging in to continuously grind away the same missions so one day you could get some new loot which is pretty overrated anyway. Other than the questlines the game is pretty much the same as the iconic “Another settlement needs your help” From Fallout 4 on steroids.There are still tons of bug which make the game overall frustrating and unplayable and bug patches or updates that fix these bugs only come every few weeks and even these only fix a minuscule amount of bugs leaving tons remaining. In the future, if these issues are addressed properly then yes I would suggest this game, but as of now I cannot

I'm not expecting the gunplay fluidity of CoD or Battlefield here, but Fallout 76's gunplay feels like it's still stuck in that weird 2009-2011 era. The Atomic Shop is still the most vile thing Bethesda has ever done to this franchise (I take that back, that would be Fallout 1st) and... the caps limit. Why?This game does have some good things going for it though. Ever since they added NPCs back into the game, the stories and quests from them have been pretty good. The weapon variety is great (pipe guns are still a thing Bethesda adamantly does NOT want to get rid of for some reason) and the content updates have been pretty consistent and done well enough. _childDocuments_.review: I've had the game since launch and back then it was a buggy mess (that wasn't ready to be released) so I put it aside and thought "I'll give this one another try after a few years". Now years later, I came back to find what in my personal opinion is the best PVE-coop multiplayer looter/shooter on the market. It surpasses Destiny 2 by a landslide in my opinion. But I'm a huge Fallout Fanboy so having a sandox-y looter-shooter in the fallout universe is a real treat to me.In 2024 this game is fixed and i'm not just saying that, in over a 100 hours of gameplay I might have seen 1 bug which is very acceptable. The server stability is not 100% reliable but it's also not bad either i'd say 90% reliable which again is very decent to today's standards.Gameplay wise they added a whole new campaign with the arrival of NPC's which transformed the game not by a little, it is an entirely new experience if you knew the game from before the Wastelanders update. There's a lot of factions and all the NPC's are voiced by brilliant actors and the writing for most of it is very pleasant. They also have a bunch of RPG elements, like stat checking to give you different options to interact with things (inspired by new vegas) and although your own character doesn't have a voice (like in FO4) this game isn't a full RPG either, it's a shooter-looter with RPG elements. This doesn't mean the stories are bad though, I've been enjoying the new bits of lore this game brought to the Fallout universe and spending time in Appalachia is really enjoyable to me.As a final note, the game is catered to a more casual gameplay-style, you can do everything and experience it all without being a try hard sweat lord. The option to grind and being sweaty exist but it's to unlock very end game builds & armor/weapons which aren't mandatory to experience the entirety of this game. And special mention needs to go to the community which is one of the nicest and non-toxic out there, veterans often enjoy helping new players by giving them lots of gifts and help.Final Final note (lol had to mention this about their monetization) the subscription "1st" is costly but it's purely cosmetic unlocks and convenience related with the field tent, extra ammo & scrap boxes. I believe that it's worth paying for it, you get your money worth with lots of extra collectibles unlocks and funds for the store. But only get this if you are gonna play the game actively otherwise, the gameplay itself is 100% unlocked and you can easily play through everything without the subscription. I wouldn't call it mandatory and I wouldn't call this formula predatory either. Also don't buy any DLC's (they dont unlock gameplay) they are just overpriced store items. If you wanna give them extra money the monthly sub is more than enough, if you are in for the long run you'll unlock all that you want cause you even get store credit from achievements (without real money). Conclusion,The game is a very solid multiplayer PVE looter shooter (PVP is technically in the game but it's non-existent as everyone seems to be opted out) being in Fallout universe this makes it for me the best as I really like the Fallout universe. There's so much to do it's incredible to be honest i'm closing in to 200h played and i havent finished all the factions yet. I'd say if you go at your own pace and like to explore and wanna try to 100% it, you are looking at a 250-300h of gameplay easy.My personal score:In my books this is a 9/10 in current state. loosing the 1 point for the few bugs that are still present (but non-game breaking) I haven't had so much fun with an online multiplayer game in a very long time... this says a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: It is 1st/3rd person open world RPG.+Story+Graphics+Playtime+Coop/multiplayer+Weapon/armor modifications+Updates+Radio+Events-Bugs-Trading-Repetitiveness-Endgame-No chatMostly for fans of the previous Fallout games or anyone familiar with at least a Fallout 4 game.It may not be perfect but it ain't a bad game either, there is a lot of content to play through and game changing updates every few months. 50+ hours easy / time consuming  (may contain spoilers)The story was garbage at first, just listening through the holotapes scattered around and reading terminals..., this changed after the Wastelanders update which added human NPCs to the game.Now the story quests are 30% garbage and 70% good or better since the holotapes/terminals are still part of the questlines most of the time.Steel Dawn questline added in the newest update is finally something that we were waiting for, an actual questline with NPCs. I enjoyed playing through steel dawn quests and helping the Brotherhood of steel.Playing the game feels smooth, most of the hit registration problems were already fixed. Melee build is not very satisfying though in my opinion compared to other games and hitting something from 3rd person is sometimes impossible.It is pretty much Fallout 4 with some new stuff and multiplayer.But do not expect to one shot everything with your sniper rifle, unless you play a very specific build. It is not as easy to get overpowered compared to singleplayer Fallout games.Understanding how all the perk cards work can be a bit confusing at first, but it all makes sense in the end.It does not take the crown for being the best looking game in the world, but the graphics are on point. Character and weapon models look great. On the mid-high settings, the game looks amazing, and you can use the photomode to take some beautiful pictures that will replace the default loading screens.I always liked the Fallout radio stations, this is the one part where they did not go wrong.It is a big part of the game, unfortunately pretty much all the songs are copyrighted.Trading / currency and other limiters.Let’s start with the trading.You cannot trade in this game, you can only BUY and SELL you cannot trade an item for an item.Trading was a huge part of the Fallout series in my opinion and taking this out is very annoying.Trading with other players is all based on trust since you can only drop your stuff on the ground and hope that the other player does not take it and leave, I luckily had only a good experience so far.The second thing is the currency.There is a limit on how many caps, scrips, and gold bullion you can have at one time, I did complain about these in the past. All the limits were increased to a reasonable point and it takes a while to reach the maximum cap.Unfortunately, the main issue that the limits introduced stays in the game, the high tier items are valuable way more than the caps and are only traded item for item between players.It also feels like once you reach the endgame there is not much to spend your caps on anymore.Now for the third thing, the limits in general.I have to say that the stash limit is more than fixed, it is now double the amount it was when I have written this review 2 years ago.What else is limited?You are also limited on how many caps you can get for selling items to the vendors this resets daily, also you are limited on how many gold bullions you can get each day and how many items you can scrip.Thankfully these limits were also increased to twice their original value, and it is now way more player friendly.Nuclear Winter - R.I.P. was a Battle royale style PvPvE which was finally removed after all the time it was still in Beta and mostly broken. The 1% of players that played it cried about it in discussions but that’s about it.Fallout Worlds replaced the Nuclear Winter, in this mode, one of 5 settings applies and shakes things up in the Appalachia, for example, infinite ammo or increased enemy difficulty and such. The progress from the Fallout Worlds does not affect the progress in Adventure mode. You can create your own Private World with your specific settings if you have Fallout 1st subscription.I have to say that Bethesda did a good job at keeping this game alive, there were way more problems when I started playing it. A lot of the updates introduced new features and stuff.They made playing with other random players easier, by adding team groups.Allies are cool, but they don’t do much in the camps, they were way more useful in Fallout 4, in Fallout 76 they just stay in your camp and walk around.You can always play solo even in public sessions, the only problem is with the bigger events which are impossible to do without help from other players.Shelters! Added in one of the updates, they are actually pretty cool, all of them can be purchased without subscription now, I feel like they could make it easier to build inside since there is still a lot of limits but it is better than a camp workshop.Legendary perk cards are also a great way to reward players that have been playing this game for a while.I would say that all the updates were actually good and did improve the overall gameplay.I also have to mention the legendary crafting, which now allows players to have legendary Power Armor mods.Trading is still bad and pretty much does not exist.No ingame chat only voice-chat is just not good for multiplayer games.The game can feel empty once you complete everything.The co-op aspect is not as big as you might think, you will have to complete most of the quests solo.There are some game breaking bugs that are reoccurring way more often than they should.I was not sure if I should buy it, so I waited. Then it was in sale during a Free weekend, so I tried the game, played it for more than 20 hours in 2-3 days. So yeah, I would say it was money well spent.If you are deciding between Fallout 4 or Fallout 76, I would go for the Fallout 4 since it has way way way more content, the multiplayer does not add that much to the game, and most of the time you will be playing alone anyway.Sure, but can I recommend it to everyone? That’s the real question, I would say if you played Fallout 4 and liked it, you will most likely like Fallout 76 too, otherwise you better wait for some Free weekend to try it out and find if it’s your jam or not.Just because I like the game does not mean everyone does, I was going to buy it anyway, it was just a matter of time.👻

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I get it. At first, a ton of us didn't know what to expect. We saw stuff that didn't really suit our palette. We were looking for the next big Fallout game that we could dump a ton of hours into, mod, then dump every few months until you wanted to play again. But I see 76 as an evolving project. It took a lot of work to get the online working correctly, and if you weren't around during the early days, you might not be able to see how much better the networking and performance has gotten.I knew the second this released on Steam people would completely dog on this thing. That's fine. None of our opinions on this game matter, ultimately. But if you don't like this game, then I guess you can find something else. Steam's huge. You probably have a gigantic backlog that you never touched. But what does Fallout 76 offer? I guess first off, get some friends to play. This... Might be harder to sell to some people than others. Honestly, things are solid after the initial purchase. You don't need Fallout 1st or any of the extra crap. You don't need to buy Atoms either, since the game just gives you them. The stuff you buy with Atoms are mostly cosmetic or novelties. Nice to have, but you can totally live without them.Anyhow, Wastelanders (which is not a DLC, and never was planned to be) is making 76 shape up to be a lot better than it was at release. While yes, this is probably how the game should have released, I only want to imagine that it would have been a lot harder, and take much more longer to implement working online in Creation with complex NPC dialog, having more instanced areas, and still have the game run at a decent frame rate.Mod support was surprisingly more painless than I initially thought. Cloudy01 did a great job making a mod loader/installer that can also disable mods if you're going to be playing Nuclear Winter....Which brings me to the final bit. Battle Royale.So, I played it with friends, and the combat was solid. It's surprising how dead simple it was to get into, and unlike certain other titles, it's not a matter of out-scumming your competition. Rounds are short, and you can just click on where you want to spawn (of course, you'll get to see where everyone else has, making for some heated melee fights). You get the benefit of leveling your current open world character while you play, but there's progression you get out of NW. I didn't get far yet, but I figure it's nothing too fancy.Overall, 76 is decent. Get it on sale if you don't feel confident, but are still curious about it at all. The worst you'll probably feel is just bored. I think the environmental design is a treat, and maybe if someone whips up a SP mod for the game, people will give it a go. But otherwise, we'll just have to wait I guess. Who knows.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Run away if you dislike MTX, memberships, battle passes, and heavy RNG.I’ve played Fallout76 ever since the B.E.T.A. release on xbox one. A lot of players say that it’s had a redemption since it’s launch, while somewhat true, it lacks sustenance. Let me explain, Atoms are a currency used purely for the atom shop, you can earn them in game or purchase them. The atom shop started out as purely skins, but now it’s updated more than the game itself in terms of content. You cannot acquire atom shop items in game. Yes, you can earn atoms through completion of tasks, but why not just also add them to an in-game vendor? Some items end up being useful, such as collectrons that go and collect scrap materials, or a coffee machine that generates a canned coffee that can restore AP cost.Bethesda has become the master of creating a problem and selling a solution. A year or so after it’s launched they nerfed the spoilage timer on consumables, wait whats that! It’s a fridge in the atom shop that now decreases the spoilage of food when stored inside of it. While in game perks are more beneficial than the fridge, why do that? The same can be applied for stash space. Your stash is where you can put all of your loot. It’s increased over time to 1200/lbs but with Fallout 1st monthly membership, you now have a separate box for your junk and another for your ammo, with unlimited space! You just have to pay monthly to use it and not have to worry about those taking up stash space.Not to mention, if you want to play alone, you have to have Fallout 1st to enter your own private world.Now let’s talk about actual in game content. 5 years after release and there’s been 3 additional bosses added, making 4 total. They’ve had 2 major storyline DLC’s released Wastelanders (2020) and Steel Reign (2021). The anticipated Expeditions: The Pitt DLC (2022) which ended up being a Daily Ops 2.0, essentially entering an instanced area, killing stuff, and leaving. Which they plan on adding another instanced location with Atlantic City. All other forms of introduced content are quests that can ONLY happen when it’s in their cycle. Typically one/two weeks on, one/two weeks off. Such as Faschnacht Parade, Meat Week, Mothman Equinox, Invaders from Beyond, Nuka World on Tour, etc. Now with these events they do add really cool new items, but these items are only available when the quest is available. Not to mention, that certain recipes, plans or apparel have an absurdly low drop rate, meaning, if you didn’t get what you wanted, you have to wait until it’s cycled again. As well, the game is very mobile-game styled. As in, log in, do your daily quests, do a Daily Ops, and then doing an Expedition. Daily Ops and Expeditions to receive rare loot and legendary items, Daily Quests to earn scrip. You might run some boss fights but after you’ve done 100 of those, it becomes real repetitive, just like the above mentioned. But wait! All of that RNG legendary gear you just farmed can be turned into scrip, with a 600 daily scrip limit exchange of course (was 300). And with that scrip you buy legendary modules and you can re-roll your gear and pray to the RNG Todd God that you get something worthwhile. While it’s a massive improvement from just rolling your scrip randomly and hoping you get the right legendary effects on the weapon you want. Spending a quarter of your daily scrip limit to buy 3 legendary modules at 50 scrip a pop to re-roll a piece of armor ONCE, sucks. I’d much rather spend a daily scrip amount on a confirmed legendary effect, with most weapons and armor going up to 3* it would take half a week to get what I truly desired for a weapon, and 2 weeks for a full armor set. Hell, make it a weeks worth of scrip for one re-rolled effect and it would be a massive improvement.This is why it feels like a mobile game, log in, try your luck for an hour or so, get shafted, and log off. Really meant to show investors that X amount of players regularly log in X amount of time per day. There is no end game besides doing daily’s and hoping you struck out with RNG.Not to mention content that hasn’t been released, such as 4* legendary, expanded player trading, mods, etc.Don’t get me wrong, this game is fun to load up every now and grind for a bit, and you can certainly get your money’s worth when it’s on sale. But, it 110% has the potential to be an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game incredible? No. Is this game bad? No.Fallout 76 is a good game with great quests and solid yet stiff gameplay. The visuals could be better but again they are not terrible on max settings. I have had a blast playing this game from the Bethesda launcher and even transferring over to Steam. I really enjoy the aspect of playing through a Fallout game co op with my brother or joining up with randoms for public events. You can still play this game completely solo and I actually do that quite a bit myself.There really is not much of a grind in this game until you get to the endgame which you can ignore if you want. If you do want to grind there are factions to rank up and gear to chase. The legendary armor and weapons system it's actually pretty fun. The other grind would be the seasonal pass (it's free to everyone). You can grind dailies and weeklies to level up a pass and get cool rewards. I have never gotten to level 100, but I do enjoy getting the free items from the pass each season that I play.The new "The Pitt" has been great so far, and I am exited to continue going back to The Pitt and exploring and grind out those missions. Just a tip for people who are complaining about The Pitt update. Think of it as a new location that you can freely explore as long as you want (it even has a checkpoint system). I did this and took my time and explored everything in the first area, and read all the lore and listened to what the enemies were talking about. I found if you treat the experience as a new location and not some daily that you need to rush through as fast as you can. It is by far a more enjoyable experience. After you complete that the devs are now giving you a way to grind out those areas instead of a one and done thing which I appreciate.All in all, I really hope the devs continue to support this game. _childDocuments_.review: "Fallout 76" is a game that I regret purchasing on a daily basis. I used to be a "Bethesda" fan, I would play their releases as soon as they came out and thoroughly enjoyed myself, immersed in the worlds they created, with the only thing breaking my immersion being the immensely large amount of bugs their games held. Like with all of the previous titles, I was excited for this game, I'd bought it ahead of time, like I used to do with all of their games (huge mistake, never pre order again), and I played the B.E.T.A, I was not enjoying myself, and I still cannot believe I didn't cancel my pre order. I played the game for roughly 15 hours before I uninstalled it and never looked back, with the arrival of this new "Wastelanders" update which would finally add NPCs, I was excited again. However, I knew not to be too excited because I had been let down beforehand. This was another letdown moment, the game still runs like a 83 year old man in a wheelchair with Alzheimer's disease, dipping below 40FPS on literally any settings at any time, it wouldn't matter if I'd place my settings onto ULTRA or LOWEST, the game would run the same way.This isn't a hugely long in depth review of the content available in "Wastelanders" but a simple recommendation against supporting these developers and this terrible company. I cannot recommend playing the vanilla experience, which you will have to play until you level up to LVL 20 and unlock the level barrier for you to access the rest of the "Wastelanders" content. Is that worth it? No, because the vanilla experience is so awful, that I cannot recommend the game itself.I hate this game, I hate the graphics and the way it performers, I hate the bland song selection which is just reused from the previous Fallout games, I hate the monetization that people giving positive reviews seem to just forget about, and I hate the gameplay itself. It is so bland and boring that I could barely get through the first hour after re-installing it on Steam. I'll probably never play it again, or at least until the performance is finally improved, which I feel like is never.Score: 2/10

_childDocuments_.review: Like Fallout 4 with a more diverse world space (all biomes are unique and distinctive), more refined gameplay systems (real-time V.A.T.S., more perk diversity, a more in-depth crafting system where you learn plans or scrap weapons to get new upgrades, and better base-building (place anywhere, more buildable items)), and, the ability to play with friends.The main negative is that there are no mods which means once you've done all the quests and explored the entire map, you've beaten the game. (In my opinion trying to get an infinite amount of play-time out of a single game is unhealthy, so this doesn't bother me much.) Getting to that point still takes probably 100 hours if you take your time and explore the world though, so it's not like the game is short.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially avoided this game due to the disastrous launch, but decided to give it a shot after some of my friends started playing. To my surprise, I ended up enjoying it immensely... for a time. There are still many issues with the game, but by far the worst is the presence of hacked and legacy weapons. These weapons allow for the other players to instantly destroy any enemy in the game, from nearly any distance, at scale. Duplication glitches have allowed players to create a nearly infinite supply of these weapons. The presence of these weapons removes any sort of challenge from the game. Nearly every public event has at least one player using one of these weapons, sometimes making it impossible to even participate by eliminating enemies before a single shot can land. Bethesda refuses to act, possibly because they do not want to risk alienating part of their fanbase, but in doing so have ensured that the game remains unbalanced and stagnating. I have cancelled my Fallout 1st subscription, and nowadays only log in to complete the daily challenges, hoping (perhaps in vain) that the purchase of Bethesda by Microsoft will force them to change course. Until then, I can't recommend that anyone play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A tedious and incredibly grindy game that is merely a reskin of Fallout 4, and yet much worse than Fallout 4 from a gameplay and story standpoint. The constant stream of micro-transactions combined with a seriously lopsided progression system makes this game feel like a blatant cash grab. It completely lacks any soul, identity, and is nothing more than the epitome of the worst of the micro-transaction riddled modern gaming sphere we find ourselves in. A battle pass to incentivize daily logins, cash shop, monthly subscriptions all riddled on the screen as you open the game.Do yourself a favor and grab Fallout 3, Fallout 4 or Fallout New Vegas instead and enjoy Fallout as it was meant to be played. This game is nothing more than a soulless husk designed to extract money and time from people. It is boring, unimaginative and just downright not fun. Features and items that should've been in the base $40 game are locked behind paywalls. Gameplay is dull and unimaginative, there is a lack of meaningful choices that impact the story and the world around you, no NPC companions, no real dialogue, all core features of the fallout franchise simply gone in this title. The multiplayer aspects are horrid. Trying to play this with friends was a nightmare, voice chat in-game not working to talk to others not in our group near events not working. There is a great deal of lag during events if there is anymore than 4 people near it.  The events are just endlessly looped and you have to replay them just to unlock a "rare" item. The game definitely can not handle the multiplayer aspects at all. There are multiple "legacy" items that have since been removed and some higher levels will have, leaving you feeling very underwhelmed in a boss fight when they whip out a one-shot weapon. This means you're SOL when it comes to getting the drops for said boss.While I can somewhat appreciate Bethesda trying out a multiplayer Fallout experience, I think this was a very heavy miss from the studio with just downright insanity from a micro-transactions standpoint.2.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: -PROS--The world looks incredible, I love that the map has a bunch of different biomes that have all been affected differently, one area is completely burned out and charred, then you have lush green forest areas and swampy areas and quite a few others. Its fun to start on one side of the map and walk across it and just see the changes as you enter into a new biome.-Gameplay feels a lot like fallout 4 which i love , ESO feels nothing like skyrim or oblivion more like an mmo so i had a feeling this would feel more like an mmo rather than a fallout game but thankfully it feels like a fallout game.-Gunplay is great and there's tons of new guns that weren't in fallout 4, its awesome when you go out exploring and stumble upon a a cool weapon you've never used or seen before-Base building is fun and i really love being able to place your base down pretty much anywhere you want. I also love that you have to find the plans for certain things out in the world, it gives you a reason to just go explore and see what you can find-The new enemy types are great, the scorch beast is definitely my favorite and i hope it makes a return in future fallout games, its crazy when you're out exploring and hear the wings above you and you know you better find some cover to hide from this thing. I actually wish enemies weren't all around your level though because its more exciting to me to be out as a level 5 character and a level 50 scorch beast appears and you know you have no chance you just have to hide and focus on leveling up to one day kill this monster.-Tons of cool characters and stories found scattered throughout the map, its fun exploring places and finding holo tapes and notes left behind by people from before and during the bombing and getting a bit of history- I also love when you're out on a mission and you get the warning from the lady that someones about to launch a nuke, you open your map to see where its about to hit and I've been in the zone and when you're low level its the most frantic panic filled moment ever and you take off as quickly as you can to get out of the area. I've also had a very high level character on ps4 and running into the nuked zone is WILD especially the first time you do it, everything is on fire and burning and you and a bunch of random people are just blasting on a high level scorch beast and all kind of other crazy enemy types, its a very cool experience-CONS--Crashes happen but not often at least for me-Graphics could be better, they aren't terrible but they aren't great either-I dislike that every enemy is your same level or close to it, its too easy that way, i want to stumble on a level 30 deathclaw when im only a level 5 , it adds suspense and it makes leveling up feel more rewarding-Support for ultra wide is pretty much all there except when using power armor, the HUD doesn't stretch across the entire screen as it should so using power armor is an awful experience just like it is in fallout 4 so i pretty much avoid using itOverall its a great game I play completely solo and have enjoyed every second of it so far

_childDocuments_.review: Ive been playing Fallout 76 since the beginning and ive played all other fallout games as well. Ive also felt like FO76 was an okay game. Not exactly bad but not exactly good and it felt like something was always missing.  Bethesda has been slowly but steadily improving the gameplay, mechanics and bugs in this game. With the Wastelanders update, 76 finally feels like a true fallout game and id say i no longer consider just OK but good.The game retains its original main quests and also adds a new quest line involving the new NPCs. There's tons of random events that periodically happen across the map along with seasonal events bethesda runs.The main game mode, adventure mode, is PVPVE but leans more towards PVE. The game also features in depth base building, armor modding system, weapon modding system and player run stores,There is a subscription service that allows you to carry infinite "junk" or crafting material. Some people claim this is pay to win or pay to play but when i started playing there was no subscription and your allotted storage weight was only 400 pounds. Now the storage weight is 1200 pounds. There are also limtis to how much caps, scrip (legendary vendor currency), Gold (end game currency) and stamps (the new pit currency) your character can carry but unless you play 40 hours a week, it will take months to reach those limits. This game is great with friends, but can also be played solo. The only time i felt like i needed people while playing is for the boss events, but theres usually a ton of randos also doing the event, no one ever talks to eachother and you just shoot at the boss until it dies and everyone gets loot.

_childDocuments_.review: After 3200+ hours since B.E.T.A. I think it's time to tell anyone who's new or plans to come to the 76 universe my thoughts on the game and how it evolved in 4 years to what it is today. I'm choosing to write a review here because it's probably the only place Bethesda cannot delete any criticism, unlike the official discord and now the retired official forums where moderators erase any post that resembles anything else but a praise to their games. Since this will be a mostly negative review I'm going to start with the cons instead of the pros here:1) Communication with the player base exists as long as the player base does not criticize the features of the game as they were designed by Bethesda. After 2 years of testing the changes on live servers - with disastrous consequences - a public test server has been made available to the fans - but still the bugs make it to live servers and the feedback is mostly ignored by Bethesda. All in all it's a "yeah, we hear you, but we're going to do things our way anyway because we know better".2) Every patch is a russian roulette. It may break some minor things or may take out the game entirely for a couple of hours/days depending on the severity. There is no patch that doesn't mess something up.3) Development is atrociously slow. Took them 2 years to bring NPCs to the game, one year and a half to bring the BOS questline, another 2 years to bring the expeditions to the Pitt. The new content is also becoming less and less polished and feels more like "we need to copy something from the older fallouts so we can keep people interested". Lately it seems they do the bare minimum when adding new content, because sometime ago they put on the roadmap and they can't postpone it anymore.4) There is an overpriced shop and a subscription fee. Both are optional, but without them you'll be missing some important quality of life features. The shop items are rotating thus you don't know when something you like may be available again and that's how they create the fear of missing out, putting pressure on you to buy it right now. Some goes with special offers for a limited time. And regardless of the subscription, the really cool stuff will be available in bundles that can only be bought with real money. It's not quite 16x times the details, but it's definitely 16x times the cost or more if you're not careful.5) There is a new battlepass every three months. It's called a season. Every season we get daily and weekly challenges that force you to login almost everyday if you want to get the cool rewards and those cool rewards are among the last on the battlepass. Sure there might be one or two in the middle to keep you going, but if you really want the good stuff you need to finish the season. It's considered new content. Used to be cosmetic only, now they're adding actual items to it so if you don't wanna grind like crazy afterwards, you'd better login daily and finish your battlepass. They're designed to keep the players paying the subscription when there is no actual content being released.6) It's a looter/shooter in the end. The endgame is getting good gear. But unfortunately this too has a major twist. Welcome to Casino 76, where you will re-roll everyday - for a limited amount of course - the stats on your gear. Legendary gear has a maximum of 3 attributes. Let's say you need a good chest piece and rolled the dice, you got 1 good attribute and 2 crappy ones. Next time you roll you do not get to keep the good attribute, you roll again all 3. Chances are you'll get 3 crappy ones and get pissed. Getting a good set of armor with the perfect stats could take you years - I am not joking. Next game that I buy with such mechanics inside it will be a straight refund.7) Nerfs. Every year or so, Bethesda decides to break something willingly. In the name of balance, or in layman's terms, whatever the kids on reddit are crying about. I will not get into everything which was nerfed to the ground, like melee and now explosive. Combined with what I've said in the earlier phrase at no.6, after gambling for a long time to get your desired legendary, when you see it nerfed into oblivion you'll be one angry customer.8) Now we go into the dark side. Which is stricly related to the gambling mechanics on gear and broken balance in the game since day 1. The dark side is the black market, the illegal trading of items for real money. Regardless of any speculation Bethesda is in on it too, it is real and it's breaking the game. Hacked items, duped items, things that were never supposed to be in the game are available to buy and use. Hell, there are even legit items for sale. Say you need a full set of armor and you're looking for certain attributes on it. Will you spend years trying to get it yourself, and by that time probably the thing is obsolete anyway, or will you be tempted to buy it online ? 9) PVP. Many veterans of the fallout franchise are not avid PVP-ers, so I suppose this was implemented for getting the attention of other types of players to the game. It's something they've been toying with since day 1 and failed in all possible manners. From game modes that got scrapped, like Survival (free for all PvP) and Nuclear Winter (battle royale), to forced PvP in certain areas of the map. Also PvP is plagued by black market items, without a proper set of armor, weapons and consumables any regular player has absolutely no chance of making it.10) PVE. For a new player there is enough to do to keep you busy for a good amount of time. It's not as bad as it was 4 years ago, but the content is limited to some degree. The real problem is what the future looks like, new content is becoming less and less exciting. What do I mean by that? Well, the first world boss was flying. The second world boss was walking. Now the third world boss isn't even moving. See where I'm getting at ? Wastelanders brought NPCs to the game and it was a major and a good change, then the Brotherhood of Steel arrived but it was way less content there, next we had the Pitt which is a glorified dungeon and now they're bringing a very over simplified version of Nuka World from Fallout 4 into 76. And they'll keep doing that, put up the minimum amount of work into features as long as the subscriptions keep rolling in.Here comes the pros now:1) You can shoot super mutants with a MG-42 machine gun while you're chugging down Nuka-cola Quantums and flying in your power armor like you're Aluminium Man. Basically you can go do whatever the hell you want as long as it puts a smile on your face.Conclusion:Take it with a grain of salt. This is Fallout 4 multiplayer with pretty colors. And a ton of bugs. What Todd Howard said in an interview a while back sums it up pretty good: "We sold 12 million copies of Fallout 4 and now we can't reach those players anymore". And by that he meant reaching their wallets. They've tried with Creation Club, but anyone in their right mind would get free mods instead. 76 is the answer, it's where they can put up a shop and slap a subscription fee to a beloved franchise. Everything is done so you'll spend more time in-game and buy buy buy and then buy some more. That's why there is no mod support, even if they promised it a long time ago. That's why there are artificial problems created in-game, like the limits on stash size and the durability of items, so they can sell you the solutions. Of course you're not forced to buy them, but every year they tease you with the benefits of having a subscription and give you little doses of quality of life for free in the shop. Just like a dealer they try to hook you up and then milk you dry. So be careful, buy it on discount and use it at your own risk. Go through the story, because now there is one, have some fun, but don't make the mistake of getting too attached to it and have great expectations. You'll only be hurt in the long run.

Regardless this was when I no longer would recommend the game. Maybe for free, but to have to buy a base game in this state, then to ask for monthly dues for the most basic of required items that is really nearly required to properly play said game is just unacceptable.  What us early players begged for for all those months to their reddit slaves was finally given to us, but of course only for extra money. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it, It's come a long way since Original Release and all the sins they committed back then.That being said, A lot of the cool stuff is locked behind the Premium Fallout 1st sub which i caved in and bought for the NCR Ranger Outfit from New Vegas.Unfortunately, This kind of game is not my cup of tea and while it has indeed improved greatly and looks 10x better than any other fallout game i've seen even with mods the game didn't captivate me like normal fallout games do. The thing i like about Fallout is that sense of despair and loneliness but Fallout 76 feels way too alive and cheery for my liking. Settlers as far as the eye can see, No shortage of animals or robots and seemingly all the buildings survived the nuclear detonations relatively unscathed aside from a couple locations.It feels way too alive to be a Fallout Game way too many NPC and way too few threats, They made Meele enemies into a joke i just ignore them for the most part the only threatening meele enemy are ghouls cause the radiation damage. Deathclaws don't feel threatening i beat one to death with a boxing glove that does 5 damage per hit. Wendigo and the Alligator looking enemy were cool for first couple times i encountered them but after it became a game of "I'll slowly walk backwards and headshot you with my sniper rifle"The game is worth money if you're into that kind of game, I personally am not. Especially when it seems like it is running on Default or lower difficutly and whenever i played Skyrim or Fallout 3 - New Vegas - 4 i shot the difficulty slider to max. I really don't like the Card system for traits either.TLDR; If you like Fallout on base difficulty you'll really enjoy this title, IF You're anything like me and enjoy challenges? Keep looking. Can be fun at times, The Basebuilding was okay i liked the concept of farming recipes for buildings.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of hate online about this game.  I've even encountered people who tell me this game is ♥♥♥♥ without having played it.  These people are basing their opinions on nothing but what a bunch of loud dorks on reddit are saying.This game is awesome.Granted, there are quite a few bugs that can be pretty annoying.  That being said, nothing that breaks the game.  It runs like ♥♥♥♥ but if you tweak a few of the graphics settings in the game's .ini, it runs a lot better. The workshop/camp building system has been refined and made more flexible in comparison to Fallout 4 but the controls can be a little cumbersome at first. The survival aspect of the game can be a little difficult to manage in the beginning but once you start doing quests and establish a camp, it ceases to be a hindrance and can actually be used to your benefit.The atomic shop is a little bit of a ripoff but with Fallout 1st you get an amount of atoms every month that basically amounts to getting all the other features for free.  Once you really get going in the game, having Fallout 1st will make your inventory and resource management MUCH easier.  I'd go so far as to say that it's a necessity.  I haven't played many MMORPG's in my life but the ones I did pay required a monthly subscription fee so I'm not grumpy about paying extra money per month for some quality of life perks in the game.If you liked Fallout 4, you'll like this game even more.  This is an improved version of Fallout 4.  There isn't as much to the story or as many quests but it's a compelling game that is very fun to play.  The amount of detail that they put into the world design alone is incredible.  All the towns actually look and feel like they were real towns before the war.  Wastelanders really upped the immersion factor and you'll experience lots of random events with NPCs.  The amount of weapons and armor, along with the mods that come along with them, gives you tons of options.If, for some reason, you haven't had the chance to try this game but have been curious, I'd recommend trying it out next time there's a free trial.  It's very fun and if you liked the previous modern Fallout games, I would be surprised if you didn't enjoy this game.

Also in pvp... if someone starts shooting you, doesn't do anything... but once you shoot back and hit them it initiates the pvp and then anything goes. Can be fun when you're in the mood ;). I love how you can find plans/schematics and other cool gear and then sell it at your shop for other players. If you want to quick travel you can usually find someone in the area you want to travel to, team up and instant travel at no expense (usually costs caps to quick travel unless it's your base, a main event, or a teammate/teammate's base).People are pretty cordial. High lvl peeps always helping me out... throwing a bag of schematics at my feet, and some high lvl weapons that match my build. Won't say it happens all the time but it definitely isn't rare.Some quest lines are meh but lots of them are pretty fun and entertaining. Sometimes when I'm in a reading mood I read those terminal entries and it really does help with the immersion in this recovering apocalyptic world, buuut if you hate reading you'll still have a good time.All in all I love it. Sometimes I take long breaks from the game, years even, but I always find my way back.... to the wasteland.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on sale for $10. It was worth the money at that price. While I'm sure there was hard work put into this game, I just can't see myself playing it for any real length of time. It is sort of a multi-crew FPS with very weak base building elements. I was hoping that the base building would be cooler than it was. It just felt so underwhelming in every regard, especially getting the tiles to snap together right. However, the key feature of this FPS game is the breaking point for me. I'm not sure what is going wrong in the netcode, but my point blank range shotgun rounds miss ~50% of the time. It is like the server has already decided that the enemy hit me rather than taking my perspective into account whatsoever. It is super irritating watching my bullets spray past an enemy that should be now headless in my estimation. The less than a second of latency is really messing with the CQC feel. It should feel more epic like Doom Eternal, but it doesn't. For that reason, I have to put this one down before finishing. Lastly, what could also be improved upon is the gathering and environment alteration. Collecting wood and mineral from nodes that don't disappear is pretty unacceptable in 2023. I mean in ESO, the rest of the game makes up for this contrivance. FO76, not so much. Similarly, with the game being set in WV and therefore having hilly terrain, I would have liked to have seen an option to temporarily level the terrain where my base is, rather than using the workaround of stilted foundations.In the end, if you are paying more than $20 for this game at this point, you are doing it wrong. Anyways, that's my two cents.

_childDocuments_.review: So Fallout 76: Wastelanders has released on Steam. This game has done some things right. It looks better than Fallout 4 (at times). The world is more laid out and feels more open when compared to Fallout 4. This game has a better spread of color and design, and seems more inventive than Fallout 4 with its locations and enemies. The base building is somewhat refined. One of the biggest pluses is the quality of life improvements to  dialogue and UI in general. Unfortunately, this game is also still broken in fundamental ways this long after its initial release. Graphical errors that seriously hamper the experience abound, with shadows and textures turning static and messy. The AI struggles to move and function, oftentimes remaining a total non threat. Damage against players wearing the lightest of armors is negligible and does not provide challenge, especially when playing with friends. However some special enemies swing to the total opposite scale, dishing out sizable damage and acting as total ridiculous bullet sponges. Balancing is hard, but is not done well here.While only just being populated with friendly NPCs and quests (only some not involving listening to hours of holotapes and reading notes), the world itself feels dry and almost totally static. It feels as though the real story happened before the game began, and the player is simply listening to all the fun the real protagonists had before the player assumed control. The end result is a sad and disheartening glimpse into good ideas executed very poorly. The worst part is, the game in this state is much better than it was at launch. It has only just climbed up to a mediocre albeit poorly built game. I will say I have fun. Exploring new worlds is always cool, and much love was put into crafting the world. But there is no real depth to much of anything. Every note, quest, hidden story, ect. is made to be so shallow that no one would miss much by missing it entirely. The end result of this either ignorant or willful philosophy is a pretty world where nothing that has happened or is happening really matters all that much. Finally, relying on other players to form a more engaging story or roleplay is an interesting idea, but simply does not work. With a lot o Fallout fans being single player gamers, the whole feel is awkward and jarring when no one uses microphones, and everyone seems to mostly ignore or actively avoid other players. I have encountered other players who would emote, but the total lack of verbal communication leaves the crux Bethesda gambled on in this game totally flat.If you like MMOs, if you like basic gameplay cycles with mindless hoarding, if you like a fleshed out base building game, if you don't mind the poor optimization and storytelling, if you don't care that much for polish or game design, this game is only worth buying on a steep sale. And never buy Atoms, the premium currency, from the store. It's a terrible idea concocted to further a "games as a service" stance, and is designed to deprive or seriously hinder average players in order to drum up repeat purchases. It is disappointing and ridiculous that items in the base Fallout games from before now cost anywhere up to 10 or more US dollars, which translates into at least 14 to 24 hours of consistent progress in game. While you can technically save up these points for "free", it took about 7 hours of normally paced gameplay for me to saver about 230 atoms. Most items in the store can cost anywhere from 700 to 1400. The fact that these microtransactions extend to things like WALLS, FLOORS, CEILING TILES, AND EMOTES only further shows just how odd and alienating the whole experience is.It's not horrendous, but it often comes close to being so. I feel sorry for everyone like the dedicated designers and programmers who obviously put so much love into a corporate money grab. Buyer beware, and maybe don't buy this game to show Bethesda that these ideas don't translate into financially lucrative transactions.

_childDocuments_.review: Every serious gamer has that one MMO game that they keep coming back to over and over and over.  Maybe it is the theme that they love, or the underlying story, or the world building.  For me, the Fallout universe has captured my imagination more than any other video game universe.  It strikes a balance between the twisted and the hilarious, the serious and the absurd.  Fallout 76 has been much maligned over the years - and rightfully so in so many respects.  It was half baked in the beginning.  It does play on all of the tropey mechanisms that are typical to an MMO.  It presents opportunity to micro-transactions.  BUT, at the end of the day, it is Fallout through and through.  The building is a blast.  The RPG elements are great.  And the entire cast of factions that we have grown to love are present in this game.  For me, this game was about showing up for the lore and staying for the fun.  I play lots of other games, but this one always takes up a few hours of my week because I love the world and I love coming back to it.
