_childDocuments_.review: After over 500 hours and completed all the main missions, i have to say, this is really fun and addicting game. The game feels more like MMO than a regular Survival Game. The CAMP you built isn't tied to the server like most Survival Games, so every time you log in, your CAMP that you built for hours will still be there. The open world exploration is still fantastic as ever, a hallmark of Bethesda games. RPG element is light, but most missions offers multiple dialog choices that affects the rewards and outcome of the missions. Which is rare in Survival Game genre.The game world feels more alive since Wastelander update, you'll encounter a bunch of NPC trying to survive Appalachia, chopping woods, building settlement etc. as well as raiders.CAMP building isn't as big as in Fallout 4 but a little more robust.Perk Cards, Legendary items and Mutations really gives us quite variety of builds. Mutations are especially fun! Weapons, armors and power armors modifications are also improved as well.Atomic Shop are only cosmetics and most cosmetic items you can already get in-game without spending Atom in Atomic Shop. You can also get hundreds of Atoms just by playing the game.FO76 community is really one of the best, helpful and nicest out there.My complains are the stash is very limited to only 1200 pounds and the only way to counter that is to get Scrapbox by subscribing to Fallout 1st. There are some people that's good at managing the limited stash, but i'm a hoarder, and that's quite a problem for me. CAMP budget limit.No real mod support yet.Overall, this is really fun and addicting game. Most of my 500 hours i played mostly solo(I'm always a solo player), you can just do every missions and even most of the events, solo.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game makes me appreciate Fallout 4 a lot more.It's been out for nearly 2 years and yet it doesn't lower the base games price on release (Bl3 and Metro Exodus did) as well as it offers a premium subscription for a premium game. I can't give this a positive review, because the game shouldn't be this expensive for the lack of content it has and the paywall it has to get more content. I'd say this would be worth it for 20After playing the game again, 3 years after its release- I have a few thoughts.1. Base building in FO76 is incredibly complicated- the control scheme isn't nearly as fluid as FO4's base building- and honestly with the Desync from bad servers, the building is just over complicated and frustrating in FO76. How did they mess up what FO4 had?2. You can't adjust your game settings unless you back out of the FO76 session and go to the main menu. This is just a horrible design choice for a plethora of reasons.3. The Desync. Quests don't trigger properly when I complete objectives such as reading or listening to a holotape, building is painful with how unresponsive it is. (it can take up to 20 seconds for a wall to appear after I attempt to place it. And my internet is really good so I know its not on my end.4. The servers aren't reliable. I think that if you want to play FO76, you need to understand that it's not a "Fallout" game like NV, 3 and 4. This is a buggy, unpolished multiplayer MOD that can barely function properly. However, there is something cool buried underneath all the junk on the surface. This game has interesting in-game events and areas you can control. It has interesting lore and locations too. It just suffers from a team of devs that honestly don't seem to know how to make their game stable 3 years in. Don't buy this game unless you're willing to deal with all of the pitfalls to experience some neat moments here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be tiresome to say "If you enjoyed Fallout 4 you'll enjoy Fallout 76", but the fact of the matter is that this is a direct successor to Fallout 4 in multiple ways. For one thing the shooting and general gameplay loop of exploring, fighting, and looting is almost identical, as is the ability to build your own encampments. Likewise, although there are now plenty of missions with NPCs, the story and characters definitely take a backseat compared to earlier instalments in the Fallout franchise.Not to say there isn't worldbuilding; Appalachia is festooned with a variety of locations which are fun to explore and have little stories associated with them, and the size of the world is impressive. But the overarching narrative is weak and most characters you speak to aren't particularly interesting. You can play 98% of this game completely as a single-player experience if desired, and only certain end-game missions or events require or encourage you to act as a team. There are some limitations which are frustrating; the artificial weight limit on your stash box which can be partially "fixed" by subscribing to Fallout 1st (granting you infinite scrap storage and from December, infinite ammo storage) is a particularly sore point. But truth be told Fallout 76 is relatively tame in regards to microtransactions and most in-game rewards must be earned rather than simply bought.Fallout 76 is a generally fun and satisfying open-world shooter with an interesting world and quite a positive community. It has plenty of content to entertain players for many hours and compared to many MMOs, does not nickel and dime you while doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are two halves of the same story and can't really be broken up. Thus, I will be reviewing them as a whole.This is my favorite VN of all time. The story, characters, sound, art, world, and gameplay all come together to make something magical and I think a lot of other people- even those new to the genre- will be able to enjoy it as well so I’m just going to gush about it and hope that convinces you to try it.Overall, the story will take you about 80 hours to get through on your first go. It seems like a lot, but that time is used very effectively. The characters are organically built up and the way I got attached to them over time is something I’ve only really felt the likes of in the original Mass Effect trilogy. The world gets very fleshed out with both ancient secrets and more mundane details that make it a very rich, interesting place to be. The story takes its time setting up big scenes so they hit like a truck and then paces itself with more lighthearted moments like wannabe Robin Hood pitching gold bars through people’s windows or giving a catgirl a suggestive backrub or getting drunk and stupid with your bros. Then it’s back to political maneuvering, destiny, war-crimes, mecha Godzilla battles, and suffering.The 2D artwork is absolutely gorgeous. The style is distinctive, the artists actually know anatomy, the sprawling landscapes make the world come alive, and the coloring is superb. The 3D sections were designed to run on the Vita so they’re chunky, but they don’t really distract. The screenshots can tell you more about this than words can, so I’ll move on.I still listen to the soundtrack on Spotify on a regular basis. Not every track is fully orchestrated, but even the parts where they didn’t splurge on the production values have excellent compositions that pull you further into the mood. When Utawarerumono pulls out all the stops, it won’t lose to any other video game OST and the way those songs are placed elevate the already good scenes into another world. It almost feels mean at some places. Like, I’m already an emotional basket case, why do you have to rob me of any semblance of dignity I have left by putting that on? On top of that, you have great voice acting for every line in the game. My only complaint about the audio is that one track, Sadame, is underused for how good it is.Utawarerumono has tactics gameplay sections but they’re by no means the main attraction since they only make up 10-20% of the playtime. They’re not going to dethrone tactics giants like Disgaea, but that’s not their job. Their job is to compliment the story, bring you into the action, and break up long sections of reading. For that purpose, they do quite well. If you’re a tactics veteran, there’s enough depth and polish to keep you entertained to the end. If you’re a tactics noob, there’s a turn rewind feature that will make sure you get through just fine. For major encounters, the gameplay is integrated surprisingly well with the story, and the final bosses of each part are made with a lot of care and extra touches so they don’t lag behind how bonkers the story is going.(Truth) This part is the non-stop emotional roller coaster. I can’t keep track of how many times a scene floored me. Prepare for a treat. Oh, and as a tip, when you get to the super obvious final boss, make sure you have the next 6 hours free because once you start nothing is going to be able to pry you away from the screen until you’re done.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Truth aims to provide a satisfying conclusion to the many plot threads set up in Deception, and it does it masterfully while also being a perfect tribute to everything that came before. The gameplay is mostly the same aside from new characters and some additional moves and skills for returning characters. One neat feature is that the game allows you to carry over some items from the previous game which makes the experience easier. As my friend put it, The soundtrack for Deception is already a treat for the ears, but the additional tracks in this game pushed it to one of my favorite video game soundtracks. And if you’re a fan of insert songs in key moments, get ready cause this game has a feast waiting for you.There isn’t much for me to say on the story because my words cannot do it justice. This entire trilogy is an experience, one that will have a special place in my heart for a long time. “Catharsis” being one of the features listed in the Steam page is no joke.The entire final battle made me have what I could only describe as an ethereal experience. And despite being one of the happiest endings I’ve read, this game made me cry more than I could remember in the last year. You will not regret a single moment of investing your time into the world and characters.Utawarerumono is my favorite series of Visual Novels ever. The entirety of Truth is one roller-coaster of emotions and by the end, it wrung out every last tear it could from my soul. All in all, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game and the trilogy as a whole to new fans and veterans of the Visual Novel genre alike, as well as anyone else that is curious on how “Catharsis” can be an actual game feature.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to Mask Of Deception. It is undoubtedly necessary to play the previous game for the best gaming experience. This game can be said to have reached the peak in the game plot, presenting a shocking epic story. The main storyline of the game, as always, is very long, but despite this, there are still many plots and characters that are handled too hastily, while some other parts take too much time to describe. Frankly, I personally think it might be better to split this game into two more games. The game's music also brings players a great gaming experience as always.Nonetheless, this time the game's gameplay is arguably terrible. As a visual novel game with RPG strategy as its selling point, this RPG battle made me feel inferior to the previous one in terms of experience, and even the unreasonable design of several later battles was embarrassing. In the course of the game, the number of vicious bugs encountered is much more than that of the previous game.All in all, I would recommend this game to fans of the series, it won't disappoint you in terms of plot. But in terms of gaming experience, this game can be said to be quite unsatisfactory.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Best gameplay of the trilogy, shakiest story of the trilogy, longest game in the trilogy, and a must-play if you enjoyed either of the first two.Each Utawarerumono game has its strengths and weaknesses, but it should be safe to say that if you enjoy one, you may as well play them all. However, they shouldn't be played in any order. Mask of Truth practically REQUIRES that you've played both previous games; very little of the plot will make any sense if you have not at least played Mask of Deception. Also, Mask of Truth allows you to transfer over a save file from Mask of Deception, a la Arc the Lad 2 or Fire Emblem Radiant Dawn. Mask of Truth is the longest of the trilogy, by a wide margin. While Prelude to the Fallen took me around 21 hours to complete, Mask of Truth's took me 43 (33 hours on the main campaign + 10 hours on the postgame). It's certainly one of the longest games I've played recently. At times, the length was a problem. I felt that there were many scenes which could've been drastically cut down, and they would've been better. In particular, the Nakoku arc took too long, and the entire ending sequence lasted longer than it probably should've. The main villain's motives were questionable; the game doesn't provide a compelling reason why he waited until the final act to play his hand. There's also a part in the final act where the characters talk about why they should NOT bring any soldiers to the final area... Five minutes later, you see that they brought soldiers to the final area. Some stuff in the game doesn't make much sense.Many battle/war scenes are predictable anime fare: you have the enemy on the ropes, but then the enemy activates some super secret power, but then an ally arrives at just the right moment to thwart the enemy. We've all seen it a hundred times before. I get the sense that the writers of Utawarerumono were more adept at writing comedy/slice-of-life than they were at writing wartime SRPG stuff. This is another reason why I feel that Mask of Truth is the weakest of the trilogy, storywise. While Mask of Deception was mostly a whimsical comedy, Mask of Deception is mostly a wartime drama. The former allowed the writers to play to their strengths more. As another point against the game: Fumirul's entire character was entirely pointless and added nothing substantial to the story. On the other hand, Mask of Truth features the best gameplay of the trilogy, and it's not even close. BP allocation is more complex now. Battles have multiple phases now. Enemies actually scale well. AI is improved. The postgame Dream Arena battles absolutely trounce anything that the first two games offered. Dream Arenas #12, #14, and #15 were especially enjoyable and actually made me think. I appreciate SRPG battles that make me think. Completing the trilogy was a fun experience. I'll have to keep an eye out for other hybrid Visual Novel/SRPGs in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, if you’re not familiar with the Utawarerumono series, you should start by playing through  first as it otherwise will spoiler the whole experience. .After playing Mask of Deception, I knew that Mask of Truth will very likely not let me down, especially since many people assured me that this entry focuses even more on its story. Besides, the prequel just left too many mysteries unsolved, so that I couldn’t wait to get to know the whole story. And of course, the cast is too adorable so I was delighted to read more about them and even if the story ends up being disappointing, I could still have fun with the events that revolve around the characters. Luckily for me, the story, as well as character development, is splendid here as well.Usually, I do give a summary of the story so the reader knows what they’re getting in, but in this special case, I’ll refrain from that as only those that finished Mask of Deception will probably read through this review. And those who didn’t won’t get spoiled. That being said, Mask of Truth directly follows the events after its prequel and a bit lengthier although that only means that there is more room to develop a proper storyline. Other than being the last half of the game, it becomes obvious that both games are meant to be played together and could as well be seen as a huge visual novel overall.Although there is a brief explanation of the storyline in the previous game in Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth, it only has the purpose of refreshing the reader's memories in case it was a while ago they last played Mask of Deception. Of course, just the summary isn’t a replacement for the previous game since the whole character development is missing here and hours of gameplay cannot be replaced with a brief summary. Plus, I can say that the experience definitely wouldn’t be the same when I didn’t get familiar with the characters first, even if that meant I had to go through a lot of hours just to read slice-of-life scenes. After all, the player wouldn’t understand the relationship of the cast otherwise.That being said, Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth does seem to only contain minor differences compared to its prequel. I heard that this entry is supposed to more story-heavy and whilst I certainly do agree on that statement, there are still a lot of slice-of-life moments implemented in this game, especially in the beginning. While I couldn’t wait for the story to unfold, I enjoyed that I still got my precious comedic moments with the whole cast although our dream team isn’t together the whole time. There is a similar pattern available here as Mask of Deception started light-hearted as well, only to catch its reader off guard with the story-heavy elements.Talking about the story, whilst I already found the prequel very emotional, this game even managed to surpass it. It hurts the most when I notice how close the cast is when something bad happens to them, yet it was inevitable. That’s the reason I really do appreciate the fluffy moments in the beginning since it only makes its reader getting more attached to the characters – once again. The good thing here is that I found out new aspects about the cast even though I thought I already knew everything about them after having played through Mask of Deception which made me fall in love with each of them a second time.After the end of Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, I was hoping that Mask of Truth was going into a slightly different way. By that, I mean that the relationships of the characters would become.. well more romantic. Sadly, romance wasn’t one of the main genres at all although it does indeed get more romantic in this entry. It’s very minor though, so a change is barely noticeable although that could mean that the character development is so well executed that explanations regarding the character’s relationship weren’t necessary at all. After all, there were way bigger issues to deal with than romance ones although it was heartwarming when they started to notice how they do feel about each other.The main focus in Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth would be the story, especially in the latter part of the game. I found that this entry even felt gorier than its prequel. Although there isn’t an explicit and detailed presentation, there seems to be more blood spilling here. The reason is probably that the whole game takes place during the war, yet I still found that the events were displayed, well.. redder than I expected. Even when unknown characters died, it made me feel quite uncomfortable, but that’s actually a good thing as the whole theme is supposed to make its reader feel rather gloomy since war isn’t exactly a pleasant thing.Graphic-wise, Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth looks exactly like its prequel: Pretty, beautiful and gorgeous. The only change that I noticed was that the game is divided into sections and when completing one, a menu pops up that lets its reader use their BP points, do different kinds of battles, equip their party members with items or simply save their progress and much more. I liked this menu because I could conveniently spend my BP very often, which I admittedly forgot way too often in Mask of Deception since it does pop up right before a battle as well. You see, the issue with the prequel was that the menu didn’t pop up often during the playthrough. When the player progresses with the story the icon next to this option also hints whether there are different events to go through, a battle or just a longer part of just reading.Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is a satisfying conclusion that answers a lot of mysteries that were still left unknown in Mask of Deception. Both games should be played together, and those who played the prequel will know what to expect of this game. In the beginning, there are still a lot of fluffy moments although the story will get serious and emotional soon enough. Like the previous game, the battles are engaging and greatly helped with the immersion since it fired me up even more and made me feel like I actively helped the characters out. All in all, Utawarerumono is a series that should be played by everyone who enjoys a good story-heavy game fueled with plenty of slice-of-life elements, plus an adorable cast.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR don't sleep on this title.  Despite being someone who avoids visual novels as a rule, I cannot recommend this game highly enough.As a player I tend to avoid the visual novel genre.  This game (and its predecessor) are most certainly visual novels first.  The vast majority of your time will be spent reading text and letting you choose which sections of the text you will read next.  For my part I typically gravitate towards games that are more focused on delivering their story through solid game play.  I remember going into mask of deception with more than a little disappointment when I realized what I'd just gotten myself into, and I wasn't expecting the experience to leave much of an impression when I was done.  That being said, this series absolutely blew me away.  Since I'm a game play guy I'll start with that.  Combat in this game is highly nuanced and provides the player with a wealth of strategies that can be employed while keeping the superficial mechanics fairly simple on the surface.  Characters interact with their targets through the use of "Action Chains" which can require the player to time a button press or hold a button and time the release (or a combination of these 2 inputs) each with their own visual cues.  As your characters level up they can perform longer chains with more inputs that are, in most cases more effective.  Surface level strategy requires the player to select the appropriate action chains to use while positioning their characters advantageously.  But as most veterans of the series will tell you there is MUCH more to it than that.  Additional mechanics that can (and in certain encounters MUST) be exploited are: hidden inputs for action chains, action chain cancelling, elemental type advantages, Overzeal (kind of a burst mode for each character) management, passive abilities that significantly impact combat, equipment management that drastically alters your tactics, facing and positioning, counters, stat allocation, and status manipulation.  These mechanics give this combat system a truly impressive amount of depth, and while the game does a solid job of introducing each of these systems to you, it's up to you to master them.  Each character in your roster plays VERY differently, but each character also has enough variety in their tool kit to work well with whoever else you bring to a fight.  Team tactics are a must for the endgame, and the sheer volume of strategies the player has at their disposal does more to recommend this combat system than anything I've seen elsewhere.  Do not be fooled by the fact that this game is a visual novel.  The combat system is one of the best I've seen in a long time.  As far as the story goes, I'll simply say: get ready to feel things.  For the most part the narrative is fairly lighthearted until all of a sudden it very much is not.  The ending of mask of deception hits like a truck, and mask of truth somehow manages to improve on even that.  The plot is well crafted, loose ends are tied up appropriately, and characters are well defined and act according to their nature.  While the story has its silly moments (and no small amount of fan service), it never feels arbitrary, and it serves to shift the tone away from what is actually a deadly serious narrative.  This series is amazing, and I hope to see more work from this developer on Steam in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be alarmed by the playtime, I've finished both games on the PS Vita and bought them on PC because I just love the series so much.This is sort of a sequel to my Mask of Deception review as much as the game itself is a direct sequel, you should read both to get the full picture.Man, where to even start with Mask of Truth..... Mask of Deception ends on a brilliant sequel hook holding amazing promise, and Mask of Truth delivers IN SPADES on that promise. Like I said in my other review, by the end of it all, it almost feels like Mask of Deception was just a massive prologue for what's to come. And Mask of Truth is simply amazing.... The story here is a lot more action-packed (though there are still the classic "slice-of-life" moments the series is known for) and there are a lot more battles. The gameplay has some adjustments that make it feel better to play overall, and some neat new mechanics, it's very solid overall.There's not enough that can be said about Mask of Truth, but at the same time, I can't really say too much without spoiling it all. The very beginning of this game is already a DIRECT sequel to Mask of Deception's ending, which is a huge spoiler in and of itself. All I can say is that this game takes all the qualities of Mask of Deception, and turns them all up to 11. Mask of Deception laid the groundwork that made Mask of Truth possible, and this game absolutely does not disappoint. I already loved it since the first game, but It's here that the series TRULY shines the brightest.Haku is my absolute favorite protagonist out of any game, the development he goes through here is absolutely INSANE. And Kuon is also my favorite heroine, she's such a complex character with a wealth of emotions.It is my absolute favorite game of all time, and the best one in the series by far, that ended the trilogy in the most satisfying way possible. It's really THAT good.I really don't have enough words to put on this review at this point that wouldn't be repeating myself, and there's not much more I can say without actually spoiling stuff, so I'll just finish it by saying...I love Utawarerumono so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not really review games, but I cannot skip this one. Finished this, and Mask of Deception on consoles, bought on Steam to replay it and be able to review/recommend it. If you are not a fan of text heavy games/VNs but want to try at least one in your life - please choose Utawarerumono series. Fantastic story packed with feels, phenomenal music I still listen to every day, lovable characters, beautiful art, has actual gameplay too, so it's not just reading. It will make you smile, laugh, and cry. It was also made before the whole political correctness fad kicked in, so expect some saucy jokes! I cannot recommend it enough; one of the best things I have experienced in my life. Play in order: Utawarerumono (2002 version or its remake Prelude to the Fallen) -> Mask of Deception -> Mask of Truth. Do NOT start with this one. I promise you will not regret it.Rest in peace, Keiji Fujiwara.

So here the cast sort of just acts like Haku is still there in a wink wink sort of way most of the time even though they don't know it. This in turn made some of the stages pretty difficult. You aren't going to steamroll the game like the first or second.Unpopular opinion but I liked Mask of Deception better. No one can blame you for not wanting to suffer through the long and slow slog that MoD is.Disclaimer:I've already finished the game on both vita and PC. It took me about 80 hours of slow reading to finish main story for the first time, but i've skipped nearly all text on PC and just got all achievs. Hence the "short" 35 hours time.---Review:Follow the epic sci-fan tale of  Hakuoshtor and his mindless followers to reclaim  Yamato . Shed liters of tears with Jesus as he struggles to deceive not only his people, but himself as well, of not being a lazy asѕ drunkard in one of the most recent Visual Novels to join the top ranks of big names like Steins;Gate, Clannad, Fate What/ever, Muv-Luv and Fata Morgana.Honestly, there's a lot more to the story but spoilers are plenty. The short description above only illustrates the setup that Mask of Deception left us with, which is not the biggest part of the game (but Haku's sacrifices for his dead brothers makes it the most beautiful). The story potential and all the mysteries that MoD gave us with its ending events weren't left to waste, and MoT only gets better. Hurray for not spending dozens of hours with pointless slice of life!The translation is one of the better ones i've read in JRPGs, you can cleary notice that it was done by people who knew and cared for the Utaverse. Voice acting is good, but Hakuoshtor's forced voice sounds a bit silly, especially during emotional scenes, but it's bearable.The PC port is quite good as well and i didn't run into any problem during the whole game. Actually, the port is so faithful to the console original that we're stuck playing at 30fps with upscaled assets from 720p up to 1080p. Being a VN, that shouldn't be a huge issue... but the strategy RPG parts of the game require proper timing, with visual/audio cues, for landing critical hits and the 30 fps doesn't help much there. There aren't many SRPG parts compared to the text walls, but they were given proper care for fun, and with a good balance and a bunch of mechanics that you'll actually have to use to see any success... unless you exploit Haku and Fumirul's Overzeal loop. Oh and uh, there's mouse/kb support.Pros:+ Amazing story. No wonder it is so highly praised.+ Translation is pretty good as well, but some terms/names could've gotten a better work.+ Combat is well thought mechanically, and you can fast-forward the animations.Neutral:* Cliche anime characters.* Soundtracks can range from really good original songs to some generic sounding ones, but it's fine overall..* Port is fine, but locked @ 30fps with 720p assets. Shouldn't matter much though.Cons & nitpicks:- The third part of MoT is a powercreep-fest and isn't as interesting as the others.- All the supernatural crap, like the thing about masks turning you into Ultraman/Kaijuu, are so silly. Sometimes it feels like an edgy version of The Mask.- Cringy shounen battles.- Magic or a magical being will solve/screw anything that can't be explained with pseudo-science.- Too many OP chars in the story. Uta1 chars are op just for the sake of them looking cool for the fans, but it's stupid lol.- Protagonist has a terrible time trying to do some sort of "batman voice".- Some of the party members sole reason to exist is to be convenient for the story.- There's always that scene where everyone will encourage the MC, or the other way around, before anything remotely important happens.- The main villain.- Maroro.-  is a dicк.- Anyways, as you can see above, my issues with the story are mostly typical anime things, and Uta2 is still one of my favorite VNs/SRPGs.May the Lord  be with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Not everyday you come across something that is truly special enough to change certain aspects of your life. Even more so, when it's a video game. It would be a disservice to consider this trilogy as anything but that. I was fortunate enough to go through the entirety of the trilogy without getting spoiled and I can confidently say that this is one of my most favourite experiences with any form of media. The final third of Mask of Truth is the stuff dreams are made of.Haku has straight up become my most favourite protagonist. The main cast of Prelude to the Fallen will always have a special place in my heart, but the main cast of both the Mask games will be the new standard against which I will judge a main cast of characters hereon. They truly are special and I deeply mourn the fact that I won't be able to spend my time with them again in the near future. I was beyond satisfied with the ending of the game that managed to provide an excellent conclusion to the protagonists titanic character arc. I couldn't have hoped for a better ending. The final stage/battle is one of the greatest final stages I have played. It's up there with the likes of 13 Sentinels Aegis Rim final stage. Towa Ni is such a precious song, that perfectly complements the overwhelming emotions running throughout the final stage. Many a tears were shed.If White Album 2 didn't manage to convince me about Suara, this trilogy certainly does and there's no Japanese vocalist out there whose songs flood my spotify playlist as much as hers does. I can never hear Kimi ga tame and Koi Yume without tearing up a bit. Nuedori is my most favourite opening song of any game and within a month, I have listened to Rakujitsu no Toki on repeat for over a thousand times. The VA for everyone was top notch, but Haku's is the best voice acting I have seen in a game. The gorgeous artwork of the CGs in this game are second to none, and most of them are going straight into my desktop wallpaper list.As it is always with such memorable stories, I wish I could forget it all and start again from scratch but I am truly grateful for this game which has given me so many wonderful memories, stories, songs and characters to cherish forever. I will never forget this, this joy of having gone through such an epic. Words fail me, in trying to justify the long lasting impact this game is bound to have on me, and I will eagerly look forward to the Aquaplus 30th anniversary next month...hoping, praying that we get even more Utawarerumono content than that was promised. I wish for that, with all my heart.

involved in an all out war while uncovering the secrets of yamato. all the foundation built in mask of deception finally pay off. tons of character development and parts of the world that was mentioned in mask of deception finally revealed. imo it is a great conclusion to the series. if you like deception, there is no question you will love mask of truth. my only complaint with the story is some part of the end feel kinda off because it is the high climax of the series and it assume you to have played the first uta game (mask of deception is the second game and mask of truth is the 3rd) the first UTA game will come out on steam later this year, and to be honest after spoiling myself of the first game plot, the conclusion become really satisfying and tied up the 2 sagas in a neat knot while also leaving some room for speculation or even a potential sequel.now let's talk about combat. the combat is mostly the same, with new characters with new movesets. the problem is mask of truth encounter can be a bit . . . overwhelming in a bad way. it is still relatively easy and simple but sometimes there are just too much and the enemy HP are too high (especially towards the last _childDocuments_.review: The first 35 hours of this game are fantastic. Some of the best storytelling and writing I've ever seen in a VN, or even in a video game of any genre. The gameplay is great, the maps are well designed, the pacing is good and the antagonist is compelling and a good foil for Haku.However, the final 10 hours are terrible...It feels like they try to fit an entire games worth of story, exposition and events into the final 10 hours of the game, and so coming off the first half of the game which was paced well and was interesting throughout, you get a conclusion that feels incredibly rushed and confusing, that leaves a ton of plot holes in what is supposed to be a "definitive ending". A lot of people don't mind the rushed ending since the final boss and epilogue is so good, but at the end I never felt the advertised 'catharsis'. The final arc just left so many questions, so many plot holes and unexplained contrivances, LOTS of asspulls (such as characters being able to run across an entire continent in only a few hours, knowing EXACTLY where the main characters are, setting up an ambush in a heavily fortified secret area, and running across the continent again in a few hours while being gravely wounded) and the whole thing centered around an antagonist that was so boring and poorly written compared to the one that came before. In the end I didn't cry (that much), I was mostly just baffled by what I had just witnessed and annoyed by the fact that the conclusion to the series I had been playing for the past 100 hours was so half assed and convoluted.

_childDocuments_.review: The most grandiose way to end a series. Over a hundred and fifty hours spent alongside some of the most well-written characters, each one more charming than the other. With the stakes at an all-time high, there is nothing they won't sacrifice for the greater good. A story about sacrifice, and one done well.Taking the risk of making an entire 50hr game just the stepping stool of this one was well worth it; Mask of Truth pays off with the greatest of endings. From the vast wallpaper-worthy CGs, the heavenly score, phenomenal voice acting and casting, and writing, Utawarerumono is, from start to finish, an unforgettable ride.Not a single moment is wasted, and for the first time in my life, I wish there was. I could go on another 300 hours of nothing but seeing them interact and bounce off each other like in the slice-of-life parts of the story. I hate not being able to express how good of a series Utawarerumono is, but perhaps I don't even need to, because it speaks for itself in so many ways.I will deeply miss all the characters and the unique, colorful world of Utawarerumono, but I will never forget it and everything it has to offer.

I give the game a 12 out of 10 it was amazing to the very end prepare yourself for zombification.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono. It is one of the famous Japanese franchise series developed by Aquaplus(Leaf). This series features the outstanding visual novel and SRPG experience with the focus on interesting story, nice anime artworks, and impressive soundtracks. Utawarerumono originated on PC back in 2002. Since then, it has led to a variety of projects, including animation series. According to the official announcement, the series has sold hundreds of thousands of copies in Japan. This time DMM GAMES and ShiraVN played a great role in bringing Utawarerumono series to Steam globally.The second episode(Mask of Deception) is close to the prologue and depicting daily life in general, this third episode(Mask of Truth) focus on the main story parts. This game summarizes both episodes 1(Prelude to the Fallen) and 2(Mask of Deception). So it's good to enjoy everything of Utawarerumono series as much as possible, but if you can't afford it, it might be a good idea to choose Mask of Truth first. The story unfold is quite similar to the first episode. Each one has a different reason, but the protagonists face inevitable wars, struggling to protect their loved ones, and building up the nation. Play time is over 50 hours and provides intense and deep game experience.Gameplay is pretty good. There is quite a lot to enjoy. More game systems have been added than the second volume. For example, there're splendid new co-op final finisher moves. And in the exercise mode, you can randomly divide your units and enjoy mock battle with each other. Scenario battles are quite exciting, not too difficult or too easy. In other words, the game balance is fine. The fan-service contents we expect are well prepared. Such events are quite hot, sometimes funny and heartwarming. Animation and character voices have the highest quality. And you'll fall into the soundtrack of this game. It's quite impressive. As well as, there are extra contents that you can enjoy the whole Utawarerumono series. This shows that the developers put a lot of effort into the game itself.Translation and localization are particularly important in the story-driven games. In that sense, the global Steam version of this Utawarerumono series is fine. The gameplay time for the two episodes of the trilogy will be at least 80 hours. The translation may be somewhat straightforward, but it has given the impression that the most context is smoothly presented. Fortunately, translation doesn't ruin the quality of this great game. The time you spend in this game will be well worth it.Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. This is a pretty good anime game. Of course, it's a game that anyone can enjoy, but it's probably not for everyone. The preference for the anime game such as this text adventure can vary from user to user, even if it has some RPG elements. As you may know, Utawarerumono Mask series released as the PlayStation version first. This PC Edition is a port from the PlayStation version. So the exposure level for the hot events may be soft. Nevertheless, the game is exciting from the start to the end. Therefore, if you've been interested in this kind of game, don't hesitate. This will definitely be a game for you. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: If you haven't played Prelude to the Fallen and especially Mask of Deception, I would advise you not read anything about this game yet. AT ALL. Except for this review, it's spoiler free :)The final game of the Utawarerumono trilogy, there is a lot of payoff here to the setup of the second game and the first game's plot. The story is magnificent and very emotional, the characters shine and have surprising depth, and an amazing conclusion for the well crafted world's story awaits. If you haven't played the first and second games, Prelude to the Fallen and Mask of Deception, you really should play those before this one for its plot to be understood.(I'll try and write a review for Prelude to the Fallen once I get it on Steam, too...)The gameplay is a lot stronger than in Mask of Deception, and is pretty good with a lot of nuance and fun mechanics to it, as well as generally good map design. The units are all pretty fun to use, and the balancing is solid as well.The tropes and fanservice of the story are also cut down as the plot heads toward its conclusion, and the flaws of the story are rather minimal, though I won't pretend some don't exist at all. Regardless, it's one of the greatest stories I have ever read, is very thought provoking, and consistently is amazing throughout its length with a conclusion that lives rent free in my head. The story balances calmer scenes and more intense ones very well, and is incredibly engaging, entertaining, and emotionally charged. Play the trilogy, especially for this. It's so incredibly good.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------If you have questions, consider joining the Discord through the subreddit :)

_childDocuments_.review: Among fans of VNs in the West, the Utawarerumono series has taken on almost a mythical status over the year. As a result, I was very excited when the games got ported to PC. However, after playing what is essentially an $80 game, I'm left feeling very conflicted. I enjoyed the game at certain points, but it also frustrates me greatly. I just felt like maybe I'm getting too old for these anime storylines. What bothers me the most is the game’s overuse of what I’d like to describe as masochistic writing. After every battle that you won, it’s always either “Haha you fall into my trap” or “Haha I didn’t even use half my strength” or “Haha I’ll just walk right out of here like nothing happens even though you just finish me off with that awesome 1k Co-Op final”. Seriously, the gameplay eventually becomes nothing more than side distractions and has no bearing on the story. The game is obsessed with putting the MCs in these scenarios in which they are utterly helpless and overwhelmed. Scenes in which a friendly character is mentally and/or physically tortured would go on and on and on even after the point is made. About half of the game’s scenes consists of some random dude or dudette talking down on the MCs. The MCs never had any decent riposte to these verbal assaults. Usually, the MCs would start crying or are stunned into submission.The gameplay does improve compared to Mask of Deception. Damage is scaled much better now so strategic options actually matter. There are also more variety of maps and objectives. Some battles last a little too long though, but overall I had good experience with the gameplay.If you like SRPG and VN, I still think you should give this series a shot. I just think the series are too expensive and are too long for the amount of enjoyment I got from them.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with this game despite it being the first one in the series I've played. I had knowledge of the previous games through their respective anime and I'm still floored by how much I loved this game without playing the first two. If you're interested in this game, you'll only need to play Mask of Deception to understand the majority of this one as MoD and MoT are one story, while the original is a bit disconnected.GAMEPLAYIf you're interested in playing Utawarerumono: MoT for its combat rather than its story, I suggest you look for another game. However, MoT's gameplay is competent and makes for a break between long reading sessions, although there might be a few too many battles at the end stacked back to back.The game is not difficult by any means as the story is the main focus but from what I've played of Hard Mode, there is a noticeable difficulty jump.I would like to go more in depth on the gameplay but my knowledge on srpgs is lacking but I will say that it was enjoyable, moreso at the end when everyone felt much more powerful. SOUNDTRACKWowzas. I loved the soundtrack for this game. I have the last song from the epilogue playing as I write this review. Many of the songs in this game have a very distinct flute sound and are quite memorable. Unlike other games this long, I didn’t get tired of the soundtrack at all.The music beautifully compliments the scenes with the voiced songs usually emphasizing important moments in the story. The music also switches between comedic and light to serious and emotional perfectly.I’m super glad that there’s a music viewer in the main menu or I’d have a hard time finding these songs. STORY & CHARACTERSThe story is a direct continuation from MoD and tied to the original Utawarerumono. The following will contain spoilers for the first 1-2 hours of the game, though there’s nothing to fear if you’ve already played MoD as the first 2 hours are essentially recap.Following Oshtor’s death in MoD Haku has taken up his friend’s name and is now leading the effort to restore Anju to the throne. Haku and Nekone, Oshtor’s younger sister and the only one who knows Haku’s identity, must now try and keep the image of Oshtor alive as his name is the only one that commands enough respect to see the war through.What follows is some of the most gripping storytelling and characterization I’ve seen in any game. Everyone realizes just how much Haku meant to them and the weight on Haku and Nekone’s shoulders as they continue to lie despite their friends’ sorrows in order to honor Oshtor and bring peace back to Yamato is absolutely heart rending. I’ve lost so much sleep binging this game and can’t help but relentlessly search for more news on possible new games.The pacing is great, though I think the lead up to the ending is a bit weaker than other parts, and the balance between light and heavy scenes is near perfect. If I could erase my memory and play the game for another 50+ hours I would. I didn’t dare think that any scenes would match the early Haku and Nekone scenes but Haku and Kuon scenes come around to prove me wrong.OVERALLIt is only after I finish this game that I realize how much of a fool I am for thinking the anime was "good enough" and I just had to go and buy the prequel. I don't know how my experience would have been if I had played MoD first but hopefully it can help me move past the void this game left in my life.10/10It’s obviously not perfect as the battles dragged sometimes and there was no autosave feature, which would have been wonderful as I screwed up and loaded a save instead of overwriting a save meaning I had to replay an hour of the game. However, there are few stories that manage to draw me in as deep as this one did and my enjoyment of this experience is worthy of a 10.Here's to hoping for more utawarerumono games in the future (Not mobile ones though >:( ).

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying conclusion to the trilogy, tying up all plot points and conflicts presented in the previous two games. There is just something distinctly emotional about seeing all these characters, this world, this story that I've spent the over a hundred hours becoming invested in all come to a head. Maybe this will truly be the end of the series, or maybe it will not be. I really hope it isn't. I've truly grown attached to this universe, and it wouldn't be so bad to see more of it in the future. If you are interested in epic fantasy storylines with lots of characters and worldbuilding that you can become invested in, then by all means, pick up the utawarerumono series. Now that i've praised the game, I need to point out its flaws. Would I consider Mask of Truth to be the Muv-Luv Alternative of Utawarerumono? Not really. Muv-Luv Alternative went all the way with its story, pulling absolutely no punches and subverting your expectations at every turn. Mask of Truth, however, sometimes fell back on predictable tropes and tedious narrative padding. I was baffled as to why the story kept continuing at certain points. There were definitely much quicker ways to resolve some conflicts presented in the game than what the game actually did. The story didn't HAVE to end the way it did and it felt like the writers weren't organically guiding the story to its conclusion. Rather, they were forcing the story down a certain ending that they wanted, and as a result, some plot developments felt torturously prolonged to reach this ending. From a narrative standpoint, was it a satisfying ending? Kinda. Was it really predictable though? Yes. In addition, I fully suspect that some of this narrative padding was done to fit more gameplay into the plot somehow. The last few fights of the game felt like a token "insert final boss fight here" moment for gameplay purposes. Ideally, gameplay and story should compliment each other, like two sides of the same coin. The gameplay should help immerse players in the story, and bring an interactive storytelling element to the experience. At the beginning of Mask of Truth, the gameplay was succeeding in that regard. I felt more and more involved in the story with each gameplay segment. However, towards the end, the gameplay dragged me away from the story. I just wanted to get it over with. It had overstayed its welcome; it had padded out the story to accommodate itself. It's not that it wasn't fun anymore; it just wasn't needed anymore. But even despite these faults, this game is still one of those games that makes me glad I read visual novels in the first place. It will always have a special place in my heart. Buy it and read it.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is the deeply satisfying conclusion to an epic trilogy. It nicely ties up major plot points set up at the end of the previous game, Mask of Deception, while delivering no shortage of emotional high moments. The game's combat (i.e. the actual gameplay part), which takes up between a fifth to a quarter of the overall play time, is satisfactory. Combat mechanics are relatively simple like in the previous two games and there isn't a whole lot of strategic depth for fans of tactical RPGs to sink their teeth into. Nonetheless, there were enough meaningful decisions to keep me engaged during fights.As has always been the case with the series, the characters are its strongest point - while Mask of Deception spent most of its run introducing the cast and building up the dynamic between them, we now witness their growth as they persevere through loss and adversity. Mask of Truth is the definitive payoff in a trilogy that I strongly recommend to visual novel fans and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: What a trilogy. After finishing this game, I went into to bonus options and went through everything, not quite ready to let it go just yet, then I realized how much I really adored these games.  Going back to the first in the series, it had me hooked after the first hour, the music, the setting, the characters, and the game play. The game play was serviceable enough, but the story is where it really shines, so if you're looking for a well written and long story, you've found it here. There is a lot of slice of life moments through all 3 games, and some people will list it as a negative, saying it's slow, and that's one opinion, but to me all those slice of life moments really help you connect to all the characters, and sets up for all those emotional moments later in the story. I really really recommend this game to anyone who are interested in these types of games!

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Truth has a hell of a job to do. Not only has it got to find a way to wrap up the previous title, Mask of Deception, but also tie up all the once resolved threads of the original Utawarerumono that have been significantly loosened. It’s the kind of ambition we’ve seen crash and burn numerous times across all media; trying to find a satisfying conclusion to hours and hours of patient build. Mask of Deception wasn’t shy about how it was more or less one big lesson in world building done right in order for Truth to drive things home. It does that. It does that in spades.I’m talking around the point a little because the big twist ending of Deception shakes all the monkeys out of the tree, then asks Truth to put them back. Except now the tree has gone. And all the monkeys are on fire. I know I should absolutely discuss that, except I can’t without wading full stride into deep spoiler territory. So I’m going to pick at this carefully and point out that interested players should categorically play at least the previous game before attempting this one.Yamato, then, is having its share of problems. Once a ridiculously prosperous country that knew few hardships, it’s now been thrust into the slow rumblings of a civil war. There’s no one big reason for all this; for the most part, the people on both sides are just trying to do what they think is right. But you’re probably the rightest! Forced outside the capital into a remote corner of the country, the plot mostly follows Imperial Guardsman, Oshtor, as he and the remainder of the cast from the previous game lick their wounds and start planning a way to take their country back. Only sometimes, it’s more about dethroned princess, Anju, who needs to come to very quick terms with the loss of her entire family and the absolution of her rule. There’s an impostor on her throne, but she needs to accept that if she wages war to reclaim her birthright, a lot of innocent people are going to suffer. A lot of people are going to die. It’s a lot to take on; she might have been bred specifically to rule, but she’s still just an uncertain, mourning child underneath it all.Sometimes it’s not about either of them. Sometimes, it’s not even about Yamato, but harkens back to the location of the original game, Tuskar. Kuon took a leading role in Deception, but its heavy-hitting conclusion perhaps hit her the hardest and she’s returned to the country of her birth. Here, she needs to reassess the things that really matter to her; the loyalty she feels towards her friends and the plight visited upon the country she came to love. But she also has obligations to Tuskar; family she’s neglected in her travels. Whatever she does and wherever she goes, she’s letting someone she cares about down, forcing further hurt upon people already suffering.Everyone in Mask of Truth is suffering. Everyone has lost something once thought irreplaceable, that I’m really trying very hard not to address directly. It features a cast lifted from a previous game that you rarely saw in low spirits, and that so many of them are now a little bit broken in their own unique ways hurts. Truth starts with a cast trying to pick up the pieces, with people trying desperately to lift the more fragile of their friends with vacant smiles and empty platitudes. They poke at the embers of their world, unable to avoid the occasional wallow in self-pity or grief or guilt. And then they pick each other up. And then they chose not to accept the hand they’ve been dealt. And then they fight back.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is the sequel of Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, together they have a total of 90-100 hours of gameplay. The difference between the first and the second is that the first was more slice of life like, Mask of Truth is a rollercoaster of emotions between a group of friends, having to keep a painful secret for the greater good, not being able to tell the one you love and admire about it, fighting against overpowered evil all the time and making huge sacrifices. Utawarerumono beat my score for the most played visual novel 3 times, became my favorite VN, one of my favorite animes (if i can include the VN as an anime, the anime adaptation surely skipped a LOT of things for the lack of time in just 26 episodes) and it shall stay between my favorites, especially Mask of Truth!I have been playing for hours in a row with small and few breaks, and with that i mean 8-12 hours. The voice acting is very good and my favorite part in both games is that if the like after a voiced line is a thought or a break and has no voice, the last one keeps playing until another one starts, it brings that atmosphere! It is indeed a very small thing, but it brings me a lot of joy.This one also has some extra menus between chapters where you can train your characters, do challenges, replay old fights and allocate BP, which is a nice addition, i would feel the lack of it if i play the first one again. MoT also has a lot more gameplay, fights are quite expected for the part with wars against rebels, monsters, brainwashed people and even gods, stuff that happened in Mask of Deception too, but A LOT less. It is the reason to try New Game+, you can ignore the story if you want and keep on playing the game, everyone will be so much weaker the second time as you keep everything on your characters, but if you decide to train between them it will be a everlasting battle. The quality of this game is memorable, the soundtrack (over 90 tracks!!!), the artwork of the characters, even the animations look pretty good for their budget, but most importantly the writing, the writing is amazing. It is that big heavy book or set of books that you don't expect finishing but somehow you start the first one and read nonstop until you finish them, can't wait to know more while reading and sad when finishing it, the sadness coming from not having more to consume.The protagonist never thought highly of himself, never thought he valued anything and that people cared enough about him until he had to cover someone else's death and kill his old self. Being dead, playing someone else's role and seeing his friends leave heartbroken of his death without him being able to shout their name and bring them back. We all have someone, someone has us, we are never truly alone, us leaving forever would only cause pain, for this we must live and smile. 10/10, a moonlight flower <3If you want more detailed reviews on awesome games consider following , our curator page.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a whole lot to say. If you're about to play this game, you have most likely played the previous half, Mask of Deception, and the first game, Prelude to the Fallen (if you haven't, go play them and don't look at anything from this one if you don't want to get spoiled). So you know what to expect.This is where all the setup from Mask of Deception (and partly from Prelude to the Fallen) leads to. For me personally, this is one of the most epic, pure hype stories I've ever experienced to this day. You know how some of your favorite stories have that one or two grand moments where everything about the story just clicks together for you, usually while an insert song or anime opening is playing in the background. These are the moments that you'll remember for a long time, if not for the rest of your life, and which cement a story as one of your favorites. On a rare occasion, these might even be moments that make you sob.Well for me personally, Mask of Truth doesn't have one or two of these, but at the moment I'm counting 9 of them in total. And even though I'm not one to often cry even once while watching/reading stories, this game made me shed tears 3 times in the span of one week. After finishing, I'm completely emotionally exhausted from this ordeal.But to actually provide some information other than my personal, overwhelmingly positive impressions: The combat is pretty much the same as the previous entry, but this time the improved mechanics actually matter a lot more. The main story is capable of throwing some actually pretty difficult boss fights at you every once in a while in order to force you to better utilize some of the now more varied character kits.The story is on another level. If I were to mention at least something negative, it would be that most of what I said applies to only the first 75 %  and the last 5-10 % of the plot. At a certain point, one of the main conflicts and antagonists gets resolved. After which a new, shorter arc begins. This arc is necessary, sure, as it concerns some of the global/large scale loose ends and conflics that had to be left for the end of the story. But this along with the way it is executed just felt to me like such a vibe-killer compared to the emotional rollercoaster that is the main chunk of the game, especially with how meh and frustrating the "new" antagonist felt. Thankfully after you rush through it, the game ends on a high note as the ending puts you back on the hype train and delivers some of the most cathartic moments of the entire series (and for me personally, some of the most cathartic moments of storytelling I've seen in my life so far).

As for the game itself....Gameplay wise, It's TRPG like the others but with more balancing.Has very good keyboard and mouse support too.The soundtrack though, 10/10 majestic.Especially the vocal tracks, Their the bane and plays A LOT during important scenes.The game has the tag Sexual Content but it's a lie. _childDocuments_.review: A good conclusion to the Utawarerumono trilogy (yes, including prelude to the fallen). While Mask of Deception was mostly lighthearted, Mask of Truth has a serious tone where there is a nearly constant threat to our MC's, but it doesn't lose the banter and slice of life moments you like (or dislike idunno) completely. This franchise pulls it off to have some lighthearted slice of life while still having an actual deep plot at the same time.Mask of Deception's overall plot seems to truly advance in the latter half, while Mask of Truth's plot advances steadily throughout the whole game. Utawarerumono's cast has some of the usual trope characters, but plenty of them are likeable and well built. The worldbuilding is great, the storytelling is great and the music + high quality 2D visuals do a great job to pull you into this fantasy world. Overall i would say Utawarerumono has one of the better stories in its genre. It additionally gets some personal bonuspoints for providing some really good emotional/impactful moments .The battle system is the same as its predecessor: fairly standard tactical RPG combat. I didn't really feel joy in challenging myself with it TBH. Also had a few occassions where the rapid forward button in combat made my game crash... losing 30+ minutes of battle time in the progress...I WILL give kudos to the final boss battleThe end itself is.. satisfying, but bittersweet. It also is an end that once again confirms that you should not skip the prequel (prelude to the fallen) to Haku's and Kuon's story. . Once again i recommend the whole Utawarerumono trilogy to anyone who wants to try out/likes:The final score will remain a 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked the first game, you'll almost certainly love this one and if you enjoyed the second game, this brings the overall story to a close in a very satisfying way. While the game establishes the plot enough that you can play this as a standalone, I highly recommend you play the previous two games first.Long Version: Thrust into the roll you accepted during the finale of the second game, Haku must now lead his friends and the allies found in a small border nation, to somehow reclaim the enormous kingdom they once knew from the powers that usurped it. While the answers as to who and why of the previous game's betrayal are not fully unearthed until late game, there is plenty to keep the group occupied in the meantime. The balance between story and combat elements is much better in Mask of Truth than it was in Mask of Deception (the second game), and the complexity of the combat is back to Prelude to the Fallen (the first game) levels. (Though as a tiny side note, breaking objects never matters in this game). In a lot of ways, it does the good trilogy thing of incorporating the best bits from all the previous games and implementing them properly.The anime-ness of the story continues, again, for good or for bad. The plot is actually really interesting though. The ending is largely satisfying despite going against a few of my personal preferences. (You will have to watch through the credits, broken up into... I wanna say three sections? Just wait until you actually get to the FIN screen.) Saying much else about the game treads into spoiler territory. Really though, if you've played the first two games, you'll want to play this one. If you haven't, stop now and go play them instead. If you enjoy game one you'll like this one almost guaranteed.

For a few specific types that really just like long slow stories, want one game to play for weeks or months depending on how much time they have to commit to them, and are ok with some jank and problems in a story and setting, then it's decent. But it's just... really slow, and so often I'm wanting it to be over or move along faster, and the plot itself has more holes than a colander. They can get away with some of that jank and BS, but they push a LOT at the player as parts of the main story and key elements and problems the player/story is dealing with. So many cases of why is the character so bloody incompetent? Especially when the repeat the same obvious mistake four or five or six times in a row in the story... like... really? It was an obvious mistake before you even did it, but you can't learn at all?Oh well, just lots of issues that pulled me out from getting to invested in the story. The gameplay is ok... not great, kinda slow, but itself often clashes with the story itself in how they present things, even more than the first or second game.  Overall, It's an ok story and I do kind of like some of the characters, but it's just not up there with the first game, so I can't feel like saying yes, buy this, spend tons of time on this one story, it's worth it... when there are plenty of other stories that are faster, better, or even both of those and just free. A few people and types will still enjoy it though, and it's not terrible or that bad, just mediocre... and not quite worth the time investment in my opinion, or the cost once that also gets factored in for most people.I liked the first one, if you are ok with slower paced games with good character development, I'll recommend it. If you just like it, probably stick with only it, if you absolutely love it, then I guess get 2 and 3.2 was frankly just bad on the gameplay and very meh with some bad on the story, though good on some characters, 3 (this one) noticabely improved the gameplay by moving back towards the first games style for stuff, with a few tweaks of it's own to help here or there, but still nothing to write home about. The story is for the first half overall much better than the second, and compares to the first one in some parts, though doesn't have the nice feel I liked from that first one, second half though... gets more mixed, both more interesting and posotive in some points, but also more frusterating as they start seeing how many holes they can punch into the story in order to try and wrap up some ideas they had. I mean.. an enemy unit, that has no access to teleportation or any special logistics, that frankly would probably have trouble even getting out of their starting location... are supposed to somehow know exactly where the players are whey they shouldn't, move half way across the entire country, do a questionable attack, and then return... all in just a few hours. That trip should take days if not more even in the best of conditions, but no, just let it happen in a few hours. Let them know where they are because plot demands they show up to do X thing to the players group... Ya, logic just goes out the window at several points here, but that was one of the worst ones....So in the end, all are slow games, but the first one I enjoyed and felt mostly satisfied by... the second one was mostly just annoying and problematic with the key upside of some characters, and the third one here is too long and drawn out at first, and then rushes to finish up and wow you with a bunch of major story turns and events at the end... but doesn't know how to make them actually all work together so... it's all really forced and kind of pulls you out of it if you tried to get invested in the story and characters actions and stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: "None of your decisions actually matter, now slug it out against these BBEGs for the sake of vague notions."Wow. So original. The journey was fun but the last 18 hours of play were just railroaded padding to mandatory extend (finish?) the game out, and I hate that. If Mask of Deception felt like it ended too soon, then Mask of Truth felt like it just dragged on for eternity towards a foregone conclusion. I get the impression that the director wanted to have a 4th game covering the last 1/4th of this game, but he knew that kind of episodic format wouldn't be acceptable. The journey was fun, it's more Utawarerumono good stuff and chances are you've played 1 and 2 (if not the game assumes you haven't with hours of review of 2's content in the opening), but the ending was Mass Effect 3-tier bitter. If you're reading this planning to purchase the three as a set, just play the first game and consider it ogre for your own sake and time.So without spoiling the plot (since the ending involves spoiling about the last 1/4th of gameplay), the last segment of the game was basically slugfest after slugfest after slugfest in traditional attritional JRPG style. Utawarerumono is known for having villains that act "real" but the last like four fights are just BBEGs as part of what feels like was supposed to be its own game or bonus post-game content, but got tacked on to the end of Mask of Truth because the budget ran out, so you're sitting there going "is THIS the final battle? Is THIS ONE the final battle?" instead of being invested in each fight. The third game features the tragic loss component of the first game, except instead of losing anything you actually care for you are just shown mass suffering of, well, masses, because the BBEGs have to be established as the BBEGs. Going into a little more detail...The last 18 hours of gameplay could easily have been condensed into 3-4. The director opted to have every single character have a quip for every single scene instead of one or two characters commenting on a situation for effect which lead 30 second scenes to be 5 minute scenes instead. If there was something of substance being added that would be fine, but each character's interaction with the scene was equivalent to a reaction video (not adding anything to the conversation) which gets old when there's 10+ characters. You can predict the series of events that will follow pretty much word-for-word from the 12 hour to ending mark onwards. The game gives you a sense of finality on four different occasions and then just proceeds to keep lurching along like "oh yeah nah that wasn't the ending that was just closure" despite major events taking place. That wouldn't be a big deal if the 2nd game and majority of the third game hadn't been slow-going from one event to the next making the sudden acceleration of plot incredibly jarring.The last two boss fights are completely scripted based on your level so that they will drag on and on and on some more, but you can see where the battles are going from a mile away; they're just long for the sake of being long attritional battles (in the second to last boss fight for instance, you're fighting a completely pointless battle against unkillable enemies while only the MC is allowed to fight the BBEG in a way that is 90% scripted and 10% soft lock probability that could force you to have to restart the entire nearly 1 hour fight). Then the game just straight-up copies the first game's ending which is a spit in the face of the first game which had proper pacing and none of this padding for the sake of padding. Then during the epilogue (the only redeemable part of that last portion of the game) goes on and on and on covering what happened to each minor character in the second game, yet despite spending the last 4 hours nostalgiablasting you into oblivion, they can't even wrap up the loose ends from the first game that would have been seen in the third game.The journey was fun, but the ending left an incredibly bitter taste in my mouth. Not bittersweet, just bitter. It was one of those "everything you did for two games doesn't matter" style deus ex Shakespearian endings and I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate those. The plot holes, contrivances, and arsepulls at the end were just too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews. This has to take the cake as my favorite story of all time, and I love it so much that I had to write about it lol. I love every bit of the aesthetic that the game gives, and playing Prelude and Deception before it, this game is the perfect finish to a beautiful trilogy. If you're a fan of anything of deep lore, this game is for you. There is many pieces to a puzzle to put together throughout. Some will dislike the filler that the story provides in between the progression of the story, and that is understandable. At the least, this gives you a chance to understand the characters and their motivations more there.The character design is one of my favorite things in this game, iconic designs that you really see anywhere else, and that flair is only one of the things that this amazing series offers. Genuinely funny moments, cute characters, a story with stakes, and easily pulls you in from Prelude all the way to here, your final point. Beautiful music that resonates the emotion that the game wants you to feel, and unreal art.The game play is great as well throughout the series, testing your brain on harder difficulty. Leveling up the characters feel fulfilling, and it's hard to get tired of it at any point. Every battle and map feels fresh, and the hype around almost every fight is there.I mean it when I say that I recommend this to everyone who likes a good story. I think this series deserves much more recognition in the West, and it's a gem in the sand that if you uncover and face for yourself, you'll like a lot more than you think in most cases.
