_childDocuments_.review: Nearly three years after it was first released in the west on PS4 and Vita, us PC players finally get the chance to play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the second and third games in the Utawarerumono series. It's about time honestly, as these are some games I have been wanting to play since I first watched the anime adaptation years ago.So for those unfamiliar with it, Utawarerumono is a series of visual novels with tactical RPG elements. The gameplay consists of the player going from reading various story events and dialogue to tactical, turn-based battles on a grid. As with most VNs that have gameplay elements, the focus is not on the gameplay, but rather on the story. However, with Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the gameplay is actually pretty good and doesn't feel like it was just tacked onto the experience. It may be no Disgaea, but it has a decent amount of depth to it at least, much more so than I often see with such VN hybrids. The game also provides a couple difficulty options to accommodate for both those that just want to experience the story and those that want more challenging gameplay. On normal difficulty, the battles are pretty much a breeze, but on hard difficulty, not so much.As for the actual story, well, that's something that Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth do really well. Although Mask of Deception is technically the second game in the series, it is set up in such a way as to make it easy for newcomers to enjoy. I personally have never played the first game (which is simply titled "Utawarerumono" and does not have an official English release yet) and had no problems getting into Mask of Deception. The same cannot be said for Mask of Truth though, which absolutely requires that you play Mask of Deception first, lest you be really confused as to what's going on. For those that still want to experience the first game in some form, the 2006 anime is generally considered a good adaptation. I watched it years ago and, while I may not remember much of it, I liked it enough to want to get into the games.Once you actually get into the story, you'll be met with some well-written characters, a vibrant fantasy setting that's big on world-building, and some pretty good overall pacing. The games provide a good mix of serious storytelling and more character-oriented slice of life scenes as well. In fact, I like to think of the two games as brothers. Mask of Deception is the younger brother, who is rather innocent and just wants to have fun in this fantasy world with all of its neat characters. Mask of Truth, on the other hand, is the older brother who has lost his innocence and has experienced the hardships of life. While Mask of Deception does have its serious moments, Mask of Truth is when the real story story kicks in, when everything starts coming together. It's quite the ride and there's a good reason why Mask of Truth is sitting at the #12 spot on VNDB's list of highest-rated visual novels.The art and music, as with the story, are also pretty good in both games. I ran the game at 1440p and, while that is an upscale from 720p, the art looked fine and I didn't notice any blatantly blurry assets or backgrounds. It was definitely some good news, as I'm a big fan of the fantasy aesthetic that the games go for. The music also perfectly matches this aesthetic, with a great blend of energetic battle themes and more laid-back, traditional tracks for the game's dialogue scenes. As someone that has already been listening to these soundtracks for years, it was cool to finally hear this music in-game.And of course, seeing as how these two games have never been released on PC, I should mention the quality of their port. To sum it up, it's pretty good as far as VN ports go. There's all the standard settings one would expect in a VN release, including text speed, auto-mode speed, skip options, and a voice cutoff toggle. However, both games go one step further with fullscreen, borderless, and window options, multiple resolution support, completely rebindable keyboard controls, protagonist voice toggling, and even customizable button prompts dependent on what type of controller you're using. Some of these may sound pretty standard, but with visual novels, sometimes they are hard to come by, so it's nice to see them included here.And before I wrap up this review, I should bring up the censorship question. Both games were released as 15+ titles in Japan, so there's no H-scenes like in the original 2002 PC game. This version of Mask of Truth is the exact same as the Japanese version, but this version of Mask of Deception has one CG that has been changed from the Japanese release. I'll go ahead and throw that CG up on-screen so you can see what was changed. It's a very minor change, but I know that a lot of VN fans are passionate about the subject, so it needs to be noted regardless.Overall though, both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are solid games all things considered. Great art, great music, gameplay that actually doesn't feel like a distraction from the main story, and a story that's both unique and well-written. The two games have a lot going for them and the fact that they're actually decent PC ports is also a nice bonus. It's about time we got them on PC and now it's just a wait to complete the trilogy with the release of Prelude to the Fallen, a remaster of the first game that is also slated to release on PC.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This is game 3 of a series. Play "Prelude to the Fallen" then "Mask of Deception" first.Disclaimer:My 55 hours of playtime represents one complete play through on Normal difficulty, Played entirely on Steam deck.Short Review:This game is the perfect finish to the series, they really went all out.The only reason you should be here is if you completed the other two games in the series.If you did then buy this one as soon as you are able.Taken as a whole: the entire series is a incomparable masterpiece. Go in as blind as you can, I wont spoil anything but don't even read any more of this review.More details, no spoilers:Once again the pacing is just relentless, playing for just an hour or two a night I was always left with some new development or twist or revelation. There's so many plot points that get woven in and resolved properly that the game goes on for like another 10+ hours after any other game would have wrapped up. There's even a whole load of post credits scenes with some major developments.It never felt rushed despite this. Everything is given its proper amount of time.I will say this game on Normal difficulty is the hardest yet. I never had to grind once but there were some crazy difficulty spikes. Sometimes certain characters were only doing like 1-3 damage and I don't fully understand why.All I'm going to say is save before every fight so you can change your roster if needed, use your brain and look at the win/defeat conditions as well as the type advantages.Welp, Gonna be honest here I enjoyed this series immensely. Probably the best JRPG series I have played in 30+ years of gaming.If this was made with Final Fantasy production values it would likely never be surpassed.I am so glad I got to play it and also really sad that its over. I doubt I will find a game that is anywhere as fun and well written as this for a while but, I haven't played Monochrome Mobius yet so lets see...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the conclusion of the Utawarerumono series, and what a conclusion it was! I had high hopes for it after the dramatic ending of Mask of Deception and it did not disappoint one bit.This is a heroic tale of a man carrying on the will of his late friend, no matter what sacrifice he must do in order to protect those that were important to both his friend and to himself. The character development is one of the strongest point of this game. Watching the characters grow together through the many hardships that they face is very heartwarming. The pacing is generally very good. It does slow down a little near the end, but it picks up the pace again right in time for the grand finale. Giving a good ending to a long series is always tough, but in my opinion I would say that this game nails it. It's an epic story from beginning to end, and I'm happy to have read it all the way through.The gameplay is for sure at it's peak in this game. For the most part the mechanics are identical to Mask of Deception, so the transition from that game to this one is pretty smooth (whereas there is a bit of a learning curve when you move on from Prelude to the Fallen to MoD as there are substantial differences). However, it brings back the display for battle preparations that was used in PttF and adds some improvements, which is great because that one felt better than the battle preparations menu from MoD. Also, co-op attacks are back together with co-op Final Strikes.Difficulty is at its highest in this game as well. While a good number of the story maps aren't too hard, there are at least a couple that are actually rather challenging. The Dream Arena post-game maps though is definitely where the difficulty goes off the charts. The early ones aren't too bad, but most of them are a good challenge and the toughest ones I can only describe as being brutally hard. These maps will test your game knowledge to their limits. While they can all be beaten without grinding, you might have to repeat some stages to farm BP and items if you ever get stuck. I thoroughly enjoyed this game, both as a VN and as an SRPG. I think this game is one that everyone should play, and even though I only recently finished playing it I can say that it's for sure one of my favorite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic end to the trilogy.Utawarerumono is what happens when you cross cat girls, Fire Emblem-like tactical gameplay with a visual novel that follows a Nakige formula reminiscent of Key (slice-of-life build up, followed up by the emotional and climatic payoff), only that the setting is not the contemporary city setting, but an Oriental one in the "ancient past". It shouldn't work on paper, but the writers clearly had a lot of heart and conviction put in to the story, enough for me to suspend my disbelief and fall hook, line and sinker and love th characters. Prelude was a nice prequel set-up to the world and the seeds of conflict that would rear its head in the subsequent duology. Deception was that nonsensical and utterly hilarious slice-of-life common route (admittedly, did get a bit wee too long with the Haku masochist hijinks) that got us enamored with the cast and cleverly foreshadowed all those hand-to-mouth moments in Truth. Truth laid it all bare; the world, the story, and raw feelings of Haku and co. And it hit it right off the park. I have to say, as much as I am not a fan of Harems, Haku is fantastic Harem protagonist and even just an all-around good guy in general. Like all parodoxical humans, he is flawed and genuine, lazy and reliable, dense and intuitive at the same time.We could with more of him in stories, and our world.

_childDocuments_.review: The moment I booted up Mask of Truth, I knew I was in for something special. It gave off a certain air or feeling that was very similar to when I first booted up Muv Luv Alternative for the first time as well, and boy howdy those feelings were not betrayed. What a beautiful, wildly fun, and heartbreaking journey this was. Many reviews I noticed echoed very similar sentiments to what I was wanting to toss into this review as well, so I'll just say that I 2nd a lot of the highlights of Truth  that other's point out. What I will toss into the thunderdome here is, while Mask of Truth continued that high bar already set for it's top tier VA work, amazing soundtrack (which they went above and beyond for the finale here), and stellar writing and world building, what surprised me the most was the creative liberties they took with the combat encounters. I won't spoil the goodies of course, but with the reintroduction of certain mechanics and setups for said combat encounters, the battles definitely  became just as much of a high point as the story itself for me. The ending as well, was just the perfect bow that tied together what was  a 150 hour journey from the start of Prelude, to the end of Truth here.The entire package of Mask of Truth reminded me a lot of Xenoblade Chornicles 3. It truly felt like this was the developers swan song, like this was the last game they were ever going to make. What an unforgettable journey this was. Thank you Aquaplus, for gifting to our big blue planet here this beautifully crafted epic that you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: This game ended up being the perfect ending to a 140 hour trilogy. I was worried that its rating's wouldn't live up to the experience, but count me wrong! Mask of Truth combines all the knowledge you have from the first Utawarerumono game and Mask of Deception into a compelling, high stakes story with characters you love, who only get better as the game progresses. It has all the SoL from Mask of Deception and more; it has all the touching, endgame moments from the first game but better and further explained. I was a little confused at the end of the first game, and Mask of Truth sure did explain it well. Not to mention that this series has some of my favorite characters I've seen in fiction, and its protagonist easily ranks at the top of my list. With more amazing music from Aquaplus's sound team, and beautiful art that hits at all the right moments by Amazuyu Tatsuki and Misato Mitsumi and all the talented, hardworking graphicers at Aquaplus. While the bosses and events have never been a strong part of the series, the gameplay has improved and gotten more complex (in a good way) from Deception. Now that was have Uta 1 remake, the series has a slow incline in improving gameplay, which is exactly what you want from this trilogy. In any case, I could talk forever about it since there is so much to unpack, but I will say that this series surprised me in the best of ways, and shook my to my core, easily one of the most compelling games I have had the pleasure of playing. I hope that more of Leaf/Aquaplus games get released on steam, like an official White Album 2 (never happening) but we are getting Utawarerumono Zan and ToHeart Remake!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying end to the trilogy. It's not without issues but it really is a great game. The first half of the game with the party coming to terms with what happened during the ending of Mask of Deception had some really great writing and strong character moments. The characters really are where this series excels, with Haku and Kuon (can't forget Maroro too) becoming some of my favourite characters ever, their voice acting being especially great too. Unfortunately the second half kinda forgets most of the party exists and a few of them barely get any screen time.There are a few weak arcs throughout though which really did bring down the enjoyment and the pacing. And there were quite a few moments that seemed like they'd be a big deal but nothing really came of them. Like when I also found the main villain to be pretty weak, with his stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ followers. Pieces of ♥♥♥♥. But the final boss after his ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was so hype that I stopped caring. Easily one of my favourite final boss fights ever, it was so damn good. And the ending itself was really satisfying, though I wish they expanded on it more by seeing more people's reactions to things.Can't forget the great music too, consistently good through the entire trilogy. There's a lot of tracks that are just okay but a lot of standouts too.It's got its fair share of issues but this trilogy is really worth investing your time into. The writing is really great (most of the time) albeit very slow, especially in the second game, but the payoff at the end is one I haven't gotten very often from games. There were ups and downs, but this trilogy really has had a large lasting effect for me after beating it. Haku, the GOAT.

_childDocuments_.review: The tactical JRPG part of this series was never the its strong suit, lacks depth gravely and creativity specially in Prelude to the Fallen, although they improved this part a lot in Mask of Truth yet it's never a good "game" but as a Visual Novel, it might surpass Muv-Luv Alternative in some parts for me.The story in Utawarerumono is nowhere near prefect, some might say it's a bit jarring with loopholes yet its story and world-building, music, character development combined throughout the series despite its fatal flaws in gameplay is what make Utawarerumono great.I dropped the first game after slogging through Prelude to the Fallen's awful gameplay after 10-ish hours, it's really not that engaging and sometimes boring but I am glad that I finally decided to pick up Utawarerumono again and finish it, get used to that sluggish gameplay of the first game and eventually it grows a little on you, once the characters get developed enough, it becomes easier to engage with, then before you know it, you can't stop playing more and more just to know what happens next, how the story goes.Utawarerumono on the surface may be just your typical dating sim but in its very core, it weaves a captivating narrative that brings together a diverse group of characters bound by fate or pure luck, beyond the surface allure of romance, the game delves into the profound journeys of these characters as they navigate personal growth, confront challenges, and ultimately strive to fulfill their individual resolutions. It is a narrative-rich experience that goes beyond the conventional boundaries of its genre, in the later arcs you can really understand why all of these girls fallen to the main character.Just like Muv-Luv, Utawarerumono if not as same is just as great as a emotional catalyst though the feelings it evoke might not be enough to surpass the Muv-Luv trilogy yet the journeys throughout the series can still strengthen the bonds between the characters and the reader.Tragedy is not just a plot device, it's also a catalyst that propels a story into the realms of depth and emotional resonance, a good story necessitates struggles and the Utawarerumono series definitely achieve this narrative successfully.If you like me who enjoys a strong storytelling, well developed characters, engaging plots, not to mention the huge amount of OSTs and CGs/fanservice it can offers, you have it to give the Utawarerumono trilogy a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, this game is the last of its series, and is the second-part to a two-game story. At the minimum, before playing this game, you should play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception first. If you're interested in what this story and its gameplay might be about, you can find my spoiler-free review and recommendations on the Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception page on Steam. It's been a long time coming, and honestly, I have no idea why I never wrote a review for this game on this platform, but to put it plainly, . I'm going to briefly talk about myself, but feel free to scroll down for my actual review. You see, back in 2019, I bought both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth at a local game trading store for under $20 total. I didn't buy them for any particular reason other than because I was buying them on a whim. I figured since they were sequels, I might enjoy them one day, but I honestly didn't have any expectations for them at all. In fact, I completely forgot about them and didn't touch the games until a whole year later when the COVID pandemic started. Jobless, I saw these two games on my shelf and decided that I might as well play them since I had already bought them. At the time (I was 25 years old), and for most of my life, I was unmotivated and depressed, truthfully an empty and pathetic shell of a person who spoke with hypocrisy and let the world mold him. Who I am now is unlike anything I was before, and the only time I look back at my old self is when I look at this game or think about it and its music. This two-game story is the only game(s) that has ever brought me to tears. This story and its characters moved and inspired me to become a better version of myself with each passing day, so I am not exaggerating when I say that this game changed my life.. I still remember everything that I felt from every scene, from every soundtrack, from every voice and the cadence in which these characters spoke. When I finally finished this game, I felt so empty, it was as if there was a massive void inside of me, continuously eating away at me. I couldn't enjoy anything anymore; there was no food, no alcohol, no song, no game, nor story that appealed to me. Yet as empty as I was, the game had also brought me.. life. I applied for a job at a local warehouse, got it, and worked there for months. I hated working there, but every time I felt like quitting, my thoughts would race back to this game, its story, and its characters, and I'd continue pushing on. Fast forward to now (29 years old), I work in a control center, enjoy my work, and I am also studying other material so that I can continue to work towards my goals and better myself. I will forever cherish this story for as long as I live and that is why I bought the games all over again on Steam and replayed them all once each. Story: 9/10The game begins with many heavy feelings as the plot transitions from the end of Mask of Deception. If Mask of Deception is like enjoying a cup of sake in the company of your boon companions under the night of a full moon, then Mask of Truth is nothing less than a fist that slugs you right in the face with the weight of a roller coaster of emotions. Like the characters themselves, you as the audience may find yourself confused, uncertain, and possibly even broken with each development. At the center of political intrigue, you'll experience an unforgettable story about war and death, loyalty and love, hopes and dreams, duty and desires, and.. memories. Oh, gone are the days of enjoying a nice bowl of rulu or lazily resting at the Hakurokaku Inn.. All-in-all, although there are some developments that feel oddly inconsistent when you compare them to the overall fantastic and consistent world-building of this world, they are simply outliers that do not take away from the greatness that is this story. Music: 10/10The OSTs are amazing. Some soundtracks were designed with the intention of playing around motifs which beautifully tugs at nostalgia when you hear them. The music in this series brings many scenes to life, especially the heavy ones.Gameplay: 9/10This game builds on the previous battle system found in Mask of Deception. Several changes include rebalanced abilities and skills, but the best change made is that characters who do not actively participate in battles (due to deployment restrictions) will still gain some experience at the end of a chapter battle so that they do not fall too far behind like in Mask of Deception. Additionally, there are plenty of extra battle-focused content the player can indulge in, unrelated to the story. Difficulty: 7/10Although relatively easy, the game is more difficult than Mask of Deception. Thank you for the memories, Aquaplus, and thank you, _.

Starting from Mask of Deception however you can see the improvements in writing almost instantly (at least imo) and from about the 4th quarter onwards through Mask of Truth it stays pretty high on the plot diagram.Mask of Deception is  before starting Mask of Truth while Prelude I guess you could skip but its highly highly recommended for worldbuilding and certain plot points. _childDocuments_.review: After completing all 3 games (Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth), this was an absolutely stellar experience. I looked forward to every day I was to get back to the game and progress the story. I wish there was more but am very happy nonetheless to have had the chance to play this series. Although I’ve now completed the story, I still get to play Monochrome Mobius, so there is yet a bit more of this world to enjoy.If the “visual novel” tag tends to turn you off, then please understand this series is a “kinetic” novel. There are no choices, no routes and no self-insert character. It is primarily a narrative experience that you can simply set the dialogue to auto and enjoy watching as though reading a book or listening to an audio-book. There are tactical RPG gameplay sequences when story battles come up, but they are not difficult and largely you will simply be watching the story.I highly recommend the entire series.

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasing conclusion to the series of tactics games.It wraps up the story threads left open by "Prelude to the Fallen", and is pretty much the second, better half to "Mask of Deception".Tactics battles with timed button prompts and hidden inputs, pleasing tactical combat, and a forgiving "rewind" mechanic that lets you turn back time to practice your button timings and to change tactical decisions instead of reloading an earlier save.The story actually got a few tears out of me, which is a somewhat rare thing for a game nowadays.And then there's the music... _childDocuments_.review: The finale of the Utawarerumono series which began with Prelude to the Fallen, the story picks up where Mask of Deception left off and gives a satisfying amount of screen time for some of the original crew from Prelude to the Fallen, if there are any fans that played the first title and are considering to play through the sequels. You don't need to play Mask of Deception to enjoy the game or be able to follow the story, but I would recommend picking up Mask of Deception, which allows you to get the full character development and world building that happens before the events in Mask of Truth. There is about 1.5 hours of story review to fill you in at the start of the game and tutorials that help you learn the battle system for people new to the entire game series (or get reacquainted with it). Overall the gameplay has improved compared to Mask of Deception and the game is balanced with reduced difficulty so it doesn't feel like you're on the verge of losing a battle after making a few bad moves and needing to rewind as much. There is actually a built in tutorial that's optional but recommended as combat gets more complex and tips on how to use each character's skills best against certain circumstances.The game is also better organized compared to Mask of Deception in its navigation menu and it's quite visible where to access the replay battle function to pick up any accessories/equipment you may have missed and get some EXP plus BP points. Pacing of the story keeps things exciting and battles are spread out more evenly compared to the lighter tone Mask of Deception that focused a lot on daily life interactions vs. the ongoing strife that encompasses the entirety of Mask of Truth. It's not completely free of bugs but I haven't had any issues that would break the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: A great ending to the Utawarerumono trilogy.The combat continues to improve slightly over the previous entries, with more depth of action choices and techniques that reward positioning and timing. The training mode also gives more detail on the more advanced tactics and situations that occur, making the optional battles more engaging than in the previous titles.The story and characters continue to be the strong points though, with great writing and a commendable translation. The emotionally versatile voice acting brings a lot of life and colour to the characters, solidifying this as a must play if you are even remotely interested in visual novel style games (I mean, this is that third in the trilogy, so if you made it this far you know what you're getting in for).P.S. I'm not crying! You're crying!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic entry that completes the story that started all the way from Prelude of the Fallen.Mask of Truth, however, is far more fitting to be called the second part of Mask of Deception rather than its sequel due to the stories of both titles being closely related; you can't have the full experience without having previously experienced Mask of Deception.As a Visual Novel, Mask of Truth has:- Deep and intriguing lore and main storyline- Serious as well as hilarious sub-events that expands character development (some are straight up memes)- An incredibly likable main cast and some of the side characters- Surprisingly consistent use of characters- Stunning artwork (a lot of it are considerably NSFW so be warned)- Top tier musicAs a Tactical RPG, Mask of Truth offers: - An unique take of TRPG combat using a timing-based combo system- Newcomer-friendly due to the rewind system and tutorials- Plenty of curious stages that will test your wits in the post-game In summary, it's highly recommended to purchase Mask of Truth alongside Mask of Deception (the DLC characters carry over, don't worry!) Also, it's best to treat Mask of Truth (as well as Mask of Deception to some extent) as a Visual Novel with an extra TRPG attached to it, but trust me, if you're a fan of Visual Novels the story alone makes it worth the money, just beware that some events might have NSFW CGs attached to it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game. As this game is a direct sequel to Mask of Deception(Itsuwari no Kamen), you have to play it first or else you will be spoiled with most of it story as soon as you start a new game. But, I will try to review it based on this game alone as much as possible.First thing first, as I said in my Mask of Deception review, anyone looking to play a great Turn-Based Strategy game may be dissapointed. It's not because this is a bad Turn-Based Strategy game, it's because the game itself more focused on story aspect so play this with a Visual Novel in mind. BUT, the system got improved in this game. Co-op chain system is a good addition to Overzeal system so there are more benefit to staying in Overzeal state. Some character got new moves and of course there are some new playable characters. Also,the new Co-op Finish system is just cool. Other than that, since I have some experience in this kind of genre so I play on Hard difficulty. Even on Hard difficulty the game is not that hard and you don't need to do any grind to beat the game.Now the story. The story overall is really good if you consider all of the game or at least just Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. I, myself will consider it a masterpiece. But if you only look at this one game, first, as the situation is not very good at the beginning for the main character, so there will be high amount of emotional conflict between characters as the MC need to take the burden from Mask of Deception Ending. After the situation around them stabilize there will be a bit of leisure time where everything seems peaceful even though it shouldn't be. Unlike Mask of Deception though, this will not last too long and the story will progress excitingly soon. After that there will be great story writing until the end of the game. You will also feel character bonds from the peaceful time from the first-half of previous game affecting them so much here.And now for the pros and cons.Pros:-Great character and in game event arts. I really love the art personally.-Good 3D battle graphics. Not that cool, but good. The animation and special effect is good.-Good Turn-Based Strategy gameplay. This got improved from previous game. There are new moves and Co-op system. Co-op Finish is just so cool.-Great story with a really good pacing. With all game combined, I personally consider it as masterpiece.-Each character have their own personality that build up as the story goes.-There is level system but you don't need to grind any of your character. Your usual party setup is enough to beat the game without you going out of the way to grind you characters even if you play on Hard difficulty. And now your unused party member also got first time stage clear exp bonus(but not BP) so they won't be useless later even if you don't bring them to battle often.-Many famous Japanese Voice Actress/Actor so those who enjoy it will love it very much. Overall all VAs doing great jobs on this game.-Great English translation. If you understand Japanese you may feel "Wait, that he isn't exactly say that!", but looking on the context it is not a really wrong translation and is still in line with those characters.Cons:-Battle system gameplay may pale in comparison with many other Turn-Based Strategy games.-Free Battle mode(play previous cleared stage) only useful to get missed achievement and grind for small exp. So, most people may not even need to play it.(I don't even play them until I beat the game)-This is a direct sequel game, not a standalone one, so it is much better to play Mask of Deception first.Conclusion:A really great Visual Novel with Turn-Based Strategy battle system as bonus. The story is really great. As it is a direct sequel to Mask of Deception it is highly recommended to play that first. It is even better if you play the first one(Prelude to the Fallen) too either prior to starting this two games or after finishing them. The story got really good pacing and have so many exciting part.If you want a great story game and don't hate Turn-Based Strategy battle system, I really sure that this game series is a really good one.Really, personally a Masterpiece story for me.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. The SRPG gameplay is finally great, not just a fun complement to the actual visual novel and story. The quality of the story goes without saying. Maybe a little too much happens in the third act, but there are more resonant and soulful moments than I can remember. It's hard to imagine a better conclusion, both to the Mask-Truth duology and the series as a whole. This is the kind of series, like Trails in the Sky, that I am grateful to have experienced during my life. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a great story and as a VN its got great production values behind it. I was particularly impressed by the sound track. You do need to play Mask of Deception first though, as they are two chapters of the same story.However, its not perfect. Mask of Deception showed some pacing issues, and these return here, along with entirely too much selective character stupidity because the plot needs to hide information. Moreover, I did not find that Mask of Truth hit as hard as the previous entries, partly because there are no major mysteries to unveil left, and second the game does not know when to stop, leading to what might have been satisfying climaxes being under-cut as the writers need to contrive reasons to keep the story going.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece honestly.   I take back what I said about the last game in terms of strategy depth; it may actually have more depth to it than Disgaea. _childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono Mask of Truth, the final game of the Uta Trilogy, fantastically wraps up the entire storyline, the entire trilogy is top tier in almost every single regard, besides acouple small misteps. While a good portion of the game is a fantastic VN, the SRPG combat is also now finally developed and is honestly one of the most engaging systems i've ever had the pleasure of playing. This accompanied by one of the best overall casts in any game series i've played, ontop of stellar art, fantastic music, heartrending personal character moments. The series is also not afraid to show the horrors of war, and I respect that quite a bit. The series also has a fantastic bit of lore, that just builds on itself with each game, and makes moments when stuff introduced in previous scenes and games come back, you go "OHHH THAT MAKES SENSE" it's absolutely wonderful, everything ties together. If you like VNs, SRPGs or serious fantasy storytelling, you owe it to yourself to play Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception and finally this game, Mask of Truth. You won't be disappointed. These games now mean a lot to me, and I hope it touches your heart, makes you laugh, cry, smile, and CHEER for your heroes like it did for me

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, it had come to the end. It took me extra 50 hours to finish the brutal dream arena after completing the main story but it was worth it. Only one word can describe the ending of Utawarerumono trilogy which is…AMAZING.The story about war and loss, about honor and betrayal, about guilt and deception and most importantly it was the story about love and truth. Utawarerumono was one of the best work of art in term of world building and character development. I love how every important characters including antagonists had the own arc making them closer to the readers. Haku was an extremely well-written protagonist, the last time I’ve seen any protagonist with this much characteristics and development was Takeru from Muv-luv trilogy and it was ages ago, Haku will forever be the only good harem protagonist. The game mechanics have improved a lot compared to its prequel, many characters had better buff and some overpower one was nerf making the gameplay more balance, the tactical side became more relevant than the prequel thank to the variety of status aliments, terrains and overpowered enemies which can make most JRPG fan satisfied. The ending was a bit controversial since it neither conclusive nor opened but in my opinion it worked really well with Utawarerumono universe, it made me not only feel like wanting to know more but also think that it was enough, truly a unique experience. Words cannot describe how much I love this story, it really is a modern classic of Visual Novel medium.Whenever I remember Haku I will remember  this idiom : “For he the man who wear the mask of deception   For he the man who walked through the path of carnage  For he the man who brought hope and salvation for others   For he the one whom legends are sung  For he is the truth Utawarerumono.”

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this story. Is it groundbreaking? No. I was confused at times as to what was going on but there was a gallery that helped answer the questions I had. However, I absolutely loved the soundtrack, and I was so involved with the characters that almost every moment was enjoyable as I cared about what was happening at all times. If you made it this far in the series you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one story told through two games in case someone who doesn't know. You also can't play just Mask of Truth without Mask of Deception and expect to understand everything, there's no point.Mask of Truth is a lot different from Mask of Deception. It picks up right where Mask of Deception ended, but the tone of the game quickly shifts from lighthearted, to outright depressing and sad. It also keeps the battle system from the first game, but adds some content, like Munechika's trials and the Training battleground which are a nice way to earn some items, learn more about mechanics and just grind some levels. Not to say there aren't any funny moments (which are needed to be honest), but it almost completely turns 180 and has a lot more serious tone. This is where the characters get even more depth and start shining, especially Nekone and Haku. I absolutely loved how their relationship slowly developed and in my eyes it's one of the big highlights. Speaking of which, it has too many to count. The story can be predictable at times, but it has a lot of genuine surprises, huge reveals and it's one of the best stories I've seen so far, if not the best. It deals with a lot of topics like going through loss, forcing yourself to accept lies for the greater good, losing your own persona, value of life, etc. The ending is bittersweet, but I feel like it's a bit more sweet than bitter.The following can be said about both Mask of Decelption and Mask of Truth, there were some music I really disliked, but there are a lot more that I absolutely loved, they were outright beautiful and filled with emotion, so overall I was more than pleased. But what I wasn't pleased with was how it's a 720p/30 fps port. The game came out in 2020 and this is absolutely unacceptable. While it doesn't hinder the experience, this kind of lazy port is a big no-no.It's a huge emotional rollercoaster with a lenghty and fantastic overall story through both games with a fun and deep cast of characters you'll most likely end up loving. This is a must buy, especially if you like VNs and don't mind some turn-based strategy battle system.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a great story. Bought this game immediately after completing the prequel mask of deception due to that outrageous cliffhanger, then proceed to eat this second part of the story like a madman. This game has much better distribution of battles sections in-between story sections, unlike the previous game which had 3 to 4 hours of uninterrupted text reading.Multiple times ninja cut onions; significant amount of tears shed.Very satisfying ending, with perhaps one the greatest end boss experience I've ever had.Game's tactical rpg side might seem like a sideshow, but has surprising depth that is fun to explore. The added trials missions makes it a lot easier to understand the finer points of the battle system, and post-story battle dedicated section allows you to have fun with the battle system. Combat can be hilariously fun once you know how some characters can become absolutely broken (oshtoru = raid boss, Kuon = nuke, Kiwru = ICBM, Fumirul = Speedwagon).Anyway, strongly recommend, but only after playing Mask of Deception first of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mainly writing this review to be spoiler-free and to show my appreciation for this game, which feels very underrated for a great game. It is a strategy based VN where the main selling point is the lore and world-building of the game, which I personally really liked. This game is the 3rd part of the Utawarerumono Trilogy:1st:  Prelude of the Fallen2nd: Mask of Deception3rd: Mask of TruthAs the stories take place chronologically, I would recommend playing through all 3 of these games or watching the anime before you jump into the 3rd game. However, the anime doesn't capture that charm in my opinion, so I would just recommend playing the game instead. Playtime is approximately 20~30hours per game if you do not grind for experience points and concentrate on the story solely. Pick up this game/trilogy during a sale and enjoy the emotional roller-coaster as you play through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this is part two of the the Utawarerumono Duology, so if you haven't read part one yet GO READ IT FIRST  AND THE ANIME IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE. It leaves out many important key plot points and thus if you only rely on the anime as your experience of part 1, part 2 will be very confusing. also DONT SEARCH UP ANY MUSIC INVOLVING THIS GAME UNTIL AFTER YOUR DONE READING IT. many of the videos on youtube use cg from the game as a background, with many of them being big spoilers for certain things (i got spoiled this way T^T).Now that i got that warning out of the way, on to gushing about the series.The Utawarerumono series has now officially taken the spot of my Favorite series of all times. everything about this series was just fantastic heck its more then fantastic and i cannot even begin to express how much i love this series. Part 1 end off on a suspense filled cliffhanger that gave us many burning questions and part 2 fully lived up to the hype built up around part 1 while answering everything. This was a fantastic second half of the series and brought about a plethora of memorable moments in the world of Utawarerumono. If you read and enjoyed part one, this is one you definitely want to pick up trust me you'll regret nothing from grabbing this game. The story is fantastic with suspense filled plot that will keep you at the edge of your seat, tearjerker moments that will just make you want to bawl your eyes out, and comedic scenes that will remind you of part one that will feel all the more meaningful among everything else that is going on at the time. The already super loveable characters in part 1 also go through alot of character development that is just amazing to watch and become even more lovable. Overall a fantastic series and i cannot even begin to express how much i love this series its so good that i wish there was more. T^T If there is one issue i have with the game though is the strategy game sections of the game. This has been improved upon greatly compared to mask of deception with many of the battles requiring more strategy while nonetheless still being relatively easy, especially with the 50 turn rewind function the game has. The strategy section also adds to the atmosphere of the game really immersing us with what is going on, however i personally did not like the strategy sections too much due to not being the biggest fan of turn-based strategy gameplay. However, this is only a small component of the game and it only felt like a issue in some of the longer battles which are few and far between.Overall, fantastic game 10000000000000/10 i love this game to pieces and will probably play again sometime in the future. Kuon best girl btw <3

If fantasy settings are not your scene then you will not enjoy this as much, and this is a game that deserves your full immersive attention. i cannot reccommend this game highly enough, to spread it's popularity and to let Hakuoro and Haku become household names for the legends and weight that they carry.This is the conclusion of a trilogy, and it's a conclusion I found myself in tears over, now that it's finally over. _childDocuments_.review: First off, this review might be biased because I just finished the game and its final scenes are still fresh in my mind. With or without recency bias though, I can confidentally say that Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth was an amazing experience and thus I cannot recommend this game enough.As the third and final installment of the Utawarerumono games you most likely shouldn't pick up this game before you got to experience the previous two. Fortunately there is an anime adaption of both the dated first  as well as the 2nd game for those who do not want to dedicate too much of their time to the trilogy since every game can take well over 60h to complete, although playing the 2nd game "Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception" will give you a deeper understanding of both the world and characters of the Utaverse than the anime will.Now then... First off, while Mask of Truth most definitely isn't without its flaws, the one thing that I thought would bother me the most actually turned out way better than I was expecting. Of course I'm talking about the combat system. While it's not the best turn-based strategy RPG out there (at least gameplay-wise) it does have some very intriguing aspects about the combat that prevents combat from being too repetitive. Mixing in QTEs with the for the genre usually rather slow gameplay combined with some other mechanics give the combat system a surprising amount of depth which makes it quite enjoyable in my opinion.The best part about the Utawarerumono series is without a doubt its worldbuilding, memorable characters and hard-hitting storytelling.  If you've played games like FF or one of the Tales of - games then I am 100% sure you will love this piece of art. This was one of the very few games I would give a lot for the chance to replay them completely blind again. The world and story was just that immersive and gripping.Anyways if you've come this far, I'm sure you're at least interested in the Utaverse to some degree and so I highly recommend you check out the anime of the 1st or 2nd game (or play the 2nd game) first and then decide and hopefully see for yourself just how amazing the conclusion to this absolutely incredible story really is.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a journey these two games have been. If you haven't played Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, turn around and play that first! To not give away any spoilers I will just speak about my feelings while playing the game. You really feel immersed in a grand, mysterious fantastical world. This game really spoke to me. Seeing the characters all struggle to overcome sadness, guilt, betrayal, loss, and love was very touching. There were moments in this game that broke my heart and moments that made you feel on top of the world. The combat isn't especially fancy, but it is deep enough to keep you invested, and it requires enough strategy to keep you on your toes. Overall I would absolutely recommend this game, and this series, for anyone who loves visual novels or is interested in visual novels. This is a good entry visual novel because it breaks up the large amount of reading and text of the novel with gameplay and combat, which keeps you from getting too burned out from reading.

_childDocuments_.review: The final game in probably the best strategy rpg kinetic novel trilogy made yet. In my opinion it is also probably the best game of the three. It acts on and wraps up every story thread from Mask of Deception, as well as spinning it's own story from the world building done in MoD. It has a place for every character from MoD and the majority of characters from the original Utawarerumono. My only criticism is that the last act is very long, the opposite problem which Mask of Deception had, without spoilers to put it in words; there are several times I thought the game was over, then it built up for another climax. By the time the credits rolled I was emotionally exhausted, but a smile was on my face so I suppose it's fine.If you play this game and like it but haven't played the original Utawarerumono from 2002 I would tell you to go play it now. It's still good, though obviously dated. Unfortunately you have spoiled a fair bit of the story for yourself by playing this first, but you are still missing the complete picture, so I think it's still worth it.

detailed_description: Wake up, Hakuowlo. It's time to face the world again. You come to in bed, gravely injured, attended by a girl with twitching furry ears and a lush, bushy tail. In time you come to lead the villagers, to whom you owe your name and your life. When the local nobles threaten them, you threaten the nobility right back... Are you a farmer? A scholar? A traitor? A beast? You've forgotten your past, but has it forgotten you? Command your comrades and fight to defend your family, and discover the secrets of this world—and your own lost history! The first game in the hit Japanese tactics-RPG visual novel series Utawarerumono joins its sequels back on PC! Features 30+ hours of story and gameplay Thoughtful, slick, and active tactics-RPG combat Dynamic Chain Attacks and flashy Co-op Chains All-new Auto-Save functionality Customizable keyboard and mouse controls An unforgettable, evocative soundtrack A touching narrative with a moving ending

_childDocuments_.review: Reading about them in the Glossary is fine, just don't touch them in character select. The game thinks it's clever by enforcing continuity, except in the continuity play order, new players like me play this first. If not for the Complete Bundle, I would refund all the DLC for spoiling later games :/Really I just wanted to save others from my own fate, but if you want an actual review: it's an alright game; plot and events follow a lot of anime tropes but is still pretty cute and charming.The gameplay presents no challenge. I went through the first third on normal without increasing a single stat on any of my characters. Even after changing difficulty to hard there wasn't much difference. The game mechanics are a lot like Fire Emblem (or so I've been told; I've only played a bit of the GBA FE's). However, there is a very convenient built-in rewind function, and optional QTE for critical strike which rewards interaction with the combat animations.As a whole, this game should be taken as an introduction and prologue to the world of Utawarerumono, setting the stage for the latter games. Like stated previously, this game's cast are a bit generic but lovable nonetheless. Still any emotional investment in these characters will be well rewarded in the sequels. Of all the copious amount of media (games, books, movies, etc) I have consumed, Utawarerumono is one of the best if not the best franchise that handles its returning cast in its sequels, showing growth and charming interactions with latter casts.Bit of clarification on series as a whole to those who are completely new to the series as I was:

_childDocuments_.review: The complete Utawarerumono series is finally available on Steam and I want to recommend it, so here goes my review even though I still need to finish two of the three games. It's one of my favourite series due to its great story and storytelling (with both comedy and dramatic scenes done right), impressive world-building, and actual (and good) gameplay. So if you like VNs or RPGs and don't mind slow burners, here's an awesome VN/TRPG hybrid.The first game is Prelude to the Fallen (or Lullaby to the Dying) and works as a standalone game, Mask of Deception is an indirect sequel that's more enjoyable with knowledge from the first game, and Mask of Truth is the finale and requires having played both. I'd recommend playing through them in order now that they're all available, especially with Prelude being self-contained. DLC characters are completely optional, and in Prelude's case I'd even advise against buying them since they're related to MoD and MoT and might spoil things. By the way, don't look anything up about MoT lest you get spoiled.Also, you might have heard about a 18+ version. It's because Utawarerumono was first released as an eroge on PC in 2002 at a time where sex scenes were mostly added to sell more copies; an improved version without H-scenes was released on PlayStation 2 in 2006 and served as the basis for all subsequent re-releases of the game, including this one which is a remake in line with the sequels' style. So basically all versions tell the same story (with extra characters in the "console" re-release), and such scenes were not the main focus in the original release. And worry not, actually relevant ones are still referred to. The sequels however were made without 18+ content in mind due to being made for consoles and Aquaplus moving away from adult-only games.While I'm at it, if you're considering watching the anime instead of playing the game, it's a good enough alternative for the most part. Lemme explain: the adaptation of the first game is overall good and gets most important plot points, but doesn't include elements added in the enhanced version and omits some others that ended up being relevant in the sequels. OVAs however *do* contain characters that were added in the 2006 re-release. Then you have The False Faces, which roughly follows the story of Mask of Deception and is enjoyable if you've played it but is in no way an acceptable substitute due to the sheer amount of changes. Ah, and don't worry about not finding a HD version of the original anime, many shots and 3DCG elements actually held up better in SD; the rest looks great in HD though.Finally, a word about the port. It is unfortunately 720p and 30fps, just like the original console version, however it does not impact the game's quality. I feel like 3D segments in particular would benefit from being rendered at higher resolutions, though other elements might scale poorly and there's a chance the UI was drawn at that resolution. I won't complain about the framerate lock though, since I've seen way too many games end up broken when trying to reach higher framerates. And more importantly, the port has PC-specific features bringing almost everything you might expect from a VN/RPG on PC (yes, that includes proper mouse and keyboard support), as well as customisable button prompts (say, to use DualShock 4 icons). They even added an auto-save feature during battles to all three games and polished the translation, fixing typos as well as awkward sentences (like the infamous "Who the ♥♥♥♥ are they?").I'll massively update this review once I've finished this game. In the meantime, I hope it helps introducing people to the series and clearing things up!

_childDocuments_.review: The pioneering work of the Utawarerumono series shows players another wonderful and magnificent story. As always, it cleverly combines SLG and visual novels, and compared with the other two works in the series, Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen has its unique characteristics.The soul-stirring music and exquisite original paintings allow players to enjoy a retro Japanese traditional visual novel experience, and this SLG battle design is more humane than the other two works, players will hardly encounter excessive difficulties during the game. At the same time, the shaping of some characters in the plot and the description of the daily plot are also very vivid.Still, the game's flaws are pretty glaring. As a visual novel, the plot of this game is obviously weak in the middle stage, which is mainly reflected in the too-fast development of the plot and the insufficient shaping of some characters. And many of the foreshadowings buried in the plot are just passing through or simplification. Even considering that the script of this work was written in 2002, it still has many unqualified places.Overall, this game is worth playing for players interested in the genre, as well as fans of Utawarerumono and Visual Novel games - especially those who played Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth first. But please note that if you haven't played the above two games, then please play Prelude to the Fallen first, you will get the best gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "A journey that is only yours"Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is a game I have hard time writing about. I want to talk about the game, but I don't know how to put my experience into words. I'll try my best here.Gamers in their 30's, like myself, rarely change their opinions about what or which games they consider to be "the best ever". I've never had a clear number one myself. I enjoy almost all types of games. However, I'm a story guy. I love good stories in the media I consume. I've seen thousands of films and series, played thousands of games since the days of the NES... but I've never cried this much during anything ever.I had to stop multiple times during my journey to cry and think. There are many sad, touching and deep scenes in the game. At one point, I spent an hour just sitting silently on my balcony at night. I wasn't sad. I was touched by the story, storytelling and everything I saw and heard, from the pictures to the music. This particular scene was constructed in such a way I'd never seen in any form of media; the most multilayered scene where everything was perfectly executed. After the scene, I was fairly certain I'd found my all-time favorite game... maybe even my all-time favorite piece of media.These characters, especially Hakuowlo and Eruru, are so well-written good people. I hate watching modern media where there are no good characters, only ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. To experience this god-tier story with these characters, has helped me to feel better about myself and life in general. Younger players might not understand the deeper scenes correctly, only because they lack life experience. I know I wouldn't have if I'd played this 10-15 years ago. There are subtle scenes that are not explained to the player. This reliance on the fact that the player understands what's happening is a rare treat.I had some idea where the story would go, but I was so, so wrong... and many times. I was shocked and jaw wide open time after time. I didn't expect this journey to be so real, brutal and even disgusting at times. I though I was going to play something happy and cheerful. How wrong was I. I did get those moments too. Some comedy in the mix too. But to me, this game is probably the most adult I can think of.The gameplay itself is completely secondary when compared to the story, but it's mighty fine too. Battles on normal are fairly easy for people who have played plenty of turn-based strategy games before. I did fail couple of times thou. Overall, the battle system is good and it has a nice flow to it.After finishing the game, I had to install the next one. I need to complete this journey and see if the other games, and the anime I ordered, are even close to being this great. Can't wait to move onto the Mask of Deception.This is my all-time favorite game. My review can't express how I feel about the game. Many tears of sadness and joy were shed... and will be when I get to playing this one again. I loved every second of this. I hope some of you experience the game like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point: I've been gaming, reading, and watching TV/movies for 30 years, and the Utawarerumono trilogy is, as a whole, the most impactful work of fiction I've ever read.  I cannot recommend it highly enough.  I've been a fan of the series for 15 years now, and every time I come back to it, I'm reminded why I fell in love with it in the first place.This is a modern remake of the first game in the series, and as such, it's the best entry point.  I will say that I consider the first game to be the weakest one in the series -- but saying that is misleading, because it's still a great visual novel that I would recommend to anybody who likes serious fantasy stories.  It's a story about war, personality identity, found family, and the hubris of humanity.  On its surface, it can sometimes seem lighthearted and colorful -- and there are a lot of genuinely heartwarming moments of bonding and familial affection -- but it's also not afraid to have serious drama with meaningful consequences.What makes this game stand apart from the crowd?  One is its cast of characters: the protagonist is an adult man who is level-headed, reliable, and intelligent.  He's not a schoolchild or an idiot; he genuinely earns the trust and affection of the people around him.  The rest of the cast is also a wide range of characters who all may seem tropey on the surface, but all of them have a surprising amount of depth and characterization.The artwork and music are also great; they stood out in the original 2002 version of the game and have been polished up and remastered here, and they're still some of the best in the business.  I would also be remiss to not mention the game's combat system; adding a turn-based, tactical combat system into a visual novel was unheard of in 2002 and is still rare now, and Utawarerumono's battles both help to break up long stretches of reading and also get the reader more immersed in the seriousness of the conflicts.  If I had one complaint to make about the first game, it would just be that the combat system is pretty simple; it's enjoyable, but it won't challenge SRPG veterans.  Like every other aspect of the game, it keeps getting better in the sequels, and Mask of Truth, the final game, is also the best SRPG I've ever played.I will say that the PC ports of these games have one technical issue I'm not a fan of: they're locked at 720p/30Hz.  It's not a huge problem; you're going to spend 80% of the game just looking at still images and reading text, after all.  It would be really nice for the 3D battle sequences to at least be rendered in a higher resolution, but sadly, that's not an option.Despite that, I'm still confident in saying that this is one of the best hidden gems of fantasy storytelling to ever come out of Japan.  Please play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: The wait is finally over. 19 years after its original release, us in the West can finally play Utawarerumono in English and on PC. It comes a year after we got the two sequels Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, completing the trilogy on the platform. Now, before I begin, I should give a brief explanation on what exactly this game is, because I know a lot of people just look at the title and are scared off by how long it is. In short, it’s a visual novel with tactical RPG gameplay segments and the first in the larger Utawarerumono series. It’s a bit confusing as we actually got the second and third game in that series (Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth respectively) released on PC last year, so it may have been released out of order, but at least the trilogy is complete now and those that have been holding off on the two sequels can get started with this one.Having watched the 2006 anime adaptation of the game, I went in already knowing how the story would go, but somehow found myself sucked into it yet again. Before I knew it, five hours had passed, a rare occurrence for me when playing visual novels. It starts off relatively slow and mostly lighthearted, but eventually builds up into this bigger, more ambitious fantasy story – one full of likeable characters, interesting plot developments, and a nice overall sense of pacing.In fact, the pacing was largely the reason why I was able to keep reading without noticing the time passing. That and I’m personally a huge fan of fantasy stories with a good grasp on worldbuilding, which is exactly what the beginning of this game offered. However, even when it does get a bit more serious, it never quite loses that lighthearted charm that it starts with – similar to how the plot develops in Mask of Deception. It’s quite unique for the medium and a welcome change of pace as someone that plays a ton of these games.And for those that have seen the anime, the game provides some really good context and insight into the events from it. I watched it many years ago and had a good time returning to that story while also further immersing myself into it – I was actually surprised with how close an adaptation that anime was now that I’ve been playing the game. It is a long one though. The anime may have been 26 episodes, but this is a 30-hour game, so there’s a lot of ground to cover – even if it is the shortest of the trilogy.There’s also a sizeable tactical RPG side to it that comes in the form of turn-based battles on a grid, similar to the Disgaea games. The gameplay during these segments is pretty straightforward and not too in-depth, but an otherwise nice distraction from the story. There are character-specific skills, equipment bonuses, usable items, a leveling system, and even boss fights. It’s not too bad on normal difficulty, but can be ramped up to hard for those that want a challenge. I personally found the normal difficulty to be a nice balance between being able to enjoy the story and having the occasional challenging fight.Right off the bat, what I immediately noticed was the difference in art style between this game and the two sequels. I mean, there was a 13-year gap between them in Japan, but I had thought the art would have been updated to look more in-line with the sequels given that this is a remaster. And honestly, I’m glad they didn’t. The art has been brushed up since its original release for sure, but it still maintains that distinct early 2000’s anime aesthetic. It’s hard to explain exactly what constitutes that, but it was actually quite nostalgic as someone that has seen a lot from that era.Then there’s the music, which is just as good as it is in the sequels and even expanded a bit here. You’re able to choose from the original music and the new “special extended” music when starting up a new game. I tried and enjoyed both of them, each providing the story with its range of laidback, slice of life fantasy tracks and more energetic action tracks for the gameplay parts.I should also talk about the port, as this game is based on the PS4 version released last year by NIS America. Just like the two sequels, it runs at 720p and is locked to 30 fps. However, it does offer in-game options for higher resolutions, it just scales the game to display at them rather than do so natively – the opposite of most VNs that simply change the monitor to match the in-game resolution. These specs are the standard for most visual novels on PC, but I won’t deny that it would have been nice to see higher-res art offered, especially because there are gameplay segments and you can easily tell they are being upscaled.Otherwise, the port is alright. It’s got the usual VN settings, but also offers remappable keyboard controls on top of that along with controller support. This release is actually the definitive edition of the game because it also adds auto-saves and improves the translation a bit compared to its release last year.For those wondering if there are any H-scenes, the short answer is no. The original 2002 release had them, but all subsequent re-releases and remasters had them removed – and it’s honestly for the better given that many compare them to Fate/stay night’s case in that they are completely unnecessary and even detract from the overall story.With all of that said, Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen easily earns my recommendation. It’s an excellently told fantasy story that pretty much gets everything right, with likeable characters, good worldbuilding, and some really nice pacing – enough so that I hardly noticed the time passing while playing. Then there’s the solid art and music backing it up, cementing the game (and by extension, the series) as one of the best fantasy VNs on the market. Honestly, I could see myself using this as a recommendation for those looking to get into visual novels, especially for fantasy fans.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Is Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen a good game? Yes. That's the shortest, and probably best answer I can give you. If you want to hear more, the following will be some of my ramblings on the game, but be warned they may not be well organized.There are dozens, hundreds of things I could say about this game, how it's a quality remake of a huge piece of my childhood, how the world it presents pulls you in with character-driven world building, a convincing main character, while still keeping a lighthearted tone that stops you from getting tired of worn out. How when things get serious, you feel it, deep in your heart, how even now 12 years after I first played this game, the story still cuts through me, makes me smile, makes me laugh, makes me cry - it's such a ride, and it's such a joy.The biggest changes from the original version I remember playing are the ttrpg segments and the soundtrack - even with the original ost option turned on (which is a very nice touch by the way) the songs are all remasted in higher quality, often with new vocals. The additional songs from the rest of the trilogy added by the extended soundtrack blend in rather seamlessly and the having played through the game with both (a new game plus run was rather mandatory for me) I can comfortably say I like the extended one better, despite my nostalgia.The ttrpg gameplay has been improved a considerable amount. Issues the original had were hammered out by things like equipment, consumable items (you can give healing items to other character so Eruruu isn't your only source of health anymore!) but ultimately it isn't super involved - this is more of a story than a game and while there's enough depth to lose yourself in, nor anything groundbreaking, it's entertaining and a good diversion from the extended story sections - kind of a way to take breaks from all the reading the game has you doing. The new training mode is a perfect example of this; play meaningless, non-story related battles over and over for items, gear, exp - but more just to take a break when you feel like it.As for the story itself, there's far too much to even say. We start, as I'm sure you read by now on the store page, as a man with a mask waking up with no memories. The story is told entirely through his eyes, narrated by his inner thoughts and dictated by his choices - there are no "routes" in this vn, the story is linear. However the large cast of characters, each filled with quirks and unique appeal has a way of drawing you in, while the medieval fantasy setting helps to keep things quite grounded. When our protagonist tries to explain how to grow crops using fertilizer, the villagers simply call it a magic charm and put their faith in him, despite his attempts to explain.Visually, the game is very similar to how it first appeared in 2002 - the resolution has been improved and there has been some cleaning up done to the art, but the style has been preserved and it is stunningly beautiful. Paired with the wonderful soundtrack, I almost find myself crying just looking at the cg gallery and remembering the bittersweet happenings of the story.I'll admit, I'm not very good at this kind of thing - especially when I'm trying not to spoil things, so I think I'll just stop now. Ultimately it's your call, but I honestly cannot recommend this game enough. If you've played either of the other two games, this one is a must try. If you haven't, this is the best place to start the series. If you have any interest in fantasy stories, in visual novels, hell even just in ttrpgs, please, please PLEASE give this a try. You won't regret it.
