_childDocuments_.review: "Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen" is a remake of the game "Utawarerumono (2002)". As the author of this review, I'm very fortunate to be able to experience such a masterpiece. I also took this opportunity to watch『Utawarerumono』, a TV animation adapted from the game of the same name was broadcast as early as 2006. At this moment, in order to preserve the touching and joy of this group of works in my heart, I hereby use this article to express my emotions, as well as my views and understanding of the work.Let's start with the battle link. The battle of this game is a typical SLG war chess game. Its exquisite battle scenes and combat operations with a sense of impact require players to experience it themselves, I’ll not go into too much detail. In contrast, the battle scenes of the anime "Utawarerumono" appear stiff and rough, which does slightly affect the viewing experience. But one thing needs to be explained: in the game, when the gorgeous and cool pictures attract ur attention, u’ll feel restless in a long section of ordinary daily story, and u’re eager to have a battle can bring pleasure and not pay attention to the dialogue of the characters, even if the plot isn’t bad or even lively and interesting. In addition to the battle, I prefer to put the highlight of this review on the core plot, so I’ll talk about the particularly exciting parts of the plot separately.Some villains portrayed in the story have a way of thinking and actions confuse that some people: Nuwangi who bullies the weak, Niwe who’s a fighting maniac, and the emperor Olikakan who vents hatred, etc. Although these villains are in high positions, they have no mercy on the civilians of other countries or even their own country, and are 'proficient in everything' in burning, killing, and looting. This can be called 'individualism' that acts for one's own selfishness and according to one's own wishes. Dii, as the leader behind this series of events, is also「The Great Liberator」who can bring happiness and disaster to people in the setting. He’s a special existence and cannot be simply classified as one of these villains. In addition, Kuuya of Kunnekamun, who is against the White God Hakuowlo in the story, is also the only character who survived the struggle with the protagonist. As for whether it also belongs to the 'villain' I mentioned, it depends on everyone's understanding of the work.Hakuowlo (ハクオロ) is the protagonist, also known as the White God. Hakuowlo is a different emperor in my opinion. He is 'weak', although he’s the ruler of a country, he doesn’t have the domineering and tyranny of the villains, and the decisions are always made by subordinates. Especially the helplessness he showed when he was tied up along with his bed by his 'servant' Karulau and taken to another country to participate in the war was really comical and laughable. In addition, he’s also 'capable', I believe everyone has no doubt about this. After all, he was originally「The Great Liberator」who created the sub-human world, whether it’s politics, military, science and technology. It's just the combination of 'capable' and 'weak' makes the character image of Hakuowlo stand out. Is Hakuowlo a gentle and kind person, or is he not suitable to be an emperor? This’s also left for everyone to think about, I’m just talking about it in general.Love bound by a pact refers to the feelings that the heroine Eruruu(エルルゥ) developed towards Hakuowlo after signing the pact with him, her soul bounded by restrictions of the pact. I think this part can be regarded as one of the places where the artistic effect brought to the audience is 'explosive'. It's just the depict is not in place enough, but it's enough to move the audience.Eruruu is one of the highlights of this work. In the story, her feelings for Hakuowlo seem reasonable to others, but painful to herself. From the beginning, she accompanied Hakuowlo and treated his injuries, to the death of her grandma Tuskur, she and her sister Aruruu were entrusted to Hakuowlo to take care of them. The three of them were like family, this process all explained the rationality of Eruruu's feelings for Hakuowlo. Although the true face of Hakuowlo is「The Great Liberator」, he treats all his companions kindly, especially Eruruu. However, after knowing the pact with Hakuowlo,she hesitated and even denied her feelings. She believed in the so-called "complete dedication from soul to flesh and blood, even a hair" pact, abandoned feelings which had buried deep in her heart. The funny thing is the pact Eruruu has always abided by was neatly abolished by Hakuowlo who knew the truth.This duel is the finale of the story and also the highlight. It’s not only the key to unlocking the mystery of Hakuowlo's life experience, but also the output of different values of this fictional world. The focus is on the dialogue between「Empty Shell of Mine(空蝉)」and「Doppelganger of Mine(分身)」. Note here I deliberately do not use "Hakuowlo" and "Dii" coz I wanna separate the will of God as a「The Great Liberator」from the human. This's a fight between god&god, and a fierce collision of two ideas, not grievances between people.The essential reason for the duel between「Empty Shell」and「Doppelganger」is that the two have different views on ruling the world. 「Empty Shell」believes the world should implement the policy of helping the poor and the needy weak, and harmonious coexistence between races; 「Doppelganger」believes the world is the law of the jungle, and the survival law of the strong survives and the weak perishes. It’s worth reminding although the whole story is narrated from the perspective of the protagonist, but the non-protagonist isn’t necessarily evil. Ofc, there’s no need to refute the individualistic villain mentioned above, and it’s recognized by anyone as bad.Think about the above problem from another angle. Can't both ways of thinking be adopted together? Although the two seem contradictory, there’s still a solution. Recalling the ancient Chinese thoughts on governing the country, there are three famous ones: Confucianism, Taoism, and Legalism. When the society is turbulent, the country is governed by ‘Taoism’, and when the society is stable, the country is governed by ‘Confucianism’. As for ‘Legalism’, both are taken.  It can be seen from this the confrontation between「Empty Shell」and「Doppelganger」isnot unsolvable. Videlicet, the two can take turns to govern the world. Therefore, tracing back the cause of the whole story, we have to blame early awakening of「Empty Shell」. In the end, after discovering he was the embodiment of Uitsualnemetia's good half, Hakuowlo challenged「Dark Witsuarunmitea」Dii, the embodiment of the darker half, and emerged victorious by fusing with it, unifying the「Uitsualnemetia」. Afterward, Hakuowlo asked to be sealed away for a while to prevent any more damage to the world but promised Eruruu that he would see her again. Eruruu and others will uphold the will of「Empty Shell」and continue to develop the world in the direction of their ideal.._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._.In general, this’s a masterpiece that combines rich emotional descriptions, the collision of different political ideas, and the inheritance of spiritual culture. Its unprecedented worldview setting also shocked me a lot. In the final analysis, when it comes to the explanation of the game title, 'Utawarerumono' means the person or thing (spirit) that is praised. I think the game praises the spirit of「The Great Liberator」of Hakuowlo who sacrifices himself for others, loves the country and the people, and values friendship and righteousness. Even if the god will be destroyed, his spirit will be praised on forever.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a widely praised and beloved trilogy of RPG-Visual Novels, with Prelude being the first game in the series, followed by  and .Within the first few hours of gameplay, this story is sure to suck you in with its lovable cast of characters, comfy atmosphere, and thriving world. I'm not really a fan of RPG gameplay in visual novels, but Utawarerumono seamlessly integrates the RPG gameplay into the main story while not breaking my immersion. The combat while simple, is pretty fun and offers a challenge when it needs to. It takes a while for the story to pick up, but once it gets the ball rolling, you'll be thrust into an epic story filled with conflicts, friendships, love, family, sacrifice, world-changing twists and an ending that will stick to you for days. Definitely an experience I will cherish for years to come and I couldn't be more excited to play the sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out super good.  The combat is fun, the writing is good, the voice acting is good.  The story begins with a very dramatic core, (minor spoilers for the very first part of the game) the tale of a people rising up against their unjust rulers.Sadly, it quickly abandons that tone and becomes a waifu-collecting harem hijinks game.  That's not to say it's awful necessarily, if you like anime about a harried male protagonist being pulled in all directions by an ever-growing collection of fawning women, then this might be a good game for you.  For me, I don't really care for those types of stories and more importantly the constant tone switching was too much to bear.  One moment we're in a meeting room discussing the possibility and ramifications of being dragged into a war, the next moment we're being kidnapped by our gang of waifus and dragged into a plan that is definitely going to cause all those awful things we just had a meeting about.  The writers weirdly seem aware of of the political complexities inherent in their story, they just can't resist doing silly anime hijinks anyways.

And this trend continues throughout the whole game!Story-wise, it's very good. The story will bring you to an incredible emotion roller coaster that is not forced and feels natural. _childDocuments_.review: Read the full review here: Utawarerumono may be nearly 20 years old, but this port represents the first time the game has received an official English translation release on PC.If all you want to know is whether this is a good port, I can say that I had no issues with the game.  This port is an adaptation of the Vita remaster, so this game can run on a potato.  I should note, however, that some AMD graphics card users reported some screen tearing, although I do not know how bad or widespread this is.The textures are detailed, but the polygon count of character models definitely shows its PlayStation 2 era roots.  Graphically, the game runs at 720p, and is upscaled to fit larger resolutions, resulting in some minor blurriness. The game is also locked at 30 FPS, like most games of the era, although being mostly a visual novel and tactical game, you will notice this less than you would in an action game.The game comes with a multitude of options, with full controller support and an option to change what button prompts are given to you on-screen (from PS or XBox or Switch controller to keyboard icons), and you can rebind keyboard keys, but not controller keys, at least without a 3rd party controller rebinding software.  The game can almost entirely be played with the mouse, however, and you only need a few buttons on the keyboard even during combat sections, since this game is fairly menu-driven.If however, all you are here for is the "plot", keep in mind that no version past the original 2002 release had sex scenes, the game's story was rewritten and expanded since then, and there is zero chance those scenes are being patched in.  If you're adamant about only buying the version with sex scenes, this probably isn't the game for you, anyway, since there's only about six to start with in a 60 hour game.  There was a fan translation patch released years ago, if you can LEGALLY find a copy of the original game.  Keep in mind that the effects of the sex scenes, I.E. the main character having children that are plot-relevant to the sequel games, are still in the game.Gameplay-wise, Utawarerumono is a split between "Tactics" JRPG and a traditional visual novel.  This split skews  towards Visual Novel for the first half of the game, with hour-long novel sections punctuated by 5-minute battle sections.  Utawarerumono takes its time setting up plot threads and raising tension in them before paying them off with a conflict, and the fact that they can be keeping several plot threads baking in the oven at a time can lead to very long stretches between climaxes to individual plot threads.The protagonist of the story, Hakuowlo, is treated as a strategic and political genius by the text itself, but I find it hard to keep up with, as Hakuowlo doesn't just have the typical harem anime protagonist obliviousness to the fact that all the girls are in love with him, he seems to lack any awareness of human emotion whatsoever, needing people to tell him that the guy screaming how he hates him and will kill him is actually angry at him for him to understand.  It seriously undermines the way that the story tries to present the main character as hyper-competent in every way to have him bumble on something so basic.This isn't as serious as the way that the absolute baby-eating cartoon villains of this story undermine the tone, however.  This game wants to be Game of Thrones, with serious intrigues and games of political one-upsmanship, but the villains make Bowser look competent.  The emperor that starts the rebellion that starts this whole mess originally drove the villagers to the point of rebelling against their taxes being so high they faced starvation because he was literally bankrupting the empire paying for hair product to give himself an afro.  I'm not kidding.  The super-serious general guy who the story is trying to play as being torn between loyalty and duty then tries to suggest that maybe burning the empire down for hair product is slightly short-sighted only gets beaten over the head for his troubles... and yet, they still want to play his loyalty to the emperor as serious and tragic, not absolutely moronic.  Sure, Joffrey was manifestly unfit for the throne, but he at least didn't spread the rebellion by burning the villages that  rebelling against him so that every remaining village felt the need to join the rebellion against him just to survive.  Did I mention that, because they didn't have enough screentime for some villains to make you have good reasons to hate them, nearly all the named villains that you're supposed to root for getting killed look like pigs vaguely contorted into human shape that also have weird accents and verbal ticks so they laugh like "NYEHYEHYEH"?With that said, this story is still being re-released for a reason, and it has a full-length 2006 anime available on Funimation for you to watch, so it does eventually get past some of the absurd elements... although some of the later twists can also be considered absurd. (The anime can be a better viewing experience than the visual novel, as there are a lot of fights that are just narrated in the visual novel section that are just text descriptions and sound effects.  Having actual animation and not relying upon a small pool of still images of characters makes the non-interactive story parts much more interesting.)The actual tactical battles feature characters with limited abilities, most similar to games like Fire Emblem.  For example, the healer characters can only heal, never attack.  Mages only use magic, and fighters only physical attack.  You get three main stats besides HP, which are attack or healing power, physical defense, and magic defense.  Each character gets their own turn in the queue, but there is no apparent speed stat, and ending a turn without attacking or moving does not make your next turn come faster, so staying out of range to make an enemy waste a turn is often a good move.  In fact, playing defensively in general and giving your healers as much time as possible to restore your allies is a much better strategy than trying to act aggressively to take down enemy units, even when they are capable of healing, themselves.  Attrition favors the player.The only action elements to the game are a pseudo-quick-time-event where you hit the "confirm" button (left mouse) when a ring lines up during attacks.  This does not actually increase damage or make attacks hit, however, it just adds percentage to a Zeal bar that gives you a special attack when it is full.  In fact, the game is very deterministic in its random elements, even to the point of telling you in advance that you'll do 0 damage when attacking a character with a "chance to deflect arrows" ability when that ability will activate.  A "rewind" function lets you go back up to 50 actions in the move order to allow you to turn battles around, and the dice rolls will be the same every time. A unique way to cut down on save-scumming, for sure.One sour note is the day-one DLC.  These are all characters from the sequel games that are just plugged in as extra party members during battles, and they have no plot relevance.  It might be a version of pay-to-win, but since you have unit deployment caps equal to the number of plot characters you would have anyway, you'd have to take the plot-relevant characters out to field the DLC characters.  It's a transparent no-effort money-grab but at least it's one that's easy to pass up with no negative consequence? I'm not sure if that makes it better or worse.All told, if you're the kind of gamer that hears "visual novel tactics RPG", and thinks this might be your sort of game, you probably won't be too disappointed, some of the narrative elements aside.  If you like the series, and want a "future proof" version that won't die with your PS4, this is the one to get.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I really liked this game/VN, although it's probably one of those cases where my rational brain tells me it's not as good as I feel it is. It's probably not worth $60, but if you can get it on sale, it's a good recommendation.The characters are likable, although almost none of them really have any time to develop. They remain mostly static throughout the entire story; for instance, one girl starts out as an innocent child who likes honey, and ends the story as an innocent child who likes honey. Character development is certainly not a strength of Utawarerumono, even if, again, characters are likable enough. It more-or-less plays out like a slice-of-life anime, but that's still no excuse to not develop your characters. Look at what Cowboy Bebop did, for instance. Given the "harem" nature of the story at times, I'd say it was a wasted opportunity for the game to not include more in the way of player decisions. Several women in the story throw themselves at the main protagonist. But you can never alter the trajectory of their arcs in any way. It would've been nicer if we could've chosen to foster these relationships organically, a la Sakura Wars. Instead, the story is entirely linear, with 0 decisions that the player ever has to face. One area where Utawarerumono shines is in its worldbuilding. I found myself far more engaged with learning about the different nations and the world's backstory, than I was with some of the characters' relationships. Utawarerumono's setting feels like everything that God Wars should've been, but wasn't. That being said, I won't claim that the game's setting is anything exceptional or revolutionary, as pleasant as it may be. If you boil it down, it's mostly a predictable romp through a Japan-esque world with light sci-fi stylings. And weird, convoluted names. Lots of them: Uitsulnemetia, Amrulineulka, Hakuowlo, and Omkamiyamukai to name a few. (Then there's Dii, as a nice change of pace.)As a strategy RPG, it's mediocre at best. Battles are all extremely easy, to the point that my characters were one-shotting almost every enemy throughout the entire game. AI is mind-numbingly moronic. Even the final boss did not pose a threat to my team, and I didn't grind AT ALL. Oboro in particular is absolutely busted: he has the best mobility in the game, a very high "speed" stat (which functions like in Shining Force; he takes his turns more often than other units), and one of the best attack growths in the game. In Utawarerumono's defense: the SRPG stuff is at least not a detriment to it. This is more than I can say of some other games. It's somewhat disappointing that the game was not more strategically engaging than it is. But meh, it could've been worse, so I'm fine with it. One thing that's particularly odd about the game is how many of the CG backdrops are straight-up recycled from earlier parts. You'll find yourself revisiting the same cliffside road many times, despite the story taking you through the entire continent. Was it really not possible to do better than this? Especially in 2020? For a $60 game?It took me around 20 hours to finish the entire thing, so yeah, probably not worth $60. Yet, all this comes to say: I really did enjoy it, even if my rational brain can pick up on all these areas for improvement. It's possible that Utawarerumono is a worse game than I think it is, and that's fine. I'm looking forward to experiencing the other two Utawarerumono VNs that are also on Steam. I'd be interested in seeing other Visual Novel/Strategy RPG fusions, since it's a rather unexplored concept.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for so long to begin my Utawarerumono journey that when I saw the then upcoming PC release I couldn't believe my luck. An instant day one purchase and 40 or so hours later, however, I can't help but feel I might've been building myself up for disappointment right from the get go. In terms of narrative, gameplay, & production, there's so much to I enjoyed but also so much I truly disliked - I'll do my best to cover all of it.The visual novel elements are beautifully illustrated with each character having a fair collection of sprites & emotional portrayal, which really helps to develop the world early on in the read. The backgrounds are also vivid & detailed, making this near 20 year old VN an absolute pleasure on the eyes... Until you get to the SRPG sections. I'm a realist, and I understand there's not going to be much potential for a major graphical overhaul in a title as niche as this, however I don't think that excuses the art quality of the SRPG sections when a game is priced as high as this one currently is. Despite being shorter than both of its sequels, it's currently 50% more expensive than either of them in the UK, which is a bit of a bitter pill to swallow. At near-AAA prices I'd hope for a little more than what's perhaps best described as upscaled PS2 visuals, but hey, it's not that the game is ugly during these periods - it just isn't anywhere near the quality of the VN segments which have aged incredibly well.Gameplay is also a bit of a hit & miss, with the combat starting off relatively tactical & interesting before devolving into one shotting nearly everything until the final chapter even without any sort of out-of-story combat training. Perhaps this is something that's addressed with the higher difficulties (I played on normal), but again, it's hard to excuse a difficulty curve that looks like an incredibly wide valley (\____________/). Perhaps that's a benefit to those who are just seeking to enjoy the story, but for me, the combat quickly went from engaging to disinteresting, & every time it popped up it seemed like more of a chore than something I was actually enjoying.The story is perhaps the most disjointed & bizarrely paced I've read in a while, with there simply being too much crammed into some (gameplay & non-gameplay) periods & absolutely nothing packed into others (although I've always been a fan of good slice of life, so that's alright with me personally). The ending especially feels incredibly rushed in its pacing which did leave me feeling a little bit empty afterwards, but it's a problem that's fairly consistent throughout the read. There's other issues I took with the story that others might think tread into spoiler territory, so while they're mild at best, I'll mark them as a spoiler (you've been warned!): That said, the world & the lore itself is fascinating. You might find it all to be pretty dense early on, and you'll almost certainly find yourself referring to the in-game glossary to make sense of certain names & their associations, but it's something that pays off in the end, & hopefully over the following installments as well. On another positive note, the cast itself is great & plenty entertaining throughout, which helped turn what would otherwise be an overall negative experience into a pretty positive one, which gives me some hope for when I finally dip my toes into MoD/MoT. The OST, while rarely mindblowing, is enjoyable throughout & compliments the story nicely, though there's little to nothing there I'll be going out of my way to listen to in isolation.On the technical side of things, I experienced zero issues with the PC port. Everything is really well presented, & it controls very well with both KB/M & the good ol' trusty Xbox controller.Overall, it's a recommendation, but a very tentative one (especially at the current price). It's value to me will very much depend on just how much better it's sequels actually are, because while Utawarerumono really does lay the seeds with its strong cast & lore, it really doesn't give them the light they need to properly grow into something beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is pretty terrible, honestly.  Especially when compared to similar games like Fire Emblem, Langrisser, Tactics Ogre, Symphony of War, just name a grid-based combat game and Utawarerumono will seem rather unintuitive.So why am I recommending it?  Because it's a Visual Novel pretending to be an SRPG.  While games like Trails in the Sky do the "I'm actually a VN even though I pretend to be another genre" better, Utawarerumono manages to have its own charm, with realistic (so far at least, I'm about 3 hours in and some of that time was a bit idle admittedly) characters and a compelling plot.  A VN lives and dies based on its writing and characters, and this game seems to be compelling enough to be worth a read.If you're looking for combat or gameplay, sure, I'll bet other JRPGs like Trails in the Sky and Persona 5 would better fit your needs.  The aforementioned Fire Emblem or Langrisser definitely fit the SRPG itch, including the more recent Symphony of War.  But this game seems to be more of a narrative and story experience than having great gameplay.  If you're cheap or want a free experience, you can try Exit Fate as well.If you're read this whole thing, you're the kind of demographic who might enjoy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is the recent rerelease of the 2006 PS2 Japan-exclusive game Utawarerumono: Chiriyukusha e no Komoriuta, which, itself, was a rerelease of the 2002 Japan-exclusive PC eroge Utawarerumono. The game has had both significant and minor alterations made to it during its near 20-year (official) Western release, the most obvious being the removal of the eroge scenes available in the original and the massive improvements made to the turn based combat. These scenes being removed does make sense, considering they were always going to fail the Sony check when making the move to console, but it would be unfair to suggest their exclusion is completely painless. Never a hard eroge at heart, Utawarerumono used these parts sparingly, usually to highlight each character’s vulnerability before then being harem’d by the protagonist. This all now happens off screen before the game moves on, hoping you didn’t notice the small hole where the content used to be.If this bothers you, you can do what many of us did back in the day; lean on the excellent fan translation of the original and play it as 2002 intended. But you’d be missing out on a lot. Though the Utawarerumono series is basically a visual novel with turn based combat included, the scope and the competence of said combat has been massively upscaled. Advancements like offering equipment you can win from conquered battles, or discover by destroying hidden objects placed in inconvenient locations around skirmish maps. Depending on their relationship, adjacent allies now have access to blistering co-op attacks that can decimate large swaths of the enemy force if used correctly. There’s extra chapters focusing on the characters most neglected by the original and Easter eggs hidden away for those willing to put in the time to search them out. All the game’s battles are repeatable should you want to delve back into mêlées already beaten to grind levels, or hunt down evasive items you couldn’t claim on the first sweep. There’s exclusive training missions you can trigger any time you like after a certain point of the game. I used them to try and break up the mountains and mountains and mountains of words.There’s a bazillion words no matter which version you partake in (though the original doesn’t have the stellar Japanese voice acting the other titles do), so without a decent story, all the improved combat would be particularly meaningless. Utawarerumono, then, is the tale of an amnesiac man, who is rescued by a rural village and nursed back to health. Not the most auspicious start, but the tale gains strength in how hard it invests in the cast. Given the name Hakuowlo until the time he’s able to remember his own, he spends his initial days carefully recuperating and learning about the world around him. It all seems a little out of place to him; for example, everyone else seems to have little fluffy tails and floppy ears he seems bereft of. It doesn’t seem normal, but what does he know? He’s an amnesia trope, after all. Maybe he’s the weird one.Utawarerumono never, ever hurries. Instead, it patiently builds. Hakuowlo’s saviour turns out to be a timid young healer-in-training named Eruru, who is his main source of companionship while bed-bound, nagging him gently every time he overexerts himself. Slowly, he regains some strength and integrates himself with the village. He discovers how to get past Eruru’s younger sister’s severe stranger anxiety and carefully establishes perhaps his strongest bond throughout his tale. He helps cultivate the village’s farmland with knowledge he didn’t know he had, and is able to bypass problems with a sense of wisdom that even he is surprised by. He grows by helping the people around him and, as he grows, they grow. It could have been a simple, idyllic existence. But that was never meant to be.Slight things escalate. Diminutive enough that they barely register as an issue until they’ve become near insurmountable. The game’s first inkling of antagonists flirt at being stereotypes; the greedy lord who’s found his position in life due to nepotism rather than any particular skillset. His obnoxious son, who thinks his station in life gives him credence to do or take anything he pleases. Except, they’re rarely so two dimensional. The son, Nuwangi, used to live in the village, but his ascension into the noble ranks has rotted away his humble groundings. He wants to catch the eye of the girl he likes, but his mimicry of the corrupt ruling class sees his meaningless power trips take him further and further away from the person he used to be, and estranges him little by little from the affection he seeks. Confused, infuriated and heartbroken, he lashes out. There’s consequences. He can’t deal with them, and he makes things worse. People are forced to take action. Hakuowlo is forced to lead.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time here but struggle to say this is a great game. The actual gameplay while unique for the time is easy and the story is mostly SOL/politics until the very end. The game has a great cast of characters and their interactions were well done. But if you are expecting the mystery of the main character to be the focal point you'll likely be disappointed. GameplayThe SRPG portion of the game for the first couple hours is non existent but quickly ramps up and eventually you have 30+ stages to complete. Even on the hard mode it is laughably easy without grinding at all. After a stage you get BP which you use to further level up one of three stats (attack, defense, magic defense) but only attack needs to be done. Not long into the game you can then one shot most enemies and slightly further in you can one shot everything including all bosses. The balance is way off since the AI isn't smart or have the raw stats to compete with you. The longer you have a character the stronger they will be since they'll have all the extra BP. Late game characters therefore never really shine unless you go out of your way to grind an already easy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: After completing all 3 games (Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth), this was an absolutely stellar experience. I looked forward to every day I was to get back to the game and progress the story. I wish there was more but am very happy nonetheless to have had the chance to play this series. Although I’ve now completed the story, I still get to play Monochrome Mobius, so there is yet a bit more of this world to enjoy.If the “visual novel” tag tends to turn you off, then please understand this series is a “kinetic” novel. There are no choices, no routes and no self-insert character. It is primarily a narrative experience that you can simply set the dialogue to auto and enjoy watching as though reading a book or listening to an audio-book. There are tactical RPG gameplay sequences when story battles come up, but they are not difficult and largely you will simply be watching the story.I highly recommend the entire series.

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of the first installment of the series finally makes its way to PC! Again, the playtime here is inaccurate, as I have played the OG version already a couple years back.I've already said everything that needs to be said about Utawarerumono on my Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth reviews, but Utawarerumono is my absolute favorite series of VNs, even after having read Umineko, it remains the king in my heart.Prelude to the Fallen, while not reaching nearly the same heights as the Mask games, is still an excellent game in its own right. Featuring a very rich world with a fun cast of characters and a mind-blowing ending, it's still a very good experience that you have to read in order to get to the Mask games that are genuine masterpieces."Pacing" is usually a very misused term for criticizing media, particularly video games, but in this case, I think it's very accurate to say it does indeed have pacing issues. The prologue of the game sets stuff up very nicely, and even manages to have an emotional impact, but the middle parts of the game drag on quite a bit, so if you aren't already invested into the world and characters, it's easy to lose interest. However, the ending MORE than makes up for it, and it's absolutely essential to play in order to continue the series.The sequels are where it TRULY shines, and I've already written reviews on them, but please do not pass Prelude to the Fallen up! While it gets a bit of a bad rep nowadays, and is outdated in some ways, it's an essential first step into an absolutely unforgettable series. If you're having difficulties getting into it, I promise you the ending and the Mask games will blow you away and you'll change your mind about the series.

_childDocuments_.review: For years, I've only managed to watch the Anime and the bits and pieces of the OVA that Youtube had, but by the Gods do neither do this game justice on just how compelling it is. Utawarerumono as a whole, all three games (I've 100% Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth on my Ps4, hence why neither show as complete here, but I intend to rectify that) are an absolute life-changing experience. I laughed, I cried, I cringed, I loved, I lost, I hated. The Visual Novel here is at its finest, with bits and pieces of a... decent combat. I played it starting on Hard, since, as aforementioned, I played the other two games first, and I blazed through it once I figured out how the combat works here.... but enough about the other two games, this is the first game.Pros:Story, as should be the case for any story-based game. Visual Novel or otherwise. If you're used to tropes, you may be able to predict some twists, but predicting twists does nothing if it weren't for the characters. The story on its own, I'd put it at a 7, maybe an 8. With the characters, a solid 9Characters. By the gods, are these characters some of the best well-written masterpieces I have ever came across. You will get attached to them. You will laugh with them, love them, cringe with them, and hate the ones that need to be hated. They have their flaws, they have their quirks. If the scale of rating tops at 10, I give these characters 12.Combat. Strategical Tactic turn-based grid action. If you've played games like Fire Emblem, this will click in no time. Each character has their Element, Elements are either Strong, Weak, or Neutral to each other, barring Dark and Light which are both Effective to the other. Stats are simplified, but that is fine. Again, I personally thought this was fairly easy, even on Hard, but keep in mind that I've played the other two games. With all of that said, the Story to Combat Balance is an easy 80%-20% ratio. If you're buying this game, it's for the Story. 6.Final Encounter Combat. I'm giving this a separate section, because due to the Spoilers, each character gets a new set of dialogue for their attacks, and even their 3-D Rendered expression change during their Final Strikes. Solid 8 for the emotional factor.Art Detail. Alright, we're entering the sections I don't have much... expertise in. I'm more of a gaming nerd than an artistic one. I believe the art is well done, each character has their set of looks and expression, which even goes into the combat sections, uh... 9?Music. Ditto to the previous section, I just simply don't have a good ear for music and my tastes are all over the place. Though, I did get the OST, and as far as I'm aware, each track fits each section. Hell, some sections actually omit all music and give you background noise, such as birds chirping. Again, not my strong suit. 9?Length. You're obviously going to watch all of the Skits and Events, as with any good story, expect to start hitting the 50+ hour mark.Voice Acting! Pure Japanese, and while I can't understand it, I can definetly hear the emotions in their voice. No line 'feels' forced. Huge props to the VAs for this game.Overall, this is a game I'd recommend to any fan of the Visual Novel genre. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it. If you want to experience visual novel for the first time, try this one. The story is amazing and the mystery is also really damn good. Character writing is also really damn good. Each character is very unique and unforgettable. Gameplay wise I think it is okay. Although there are systems that I found to be kinda meh but I still think the gameplay has its fun side. It is been quite some time for me to actually cry from a fictional story. My favorite character is Eruruu, btw. Yuzuha is probably the second and Aruruu or Camyu is third.I love this game so much and I will never forget all the moments I had from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally playable by most audiences, this game currently is the chronological start to the "Utawarerumono" series of games.It is set before "Mask of Deception", though after the (at the moment of writing) upcoming "Monochrome Mobius"."Prelude to the Fallen" is a hybrid between tactical, turn-based combat, and a visual novel.Set in an alternate feudal Japan, it tells the story of the initially nameless protagonist. After suffering a severe injury and losing his memories, he is brought back to health in a poor mountain village, and resolves to pay back what the people there did for him. The story evolves from there, following a string of heartwarming, brutal and bittersweet events.The first version of this game was only playable by adult audiences, meaning that many began their journey through this series with a later entry. Now that it has been made available for most players, I highly recommend it to anyone who likes tactical games similar to "Final Fantasy Tactics", or who already knows the later games. Be aware that the start of the game is slow, and combat only fills about 1/3rd of the story's total length. Even after "Monochrome Mobius" comes out, I assume (!) that this will probably remain the best starting point to the story of this series.PS: Stay away from the DLC characters. They spoil major story elements of later games.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I have and completed this whole series on the Vita. Now, it's extremely difficult to talk about this series in detail without spoiling it, so I'll just say this. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved every minute of this series(except for one very short segment in Mask of Truth, but it was insignificant overall). If you don't have a favorite character by the end of this, something is wrong with you. It's a ride, and I can wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who is even mildly interested. If you have little experience with visual novels, it's great, since you get a break from reading with the SRPG battles. The characters are great, the story is excellent, and the SRPG levels are fun. Even though this is a remake of a 20 year old game, it's still enjoyable to play.Just, whatever you do, do NOT play these games out of order. If you want to be lazy, just skip out on this series. Play them in order. You are only doing yourself a disservice if you don't. The order is Prelude to the Fallen, then Mask of Deception, then Mask of Truth. Do NOT play them out of order. While you can skip the first game and play Deception, it's highly recommended that you don't. It ties into Deception, and there are plenty of connections you won't be able to make if you don't play the first game.Again:Likable, memorable characters? CheckProduction value? Bro, the artwork and OST are excellent, and damn near everyone in the game is voiced.Story? Excellent, and it gets better as you go.Fun gameplay mechanics? Prelude's is a 20 year old system, but it works well. The latter two games change things up a bit, but are even better, I'd say.THE WHOLE SERIES IS ON SALE FOR 30 DOLLARS. JUST DO IT. I would have bought it twice at that price. Oh, and don't play with the DLC unless you're replaying the game. Those are all characters from the following 2 games, and you WILL get spoiled.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of the Utawarerumono game originally released in 2002, so considering that I think the story held up pretty well. It is recommended this game should be played first, followed by Deception, then Truth, then finally Monochrome Mobius(which takes place between Prelude and Deception). I didn't buy any of the dlc's for this game since it would spoil the characters introduced in Deception/Truth. I wasn't sure how I would like tactical rpg elements mixed with a visual novel but the battles were a nice break from reading so it balanced out. Overall I had a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono will unfortunately always be a niche classic outside of Japan. Because you will have to go through the 2/3 of the playtime that is made out of slice of life, slow-paced, visual novel to reach a surprisingly good story.  Also, absolutely do not buy the game(s) if you expect them to be heavy on RPG combat. This series is Visual Novel first, and RPG second. I can guarantee that maybe 10 or 15 hours of my playtime was combat, and that's even after me replaying the fights for achievement hunting.

_childDocuments_.review: The Utawarerumono series tells one of my favorite stories of all time. It's been a long wait for this title to finally arrive on Steam, years after I was first enthralled by the anime adaptation. If you want to read paragraphs of me gushing about this franchise's world-building, art, music, story, and characters, go read my review of Mask of Deception, this game's somewhat-indirect sequel, since it's largely unchanged from that (and spoiler free). What I will say is that despite having watched the anime for the original title twice through, reading this VN still captivates and moves me like almost no other. Usually, when I know what's coming, my reactions are diluted due to having experienced it already, yet with Utawarerumono, it only gets better with each time.  Especially with so many hours of character development and lighthearted slice-of-life content present that was (understandably) cut from the show, everything feels so much more vibrant and atmospheric, leading to a totally one-of-a-kind experience, provided you're cool with a lot of reading and not so much gameplay. The combat is kinda mediocre, but it only makes up about 20% of game time, so it really isn't the primary focus compared to the story. Basically, if you have 100 hours or so to kill, buy the entire trilogy, and prepare yourself for tears.

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of first Utawarerumono game on the engine from the sequels. It has all the content from PS2 rendition of the game, so it includes some additional characters not accessible in the original, and few additional missions. It also lacks all the adult scenes, but those are replaced with safe for work versions, often with a new CG. The game's story is unchanged, and I believe it uses exactly the same voice clips as the PC original. You're playing as Hakuowlo, a man with amnesia who gets attached to people of a small village. As those people are threatened Hakuowlo leads them into a war after war, while his army grows.The game plays as a visual novel most of the time. You will be reading, and reading, with occasional choice of where to go in sections when there's no war going on at the moment. Unfortunately you can only choose a place to go, but you don't get an info who you'll meet there, so the choice feels very meaningless. I just chose randomly all the time. No matter what places you choose after few scenes the game will follow to the next linear path. There are no choices affecting the story.Between visual novel segments are short tactical missions. Those are very easy (even on hard mode), and the mission design is pretty uninspired. Usually both your and enemy units will be placed with no sense or reason. The missions then end up with just busywork to kill all enemies. Sometimes you will have alternate win condition, like getting to some point, which you will have to do even if all enemies are defeated. Sometimes that means moving for many turns with no obstacle in sight. The game allows you to increase your stats post-combat, like in "Mask of" sequels, and I'm not sure if the opponents were updated in any way from the original to account for that. Around the middle of the game the party members who used stats-up were so overpowered the enemies would die in one shot, wouldn't be able to hurt them and so on. New members, even if their level matched the old members, would be on par with the enemies. If you want any challenge you might do well not to increase any stats.The fights consist of very low poly characters and environments, which shows Vita origins of the engine(and character models). There are animated cutscenes for each final attack, and many co-op attacks. Those are cool to be seen once, and fortunately you can skip them on future views. During regular combo attacks you will have to do simple QTE for hitting button at proper timing. It's not optional, as not pressing a button at all drops the combo, but you don't have to do it with right rhythm to get full damage. There are no "fill the bar" combos and "hidden qtes" from the "Mask of" games.For most of the missions you also get no choice in the units you can take on the mission. You might have 7 slots to fill, but with only 7 members there's no real choice. Unless you get the DLC characters, but as they are not included in the story (and are actually from nearly two decades into the future) it's hard to actually use them. The only place to really use them are additional missions, which I didn't really want to do, as they felt like a waste of time and unnecessary grind.The story is the winner here. It's presented with nice looking backgrounds (remastered from the original game), nice looking character portraits (also remastered), and great music. The game uses much higher variety of music than the original (although you can disable new music and enforce only old one). There are many songs sang by Suara, the same singer as in all the openings for the games.Unlike the sequels which focus on moe fanservice for dozens upon dozens of hours the original Utawarerumono is more grounded and more serious. Even peacetime events, which often have jokes and funny things happening aren't focusing on fanservice most of the time. The pacing of the game is also much better. Even during first part of the game when Hakuowlo is lost there are few missions to go on, and Hakuowlo actually solves crisis or two for the village. There are multiple wars this game manages to depicts, with escalating severity of the conflicts. It's paced much better than the sequels.There are some issues one might find with the writing, some of the jokes aren't too great(although at least not as repetitive as in sequels). Many of the enemy generals are comically evil, just so over the top it's hard to take them seriously. Also the final stretch of the story introduces a lot of new concepts, but I don't feel like those are explored well enough. It's a bit rushed.There are many world-specific terms in this game that are introduced. It's easy to get lost. Fortunately the game has a glossary to look up terms if you forget what they meant. Less fortunate is the fact the glossary has so low amount of terms it's basically useless, and none of the terms I forgot were ever in there.This game has pretty good cast of characters, and even those introduced later on get some development. Those characters also have their own connections, place in the world, and aren't becoming empty husks as soon as their join your army. There are also few non-combatants that you'll spend time with.In some of the most epic scenes the music becomes very loud and you can't hear the voice acting. You can adjust music volume, but then it's not loud enough in regular scenes. This could be a problem for some, but I actually liked the epic music in those scenes.Overall it's a good game. Best of the trilogy. There's a good reason why it spawned a whole franchise, including anime, sequels, and even spin-offs.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the good. The story is one of my favorites, and all the important bits are still intact from the original PC release. Expanded soundtrack is welcome, and even includes a bunch of songs from Suara. Also, you can swap confirm/cancel buttons, which is always a plus.Expanded soundtrack is a mixed bag unfortunately, the aforementioned songs happen on the most impactful scenes and overlap with dialogs, which is not great in my opinion. Camera in most battles is fixed in rotation to 90⁰ only. All DLC characters are pure fan service, you won't use them during normal playthrough anyway. If you're new to the series, don't buy them, you won't miss anything.If I had something negative to say, it would be one extraneous addition of a game trailer included after the prologue, which quickly flashes through the whole game, including the ending scenes. I'd suggest you skip it entirely.On the technical side, it's not great. Base resolution is locked to 720p and targeting 30 fps (including 3D battle sections; also, fps fluctuates a lot with some effects). DirectX renderer has some spec conformance issues, which sometimes result in weird rendering artifacts and/or flickering.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp. I didn't expect anything from this game but man... Like holy crap it made me cry so much...The story does an incredible job of setting you up to really care about each character. The lighthearted sections are fun and airy, but the heartbreaking sections are devastating. It's got a few things that are a little outdated for the current era, but all in all it's a solid and honestly fantastic story. Don't expect too much variance in the story, though, it's a linear story.The pacing of the game was interesting, to it's benefit. The first two hours confused me at first because it was purely visual novel, but I realised it's setting up the battle sections so that you care more about your units. You could go for a few hours having visual novel sections, and then suddenly be faced with back-to-back battles which... actually works for the game.The art isn't bad, it's just very 2000s anime. It's rather nostalgic. Character design is well-thought out, you'll never mistake someone for someone else (with the exception of the twins, obviously). Also the music is great, though there aren't any stand out themes in the game.The battle gameplay is... more or less what you expect from other tactical games like it. It does some things that are interesting and require you to be more actively involved, but otherwise it should feel familiar to others who've played games with similar tactical games.I'm tired so I'm probably not hyping it as much as I should but... man, wow, I'm still pretty shellshocked by how actually solid and emotional this game was.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished playing the game and I have to say, overall, I thought it was pretty good.  However, I don’t think that it’s the best turn-based tactics game out there, far from it in fact.  The story starts off with the main character crying out for water, when a girl comes to his rescue.  The girl’s name is Eruru and you stay at her place together with her grandma Tuskur and her younger sister Aruru.  You soon become a part of their family and you help around the village introducing agriculture that is far more advanced than what’s currently being used. When a person named Uwangi a former villager who was adopted by the Owlo (king/emperor), arrives. He harasses the other villagers and increases their tax because they have better farms now. It becomes clear that there isn’t a great relationship between the ruling class and the villagers. Nuwangi continues to harass the villagers and becomes more violent until an incident happens, and the villagers have had enough and starts a rebellion he teams up with the villagers and are able to live somewhat carefree until they hear of other villages in the nearby areas have been raided by the Owlo, you arrive and see and inferno with bodies spewed around, this being the catalyst for the other villages to pledge their allegiance to you. With the people you now have recruited you are able to overthrow the Owlo. Since you lead the rebellion and the other villages gathered under you, you became the new Owlo of the area.  From there, your neighboring countries in the area start invading, and the broader story kicks off. I don't want to spoil it, but there are a lot of twists and turns that keep you engaged, much like the Xenoblade games. The ending is particularly impactful and can change how you view many of the interactions between the characters, especially if you decide to play through the New Game+. Now, let's talk about combat. In my opinion, it's pretty lackluster. If you're looking for a turn-based tactics game that challenges you, this isn't it. Combat works like your typical turn-based tactics game but without terrain changes it’s a slugfest, you also instead do multiple strikes each attack. If you time your clicks of the LMB or spacebar correctly, with the strikes you can get 2 zeal with each strike. However, if you just spam click or not click at all, you won't get to the other strikes, and this can really hurt your zeal gain.  The damage of the overall attack won't be decreased, but if one of the strikes had triggered a critical hit, it would be lower than if you went through all the strikes. What's zeal? It functions as your special attack bar. If you get it up to 100, you can unleash a really strong attack which gets added as a strike so if you ignore clicking you won’t get the attack.  Many of the passive abilities of your characters, like projectile dodge, melee dodge, and critical hit, are more likely to trigger with higher zeal. The main character, Hakuowlo, can also revive once per fight if he dies with 100 zeal. You also gain zeal from taking damage. There's only one healer in the game, and she also doubles as your only buffer. I didn't find her buffs very useful during my playthrough on hard mode, but I'll get to that later. Each time you attack, you gain experience points (XP), and if you happen to level up during combat, your character's HP is fully restored. In most fights, there are inanimate objects lying around the battlefield that drop consumables and equipment, which is kind of weird. It can make the actual objective of clearing the stage feel less important than your hunt for rocks. Items are also somewhat limited. There isn't a merchant who sells or buys anything, but you can run training missions for a few items. This really isn’t a problem tho, I didn’t use items or equipment besides two fights which I’ll touch on later. When you finish a battle that isn't immediately followed by another battle, you have the option to do free battles which is just the same battle again, if you want the items, additional  XP, or BP. Additionally, after each battle, XP is distributed to all characters that this means the characters that weren’t in the fight also gets to level up, and the characters who were in the battle gain BP. So, what does level up actually do? It increases the character's max HP that’s it. BP however is used to increase a character's stats, which are ATK, MDEF, and DEF. You can spend BP however you want, and each character has an "intended" stat that has a lower BP cost than the others. However, this introduces the biggest problem with the game for me: the lack of character customization. Each character has the same 3 stats besides Eruru which has Heal instead of ATK. There's no way to specialize your characters or make them unique beyond choosing which stats to increase. It's a missed opportunity, and it makes the combat feel repetitive after a while. It makes it hard to use other characters since they don't have the stats needed for the later areas. Like I started using speed hacks later on to speed through the training missions which I’ll touch on in a bit. The best stat no question asked is ATK kill everything before they can kill you ez pz. You might be wondering what I was doing in training missions if I didn’t really use items at all, the hardest fight in the game is unlocked by getting every item in the game. A lot of the items comes from training missions and killing rocks and whatnot in the campaign maps, there are also 2 missable items, but this fight truly was something all the characters you have become level 50 and have a pre-defined stats and no equipment and you then face off against most of the bosses in the game in an arena truly fun had to think for once. Still easy though don’t get me wrong you can just actually lose this time. Now the 2 items I used items, first is in a story mission where you have to rush to someone’s aid, but they kept dying over and over before I could reach him, so I threw some healing stuff on him and finished it. The second one was after defeating the hardest fight I talked about you unlock a harder/easier version this time you can use your actual characters at the lvl they actually are at which are most likely below 50 which required me to actually use items and equipment fun fight. Now about the game as a visual novel, it has the standard features backlog where you can read previous text it only shows one quote at a time, you can also replay the audio from said dialogue. Which is nice since some of the audio isn’t actually written, had the mc remark about him hearing a waifu say “Darling” at the end it didn’t show up in the text bubble but sure enough she said it. The overarching story has skits in between them which are quite funny but also introduces another part I don't like. You are limited to the number of skits you can see in between overarching story parts and you’ll lose out on some genuinely funny content, one of the missables items comes from a skit. The missables items are easy enough to get in new game+ takes a few minutes at most. Technical stuff, I crashed thrice it seems to happen randomly when you take control of a chracter other than that nothing really. Overall, I think the game has its strengths and weaknesses. The story is engaging and full of twists, and the characters are memorable, likable and well-developed. However, the combat could use some work, and the lack of character specialization is a missed opportunity. If you're a fan of turn-based tactics or want a gateway into such games and you are looking for a game with a good story, I would recommend giving Utawarerumono a try.EDIT: I forgot to mention about DLC characters they will add healers and such I didn't use them however and I recommend you don't either they are from the sequels and I heard they either spoil main story plots in this game or the sequels better not to use them at all than get spoiled.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to what anyone says, this is the best Utawarerumono game and one of the best JRPGs of all time. Features a lot more combat than its sequels (%20 SRPG %80 VN discourse used for Mask games isn't valid here). Fights also aren't as boring as main game fights of Mask games (their post games are an entirely different story though). Story is also the best in the trilogy imho. The mystery, build up, pay off etc are the best I've seen in any game. This game has the best plot twist I've seen in my entire life, even better than the likes of Shutter Island and The Prestige. Characters are also the best among the series. Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth have some REALLY terribly annoying characters (Anju might be the worst thing ever created in existence), but Prelude's cast overall is really solid. Only exception I'd make is Aruru (I really hated her guts through the entire game and she never got better) but rest of the cast was amazing, especially Karulau and Oboro. Hakuowlo is also one of the better VN protags.Long story short: If you haven't played an Utawarerumono game before, %100 play this. If you've played the Mask games and liked them, still %100 play this. This is a must play game if I've ever seen one.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a fantastic "kinetic" Visual Novel (Theres no choices, its just a purely linear story) with a pretty basic but still solid and fun SRPG gameplay element. Do note that the VN part is very much the focus, expect to be reading for hours between any meaningful SRPG elements (It takes around 2 hours to even get to the first fight).This is the 3rd game released in the series, but since its a remake of the original 2002 game, its the one you should actually start with, and whilst it being made last means it has some upgrades in combat over the Mask games, most noteably Mask of Deception, the game sticks fairly faithfully to the simpler mechanics of the original game, where characters dont have skills, they just have their basic attack chain/finisher with very set attack ranges, whilst the sequels expanded on that a bit with multiple attack skills with different ranges. The only new mechanic to this remakes combat is the addition of some character specific co-op attacks.Yes the OG OG release was an R18 game with some ero scenes, but it should be noted that they never felt very essential to the game and the new scenes in their place still insinuate some stuff still happens off screen in some cases, but the loss is basically non-existent and you can know that this isnt some inferior version that gutted key plot related sex scenes like some other games that made their way to steam in neutered forms.If there is one main criticism to take with this series on steam, and this applies to all 3 Utaware entries, its the quality of the ports. All 3 games are optimized for 720p, all assets and internal rendering are set for that resolution, and the games are locked to 30fps. There is a dll you can find in the discussions for the mask games that will also work with prelude that will bump up the internal rendering resolution to your current window resolution, but theres nothing that can be done about the 30fps and hud elements sadly. At least since the game is 90% VN and then a Turnbased gameplay style, the 30fps doesnt hurt it too badly compared to other more action oriented gameplay styles.All said and done, I very much recommend this series, and to start with this game for maximum enjoyment of the sequels.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even start with this game? It's so incredibly good. It's like a mix of Fire Emblem-style combat (closer to Shining Force if you've played that) and a visual novel. The visual novel aspect might be a bit much for people just looking for gameplay, but all the dialogue helps build up an appreciation for all the characters as you go.The music is great. The story starts off meh but quickly becomes just fantastic. Gameplay trades the immediate counter mechanic in Fire Emblem for a positional system, where both you and enemy units take more damage from their sides and back, so you have to consider which direction you face your units at the end of every turn. It's a neat mechanic that presents elements of risk and reward as you can go the safe route and attack an enemy from the front, or go behind them and risk getting ganged up on by the other enemy units.If I had any complaints, it would be that the game coddles you until about 30% through and then just turns the difficulty way up. I was unprepared and hadn't seen value in focusing on raising my characters' attack up to that point, so I had made them tanky, and that came to bite me as the game suddenly made it obvious that Attack was the most important stat by far. Your units can tank hits pretty well already, but you have to kill enemy units fast to make sure that doesn't stack up. That and, it takes way too long to get a mage unit in combat.For tips though, if you buy any DLC characters, I recommend Anju and Mikazuchi, and ditching the archers you get. Both Anju and Mikazuchi have the raw strength you need, Anju having about the highest attack stat possible next to the ninja you get. Also don't invest in Teoru. He starts off good but then just costs too much to keep upgrading his stats, and quickly falls behind. I like him as a character so it's a shame. Invest primarily in Attack. Make sure you give every unit at least one Attack point per battle.

_childDocuments_.review: A must have if you enjoy JRPGs with rich story.As others have said, it focuses more on the story than the actual combat, but that doesn't mean the combat isn't fun. Expect more VN than action, but maybe that's what you're looking for.As someone coming in here spoiler free I was very satisfied with the ending and the story overall, some things were easy to figure out while others snapped in place like a puzzle.Overall very glad I got to experience Utawarerumono, a great remaster to a story that aged well.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is an amazing story that cannot be described in few words. Its world-building is second to none, easily compared to the greats like Higurashi or Umineko. The story of an amnesiac woken up in a weird world, in the backwoods of a village near the mountains with heavy injuries, no memory, and a mask he cannot remove. After being nursed back to health, he starts to view the village as his new home. But when an oppressive ruler threatens the peaceful life of the village and his newfound friends and family, they find themselves hurtled towards war, chaos, and a destiny far greater than any of them imagined. All characters are genuinely beautiful - they are all unique, colorful, and work perfectly in the story. There is not a single moment where an interaction doesn't add to the story or development of the characters. The highs are really high, and there are really no lows. In the laid-back moments found in the SoL scenes the comedy shines - I found myself laughing out loud way too many times to count now; from subtle jokes to over-the-top comedic scenarios, there is not a single moment to make you feel bored. Everybody complements each other perfectly and they work great as an ensemble.When there is no comedy, there is always the progress of the story. I found it astonishing the way that they always hit the nail on the head when it comes to pulling at the reader's heartstrings. The way the characters change for the better is nothing short of beautiful; whether you will be happy, sad, inspired, motivated or hopeful, Utawarerumono manages to make those feelings come naturally with the help of the amazing writing, characters, and plot.It was my first visual novel containing turn-based gameplay elements, and I must admit that I never knew I would enjoy them so much. Speaking from a novices' point of view, the battles are smartly arranged, perpetually changing, and bringing something new to the fights to keep you thinking. They are the perfect amount of hard - while the victory is dependent on thinking, you won't be taken out of the experience for gameplay matters like levels that are way too hard or grind needed for you to pass. Although not needed, it is definitely fun coming back to previous fights to improve your stats and see how much you and your team grew over the course of the story.Going from a grounded story, to a fantasy-filled ride with some of the most interesting ideas, the second half of the story starts at a slow pace. Hours full of events of now characters you know most things about - fun times that you wish would never end. The lack of urgency now creates this sense of comfort and ease for the reader, who has yet to find out what will happen next. Once the calm before the storm ends, the story picks up in pace quite a lot. The last quarter of the game truthfully has some of the best plot twists I have seen in a while. I could keep praising this game on and on for all its amazing qualities, but the thing that hit me the hardest was the ending/epilogue. In my life, there were few moments where I cried like this, and this one is one of them. I could genuinely talk about this game for ages, but I will end this review by saying that Utawarerumono is a story that must be experienced by everybody. There is so much love put into this story and characters that it's impossible for you to have a bad time. As the first installment of the trilogy, Prelude to the Fallen is a great title and an amazing setter for the next two parts of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: After all these years since playing the fan translation of the 2002 Windows PC version back in the day, I am still very fond of Utawarerumono and the world it builds.That being said, as much as I like the story, I really REALLY wish that in this remake they had done something to make some of the really annoying maps of the original game more interesting. This combat system is not particularly fun and it takes forever, even if you cheese it by using putting every single point of BP you get into attack like I did (trust me, you will never need the defense or magic defense). If you're looking to buy this for a good tactical RPG, this ain't it, although the sequels deliver much better on that front.

_childDocuments_.review: So Utawarerumono, if you think this review is unbiased go somwehere else. First things first ignore that tiny number of hours above, imagine that it's 45 hours or something like that because it's how much it takes to complete the game, actually make it twice, also I'm going to make review for entire trilogy in one go, from remaster of remaster of a remaster ported to pc called Prelude to the fallen then two firther titles.Before I end this lengthy introduction it is time to say something quite important. Well it's trilogy just like mentioned before, best to start here and avoid starting with deception which is part two, though absolutely dont look at anything more than buy button on mask of truth because it's big spoiler minefield, seriously entire game revolves around really big spoilers so there is no way you could write anything without throwing big spoilers.Why utawarerumono? There are few factors which im going to write about in this review:1story2characters3musicPart 1:I'm going to talk here about 1 and 2(im going to reffer to games by numbers since its going to be lengthy anyway)So let's start with 1 it starts with your good old amnesia start, what I love about the story is that you dont get final goal, Hakuoro is not some kind of chosen one slapped with ancient prophecy in the face the very moment he opens eyes for the first time. All you have is some things happen and you end up running a nation and then what? Care about it, and that's all, story escalates, things about his past surface and story gets quite interesting from that point.2 Here things get quite original, in this story you are not hero saving the kingdom, you are his little helper, this game is slower than 1 since you can treat it like just half of a game, just like Suga(writer of the story) made a game and higher ups told him that is two game material and they released it so(not blaming them, this game is reaaaaaaally long), this part is more about building the world, and introducing new region to the story, and laying ground for events from final part of the trilogy, it takes it's time but it's not empty, story happens it's just..well first half of the game, all spicy parts are always for 2nd half which is separate game even longer than this game(60-70 hours compared to over 80)Story is lead through two phases, first you have your good old slice of life till things start to happen and you embark on adventure or do some task important for the story, and once it's complete hero comes home and lives his daily life while you get to know more of the characters he accompanies which leads us to:part 2 charactersThis is where strength of utawarerumono comes from, imagine spending tens of hours with characters, you know their best and worst, and they are written very well. You really get to like this bunch of characters, main or companions or just episodic characters.Hakuoro, main character of 1st, it is your responsible likeble leader, nothing exceptional which doesn't mean that it's not a great character, his supporting cast is absolutely top notch you really feel life in them, even opposition is more like someone being unlucky to be on wrong side of a spear rather than villain doing evil for sake of it.Haku, which is main character of 2, here is what i absolutely praise and love. Imagine slacker always looking for chance to talk his way out of thw work and go drinking with bros, but when situation is dire he can think really quick. The point with this character is to see how he changes in span of two games, the point where he starts and where he ends. It is absolutely most heroic character i ever seen, after what happened in the story you really give him respect for his acts, he may not have power level over 9 thousand but compared to who he is, and how much he can it's quite high ratioAs for supporting cast, since this games have ridiculously good quality of main and side characters, seriously Suga did absolutely amazing job with his writing. You can feel like thay could be actually alive, and they tend to not be one sided and often get depth to them. Part 3 music1st and 2nd game have diffrent composers, 2 gets few of tracks adapted for new but it's 3rd game which combines both as it combines two regions and stories into grand finale.When 1st game doesn't have really great soundtrack it catches up with songs sung during the game, and now you have option to include newer soundtracks, but i would recomend to turn that option off for two reasons. First is that this game loses it'a distinctive feeling to it, story of Hakuoro(and i'm going to use it because Hakuowlo sounds worse and sinc game has lots of Ainu refferences i go with that one) while newer soundtrack has next main character. Second is that Mast of Truth combines not only soundtracks but those two games into one so it takes away from that effect.Similiar situation happens with 2nd and 3rd, while those have new composer and singer, soundtrack on itself is way more solid and songs are kept in same really high quality state.So final part without number but word:epilogueIf you are here, wow that's quite long review here and you are at this point. So bit of my personal experience with the game, part where it's about me and the game not game itself. It started quite standard, i watched anime, it was absolutely top tier, really high up my list. Year later i decided to give a try to it's source material, at first it was quite pleasant experience but soon i was completely in. Anime suddenly from 10(given quite rare from me) went to medicore and i realized how much utawareumono lost due to shortening the slice of life parts, despite knowing how it ends i went through it with pure passion about it, then it ended, instantly went for sequels. 2nd was worst out of trilogy(dont get me wrong, 1st is full story 2nd is first half 3rd is 2nd half) but i had quite a lot of fun with it, then 3rd and then it was over. This game doesn't hold back on punches to the feels, when it wants you to laugh you laugh at the top of your lungs, when it wants to be serious or sad, it conveys it really hard. And here I am, now finally I can own entire trilogy on my very own steam account. And so my story with it ends, i'm probably going to replay it each few years just because of how good it is.Is it worth it? Absolutely, best story i found to this day, and i'm looking for over 4 years for something that might topple it from the top.As my final words of this review my highest praise reserved only to "that one and only" story:I hope I can live long enough to find something better.
