_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game, if a bit flawed.Chorus is an arcade space combat game that leans heavily on its story and RPG elements. If you don't like the character dialogues or the story you're not going to like the game - but if you do, it's worth it to see it to the end to see what happens in the story.The combat alternates between easy, challenging, and damned near impossible, and not in any particular order. The gameplay is fun, but the strange difficulty spikes/lulls mean that you either feel disgustingly overpowered (especially when your space magic is leveled up) or totally hopeless (against the boss encounters of the game).There is also a bit of a lack of enemy variety, as later-game enemies are just harder versions of earlier ones, which ultimately ends up giving every minor enemy a hitscan laser weapon that requires a perfect dodge to avoid damage.I played the game with a HOTAS setup - multiple controller input/mapping is natively supported as of a recent patch, and it's quite an enjoyable way to play if you have that hardware. Ultimately, would I recommend it? Yes. It's a fun space game that has a dark space fantasy feel and a universe you want to explore. I want to see more, but I'm not going to deny that the flaws exist.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. The core aspects of it, namely the power-infused flying and combat, are worth the price of admission. And it has a really cool world concept that feels like a homage to some other great space opera stories.It has some questionable design decisions. I don't think the open world does anything for it, beyond creating a slightly greater sense of scale. The random mini missions get tedious quickly, and most of the side missions are just okay. The challenges are also not great, the force you to play very unnaturally until you complete them. They should have had lower completion requirements, just enough to teach you the techniques, without having to farm them.The main story missions are great though, I wish they had focused on making more of them. The larger space battles are very cool, especially with the amazing soundtrack urging you on.The story is good and I liked most of the characters, but they both fall short of being something truly unmissable.I wish it would get a sequel to develop some of its good ideas, but I doubt that will happen.In summary, a flawed gem, one that is worth your time and money if it looks interesting to you. I really applaud the devs, I can feel the love in the game, I just think they made a few bad design decisions in some of the peripheral and progression aspects, and spread themselves a bit too thin with the open world and optional missions. But they should still be commended, they made a very enjoyable game of the kind we don't see much of anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, this game.. where do I even begin?First of all, the combat feels *very good.*I really got into the game, the tutorial did a decent job too.I picked up new skills quite easily.I also learned to weave all the abilities together to become a near unstoppable killing machine.And then the side quests, they're so fun, I did as many as I could find.This game blew me away, but there *are* some negatives.Some of the side quests are not entirely pointing you to where you need to go until you trigger certain steps. These steps don't always appear, but I think it was more down to one or two sidequests that glitched on me.Once you start a quest, even if by getting near one by accident, you need to continue or abandon it before you can pick a new quest to do.The combat was really neat, I also REALLY loved being able to control a capital ship as well. Though I feel more dangerous in my fighter than in a capital ship. The abilities feel very good. I won't spoil too much other than this.All in all, I'd rate this game a 9.7 out of ten.  THIS game really  was amazing. I wish for more games similar to this, more games that have this style of flying too.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and controls are easily the best part of this game. Whipping your arm across your mouse pad as you do a tight drift turn and blow up 3 space shifts feels soooo good.The satisfaction in the dogfighting in this game is almost comparable to character action game like Devil May Cry or Bayonetta. Unfortunately, that's about where my praise for this game stops.One last thing before I go over the negative: The game is very pretty. Having a space sim where you can free fly around and see and imagine the void of space is really cool. I love the atmosphere of this game and being in space at all times is really cool and a fun direction. Onto the negative: the story and writing is pretty bad. I figure you can mostly ignore it but the characters, writing, voice acting and cutscenes are boring and amaturish. I will give them props for voice acting the entire game, though.This game also sucks when it's in tight and cramped spaces and expects you to fly at high speed. You don't have much control about manoeuvring left and right when you're traveling at high speeds and I died more to crashing into things.Yeah, that's about it. I think Chorus is a game with fantastic controls and space combat for the most part but it falls flat in other areas. And that's okay. 20 hours for a playthrough feels perfect and like it didn't overstay its welcome.I'd possibly recommend waiting until it goes on sale unless this is a game that seems to really speak to you.Also, try the demo if you're not sure!7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Open world, can tackle missions at your own paceInnovative gameplay through the use of powersEasily a contender for best soundtrack Cons-The open world is a bit barren, there is some variety later but it comes after a while of kinda samey asteroid belts.The story is genuinely written but poorly paced and goes over the same beat several timesThis game is amazing. You'll only have the starting ship till you find your "old friend"(which is the only ship you can use thereafter), it would have been nice to customize the main ship's visuals but that is forgivable. THE POWERS THOUGH! The difficulty curves very nicely as you become familiar with your powers and they really do make you feel bad ass.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is an awesome game!A truly underrated gem.Space flight simulator with aerial dog fighting, all while haunted by Senua's whispers in the alien aesthetics of "Control (2020)". Humanity discovered 4th dimensional eldritch entities, shoved them into machines to serve as AI and made a religion out of it, while gifted pilots basically became Sith lords.The gameplay is intense and epic. Unlocking more Sith abilities closer to endgame makes you godlike.Side activities could be called repetitive, but their purpose is to always lead to more combat.The story and lore is well thought out and deep. Very cool.The sound design and music are amazing too! Just check out:"Pedro Macedo Camacho ft. Uyanga Bold - Chorus Main Theme"From the technical side, game never lagged or had any bugs.I could leave game running overnight and PC didn't complain.One tiny flaw that I want to bring up is: how conversations are triggered while traveling and can be interrupted by side activities popping up or nearing a mission. This cancels the conversation and starts the next one without finishing the previous sentence. What did I miss?!?I played carefully after discovering this but not always could be avoided..I played only a few flight games ever, I can count them on one hand:The horrible w40k "Dakka Squadron",The F2P PvP dragon dog fighting "Century: Age of Ashes",Nintendo 64's cool "Buck Bumble" and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "Star Wars: Rogue Squadron".CHORUS was the best one yet!From the physics to combat and drifting. A true game that tried to be more.Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: GAME MADE WITHOUT ANY CREATIVITY! DON'T PLAY IT!Another one space-game where you need just to hold W button to fly forward and left-mouse button to fire. No tactics. Ship customization system is just meh... upgrade weapon to deal more damage or buy module to get more health or deal more damage. Thats all. Story just meh. Controls ugly ♥♥♥♥, please fire person who said such controls would be great. Tried to play once on gamepad - totally unplayable, can be played only with keyboard and mouse and still badly.I clearly see there is some things taken from Control game, which is completely different, but if you played Control you know that character have major similarity.Music good, thats all.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Nice story, great voice actors and mice music. Great graphics and all that, BUT! Sometime controls feel a bit stiff when fighting some smaller ships - almost impossible to track them (literally was circling 360 just to try and get behind them.HUGE drawback of the game is the main thing of the game...this sense thing on 'E' button...YOU GET ALL THE CLUTTER ON SCREEN INSTEAD OF WHAT YOU ACTUALLY NEED!!!!!! Like you have a mission to find some drones..what should you get in this sense? - drones? NOPE! - you'll get markers of not selected missions, markers of random visions (not related to mission), cargo markers, your garage marker and tons of other stuff. sure, you get the distance and you can get the idea that those are not your objective, BUT THE CLUTTER IN UI IS CONFUSING! You get like 9-10 markers on your screen and you can't figure out what is your actual goal, unless you actually see them directly on screen. Also, some missions ask you to pick up something and...guess what? - NO MARK! Just brief location on the screen, when you done fighting...good luck trying to find the item, when you were upside down.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it starts quite strong but gets rather weak until the end. Story is sometimes quite philosophical, it somehow carries you through the game but it's far away from being great. Controls are fine (I played with keyboard and mouse). Quests range from standard (kill all enemies in your area) to boring (collect x pieces of cargo near the wreckage) to plain stupid (emergency call - go there - "oh hello, our ship computers got hacked, please help us and remove the virus" - press one key - wait a few seconds - "thank you, here's your reward"...seriously?!? Same with "Oh, we ran out of fuel, can you spare some?")...Sometimes random dialogues start but they get interrupted if you get near your destination. Even reloading does not restart them. I think I missed some interesting lore due to this. There are only a few levels, they all look great but only the first ones are actually fun to play. The others seem unfinished, big distances to travel but only a few quests. Some of these quests require travelling between those levels and going big distances in the levels just to be forced to jump back again to get your reward. This makes me think the developers ran out of time and just artificially stretched play time. I had some fun with the game and was really not sure how to rate it. In the end I must say, I just expected more of it. More action, more diversity in fights/quests/weapons. But sometimes it just felt like some kind of a space flight simulator,  activating your boost to get to your destination, do the same stuff like a few minutes ago, get some reward and repeat. Exploring the area for hidden extras most of the time just brought in some extra credits, but no fancy stuff. In the end they also squeezed a couple of video sequences and dialogues into the game which just ruined the flow of it. I wanted to fly and shoot, use the superpowers I was blessed with to bring havoc to my enemies. I did not want to listen to some whiny main character being afraid or just sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: While yes, this game does have a shorter story than the big titles it makes up for it in so many other aspects of game play. First of all, this game is just stunning to look at. I found myself just flying around in the different systems after completing the story objectives there, taking some really beautiful game play photos I use as desktop backgrounds. Second, while I did predict and already understand what the ending of the game was/would be and understood the connection between Nara, Forsa, and The Prophet, I still sensed a theme of unity and oneness even when fighting enemy's. I think the Devs tried to put this theme into every part of this game and the end scene was just perfect. I really hope the Developers in time do another much bigger and longer prequel story of Nara, Forsa, and The  Prophet from when she was rising in the ranks of The Cultists leading up to her breaking moment. I would buy and play it straight through.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I recognize that Chorus comes from a smaller studio/company, and they may not have been able to polish this as much as some other games.Secondly, yes the game has a bit of a style about it that feels like it would be at home on a gaming console. This is not a hard core space sim, movement is really only look around, move forward, and stop.Overall, I enjoyed it, and am happy to have bought it to have the experience of the story that it told. I appreciate media that carries a meaning with it, and this accomplished that well. I plan to play it again.I think that some mechanics of the game became a bit annoying (random audio comms getting interrupted by quick events) or a bit of a chore (quick events that just take time). As well as the odd bug, like the red haze of damage getting stuck on for a bit till another event reset it.But I never felt like I was grinding. There was a good pacing of things to do, or at least I mapped my things to do, so it worked that way. I appreciate that long travel can be broken up by quick events to give you something to do other than just fly. And while the progression of enemies can have a bit of a pattern, it was never something I felt tedious about. Instead I found myself experimenting as I became stronger, with different ways to combo things together to clear enemies. So to me no design choice or mechanic was offensive or off-putting. It actually flowed pretty well.Overall I enjoyed it, and plan to play it again. To me this actually falls a bit into the same category as Halo. Where in both games, while there may be some odd annoyances, it is solid and fun to come back to now and then, and try something new or different. I also enjoyed the music, seems well composed, and helps give a good feel to the world and story for me. It was a bit shorter than I originally expected, but I think the pacing works. If there are updates, I look forward to them to see what changes, as well as future games. To anyone who has worked on making Chorus a reality:Thank you. This game and my play-through, came at a time where I needed the message the story tells. It resonates deeply with me. I wish you much love. You did a good job with Chorus and I think it will always carry a special place in my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: The best praise I can give this game is that at moments it made me feel the same joy I remember when I had first played tar Wars Jedi Starfighter. The game controls smoothly, has an enjoyable story, and gives you just enough extra options with your rites (powers) that sometimes you just find yourself hitting a groove where you are teleporting around the battlefield, gunning down enemies, and drifting into that perfect run to take out a battleship in one go. The game started to drag just a little by the end, but that was in part because I found myself pushing to find every side-mission, and scouring each map for locations and collectables. Other than that, the pacing for introducing new enemies, holding out for the really big space battles for a few key moments, and also letting you fly into enemy cruisers to take out their power cores from the insides all came together quite nicely for me. At just under 20 hours for a playthrough, this game felt like it knew how to pace itself out and when to bring itself to a close.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmmm, I want to like this game more than I do, it has a lot of notes of proper old school space-shooters like Freespace but the fact that it's so on-rails and your freedom is so limited to the confines of the (not too great) story let it down. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty easy to control the ship. Cool character. Nice to be able to upgrade and modify your weapons, armor, shield, outfits, etc. The difficulty level increases dramatically as the game progresses and very quickly though.It  manages to get the feeling of a classic arcade game in 3D, which so many games have failed to do. The quick progress through the story and incredibly fast increase in difficulty make the game extremely frustrating  though. Before I knew it I was facing the final boss and it was killing me over and over again.Not that bad of graphics. It defaulted to epic graphics on my computer though, which overheated my system before I noticed. I don't think the graphics are that great to warrant that but it does seem to do a good job with Crossfire.I think the worst thing about it that I've noticed is the HUD. It's tiny. It's often really hard to see where you're firing if you aren't right next to your display and there's no setting in the prefs. I ended up lowering my resolution until I can figure out another workaround and it's still too small. Really not good from an accessibility standpoint.Worth getting, as long as you don't have vision problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Even at full price I would say this game is worth every penny.  I haven't had so much fun in a game in a long time, if anything my biggest complaint is that it was a little bit shorter than I would like but I would take that over how some games have become so bloated with side quests that you feel like it is more of a chore than a game.Pros:Fun space combat - Once you get the hang of the "rites" and how to quickly switch weapons depending on the enemy type this becomes an excellent flow of absolute destruction and it makes you feel like a total badass.  The controls are tight, even with mouse and keyboard using the different powers was easy and I didn't feel like I needed to remap the controls to different keys.  Graphics - the game looks beautiful and runs smooth.  I never had a single stutter or dropped frame even in the final battle scene with so many ships fighting each other.  Sound - the soundtrack and the sounds are excellent in the game.  The weapons feel like they have some power behind them and the sound of ships being blown to bits around you is great.Story - I know some people might not agree with me on this one, but I actually enjoyed the story.  The voice acting (especially for the side quests) could have been better, but the overall story made me keep wanting to stay in the game.No micro-transactions or attempts to make multiplayer out of the game - I love a game that decides what it wants to be in the beginning.  In this case it is a single player space combat and that is what it delivers.  There was not money wasted on multiplayer that nobody would play because that isn't the focus of the devs.  I wish more games would chose to be either a multiplayer game or a single player game from the beginning so it can keep the money focused on what it is good at.  And also I hate micro-transactions, I don't mind DLC with new campaigns but some of the pay to win type DLC I abhor.Cons:Final Power - the final power you don't get until the game is almost complete and by then it is really too late to use since the other powers you have had for much longer and have already adapted your play style to bring in this power.  Plus it really doesn't feel like an ultimate power.Voice Acting - I found the voice acting for Nara and Forsa to be fine for the most part, but all of the side quest voice acting you can tell was not the best.  But then again this isn't a AAA, 70 dollar game so they had to make cuts somewhere and the side quest voice acting I am willing to forgive since the gameplay is so tight.Tight quarters areas - I did not really enjoy the missions that were in tight quarters as I found that it took away from the fun parts of the gameplay as I didn't find the ship to respond as well in these tight areas.  It could be if you play with a controller that this is not the case but with mouse and keyboard I just found it a bit more tedious than I would have liked.  Fortunately there are not that many of these areas in the game.Final Boss - I found the final boss to be easier than the 1st main boss (although it took longer due to how to fight the boss).  But that could have been because I just became so much better at controlling the ship and so it made it easier.  Bugs:I really didn't have too many bugs in the game.  The only bugs I had was that at one point I couldn't bring up the main menu so I had to keep playing the mission until the bug finally fixed itself and I was able to save and quit.  And the second bug I hit actually was a benefit as it keep playing a particular random encounter which gave me extra rite energy.  Finally it seemed to correct itself and the random encounter stopped repeating itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy... this game. Its got so many things going for it and it seems some people wanted to try their hardest to ruin every redeeming quality it has. Where should I start?The missions. The damn, tedious pointless missions. It serves as your standard time wasters, because the game itself only would take 10 hours to beat if not for all the side quests. Its all basically the same thing, kills some guys, pick up items, rinse and repeat. Over and over and over. And the voice actors and writers? Holy crap they are SUPER bad. Honestly with a few main story plot exceptions the game would be better off if you just cut out all the dialogue.The main character, for some reason, decides to whisper stuff all the time (usually something extremely obvious) in the most annoying way. Imagine you went to work and your boss talked to you regularly, but then under their breath audibly whispered (Micheal never shows up on time... today is going to be a long day. I left a sandwich in the fridge, I should... go ... get that). You'd probably want to punch your boss in the face and its the same deal here, the main character is terrible. Can't stand her.They don't actually explain anything in the plot either, why the factions are the way they are, where the dark entities come from or what they are about. They DO wrap up some of the really awkward stuff at the very beginning and fortunately, they do wrap up most of the story at the very end. But really the rest of it I just couldn't wait to just get through it.You are supposed to be fighting this epic space fairing battle against inter dimensional demonic forces and the cultists who worship them. Oh and by the way, they supposedly corrupt people at the very beginning with this.... psychic totems. Its not really explained, and the effects of the brainwashing or whatever the hell is happening goes away the instant the psychic totems dissapear. Where do the psychic totems get their energy from? None of the cultists themselves ever reference them, none of the cultists use their own powers to activate them. They are just kinda there, no explanation. A running theme in the story.And about the cult itself, seems like a cult, talks like a cult, acts like a cult. Except you find later on in the story people are oddly kinda... normal in the cult. Theres even a large faction of the cult that had captured a system that the main character helped destroy in the very beginning of the game. But Nara left the cult of her own volition. She didn't doubt her choices up until apparently killing billions of people. That never gets explained either. She opens this interdimensional rift I think? Or the prophet does? She claims to have started this series of events but later claims she doesn't understand how they totems, rifts, and cult technology works? Shes the right hand man of the prophet himself, but yet hasn't learned all the requisite lessons to become one of their elders, like the rest of the cult guardians have. Look I could go on about the story for a while, bottom line it doesn't make sense and its very poorly writtenWhich is a damn shame. Because the concept of the story, awesome. 10/10. The execution? 2/10. That might be what really bothers me, you don't get worked up over something that is just bad, but this game had potential.I'll leave the rant here for now. I could go into exhaustive detail over every single aspect and point in the game but I think most people will get the picture at this point.So lets talk about what the game does rightPros:-excellent combat 9/10The ship handles, very very well. Surprisingly so. The game is disorienting and confusing sometimes but thats kinda to be expected, its space. But im just saying, starfox managed to pull it off. Maybe if they added markers that were red or some other sort of color instead of every single marker being white, to show that the location is out of view behind you and not actually at the peripheries of your vision. Its good, but it could have been better. (The brilliant implementation of drift, even if not realistic, is really well done and elevates this games combat. Raises 2/10 points by itself)-Lore 7/10Its a very interesting premise like I said. A story about these demonic entities coming through and corrupting the universe and leading brainwashed minions to do terrible things to their own loved ones all in the name of unity and peace. Rock solid foundation, not at all fleshed out. And the game has the awful habit of "Tell Don't Show". (pro tip for writers and directors out there, if you are constantly needing to narrate what is happening you are doing something wrong. Let the sequence of events explain themselves, limit your narration)-Aesthetics 8/10Chorus for the most part, looks pretty good. Its got this nice dark thematic thing going on and it works, even if the space feels really empty and lifeless. I can get that making some world-building thats done in space can be really graphically and labor intensive and won't always be worth it. Cutting costs here makes a lot of sense, but it really does feel like something important is missing. Regardless, the game looks appealing and frankly is why I bought the game. How it feels to play is another story-Complexity 6/10This one is kinda harder to describe. Theres a lot of powers and the progression of those powers you get really fits. The weapons in the game however are completely garbage, theres no point to doing any of the side quests to earn more money because you get more than you can do anything with very quickly. Theres literally only like 6 weapons you'll ever need to buy, and the game would massively benefit if they just completely cut all those out and made weapon upgrades just happen automatically as the story progresses. However as you do get those upgrades, it feels like a very natural learning curve.So would I recommend this game to most people? No. Sadly. I don't think it was worth what I paid for it myself. If you are looking for a compelling game with a decent enough story to hold your attention, this is going to be a hard pass because its only going to frustrate you the entire time you playHowever if you are just looking for a cool spaceship game where you can go pew pew and use psychic powers to blow stuff up, then yeah its kinda fun. The combat is frankly too easy and makes up for that by just being unfairly punishing at certain points in the game. The Boss Battles are really a big highlight but those are few and far between. Theres only like... 3-4 note worthy ones? Both faceless boss battles are admittedly pretty cool. They could have done a lot more to make the combat fill itself out, maybe multiplayer (but not necessary) or some sorta extended fights where it was more than just a simple point and click every single time. The ship fights where you have to disable their shields KINDA do that, but its the only real meat of the combat and there isn't much to it. Once you've done a few of them you have done them all.So yeah, final verdict a disappointing high octane game with some borderline revolutionary space combat mechanics and handling. I wish they'd done more, and they just cut out or reworked the writing and got better voice actors. Whose idea was it to make the main character whisper all her inner thoughts (which apparently the AI companion can sometimes or sometimes not hear)? Do me a favor, slap that guy. If it was the CEO or marketing team, even better.

_childDocuments_.review: It may not be Freelancer when it comes to charisma or charm, but it's certainly a good enough space shooter. Following an ex-cultist by the name of Nara, who has a lot of PTSD to deal with since she did something utterly terrible, had a subsequent change of heart and now feels that she has to redeem herself afterwards by going after the powers that be, namely the Circle and their vanished leader, the Prophet. Through this, the game wants to be more grandiose but the campaign is in tens of hours, not hundreds of hours. I always like to take a game slow, especially if there are plenty of places to look into, and so the side missions got a little bit repetitive and there wasn't as much of a connection to other characters. There's no cutscenes of physical interaction with other (human) characters so that detracted from the impact of the story arc. The RPG elements are very light, with the ability to upgrade your ship (which gets switched out early on to something that talks to you, a version of KITT but in space fighter form) in several different ways - gatling gun, laser, missile system and then three mods you can trial. Depending on how you set up your ship, you can get different buffs for different sets of mods and weapons. The battles are either multiple ships on you affairs in space, multiple ships on you in close quarters or multiple ships and mini/full-bosses in space and close quarters. The close quarters ones are where you have to be the most careful and after you develop more powers or 'rites' then it can be damn fun in grabbing a spaceship in the sky and throwing it against a building, with a rather satisfying explosion afterwards and a nasty little laugh from yourself.This is a very much an AA title, but I didn't really come into any bugs except for an annoying one with the mouse pointer in the menu system, so I just switched to arrow keys and 'enter' instead there. A lot of the money seemed to have gone into the final mission, where the music rises, there's a brilliant cutscene and the game suddenly feels that's it's all come together and you're just kicking everybody's backside. After twenty hours into it (the game is probably only around about the 15 hour mark but as I said, I'm sightseeing, leave me alone), it was totally worth the last 15 minutes of fighting off hordes of enemies. And after this it ends and you're left to your own imagination of what's in store for Nara and her friends. Games have a habit of ending a story too abruptly and this also nearly crossed the line, but it saved itself at the end there.Oh, the irony.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Chorus is a great spectacle. The game looks gorgeous on max details, and the space battles look amazing when you get a few of your rites back. The story is intriguing without many plot twists and somewhat predictable towards the end, which is fine – it leads you from one epic space battle to another and gives you some context to do battle. Controls (played on Xbox Controller) feel great; switching weapons, using rites, drifting, and boosting all blend into a beautiful space dance of explosions and tight evades. The side missions are also fun and well-written and there are plenty of them to break up from the general events that spawn around you. Overall, it would be a contender for 10/10, but there are two major things that bring it down to 9/10. First, I love achievements, and when the game has so much grinding as this one and does not give you free after the main story is done, it loses a point. Second is the last boss fight, specifically the tunnel chase… whoever designed this one, please just don’t make fast-paced space shooters. The combat in this game feels great, destroying massive battleships is satisfying, and you are telling me that for the final big bad boss, you have me navigating a narrow tunnel with so much **** spawning and blocking your way that you barely are shooting anyone? The snake phase was much better, should have just kept it there.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus can be likened to games like Freelancer and Everspace 2. At least that's what you get from the core gameplay - third-person, action-oriented space combat. The twist is a fantasy element which adds special powers into the mix. This makes combat stand out from similar games and adds a certain chaotic power fantasy element to it.The story embraces the fantasy element and tackles metaphysical connections between realities and humanity's place and purpose within them. The overall story is interesting and gives you enough threads so the more observant may pick the final revelations earlier than some. A sign of good writing, which unfortunately isn't shared with the dialogue.The characters, including the protagonist - Nara, are mostly uninteresting. Support character dialogue is largely meaningless and has little connection other than to direct you to the next task. The conversations between Nara and her ship's intelligence are a little better, excepting her inner monologue, which is mostly unnecessary and delivered in the most annoying cadence. If you've played Control and didn't like Jesse's thoughts interrupting the dialogue, you won't like Nara's soulless loud whisper.Combat has a hectic flow and you can customise it to your play style with a bevy of ship upgrades. You might choose to favour weapon or ship strength, or enhance your powers. Take note of this for boss fights. Since you can swap out upgrades on the fly, this can be helpful in what are sometimes difficult encounters.This game has enough polish for a budget title to make it worth a play for fans of the genre. It's a decent way to spend up to 20 hours while waiting for a full release of Everspace 2.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 Hours in so far and I can say this was money well spent.*The controls are tight with adequate customization options.*The graphics are good, sometimes great. The facial expressions and rendering are top notch.*The story in this is good! A few interesting surprises in the story telling that will catch you off guard if you can keep from watching other playthroughs. Surprising depth for a game this heavy in shooter mechanics.Chorus stands out from many modern games in that they have carefully crafted the experience for the user. Rather than relying on clunky multi-player mechanics to create unpredictability and make their game periodically interesting from the chaotic nature of multiplayer combat, the developers are comfortable enough telling their story to let the player campaign experience speak for itself.Far too many developers struggle with actually creating content for their games. Chorus is a pleasant shift away from the decades-old trend toward leaning on multiplayer unpredictability and allowing that chaos to supplant a curated experience. Chorus is successful as a standalone game. It tells its story confidently without coddling the player with lengthy cut-scenes and superfluous eye-candy.Chorus shows visual restraint, and in doing so, allows modern gamers to experience an action-driven narrative that will have them exploring and asking questions about the universe they are experiencing, rather than simply grinding through to get to their next shiny trinket (next stage, bigger guns, better shields, etc). Those trinkets are there, but they are not the game, they are a tool used to further the story.Chorus for me is difficult to categorize. Shooter, yes. Bullet hell, at times. Sci-Fi/Space Opera arcadey flight sim? Yes. That's probably the best way to describe it; Sci-Fi/Space Opera, arcadey bullet-hell shooter. Oh and with interesting choices while upgrading and kitting out your ship. You can't take everything that you want and it makes for some interesting trade-offs.

_childDocuments_.review: While pretty simple, and not very deep, this sleek, modern space fighter has alot to offer.I mean I liked it. On my computer it launched immediately, the controls were fluid, and the side missions and the backgrounds were actually relatively diverse while also being repetitive but only kind of? Its hard to explain but I personally found it to be pretty dynamic in the way NPC's said what, when and why. Where each side mission was located and the routes they took, and most of the Ai in this game is pretty decent. On hard and extreme mode, fun is something to be left desired but playing there makes you feel accomplished and invested in the story. The writing was honestly great with the voice acting being absolutely amazing. I got most of the stuff in under 20 hours and there isnt much left to do after that it seems like but piloting the ship was awesome, becoming over powered felt awesome, the game gets super easy towards the end if you do most of the side missions... that being said i give it a solid 7/10.As a side note to make aiming and turning a little easier, my settings were (For mouse and keyboard);Aim Sensitivity - 75 @800 DPi / Aim Acceleration - OFF / AA Time - .20 / AA Stregth - 0 / Auto Hit Radius - Medium OR SmallAlways make sure to drift and level out your ship for maximum maneuverability.Hope that helps.Also not worth $40 because this game is a masterpiece in more ways than one and the whole game felt like an extension of the demo. Wish there was more to it because I woulda payed for it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game. Might not be perfect (it gets repetitive in the 3rd act), but it has fantastic gameplay, a wierdly unique story, nice graphics, an epic score and most of all: great atmosphere. It had one of the most enjoyable campaigns I have played in years, and definitely the best arcade ship combat in a long time. If you like spaceships and sci-fi, Chorus is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with a caveat. The game looks great, has a great aesthetic and at its heart is a very solid starfighter game. However in addition to enemy starships, you will also be fighting enemies called the Faceless, weirdly shaped red things that get increasingly annoying to deal with. These things make up most of the late game and the boss fights. I wish the game trusted itself more and stuck to its well executed starfighter mechanics. Instead of throwing these weird and frustrating enemies and boss fights at the player.

_childDocuments_.review: it is really funny iust how precisely chorvs fixes the issues i had with everspace 2.... like main character everspace 2 - generic white guy with no discernible personality. main character chorvs - ex war criminal butch lesbian who is wracked with guilt for her participation in genocide. combat everspace 2: circle strafing and holding fire with no real challenge. combat chorvs: Tokyo drift around enemies at high speeds (no strafing here bay bay, except for your dodge roll) and use your blink/dash ability to jump behind enemies in the middle of a dogfight. progression everspace 2 - overdone looter shooter with boring upgrades in a open-ish world with no real consequences. progression chorvs - get new abilities in a metroidvania like fashion (drifting at shrine which you need to escape, lightning to enter the rift etc) plus investing creds as upgrade points into shield, hull, weapons, or mods. art design everspace 2: overgrown generic mobile game ad. art design chorvs: weird utilitarian retro-ish sci fi mixed with modern fighter jet/aircraft aesthetics. story everspace 2: wow your friend got hurt and now it is time to fight villain for reasons. story chorv: deal with your paralyzing guilt over the genocide you committed while also ruthlessly hunting down the guy responsible, (who is also your former mentor) incurring more and more deaths.also did i mention the combat is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GREAT????? ♥♥♥♥ i love the drift and the dash and the dodge roll. incredibly special.chorvs is good and ppl are sleeping on it.also i refuse to call it 'chorus' when the logo is CLEARLY chorvs.

_childDocuments_.review: Theres alot i like about this game, it reminds me alot of old action oriented flight games from back in the 90s and early 2000s. Games like Fury 3, Hellbender and of course Descent.The controls and handling feel nice and responsive. My flightstick broke ages ago but mouse and keyboard does the job well and the amount of fine tuning you have access to in the options menu means you can make your deadzone as large or small as you desire, going a long way to making the ship feel natural to you.Visuals are very impressive, i can see the engine at work sometimes and admire the memory saving tricks as i notice them.Sound is probably the weakest link in the chain that is Chorus (ironic) but its far from bad. Sometimes voice lines come off flat and i feel like overall sound could be more intense.That said theres some fine attention to detail here, (i'm a sucker for casually cruising thru debris fields and hearing the faint sound of rocks hitting my hull)Story is interesting to say the least, theres alot more story here than i bargined for and i'm enjoying it so far, usually games of this type put the story in the backseat and the explosions up front but Chorus does a good job balancing the two.If you ever enjoyed old arcade space shooters or a fan of starfighter combat in general give the game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a very hard time understanding why this  game has a "Very Positive" rating. * Extremely clunky controls, even on PC.  * Why the f is there no L/R and U/D strafing controls? Just a dumb roll maneuver, which is infuriating to evoke randomly when you just want to navigate around a corner or a small obstacle.* The graphics are rather dated, with dull looking textures and low detail objects. Ray tracing does literally nothing in this game. It still looks flat and boring* Due to the lackluster graphics, the sensation of distance and depth is literally non-existing. You keep crashing into objects because you have no clue how far away they are. Or you want to pick up an object, but you have no clue how far away it is, so you slow down way too early* The insanely annoying never-ending whispering of the protagonist. Just why? Why? Jeez.* And why are missions auto-started whenever you happen to get near the objective? Some mission you simply don't want to do (yes I'm looking at you "Pilot training"), but everytime you get even a few kilomtetres near, it will trigger. Oh ffs...* And finally the worst HUD and mission markers every seen. Yes, the mission markers. They are everywhere. And they look all the same. And they don’t really indicate direction, or distance. Why couldn’t they at least have different colours? Or different icons for different types of missions/objects? Did I mention they are everywhere? And they all look the same? Holy cow such a bad implementation of mission markers…Just buy Everspace (1) instead if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: The best space combat games I've played are House of the Dying Sun, Star Wars Squadrons, Star Wars Battlefront 2 (the space maps), Freespace 2, Battlestar Galactica (itself a Freespace total conversion), heck, even Rebel Galaxy. For me, Chorus did not compare. I was left disappointed by:- railways in space (literally, if you want to get somewhere 5% faster)- the most underwhelming capital ships I've ever seen- and other ridiculous elements, like my ship being the only one with a scanner (and even that one powered by "magic"), the enemy base being 1km away from the friendly base, or stealth "disable station" missions where our fleet is 100m ahead of the enemy station yet somehow "hidden". It's just stupid. The boosting is fun, the drifting is fun, but the enemies are predictable, repetitive, and usually destroyed in one of only 2-3 ways. I won't mention the forgettable story etc. I stopped after 40% in the game, not worth continuing.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all I loved playing this game and there are many neat things it does, but there is also quite a bit of jank ...I recon you can sink 15 to 20 hours in it, depending of how many side-quests you do. While the story is flawed and not groundbreaking, it's original and I have never quite seen something exactly like that before.I will be complaining quite a lot, because I feel like this game was this close to greatness, it's sad where it ended. I genuinely do love the game, which is why I am seeing all these flaws in something that I think could have been excellent.I think it's worth playing but there are a bunch of issues that can probably make people quit quite early on.The good things first:+ The combat is pretty good, it's quite satisfying and you often get new abilities that keep things fresh+ Music, sounds and ambiance are great+ The game looks amazing+ The game runs very well, and the loading is very fastAnd then the jank ... - The game looks great, the cut-scenes don't. They  show extreme closeups of Nara's face, and the tracking is just not great: It's uncanny, and the emotions are not really readable ... It's kinda like the VHS in the resident evil 7 remake. It's just realistic enough to look bad.- The side-quests lack polish, and sometimes even main story missions do. You'll get voice-lines referencing things you have not done yet, or saying you still need to do something you have already done, because the game did not expect you to do the quest when you did.- The game starts quests while it's still explaining them. If I got a penny for each time I had to  kill an attacker, but the attacker was dead before I knew it, I'd have two pennies. Which is not a lot but it's weird that it happened at all.- The game gives you powers as you progress ... But you start with a pretty bad ship without any powers and bad weapons, so the first fights are insanely hard, I nearly gave up while in the first zone because even in easy mode a fight against a few pirates was frustratingly difficult.- The equipment system does not have a lot of very interesting items, I had three equipped items that I kept during most of the game, for weapons it's only a case of "do you want it to shoot faster and do less damage, or shoot slower and hit harder?", but at least there are more upgrades- The game loves to play voice-lines depending of where you are, but there is no safety to keep your current dialogue going, so you can very easily cancel a conversation about the story by flying too close to a side-quest.- In a chase missions, the game punishes you for being too close, as obstacles will spawn just behind the chased ship. The problem is that there is no way to know where the obstacles will be, they just spawn in your face ... so the game really just wants you to follow at a very specific optimal distance where you can shoot/hack/etc. but still dodge the spawning obstacles.The story is all over the place. Maybe it's translation, but sometimes it's like there is a carbon monoxide leak in the ship. The game starts with  which drown you in names, to try and give you some context.It's pretty easy to understand the main story arc, but the finer details are ... blurry ...Often the game will drop you little morsels of lore in conversations, but there is a bunch of contradictions, or very surface-level stuff. It sometimes feel like they were completely improvising the details.Even with all the conversations you will have, sometimes you go somewhere without really knowing what you'll do when you get there. Then the game either surprises you with a word salad to justify the puzzle or deflects you to do something else with new story elements that come from a greater lore that you don't know about. At one point, circle pilots will see your ship and tell you that they "are honored of your presence, venerated elder", and then supposedly you can be sneaky in circle territory mere minutes later ? It's a whole plot point that you are in a circle ship and that your allies will be wary about you, but after a while it's dropped and not mentioned ever again.Characters die of easily avoidable deaths, the game says you can't attack X ships for story reasons while the random side-quest you just did had you kill 20 of those guys, Nara will be surprised to learn about something you were explicitly told  before, the circle inner politics and practices are utterly incomprehensible (), tho that may be on purpose.... And

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying that I have barely any experience with this type of ship flying game, but I got hooked pretty quickly on this.  The graphics overall are excellent, I love the universe they created with tons of detail and flying around just feels great. _childDocuments_.review: Great arcade space shooter! One of the best I have ever played. It reminded me of old Freespace games which is a big praise in itself.Graphically its amazing and runs smoothly on GTX1070 in 1440p. Its not easy to make interesting locations in this kind of game, but I found all the maps in this game interesting and distinct. Especially locations that are Cult themed or encased in ice - just gorgeous. Light effects are especially great, even without using ray tracing. Special effects during combat add a lot of flare to dogfighting and visuals of your special powers are fantastic.Not much to say about music, its good but not great, its just kinda there. Voice acting on the other hand is pretty strong especially from our protagonist - Nara. She is a real badass and brings so much emotion to this game. I loved how ruthless she sounded at times, but at other times she was very compassionate and fragile. Other characters like Great Prophet and Rasar are also great. Voice acting really helps to flesh out the story of this game.I found the story to be enjoyable and interesting. Its not amazing, but strong protagonist, her relationship with sentient ship Forsaken and her mysterious past with The Cult kept me interested throughout. It could use some lighter moments, because its all super serious all the time.Gameplay is one of the greatest strengths of Chorus. I am playing using keyboard+mouse and find it to be very enjoyable way to play. Default button layout is great, giving you quick access to all your powers, weapons and moves. Game starts you with some crappy old ship, but you quickly recover Nara's old ship - The Forsaken. Your ship will gradually become stronger thanks to Mastery system that improves your weapons and attributes by completing combat challenges. You also have Nara's Rites which are special "magical" powers, allowing you to teleport behind enemies, shoot lightning, ram everything in your path and more. Your ship can also roll to dodge attacks and drift. Yes, drift. Not something you expect to see outside of racing game, but its such a great mechanic in Chorus. It allows you to fly in one direction while turning your ship to shoot at the targets behind you without losing momentum. You can pull many advanced maneuvers using drift and it never stops being satisfying.My only real gripe with this game is that it sometimes requires you to do puzzles or combat in very confined spaces. It doesn't feel good and your ship's movement doesn't seem designed for this kind of close encounters.I highly recommend Chorus to any space combat fan that enjoyed Everspace or fondly remembers Freespace games. We are long past the golden days of this genre, but Chorus feels fresh and brings many original ideas and mechanics to the table. It does scratch that Freespace itch pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Freakin' space cultists.  Would perforate again.Controls feel awful at first but start to feel natural once you get a few skills (drift, mainly).  And the finale is top notch, hearkens back to Freespace/Freespace 2 where you're blowing off parts of battleships and then flying inside to strafe the core and then escape. And it happily didn't overstay it's welcome - took about 20 hours to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm basically in the early stages of the game, enjoying side quests and tier2 of the storyline.  The game plays like StarFox + WoW in a way.  You upgrade your gear, improve your "mastery" (achievements that lead to in-game benefit like dps increases), fetch / murder / escort / explore as quests, and learn to use your special powers --> rites.  It's a fast paced game for sure, probably not great for watching as an observer as it'd be disorienting, but it's quite fun and open world.  One thing I appreciate is how much control you have over your ship's movement speed.  It's a seamless and potent feeling game

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a surprise that it was this good. I picked it up on the sale for $15, and it was worth every bit of that. It's a fast pace space shooter with very good mechanics which make it a stand-out. It took a bit for me to get into for the combat, but once you get a hang of it, you feel really into it. The sound hits it, the music hits it, the combat hits it. I wish there was more opportunity late game to just destroy more and more with everything unlocked. The only complaint I would have is if you miss the threading the needle opportunity in tight spaces, you feel like a dummy in potential chain crashes that follow. If you don't crash, though, there's I felt a genuine sense of euphoria in fitting into the tightest of spots going at a stupidly fast speed. Solid game, do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- Flight controls feel really good, the best I have ever felt it. - Loads fast, plays well, and looks good even on my aging GTX 980- I feel that the voice acting is actually pretty good- I like the dynamic between Forsaken and Nara (main character - you)- Space powers are really cool too, adds another dimension to typical space combatCONS:- I think the story can drag a little and get somewhat muddled. There's a lot of little subplots going on which aren't too well explained. I would have liked a tighter, more focused narrative.- Some of the side missions get a little repetitive- You gather a lot of credits but you don't have a lot of use for them. Also, hangars (in game stores) are not marked. Hard to go back to them. Overall really good, I enjoyed my time with the title. As far as how the game feels and plays on my computer and how fun the combat is? 9/10. Story-wise, I was really hooked in during the first act of the game, but as time went on, I think a lot of the threads got muddled. Balancing story/narrative against combat, I think Chorus is overall 7/10. If there was a sequel, I'd play the crap out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything Jedi starfighter wanted to beChorus was a fun game with great ideas. It took some time to get used to the ship's mobility, but it was amazing once you got a handle on it. The abilities were great and added a dynamic I have not seen in other space fighter games. The story and designs were well put together.  Enemies were distinct and required varied weapons/abilities options to take them out which led to fun ways to fight battles. While I thoroughly enjoyed the game, I felt there was an issue with content quantity. The game overall was 15 hours with a chunk being me actively looking for side quests. Based on the achievement list it looks like I may have missed some side areas but that just means they were really hidden or it was bugged. Either way, it is not that long. This is a shame because it did not allow enough time to utilize all the powers. While there were occasional larger enemies to face, it felt like there could be more content with fighting them. Just when you get used to fighting one you will not see another until you already forget how to take it down.My biggest peeve with the game is while you are traveling long distances between points dialogue could trigger but gets turned off right as you get somewhere or into a fight and never comes back where it cut off or restarts. My second peeve was there was very little to spend money on, There was so much money by the end of the game but nothing to spend because there was better stuff in the side quests and I could only upgrade the ship so many times. I also could not sell things I did not want which cluttered up the inventory. Lastly, adding one or 2 more fast travel spots per area would have drastically improved moving around maps. I hope this developer gets a chance to work on a similar title with a larger budget.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: The best space shooter EVER! I feel like such a bad ass piloting Forsa. I really hope that they expand on this game. The theme is mature. Game play Bar none. VERY well optimized. Graphics could use some work on the models but your are moving so fast that its irrelevant. I would love to learn more about the universe via different content like an anime. _childDocuments_.review: I just can't get into the game. If I could have just switched the story off, I probably would have kept the game and ploughed through the missions. Immersive.Gameplay - mouse and keyboard are somewhat off, wide/tight/fast turns are nearly impossible in any smooth mannerSaving is the usual autosaving nonsense that robs you of the liberty to save as and when you need to. If you need to close the game halfway through a mission, tough.Story - meh. You can see it a mile away and the character redemption arch is rather obvious. You wonder why bother. _childDocuments_.review: It's a great space action game with a few caveats. Because of this I think it's probably most informative to do some pros and cons.Pros+ Excellent arcade action gameplay+ Great sound design and voice acting (for the most part)+ Excellent graphics, particularly partical effects and lighting+ Interesting mechanics in how to manage dogfights+ Different enemy types requiring different approaches, weapons and powers to defeat+ Lots of side missions and a decently-paced story campaignCons- The story starts out quite intriguing, but eventually goes off the rails- Probably linked to the above, the story is poorly designed and paced. - Technically you fly 3 ships, but really there's only 1 that you'll use for 90% of the game- Although there's different enemy types, they're common between cult and pirate factions, and enemy variety is lacking- Fights against capital ships sound fun in theory, but end up getting boring with huge gaping holes and weakpoints- Random in-field events have the ability to interrupt story dialogue, and if they do you will not hear that story dialogue again- While Nara has a character model and mo-cap is used to good effect for her, all other characters have generic still head portraits. That's only for a handful of the main characters too. The rest get generic portraits of pilots helmets.- The final power (known as Rites in the game) is not introduced until just before the last mission and it ends up being completely useless and underwhelming.- No Endgame content. Once you've completed the story and side-missions there is absolutely nothing else to do in the game.So with the above you get an idea of what to expect with the game. I still recommend it because if you can get over the horrible story and some obvious cost-saving design decisions the gameplay . If you want to experience it yourself then feel free to stop here and go get it, but if you want to stick around I will elaborate on the problems I have with the game and , so you've been warned.My first big issue with the game is its lore. For the first act of the game you will be hammered with various lore-building concepts that establish the basics of Chorus's story, none of which will really be explicitly spelled out for you other than Nara is in hiding after being responsible for the destruction of a planet while being an Elder of an organisation known as The Circle. This is when the story is at its most interesting as you are given just enough to speculate on what is actually happening, but not enough to just write it our in front of you and tell you what's going on. In the second, and largest act of the game, you spend most of your time with Forsa (short for Forsaken) who through various story missions and conversations you learn isn't just an AI, but someones soul intentionally pulled from another dimension and jammed in to a containment device aboard the ship. The problem is you find this out in the most confusing and ham-fisted way possible: You're tasked with a mission to visit the station where Forsa was built, but it's been destroyed - yet there's no explanation as to why. The most confusing part is that it's still in use and operational by Nara's mentor who built Forsaken. Later on in the story it's mentioned that the station never belonged to the Circle and was destroyed by them as part of their war with the Najarans. So this all of a sudden becomes a Najaran station that was destroyed by the Circle - but The Circle then used it to build Forsaken and the other Elder ships? What?From this point in the story more contradictions start piling up like the game is actively attempting to retcon the story it was playing out only a few hours earlier: When you reach the final act you enter Nimika, which is entirely under the control of The Circle. The first problem here is Nimika is supposed to be the planet that Nara destroyed which prompted her whole change of heart and fuels her guilt that makes up the 80% of her personality. Except here, with no rhyme, reason or explanation it's still there with just a small chunk missing from it, with what ends up being the most powerful space hub in the galaxy floating outside it. The second problem is, with the entire story up until this point (and Nara herself) trying their darndest to convince you that the entirity of The Circle are religious zealots who brainwash or kill anyone who refuses to join them, all of a sudden 90% of The Circle are peace-loving pilgrims who are embroiled in a civil war against a single militant sect of The Circle who have been the ones causing the problems all along. Are you sh*tting me? The worst part as well, and major spoiler for the ending here so if you really don't want to know how the game ends then don't read further: The soul that was forced in to Forsakens core to make the bloodthirsty 'We must kill the Prophet' AI ends up being , and that's the reason Forsaken is so hell bent on killing his corrupted shell that was left behind when he went through to the faceless dimension and failed his trials. You couldn't make this sh*t up, there are no shortage of scenes and memories Nara goes through showing her with the profit, inside Forsaken before he decides to take up this trial, so how the hell is his soul inside Forsaken when it hasn't even been split from his body when Forsaken is built?Now all of this could be down to me just completely misunderstanding the story, but I'll tell you what would have helped: not having important story conversations between characters interrupted for the 20th f*cking time by a civilian who's ran out of fuel, or a salvageable wreck appearing near me, or Circle ships appearing. Every time this happened, it stopped whatever conversation Nara was having with Forsa or other main characters, and it wasn't picked up again afterwards, so I missed out on so much story content that it's possible I just couldn't have possibly expected to know what was going on at times. Was it ever mentioned that not all of The Circle was evil? Was it ever explained how a soul of a person was made in to an AI while it was still in their body? I'll never know, because once these conversations have been had in the game, they don't happen again unless you start a new save.I realise I've rambled on about the story and how much I disliked it, but the reason for this is the story is the turd that was dropped on a perfectly good bowl of Spaghetti Bolognese. The rest of the game is great, and I can recommend it on the sheer fun of the gameplay alone. That unfortunately just made the fact that the story is so disappointing by the end so much more jarring. Give the demo a go and see if you like the gameplay. If you do, blast through 20ish hours of fun and ignore the story completely.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, if flawed.The game excels in the space combat, particularly as you level up and access more abilities- being able to blink behind a enemy and take them out, or shoulder charge through swarms of enemies to destroy them. The more you play around with them, and your drift ability the more fun it gets. That said, the HUD could do with a lot of refinement - particularly enemies on your radar - its far too easy to lose track of them, especially when your concentrating on dodging incoming fire. I had most fun when taking on the occasional capital ship the story throws at you (though again, knowing what to destroy on the warships could be signposted better).It also has a really good soundtrack that's very middle eastern sounding (almost like Homeworld)- not surprising given the whole title and theme of "Chorus". The voice acting is also good - I really liked the voice they had for the Prophet - reminded me a bit of Bill ♥♥♥♥♥, in a way. The way Nara whispers her thoughts did get a little grating, given shes alone for 90% of the game, and is usually doing it to undercut something she has just said out loud, usually to Forsa.Where it falters a bit is as others have pointed out. Its not that the story is bad - far from it, its a good space opera, but as we are stuck in our ship all the time, it can feel a bit disconnected. There are cutscenes, but most of the plot is passed to us by static talking heads in a comm panel, so it can be a bit hard to follow in places. At one point, you meet up with both your old mentor and your old student, and I found it hard to understand why they join your rebellion. The student in particular- you see his memory of fighting for the Prophet, then later he shows up as a renegade himself with little explanation. Part of this problem I think is that you can encounter memory bubbles as the game progress', giving you insight into things that are happening, but again this can feel a bit disconnected. I did wonder at one point if this was all setting us up for an unreliable narrator moment - like everything we were learning was just peoples perceptions of it, not the truth (Spoiler: I was wrong). The maps can feel a little empty, at least until you get to Nimika, I felt. I suppose that's not uncommon to any space combat game, but still, its a point.Others have also pointed out the difficulty spike in several mini bosses (one in one of the temples in particular). What doesn't help is that these tend to be inside structures, limiting your manoeuvrability, as well as the constant weapons fire laying into you, not giving you much room to work out what your doing. What would have improved things, I think, was to have several hub areas where you leave your ship and walk around. You could talk to the other characters and learn things that way, maybe through a dialogue tree, and pick up missions from them if story related, or have a bulletin board for non story missions. Perhaps even a bit of minor RPG elements? Instead of having a slot for equipment to improve your rites effectiveness, you could spend points on upgrading the bits you want to?A bit more customisation would also have helped- the in game shop for buying upgrades was really underwhelming, to the point I really just used the stuff I scavenged or got given as mission rewards. I finished the game with around 70K credits, but there was little if anything to bother buying. Heck, maybe the option of buying additional inventory slots to load more equipment? You cant even buy custom paint jobs for Forsa (although there is dlc to get one skin).I also said earlier about adding RPG elements - its interesting that Nara is so broken by what she did at Nimika that she doesnt want to lead anyone ever again. That slowly changes over the game as she becomes the rallying cry of the galaxy, and it would have been interesting to see it play out on a dark side/ light side way.So would I recommend this game on balance? - yes absolutly. This game is a lot of fun and well worth getting - how many space flight games come out these days after all?  We don't get enough games in this genre anymore, and that's a sad deficit. Id love a sequel but with a little more tweaking to improve it in areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a fantastic game that plays like Everspace from a third-person perspective and keyboard and mouse controls, but instead of just upgrading the ship and the guns, you also upgrade the player, which makes the middle to late game very interesting. The use of rites makes it plausible that Nara can turn the tide of any lopsided battle like she’s Anakin Skywalker in the Clone Wars.  There’s a good variety of enemies and counters, from simple skirmishes to outright fleet battles. The late game adds some extra-dimensional entities that are not even spaceships in the conventional sense which shake things up. There are some set pieces and a nice “assemble” moment at the end where almost every faction that appeared in the game before shows up for the big finale. The production values are very good, the game is polished, looks great, has tight controls and a good soundtrack. Not much to talk about here, it’s a solid game.The story is mostly excellent, with fascinating lore. It takes itself seriously, almost too seriously. While some complain about the dramatic inner monologue like in 1984’s Dune, it’s well-suited because the Jungian theme is perhaps more about internal than external conflict. That's likely why it mostly focuses on the inner struggles of Nara and the ship Forsaken, which is a complex character himself and more than a sidekick to give expository mission dialogue. Chorus has a nice length and while I usually don’t care to get 100%, it was a pleasure to do so because the game is so good. If enjoy this genre, and especially if you remember Wing Commander, this is a hidden gem that you should check out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so good. It's also kind of refreshing, at least when it comes down to the gameplay.I recommend it even at full price, there is not much replayability for those who loved everspace but I think it's far better than the second opus of the said series.I loved many things and also hated others but overall it's a really great game.It's not too long, 20h or so, not like every stupid RPG which need more than 50h of almost nothing to complete the story.First, the good points. - .It's pretty good. From the general plot to Nara's evolution through the game. It's feel pretty great that just a little tweak to the usual they are bad so you fight them can make such a good story.I saw review saying "It's creepy how the main character talk to herself in her head" well I want to say if you never do that I think you are a machine. - .It's the best point as well as the worst since some people might not enjoy the game because of it.It's not the usual space command with zqsd (wasd) to move on the 2D plan you are on, ae (qe) to roll and space/ctrl to manage height yet it feels pretty natural after 1 or 2 hours at most.Still be aware that at first you might die because you're still thinking with typical control and do a dodge instead of going left or right. - .They're are really good and fit well in the game and in every situation.Weapons sounds are also good shoumdn't give you a headache after 30 minutes.Some sounds feels strange though since I sometimes encountered a rock and it made a metal colliding sound. - .I don't have many to say here apart from they are pretty great and fit well in the game.Now, the "meh" points. - .You will experience in the game some frustrating moment especially in temple or in some fight (boss fight in general) which comes from the poor level design of the places or the ennemies, ennemies in question are big enough and what's asked from you make it a level design problem.In this game, you always go at full speed since the game clearly says to you "do it and you shall not die".But in tight space it's often the very reason you die because you are way too quick and your breaks are those of a train.You need time to slow down and even the drift might not help you since drifting is just freely moving your orientation while you are taken away by your initial speed and direction to make tight turn but it's not that easy to use in tight corridor. - .It might be lacking for some people. - .You have 3 types of weapons: Gatling, does hull damage. Laser, does shield damage. Missile, does armor damage.There is some interesting features inside those categories like some gatling do massive damage at short range or fire heavy ammunition resulting in low fire rate etc.But you'll mainly use the gatling and missile since shield are not that resistant especially in late game and even armor can be taken out with the gatling.I didn't feel the use of the laser since, as I said, gatling do decent damage to shield and since shield can regenerate after some times without taking damage.And changing weapons during fight is sometimes tedious because if I roll too hard on my middle mouse button, I might skip the one I wanted to use. - .It's a passive effect on equipment and need you to have 2 to 4 of those perks to apply an effect. Most are interesting but since you can't upgrade or level up your gears you might have to abandon a gameplay you like because they are not good enough, especially since some of those perk are attached to your weapons which might also forces you to play with a weapon you don't like. - .Money feels useless. It's not the case in early game but once you do some secondary mission or take a bit of time looting you become way too loaded.I think I finished the game with 50k with everything bought in the shop.Looting also feels pretty boring and useless since most of the time you get money, some time you get hull or shield upgrade but since you can buy them in a shop  you are quickly loaded with money  the game stop you from getting them too fast it's also pretty much useless. - .While some are quite easy to take down, most of them are a pain. Their not dangerous but most of the time they are timed objectives to take down and if you fail you gotta do it again. It's better than a massive count of HP but it's still pretty bothersome at times.Finally, the bad points. - .The true first boss to me is the first one you fight in the void.And it's tedious and frustrating.  - .I know. It's a bit too much since every map are not that big but still. To go to a place you need to go to the jump gate or teleport to it if you already visited it once (and it's never said anywhere I discovered it by chance) then you take the jump gate of the system you want to go to and you have to travel all the way to the point you wanted to go to. _childDocuments_.review: A good time for about 10 - 15 hours. The gameplay is pretty tight, if not a touch basic. _childDocuments_.review: "I meant to do that." -Great Prophet, probablyChorus is great. Medium on story/script, but long in starfighter arcade style gameplay. I thought it was a slog to get from place to place until I noticed you can warp to any jump gate at any time. Exploring the areas and finding the pickups and upgrades was fun and flying anywhere around the environment always feels cool. The space dodge and space drifting never felt old. Weapon upgrades come slowly but are absolutely appreciated and feel fresh every time, even for similar weapon classes. The inclusion of set bonuses on upgrades is interesting but feels shoehorned.Chorus is absolutely worth the 15 bucks I spent. Perfect length, content, and entertainment for the value. I would definitely appreciate a sequel with more Faceless encounters and frontstory. Call it Chorus:DISCORD.

_childDocuments_.review: Jumping to  after “finishing” another space game , felt exited, due the space combat itself wasn’t the strong point on my game experience with NMS. Completing the game still felt as an empowering experience overall. From movement and weaponry standpoint you are provided at least 3 different weapon types with special abilities. Utilizing the abilities is the key aspect to make the combat feel responsible and excited, from sliding in zero gravity past swarm of enemies to give them full blast of rocket barrage or having intensive dog fight with elite pilots. You either adapt to the gameplay or enemies will whoop your thrusters hard.Missions are following the typical RPG quest types (search and destroy, deliver, escort, defend). _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the Wing Commander series of games, then you will likely enjoy Chorus.  The game has beautiful graphics, a good story, and works well with an XBox controller.
