_childDocuments_.review: Review after 4.8 hours of gameplay - before using the first jump gate: It's basically Space GTA meets the coolest re-creation of Descent you could come up with. Nice edgy story that entertains while not getting in the way. Great graphics and great audio. Easy to play in bite-sized chunks or in long sessions. Def a 9/10 from me. Add 1 if the devs add VR.I really, really, really wish this game had VR. Third person VR is fine. Just let us view this in stereoscopic 3D, and move our head around independent of what's going on with the ship. Don't slow the view down, don't do any of that anti-nausea stuff, people doing VR know what they're doing. Just do basic VR like that. It'll be great. It'll sell a shedload of copies to VR enthusiasts for little work on your behalf. You'll probably have to fix some shaders or the way you display some of the models so they don't look flat, but it'll be worth it. To anyone suggesting it: VorpX doesn't help this game. Some of the geometry ends up looking flat. That's not so great.The game is kind of built up like GTA IV or an open world RPG. You don't steal other cars/ships/whatever, although some missions put you in other ships. The fighting is cool. The audio visual aspect of the game is 11/10, eh, maybe except the human models which aren't so... perfect, but they're fiiiine. The gameplay loop is fun and rewarding, even the repetitive stuff. Pick the game up, shoot some bastards, leave it when you're done.The bad:It's really not so bad so far. I'll point out some stuff that's not really even that annoying, just, eh, kind of "growing pains" I guess.There are some bugs with the game: when you scan, you get markers for stuff you've already done, which seems like a bug. There are "memories" or whatever they are called that are there and give you markers but you can't interact with them. I don't know what they're for. It's weird. Some missions feel slightly buggy or like they could use a little polish, but nothing game breaking or frustrating. For example, I had to restart a mission where I'm chasing a ship that stole some plutonium, and it wasn't clear I was supposed to get in their vicinity, so I chased them for a while and then they "got away". So I had to restart from check point. But it's not so bad because the checkpoints in the game are good and I lost like, eh, 30 seconds of easy flying. So next time I hauled ass and I basically rammed into the ship and it stopped right away ... it was funny in a janky kind of way, but I don't mind. It kind of feels like this project is a little bigger than the team could handle, but they did a great job none the less. Sometimes, you get those intermittent conversations with random people for world building, but if you approach a mission marker, that gets cut off - and you don't hear the rest of the conversation. This one kinda sucks, but eh, the world building isn't ... really that important. Like, those conversations, they add flavour, but they feel like they could be deeper or a little better written. I'm talking about conversations with the station chief in the first part of the game, he kind of feels naiive or something. On the other hand the stuff that Nara says to herself feels cool. The barks from the ship during dogfighting feel a little... juvenile, but I guess they haven't annoyed me yet enough to mind. The whole "metaphysical" part of the world is great and it gives it a nice mysterious atmosphere. Speaking of conversations, it would be nice if other people were actually people, not just helmets, eh, that kind of makes them all sameish. I get it, that's extra budget. Maybe in a patch once the game has earned some money. That is one world building aspect that would make the game more engaging. Also: nara's mouth and teeth cast those weird shadows. Human skin and teeth are actually translucent, so it makes it weird. Maybe the devs could work on that a bit.This game could easily be a new, edgier GTA-like franchise, it's really fleshed out well, the world building is really good, the structure of the open world is similar to GTA IV, you could easily go miles further with it.If you make this one do VR, every single VR headset owner will buy it, guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 There are some things I really like:It runs well on my desktop and deck, cross saves seamless. Don't know if I had a single graphical hiccup,The combat CAN be very fun. Especially the standard enemies and the bigger ships you can go into and blow up.It introduces a drift and blink mechanic to dog fights. I often find that genre struggles to not devolve into endless banking/flipping/barrel rolling. Another way the combat CAN be fun and creative.I did not like:The story. I don't mind a subpar story by any means. I openly admit that I will skip ahead to get back to combat, which is usually what I look for in games. But I think this game had about 6 hours of story to tell and then it pads it out another 6 hours with redundant retreading on story points. Which, given the story isn't very good to begin with, was redundant. Just not very fun.Speaking of not fun, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are some of the end game enemies annoying. Not challenging. Not interesting. Annoying. The game started out strong, but like the story, I don't think the developer had a lot of depth. They started running out of ideas and came up with some subpar enemy types later in the game.So it does some things I really like. But it also does things I really dislike. YMMV. But very mid 4 to 6 out of 10 depending on what part of the game I am playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally review games, but I think this time I will.  In an age of rushed, buggy, incomplete, and perpetual early access game releases, this game stands apart.  The gameplay is crisp and solid, the weapons and abilities are fun, and the game is pretty and I need not brook any compromise with graphics to achieve a solid gameplay experience.  If you're looking for a new game that will run on old hardware during this PC parts crisis, Chorus will do the trick.  My PC from 2016 has had no issues whatsoever running it with a GTX 1070 at max settings.  I did have one crash fairly early on, but that was only due to my overly aggressive overclock, which only took one adjustment to correct.The story can get in the way a little, there are a few extended cinematics during story missions which can prove to be a bit of an interruption, and a couple of the time limits are quite unforgiving but I suppose the game does play on go fast or die.  That said I actually do enjoy the story.  It also has great potential for some open world qualities, but what you have is ~40 hours maybe of game world content.  It's enough, and I suspect someone will eventually post a vid of the 100% Completion+Hard+Permadeath run.Also I may just be biased because the whole concept of space fighter pilot ace on a quest for redemption with her AI space fighter partner against totally-not-a-Chaos-cult with warp frakery appeals to me on many levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magic induced space shooter with a little twist to it's controls: you can't really strafe! A and D just gives you a little evade manuver to left and right (that you actually need for some enemies to not getting hit). So you can't "circle" enemies while firing at them. This game is all about gameplay and how you manuver your ship with boost and drift. Holding right mouse button lets the ship keep "drifing" in its current direction while you can turn it around towards enemies. It needs some getting used to and can be frustrating at first, but is soo much more rewarding if you get the hang of it. You need to be aware of sourrounding objects and walls to not crash into them. The ship can withstand 1 heavy impact (looses the shields), but explodes if you boost full speed directly into an obstacele.You need to switch weapons a lot depending on weaknesses of the enemy. And taking apart capital ships bit by bit till flying into them and destroying their core is a blast. There are also magic spells called "rites" like spark shooting to disable shields of ships.Sometimes it feels like a mixture of Doom and Horizon: Zero Dawn with magic - as a space shooter.I really liked it, it felt kinda new to play like a new mixture of things that were there before but no one ever dared to combine them into one game plus something that could be a new control scheme for fast pased space shooters. And if you do everything there is with sidemissions and searching all the hidden reward boxes, you get at least 20 h out of it.

YES!!!If you like the 90's Decent game or Overload or any space fighting game or spiritual journeys, you'll love this.Story: 8.75/10Music: 7/10Graphics: 8.5/10Gameplay: 8.5/10Notes (no-spoilers): The combat was exhilarating and itched that spot I was missing. The story and theme was pretty great. Enjoyed it on a controller.Complaints (no-spoilers): I could see they were rushed. Shrug. But again, the game was enjoyable and the gameplay & plot really made it fun and kept me invested.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I finally managed to play some Chorus and quickly realized why it never made it into any of the charts or made a lasting impression.While story and general gameplay seem to be engaging, the usability aspect of the game is abysmal.I have a Warthog/VKB HOTAS setup for Flight Sim games and Chorus does recognize it. But how it assigns the Joystick is beyond me, Flightstick left/right is accelerate/decelerate. Selection buttons are completely unintelligible since they are on the Warthog throttle POV-hats ... somewhere.Oh you say "just change the control scheme"? Right, The issue is that the auto-assignment kicks in immediately on game start and I ahve no friggin idea how to gt into the control scheme. Plus, to make it really interesting, the game does not save controller settings. I managed to switch to mouse/keyboard since figuring out how to use my 1000€ Flight Sim setup wouldd have taken half a day. But after a restart the game decided to be back on the "Controller" scheme (of all things) making everything else useless again.Then the game itself. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is pretty much the best space combat I've seen - at least when talking about fast-paced, arcade-y games. Here's some of the parts that make it different and might not be obvious from viewing trailers or videos:- The drift button. While holding rightclick or L1, your ship will continue moving to the same direction, and allows you to eg. turn around and shoot backwards. Eg. when killing stationary turrets or slow enemies, you'll set up your movement so that you'll boost past the turret, enable drift mode, and basically do a drive-by while drifting.- "But why can't you just strafe?" - good question. The drift button is a bit weird to get used to, but once you figure it out, it just makes you think about your movement in a different way - which I personally find fun.- Dodge mechanic - there's a few enemies which require you to press dodge button just before they hit you. I haven't seen this mechanic used in a spacesim before, but it feels nice.- You have 3 weapons, switchable with a keypress at any time. Use laser beam to destroy shields, gatling gun to finish off small enemies, and use rockets to kill slow armored enemies. Standard rock-paper-scissors, but it still works well with the fast combat.- Along with weapons, you also have 3 different abilities which cost slowly recharging energy. One teleports behind the target, one zaps the target destroying their shields, and one is a charge forward which also hurts anything you hit with it. Noteworthy: 2 of your abilities also gives you additional options for mobility. Movement is a huge thing in the whole game, and plays a big part in making the combat feel fast and fun.- Then one thing which I can't fully explain: the highest difficulty (Extreme) makes enemies hit so hard that you die in a couple of seconds if you fly in wrong direction or even slow down too much. But even with the big damage intake, the combat is manageable - I rarely die, but if I die it's always because of a clear mistake which I can learn from (eg. "next time I won't fly directly towards that enemy"). In most space flight games, it usually feels a bit random when trying to dodge hits - I'm really not sure why Chorus is so great at this, but it just works.- Basically if you set the difficulty up to maximum, the game will require spatial awareness, good shooting and timing your dodges properly - it's difficult but in a fair way.The graphics are great both technically and aesthetically. There's really not much to say about it, . It also runs at unlimited fps, which is always nice to see.Music and audio design are also great through the whole game.I also haven't faced any notable technical issues - no weird fps dips, no crashing, the game loads quickly, etc. It's a well made game.Just to comment about the story: I feel like the story by its self is fine and I find it somewhat interesting (history/lore, character arcs, etc), but the storytelling is mid-tier at best. Every now and then the characters and dialogue just gets so edgy or overly dramatic that it makes me cringe.

Well worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If the really really bad storytelling does not give you several strokes, this is an enjoyable game. If badly written stories and voice-acting that feels forced do induce bodily harm on you, this one should be a hard pass.If you want to buy this, wait for at least 50% discount. Do not repeat my mistakes.+ decent graphics+ smooth combat experience+ refreshing special abilites (rites)+ sound design+ no in-game loading screens- really awful story (maybe it's good if you're a member of generation snowflake)- cringy voice-acting and awful subtitling- the TUTORIALS on some rites can get really frustrating (no joke)- cutscene character animations are awful (luckily you can skip)- UI could be better (enemies, friends and neutrals are just white squares unless you have them in direct view)-------------------------------------------------First things first:Valve, when asking me if I would recommend this game, a "Meh" rating would be really nice.This game would earn that rating in particular.It actually is a pretty decent space-shooter. If you can accept that this space has an up and a down.However, the quality of this game is severely diminished by really bad storywriting and voice-acting. The fact that for some reason quotes are quite overused in the subtitles doesn't help either.Let me give you an example:You take on a mission in which you have to kill a couple enemies. You do that. and then your ship AI says: 'We "killed" them!'Well yes, you psychopathic moron. We DID kill them, no need to put that in quotes. And it goes on and on and on like that. All the time.The constant whisper-thinking of your character doesn't help either. Please let me have my own thoughts.I also can't get over the fact that your character killed billions and now is on a guilt-trip. Here's a small toke of insight for you. If you butchered billions you already were a proper psychopath to start with. And if you are a psychopath the murder of billions of people would not weigh down on your conscience, as you would basically have no conscience to speak of.That being said, the game itself (story and voice aside) is pretty good. The flight mechanics are enjoyable and a refreshing touch (I played with an XBOX 360 controller). The missions are mostly fun and -although they technically are- do not feel like a repetetive slog of a grind. The graphics are somewhere between decent and good (epic preset) and i really do like that you have no loading screens between systems.So, is this game for you?Well, if you can endure the torture of going through the story and enjoy mildly challenging combat mechanics, then yes.If however, you like games with at least decent story-telling and character development, then please gain as much distance to this game as you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Trying to pilot your ship is like pulling it out of the mud. _childDocuments_.review: A solid AA experience, which never quite hits the heights you might hope for, but makes for a fun space shooter. At first it seems hard, but once you stop treating it like a standard space sim and drift instead of turn you shouldn't have any problems with the standard fights. The art and music come together to make every fight feel epic.It does suffer from a couple of nasty difficulty spikes around some bosses, but has a very generous checkpoint system which means you're rarely starting boss fights from scratch.My only disappointment with combat is how allies exist only to look like they're doing something with capital ships only shooting FX. Every fight is you versus the enemy, and that takes something away from the bigger encounters.Story clearly wants to be more epic than it is, with the AA element really showing its hand. It ends up being a bit of a light weight, slightly confusing, and never commits to really following through on any one character.Overall though if you treat this as a fun, arcade spaceship combat game then you're in for a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's what you need to know.  This game is good, but it isn't great.  The combat dynamics, soundtrack, graphics and environment all score 10/10.  The story, depth of characters, and results of decisions in game..all score 4/10 at best.  I'll give it a conditional thumbs-up.You enter the saga not having a clue who you are or what you stand for and those things would be OK, if at any point someone explained it to you.  Only by paying very close attention over the course of the entire game do you even garner a murky understanding of what this story is about.  There is no reason to care about the outcome of any portion or the characters or even the story line because none of it matters.  In the end, even the finale` cut scene is rushed, confused and leaves the player asking themselves "What the hell did I just go through and why did I bother?"  Hardly a fitting reward for saving the entire universe from even a poorly developed everlasting darkness.The answers to these questions can only be found if you play it for yourself and if you get it on sale it's probably worth the money.  (I spent $5.00)  But, be warned, Chorus is an experience that is best compared to ordering a sandwich and only getting the bread and some mustard.  High-quality bread and mustard to be sure, but that's it.

There were some really frustrating flying moments where the response time of the ship was highly over estimated by the developers, and some of the boss fights were down right infuriating. But it wasn’t dog excrement as most games are these days. There were no micro transactions, live service links, and there was enough polish that I wanted to keep coming back until it was finished. It was a decent experience. Buy it on sale. Oh and one final note, the $5 Elder armor skin set is a joke. My one only true beef. I hate it when developers cut off an already developed content package and sell it back to the player at a premium hitting on FOMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a wonderfully executed game for the first 3 quarters of the game, that allows the player to fly their starfighter light an actual spaceship instead of an airplane in space. Featuring dual protagonists, one Nara, burdened with the guilt of committing mass genocide, and the other  her bloodthirsty, and  vengeful starship, Forsa.   Note that  on the last quarter, the devs decide to kick their legs out from under them by forgetting the rule of 3.If you want to pick up this game, you're liable to enjoy up until you come up with a plan to "give the great red space sphincter a laser enema, and fly inside to complete the space-Colectomy."Despite the frustrating last quarter of the game, I still like it's sequences where you fend off massive squadrons of smaller fighters, punch way above your weight class by shredding frigates, carriers, and even a space station or 2, and even get to fly around in a capital ship of your own.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this game seems to divide opinion and mine is that its very good.  Chorus had been on my watch list for for a  while, mainly due to mixed reviews and it not fitting the usual genre of game I play.  That said, when it popped up for £5 or so, it was time to jump in the cockpit and I was completely addicted in the pursuit of concluding Nara's story.Very early on the game play is smooth (Played on PC), fast, intense, the sound effects are as sci-fi as you can imagine and the main story moves along at warp pace.  It is way to easy get wrapped in the main story, you're literally flying along towards missions or challenges in the game that you simply will not have the craft, skills or mods to complete.  Given Chorus is a challenging game, if you find yourself in this situation, missions become insurmountable, quickly.  My biggest piece of advice is to clear most of the side quests in the area before moving on to the next asteroid belt/planet, the mods and cash are going to be essential for upgrades.  There will come a point where you feel a little OP to be honest, but when you come up against bosses or certain parts of the story you'll die a fair few times before you crack it!I found the story quite compelling, and without giving away spoilers, you become quite attached to a character in the game.  There are points in the game, firing barrages or rockets at large attack ships, flying past turrets and blowing warships up from inside as you fly out of the explosion, that are genuinely thrilling, especially to the backdrop of a musical score that would not be out of place at the cinema.  Epic.I appreciate the game isn't without its faults.  The voice acting starts badly for the first few hours, but the actors seem to grow into their roles as the game moves on and it does help that you spend more time with Nara and your ship later in the game, therefore the dialogue is less varied.  I got the feeling the actors probably didn't have the right character brief to set the tone, there were some rather giddy folk floating around religiously oppressed space. Oh and the whispering, the inner monologue, you'll either let it wash over you or you'll be super annoyed.The quest selection can be a little funky, but not to the point you want to quit the game, as some others have suggested.  Twice I had to drop out to re- trigger a quest or on a couple of occasions you need to fast travel to a new world and back to kick it off again.  Sometimes its a little ambiguous but to me this felt like an older game whereby you have to figure things out a little bit. Which goes hand in hand with the challenging difficulty of the game, there's no hand holding.If you're into this genre or looking for a change, pick it up, its very reasonable and the devs has made an effort here to build an exciting space shooter with a captivating story , with some interesting messaging, you'll just have to fight hard through the frustrations on occasion.  But once you win a tough dogfight or defeat a boss, it is very rewarding. In Chorus!

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up thinking "you know what I haven't played in a long time? A good space combat game." And after a couple of hours, you know what? I still haven't played a good space combat game in a long time.For starters, how do you not have 6DOF in a space combat game? Interplay was doing it over twenty five years ago with Descent. Overload has it (killer game btw), but Chorus? They make a "mission" about getting some ship that talks to you and allows you to "drift"... and that's about as close as it gets. You will die in combat a lot because the concepts behind the controls are frustrating and poorly thought out. But don't forget to boost then LB and right thumbstick and drift derp derp.The second big thng that almost makes this one unplayable on its own is the constant dialog between the main character and herself. She is constantly whispering to herself and it's cringe. Had I known this was going to be an interactive novel that was being whispered to me by some edgelord lady I'd have passed from the outset. Now I'm trying to see if I can get my money out of it and its just painful. There's a thousand ways to tell a story that don't involve nonstop whispering voiceovers. If it's trying to build drama or suspense it's failing miserably. I'm sure there's some story that is being explained but I'm kinda tuning it out because I am so sick of this dramatic whispering stuff.The presentation I guess is nice? The graphics don't look bad. But that's about it. Oh and it works under linux so yay for that. Whatever is there for a story is so annoyingly delivered that I've tuned it out, and the controls are just terrible. I've played this over the period of time where Steam will give me a refund, so I'm stuck trying to see if I can get my money out of it but if you want a fun space combat game go pick up Overload. You won't find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly it's a no for me. The premise seems interesting, looks nice, the space combat seemed generic (pump the enemies full of bullets), but I only played over an hour, so it may change for the better. Nevertheless, mission design and control messed up the game for me. There was a mission where I had to pick up mines and despite using the scanning ability, my screen was populated with literally dozens of POIs with no idea which pixel is the next mine I should pick up. Obviously I could have used trial and error, but seriously?Also, there is a story mission where I had to control a battleship, yet, no indication how to change position vertically, so I couldn't reach the waypoint. I tried to remap the control, but lo' and behold', it's impossible. You are only presented with the controller setup, but if you play with keyboard (like me), you have no idea to remap and/or overview the button placement. Again, I may have googled it, or could do trial and error (again), but seriously? For a game released 1.5 years ago you can't even check/remap the control buttons?

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent combat mechanics which take a bit of getting used to but flow really well once you are able to acclimate. The story itself was ok, it felt a little 'choppy' sometimes which hampered immersion and the side missions were drawn between intriguing and outright annoying. The one major shame about the game was that the areas you visit feel very empty, this is made even more stark when set against the wonderful visuals both in the background and of the actionable elements.Overall I would recommend this game to anyone that wants to play a more arcade-like spacefighter and I found it to be a very enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must buy for everyone who loves games like Wing Commander, Starlancer and AquaNox 2.The "flight-feeling" is great and I recommend playing it with a controller - the Steam Controller works great, but I strongly suggest to switch the (left) analog stick with the right track pad as the analog stick is much better suited for control.I really enjoyed the fact, that it is not an openworld game, but instead gives you hubs to explore which contain several unique side quests as well as some generic ones. Besides the obligatory rewards (items, currency) the offer a little insight into the world you are playing in.Being mainly story-driven the game truly ends after the final quest.I bought the game for ~30€ during a sale and given I had about 20 hours of fun in my first playthrough that is completely fair.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a fun and well-designed arcade space fighter game. I picked the game up because I enjoyed Fishlab's Galaxy on Fire 2. This one amps up the excitement of the dogfighting and leaves out the space trucking and mining found in other space games. It does not suffer for it. The story is tight, well-voice acted, and with good writing, though it's a bit melodramatic and in its feelings sometimes, The music is phenomenal. The game took me about 30 hours to complete. It'll probably be a couple hours shorter if you don't try to 100% the achievements. Attaining 100%, however, is possible on a normal playthrough–with no extraordinary effort–with the exception of achievement you receive from getting permadeathed.

_childDocuments_.review: The best review I read on here that sold the game to me: If you liked Everspace 1 or 2, Freelancer, or any of the same flight shooting genre, you'll probably like this.The controls take a little getting used to.  You fly a jet fighter in space essentially.  The story is paper thin and the upgrades even more so.  Only one ship you fly and only three weapons really.  The worlds are static and don't feel alive.But what does feel alive is the combat.  It's definitely tight and enjoyable.  30 hours to get through the game, worth the value.  I enjoyed it and I think you might too.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly awesome experience. I really had no idea what to expect going into this other than it looked "neat", but this game surprised me in a lot of ways. Surprisingly great gameplay, surprisingly great combat, surprisingly great world building, surprisingly great voice acting, surprisingly great graphics, surprisingly large open-world environments, surprisingly long story, etc etc etc. Meaningful pickups to fly around and collect, interesting quests and side quests, awesome combat against capital ships, this game has it all, and it feels like Freelancer. If you know what that is, this is probably something you'll really like. If the devs did a sequel in a truly open galactic setting along the same lines as Freelancer in the same universe, I'd definitely buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I've already played through it multiple times on different platforms - i love it!Once i came clear with the controls, i really enjoyed the chemistry between Nara and her ship Forsa, great voice acting and interesting story. Although the world is rather small and some side missions are a bit annoying, i can recommend this to anyone who likes scifi and space battles.Graphics are also very nice to look at, on PC and PS5 both.Buy it and hope for Chorus 2! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This would have been somewhat okay if not memorable in the slightest if it didn't have one idiotic mechanic that you absolutely have to master to progress the story.Pros:- Great visuals.- Exploration. - Cool ship designs.- Runs smooth and bug free.Cons:- Clunky controls.- Combat is average at best.- Silly and non-sensical "space wizards" story.- Character often whispers in dialogue like a mental asylum escapee.- Completely idiotic "drift" mechanic that highlights the clunkyness of controls.- Repetitive side activities and poor side mission design.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely solid arcade-y space shooter. Moment-to-moment combat is incredibly fun and the demo reeled me in immediately and the full game didn't disappoint. A small but satisfying amount of customization makes story and side mission progress satisfying and worthwhile, and the Rites/powers pull it all together and make you a ridiculously overpowered fighter, which is good in a PvE game like this.The voice acting and writing in the game is a bit "meh", but not offensive or bad by any stretch. Just a bit predictable and standard fare.Great game for what I've heard dubbed as a "AA" game. Looks pretty great visually, plays fantastically, and doesn't overstay its welcome with tedious and unnecessary side missions that add nothing. Overall great package.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I am barely able to put this game down after 8 hours. I don't know how long it is, but I feel like I could play it all in one sitting regardless. The gameplay loop is fantastic, and the pacing is perfect. Just a smattering of side missions. There's never so many side missions at any given time that you feel like you're being pulled away from the main story. For the most part, the side missions are highly relevant to what you're doing in the main story anyway.Don't expect the story to be terribly deep. And it's pretty much a fantasy game, and not at all a realistic space sim (I don't think it was ever advertised as such anyway).The combat is intoxicating. I think the whole point is to make you feel like a dogfighting god. I highly recommend using a controller though. All the abilities/weapons I've unlocked so far are easy to use when and how you want to use them. Incorporating everything into your tactics is seamless and intuitive.The game performs quite well. I haven't personally run into any bugs whatsoever. There were a couple of times I thought I encountered a bug, but in every case it was just that the game didn't do a good job of showing me what I needed to do. That has been pretty rare so far, however.Absolutely enjoying the hell out of this game. Thank you, devs. Good work!!EDIT: I finished the game! It only got better! The only thing I'll add is that I want more...MORE!! Scratched an itch I didn't even know I had. I am extremely satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, felt compelled to do so for this game. I'm a 'old space game'  dude, for context.Open world-ish space shooter, with a good 'dark space fantasy' setting. I've got great performance out of it, runs well at 144fps on my rig, looks beautiful. Great aesthetics. Feels polished, and slick, I really like the way it looks, and the controls are really snappy. The ship feels great to fly around, very responsive, enemy ships pop in a very satisfying manner, explosions look good. Like a much faster, crisper version of what freelancer did back in the day. I'd take this combat over freelancer's put it that way. I really like the story elements too, the main character is great in a sort of 'melodramatic dark scifi' way. Really like the cutscenes.Great AA game, good price for a polished game, that looks and feels punchy. Took a punt on it and bought blind without reading anything about it, 100% don't regret it. More games like this please!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: So, uhm, quite simply put - it's an arcadey space shooter with a female Darth Vader who turns into an ASMR fighter pilot - It has a few Wing Commander vibes and tells its story through some Dune-type whispers within an atmosphere that tends to be Hellblade in space. Make of this what you will. - Would drift with a spaceship and fail again, just like in Forza!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is an interesting fast paced sci-fi action adventure shooter, which follows Nara and her sentient ship on a path of redemption and escape from religious zealotry, indoctrination, rebel uprising and other-dimensional entities culminating in a reckoning with her past as the Circles once premier chosen.The gameplay itself takes place entirely in the ship, going through a handful of side- and main story missions, revolving around a couple of different locations. There isn't much to see or do outside following those missions, apart from the odd pickup or two. Although there's a what feels like a tacked-on RPG system, that doesn't have much of an impact on the gameplay, outside swapping a couple of different weapons and ship modules around, although the majority of them have no use. Ultimately a handful of weapons and Nara's incredible powers resolves most situations the game throws at you.The action is very fast paced, whether it's in tight quarters or more open areas, the pedal is pressed down to the max and Nara can strafe around outmaneuvering just about all opposition and has the upper hand in all but a choice few boss fights. There's a sense that the game doesn't really scale in difficulty as the story progresses, and it's really no more difficult than when you start the game, as it gradually gets easier the wilder her powers become.Chorus is a visually good looking game and it runs very well, especially with DLSS. Although it does have a tendency to microstutter at times.Hopefully we'll see more to Nara in the future, or more to this universe whether in a similar format or a different genre. There's a lot of potential to explore in the universe Chorus takes place in.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun, tight gameplay, combat is a lot of fun with some really cool powers. Mixed with solid visuals & art direction with really good sound effects and a mostly awesome soundtrack it's a solid experience all around and well worth the price especially on sale. What's not so great is the story. There's a sense of over-ambition, trying to achieve more than they were capable of or had the budget for. Story and voice acting is all over the place. Some moments hit but mostly just wish they'd stop talking so I could start shooting. Some cool gameplay ideas and unique missions are explored in side-quests exactly once, only to never appear again. The main character is the only face model that appears in the entire game, cutscenes all involve masked figures or shadowy spectres. Missions are given by ships hailing over voice with static portraits so clearly they were working with a limited budget. But technically everything is top notch, game is well optimized, looks great, controls well and sounds good. Narrative jankiness aside, what matters - the gameplay, is really well done. Solid 15-20 hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A great space shooter.Flight and combat are really fun and dynamic.The visuals/graphics and sounds/music are beautiful.The world and its lore are interesting.The story is alright and I appreciated its core message.I absolutely loved GoF2 (Galaxy on Fire 2), an older Fishlabs game, but was very disappointed by GoF3 and GOFA.I'm glad that they are still able to make good games and hope to see more from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a fantastic game in terms of gameplay. It is controlled different to other space fighter shooters and it's the controls that make the game feel so brilliant. the flight controls make for a great experience. Your ship can drift meaning you can pull off all sorts of hairpin turns and combined with your powers allow for some real fancy moves. As you zoom around weaving in between waves of enemies to  make a run on the reactor core of a capital ship is excessively fun and for this alone I recommend it.  the story seems like it is in 2 parts though. The first part, the defence against these religious nuts was phenomenal. the writing was fantastic. And the big set piece battles are beautiful. But after about the third zone the writing turned into complete garbage. I had no idea who or what was going on. Why was I all of a sudden helping the enemies? fight my enemies? but are they? and then I had to find my religion , find chorus which is not really fully explained as a concept. Minus the last battle there are no more of the big set piece battles and it felt honestly, like a different game. I am honestly not even sure what happened at the end. it is beyond bizarre. But despite the rubbish story writing, the gameplay, world design and music more than makes up for it's negatives. well worth a purchase if just for the combat alone. You will feel like an unstoppable war machine in no time!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: 8.2/10 - Fantastic Game.Pros: - Combat that makes you feel like an ultimate badass, the progression of your equipment and psychic abilities combined with them let you do stuff that, if you were to stream it, you would get viewers. There were multiple times that i was in large combats and i Just felt like a badass, drifting through space and pulling cool maneuvers straight out of action flicks. - The Story, I have no idea how this lost people, a story of redemption where a lost sinner deals with the echoes of her past while a Cult conquers the galaxy all while mysterious entities are noticed manifesting in our world. Are they connected? And how? Its done very well, doesn't hold your hand. and the protagonist is a traumatised deeply flawed darling. She's great.-Visuals / World design: The visual designs on the bosses and areas were fun, different from each other and good to fly around. The Sandboxes had life and felt real and practical. Flying around in this world was almost as cathartic as swinging across new york in spiderman.-Sound Design: Rather unique from acceleration sounds to general combat, it was better than most space fighters for sure. Cons: - Enemy Diversity / Amount: One of the things i didn't like in this game was the scope is always kept rather small, except towards the end. Never more than 10 or so enemies at a time and the biggest ships register as about a light cruiser in star wars. When you feel SO POWERFUL you want to fight star destroyers and be he hero in huge conflicts. it was a missed opportunity. Hope its added later. There is 1 conflict that does this in the game and it feels SO GOOD to get there, but it needed a lot more of it. - Weapon diversity: There was some, but i would have liked there to be more sets of weapons, Its likely i didn't FIND all of them, but with 3 slots of weapons, each of them having only really 2 variants between more or less rapid fire. I would have liked more diversity here. Scatter blast weapons like shotguns, explosive lasers, mini nukes, weapons that riccochet. They could have gone wild and kept in theme with the game. Overall, the game was wonderful with a couple of flaws which i hope if there's another game done by these people in the same world (which there better damn be!) They focus on making the scope of the game grander. I would love a prequel set before key events here when the war was raging at its height.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: It's a close call but I don't recommend this.The combat dynamics are not too bad but the incessant "whispering" by the main character is enough to make you want to jump naked out of an air lock, not to mention the protagonist is so visually irritating that I have to skip every single cut scene so as to not cause damage to my eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I sort of forced myself to finish this game. The combat (minus piloting capital ships) is really fun and I was pleasantly surprised by the endgame weapon and set bonus options but basically everything else in the game isn't that great. The music and visuals are awesome, but the facial animations are up there with Mass Effect Andromeda. The fundamental ideas of the story and character arcs are interesting enough, but it's spoonfed to the player and the writing and voice acting are at times terrible.I don't think this game is unplayable or unbearably bad, but I also wouldn't recommend it to a friend who wasn't already into this type of game. If that's you, or if you really just want to try the combat and don't care about the rest, it's definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Usually not a fan of flying games, but the mechanics in this give you so much flexibility and movement it got me hooked. 10/10 visuals.FYI the demo s*cks, it just throws a list of descriptions at you all at once and confuses you. Meanwhile the campaign does a much better job at it by introducing you to the mechanics one step at the time. The demo needs improvements, I almost avoided the game because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: After several hours i finally decided that NOT recommend is the answer. I was waiting for this game for so long and it took maybe one minut to was completely disappointed. I hoped that this game will be like Freelancer or Everspace but in different design and better overall but then i started the game and first few seconds you are able to control your fighter you will realize that something is wrong. There is no strafe! Every single game that has space fighters does have strafe. Why? Because its so obvious. But seems like Chorus didnt think so. So you can go forward, you can go back... oh yeah you cannot go backward...so again, you can go forward, you can.... hmm and thats it. All your movement is by using mouse, no rotation, no strafe, no backward movement. Now lets pretend you dont care about it, well ok. Every fight you will have you will just spam A and D button for "dodge" maneuver, so your ship looks like helicopter rotor all the time.Just imagine playing some first shooter where your character can go only forward. We are in 2021, not in 1980s....Then when we skip the movement, there is the UI i just dont understand. Map control and map overall looks like game from 2000. Unintuitive and completely useless. After several hours i still dont undestand where are directions, where i am NOW and what is important for me to do and what is just some station outthere.Regarding the UI - ITEMS. You have 3 weapons for whole game. Yes.... only three weapons. So what are you spending your credits for? Well for so many weapons that are completely same type (minigun. laser, rocket launcher) just with different stats. Some better fire rate, some faster recharge, some damage etc. But in the end, just three same weapons. And that is not all, you can of course buy utilities and some MODS to improve your ship, but understanding those items is big confusion question mark. What is equipped, on which slot, what is better? you will ask those question yourself....then you will find an answer and you will be like....hmm ok ...but to say some POSITIVES:When you skip all those things that are bad on this game, combat is actually fine. It is somehow fun but overal its not like "i am the galactic master of flying skill in amazing space ship".... no. You are Button spammer, thats all.Campaign is average as story somehow is totaly stupid, but some parts were really interesting and i could emerge into the character just to be fired off another minute because bad sound design. In one moment, you can literally hear and feel emotion of your character, then your character is emotionless robot and her speech looks like something exported from google translate.Overal i would be able to close my eyes above everything bad this game has. But being not able to control ship properly (THIS IS SPACE SHIP SIMULATOR!!!) this just kills me everytime.I want to finish this game to see what it offers overall but my final rating would be 4/10 at most
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this is a damn good game. BLUF: Smooth gameplay, decent characters and a good story with fun and engaging combat. A bit on the shorter side, but still worth it IMHO.time in game ~20hrs and have beaten the game on Normal difficulty. Pros:Visuals - great. enemies are distinctly identifiable, games ares are nicely varied and rendered. Lastly, the color pallet is futuristic without being neon Combat Mechanics - rock solid. each ability and weapon alters things enough to change how you fight.Weapons - diverse enough to have meaning/consequence without going over the topCharacters - arcs are pretty decent with good voice actingStory - Pretty linear but with enough extras to not make it feel weirdly artificialCons:Length - i wanted more. not because it felt super short, but because i wanted to keep playing. ~20hrs to finish every quest line i could find without spending another 20 looking.Character - everyone is in a ship. most of them are in ships way to big. why would a run of the mill engineer need to take something the size of a small freighter to work? not that big a deal, but for me it was a little immersion breaking head scratcher.Conclusion: if you want a fun game where you can blast enemies away and feel both powerful and challenged while enjoying the story this is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. In its own right, it delivers an action-packed, well-designed experience. Could it be better? Sure, the game is not perfect, but it's well-tuned and knows its strengths and weaknesses. If you enjoy fast-paced action gameplay with fun mechanics and a dark story, then do not miss this game and consider buying the soundtrack. It's quite marvelous, like the game itself!And there are even some nice in-game cutscenes!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a ride. Completed the game shy of 20 hours and finished most of the side missions. To be honest I "cheated" a little - mostly played on medium and in the major boss fights I switched to easy difficulty.Some of the boss fights and missions are way tooo tough and repetitive. I almost gave up on the 3 sentinel mission but managed to punch through that despite replaying it for like almost 20 runs (on EASY)!. The finale was quite rewarding from a story perspective, but I must admit - the developers did "shove" a lot of the story and lore to you, but it'll make sense towards the end.The piloting of the ship to the combat and the powers (called rites) are fantastic. It makes me feel like a super-fighter-pilot on steroids. What I didnt like was the save game system where like some have commented, it saved and loaded back in odd places or when you did, it gave you unskippable mini-cutscenes with dialog. That's just annoying.Sadly there aren't too many variety of weapons and loot, I wish they did more there. However this game is still a blast and I would recommend getting it on a discount (not retail price).One thing that I couldn't figure out how to solve and many online forums have said its due to the game engine - is that there are times during certain scenes it produces micro-lags. I played this game on my ROG Ally on 18W TDP with mostly high except post processing, anti-alasing and viewing distance (if i'm not mistaken that's what its called) - on medium.I have read that even high specced NVIDIA systems face the same issue so i'm pretty sure its not the Ally that causes this but the game engine. But if you can get through that - you really have fun and I really love the power/rite called "Rite of the hunt" where you teleport at the back of the ship and just blast them to pieces. Really fun mechanic and you might think its overpowered but it isn't. Try the demo and have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Chorus is a very good game because of the ability to fly a spaceship without issue. Unlike Star Citizen which is over budget and long past due, who's ability to deliver a passable flight sim is utterly lacking, Chorus more than makes up for their failures. The story is good but I would have preferred to have a better back story. Some of the side missions are too simplistic to complete, press a button and you're done...absolutely no challenge.  If there's a sequel then they must have:- A better engrossing story- A map that's more detailed, dash of color, etc.- A 1st person experience and not just cut-scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this game an 8/10 solely because of the gameplay, combat mechanics and atmosphere. The game world is beautifully built and there's a lot of different strategies for obliterating your opponents. The modifications allow for some customization and I'd wish there were more ships- owning/customizing a Spirit Class Ship would've been awesome. The story and dialogue felt a bit empty to me, as the fact that I didn't really get a feel of the characters, it didn't get me invested at all. That being said, I think this is still a very good purchase, especially if you're in the market for an arcade flight/shooter game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Holy moly, this is some kind of BS I haven't seen in a long time.Gameplay is ok but get's boring pretty easily. Graphics are ok for what it is.The story, however, is utterly nonsensical and the dialogues are painfully awful. I'm not quite 8 hrs in and I really hope that I'm close to the last mission yet (haven't done a lot of side quests) and the story line gets more and more confusing. In the beginning I had kind of an idea what was going on, but the closer to the endgame one gets, the worse the storytelling becomes.I mean like srsly: Why do the protagonist and her grumpy side-kick sound like a medieval drama theater play? Are they both schizophrenic? Better play X series games for space stuff with story, Hellblade for mental illness and Everything for "wat?"I'm being honest: I've played quite a lot of games during the past 25 years and I think this might be the first one which's storytelling doesn't just not interest me, but also annoys me to a level that I wish to see the political scenes in Star Wars Ep 1 again to calm down. Heck, I don't even need to see the rest of the game. Protagonists do protagonist things and save the day. Probably some more WEEEEEEEE SPACE FANTASY MAGIC WEIRD CREATURE WOOOOOOOOOSHH BOOOOM wtf just happened.Cannot recommend. Clean your toilet instead or smth.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a very fun game. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys more arcady spaceship fighting games. The story can seem a little over-the-top with it's supernatural elements and some of the side quests can get repetitive, but the flying feels incredibly responsive and fun, smooth and agile, there is a decent, albeit not overwhelming number of equipment, so different playstyles can be used and the game looks really nice.I didn't run into a single bug or technical issue, ran smoothly and on a technical side there is nothing I can complain about.For all the side content I took about 20 hours, though if you are not doing every side quest or loot every random encounter, you can definitely beat this game a lot sooner. The price is a little high for the content, imho, but admittedly the polish is most definitely there!All in all, very much recommended, but maybe wait for a sale unless you REALLY crave an arcadey spaceflight game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: What a shame.  This could be junk food enjoyable if it wasn't for the dysfunctional controls for both keyboard/mouse and gamepad.  They were obviously designed by someone whose brain got confused somewhere between 2.5d and 3d.  The lack of actual strafing or roll control is almost as laughable as the protagonists inner dialogue.  It amazes me how the majority of space combat games still fail so spectacularly when it comes to basic flight controls.Don't waste the effort of a full game worth of production if you can't get the basics of movement controls right first!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty and the story isn't bad but it's super unclear what you're doing or where you're going so often and then you just get massive difficulty spikes that require what is essentially spamming quick time events.If you don't like boss fights where the 90% of the mechanic is just quick times, don't get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Super nice space dog fight game. Pad in the hand gives great fun and great sense of speed and control.The story is good and dark, the gameplay is pure fun, thousands of skirmishes and few very good big space battles.I can't say it is a perfect game... But, guys... it is a perfect fun for arcade space shooters lovers!Haven't got so much fun since the times of Tie-Fighers WOW!Extremly good to use with 2-sticks-pad.Just pass the first 10 minutes of tutorial and you will got it in your hands
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game! The visuals are gorgeous, and the combat/flight system is really fun and very intuitive once you get used to it. The story is interesting, but also somewhat convoluted, and the narrative style is not the best -- sometimes so downright goofy that I laughed out loud. There are also some missions that make you ask why or how someone would even do them in a ship, which hurts immersion a bit as well. But overall, the flight and combat mechanics make it so fun you can ignore the cheesiness.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: great space shooter. takes a minute to get used to the drifting with the controller. but after you get the hang of the mechanic man does the ship sing in space when dogfighting.the cinematics and the voice overs are all well done as well. honestly i started the game expecting it to be bug filled, non playable, and graphics all to ♥♥♥♥.. like every other release this year, but after starting it up and playing it for 3hrs now, i have found not a single hitch. so confused, thought complete and playable great games werent on the menu this year, wonderful to see one though finally. other devs take note.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice spaceship battling game. Everything is made so the ship is responsive, battles are lightning fast and the game offers you multiple powers that you'll have to use in order to win. There are no big low times unless you want it to be, as the game will pop some random events to fill a few gaps.The quests are varied, mechanics too, usually in harmony with the powers that will have to be mastered.Graphics are simple but effective, gameplay is a fast-paced fighting where each boss brings a new challenge, you can customise your loadout to adapt it to your play style, but not one is superior to the others, fights are fast paced but do not require you to mash buttons like an idiot, soundtrack is amazing, voice acting is good, maps are big but not immense with various things to collect if you have a keen eye/sense.Go for those nasty enemies and become... in chorus.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun arcade shooter. It seems to have a deep story line, and if you take side missions you get to hear even more. Also bits of it keeps coming in while you simply fly between missions. The flight model is arcade'ish and more like a fighter plane. And sadly no first person cockpit view. Highly recomended if you just want a simple arcade shooter with a nice story.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: loved this game, ive played quite a few space games lately, and this has been the best, good story, great voice acting, graphics are nice, there's a fair amount of content, such as different weapons, upgrades and mods for your ship, some can be bought, some can be found, or looted, and some upgrades are earned through combat (mastery). Its basically a story driven space based shooter.Took me 23 hours to complete on normal difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: For an older game, its actually pretty good. M&K controls are good..... similar to Everspace 2. The story is meh, but the visuals and game-play are fun. Game needs more save points. It leads you from mission to mission with no time in between to save and of course it won't let you save once you're in a mission.Got it on sale for $6. Get it on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this, but no matter what I did, the controls just wouldn't jive with me. for some reason, lowering the sensitivity to 0 doesn't affect vertical sensitivity but it does affect horizontal sensitivity, which is an issue when the vertical sensitivity is just way to high to feel like I have fine control of the ship.  There is also no way to control the ship's roll, you can only affect it by resetting it. Like at least give me the option to control it? I understand it's supposed to be arcade-y but even Halo Reach's sabres have better controls than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, Chorus is a lot of fun to play. You start out in an asteroid-ridden zone with a rickety ship and zap your way through a mostly linear story which is all about overcoming one's past. Flying is smooth and arcadey, and as the game progresses combat becomes a dance where you are a force of nature. Gotta hand it to the the devs for a drifting tutorial/mission that actually taught me how to drift and shoot (in space!). Yes, there are some rough edges. The writing is a bit thin, and triggering/finding next step of a mission can take some flying around. A few rough boss difficulty spikes. And the beginning has a lot of the main character whispering hints to herself (ie: you).However, with those aside, the flying itself feels good, has some neat boss battles, and it ends with a metal, satisfying conclusion that leaves you wanting more. If you wanted less sim and more power fantasy than you got in Star Wars: Squadrons, this might be right up your alley (when on sale, of course!). Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I wish Steam could let you rate a game as 'Maybe'.I mean the current reviews are rating it Mostly Positive (75%) and I think that is what I would give this game 7/10.Over all it isn't bad.  But there are a few gotcha's going into it you should know.   It is basically an free-roaming arcade space shooter with optional newtonian drift along the vector you are currently traveling.   Meaning you can blast forward, turn on drift and shoot enemies behind you without a change to forward momentum.  You can also drift past a target and fire on them. However, you have NO lateral or vertical thrusters, so no side-slipping/thrusting or vertical-slipping/thrusting.  And this game could have really used that. In general the enemies are diverse, and will require different tactics.   As you earn new weapons  they do feel worth it, but there are no homing missiles until late in the game if you can afford it, and that is annoying.Listening to Nara's inner monolog gets old, but the story and the world building is good story-wise in the game.   I just wish there have been more to explain how the universe got to the state it is in for the game.Finally,  this game is not easy.   Even on easy difficulty, be prepared to die, a lot.   Missions can be long with long gaps between save times (you can only save out of a mission)  although the game does some autosaving at check points in missions (but probably not where you hope it will be).Finally, and this needs to be said.  There are two boss fights which are abnormally long and tedious, one being the Final Boss of the game itself.   In fact the final boss fight is sort of infamous, because... well it is not very fun.   The game developer do not throw any new mechanics at you.  The do stick to the rule that the final boss fight should be highlights of the major mechanics you have already learned in the game.   But they implement them to be used for the most irritating ways possible.   If you can over look those two boss fights, Chorus is a solid game, but it is just a good game, not a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the single coolest arcade flight game ive ever played.  The game provides combat and flight mechanics that feel so good to use once you master them and feel so rewarding when you conquer a fight and no one touched you... top that with semi-deep RPG mechanics (ship customization) and so much content with deep lore... this is my surprise game of the year, hands down
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have religious trauma? Would you like to embody a character that awoke from a cult and realized certain things were really ♥♥♥♥? Well, this is the game for you!Seriously, the lore is intriguing at the least. The game-play is tricky in that the controls are not bad, but could use better mapping.Honestly, for a space game this is fantastic and fun. Mostly easy to burn through the entire game, but getting all the achievements just requires not finishing the last mission until you are ready...Ultimately, I recommend. I would also love this game in VR. Something about the flight controls and space combat want me to experience it in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: While chrous is far from a perfect game all in all it was enjoyable.The space wizardry story wasnt exactly my cup of tea, but i see others enjoy it, although the presentation was a bit mixed. The Cutscenes were cool, so was the main charackter design. I liked the voicework, but the delivery ingame was incredibly stiff. Most is delivered via comms, while you just stand there and listen to it, or visions, where you also just stand there and listen to what is basically a distorted voice comm.Gameplay was pretty good. The drift mechanic feels great and enemy designs have a decent variety. Some parts of the game are way to easy thought. The gameplay mechanic of big capital ships you have to fly into is awsome, but their system have too little HP so they go down in a single flyby, which sucks. The last part of the game is way, way to easy in generell. You get "spells" aka rites, that just shred through several enemies on a miniscule cooldown and neither enemy HP or numbers keep up with your increase in power.The final battle and endboss were incredibly cool thought.So if you like the thought of an arcady space combat game, chorus is worth your time and money even if its not perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a roller coaster of love/hate for me.  Twirling around like an anime spaceship of destruction, I loved it.  When forced to listen to meaningless mumbo jumbo dialog, I hated it.This game has two things going for it.  The spaceship combat is an absolute blast and the world looks absolutely beautiful.  I was doing every sidequest I could find early on because I couldn't get enough of the sights, sounds and combat.Unfortunately, once I got into the meat of the main story, I grew exhausted of the main character's dour melancholy and whispering inner monologue.  The game desperately lacks levity and takes itself dead seriously despite having little of interest to say.  There is an overwhelming amount of spoken dialog that you're forced to listen to, but 90% of the time, it adds nothing to your understanding of the world. It's just filler.This game would be amazing if they abandoned their attempts at storytelling and focused on making a fun arcade spaceship shooter with deep progression.  That's what's frustrating about this game.  It's a blast to pew pew, but that is constantly interrupted by inept storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I wish there was a recommend with a big "...but." I'm writing a negative review just so I can help balance the reviews of the game. This game can be flashy and even at times, it feels reminiscent of Starfox64 (you can do a barrel roll!). However, it has a lot of flaws that I can't overlook. I found myself reloading autosave checkpoints (which happen seemingly at random as there's no indicator the game is saving) when I would trip up game objectives and events. I would get to a spot and the objectives would not load properly. The pacing of the game also feels very off. For an "sandbox" like game there's not a lot of sidequests or random encounters that will aid you in grinding out some of the mastery challenges. The story is boring and cliche, with subpar cinematics and voice acting (which I'm surprised there were any cut scenes at all).The atmosphere of the game can be beautiful but sometimes feels like a slog to traverse. The gameplay is fun and can provide a challenge at times, but some of the mechanics of the game just feels underdeveloped or superfluous. I would recommend this game on deep discount just to match how cheap this game can feel at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun. I am glad I didnt let many of the critical reviews sway me. Reviews are really less useful these days because reviewers can get so super "nit-picky". I just want to play a "fun" game. This is one of the flight game formulas I have had fun with in the past. and it delivers. It IS fun, lots of dogfights lots of missions, free to do side mission in any order I want. easy to learn and although i feel the story is a bit overwhelming i actually really do sympathize with the protagonist. There are a few wants I have been left with but I only have 5 hours in and I am having fun. That's what I wanted. I got it on sale like 30% off I think? I am super stoked about  that too! looking for a fun flight sim that has the easiest flight mechanics and engaging sci fi story? want some fun dogfights? wanna strafe bigger capitol ships and destroy subsystems? your going to like this game. I think the devs here really made something fun that they should be proud of. that my two cents. enjoy

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really expect anything from this game. Bit the bullet and bought it after trying the (free) demo and liking combat.Oh, boy, is this a REALLY good one! It's basically 6-DOF shooter (definitely not a sim) in space with a few RPG elements.So far, enjoying pretty much everything about.Combat is awesome, there's plenty of (side-)quests, interesting story, good voice acting, very nice visuals, solid performance and no bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: ChorusPro:-Beautiful graphics and some stunning vistas.-Good, glooming atmosphere and "underdog" story line with a silver lining. Beautiful dynamic in between the two protagonists.The story manages to go without any deus ex machina moments (i'm looking at you, Mass Effect 3). The factions you allie yourself with, actually play a role.-A lot of additional lore bits and continuous NPC stories to find through all the side quests. Some have a good amount of charme to them.-Everything is fully voice acted. And the voice work is pretty solid, for the most part.-Very good sound design. Everything sounds really meaty and visceral. You can really feel the mean high-tech acceleration of your advanced engine, the sheer destructive power of your weapons and the explosions of your poor enemies as a result.-Frenetic yet tactical, skill-based gameplay.(3 different weapon types for different jobs and situations you have to switch through at the right moment;Different enemy types coming with different priorities;You can use tactical positioning and cover to your advantage; big ships you have to fight by destroying their sub-systems in order to find and destroy their reactor core inside of them etc.)And then there are "rites", Naras special supernatural abilities by "tabbing" into the void dimension. These include a 6th sense to see visions from the past, the life force of living beings, important mission objectives she's concentrating on etc., a teleport bringing you to a targets six, a lighting blast shredding shields and incapacitating and more.-Adequate upgrade progression.By spending earned credits on (or finding/earning through exploration and side quests) shield upgrades, additional hull armor, weapons (you always have machine guns, lasers and rockets and can chose and switch out each) or subsystems (3 slots) for different effects (increased damage types, lower cooldown on repair-bots, less costs on special abilities etc.).Some items have additional "set" effects on them, leading to interesting build-possibilities and an accentuation of playstyles. The sets also make sure to dampen potential power creep, by its "sidegrade" nature in an otherwise linear upgrade progression.Oh and there is passive leveling aswell. The more you do or use stuff, the better you become with them.-Tight control scheme. Played through the whole game with my Razer Wolverine V2 and enjoyed how it felt. I just barely tested out M+K at the beginning and it felt good aswell.Neutral:-Apart from the AWESOME theme, the orchestral soundtrack is often not very catchy, but still good enough to support what's happening.-Using a characters inner monologue. I'm almost sure this is inspiried by Dune. You can hear Naras true thoughts being mediated to the player by whispered voice acting. I don't have a problem with it, but it is a bold choice in a narration sense and i have  read a lot of people disliking it.Contra:-The indie nature of the game sometimes shines through, with some odd facial animations.-Some side missions can feel a little generic.-The game only comes with english voice acting. And there is a looooot of dialogue. Especially during combat. (Not a problem for me personally, however: People who aren't good at actustical comprehension when it comes to english could have problems to follow all the dialogues. Reading subtititles during combat could be really hard to do.)-No deep ship costumization in an optical sense. You fly Forsaken and he always looks the same, that's it. The only thing changing are the weapons and their models.---Conclusion:Chorus is a gem. I have enjoyed my time with it wholeheartedly. It's a tight, story driven experience with awesome arcade-like space action dogfights. What more could anyone ask for? To be honest, the story comes with some highly esotherical and philosophical concepts and therefore demands the players full attention to be understood. Everything gets explained, but by a lot of small puzzle pieces. Adding them together to get the full picture is in the players hands. It's a shame there was almost no marketing for this awesome game. I've found it by sheer luck and i'm glad i did. Best 15€ i've spent in a long time.Big recommendation.
