_childDocuments_.review: Was really looking forward to this, huge fan of the original and was looking forward to playing a modern take.  Firstly the graphics are completely different, this was probably the most notable thing about the original so it seems like a strange choice.  I actually think its looks quite good but still would of preferred the original design.  However there are some major issues with this.  The glitches...second level I fell through a solid floor to my death.  Dead enemies floating upside down with their legs in the air.  I've currently got to a point where for some reason the next part of the level just won't trigger, this has happened a couple of times in different level.  Some of the animations are very funny, every downed enemy seems to die the same way in this slightly delayed staggered way, doesn't matter how they've been killed, whacked in the head with a chair, headshot, body shot, the same strange animation.  The AI is brilliant for all the wrong reasons.  Sniping people from distance stood with their mate looking directly at them...they go down, their mate either does nothing or moves directly to where they are and looks down and does nothing allowing you to then make further shots! Sometimes whole groups of enemies will do this and it ends up becoming really quite funny.The sound is all over the place especially with voices, you'll keep hearing the same bit of dialogue over and over(usually from the previous cutscene) and its loud like the character is right next to you.  But then you'll be in a room where a character is talking right next to you and you can't hear it all.  It does have the original voice cast though, including David Duchovny's lethargic delivery plus all the enemies shouting "Alert" every 2 minutes so thats nice for those looking for some nostalgia.Then theres the multiplayer which just seems pointless, no bots so from what I can tell all you have is local splitscreen which seems a weird choice in this day and age for a PC game.  Plus there appears to be deathmatch and team deathmatch which is less than what was in the original.  Really disappointing all in all.  I'm sure the developers could turn it around with post release patches but it leaves a slightly sour taste in your mouth the way it currently it is and it is very hard to recommend in the state its currently in.  Whats even weirder is that I think this game got delayed a year, I'd have loved to have seen the state of it when it was originally planned to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original a lot, to the point where i can remember about 80% of the dialogue word for word, and other game play mechanics like spawns of enemies / items. So when i saw that there was a remake of my childhood game i was so happy that i couldn't shut up about it, and wanted to play it badly. Now that i have, i wished i didn't, so many things wrong with this game that a bug fix wouldn't help it.    >Core Mechanics:- ADS: It breaks the AI and how the game works, being able to snipe enemies from afar removes the challenge of trying to work around certain weapon arch-types. You can sit back with any ranged weapon like a pistol (.44 mainly) and head shot everyone- Sprint: The AI's aim was bad enough already, so having the player move faster in a game in which the arenas where meant to be played at a slower pace (slower movement speed to allow enemies to hit their shots) breaks the flow of the combat. You can run around everyone in game and get an easy headshot and take barley any damage, also there is a delay when activating sprint and being able to shoot / reload, so that's fun.                                                                                                                                - Weapon Wheel: Being able to hold only one weapon per weapon arch-type kills the fun of having variety with your engagements, having to decide whether not to switch out one weapon for another takes away player freedom.- Cut Scenes are drawn out for no reason but to add that little 'detail' before playing again, it's nice, but having a 15 second ingame cutscene be a 30 second scene because of details gets old fast.                                         >Other Things I Noticed (A short TL:DR One the small things that was off)- Animations looks scuffed; from enemies dying, to use of items, melee items, picking up bodies, etc. It tries either to be too realistic or too fancy with it's animations, which doesn't work well with the arcadey game play.- Sound effects for weapons, reloads, and items are completely gone and replaced with generic audio files found online. The heavy impacts from weapons is gone, reloading is boring, and sometimes it just outright won't work                                                 - The looks of it is completely different from the original, it went from Cel-shaded artstyle with comic strips thrown in there to a dull rounded look. Characters looks like something you would find on Fortnite, and weapons was replaced with a more 'modern' look that makes it looks smaller.- Certain weapons feels weaker in comparison to the original game, probably due to the fact that ADS exists and balancing it would take too long- Ingame events breaking / starting without me being near the trigger causing the AI to stand around doing nothing until i'm directly in their face- Music just doesn't work when it's suppose to or plays after it's intended trigger- XIII and Hard difficulty is a joke, both the AI's terrible aim and aiming from a distance makes every engagement a cake walk. Only died once in the beginning of the game because of learning the controls fully, other than that, flawless playthroughs  - And many more bugs and glitches that it's laughable I love XIII from the first time i played it with my father till now, I even got my friends to play the original and they are enjoying the game. But this newer edition makes me both tilted and confused by it's changes and bugs that I can't even anymore. I would not recommend this version of this game, play the original, and have some fun.    - Also just found out that after downloading this game, my other copies of the 2003 version is breaking or just not working correctly so thanks for that too

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare to see such backlash towards a game- but in this case, it's absolutely warranted.I didn't expect much because I obtained it in a bundle and wanted to play it out of nostalgia. Product. I wouldn't be as critical as others regarding the graphics, but the gameplay, oh my. Normal difficulty is much easier than in the original and the upper difficulty doesn't make the AI smarter, which the big problem. Ennemies like to reload out in the open, fire at non-destructible pieces of the environment or line up in your scope like lemmings. Even playing without too much effort or focus, I mowed them down easily.Bosses are the most pitiful specimens of the bunch : each of them is a non-challenge, charging you mindlessly, getting stuck in nothing, getting dazed too easily. The game itself is quite playable but the few additions - like the waypoints - are plainly not needed.I didn't double check by replaying the original, but I'm almost positive they've also skipped several sections, in the levels or narratively-wise, some transitions between levels are more than abrupt.The barebone multiplayer mode is, of course, completely dead. Even with the lowered price, wether you are a veteran or new to XII, don't bother. Play the original instead.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, Unity 3D.Who thought this was going to on the Unity 3D engine? Anyone? Nope. Why is it on the Unity 3D engine? Who knows. Whoever made that decision is the reason why this game has such horrific reviews. The animations, Frame Rates and over all clunky feeling the ENTIRE game has is most likely due to the engine being Unity 3D. Watch as you get a solid maybe 70 frames, then your sensitivity will skyrocket as your FPS dips to like 20 and it picks it back up. I ran this game in 1440p, on the lowest settings with a 2080TI and the entire time the game is open your GPU will be hard stuck at 99% usage the entire time this game is open.  Thats the Unity 3D engine for ya.Second stop on this ride is the Animations. A disaster in itself. NONE of the animations I saw ran smoothly/correctly. Many times your gun (Especially the magnum) will clip back to the last frame of the shooting animation, so it just jitters back and forth sometimes. The enemy movement is choppy, and whenever you kill anyone they all to the SAME EXACT death animation every single time. Think of a T pose, but with them holding a finger pistol and then just toppling over. On every single enemy. Completely ruins the immersion every time you kill someone. In a nutshell this is how animations are -  : 3 minutes of just WTF. Basically in the entire gameGraphical wise - I didn't see many issues. It looked good when standing still, hence why the screenshots make the game look amazing on the store page. AI in this game is also just a mess. I played on the second to last hardest difficulty. So basically hard, and in-between trying to aim correctly with the  and messed up animation you can basically just click once on their head and their dead. I barely ever even checked my health unless I was getting sniped, without the snipers and bazookas the damage input to you is next to nothing.I played up until the mission where you go into the tent to bug the guys office. No matter what I did, I always failed the mission as soon as I planted the bug. I hid bodies, did everything but as soon as the guy spawns in it was game over. After 2 tries at that, I gave up and started writing the review. In a nutshell, I do not see many of these issues getting fixed with the current engine and I do not ever see this game going above "Mixed" reviews on steam. Why they thought this was ready to roll out as a completed game is beyond me and is now on my list for THE worst remake I have ever played. For a full playthrough of what I painstakingly went through, you can watch the stream and click anywhere in the video to see this game in its full, depressing glory. By about minute 10 I realized I was in for a treat, and now cannot refund due to steams 2 hours rule. My playthrough - Some dumb lookin deer that just stood there and did nothing, but I remember it being in the original with animations. Just a derp deer -

_childDocuments_.review: Man... where do i start...Just a premise : The game itself currently is not even half bad. The shooting feeling has been improved a lot and there are a couple mechanics that make the game feel more like a compact title that is flowing constantly.But.... yes, BUT... This game is a good 6/10The gameplay itself is almost identical to the original, the maps look really similar to the original, with some obvious reworks of the big ones (Canyon is one of them, it's more compact and there are less empty pointless spaces). Overall the game flows flawlessly, too flawlessly.... There are a lot of mechanics that have been introduced pretty much from the beginning of the game; and this makes it WAY easier than the original.Speaking of difficulty.... Well, there is none.... The original forced you to think twice before acting, you had to sneak more and rethink some strategies.... and this, well... it feels like a linear run and gun. The AI is utterly useless and easily cheesable, especially the bosses. From all the bosses i fought, only the one in the submarine was somehow responsive to reason. The Doctor and Soldier were absolutely clueless. They just stood aimlessly and glitched out giving the opportunity for the player to just fill them with bullets. Speaking of filling with bullets, you can pretty much get trought an entire mission and not die. Most of the time the enemy can be one shot, maybe three shot with the M16, there is no difficult situation, just gun everyone down. The new mechanic of aiming down sights is a great improvement to the shooting, but it makes the game absolutely easy to rush trought. You can shoot enemies down from miles away and they will be absolutely clueless of what's going on. A clear example of this the massive empty space just before getting into the submarine; you can pretty much gun down the entire area from up above. Other than that, the game has been gotten rid of the annoying bits, that gave it a bit of puzzle like approach, probably this decision has been made for the new gen of players that are not famous for patience and thinking.The recreation itself is pretty accurate, there are some bits and bobs that are missing that are minor, but some of them are absolutely immersion breaking. An example of this is the cameras in the mission to free your prisoner. There is a bit where in the original you can see an enemy on camera, prompting one of the main characters to joke about it; they left the text but there is no camera to give more immersion. This goes also for the first bit of that mission, where you cannot look into the monitor to see approaching guards.Overral it's a meh remaster and definetly not worth the OG price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend this, however, there are some caveats. I have played the classic version before too. I will say that the graphics here are an obvious upgrade. The low polygon counts in the original make the older version of the game look incredibly dated. This, in comparison, looks much more modern. However, as others have noted, the "comic book" art-style and aspects are quite toned down in the remake. I honestly wouldn't have known that it was trying to even have a comic book aesthetic in the remake if it weren't for the borders appearing sometimes and the speech bubbles. The game is cell shaded, yes, but not in a way that screams comic book to me, per se. The original definitely had a comic book vibe woven throughout the game, whereas here, it feels more like an afterthought. Secondly, I can't put my finger on it, but this game gave me the worst eye fatigue with its color palettes. Environments often feel really bright, busy, and washed out. I don't really get eye strain from playing games, however, looking at these environments started taking a toll one hour into playing. This is something that the original classic version didn't do to me, so, I think that a better balance of highlights / shadows / midtones should have been used here. That being said, it was a good game. I only encountered a few glitches, which is apparently a far cry from how glitchy it was upon release. Once, I completely clipped through the floor I was standing on, and fell through it. Secondly, I got stuck in the walls of the submarine. Thirdly, my game did crash randomly twice. And lastly, I did see one NPC stuck between the floor boards, Jumanji style, on the yacht. I'm recommending the game because it does quite a lot better than the original, however, it still trades blows with the original. This will definitely feel more modern on newer PCs. I didn't play the original back when it first released. I was a bit late to discovering XIII, so, I didn't see the classic through the same nostalgia glasses that many others did. If the slight bit of residual glitchiness got patched, and if they perhaps adjusted the color scheme to be better, this would be an easy recommend. However, as it stands, this is a lukewarm recommend from me. I feel as though the art style is Borderlands-esque, yet misses the mark. It's still a slightly glitchy and janky game, however, it is undeniable that they modernized the remake and made it far more palatable for players who are allergic to outdated graphics. _childDocuments_.review: XIII is a remake of the eponymous 2003 shooter by Ubisoft, developed by PlayMagic and published by Microids in 2020. It is a remake no one asked for, and a few played. Those who did play the game reported numerous bugs and extremely poor performance on launch day. Note that I purchased the game some two years after release when many bugs had been patched. I was someone who really enjoyed the original game, having played through the entire thing in 2022 and then immediately bought and downloaded the remake. At first, I liked the remake, but with the first NPC death animation, I started realizing how mediocre the entire thing is. Where the original oozes with style, charisma, and fun, the remake manages to do the same worse. The cutscenes look bland, the characters are uninteresting, and the music and ambient sounds tend to either disappear or warp like a broken tape recorder. I didn't experience any game-breaking bugs on my playthrough, but I saw a bunch of characters T-posing or making incredible John Carpenter The Thing-like poses, which is both horrifying and funny. I won't get into the game's story or characters, as that is better experienced in the original game, but I will say that 2020's XIII may not be as bad as the reviews make it seem. In its present state, the game is playable from start to finish and performs much better and more steadily. I think the best way to play XIII is the original, but if you ever wish to beat the game or revisit some of the old levels, try the remake, as it can be fun when it works. There is no excuse to release games in a state like XIII was on launch day, but giving credit where it's due, PlayMagic fixed the game as they promised to, and for that, the remake deserves to exist, even though it will never replace the original.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Let's get this out of the way first, I wasn't there to experience this remake when it was first released. I don't condone developers releasing broken and unfinished games, but it is what it is. With that being said, in this game's current state, it's a significant improvement over the original from 2003. I'm not kidding when I say the addition of aiming down sights and a revamped checkpoint system alone, are enough for me to recommend this remake over the original from 2003, even if it's your first time playing XIII. The original from 2003 may have better comic-book and cutscene presentation, but that's not enough for me to recommend playing that over this, if it means putting up with shoddy shooting mechanics and scarce checkpoints.+ Great soundtrack.+ Good replay value.+ Good weapon variety.+ Bosses have less health.+ Weapons have good impact.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.+ Vastly improved checkpoint system.+ New sprint mechanic improves mobility.+ Switching weapons is much faster. Which is needed for this kind of game.+ New aiming down sights mechanic vastly improves the shooting accuracy.+ Escort objectives are no longer an issue as the escort NPCs are now invincible.- Every level transition removes most of your inventory items.- Cutscenes are unchanged from the 2020 version. The one before the sanctuary level is outright missing.- Stealth sections with instant failure. To be fair, this game wouldn't be a remake if these sections were removed outright.

_childDocuments_.review: I confess. I preordered this game. They managed to lure me in with the digital copy of the Original as a pre-order bonus and i was like "The original was pretty cool, so how can this new version possibly be bad, right?" Oh Jeezuz, what was I thinking?It's superhard to figure out where to even start with a review of this game. The original had its problems, like the at times pretty confusing level design and horribly unrefined stealth mechanics, but instead of improving on those things, the "Remaster" just adds a sh*t-ton of even worse stuff. After the horrifying reviews this thing got immediately after its release, I waited close to one and a half years before actually playing it, hoping that some of the biggest problems might get patched away with given time. And to be fair, as far as I can tell, the game is in a somewhat better state now than in late 2020 / early 2021. I didn't encounter any of the major grafics glitches that I saw in some videos shortly after release, and in addition it seems that they listened to at least some of the backlash and made some small improvements like adding an FOV slider, ditching the two-weapons-limit, getting rid of the roughest bugs and finally heaving the game into an at least somewhat playable and stable state (even though I still experienced occasional stuttering despite the grafics being mediocre and underwhelming at absolute best).But to be honest, that is not saying much. The visuals went from the charming and "pure" cell-shade look of the original to a somewhat semi-realistic appearance. They are still cell-shade (sort of...), but the distinct visual style of the original has been toned down significantly, making the game look average and boring at absolute best. And even though I didn't notice any major grafics bugs, that doesn't mean that there weren't any bugs at all, like bodies of dead enemies suddenly floating in mid-air and stuff like that. Not game-breaking, but just embarassing. Speaking of embarassing: The extremely crappy mouse aiming controls, stiff and lifeless animations, samey character models and downright inept and unresponsive AI belong in that category as well. A prime example of how generally and utterly bad this thing is are the laughably bad first-person-animations when you lockpick a door: You aim at the door and your character just starts aimlessly wiggling his lockpicks through the air, even when you are not even close to the door knob. At other times the enemies just keep standing there and not reacting to your presence at all, their backs turned to you and not moving a single muscle while patiently waiting for you to shoot them from behind. It's a mess.But wait, the game can do even worse: The audio is close to completely broken. Soundeffects would constantly start to stutter, loop endlessly or cut out entirely and only a complete game restart could fix this. The nicest thing you could say about the sound is that the voice-acting is lackluster, but not a total trainwreck at least. Gameplaywise the worst thing are still the nearly unbearable stealth sections, that make about a quarter of the game. Here, the original had significant potential for improvement, but the Remaster doesn't even bother and still has no indicators for how visible or audible you are and in combination with the broken AI, inconsistent damage of the stealth knockouts (some guys require just one hit, others need two for whatever inexplicable reason) and generally glitchy gameplay, the stealth sections become even worse than in the original: At best they are tedious trial and error, but in many cases passing those parts is just a matter of pure luck. Even when you don't have to deal with the infuriating stealth mechanics, the game often manages to p*ss you off with its broken design. For example, sometimes the game updates or changes your mission objectives without properly telling you this, unless you randomly open your inventory and notice the changed objectives by accident. This lead to more than one annoying and unecessary mission failures during my playthrough. To no surprise, the story is unchanged from the original as well. In harsh contrast to the comic book visuals, the narrative takes itself way too serious, even though some situations depicted in the game are generally stupid. Not in a "Michael-Bay-tongue-in-cheek-unbelievably-over-the-top"-way, but in a "This-is-just-generally-too-stupid-as-in-very-unintelligent"-way. In the end, the story is still pretty short (not even 6 hours), but not sweet.So, are there any positives? The guns are okay I guess, and the kind-of-cell-shade artstyle still looks decently cool, sort of.What it all comes down to is that if this game wouldn't have its myriads of bugs, glitches and technical f*ck-ups, it could easily be a 4 or 5 out of 8, since it's basically the exact same game as the original, and the original is a good and somewhat unique first-person-shooter. During the first handful of missions I got the impression that the 2020 version of XIII wouldn't be as bad as i expected, but as it went on, it got increasingly buggy and annoying. When the game was not freaking out, i had a decent amount of fun at times, but fact is that there are literally hundreds of first-person-shooters, including the original XIII, that are far superior in every possible way. The XIII Remaster on the other hand is one of those games that make you asking yourself what you are doing with your precious spare time and why you are wasting it with playing total garbage like this (even if it is just a handful of hours). The XIII Remaster is shockingly bad. It is even worse than notoriously bad games like Aliens Colonial Marines. Yes, you read that right: It is worse than Aliens Colonial Marines (say that out loud). In fact, as far as I can remember, it is one of the worst first-person-shooters i have played in my entire life. FPS fans should definitely check out the original, but stay the hell away from this miserable travesty of an action game, that still has the incomprehensible audacity to sell for a whoopin' FOOOOOOOORTY EUROS (!!!). It's trash, it's garbage, it's sh*t, it's a rip-off, it's barely worth a couple of cents._________________________________________________________________________________XIII (2020 Remaster)Genre: First-Person-ShooterRelease: Q4 2020( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. Don't waste any money on this.(X) 1/8 Bad. Seriously flawed with barely any redeeming qualities. Worth a couple of Cents at best, if at all.( ) 2/8 Sub-par. _childDocuments_.review: Such negative ratings are not justified. It ain't half bad. But truthfully, it ain't half good either.If you loved the initial game, you'll be happy to see that this is purely a remaster. I could navigate through all levels with my eyes closed. Graphics is better than the original and they added some detail. If you want to replay XIII, but want it to feel somehow different, go for it. The tab-overview of your weapons and objective is also nice.Now the negatives. 17 years later than the original - yet the mechanics fall short. It's weird. Jumping while running isn't possible and I had to restart checkpoints many times because I couldn't make the long jumps and fell into the void. This isn't difficulty, it's just bad. Movements generally feel sluggish. The hook-gun sometimes won't coil and you cannot use weapons while hanging, so you're just hanging there like a fly in a spiders' web. Medikit isn't used immediately, and takes some seconds to heal you (which is fine, I guess. Just different from the original). Enemies spawn and move worse than in the original. They often run at you with all their heads aligned and just can't wait to die at the sight of any bullet that vaguely flies in their direction, even on harder settings. Hit boxes are ridiculously large and health is low. Already the original game had comfortably large hit boxes, but they still were acceptably large. Granted, the old game wasn't very aim-heavy either but it had the fast-paced Unreal Engine. The new one just isn't as much a dynamic shooter.My verdict. Buy, only when on sale. If you could only play one, I would actually recommend the old one, it's the better game. The only reason I played the new one is because I wanted to replay XIII but change it up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: What is XIII? A stylish and compelling FPS. While it doesn't exactly make any enourmous improvements to the genre, the story element is strong and the comic - style gameplay is truly enjoyable, even today! Multiplayer is another string to this games bow but hardly cutted. Overall this is a slick, enjoyable game so far (ONLY STORY WISE) - well worth owning and the multiplayer will hold your interest for ages.You are the victim of a conspiracy! Find your way out and uncover the mysterys behind the assassination of the President of the United States, William Sheridan. His death is a nod similar to real-life former President John F. Kennedy who was killed by a sniper bullet to the head in Dallas in 1963.This is a stylish and fun game that sadly did not get the recognition it deserved. Too many reviews gave it a thumbs down back in the days because it "wasn't as good as Halo."... Well, it wasn't trying to be Halo. XIII has a very well written and compelling story that will keep you interested and guessing throughout the whole playthrough until the cliffhanger ending. The music is superb, the voice acting is good, the cell-shaded graphics are very cool, and it is a very fun game to play (after that many patches on the remake). Some folks may not like that you can't save anywhere and that it builds up on "checkpoints" which are not that "well placed" sometimes, especially once you hit 6 enemies in a row and placed a checkpoint. Once you die, you respawn on the checkpoint with six enemies right in front of you, but I highly recommend it. After all the games I've played so far, this is still one I think of fondly and plan to play again. Plus there are grappling hooks!The Downside: It also has some bugs (Not gamebreaking ones) in the campaign. For example the german subtitles include some errors and could've been handled better. Dead enemies do not give you armor, despite them wearing some after death unlike in the original where you could pick up a certain amount of left-over armor from the dead body and I do not get why this feature didn't make it into the final game.The last level also includes cameras that could see you in the original, but can be completely ignored in the remake. Another thing completely missing from the original.The good: There are also collectables (golden statues and documents) to find all around the levels and it gives you extra content to find and stuff to read. It overall looks pretty good. Just do us all a favor:

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Lord... Oh good Lord what in the world has happened here?You know, I seldom try to be a contrarian. I pre-purchased XIII 2020 right before it released, but had other things to do, so I let it sit for a day. Then I come back, really looking forward to play, and I see a "Mostly Negative Reviews" score, now dropped even further to "Very Negative". And I thought, surely, this must be partly because of a couple crashes and the new look. Yeah, it kinda looks like a generic Fortnite-esque cartoon art style (which I absolutely despise, I might add) instead of that superbly stylized comic art, but I can deal with both that and the occasional technical hiccup. As long as the gameplay and presentation is fine.But lo and behold, both of which are not. It absolutely is not fine, in all the major aspects actually. So to start, and this has been mentioned by another user before, the intro is pathetic. An FBI agent walks into a presentation room and literally watches the original 2003 comic-book intro sequence. In all its low-resolution goodness. This looked amazing 15 years ago, when I was 11 years old and played the demo on my crappy 2005 laptop. Not so much nowadays. Especially not when it's stretched across a virtual canvas within the game itself. And especially, especially not when the art styles don't bloody match anymore!I guess they thought this was cute fan-service, I personally find it horrifically lazy and insulting. They probably wanted to copy/paste the intro but then realized themselves that this would've looked *too* crappy. What we got now isn't any better though... And it doesn't really make sense for an FBI agent to watch what is essentially a conspiracy plot setup, does it?Oh man... Now, that soured things for me. However, eh, I thought, as long as that sweet, sweet gameplay is fine with the in-game presentation to match, I can swiftly forget this massive blunder. How wrong I was...So, the entire first level, beginning where XIII awakes at the beach and is found by a lovely lifeguard with her eyecatching attire, is arguably one of the most iconic beginnings in video game history. To me, at least. And the first thing I see in the remake here is XIII stretching his fingers, cracking his knuckles, in a "let's do this!" manner, as he groggily gets to his feet, close to death still. I suspect he will do this later on (it is in fact his idle animation), and they forgot to remove or misplaced the animation here. This is followed by the camera glitching out, and the eye-tracking on the lifeguard breaking, so that her eyes turn inside her own ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ skull.I'm sorry, guys, at this point you already lost me. When the intro of your game is so messed up, I am fast running out of things to defend it with. But it gets worse. So, after a couple more animation glitches, XIII passes out again and awakes inside the lifeguard cabin. Again, an extremely iconic scene, as the lifeguard wants to get him to a hospital, but is startled by the sound of a cocking gun outside, approaches the door to investigate, moments before she gets perforated by a couple AK-47 bursts. Following that, the entire room is filled with lead, as the unknown assailant reloads and sprays bullets along the walls in an effort to shred the entire cabin. Assassination style, cause you know, that is what this is. And the only reason XIII survives is because he lays on a bed behind cover.I'm not describing the scene in this game though. That was the 2003 original.And in the 2003 original, this instantly got the player moving. Unarmed, you jump up and a comic panel indicated to you that the dead lifeguard had a throwing knife on her. You pick that up, throw it at the guy at the door, to have several comic panels in slow motion show to you the brutal outcome of that hit. You are instantly aware that this game is going to be good. And here we are, in 2020, and they changed the scene to where it literally doesn't make sense anymore. The attacker fires TWO BULLETS at poor Janet (the lifeguard), and then stops. This alone, if you have the original game in the back of your mind, kills the entire point of this scene. Apparently, the assassins were just out for her. Ok then...Better yet, instinctively, I looked for the throwing knives on her corpse and in the adjacent room, to find that they appear to have been taken out of the level. You will find your pistol and a bottle to throw, that's it.So you have to confront your first enemy going out of the back door, immediately realizing that combat is completely broken too. Firstly, a headshot makes enemies literally freeze-pose for a whole second, before they flop over. No cool blood fountains accompanied by the comic panels detailling the shot. Satisfying combat? Nope. No more.Shortly after, you will realize that there is a tiny delay when firing. And aiming down sights will reduce your mouse sensitivity to the point where an entire sweep across your mousepad results in a 45° turn at most. And the weapon sounds suck balls. I could forgive the pistol, not the AK-47 that had a beefy bang to it back in 2003.And all of this is accompanied by an AI that slowly runs at you or turns away at an angle, getting stuck there for several seconds. They pose absolutely no threat unless you actively ignore multiple of them and let them shoot you. I played this on the hardest difficulty and literally ran-and-gunned through the level. That's not quite how I remembered the original game, either...Other points of note are horrendous sound direction (as in, the mixing of sounds overall. The actual VA and many sounds are directly from the orginal), bad menu navigation (you cannot click on the "Apply" or "Back" buttons for instance), bad animations and boring art direction.So yeah, I'll put it bluntly: This game sucks. It's a remake that should have been a remaster, upscaled with modern resolutions support, at most. It's one of the first games in a long, long, long time that I have played this little and immediately uninstalled and refunded. Like I said, if your first level sucks THIS bad, there is absolutely zero inclination for me to believe that it gets any better later on.I suppose a lot of this could be fixed, still. Controls and animation glitches can be fixed. Sounds can be improved.But the overall direction of a game cannot. The most memorable moments from the original have evidently been altered too much for that. Even if this game ran perfectly and the combat was great, it would be a generic cartoon shooter now. And the only thing that would set it apart is the story, which is of course entirely from the original. So, not enough.I really do not say this often, usually my most negative review will conclude with either "hold off until it's fixed" or "really put deep thoughts into if this is worth your money". For XIII 2020, I will conclude with: Do not buy this game. Especially not if you are a fan of the original and / or have played that recently.[Update]: So, I've followed a stream now to see how this game progresses later on. And it absolutely confirms my negative thoughts on it. Unfortunately, because I really, really would have loved for this game to be awesome. But even later on, it just doesn't stop to be an embarrassment.Example? Well, there's a scene where XIII and his comrade, Jones, escape using a VTOL. In the original game, this VTOL is a Harrier Jump-Jet. In the remake, it is an F4 Phantom... a plane which does not have any vertical take-off capabilities. And yet they lift off vertically.Like, it's just baffling to me. Switching models around is one thing, but it's another to switch them around to where they do not make any sense in the context anymore. And it just shows the lack of love on display here...I guess, after several months of patches and fixes, and IF you can turn your brain off, this game might be worth half its current price.Other than that, I remain by my above criticism even more strongly.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when I was 9 or 10 and I played the original for the first time, I instantly fell in love with it and have been a huge fan ever since. The art style like it was a comic book, the three panels at the top of the screen when you hit a head-shot with the iconic "DUN-DUN-DUN" is something I remember very fondly. When I found out about this remake a year or so ago, I was very very excited, and even preordered months ago and was ranting and raving to my girlfriend and friends about how I remember the good old days. The iconic three panel head-shot thing is still there, but the sound effects are not. There are typos in the subtitles as well as the loading screen "hints and tips" for example when you meet Major Jones on the rooftops for the first time, she mentions "general Carrington" and in one loading screen I noticed I can "zoom in with the sniper riffle for better acuracy"The gunshots aren't impactful and it sounds like you're being shot at with Nerf guns instead of an AK or an SVD. The AI is weird because I can head-shot a guard and all his friends will come inspect the body and I will finish stealth missions barely moving. The ragdoll is bizarre but it always got a laugh out of me when it happened. There are cutscenes missing as well, especially in the later levels for whatever reason. I spent one whole mission listening to very loud repetitive machine gun SFX despite restarting the game completely and everything else available to me to no avail, so that was very fun.One thing I will give credit for with this game is the updated graphics and character design, but I believe that's all I can say that's good about it. The rest of the game needs serious work, and I can only pray this game has No Mans Sky syndrome where the devs turn it into what was promised, hopefully with more.

_childDocuments_.review: Mr. Rowland? It's been such a long tiiimmeeIf you played the original I am sure you will love this (if you buy it on sale)! I played the original as a kid and it was one of my most memorable games so I always hoped for a remaster or a sequel. I waited playing this game because of all the bad reviews and I am glad I waited because lot's of bugs have been fixed and one of the more recent updates (09-2022) greatly improved the comic style graphics as they were really lacking before this. Also props to the developers as the most recent update was in January of 2023 so it seems like they want the game to be good.Pros- Original audio so voice acting is decent and soundtrack is amazing, mixing seems a bit off though, especially for XIII himself- Modernized controls with ADS and sprinting. I've seen people criticize this but as a fan of FPS games and somebody who likes to explore every nook and cranny they were a very welcome feature!- FOV slider and decent 21:9 support- Maps are greatly modernized with a bit more detail without straying too far from the originalCons- ALERT!!- Remade cutscenes are not great and are still in the old Fortnite looking style before the 09-2022 update- Some cutscenes are missing making a couple mission transitions weird- AI can be a bit dumb like a lot of modern games - I noticed a few bugs but nothing game breaking- Multiplayer is dead (obviously)I recommend it on sale but probably only if you enjoyed the original. For me it was a great nostalgia trip that I finished in two or three sittings.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating the review now that the big update released:The Positives:+There's Ultrawide support+FOV slider is there (though It should let me go a bit wider, one Issue I will address below)+Music sounds loud (has a few issues I will address below)+Shooting feels good with all weapons, I don't like that I have to ADS to be more accurate when in the first game it was all based around hipfire (just my rose tinted glasses mindset)+Graphics are much improved and have more of the old cartoon cellshade but modern look.The Negatives:-FOV slider range should extend a bit more, but the biggest issue is that when you sprint, the camera zooms in, which is odd, as if the effect was built with low FOV console in mind. Please fix this.-Music sounds great and all, but certain areas in the game (like at the bank) the music doesn't trigger when it should.For example, when you open the safe at the bank and you get a flash back, when you come back from the flashback, it's all quiet until the bomb goes off. The song has to start as soon as you come back from the flash back. The tense melody that plays before the song starts was there to increase the tension from the bomb about to go off. -The AI needs more work: the AI is improved over the original release for sure, they are more accurate so your health tends to go down more often, but they still mindlessly run towards you, making them easy kills. I suggest increasing their accuracy more and make them be a tad smarter by making them hide behind cover, or try to run away to their buddies to gang up on you as a group. I didn't try the Online Multiplayer, that's why I left it out.Overall it's a lot better, but still needs a bit more refine to be good. I really hope the new team who is working on this keeps improving the overall game a bit more. 2 to 3 more patches and the game is good.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review:It's been 3 updates now since release (2 more than i expected) and the game became very slightly better.To make it short: it is still god aweful. i won't elaborate on it now and leave my original review down below for details since almost nothing changed.First-Person animations have improved. By that I mean they look less glitchy or as they were intended but still like the wrong guy was tasked with it.Enemies are noticably less stupid.Dead bodies almost never flop around at the price of making the act of carrying bodies even more of a chore.Cutscenes still suck, even if the patch notes claim they have improved (I guess they did slighty), gunplay still sucks and on a technical level this is still on par with some 2010 slenderman fan game. It reeeaaally likes to stutter when loading something new, voicelines still cut off, even if much much less frequently and somehow loading times have increased.So, better keep your (probably not so) hard earned money instead of buying this.If the devs are reading this, you might aswell contact me directly, seriously, it really seems like you guys don't understand what makes a game fun or good.Original review:Some comparisons for context:how excited i was about XIII getting a remake...too bad it sucks.what i personally liked about the original was the gunplay and the style of it and even though this is XIII with a new face they messed up both.you can sprint for some reason, but you need it because your walking speed is slower or atleast feels like it.the whole game feels slower and here's why:- the janky enemy AI flinches for a long time- the UI requires more input for proper weapon switchingthe result? boringly easy 1 on 1 confrontations or tag team scenarios.but that's just two things making the whole experience pretty bad.the guns are not comfortable to use.for example: when fanning the hammer with the revolver you use up all six shots, aiming is introduced and the guns are straight up useless when fired from the hip if the enemy is even at medium-close range, headshots are very powerful and almost required so you dont waste too much ammo so you need to slow down and take aim, you can't sprint out of crouching, even with auto-reload enabled if you switch to an empty gun you have to reload manually (may get patched, who knows), key items have to be picked up manually and so on and so on.so now you know how the guns have been messed up, lets get to the presentation.it's very bad.sure, the graphics are a huge step-up, but even though the original XIII had very few polygons to show, they were used very well, the faces had all the details, the hands looked like hands, NPC animations were stiff but got the job done, guns looked as well as they could and the maps were servicable.the remake kind of ♥♥♥♥♥ on all that.NPC models dont look that good (speaking about everything below the neck), your hands are flat with thin sausage fingers, NPC animations... oh boy... they are pretty janky (enemies walking around wiggle left and right as if they just learned walking), guns are real pretty and detailed but look just a tad too realistic. the maps however look really good, you can easily tell that a lot of work went into those but that's got to be my only positive thing to say about this game (except for maybe the more precise presentation of footsteps)."tell me about the cutscenes already!" you scream at the screen and i will.right after a word from our sponsors-no, seriously, the cutscenes have much less cuts, the people in them somehow look just as emotionless as in the original and there are much less frame in frame animations or blend-ins of comic panels.in gameplay it's mostly the same but i was severly dissapointed to see that the 3-frame headshots don't really show the headshot happening but just show the hit in 3 not so different zoom levels, probably a technical issue.all in all the game looks like it tries to be realistic with smooth shadows (which i don't like at all after the harsh 1-0 shadows in the original) and realistic textures but then it also slaps on thick black outlines here and there and still makes the "boom" and "tap" sounds look out of place.to wrap up my rant: if you're STILL curious about the remake (somehow), i recommend you maybe replay the original and watch a walkthrough of the remake. save your money.i swore to never write a second review on steam but if this saves somebody his money it was worth it so hopefully some people will read this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!oh hi donny!

Everything about this game is just a huge scam and I'll be sure to never buy any game from this studio ever again. I just played through the first mission and I'm now in the second part of the story where you bust out of the FBI building. By now I have played about 45 minutes and already found way too many things that bother me;- Guns feel weird and not powerful at all. In the original XIII, wielding a .44 Magnum felt powerful and it really packed a punch, same goes for the AK-47.- Steve's way of holding weapons is the weirdest thing I've ever seen in a game, why the hell would you put your thumb there when holding the .44?- Reloading a weapon feels weird and way too fast compared to original, and sounds don't sync up with the animation- Voice acting is really weird. I think they literally copied Ubisoft's work in voice acting but actually managed to make it awkward looking and also out of sync with character animations- Sounds cut out sometimes- "Ragdoll" animations are non-existing, instead they chose to go with a weirdly stuttery and low fps-like animation of dying for the enemies.- Multiplayer does not work and features only 2 game modes as opposed to 3 as far as I can remember, and only 3 maps in total.- Weapons now feature a iron sight option which is just weird. Why even add this if it wasn't in the original? Its not needed at all in a game like this and just feels weird.Then the good stuff;- It looks pretty good. I get why they went with better graphics. People that did not experience the original will want to see better lighting effects and textures and that they deliverd upon. People who played the original might be less pleased with this change.That's about it. All in all this game feels like a Garry's Mod mod that someone created for fun.. I don't get how the studio got away with this. I do not recommend this game in its current state. Microids will have to do a lot of work to make this a worthy remake of the original. Until they fix all this stuff, stick with the original, which is way cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: The original XIII is a memory from my childhood, a PS2 game I didn't own but would typically pick up and play through as much as I could once I arrived at a friend's home, before I inevitably left. I've never been a big fan of cel-shaded games, but XIII was different to me, utilising its spy/60s basis to present something much more comicbook-like and stylish. I always thought it was cool and enjoyed sneaking around, sending throwing knives into the back of unsuspecting guards' heads.So, I was of course excited to see XIII getting a remake, particularly given the qualities of recent remakes to deliver a faithful, yet refined and still nostalgic experience ("Destroy All Humans!" in particular for me). However, having progressed through the game's first four levels and experienced a myriad of bugs and faults in the little over an hour I played, it deeply saddens me to say that this experience is truly not one that achieves that which it aspires to.Here's a few of the main issues I faced, playing XIII (2020):- Music and audio in general has bad clipping issues, animations sometimes don't have any sounds at all or are delayed (when I first began, I was astonished to find my pistol didn't make any noise when I reloaded it).- Enemy AI is laughably inept, proceeding towards you in a straight line, more often than not. Consequently, I found the levels I played an absolute breeze on the game's hardest difficulty, despite it toting to me of how the AI was decidedly more competent than at more moderate difficulties.- Inconsistent collisions. In the third level, I found myself in a series of vents and on more than one occasion ended up clipping out of the vent and falling out of the world. In addition, I've found it repeatedly difficult to pick up basic items, sometimes unable to acquire weapons and armour even though I'm stood right on top of it.- Gunplay is awful. The sensitivity of the mouse can barely be altered meaningfully when ADS-ing without putting up your regular mouse sensitivity to sky high levels. While the enemies aren't too bad to deal with, it's hardly satisfying to barely have a fight, reload your gun that makes no sound and then struggle to aim at badly moving enemies, shooting without any sound coming out.- Cutscenes and character animations. They're bad, particularly when the audio fails or is so minimal you feel awkward watching other characters move around on-screen. It's especially daft when my character's POV turns left and right to inspect an area before the cutscene abruptly ends and three enemies have spawned in front of me out of thin air. Many moments like these butcher the atmosphere.The end result is a corruption of that nostalgia. Instead of building upon it, this remake tears it down. Despite all the resources available to cultivate a modern interpretation of that rich, atmospheric background, XIII (2020) fails completely. It is a shame.To put it bluntly, it's apparent to me that PlayMagic were not the developers to do this job right. While I would have loved to stay on with this and finish it, the more that magic of the past wears off, the more apparent the faults and the more I feel like this should have been a £15/€20 title than anything more than that. Subsequently, I'll be refunding this title.I may pick this back up in the future, as the achievements were a nice touch. But without considerable patches, there's no chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I have never reviewed a game ever but I feel so compelled to now considering this game was easily one of my all time favorites. I played this game and beat it all within the same day on the game's offered hardest difficulty. I'll start off with the pros because there are a couple, not many but certainly some to make not of.PROS:- The graphics are decent as well as the lighting and reflection. I actually do appreciate the amount of detail they went into building the scenery around you. In the Original XIII much of the scenery around you in the distance were merely blobs or cardboard cutouts but here the world feels a bit more alive. Also the final details on anything from furniture to electronic equipment, they all had improved detailing.- I found the sprinting convenient to traverse some of the larger maps helpful, whether it was necessary or not I did find it helpful. Also being able to ADS with the weapons was such a strange feeling at first considering there was no ADS'ing in the original but it was appreciated. NOTE: The Sprinting and ADS'ing could be up for debate as to whether they should even be in the game, but added it as a pro considering it does add a convenience to playing the game, if not im sure people played this game true to the original and just hip fired and played at normal movement.And that's about it for Pros that I can't really think of currently for this remake.CONS:- GLITCHY BUGGY MESS. This game is a glitchy buggy mess this its so obvious. So many instances I've had player models just having deformed facial expressions its so pathetically laughable, as well as their death animations. Something about their ragdoll animations are just so not smooth, like at all. It looks like stop motion lol! and sometimes they'll phase through walls or the floor and sperg out. Cutscenes are missing audio completely and dialogue is completely silent. - CHARACTER MODELS. While I do appreciate the updated remastered look they were going for they just don't look right to me. Just too cartoonish and I saw someone mention it but they really do look like Fortnite characters. I'm not a fan of how they look, and I know the Original also had cartoonish features because of course they were trying to emulate a Comic Book Cell Shaded look and it worked there, it was serious but also a cell shaded look at the same time. Here they just simply look cartoonish.- ROUGH BUGGY GAMEPLAY. In addition to the glitchiness of this game, the gameplay is super clunky. Combat is so rough and buggy it's discouraging a lot of the times. Which is a damn shame considering that was one of the biggest reasons I enjoyed the original so much. when simply traversing the map and nothing is happening, the frame rate is fine and pretty smooth, but as soon as the screen is filled with enemies and we are all shooting each other, the Frame rate takes a massive dive and its sooo painful to deal with sometimes. - ENTIRE CUTSCENES REMOVED. Why? why would you remove entire cutscenes from this game? And honestly because of this and the many other reasons, I feel like this game just wasn't finished despite having so much time in development. The obvious cutscene that is missing is after you destroy the Apache Attack Helicopter AFDM 10 when you go to infiltrate the Willard Estate, that whole cutscene sequence is missing. Another whole cutscene missing is when you arrive at the camping grounds to find Kim Rowland's Cabin, that cutscene is missing as well. When you stow away on the Submarine behind the curtain, the cutscene of the submarine being alerted of your intrusion is also missing entirely. I really don't understand why, maybe because it has to do with the glitchy mess that this game is?? I don't know but that was annoying.- FLASHBACK SEQUENCES. Honestly not a fan of the new flashback sequences, it's pretty dull and not anywhere near as impactful as the original's. There's no ominous ambiance like in the original with that cool filter they had. And I don't know if the devs did this on purpose but the flashbacks began having colored models instead of black and white. Also I've had many glitched moments of carrying a weapon into the flashback sequence. - DIFFICULTY. What difficulty? This game was pathetically easy, and I played this on their Hardest "XIII" difficulty or whatever it's called. AI is stupid, plain and simple just really dumb AI that clearly have a hard time noticing you. But then again its funny because they can spot you through heavy brush and trees without you even noticing so its very inconsistent. Every weapon in this game is now a one shot kill to the head, EVERY WEAPON. No need to spray/unload bullets and conserve ammo like in the original or plan your action of attack, just ADS and pop their heads with the M9 or M16 or practically any weapon in the game its hilarious. Enemies don't do that much damage and honestly this game's "hardest" difficulty is the equivalent to the Original XIII "normal" difficulty. Bosses are also pathetically easy, I remember in the Original I had to retry the Mongoose Boss battle at least 15 times or so on the hardest because he just moved so quick and sprayed you with the duel mini uzis. Here I killed him on my first attempt with just unloading the M60 to his face and I think in part because they also added this new stun feature where he was just completely immobilized and died in like 10 seconds lol. Also he doesn't even fall off the ledge like in the original he just slumps to the ground like a ragdoll and dies. - SOUNDTRACK. Okay this is the biggest disappointment easily. One of the greatest soundtracks I have ever heard in a video game and it was massacred! Really?? The music is so quiet you can barely hear it a lot of the times in many of the maps or it's not even playing at all! The original XIII had so many great audio cues and musical cues it was so engaging and immersive with the high tension of gunfights or escaping danger and here it fails so freaking miserably bad. Music cues are missing entirely, making a lot of the greatest moments of this game completely anti climactic its absolutely criminal. For example, exposing the snowman as an actual person underneath and sudden scaring strings or violins. Missing. When the fireworks go off when you're on the Lady Bee talking to Amos and Carington and they think its gunfire they both pull out their sidearms and the intense awesome soundtrack pops in, but its a false alarm. Missing. When Number 1 reveals himself to you at the end asking if you're not enjoying the fireworks and the big reveal in the soundtrack plays. Missing. There are more instances but my goodness this really screwed up the experience for me. There are probably more cons I could pick this game apart for but this is enough honestly. I'm so disappointed and I really wanted to enjoy this game as I got through the campaign the worse and worse it got. By the end of it I just didn't feel like returning to this at all. I can't even enjoy the multiplayer and that's a whole other issue. There were glimpses of hope I had while playing it but at it's current state, you're much better off playing the Original XIII.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really disappointed. This remake really pisses me off, it's the first time I've ever preordered something, and now I remember why preordering is such a bad idea.I love the original XIII game from Ubisoft, so much so that I bought it both on Gamecube, PC (from GoG) and on steam, since it came on a bundle with the preorder of this game. It got me into the franchise and made me start reading the comics which are overall really good."XIII 2020 is just XIII with "better" graphics" that's the first thing I thought when I booted it up, and to be honest that's kind of what I was expecting since I saw the first gameplay reveal, but to begin with, it is not.The story is pretty much the same as in the original game, (It even has the nerve of showing the original's game intro, which has an entirely different art style, as an scene where an FBI guy puts on a reel and plays it, also having constant unnecesary changes on camera angles.) For starters, the first thing you'll notice is that the in game graphics are not cell-shaded like the original XIII, or games like Borderlands, Killer 7, and so on. Instead, it has this cartoonish style more like Fortnite and to be honest I'm not a huge fan of the change but also I don't mind it that much, it's just soulless and mediocre, although I'll say that there are a few scenaries that look really good, which unfortunately are very scarce, in other words, the game's visual quality is all over the place, with some models looking really ugly (Col. Amos for instance)From the technical standpoint, it's a cluster♥♥♥♥, the first bad sign I had when I first launched it was that my native resolution (1440x900) wasn't natively supported, so I had to go into the registry edit and ♥♥♥♥ around with the settings until I got it to work. Then, inmediately I noticed that the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mouse sensitivity is just a mess, the normal  sensitivity was too high so I naturally lowered it, just to notice that when you aim your weapon the sensitivity gets lowered dramatically, hell I'd bet that it was maybe a quarter of the "normal" sensitivity, so I had to go back into the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Cocacola overdose setting.Then there's the gameplay changes, yes, there are, and they're not good at all. It's the classic "What if we take this game from the late 90's-early 2000's and make it now with modern games' mechanics?". So we have mechanics like sprinting, aiming down sights, only carrying one of each class of weapons at a time. Now I'd assume that this later change was to "balance" the game, if that makes sense, since with ADS the game's easy, way too easy, every weapon is a lethal 1-shot kill on the head (Duh) and if you have a decent accuracy (because good accuracy is impossible with the sensitivity ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) you'll need nothing more than a fast firing weapon, and this makes ammo quite plentiful, making the ammo management from the first game take a trip to Uganda only to get lost in da way.The checkpoint system is the same as in the original game, THE THING THAT WOULD'VE MADE THE MOST SENSE TO CHANGE ENTIRELY, so it suffers the same flaws derivate from it as the Ubisoft game did.The AI is just horrible they try to put them as "Look how clever they are, if they spot a body they'll enter a high alert mode and will look out for you", this mechanic ironically triggers itself quite often when the enemies execute other npcs during a scripted cutscene only to inmediately react to the corpse right after it's done.Also one change they made is that they'll stop all form of engagement once you're out of their field of view and will go back to this "alert mode" (which is them just standing around usually giving you their backs just to get shot in the head). I can see why this change was made, since one of the complaints about the original XIII was that once one enemy, just one, spots you, all the enemies in the area automatically know where you are, and that implies that you cannot disengage and go back to hiding once your cover is blown, however, this sure wasn't a "fix" for that problem, it just created a much major one.It's filled with bugs that I found just by normal gameplay, some sequence breaking bugs that I accidentaly tirggered.I could go on, and on, and I'll do it eventually, but not here, i guess I'll do a youtube video ranting and eventually getting wasted, because, jesus, this game is awful.It is a slap to the face for both people who like the original game and newcomers alike.I regret preordering this and not just sticking to the original. Buy that instead is way cheaper and much more fun, also it runs in pretty much anything.Edit after finishing it: The bossfights are a complete joke (I played on XIII difficulty which is supposed to be the hardest), they introduced this stupid mechanic that after dealing X ammount of damage in a short period of time, the guy gets idiotized and stays still in place for like 5 to 10 seconds, enough to keep doing damage to him only to trigger this mechanic again, which ends in bossfights that only last a couple of seconds, THEY ARE EASIER TO KILL THAN STANDARD ENEMIES.The last parts of the game are really easy to break, I've had to restart the last mission multiple times due to bodies getting stuck in places where they could be spotted, knocking out enemies to only get clipped through the roof and get stuckMany cutscenes are broken and even if they weren't they are just bad, there isn't that sense of build up and tension that the original game had, making every twist in the story exciting and hooking.PS: This game overheated my PSU and killed it, not kidding.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After a few years, Microid decided to give the project to another company to rework the project, and honestly now, it is quite good and playable.TL:DR; It's a fully playable FPS with good nowaday standards, it can be bought and played, but I would still recommend personally the remake, if you're not afraid to play something different from nowadays standards.For the people not used to FPS (or to nowadays FPS), it would be the go-to, as it has HP regeneration (partially), showing where to go, aiming, sprinting and collectibles. It also fixes many AI issues, performance issues and some design choices (you can have all the weapons and don't have to chose which ones to keep).However, if you're used to FPS and you're not afraid by the old graphics and an older style of FPS, I would still recommend you to go by the classic version, being more nervous and making more sense.Currently, the game still has bugs and some polish (like SFX duplication, the cinematics being in the old graphic style, not keeping your inventory between two sections of a mission) and how it has been programmed/designed, it prefers the player to be more frontal and gunning their way through than being sneaky.The game is being more generous (towards the player advantage) with the enemies' health, behaviour and even bosses (as the final boss in the original game would take a few minutes to beat in normal, whereas in hard in this remake, two dual wielding mini gun + one assault rifle magazines and they're down in not even 30s).====================================================XIII was an underestimated FPS during its time, and the fact it got a remake would maybe give the justice the game didn't have.Unfortunately, with this remake (and as the negative reviews prove it), it's really not up to the classic.By trying to be smooth and more nowadays like (as for an example, having "weapons slot", which means you can't have the 13mm and the colt at the same time, the game loses a good part of its core gameplay that made the game really good and play nice. It really lacks that juicy and "hmpf" impacts (like just by doing the headshots with the sniper or crossbow) which would often be followed by a vignette of the enemy falling or dying, really adding more impact on your actions.Let's add the fact we don't see XIII getting "better" as he recovers his memories with time (as an example, the dual wielding of the 13mm would be unlocked after finding an hidden document (which would bring back memories).Aside the bugs (as it's something can be fixed, and making games is not an easy task), the game has still potential, graphically it looks nice, the audio is still good (and I hope it will be fixed to have more dynamic as the classic), the story had a good start and concept, but by trying to be that "You're the hunter" with cool animations and swap, the game loses in dynamism by trying to be complex whereas keeping some stuff simple would be better.Another example would be the cinematics, the classic one would "hide" its issues in animation by using the comic panel to illustrate, and really embraced the comic element to correct/hide some elements it couldn't do (like doing a full animation), which gives an additional esthetic and uniqueness to the game.For now, I would recommend the classic one which still stands up on nowadays standards (just think to install the latest patch and the mouse sensibility fix) for a 2003 game.I'm really looking forwards a few months to let time to the dev team to gather the players feedback, reanalyze what made the classic XIII feels good to play and improve the game to give a second shot to it, as it deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original XIII, I have fond memories of playing it back on the original Xbox, and loved every moment of what the game offered, a nice blend of both stealth and action set pieces combined with an interesting story plot, and I was gutted when there was never a follow, especially considering the games cliffhanger, so to no surprise I've been awaiting the release of this quite eagerly, and sadly, it doesn't quite meet the expectation, don't get me wrong, I wasn't expecting full triple A quality polish and graphics here, but there are some things that just let this down in so many ways, and considering it was delayed for a full year as well, they are things that should not be present. A few examples: the odd sound equalization, some sounds are super quiet, whilst others were ready blow out my ear drums, the 9mm pistol literally sounds like a spud gun/pea shooter, and the music is very distant in comparison to everything else going on. The animations are very sub par, upon killing an enemy they literally just hold their arms up and flop to the ground stiffer than a wardrobe toppling over. The voice acting in some parts could have benefited from being completely redone, more the random NPCs than the main characters, they just sound overly cheesy and sometimes don't quite fit the image of the appearance. This is just to name a few issues here, then take into consideration the large amounts bugs present in the game, and everything you get just sort crumbles in on itself, which is a shame really because there is a lot potential for something so much better, perhaps if they had taken just a few more months to iron the issues that could've prevented such a shameful release of a cult classic game.All this is not to say that there isn't hope for this yet though, perhaps, and hopefully, the developers will patch these inconveniences over time, so that the full potential of what should be something great can be reached, but until then, I'd most certainly wait and save your money for something better in the time being.

Not only that you also have a melee fist attack which is super OP and basically removes any need for stealthily taking down your opponent as in the current state you can just rush to them (again with the scripting issue the enemy will not likely register you sprinting to him from behind) and knock him unconscious with a flurry of fists. You also have a weird limit on guns (so you can no longer carry a pistol and a revolver), and most tools are now context sensitive which again with the scripting issue is a big problem as they do not seem to register properly. If you really want to experience this, I'd suggest going with the classic version now as this isn't worth it currently, besides you'd have less problems setting it up for modern displays than playing through this version.

_childDocuments_.review: XIII (2022 Version)Positives:+ Stylish and improved cartoony graphics+ The sounds and music from the original is kept+ The bad voiceacting of david duchovny+ Some environment improvements+ Some parts are quite fun+ Exploration is rewarded+ Collectables+ Nice length (7-8 hours)Negatives:- Low FOV (cant be adjusted high enough)- Feels a bit slow, tenacious and slothy- The gameplay has not aged very well- Feels like most of the soul is gone compared to the original- Some more variations in sounds would have been preferable- The music is set at a very high volume- Gunplay is not the best- The stealth parts are not improved- Some parts are not very engaging- Very slow walk and carry speed- Stiff and unnatural animations- The AI is bad (especially in the boss fights)- Still a lot of bugs and glitchesI have not played the version released in 2020, but Ive seen gameplay from it, and it seems to have improved a lot since then.A least the graphics are now a lot more like the original, rather than the "fortnite style" released in 2020.If you like cartoony fps games, or the old XIII from 2003, you might like this remake.But be aware that almost nothing other than the graphics have been improved, some parts are actually worse than the original.And the gameplay is still like it was in the early 2000s, so dont expect too much.I would prefer the original to this 2022 version, but now at least its playable and doesnt deserve to be slaughtered like the original 2020 release was.Total Score: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: For years, I have waited for XIII The Conspiracy Remastered to come out. When I got hold of the news saying that it would be made, I couldn't believe my eyes. I prayed that it would bring me as much joy as the original did. Even when it got delayed, I figured that was a good thing because it means that all the kinks would be worked out before release.The day it finally came out and I'm sitting here waiting for it to download on my computer, I kept seeing nothing but negative reviews. I kept seeing people posting that they're getting refunds because it was that horrible. I was not believing them. I didn't want to read such foul reviews. So, I logged on and immediately started playing.My disappointment is tremendous with with I had experienced.This game's music is one of the best soundtracks for any game that I have played in my entire life. And majority of the tracks were not playing correctly. During every fight, whether you're facing regular enemies or bosses, the music is supposed to get you excited. It's supposed to be in your face-sounding. Instead, it just kept messing up whether it wanted to be calm or excited during whenever you did anything. And the fight against the Mongoose, the music was just not even playing the most awesome piece. It was just playing that calm organ piece that played after you canceled Operation Red from happening.Glitches were everywhere. Enemies refused to die with one-hit arrows to the head. I'm literally seeing the arrow stick in their heads and somehow that did not kill them. Even with any guns, the original made it where head shots were instant one-hit kills. It was random every single time. I either got the instant kill, or I had to keep shooting many more times. The NPCs though are either a joke or horribly cheap. The joke NPCs just kept running away without firing a single shot. The cheap NPCs were shooting me without even me being in their sight. The boss fights were a joke with the exception of the Mongoose. While it was a slight nice touch to make them "dizzy" when they kept getting shot at consecutive times, they hardly were a threat to me. The only one was the Mongoose and that was because he was broken. He moved way faster than he was in the original, his guns would just tear you instantly. And for some reason, the area you were fighting on, you can legit stand on the railing if you run towards them, and fall off the map. I swear I also feel like the map shrunk because I've never fallen off the edge of this level ever. And I unfortunately did twice.A lot of material was cut. I don't understand why the Psycho music didn't play when you revealed the dead hitch hiker in the snowman, or why the insane soldier wasn't calling McGall a Pinhead. Those little details made me cheerish XIII even more, but sadly those minor details were nowhere in the game.I cannot appreciate this. I thought Dark Summit was the worst game I've ever played, but this may have topped the cake. I couldn't tell you how many times I had to kept pressing the sensitivity button on my mouse to adjust to the weird changes I kept encountering every so often. I honestly thought this would revive XIII to where it would get the sequel many people wanted that actually DID play and DID appreciate. Granted, if I truly wanted to know who Number 1 is (despite it was extremely obvious at the very start), I could just pick up the comic. But I really thought that it would do well to where we can continue.The game didn't even had the "To be continued..." part at the end. It just ended with Number 1 and two guards aiming their guns at me. Then some weird glitch thing happened, next thing I'm seeing are the credits. This wasn't a remastered game. This was something I honestly cannot recommend people to play no matter how much I keep saying that the original XIII was an awesome game. I'm incredibly disappointed this didn't hold up.Disappointing.EDIT:Been a while since I last touched this game. Nothing really has been improved. The music doesn't change with the action. The bosses are stupidly easy to defeat that I can just stand in front of them while they're shooting at me and just demolish them. At least with the original, it HAD a challenge, it HAD difficulty, it HAD  everything right. This game just feels wrong and I hate that curiosity got the best of me to give it another try with these so called "updates". Nah, again just a waste of two good hours.I can't believe I was actually excited for this game.

The ragdolls bug out, the sound is too loud/bugs out/plays at the wrong time.The gun sounds also sound so boring.
