_childDocuments_.review: Yikes.This is a remake?  You sure it's not a beta for the original 2003 edition?I am terribly disappointed with this remake.  I played the crap out of the original XIII on Gamecube back in the day.  This remake is hands down worse than the original in every aspect.-Audio delays or complete audio drops for various animations like reloading or AI death.  The bank explosion had no audio on my game.  Gun sounds are awful...probably from the original, but come on, put a little effort into it.-Animations are clunky as hell.  Death animations are awkward, enemies go from standing to dead on the ground in a millisecond.  Attacking with environmental weapons like chairs, bottles, and ashtrays is not pretty.  Reloading animation is hit or miss.  Picking up and dropping bodies is...oof.  They also seemed to remove a lot of small bits, like extra dialogue and many headshot kill frames.-AI are possibly worse than from the original game.  They will stand around aiming at your feet as you walk up to them and blow a hole in their head with a shotgun.  I stood in front of some enemies as they unloaded at me with AK47s for 5-10 seconds; no cover, no dodging and lost only about 25% health.  And that was on hard mode...What is this crap?-Graphics update is cute, but even that was not terribly impressive.  Looking around for a bit started making me nauseous.Anyways, I'm not a game reviewer, but this remake made me so angry and unhappy that I stopped playing it and wrote this review.  The amount of issues this game has and for how long it's been in production, I'd be surprised to see any significant fixes any time soon.  Just play the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to popular belief, this is no longer one of the worst remakes ever published. Instead, it's just kind of ... average, now. I finished the remake, and walked away feeling like what I experienced was just...fine. Nothing as groundbreaking as the original XIII, and even the QoL changes couldn't stop me from feeling like the experience was more disjointed than the original game's vision. It's nice that XIII got a fresh coat of paint, but the original is still the definitive way to experience this game.My issues with this version are primarily as follows:- It's unbelievably easy to get softlocked in situations that don't occur in the original game. I had to restart 2-3 different checkpoints because the game would fail to trigger a script needed to progress to the next part of the level. - The sound design  Broken, maybe? Some levels that I distinctly remember having music in the original version are just dead silent for long stretches of time, with no ambiance or anything to pad out the sound. The submarine dock in particular felt very hollow. - Some cutscenes seem to just not exist, just dropping me into random stages with no explanation when there'd normally be a comic sequence or something. On the note of cutscenes, the graphics aren't exactly 1:1 to the gameplay graphics, as they're using pre-rendered cutscenes from the old 2020 version, which is kind of jarring at times.For $2.30 CAD? It's worth at least one playthrough, even if I wouldn't ever recommend buying this at full price. You can buy both this and the original for $4 until November 12th, and compare and contrast them yourself. I think one strength this version has is feeling smoother with a controller, so getting up and running on the Steam Deck is a breeze, but if you're playing with a keyboard and mouse, I think you'll have a much better time in virtually every respect with the classic version.

_childDocuments_.review: I always had a feeling this game would under perform from the first gameplay trailer I saw, it was rough around edges then and it's rough around the edges nowFor the price they're asking this is no where near worth the priceTo break it down for youPros:They kept the original Voices, it's nice to hear Adam west again and the quality (when you can hear it) isn't half bad eitherThe menu looks prettyCons:No FOVAim Assist doesn't turn off when you turn it off (Why this is a thing for mouse alongside a controller I'll never know)The Game has Mouse Acceleration... which you CAN'T TURN OFF, NOT EVEN VIA A CONFIGFrame-rate issues on a RTX 2080 Super/Intel i7-770kNo option for a separate ADS sensitivity (it's really slow regardless)Gunplay is really dullGuns sound bad, animations looks stiff and bug out frequentlyAI is awful, unresponsive and dawdle for about 10 seconds before realising you're theresound mixing is dreadful, music cuts out randomly or you can hear the voicesBugs, Bugs, BUGS!The Graphical charm from the original is lost with the new visualsThe "pre-order" bonus will disable itself each level and after each restartMultiplayer is back! and it's local only and has like 3 maps... Local multiplayer only... for an fps... on pc...in 2020If you want my recommendation, go buy XIII - Classic, download the community patch and play that insteadI hope they patch it I really do, I was so hopeful for this, I'd love to be able to change this review down the line to positive, but I have a feeling they'll give it up after a week or two, you're called Playmagic, use some of that magic and prove me wrong

_childDocuments_.review: Nope, gotta edit this once moreHey kids, want to have the 'beat the game on the hardest difficulty' acheivement? Just load the last mission up on it, run to the end (there's no enemies) and hey presto, acheivement.---Okay, SO. The amount of work put in to the re-remake is definitely notable... But honest I still can't recommend this after having fully completed the remake now. They've polished a turd because unfortuantely there's still way too many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and things that are just off - Audio cues that are different or just don't work, the fact it feels like stealth is non existent when most the AI just zergs the player. The fact it still uses the same pre-render cutscenes that look like they've been made in Garrys Mod on an open plains map. The fact that some of these cutscenes are just missing, expecting a transition after rescuing Carrington? Nah, how about after the FBI sting and heading to the Sanctuary? Nope. Not even a 'To be continued' stinger at the end.Whilst the effort to fix the game -is- commendable, this ain't an FF14 ground up rebuild. It's just a bug and graphic fix, of which there's still a lot to deal with. Oh, oh another thing, how about those headshot zoom ins with deadpan faces, vs the dramatic 'Noooo' faces they did in the original XIII, or the fact the 'Oh no bank bomb' music stinger happens -after- the bomb has exploded now.Or how some NPCs have moving lips, some don't. It also still keeps the sprint/aim down sights features... Which honestly make the game trivial. Which is probably there because they can't keep track of what ammo and weapons you have between levels.What point is the 'preserve your ammo' tooltip when going through a load zone will get rid of most of it, leaving you with a pistol or an AR with a single magazine? In short. No. Just no. Save your £25 for something else.

_childDocuments_.review: A nameless FBI agent walks into a projection room and plays the unaltered, opening sequence from the original XIII on an in-game screen. You then watch the nameless agent sit down and watch the opening scene from a dutch angle below the nameless agent's chair. This is the first of many bizarre and poor choices made for this remake.Fans of the original will immediately notice many things missing. Multiple audio queues are missing from scripted sequences. Multiple comic book panel pop-ups are missing from scripted events and objectives. Comic-style onomatopoeia and effects are missing from some actions, including melee. The music queues are missing or just poorly timed (it's hard to tell which). Character voice queues appear to be missing for deaths and other scripted events. These problems are the most egregious because the Comic/Graphic Novel aesthetic and the 1970s vibe are almost entirely gone from the game.Besides what's missing, what's there isn't great. The character animations are terrible and unrealistic. Some character's animations, like death animations, appear to be replaced with ragdoll physics at times. Enemy death animations look strange and are hard to differentiate from wounded animations. The melee animations are slow and mess with the flow of stealth and combat. The character design is a cross between Fortnite and a Telltale game. Several characters look drastically different for the original,  These stylistic choices wouldn't be so bad if the whole game wasn't missing the spark that the original had.On the positive side, there is Aim-Down-Sight and sprint.

_childDocuments_.review: It genuinely hurts to leave this review, because I loved the original XIII. I had the game on PS2 in 2004 and it was an absolute blast. The game had solid gunplay, clever game design, fun gameplay, a beautiful and unique art-style, wonderful sound design and an intriguing story. I really, really hoped that the negative reviews would merely be people whose rose-tinted glasses perhaps made the remake feel less great - but nothing said before me is an exaggeration.About the only thing the remake has going for it is the story element, but I literally cannot see how they would mess that element up. Even though the graphics are prettier, the art style has been lost completely. The guns feel like garbage, the sound design is atrocious (including random sounds cutting out, music stopping/not playing), the weapon selection menu works when it wants to, the AI is barely functional, and every action in the game is a struggle against the clunky controls. It's simply not fun.As an experiment I kept both the original XIII and the remake running, and I would do one mission at a time - classic first, then remake. It is night and day and clear which version is better, and it's not the 2020 release. The classic XIII has everything that the remake does not, and it's tragic. Deeply tragic.One of the biggest disappointments of 2020 - and that's a high bar to set.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh how we wept when we remembered the wasted potential of this "remake".It feels more like a techdemo, which tried to show how XIII could have looked.Pros:- Good graphics, it looks really nice.- Keeping the horrible voice acting for traditions (and financial) sake.- The ability to aim down sights.Cons:- The AI is so much more stupid, compared to the original.- Your mouse sensitivity gets lowered as soon as you aim down sights and you can't edit this setting.- Soundbugs, soundbugs as far as your ear can (not) hear.- The multiplayer is just a split-screen multiplayer, without the ability to add bots. The original had online multiplayer with    the ability to add bots.- As good as the animations look, they are generic.- It's priceI really hope, they'll get their sh*** together and patch this good. At it's core, this could be a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointing mess. I was looking forward to this game and had hoped it would have capitalized on the aspects of the game that made it unique and brought that into a true remake. It does not, at all. Firstly the new art direction feels more generic than what the original tried to do with it's cool comic book style. I wouldn't have even minded the new high quality models if they hadn't botched the cell shaded look so badly. The comic book aesthetic is just completely flat and downgraded. Secondly, the gun play is just completely broken and unsatisfying. For one the sensitivity never stays consistent because for some God awful reason it seems to be tied to the game's FPS. Not only that but as some others have mentioned, aiming down sights actually breaks the balance of the map design where sniping is needed. Who needs a sniper when you can ADS with an m4 across the map? To make things even worse the ADS has a separate sensitivity that cannot be changed and feels like you are aiming like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ turtle. Thirdly, the game has a lot of bugs. Yeah I know the game just came out, but most of this ♥♥♥♥ is unacceptable after being delayed as well. Ragdolls seem to be at like 10 fps and can turn into a glitchy mess, audio cuts in and out, sometimes guns can't properly reload, and the A.I is a complete joke. The A.I might be the most frustrating thing for me, like you can literally shoot in the sky in a stealth section and not get caught. Not only that, but they don't pose a threat whatsoever. Even on the hardest difficulty they feel like they barley scratch you at times leaving the game to feel way to easy. The only time the A.I felt like a threat was when the armoured enemy was introduced, but for all of the wrong reasons. They have a health pool way larger than they should be completely sucking the fun out of any engagement with these guys where they feel like a bullet sponge. This is completely unlike the original where it felt more like an even challenge with headshots and explosives doing the job. Now, they just soak up so much punishment and it feels like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore, not a challenge. So in conclusion, this game is a complete waste of money. If you want to play this game, buy the original. The original has more style and is 10x more polished than what the remake will probably ever feel like.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this game is pre-alpha early access garbage that they're charging £40 for in order to keep the lights on in their offices. It's pretty janky, movements have no fluidity, animations are weird, controls are stiff, enemies are brain-dead and the ragdoll? Don't even get me started on that; it's so un-lifelike, I've seen better ragdoll effects in porn.The original game is near and dear to my heart, and I played it to completion about 4/5 times in anticipation for the remake. I was expecting to be blown away with this remake, but after playing it for less than an hour, all I feel is regret and shame, like spending the last of your rent money on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ takeaway.I pray for a patch that fixes all the glaring issues, but it's insane that in this day and age we have to wait for a patch for a game to be playable. Shouldn't that be the case from the day of release? I would have preferred the game to be delayed like they did the Switch port if the quality was to be improved.In its current state, don't bother, unless you want to see for yourself just how jank this game is. I would wait, because I know this game will be something special once it's fixed.EDIT:Why can't XIII carry more than 6 weapons at one time? In the original you were able to have all the weapons at one time, but now you have to swap weapons for others? Ridiculous addition, takes even more away from the game. Now I have to swap the 44. for the 9mm, and the AK47 for the M16? Get the ♥♥♥♥ outta here, what a terrible idea. Hope this 'feature' is removed in a patch...EDIT EDIT:They have finally patched the game as of June 2021, but it has not changed my mind; the game is still a hot pile of turd. Yes, XIII can now carry all the weapons in the game, but that doesn't really alleviate the bad taste this game has left me with. There needs to be a major overhaul in the fundamentals of the game before I could even fathom to recommend it. The AI is still bad, the physics are still atrocious, the animations are still broken, and the audio is still a mess. I can definitely appreciate that the developers are actively taking steps to fix their IP, but come on. The game has been out since November, and there are still these glaring issues that haven't been properly addressed? It's a shame, because this game can definitely be something special, and could be the anchor that propels the XIII franchise into the mainstream light. Unfortunately, as it stands right now, that is just a pipe dream.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't express how excited I was for this remake. The original XIII from 2003 was an underrated gem back in the day and this remake will surely not help its reputation. In fact, it's going to completely demolish its reputation because this remaster is sadly pure trash. The gunplay feels off, the ragdoll physics are broken (I didn't encounter a single body that didn't shake like jelly when puting it down), the graphics are ugly (seriously, the original looks better), the atmosphere is gone and the sound and music engine is working on random occasions, just almost never as it's supposed to.This is the first game I've ever refunded. I really wanted to support this believing we'll get a true sequel, but I'll rather read the comics than be forced to play this ever again. I'm sorry, but this is completely killing the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's just say that I've seen entomology museums with less bugs.I pre-ordered this game, like most people, because the original was such an amazing experience, and boy was I let down.Day one the game was so broken that it was practically unplayable. From missing textures, to glitched character models, it was a huge disappointment for a highly anticipated release.I was willing to let the changes in the graphical style slide. Sure, the great cel-shading of the original was a huge part of how good it was, but the new graphic style isn't horrible.But after trying for hours to play a broken game on release day, every little thing starts to bug you (no pun intended)."At least they patched it!"Yeah, if you can call it that. The game is now playable, but glitches and bugs are still abundant.And anyone who pre-ordered it can't get a refund, because that two week grace period counts from purchase date, not play date.Honestly, it's like they took one of my favorite games and just did everything they could to make me hate it.I would have rather had the devs ♥♥♥♥ in my mouth.I will amend this review of, and when, this game gets fixed, but it might be too late to make up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I beat this game for the xbox back in the day. I was left wishing it had more to the plot as it ended on a cliffhanger and didnt really resolve anything but I had fun playing it.  Playing this new version, I waited until they fixed whatever they were going to to buy it on sale for 4$.  They definitely improved the graphics, and it feels a lot like the original.  People who are upset that it isnt a great game should go back and play the original, it also was not a great game.  I honestly think the thing that I dont like about this game is they seem to have made it exactly like the original when coding it.  Little things like not being able to use a grapling hook unless in a specific spot even though the distance should be fine.  Its less of a sandbox game that were all so used to now and more of an event trigger game where everything has to be lined up and then the event is triggered.  That being said it is probably worth 4$ if you like games like goldeneye for the n64 or run N gun games like doom, but its not going to live up to a childhood memory for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has problems, and there is no missing them. You're going to fall through the floor. You're going to have to reset the game because the audio stops working or your guns won't fire. The enemies are duuuuuuuumb.But you know what? I really liked it. For better or worse, they don't make 'em like this anymore. It feels like a game from 2003, and that's just fine with me. In fact, I vastly prefer it over XIII Classic.There's no excusing the bugs. We should expect better. But the truth is, they didn't ruin my experience. They keep this remake from being GREAT, but I still had a lot of fun, start to finish. When it works, it's a great-looking, classic shooter with terrific music and amusingly terrible voice acting (with the exception of Adam West, who is perfect). When it doesn't, it's frustrating. It's disappointing. But it isn't the worst thing in the history of video games, or whatever other hyperbole you've heard.It's a very good game with very real problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Nope.Just nope.I really dig the Original XIII.But this one is just disappointing. I had high hopes for the Game, but everything except the Graphics are Horrible.Shooting feels bad.Animations are somehow worse than the ones from the Original. Sounds are meh.No Bot Support.cant enter Multiplayer because i cant choose a Character when i should.And most Importantly. EVERYTHING even in the Singleplayer has either an Input lag to it or an Lag overall. You press Left click to shoot, you have .. and i kid you not, to wait like a Second before something happens, even tho your standing still. Enemies need atleast 1 Second to recognize they are Dead and another whole second to play their Death animation. Changing Weapons? You press a Key, wait 1 Second then your Character starts packing away your weapon and unpacking the other Weapon. Sometimes the Game doesnt even notice you Press Buttons, like when you reload you have to wait 1 Second after the Animation finished before you are able to shoot again, otherwise nothing will happen. Enemies need sometimes several seconds to notice you even tho you run infront of them. They Ignore most of the time Gun Shots and they take several Seconds (if they notice at all) to spot Dead Bodys around them. Also, you can press C to knock out Enemies.. too bad when it just wont notice that you pressed the Key, or the Enemy spotted you already but the Game still shots the Option to knock him out, the Enemy also continues walking his way until 1-2 Seconds later he instantly turns 180° and starts spraying his Mag into you.Thats... just not acceptable at all, especially because the Original Game was better in these regards.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the last game I pre-ordered before Cyberpunk 2077.Yes, two stinkers.I waited for the patches.Gave it a fair chance.They did improve it a lot, it's fun on the Steam Deck. But it's definitely a cheap remake still, the artstyle being semi fixed doesn't change the Fortnite-esque models you've thrown Cel-Shaded Textures to. I just wish Nightdive done some kind of remaster. Cause while a lot of folks clearly tried; they didn't do it justice.Been more than 3 years since the remake came out.No saving in-between levels, if you quit mid mission, you are going to have to restart it. Which isn't so bad, when you quit at the start of the mission, but if there's a lot of fluff and slow clunkiness (which was in the original nonetheless but the saving was more fluid in that), then the only up sides to playing this version is native controller support, Steam Deck support and achievements.And in turn you get a worse experience.Get the original.And for the love of god I still will forever wish that this got the Nightdive remaster treatment and it's another reason why I'm always in favour of hi-res ports of games with only QOL features, gimme controller support, gimme Cheevos, maybe a nice save system, or just maintain the original save system. But don't mess around with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 Update:It's still a pile of dogsh1t.Original:I have never been so excited for this game as much as I was here, and received the disappointment bill upon starting the game.The original XIII just was at it's best style, it was THAT comic game that the community knew and loved, hence why communities like InsideXIII existed.Now however, I'd be surprised if anyone were to create a mapping/modelling community that is dedicating itself to this... this... utter trash product... there is no other term for it.The animations of the models look too chunky, the voicelines are exactly the ones from XIII 2003, these scam artists literally made you pay for the same product, just that is has now actual physics (or partially...) regarding ragdolls.Headshotting your target has NEVER been so blandly shown off, headshot somebody, what would you expect? Aye! The head makes the rest of the body a turn (Considering it's a physic based game), what actually happens? nothing, they first keep on standing for an average amount of a scripted sequence that takes 3 seconds, and then they just drop down like a sack of potatos... VERY EXCITINGCharacters? What do you mean with characters? Some say it reminds them of Borderlands, others agree upon Fortnite, what did Ubisoft actually do? Is this just a late april joke? _childDocuments_.review: One of the worst attempts at a cel shaded art style I have ever seen. The original XIII had a far more appealing art style. The textures look...wrong and the black outlines on objects have a draw distance. The animations are stiff and the character models look off. I love the cel shaded aesthetic, but this just ain't it.Movement feels floaty, janky and frankly disgusting. The guns are not satisfying to use and have no impact. The FOV is broken. Even at 120 it feels extremely claustrophobic making it very difficult to play the game. Running lowers the FOV making me hate running in this game. I haven't progressed deep enough to critique the enemy variety but from the first few levels I played, it feels like they went for a generic shooter mixed in with the original XIII and they miserably failed. Edit: After beating the game, I stand by this statement. It performs very well but given the sub-par visuals and bland environments, it better perform well. There is no shader compilation stutter and the frame-times are very solid. The settings menu is terrible with only a handful of settings and there is no upscaler (DLSS, FSR, XeSS), this is fine as I doubt most people will need one to enjoy the game. It's still unacceptable as the game had a large overhaul recently.  Some aspects of the game I liked are the music and the weapon variety, even though the weapons suck and they take away most of your weapons after a load screen checkpoint. Stay away from this game and play the original (which is still on steam and is really cheap!).tl;dr: Do not buy this game even at a discount. Use the money you will spend on this game and buy the original XIII on steam and you can even buy a tub of ice-cream with the leftover money.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now, on November 2020, this game has the worst reviews a game can have. Why? Those reviews will make you think this game belongs with Big Rigs, Daikatana or Superman 64, but the game is certainly not abysmal. The disastrous release created a tsunami of bad reviews for many reasons: the outrage for feeling ripped off, having idealized the original too much (and believe me, you had to idealize the first game to love it. I know it because I was one of those players!)... Now, the reputation of this game is probably harmed forever, but believe me, it's a very solid 7/10 game, nicely done and very playable. I don't know if it will ever be judged fairly after this, but believe me,  it's not that bad as they say.This release had a lot of bugs at launch but hey, try to release a game during COVID while working from home and see how it turns out. They actually did a very good job in creating the game itself, but it needed more testing and bug-fixing. Way more. Anyway, I have played it to completion getting 100% of the achievements using the Level Select trick to avoid extra playthroughs (about that: sadly, the difficulty achievements don't stack. *That* was a bad decision, developers). And there's no doubt that the game is very playable right now because a big section of the game is based on stealth and it works as intented. Have you ever played a game with ill-conceived and badly executed stealth insta-fail sections? It can be the worst thing in gaming, next to escort missions. But here, they pulled it off, so that's how you see they knew what they were doing.The graphics look great to me, finding a good balance between realistic and cartoony, IMHO. Other people think they look too realistic (well, they actually say "this remake has no cell-shading!, which is not factually correct), but if you want plain, simplistic graphics, you can always go back to the original. Loading times in this remake are instantaneous (a quality-of-life feature we all loved in Super Meat Boy and Hotline Miami but that you can't find in many FPS. In fact, I only remember the also-recent Ghostrunner right now), and that's really nice. The game just sends everything back to the checkpoint point and spawns everything back in the blink of an eye after you click "Continue". It mostly works (well, only once in 20 hours I got sent beneath the ground, falling to my death in the digital void beneath the map), trying to set you a little bit above the ground with a nice "drop in" effect. Again: maybe when you read this you are already used to the absence of load times in your cool PS5 or Xbox Series X, but believe me, every FPS player hated to wait for minutes until the game was ready again. That was the standard back then. So yes, this game has great features, and reviews should mention that.So everything looks just how I remembered it (memories are deceitful: I have just watched some videos of the original Gamecube-era game and it looks terribly blocky and simplistic), and the cool-as-heck dynamic music and voice-over (with David Duchovny as the English-language lead, Daniel Beretta as the French lead, Ramón Langa as the Spanish lead, etc.) are exactly the same, sounding great. What's not to enjoy? XIII is a nice old-school shooter with lots of style and content (it's quite long and varied), they did a great job and I think it deserves to be played. I enjoyed these 20 hours, and I know that I will play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome back, agent! "XIII" (2020) aims to revive the cult classic from 2003 with a fresh coat of cel-shaded paint and updated gameplay. Unfortunately, this remake struggles to balance nostalgia with modern expectations, delivering a mixed experience that’s as intriguing as it is frustrating.The game’s aesthetic is its standout feature. The cel-shaded graphics give XIII a unique, comic book-like style, staying true to the original's roots. The visual design is playful and vibrant, evoking the feel of a graphic novel coming to life. However, this charm is often overshadowed by technical issues. Bugs, glitches, and inconsistent frame rates can pull you out of the immersion, reminding you that this isn’t quite the polished update fans had hoped for.You step into the shoes of XIII, an amnesiac super-soldier accused of assassinating the President. The storyline remains compelling, with conspiracy theories and espionage woven into the narrative. Voice acting is generally solid, but some performances lack the punch needed to elevate the drama, leaving certain moments feeling flat.Gameplay tries to modernize the classic first-person shooter mechanics, but it’s a mixed bag. Gunplay feels satisfying when it works, but clunky controls and AI issues can turn intense firefights into frustrating endeavors. Stealth sections offer a nice change of pace, yet they too suffer from inconsistent enemy behavior, making some segments feel like a chore.Sound design is a hit and miss. The soundtrack captures the retro vibe, complementing the comic book aesthetic perfectly. However, audio bugs can disrupt the experience, with some sounds cutting out or misfiring at crucial moments.In the end, "XIII" (2020) is a nostalgic trip marred by technical setbacks. It’s a game with a lot of heart but lacking in execution. For fans of the original, it might still hold some appeal, but new players may find its charm buried under a heap of frustrating flaws. Approach with caution, agent—you might need more than a few retries to see this mission through.

_childDocuments_.review: A remake of the beloved original 2003 version by Ubisoft Paris (now humbly called XIII - Classic).It had a rough start on its way to provide a worthy modern successor, when overambitious goals met a tight deadline and limited development resources at the developer PlayMagic.Luckily, Microids (the publisher), despite the disastrous reviews, still contracted another team, Tower Five, to address a lot of issues and even though it's not a perfect superior version of the classic one due to the large band-aiding, it's perfectly playable and the multiplayer is stable and has smooth gameplay.Unfortunately though, this is the only treatment done, bringing the minimum of playability that is expected for any game, inclusive a different graphic style that is closer to the original, but still has its drawbacks.The single player, when it comes to the general gameplay, now does smoothly, but lacks a few cutscenes, means someone experiencing the XIII story for the first time would be thrown into a new environment without knowing their actual purpose at that place. Likewise, other details are missing (like being able to shoot down the chopper on Brighton Beach).The multiplayer, while providing an incredibly smooth gameplay thanks to the foundational overhaul of the player controls, it severly lacks of maps, modes, customization features.The  is literally a matchmaking service with zero options. The only mode is "XIII kills", an up to 13 player large deathmatch session. The maps, player name and skin are picked randomly. But it doesn't matter anymore since the matchmaking is broken. It's unknown whether the service itself is still functional or if it only struggles at achieving a match within a smaller playerbase. It was more or less reliable when the update rolled out and many players wanted to try it out, but obviously the number declined and several recent tests with fellow users actively trying to join a game together haven't succeeded since.The  is an existing option from the initial remake version. This one has not received any updates and is completely different to the online multiplayer. It provides three maps to choose from as well as deathmatch and team deathmatch with a max of 4 players of which each one is required to provide a game controller. You might come to the idea of using Steam's Remote Play Together in order to bypass the broken online service, but given the latency in this mode (and the awkward splitscreen view) it's anything but an enjoyable option.It's great that Microids contracted another development studio to remedy the most severe flaws, but it's the bare minimum you'd expect from any game, yet they called it a day for good, not caring about the still heavily blank multiplayer that would play great and attract players if it had actual working online servers, a leaderboard and the features from the original.

_childDocuments_.review: 39,99€ seems a lot for this, considering that some people even own the original game and it's state on release (at least they made release day..) . I've bought the old XIII twice now, now on steam and once back then in CD Form "2003-Style" and I loved it! It was one of my fondest multiplayer experiences from back in the day and I loved the story, too.I then recently played it again, the Steam version, but didn't enjoy it quite as much. I seem to have forgotten many bad moments of the 2003 XIII in the past 17 years. The hit reg was horrible back then, plus the saving mechanics were all 100% manual, no autosaves. nothing was done automatically. Then there's the max distance of weapons, weird controls and horrible resolution and graphics (WE'RE SO SPOILED NOWADAYS!!). That being said, it was still a great game, and I had fun, but I wanted the remaster!!Now it came, it launched and honestly it ain't that bad, but it COULD have done sooooo much better and for what got delivered NOW the price seems kinda high. Maybe it will become decent after a few patches? Right now, only the single player campaign is enjoyable, as you can kinda get past the odd-stuff, like most prominently the extremely easy difficulty of the game and the lousy NPC-AI. I played on the 2nd hardest difficulty, thinking it would be hard. It was not. I died precisely when I meant to, that one exact time, 50% through the campaign. The original XIII has better AI! And that is not a joke. The damage inflicted by enemies on the HARDEST difficulty is so minimal.. the only thing that does damage is the rocket launcher, that thing "could" potentially kill you. Plus the NPCs barely move unless they get alerted and want to run to an alarm. Back in the old XIII, you didn't "just" finish a level on the hardest difficulty. It was a walk in the park, the new park!!The multiplayer feels horrible.. I don't even want to put time and effort into it at this moment. It needs a lot of patching!The only positive things to be said:Good graphics overhaul, looks good. Needs optimisation, though.Still fun, although too easy. Story is still good. There's waaay more enemies to fight now. Games has collectibles and achievements, autosaves and a new mission select for those who might care. Then there's the better feel to weapons and better hit reg in single player. You can finally shoot at enemies with pistols and rifles over 30m away from you! (It's kinda broken and makes the game easy, especially if you can aim like me). The gunplay and movement actually feel good, it's a start!!! :)Soo final statement:-Fixed some aspects of the old XIII-Created MANY new problems-Needs fixes, big patchesWhat has the be said: Patience! It might go somewhere.. there's still hope for a postive multiplayer experience in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: XIII:~~~ President Sheridan has been assassinated and the American people can’t believe what just happened. The entire country is gobsmacked! Who would want to kill the well-beloved President? Well, holding the office of Leader of the Free World has its . . . how can we put it . . . deadly downside.  As the FBI tries to figure out who is behind the assassination, you wake up somewhere on a beach with a dreadful headache, and you don’t seem to recall who you are or what happened to you.  The only hint you have is the tattoo on your upper left Pectoral muscle and that everyone is after you. That’s a good start, shall we say?! Good luck to you XIII!XIII (2020) is a remake if the iconic (2003) action/first person shooter game. This version was developed by PlayMagic and Published by Microids on the Steam platform on 11th of November 2020. The game is also available on PS4, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch.Before I start this review, I would like to mention that I am a very big fan of XIII; I purchased the original game in 2003 on it’s release day and also purchased the game (XIII Classic) when it hit the Steam store a few months back. I also vividly remember the bugs that the 2003 game had, and the first big one was at the bank level where the game crashed over and over again. Those days, we didn’t have Steam or other platforms with automatic updates, and it took a couple of months to have a decent patch. Nonetheless, I stuck by the game and I am glad I did!This version consists of a campaign of 16 levels which you can play in one of four levels of difficulty, and a multiplayer mode which I couldn’t access. The multiplayer mode seems to have three maps and you can play a deathmatch or a team deathmatch. What I really like in this version is that the developers were faithful to the plot, the graphic style (which is now better) and all the weapons of the original. Each level has a few collectibles to acquire, in the form of dossiers and golden statuettes, which are cleverly hidden somewhere around the level; so make sure you explore every corner to find them. I actually finished the game in the normal difficulty mode and started another game on the next level of difficulty, and I must say the game should have been pushed back due to the sheer number of issues I encountered. In regards to the audio, it seemed to work fine until I reached the Kellownee Lake stage, when the audio started having some sort of a fit . . . it was all over the joint! The weapons started to shudder and in the middle of it I heard footsteps and god knows what else was in there. I had to shut down the game and restart it.  This occurred randomly several times. The frame rate dropped on and off, which is also frustrating to say the least. In terms of weapons, well, I had my fair share of frustrations especially when I couldn’t reload my gun or when I needed to sneak my way through and use my knives to kill enemies (I had a bad case of superglue fingers on the steel blade!). To be honest, it didn’t matter too much, as the enemy’s AI kept performing some sort of dance before attacking me (still trying to figure out if it was the Tango or the Lambada)! In any case, I had enough time to swap weapons. It is such a shame because the original was a great game and I have no doubt the developers will fix these issues as fast as they can. But I must say that I was bitterly disappointed, and it might have been better to push back the release date to fix these major issues prior to the launch. Despite this, I still believe XIII (2020) will improve with each update to give us what we deserve from this great title. What I really appreciate from Microids is the fact that they have posted an apology and are listening to the community, and I commend them for that. Yes, the pandemic might have created delays, but you surely knew these issues when you released the game.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Nice graphics+	Good soundtrack+	Faithful to the original in terms of level designs, weapons and plot+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet-	Plenty of bugs (Audio, frame rates, weapons to mention a few)Who killed President Sheridan? And who are you? You’ll find out in XIII! 5/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of the original XIII, I really want to recommend the remake. In some ways, it's like a love letter to the classic game. The graphics are refined and crisp, some quality-of-life improvements have been made, fun additions like collectibles have been added, and splitscreen multiplayer is now an option. However, the glitches and missing content are too prominent for me to overlook. This really needed more development time to iron out its issues, and while the September 2022 update improved some aspects of the remake, not enough has been done to make the game worth buying.XIII's story is the same as in the original game, so I won't bother going through it again. The same voice acting, levels, and characters return for the remake. Collectible documents and character trophies expand on the central conspiracy and the factions involved in the game, encouraging players to search for more answers. The remake handles the storyline just fine. However, one of the biggest missed opportunities is that the original game's cliffhanger ending remains unresolved...except now there isn't even a hint at a continuation. This could have been a chance to resolve that mystery and bring the plot to a conclusion, but it sadly wasn't touched upon.Some parts of XIII have been improved, while others are weirdly lacking. Combat generally feels more responsive. All of XIII's abilities are available from the start, meaning that you won't randomly gain improved sniping abilities midway through the game. You can aim down weapon sights to improve accuracy. The dual pistols now fire whenever you pull the trigger instead of their strange two-round burst from the original game. Some underused weapons from the classic version now appear in additional levels, like the double barrel shotgun and Uzi. Stealth is more forgiving than in the original. A small portion of your health can now regenerate if it goes too low.At the same time, features from the classic version of XIII are absent. Weapons like the Shotgun, Harpoon Gun, and Bazooka now lack their alt-fire melee attacks. Multiplayer is missing several modes and bot support. Some smaller details that made the gameplay rewarding, like shooting down the first level's helicopter to cut off reinforcements later on, are not included. The complete Golden Guns bonus from the deluxe edition of the remake is unavailable...though, for some reason, enabling and disabling that setting can give the M16 its golden skin. If the files are already in the game, why not add them to the pre-order bonus or unlock them for use by everyone else?Then there are the bugs. Man, oh man, are there a  of bugs in this remake. Some are harmless and humorous (female corpses flopping away when you set them down, the Pistol being held at a different angle when carrying someone and dual-wielding, enemy bodies getting wedged into doors). Others are distracting (the Shotgun reload sounds often being off-sync, the dual-wielded Pistol's slide being locked back until it is reloaded, silenced gunshots coming from the unsilenced second Pistol). There are more than a few that can hinder your experience (Dual Uzi reloads being bugged and failing to give the correct ammo, collectibles appearing in levels after you have obtained them, knives sometimes locking up and failing to be throwable). All of these issues combined with glaring spelling mistakes and tips referencing missing features (like the Shotgun melee attack) make the remake seem shoddy and poorly handled.In spite of these issues, I had fun with the XIII remake! It's more playable now than it was on release. I had to lower the resolution from 1920x1080 to 1600x900 for it to run well, but only a few levels (like the Bank) had framerate issues after that. The gameplay and secret-hunting elements are a blast when they work. The story still has a lot of intrigue and mystery to it. The art design is also charming and provides a good mix of cel-shading and more cartoonish character designs. It's one of the rare games that I enjoyed enough to go for 100% completion.That doesn't take away from the XIII remake being a bad game, though. I really wanted to enjoy it, so I ended up doing just that thanks to my own biases. If you're an average FPS player or a fan of the XIII comics, I would stick to XIII - Classic instead of the remake. The original still delivers a solid gaming experience and comes at a much lower price. I can't recommend the remake until more of its bugs are fixed. It would be nice to see more of its missing content restored, but having its glitches fixed should be the main priority of the developers now. The September 2022 update was a step in the right direction - now I hope that they keep the momentum going and turn the remake into the polished experience that it deserved to be.

_childDocuments_.review: XIII is a remake of a classic, first-person shooter that I already reviewed so I wont repeat myself here again, instead I will talk about what changed, the good and the bad.This time we can sprint and aim down sights with all weapons which is great. Healing is just a simple button press or hold. When I first saw the graphics I wasnt really into it but after playing through the game I started to like the different look and now I prefer it, the game is prettier to me especially the lightning, looking back at the original, im happy with how the game looks.With that being said, this game still has and probably forever will have plenty of bugs. Let me try list some:( my first playthrough was on hard difficulty and I had small number of issues but during the second playthrough on easy - for achievements - I encountered more problems, it got to a point where I couldnt progress so I switched to hard difficulty again and it was fine, I dont know why or how does difficulty create bugs but oh well )- enemies sometimes behave in a weird way, they freeze completely, stare into the ground or straight up ignore you ( you can still kill them but they wont react, making stealth sections not stealthy )- models bug out, arms get stretched, heads are see through- sound turns off when shooting- weapons dont reload half the time even though the animation plays- enemies seem to be also deaf to gunfire ( on easy difficulty )- you can get stuck in textures or straight up fall through them all the way down to the abyss which is just flat grey space- enemies float above ground- dialogue still plays even if you kill whoever is talking- friendly npcs love to stand still in one place and then teleport instead of walking/running- headshots show one picture three times- everyone looks emotionless which is awkward during serious cutscenes- lifeguard lady at the start can roll her eyes to the back of her head which is creepy- comic book text on alarms keeps playing even after restarting, making it look like alarm is activated when it isnt- enemies ignore hits from objects like chairs and brooms - death animations dont exist, everyone just kinda freezes and leans on the floorTheres probably more but this is enough to see that it just didnt work out. While im glad someone decided to remaster this game, it obviously went south and now all I can do I warn others to stay away from this mess.If you want to experience the story, play the original.

And the fact that they used the original audio dialogues for the previous game is so cool (I still know some of the lines by heart !). The character models seems more true to the comics than the old game and it's a nice touch !But that's about it. Graphics and dialogues can't do everything and can't save this mess of a game.Get the original version, really you'll enjoy it. It's the precursor in terms of cel-shading in gaming, and the immersion is so great.Please, I'm begging you, make it better, update it, fix the many bugs, correct the audio and all the other things people are talking about in the reviews. I'm ready to wait more, and change my review in the future. _childDocuments_.review: "Mr. Rowland? It's been such long time!" Unlike others, I've experienced no issues with the audio. Sounds come from the original version from 2003, which I actually don't mind.I have finished first 3 missions and i'm just gonna state issues that hit me right in the face. I have played it on the highest difficulty.- The animation of the lifeguard lady is terrible. Her face looks like she comes from some kind of Japanese cartoon. Until you see her white-then red eyeballs turning around until pupils show. That's some horror stuff right there.- When I killed the first guy with Kalashnikov, I could not pick the weapon up. I had to take another one, that was comfortably prepared for me a step further.- When I jumped into the water, I was suprised I can't hold any weapon in my hands; the inventory showed them locked. So I have swum above the water line. The weapons were no longer locked, yet I couldn't equip them.Also the transition between below the water and above it made me think my GFX card is having a stroke.- With the weirdest lighting I've ever seen, the teller behing the counter in the Winslow Bank looks like a ghost.- In the reminiscence in the bank safe, if you step into the Jones' path, she will start pushing you around, making you crouch and jump uncontrollably. What an odd experience.- Everyone needs to be hit with 2 chairs in order to "sleep". Sometimes with 3, who knows how aiming with furniture works. One bottle is enough, though.- Oddly, every bank security team member has 4 bullets in his .44.- Every single enemy has the same animation for being hit and for dying as well. If you score a headshot, the enemy takes his time to reminiscence about all his life choices, about his failed attempt for lacrosse career, about that time his now-ex-girlfriend wanted a baby and he rather left her alone with her dog and remembers he forgot to feed the dog on the 2nd of July 1997. Feels sad and somewhat angry. Then he slowly  gets back to the present, realises that he got shot in the head, lists all the gods he knows, choose one and say a prayer in his mind. Then he snaps back to reality, realising he's taking good hour before dying from headshot and throws his body against the floor immediately. Yes, that's how long it takes any enemy to die from a bullet in the head.- And the "best" for the last part. The horrendous AI. Remember, I played on the highest difficulty. Its description says "You're not supposed to make it." or something like that. Yep, I'm not gonna make it. Sane. Because I've never seen something so terrible. The description and tutorial tips say the AI is sharp and reacts to dead bodies. Sharp as a bowling ball and their reaction is audible "Hmm?". That's all.The AI just stands there, looking at you, pretending they are a flower pot. The "?" above their head occasionally changes colour.The AI is able to storm into the room it heard gun shots from and perplexedly run around you trying to figure out what does that dead body means.You can run towards AI from 50 meters, they will just point their gun at you and take 3 steps back, letting you punch them into oblivion with your bare hands.And the ultimate, godlike move to confuse the AI: closing a door.TL;DRDon't even look how they've massacred our boy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original game, I cannot reasonably recommend buying this remake in its current condition, even through I've only played the first level. This won't be a review per-se, but a summary of the problems that immediately arose in less than half an hour.The level played out like the developers didn't run any proper degree of QA on the game. Although the game would seem like the animations of the cutscenes are on point, they are a bit buggy. The gameplay itself didn't feel right at all, with the audio balance being a complete mess, there being times when I had no idea I was being shot, let alone shot at, and with the reloads bugging out a few times, playing out but not actually reloading the gun. I'm also not completely sure of if you're meant to have the full weapon selection available like the first game or not, but having a Wheel with eight slots for things to go in, but being only able to hold two weapons is deeply confusing me to the point where I can't tell if it's a design decision or a bug.Outside of that though, there's no FOV slider whatsoever, although I feel like what it runs at is adequate, but still not ideal. Not only that, but if you bought the game expecting the same multiplayer with bots that the first game had, you'll be shut down. It's local-only, and there's no bots at all. You can't even load a map on your own.So as of right now, I'd suggest just buying the original game, and use the Steam Guides to get that running at 1080p and with a playable FoV, and hold off on this remake until this review is amended when (and if) it's patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking forward to this remake, played the original on the PS2 when I was a baby, and played it on PC a month prior.So many things to talk about that are wrong about this game within 1.2 hours of gameplay I've encountered.Visuals:I actually don't mind how the game looks, besides when it goes into the flashback scripted sequences. I actually think the game looks really nice, though a bit dated on tech. The animations however just ruin all of that glimmer with random cut-outs and just odd choices. Gun animations feel like they're trying too hard to be over-the-top, which in the original game, it had a subtle comic feel to them. The character animations are not bad, but needs more variation, like in the original game. Enemies seems to have similar animations that doesn't match the kind of damage they've taken, unless you use a shotgun at time, which they go flying back a little bit.Gameplay: So you can't carry all of the weapons like in the original game. Can't carry a AK and an M16 anymore. Shooting enemies do stagger when shot, but it still doesn't feel right no matter what weapon you use, but what's the point of shooting everyone with all the neat looking weapons when I can just kill an entire room of enemies with a headshot with the starting pistol.The stealth doesn't work like the original game. It use to just be a sight-based bare-bones stealth, where you just knockout or kill enemies without being seen and hide bodies, and it did have a some thrill to it. Trying to land blows in this game is a hit or miss chance, and I've died multiple times in the Winslow Bank area because of weird bugs like that.There are other bugs with the gameplay, like how areas are not completely reset when you restart from the last checkpoint, some scripted sequences, like the bridge section in third mission can lock-up mid animation etc etcI've seen small game developers create such great games, so I don't see that as an excuse.This game really needs a lot of polishing and fixing up to do. Really disappointed how this game was just released like that. Refund while you can, or be hopeful they will fix this game with updates, otherwise I'm not gonna touch this game again. However I will keep it installed, just to check if any updates have improved the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The President of the United States of America has been assassinated. You wake up on a desolate strip of New England beach. The near-fatal impact of a bullet has left your head pounding, and your memory erased. What's more, the number "XIII" has been mysteriously tattooed on your chest, while your pocket holds a key to a New York City bank box. Head swimming in amnesia, you struggle to your feet only to encounter more assailants intent on finishing the job. To your shock, you handle the hitmen with the killing skills of a professional - before heading to the bank in search of any shred of information about your lost identity and your involvement in the President's murder. What lies ahead is a deadly quest not only into your shadowy past, but America's darkest corridors of power. [Ubi Soft]

name: Going Under
detailed_description: Going Under is a satirical dungeon crawler about exploring the cursed ruins of failed tech startups. As an unpaid intern in the dystopian city of Neo-Cascadia, you’ll wield office junk as weaponry as you make your way through the offbeat procedural dungeons beneath your company campus. The Future is Wack Failed businesses no longer just cease to exist--they sink beneath the earth, and their employees are cursed to wander the halls for eternity as monsters. It’s your duty to put these monsters out of their misery and repossess their assets--so that your boss can afford a new car, or something. Not All Heroes Get Paychecks Battle through the remains of failed startups themed off of gig workers, dating sites, and cryptocurrency. Uncover the true motives of your employer, a carbonated drink startup known as Fizzle, and their parent company, a subscription box manufacturer with an army of helpful shipping drones. Make friends with your co-workers! Hire a freelance goblin! Date a slime! Invest in crypto! Set a rideshare on fire! Fight Flexibly In the dungeons of Going Under, almost everything can be used as a weapon, from laptops to brooms to body pillows. Proper weapons can be found as well, but even they can break at a moment’s notice if you aren’t careful. Playing cautiously and picking the right weapon for the situation are musts if you intend on surviving your internship. Horrible Bosses And you thought your boss was a monster. At the bottom of the dungeons lurk the founders of the cursed startups, getting rich off of investments while their employees fight amongst themselves. Defeat them and return to the surface with their enchanted relics to empower the company you work for. Get Paid in Experience As you explore, you’ll encounter powerful Skills that change the way you play. Learn them at the Cafe and they’ll show up in future runs. Use a Skill often enough, and you’ll get it “endorsed” and available to start your expeditions with. Combine multiple Skills for crazy synergies, and you’ll be cleaning house in no time. A World of Characters Complete Tasks for your co-workers to gain Clout with them and unlock their unique bonuses. Learn more about Neo-Cascadia, the origins of Fizzle, and how the drone shipping empire known as Cubicle came to dominate the city. Can you save your company and yourself from going under for good?

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game feels remarkably similar to My Time at Portia (which isn't a combat-focused game).  I wouldn't really compare it to Hades because it isn't nearly as smooth and you don't really build up a "godly" combination of powers like you do in Hades/Risk of Rain.I think the appeal is more from the jokes told in the conversations and the atmosphere of the dungeons.  I think the combat is a bit clunky and can be difficult to aim but at least if you are used to i-frame dodging think it's not too difficult to beat everything in the game.  Instead of learning how to avoid attacks, I think it's easier to just hit spacebar at the right time and keep smashing them.  I found it way more difficult to figure out how to avoid attacks, especially for the "final" boss.I'll probably check back in after 100% achievements but I can say about 8.8 hours in that the achievements so far seem very doable in a reasonably short amount of time.  I doubt it'll take up to 100 hours like Hades did to reach 100% achievements (which is a relief).Edit: In retrospect after beating the Imposter mode for the first time, this game is a bit too grindy for me.  It feels so repetitive that it's hard to stay focused to remain at full health and the Rolodex achievement is too frustrating because cards come so rarely and some enemies bounce around too easily without any sort of aiming mechanism for the Rolodex cards.

Needing to get new weapons every other room or sometimes every room is really annoying and when a weapon does break you don't auto equip another weapon you're carrying is dunce level bad design.  Not showing any time of durability rating is weird when that's one of the things you'll constantly be worried about.A better camera and some polish to a few aspects of the combat would have meant a world of difference here.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stellar game! Easily one of the most enjoyable and creative rouge-likes I've played. Style is absolutely gorgeous and the soundtrack is a blast. Each dungeon has so much personality not only in enemy design but environmental and game-play factors as well. Story and characters are incredibly interesting and serve as wonderful motivators to keep pushing forward (not that I needed another excuse to test my metal in those enjoyably deranged and anarchic dungeons). Combat feels great and the chaos it presents is wonderfully highlighted by the interesting perk/shop/mentor systems they have in place. For only $20 this is definite must buy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was tons of fun. It has very addictive gameplay that is a perfect blend between dungeon crawling, rouge-lite mechanics and a simplified souls like combat. All of this tied together by the story and art direction which just oozes charm. The game offers up some very good challenges but does a great way of leveling that with a huge amount of passive skills that you unlock and use as you play. There is just so much to do and find here which makes the repetitiveness of its rouge-lite nature not get stale. The game does have a bit of an indie clunk to it but I think even this adds to the charm and the overall challenge sort of in the way a retro game does. Over all a high recommendation from me, might even be trying to 100% it. And it’s only Aggro Crab’s first game which just gets me pumped to see what they will come out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Going Under is one of my favorite rogue-like games, and I play a lot of rogue-likes (check my library). The best thing about this game throughout all the hours I have played is the satisfying, fun combat and the amazing characters that I would want to know (and already know. I'm looking at you Swomp). If you want an easy chart, here it is:Pros-Great character chemistry and story-Tons of items and weapons-Great combat with weapons that break, heightening the frantic nature of fighting goblins. (It feels like Breath of the Wild combat)-Distinct dungeons with different enemies-Jackie embodies the working spiritNeutral (Personal thoughts)-By end game (for me would be about 11-13 hours in), the other characters ran out of general things to say. I had played so many runs that this was inevitable, but you will hit a wall where runs will be your focus to see the credits-I ended up having a lot of similar runs because of certain items being dropped more often than others. This may only be my instance but YEET and Thunder Cloud were in every other run when I have a large percentage of the 100+ items unlocked.-Some of my later runs in the games would bug with the luxury car app and I would phase through enemies until the car ran out. (Some characters get stuck in geometry and ragdoll out, but I found these instances funny. I was never soft locked.)Cons-Not that many bosses (though each one is a highlight of the game)That might be it for cons, but I'll update it if I find something on my second play through. Overall, I really liked this game. The story was well paced and I loved the characters. I would love more content, but it is absolutely worth buying right now if you like this style of game.Original review at 4.9 hours:This is a really fun game where you fight failed startup company goblins and talk to coworkers that are a bit uncanny in how familiar they are. It's worth playing for the characters alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Going Under does a great job of bringing its satire and personality into its rogue-lite elements.  Even though the exploited intern isn’t a newly relatable tragedy to dissect, the game’s continuous and unexpected references to it as well as modern work life and the oxymoronic habits of technology conglomerates kept the occasional rogue-lite mundanity at bay. However, whether the pop culture gags will hold up well over time is something that remains to be seen.A favorite example of this thematic/gameplay dynamic is how the “student debt” curse creates a heavy ball and chain that restricts your movement. The concept of having a pinned skill is another clever addition that aligns with the interning premise. Roguey games often have a few busted skills that every run is basically leading up to, so picking one preferred power to start out with seems like a good compromise. It’s worth noting that the music is pretty catchy too (although the final boss theme drove me nuts).Switching between several breakable weapons was jarring at first, but as the rhythm of the game began to settle in, planning around the impermanent tools and understanding the properties of each one became quite rewarding. Nothing is there to directly teach you the technical details of weapon types, but I’d rather be confused than bored in this context. A few skill descriptions could be a little clearer though. I’m looking at you, Yeet.While their assistance can be pretty useful, the mentors’ sub-quests were usually bizarre, highly situational, and opposed to ‘main’ progress. Going out of the way to progress them a bit felt tedious, didn’t lead to any noticeable story changes, and was probably unnecessary. With the right luck, you might not even need those unlockable bonuses since Going Under can be inconsistently easy.While it’s not particularly strong as far as rogue-lites go, the strangely unique gameplay serves the comedy nicely. Just the concept of a rogue-lite (difficult, endless, and unpredictable with fragments of continuous progress) is an apt allegory for building a career. Every time the randomness or unpredictable physics deceived me, there were a dozen cheeky details that kept me engaged until the end. Since you can’t tell the same jokes forever, it’s for the best that Going Under can be reasonably short.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing rogue-lite, it's a shame it got overshadowed by Hades.Having played both games I can say with 100% confidence that they are both worth your time.The experiences they offer are completely different despite being part of the same genre.Going Under offers a unique take on rogue-lite, where weapons have durability and break.It's full of good writing and humor! It might be a short game (I finished the main story and all the quests within 16h of playtime) but it doesn't need to be big to be good.You can definitely feel the passion that went into this project, and I loved the story.Gameplay-wise the game is brutal and challenging at times, especially in the beginning, but once you get the hang of it, it's really a matter of whether or not you got the right setup (just like most rogue-lite).In Going Under you can pick up various weapons that are part of the environment or dropped by enemies. This ranges from thrash than you are supposed to throw at enemies, water guns, clubs, maces, spears, etc.While in the dungeons you can also find Skills which are basically powerups, stuff like Increased Crit, your weapons get bigger, objects you throw light up on fire, etc. (all of them have awesome names btw).Picking up the same skill on different runs gives you experience with said skill, and eventually, you can choose to start a run with (you can only start the run with 1 skill tho).There are also apps to be found within the dungeons, which grant you one-time-only powers, like transforming into a rainbow car for a few seconds or healing 1 heart.Finally, the various NPCs give you quests and are completing said quests to equip them as mentors. Completing more quests for the same NPCs levels them up, grating you more benefits from equipping them. These range from gaining more money to getting monsters to join your party in the dungeon, etc.I loved this game and I'm looking forward to the post-game content now!

_childDocuments_.review: If this game could have taken its first half and doubled its length or completely eliminated the unremarkable second half of the game, then this would have been an easy recommend.  Minor spoilers following:The opening up to the mid-point of this game is incredible: the setting, the art style, the characters you meet, the writing - all well done and overall charming.  The humor is varied, from explicit to subtle, but it never feels cheesy or cringey.  However, with any rouge-like, the gameplay is the bread and butter.  And here, the bread wasn't fully baked and the butter was over-melted and made everything a bit soggy.  What do I mean?  The combat feels like Katamari Damacy physics in a rougelike Zelda format.  Initially, this isn't bad - working your way through the first 3 dungeons is an enjoyable time as you make mental notes of different weapons, enemy cues, and power-up combinations along the way.  The enemies are wacky parodies and you get a feel for how to weave in and out.  However, the dodging and animation cancelling feels off, but everything is doable.  The fourth dungeon is an amazing take on the the rougelike genre itself within its own game - straight 'clear the enemies' objective, grab a weapon or powerup, move on, keep going, it gets harder, fight the boss, win.Then the second half of the game opens.  This is where the game ultimately becomes a rehashed and lackluster shadow of its first half.  All the NPC dialogue that was enjoyable between runs?  Eliminated.  The clumsy dodging, odd animation cancelling, and Katamari Damacy physics?  Frustrating and unwelcome against quick enemies who have now become damage sponges.  The dungeons are remixes of the first 3, but boredom, tediousness, and a lack of NPC interaction makes the world feel utterly dead.  Your coworkers simply stare at you between runs instead of having quirky dialogue that breaks up your attempts.  Clearing out the remixed dungeons in the second half wasn't a matter of them being hard, but dodging being 'janky' for lack of a better term.  Gameplay never sank into frustration, just boredom.The only thing I could perceive as fixing these issues is having a fixed camera angle and/or pulling the camera back.  Too often, especially in the later stages, the action was too chaotic to have any reasonable chance of dodging everything.  This is mostly in latter mob rooms; boss battles did not suffer from this - boss battles were extremely fair tests of skill.I absolutely enjoyed my first 4 or so hours of this game.  But the second half has soured the taste and ruined the meal for me.  However, I am looking forward to Aggro Crab's future work as they seem to respond extremely well to criticism and have made improvements to the game after its initial setbacks.

Throwing an item gives you a guide line that is seemingly meaningless to how far you'll actually throw or what kind of trajectory the item will have and with every item felt so slow that the enemies would just mosey up to you completely avoiding it and hit you before you could finish and most of the rooms weren't even big enough for the throw to work properly.The power-ups or artifacts or whatever they're called also presented a problem for me in that they are intentionally obscure opting to use flavor text for the actual description which didn't really add much to the experience other than obscurity for obscurities sake.The rogue-lite parts of permanent progression only seemed to be being able to pre-equip a power up if you played enough with it and having a mentor that did something like gave you slightly more money by choosing them after unlocking them through a task.At the end of the day, nothing is fundamentally wrong with the game, as in I didn't run into any crashes or technical issues and everything seemed to function as they designers intended, I just really disliked the game and after 30 mins I'm tapping out with no motivation to play it again especially if you compare it to the responsiveness and depth that similarly priced games in the roguelike genre have to offer, this just really isn't for me.

However, the latter half of the game falls off a bit in my opinion. The amount of story and dialogue becomes almost non-existent compared to the first half of the game, and literally no new mechanics or unlocks are introduced whatsoever. The game just becomes more significantly more difficult, but provides no rewards or tools to help you with your journey. You would still be using the same weapons, skills and mentor perks you used for the first half of the game, and it got quite tedious near the end of the game.I don't really understand why the difficulty ramps up as much as it does. The game is not mechanically deep enough to justify it, and it also heavily based on RNG. This made the game incredibly frustrating to complete and reach the end of the story.Despite all this, I still recommend at least checking out the first half of the game. The concept is fresh and awesome, but I hold a grudge because the endgame difficulty tilted me off the face of the Earth.

_childDocuments_.review: Legitimately one of the funniest games I've ever played - anyone who's spent time working in an office (especially a younger startup) will find the story and characters painfully relatable. Ray and Marv are basically every boss I've ever had.The gameplay is a really fluid combination of roguelike dungeon crawling progression with Breath of the Wild style weapon management and Soulslike combat mechanics with armor frames and invincible dodge rolls (there's also some hillarious references to souls bosses which I won't spoil so you can laugh at them yourself). It's challenging but always feels fair and the bosses are well designed and fun fights.Enemy variety can get a little samey sometimes and I wish the weapons and powerups were a bit better balanced - there are lots of situations where you don't really have a meaningful choice over what to pick up because there's one option that's clearly better than the rest. That said the ways powerups and weapons combine and interact lead to wildly different playstyles across runs (as a good roguelike should) which help keep the game feeling fresh even once you've seen every enemy type. Overall an extremely solid first game from a young studio that I can't recommend enough and I'm really looking forward to what Aggro Crab does next.

_childDocuments_.review: ~Game finished and all achievements acquired at the time of this review~Pros:-Hilarious satirical dialogue most can relate to in some way.-Movement and striking is very fluid and responsive.-Very large variety of skills and weapons in the game to acquire.-Music is outstanding and probably will be very overlooked!-Intuitive and unique quest system to unlock "Mentor" perks.-You can pet a wiener dog named Eclaire.Cons:-Progression permanently locks you out of older dungeons.-No replay value after the final encounter outside of just unlocking remaining skills.-Enemy ability to stun-lock you into taking successive hits can get absurd and frustrating.-Dungeon runs are far too short (took about 10-12 minutes or so on average).-Needs more than 3 base dungeons (not including the special 1 off encounter areas).Overall I find myself hard pressed to not recommend this game because frankly it was just an absolute pleasure to play through.  Every new experience had me chuckling to myself and it was quite relaxing despite successive failures.  I will say this; if you come into this expecting a typical rogue-like gameplay loop...YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED.  Do not go into this expecting a Dead Cells/Undermine length run that will slowly power creep your base character for hundreds of enjoyable hours.  While that is the case in this game too you will find reaching those caps will not take very long at all.  I took my sweet time and manage to fully unlock all skills and fully complete the game, both the achievements and bosses in about 21 hours give or take.If you want to pick up this game and truly enjoy it.  Just know going in that it is a more linear rogue-like with a distinctive ending point in my eyes.  It is absolutely fantastic don't get me wrong but I would love to see some content added for those of us who would like to push the envelope and be truly challenged by a game, as so many seeking rogue-like titles are also looking for.
