_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the finest, most rewarding RPGs I have ever had the pleasure to play. Though the graphics are simple, - thoughtfully crafted - isometric pixel portraits, the layers of detail are deliciously good. From intricate loops of music (varied for unique events & encounters), to expertly written prose (to get acquainted with your surroundings & dialogue options), this gem of an experience ate up my time with this first play-through/campaign (40 days on the peninsula) in big, chunky morsels of 2-4 hours at a time. I genuinely recommend this game to any fan of RPGs of the medieval variety. Yes - there is a LOT of reading, but please don't let that intimidate or overwhelm you. This is a true labor of love from a small team that deserves your time, and I'll be checking out the developer's first game, as a result of my successful time here, as a 'Roadwarden' !!!It is a gaming experience you won't soon forget (nor ever regret). I'm already anticipating (and planning) my next play-through, and it welcomes such a nuanced approach to problem-solving, relationship building, & resource management, journeying a land of villages, beasts, & mysteries a plenty. _childDocuments_.review: Although I can not claim to be an expert when it comes to games that are text-based, with my only experience of it here on Steam with Zombie Exodus and a couple of Flash-based titles from back in the day, the type of game that primarily focuses on text lends itself well to storytelling and those who are less focused on the visuals than they are immersing themselves into a world that is as deep as it is wide.That is to say Roadwarden has a lot to offer where the typical Roleplaying Game experience typically shines in, as you take the role of either a Fighter, Mage or Scholar acting as a 'free-roaming lawman' tasked with investigating the disappearance of a fellow roadwarden that previously visited the northern area some months prior, in which one has to explore the roads connecting the various villages and hamlets together alongside other places of interest.How you go about this is a specialty of the RPG genre, seeing as just simply surviving can be quite a challenge depending on the difficulty chosen as I would personally recommend the Standard difficulty for starting off with to see how far you can go and if it's either too easy or perhaps too tough for you on your first go. (With the 40 days being the standard time limit for how long you are allowed to explore the region, as the Casual difficulty removes this time limit altogether and starts you off with increased resources whilst Restrictive reduces the time limit down to 30 days and makes roaming around in night time more dangerous and even possibly life-endangering!)Though it should be noted that this is far from a hardcore RPG that punishes you whenever it can get the opportunity to, as any failed combat encounters resulting in your death will allow you to step back and try it again which, when combined with the ability to make upwards of several dozen save files, should allow a prepared player to not softlock themselves out of some better outcomes for particular quests or factions.Touching briefly upon the three classes, each one has their own unique advantages that should come expected for anyone who knows their RPG games well, with Fighters having a better melee weapon and specific combat options that guarantee a good or advantageous result over the other two, Mages allow the usage of spells via 'Pneuma' which slowly restores itself each day alongside the use of Spirit Rocks to refill it that can aid you in certain situations where a Fighter would struggle whilst Scholars take a more passive role, choosing not to excel in anything combat-related in favour of using their vast knowledge of the lands and it's mysteries to have a much easier time communicating with the local tribes and solving most puzzles and riddles easier than the other two classes.As far as the survival aspect of this game goes, seeing as I did hint at earlier, the four core stats you have to pay attention to are Vitality, essentially your health that acts as how well you are currently doing that plays into a few physical and endurance-based encounters, Hunger, which primarily acts as what allows you to overcome physical struggles, Gambeson, which acts as your armour and protection from various strikes against both monsters and human enemies alike, and Appearance, which is a surprisingly important factor that many end up neglecting as this impacts not only the prices offered by various vendors (both goods you sell to them and their own goods bought by you) but also how must they trust you, which affects what services they offer to you as well as the quests they give to you. (A fifth does technically exist, but it's class-based and varies from one player to the next)Now for a point of contention here, seeing as one may glance upon the game's description here on Steam and read that it is a 'Text RPG', giving them the vibes that this is some archaic and truly outdated artifact from the early 70's, and feel justified in dismissing this game outright.I can happily confirm that Roadwarden is not THAT old as far as inspirations goes thankfully! Seeing as it offers various charming illustrations of each of the game's many areas that you are likely to be visiting on multiple occasions, which helps to contextualize where you are and give some nice 'flavour' of sorts to the well-written dialogue that you'll be reading throughout your adventures in the north, giving some much-needed background variety that such titles as Zork and Night House (does anyone remember these games truly?) lacked due to the technology being so limited at the time.If there was any criticisms that I did have to raise, personally I would have liked more of an emphasis on the dangers of the north that you are tasked with exploring, seeing as you will rarely die on even the standard difficulty outside of certain battles where choosing the wrong action will guarantee death, (even with the upgraded gambeson and at full vitality + hunger!) since it would have made for a nice addition to throw into the Restrictive difficulty to make it even less forgiving for veterans who may know mostly how the game is played and desire some 'RNG' to a variety of possible encounters, most of whom are more dangerous and present some serious challenge to them!Other than lacking a little of that juicy 'roguelite' spice that I feel would have complimented this otherwise excellent story-focused game and a problematic bug with a specific NPC  that made progression a tad more frustrating than necessary, I feel like this is an overall satisfying experience for those who are after this type of RPG here, given the sheer amount of endings one can experience depending on how much (or little!) they did during their time in the region!In conclusion, for anyone who is after a medieval-themed RPG that takes homage from the likes of the Witcher series or Darkwood and puts the narrative in the limelight whilst gameplay takes second-stage and supports the wonderful storyline crafted by Moral Anxiety Studio, I would highly recommend giving Roadwarden a shot as it's the closest you will get to a modern text RPG that welcomes casual gamers who are willing to give this niche genre a shot which, given all of the effort put into this indie, is a journey that'll stand out from the crowd!Arriving at the post-review section for those who made it this far, here's some tips that I'll put under as spoilers for those who would rather explore and work out the game's mechanics for themselves, however for those who need a helping hand here:

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a wonderful call back to an almost forgotten genre of gaming - text adventures! There's a lot to love here - an engaging world awaits you, brought to life through terse writing, pixel art drawn in dirty sepia tones and a solid soundtrack to accompany your journey. This game really does ooze character - it's you and your horse, in a new world that you don't understand yet - but you will, if you're brave enough to search every nook and cranny!Keep an open mind while you're playing and you may surprise yourself with how much you can get wrapped up in this title. I hope you have a great time with Roadwarden - good luck out there on the road!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I immediately bought after playing the demo; I'm not disappointed at all! This game is filled with lore and mystery, sprinkled in with side quests. The character's personalities are touching and impactful, even those I don't really like. The option to choose what you say adds to the experience, and it actually affects the outcome of a situation– either right in that moment, or later down the line. And while the time limit (at least in easy game) is a challenge, it doesn't feel restricting or irritating. I love the characters in this game, their dialogue, and histories with each other. It feels like a real world I've actually stepped into! Initially, I thought a text-based game would upset the immersion, but it does the exact opposite. The combinations of art and descriptions really give me something to ground on, while allowing me to imagine the setting even further. However, I do have a nit-pick with this game, as great as it is. The journal. While it is such a helpful tool, and keeps track of characters, quests, dialogue, and lore– I would have loved either a section you can write on yourself, or have a more in-depth explanation of quests and events. There are plenty of little side quests, or extra info, that aren’t noted down in the journal, and the only solution is writing down on paper. And I completely understand why this wasn’t added! There’s more than enough information already given in the beginning, with lore and enemies you’ll encounter in the game; and if everything was added into the journal, it would get full and overwhelming quickly. Not to mention the amount of space it would take up, along with the game itself. And to be frank, if the main issue I have with a game is having to write down extra info– while it may be a hindrance, it doesn't make or break the game (for me, at least).

The musical score creates an atmosphere immediately and I found myself at times "hearing" the escalation and then with some literal dread pouring over the words that were slowly scrolling the screen. My eyes scrambling, yearning for the "thing" that happened hoping all the while I still have reliable options to progress forward.I love the depth of the NPCs, but the females seem to get a little more love than the males regarding their visual descriptions (just imo). _childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden provides a core RPG experience and a very good one at that. You can already see the mechanics of the game by looking at videos or reading other reviews. Here I'll try to focus on what makes Roadwarden uniquely good.If you're the kind of person who maybe likes things like levelling up, skill trees, inventory management, party management, but understand that these things are not critical or core to what makes an RPG, then there's a good chance you will enjoy this game. The only other question is your tolerance for reading.Note that this game still has satisfying and good inventory management! It's neither the primary draw nor the secret sauce of the game...Roadwarden rewards the player for entering the role of a roadwarden managing the Nameless Peninsula. You are rewarded for paying attention and for making guesses and deductions based on in-world information.Most RPGs are so bad at setting up the world and making it feel rooted and consistent, that I've been conditioned to automatically do some casual level of meta-gaming. While playing Roadwarden, I unthinkingly looked up on the wiki where can I sell furs and metal for the most coin. But then I realized, that Roadwarden is a game where I don't need to do that. Because if I consider what I know about the settlements -- where hunters are, what kind of wildlife exists in that area, what is their access to metals -- then I can easily deduce how prices would vary.A lot of things are like that in Roadwarden -- you can make reasonable assumptions and not get screwed over. And this is largely due to the healthy amount of respect for consistency and richness of setting that this game has.Instead of feeling like you need to meta-game in order to not waste your time, you end up wanting to take responsibility for your decisions, because it's so rewarding to make them, even when things don't work out perfectly. It validates your preferences and your understanding of the world. This is the hallmark of a good, core RPG experience. Roadwarden looks modest but stands at a zenith in this regard.At the end of the game, I found myself tearing up and I was surprised I got that attached. That attachment was fostered by how the game managed to make the Nameless Peninsula come to life. From detailing humble flora, to detailing the weird mix of familiar and alien fauna; from describing the activities and life of each village, to creating complex interlocking interests and conflicts between those villages. I was sad my journey was over because this world had captivated my imagination.The game is not as flexible or as reactive to your decisions as it might seem. It does do some intelligent smoke and mirrors. It appears deeper by some amount of obfuscation of the numeric values behind the mechanics. But the balance is tastefully struck and appropriate for the kind of game that Roadwarden is.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that had never touched a text-based RPG before Roadwarden was, for me, an all new experience and one I will likely never forget. Though I wish I could, just to experience it fresh again.The sombre music and charming visual style would be enough for me to recommend this to others. Hell, I even voted this as my best soundtrack of 2022 as it is one that, despite having finished the game a short while ago, I keep coming back to just to listen. Yet to compliment the sound and style of this game there is an equally compelling story. Suspicious locals, occult activity, and classic bandits, all staples of any solid fantasy world, are just a handful of obstacles you will encounter whilst unravelling the mysteries of the wild peninsula you are tasked with exploring and securing after the former Roadwarden abandoned their post.From the gruff owner of Pelt to the carefree folk of Creeks there are plenty of interesting people to interact with, learn about and even befriend, and yet, despite this definite presence of others, the tone of this game is one of solitude. Being the titular Roadwarden you have no choice but to move on eventually to aid other folks and continue your work.Be it the vivid descriptors and charming dialogues or the many mysteries of the land, something will keep you coming back (if you somehow manage to not binge it all in a couple of sessions as I did).A long and somewhat meandering review admittedly but all to say one simple thing: This game was an absolute delight to experience and I hope that it gets more attention than it already has.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game in my wishlist for a while now and I finally decided to go for it with the 2023 winter sale. If anyone is having doubts about purchasing because of the reading aspect, DON'T! JUST GO FOR IT! It's absolutely worth your time. Even if you're not much of a book reader, the writing is so smooth and captivating that you'll never feel bored. It gives you the perfect amount of information without getting too lengthy, plus you get a vivid picture of the characters without having to see them. You'll find yourself very eager to continue your journey and discover new places, wondering what kind of dangers you'll encounter... Take the leap and become the Roadwarden!Most importantly, if time limits stress you out, play the casual mode and you can take your adventure at your own pace. _childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played text games by Infocom back in the early days of PC gaming, Roadwarden should be right up your alley.  It's like playing the later Zork games where graphics were added to supplement the text story.  This game adds nice music to enhance the experience.  The overall interface of Roadwarden is really stylish - pixel graphics, a nice text font, and as an old school gamer, I fell right into the groove.  I haven't played much of this game yet, but wanted to give a quick review of the aesthetics and gameplay because it's unique and is the main draw to enjoying this game.  The story, what little I have played of it, just drops you right into a dire situation, and you are presented every step of the way with different ways to ask or answer questions when meeting characters, and you have access to typical RPG game elements such as inventory and other things.  Happy I have this in my collection.  I will be playing this to completion, and hope more games like this appear in the future.  Just looking now, I own almost all the Steam games by Assemble Entertainment.  I never knew this publisher, but I guess they release a lot of games that appeal to old gamers like me. If you gamed on a Commodore 64 computer like I did, then you might want to give this game a try :)

_childDocuments_.review: Its a masterpiece. _childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, I had a wonderful time playing it. I came into it having never heard of it, I just stumbled on it during the steam sale, the art style caught my eye, and after trying the demo I very quickly realized I would enjoy it and bought the full game.The world and story really immersed me, I found myself thinking about the game when I wasn't playing it, what I needed to do next, what decisions I should make. The writing is good, the cast of characters is varied and interesting, I enjoyed getting to learn more about each character I met, there was often a lot more depth to them than I expected.I played through it twice, the first time my Roadwarden did achieve their goal, but I failed to accomplish a lot of the other things I hoped to, so I almost immediately started a second playthrough! Which was much more successful, although I'm still tempted to play it again sometime soon and see how differently things can turn out.The choices around your Roadwarden are nice, I really like the dialogue choices and the moments where you decide who your character is, as well as building up skills and collecting items to be able to get through different encounters. I struggled a lot more with money in my first playthrough, the second time I got to the point where it largely wasn't an issue for me,The lore around the world felt like it was introduced at a good pace, and I enjoyed the general concepts around it too, like the different views on the wilderness and the creatures, it made me want to know more. The length is good, I'm a pretty quick reader so I probably got through it faster than others might, I was definitely disappointed in a way when it ended but that just speaks to the quality of it, it didn't overstay it's welcome by any means, it didn't feel padded out unnecessarily, it's a nicely contained story.There's more eloquent reviews, (I think this is actually the first ever review I've left) but I wanted to sing the praises of this game because it hit in exactly the right spot for me, and if you enjoy text-based RPGs I would say absolutely pick this one up, heck, even if you don't, just try the demo! See if it draws you in like it did to me. Excited to see if the dev makes more games like this, because I'll certainly play them :) (and coincidentally noticed I own their older game, Tales From Windy Meadow, through a bundle, so I'll be trying that!)

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most delightful world's I have ever had the esteemed pleasure of playing. It deserves a thousand compliments for its story, mysteries, adventure, world-building, intrigue, characters, and so much more. Playing as the titular role of Roadwarden, you are to explore the Northern Peninsula with the intentions of establishing trade relations with your home city of Hovlavan. You have 40 days to accomplish all you can and return home. A piece of the game I cannot get enough of is the fact  Everything about your character and your home town of Hovlavan is designed by you as you play the game, with NPCs asking you occasional questions of what it's like in the cities. This small detail is one of my favorite parts of the game because as you yourself learn more about this world and its system, you make a true and deep connection to your character. There are many missions to accomplish, and the game makes completing those missions so rewarding. Every quest is its own saga-length adventure, I can hardly recount all that I've accomplished in my 40 days. After this review I am certainly going to play the game again; while I know some of the world's secrets now, there are many quests I never finished in time. And I am eager to see a whole new side of the game by playing as a different class. Perhaps I will be a Mage this time around.I have never before written as long of a review, because I have never before had so much to say about a title. TLDR, It is simply one of the most intriguing and rewarding worlds I have ever experienced. And I'm so glad that there is enough mystery to play through it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a fantastic game that transports you into a rich and well-crafted fantasy world, similar to a D&D campaign but with an open-world RPG twist. It's not just a "Choose your own adventure" story with branching dialog options - you get to explore and create your own path.When I first heard about Roadwarden, I was hesitant to try it out because I'd never played a text-based RPG or visual novel before. But I'm glad I gave it a chance because it turned out to be a really enjoyable experience. It reminded me of the illustrated skill-check sections in Pillars of Eternity, but fully fleshed out with more depth and complexity. It's not officially "Steam Deck Certified" yet, but I haven't had any major problems playing it on the Deck. The only minor issue I had was with the touch-pad cursor being a bit finicky when selecting small UI elements like the scroll bar.Overall, I highly recommend Roadwarden to anyone who loves fantasy fiction, D&D, or well-crafted RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange mix of death stranding set in the witcher world. _childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is an  title for anyone who craves a superbly-crafted, meaty, and mature role playing experience.For fans of Disco Elysium, The Witcher, Citizen Sleeper, Planescape Torment — Roadwarden is its own beast yet sits with the greats in terms of ambition and execution.From the moment you reach the title screen and are greeted by random tidbits of lore, to the introduction of the conversation system, and to the unveiling of the player inventory and journal with their wonderfully-written (and evolving!) descriptions — a lot of love and care went into Roadwarden's creation, and boy did it pay off in spades.Support this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game expertly cuts away a lot of the cruft of the RPG genre, while still keeping a lot of its mechanics. Instead of overly-complex or abstracted combat and traveling, the moment-to-moment play resembles more of a visual novel, with you keeping tabs on your reputation, managing your time, maintaining your needs, and thinking critically about the words you're reading. Every part of the game is delicately interwoven - the narrative, themes, UI, and mechanics - and it all comes together to create a melancholic whole, every piece reinforcing the desperation, not only to remain alive, but to remain whole, a struggle that every other character in the game also faces. The art is occasionally a bit crude, and I don't feel like it's particularly well-served by pixel art, but such choices are cost-effective, and the art is primarily used to accentuate the writing anyway. Also, as is often the case for games with this many words, there are several spelling and grammatical errors, but rarely did they take me out of the experience. The writing allows for a lot of player agency, and it's high-quality enough to make more reading feel like a reward as opposed to a slog. Overall, I'd say the structure of the game alone is enough to make it one of my favorites, fitting itself snugly between two good genres to make a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like Roadwarden is the perfect introduction to the text-based genre of RPGs for people who haven't played them before. It's simple enough and has *some* visuals to the keep the casual user engaged, while also delivering a compelling narrative and immersive atmosphere. My one and only criticism is that there is a lack of meaningful choice when it comes to dialogue, so talking to characters can sometimes feel like an exposition dump. Ofcourse, there are moments where how you choose to conduct yourself actually matters, but it's less roleplaying a personality and more like "what do I say to this guy so I don't have to earn his trust by doing chores instead". Overall, an easy 8/10 if you're into narrative-driven experiences and don't mind reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It is a modern take on old school text RPGs.  It is essentially a choose your own adventure picture book mixed with some classic rpg management of things like, gear, food, hp, ect. You get to choose where you want to go and when. Doesn't hold you hand by telling you where to go, the player needs to make some inferences to figure it out.  I like the story and found it pretty compelling and a bit hard at times. There isn't really any modern game like it and fits into a really niche category. I will be trying some more games from this dev studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The positive reviews couldn’t be further from the truth. What kind of garbo do people read that the writing in this “game” feels like gold to them? Usually, I can appreciate good writing regardless of whether I like the story, but this is just a glorified fan-fiction level of writing. It’s wordy where it needs to be short, and short where it needs to expand, but most of the times, it’s wordy everywhere…Although the Pillars of the Earth was largely disappointing for me, it does a much better job in being a game, visual novel and book. My advice is, play the demo and don’t expect it to get better. P.S. (to myself) If it's a visual novel, don't put off playing the game soon for at least two hours. Otherwise, it'll be too late to return it. I was too late with this one...
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The worst part of this game is loudly proclaiming "This is made in the anime tiddy game engine" and it being correct.Phenomenal game thus far.  Only gripe in writing I've had is seeing the same text for magic used in two different situations.  Otherwise the characters are likable and well written.  I think it will lend itself to multiple playthroughs, I'd estimate I'm at about 1/4 of the way through based on me being on day 10 of normal difficulty
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed playing through this game. It has some fantastic world building that really draws you in, and it has that can't-put-it-down quality that you get from a good book.It plays mostly like a puzzle game in my opinion: the jist of each settlement is that "you turn up - you get told you need to earn the trust before they'll help with anything - you do odd jobs to earn trust to get info", with most of these jobs requiring you to carefully plan your traversal of the map in order to preserve your health/resources/time - hence the puzzle element. This can feel a little tired during a second play through, though, as you go back and forth again and again.For anybody who enjoys a narrative-driven, thoughtful game, that is set in an engrossing game world: this is a must-play
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I usually play the games for 10 minutes and unistall them, this game has keeping me reading for 10 hours, it's really well written.If you like to play easy and discover everything the game has a console with cheat commands that makes the experience easier so you can explore everything in just one play.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is reminiscent of those CYOA adventure games on paper where you make a choice and flip to a speicific page. To be honest with this review, I played on the easiest difficulty (without time limit) so I can see as much as I can in one playthrough. With that said I can say that the story and the different choices given are thoughtful and are indeed consequential. Overall if you like text-based adventure games, it's a solid 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Can't remember the last time I played a text-adventure, but this is a good one. World-Building is nice, it's fun to explore the villages and forests, foraging for food and chatting with strangers. Writing is great as well, no lore-dumps and it has enough little details to make the world come alive without reading it being a slog.Definitely give this a try if you find the setting interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: There's something incredibly charming about this game. It's got simple yet pretty pixel graphics, and while very much a visual novel it has a lot of interesting choices and interactions that come up. Unlike most VNs I've encountered it's still very much an RPG, you get to make a lot of choices about who your character is, what they want, and where they came from. Also, there's a lot of work that went into actually studying the daily life of folks in the middle ages. Despite how fantastical the world is the people in it feel very grounded and real because of this. (Bonus points: has queer people existing in a way that doesn't make you feel like there's a dev giving themselves a "world's biggest ally" medal for doing the bare minimum. There's just, queer people that exist in the world and it feels natural and nice.)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden was a game that I could not stop thinking about days after having completed it for the first time. Yet, even now, I struggle to gather my thoughts about the game in anyway that might prove helpful to would-be players without simply saying "It's great" or "I love the vibe".I am someone who struggles to read for long periods of time, preferring audiobooks over the written word (it's easier to listen than it is to actively read, at least for me), I found myself utterly absorbed in Roadwarden. I hadn't truly played a proper text-based RPG up until this point and was unsure how I would fair, but I was nonetheless intrigued by Roadwarden's visual style and music; it was strong enough for me to take a leap of faith and give the game a try.I am very glad I did for I found Roadwarden to be an immersive and engrossing adventure, the likes of which I wish I could find more often in video games. The game is full of struggle and hardship. It focuses on the problems of the commonfolk in place of any Dark Lord or Ancient Evil, something I found to be entirely refreshing, with many villages wondering how they are to survive the coming Winter and what they may have to do or sacrifice in order to see Spring.The music in the game is wonderful, both relaxing in town and mysterious on the road, yet remains solemn and lonely. It never quite lets you fully let-go of your concerns and paranoia, even in the relative safety of a village or in the walls of a house, thanks to the ever-present danger from both the wildlife and those who do not trust you or seek to use you for their own ends.Suffice to say, I heartily recommend the game to anyone who has an interest in roleplaying and stories involving exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best gaming experiences I've had in recent years. An old school text adventure that's deep enough to make you really feel like your choices matter. I've uncovered ancient secrets, made and lost friends, fought bloody battles and gotten embroiled in complicated political intrigue... and that was just my first play through. The character creation options are just enough to make you feel like a unique person without having to get bogged down with character sheets and the like. At points I found myself genuinely moved by the story and you can't ask for much more than that from a narrative driven game. Spoiler Warning...When you first leave the camp instead of heading west to the inn, head east to the little stone building, inside look for the trapdoor. there's a box in there with a health potion which you can give to the trader in Howler's Dell (West of the inn and then north of the ruins). Pretend I left it there for you, safe travels Roadwarden.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Maaaaaaaaan, if you grew up with old school text adventures, I highly recommend this. Interesting plot, good replay value, fairly fleshed out characters and some little moral dilemmas. It's honestly criminally good for what it is and at just about $10, I think it's a great buy. Definitely got my money's worth and more - art its pretty lovely, soundtrack is great, and you just can't beat that nostalgia factor. If you're not super into text adventures/visual novels; this is the one to try and maybe even stoke a love for this simple but classic genre.  5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is far and away the best narrative game I've ever played, and I do not say that lightly. This the game I have always been looking for since my early exposure to text adventures on the Commodore 64. There is enough of all the elements that make such games work, and especially the writing and music are exemplary—which matters a lot since you'll be reading a lot. In most games this begins to feel like a chore but I happily did so for hours on end. The balancing of goals with very realistically portrayed NPCs is amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I gave Roadwarden a chance. A slower paced, interactive novel game isn't normally my first choice, but I do love a good story with memorable characters. While it is heavy on the reading, it is beautifully written. It gives me subtle hints of Patricia Mckillip (if you're familiar with that fantasy author), and it had some unexpected twists that gave me a gasp. I love how distinct the characters are, as well (Foggy, don't ever change). If you're looking to read a solid mystery story that includes you in making important decisions, consider Roadwarden. You will not be disappointed.I don't typically like time limits, so I chose the casual play-through. It allowed me to explore every bit of the map and dig into all the quests without pressure, but if you like that added tension, there ARE time limit options =)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A text based, great immersive indie RPG. Cheap and great play over a weekend.    4/5+Music and Sound are great at carrying the tone and environment it wants. Whilst there's maybe less variety than i might want whats there will keep you in the spirit of things.+ Lots of good world building and lore if you look for it.+Seemed to be a great deal of freedom in how you go about things. you can play a psycho brawler and be treated as such, but its completely up to you and there is rarely a perfect solution to any problem-/+ Old School RPG. (This is a + for me, a - for others) Its entirely Text based with very few visuals. It wants you to be reading and paying attention. take notes (only a few are taken for you) and use your head, you will not have an objective marker or guide beyond its very quick tutorial. -Some might find it a bit shortIf you want a RPG that lets you experience being A Ranger in a fantasy setting, this is a pretty decent choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Only played for a few hours, but I'm definitely hooked. This is one of those games where the entire appeal is the mystery of discovery. You know nothing. You start from scratch and build in true RPG fashion of what kind of person you want your character to be. I highly recommend it. You can tell they took a great deal of time writing out a ton of dialogue options and fully fleshing out the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: There's definitely a bunch of text-based adventure games I played on browser and mobile long time ago, but none of them are as intricate or fleshed out with their systems and quests as this game.The game gives you a big piece of land to explore and do quests on but you have to manage your time carefully before you have to finish your campaign. For a first playthrough I did not look up any guides - figuring out the mysteries is half the fun. For my second playthrough, I instead tried optimizing using knowledge from my previous playthrough because I got some bad endings for certain quests.Fun stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique storytelling in a good way. The game rewards you for exploring everything and you can find lots of hidden stuff simply by being inquisitive. In certain sections the game takes on a zork like method of finding things and you have to visually analyze the setting and type what to search for. This game is like a modern classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply engaging game where choices truly matter. Beautifully written but the text never bogs the player down, as so many other text-intensive games do. After completing my first playthrough, I can't stop thinking about the story -- the secrets I learned, what I could have done differently in light of those revelations, and so many micro interactions that have a macro effect that I didn't realize until hours deeper.I don't usually feel compelled to play a narrative game twice, but Roadwarden has given me every reason to do so by providing storyhooks and beats just out of my character's grasp.This is the one game I would rate 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game, there's not much bad to say about it, except the fact that it's kind of boring and dull. If you enjoy reading an inordinate amount of dry descriptions, this game may be for you. It's filled with basic characters, the usual light fantasy monsters, and tidbits of worldbuilding we've seen a hundred times.The game promises a gritty adventure in a realistic world, and delivers it, but in a way that is simply not that entertaining. There is a striking lack of sound effects, visual effects, or any kind of support to make it more palatable.Perhaps text-based RPGs aren't for me, again it's not a bad game, and kept me engaged for a while, but at some point I realised I didn't really care about 90% of the text that was presented to me, and I don't really care about any of the characters or what's happening in this little piece of the world. It's as if in pursuit of realism, the game sacrificed entertainment value. All of these scenarios that happen are very real, feel very immersive, and that's something I value greatly. But that's not enough to make something fun. And if it's not fun, why bother?
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps one of the most compelling games I've played in recent memory. Narratively it is unmatched by anything else you will find on steam with perhaps the exception of the first two banner saga games. The time mechanic forces you to choose between a plethora of bad decisions. The characters are excellent, the writing is excellent, the pixel and and sound track are out standing. For those seeking a proper story driven game I cannot recommend this highly enough. A shining example for other developers to follow. Excellent / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: must buy for everyone who likes himself a good RPG, (visual)NOVEL. Id say its a tat better then degrees of degeneracy which is an adult game. Anyways both games do a great job at writing, mystery, adventure. Also roadwarden is surprisingly cheap for what its worth for me. 9.3/10 if you buy it for 6bucks id say 10/10 purchase. 100% worth (if you like to read)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours in but I already know I will have multiple play throughs of this game. The characters are just as dynamic as the world itself and the game lends itself to replayability, I have so much left to explore but as one other review below mentions, this game has made reading cool again - and I couldn’t be more excited to read everything I can. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One time I got a fantasy book from the library and it got recalled and I never read the ending. After 13 hours, this was my experience with Roadwarden. By my story end I solved no mysteries and failed the main quest because the arbitrary time limit ended the game before the story was done. A game about exploration punishes you for exploring. The writing is not good. A few compelling set pieces are buried in an avalanche of boring exposition with forgettable characters that explain their backstories rather than show any agency or character. Maybe there's an interesting story here but in a the time it took to watch a full season of Game of Thrones plus one of the Lord of the Rings films, I couldn't find it. Play Disco Elysium or Planescape Torment or Choice of Robots. This is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptional game that I liked very much. The descriptions combined with the art style are evocative and thematic and fit very will with the atmosphere of the game. This is one of the best "make your own adventure" games I have ever played, and I have played a ton of them. Decisions matter in this game and you will find yourself stressing about them. For a more casual experience, I would suggest playing the "Easy" mode which would allow you enough time to do most of what you want to accomplish and make a lot of money by gambling etc. However, the absence of a time limit of the easy mode does detract a bit from the atmosphere of the game, so for those willing to play and replay this game (and it is good enough to justify at least two playthroughs) I would suggest the normal difficulty.Eudocia for the win.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden has been one of my favorite games this year. Almost like a single-player DnD adventure game with a wonderful mix of character building, combat, and exploration. At some locations you need to type in actions that you want to do in that location. I've heard that some people struggle with these more open-ended prompts, but I've found that an open mind and a couple tries are enough to solve them. I love the exploration style in this game and how the map style doesn't clutter the locations too much. One problem I've had is that I never seem to have enough money or food, even with fish traps (yes, plural), foraging, and selling every bit of antler, horn, and pelt I can get my hands on.  A fair warning, however, this game is very text-based and if you skim through the lore you'll likely miss a clue for the quests. I've had some problems with the quests in Gale Rocks as the mini-tasks for the villagers are not put under quests and if you need to look back at them you have to scroll up into the archive, which gets deleted after a certain point. The quest information is organized in massive paragraphs in chronological order, which is honestly kind of painful to read and makes it difficult to look back at any info you forgot.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully written, with complex characters and true moral ambiguity. Too many RPG's rely on grimdark, sensationalist violence to convey a sense of high stakes. Roadwarden genuinely creates emotional investment through fully fleshed-out, flawed characters whose arcs are influenced by your choices. And it's not afraid to showcase the full spectrum of human emotion, bringing moments of joy and connection along with wrenching choices and tragic backstories. It's right up there with Spiritfarer in how deeply the game imprints itself on your psyche. Based on other reviews, I initially played with the 40-day time limit, but the deadline really stressed me out. I get why some people like the time constraint, but I love that it can be disabled. Removing it allowed me to fully enjoy both the story and the mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of my favorite games since I first picked it up.The story and the world it's set in is highly engaging. As you travel through the world, interact with people, and make your choices, it really feels like you have a sense of autonomy as a character. The people you meet on your journey feel interesting and believable as well. As you progress, you feel a sense of consequence, and I've personally enjoyed trying the different backgrounds to see how they affect each playthrough. It manages to be challenging in places as well, which only adds to the fun.If you enjoy a well-crafted story, this is a truly excellent game to try. The world, the characters, and even the soundtrack help weave a compelling narrative that's absolutely worth taking the time to explore. This is one of those games that I'd love to experience again for the very first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A simple and beautiful game with a surprising amount of complexity! I loved the dynamics between the tribes and the characters in them! There was a point where certain characters surprised me with their true goals and motivations, and I feel like there were layers of intrigue that I missed by playing a mostly honest character. Above all though, this is a game about finding your own purpose and meaning in the struggle to survive and make a better world for yourself or others. For example, your character's religious outlook is entirely dependent on what you choose, but also what choices you make.  Different characters react differently based on the beliefs you have, which is so rare and cool for a game. For me I fell in love the land and the strange differences between it and our own. It was a lovely experience of difficult and meaning moral choices but above all I fell in love with is strange and surprisingly detailed little world. I am looking forward to what this dev does next!All in all heartily recommend if you like text based story RPGs at all, what a great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I certainly liked it. Has a lot of charm. A lot of attention to detail. Its not too difficult...but its certainly not easy unless you on your second play-through or being really careful about your plans for the day(s). Cute graphics, dialogue, sound and music. And a lovely coherent narrative/world to explore. Plenty of choice. but be very careful. U can easily spend too much or waste valuable rare items/potions if you not careful. Its a lovely story with plenty of choice and intrigue. Give it a go. X.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely game.  Well written, with an enthralling story, immersive world, and charming retro pixel-art style.  Fantastic sound design as well (both music and ambient effects) that pulls you in.    If you enjoy sword-and-sorcery text-based adventures, this is a must-buy for the (very reasonable) price.======UPDATE after having completed a couple of playthroughs.  I was continually surprised by the depth and quality of lore, story, and characters.  Writing is first-rate.  Encountered a couple of trivial bugs that did not detract from enjoyment at all.  Recommend even more strongly after continued play.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, I cried. I think this is the first review I've ever left but I enjoyed this game so much I just have to share.The story, characters, setting are all beautifully written. First game in a long long while where I knew each of my decisions would matter in both the short and long run. The lovely pixel art scenes add way more than I thought they would to such a text heavy game.There were a few point I wish I had saved beforehand so I could see how they would change the ending but I'll have to put that aside for another time as each full play through is quite a time commitment. I fell asleep thinking about this dang game during my whole first play through, I hope the developers are able to make more worlds and stories like this one because I'll absolutely be playing anything they put out after this. Amazingly done.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's not too big, but well-made. The roleplay part of the game nicely crafted. I love the narrative part of it, the story is pretty simple, but interesting, mysterious and unpredictable in some cases that's really nice if you ask me. Overall color palette and mood left some good memories. Also the large amount of text created a pleasant impression, as if I was reading a book.Have just one issue though — music design. It is kinda annoying after half hour playing. But no worries, I just turned it off and launched youtube ambient music, including 10 hours long ambient music about deep space, really nice one.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It is a beautifully written game, the story is really rich and can vary wildly depending on type of game mode you pick. I did the one where there wasn't a time limit just so i could have the chance to sort of explore the game a bit more. The choices and there following consequences make you question whether your doing the right thing even when it doesn't feel like it. Beautifully done and I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Since this is a visual novel-like game, I expected some good writing, which is lacking in modern games. But the game meets you with California-style writing, where no matter of setting, the characters speak and act like modern days college kids and things like mix gendered military units are more common than nowadays. I do not mind this, it is just already too much of this on the market, and sometimes you actually want something that feels creepy-authentic.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played very far, but I love it so much, already. There's so much *character* in the writing, and the orange/sepia graphics calls me back to my youth (I only wish there were an option to turn it green, in case I wanted more of an Apple IIe vibe than my old 286). Every NPC I've met was characterized well and the lore is very interesting. The world as portrayed is grimy and I'm here for it 100%. And the music! If you think you might like it, just get it. I don't think you'll regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked those "Choose you own Adventure" books as a kid, then this will probably be right up your alley. And you don't have to keep a notebook (unless you really want to) since all the info is tracked in game. Took 8 hours for my first playthrough and I didn't even get close to 100% completion, so good replayability along with character build and NPC interactions.The writing is very good and the characters don't feel flat or forced. Standard difficulty is not too easy nor too difficult, although it does require you to actually manage resources. If you don't like being constrained to a time limit, Easy mode doesn't have one.Definitely giving this another playthrough or 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst this kind of game isn't for me personally I can see an audience for this. So I'm going to give a postive review despite me not liking it.Great lore, punishingly difficult (a little too much imo) and a nice little plot wrapped up in a simple RPG. You will have to enjoy reading though, a lot of prose.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is, by far, the best game I've played this year. Estrangement is a difficult feeling to create in fantasy nowadays. And yet, this game managed to create a universe so rich, so special and so unique that I felt it in the first twenty minutes of playing it. Never had choices felt so important. You're always doubting your place ; you are important and you don't matter, your actions may bear grave consequences, but you're bound by the choices of others.The ambience in this game is mind-blowingly good. The music, the writting, the visuals ; it's a perfect mix. You should play it. You will not and cannot regret it. It will follow you all day long, and after playing it you'll hardly forget any minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Went far beyond my expectations. The story, characters and quests do well to make the world feel alive, and your roadwarden feels like less like the main character and more like someone surviving in a land that does not want them there. While I had a couple issues with the sections that required inputs, I enjoyed my experience thoroughly and hope the developer goes on to create more. Now stop reading this and spend the rest of your braincells reading the text in-game!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. A simple text based RPG with some images in the background, except it's not as simple as it seems. I love especially that throughout your story, you can develop your background and character very deeply. However, don't expect all of it to come before you load into the game. The more you talk to other characters, the more you can set the world up and give it background. Only thing I wish is that there was more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game an easy 9/10Positives:Great price for the size of the game. A single playthrough in normal difficulty will take around 15-25 hours, and there is some level of replayability if you want to find other endings and with a different class.Amazing OST, it really fits the atmosphere and was very enjoyableIt can be very rewarding for the more observant players, as there will be some events or interactions where you can really mess up and lock yourself out of interesting storylines if you weren't paying attention.Active dev in the community forumA VERY wide diversity of endings, not just for the main character but for side characters, locations and storylines.Easily one of the best games I've ever played, I'll be sure to be on the lookout for games in this style or by this developer in the future.Negatives:You'll probably have to save-scum a bit at one point or another. Either you'll run into a big cat and lose all your life, hunger and armor or you'll make a trip somewhere only to realize that the trip was useless and you've lost half a day, or you'll fail a quest because now you can't get to were you neeeded to be in time. Without a bit of save-scumming your first playthrough will have some very annoying parts, and you'll probably have to play the game again to get a resolution to all the main storylines. Obviously save-scumming isn't the end of the world and it's a nice way to change the difficulty, but if you end up abusing it too much it really takes away a lot from the story.The diversity in the game can be a little excessive at times considering the setting. There are gay, lesbian and bisexuals individuals, a polyamorous couple and even a nonbinary person. If this were Cyberpunk 2077 or a game in a setting where that makes more sense then it won't break your suspension of disbelief, but in a game that has a very medieval setting it absolutely takes you out of the setting. Maybe if it were addressed directly or involved in the story, e.g. the main religion in the game opposes these beliefs but the pagans are accepting of them (so it becomes another plot point in the game) or vice versa, it would be less noticeable and wouldn't break the player's immersion, but as it stands it did end up doing that a lot. However, the way that diversity was added was the correct way. Instead of it being something that you immediately discover about a person (which can end up feeling like forced inclusivity with no purpose other than pandering), their diverse sexual preferences were usually something you'll only discover after talking to them for a bit, and the way it was mentioned was very natural and logical and did not feel forced. So maybe the setting wasn't the best for this kind of inclusivity and it could have been integrated into the story to make it more reasonable, but at least it never felt very forced, just a bit jarring at times.The pace falls a little bit halfway through the game and it occasionally feels like a little bit of a struggle to continue, but it picks back up. Or maybe I only felt that because I completed it in two sessions so I just got tired halfway through, who knows.Occasionally you will make decisions that seem very small but will actually completely affect the ending that you get, which can be a little unexpected. This one is less of a con and more of an in-between, as it leads to interesting and unexpected endings but can sometimes lock you out of desired endings simply because of a small decision that you made much earlier on.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A breathe of fresh air. It has the old school RPG feel without the tedious mechanics or weird puzzles. You still have to do a decent amount of connecting the dots, but you don't ever feel lost and the game never stops feeling fun. The text never gets too out of hand either, they give you enough context to really bring the world to life without it getting exhausting. If you are a fan of fantasy RPGs, especially the Witcher series, and don't mind reading a ton, then you will absolutely love this game. Definitely hope we see either DLC or a sequel or something to continue expanding this universe!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing Roadwarden!Good writing, great worldbuilding. It's a "simple" style of writing, wholly in the good sense. The focus is on content and clear descriptions instead of a fancy wordy style, making it very easy to immerse yourself in the world. The illustrations also do a great job supporting the writing, by always providing the player with a quick impression of their surroundings before reading the details in the text.The challenge level struck a perfect balance for me. Not so difficult that every decision and journey becomes a stressful endeavor, not so easy that it feels like there are no stakes and you're just cruising through. And since you can save and load at any time, every player can fine tune their own difficulty level depending on how often they save.There is a very good balance of choices and consequences. The choices you make allow a good degree of freedom and agency in how to explore the world and how to approach things, without becoming unpredictable, disjointed or overwhelming. I also love that character skills are neatly integrated into gameplay, rather than increasing a bunch of your character numbers.The combat worked really well for me, placing relatively little emphasis on character stats, and a lot on the preparedness and knowledge of both the character and the player. You don't fight a beast with your Axe+2, you fight it with the specific gadget or, even better, piece of knowledge that you encountered along the way.I rate it awesome/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

When it says text based, it is the primary centerpiece of the game. This is closer to a book than it is a visual novel. Think of it as one of those books you picked up that has occasional illustrations in it showing what's going on.  No. It is fully released.  5 months.  I'd say get it on sale. Right now I got it for 30% off. I enjoy it quite a lot and it is engaging, but I would heavily recommend a sale.✅ Highlighting people's names as they're speaking in a lighter color✅ Slow and direct introduction to in game mechanics✅ Noise transitions from place to place, from day to night cycles, etc. ✅ The characters pop out, have good personalities, and the writing is nice.➖ Focus is on text, and if you don't like reading and using your imagination other than the illustrations, I wouldn't recommend this game.➖ It reminds me of a choose your own adventure story.➖ If you have a good memory about what you have read previously in the game, it will serve you well with understanding how the characters interact.❌Mostly brown/neutral colors in illustrations. _childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I need a cup of coffee to focus my wits and eyesight before diving into a session of this game, and it is a lot of fun, much like playing a game of D&D by myself. The characters are interesting, and the ever-present danger makes me feel simultaneously very weak and also like a badass whenever I overcome some crazy monster through patience, magic, or steel.I love it. I would definitely purchase another adventure as the Roadwarden, along whatever roads my character travels after securing the wild peninsula for Hovlavan.NB: this game is not for the impatient, or anyone craving action or a dopamine hit, or anyone opposed to reading for hours on end. The gameplay is exclusively three things: reading, thinking, and making choices.Knowing that, if you think you might like this game, you'll probably love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of fantasy, Roadwarden truly delivers, maybe not in the mainstream idea of your high fantasy story where you progress through the game until you fight or become a god.  Instead roadwarden’s world presents you a subtle yet realistic take on a wild and untamed Archipielago with characters struggling to survive and settle, each with interconnecting stories, motivations and a past for you to discover all while never stripping you from your own deductions until you discover the truth, or not. While simplistic and bare-bones as it is, Roadwarden sticks to its strengths and does them real good. To some it might seem just like a glorified choose your own story book. But damn it’s a good one. Truly incredible, really does make you feel like batman 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a great hidden gem! I love a good story, and I'm super engaged and invested in the subtle lore and world building Roadwarden offers. Gameplay is literally just making choices and managing your stats and items, but super fulfilling. The NPCs are so well fleshed out and have so much more to offer. I played 7hrs straight and Absolutely love this game. FYI: It has a built in  console if you ever need to tweak things, by pressing shift+o (the letter o). A few helpful commands are:- pc_hp = x (for example 4) for health- mana = x (magic)- coins = x- cleanliness = x- armor = x- pc_food = x (nourishment)items are all in the form of item_nameoftheitem = xso for example item_rations = x

_childDocuments_.review: I know that not everyone likes text-based RPGs, but Roadwarden does a fantastic job establishing a world and a story in an intriguing way that really drew me in. _childDocuments_.review: This...is an  game.  As the description states, it's text-based; a lot of that is the sort of see-a-lot-of-text-and-select-a-choice you'll see in visual novels or choose your own adventure or dialogue choices in a standard RPG, but on top of that are exploration, combat rolls, and occasional text-entry.The main loop is a lot of travel and exploration trade and dealing with people and events.  When dealing with some things, the text prompt gets added - some towns and locations allow/force you to look for things based on text entry rather than choosing from a menu.  What you're looking for can be something visible in the little map shown on your screen (the bushes you can see over there), something that should obviously be present (a trader in the town you just reached), or something mentioned in a quest or dialogue.  That makes it harder to 'find' things than just noticing a new menu option appearing - so you have to pay attention!  There are even a few 'combat encounters' that can be drastically affected by a text entry reaction.The setting is... not grimdark, but on an obvious deathworld, where people can't just do what they want, and Nature actively fights back.  I wanted to type 'humanity', there, but it's not clear that you're actively  with humans, or even that your character is human - there are various mentions for various characters of fur, purple skin, or gills.  There's not a lot of description of  how alien the people of the world are, but it's made obvious it's an alien world and an alien people.So far I've been quite impressed with what I've seen of the people and the plot - there's not a lot that's just  to you, so you've got to  it.  The immediate impression you get of a character is  always correct; not everyone is as nice or as nasty as they immediately seem, and there are  floating around in the villages that you may not even find - though you'll certainly want to look.Villages and certain characters can be befriended or angered by your actions, which can affect the quests/jobs available to you, the price of goods, and the options available for interaction.  Items that are too expensive to afford at first may become far cheaper if you successfully befriend the shopkeeper, and quest rewards aren't necessarily just money or items.Quite enjoying this title so far- the questing and exploration and interactions are far more than I've come to expect from most implementations of the engine being used, and it's already been well worth the sticker price.

There is a polygamous family of 3 people one of whom is non-binaryThere are at least 5 mentions of homosexual relations in the gameThere is a village where exhibitionism, public sex and open relationships are allowed and actively encouragedI am not an anti-LGBT person, but when the agenda is pushed so aggressively, it becomes impossible to ignore it.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but some games are just that good I had to.Amazing Game, a must buy for anyone interested in a great story game/RPG/text-based adventure game/ or maybe a more relaxing game to wind down in the evenings.I ended up loving this game so much I binged the entire thing in two days. I got immersed in the world like I never have before in an RPG, i cared about these people and the world and stuck to my roadwarden's morals and I didn't do the usual RPG game thing of rapidly changing my personality to get the best out of a situation. My Roadwarden dreamed of being a hero, and a hero they would become. I made them act heroically and protect the roads, and they never told lies or betrayed the trust of others and it felt great. I was even rewarded by this near the end of my playthrough where after enough Heroic acts I felt as if I could be called a Hero and got a permanent health increase.The music and sound design is extremely well done, it has catchy light tunes that aren't too in your face but make for a very nice passive listening. Sometimes in certain areas more enviromental sounds will play like animals far off in the woods and it really plays into how untamed this area is compared to the others and that you should be more careful around here.I really appreciated that you build the world in the game. Throughout the game people will ask your Roadwarden of where they come from and you will get various options to choose from, I remember there is a person that asks you of an old Inn in the city down south and you can say it's still there, or has been gentrified or it has taken a dive in quality and reputation and is one of the roughest parts in the city. This is great as you can choose the world you live in, is it cruel and the poor are downtrodden or things not so bad in the south. And Honestly, I can't even think of anything to nitpick about, there was a fly sound effect for like 5 minutes that was a bit annoying but it really is a perfect game and for that price you really can't beat it. I've gotten nearly double it's worth in playtime and I'm already debating going back in for a 2nd time.Couldn't recommend more, PICK THIS GAME UP!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A text based CYOA game with survival mechanics such as an inventory and food/health/sleep/cleanliness used as modifiers for your decisions. Great worldbuilding and fully realized characters. Good writing and setting get you interested in the villages and people you meet. A sense of mystery pervades many locations and can be solved through the right questions and travels.Your decisions and actions have will have effects on both the final outcome and how people around the game-world will treat you. There is a time-limit of 40 days on regular difficulty (with options for 30 days or no time-limit) which will force you to prioritize what you want to do by the end. I had not completed all the quests or solved all the mysteries by the end but it felt natural with the coming fall. This combined with 3 different classes (I chose fighter but there is also mage and scholar) leaves me wanting to do a second playthrough to focus on some of the issues left unsolved in my first playthrough.Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I'm *really* enjoying this game. It's the first text-based game I've played, and I'm more of an RPG player. It feels significantly more grounded in reality than most other RPGs I have played, which (speaking as a reenactor of the medieval and renaissance periods) is a huge breath of fresh air.Pros:+Rich lore: The game takes place in an area with well-connected NPCs, quests have branching storylines, and the Roadwarden's deeds have consequences which impact others. I would classify it as "low fantasy." Humans are the only "race," but there are fantastical beasts and magic present.+RPG elements: The Roadwarden may choose from one of 3 classes to start with, which drastically alter the way the character interacts with the world. In addition, your character's skills improve as they progress the story, and they acquire equipment which aids them in their journey.+Gender-neutral terminology for both the main character and their horse: The Roadwarden and their trusty mount can be whatever gender and color the player wishes.+Great music: sets the atmosphere of where your character is and the situation in which they are involved.+Replayability: With 3 different classes to choose from, 3 different difficulties, several different dialogue trees to follow, and multiple endings, players can find themselves returning to a different experience with each playthrough.+NPC diversity: I personally appreciate the deliberate inclusion of NPCs of many different skin colors, body types, and hair types, as well as people of different life partner preferences.+Generous save system: Learning to use the F5/F8 quick save/quick load combo is essential to ensure your playthrough goes (mostly) the way you want it to.Cons:-A lot of reading: It is a text-based game, after all. It is an interactive story. This requires the player to pay special attention to the details of the dialogue and text describing the scenarios.-Low visual effects: Again, it is a text-based game. It does include visuals with each scene, and those scenes change slightly as the character accomplishes goals, however the color scheme is less-than-vivid ("OK, apply the medieval filter") which may not appeal to some players.-Can be vague: Some puzzles may drive the player to frustration, simply because they don't know the exact word to type to solve a particular puzzle. I had to rely on the internet to solve more puzzles than I would like.-NPC dialogue learning curve: I appreciate the level of detail that the creators went through to give NPCs from different areas different accents and dialects, it added flavor to the lore. However, some of them require quite a bit of re-reading to ensure you know exactly "hwat" they're saying."Ne ye worry t'much though, 'tis doable."-Some minor grammar issues: Normally not a big deal, but in a text-based game, correct spelling and grammar are critical. It's not rife with errors, but some further editing wouldn't go amiss.-Limited replayability: Once a player knows exactly what each scenario presents, it becomes somewhat trivial to read it through each time. I found that much of my time spent replaying NPC dialogue trees and areas that I knew well was simply tedious. The fun comes from doing things you haven't done before, or finding something new because of a different style of play.I highly recommend this game if you're looking for a low-stress, dark, historical fantasy story where choices matter. If stunning graphics and slaying hordes of demons with your greatsword "Doombringer" are more your thing, perhaps save this game for later.

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to be turned off by text based games.  Make no mistake, I have always been an avid reader until recent years so it isn't hard for me.  I just feel like a game would have to pull a lot more through just words alone.  That being said, I found Roadwarden to be an exciting experience.  Not only does it provide an intriguing story, it gives you free reign to discover the world you live in as you please.  The roads are dangerous, though, and you will often find yourself save scumming after biting off more than you can chew.  Yet the story and the thought of what I might discover brought me back every time.  It has been forever since I literally did nothing but sit on a game all day long.  Every time I felt I spent too long on the game I would take a 15 minute break and come right back.  I even turned down multiplayer with the guys to play this game.  The normal difficulty gives you 40 days to fulfill your main quest along with a personal goal and whatever side quests you choose to partake in.  There are factions and characters that respond to every choice you make.  You will never feel overpowered in this game as combat is such a minor part of all the things you can do here.  Bargaining, exploration, fishing, foraging, meeting new people, diplomacy, and combat all come together however you feel like going about it.  As there is a time limit you will be forced to organize tasks by importance and convenience.  You will make things easier for yourself the more you do in your short time.  I have had a single playthrough so far and I feel I will definitely return to try new paths and finish quests I had to leave behind for the sake of time limits.  Overall great text based game, it is worth the dosh.

Captures the feeling of a pen and paper game fairly well with detailed writing. I strongly recommend picking this one up, especially if you're a fan of games with interactive worlds. (FNV/Pathologic 2)
