_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game!  Sure, it's text based and you've got to do stuff like... read, but the writing is superb and the stories of the tribes and people you meet are compelling.  The music is relaxing and I find the game a great way to wind down for a couple hours after work.  It's simple in its make-up but managing your money, food, and appearance can be difficult... especially if you go around buying stuff just to see what it can get you in different situations.  And of course, on first play through you don't realize that some items from some people can be bought at pretty big discounts after you reach a certain friendship threshold with them.   I played on normal difficulty which gives you 40 days to complete your mission to open trade up to the peninsula where the story takes place.  Simple, right?Of course, pretty much everyone hates people like you with the stink of the city and an air of sophistication above the average dirt farmer.  So you've got to get the people to trust you and believe that you're a force for good in a world which seems to have abandoned them to their fate.  They're hard, self reliant people who don't think they need anyone's help and in several cases, are dying out because of it.  But that's just the base story line.  There is so much else going on if you really dig around.  Lots of little mysteries to solve and relationships to groom.  I got a bit scatterbrained around the middle and probably wasted a bunch of time being inefficient.  Though I "finished" the game, I'm pretty sure I didn't complete it.  There were several stories I did not finish, hints I didn't understand or couldn't figure out how to follow up on, and a couple settlements with no trade agreement.The game is also short enough that I have no problem playing through it again.  Sure most of the content will be the same, but I have this burning need to figure out a couple of the mysteries I left behind.  I can honestly say the game has been one of the most enjoyable I've played in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is not a game that I expected to enjoy too much, as I hadn't played many games like it before. I only bought it because it was on sale and I was running out of other things to play, but man am I glad I did. Roadwarden has so many elements built into it that I didn't expect to find when first playing. I think this game is best to go into mostly blind, as much of its charm comes from learning and adapting to this world that feels familiar to our own, yet noticeably different and more  dangerous. The people you meet and locations you travel to are all changed based on your choices, and I loved seeing my actions slowly shape and even tame all of the different places I once knew nothing about. This game constantly surprised me with just how in depth I could get with different locations and characters, and I truly think its worth a try especially if you haven't played anything like it before.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was curious how a text-based rpg would work in this day and age but Roadwarden really shines. There is plenty to do on the peninsula, from exploring new locations, discovering secrets, and interacting with unique NPCs. I enjoyed the story and need to go back to play it again with a different class and approach. Both the story and the soundtrack are great and the pixel art is well done. While the game may look simple from the outside, there is a lot more going on. Recommended if you want a low stress story game with a great soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: "Text-based rpg" is a very off-putting tagline for most gamers, myself included. But trust me, this one is so worth the reading. After playing this absolute gem, I can confidently say it's not only the best text adventure game I've ever played, it's one of my favorite narrative-focused games of all time. The quality of writing and the brutal but fair gameplay have skyrocketed my standards for rpg narratives going forward, and no matter how much I look for the feeling in other titles, I keep coming back to Roadwarden. Do yourself a favor and give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first text-based RPG I have ever played. Usually, I am put off by the genre due to presentation issues such as a boring interface or plain text. Roadwarden, in contrast, stands out with detailed art of each location, a readable map, and a really nice original sound track featuring unique music for most (all?) major events and places. On top of all the pretty stuff, the foundations here are also quite strong, in my opinion. The many towns each have distinct culture, industry, ambitions, and conflicts both internal and external. Characters and dialogue are equally colourful and detailed; I never once felt like I was simply talking to just an Innkeeper or just a vendor, always a person. The setting, an isolated peninsula overrun by wild beasts, is utilized very effectively as well. For instance, many people are intimidated by the player character's horse since most large animals they are familiar with are violent.Roadwarden seems a true labour of love and is absolutely worth your time. Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a fantastic game. It perfectly captures the feeling and aesthetic of being a Roadwarden. I fell in love with the storytelling, both text and visual. The game is incredibly pretty, despite being a text adventure. You can tell that the developer really cares about making it as good as possible. I'm not sure if I could entirely call it a criticism, but when playing this game make sure you can actually focus on it, you lose a lot of value by playing it without sucking in the whole experience and just mindlessly clicking options9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a reimagining of a 1980s text adventure or choose-your-own-adventure novel, but with the rough edges (most text input, unfair death, etc) sanded off. Autumnal and melancholy in tone - not unlike some Westerns - despite being set in mid to late summer.Genre-wise, it straddles visual novel and RPG. (So there's lots of reading that forms the meat of the game, if that's not obvious.)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art panel that shows your environment adds a great deal of immersion to the stories. I didn't find it quite as brutally difficult as I expected - in fact, most of the time my failures were only met with minor consequences that I could deal with relatively quickly, but I still greatly enjoyed it.

To be fair, if I really were inside this world I would totally avoid fighting with any of the monsters if I could.Playing this was a fun, unique experience! _childDocuments_.review: As a child, my mother would take me to the library and by pure chance I discovered the Lone Wolf gamebook series. As a future gaming enthusiast, I played all 28 of them, with the last one still in reprint. Unfortunately, the series never ended due to the author's death.Roadwarden is the heir to those adventures and to the early text-based video games, infused with the same fantasy setting. In this case, it takes place on a forgotten peninsula, which forests are teeming with monsters ready to punish those who disrespect them.Our role is that of the new roadwarden, the one who keeps the roads safe. This quickly leads us into a whirlwind of people, places, and missions described through isometric maps, a handful of simple yet impactful music, and, of course, a lot of text.It's a strange sensation for a visual zoomer like me. Certainly, the imagination is freer to roam, but it also becomes harder to associate names and concepts. Immediately, Disco Elysium comes to mind, where the protagonist was also exploring a city in search of someone (in his case, himself). I can't say that the level of writing is comparable, nor the added visuals and voice acting, but Roadwarden certainly doesn't disappoint in terms of the depth of its environments, of the situations that arise, and of the subsequent choices to be made, further constrained by a 40-day time limit before winter arrives.4/5

In the beginning, I kind of wished I had a bit more guidance but once I read through the Glossary everything made a lot more sense.  Seems like there is some replayability though I think I am fine where I left it.  Looking forward to see more of these from this publisher.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; It's a lot like playing a good book you can't put down.If you don't like to read you're really not going to like this game, but if you do like dark low/medium fantasy fiction and if you've ever enjoyed a text-based adventure, this is an easy recommendation.The time limit can be a little stressful, but I walked away with an ending I was pretty happy with (but only JUST made it). I would have liked to have explored a few other threads and tied a bow on things, but that also adds a replayable angle to the story, giving you an opportunity to explore other paths or optimize how you approach things on another run.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: It's a drag.After a while, you'll have amassed a dozen quests which all rely on the same pattern: go somewhere, do some chores until you're deemed trustworthy, get some hints for one of the quests. Rinse and repeat until someone pays you. The stories are an accumulation of small chunks and none of those I've seen contained an interesting twist or had an epic feel about them. Character interaction feels awkwardly artificial and comes with very little options and combat is frustratingly obscure, as there is no indication of how much the outcome was influenced by the dice. All you can do is quicksave and guess which of the choices might work.My conclusion? If you enjoy reading stories, stick to a good book, as the interactive elements of Roadwarden don't compensate for the lack of a good plot and interesting characters.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is not good. _childDocuments_.review: So had my eye on this one, wasn't sure how I'd feel cause I'm not that bright with word games(there's points where you'll have to type in actions or commands which can feel confusing at point[hint; just type "blood"]) and was worried all the text would get pedantic, but it's a solid story. Everyone's game is going to be different cause there are tons of choices that'll impact what happens, but you'll probably be just as surprised as I was when you finish up after you thought you'd done the "right" thing, yet lo and behold, every action has consequences.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 7 hours straight.You're a Roadwarden, someone who keeps the roads free from monsters, obstacles, and highwaymen, while building relations with the locals and relaying messages between towns. Your primary task after being sent to the Dragonwoods by the capital is to track down the previous Roadwarden named Asterion. You get to build relationships with the characters (which is sometimes helped by your chosen faith - mine was pagan. Go druids!) and slowly uncover the land's secrets. You get to meet a reclused sorceress who may or may not have an addiction problem, a bear of a woman who owns an inn, a vain and cunning (but sincere once you gain her trust) mayor who is deeply connected to a tragic incident that befell a local town years and years ago, several monks, a lot of druids, a male version of Poison Ivy, a lotta undead (burn 'em or not, up to you), and if you're lucky - a unicorn.There's tons of little aspects to the game like dragonbones (turned into shillings. I'm not kidding), timed quests, whether you're a fighter or pacifist, class perks, unique inventory items (that bait you into selling them only to regret doing so later on because oh ♥♥♥♥, they're important), how each town thinks of one another, bed-and-breakfast which slowly becomes free (if you're dedicated to establishing good reputation), influence on your character's worldview, and more.Creeks was my favourite town by a long shot. I'm not sure if the Roadwarden can choose where to settle down yet but I'm settling down in Creeks. It was also interesting how no one had seen a horse before save for mine. The capital, Hovlovan, vaguely reminded me of King's Landing though some dialogue options seem to help you flesh out/choose how you want it to be like. Trust is a great factor to learn more information in the game as well as get better endings (and achievements).This is the first time I've played a text RPG like this. I honestly didn't expect it to be so well done. At first I thought it might be like D&D, but no, the story is pretty centered though there's a lot to unpack. it's like a little CYOA because of how varied the endings each character and town get - it all depends on what you choose to do and not do with the information you have. The story, gameplay, and characters successfully kept me at it even until my eyes were begging me to go rest. I'm going to play another round of this to unlock the other achievements, mainly find . Cheers. 8.9/10Update: I did it! I moved into Creeks! Got an achievement for it too. Still unable to unlock Bed Connoisseur though
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so let me start out by saying something.This is one of the most well crafted, diverse and beautiful games i have played in years. About half a year ago, i had a sudden bug to play a text based adventure game that was in the style of old school DOS adventures (Think "black mirror Bandersnatch") but was having EXTREME trouble finding any of them that were worth their salt. I searched high, low, looked on the google play store, picked up a few games that were designed for flash, but none of them had "good enough" quality that seemed like they were worth the hours i put into them... until i found this.Roadwarden is a game that will reward you for staying true to your principles, however you wish to play it. Be it a positive influence, or a negative one. The possibility and diverse interactions of each of the characters, and how they inter-mesh together is incredibly vast, and all of the choices you make ripple effect across the land.This game is not for the light reader however. Extremely important information can get omitted from the mind in a large wall of text. Read carefully, and snuggle up with a cup of hot cocoa as you take on the role of a witcher-like constable keeping the roads of the peninsuila safe.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What an experience!I think in a way I played this game at the perfect moment in my life. As I tried to become a better DM in our weekly tabletop RPG campaign I was thinking about fictional worlds, the structure of stories, and how characters interact with each other and the player a lot lately. Then I played the fantastically written Roadwarden. A game that would best be described as a chimaera with the head of a visual novel, the body of an RPG, and the legs of a text adventure. In the beginning, the game lulled me with its beautifully atmospheric pixel art and its equally fitting melancholic music. But it wasn't long before I was fascinated by its world. A rough world, where survival isn't a given and death lurks around every corner. Where every little hamlet, every path through this land had to be painfully carved out of the wilderness and relentlessly protected against the wild beasts (one of which is humanity itself). But the aspect that really made me fall in love with this game was how it handled the player's involvement in this world and the web of relationships the player has to navigate. I never felt railroaded, always in control. There was no clear direction to take, not even a clear goal. And so it felt more like a real world, like a real life I was living. I was trying to improve things, yes. But ultimately I was just a small cog in this machine that will keep on running long after I finished the game. Every decision I made was mine. Every path I took belonged to me. Every friendship I made along the way was personal. In the end, there isn't the best way to play this game. Not the right decision to make. Not the correct path to take. Every player's story will differ, no outcome will be the same. It was my story and my story alone. Never has a story in a game felt so personal to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: You can honestly skim a lot of the dialogue and be fine. Combat could be improved dramatically. The game grows on you over time, the last half was dramatically better than the first half. The character writing is phenomenal but I wish the game told you that it is often better to not choose every dialogue option as the game will heavily punish you for saying some things. The final mission is really where the game shines when all the preparation comes together. All in all worth the time and a solid 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.  Like the choose your own adventure books from the 80's and 90's with a little more RPG.  Time limit is a double edged sword.  Without that pressure the game would be too easy, but it adds some stress to the journey.  Managed to complete everything I could by day 40 though.Don't know if I'll run through it again but multiple options are clear with a few classes to choose from so there is good  replayability.  Was NEVER bored and there is no grind.  Was always excited to come back and play.  A true gem and well worth the time to complete for those interested..
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game. Each character is incredibly well written, with unique interactions at every turn. The story is so rich and immersive, it's easy to get lost for hours in the lines of text that paint a beautiful and wild world in your mind. The game does not hold your hand, and will throw you into scenarios that you will be unprepared for, but always allowing you to escape with your life if you manage your skills and equipment carefully. As you answer prying questions from characters in the game, you write the back-story of your own character as you go. A unique features that allows you to really feel in control of the story, while still learning about it. All in all, the game is incredible. I HIGHLY recommend it to anyone that enjoys reading or text based games, or RPGs in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A masterfully crafted text-based adventure that immerses you in a beautifully detailed world brimming with lore, intrigue, and adventure. This game stands out for its narrative depth and the choices that shape your journey. Roadwarden is a gem for fans of interactive fiction. Its rich storytelling, atmospheric world, and meaningful choices make for a deeply engaging experience. While it may not appeal to those seeking fast-paced action or dynamic visuals, it excels in delivering a captivating narrative journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent choose your own adventure rpg. Difficult enough to keep me on my toes but not so tough that you'll just get killed out of nowhere. You don't have to read every word but you do have to pay attention - the quest log provides info but not all of the answers. The game has a great loop where there's always one more thing to do before putting it down.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is an excellent text-based adventure and well worth a look. I thoroughly enjoyed the roughly 12-hour playthrough, where I met fascinating characters, unravelled intriguing mysteries and burned an alarmingly high number of corpses. If you’re on the fence, do keep in mind that, like Disco Elysium and Citizen Sleeper, there’s a ton of reading in this game (obviously). Thankfully, there’s a demo you can check out before purchasing to see if it’s your kind of thing.It’s well worth the entry price, and I’d say there’s some replay value. When I finished my playthrough, I immediately started thinking about what I’ll do differently the next time I ventured into the peninsular.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update this review down the line.I've been watching updates from MAS for what feels like years. I've no idea what to expect, but it's a cozy, yet thrilling, unraveling story. The music is great, the pixel art wonderful, and the writing enthralling! Now that I've finished gushing - This is a $10.99 game. You might not have your socks blown off, but you might have a few stories worth telling once you've done your time as Roadwarden.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Video games have always been a huge part of my life. As I've gotten older I find it harder and harder to get totally absorbed by them like I did when I was a kid. I'll pick up games for a few hours and then get bored and never touch them again.Roadwarden is one of those rare titles I play once a year, maybe once every few years, that reignites my passion for video games and makes me feel like a kid again. Undertale, hyper light drifter, hollow knight, rimworld, disco elysium, celeste; roadwarden deserves to be mentioned in the same breath.The compelling but simple mechanics are a testament to the timeless genius of traditional D&D tabletop elements. The writing is inspired (good video game writing? what the ♥♥♥♥?), the sepia pixelated art-style is immediately impressive, and the OST is start-to-finish bangers.The main draw is that (much like DE) information about the world is doled out slowly and methodically with a few major twists and turns. At the beginning of the game the peninsula feels massive and unexplored, harboring a near infinite variety of strange beasts and magical oddities. As you progress the map quickly begins to feel smaller until every nook has been searched, every creature slain and every NPC dialogue option exhausted. The illusion of infinite depth cracks and you see the game for what it is.8-10 hours of near perfection for $10. For me the game is a 10 because anything that feels a bit unpolished only contributes to the intimate indie feeling and my only legitimate complaint is that there isn't more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was sceptical about how a text adventure would suit me, but Roadwarden was one of my favorit games i played in the past few years.The story is interesting and has a good myth for you to discover peace by peace. The quest design is incredible, where you are given a vague goal at the start of the game and have to make the most out of it. That means that every side quest helps you with the main quest sort of.I also liked the setting. A world where humans have not yet mastered the wilderness.All in all a real gem :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic indie experience. Delicious pixel graphics. The Worldbuilding is on point, total classic fantasy; this would make a great D&D setting. Very few plot inconsistencies especially regarding the vast scope of choice combinations. The NPC Trust system really works and actually matters. The combat encounters favor preparation and incorporate luck, as they should. After 20 hours I haven't plumbed the depths of this game -it's a great value. Overall, big recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Flipping excellent. Some of the best writing I've seen in this medium, scratches an itch I never knew I had. Only gripe is some strangely colloquial phrasing at times that feels at odds with the setting. Plus a very very slight bit of continuity error regarding a certain fisherman (though the narrative is generally excellent with this otherwise). Climax was a little underwhelming, but what can you do with a game that has so much variance. Loved it and am very sad no one I know will ever touch it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Exactly the game I was looking for. I wanted an choose-your-own-adventure with moral decisions, and branching paths with strong narrative and hard choices. Great story. The choices can be intuitive, but require understanding non-player character motivations and personalities.  Very interesting, moral choices!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A really special game--punishing but there are difficulty settings if you decide you want an easier time. You will still have to make decisions and pursue options and deal with consequences etc. The atmosphere is so strong, so focused, so effective. The world is rich, vast, and well thought out. Everything is intentional, focused, this was all built around a few principles gameplay and storywise. And the taste level is basically always there, from art, music, UI, writing, etc this is a sophisticated game in many senses.  The art is stunning, the music (which has maybe too short of a loop at times) will never leave you. I think of this game and I think of that music, and the color palette. Those hold all the ideas and themes and tones.While you're really just clicking options that simulate your next step, it's a meaty game not a lite-simulator or CYA.  So much to discover. I really hope to see more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: AAA games have their own problems these days, and I foolishly seek refuge in indie games...only to have discovered time and again they have just as many flaws - albeit different ones.It really is an equal and opposite issues situation, although I do pay much less for indie games, so...What I find is that indie games inject artificial difficulties...I guess to keep up with AAA games?To show we're too cool, and don't make no easy games, man!?I do not know.I only know that like Darkest Dungeon, I was supremely frustrated with what would otherwise be a perfectly fine - if not a great - game, ruined into tediousness by some artificial standards.In this dumb indie game's case it is:AppearanceYes, dear reader, if I do not wash or mend my clothes regularly, then people will not have anything to do with me, and I am in a soft fail loop not knowing how to fix it.I was low on life and rest, and suddenly NO inns would rent a room to me.AND it cost me a LOT OF RESOURCES to clean 1 or 2 points.Up until this point - I was actually enjoying these games as they resembled the excellent Lone Wolf series of books from childhood.Indie Game Developers: THERE IS NO REASON FOR ARTIFICIAL, CRUDELY INJECTED DIFFICULTIES!THIS DOES NOT MAKE YOUR GAME "COOL"!A well-balanced game is good - not something like "appearance" as a stat which affects EVERYTHING!Also, the main character stupidly gives away the REAL reason for his mission - essentially to pave the way for his merchant city to conquer the free-region.So, secret, secret, cannot tell anyone, only hinted at even to the player THEN:"Yes, my city sent me to provide information and contacts to directly control this area not claimed by other great powers."I felt like I was watching The Phantom Menace with characters simply announcing to enemies, passerby and the audience key and secret motivations.Ultimately, this game could have been great, but an amateurish obsession endemic to indie games set in and ruined it.Not worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Life on the Peninsula can be summed up in one word: challenging.From the very beginning, I knew this journey would be difficult. At the same time, I was both right and wrong. Right, because indeed, life here is difficult. Wrong, because the extent of this difficulty was so great that I was forced to redefine the meaning of this word for myself. What I used to call "difficult" before is very different from what I now call "difficult".I have faced many trials and made many difficult decisions here. The decisions, dangers, secrets, people, and leaders are so numerous that the 40 days I had to fulfill my mission felt like a single week.Life here is plural. Numerous villages and people need help, work, items, messages, protection, and even people seeking revenge... wherever I went, my mind never ceased to find objectives and challenges to fulfill.A major challenge was prioritizing whom to help and where to go. These were the shortest 40 days of my life. Time seemed extremely limited here: the Peninsula is vast, and the wilderness is untamed and brutal - many days were lost on these treacherous roads.Every soul in this place has their own goals, needs, frustrations, and individual difficulties, and they struggle fiercely to secure what they believe is best for them.It was my job to explore as much of this Peninsula as possible, while simultaneously ensuring the road was safer for myself and everyone else. All of this while I faced my own difficulties: being attacked by wild beasts, struggling to find safe shelter, and striving hard to keep both my pocket and stomach full.Autumn has finally arrived. And with its arrival, I begin my departure. Today, I embark on my journey back to the Cities, proud of my accomplishments here, yet frustrated by my inability to do more.My impact on the Peninsula was real - I know that. But I have but the strenght of just one man. Clearly, I failed to do everything I promised, which weighs heavily on my shoulders as I leave. This weight is alleviated because I also directly and indirectly improved many lives with my work in this place. While I saved entire villages, at the same time, I abandoned others completely to their own  luck.I bring back to the Cities everything I have learned about this place, its people, their difficulties, and - perhaps the most important for the Cities - the wealth that can be found here.Roadwarden has a LOT of content. It's definitely worth playing and even replaying the game. It's highly unlikely that you'll complete 100% of the game's content on your first playthrough. There are many details that, depending on the priority and order you complete each individual mission, take more time to discover. Having known such details earlier could be a huge time-saver for you, leaving you with more time for adventuring on the Peninsula.The game is immersive, and the atmospheric music/sound effects are good and help a lot on the immersion. In the first few days, I felt an uncomfortable repetitiveness in the music, but that quickly passed once I uncovered and opened up new routes for exploration.Personally, I give this game an 8/10 rating. It's a narrative-driven game, which may not appeal to everyone. If you're not willing to read (and read A LOT), narrative games may not be your thing (and that's okay, if you don't enjoy it, refund it).My biggest issue with this game was the feeling of being poor, extremely poor.Narratively, it makes a lot of sense, considering your character's mission is to explore a place facing many hardships. The help and services you provide are hard and demanding, and the payment for your work - in most cases - does not meet the effort you input.And as you face all the hardships of this place, all while paying for shelter, food, and services - this all combined quickly drains your pockets. With an empty pocket, you need to work. By working, you can't explore. Without exploring, you can't fulfill your mission and uncover the various secrets and stories of this game.That said, I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal. If you only plan on playing through once, and want to be sure you see pretty much everything, be sure to play on casual--I really took my time, got to meet everyone, and committed hard to getting the ending I wanted, and it took about 110 in-game days, while the default difficulty restricts you to 40.From what I see, I was extremely slow compared to others, but I feel very happy that I played it the way that I did. _childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I think this of one of the few games that has the best written material out there, it is very atmospheric and it has an immense lore that you can absolutely fell into comfortably and get lost. It remind me of my youth and all the time spent playing "choose your own adventure" books that I grew up with.THE GOODGraphic: It is super super nice, I wished that there was as well visual pixel art for the unique monster of this place.Music: Perfect match for the game, very enjoyable.Game: - I loved the intro part, it put you right in the tension mood of danger of the world. It really inspired me for a couple of quest that I will run in d&d. - I adored the idea of getting your journal expand as you learn more and more about the world. It makes you want spend all the time of the world to get all the information in the world. - There are so many good characters with their quirks that makes you love or hate them (in a good way)- Surprised with extreme pleasure that depending on your choices people would not talk with you about certain things, there are actually stakes in this game on your talking choices!- Having the chance of inputting free content it is a great addition, for example "licking the tree" it is a great chance of being creative on what we can do with this interactive digital medium respect to books.THE BADGame: - The time-sensitive adventure, I abhor any game that give you a time limit to do something, and unfortunately I couldn't checkout on this feature without making the whole game easier than intended. For me, and I guess for me alone, anything that make me rush instead of wanting to spend more time with your game, it is an absolutely negative idea. I am not gonna have time to replay your game, and neither I have gonna have time to just finish it because I am gonna get distracted by the next hot game that is gonna pop out and distract me from yours (I am saying this with all honesty and love for this game because it is the hard true).- Because I have played a lot of "choose your own adventure" games, I felt that the game was more about talking with the characters than actually doing any real adventuring, and I felt that was lacking in adventuring. So I am obliged to compare to the rhythms of those games and I felt that sometimes the investigation of cities was a bit overwhelming with a lot of unnecessary fluff content just to get some titbits of information (which I have still wanted, but was boring to do so continuously). It made me want to skip it all, and I am a person that I am used to read a lot of books in a year. I wish that the game just cut to the core of things, and keep the interesting part ups than just aimless talking to have your journal expand with info. I want to spend time actually using that info, than instead acquiring it.- Sleeping even in the ground should anyway give you energy, not removing it even if feel a bit uncomfortable. If these people are medieval people and at least hunters they would be used to be on the road, they are not rich nobleman on the first trip (this for me it is the biggest incongruence of all).- Having to write the exact spelling of a names going through the journal, instead of clicking directly on a selective of choices that I have already unlocked.VERDICT:Buy it, but play it with moderation a little bit at time, all the reading on screen is more tiring than usually on books. If this game was voice acted it could absolutely be a masterpiece at the level of Disco Elysium. I hope in future games the developer will find the budget to pull this off.NOTE: I give up on the game, because unfortunatly all the investigating was quite boring for me (and reading text on Twitch Stream it is not very engaging), but the game absolutely deserve praise and attention for introducing a different way to "Choose your own adventure" games, have various twists and turns and evolve the genre. The best out there like "Choice of Robots" or "Sorcery!" they feel old in comparison.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you like text-based adventures/interactive fiction, this is probably a good game to choose. There is definitely more to it than a few other text-based games I've played - I especially enjoyed doing the puzzles, though the ones that require text-input can be a little tedious as you have to be quite specific. Naturally, this game has a LOT of reading, so keep that in mind. You also have to be really good at time/resource management, so a great game to play if you're one of those people in RPGs that never uses items 'just in case you need it for later'. Also, if you like The Witcher games, you might also like this - not in terms of gameplay but there is a very similar atmosphere to this game. Overall, I very much enjoyed playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that is not for everyone. You play as a roadwarden entrusted with exploring the region, forming relationships, building alliances, solving problems, and occasionally fighting foes. It's a text-based RPG that shone brightest for me when certain relationships with people or villages blossomed after putting in the work with various quests and mundane jobs. However, it is a slow game that often lacks clear direction, even in the end game.I completed the game once and was fairly satisfied with my ending, but I probably won't play it again anytime soon. The combination of your character's gradual progression, the amount of back-and-forth traveling it takes to complete most quests, and the hard limit (unless you're on easy mode) on the number of in-game days means that the game generally follows this path: an early game that is a slog of rarely ever having enough health, armor, money, or time; a mid game that is the most satisfying part of the game where starvation and poverty are no longer concerns and you can finally make progress with all the different quests you've accumulated; and an end game where you eventually run out of having enough in-game days left to complete most of the quests remaining, so you kinda just move around doing mundane work until the end approaches.This game has its great moments, but it does feel like a chore at times and the pace can unexpectedly grind to a crawl. Few things are more demoralizing than talking to a minor character and being faced with a wall of text to read that is more filler than meaningful to your journey. I also had to regularly stop and check my quests, check the map, check my inventory, and read through the glossary of characters I had met to figure out what to do next. I think that could have been addressed by having more prompts about what quests certain items or characters were related to - too often I had collected a bunch of items and had forgotten who they were supposed to be for.As for the good stuff, the characters and relationships you run across throughout the game are great and it's very satisfying to see your character go from a relatively blank slate to someone with alliances, a reputation, and maybe even a few enemies. Unfortunately, due to the time constraints this game imposes, I don't think it's possible to end up on good terms with everyone or even complete every quest unless you're on easy mode or really figure out how to min-max the game, so choose wisely when deciding who to please and piss off.I like the game and would still recommend it, but I wanted to like it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Rather then toss out vague praise about this game, I'd rather share one of my encounters in Roadwarden.I returned to the riverside where I spotted a howler with an abandoned hide. I chased it off earlier and took the hide to Creeks, where I asked if any hunters recognized it. They did; it was common equipment for any hunter going on long hunts. And with three hunters still missing from the village, I concluded this riverside was a prime spot to track one of them down. As I retraced my steps to the spot I found the hide, I noticed tracks and drag marks along with the worrying signs of dried blood. A large predator might have carried off one of the missing hunters. As I followed the tracks, the painful screams of howlers filled the air. When I looked around, I spotted nearly a dozen of them. All of them sat on trees, alternating between shrieking at me and throwing anything on hand at me. I wasn't prepared to face this many howlers. So I turned back, determined to find a way through later.A few days later, I returned with a rather smelly jar. A drifter, I escorted to safety, promised its contents would scare off any howler. I opened it and tossed out the troll urine from inside; it stank so much it could make the dead turn their noses away in disgust. Yet it worked. Half of the howlers turned tail and ran deeper into the forest, leaving the remaining braver howlers. Next, I pulled out my willow wand and focused all of my pneuma to unleash a powerful shock-wave. It tossed some of the remaining howlers off the trees, and they scattered like the other brethren. With no other tricks in my pack I put my trust in my axe and gambeson, and charged forward against the remaining howlers. The fight against them was messy and my gambeson would need serious repairs, but I eventually reached the end of the tracks and drag marks. At the end of it lay human remains. I consider ending my investigation here and returning to Creeks, only to discard that thought. The lead hunter might not accept my words alone, so I gathered any unique belongings left behind. The enclosing screams of other howlers soon surrounded me. They won't risk another fight, however their collective screams already made my head split and my stomach churn. Even though I didn't need to, I gathered the bones too. The village deserves a chance to give their respects to the dead hunter. With that finished, I quickly left the howler's territory. Even after I reached the riverside, my head and stomach still ached. When I returned to Creeks, the lead hunter accepted the hunter's dead belongings and bones with shaking hands. He quietly handed me some money in return and hoped the other hunters were still alive. I had a feeling they weren't.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Grimdark people pleasing simulator. Your role is ultimately to play politics between a bunch of factions that have not-always-friendly relations with each other, and the game does a great job of putting you in this role. Sometimes those politics involves doing things that are Objectively Good, and sometimes people will complain even when you are doing things that are Objectively Good. Other times you have to bend the truth a little to achieve your ultimate goal (colonialism). Just like real politics!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The story was rich and atmospheric. Every interaction was like a puzzle, as I had to make the most out of every travel. In the end, I barely made the time constraint for normal mode, and I think I'd recommend the easy mode so you could take the time to unveil every mystery, but for what's it's worth, the time constraint made the experience more atmospheric. It was not quite as casual of a game as I anticipated, but completing the story was cathartic. Not sure if I'd ever replay the game, but the first playthrough was certainly worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a worldbuilding, wow.Perfect RPG for a tired soul like mine.Every little increment of progress was perfectly in my awareness, never got lost among my newly aquired information nor the fresh items, yet there were tons of them. I attribute this to the extremely well story telling. My memory only works best around narrative devices, and very poor on details. So the story's flow was so smooth, every story device placed so geniusly, I was able to keep track of everything, enjoying the game like a heavenly delight.Just wonderful.And the themes of pagan culture, wilderness, freedom, balance and neutrality: I am captivated by this universe now, I am ready to be a roadwarden in my next life now, thank you very much.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie it took me a bit of time to properly get into this game as I wasn't really quite used to text-heavy RPGs where there isnt really any voice acting or stuff like that. But once I properly sunk an hour or so into it, I really started enjoying itCertain things I liked:- Music fits really well, it feels somber and melancholic but certain locations like Creeks and Old Pagos once you fix their problems are kinda upbeat, which is a nice touch- Actually  about how to do certain things is really cool. For example, paying attention to certain details can help you figure out things really quickly and unravel the mysteries about the peninsula- Story overall is good, and you can see the impact your choices make on the game affects all the locations and NPC'sSome things I think could have been better- Some quests feel pretty annoying to do, I think they might have just bugged out for me and I wasn't able to fully complete some in the game? Specifically  Might have just been a bug or maybe completing certain quests or failing some prevent you entirely from finishing them. - Some of the 'input' choices feel very weird. Basically in a select few locations to search stuff or asking NPC's about locations or people, you have to put the specific thing you're looking for. But I think some of this could have been removed entirely, atleast for places like .If I were to put a number for what id rate the game out of, I would give a solid 8/10. Good story, good music, and each of the three classes have unique variations on the same situations so you will have a nice amount of different things to do. The game also doesn't take very long to finish, maybe 10 hours or so if you're going for a more completionist run.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim and was pleasantly surprised, couldn't help but binge through it in 10 hours straight - very much like a good book you just can't put down and end up reading way past your bedtime. Great narrative, great soundtrack, good gameplay flow.Very forgiving, maybe a little too much. Despite the beautiful pixel art illustrations, it indeed plays more like an interactive book, so be prepared for lots of reading and learning about the world.There's a journal with a quest log and a text log to aid with remembering info, however if you allow yourself to be immersed into the world you'll hardly ever need them.Lastly, my biggest gripe with it is that the writing deteriorated towards the ending. Found myself skimming a lot because the details rapidly became less and less consequential.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's like somebody took some of the best choose-your-own-adventure novels from my childhood (Lone Wolf) and made it into a Steam game. It works very, very well. Just beat it, and I'm already planning a replay to vary up my play style and go after the things that I missed. The flavor of the world is good, there's a nice degree of ambiguity in the decisions available to you, and it never feels just like a visual novel: the game decisions still feel like they're from a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of interactive fiction, visual novels, and choose your own adventure books. Roadwarden easily scratched all of those itches. I originally started playing a while back, back in July, but took a break for a while when I got swamped with life. I started a new save sometime after the Anniversary Update before being swamped again. However, I was able to pick it up again very recently and I practically couldn't put it down. I absolutely love the lore and the setting for the game, which is one of the easiest ways to get me hooked into a game. I loved the Bestiary and the other tabs that collected the knowledge that you gain throughout your playthrough. I did use the "new" advanced settings from the Anniversary Update to give myself unlimited time, because I am all about experiencing a story without being rushed. I'll likely play a standard run at some point in the near future, but for now I am very pleased with what I was able to experience with my technical first playthrough. It took me around 28 hours from start to finish and there were even more things that I forgot to do on the side that easily could have added a few more hours. Absolutely fantastic game and I wish there were more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Good text adventure. The grammar are typos are bad to the point of sometime I have to guess at what the author meant, but you get used to them eventually. That said I would definitely pay for some cleaned up text DLC. A lot of the "right" decisions are possible to figure out by talking to people which is great, and more than a lot of adventure game I play, though there are still a few "you had to think like the developer" ones that feel cheap. Still worth a play though if you like adventure/rpgs and don't mind typing!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game.  Allowing our own imaginations to fill in blanks and flesh out a world is a good thing.  A good writer is better than the best produced movie any day.  My only gripe is that it's over.  Right now I feel like I"ll play it again, but I feel like the normal difficulty time limit is unrealistic.  Less than a month and a half to unravel the tangled social web of the Peninsula, earn everyone's trust, right all present wrongs and uncover all its mysteries seems like a very tall order.  A whole season seems more like it.  A time limit does add some interesting tension, but I'd prefer it to be a bit longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden does a brilliant job at evoking the immersion and beauty of text-based RPGs of ages past.The character customisation may be lacklustre, but it's in the dialogue and available actions that the freedom of role-playing truly shines!Worthy of mention is the worldbuilding, gorgeous and insightful stories that weave the lore of the world with its people and the actions you take.Ultimately, I found myself replaying Roadwarden and quick-saving often due to how enthralled I was with its storytelling and narrative design.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An otherwise fantastic game plagued by the constant interjection of wokeness into the script.In a fantasy medieval setting, on the literal outskirts of civilization, in the land of shamanism and paganism, where merely chopping too many trees results in the locals loathing you, homosexuality is somehow fully accepted.Also, almost every settlement/outpost/squadron/brigand leader is a strong and independent woman. Crazy!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t encountered writing anywhere near as good as this since Disco Elysium, yet that isn’t to say one is better than the other. Roadwarden is sort of dark fantasy, while Disco Elysium is an irreverent inspection of human psychology, society, and the Apocalypse. At about thirty hours, I cannot complain about my time with Roadwarden. A part of me is terribly sad to say goodbye to this world and its people, but it certainly didn’t overstay its welcome; that’s important. While I experienced amazing successes, I also made horrible mistakes and oversights that the game punished tastefully and forcefully. I don’t need or want a perfect adventure where everything ends with a neat little bow on top, and Roadwarden delivers just that. Some mysteries were left unsolved, while others were solved a little too well. Succeeding is sometimes a form of failure. So much to chew on, and I am thankful for the adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Tired to think about a clever phrase to write, just know this game is not for everyone, but for those it is, it may be the best game they have ever played. Myself, playing it feels like a mix of Disco Elysium at some times, a serious VN at others, with a management system that grows into RPG, but very slowly... nothing is free, nothing is cheap.But the most important thing about this game is the power to forget about real life problems and focus on the adventure, being creative enough to put yourself in the shoes of a roadwarden. If you like to read, if you enjoy remember details, if you just need a break, get this game, it's too good and unique to pass it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden has a deep and beautiful world filled with very interesting and human characters.To start with the Cons:-The classes are fairly unbalanced with the best easily being -One particular character resource feels useless. Even if this isn't the case it's impossible for you to see the the pros of investing into it or the cons of ignoring it. It basically is like a trap for you to waste time and resources on.-A few dangerous encounters could be more telegraphed. There are some indicators of danger but certain encounters are deadly with very little warning and can sometimes feel unfair.-That's it. Pros: -Very deep and human characters with interesting goals, conflicts and relationships. Building connections feels rewarding whether you are creating enemies due to moral differences or forming allies for discounts and reinforcements.-A beautiful and immersive fantasy world that houses rich lore and fascinating creatures. You find yourself thrown into a world with many different cultures and practices and how each of these cultures deal with the horrors of the world, from necromancy, to spiritual guides or just pure optimism. Each area feels unique with how you can engage with them and how they will engage with you.-Meaningful and impactful choices, some of which with immediate ramifications. Almost every dialogue option feels important whether you are unraveling secrets, challenging someone's moral compass, or engaging with the world. Every choice you make or don't make, whether you lie or tell the truth, all accumulates to an ending unique to you. -Gorgeous soundtrack and art. The backgrounds give you a solid understanding of your environment while the text fills you in on the details. The ambiance and music fully immerse you into the game until you don't realise that hours have passed.-Interesting puzzles and engaging quests. The game is fantastic at giving you clues and pieces of a puzzle that can come from many different sources. The resolutions to questlines and main quests feel rewarding and earned. The choices you make and the knowledge you gather accumulates to whether you fail or succeed grand conflicts.Seriously, stop looking for a reason not to try the game there is a free demo and glowing reviews. The only issues I have are nitpicks. Classes feel unique and challenging encounters make the world seem hostile and dangerous. The real criticisms are in the positive reviews and unfortunately, there are too many people in the negative reviews who are scared of gay characters and powerful women.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of, if not my favorite game. The mood and atmosphere through the music and interactions with every character you meet are incredibly memorable. Balancing whether to do your job as Roadwarden, satisfy the merchants at home, and completing your personal goals all while facing the dangers of the untamed land leads to challenging decisions and rewarding outcomes. Can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't leave reviews, but after completing the game (and maybe doing it again for another ending), I feel that the game deserves praise.While this RPG is certainly for not everyone (it's mostly text-based, old school RPG with lots of reading), for those who would love to experience a lore heavy, low magic dark fantasy setting, there is nothing better. You arrive in a harsh, dangerous land with monsters and people who can also be monsters. You can build alliances in the different settlements and the options to do within the 40 days limit on normal is simply staggering. Your choices truly matter in the game, everything has consequences in the end.A fantastic game and a true hidden gem of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A low-key fantasy "road movie" in the form of an illustrated text-based RPG. Crafted with love, lore, and exquisite storytelling.Games like Roadwarden heavily rely on a compelling story. Fortunately, this aspect of the game is what makes it worth playing. Levitating between fantasy adventure and detective mystery, it features rich worldbuilding, dry humor, captivating characters, and well-versed descriptions (to be fair, there were errata and text inconsistencies; overall, the story is very well-written). I would probably read this as a book, but having it as a game where you can influence the outcome is even more satisfying. In a nutshell, it is a "visual novel" designed for those who still fondly remember text-based RPGs and text quests.The world of Roadwarden reminds me of the Witcher universe. Maybe because the author is also from Poland? Or, because it is hard to imagine a fantasy setting without being influenced by Sapkowski or Tolkien? Probably both. It is more down-to-earth (not down-to-Middle-earth, heh), though, with no superheroes or supervillains. That makes the lore more credible and distinctive than usual.The RPG aspect is also convincing with this one. Choosing starting traits and beliefs influences how an effective playthrough looks like. I replayed the game several times to see how that would work; the results satisfied me because every playthrough turned out to be a little different despite having more or less the same core progression.The morals and raised questions felt subtle and nonjudgmental, even when they touched on topics like environment, religion, politics, etc. Of course, you can influence how plot twists resolve and what happens to the Peninsula. Despite this, the game ending ensures that any outcome is OK and will have "something positive" and "something negative" in different proportions and for conflicting parties/causes.Music deserves mentioning. The main piece complements the narrative and its sepia-toned illustrations, maintaining the melancholia very nicely.Lastly, a few words about playing Roadwarden on Steam Deck: the experience is not as smooth as, let's say, Disco Elysium, though the game is perfectly playable as it is. The text is readable; controls are clunky (you must use a pointer most of the time) but manageable. Overall, it is an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: In a world full of mechanically intensive shooter games and graphically intense RPGs, Roadwarden finds a way to do far more with far less.If you're open to a game that allows you to pursue a rich story that your actions greatly impact, detailed only by words and pixelated graphics, then this game should be what you're looking for and should even exceed your expectations.I genuinely hope this isn't the last we see of the "Roadwarden" universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: i played this over a few days while sick and it was honestly one of the best gaming experiences i've had in a long time. the worldbuilding is insane, it felt really exciting to discover all the new aspects of this world and to have my characters' belief system tested. will definitely play through again with a different role in mind to experience the other side of these interactions
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very good so far. If you like this style of choice-based narrative games you will love this. If you don't know what I mean by that think choose your own adventure books or the older text adventure games like zork. That sort of idea on mega steroids. You are a roadwarden, basically someone who has been assigned to this region to patrol the lands, make connections with the local people, and explore the place. There is a lot of story and lore as well as some strategy and moral choices. If you are the kind of person to skip through cutscenes and story to get the "real" gameplay, you might not like this. On the other hand if strategy, story, and lots of role-playing sounds fun roadwarden is for you.For more modern examples of similar games than Zork, on the off-chance you have played the Sorcery! series, this is very comparable to that level of high quality gameplay and writing. Similar to the banner saga as well, besides the turn based tactics gameplay. Suzerain is another example. King of Dragon Pass too.3 hours in and 9/10 so far, I see myself playing this quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. You're not the chosen one, you're just a person with a horse and a job to do. Depending on what class/religion you choose, your view of the world completely changes, and you get differing opportunities as well. Playing as a Pagan Warrior or as a Mage Wright-Worshipper will give you very different playthroughs. The dialogue is rich, and the characters are diverse and have motivations and worldviews that make them feel like real people. 10/10, just play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Wonderful writing, with many intriguing characters, and deep storylines.✔️ Good variety of outcomes, with a lot of choices having significant consequences.✔️ Great ambience, with beautiful music.✔️ Pretty pixel art.✔️ The minimalist game mechanics are at the service of the narration.Great game overall, I definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys a good narrative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: As a narrative and graphical throwback to simpler game design, this manages to capture the feel of 90's RPGs, 80s text and SCUMM scrollers, as well as forge a new path in an already crowded genre market. Since buying the game, I've managed to play through 3 different tries to explore different possibilities. Unlike Disco Elysium (which has been mentioned as a narrative competitor) this game offers actual choice, not the illusion thereof. My only minor complaint is that the narrative feels less polished than it should be, but I chalk it up to being either young or new to narrative design. This is a minor nitpick, as the game shines in every other way. I'd highly recommend to any fan of fantasy fiction, choice-based gameplay, or casual retro fantasy gamers.Kudos to the dev!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game has amazing writing but falls flat when it comes to freedom to play the game how you want to play it; It's a fairly linear map progression and the order in which you encounter People/Beasts seems to be predetermined ruining the sense of an open world. In my almost 2 hours playing I created 3 characters both getting them to the 2nd crossroads hoping that there was some sort of randomness or sense of variety in the game, alas it was the same 3 runs with the very similar 3 dialogs with everyone you encounter and finding the same items in the same places. It seems the only "random" aspect of the game are the small moments where there are dice throws to determine outcome but even those are preset to be in certain areas and at certain times.I really came into this game wanting to love it and I did enjoy the writing but if you're looking for an open ended adventure with a sense of replay-ability and open-endedness this isn't the game for you. I'll be waiting for Adventure mode in Dwarf Fortress to come out and have a truly open world adventure, until then I'm getting a refund as I don't find this game's game play loop to be what I was hoping it would be as it presented to be  something close to D&D but it's too linear for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best text adventures I've ever played. Beautiful and detailed setting, tons of choices but never overwhelming.The writing is extremely competent, with plenty of interesting characters, story archs, and different outcomes for each questline. Every choice you make does matter, even way down the line, and they all come together to shape the ending of your adventure, at which point I cried a little bit. If you enjoy reading and role-playing you will love this game, I promise you.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Before I hit the part of the story where they decided to go full-on Panderverse, it was fairly enjoyable, but a little short on things moving the plot forward for my tastes. When I ran into the quest to find the polyamorous set of 3 people including a trans dude, I was like, 'I'm done.' And to be clear, it's not that I didn't like it; it's that I was physically repulsed.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Hope you like reading!Roadwarden is a really cool text adventure. Oldschool style. No animations or nothing. Just you, your reading comprehension skills and words upon words.But in those words you'll find really cool stories. I found myself really invested in the characters I met and genuinely disappointed when I messed up earning their trust or something similar. Really neat stuff. Hats off to the devs because making a game that is captivating from minimal visuals and writing alone is very tough. The background music provides a good backdrop to your journey as you get to know the land and the locals.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't say enough positive things about Roadwarden. If you've ever enjoyed a Choose Your Own Adventure book, this game's for you. The writing is excellent; if you're a fan of the genre, I'd compare it favorably with what Inkle's done with 80 Days, and the Sorcery series. All your decisions are weighty, and you're afforded lots of them. Check out the demo, if you're on the fence. This game is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent text based narrative game.-Great worldbuilding with fresh, interesting and coherent fantasy elements.-Solid writing throughout.-Strong sense of freedom and player agency.-Lots of places to discover and explore; three dimensional characters to meet; complex factions to approach; deep secrets and mysteries to uncover; monsters to fight or fear.-Constant decision making, from character creation/progression to money/equipment/time management, combat, political relationships. So many choices and actions will shape the experience differntly.-Impressive balance between time limitations of the objectives and scale of the game: all the freedom and opportunities clash with the time constraints in a thrilling and thoughtful way, especially towards the end where every minute and tiny choice counts; and you start seeing the weight of your failures and anchievements.-Small gameplay choices that enhance interactivity and immersion.A surprisingly strong, novel, smartly designed, "ambitious in a good way" narrative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say, even though this is my first text-based adventure game, I think it is a masterpiece. Coupled with my horrible focus for reading (keep spacing out all the time, need to read the same paragraph multiple times), I frequently have a terrible time sticking with a game to it's end, let alone playing through the entirety of one in just a weekend, but I just couldn't stop myself from coming back to this one until it was over. Bought it on a whim, thought I'd never play it, but now I don't regret it one bit and am in fact happy to have done so. If it floats your boat, or if like me, for some reason, you crossed paths with this game and thought it might be fun to play something wholly different, even if you're a bit conflicted about it, give it a shot.Safe travels, warden.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: great game. It would be much better with more content such as leveling up, skills, and some difficult tasks. I don't particularly like the time limit, feels restrained.Anyway, I enjoyed the game very much, it's impressive for a single developer. I hope the author will make a dlc or a similar game soon. I'm willing to pay double the current price.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXCELLENT. BUT ITS VERY SHORT.It's detailed, fun, has a decent story and choice are meaningful but I've gotten as much or more gametime from Choice of Games/Hosted Game stories and the graphics on this and the map mechanic arent worth the extra money when compared to some of the high end CYOA titles that are half this games cost.Graphics are murky/blurry pixels nothing to praise but better than what you'd find in traditional games like this.The soundtrack is  amazing, I'd listen to this as a background track to life.No leveling, no relationship tracking, everything is measured in achievements and progress. You're characters morality is kind of questioned, and you're given opportunities to lie or be greedy vs honest and kind but sometimes when you'd expect an option there isnt one which is kind of shocking and makes the game less appealing. Oh and you can battle hordes of monsters but a couple humans with sticks are stronger than  45 magic apes...When you finish the game you'll have reached the point in which you think, cool I'm ready for the next chapter, but itll be the end and you'll be torn between this was pretty good and it mightve been too short for my money's worth.In short: buy the game while its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Ah... Roadwarden. This game is best enjoyed like a good book by a warm fireplace. This is an awesome visual novel with many different "butterfly effects" and endings.The 36 hours i spent were just one play through on regular mode (40 days). At first, I was concerned about the time limit, but this game is not about being a completionist. I tried to do as much as possible, and left no time remaining. This is a game about role playing. I played as a naive fighter who trusted far too easily, and I enjoyed the whole ride.Feel free to save scum if you want to see how things play out, and do not buy if you do not enjoy reading! Happy Adventuring, Roadwarden!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I love adventure games but often find text-heavy games a struggle to get immersed in. This was true for the first couple of hours of Roadwarden, but if you put your faith in the world it's very rewarding. Excellent characters, plenty of exploring and choices which feel like they actually affect your in-game experience. Beautifully crafted, great writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Man... I don't normally ever bother writing reviews, but this game... Actually, this isn't just a video game, it's a work of art. It deserves a review more than vast majority of games in my library. I have not played a refreshing, unique, breathtaking game such as this since Obra Dinn. Granted, I am not someone who is a visual novel/rpg enthusiast so I may have missed a gem like this in the past. (if I have, feel free to recommend anything remotely similar in the comments)  To get the missing point out of the way - half a point goes for lack of optimisation for Steam Deck. It might have been me, but it was very cumbersome to use. I wish you could use D-Pad to navigate between dialogue options.The other half of the point is the missing cloud saves - although that did prompt me to start a second playthrough on my PC, but I was more than happy to do so (due to the game mechanics) hence only half a point. With that out of the way - onto what I liked about this game. Right from the very start, the game is shrouded with mystery, it makes you curious about the world, about the people, about the secrets... about your purpose as a Roadwarden. The mystery and intrigue is extremely well maintained all the way through to the end of the game. The second thing I noticed was how fitting the audio loops were for each scene. The music and the sound effects selected are simply masterful, I didn't really get bored of listening to any particular one and I heard some way more than others (sue me, I am a  supporter through and through on my first playthrough).If you start with the medium difficulty, in which you get 40 days to do your job. And I have to say, much as I loathe to admit it, I like that in the end. It gives you purpose, it makes you think ahead. You can't dillydally and it makes sense because of where you are, what you're surrounded by and the dangers lurking behind every corner. By the end of it all, you will feel like you've failed or succeeded (if you make it to the end that is...).At first I thought the time limit was ridiculous, but as the days went by I realised the mistakes I've made and where I could have improved - which was exactly what I needed for my second playthrough. From my point, game encourages you and thinks you'll do at least two playthroughs. Why's that? Well, there are three classes to choose from, to start with. Secondly, even on second playthrough, if you role play, you can end up with a COMPLETELY different outcome, which in turn unlocks and explains some mysteries you will have missed the first time round.And boy are the mysteries, the characters, the world rich with background, detail, motives and all the other fancy words. I was hugely impressed by the amount of effort that went into to intertwine all the lore in this game. If you're still reading this... why? Why are you reading this drivel? Open the game, and read about the world yourself. Or do you not have what it takes to become a Roadwarden?
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's unlike any text RPG I've ever played. It has beautiful pixel art of the scenes with new sections being revealed as you explore them. The dialogue is well written, the descriptions are vibrant, the choices are extensive, and the story is very adaptable to each player. Highly, highly recommend. I've put in 27+ hours into it and still haven't finished my first run through cause there's so much to do. <33 (I am trying to 100% to be fair XD)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I found this to be an enjoyable game. It's certainly not for everyone, the vast majority of gameplay is just reading and making choices. I find it hard to get into fantasy most of the time, but this had a decent enough mix of fantasy and reality that I found it mostly immersive. The overall plot was interesting and you get to interact with a lot of different characters with varying backgrounds and religions. It definitely scratched the "adventurer" itch. My personal ending was pretty much a downer across the board, even though I felt like I made pretty good decisions overall. Not sure how many different endings there are. In any case, I wouldn't change my choices and I wouldn't play through it again, but it was a lot of fun in that first play through.If you enjoy text-rich narrative games, you will want to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, well written, and an amazing theme. I have fallen in absolute love with this game, its world, and the characters. It's such a brilliant story, and definitely had an emotional effect on me.  The natural world is so beautifully represented, it brings great danger but also inspires the player to respect it. I love being able to play as a pagan, especially since I myself am one. This is my favorite game of all time, surpassing even Baldur's Gate 3's story imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: First game I've ever left a review for.A genuinely amazing experience, start to finish, Roadwarden tells a beautiful story while allowing you to influence the world just enough to make you really care for the people you interact with, while keeping the game grounded and real.It's not the longest, but I will without a doubt be coming back for more once my memories of the game have time to fade a bit.A++
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: [Preface] I heavily suggest choosing the Casual game mode. A time limit adds a bit of challenge, but if you wish to explore every nook and cranny of the peninsula, you will find yourself cursing the passage of the season. A timed mode is more applicable to those who have seen what is available and know how to navigate the game. Easily one of the best games I've played. Your chosen quest at the beginning of the game isn't a binding contract; you can seek to fulfill it or you can choose directly against it. Your identity, while exerting certain influence, does not gate you from certain choices or outcomes; at worst, you'll have to put a little more effort in. There is an onslaught of decisions with dire consequences, but judgement is never thrust upon the player. You can savescum or you can live with the consequences to your actions. At first, you'll be totally mystified by the world you're in, grappling with strange vocabulary, attempting to decipher the words of the locals, each group speaking in their own heavy accent, expertly portrayed through text. As time goes on, the veil lifts, and you find yourself among a greatly flawed populace. Some are greedy, some are liars, and some are addicts; their first impressions collapse and you're left with people of imperfect action and worldview. Petty squabbles amplify, yet are increasingly seen as fruitless. This coalesces into a theme-defining moment which whisks away one's soul, effortlessly demolishing any image of the peninsula one has so confidently concocted over their journey. It leaves the player, again, with the question they have asked from the beginning: what am I to do?
