_childDocuments_.review: An intimate (and sometimes oppressive) storytelling experience that delights in building a compelling narrative at the cost of traditional gameplay elements. True text-based adventures such as Zork are a relic of the past, but Roadwarden attempts to lightly modernize the experience for those nostalgic for it. The game features useful user features where it counts, with helpful icons on the overworld map and a well-populated, yet not over-saturated journal. The writing is good, playing to its strengths by focusing on the setting and atmosphere, with characters feeling like they're a natural feature within the peninsula's sordid landscape rather than larger-than-life personalities.The game has delightful pixel art, but chooses not to depict any of its characters. The game lets you decide for yourself to embrace its forceful difficulty on its terms, or set your own through an extremely generous save system. You'll no doubt become familiar with the handful of tracks that play throughout your adventure, but much like the game itself, it does not overstay its welcome. The topics addressed by the writing did an excellent job of addressing darker themes and difficult choices, without souring the experience by trotting out unnecessary gore or sexual violence. For those weighing the value of the game, I would encourage you to buy it if you would similarly find value in a dark fantasy novella. Roadwarden achieves its clear objective in that it focuses primarily (both through pixel art and through its textual descriptions) on the places you go and the path you take to get there. I encourage all interested to try out the demo, as the opening hour of the game presented there is an experience that sets the tone, but flourishes further throughout the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Please make more of these, I haven't enjoyed an RPG like this in years! This is an unyielding, deep, dark fantasy text-based RPG, bursting with flavour and adventure. This to me is what life really feels like in a small rural community - the world zooms in to a level where people can directly see the fruits of their labour: clear a road and you open up trade for a village, make a friend who then passes the word of your good deeds on to someone in the next village, and so on. The two greatest strengths of this game are its writing and its choice - there is an absurd amount of branching depending on what choices you make and how you talk to the locals, which really gives you a feeling of true choice. The writing isn't florid, but has a very clear style and tone which sets up the tense, distrustful mood of the peninsula as you slowly battle through the wilderness - the world feels alive with its own culture (and villages have their own individual accents), groups have realistic ambitions and foibles, and you very much feel like an outsider. Speaking of which, your exploration of the world carries genuine and thrilling risk - while there is a map, it starts entirely coated in fog of war; you rely on verbal directions and uncover a rough path one careful step at a time. Your patience, local knowledge and foresight are rewarded more than any other game I have ever played.With this type of game, there is usually a very real risk of boredom - you have to chew through thousands of words and the pace is decidedly slow - but I found the game's pacing impeccable. You transition from tense path-finding and diplomacy early on to finally emerging into the late game as a political player on the peninsula, all while keeping an eye on the clock as your allotted 40 days on the job bleed away.Buy this, curl up with a mug of tea and a blanket, and wile away an evening in the vivid Hovlavan wilds.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I've played anything resembling a text RPG and I'm glad I did! In some ways, I find it a much cleaner experience compared to isometric style games - no needless running around, for example.There is an optional time limit if you play the game (based on the difficulty you select), and honestly? The time limit seems pretty fair. You probably won't be able to accomplish EVERYTHING if you play blind with no save scumming, but you'll certainly be able to accomplish a lot. If you're the type of player (like me) who will only play the game once, some mild save scumming will probably guarantee you can accomplish almost everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great world building. Excellent dialogue. Enveloping music and atmosphere.A little light on inventory management and character development, but this is not your typical action RPG. Im really excited for a sequel of some sort. I'm not into these type of games but I gave it shot and absolutely loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a narrative RPG about understanding and changing (or deciding not to change) a wilderness and its inhabitants. It pairs lovely writing, minimalist art and excellent music together with a really rich RPG system that is packed with branches and responsive characters, rather than dice rolls and statistics. The game almost feels at home alongside games like Outer Wilds or Her Story, because it emphasises information and player knowledge so strongly. I loved every moment with the game, and it's really worth dipping into.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Really an incredible game. Absolutely loved the story and how the pixel art accompanies it. If you like dark fantasy, RPGs, bleak scenarios, and thorough and meaningful decision-making, then this game is for you. I beat it with two endings in 12 hours. You could easily pump way more into this if you made a few save states before critical decisions and made differing choices. Also the soundtrack really is the cherry on top. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I played this for 2.5 hours. It is a text-based game where the player clicks on choices in response. It is a very simple game in mechanics. It's often not easy to know what to do next. This is why I stopped, though I had already covered most of the map. Fortunately, I bought it as part of a bundle. If one wants to give it a whirl, pay no more than a dollar or two. 40/100
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from someone that is not familiar with text based roleplaying RPGs, my only experience with this type of game is Disco Elysium, which is also the reason i picked this up. Disco Elysium left a mark, an itch for more like it, more to sink into, and this delivered.This game reminded me a lot of the book "Spook's apprentice" i read some years ago, it's a more grounded approach to fantasy which i really like, i guess the term would be Dark fantasy? I loved the setting, it feels fleshed out and real, and the ways you affect little bits of the world with you decision, as in, choosing whether [city] did great after the war, or if they are struggling and starving, all in a passing conversation with and NPC about your time there, that's really charming, and helps setting up the world for the character you want to play.The gameplay really gripped me, too. The resource management, including time management, leads to interesting decisions which feel impactful and satisfying, and have repercursions in the rest of the game. And there were parts which i was a tad bit surprised by some gameplay mechanics, but i'll not spoil that. Overall an ejoyable experience, that i'll definitely give time for a second playthrough. This was good! real good.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a good roleplaying experience with rich and fascinating worldbuilding, you will love Roadwarden! With a relatively simple premise and simple pixel graphics, Roadwarden manages to weave a deeply evocative world full of real people and real danger. I've never had a text based rpg capture my interest so entirely!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Disco Elysium, give this game a try. Unlike Disco Elysium, it is almost entirely text-based, except for maps and your inventory, but it offers an equally compelling story, characters, and challenges. You might also enjoy Roadwarden if you like the Divinity: Original Sin, Pathfinder, and Pillars of Eternity games.A little bit about the game: You get to pick a class from three choices: fighter, mage, or scholar. I really enjoyed playing a scholar on my first playthrough. If you play on standard difficulty or higher, you have a limited number of days to complete your overarching mission, so the game also involves a lot of strategy regarding how you spend your time and resources (e.g., food, money, health).My first few hours into the game, I found myself frustrated that my character was low on friends, money, and food, but once I read some advice online about making a little money from  (both available very early on), I started to get a hang of things. I ended up getting really engrossed and completed the game in a couple of days. In the end, I felt happy with my character progression and the outcomes of my decisions. I think the game has a lot of replay potential, and I am sure I will pick it up again. It's well worth the $10.99 at full-price.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very well written and immersive text-RPG. If you're like me you will find yourself caring for the land and its people and do everything in your your power develop it, clear and protect the roads, improving communications and trade. The atmosphere and writing is very good and discovering the different towns, their story, culture and inhabitants gave me the same feeling as reading a good fantasy novel as a teen. The game is visibly a labour of love and the universe is very well thought out. I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The world is rich and interesting and filled to the brim with secrets to uncover. There are still things left unknown even after completing the game, making the time you spend connecting with the people and their intricacies even more precious.There were a few annoyances with having to remember the specific spelling of people's names in order ask about them but overall, I really enjoyed my time as Roadwarden and would recommend it if you are a fan of deep text-based narrative games with light RPG elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An acquired taste, Roadwarden is not going to be for everyone - and not just because it's text-based.It took a surprising amount of time for me to warm to this game - something I hadn't expected as an experienced RPGer who's played many a text-based RPG (including the old school MUDs from the 90s).--  --Roadwarden delivers what it promises on the tin, and offers up rich world-building, story-building and character-development, plus role-playing opportunities in spades.The text is often copious but, if you're a reader, it's nothing you can't get used to. (The ability to skim read will probably help a lot though).Once you find your groove, it's genuinely exciting and easy to immerse yourself in Roadwarden's world. There's no lack of things to do - wild creatures to vanquish, knowledge to discover, ages-old mysteries to solve, fish to trap, bargains to strike, and entire villages of people to win over. There's also so much to do that one playthrough is nowhere near enough to achieve everything you'll no doubt  to do once you really get started, so replay value is high.--  -- Unfortunately and unexpectedly, it took me quite a while to find my groove in this game. I trace this back to some of Roadwarden's decisions around gameplay and mechanics.For instance, your character has a maximum of 4 HP ('vitality'), which are depleted through combat, hard work or, strangely enough for a roadwarden, sleeping in the rough. This means just having one rough night's sleep is enough to have you teetering on the edge of death and unable to fight or work. You also spend quite a bit of time and money making sure your belly is always full since, if you're hungry, you suffer in-game penalties. This was probably my only real complaint about Roadwarden since the hunger mechanism added little to the story or the gaming experience. Instead, it took up far too much headspace than it was worth in terms of ensuring your character was always in good enough condition not to suffer debuffs.Also, unlike classic RPGs, the weapons, armor and combat systems aren't well-formed. You have one gambeson and one battle axe, and that's pretty much it for the whole game (unless you spring some coins on a crossbow to fight flying creatures). The foes you fight in the wild have no visible level or HP, so there's no way for you to make informed decisions about when to fight and when to flee. All combat in Roadwarden feels like swinging your axe in the dark and hoping for the best.All the above meant it took me about 15 in-game days to find a good balance and actually start enjoying everything that Roadwarden has to offer, which - admittedly - is a lot.Unfortunately, the slow start together with the game's time cap (40 in-game days on 'normal' difficulty) meant my game was suddenly and sadly cut short before I could see things satisfyingly play out. --  -- Roadwarden is not without its shortcomings, but it is a promising little game. I say 'promising' because I have yet to finish and experience it properly - and by all accounts it seems there is much more to experience.Will I come back to Roadwarden? Maybe. The game is good enough to make me want to come back. But its shortcomings are also just annoying enough for me to consider booting up a different game in my library instead.Rating: 7/10---** EDIT: I did end up coming back to Roadwarden, playing it on story mode the second time around - with no in-game time cap. This made a genuine difference in my enjoyment of the game and I'm glad I had another try at it. I'd highly recommend playing it this way. It's still worth noting that Roadwarden doesn't offer the 'classic' detailed mechanics of ye olde RPGs, so approach it with an open mind. **EDITED RATING: 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a treasure. Roadwarden is a robust, text heavy adventure RPG unlike any I can recall having played. The closest recent experience I can compare it to would be Disco Elysium or Citizen Sleeper, though less like Disco primarily for the absence of an isometric UI, favoring instead a fairly simple renpy-esque design. The premise is fairly simple, and I won't give away too much as the world is a huge part of the beauty of this game (and discovering / exploring / drinking in that world): you are a kind of mixture of an adventurer, guard and mercenary, the titular Roadwarden. You have been sent to an untamed land in the north to fulfil the duties of a Roadwarden, namely to guard the rural portions of the Empire of this world which are too vast to be secured through patrols of the army. This world contains an abundance of dangerous flora and fauna, and while many may have familiar names they are in almost all ways uniquely redesigned in this world. You move through the world guided by simple static images accompanied by lovingly crafted robust writing that fills your mind with the details and images of this world. Immersive is the word that comes to mind most insistently for me when it comes to the flavor of this game, I truly felt like I was living in this world while I played this game. Choices range from complex to simple, mundane to fantastic, and from guaranteed to chancy (though your true odds are hidden except by discerning the context, randomness indicated only by the presence of an unclarified symbol of a six sided die). Choices are a driving feature of this game. With the time allotted in a standard session (though you can turn that time limit off) I don't think it's possible to do everything in one play through. That's even more the case because some choices are exclusive: there are a variety of decisions you make about your  character at the start, for instance, that heavily influence the nature of your playthrough. Further, almost anytime you meet someone new you can decide the verbal and non-verbal 'tone' of your interaction from five choices, in theory altering the initial character of your relationship with nearly anyone. While many of the 'quests' might be repeated between playthroughs, many have a variety of possible outcomes. If you love to feel like your choices matter, I feel you ought to be very satisfied with this game. I just finished my first playthrough and it was delightful. I really can't give more glowing praise to it, with only a couple of asterisks:First, it is text-heavy. Big time. If you aren't a reader, or if the quality of a game's writing isn't enough to make you enjoy a text-heavy experience, you may sadly need to take a pass on this one. Secondly, and this might be totally me specific but...the name of the studio, Moral Anxiety studios, couldn't be more accurate. Sometimes I don't have the mental fortitude to boot the game up because the immersion is so intense and the burden of so many of the choices so visceral that I just don't have the heart for it. Its a hard world in so many ways, and with things as they are in our own real world, heavy games are not always what I want to boot up. That said, the game is underscored heavily by a funny kind of optimism. The characters feel very believable. There are only a few (honestly, maybe just one) characters I might accuse of being evil; generally, they float around neutral in a way that feels very believable and authentic. Most people, in my experience, aren't good or evil in clear terms - they are just who they are, good and bad. Do with all that what you will.Long review summed: 9.5 / 10; a treasure for the right player who can look past a writing heavy UI.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.  A well-written text-based RPG, and maybe one of the best I've ever played.  Beautiful pixel graphics and a subtle but engaging soundtrack add depth to the nuanced story line.  You definitely want to go into this game blind the first time, as the initial experience is part of the beauty and joy of a good story-telling.  Like any good story, you'll still want to re-visit it and re-tell it from time to time, and the latest updates included with the 1-year anniversary have made the story even better for the next re-telling.  Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An engrossing story and setting delivered through elegantly simple presentation and mechanics that keep me coming back for more. I wish I was half as adept with words than this game is so as to give it the lavish praise it deserves, but I shill have to content myself with saying that it is well worth your time and one of the most enjoyable offerings I've experienced this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A part of this game reminds me a little bit of Darklands (an early 1990s text based RPG) which is a great thing. What I like about this game is that while the setting feels grim and hopeless at the beginning, the story does bring a bit of hope if you make the right choices. It has a good story-line and will keep you entertained for several hours.If you like the visual novel / choices matter genre then this a great game to play. If you're also a cheapskate like me, buy it when it is on special for <$10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I dont play many text based games, but I have played this one through twice now. What a beautiful, brutal, aching, and inspiring world this creator has made. The world building drew me in immediately and the strong character writing kept me going. I felt like all the characters had their own perspective and none were weighed down by out-dated gendered ideas. The women could be aggressive, evil, brutal. The men just as kind and emotional as anyone else. A truly beautiful story with an incredible soundtrack to back it up. Even the pixel art felt so in-tune with the aesthetic of the whole piece.A beautiful work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game - austere and brutal, thematic and flexible in its mechanics and story design. Highly recommended for those who like a deep RPG experience. A few things for the Devs:- it would be helpful if names, dialogue, objects, and key words were highlighted in the text like place names are. As a skimmer, I often found myself missing key information - the lack of a hint system is quite punishing and took the steam out of the game for me. It doesn't need to be explicit. In an example, if I'm trying to get someone to trust me a line suggesting 'they might trust me if I offer them X' would be extremely helpful and make me feel I can make progress. If I'm to solve a puzzle I appreciate a clear view of the puzzle I need to solve. This systems presence could be an optional mode of the game for users less interested in a long term grind and more interested in exploring the wonderful story this game offers - the user entry "what do you look for" sections would benefit from a great deal more guidance, as I found the lack of steering really difficult to overcome and I ended up ignoring those sections, probably to the detriment of story opportunities- the lack of active quest logs with waypoints and instructions makes coming back to the game after a time away a real chore; reading back through all the logs is a big taskThanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is essentially a text based rpg where you role play a roadwarden who naturally travels the roads of the land delivering messages, fighting mosnters, doing odd jobs, etc. This game has no real time combat, only dice rolls. I bring that up because for many people that may be a deal breaker. However, if you are ok with a completely text based game this is an amazing experience. Perhaps what I enjoy the most about roadwarden is that the world doesn't spell everything out for you. You're forced to pay attention to the information you gather from npc's or the world in order to understand what is going on and make your own inferences whether they be wrong or right. For the right person this results in an extremely immersive experience. Throughout the game you will travel the roads completing quests for the various villages and villagers which in turn increases their trust in you as their roadwarden. Once you get in good with a village/villager they may be willing to share more information about themselves or the world around you, not to mention they may toss a few draon bones your way. (money) Which you can use to upgrade your gear or maybe buy a room at a fancy inn for the night. basically what we have here is an old school rpg done right that has a very interesting world with many things to do and places to see. Its a very fun time and i have no complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, as soon as I bought this game I played nothing else. I never played older text based RPGs but once I finished this game I immediately was searching the web for anything even remotely similar. The makers do a wonderful job of creating an engrossing atmosphere. I was thinking about the connections of different people and recalling the lore that characters had passed to me at my day job. I couldn't wait to get home and become one with the world.I appreciate the options to put a time limit on the game which makes it a little more strategic and also the option to fully focus on the story. The options to choose different goals and also belief systems for your character are so cool as well and is fun to see what traits you gain from this later on. Once I let this play settle I'm definitely starting a new game with a whole new character personality. This is one of the few games that makes me want to achievement hunt and explore every inch of it. I can't wait to see the developer do more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this over a year after I played it, it is the deepest and most engaging choose your own adventure novel that I ever played. The game is filled with lore that is relevant and felt throughout the experience, and manifests in a lot of narrative and strategic choices. Among the best stories I have had the pleasure of experiencing in a video game. It is very heavy on reading, so I wouldn't recommend it if that deters you, but otherwise as someone who doesn't have much experience with text heavy rpg games, I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game with really intriguing lore. Thanks to the well-written descriptions, you can feel the personality of each individual character and easily imagine what everything looks like - the world around you, the characters, the wildlife and your own actions. The story is also very enjoyable, presenting fantasy elements coupled with gritty reality, and your decisions truly have an impact. After 100%ing the game, there are still some interactions I've not seen, so there is some replayability aswell.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: what a game.....ending & central storyline at times felt a bit lackluster, but other than that minor & personal complaint it was a stellar experience. delicious prose, captivating soundtrack, heartwarming and thought-provoking characters. well worth a play, esp for fans of games like disco elysium and planescape torment
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I wouldn't like it, boy was I wrong!Game plays like a well written book without taking away from the feeling that you're the one making choices, and you can feel like a badass without feeling stupidly OP. There's always a beast around the corner to put you in your place and humble you.10/10 will play again!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gem, a masterpiece.It remembers me the books "choose your own adventure" I read when I was a kid.All in this game has a great quality: the setting is original, the quests and characters are very interesting, the art and music are attractive, and I like the invetory management and interactions.90% is reading, but what you read is very interesting, even for me, who has a medium level in English and must translate some words, spending more time in the proccess of reading.In my opinion Roadwarden is one of the best games of the year. Very recommended.Congrats to the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a fascinating game!If you enjoy role playing and a more laid back, story and character driven game where choices really matter, this will likely wind up on your top ten list. Well worth the money and there's a fair amount of replayability to it as you attempt to tighten up your run, earn all achievements, and earn the perfect ending.9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and well written texted based rpg. Excellent writing and plenty of options on how to go about everything from simple bartering, doing side quests, and most importantly exploring what the peninsula has to offer. The ending is a great reflection on how you did and encourages multiple playthroughs since you will curious to find out how you could have changed everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, but this is one of the best stories I've ever played. It's actually really queer and trans in a casual way which made me feel like, I could really be a part of this world, and I got immersed in a way I normally don't in fantasy games. Please try this game if you're at all interested in RPGs, and you're OK with reading a lot. I'm not a very patient person, I can't believe I spent over 20 hours reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of my new favorite indie games. has a great atmosphere and story if you are willing to read the text. I never skipped the dialogue or description boxes and I think it added a lot to my playthrough. Really well done dark fantasy. And its a masterpiece for your wallet. Took me 16 hours to complete the game on one class. A bit less than that on my second character, but the game has high replay-ability since you learn so much more on the second run after you know what you are doing.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Something rare and special. This game reminds one of the old "Choose your adventure" books, where disaster feels constantly at your door. This is an RPG in the truest sense, allowing a player to choose from many pathways and moral stances and no matter how well one chooses, you are always left wondering how you could have done better. I left the game inspired. These characters and this world, from the long hours of night to the winding pathways of the woods have left a mark on me. Thank you for something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful world creation.Despite simple starting goal the plot is surprisingly deep and intricate - if you're willing to explore it.The world seems to be alive and reacts to your actions. Not all of them will be rewarded, because as in life, different sides will have different views on the situation/problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect reminder of what a good game actually is, right at the core. There is no need for AAA graphics, shaders, production and effects, to make a game world come true. With little more than words, this game crafts an amazing universe, as complete as any of the top RPGs'. The picture of the game universe you build in your mind as you play through the game is clearer than any level of graphical detail could portray. The lore is astoundingly cohesive. One of the best RPG games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: My first steam game. I was a pc gamer way back in the early 90s up to 1999 and love text games. So for me this is a joy to play & takes me back. If you like text base games give this a go it has quite a bit of replay to it as well. If you don't like to read then this game is not for you.PS. Thank you  for  reading my review8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Tried out the demo, was immediately hooked! I was enamored by the world and I adore the writing style. My only gripe is that it felt a bit lacking at the end. I had managed to complete everything I wanted to see in my first and only playthrough and even though I would've loved to play more, I was struggling to figure out what I would explore in my second playthough. It felt like some plot lines were dropped a bit at the end and I'm not sure if that was because I missed something or if it was just ending more abruptly than I expected. All in all, 100% recommend, but there is something missing at the late/post game part. This is not a huge gripe though, since I would definitely put this in my top ten list for being very good at what I love from these types of games!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what to expect playing a game like this, but after putting more than 200 hours into Disco Elysium on the old Steam account I called mine before I decided to give it all up and become Golden Hat Mick, I was pretty confident Roadwarden would be a worthwhile journey in the early days of my new gaming identity. I was wrong — it was way better than merely worthwhile. It shattered those humble expectations, crushed them as if they were a fragile human shell in the hands of an enraged frightape.After five playthroughs and just over 80 hours, I've managed to uncover a good chunk of what this game has to offer, and I can confidently state that it's a world more gamers need to experience. Whatever is lacking in the graphical element is easily replaced by competent sound design and sufficient geography artwork to stay connected to the environment. This is largely a text-based experience, but presentation quality is superb, and I don't mind reading, especially prose as polished as Roadwarden's.Each of the major locations is unique, its characters memorable, and the impact you as the roadwarden can have on the final outcome is significant. You won't get far in your first investigation unless you're playing on the easiest setting, and if you're like me, you'll be eager to jump right back in and start anew regardless. Even now, after having finally finished a satisfying run that cleared my lengthy quest list, not everything went how I planned, and I forgot to tie up at least one loose end. And echoing thoughts of others, the ending narrative never feels quite as satisfying as it should.That's a small matter, however. Credit to Moral Anxiety Studios on a fantastic adventure. I hope for further content down the road, if not in Roadwarden, then in other creations. I'm a full believer in the talents of this small-but-promising studio, and I'll be following their progress closely. As for me, I don't think I can stop my visual novel momentum at this point. I've already got my eye on several other titles like this one, and I'll be mixing plenty of them in along whatever winding path that gaming takes me.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I adore the world and story the developer made. Piecing together everyone's background and intentions was great. Yall have very nice writing styles. It's soundtrack expresses a variety of emotions, and Foggy's is probably my favorite. I really like the artstyle, it feels hostile and comforting. Thank's m80
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden feels like a cozy tabletop RPG session with one player (you!) and one very ambitious dungeon master. Placing players in the dusty boots of a Roadwarden, which is basically a hybrid park ranger/highway patrolman, the game lavishes you with rich descriptions of a living, dangerous world where survival is paramount and a single misstep can mean doom. Every choice feels weighty and important, and your decisions also go far in shaping the world in many unexpected ways. This game also provides one final stroke of brilliance by allowing your character to choose their motivations early on. With the railroading nature of most CRPG plots, this simple addition seems so obvious in hindsight but is usually entirely overlooked. If you're missing a tabletop group in your life, Roadwarden goes far in filling that gap. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for the full release since the very first time I saw this game on a YouTube gaming channel, and I have to say: the wait was worth it. Roadwarden, in a effort to bring back a forgotten RPG genre, managed to not only succeed on it's goal, but also to exceed all my expectations. It's a marvelous, beautifully written text based game, with memorable and diverse characters and a vivid world that brings a breath of fresh air to a genre that desperately needed it. I'm not a big fan of text based games, but Roadwarden does it's job so well that I'm sure that many others, like me, will be surprised with what this game has to offer.Wait no longer, my friends: buy it, support the devs for this masterpiece and enjoy many hours of gameplay like I did ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because of all the reviews recommending it and commending its good writing and story line.  Now I have joined that crowd.   This game is well written and has a great storyline(s).This game is old school, only a few steps up from the text only RPGs of the 1990s.  The neat thing is that a game like this does not need to be any more technically advanced.  It provides a good outline and gives you enough aids to your imagination to fill in all the details - at least if you happen to have an imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than expected. Roadwarden plays like a very well prepped old school pointcrawl exploration tabletop RPG, because that's exactly what it is, adapted to the electronic medium. Bonus points for letting the player participate in worldbuilding through dialogue options.Get it. Play it. It's really, really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I just have to say: this is such an underrated game, and I wish it got more love and attention! In all of my experience of playing point and click adventure games, this is one of the best. It's immersive, calming, inspiring, and incredibly engaging with its colorful writing, fun NPCs, mysterious storytelling, and spectacular world-building. Hats off to Moral Anxiety Studio and Assemble Entertainment for this one-of-a-kind adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of world-building done here is incredible. I spent over an hour reading through the glossary and bestiary of the world before even starting the adventure. Few peoples' experiences with this game are going to be the same with all the many paths and people that will be constantly pulling you in different directions.Be prepared for 16+ hours of reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game, just the right length and depth for its genre. It didn't meet my expectations going in, but the quality of what it actually was proved enough for me. I played it over the course of a few slow, rainy days, and if anyone finds themselves in the same circumstances, I heartily recommend Roadwarden.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It felt truly immersive and i love all the small details added to it. The monsters, their characteristics, knowing if you can try scaring it or plainly running away. The world is magical, and extremely challenging, and it just makes you want for more. I hope the author will make more stories within the same world.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the best writing of any media I've ever consumed, and a remarkably well characterized world. The gameplay mechanics are interesting and there is plenty of questing to do, but if the idea of exploring around helping various people and staying alive doesn't pique your interest, I'd still recommend it but a second thought may be warranted.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: When I first picked up this game I was pretty neutral about it.But after getting back into and really paying attention it just scratches an itch I never knew I had. In the text based conversations where you have to input your own text to act it is so satisfying in comparison to just choosing an option.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible, engaging story. The world of Roadwarden immediately draws you into the story. You walk in with a clear objective, and then many more soon follow. I found myself driven to help the people I met. I wanted to be the dedicated Roadwarden. The game is reading and thoughtful choices. There seem to be many different ways to solve the same problem (some paths easier than others). This is an excellent, must-play game in its sphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A great gem of a game that checks every box that a story-book RPG should :Great atmospheric music, simplistic yet evocative pixel art to help set the scene,Decisions that have real consequences further down the line.An exciting world to discover filled with interesting characters.And a rewarding time / resource management system.To sum it up, its a great story that is absolutely worth a try.Also it has a demo, so there are few excuses not to.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Well written rpg game. Mysterious land, some political issues, grey people and decisions. If you willing to read some texts you must try this game. My advice first try the challenging difficulties then start a new no time limit playthrough so you can discover what you've missed.I really hope they will make new good games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Well, as I play games based on what catches my eye I gave ROADWARDEN a try. This game is so well made i had to gave it a thumb up.This game is rich in terms of decisionmaking and characters complexity. I really felt the consequences of my choices. I think that's rare nowadays. It is worth to note that if you don't like reading you should not play this. The walls of text are just showing one after another which lets's your imagination do the work of GPU. The main and sub stories are not simple ones so you have to make hard decisions with little knowledge on a subject sometimes which is nice.  Worth to note that acoustic part is awesome in my opinion. I recommend this especially for those who wants something different than mainstream games. Really refreshing game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptionally written, beautifully crafted. I enjoyed the bits of medieval history and sociology that were incorporated into the story - such as two-phase sleep, which I've never seen incorporated into a video game story before. Roadwarden's world is so finely crafted that it gives you the impression it continues to exist outside of your observation of it. As you meet people, observe (and fight) monsters, and visit new places you'll slowly piece together how the little villages and societies of Roadwarden function. The thrill of that discovery is a feeling that persists through the entire game. It also has my favorite party-based exploration event since Mass Effect 2's suicide mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Its been hours since I completed my 3rd playthrough yet this game is still ALL I can think about. I am SO incredibly enamored and obsessed with Roadwarden, I love everything about it!!! The writing, worldbuilding, mechanics, art, soundtrack, meaningful choices... all perfectly tuned to create a deeply immersive experience that I desperately wish to relive again for the first time. Also, its such a refreshingly unique take on the visual novel/IF style and really explores the potential of the genre! The story connected with me in ways I couldn't even begin to describe, and my heart is sorely aching for more :( Easily my favorite game of all time!True that its not a game for everyone, but I will Still recommend it to everyone because its THAT GOOD. The amount of text to read is definitely a valid obstacle for some players, but if you can get through that, I promise that its worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I just finished my 1st 40 days on medium difficulty.  I suspect I've only scratched the surface here, so I jumped straight back in for another 40 days.   A good chunk of my early teenage years were spent w/ fighting fantasy books and this brings all those good memories back.  Game absolutely deserves the glowing reviews <3
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I completed my first playthrough of Roadwarden in around 12 hours, on the Normal difficulty, which has a time limit of 40 in-game days. Normally, games with time limits give me anxiety that makes it difficult to complete them. Roadwarden's time limit never gave me anxiety - it gave me a sense of purpose.You see, in most RPGs, it's sensible to snatch up every quest you can, pick at every loose thread, ask every character every question available at any given time. In Roadwarden, you are encouraged to and rewarded for prioritizing your goals - and the game leaves it up to you to decide what your goals really are. With only 40 days to explore the peninsula and meet its inhabitants, there is simply not enough time to do everything for everyone. It's a beautiful change of pace from the average RPG, and its world is masterfully presented through a combination of text and lush pixel art. If you like fantasy stories and/or visual novels, Roadwarden is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game had been on my radar for quite some time during it's development since the aesthetic of Roadwardens from Warhammer Fantasy always appealed to me. Now that it's out it has surpassed all my expectations and the writing has left me compelled to keep playing. 10/10 would steal freaky magic seeds again

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very nice slow text based game. Fair warning though, it's very slow paced with little combat, with stats mostly being gained or lost from more menial things like getting a bad night's rest. Most time spent is you walking the outer forest paths to meet the villages and pass news between them. It's a very specific story for a specific audience, if the idea of just being a person walking around in the woods helping out any random people you see doesn't appeal to you then maybe skip this game. I've also often heard the setting being compared to the Witcher, particularly the books.For a review on the basic game mechanics, I'd say it's pretty solid as far as text based adventures go. The game very rarely asks you to input specific words, and most of the time the answers to those situations are pretty obvious if you're paying attention, with one exception being a certain spider. Otherwise the game generally presents you with a wide array of options that never felt too restrictive. The game also has 4(5 if playing as the mage) stats that change how events play out. As a general rule, being full on food and health helps you be strong, appearance will generally save you time because people will be more likely to give you/progress quests when you first meet them, and armor stops the other stats from going down as often. Just vaguely try to keep all the numbers up and you'll be fine. The game also has 3 classes, Warrior Mage and Scholar. The game recommends warrior at first, but they all have somewhat similar capabilities in general life. The warrior starts with better gear and has strength based abilities while at high health, the mage has a magic pool to use on stuff but has a few input issues which are annoying, and the scholar can gather potions and herbs and can read which comes in vaguely helpful at random times.The game has 3 difficulties, but I'd only recommend the hardest for challenge runs after you've beaten the game once. The other 2 mostly decide whether or not the day limit will be active, which is a bit of a point of contention. Personally, I like the idea of the 40 day limit because i'm a weird person who thinks that endings that don't answer all the questions are cool, but if you're not good at rpgs and tend to do things slowly, or want to see all the quests and not get any bad endings then that's what the easy mode is for.Oh, and this game has a lot of transcribed accents. I dinnae think it much a problem, but ye may ne care for it

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. You can tell there's been a lot of love poured into it and as someone who usually struggles with holding attention while reading I must admit the writing is very engaging and keeps you intrigued at all times. The pixel art and the soundtrack are lovely and together with the interesting story form a truly deeply immersive and atmospheric experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun narrative adventure with multiple ways to approach the challenges. Make sure to take notes, LOTS of notes. The bulk of the game is text, but there are images and some simple animations to keep it interesting. As Roadwarden, you travel around the wilds, help people, chase off or kill monsters, and try to stay alive. Each action takes time, so you have to plan your routes and where to lay your head at the end of the day. The story is engaging and worth taking the time to tease out the secrets of the wilds. It has a good length and doesn't wear out its welcome. I would love to see more adventures in this series or other stories with similar gameplay. If you're looking for a visual novel that doesn't devolve into a romance simulator, give this one a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: The wall is still standing. There are no wolves around, no stench of blood. Good signs.	This should be the place I've been looking for. I was supposed to meet with a group of soldiers, but I hear no voices, no sounds of labor.	The gate is ajar, the camp isn't safe. It may keep out the goblins and pebblesrs, though not the beast folk, nor trolls. Night is drawing near.	Fara breathes heavily, she's had a long day.	I dismount her, my heavy boots hit the ground. Pain of the long ride catches up with me. I stretch out, bringing my back and legs some comfort. 	All I want now is a table , a decent chair, a nice mug of mead and some warm stew.	With any luck, my axe won't be needed here.	If this is a military encampment, it doesn't look the part. Plenty of wasted space, and the fire pit is cold.	Two soldiers are sitting at a table, they appear tired and disheartened. They look in different directions, paying no attention to one another. One of them is holding a cup.	As I approach, it takes them a few breaths to glance in my direction. The first soldier greets me with a wave of his hand. There are bags under his eyes, his beard is unkempt. Despite his simple shirt, he's wearing durable, decent boots.	A mace, with a head covered in iron hangs at his side, though he doesn't reach for it.	I look at the second solder, and just like me, she's wearing a gambeson. It fits her a bit loose, as if she took it off a corpse. Her head is shaven, perhaps protection from lice. Her eyes weary, yet kind. She smiles at me.	Considering the detachment was sent here half a year ago, these two certainly look the part. Though there should be more of them. Eight, I believe I was told. 	"It's nice to see an unarmed traveler in this forsaken ♥♥♥♥ hole, makes me just a tiny bit hopeful." The bearded man says in a strong, yet timid voice. "You'll be staying the night with us, I guess?"	"We're soldiers, he and I." adds the armored woman. Her posture switches from half asleep to relaxed.  "We'll do our best to keep the camp safe, if you were to take the first watch, it would be a huge help. Travelers ought to help each other, wouldn't you say?"	I think for a moment, to fully rest, I'd need a good nights sleep. Reluctantly I agree.	"Fantastic!" she rubs her hands together. "I don't remember the last time I had more than half a nights sleep. The hours before midnight should be the calmest. Just wake us up if anything happens".	The man flashes me a wide smile, "It's easy to wake us up, just yell." then takes a drink from his mug.	"I was hoping to meet with your sergeant, could we talk for a bit?"	The woman lets out a loud sigh, dusts off her gambeson, and steps towards me. She pays little attention to the sword at her side. 	"We most definitely can, you and I, though holding this rank is still somewhat new to me. Are you a messenger? Did you lose your mount?" Observing me with curiosity. "Or are you looking for help?"	"I'm your new roadwarden, my horse is tied up outside." I reply.	"Really?!" The solder in the shirt leans forward. "That explains how you arrived here in one piece, and all by yourself."	"Better bring your horse inside the palisade." adds the sergeant. "We have no hay, but I bet it dreams of dropping its saddle." A long pause. "I'm Tulia by the way." 	She reaches out her hand. "Haleth." I reply. 	Her grasp is confident, the shake is slight. "Just keep your horse away from the tent." She steps away. "We don't need to smell it's dung."	"Ah, there's one issue." The soldier in the shirt rises to his feet. "We've no tent to spare, you'll have to use a blanket or something." 	"I should get accustomed to sleeping on the ground anyway." I reply. 	I walk through the gate. Fara looks around and snorts anxiously.	Not many humans could ride a horse. She's not only taller than I am, she's also bulky, and as heavy as she's strong. I can get into the saddle within a single breath. Most people wouldn't know where to even begin. From every side, she's a wall of flesh.	Horses were brought to The Dragonwood from the conquest in the South. They can trot for a long time, though won't outrun some of the local monsters. My palfrey needs me to survive, though, without her, I too would be lost.  	She's my only companion here. I want her to feel at ease.	Fara takes a few steps towards me, scolding me with another snort. I scratch the bottom of her neck, with strength and confidence, just the way she likes it.	Humans see useful animals, and even pets, as monsters in disguise. Getting emotionally attached to them is believed to lead humans to their doom. 	I know horses need companionship.	I speak gently and lead her to the fire pit. Removing the saddle makes her nicker with relief. I take a couple of minuets to examine her back, just in case. While the riding equipment is not that heavy for such a strong animal, with enough time it starts to chafe. 	I wish she had something better to eat than this shabby grass. I should look for an inn.	I need to unpack.	I haven't brought that many things, and I lost one of the sacks while fleeing the Crimson Corps Eaters. Worst of all, I have no rope left, maybe the soldiers could spare one. Shouldn't cost more than a dragon bone.	Aside from the travel set, I own a few valuable possessions, essentials for my trade.	I spent my life's savings on decent combat equipment. A fine gambeson, an axe made of steel and a reliable crossbow with bolts.	I unpack and inspect my belongings. My water skin isn't pierced and the spare clothes are still here. Just in case, I take a look at my wooden bowl and mug, my cape, tinder box, bandages, food rations, knife... nothing special or too cumbersome.	From time to time my routine helps me avoid mistakes, this doesn't always make it any more exciting. 	I return to the soldiers, who are sitting at the table again. They are observing my horse and chatting between themselves. My stomach growls at the sight of them eating out of wooden bowls.	One more bowl was put at a previously unused end of the table. I can sit down on a tree log.	I join them and take a look at the meal. 	It is cold gruel, the meal eaten in times of hardship. This specific bowl is filled with water, hog millet, some strange looking cereals and blueberries.	Welcoming me with a meal, even a humble one, is beyond their duty. Soldiers live with and for their companions, constantly on the move from one part of the realm to another, making sacrifices to protect their group as they face dozens of hideous creatures. Their lives are filled with discipline, hardship and camaraderie.	Roadwardens, on the other hand, learn how to work by themselves. We seldom engage in open combat. Patrolling the same roads for years on end. We help the settlements stay in touch, maintain commerce, settle down, and forge friendships. When there are no laws to follow, we use our own judgment.	Different responsibilities, different lifestyles.	I eat quickly, not focusing on the taste, then speak with Tulia.	She looks focused and is choosing her words carefully. Looking away when gathering her thoughts.	"I'm afraid I can tell you less than I would like and less than I should." Nodding toward the other soldier. "As you can see, there's not a lot of us left. At the beginning of summer there were eight of us, including our previous sergeant. Five are dead, one has run away in tears."	"We're also strangers in this land." adds her companion.	I smile. "Any piece of information may help me do my job."	The man leans forward, his legs shake nervously. He sounds like a kid asking a bard to sing on more tale, tell a joke, or do a magic trick. Whatever it takes to escape from boredom. His untrimmed beard hides a much younger face than I originally thought. 10 of 10 so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden takes a fairly interesting premise and implements a mechanically competent game about it, but is fatally dragged down by wordlbuilding that's in practice fundamentally uninteresting and moderately unpleasant to inhabit.On a technical level, the game is impressive. If it weren't for the familiar save menu I would have no idea this was derived from a standard RPG engine, and its writing and art are really consistent with their tone and aesthetic. There were only a couple spots where the mechanics got in the way of the game, and I particularly praise Roadwarden for only having a couple examples of the classic RPG problem of selecting a reasonable prompt resulting in an insane course of action - no, when I said to make some space I did not mean you should blindly step back toward the growling you heard behind you.The only consistently bad mechanic were the bits where it asks you to manually query a text box. These were always a bit frustrating, frequently missed obvious potential inputs, and in a couple places were maddeningly obstructive. For some reason the big spider in front of the bandit camp has one of these, and it wouldn't accept any of the reasonable courses of action I tried - fight, look closer, go around, distract, nothing. No idea what the issue with that one is.Roadwarden also has a setting with a fairly interesting base premise. Medieval humanity, but the wilds are harsh and aggressive, full of beasts. If any settlement cuts too far into the woods, a tide of monsters will be roused to anger, and everyone gets their torso atomized by unicorns. Neat idea!The problem is in the execution of this - the world turns out to be basically the same as reality, except there's some magic around and everyone's kind of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ [meaniepants]. On the worldbuilding side of things, it's just weird that there's no response to this new aspect. The cities have some form of walls around them, but nobody is trying to develop solutions or defenses to the monsters. There are no specialists who train to kill them, no movement promising to eradicate and tame the woods for good, nobody theorizing a way to mitigate this issue, no real exploration of the smattering of different opinions people have about humanity's relationship to the wilds. The more fatal problem is the second half - everyone in the game is kind of a shallow jerk. I made it through a ten-hour playthrough without finding a single character I was invested in. Nobody with big dreams, only a couple people that were nice to talk to. People charge a fortune for everything - the important secrets or services seriously require the majority of the cash in the game, you can probably buy like 1.5 of them, maybe two if you buy nothing else. Beyond selling, nobody's willing to tell you anything? People are so tight-lipped and standoffish it genuinely stretched my suspension of disbelief. Seriously? There's not a single person on this entire peninsula that will tell me what happened to that town, except for the one innkeeper that wants to charge the equivalent of two months of room and board for the info? Nobody mentioned the tribe that lives off to the east and keeps to themselves when I was asking about the major settlements of the area? It feels less like a realistic part of the setting and more like the developer reaching out from behind the scenes to gag the setting because it would be too easy otherwise.I ran out of time after uncovering what seems to be the main mysteries of the game, and just went home because there wasn't really a financial path forward and I didn't care about these people. Got a postgame report that the merchants guild decided not to expand north, every faction either died under a horde of undead or barely held on, and I felt nothing.I went to start another run, to see if I could figure out the grand mysteries of my predecessor on the secret island or awakening the spirit of the forest to cure a plague or figuring out what the deal with those bandits was or learning what happened to that town... but while I was selecting the difficulty for it I just stopped and took stock. Why bother? I don't actually care about any of it, really. I'm not invested, in any of these people or places or groups. Hell I'm not even invested in Leto's wellbeing, the game really feels like it should be a roguelike but the one time I died (killed from full health and armor in one hit without any real recourse, thanks for that by the way) the game just lets you restart that one encounter and continue on your way. The game claims to be about razor's-edge survival in the savage wilderness but the moment actual stakes rear their head it automatically savescums for you. The only real failure state is the time limit - the game would actually be much more engaging if it was as lethal as it claimed to be and reset the run when you died, letting you get a little better each time as you gradually uncover the mysteries of the peninsula and work toward a successful run.There's a critical lack of dynamism in the world here. The only group that wants to change things are the merchants that sent you north to scout, and you only talk to them, briefly, once. No people or factions with great dreams or aspirations, nobody that even wants to get along. I mean, get this - for most details about the civilization you come from to the South, y'know the only source of change in this setting, when you're asked about them you have a full range of options to essentially make up that bit of the setting on the spot. When the most important aspect of your setting is so nothing that its details and relationships to other elements can accommodate a full range of different and even contradictory options with no impact on the broader setting, that's... I don't even know what that is. Not a sign of interesting worldbuilding, that's for sure.Why would I want to keep playing a game that's just like real life but worse? Humans aren't like this in real life, the universal and inexplicably ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ [meaniepantsness] is a bigger obstacle than the monsters, and there's no aspect of the game that makes me curious or interested. For a fantasy game, I can't think of a more fundamental condemnation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's understated art style and music allow the audience's focus to settle onto the writing, which evocatively describes a harsh but intriguing world. Even more impressive is that unlike so many visual novels, ROADWARDEN is only very rarely overwritten and barely ever does lore dumps for the sake of lore dumps. Everything you learn about people, places or creatures does end up having a practical purpose in-game. Learning one village's backstory helps you make appropriate offerings to them when you first meet. Learning about the ecology of the setting's monsters helps you make better tactical decisions in combat. The game's RPG elements are also brilliant, and a welcome addition to the VN formula. There is a surprising diversity of builds or strategies to pursue, especially for such a mechanically light game.Roadwarden is a beautiful narrative game and many of its details and questions will linger in your mind for a long time after playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the best text-based adventure game I have played. And a rarity even in that because there actually is meaningful replay value that is not based on random generated stuff. Obviously there lots of reading and often you may lose the idea of what your character actually knows or should be doing, especially if you have some break between playing. But that is more or less the problem with the genre rather than this game, rather this game does these things better so that you can roleplay it rather than trying to do the correct things and still achieve, something. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. If you're looking for an extremely unique text based adventure with beautiful pixel art to match, this is the game you're looking for. Just finished my very first full play through as a mage, and I'm left wanting more. Every village is unique and interesting, every quest line is immersive and truly makes you feel as if you are in the shoes of the Roadwarden. My only criticism is that the text based search feature can often leave you confused as to what to do. I would love to see a sequel where you play as a different Roadwarden in the future. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a game that is really solid, as long as you know what you're getting into.Chill music, understated visuals that let you fill in the gaps, an epic adventure that you get to control, but make no mistake- This is a game about reading. I thought all the writing was great, so this wasn't a problem (I also knew more or less what the game was beforehand). It's like Yojimbo plus Watership Down in a grim fantasy setting.The mechanics of the game are not super well spelled out, so a decent amount is trial and error, assuming you also don't want to look it up. You mostly chose dialogue options, some of which are story related and some that are more role-playing focused (how your character sees themselves and the world).As long as you're not expecting a rules-heavy table top rpg sort of thing and enjoy the world and the vibes, it's well worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What an addicting fun role-playing game! It's mostly text based, but choose your own adventure style has never been better. A lot of reading here, so if that's not your thing you might want to skip this one. The story is richly in-depth and gripping at times. The graphics, music and ambiance adds a lot of fluff and flavor to the game. The text is very descriptive and the choices you make actually matter and make a difference. This gem of a game kind of reminds me of the old solo role-playing adventure paperback books I used to play when I was younger. I used to really like the ones that you had to keep track of stuff on paper, like items and skills. This game also has that and your journal keeps track of everything, including quests, people and places etc.  I can tell there was a lot of work that was put into this game, and the journey is excellently crafted. I haven't got to the end of the game yet, but I have died a few times. A great adventure is to be had here! Have fun and enjoy the experience! Just writing this review makes me want to play it some more. I might start over and try a different type of class, not sure yet. 10/10 - Tell em' Large Marge sent ya! Hahahahaha!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well written and engaging.I was positively impressed with the quality of the text and the number of missions and characters to be explored.The dialogue options can be slightly limiting but this goes unnoticed due to how well the game immerses you.If you like gamebooks and slowgaming this is an excellent pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game enough. I loved every second of it. Of course no game can ever be perfect, but for my tastes this was about as close as I could get. I loved this thing, and still do. At LEAST top 5. It's not really a "game" in the normal sense. This was a book. And a damn good one at that. A book where I was intrigued with the characters, drawing my own conclusions, and fighting for what I thought was right.  Feeling on top of the world, and powerless. If this was a novel, I'd buy it, and read it a thousand times.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hidden gem I hope heralds many more such games. The story is beautiful and haunting, your choices have immense depth and unexpected consequences, and the characters you meet feel like they actually live in this terrible world you find yourself in. There are no heroes, but maybe you can one person's life a little easier, to push back the seemingly inevitable entropy, if only for a little while.You'll have to manage not to starve to death first.Quick tip - this is heavily "old style" RPG of ye olden days, so have a notepad handy and take good notes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it. A lot f reading and less seeing. The time element is a bit of a damper, because I would like the normal difficulty challenge with less of a time constraint. _childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most refreshing executions of a game i've seen in years. Beautiful writing, meaningful choices, and one of the most interesting and engaging fictional worlds i've ever explored. This is the kind of worldbuilding that leaves us forever wanting more as we get to briefly peer into a small corner of this deep and dark universe. It's the kind of game where halfway through you start to savor and dread every step of progress as you realize the experience will soon be over. I can easily say to anyone who isnt shy of text based games that this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game thinking it would be a cute little choose your own adventure but got sucked into the world of Hovlovan and the peninsula. The atmosphere of this game is so thick you could cut it with a knife. Thanks due to a combination of the AMAZING soundtrack, beautiful pixel art, thoughtful and descriptive writing, as well as the deep rpg mechanics / freedom of choice.  I felt like I was a messenger, a trapper, a bodyguard, a private investigator, a treasure hunter, a peace talker, a trade ambassador, a cave spelunker, a hero, and an adventurer all at the same time. Best game i have played in a long while

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this experience.  It was the first text based RPG that I've ever committed to finishing, and I wasn't disappointed.  The development of the characters that you meet on your journey as a Roadwarden is really satisfying.  During my play through there were decisions that had to be made, and I was so invested in the story, I could actually feel the weight of those decisions.  Reading through the dialog, and investigating further through some of the areas of the game felt rewarding.  I will probably play it again with the other classes.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible adventure with numerous choices, and beautifull writing. Both characters, and their actions are belivable, often morally gray, vast majority of NPc, just wants the best for their tribe, and closes companions. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent and atmospheric experience. The writing, visuals, and music draw you in and help you to stay focused in a way I rarely encounter. _childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I'm tempted to categorise Roadwarden as one of my favourite... books? Texts? Literary experiences? It did that thing that all art aspires to do, it challenged me. It challenged my sensibilities and emotions, made me feel at turns desperate, confident, outmatched, prepared, ashamed, proud, and loved. It dropped me into a world in which I was hopelessly out of my depth and said "go on, figure it out". In this regard it is a uniquely human experience among RPGs - there is no power fantasy here, just your wits and useful yet limited skills. This is a game that rewards paying attention to its world and characters, solid preparation, and care. The writing is excellent - the world and characters of Roadwarden are among the most grounded and immersive I've encountered. If you like text-based adventures (Citizen Sleeper or the Sorcery! series) or just regular RPGs, please give this a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative is compelling yet the choices you can make are strictly determined by roster plus some RNG thus lending to a 'map by scum saving' Not a show stopper but coupled with the three 'modes of play' it seems to be pointless to try it on anything other than casual.PROSWhat I liked was the overall ambience in the story-telling. It encouraged me to be nosey yet polite as I was compelled to garner trust. I admire these principles and enjoyed pursuing the individuals stories which hinted at a wider world.CONS:Some basic explanation of the temporal rules afore playing as time is everything yet I have no idea what time it actually is, occasionally told how long an action will take, yet double clicking a previously explored region does not and so reinforces scum saving techniques as a faux kind of tutorial to learn these essential rules.For casual play, this is a fascinating game and well worth the AUD$11 or so, I feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is simply amazing at what it does. The feeling it gives from the its art, music, and writing really helps you immerse yourself as the roadwarden. The world itself is interesting and there are tons of things you can explore from the world's histroy, it's places, it's people, and so on. The decisions you make in the game have meaning to it, for better or for worse. The game's cast of characters are also very diverse with many having many layers to them. As someone new to this genre, I think that this game is a great introduction and I would definitely recommend it to those starting out just like myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this well-written dark fantasy.You're an outsider in a harsh world. Some may rely on you, but you're not an infallible hero; many are slow to trust, and you aren't immune to backstabs nor ambushes. There are several great mysteries, and solving them unlocks choices to bring closure to each story—whether to benefit yourself, the people of the peninsula, the cities that sent you, or a goal more nuanced (after all, the people of the peninsula are not homogeneous, with a few being selfish and antagonistic).Some unique worldbuilding really sells the grim fantasy setting.Narrative choices really do matter, particularly for the epilogue—which explains how your actions affected the politics of the peninsula (or utterly failed to) and the well-being of those you met.: it's slow and purposeful, haunting and appropriate for each scene. You can listen to most of it here , though it's missing some notable tracks like the "happy" version of  and a couple songs that aren't original to the game (so obviously aren't included in the game's official album); luckily all the music is in the game files!However, listening to its music  experiencing the narrative will feel much more emotionally hollow... the 2nd half of  just hits different once you actually get inside the cave. So, please, play the game if it interests you!

_childDocuments_.review: This text-based expedition adventure into the untamed wilderness of a dark fantasy world is a triumph. The game features amazing writing that is implemented perfectly in its dynamic setting. It has crafted a great world that is a absolute pleasure to explore.The game has a great system of choices and consequences that bolsters good roleplay. Your decisions have real impact and shape the story in meaningful ways, even if you don't notice it right away. I found myself fully immersed in the role of the protagonist and cared deeply about how my choices would influence the inhabitants of this world.There is a staggering amount of content and depth in this game. It took me over 25 hours to finish one complete playthrough, and at the end it made me wish to have been longer. The story is so engrossing, the characters so complex, and the world so richly developed that I never wanted it to end.For those seeking a narrative-driven roleplaying experience, this text-based adventure game delivers in spades. The amazing writing, great world-building, and branching story with impactful choices combine to create something truly special. My time exploring the dark fantasy wilderness and interacting with its inhabitants was some of the most fun I’ve had in a game this year. This is a must-play game that I highly recommend to all.
