_childDocuments_.review: Bug-free 0/10 - has critical game-breaking bug, the one that made me drop the game is following: enemies can't finish the turn, must be something to do with double Raven and speeding-up the animation. And it's double nasty since you can't save mid-battle and these were super-hard battles that can't be circumvented by lowering the difficulty. Feeling bad to load early and put the region aside since I cleared the rest of location. In other words you lose almost an hour of play with that bug. This is the only reason "King Arthur: Knight's Tale" gets no recommendation, even though the game is very polished and optimized.One more battle syndrome 8/10 - strong enough to skip a bedtime. Metagame 4/10 - global map is there only for graph-like campaign, where your decisions are very limited, could be easily 7/10 with a bit more buildings, extra easy quests for levelling and basically a bit more decision-making on a global map.Tactics 7/10 - I've seen better tactical variety and difficulty adjustments. Extra points for some super rare but satisfying combos. Some battles feel way too puzzle-like and AI deliberately puts you in bad battle positions. It seems that the game is pushing you to specializing to combat some races differently, which is not my thing, I love having more or less universal types. Items 6/10 - Very boring, not a lot of variety, some seem way too random and beg for a building that lets you change one of the parameters for gold. Most of various items and scrolls are useless to take a slot. So you end up getting a lot of similar looking things that do not make you excited. Min-maxing 8/10 - very satisfying, you want to level-up your characters and keep them alive. Some skills and their progression seem useless. Some characters have way too many underwhelming skills and passives. Got my best fighter dead after healing, it seems this mechanic is not explained and you don't even get a screen on the fact someone has died and why.Production value 9/10 - close to "XCom", better than "Expeditions: Rome" and "Wartales". Cool cinematics and animations. Writing and story 7/10 - not bad, but anticlimactic. Nice writing, a lot of texts but not too bloated. Good voiceovers.Region layer 5/10 - the region levels looks awesome in terms of graphics assets and variety, but doesn't offer many options for decision if the intention was a rogue-like layout. The map option is useless, doesn't show unpassable and passable way. You spend too much time going back while not having any way to speed-up the animation or pathfinding over the map or fast travel. I'm not sure about WASD controls as well. The engine and rendering for the region level is good though. Region-level design is also bad because you are constantly stuck in something that looks passable but it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a top tier party-based tactical RPG with turn-based combat. You get more than two dozen characters to choose from for your party, pulled from a variety of source material on the Arthurian mythos, but largely inspired by the 1981 movie "Excalibur", a timeless masterpiece. The lore and writing may seem a bit convoluted to the hardcore history and mythology buffs like me, but it remains an interesting and entertaining take on the subject. You play as Mordred, Arthur's son and nemesis. His alignment is determined by you. There are morality checks in the game that steer you towards tyranny or righteousness, christianity or paganism. For my first play through I had a lot of fun playing the pagan tyrant and recruiting The Black Knight, The Red Knight, Morgana et. al. ("The Black Knight always wins!" At one point he actually says "it's just a flesh wound.") But I honestly think that the righteous path has better battle perks so I'm looking forward to a second playthrough to unlock The White Knight, Lancelot and the others. With very high production values, the game is beautiful and interesting to look at once you remove the screen film typical of this game engine.* The character and NPC models are highly detailed, like meticulously painted miniatures. I love the attention they put into each one, it really brings them to life and makes them easy to discern in the field. Voice acting is also top tier, very high quality and complete, no half-read lines here. Enemies are fairly diverse and just as detailed as your party. Animations are smooth and realistic. Soundtrack is epic. Combat is closer to Gears Tactics or D:OS2 than XCOM2 or Phoenix Point, but they pull the best of them together here so it has more predictable ballistics than its predecessors. Overwatch is more precise and more effective. The focus here is on melee and magic, archery to a lesser degree. There are a lot of skills to unlock. The skill trees are individuated for each character, so it stays fresh and interesting. My only complaint is with skill progression and dps; for the majority of the game, all your skills do about the same damage as your default basic attack, so there isn't any incentive to use them other than mixing it up. Later in the game, you will start to unlock some really cool AOE magic attacks though. Poison and DOT affects are relatively weak, with the exception of bleeding. But none of the DOT stacks afaik. All in all, this is the best turn-based rpg to come out this year so far. There are others, but this one tops the list. I abandoned them to play this one a second time, and I rarely play a game more than once. It's that good. This is a must play for any turn based tactics fan. *I made a ReShade preset that removes the screen film and clarifies the image, deepens colors, darkens shadows and illuminates globally. Made for 4k UHD OLED, 2k mmv.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rock solid at 1.0.  Well worth the wait, but it's not without it's problems.Great storytelling, excellent combat (AP is shared between movement and combat), and good difficulty (it's no cake walk and you will almost certainly replay a map or start over).  There are different ways to play and engage in combat.  You can freely roam maps, unlock which skills to acquire, choose who to take in combat, who to go on missions, and more.  There's equipment drops (in the form of sigils, jewelry, and accessories) like weapons, armor, and most of these are class specific.  But, it does add some theorycrafting.  Also, choices really do matter because of the morality system.  You can be an evil tyrant or a holy knight.  Want a tank or dps?  Your decisions will determine who you can recruit and who can't.  The alignment also affects damage bonuses per loyalty.  The more loyalty, the more damage and AP you can have per character.  There's also your keep, where you can heal your units from injuries (think Darkest Dungeon) and a market to sell and buy gear.   There's also a few other base features that give bonuses to loyalty (which increases unit damage) and training that you can send units on to level while you leave them.  Adding a character to maintain one of the areas can add more specific bonuses to all your characters as well.What I like:32:9 SupportFree roam, rotating map (though it can be confusing , but I think that adds a little to the mood)MusicVoice acting - sometimes very excellentDark Arthurian atmosphere - Think The Green Knight Good amount of character craftingWhat I don't like:Cannot disengage in combat without getting hit (unless you have movement skills or the enemy is taunted)Sometimes terrible VA.  Yvain and the Hermit (aka the Cadbury cream egg guy) come to mind.  Even Mordred's voice has changed (it can be jarring).  Also, it seems like the Lorax made an appearance...End game has very little VA - when it does, it's incorrect (merchant woman has a male voice)Not enough high end relicsTraits and morality leave very little experimentationSome keep upgrades paths do not feel worthwhileSome characters seem to be 'best in class' leaving others as also ransVery little ways to tailor the gameplay - you only get difficulty - rogue-like is locked at hard and you cannot save in your keep.  After early access, this has shaped into an excellent SRPG.  Performance seems a lot better.  There still is a lot of QoL that needs to take place, but well worth the wait and recommended.

Then, you will be thrown into the middle of a tough fight at the end of a mission, which may have some challenge.  It's as if the rest of the game was just tacked on to make it soooo much longer than needed.  I'm thinking devs completed a good game, testers beat it quickly, and marketing said make it longer.Also can't switch between controller and keyboard/mouse without changing settings every time.  I like using a controller, but keyboard is a huge advantage and why I play computer games, not console.Has some good concepts, decent combat when they actually try.  It's just layered in what is basically forced grinding.  Does have a way to speed up enemy animations though, which is so nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty cool and all but can we talk about design choices?1) Skills are hidden in skill tree. The dumbest idea I've ever seen considering character leveling process. It forces you to blindly put skill points into things that will be made absolete later.2) Main character is a tank and he is bad at it. Unlike most of the tanks you don't get the taunt but instead you get useless lightning strike that at later levels does exactly 0 damage. (and "stun" that it has still allows enemies to make full attack against you)3) Speaking about characters... Most of the knights that you unlock for morality chart are terrible. They got terrible skills, terrible proficiencies.4) Unbalanced missions. Every mission is a total rng. Some crappy side mission with no apparent threat can absolutly demolish your party just because game designers desided to throw at you 4 knights with 15 armor and 6 crossbows. For no reason, without a warning. Just fk you. You can't level team B on side missions.  They will die.5) Worst of all - Rng relic loot. All relic loot in the game is rng. Doesn't matter, right? Wrong. Many early encounters DEMAND that you have a relic loot equiped in order to beat them and tbh most of the relic loot is absolute garbage that could also debuff you. Playing roguelike mode and rolling bad relics? Doomed, fk you.6) Invulnerable enemies. WHY?! At some point game starts swarming you with enemies that can become invulnerable to all damage for 1 turn (and can still attack you ofc). It's boring in best cases and makes you want to abandon melee in a game about KNIGHTS in worst cases...7) Another enemy point. (because it deserves another point) 50/50 evasion enemies. Yes, you can stun them BUT they swarm you in such numbers that it's not a reliable option and they can murder your knights in 1-2 turns.8) Point seven brings us to the last point - non-viable melee gameplay. If you have to be in melee in this game then it's better be one turn (and you kill your enemy in this one turn). All knights that got no shield are made of paper and die in two turns in melee.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy gameSome minor rpg elements, pick some skills and equipment. Choose if your going tyrant/rightful or christian/old faith. I wouldn't call this a proper rpg at all though, choices are few and you have to stick to the path your on or you lose out so its more of a few choices rather than proper choice and consequence. Story so far seems interesting, Im extremely familiar with the Arthurian Cycle and this is a fun take on it especially for those familiar. However if your totally new to the myths then its a basic serviceable take on Avalon.Building your group and synergizing skill choices and tactics is where this games bread and butter is at and it does it excellently. I can see replaying this on a harder setting in the future as I come to grips with it more. Currently going through on Moderate and its a bit easy but not too easy.I have already gotten my money's worth and I suggest this game for any fan of tactical rpgs, xcom style games etc. If you enjoy the mythos on top of that then this is a no-brainer purchase.Hope they make another game like this whether its a sequel or another in the same genre but different story. Dev's know what makes a fun Trpg!

_childDocuments_.review: very good. almost feels rouge like. its a mission then base mission then base kind of game. upgrade base, manage resources, go on mission, go back to base, upgrade things, manage resources, go on mission. very good turn based combat. whole team takes a turn and you pick what order they do things then enemy goes. i like this a lot more than 1 character than another. for instance you can hit an enemy with one character to bring target down to 50% hp then select another character to bolt them to finish them off then change back to fisrt character and move and attack again if you have the AP points for it. bringing a high lvl of dynamic fluid combat to turn based combat. its challenging as you can not see stats or characteristics of buffs from gear in a mission/combat. so you have to look at things in depth at the castle before you go out to battle and have a good understanding of how your characters and builds will synergize. for instance if you have a guy that does 10 more damage to bleeding targets.....you will have no way of knowing this during combat. you just have to know it by memorizing it from his character sheet before a mission. Very fun once you get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is early access so there are still a couple of kinks to be worked out which is to be expected. When EA first dropped it was almost unplayable. Now, however, it runs pretty smoothly. As it currently exists, the game is a lot of fun tactically. The missions are challenging and require thought to win. I've restarted several times and think I am just about through with the EA content. There's a lot of promise with things to come. There are many nods to Excalibur and even the old Pendragon RPG that I appreciated. My hope is that the game will transcend from its dark, gloomy, gray  beginnings to something more colorful and vibrant depending on your morality choices and decisions. The existing content hints at this (at least to me) and that would certainly be consistent with its "Excalibur" feel. The characters are interesting and the skill tree decisions, etc. are meaningfully different. This game should have a lot of replayability. My only serious criticism at this point is that you cannot save during missions. Some developers pride themselves on making games just that bit of extra difficult. Some players like this. I personally do not. I have no problem making "no saves" a difficulty setting option if that's your pleasure but you ought to be able to save during missions by default. Some of these missions are long. Not being able to stop and come back is problematic.

_childDocuments_.review: Gets repetitive and I got burnt out during Act 4. Events are very annoying, indirectly forcing you to send someone from your main party away for 1 mission to increase loyalty and because of this, you need to replace with someone from the backup knight which I do not care. Juggling morality and faith all in all gets tiring and basically in the end my party of Tyrant Old Faith - Modred, Black Knight, Boudecea, Morgana. Somewhere during late game, I have to dismiss almost every knight whos Christian due to Morgana's negative Pagan trait and I just realised Morgana already has -3 loyalty due to this which I am not aware of. So the main question is, why is the potion that removes negative trait came so late in the game? Treasures and loots gets predictable and most of them are just junks. Sometimes the loots has something useful. Generally, it is difficult to equip your favourite knights with things you'd like due to the randomness of the Enchanted tower and Merchant. The restocking cooldown doesn't help with this at all as sometimes only 1 or 2 items get refreshed. The side missions sometimes felt simply like fillers to level up your knights. This game is enjoyable for the first 2 Acts but after that it slowly degrades in interests. There are others small to medium things I do not like in this game but can't recall them after my first 80 hours playthrough. I am just happy able to finish up to the final mission and I guess I got my money worth. Will I go for a second playthrough? Absolutely not. Time to move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to give this a positive or a negative. I finished the campaign and played some of the endgame. The cinematics are pretty good, and the knight armours are nice. Some interesting skills and tactical decisions. Each mission is samey but different enough to keep you playing. But I can see why some people will get bored of it quickly. Some builds are very overpowered.. Sir Lancelot with some questionable items and skills... I played on hard and the end game builds were so overpowered it was basically almost god mode. King Arthur is like a concert that teases you throughout the whole experience, but ultimately never hit any high climax. It was just fun enough to keep you going. By the end of it I enjoyed my experience, learnt a few turn-based builds I have never seen, but never felt blown away by anything. The end game content (including the mini-campaign) were linear and boring I could not finish it.If you are not a big fan of turn-based tactics or knights in cool armour, might want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: So, the feeling I get from this game is that once you finish Act 1, which takes about 10 hours, including all side missions, you've seen the entire game. The combat is.....fine. Its probably the most enjoyable part of the game tbh. It gets the job done but its very simple and the enemy variety is lacking. Some enemies serve only to annoy you, and they do a very good job.The story is.....idk. I went into this game excited by the premise and setting and was looking forward to the story. But I can't say anything really ever grabbed my attention. After 5 or so hours I just tuned all the dialogue out because it all felt so inconsequential. The graphics are ..... okay. I really dislike the design of the main character, he feels like an antagonist out of an indie rpg that came out in 2010. Maybe thats the point idk. The world is very grimdark, so if grey is your favorite color, youre in luck, youll never see another color. Personally, its just not for me. In general, the graphics look a little dated, but its fine. Nothing really stands out.The "base" system is sort of cool. Im not huge fan of the injury system which 2 of the main buildings work for. The training system was good. A lot of the upgrades I looked at for the various buildings seemed not that great or interesting, but maybe i didnt look hard enough or maybe i dont remember properly.All being said, I picked this game up on a big discount and while I really looked forward to this game, after Act 1, I dont think I could manage to suck it up through another 3 acts of what I imagine are basically the same thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews for games, but this was such an unexpected gem I wanted to flag it for other turn based strategy game lovers. If you ever wanted X-com but with a medieval setting and magic, you'll really enjoy this. Pick from a squad of legendary heroes, each with unique classes, skills, traits etc. Build up your home city for improvments, gather valuable loot and equipment for your soliders. There is also a morality system that gives it a slight choice based flavour, although this doesn't seem like a huge part of the game.Story is okay, similar to other strategy games, the real meat is in the gameplay and upgrades. But you can tell alot of love went into this game.It is also absolutely beautiful, I actually wish you could zoom in slightly more to see the awesome landscapes and character models.

_childDocuments_.review: Boys cannot be girls.Changed to a Not Recommend. i got so bored, that I never launched the game again, and have zero desire to do so.ONLY ON SALEThis is an 'In Between' recommendation. Its not bad, but its also not great. On 50% sale, go ahead and grab it. Its simply not worth $45. But dont bother with the DLCs, which launch separately from the Main Menu.Its no longer 120 gigs install.. I believe its now about 38 gigs, as it always should have beenIm only a few hours in, and I can already see that its not very deep. Its very repetitive, but may have some replay value, if different [party setups are enough to make you want to play again. Perhaps some alignment choices.Its just SO SLOW! These little maps, shouldnt take more than 15 minutes or so.. But because this is turn based, each map drags on for over an hour. You cant play short session, and long sessions doesnt see much progress made. I am now 24 hrs in, and am only lvl 7. Ive not failed, or lost a hero yet, playing on the 3rd difficulty. Progression is quite linear, as missions are chosen from an overworld map, and are very small maps. Think Expeditions: Vikings, minus any dialog and role play. You will have main missions, some side missions, and an occasional event option. It is a tactics combat game, with kingdom management.THIS is whats really killing it for me:Overwatch is pointless, as the enemies will literally waste turns in order to not step into the overwatch zone. Ive even sat and tested it, and watched as they refuse to move, or even walk an entire circle around a melee character, to avoid the attack. The ai is far too binary. It sticks to a very strict script. Target the lowest armor, lowest hp, and avoid all overwatch zones and traps. This sucks! Different builds is the ONLY thing in this game that retains excitement, but much of it is void due to the ai completely nullifying some of the abilities. (traps, overwatch, creating firing lanes, ambush zones, etc) This means your only course of action is brute force forward momentum, and just eating the damage, as enemies will completely turtle!Heroes have their own talent tree, which have 3 tiers that unlock. But it doesnt do enough to change up the monotony. The combat is the same, over and over again, with the same enemies, over and over again.You can equip some items to your heroes, but nothing changes their appearance, and weapons are predefined. Anything you equip is just a numerical boost, or slight affect. Passive increases only. Later on, there does seem to be some items which grant some legendary affects, as well as powers gained from upgrades to your castle. Both of which are nice, and much needed!Movement, and traversing the maps is really bad. Partly because the maps are poorly made, and difficult to read (another Neocore staple), and the mechanics themselves are very janky. I cannot explain how bad this feels, without actually having you feel it for yourself. The character will just randomly slow down to a crawl, like hes waste deep in mud. The camera angle is a little restrictive, and the view distance is atrocious.The soundtrack is pretty awful. Its very rare to have music, and what music does play, is the type that puts you to sleep. Soundtrack is always a Neocore weak point.That said, some of this is not very informative, and is the reason I stopped to review it. Im still not understanding what armor points do exactly, or what causes some of them to be stripped. I just did a side mission, where it said not to get close to a particular enemy, but I dont know why, or how to tell what the buff is in the future, without being told specifically. Then, he obviously got close, and it didnt do anything. My archer killed him, and he exploded... Very sillyAll in all, its just very slow, and a little TOO relaxing, with the ambient music only... Im struggling to continue playing, after only 1 dayTrue to Neocore form, the graphics look a certain way that all their titles do. They also have some oddness in the way the controls work, and some mechanics of them game. They desperately need a new art designer. Every single game theyve made, has the same exact washed out color pallet, where environment is difficult to read.Al the characters are left handed, and its very jarring! It REALLY bothers me.The performance seems to be a biut much. I have an Ryzen 5 5600x, and rtx 3060, with 12gigs of RAM, and was a little surprised that i needed to lower a couple settings to high, from ultra. There wasnt much of a visual difference, but the frames seemed to be slightly smoother.Ill update as I goTLDR*Its little more than a turn based combat game. Theres not alot here. Sale ONLY!*Camelot upgrades simply serve as stat boosts*Music is non existent*Its highly repetitive, and becomes boring quickly*Map and art design are not good*Linear progression*Difficulty is just lots of enemies at once*It gets boring very quickly*Equipment and Talent trees help fuel feeling of progression, but its not enough to change up the repetitive combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but flawed. Nice twist on the Arthurian legend, and lots of opportunities for upgrading heroes. But defects include: you can't use loot in mission, you don't know what the loot is until the mission is over, you can't share healing potions/weapons/armour in mission, and unlike XCOM2, you can't save in combat. The 'moral' index is clever, i.e. be goody or a baddy and rewards/new heroes will vary. But when you choose options giving moral points, you don't know how many points you're getting, so no way of carefully choosing to maximise choices. Loot/purchasable items are pretty pathetic. The game's OK, but I soon went back to XCOM2.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off this is an awesome game, the combat system is really polished and complimented by the management in between missions. If you are looking for a one sentence review, I am a huge fan of turn-based tactical RPG's and King Arthur Knight's Tale is a great addition to the genre with a beautiful battle system however it can begin to feel repetitive at times with lengthy mission times. The overall gist of the game is that you will go on a mission that includes a short storyline through several battles that will earn you XP, loot, gold, and building materials. In between missions you will be using those currencies to select upgrades for Camelot to provide different benefits, making kingly decisions on different events that affect what kind of leader you are, and deciding what to do with heroes that are not on your missions roster such as training or healing. Certain decisions you make will affect your morale compass between Righteous and Tyrant as well as Christian and Old Faith. Progressing in any one direction will unlock new characters and other benefits. I really enjoyed the management piece in between missions. Finding a really useful upgrade and then setting out on another mission to get the currency to afford the upgrade all played into each other nicely, making it hard to find a good stopping point at times. However, after hours and hours of game play I did begin to tire of the side missions and began to only want to progress the main story. The missions are lengthy and turn-based combat is not necessarily quick. While this may sound negative, I think that is still a nod to the developers that put out a full length game and not just half a game blocked by paid dlc at a later date. Overall: 8/10 - Would recommend to a friend

_childDocuments_.review: A dang fine game! Albeit a bit unbalanced. Sir Balin be ballin'King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a very fun squad-based, tactics-y, strategy RPG. Set in ye olden days of King Arthur and Ser Mordred the Dread Knight, you wake up after the two clashed and murderated each other in a rather bloody battle. You are tasked with rebuilding Camelot, and saving Avalon (think of England, but in another world. D&D players can think of England, but the Feywild). There's a few twists in the story, but they're fairly minor, and don't change the story much. Your heroes level up, usually one level every mission, or at least every other, you take them on. You get a full cadre of 12 heroes active, but you get a few more, so you have to decide which hero you want to remove from court and which one you want to run with. You will also not be able to have ALL of them at max levle by the end of the story. But most of them, if you switch out regularly. Which you don't need. I'll spoiler you that much of the story. You DO NOT need to train two (or more) squads. You cna run with one squad from start to finish. Whether tha is good or bad is your decision to make.The heroes follow a general archetype, Ranger, Caster (melee caster and the stereotypical mass-incinerator), 2h-Warrior, Tank, Rogue, but they all have a slightly different set of actives and passives. The exception being Vanguards (Rogues). They all have the same actives and passives, from what I remember. But that's not necessarily bad, since they're also brokenly OP. Seriously.Speaking of broken, the balance is a bit off. Vanguards start out squishy and stupid stronk, and they get even more stupidly strong and they get less squishy. Archers start out nice, but they fall off for the most part their attacks don't improve that well, and their ultility becomes less important. The tanks start off doing mediocre damage and taking very little, and they basically become nearly-impenetrable walls of steel, that deal little damage, but have nice utility. Your arcanists/wizards start out squishy, and stay squishy, but they get more devastating against multiple enemies, and get more crowd control.Your melee wizards are there for support, and their damage is, and stays, laughable. Their supportiness gets better, though.I wish I could say much about the 2h-warriors, but I ditched them in favour of Vanguards very early and never looked back.The gearing of your heroes is quite diverse, you have weapons, armour, trinkets, and support items (potions/scrolls), in four levels of quality and five stages of level requirements. For the most part the items are randomly generated, but the highest tier of quality has set stats, since every one of those items has a name.And some of those are silly strong, too. The interface is serviceable, but nothing special, it IS in the way of things, sometimes. Especially when you try to move your heroes from one space to another, and when drawing the area of effect for line-based spells and abilities. Overall, there's room for improvement, but it's not ruining the game.Performance so far also seems fine. Nothing spectacular, the effects aren't anything super-outstanding, but also don't pull you out of it. A solid performance, overall.The only gripe I really have with the game is the length of some of the missions. ESPECIALLY some of the sidequests definitely take longer than they should. But they are still overall short enough. On Normal difficulty, every mission took me around 20-30 minutes. To clear the enemies and sweep for all treasures. With maybe a handful of exceptions.Overall, I recommend this, but if you want something with a REALLY deep story, this isn't gonna be it for you. It's fairly standard, but the fights are fun, the balance is broken on the fun side of the scale, and some items are good modifiers to your playstyle. I'm good with having bought it at full price. It's worth the money in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: King Arthur is a great turn-based tactical strategy game.  It has some RPG-elements without being a full RPG.  There's no real heal spells or holy trinity synergy in the game so your tactical decisions feel impactful.  It's reminiscent of XCOM but without that crazy RNG.  The graphics were great and the music always felt very moody and fitting for the game's setting.  I'd give this game a solid 8 - maybe even an 8.5.  The story wasn't my favorite and I never felt fully invested in it but it certainly wasn't bad.  Playing the "bad guy" was actually a lot of fun and Mordred has an awesome personality in his dialog options.If you enjoy games in this genre I give it a big thumbs-up and my full recommendation.  If you're more of an XCOM player or a full RPG guy then I'd wait for a sale but still recommend you pick it up.  I finished the main campaign on Normal difficulty in about 74 hours.  I'm not a great tactical mind and usually play the game on Normal or Hard but definitely not ULTRA HARD or NIGHTMARE.  If you're the kind of player who is really looking for a tactical challenge I would bump this up to HARD at the bare minimum.  The depth of your roster doesn't really get tested unless your heroes are injured and start spending turns in the cathedral or hospice.  The city-management portion of the game felt a little shallow but occasionally interesting.  It's definitely not as involved as XCOM but what it does - it does well.

_childDocuments_.review: Before i say anything about this game there is one thing we all can agree on. The game has a really high potential and it reminds me of my all time favorite game Disciplace and yes i know its super early access but still there are number of things that need to be fixed really fast First of all the optimization need work, i played threw the game and 80% of the time i had no problems with but there are times when the game drops to 30 and even to 8! FPS despite the graphics options especially on areas with a lot of fog or in fights with more the 10 enemies on the screen Second thing that bugged me was the de-synchronization between sound and the animations of attacks even in 60+FPS there where some problems with units making the animation and the sound just didnt catch up with it or the other way around The last thing that was bugging me is the flow of the game. Its slow. Dont get me wrong i dont want this game to be lightening fast or something but.... the animations even in more then 120 FPS feel like that are slowed down to 30 FPS and it feels clunky and strange like all of that was forcefully made to look like a movie but it failed. The attacks, the unit movements, the skill animations they need to be a little more dynamic in my opinion with more energy to give the characters ( or enemies ) more life to them Personally i would like the game to have better equipment animations. For example when im equipping new set of armor i want my character to change a little or with a new weapon rune to give the weapon that he or she is holding a different look Despite all of that plus some smaller problems i do like this game really its enjoyable it has the right dark fantasy setting, the story is ok and the building system looks solid ( but it needs more options like really ) so for now i can give it 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: To be frank, this game would deserve a neutral rating, but sadly there is nothing like that available. Also, it is not a bad game per se, rather than the core gameplay loop is severely broken for me. Which means that some people may perfectly enjoy it (assuming that they are content with excess grinding). On the surface it does everything right; X-Com-esque combat, dark fantasy King Arthur lore (similar to Neocore's previous King Arthur RTSes) and some of the mechanics are heavily Darkest Dungeon (1) influenced. You have an HQ you can keep upgrading and go to missions from that place with a roster of Arthurian heroes. Looks nice, plays nice, sounds nice (minus the voice talents, it really feels like not humans are behind those, but text to speech synthesizer reads the script).So what is the problem? For me, the game is super grindy and extremely convoluted. Let's start with the latter one. You can build plenty of buildings (like DD) and you can upgrade them to give more slots for treatment/training/etc. However, upgrading is not freeform, there is a dependency chart between upgrades, which you have to follow. Ok, no biggie (although it took me a while to figure out how can I open a second slot to treat vitality), I can live with that. Nevertheless, everything is expensive, so one must enter the constant loop of grinding by going through copycat missions. Fighting the same enemies, in the same scenery (which doesn't help you to visually guide where can you go and where is an invisible wall), looking for lootable places just to get 20 or 30 gold coins. Then you get the same (visually represented) artifacts, which you can equip, just one of them gives you +2 damage in overwatch, instead of giving +1 to burning arrow. After a few hours I just dumped all the ♥♥♥♥ at the merchant, because I get a headache after every mission, looking at the visually same 6 clover, same 7 tusk amulet figuring out which one suits my playstyle better.Let's be honest, Darkest Dungeon was grindy too, but fun, as the gameplay loop was interesting, engaging. You could experiment with different builds, different classes, approaches and such. Here, in Knight's Tale it's just... lackluster. First, I only encountered five classes (some of them plays fairly similar), actually four, because the wizard I received was so annoying, that I dismissed. Sadly, I didn't know that (as of level 6) I won't get any wizards, sooo I'm stuck without a spellcaster. Somebody wrote in his (her?) review -and I found it spot on- that regardless of how many heroes you have, you will stuck with a few. Because either you can't keep the ones you dig (because it conflicts with your choices/faith), or simply they are just uninteresting or outright irritating (as the heroes talk and behave slightly differently). I really would like to get rid of the womanizer crossbowmen guy from my team (as he is cheesy as ♥♥♥♥), but can't, since I only have melee heroes apart of him and another archer.Speaking of missions, usually those end up with running around on maps of a few rotated artstyles which wear out their welcome super fast. Although there are "optional" side missions, those don't really feel optional, as main story missions have a level requirement, which you better adhere to. Leveling your heroes is done through missions (or in the training field, but time there passes based on number of missions you perform, so catch of 22), which pit you against the same enemies. I encountered three types so far, with only a handful of classes. Alternative may be to focus on the mission objective and stop exploring, but that also isn't a viable approach, as you will trigger fights (only a small amount of them are optional) automatically.Again, is it a bad game? No. But it's definitely super grindy with a limited variety of enemies and sceneries, which you must perform, shall you want to build your buildings, level up your heroes, etc. And this comes from someone, who actually enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, but this type of soulless grind is just way too much for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Darkest Dungeon (the first one), but with with isometric exploration and combat. It's not perfect, there are issues with the interface, among other things, but it's mostly nothing you can't live with or won't get used to. The story has been decent so far, the sound acting ranges from good to some characters making me want to stick forks in my ears when they're in party (looking at you Sir Tristran!) and the soundtrack still kicks butt after almost 30 hours of play.This game is so heavily DD influenced it's hard for me to compare it to anything else or describe it otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: I would rate this neutral, not thumbs down. It actually probably deserves a thumbs up, but I'm putting thumbs down to balance out the reviews since I think the game's current rating is higher than it actually deserves.I've played the game on all difficulties. Normal is far too easy, Moderate is whatever, Hard is OK (other than end game HP sponges which serve no purpose other than making the fights very long), Very Hard has some issues I will go into later.The game gets a 6.5/10 (it was 7, then I came to realize a few things) here's why:-- The Good1. Interesting combat the first (and maybe second, I'm on my second time and we'll see if I can actually make it through, but I doubt it) time around, decent puzzles to solve mixed throughout the game2. Fun building of the city3. Character builds are great! 4. Some of the gear is interesting, and I do like the thrill of the RNG.5. The game looks and feels good to me, with decent UI (wish I could change equipment mid-mission though)-- The Neutral1. The story is OK. Nothing special, but it isn't bad. Not a pro nor a con.-- The Bad1. Music is repetitive/boring. Listen to something else.2. Repetitive voice lines. 3. Low replayability - long missions for no reason with static encounters    - You have to do these missions or you will have not enough resources or XP. "Side Mission" is a lie.    - You pretty much have to do these missions the "right way" and boringly slog through them, as you are almost always outnumbered and mobs become super HP sponges later.4. Characters seem very limiting. You can only bring 4, and you can only have 12 in your roster. This is OK, but what isn't ok:     a. Many chars are locked by alignment, which in itself is okay, but PLAYSTYLES are locked behind the alignment       - Want good champs and the best defender? Be a tyrant christian       - Want good arcanists? Be tyrant old faith       - Want good sages and a few really good arcanists? Be rightful old faith       - Want a mix of decent to very good hero picks? Be rightful christian. In a way, this makes it have some replayability... but it doesn't, unfortunately, because the game becomes a slog when you replay it and have seen the missions before. See point 3.5. Game Balance (There's a decent mod that SOMEWHAT addresses point A, enhanced edition, but I have my own qualms with it and feel like it just shifts the tier list) a.  All difficulties -  Marksman are flat useless (you can use them on normal because that difficulty is so easy, but even on that difficulty they are really bad and you might struggle some). There is one (arguably two in late game) good vanguard(s), and traps are just bad. Defenders are limited in usefulness (sometimes very needed). Champions and Arcanists are the best classes in this game, pretty much by a large margin. b. Very Hard - I have mixed feelings. The AI is better, but it is also worse. At least they pick targets better and actually try to kill you. Problem is, they will *always* go for backstabs, at the cost of proccing opportunity attacks. In some ways, VH is easier than Hard, because you can just trick the stupid AI into proccing opportunity attacks and it isn't smart enough to not do that and commit suicide. At the same time - this is a good move, a lot of times, with how much of HP sponges they are. But I wish they were smart enough to not commit suicide (like if they were low hp).6. Gear is all RNG (it's a pro and con)Overall, I would recommend this game on sale for a one hitter. And it's ALMOST good enough that I would wholly recommend it, but the game has some issues that prevent that from being reality.  I would definitely try out a #2 though... I would just watch some gameplay videos, carefully, first.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of things that are incredible good, expect no comfort features though.For example, the map is very hard to read in most missions and you can't click on the map to go somewhere, gotta walk there all by yourself, which is a little annoying if you wanna walk back and look if you missed something, like hidden treasures which the game doesn't tell you how to find in the first place, which I don't mind cause you'll just stumble upon it.The combat is very good in my opinion, even though it is simple in the beginning it has some some depth which increases later in the game. It makes think which of my 4 abilities I should use to do max damage here. The class system supports the combat in a good way and one class can differ for different characters which adds to the characters in the game and the character of the game. Also the characters have some personality in Knight's Tale, unlike in most games, which you can underline with your equipment if you're down for some rollplaying in your game.Now to a apparant problem Knight's Tale has that all games of this genre have. The combat is slow and the fights are many. Enemy variety is ok but to entertain the majority of people it is lacking. Need I say anything else? I don't think so. Oh and also no autocombat here, which would kill the immersion anyways. Me: "Spits on might and magic"Did I write about the amazing graphics this game has yet? Guess what, they are amazing and the best I've seen so far in this genre. I didn't know you can design so many knights in so many different ways. Sir Mordred is by far the best in my opinion though. There are a few bugs, most are just funny and I'd let them pass as features except for one I've run across so far. You can use wasd to move, but if you move into a invisible wall, which are placed sometimes on the border of the map, you can't move at all. So you gotta restart the mission. I would suggest that equipment can have any level and any character can wear any equipment, for the simply reason that a low level character becomes to much of a burden, which can be solved in a way but not to my satisfaction. _childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS =]King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a tactical RPG set in Avalon, of classic Arthurian history.  The game has an immediate plot twist, in that you are playing Mordred - originally a major antagonist, who died and has since risen from the dead, to restore order to Camelot, and lay to rest the tormented spirit of King Arthur himself.  You get all this information from the introductory cutscene.The Good----------The game is a reasonably slow-paced affair, but this isn't a *bad* thing as it gives you plenty of time to get to grips with the mechanics, the characters, and so on.One of the things I particularly enjoyed about it is that you get to hold court, as in you have to make a number of decisions along the way which drive you either in the direction or law or chaos, and Christianity or the Old Ways.  You also get to rebuild, renovate and improve Camelot and its buildings, which is a welcome strategic component to the game that makes it more than just a simple tactical RPG.I also like how you only have so many slots for heroes, meaning when you acquire *more* people in your roster, you *will* need to retire some of your legacy Knights, so it pays to start sorting them into ones you really want to keep and develop, and ones you really aren't bothered about, from an early stage.One quick tip if I may - wand your enemies to see what their movement is on the next turn.  This can help you stay outside their movement area, thereby ensuring you don't get hit too soon =]The Bad---------The decision to include some British and some American voice-actors is a puzzling one to me, as the tale of King Arthur is typically thought of as a British one, so when you have (for example "the Hermit") voiced in an American accent, whereas a number of the Knights of the Round Table have strong British accents, it can be a slightly jarring experience.Additionally, some of the text features typos which is a really *minor* thing, but ... yeah.There is one other slightly frustrating element to the game, which is that when you need to heal characters (and you will), you will need to remove them from your active roster by sending them to one of two healing structures, and they will be out of action for a number of game turns, meaning you'll have to do other quests without them.  If you aren't careful, this can mean you're missing a pivotal character (e.g. Mordred) for a mission, so you'll have to go with (potentially) a character you haven't levelled-up as much, and this can be an issue.All told the game feels solid, decent, and enjoyable.  The range of spells and special abilities makes it an enjoyable experience, and when you have a strong feel for your tactical style, you can make some serious progress with it.  Just remember to pay attention to all the options as you play, and you'll be fine ! =DI'd give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from a Hardcore play through on Hard. About halfway through Act 3 of 4. Reviewer loves Battle Brothers, Darkest Dungeon, and Iratus. Was lukewarm on Expeditions: Rome. May be overly long, but if you want a detailed explanation - this is the review for you.This game is surprisingly good and exceeded my expectations in many areas. There are some areas of "ok" quality, but it leans into what it does well and allows the player to really enjoy the game as a result. The game doesn't make the mistake of leaning into low quality gameplay loops that distract from the experience and what you get is a very satisfying tactical RPG with satisfying character and party management elements.On a scale of 1-10 and then explained:Story - 9Party and Kingdom Management - 8Classes and Customization - 6Tactical Combat - 8Pacing - 8Stay fairly brief here, but the world is a really interesting twist on Arthurian legend. The way characters are introduced is great and I enjoyed the way the game explored the individual knights and the overarching plot. My only complaint here is that there are so many knights that it misses an opportunity to add more depth to your knights.Many of these knights could, and should, have significant relationships and stories to explore between each other and the game only does a superficial job of exploring these. Understandable, but an opportunity to go from "good" to "incredible." The management of Camelot is fairly similar to what you might experience in Darkest Dungeon. This works quite well and was enjoyable. Not too complex, but not too lean either. A nice side dish on the side of the experience. Your party members may, or may not, contribute helpfully to your operation in Camelot and this makes your overall knight selection a bit more varied.The one drawback for many people is that your core party is limited to 12 active knights. In a game that offers you many more, it "feels bad" to have to make choices to exclude certain knights. I found myself wanting everyone, but I had to make some very difficult decisions about who to include and who to dismiss, or not add, to my team. The game has a morality system that encourages you to only accept knights from your alignment decisions, but it still felt like you were "missing out" when you have to dismiss a knight or not accept a knight. I learned to accept this and it is ok, but as a player, this did not "feel good." In spite of the negative feeling with it - the system just works. I have to commend it because the game is balanced quite well around it, no matter how little the player may like it. If the player was permitted to manage more than 12 knights, the infrastructure would not adequately support it as keeping them all leveled and equipped would become tedious and problematic. I believe that the system that is introduced here is fine, but it is "less good" than other systems that exist in RPGs. Your knights are limited to a specific armor weight class and weapon set. You customize their performance through skill point allocation (which is unique to them based on one of 6 classes and some unique nuances of the knight).Items in the game are really just "sigils" that modify the performance of the character. Think Darkest Dungeon, but with slots dedicated to Weapons, Armor, and Trinkets. There are no cosmetic adjustments or truly functional changes that happen here.Once again - I favor more complexity here - but the game just makes it work. The simplicity in this domain allows you to focus more on what the game does quite well, and as a result it bothers me less in this title than it may in other titles. There is just enough player agency in the way you build your characters to move them slightly into different sub-archetypes that it works out - but you are not going to get a vast array of alternatives that you might be looking for in other RPGs. In this game, you are fine-tuning your knight slightly, but nothing is going to make him anything other than the Tank, DPS, or Support that he is intended to be.The tactical combat system here is surprisingly good. Especially since it lacks so many modern innovations. A few things that, on the surface, are not great:- Very linear environments with simple battlefields that have light cover and obstruction scattered across it.- No elevation changes.- Very low RNG (could be favorable depending on the kind of gamer you are). The result? You get more of a tactical puzzle to solve where you are trying to figure out how to mitigate damage in the best way possible while maximizing your damage output. With almost no RNG, you can very accurately predict how your turn is going to go. The AI is very predictable and easy to manipulate, which is kind of needed here because you would not be able to manage the conflicts against a more sophisticated AI.In some of the fights later on your knights are arrayed against some pretty heavy odds and if the AI did not just charge into your battle plan it would be significantly more difficult. I thought I would not like this system, but at least at the difficulty level I am playing, the battles are difficult but achievable. Your knights are healthy enough that you can make a mistake or two and not lose them, and it is easy to see where you made the mistake to begin with. Repeated mistakes will kill a knight, but RNG and a couple of missteps will not. This makes the hardcore experience very engaging and very satisfying and I have been enjoying it significantly. Pacing in the game is above average. They do not waste a lot of time on crafting elements, mini-games, or other garbage that distracts from the gameplay loop. Result? You move from combat to combat, go to camelot to deal with your loot, manage your kingdom, rinse, and repeat. The only "time waster" is you kind of move around the map looking for hidden chests and loot. It is not egregious here because loot is frequently found behind battles, but there is more of it than I would like.Overall, I felt like the game is respectful of my time and I find myself doing stuff I enjoy constantly while I play it.

are fresh and interesting.but that's about where my positives end.the strategic layer is laughable underdeveloped. you rebuild the basic structures of Camelot (merchant, magic tower, healing ward, etc.), each having their own handfull of upgrades, and you can assign Knights to positions. it's okay, but very very basic.from time to time a "side"-event pops up, which is a text-bubble, and you making a choice. that's it. again very basic. and then you get to chose a mission, sometimes this means there are 2-3 side missions on the map and a main mission; but since side-missions are not bound to some sort of times, there ain't much difficult choices here.then there's one of the selling points of the game: the large roster of potential characters. and yes...there are a metric ton of games like XCOM, Phoenix or Grey Knights got enviromental destrucion, different mission targets, differences in hight, real cover which feels like a real game element (in Arthur it's kinda pointless tbh.), Arthur got: walk in a room, enemies pop up, you 4 man team clobbers em...done. sometimes you get 1 to 2 more chars (very rarely), but all the very basic combat mechanics mixed with your tiny team size, just...again plays very boring in the long run.and i kid you not: it's all the content in the game. every tiny side mission, every main mission...the hight of enjoyment is when an enemy is there's no personal interaction on the strategic layer, no talking to your advisors, no mini-cutscenes, nothing. they remain a silent, head-shot-portraits until you take em into a mission to spout their random lines again. which also goes for the unique on spin of all those small stories from the Arthur times. most end with the recruit mission, don't play any role, don't lead to nothing. there are some exceptions like characters linked to the Grail or Excalibur, but most others die the moment you finish the recruit mission. it's not a bad game, it's just exceedingly boring. the tiny skill pool, the tiny active skill pool, the tiny active unit roster, the boring skill tree, the minimal strategic layer, the text-box-events...even the good grafics never change much: it's darkish, gothic and that's that. which goes also for your characters loadout; there are 0 model changes. you don't loot weapons or armor, their budget-shortcut was you looting "runes", which in reality are weapons and armor, but they could skip the 3D-modeling work...but this also means your roster never changes their appearance (unless you get "skins" from outside of the game).as much as i like Neocore, this ain't it. there are just way to many better options around. the moment to moment gameplay just ain't there. if you never played a XCOM-like and you dabble into a light version that doesn't overwhelm you with options and possibilities Arthur might be for you, but i don't see veterans of the genre making it to the ending...i couldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with this tactical RPG. I like medieval setting in games, so I loved all the lore I found here.  The story was interesting, battles were entertaining and characters were great. Sadly, this system of "Christian"/"old faith" and tyrant/rightful was dumb and made me force myself to pick some answers and quests to get new characters and upgrades to buildings. I also think that balance is a mess in King Arthur. As far as Act II goes, everything is super-easy. Then we have Act III that is a large spike in difficulty, and then we go back to ultra-easy mode with a final fight that is a joke. Burning/poison and some relic made last fight... Well, you can guess… I didn't like that.  Overall, this is a great game for the price of $30, and it gave me 50~ hours of fun. I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Slow and Repetitive! but It's still a good game!If they could add a version of the game where the Knight rotation didn't exist, the whole healing and gaining experience, it's just all too bothersome. Rather would have fewer knights with diverging talent trees or something that aren't under leveled.Then you got the world map where quests appear and clicking one loads you into a smaller area where you can run around looking for fights, interactions, loot etc. Time spent in that area is too long, too many repetitive fights, they should halve it. Furthermore they should remove the roaming part all together. It should automatically start at the fight and give some options whats routes to go and hint what perils or rewards could be had! Because god forbid you missed a marker and have to zigzag your slow ass group back to that place.Game has too much going on I would say, less would be more in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Game story is interesting, often fun but can be super repetitive and buggy. My play through got bugged, posted it in community and  a dev asked me to provide my save file, they fixed it for me. _childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played in a while. It's a mix between XCOM (my favorite game), Divinity Original Sin and Darkest Dungeon. I'm still far from finishing the campaign but I already know I'll start another one.Story - 6/10 (I'm not done yet)Difficulty - 8.5/10Soundtrack - 10/8Gameplay - 9.5/10 (The only flaw I can find is that some people might find the combate repetitive)Replayability - 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- A fleshed out look at Arthurian Legend mixed with some of its own unique touches.- Solid amount of flexibility in regards to builds for different knights, e.g. Focusing on AOE skills early for your Champions or tanking abilities with defenders.- A bit of extra replayability thanks to the morality system.- Most of the characters I found quite charming, if you like good guys or evil tyrants their should be someone for every playstyle.Cons- Early game (particularly Act 1-2) are very dry when it comes to combat, simply put there wasn't enough enemy variety making the fights drag on.- Some small bugs/crashes while playing, such as tooltips bugging out and audio cutting out in some sections for no reason. - The music, while fitting the kind of game, became quite repetitive to the point I had to switch to my own playlist- The Endgame balance (specific to postgame) is dry and boring, didn't endure it more than a few hours before leaving it alone as I didn't find it interesting or enjoyable to fight waves of high HP enemies just for some loot. - A small criticism is the party size. Only 4 characters with the occasional guest just felt bad when you have around 30 Knights I would recommend picking this game up on sale as I did, pretty fun overall despite some of my criticisms.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this is probably a kind of fantasy X-Com with Darkest Dungeon influences. It's pretty good stuff. It has a linear rpg frame, but it forgoes the habitual heavy emphasis on narrative in favour of the tactical gameplay. Not that there isn't any narrative, and what is there is good, it anchors the action and is well-written. The presentation is "grim dark", as they say, with fairly extreme stuff (like mentions of rape), but there is a kind of levity and black humour in the dialog. The narrative is really there to serve the gameplay and not the other way around. I for once prefer this. The gameplay is fine-tuned, it feels like nothing is superfluous ; the difficulty is good, the levelling and customization has plenty of impact, the items are meaningful and have qualitative effects (and not just quantitative ones), the alignment system is quite interesting and gives the game replayability. The fights are not that hard if you pay attention - I think the game could be a bit more difficult - but as it's designed for ironman ("roguelike") play, it does require careful planning and knowledge of the different situations (which are composed of your team's abilities and the enemies'). The only real problem I have with the release (it has no bugs) is the file size, which is very excessive and quite unwarranted. Other than that, definitively a great game for tactical players, hopefully we see some interesting dlcs as a follow-up.EDIT : the devs are fixing the game's size to reasonable proportions. Very good of them, now this game has no faults, at least according to my review.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I kickstarted the game and enjoyed it.  I did run into a battle with the red knight that basically ended my play through because I just could not get through it with the compliment of companions I took.  Other than that the story is fun and it is an interesting twist on the Arthurian story.  I love turn based tactical games and this one did not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The good:This is a fun dark fantasy XCOM-alike.The bad: The plot's nothing to write home about and the voice acting is flatter than a desk.The ugly:The graphics aren't anything to write home about, either.Verdict: wait for a sale, and then get it because it's worth the 70ish Shekels you'll be paying (but not its full asking price).
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A unique hybrid between turn-based tactical games and traditional, character-centric RPGs. Knight's Tale is a modern retelling of a classic Arthurian mythology story filtered through the dark fantasy tropes, a twist on the traditional tales of chivalry.

name: Coral Island
detailed_description: Meet The Dateables About the Game It’s time to leave big-city life in Pokyo behind and start a new chapter of your life on Coral Island! Be who you want and create the idyllic farm of your dreams, where you’ll tend crops, nurture animals, and build a bond with the natural world around you. Help revitalize the nearby town and its surrounding coral reefs, and forge relationships with a vibrant community of more than 70 fellow people who call Coral Island home. Farm. Decorate. Craft. Explore. Relax. Your future—and the future of Coral Island—is what you make of it. Build Your Dream Farm Transform your overrun land on Coral Island into a lush and lively dreamscape—you decide what to build, what crops to grow, and which animals you’d like to tend. Write your own story : The story changes with each season, but life goes with the flow. Spend your days exploring, or build a life with someone special. Save the seas, brave the caves, or focus on your farm. It’s up to you! Be yourself : Choose from a wide variety of outfits, accessories, and physiques—you’ll find plenty of options to express yourself, find your style, and be whoever you want to be. Befriend a diverse cast of islanders : Get to know the 70+ characters from all walks of life who live on Coral Island. Converse with them, find out more about their interests, and try to impress them with just the right gift. Find that special someone : Meet 25 singles who are ready to mingle! Build relationships, sweep them off their feet, and find the one—and when you’re ready, embark on a new chapter of your story together at the farm. Restore an island once paradise : Make Coral Island a better place for everyone! Take part in community projects to liven up the town, expand the local museum, and discover how to restore heritage sites. Increase the town's rank and your community will thrive! Catch of the day : Island living has a lot of perks, including being just a stone's throw away from fun activities like hunting for insects and catching fish. Dive the ocean & mine the caverns : Go diving to restore the coral reef, or mine precious gemstones in the cavern. Whatever you decide to do, you’ll find loot to hone your tools and upgrade the quality of your livestock and crops.

Be who you want and experience enchanting island living at your own pace—live off the land, nurture animals, build relationships with a diverse cast of townsfolk, and make the world around you a more vital and harmonious place.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is a farming simulator with many different ideas and unusual, but interesting designs. When I say this the art style is absolutely gorgeous and detailed. The story is fleshed out somewhat (I still haven't finished yet) as of this review. The road map is a thing and I am excited to see some of the future updates for the game. So where do we begin:Short Summary: It is true to the genre close to a harvest moon like experience but better in sense of gameplay and okay with character development (It feels bland to me, but I have not finished everything). It's harvest moon on garbage island, turn garbage island into nice island. Has the genre's normal downsides (lull periods, tycoon peaking, etc.)What makes this game different from other farming sims?-You grow seeds, raise animals and sell them for profit to save your dying town.-You clean the ocean by tediously/hypnotically using a sickle to gather every, single bit of trash in the entire water map (You don't have to get it all, but I'm a degenerate).-This game's message is very clear, it's about recycling and taken care of our island home.-There are several story lines that can be interesting but personally I am more into the merfolk's part. What's the farming like?-You can farm above the water or in it (Farming underwater takes a while to get to)-You can make the farm almost fully automated without a factory like idea. What else does this game feature?-Lots to collect (Progression is dictated by this, so would say there is alot of collecting)-Simple crafting system/progression  (Gather x build y, gather x research z)-Ranking system: hit ranks to gain more things and progress the plot. -Plenty of things to aim for, however I still feel it's missing a sort of spark to motivate me to want to learn more about the island (This may also be because I've played alot of games like this). Why recommend it?-Devs are active, not always the most communicative but active. -The game is very fleshed out, lots of things to do and discover, you are encouraged to explore.-Very much so worth the price, however you can get a good deal different sales during the year. -There is quite alot to this game compared to other games, it has seen itself to full release and is very stable. Any cons? (Not really deal breakers, just minor annoyances and things I feel like people would wanna know) -I dislike the combat for caves, it's just annoying. Serves no purpose besides collecting things and mining. Plus being a nuisance. -Can become tedious, and point of time where it feels like there's nothing much else to do after about two or three years in the game. (This is just a common problem in this genre sometimes). -It's very player driven story, and collecting progresses the story. So if you miss something early in the year you will have to wait the entire year to get what you missed the first time.  - It loses steam after sometime in certain parts of the game, where it just kinda lulls until you get to the good parts. -This is probably just me but I dont feel a bond with anyone. Some of the characters just seem bland, not all characters need to pop but I just don't really like anyone. The game is fine, but the story for me is just boring. -Animal farming is boring and the normal feed animal or let them out. At least you can reskin them but I don't care for this part of the game either.-Having a horse makes no difference if i can just teleport, plus the animation just makes it feel weird.

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5 Overall, I actually really love this game. It has a lot of the classic hallmarks of a farming simulation RPG, but with enough new content to not be redundant. The main issue with it is that it is unfinished. I still think it's worth playing in it's unfinished state, but I wish that they Stairway Games hadn't marketed is as a "full release" with several parts of the main storylines still unfinished. Pros: - Characters customization: You have the opportunity to be a plus-sized character and use they/they pronouns which I love. There are nots of cute hairstyles and it's pretty easy to customize your look. - Flexible time: You have the option of making time move slower or quicker, which I think is a great addition as it allows you to play the game more casually or more intensely based on your preference. - LGBTQ+ Representation: There are multiple canonically queer and non-binary characters. - Farming: The team has chosen a great selection of crops and I really like the additions they've made to the sprinklers. I also like that they clearly took inspiration from some of the most popular Stardew Mods, like Automation. - Diving and Ocean-Adjacent Mechanics: Honestly, diving and ocean exploration might be the best addition to the farming sim RPG format. All of the interconnected mechanics feel extremely well thought out: the shells, the collectible critters, the different kinds of kelp, the dehydrator, the coffers, the research objectives and prizes, etc. My only criticism would be that I wish garbage accumulated more quickly. - Critters and Museum: I love the inclusion of an Animal Crossing-style net and bug/critter collection system. And I love that the museum combines the best features of both the Animal Crossing museum and the Stardew museum. - The Island and General Aesthetic: I really like map layout and the rate at which new areas are opened. I also really like the general aesthetic, very bright and friendly and tropical. - Character Design: All of the NPCs are super cute and very diverse. And they all have different outfits for each season, and even change into a bathing suit when at the beach!! They also have A LOT of dialogue. - Holidays/Events: I actually think that Coral Island has some of the best holidays out of any farming sim RPG. They all have a ton of little mini games that are super fun, there is character dialogue in the days before and after the event which makes it feel very organic, attending events has an impact on your relationships with the villagers, and some events even change slightly from year to year. Cons:- Combat: The combat is pretty lacklustre. To be honest, I'm not a big combat fan to begin with, so I don't really mind how easy combat is. However, I can see how a lot of people would find it boring. There are very few different mobs and they're all extremely easily to defeat. - Lacklustre Romances: In general, the romances lack, well... romance. You basically get one romance-based heart event with your love interest (the 10-heart event). And there isn't a ton of dialogue specific to dating. However, Stairway Games have stated that they plan on expanding the romance in the future. (Specifically, I know they've said they're going to add a playdate option, which I imagine will function similar to My Time At Portia). There also just isn't a lot of gameplay included in the marriage + children mechanics. But again, these are also supposed to be updated. But at the time being, there just doesn't seem to be a lot of point in romancing characters. - Typos and Glitches: Honestly, there are a lot of issues with dialogues and glitches. This is to be expected considering it's an unfinished game, but I don't think Stairway should have labeled the game as a full release while there are still so many issues. I will say, the team is extremely responsive to bug reports and dialogue errors on Discord. - Weather RNG: This mainly applies to the collection of critters. But there are many instances where a lack of stability in the RNG messes up a play through. For example: The red king arowana fish is only available for six days of the year and only appears during Rainy/Stormy/Windy weather. I have played three years of the game and have never managed to have the correct weather during these six days, meaning I've never been able to complete the museum. Things like this could easily be configured to make sure that certain days of the year are guaranteed to have certain weather. - Clicking Through Dialogue: Okay, this is probably more of a personal preference. But characters will often have 4-6 dialogues per day. And sometimes it can feel a little tedious have to keep clicking to talk to the NPC over and over again. I wish that some of the dialogue was grouped together into a slightly longer dialogue so I didn't have to click to re-talk to them so many times.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Not Reccommended" is ONLY because the game isn't finished. If/when it is finished, I will change this.If you are a more story-oriented player and the RPG and story progression elements of a game as opposed to grinding resources and doing more repetitive actions? - do NOT buy this game in its current state. I will explain more below.However, if you prefer the more "chill", repetitive gameplay over the story & RPG elements of a game - Go for it, but maybe wait for a sale. I say wait for a sale, because honestly it doesn't feel fair paying full price for an unfinished game.I'll outline the bad / meh parts first:- The game is unfinished. There is yet to be developed plot / map areas / object & npc interactions. - After the first in-game year the game gets kind of grind-y.- While you're given the chance to romance townies, there are barely any cutscenes/interactions that distinguish a romanced character from just someone you're friends with. That is cutscenes with character X play out as you earn hearts in the same way regardless if you're romancing them or not. - There are some bugs with characters getting stuck, resources disappearing from machines. It's nothing game-breaking, but it gets annoying after a while.-The weather mechanics they have in place are kind of questionable. More rainy seasons (fall/spring) and winter barely get any weather (rain/snow) at all. Yet you have game objectives tied to weather. You can't "summon" weather to appear (as of the current game version) like in Stardew Valley with the rain totem for example. So you're stuck with 98% sunny days.Now to the good stuff:- The game looks gorgeous. The animation and the style of animation and art available in the game is stunning.- There is a focus on ecology, heritage, and a strong sense of community which is beautiful.- The underwater stuff is fascinating but it currently suffers from lacking any content beyond the main story mission & cleaning up the sea. Hopefully the next update will fix that.- The gameplay flows smoothly.-Even though the game is unfinished and missing both plot, character progression, and map areas, between the collectibles & quests to improve the land and sea you have plenty to do. I'm 47 hours in and I still haven't finished the offerings or museum collections.But currently, the 2 biggest things this game has going for it is it's pretty and it's kind of chill as unlike other similar games you don't really have a deadline of complete objective X by time Y (yet). Hope this is helpful.
