_childDocuments_.review: As a kickstarter backer, I am severely disappointed and ashamed at the state of the game, especially after it showed so much promise.Despite getting out of Early Access and being version 1.0, Coral Island is NOT finished in the slightest.Worst part about it is that the early game is good until you're a couple of seasons in, which is why I assume it's been reviewed positively recently. I suspect most recent reviews just haven't gotten to the unfinished parts.I'm talking bugs aplenty, missing or incomplete features and even whole segments of the game that lead to nowhere and don't leave an impact. Missing assets such costumes characters mention they are wearing and map portraits, placeholder texts such as "TBD" and <PlayerName>, underwater critters using the wrong models and just looking like a bunch of buggy textures floating around, poor performance in certain areas, pets not moving and so much more.Progression is really weird as well.For example, getting a stable and a horse to move faster takes a fair bit of investment, yet you unlock free fast traveling to pretty much all major and important areas really quickly making the horse more of a nuisance to use rather than an upgrade. Especially since getting off the horse not only has a weird default keybind that is on the other side of the keyboard (K), but also because the animation is slow and you can't forage on a horse. You're better off staying on foot and using space bar to dash (Which the game never tells you you can do).The game also fails to tell you what to do to achieve certain things. There are these withered trees that you obviously have to restore, but despite having restored some of them, I have no idea as to how and when it happened. I just randomly noticed they changed while walking by. None of the NPCs mention it and there doesn't seem to be any reward either.There are also these weird "magic" cutscenes that sometimes happen during the night indicating some kind of change or happening that I have no idea what causes them or what they do. Nothing seemed to have changed when going to the area they happened in. There was only a single time where I found a new path that was unlocked, but there didn't seem to be anything there except more blocked off areas and a "shortcut" to a place I can fast travel to.Rewards for progressing are a joke as well. Altar bundle rewards (Think of community building rooms in Stardew) are basically useless. I haven't fully completed any of the 4 altars, and only a handful of bundles inside of them, but what I've gotten so far has not been worth it whatsoever. Oooh, wow, 8 seeds I can use next season. Thanks game, I'll subtract them from the +500 I need to buy. Sure, Stardew has the same rewards, but there you at least know you're working towards a bigger, unique reward that isn't just "this is pretty now" which seems to be a theme in CI.Mining is yet another issue. Coral Island splits up their mines into 4 different caverns with different 'themes'. But in actuality, they all pretty much look and feel the same. Each mine houses one of the 4 different ore. But here's where the issue comes in. Because you can only find a single type of ore in each mine, you often have to go back to earlier mines to grind for copper which is tedious. And ore nodes spawn way too infrequent and reward way too little ore. I'm talking whole floors without a single node and each node can give as little as 1 ore. And you need 5 to smelt into a bar. And the reward chests you get every 10 or so floors are not exciting either. You get like a couple of craftable (and in most cases useless) tools in the first few, but outside of that it's just the same food item over and over and over. You get 2 weapons across all the chests in the game. A hammer, which is inferior to the starting sword in every single way and an upgraded sword, which is decent, but you can buy an equally strong or even better weapon for just a little bit of money. The only real useful thing you get out of these chests are the explosives, but even those aren't too expensive to craft.And the combat in the mines is a joke. It's floaty, unsatisfying and unengaging. You just take the sword and spam left click until the enemy dies. No enemies are a real threat to you, they all die pretty quickly and are fought the same way. This also makes the tools I mentioned earlier pretty useless and a waste of time and resources. Even when an enemy gets to attack, their attacks are just as floaty and buggy. For example, some enemies still hurt you long after their attack animation appears to be over and others can still attack you in their death animation.But what about the other activities?-Farming is alright.-I barely touched ranching, it didn't seem to be worth the effort.-Fishing is slow and boring. I always seem to find the same fish no matter whether I fish in the ocean, lake or rivers.-Bug catching is unrewarding at best and frustrating at worst with some bugs fleeing as soon as you're in catch range.-Diving. Oh geez I mentioned diving. Not only is diving linked to one of the unfinished segments of the game, but said unfinished segment is your reward for enduring the slowest, most repetitive chore of the entire game. Your movement speed underwater is so slow and there is trash  that you need to remove. While it does do a good job at getting the game's message across, it doesn't work well in the concept of this game. Everything is just so slow, from walking, to removing to having and having to hit some trash piles multiple times. And your reward? A confusing area with no purpose and unfinished characters. Oh and kelp which is the only reason to put up with this crap as it's used for crafting and upgrades, but you find that littered all over the place.Super confusingly, there are also 4 different underwater caverns which have to be unlocked by clearing out the zones they're in. But they house nothing but rooms to farm infinite trash! Even more insulting, considering the one character that mentions these caves tells you that they might be of value to you. And the caves once again show that this game is unfinished, since they're NES Zelda-like square rooms with doors on each wall. Said doors only open once you clear enough trash. But there is no feedback when they open. No sound, no animation, the stones blocking the path just get deleted in plain sight. And the other rooms also just contain more trash.Completing the underwater quest seems to unlock another quest that seems to allow you to turn into a “merfolk” and hopefully fixes the movement speed issue and maybe fleshes out the place more, but that is only AFTER you explored and cleared the ENTIRE MAP already. At this point I was fed up with this section and never went back to diving except in the rare instances where I needed kelp. Maybe it fleshes out the underwater kingdom more, who knows, but the path leading up to it is so slow, repetitive and unenticing that I simply couldn’t be bothered to do that now as well, just for the  that there might be something more to that area. After all, everything leading up to this quest pointed towards a big, fat NO.I really wanted to like or at least "finish" the game, despite its state. But I only managed to get a few days into my first winter before finally waving my white flag.I gave up once I ran into a bug that created duplicates of all my tools in my inventory that you can't delete, drop or sell. All I did was try to enchant the tools, and once I opened the menu they just appeared.I also read that there is a major issue during the winter festival that will straight up permanently delete your tools if you don't watch out. of these issues would be actual issues if the game was still in early access and marked as unfinished. But this is unacceptable.TL;DR: Check the title.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write any reviews, but I had to write one on this game title.Overall, I enjoy playing this game, however, the music stops and starts quite randomly when walking through town, which is annoying, hearing the same music start from the beginning like 3 times in 5 seconds. Also, the theme played in the museum is the ice cave music from Stardew Valley - it's nice to listen to, but feels like a theft considering it's now being heard in a different life-sim title. The controls are dodgy from time to time and sometimes irresponsive or just make no sense (why keep switching from left and right clicking when filling or using the watering can???) and having to dash for quick movement is quite annoying on the long-run - I'm 11 hours into the game and got no horse. Some conversations just make no sense, like having a cutscene with - I think Lily - who I'd spoken to before, giving me a mission, then introducing herself to me as if we'd never spoken before. The biggest downside of this game - in my opinion - is that the hottest male char (Derek) is not dateable and doesn't even appear on the social list.Still, the above-metioned hasn't put me off from playing this game yet and I would recommend it to those who've enjoyed Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon / Story of Seasons.

_childDocuments_.review: The farming is good not much different than any other farming sim, as well as the animal care aspects as well. That is where the samey feel stops. The recycle mechanic for trash, the fact that picking up the trash matters, and crafting with it so you actually want to go searching for the garbage is very unique. The diving feature is smooth and underwater area is beautifully crafted. You can tell careful meticulous care was taken with each aspect of the land, mines, and sea. The scaling system for your town is easy to understand, and improve your rankings. The developers honestly listen to the feed back of their community and implement ways that don't make it to hard or easy to complete your objectives. The variety of the characters are amazing as well. The unique look at what a spirit is, and the culture references are amazing. There still a bit of a balance issue in my opinion with things being sold for so little but over all the game feels, looks, and plays stunningly. Definitely a triple A game being sold for an indie price in my opinion. I highly recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I wanted to love. It's in one of my favorite genres, it hits all the notes, but I just can't say I enjoy it, for a few reasons.One, it's horrifically derivative; as other reviewers put it, it's "we have Stardew Valley at home." This game does absolutely nothing that Stardew Valley doesn't already do better (and that goes fivefold if you have any of the major Stardew quality-of-life mods like UI Info Suite.) It's the _same game_ but nowhere near as well done. Stardew's characters are more memorable, the heart events and plotlines better written (and again, speaking of mods, Stardew Valley Expanded and Ridgeside Village are practically free DLC. You know any expansions this game gets won't be free.)So if there's another game that does everything this game does, at half the price (or less, if you get Stardew on sale), then why choose this game over that one when you could be playing that one?Two, it's laughably unfinished. This is not a 1.0 release as of November of 2023. It's still very much in Early Access, they just don't want to say that anymore because they apparently needed the money and released it on consoles as a 1.0 and changed the version number on Steam to go with it. Even their roadmap all but says this out loud; it'll be Q4 of 2024, or maybe even 2025, before this game is even realistically a 1.0 release.Three, it's buggy in ways that break the game. Machines don't work right, events don't fire, quests don't advance...they couldn't even copy Stardew right.And just a personal gripe, but there's a musical motif in Spring in this game that is so blatantly a Wild Horseradish Jam copy that it's all but winking at how it got one over on you.Seriously. If you haven't played Stardew Valley, buy that instead. And if you have played Stardew Valley, just go play it again and save yourself 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally get this excited about early access games as I can usually see the limits and just feel like they're going to fix bugs through development but I'm really really excited about where this game will go. Being so early in development and me being almost through the first year I'm definitely seeing some limits (That being limits in relationships, some bugs with the events and costumes, things like that which are totally understandable) but it makes me excited to see what the game will become. The developers have really focused on the core gameplay to let players explore the area, get started with their farm, and see some of the elements that will be implemented further into the gameplay as well as let them work through some early game goals which I think was a smart choice. So far the map is already large with various interesting locations (And it looks like it will expand), the graphics are pretty, the character designs and art are unique and beautiful (Props to the artist, the characters are super expressive, unique, and easy to connect with), the setting is fun and dynamic (I see inspiration from China, Japan, Polynesia, and even the Greek Isles) and the story is interesting and easy to follow. I've played through a lot of the stand out farming games with town dynamics (Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, Animal Crossing) and I've also played through a lot of games that try to capture the various elements that have made those games successful but never quite did it successfully and I feel this game has managed to capture those elements successfully while putting their own style on it to make it unique and engaging. I'm really excited to follow the development of this game and see where it goes!

_childDocuments_.review: I recently stumbled across Coral Island, and having grown up on Harvest Moons, and having played Stardew Valley on basically every platform available to man, I really wanted to try something else. The art style seemed really nice, and I got it on a discount.After having finished the first year (which took about 50-ish hours), and having made a decent chunk of progress in the main plots of the game, I can confidently recommend this game to virtually every aficionado of the genre. - The art style. The game looks  good. Every NPC has a hand drawn sprite which changes throughout the seasons, all of them even have beach sprites and of course, multiple expressions. The actual 3D game looks good as well, everything pops really well and the town really looks good with all the different decorations that are around all year round, especially around the Winter time. Same goes for every item: the sprites are beautiful, especially for all the produce that's available. As a European, I have never seen a good chunk of the vegetables and fruits the game offers, so seeing them so well drawn feels really nice.- The festivals. I feel like the festivals are, simply put, really nice. All of them have one or more minigame to play which adds to the immersion, each of them have a nice, hand drawn, animated title card and it's just really fun to play around the festivals. The winter week-long festival was especially nice because it really reminded me of those Christmas markets you find around towns.- The quantity of content. Most of these farming sim games tend to have the same gameplay loop: wake up, tend to the farm/animals, spend your stamina/time doing something around the map, sell your produce, go to sleep, repeat; and maybe do some quest, chat with someone in the meantime to build your relationships. And that's good: that's the loop you expect playing such a game, and Coral Island isn't substantially different; however it adds a couple of activities you normally don't find in most other farming sims: bug catching and ocean diving, and to an extent, the Museum. Bug catching work very similar to Animal Crossing: you swing a net and get a bug, but here you have to be careful they don't run away. The Museum is identical to Animal Crossing's one: you give new fish, bugs, gems, artifacts, and critters to the Museum and get some stuff back. This simply adds a nice chunk of playtime and activities to the game in order to finish up the museum, although this may feel grindy at times. And finally:- Ocean diving. This is Coral Island's biggest and most unique mechanic. It works similarly to a traditional "mine" in this game: you break tons of trash in the ocean, find a special item (similarly to how you find stairs in the mines) to eventually go deeper, and you can even find special forageables, critters, and a ton of treasure chest while down there. You also find kelp, which are essential to enhancing your net and fishing rod, bust most importantly: everything on your farm. This is essential to getting better produce and should be prioritized over most other activities, at least in my opinion. You also use kelp to craft a ton of items, many of which are fundamental such as sprinklers, or you refine trash into scraps which are used in the creation of most machines and then some. It's also essential to one of the game's biggest plot lines, and helps with raising the town rating. The sound and the visual design is really good, and it's really pleasing seeing all the coral heal up as you work. Diving looks good and feels relaxing, whereas the mines feel a little more invested due to the mobs.- The bugs. The game has a bunch of relatively small and yet mildly annoying bugs. My character's sidecut seldom disappears into a bald spot and I have to change my clothes. Sometimes the tile indicator simply disappears, and it's infuriating, especially in the mines. There was a bug recently that caused tools to degrade permanently but it got quickly fixed. Sometimes there are graver bugs, but so far nothing truly disruptive to my experience but a mild eyeroll. Anyways: they are there and it would feel disingenuous to not mention it.- The music. This is more of a pet peeve than anything else, but I feel like the music is... whatever. Not the music score itself, but rather how it just doesn't play a lot of the time. The game feels silent a lot of the time, and it very, very jarringly starts and stops music when you change zones in the island. I just wish it was betterly executed, but again, worth a mention.- Some minigames. Ok, some minigames are... poorly made. The ring toss in the Spooky Festival is kind of impossible to understand and I had to look up how it worked because the controls were really not helping. This also expands to most other other minigames: some can be practiced, other can't, none of them have a tutorial to them which would greatly help, even a one page scheme would greatly help this instead of just inferring what you're supposed to do. - The Spooky Festival is clearly unfinished. This isn't something "bad", but it was a little jarring: every character mentions they have some cool costume on during the festival when it's just not true. It takes a little out of the immersion, and while they mentioned 1.2 will be the "Spooky Season Update", so far it's a functional festival but the iconic Halloween thing, costumes, is so far missing. Which kind of sucks, especially when you get a lot of goofy costumes for yourself.- I really like the vast asian inspirations and influence in the game, from character design to ambience design, everything oozes this and it's lovely, especially since most of these farming sims tend to have vaguely similar ambience.- I also really like the variety in body types in NPCs and bachelors/bachelorettes. From Mark to Wakuu, from Pablo to Rafael, then from Aaliah to Eva, from Chaem to Lily, the game has one for all tastes. The recent 1.1 update even added two merpeople to the marriage pool. I also like the hangouts you can do, they're nice and short but help add something onto the very old, very established formula of run-up-to-Person-gift-favourite-item-leave to grind hearts these games tend to have. That's it then! This was a little longer than I expected, but I really enjoy the game, and I really want other people to try it out and support these talented and passionate devs. Bye!

_childDocuments_.review: This game still has a long way to go, but it is exceptional, even as is. While I question some of the writing and dev priorities, the world presented is rich, and vibrant, including unique gameplay that you don't often see in farming sims like this. The premise that you need to clean up the island is refreshing and fun. The artwork is exceptional. I disagree very much with the reviews that say the diversity is "forced" or "pandering". You're on an island in the south pacific -- it feels very natural that such an island would have many types of people. I also like that the romance options don't trend too young or seem like they're barely adults. They've lived lives, run their own businesses. They might even be single parents, and that is refreshing. Only nitpick is that the museum feels very tacked on, and is very difficult to fill up. The game is still very much in the early stages so if you don't want an incomplete game (not many festivals are finished, some dialogue options have placeholder text) but you can see where it is going, and that's very encouraging. I recommend it, especially on sale or buying when it's finished.EDIT: The gameplay of this game is really awesome and unique. The underwater portion is some of the most fun and completely atypical of what you typically see in a life/farming sim. The variety of romances continues to be great.🚨🚨 EDIT 2: 🚨🚨I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone in its current state. It has so much potential, great mechanics, interesting gameplay, and a diverse cast. Unfortunately potential is all it has. Since the 1.0 release I was hopeful that many of the incomplete aspects of the games would be completely fleshed out, as is typical of games. In just about every other Early Access game, incomplete parts of the story are completed for 1.0. There may be bugs (even game breaking ones) but the storyline is whole, the character arcs are whole, and it is by itself a complete standalone product that can be improved upon down the line. You expect bugs but you expect the main story to be complete.That's not the case with coral island. This is an incomplete game. The main storyline is incomplete. Some of the romances are incomplete. Major portions of the game that are touted as unlockable as a main function of the gameplay are incomplete and thus *not* unlockable. It seems like huge portions of this game are simply not finished. This is not a v1.0 quality game. This game is still in early access, despite the label and the price bump. Do not buy this game. There is so much to complete you should not play this game unless you are prepared for your save to be wiped whenever they eventually get to finishing the main quest line.It is completely beyond me why this was rushed to release.There are many more complete farming/life sims out there. You should play one of those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral island is easily one of the most gorgeous games I’ve ever played, and aside from some lagging, runs relatively well on steamdeck. That said…- The cast of characters are diverse on paper, but bland as the day is long. Through they supposedly all have different personalities, their dialogue, stories, and events are all like tap water. It’s there, it’s drinkable, but it’s not exciting. - I genuinely can’t remember who is who or where to find them. The map is huge, the characters’ schedules are diverse, and because I’m not engaged in getting to know anyone, I’m regularly forgetting where to find them. At this point, it’s either A: consult the map throughout a game day, or B: just talk who I run into throughout a game day. - There’s just TOO much content. Normally, not a complaint I make, but in this case, it’s a problem of quantity of content over quality. Lots of repetition in the daily activities and goals without a strong story to hold it all together. - Which brings me to the narrative itself. Rural town besieged by corporate capitalism, and lucky you called to save the day by an island goddess and all you need is your skills along with your inherited farm. I’m not one to knock a tried and true plot, mind you, but what this one lacks is the substance that could really draw you in and make you FEEL part of the story, and cheer for your side to win. Because no one is exciting or interesting, and because the narrative is weak, it becomes more of a to-do list to kick out those greedy moneybags than something to celebrate.  - The game’s budget seems to directed primarily on art. I love a gorgeous game, and the style of this one is delightfully charming, but the opportunity cost is readily apparent. The writing and gameplay clearly took a backseat to a goal of ‘make this a pretty game.’ I wish they’d spent half as much time on the story and writing as they clearly spent on the art, and the game would have balanced out a lot better imho. And now the nitpicky: - I’m a little annoyed there’s both bundles and the museum, especially since some items overlap. I love developing a museum, and getting rewarded, but it’s left me feeling like I’m chasing down stuff for duplicative work, and I didn’t enjoy that.- I hate the fishing mechanism. Loathe, actually. Supposedly it gets easier, but as someone who struggles with timing, it sucked. No option to toggle an easy mode on, and so I just literally ignore the skill entirely.- Skill maps. I usually love them and their perks, but idk I just couldn’t get excited about the levels and rewards. It felt too grindy, and not in a good way. Overall, as much as I hate to say it, this game feels like a really, really gorgeous wrapped box of basic shortbread cookies. I mean yeah, you can eat them, but is it worth $30 for them when you can find other things to eat instead? I’m going to have to say no. There’s other games to play that, while they may not be as pretty, come with better content and often smaller price tags (such as SDV and the recently released FoM) that can satisfy the cravings a lot better imho. If you want to play, buy it on sale is my best recommendation. It’s a pretty experience, just also a very flat one.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game! It's everything it promises and it's so beautiful to watch. Do I recommend it? Yes, yes, and yes.You know how there are a million farming sims out there, each thinking they added that one tiny special feature to the genre that makes it okay to deliver a completely unpolished game for a full price because people just love farming sims?Well, here you have an example of how it actually should be done. They put the whole thing to a coral island and the feel of the game is just fantastic. So many things work so smoothly. You feel like there is a lot to discover, the island seems vivid and the characters really feel like busy inhabitants rather than just decoration you can talk to. Despite being Early Access, the game feels coherent and thought through. Features that are missing (esp. mini games) are already teased and you are told in-game that they are yet to be implemented. And, I mean: scubadiving for treasures and discovering underwater, come on! The only weaker part in my opinion is mining in the cave, as it feels a bit neglected so far. This is rather a result of the details and the life in the overworld but should be worked on until full release nevertheless. However, it is absolutely okay and works in the context of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying my best to hold off on playing too much of Coral Island before the game officially releases as I don't want to spoil myself etc- HOWEVER I can say that it's shaping up to be a great game! The art is undeniably gorgeous, the farming is what you'd expect and there's some lovely new mechanics that add a unique element to the gameplay that I'm enjoying. The characters and NPCs offer great insight into the lore and storyline, and I'm looking forward to more relationships being expanded upon as the game develops.As it stands though, Coral Island still needs A LOT of work - bug catching is tedious, and fishing can be like pulling teeth. It's a slow grind to begin with as money is hard to come by and it's hard to navigate the map as your model will catch on things you expect to be 'in the background' (so to speak). The map is huge (which is amazing!!!!) however it takes so long to go from one place to another as your character is painfully slow without their dash. Animations are still pretty rough, but functional for an early access release - shows great promise for the final release.My biggest gripe is that I'm waiting (very impatiently I gotta admit) for the promised multiplayer mode to be released. I purchased the game under the promise of a multiplayer option so that I can play with my friends, and convinced them all to buy the game for this very reason. Would love to see it implemented so that I can enjoy the game with others.Please do support this game and the developers however you can, but it may be worth just waiting for the final release to be made available. It's shaping up to be a very memorable farming sim, and I'm so looking forward to what the game has to offer, even if right now it frustrates me.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a beautiful game with wonderful scenery and engaging characters. I have loved playing it and will continue to enjoy it for a long time to come I'm sure. It's been a long time since I have played a game, especially a farming sim, that just feels so loved by the creators. I can understand, overall, people's frustrations. However, my opinion on the game being released as a 1.0 without all its promised content is this: they kinda had to. What I mean by that is I can't explain how many times I came across articles and social media threads accusing the developers of this game to be scamming people, simply because it was taking a long time to come out. I'm not a game developer but I can't imagine how scary it must be to have tons of people accusing you of stealing your Kickstarter money and claiming your game is never actually going to come out. So I personally don't at all blame them for releasing it as it is and just doing updates as they finish them. So is the game perfect? No. There are typos and some glitches and a couple of incomplete story lines.Do I fully believe that the developers are doing their best and the game is going to just keep getting better? Absolutely. Tldr; there's a lot of harsh criticism of this game, but if you want to see a game with an environment that has a lot of love, is very cozy, and has wonderful characters then I fully recommend it. Just play it knowing that you get to look forward to wonderful content in the future too.

_childDocuments_.review: The game in itself is nice, and I'd recommend it on sale.It's a bit like MTAP or MTAS, from the same publisher, but this one gives the highlight to farming, whilst the other two were more focused on crafting.The scenery is nice, the ability to dive is interesting, overall, it's cool.But. There's a few things that should be known.Like, for instance, as mentioned above, the game isn't entirely finished. You got puzzles underwater that do absolutely nothing. Economy is a bit hard early game. Fishing is barely explained. There's a lot of QoL stuff that are simply missing. Fences gates for instance must be opened & closed manually, which is a real pain since you can't jump, and MTAS/MTAP both had that.There's also a few minor bugs, like monsters that'd get stuck under stones in the mines. And some crashes. Which highlights a real issue though: game is saved every morning in game. So if the game crashes in a late day festival, you loose the whole day and a big hour in winter. Plus all those 2% drops you got within the day. This can be quite infuriating.Still, that's one crash in a lot of hours, so I guess I'd still recommend the game - on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: My Time at Sandrock = 38 MinImmortal Life = 6.5 Hrs (I'm excited for this one, too)My Time At Portia = 11.7 HrsStardew Valley = 17.5 Hrs (love the music, mostly)Coral Island = 23.5 Hrs (and counting)I will admit that my dalliance with the farm-Life sim genre is low, as my library will attest. But already before purchasing,  had me entranced. The setting and artwork is SO beautiful that it reminds me how I even fell in love with video games in the first place, and the addition of underwater diving is a simple yet ingenious mechanic for the genre.Playing it, even early in this state, is definitely a delight. I look forward to seeing this title grow (pun intended).+I literally cannot think of a more chill game I have ever played. The lighting/colors are perfect, there are no annoying sounds, and the music is catchy earworms. It captures island Life pretty perfectly - just chill and go with what the day brings. I've lowered the gametime so I don't feel constant FOMO, and it's been the perfect tempo to just -enjoy the journey-, not outsmart the grind.It's become a semi-ritual to log in for a day or two after work to decompress.+I LOVE the art direction of this game. The character drawings (and their expressions) are top-notch, and the in-game models translate the cartoony-ness with true fidelity. Even the freakin' cats and dogs are expressionful.The architecture is on-point, offering different varieties but all of them still geling really well with the island mojo. And the decorations so far are varied enough that you can decorate to a wonderful degree. Thinking that  will be added over time is just Sun on the sand.+I love the character customization in this, even if -currently- the facial options don't stick. There's a decent amount of different kinds of hairstyles already, you can tweak the skin color to your liking, and there's selections for whole outfits, or bits and pieces. A trip to the barbershop allows you to entirely re-edit for $500.You can choose Mr./Ms./Mx., or you can type whatever you prefer. My dude's gender is Barefoot Farmer.🦶+There is a strong cast of characters here, from different generations and backgrounds. There's a decent number of "datables", I suppose - I don't have much time in other farm-Life sims, so I can't really attest. Tho, right now, romance isn't fully implemented, but what's there is distracting enough. And per the roadmap, can expect to see much more in the way of this down the line.+The weather is SO on-point, Mother Nature would totally take a selfie. Sunny days are bright and warm, cloudy days lull, rainy days are super chill and I could watch/listen to the rain all day, and the windy days have quite lil' wind streams roll over the land. I wasn't expecting all of this, let alone at this level of flair, so early in, and it's endearing.+It's so easy to "See something/say something" with this title. I've played many games in Early Access, but have never submitted feedback. I've submitted quite a few! Hope they've helped.+It's modest, seems doable within the timeframes provided, and they already delivered on the Feedback Update. This game is made with such a passion that I think the roadmap is pretty feasible. +Have I mentioned I liked the music? =) Wish there was an option to loop it, tho. Sometimes, it's too quiet.+I love the setting. I lived in Honolulu when I was younger, and I've always wanted to go back. I understand  is a different heritage, but the setting, itself, is totally where I'd rather be. I think that's why the others never really stuck with me. Oooo - a farm in the country. Pssht. Gimmie a farm on a beach. Portia , but  is my inner-sanctuary. It's bright and breezy!+So far, it runs pretty great on the Deck, and the last update made it more accessible having full controller implementation. Steam Cloud support makes it effortless to go from desktop to Deck.-It's just drill, thrill, thank you Farmer Bill with this one. Probably the most kindly masculine dude on the whole island, and he's gone as soon as the Pufferfish building is up. I can't even remember his name, he's gone so quick. :p Build-A-Date DLC, please! ;D 🌞👍🦩

_childDocuments_.review: If I would be able to put a neutral review on this I probably would. The game is neither fully amazing, nor is it fully bad. HOWEVER, since there is quite the list of annoying features, I decided to make a bad review. Not because I dislike the game, but because I hope for it to improve.I fully understand that Stairway Games has a lot of followers that probably have high demands and wishes for the game. Sometimes, however, I do feel like they loose sight of what is important to focus on. Generally said what I mean with this: It is way more worth to implement features into a game that are FULLY fleshed out and thought through... and not half done and then the player gets excited at first and then disappointed later.What exactly do I mean with this? Well there are a lot of sections in the game that feel fully incomplete and flat and to be honest, quite underwhelming. As an earlier comment here said, I have spend a lot of time in the game because I want to enjoy it, and I do to a certain degree, but I more and more encounter situations in which I just feel let down. I want to make a list of all the things I want to address, also in no certain order AND keep in mind I HAVE NOT PLAYED THROUGH THE FIRST YEAR EVEN!1) There is a huge (quite ugly) recycling area in the middle of the town... what exactly is the purpose of it? It never gets any interaction besides one cutscene or so.2) The "Bad guys" of the story don't give any weight to the story whatsoever. Even after  they don't do anything. What even is their purpose? 3) The dating mechanic in the game is mediocre at best. The interactions are not anywhere near romantic or butterfly-y feeling inducing. The heart events are totally non-involving for the player and it feels like you are just watching a cutscene full of lore. After reaching heart 8 and asking a character to become your partner it honestly feels just out of the blue? I watched 8 random cutscenes and then suddenly they are in love with me?4) Overall I also dislike the way Stairway Games communicates their progress and implementations. Every time they implement something I feel like I should not watch it because it is basically a HUGE spoiler to everything happening in the game. When the wedding mechanic was implemented all of it was spoilered... a nice trailer given, you see the outfits, the locations, all of it. For a wedding to be a suppose "end game" thing in a farm sim... it just feels like I got taken the opportunity to actually explore and experience the new content.5) You have way too many options, and no option is fully done. Yes it is amazing that I can choose whatever to do and progress in that area.. may it be mining a lot or clearing the ocean (I probably already by mid summer year 1 had the ocean clean)... but what then? I think it would have actually done the game some good to lock certain content behind certain achievements. YES a lot of people will get upset because they have to be patience and give it some time. I know, complicated for a lot... but this way it would ACTUALLY feel like an achievement to finally get something. If you keep in mind that clearing the ocean is supposed to be THE GAME IDEA, its just a lackluster for how EASILY and QUICKLY you can get it done.6) It is upsetting to see that so many updates are pushed out and all of this new content is supposed to be implemented, but then there are small things that really could need improvement first7) Improving the town rank feels beyond underwhelming. Yes I get new seeds and I can buy more clothes/decorations... but it feels like a big lack-luster to the game. If the town has suffered from no tourism and I am supposed to help, then why do they all have such amazing houses and even a huge villa? Where does that money come from? Why cant my town rank improvements have more impact to the town itself?8) It is unable to play the game properly without shutting it down and restarting it after 2 or 3days ingame, a lot of stuff bugs out (for example moving objects on your farm with the designed machine for it... absolutely buggy).Why do I play it? Because I want to still give the game the attention it deserves and wait for a time all of this finally gets improved. And the game is a lot of fun and enjoyable/cozy, if you are willing to accept that you can do alot, but nothing fully.

And the cursor SERIOUSLY affects the direction of tools using, which is FREAKING ANNOYING- The rice doesn't have the offering tag though it is one of the offerings- If you don't collect all of the eggs at once, the unpicked eggs will disappear the next time you enter- Stone path don't display-Cannot donate the Earth gem even though it has the donate tag

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played the game for about 15 hours now and here’s my thoughts so far:The game itself is a lot of fun and brings a fresh face to the farming sim genre. The world is absolutely gorgeous, the storyline is interesting, the characters are likable, and gameplay is enjoyable. With that being said, since the game is still technically being developed, a lot of what I mentioned above needs polished and updated to better suit players.Overall,Pros - Easy to learn gameplay, stunning details and graphics, interesting and diverse characters, lots of places to explore in the world, decent variety of crops, crops grow at a decent rate, point system to upgrade gameplay mechanics (such as increasing the ability to harvest higher quality crops or double crops), friendship/romance system is pretty straightforward, easy fishing, fast travel is unlocked early on in the gameCons - Stamina decays too quickly, stamina use even when not hitting your target object, flimsy controls and no native controller support (I know it’s coming in a future update), mines aren’t that great or accessible and it takes a long time to go down even five floors to reach an elevator, sprint speed is still pretty slow even after upgrading it twice using the point system, frequent frame rate drops and lag, missing/glitched graphics in some areas, incorrect grammar during some scenes (yeah this is just me being nit-picky but it should be fixed in the future), festivals are incomplete and while it’s nice to know they exist I think it would be better not to have them until they’re fully developedI would definitely recommend this game despite the current cons because I believe the pros outweigh them. The game is so addicting so far!(Will update my review as the game is further developed and new features are released.)

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to enjoy this game, and tried for a long time at it. It has a lot of potential and definitely kept me interested longer than Stardew Valley, the game it's pretty clearly ripping off. But it's crazy, crazy unfinished for what they're asking people to pay. Entire sections of the game are cordoned off with "soon" signs hung on them, including skills for which I have points just sitting on the character, unused. Whole systems, like the SV-style mine combat, are the better part of a year away.But even more importantly to me, there are big balance issues that I can only hope future updates address. As it stands the game is too in love with slowing you down and making everything take forever. To some extent that's the nature of the farm/life sim genre, I get that, but 20 hours in it just didn't feel like I'd made any substantial progress, and that's too many hours to still feel that way. So much is gated behind far-off milestones or just simply not in the game yet in the first place.At best, wait 6-12 months and buy it on sale. There's no guarantee it will ever be as good as it promises to be in the first few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game so much. It has the same basic vibes of other farm sims where it has 4 seasons, 28 days per, with farming, fishing, mining, and donating. The difference is the massive opportunities the creators have started to give us. It is so much depth without feeling rushed. The characters are so well written and drawn. I love how many different characters there are, both single and ready to mingle, and not. (Rafael has my heart entirely <3) Being able to grow the town's rank, cleaning up the ocean, donating to make the museum more of a feature on Coral Island, and also helping the gods/godesses take care of the Island and save them. There are a couple of things I wish were already here but that's the thing about an early access game. I do also wish that time wouldn't move so quickly somehow? It always caused me anxiety of the FOMO if I didn't get everything I needed to get done before each season is over with, but at least in Coral Island, there isn't a massive rush to try and complete everything within the 1st year. That could be an early access thing or a Coral Island thing, we will find out when version 1 is released some day. What it is so far, is the beginning to something absolutely brilliant and I cannot wait to play more and see what all is in store.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being fully released and with a 1.1 patch, I had to take a break from this game because it is buggy enough that I am scared to play it, especially with recent discussion threads where people's games have been glitching out in crazy ways including missing item upgrades, extra items spawning, and their save file being completely bricked, leading to me creating a backup save copy on my PC before continuing. Whenever I try to do something even a bit out of the ordinary in-game, I worry if it will bug out. An example being: changing the external appearance of a building you are moving will give you two buildings because it won't move the initial one.There are a lot of quality of life features missing. The biggest one is: you can't view the sell price of items in your inventory, only with the Shipping Bin open, so you have to run back and forth pricing your items, which is just silly. This is especially inconvenient because there is a festival where you score higher for more expensive items, so the sell price is actually really important. Labels such as whether an item has been donated or offered already are not consistent and are missing on certain pages too.There are no indicators on the map for when there is a new task/quest available at the town boards and underground in the hideout. You waste so much time running back and forth to check if there is a quest posted, leading to me avoiding making these checks since it causes you to lose significant amounts of the limited time you have in a day.There are arbitrary limitations on which items you can put in certain machines, and you can only put items of the same type at the same time in several machines, like the same size milk or egg or the same type of fruit or vegetable, yet other "machines," like the Bee House, allow you to put any flower you want in there.There is no way to buyback items you have sold at the stores, even right away.Buildings cannot be moved partially overlapping where they are initially placed. Sometimes you need to move something by one or two rows and cannot, because you have to place the new building somewhere completely different first, wait for that to process for two days, then move it again. This combined with the bugs I experienced made moving my building a very negative experience.If they release a bunch of fixes this game will be much more playable. It has potential.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Graphics }---☐ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☑ Good☐ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ MS-DOSLooks decent for a farm-sim game, and has cute and emotive characters and animals. The pets in particular are adorable. ---{ Gameplay }---☑ Very good☐ Good☐ It's just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don'tThis is why you play the game. Have played SDV for hundreds of hours across multiple platforms, played Harvest Moon religiously as a child, and this game's gameplay, in my humble opinion, takes the cake easily. ---{ Audio }---☐ Eargasm☐ Very good☑ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ I'm now deafMusic is fairly good, but I will admit some of the tool usage sfx seems a little rough around the edges sometimes. ---{ Audience }---☐ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☑ GrandmaAnyone can play this game, but I do feel that the game touches on enough complex topics, such as environmentalism, parental/spousal grieving, loss of culture, and others that perhaps best suit individuals who have had the ability to be somewhat educated on the matter first.---{ PC Requirements }---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computerNot a difficult game to run, but it does look good enough, and there are enough interacting systems that I wouldn't be surprised if some older computers started to have difficulties in running it. ---{ Difficulty }---☐ Just press 'W'☑ Easy☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Significant brain usage☐ Difficult☐ Dark SoulsOnly thing in the game that I have even remotely struggled with, is the fishing, and that feels about right. Not necessarily the overarching narrative, as that's fairly cut-and-dry, but the stories in between characters. On my second serious save, those issues largely seem to be resolved, although visual glitches still happen here and there. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great CASUAL game. Yes I said CASUAL. It's new, and still being worked on. Has some incomplete areas, moreso towards the end of all of the achievements. HOWEVER, if you casually play and enjoy the game instead of working to get to the end, I think you'll find it SUPER amazing. I've played this game for (checks notes) 299 hrs. Could I have played more? probably. But i'm taking my time, Farming all the things, meeting all the people, getting all the critters, and just enjoying what the game has to offer. The animals are ADORABLE, and I love the premise of combining a "clean it up" game with a farming game.  If you like farming games, clean it up games, and casual games with tasks attached, and are willing to accept that the game sometimes gets a pest problem and needs an exterminator from time to time...this is definitely the game for you. Ignore the negative Nellies in the reviews and just enjoy the game for being a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: As same as most of the reviews, I also like this game a lot and has a lot of potential. The graphics is good, the soundtrack is nice and there are quite a lot of things that you can do, than the other farming sims. Sadly, the game is really buggy right now and there are clearly still some parts that are missing. I kinda feel like this should still be considered as early access game since this feels as buggy as the other early access farming sim games.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Right now? I wouldn't recommend this. Not because some story lines aren't done but it kinda sucks when the fellas stop talking to me because of a bug T_ Tother than that, pretty good game. use your scythe to harvest crops and your pickaxe to pick up animal produce when your animals are in the way you're welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential, but if you have time on your hand and plan on playing this game as much as possible, you might be disappointed once you've reached year 2. The characters are endearing, your goal, alongside developing your farm, is to save the island from pollution by diving and healing a goddess with gifts. It reminds me a lot of both Stardew Valley and a bit of Animal Crossing! It's a very good game, I can't wait for the final result, but do keep in mind that it is currently still under development :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is one of the best games I've played. I've played a ton of Stardew Valley and a ton of Animal Crossing and I've always dreamed of a game that would combine both, and I finally found it!! When the version first came out in 1.0, there were a lot of bugs and I stopped playing eventually, but now that everything is so much better, this game has become my absolute favorite! (: Thank you so much to Stairway Games & Humble Games for making this happen (:
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, I am VERY late to the farming sim game life but I have binged SO MANY over the last year. I bought this game in EA but didn't officially play until after 1.0 released. But I LOVE this game so much. Are there bugs? yes. Is there feedback I would give to improve? yes. But I know there is a LOT coming that I cannot wait for. I don't mind releasing more content post go-live because it will keep me playing for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island provides a refreshing take on the typical farming simulator like Stardew Valley. The cast of characters is well diverse and offers a good representation of persons of color without falling to cliches or the 'token'-type of characters. The gameplay itself is exciting and definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: While I do still really enjoy this game, I feel like it's worth pointing out that it is buggy as all get out despite it being officially released. If that's a dealbreaker for you, you might want to wait it out.--------------------------------♥ The graphics are really nice, one of the most visually appealing farm games I've played♥ There's so much to do already and it doesn't sound like they are even close to implementing everything they have planned♥ Very wide cast of NPCs♥ Character customization is simple, but still gives a lot of choice♥ There is an option in the settings to slow down time, which is nice because there is soo much to do♥ In one of the buildings there is a giant chicken. _childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Currently hooked on this game after trying to find the next new enjoyable farm game. The visuals are beautiful, the world is full of personality and has a strong environmental identity which is easy to get immersed in. The festivals are full of life that actively gets you to do mini games which makes it stand out from other farming titles. There's a bunch of other quality of life things in the game such as logging the townies gift preferences for you that are a breath of fresh air. It feels like a modern farming game doing its own thing and not just a copy paste reskin of existing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game is still a wip ofc but there is a really solid and fun foundation that is very easy to get into. the characters are varied and with the games foundation in SEA culture and mythology it puts a new really nice twist on a well-known farm-sim formula. Im very very much looking forward to see the full game on release but for now this is a very solid early access.Whether you wanna jump in now or later, if you enjoy a solid, chill farming sim i think you will enjoy Coral island.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game had potential-- it's a Stardew knockoff and it knows it, with a little bit of Animal Crossing thrown in for good measure, but it had its appeal. However, I cannot recommend this game because it was sloppily pushed to 1.0 well before it was ready. The main questline is incomplete. There are bugs galore-- and not just fun, quirky bugs like your pet cat speaking to you like your spouse, but bugs that make the game unplayable. I'm not sure what the motivation for rushing a sloppy, buggy, unfinished game to 1.0 would have been, but the dev team ought to be embarrassed. A 6GB "hotfix" broke more than it fixed. As someone who was really looking forward to this game, I'm sorely disappointed. I don't have a lot of faith that this game will ever deliver a polished finished product that lives up to its promised scope of work. Disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I love it!  It's a bit clunky with the movements of the characters but I love it.  I like the story telling, the shrine ideas, the lore, the game itself.  It's going to be one that gets played over and over I think.  There is a good range of characters and I'm actually looking forward to getting to know them rather than avoiding them all and I like the fishing dynamic.  I don't think it's too much like Stardew Valley, after all there's diving to be done!  I'd like to see a lot more bugs (catchable ones) in the game, and many more updates.  The only con I can find in the game is....nope, no cons.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, fantastic artwork, and the landscape is beautiful. The storyline is really lovely as well!What it needs:-Needs a button to auto-play dialogue-Being able to save when you want (the game days are far too long to only be able to save when your character sleeps)-movement feels really clunky in-game, and not in the fun kind of wayOverall highly recommend this game, as its very relaxing and fun
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a LOT like Stardew Valley. However, you have a more realistic cartoony world instead of the pixelated world. I love the world of Coral Island from the people to nature and everything in between. The world story is much more realistic with elements like oil spills and oil companies, to the people in the game is a true representation of people in the real world. I love the inclusiveness of this world. I look forward to more that is going to come out with the game considering that it is early access and I do hope that they fix the clothing graphics for the bigger-sized characters. The clothing options clip and it doesn't look right. Highly recommend this game if you like Stardew Valley and a more realistic inclusive world.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable and overall enjoyable game with loads of content.However, I'm inclined to not recommend this game right now due to the staggering amount of bugs that can be game breaking.The developers also seemed to have removed the "I'm stuck" button, which I think is a bad call when the game still has so many instances where the player can in fact, get stuck. Especially, since so many bugs seem to happen in town events, which also sometimes happen at night, in a game that only ever saves after you go to sleep, causing a lot of lost progress in case this happens. For me personally that was enough reason to drop the game, even though I wasn't done with all the content I wanted to do yet.I'm sure I'll revisit this game at one point and if things changed, I'll change my review too.

_childDocuments_.review: You would never understand why a single-player farming game canceled your EA save file (I didn't use  bcuz in return of being forced to start over again, you could keep the money from the canceled EA save, ironically), just like I didn't. I was born into Starlet Town from Day 1 Spring, Year 1, with 150k proving that the dev was making some of the least efforts to hope you are feeling well. I believe most players are not-- I mean, your farm is gone.+ Absolutely beautiful & consistent art, both 2D and 3D.+ Variety of goods & items & interactable objects, yet some are not fully implemented.+ Atmosphere-- the above qualities made it truly immersive.- Burning your device out (meaning having your progress of the day lost).- Mining and fighting in the dungeon are a pain in the ___ especially when nearly all your productions depend heavily onto  those metal bars.- Bland characters/NPCs. They talk nicely and dress nicely, but there's not much about them for you to discover on your own...

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wish list for a long time and am thrilled it's finally out. I have completed 4 in game days and am already in love. The map is big, the characters are fleshed out and the game play is wonderfully smooth. If you're a fan of the farming game genre, you will absolutely love Coral Island. I cannot wait to see what comes next in terms of updates and new features.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm almost 100 hours in and it feels like wasted time. I bought the game in early access and liked the game and decided to be patient and wait for the full release and it became clear the game should not have been released in this state.After spending hours gathering resources to automate my farm and in general play I experienced the following:*Machines like solar panels, auto chests etc. randomly stop working and I have to destroy them and place them again to fix the issue, so much for automation.*Random crashes*I need trash to create scrap, the ocean is clean and the only place to gather trash quickly is the caves, but the the caves are bugged and a world of weirdness happens when you enter the caves, making trash farming basically impossible.*Items with "TBD" as a description as in it's still a work in progress.*Areas not accessible because it has not been implemented yet although it's suppose to be the full release.It would be better if the developers at least made a simple post with some feedback, like "Hi everyone, we are aware of these issues and the ETA for a fix is 4 weeks" or whatever but I've seen no such feedback.It's the holiday season and the developers also need a break and I suspect fixes will most probably only begin in January 2024.Furthermore full mod support was one of the stretch goals reached in the Kickstarter which is currently not in the game, why not at least get that going so that modders can work on community patches to help fix some of these issues?In summary I'm very disappointed, the game showed great promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to give kudos to the developers of this game! They did an amazing job making a farming/life sim game and putting their own twist on it. I was hesitant to buy the game at first, I was a little burnt out on farming games and I thought it was going to be just another generic one. I finally broke down and got it and I am not disappointed! The game has all the usual elements that most farming sims have, but the developers gave it a relaxed/slow island life atmosphere with dynamic and unique townies. I have immersed myself in the world and characters for hours at a time without getting bored! I also enjoy the large influence that culture and community has on the game and gameplay elements. The only thing that I have found a tad frustrating is the lack of a manual save option, the only way to save currently in game is to sleep and end the day, however as long as your game does not hiccup and crash that is a minor inconvenience.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanna like the game, I just can't give it a positive review until the full game is finally released.I bought the game a while ago (Around the Christmas sale if I recall correctly) together with some friends seeing as it seemed interesting and very promising at first.Noticed that half of the stuff mentioned on their kickstarters wasn't in the game, which fair, it was still a WIP... yet shortly after it was noted and released as a 'Full game' with the roadmap changing once again, features being pushed back ect.Don't get me wrong, I get it stuff happened causing delays... yet people have been waiting for months and months for the full game, dealing with a unfinished story line for a 'Full released' game... which is just a big disappointment in my opinion.The Devs keep releasing Dev updates mentioned a bunch of random new stuff they're planning to add which is all fine and dandy... but maybe focus on all the main things first before throwing yourself on extra side stuff for the game and finish and add all the things that were promised and mentioned in the beginning.As of the 1.1 Update, For what I've seen in the patch, it seems promising yet again lots of bugs and still missing quite a lot of promised things to make it the 'Full game' as promised, and seeing as the Devs are still working on 1.2 and 1.3 months later, its just not fair to list it as a full released game.I'm very curious to the future of the game, I personally just can't fully deal with the fact that a team is working on this game taking many months on average for a single update that is still filled with a lot of bugs and even a lot of bugs from earlier updates, therefore I would personally not recommend the game to people who are looking for the full game... I would recommend saving your money and possibly waiting another 6 to 12 months for the other updates (Unfortunately not joking with those numbers...) I'll definitely change my review once they do decide to release the full promised game but untill then...Don't Recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but I can't recommend it in its current state. IT IS NOT a "full release", it's early access at best. NPCs daily dialogues are often missing, the Lake Temple completion rewards aren't fully implemented and the whole merfolks kingdom isn't very functional - after cleaning the ocean there is nothing left to do there, as there is no additional storyline with them, gaining friendship points or romancing still isn't available and there are only stubs of functional shops. There are also a lot of placeholder NPC models, like merfolk guards being used as shopkeepers. Being halfway through year 2, I feel like there's nothing more to see in the game.I'm also not digging many of the NPC heart events. I feel like observing their lives, not like actually building a relationship with them, especially because sometimes my character either isn't really saying anything or straight up is not present in the scene, which is crazy. Often only 8 and 10 heart events feel like relationship building ones, which is wayyyy too late.I'm disappointed and left feeling like I was scammed, as I was waiting for the game to be fully released to buy it with main storyline and mechanics finished. When I realised that the game is half empty, I was already way past the time that would allow me to return it, so I kept on playing, but I'm really not happy with how it looks. This game has a lot of potential, so I'll happily change my review to positive after seeing ACTUAL full release. I like the graphic, the idea of the merfolks kingdom and the Giants village, NPCs that are mostly well written, basic farming mechanics are decent, like in any other farming game. It's just that the game is not finished, not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun farming game that is still being made! The game isn't balanced but I hope that will be fixed in the future. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, I am having a relatively positive experience so far. However, there are a few niggling issues for me that break the experience. Understandably it is an EA game. Bugs/Issues:- There are some characters that seem glitched or broken, Their thumbnails don't show up on the map properly. They also seem to get stuck in their rooms for the whole day- The other major thing I have an issue with is the standard of the writing and grammar. It's BAD. The NPC lines are unnatural and stunted, the grammar is pretty abysmal, and there are spelling mistakes everywhere. I think the writing needs to shape up majorly for the final release.- Fishing takes up too many in-game minutes- Character skits don't seem to lead anywhere- Fish and bugs in the museum float off the map- There needs to be festival specific dialogue for each character.- Furniture is SUPER bugged. A lot of the crafting restrictions don't make a lot of sense, EG, you can't place chests indoors, paintings don't work, etc.- I have bought blueprints of buildings that just vanished from my inventory. - There's a lot on in-game processes that aren't explained properly. EG: Wanted to buy a silo, but I didn't realise I needed to also get a mill in order to mill fiber into hay (ok, what even)? Firstly, that makes zero-to-no sense. How the hell does one even mill hay??- The goddess offering storyline is also not explained well at all. It's basically the same as Stardew Valley's community center offering spiel, but you're not exactly pointed out to where you make offerings. You have to figure out a lot of ♥♥♥♥ on your own in this game- There needs to be a magnifying glass tool in order to check what crops are what.This is for the devs to look into for the most part.  I would still recommend checking out the game if you're into the whole Stardew Valley thing, like I am.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: So far, and as of 1.1, I recommend this game.Firstly, I think the graphics are awesome, it speaks for itself. The gameplay itself is what I (and what I think other people looking for a cozy farm/stardew valley type game) look for in this genre. It adds its own unique approach to the normal gameplay mechanics you'd find in this genre of games!Speaking of Stardew Valley, I especially recommend this game if you like Stardew Valley, coming from a hardcore lover of it. They're very similar but different in the best ways.I also love the ability to customize how short or long your days are, whether you like your days to be shorter or longer this game is definitely for you.As for what I don't like about coral island, which there isnt much, I'm not a big fan of the mines having finished them. More specifically, the monsters inside of the mines. I don't expect or want the difficulty to be hard inside of the mines when it comes to monsters, but... just feels way too easy. The fighting is very simple with not needing to do very much avoiding, and it'd be basically impossible for you to die without trying to do so on purpose. Most of the time, I'm able to just stand there and take the hits as I kill the monster and it barely effects anything. I feel like the fighting and/or the monsters in this game could be a little bit more interesting. 10/10 will be continuing my playthrough, potentially multiple times over :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm nearing the end of the game after 71hrs or so. It's very good. It's very Stardew Valley influenced but with some great additions that are beginning to make it feel completely unique. 4/5 stars. The S.V. influence comes through in e.g. the Goddess offerings standing in for the Community Centre bundles; the centrality of collecting items (fossils, gems etc) for the museum; even down to smaller things like pigs collecting truffles. However, Coral Island really does take the Stardew formula in a new direction with its eco plot; with many more characters to romance and befriend (28 romanceables including one NB individual is brilliant!); and with life underwater. I just hope it continues to grow in the same exciting way that Stardew continues to do. It's still in an early version, and I hope there is much more to come. The game is already very engaging, but I want to see more that helps it distinguish and improve itself. Playing Stardew, you are always struck by the sheer quantity of love and intelligence that has gone into shaping the game: I'd love to see C.I. follow suit, whilst also continuing to distinguish itself. Where Stardew just really has the Community Centre plot followed by Ginger Island (excl. new update stuff), Coral Island has the Goddess Offerings AND the underwater sea-coral repairs with the giants and the mines as an early-to-mid-game subplot. The underwater plotline can be a bit repetitive (tool upgrades arrive in tandem with the 'toughness' of coral you have to cut down, so it feels a bit thankless: and there is a lot of coral to cut down!) but as the game develops I'm sure it will be fleshed out. Changes have already been made to help freshen it up (e.g. the turtles being removed). One of my favourite elements is the massive dating pool. I already want to replay to get to know all the other bachelors; I don't yet know if a divorce mechanic has been implemented or (thinking outside the box) if a polyamory mechanic could yet be implemented. The game has lots of directions it could go in. The game has a few early-version issues: spelling mistakes, your character getting stuck and having to jump to the next day (for some reason with a stamina penalty despite this not being the player's fault!) Some elements are not yet implemented like book collecting for the library; or that the panda area having no function once unlocked as of yet. This has no bearing on the rating I would like to give the game. Despite being an eco-plotted game (and presumably therefore anti-capitalist), things are held behind a surprising amount of money (bag upgrades for example), one particularly mad element of which is the gatekeeping of the horse. Your character moves very slowly around the world. So 15k coins to build the stable and then 15k to buy the horse is a bit insane. This perhaps falls into the same trap as Stardew: that the devs want you to only be able to walk around at the character's rather slow 'sprint' to create a 'relaxed' vibe that doesn't really work because of how driven and engaging the game really is. The movement slowness becomes stressful. It is a small way in which the game sometimes lacks positive impetus. Money is harder to come by in C.I. than in Stardew but it feels like C.I. has more of a reliance on money, enforced by higher prices for crops/trees/animals etc. It is strange for an eco game to be so unabashedly money-fuelled. Or perhaps another way to think about this is that *A LOT* of the game mechanics that allow you to make more money are unlocked only late-game. The same can be said of Stardew, but it feels more pronounced here. The beginning is tricky (trickier even than traditional Harvest Moon games of old). This can make the game quite thankless at first. It can become stressful, scraping together your first 10k coins or so, to feel that there are five or six things you really need to do ASAP, but you can't. QUICK POINTS: Fishing is brill (easier than S.V.'s sometimes nightmarish minigame); bug catching (for more difficult bugs) a nightmare before you unlock traps. Please expand the underwater characters. Festivals are a highlight. I hope they keep thinking imaginatively with them! The ritual trees that the Goddess offerings heal currently do nothing- it would be nice for them to gain some function. Ling's Lab's farming upgrades are fantastic and really are the main way the game gains momentum- thank you. The sapling/seedling divide is weird and a bit irritating. It feels like an arbitrary innovation to distinguish the game from others in the cozy farming genre.Overall though this is still a solid 4/5 game at the moment, for where it is at in development. If development more or less stops at finishing the most obvious issues and the game substantively now stays the same, then that rating will slip backwards as the game will pale in comparison to Stardew. If they continue to move forwards and expand it, with love and imagination, that will hopefully make Coral Island a wonderful and unique 5/5 playing experience for those who love this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I have come back to this game three different times and tried to pick it back up. Every time I get so frustrated and disappointed by the bugs and incomplete game play. I first played this game back in October 2022. There were some pretty big bugs that made the game not enjoyable in my opinion, so I have waited and played it months later. Now in February 2023, the exact same bugs are there unchanged. I reported the bugs to devs as suggested, and nothing. Biggest gripe is that the salon is bugged. When I try to change my facial features (and pay for it too!) it doesn't register, and my character just stays with the "default" face no matter what. Several months into release and they can't even add something as simple as lip color. Animals and NPCs glitch around and freeze. This game isn't even incomplete, it's literally half finished. $25 for this game in the state that it's in is a slap in the face. I have never paid so much for an early access game and yet encountered so many bugs and unplayable features. So so so disappointing because this game could be so much fun. I'm disappointed the devs haven't been able to overcome some of these really important issues and make fixes to improve the game and make it actually worth the price. I do not recommend this game at this time. Check back in several months and see if there's improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: You can modify the speed that time passes in the game. I can finally do everything in a day that I actually need to get done. edit: after sinking another 60 or so hours into this and getting at least all the way through the seasons, i would definitely still recommend this. the fishing minigame isn't impossible, the improvement of your gear isn't super tedious (and after gold, not even so necessary, tbh), and the biggest issue i have is the occasional stuttering. there was a resource that was pretty scarce to get, which was aggravating, but then i unlocked an area that had a great deal of it, so now its just refinement of my farm and all that. i do hope that there will be increases in size for coop/barn (though I cant imagine why not when you have to purchase two llamas when you get the one), but of course the game is unfinished so I'm sure there will be lots of changes still. (perhaps one to deepen the caverns as well, certainly some more fleshing out the mermaids is expected as they never have anything to say lol) most of my time in game, besides tending to my ludicrous amounts of artisan products, is to gather up all the missing museum items still out there. there are a LOT of different kinds of fish and they are very seasonal (and there are a lot more locations to fish than you might realize!) but still, as someone who played stardew as a very fishing heavy game, i dont mind spending the time fishing at sea. though i do adjust the time to go a little faster, even 50% gametime fishing is a little slow for me.as for story and quests and bugs and all that, well. i've played just about every harvesting sim game that has come out since harvest moon for the SNES. i know how the general story goes and can accomplish it rather well. yes, coral island has a interesting cast of unique characters, but the story is about the same as you'd expect. from what i can tell, it's not fully finished and is lacking in some rewards for finished shrines and whatnot, but honestly, the finishing of the shrine itself is enough for me. there are some bugs with the dialogue, but honestly, it could be worse. maybe i'm much more lax in my demands for a game, maybe i skip about every other cut scene because the story specifics dont honestly matter that much to me, or maybe they put this out a little more unpolished than the should have. all things considered, did i get my money's worth? yeah. i've got 100 hrs in this thing and paid what, 25$? so at almost 25cents an hour, i got my money's worth in time spent having fun.will you? god only knows. but I do know that i stretched that time out as long as i could per day. i think they're like 45 minutes long at 50% speed. that's bonkers. i can play one week in game for a whole afternoon. man, i just love that mechanic so much.
