_childDocuments_.review: I know this is Early access but this feels too early to even justify early access release. It takes place in a tropical setting unlike Stardew Valley but in reality, it just feels like it is taking place in a tropical resort in the middle of America. Nothing feels tropical beneath the surface of palm trees and beaches, the crops you grow are not tropical crops, the seasons are temperate with a snowy winter which makes no sense for a tropical climate. Overall, it feels like they tried to create a setting to separate it from Stardew Valley but the fact that they couldn't get even the basics correct shows that they put very little effort into research and just copied Stardew Valley at a surface level while in some cases, making the features fundamentally less enjoyable. I will return in a year to see if the game as improved and I am willing to change my review if that is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: Really excited to see this game in its final form! If you love Stardew Valley, then you will love Coral Island. The beats of the game are similar,: you play as a character starting a farm in a new community that is fighting to restore itself to its former glory while battling corporate greed. However, it doesn't feel like a stale imitation or the same game with a new skin. It adds its own unique flair and mechanisms (the fishing mechanism in this game is much better imo and the diving part is cool). I also enjoy the art style and the level of personalization of the player character (super cool to have a wider range of body types and not be stuck in a binary gender system). Since this is an early release, I can tell there are unfinished or unrefined aspects of the game, but it's still fun to play and has plenty of content to satisfy you for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: At 22 hours, I would recommend this but will note some minor detractors.I love the quality of life improvements Coral Island has added to the formula revised by Stardew Valley, who revised the gameplay of its predecessors such as Rune Factory and Harvest Moon. Earlier teleports and simple sprinkler automation at the start allows more flexibility in the day. The teleports do make the stable and horse mostly useless however. By the time I can afford the stable and horse, I have teleports everywhere. This may just be because I focused more on gifting people and completing quests rather than raw money generation early on.The ability to track people on the island using my map is also really nice. I know everyone in Stardew had schedules too, but not having to rely on a browser being open while I play is great.I really enjoy the masteries system but I do wish it was a little more than what it was. I can't describe this feeling as it is just a slight vague feeling of needing something more.I also really wish the ingame compendium allowed me to check the altar needs like it allows me to check everything else. I also wish I could sort the fish and bug lists by areas, day/night, etc. There is absolutely no rush for anything. Festivals come and go, sure, but I choose if I even care about timelines or events. Coral Island has embraced the idea of "When you feel like it, if you ever do" and I love it. It's a very fluffy, fun game and I'd recommend it anytime but with the small warning down below.The people of Coral Island are, for the most part, great with a wide variety of personalities and identities. You do have your Hailey stand in if you are familiar with Stardew Valley, etc. This game is very body positive and sexual orientation forward facing which is great. Some of the characters have similar personalities but that doesn't really make or break a game.The handy tracker allows you to see discovered likes and loves, dislikes and hates, their outfits, and where they are (hitting tab when you are inspecting their profile).To put it bluntly, it doesn't feel that heart events effect the NPCs. You will get comments from NPCs on things you complete, but helping someone in their heart event and becoming good friends will not improve how they treat you when you talk to them on the streets.No matter how buddy I get with Leah, she will tell me to screw off because I dress bad, smell bad, maybe both, or maybe it's the shark costume I'm wearing, I'm not sure.I don't need every heart event to have world changing repercussions. Eva's story is very simple and sweet and I'm all for it. I don't mind if the heart events are just simple slice of life; not everyone needs a world changing moment. What I want is if a heart event clearly indicates its a huge moment for the character, then the way they interact should reflect that. If the characters around town would also comment on me getting awfully close to someone, that'd be neat too.I do wish the heart events that are suppose to be profound...were more so. Or that if you are escalating emotions with a dateable, it really should mirror that tension. I do believe the devs stated that the release version has a bug where a good portion of the NPC dialogue isn't being utilized, but I'm not 100% on that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has rich story and a diverse set of characters- varying by age, ethnicity, disability, and sexuality. This is very exciting to see, as it really shows that the developers are creating a game with the care and compassion that centres the player experience. I specifically enjoyed that they created more gender-nonconforming player models and honourifics (ex. mr, ms, mx). The dateable characters are charming, and I like that they have different gifting preferences. I wish it were easier to figure out these preferences, but it seems like that is something that is slowly revealed the more the player interacts with them. I really love the visual elements of this game and the wide array of skills and activities you can learn to do! This game is very reminiscent of Stardew Valley, but I think the style and story-line helps it stand out significantly. For a pre-release version of this game, I am insanely impressed. I am very much looking forward to seeing what the developers do with this game. I have played now for 20 hours in the past three days and I am not even close to discovering everything this game has to offer. I also really appreciate that you can adjust the time speed of the game to 50% of the usual speed. As someone who enjoys a more casual gaming experience, that makes it much more enjoyable. Highly, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is a game I was looking forward to for a long time, being introduced to it several years ago when it was in early development. I wanted to play the game when it was fully out of early access, so I waited to get it until this summer, thinking it should be finished as it was no longer early access. In the beginning, I loved the game. The art style is super pretty and charming, the characters are endearing, and there are plenty of things to do. However, there are some major issues that really weigh the game down: - The progression is painstakingly slow. This includes the main story progression, getting higher relationships with characters and getting more money to upgrade buildings and get more crops and other relevant stuff. I also found that there is a surprising lack of quests in the game. In other farming games I have played, especially during the first year, there are so many main and side quests and so many new things to do every day that feels like it has a purpose. In Coral Island, the main quest is so slow to progress that there is a really huge lack of purpose and rewards. The main quest kinda depends on your town ranking which again just takes an absurd amount of time to get higher. It took me almost 3 whole seasons to get to town rank E (one higher than the lowest one). The character progression system is similar, and even giving two gifts per week and hanging out every week does not give you another heart until it has been at least several weeks of in-game time. It makes it feel grindy and takes away from the overall enjoyment.UPDATE: this seems to have been slightly tweaked in the latest update and I am now able to get more hearts with the islanders quicker. Additionally, it is so hard to get a decent amount of money even if you sell a bunch of crops, fruit, and foraged items every day. This means that upgrading buildings, decorating your house, getting new clothing, buying more crops and all the other things you need money for becomes such a grind that it takes away from the enjoyment of actually playing because the rewards are few and far between. - The performance of the game is not great. The lagging and stuttering, especially when diving or mining, or when there is a lot on the screen is somewhat constant and makes me think that in later gameplay, getting the farm bigger would be a certain way to crash the game. The game has crashed on me about 4 or 5 times already and I haven't even progressed that far. UPDATE: the game developers seem to be very active on improving the game, and they have just released new updates, so it's a great sign in terms of stability improvement for the game.- You can only save your game when the day ends. This means that you're constantly in danger of losing your progress as the game is still quite unstable and crashes sometimes. I think this is ridiculous, as it should be somewhat simple to add a feature to save the game when you want or even auto-saving every 10 minutes or so.- The cutscenes/events feel a bit lackluster. There is no interactivity during an event with another character and they never really mention it again. Pair this with the fact that the character relationship improvement system is super slow, and you have a pretty bad formula of an extremely grindy system. Having said that, there are of course many positives in the game which is why I ultimately decided to recommend it as the price is not that high. The game has a lot of charm, and the character portraits, the way they change each season and the fact that the game is very chill and relaxing to play are all positive. There is also a bunch of things to do and the merfolk kingdom is super cool and quite novel in this genre. The grinding nature of the game of course means that the rewards are a bit scarce and it does feel very grindy, so for players wanting a farming sim that feels rewarding and with fast progression, this game might not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game has both surpassed and failed to reach my expectations in surprising ways. The amount of characters, the details in the environment, and the attention to detail is wonderful. However, I think the story needs work. It's my understanding that it hasn't been completely finished, or if it has it was just recently and after full release. The heart events so far are... shallow. Where is the depth of character? Looking at each person and feeling their personality, everyone is so different and special, but when the interactions come it's boring. You can talk to people three times a day, but they still don't say anything substantial. One thing that irks me like nothing else is your character's idle movements in the salon/customization screen. When they stretch their torso looks like a noodle. Where are their ribs??? Are they made of rubber????This game has amazing potential, but it's like they stopped just short of creating a masterpiece. Wait for future updates before playing or buy it with a discount.

I have seen reports of the same instance since October 2021 in their discussions and more complaints, still, from players this week alone.Go play Palia or some other similar game unless this goes substantially on sale because neat characters or not, losing progress every. single. day is not worth it when devs are not addressing the issue.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR Coral Island is a solid game. I’ve seen A LOT of discussion about bugs within the game and the game crashing. I’ve been playing early access for quite some time and perhaps I’ve just been lucky but that has not been my experience. However, they are still actively adding to the game so its still a work in progress. ArtThe art style is wonderful. It is cozy and inviting but it isn’t overwhelming. Sometimes the more magical elements in these type of games can be a bit overpowering but Coral Island has grounded the magic in a simple and natural style (as opposed to the acid trips you’d get on occasion in Stardew).Character Design With the creation of NPCs the Devs strove for diversity. This is one of the few games I have seen body inclusivity (from different sizes, scars to visible stretch marks) on romanceable characters. NPCs are diverse in ethnicity as well as gender identity. Town Events There are town events, two per season, that have mini games included. The mini games are all fun and the dialogue is interesting during these events. I will say though that controllers are recommended during these mini games. Diving This is more than your standard farming sim. Most games of this genre have foraging, farming, mining and fishing. This game has a unique area where you explore the ocean world and help clean up the coral sites. It sets it apart from other games with this new area but this section is intrinsically linked to the overarching plot. FishingAs a disclaimer, I liked Stardew fishing. If you don’t like that mechanic, you may not like this fishing mechanic. The bar is horizontal and the fish type can change the pattern the fish in the water moves (vertically, horizontally, star or diagonal), the fishes speed and the rest period between reels. It’s a unique take on the Stardew-style mechanic. Tool and Skill Progression There is a skill tree which is clearly laid out. There’s no FOMO for speccing down one path like in Stardew. It’s also not overly onerous to upgrade tools - your standard 5 bar requirement. You can also upgrade your farm generally through the kelp elixir upgrades which is a unique feature.  Ranching & FarmingThere’s a wide variety of animals and they’re cute. The tools are straightforward and not complicated to use. There’s a wide variety of crops and you can get horse later on (though its value is less given the fast travel options - yes there’s fast travel). Unique Plot Lines that IntertwineI won’t say much to avoid spoilers but you have several intertwining storylines here:1. Small Island Town vs Big Oil Corporation2. Mythical Island Creatures 3. Merpeople What I like about this is that it has a feeling that your decisions actually matter. One issue with Stardew is that the tangible impact of your actions don't seem that big. Mining Area The mines are a bit bland comparatively. The area generation is all pretty similar and while there are doorways on levels, they lead to no where. That being said, it’s a farming sim first and mining is a difficult skill to make enjoyable. Combat & MonstersIt’s lacking but I’ve seen some improvement as the game has developed. I’ll reserve my judgment to see how it improves. Weather There’s not much variety and rainy days seem few and far between. Might’ve just been my experience though. There is an accessibility tab where you are able to change a number of things, including font (dyslexic font is available), and there are colorblind options. The game is playable with a controller or mouse & keyboard (with key bindings customizable). There is no manual save, it’s tied to the ending of the day but you can adjust the day length (15-20mins to 30-40mins). There is no inventory with sale prices. It’s difficult to plan or organize without an aid telling you the profit of item. Likewise, I haven’t found a quick reference for the bundles.  Overall, the game has work to do. BUT I think that it is a very solid entry into the game genre and is going to stand out from many of the other farming sims due to the interesting romancable characters, unique design and style choices and the unique underwater area and storyline. Would recommend but just know it is still getting worked on. My view though is that you can't fault the Devs for that, Stardew just rolled out an update as well many years after release - that Coral Island devs are so active and looking to continuously improve is a good thing, not a bad thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a 'neutral' option, because that's more in line with what I wish to give it.This is a phenomenal game, make no mistake about it, but for me it fell short in many areas. If you like Stardew Valley through and through, this game essentially is a 3D version of that. First off, the cons that make me go from resounding "YES!" on recommendation to "Neutral/For the right person."- You only save when you sleep, but this is unfortunately common with this type of game.- Your tools take up to multiple game days to be upgraded, artificially padding playtime.- Shops are closed all at random times, so you have to constantly check a menu or keep a list somewhere. Some things are closed on Mondays and Fridays, while others are closed on (a) weekend day(s), etc. They also all have different hours of operation.- NPCs are all over the place, all the time. Thankfully you can track them, but it's a lot of running around.- Most of the time I feel like I'm playing a silent game. There are sound effects, and some music is nice (especially the ocean music), but no voices, no voice sounds even like sims or something, anything... It's just glub glub glub when you put items into storage, and random zings and sounds related to whatever you're doing. It feels lifeless to me personally because of this, but I'm not one for imagination play and want my world to feel alive. This feels like playing a silent movie from decades upon decades ago.- The early or mid game play has way too much on the to do list, particularly for ranching. I loathe having to get up and separately feed, milk, sheer, collect from several animals. Even one or two is a task too much when I want to just wake up and go on out to whatever task I have set in mind to do for the day.- The fishing minigame is awful, requiring rapid clicks which will be torturous if you have arthritis or any other physical limitations there. I imagine with a controller you'd be smashing a button a hundred times instead.- Your farm is static, being one giant plot that's exactly the same, just like in SDV, except it's just the one. No other options.- You will encounter random cutscenes when travelling around, whether you teleport into one or just walk your way up a path into one, typically of daily conversations between NPCs or other innocuous interactions. This could be a plus for some, but as they were little more than small talk interactions and not story beats mostly, and as they'd happen when I'm otherwise focused on XYZ task without warning, sometimes they were mildly annoying.- If you find yourself/your character stuck anywhere, be prepared to lose an entire day and spawn at your house the next day to get unstuck help, or exit the game and restart your entire day. Good luck if this happens at the end of a day when you've done quite a lot (has happened to me 2-3 times).These are just off the top of my head fresh out of my 50th hour total of play. Now for the positives.+ You can teleport all over the place.+ You can semi-spam spacebar to move quickly early game.+ There's a lot of gameplay. I have my day set to the longest possible, and at 50 hours in I've probably not gotten very far. It's early Fall in game for me. Love the lengthy storyline.+ You can adopt a pet from a long list of cuties! I chose a kitty, of course.+ Sprinklers arrive early and often, if you spend enough time diving to get the resources to make them.+ You can turn off combat such that enemies don't attack you until you attack them, allowing safe mining and the ability to farm/grind your combat later at your leisure or for whatever you need as drops from enemies.+ The giants are amazing, adorable, and I love the way they integrate not only into the storyline so far but into the gameplay as well.Again, just off the top of my head right now.I just exited the game after almost getting back into it whenever I decided to go to buy a horse so I could get around easier, only to find out it's the one day of the week they're closed. It may sound small, but small frustrations add up, and honestly I don't know if I'll be able to finish the game, since it feels like work, not play, and I'm not connecting with the storyline because everyone's a silent face. If you have imagination I lack, if you like coming up with your own voices for characters, if you don't care about that at all, and if you love time management and micromanagement of various things and quests and tasks constantly to rush around doing, you'll love Coral Island. It's a love letter to SDV fans with some improvements, but not many, staying true to the gameplay style and pacing of SDV in my opinion, yet backsliding in other areas (fishing, for example).Fantastic game foiled (for me) by several small nuisances. I could overlook the lack of voices if not for the rest of it. The biggest things that will keep me from finishing this game are the shop times and feelings of too many chores to do. It's overwhelming instead of cozy, for me personally. However, it's still a game overall well made and crafted with love and care, clearly. Just not for me. Maybe for you? You decide.

_childDocuments_.review: Can you make this game less grindy. I wanted to escape reality with this game but now I feel like I'm working my regular 9-5 job again.  There's never enough resources to do ANYTHING. When you try to focus on the mining you then lack sea resources to craft things, sometimes the recipes require both ores and sea resources. And each activity takes up a whole ♥♥♥♥♥ day. Farming, mining, trash collecting. Then go to sleep. Everything is so expensive while the resources are so rare. I'm on the 35 level mine rn and I barely have enough bronze ores to use and everything requires them. I didn't feel like this at all when I play Stardew Valley or the Harvest Moon franchise. I'm pretty sure they don't even know what their own goals are.1/ Museum donation rewards are jack sh*t:I donate all the rare items I could find which if I chose to sell instead I would have got at least 2k. But then again, I choose donation. 60 items so far and all the rewards are bs. You got 5 bronze ores for 5 items.  You got ONE SINGLE sprinkler for another 5. Then sometimes you got 8 regular potato crops. See this game is so realistic for this. It depicts capitalism so well. It's like you work overtime up to 50 hours a week and got a bonus of 75 cents. _childDocuments_.review: This game has great bones, it's beautiful AF, the style is amazing, the diving skill is fantastic looking and its breath of fresh air to have a farming sim game that is on an island. I enjoy this game a lot and it will be better once it's out of EA. For now, I cannot give this game a thumbs up as it is right now for a few reasons. Gold ore: You only have access to two mines and they only carry bronze and silver ore respectfully. You have the option to upgrade your tools to gold tier but the only way to get gold ore is to buy it from the blacksmith. It's 800 coral bucks or whatever and you need 5 ores to make a bar, and it takes five metal bars to upgrade a tool, not including the coral bucks cost as well. If I wanted to update my pickaxe, with how the game is now, it's going to cost me 30,000! Hnn!Bait: You unlock the ability to craft bait but there's no bait to be crafted, like...okay, I guess, but why add it if it's not implemented?You can buy a calendar to put in your home but you can't really use it, or if you can use it, it'll have everyone's birthday on it, regardless of what season it is, maybe that's a bug that I am dealing with personally, or it might be a known issue, but like I said, why put the item in EA if it can't be used properly. There are some things like assets in the mines that look like they were just tossed in as filler space and are to be drawn or what have you at a later date, okay I guess, these are the breaks, I suppose. It's just the little things that add up but my biggest gripe is the gold ore, you have like five tools to update, that is expensive and even with all the stamina you gain with each level up, its going to take you a bit to get all that money together. I get it, 100 percent, this is an EA game but like...shhhhhhhiiiiii- some things got overlooked that should not have been over looked.Edit: FFS, many of us understand the concept of an Early Access game, we understand that things are not finish in this game, but as one reviewer put it nicely; everything in the game is not finished, every part of the game is missing something. I'll say what someone once said about a game: It's ocean wide but deep as a puddle. This game just got patch/hotfix and the hotfixes didn't address some of the glaring bugs that people are pointing out oh...but the cleanup festival is now bigger, even though you can't play all of the events there, hurray! As the dev team said, this game is playable up through year one, and that statement is shakey AF. Is the game pretty? Yes it is. Is the game good: At the place it's at now, it's just a generic farming sim with diving and you getting dunked on by a T-Posing Store clerk. Is this game worth it's price now? Absolutely not, wish I hadn't sunk all those hours in it, I would ask for my money back. I paid 25 bucks for My Time at Sandrock and Dinkum and they earned that price, Coral Island does not. And don't go on the steam discussion page with constructive critctism , you'll just get people who will tell you it's an Early Access game, what do you expect? I expect the lines for a character to be done in a main quest that is given to me and for BAIT TO BE USABLE SINCE THE GAME TELLS ME IT IS USABLE! I don't expect a polished gem at EA but I expect better than this. But...I get to woo over 25 characters, neat, wow...but also, I still can't use the calendar in my house! Wait until it's done so that you can enjoy Coral Island: Stardew Valley 2: Electric Boogaloo.

_childDocuments_.review: A graphically-superior, yet shallow-er clone of Stardew Valley. Over the past two months, I have played four different farming sims. It all started with Disney's Dreamlight Valley, which then revived my interest in Stardew Valley (which I haven't played since 2019) and I played that game for a while. Then, Wylde Flowers came out and I absolutely fell in love with that game! Lastly, I played Coral Island — it is the weakest of the four by far.The main issue with Coral Island is its reluctance to be its own thing. All of the other games I mentioned do heavily borrow ideas from Stardew Valley, but manage to add something original to the formula, giving it a unique spin. Coral Island, on the other hand, is just a graphically-updated version of Stardew Valley and feels more like a themed mod of it (like, hey, here's Stardew Valley but in Southeast Asia!). It copypastes many of the same things that I find annoying about SV (like the fact that you can only save the game by sleeping, for instance). Instead of trying to improve on the formula Stardew Valley has established, Coral Island just copies its homework without trying to fix any of its problems or use any creativity beyond the different geographical setting.Also, the most recent update to the game wiped out my save file (and I'm not the only one who encountered that issue). I've never had this happen to me before despite playing many different early access titles, so this, to me, showcases that the developers bit off more than the can chew and released their game to the public way too early, especially considering how limited the game is at its current state.

As a farming sim lover, stardew valley has always been the standard to which i compare games within that same genre, and coral island is the best I have ever seen since stardew. it is multidimensional, builds off the best parts of these kinds of games and expands in unique, interesting ways. I have nearly 100 hours in the game and I have so much more gameplay left to go - and the game isnt even completed!! I have always felt like there was something fun to do in the game, it is customizable enough that you can play to focus on the parts that you like, and the different stories unfolding in the game are fun and entertaining! I do wish that the "heart events" of characters were more focused on your players interaction with the NPCs, as they arent always,  and I feel that some of the friends and romancable characters could have more depth to them, but there are also a wide variety of NPCs of all sorts to focus on if you dislike aspects of some of the others (not everyone can be likeable, right?) Overall, I could not say enough positive things about this game and I have been thoroughly enjoying it for months, and I will be continuing to enjoy it for many more especially as the game continues to develop. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Devs continue to update the game and make good on their promises. Multiplayer just went into closed beta and will go to open beta later this month so I still highly recommend this game.If you enjoy farm life sim games then you don't want to miss out on this one and if you've never played one before then this is a great game to give the genre a try. This game combines many elements from previous games in the genre resulting in full days with always plenty to do and of course that trademark feeling of wanting to do "just one more thing" before you end your play session.There have been lots of reports of game breaking bugs but I haven't experienced anything game breaking and as of this writing I am beginning year two in the game. If you're on the fence due to bad reviews you've read about bugs, unfinished features, and rushed release issues then at least put this one on your wishlist so you don't forget about it and wait to see if the devs can get it polished up some more.I'm very happy with the game and I've slowed time down to 50% using the in-game option and it feels perfect for being able to do some of everything each day without missing shop open times and getting some NPC conversations done in addition to the farming and ranching tasks and mine delving and ocean diving.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing Animal Crossing, My Time At Portia, My Time At Sandrock, even the Sims games. You will love Coral Island. Remember it is Early Access which means there is still a lot to be done but it has been running great on my PC for over 100 hours now! I'm still in Fall season and haven't even finished a full year yet so make sure you turn the speed down for the game if you don't want it to go by really fast. I'm just excited for them to add more content! The diving reminds me of Subnautica a little bit which is fun! I haven't even started decorating yet and that's my favorite part of this type of game! This is just the beginning! This game is amazing and you will definitely enjoy it! I can't wait to see how many hours I have in it later!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for approximately one week and have thoroughly enjoyed it so far.  The stories for each character are rich.  The colors and graphics are very well done, for the most part.I've been gaming for many years and the one thing I can say about ANY game that I really get immersed in, are the DETAILS.  Any game that I've enjoyed over time, the devs have paid attention to the details, the minutiae that really suck you in.  There are a few issues with Coral Island.     - All of the animal and character models are fantastic...except for the cows.  Where everything else appears to have a        "cartoonish realism",  the cows are ridiculous.  They're like a newspaper comic version of a cow.     - The walking animation needs work.  Some of the characters walk like they have soiled themselves.  Where you would         expect a more feminine walk on some characters, you get something that resembles an ambulating version of the         Elaine dance from Seinfeld.     - When a character (including the player) or animal changes direction, it snaps to the other direction.  There should         be motion involved in the change of direction, not just...a change of direction.This is what I've noticed so far in my short time playing.  I, obviously, really like this game as I've spent time writing this review and gave it a positive mark.One last thing I will say, is that another attribute to some of the greatest games I've played, is when the devs take the time to listen to the players and make reasonable adjustments accordingly.  Hopefully, Stairway Games will look at some of these reviews and figure out what can be fixed in an update, as I see that I'm not the sole voice of issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for a good chunk of time, I can say I recommend this game, but I also can’t 100% recommend playing right away. If you enjoyed old school Harvest Moon games, or Stardew Vally, Coral Island will definitely be a game for you. It has some similar mechanics and intuitive gameplay that will have you coming back for more, while also adding new ideas and aspects that add a new dynamic to the genre. It also has a unique array of characters that all have their own personality, not to mention there are a lot of Npcs to befriend. I want to play more Coral Island so bad.  HOWEVER, atm this is a very early access game, there are a lot unpolished and unfinished aspects in this game. A good chunk of events, textures, and features are not yet implemented in game. There are also quite a few bugs that need fixing and support features that should to be added as well. If you want to get a taste of what the developers are aiming for, and treat the game as a demo currently, then 100% get it and play right now. Get a feel for the potential that this game offers. If you enjoy the life/farm sim classics I’d also recommend this game, but I’d recommend waiting till an update or two come out. If you have no patience for bugs and not having all the features right now, I cannot recommend this game as it is. At the end of the day, the potential for an outstanding game is definitely there with Coral Island. Either wishlist and wait, or buy it and treat it as a demo right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: It’s what you want when you get a farming game. _childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: solid 8/10 so farI haven't finished the game yet, and I'm nowhere near the end. Nevertheless, if you like Stardew Valley, you'll probably enjoy this one too. You have your farm, cave, and townsfolk that you can romance. The story is similar as well: there's an evil corporate lady who wants to introduce fracking into this cute town, which has lost a lot of value due to environmental pollution. Naturally, it's our job to make this town great again and clean up the pollution to make it a cute, livable place.The biggest difference from Stardew Valley is that we'll also go below the sea with a diving suit. It's nothing too fancy though and just another area to explore as of my progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has potential to be good. The biggest issue I have is that it is almost exactly Stardew Valley. The mechanics are similar, the things you can do are basically the same, the story is similar. The good things about this game are the art style, especially the 2D aspects and the diversity in the characters. Things it has in common with SV: the farm looks almost identical and the farming is the same, giving offerings to mystical creatures to save the area, a big bad corporation swooping in to take over, the friendship/relationship mechanics, the mines, literally the spring crops are the same, festivals including having one with a big stew that everyone puts stuff into to make it good.Things that are different: The characters are more diverse appearance and identity wise, however I don't get an immediate sense of any of their personalities. You can scuba dive with a little robot! That's fun! The art is way different, with a blend of 2D for the conversation pop-ups, and 3D, which I think is cool. I know this is in Early Access, however I think the core of the game is so obviously identical to SV that it's not worth it to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

You can do as much or as little as you want. The characters are fun and each have their own story. I am so excited to see where this game goes. The roadmap is exciting for the improvements!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

I'm happy there is a battle element in the mine and I really like the diving aspect...even though that damn turtle is in my way and I haven't grown the right crop lvl to get his ass to move. _childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you like animal crossing, little wood, or stardew valley this is a great choice for you. Pros:Artwork & Character design - you can see they put extra thought into including people of all kinds (my only gripe is I wish there were more options for dark mysterious types to romance)Combat - Combat is fun and simple swinging your weapon is satisfying with the movementLots to do - At first it seemed a little overwhelming but you can really pick and choose what you want to accomplishLevel System - The more you do the more you level that particular treeMusic - Nice and relaxingStory - Main story seems pretty basic but with so much to explore and so many characters to meet it doesn't need to be too complicatedCons:(This game is in Alpha so im sure many of these will change)- Minor bugs that can sometimes break immersion- A bit confusing at first, no clear tutorial on where to find things such as crafting menus ect.- The days feel a little too quick, (Time flows a bit too quickly)- Storage systems work nicely for inserting items into chest but taking out into your inventory can be a bit awkward- The main antagonist of the story is literally named Karen, like I get it but does it have to be so literal? You can see this trope throughout the story most of the time its funny but for some reason this just kinda made me roll my eyes a bit.Overall really great relaxing game! You can definitely get lost in this one for hours at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable. Great farming sim, it has a variety of plants and recipes to cook with them, lots of fish and bugs to catch. Definitely recommend.(I have over 200 hours, I've been playing since alpha.)
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: for the people complaining about it being like stardew:news flash:people love stardew because it is so many of them and the best parts combined. with modding abilities.others are complaining about well.. early access hiccups. wait until full release then. no ones forcing you to play right now. This game constantly shows you how much love the devs put into it. you see the characters do so many various animations, they hang out together, have conversations, the families can be seen playing at various areas of the games maps such as the volleyball court.everyone has personal backstories and are unique. A fan favorite seems to be suki, who has stretch marks and is dealing with leaving kids father and self improvement.theres someone for everyone.this game has the best of the farm sim game genre in it, with extras such as animal crossing activities liek bug catching and diving.NO MATTER how you want to play, it is viable. wanna farm? farmwanna catch bugs nonstop? catch bugs.wanna only fish? fish.wanna gather and mine only? do that.you can easily make money off all the side activities. you can make your farm into a huge bee sanctuary and flower garden if you want. it can literally be anything you want. things also place well beside each other no annoying gaps like in animal crossing decorating.the hair styles freaking suck but they are adding more and sculpting them right now for players. if you look at the discord and see the daily lists the devs post on there of things they actively work on its absolutely amazing and exhaustive. they are putting so much effort into this, and if you crash a lot and ask things the discord devs from the game will personally reply a lot or ask you for your crash reports/save files to fix whatever issue with very quick times!!! its the middle of the night for them and one of them is currently looking over my broken file after the patch this morning that seemed to break a lot of ppls save files.the festivals are fun and have mini games that are new to play with the villagers. and you can see a lot of signs and notes in game about how the devs plan on putting something there.this game when it is done is going to be amazing. it will have high replayability due to the MASSIVE amount of characters in it to choose from, and how you can really just do anything and have it be a viable main activity for your farm.if early access is going to bug you, and the chance of needing to be wiped and starting over will end it for you, then please just wait for full release.if you dont mind it though and still just want to test the waters i encourage you to really take your time to talk to people multiple times, and take your time looking around and watching the animations and things cause its so so so lovely.i have played so much, i played alpha and tested as well and i never rlly see any conversation repeats.  theres also the universally liked gifts that are easy to craft.there are problems sure but they are being fixed. controller was so lovely to play with in alpha but a patch broke it and its still currently being repaired. if you just take some time to look over the dev diaries on the discord and really appreciate the potential this game is truly amazing.

Its unnecessarily annoying.No characters have voices. Everything is textThere are no Genders at Character Customization just body options So this game is WOKE. One "Female?" NPC has visible stretchmarks like uhhh gross dudeNice that they have an unstuck button but the only part i got stuck on was decor mode and cant even access the unstuck button. _childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has the potential to be one of the best, new farming games. Personally I'm having a blast with it, and it works perfectly on the Steam Deck!Here is what I like:-The colorful world and diverse characters-28 romancable characters - The focus on environmentalism and cleaning up the island around you-There are quite a few festivals, that have a variety of new themes I haven't seen in other games in this genre  (although I personally find the mini games frustrating)-Theres a lot to do: farming (theres plenty of farming animals to chose from), fishing, mining, bug catching, cooking. And a museum to fill up with all your collected items -A lot of character customization options (including pronouns and body types) and clothing -You can change the exterior style of your house and farm buildingsIssues I have with the game:-The full story is not released, there are items marked as TBD-The character lack distinct personality, they have about 3 lines a day that repeat pretty often. If you date or marry these characters, their lines barely change-You can adopts pets. But only one pet and they don't currently do anything other than stand in their bed, and move around every so often-There are mermaids, but their story isn't finished yet either-I have had lag issues, freezing issues and occasional crashing issues. I assume these will be fixed in an update soonHere are some notable features coming in 2024 (unclear on if it will be free or paid. I assume they will be free but you never know these days):-Tourist system-Hangout/Dating mechanic-A big Merfolk update-Ocean farming and ranching-More story-Children update (you can have children in the game currently, but I assume this will add more to them)-Savannah access-Island visit-Multiplayer

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love the idea of this game, I cannot actively recommend buying it. SO. MANY. BUGS. It still feels massively incomplete despite being fully released as a v1.0. I've put in hundreds of hours on the beta and this version is almost exactly the same but somehow worse. There's a part of me that wants to keep playing despite the issues, but I don't know if that's mostly down to the time I've invested thus far. Fishing and bug catching are poor, but I expect that from most games. RNG for artifacts, fossils and gems is diabolical. I'm currently 27th Winter year 1 and still haven't had a bunch of quests drop that are supposed to be early game. This game is most definitely NOT fit for full release and that makes me sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly really love this game! Yes it is still "in beta" so there are features not finished and dead end quests, but I'm patient and I'd rather they take the time to make stuff right than to rush job it. I played it in alpha too. I'm on year 3 and I still haven't finished everything (romances, friendships, collections).I love the game theme incorporating a lot of Indonesian culture, it's someone I've not personally seen in mainstream games. The island theme is fun and I enjoy fixing up the environment! Farming is standard but with the addition of winter crops that most farming sims dont usually have. The ranch animals, and pets, are so adorable and I love that the pets can follow you around the farm (I do wish I could have more though!) The seasonal events are standard but with a fun twist, I can't wait to see the halloween event finished with the visuals. Speaking of visuals, this game is BEAUTIFUL. And so are all the date-able NPCS. It's a problem but in a good way. All the characters are so interesting and have background stories that feel real, excellent writing, I've even cried a couple times. & the water exploration is SO FUN. Excited for that to be updated as well. & the tech makes farming, ranching, and traveling so easy!overall I feel there are a lot of quality of life updates vs other popular farming sims, amazing writing, characters, & scenery, and just a ton of fun. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly Ive been so excited for this game, ive been following for such a long time now. To start off with not so great thoughts on it, this game is so heavly inspired by stardew that it kinda hurts at times. The map is so massive that its so easy to get lost. I feel like you have to have a solid plan on what you are doing on the start of the day bc you run the risk of running out of time in the day just trying to get to point A to point B.But other than those two, I would recommend this game so heavly. I love it so much already, its soothing, it ads new elemets i havnt seen in some other farming sims before. The sheer amount of content/nps/romanceabls its so much that it can be overwhelming. _childDocuments_.review: If you like the Farming Sim like the Old Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley you will like Coral Island. You just have to keep in mind that its Early Access. Haven't found any game breaking bug, but there are some minor bugs and a lot of missing content for the time being. Clean up your farm and decorate, there are a lot of furniture pieces currently out, 2 out 4 mines are open. I think the diving map is complete, there are some puzzle looking objects that's not complete. The seasonal events needs to be completed. _childDocuments_.review: Caveat Emptor!tldr: Don't grab this unless you're ok with an unfinished game.I hope to change this review as what there is of this game so far I have enjoyed. I generally avoid Early Access games, I like to enjoy finished products and don't get as much enjoyment as some out of seeing works in progress. Coral Island's development and the generally positive attention it has been getting left me optimistic so I purchased when it exited early access, but the 1.0 release feels like an attempt to get enough money to finish a kickstarter that ran out of cash (or worse, cash in on what's been finished and never touch it again. Fingers crossed that isn't the case).This game should not have received a "full release." While there is a lot of game to enjoy, much of it is still incomplete, including main aspects of the story framework the farming simulator hangs itself on. Much of that content is well beyond the two hours of play Steam allows refunds at though, so don't pick it up unless you're ok with that ahead of time.

Probably it's just the art-style of the game itself, so idk. I personally didn't like poor variety of things the game offers in order to create a character> Not to be a perfectionist especially when the game is not released fully (or is?) but some animations are just bad like during conversations (they are exaggerated imo). Also the conversation windows as well could've contain more lines in-one-go so that characters talking wouldn't take so long to end, you'll get tired of talking to NPCs 'cause it takes so much time. Maybe it's just me being impatient> Now's the biggest reason I feel like affected me more to abandon playing this game after only 7 hours: the buttons are just random. For example, while having a conversation with NPC to proceed to next line of dialogue - you click mouse2 (right click) which is kind of odd imo, but it's fine you can get used to it. However, when you approach some surroundings stuff (a fountain for example) it shows you the text and to continue playing (after you've relieved your curiousity) you have to use mouse1 (left click) for some reason. I don't understand this decision: you ought to be awared of this every time you try to inspect anything. And finally what's ridiculous: you know when the game gives you pop-ups with guidelines or something, like 'to plant a tree - just come to a place where the square becomes green and click on it' - well, in order to continue and close this pop-up you must use the button R. Now explain that to me, it's just something I can't process in my mind.> Inventory and chests interaction also leaves me questions. In order to automatically put the whole stack of a material (wood, for example) you click on it in your inventory with M1 whereas M2 sends it one by one. Again, you can get used to it, nothing difficult, but when you want the same operation reversed (material from chest to inventory) - you click M1 on it and... it sticks to your cursor and you have to manually put it in the inventory. Now that's just stupid. Overall I feel like the game itself might become good product like another farm-like games with plot and stuff, but in a current state of TECHNICAL issues that I've faced - I don't feel like playing it. It's just uncomfortable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've Been playing a fair bit of Coral Island recently, almost done with the first year and starting to accumulate the Tier 4 tools.  It's solid, but I haven't been able to figure out what really sets it apart from the rest of the genre.  It just seems like a straight-up Stardew Valley knockoff with more supernatural elements, and I've never really enjoyed the supernatural angle in these games.  Even Stardew built on Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons' foundation, it wasn't just a straight clone.The "cleaning up the island" thing would be a very cool hook if it felt like they did more with it, but as it stands, Portia/Sandrock did more with that in terms of you actually doing something.  Instead, you just leave offerings (the Community Center from SV crossed with the Harvest Goddess from HM), dive into the mine with something good happening at floor 40 of each area, donate to the museum, and clear trash in the ocean to activate relics that clean the ocean for you, and the improvements just sort of happen on their own once you do get a certain amount of "town points" for doing those.  The diving is pretty weak too, it's not appreciably different from the mines except you use the sickle instead of a pick.  Using kelp for permanent passive upgrades to seeds and crop quality is cool, though.Character-wise, the LGBTQ representation is obviously great (the character artist clearly favored the G part more than I'd personally prefer, but that's not a flaw, just not my personal orientation, and even that may say more about what I generally expect male/female character designs to look like), but none of the characters feel like they have much personality to me, and several of the designs kind of blend together.  It doesn't help that despite the 1.0 release, it's clearly not "finished" finished.Overall, like I said, it's solid, and I haven't stopped playing yet, but I can't tell if I actually like it or if I'm just addicted to the gameplay loop.  Another recent Steam review said "I wish there was a Neutral option," and that's kind of where I'm at too.  It's worth a look if you've already played the hell out of Stardew and Portia/Sandrock, especially if you get it on sale, but generally speaking, I can't say I'd recommend it over others in the genre.

But for people like me who's looking for something new after hundreds of hours in Stardew (AND modded stardew valley!), the first few hours of this game feels very underwhelming, and kinda boring. I do like the character design, but I wish the main story is more captivating.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. To me its the perfect balance of classic farm sim with QoL adjustments and some new innovation. _childDocuments_.review: Look, I really like this game, and it's clear a lot of thought went into its creation. The characters are fun, diverse, and there's an element of authentic/genuine cultural identity that's been well represented and upheld in the game. There is a lot of potential, a lot of fun to be had in this game. Honestly, the modding scene is going to be amazing. THAT BEING SAID - the above is what makes a good visual novel. This, unfortunately, is a video game that has been presented as a complete, finished package. It is not. The amount of little glitches and bugs in almost all the mechanics of the game is lowkey embarrassing. The more hours I play, the more I question the quality control process. The characters, storylines, and features start to feel more like an empty marketing gimmick, valuing quantity over quality - which feels a lot more upsetting in this game than it has for me playing other similar games in the past. I think it's because I'm subconsciously upset at seeing how much love, research and respect for culture went into the character and environmental design, and then constantly noticing how the poorly tested mechanics of the game let that love and care down. I'll continue to play it, if only because I have paid access to WeMod, and I like doing little tasks that give my ADHD ass that tasty, tasty dopamine, but I also see myself getting bored of it pretty quickly if an update doesn't come out before the end of the year. Do with it what you will, but as someone who paid full price the week it came out (no early access) I'd hold off for now. It says v1.0. It really should be more like v.0.75

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 250 hours and completed pretty much everything in the 1.1 update. I'll go over some topics I think it’s important and worth talking about (and that i don't see many people talking) + Not mentioning the word ''stardew valley'' for an ENTIRE review challenge.This is a very nice game, with innovative and fresh features in the genre, the world feels alive, the nature and tropical atmosphere + charismatic and lovely NPCs. You can tell it was made with passion, creativity and by people who actually cared. However, nothing is perfect and there are quite a few things and problems you need to consider, the worst of it all (at least for me) was the massive grind and boring gameplay loop, and even tho in the short term you feel like you are progressing in everything you do, the game fails in awarding you for all the trouble and massive hours of grind. Activities just like any other farming sim games, but here we got Ocean Diving, where you help to restore and clear trash from the ocean and exploring an underwater world with ocean creatures and some very nicely put mermaid and ocean folklore. It’s very nice, but it ends up being quite repetitive at a late point. , making it very grindy and repetitive as these are essential tasks for the main story progression and takes very, very long to ''complete''.Progression also feels very slow, completing the bundles, story, and maxing out skills takes a very long time, [/b]wouldn’t be a problem if the rewards weren’t so poor, unsatisfying, and even ‘’outdated’’ at the point of the game you’ll finally complete them[/b]. Getting gold is a bit hard and at the endgame when you are finally swimming in it, there won’t be much to spend on.Not to mention the amount of bundles you gotta complete that takes forever and when you finally do, you’ll unlock even more bundles to complete. 😭The objectives in general feel somewhat very ‘linear’, I truly wished things were more ‘laid back’, unpredictable and chill.Characters are one high point of this game, a very diverse cast and it makes the game feel truly alive, every single one has a distinct personality and if you are a person who likes to hear what they have to say, you’ll like it a lot!, some storylines are very good and well written, very easy and accessible to relate in many states of life.The bad thing is: there are TOO MANY of them and it takes a long time to progress in the friendship. If you decide to speak to everyone around the town, you'll lose more than half of a day doing it for sure. And of course, you won’t be interested in every single NPC, but it takes SO LONG for any kind of progression, it adds a lot of the feeling of ‘’massive’’ into the game.The romance/dating is also a bit dull, with cute cutscenes and dating events, but they won’t say anything different to you in everyday life or anything, it’s like it’s not happening at all. Feels incomplete.  ✿ Character customization is VERY CUTE and there's a huge variety of cosmetics and clothing items.  ✿ Farm customization and house decoration can be a little bit clunky in the square grid (the house has a terrible design) but you can turn out to make very nice inspired decor with tons of different sets, needs some minor improvements and polishing tho! ✿ Festivals are very unique and original, and it has actual fun minigames and cutscenes, just wished the rewards were a little better. ✿ Huge shoutout to the numerous easter eggs, from a BMO and Sponge Bob inspo decorations, to programs in the in game TV referring real shows  and movies like Game of Thrones, Masterchef and even Kpop survival reality shows (Produce 101, we love you!) ✿ The main story was very predictable and a bit disappointing, the game is very original and ambitious and I ended up expecting something new and original for the closing of the story too. Looking forward to new updates, hopefully, it’ll redeem itself in the future.✿ Few acid humor and double meaning dialogues here, had moments asking myself howtf was it even possible, they really got me. ''Groo got stoned and slept'' but he actually got stoned, became a stone for real lol  This review sounds a little too negative and harsh, but I just wanted to highlight some points I don’t see people talking about and in my opinion, are somewhat important. I loved playing this game, felt massive most of the time, but ended up appreciating a lot of the little details of it. Truly wished it were more of a 'laid back' chill and cozy game, even tho there shouldn't be pressure to complete or anything, I felt a bit of it. More updates will arrive in the future,  and hopefully, they will fix and improve some quality-of-life aspects needed for a better-polished game in general.

Also Multiplayer is on it's way. All in all I give this game a 9/10A very enjoyable farming simulator with the best of all previous games before it. If you're a fan of the old harvest moon, rune factory games but also love the more recent stardew valley, animal crossing new horizons, story of seasons, etc than this game is for you. That said, despite being listed as a fully released game, it's far from complete. There are unlockable areas that aren't accessible. Once you complete the merfolk quest line you can't speak to any of them or access the shops. The mechanics for marriage and building a family aren't complete. More than once I've resorted to google to discover the secret to accessing an area or completing a quest only to discover that I've made it as far as it's possible to go. The game is so promising, but there's no way this should have been considered a full release with so much missing. Assuming the devs continue to put out regular updates I'm not giving up on it entirely, but if you're not looking to buy a work in progress I'd steer clear of this for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Game "Farming Sim" is a very fun and interesting simulation game. In this game, you will play the role of a farmer who is responsible for managing your own garden and stables. You will grow different types of crops, raise animals and build relationships with the townspeople. This game features beautiful graphics and a very relaxing and relaxing atmosphere.One of the most interesting aspects of this game is the dynamic world in the game, where the weather conditions, seasons and time of day greatly affect the way you play. For example, in the summer, you should make sure your plants are well-ventilated, while in the winter, you should avoid freezing them. This makes the game more challenging and exciting.In addition, the island life that is presented in this game is very charming and captivating. You will meet a variety of unique and interesting characters, and building relationships with them can open up new opportunities and benefits in the game. By building connections and relationships with city dwellers, you will help make the world around you a more harmonious and vital place.Overall, this game is highly recommended for anyone looking for a simulation game experience that is relaxing and relaxing, but still challenging and fun. With a dynamic game world and a beautiful atmosphere, this game is sure to keep you entertained for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: i have hundreds and hundreds of hours in all kinds of life sims and especially farming sims. this is one of my favorite genres of games, and this is a game i've had my eye on since pre-release.so far here are my thoughts, concerns and feedback; interesting points and some pros:- very inclusive, there is no girl and boy gender, different body type with sliders!- selling bin similar to stardew- theres fishing and bug catching and a museum for them like animal crossing- a general store that has a scheduled day closed similar to stardew- mining and a villain character that wants to make the small town a corporate place like stardew- i love the character art- i love interacting with the strays and animals on the island, and them having cute personalities that show through their actions- i love the diversity of the characters, their identities and their character design- many ethnicities and backgrounds, theres one girl in the inn with stretchmarks and i rlly love that attention to detail and realism ngl- the ambience of the town is SO GOOD!! i love the details in the foliage, the interiors, the layout of the town, how big it is, and generally just a VERY pretty game :)- dating system similar to stardew but havent explored it yet we will see how far that content goes, i.e. can we get married and live together like stardew?feedback/cons, etc: (this game is in early access im not rlly that upset about these just commenting on them so devs can fix for full release)- sometimes characters have red eyes kinda scary haha- the movement is very robotic - the audio settings dont really allow for some sounds to be very low, i have some settings to the lowest possible and they are still very loud- if i lower master volume those sounds just disappear instead of being lowered further- some of the audios in the game feel not very satisfying; i.e. footsteps have no diversity, its like the same one footstep but played over and over (but they do change on the terrain youre on, like sand/wood/stone/dirt)- the town is so so big which i LOVE!! right now im in love, and very happy with it, ill come back if anything changes with my opinion and i look forward to the updates, bug fixes, and new content :) ive played stardew into the ground at this point so im so excited for this game and have been for as long as i have known about it. fingers crossed my love stays the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge farming sim fan, and have to say, Coral Island has the potential to give Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon a run for their money in terms of leaders in the genre once it is complete. In comparison to many farming sims, Coral Island has a solid story-line, and added a lot of new elements that feel innovative and fresh in the genre. ( Diving is incredibly addictive! ) You can tell the devs have a real vision with this game, and it makes a genre that can feel generic incredibly unique and memorable. This game is by no means finished, but for the first 20-30 hours, you really don't notice it. It isn't until you start to get mid-tier gear and build deeper connections with some of the villagers that has you feeling the content is less than whole. I hope that as development of this game continues they can work on better writing in regards to the townsfolks relationships with your farmer. A lot of the cut scenes feel lifeless, and often times you only have one choice for responding during these interactions. I think most people come to this genre for the dating-sim like elements and intimate feel of living in a small town. I just asked Raj to be my date mate, and every cutscene before that was related to their business with no indication of interest in my farmer. One of the best aspects of games like Harvest Moon is the subtle change in interactions with your farmer as their heart events progress. As the game currently stands, the elements I find most enjoyable are mining, diving, and crafting. I appreciate the innovation in crafting by having universal chests so you can craft items without having to have it in your inventory, and I can tell by many of those small things that as Coral Island develops, it will be an incredibly solid and great game. ( For the first 20 hours... it already is! )

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to compare this game to Stardew Valley, because it's the closest game I've played that emulates it so well:PROS:- Graphics are decent (UE4)- Obvious influence from Stardew Valley everywhere, but still has it's own identity.  Some mechanics are better implemented than in than title.  - Lots of content- All of the romance options are really really really ridiculously good looking. - Fishing is actually fun unlike Stardew Valley which is tedious. - Devs seem to interact with the Community a lotCONS:- Doesn't seem to have the same cozy 'charm' like Stardew Valley has.  It's not a bad game, just doesn't feel the same. - There's quite a lot of dynamic music, it's not bad but it's forgettable and generic compared to the quite memorable music of Stardew Valley.  I always played with the music on in SD because it was just so good especially with the different seasons, I mostly turned it off in this game.  - The changing of the seasons just doesn't have the same visual "punch", even if there's far more detail for each season in this game.  It's probably because the colors in Stardew are over saturated and stylized as a pixel art game. - Yuri hated the osmium bar I gave her, but she apparently liked it enough to keep it of course!- Text chat with the NPCs is sorta boring and forgettable, but they're hot so it makes it more bearable. - The town bar in the game has more 'events' that happen in it, but it's no Stardrop Saloon.- Does really have that small town feel to the game.Final verdict: It's trying very hard to try and be a better Stardew Valley, and it mostly gets there but still won't overtake the OG.

_childDocuments_.review: Farming/Life Simulator in the vein of Stardew Valley with a little bit of Animal Crossing (bug catching and diving) mixed in.  I'm not very far along in the storyline but it's enjoyable so far.  If you enjoyed SDV this might be for you.Pros:-Very nice graphics, the artwork and general style is great and MC customization has a lot of detail.  Beautiful character models.-The fishing minigame is superior to SDV (imo).-Lots of romance options and good cutscenes so far.-Bug catching is fun, and the museum is open 24-7 so you don't sit with a bunch of donations taking up bag space.-The farm is huge.Cons:-One nasty game bug that I ran into and I've seen other comments in the boards with the same issue.  The first time I got a coffer from harvesting trash the game locked up.  I had to use the "I'm stuck" button.  I'm glad it's there but the penalties are pretty harsh.  The upside is that this is the only bug I've had so far (I've only played full release, not early access).-The MC moves painfully slowly.  Maybe there are upgrades for this later in the game and I'm not there yet.-Bag space is very limited early on.  That's part of the experience but there are so many item options that it feels very constrained (more than usual for this type of game).-Combat, at least with the starter sword, is very janky.  You swing twice then take a step forward for the 3rd swing, which usually steps you right into the mob.-Higher level tool upgrades take multiple days to get your tool back.  I don't mind the single day wait from SDV but I don't look forward to Level 4 tools with a 4 day wait.Neutral:-SJW stuff (or human rights, woke, liberal, left, use whatever term you want...pejorative or supportive).  It's not apocalyptic like some have posted online and in the discussions, but if you're hypersensitive to things like rainbow flags and same-sex partnerships this probably isn't your jam because they're present.  Doesn't really affect gameplay as long as that stuff doesn't bother you.  The main storyline has a pretty heavy environmentalist message, common to "get away from the city and farm" type games.-Some may like this, but I prefer the option to save any time instead of just at the end of the day.  Prevents save scumming but it means you have to commit to playing a full day at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island at a glance has almost everything I wanted from a farming sim - great looking and diverse characters, a mixture of real and fantastic elements, a rare tropical setting, etc. The game also tackles real ecosystem problems. However, the game felt very mismanaged during early access, leading to it being released 1.0 while missing major content. The devs almost doubled the price to catch the holiday sale number, with an unfinished game. That alone can tell you more about the project than anything else I'm going to say.But besides being unfinished, the game feels lacking in many crucial aspects that are not easily fixed. The writing for instance is subpar. Many key characters I was excited about don't really have any character arc. Take Kenny and Rafael, for example. (Some early spoilers, be warned.) From the moment you meet them, you know they are nice guys. But after several personal events about them, and more than halfway through their heart progression, what more have you learned about them? Nothing. They are still nice guys without any nuances. Their stories are focused entirely on something besides their personalities. I still don't know why Rafael wants to forge this magic hammer, or why Kenny wants to decipher this scroll. It feels completely random. Compare this to Stardew Valley, you learn so much about each character's motivations and dreams, and you see their growth with your own eyes.The game also fails to capture the gravity of ecosystem problems. Basically all you need to do in the game is to find some kind of magic altar, donate random plants to the goddess, and the ecosystem is fixed? It sends a wrong kind of message. Oh the goddess will revitalize the island, and the mermaids will fix the oil spillage. No? Lessening damage done to the ecosystem requires knowledge and a lot of work. It's not easy and not "magical". I almost wish they haven't put the focus of the game on this topic, when they aren't capable of getting it right.One last thing, the game classified tomatoes as fruit. Tomatoes are the fruit part of the plant, just like cucumbers, pumpkins, chili peppers. But if you try to classify it in a culinary sense (fruits vs. vegetables vs. grains), it's a vegetable. This "tomatoes are actually fruits" thing needs to die. It's a misunderstanding of the double meanings of the word "fruit". Literally unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Unbalanced, unfinished, full of bugs (and dialogue typos) beta that is still being developed, yet was forceably released out of early acess as a finished game and was asked by devs to promote it for free. Cleaning the ocean for the third time? I am NOT doing that by hand again (and for what? For not getting the promised content? Yikes.)Finishing the altar offerings and the museum donations right now feels impossible because the needed scavengeables, gems, resources, fish just don't spawn, and that was my last straw to write this review. I dislike when a game should be fun, but instead feels like a chore despite its great potential.It's a Can't Recommend until it's fixed and finished.P.S.: Oh, and the game has no manual save which is a HUGE no.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have much time to play games anymore due to the amount of time I have free waning more and more each day, however, this is an expenditure of the rare resource I feel is quite well worth it.1. (Just to state what every other review has said) This game is as much of a Stardew clone as Stardew is Rune Factory clone as Rune Factory is a Harvest Moon clone. Long story short, genres are not exclusive to singular games.2. NPC's feel like people I have genuinely met before.Barring 1-2 NPCs who I genuinely have no care for, almost every NPC I have met I feel I have met throughout my life. It could make my review biased as I feel a more emotional connection due to the similarities to past friends and family members, but its my review so sue me over it.3. Balance of stylization and reality.This game clearly has an artistic style, the title of which I know not, and yet some of its mechanics feel as though its what has been missing from other titles. One of the negative reviews found that swinging and missing with tools consuming stamina was a bad mechanic, yet I found it the exact opposite. Having cut down a few trees myself (and missing occasionally missing, specifically as I was removing stumps), you do get exhausted just from the action of swinging the tool and not even necessarily hitting. And its not even as though its a severe punishment, it is a single energy point and you have a good 400 to start out each day.4. Sheer mass of content.Occasionally I will encounter some games that simply have too much going on and get lost within the labyrinths of their activities. Yet, everything seems to be well connected and every activity worth while. You may dive, fish, farm, bug hunt, to acquire your funds and do whatever you wish with them without feeling you're missing out upon another option altogether. It truly has something for near everyone.5. Level of Detail.Each character has a different outfit for each season, leaves have glistening drops in the rain, puddles temporarily appear, (I haven't seen snow yet, but please do share if there are footprints left after each step), and various other details that escape me at the moment because, well, they're small details, not monumentous achievements.6. Graphics.This is quite a simple game from a graphical perspective, but it is still quite beautiful. Water looks as actual water, sand appears as sand, and while it is stylized, the world still seems as though it is of this world. People don't strange cartoonish features similar to caricatures, they have the appearances of people drawn with artistic flare. This all without mentioning the amount of hand drawn art there is from the TV programs to the character portraits. And anything hand drawn will always bear my appreciation and amazement.Nothing is without negatives however.1. Camera.It feels extremely distant. I know some people wish you could rotate the camera, however, all storefronts and signs are from the set angle, so you would mostly see blank walls. Yet, the distance of the camera makes it very difficult to appreciate all the finer details, such as the glisten of leaves in the rain or the finer details on character 3D models.2. Music.This is very much a personal preference and bias as a musician, but a negative I feel all the same. Much of the sound track follows the same tropical theme as the games style does as well. However, constantly hearing tropical music is... sickening to me... Bright floral notes and pieces can be pleasant in short intervals, however, deeper and more resounding bass notes are much more pleasant over time as even should they grow old, it simply devolves into pleasant background noise, and not an annoying tick in the back of the mind.3. Animations.It is clear the animations are being worked on what with them not being entirely synced up per model, and the amount of animations used is quite amazing. However, the tool swing animation with the leg lifted feels awkward and strange to see. The fact snails will move at mach 10 when alerted is hilarious, however, not quite true to life. And general walking animations can feel slippery, like within a hazy dream, chasing after an ambiguous figure in a fog ridden land.4. Customization.Same as animations, its clear its being worked on, especially hair styles because... well... they're severely limited a little lack luster at the moment of review. However, I truly enjoy fashion and creating various outfits to suite different themes. Whilst there are various customizable clothing pieces with shirts, hoodies, shoes, and shorts/skirts/pants, there's a lack of some pieces such as socks, dresses, scarves(?don't see scarves in many games, could be an interesting addition?), coats, etc.However, this game has so much potential, and the approach the devs have to its creation gives me a very hopeful and bright outlook for the future of the game. Not to mention the clear roadmap of what will be available upon full release.Should you enjoy farming sims or casual games in general, you will almost certainly adore this game.
