_childDocuments_.review: i've been waiting for this game so impatiently and so excitedly that i was worried to be too expectant of what this game was going to be, so i went into this a little worried. however, in the now 9 hours that i have played this game, i couldn't have felt better and more satisfied.coral island captured me from the first second on. not only were my expectations met; i was genuinely overwhelmed by how quickly i got addicted to this charming, beautiful game.not only does the scenery look absolutely stunning (as does the rest of the game) but it also makes me feel so calm and peaceful. especially as someone who feels anxious quite often, i can already picture this game being a perfect escape to calm my nerves and help me unwind. there is no pressure in this game, you can explore and achieve everything at your own leisure while being guided by the quests in a very easily understandable and kind way.the farming, fishing and bug catching are all really well executed, not hard to understand and pursue, which to me is really important. i don't want to be rushed in such things or have to click a thousand times, so the way these things were done are very much to my liking.all of the characters are not only absolutely gorgeously designed and drawn (shoutout to david ardinaryas lojaya from a fellow artist who's super inspired) and they all have distinctively different, but amazing personalities! they're all charming in their own ways and my god i just really adore the variety of people to meet and talk to on this beautiful island.up until now my game has been running amazingly, though it's an early access and the fact that my laptop is about eight years old. there was maybe one or two text bubbles in which a letter was missing, but there have been no bugs or crashes for me! i'm usually not one to write reviews so this might all seem messy, perhaps it's my excitement overcoming me that is causing me to leave such a lengthy text. i might've missed some points i wanted to integrate into this, although i'm sure you guys got the gist. genuienly, the last time i've felt such comfort and happiness coming from a game was when animal crossing: new horizons came out back in 2020. ever since i've been longing to find another game like this, and now i've got it right here!to the wonderful team working on this, i want you guys to be proud of yourself for creating such an amazing game/xperience! i am looking forward to all that is yet to come and will continue to support you guys and your work in all the ways i can.so, long story short: support the devs by buying this amazing game, it's 100% worth it.

One unique feature is the ability to dive underwater and restore coral reefs, adding an eco-friendly dimension to the game, which is both rewarding and educational.

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't want to give this game a negative. I forced myself to play on, waited patiently for updates (took >8 months btw) but since I tell my friends not to buy it (yet) irl, I guess that counts as a non-recommendation. CI is a huge waste of potential and could've been the next stardew. The art and world setting is incredibly beautiful, and as someone from SEA I really enjoy seeing the mesh of indo culture in the game, but the praise ends here. The biggest problem with this game is BUGS. Bugs, bugs, a crash here and there, more bugs. Was their programmer hired from wish or did they come from an entomology degree? Who knows?I bought this game before the 1.0 release back in Nov 2023 but seeing as that they'll wipe your files I decided to wait for 1.0. To my surprise the mermaid content (which is literally in the screenshots on the store page btw?) was totally non-existent in the "full" release. Ppl defended the devs saying it was never part of 1.0 and was "always" part of a later update/roadmap. That's where all the "incomplete" reviews came from. But well never mind I am only interested in mermaid stuff, so I waited. 8 months passed and I'm way past refund deadline. 1.1 is finally here in July 2024. Super excited; dove right in.Gameplay wise it's your typical farming sim. Crops to sell, cows to feed, villagers to romance. A lot of things follow SV's format to the T. The harvest fest where you have to bring a crop to put into the huge crock pot, the inane mining format that unfortunately got popular thanks to SV where you have to mine rocks until you find a rope(stairs in sv) down, and every 5 levels you get an elevator. But there's a lot of unique SE-asian mini games in other seasons for you to enjoy. Oh, they give you sprinklers early, which I love, but no one tells you using sprinklers do NOT give you farming points apparently, so you'd be in year 3 with your farming level still at 5/10, but I digress.The characters are ok. The writing is pretty mid ngl and half the time I have to fight the intense urge not to hit the Skip button. I am the type of person who usually romances (if possible) or max out all relationships with every character just to read their story, regardless of gender and this is the first farming game I legit wasn't sure if I could put myself through this. Quantity > Quality is a great way to describe the writing. Here are some early heart events: You help carry a sofa because someone is moving. You watch 3 people get into an argument that has nothing to do with you. Dude broke the library pc. Dude has daddy problems. Another dude has rich daddy problems. A girl complains. Some of these are completely unnecessary to split into 2 heart then 3 heart events and could've just been squeezed into a 5 heart, then 8 heart event because the early heart ones are a serious waste of time. I got to get up for work irl tmr and I really don't care that your shoe has a hole in it bro. Btw, there's NO divorce in this game so be careful who you give that heart knot to.Anyway, you can put crops into machines (mayo maker, aging barrel, bee hives for honey, etc), but the machines break EVERY OTHER DAY. They literally just stop working. The crafting bar is full but you cannot pick up your produce or remove it. If you look this up in the discussions there's hundreds of threads dating back 1+ years about this. It gets worse the longer you play it so it's definitely some kind of memory leak but everyone refuses to acknowledge the possibility their game was programmed by a blind man and his puppy stepping on his keyboard. If you ask/beg/pray for a fix, CI's keyboard warriors will run to reply, "Just restart your game." or my personal fav "The devs can't reproduce the bug." As if that's an answer...? So if you're going to buy this game, be prepared to restart it after every other day. If you're totally ok with the devs not respecting your time, you'll enjoy this game. Here's more: The chest you put in your barn to store the milk pail/sheers & hay has disappeared completely. You post asking for help. The reply you will get (from the same few people) is, "Well you shouldn't have put a chest in the barn." Then why tf did the game allow me to and why did the chest work for 3 days?? Oh and if you put fences touching the barn your fences will also disappear. The answer to that was, "Leave a space." lol.Another one: "Bug: Quests or altar (bundles in SV) don't accept different/mixed quality of the item." The reply: "Well don't donate mixed qualities." While you might think hey this isn't a bug it's a feature, why are you complaining about this? Picture this: You are now in year 2 and most of your items are gold~osmium quality. You finally get the other 4 pieces out of 5 to donate, but it won't go in because previously you put in ONE bronze quality in yr 1 so now you are STUCK with all bronzes. How in the world are you going to find bronze quality now? But apparently this is OK and a "feature" and we should all just stop bullying the devs.....You get the idea of the kind of stellar replies from the community. But what about the devs? Well they reply maybe once every 2-3 weeks, if at all, and they'll copypasta reply "Send us your save file and a video of the bug and what you were doing before it happened." as if everyone just sits around recording their 200 hour intense crop watering sessions. If you don't, well, oopsie, we can't reproduce the bug. The game was working perfectly fine BEFORE a patch but is suddenly stuttering and lagging after it? Well the answer was, "Lower your graphics quality" or "What card are you on? You need a good GPU to play this game." (as if it wasn't working fine before the update..) "4080" No more replies. Tree planting event was working fine before a hotfix (which they had to upload 2 more hotfixes to fix their hotfix, and they broke automatic chests along the way, just sayin') but now you will faint and lose all your tools. "We are aware. Just get your tools back from the blacksmith." Ok great, what about my sword? "Just buy one." This is one of the first few events in Spring btw, and the bug affects mostly new files/new players, who have NO MONEY. The problem is all these people replying and shielding the devs have like 400 hours in the game and are way past all of these issues when they affect you the most. If you have high stamina and 5 mil gold then yeah, you won't faint and lose all your tools so this isn't a problem at all. These are the same people who are active on discord too so the devs basically live in an echo chamber.I personally experienced 2 crashes in Spring year 1 alone, then later had some weird bug where I could NOT interact with anything, so I literally couldn't sleep in my bed and I fainted. I restarted the game/day and it went fine so I just continued, but a in-game week later the same thing happened at a different location/time. Reported it, and got the "Send us a video" from the dev and a "What other apps did you have running while you're playing the game?"Everything wrong with the game is some how your fault. You shouldn't have done the thing. You shouldn't have listened to youtube while you play. You shouldn't put chests in the barn. Express your unhappiness in the discussions? Get clown badges and whiteknight replies about how the devs are poor widdle babies, never to be blamed. (And yes pls do give me more on this review to prove my point.) "Hey my bug from the last patch wasn't fixed." "I bet you didn't reply to the devs." ..I literally got a reply like this. LOL bruh.I tried my best to like this game. I really did. It would've been so good. The thought about how they royally blew their 1mil dollar kickstarter (convert this to Rupiah & you'd have AAA game level of funding btw...) and this is what they came up with is just painful. Maybe hire more staff including one who can actually program, 6 testers, and a CS. See you in 4 years. Hopefully that's enough time to fix this mess.

Then suddenly you're the predestined to save the situation. Dude, I cannot even save myself. I have a house with no cooking equipment I survive out of eating random sh--- in the street! The stories, artwork, music, and gameplay are phenomenal, making every penny spent well worth it. As someone who values the '1 Dollar per Hour' dream for PC games, Coral Island fits this bill perfectly. It's a purchase I'd recommend to anyone who loves immersive, beautifully crafted games.

You must try this game if your also a fan, or someone new to the genre willing to get their feet wet. I highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Just a reminder that this game is in Early Access and that production is ongoing. That being said...This world is stunning. It is a beautiful remake of an often cookie-cutter genre. Farming Sims tend to be the same at the core, with very little to differentiate them, but Coral Island strives to break that mold by adding features usually reserved for mods of other farming sims.Coral Island has a variety of crops not seen in any other farm sims, animals that are usually hard to obtain, or not obtainable at all, and a story that breathes of culture and history. Without spoilers, there is more to the world than what you see on the surface. Yes, you have your farming, ranching and mining, as well as fishing, gathering and romance. But you also have deep cultural significance, hidden gems and secrets, and entirely new worlds to discover.

Not angry, just disappointed. For a game attempting so blatantly to rip off Stardew Valley, Coral Island really didn't have anything that drew me in after 2-ish hours. It's got nice art, okay music... It needs some QOL on the farming/mining/logging stuff, the characters don't really get a lot of fleshing out besides 'oh you're the new person'. And the set-up is *aggressively* basic.It feels unfocused, and while it's not a *bad* game, for me, it felt insubstantial.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I'm giving this game an 8/10! There is a LOT of potential here, and what's already playable is insanely fun.Pros:- Variety: You can do SO much in this game, from farming, to fishing, to diving, to mining. It's not JUST a farming simulator or a "stardew valley ripoff". It takes what made Stardew Valley great and BUILDS on that, adding unique features unseen in any game like it. - Setting/Characters: I absolutely ADORE the setting, the culture inspirations, and the art style of the game. It reminds me of the 2000-2008 era of Disney movies, but in a 2D format. I love all of the characters (except Karen), and can't wait to play through all of their stories. There is some obvious hints of Japanese, Hawaiian, Hispanic, and Australian culture and it's so well done and meshed together to make a real "Coral Island" culture feel.- Farming Options and Size: One of the HUGE pros for me is the size of the farm and the options you get to fill it. While I haven't unlocked everything yet, you can get sneak peaks of what you can unlock for ranch options by visiting the ranch shop, which has animals positioned outside and roaming. So far, I'm psyched, because you can do more than just your standard cows and chickens (which I'm somewhat fed up with). There are hints of peacocks and some kind of mink as farm animals, which is almost unheard of in these games. Yeah, Stardew Valley had dinosaurs, slimes, and rabbits, but they weren't all that special and getting them was a hassle. I'm excited to turn my MASSIVE farm into a mink/peacock haven. More on that point, you can farm a variety of vegetables, fruit trees, and flowers. Sprinklers aren't too difficult to unlock, so tilling, watering, and other various farm work isn't the majority of your day if you don't want it to be.- Updates and Roadmap: The game's title screen features separate tabs for recent updates and a road map! This is super fun to look at, because you can tell the developers aren't going to just cash out and leave and that they really care about the game. There are so many upcoming exciting updates, that I can't wait to start a new save once 1.0 comes out. This also helps negate having to navigate steam to find updates, which is handy.- Day Time Speed: This is a feature I've NEVER seen in a vanilla farming/life sim! In the options, you have the ability to change the SPEED OF TIME PASSED. I've slowed mine down to half, and I've gotten more out of the first season that you could ever do in Stardew. This can be a downside if you run out of stamina in the first few hours of the morning (which will happen a lot), but there are plenty of edible scavengables to *somewhat* help this. But you can always play at a normal speed and not drag the days out like me!(SPOILER)- Fast travel: One of the BEST features in the game you can unlock by doing the main quests, which is fast traveling. It costs nothing in resources to do, and there are several fast travel points. Starting out, you'll only have access to 2-3 points on the map, but even that helps rather than taking 1/3rd of the day to walk to the other side of the map. This really helps offset the negative aspect of having a very slow moving character.Cons: - Stamina: This could be because of my day time speed set to half, but it feels like you run out of stamina ridiculously fast. Eating food barely helps unless you're eating the most expensive crops. You get a little stamina growth each time you level up a skill, but it's incredibly small. We're talking +3 extra stamina when you have a pool of 450 and swinging a bug net once is almost 10 stamina. It does feel a little unbalanced.- Controls: This is by far my biggest complaint. I feel like this might be a personal gripe since my friend didn't share the same feeling, and I'm primarily a console/controller gamer. It feels very frustrating to have your character move in the direction of your mouse, even if your mouse is in the corner of the screen. I wouldn't mind this if the mouse was next to my character, but no matter where my mouse is, my character will turn towards it. This has resulted in me losing MANY bugs, which is upsetting. I've turned off this setting in the controls (which is an option) and it STILL happens. I'm not sure if this is a bug, but it's very frustrating. 14 hours in and I've sort of gotten used to it, but I just wish it wasn't like that in the first place. - Content: The game is early access, and I totally get that, but the content is very lacking in terms of story, quests, town activities, etc. They didn't really finish the first season. There are 2 major events in Spring and I wasn't able to participate in either of them, because they weren't added in yet but they obviously plan to. I really wish that they had finished the first year before deciding to release it, but hopefully we won't have to wait long for an update. I'll be starting a new character once 1.0 releases, but for now I suppose I'll just work on building a massive farm and goofing around.That's my review on Coral Island. The positives far outweigh the negatives (which I think were mostly personal), and I've really enjoyed this game so far. I'm extremely excited to see where it goes next! I highly recommend anyone who enjoyed Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, or Rune Factory to pick this up. I have a feeling it's going to be another game that's talked about for a long time. If you're worried about the lack of content, then I recommend waiting, wishlisting, and following for updates. Possibly even pick up while on sale, though I have to say I don't regret the $25 I've spent.

_childDocuments_.review: With early access since October 11, 2022, Coral Island, the newest farm simulator game, was officially released on November 14, 2023.Highlights:1. Narrative and Freedom:Coral Island offers a compelling narrative for farm simulation enthusiasts, reminiscent of the beloved Stardew Valley. The game provides a relaxing and enjoyable experience as players embark on a new farming adventure on the paradise island of Coral Island. The freedom to pursue personal objectives without the pressure of meeting predefined goals enhances the immersive gameplay.2. Rich Character Interactions:The game impresses with its well-developed characters, each possessing unique traits, preferences, and even favorite items. The attention to detail in character design and the inclusion of NPCs with distinct personalities contribute to a vibrant and lifelike in-game world. The ability to build relationships through gift-giving adds depth to the gaming experience.3. Aesthetically Pleasing Design:Coral Island stands out for its well-crafted design, blending 2D and 3D elements seamlessly. The soft and delicate designs, coupled with beautiful, colorful, and unsaturated visuals, create a visually appealing and cozy atmosphere. The game's soundtrack and ambient sounds enhance the overall immersive experience.4. Diverse Gameplay Elements:The game offers a variety of gameplay elements, including character customization, exploration, missions, and farm management. The inclusion of a journal tracking achievements and statistics, along with a reward system tied to skill improvement, adds depth and engagement to the overall farming simulator experience.Bugs:1. Technical Issues:Despite its visual appeal, Coral Island suffers from notable technical issues, particularly in terms of system requirements and gameplay performance. The game's recommended specifications may not be sufficient, leading to freezes, crashes, and a less-than-fluid experience during transitions.2. Progress Loss and Transition Delays:Players may encounter frustrating setbacks, such as progress loss due to unexpected game closures. Additionally, the game's transitions between locations, despite being part of an open-world concept, suffer from delays, affecting the overall fluidity of the gaming experience.3. Lack of Language Support:While Coral Island supports multiple languages, the absence of an interface and subtitles in Portuguese may be a drawback for Portuguese-speaking players. Expanding language support could enhance accessibility and cater to a broader audience.In conclusion, Coral Island impresses with its engaging narrative, rich character interactions, and aesthetically pleasing design. However, the game falls short in addressing technical issues and could benefit from additional language support, improving the overall player experience. However, everything mentioned here may change.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 4 hours now in the game, and from what I can see, I like it. Full disclosure, I kickstarted it on the art and premise, but have largely stayed away until the 1.0 release.I recommend the game with some caveats. First, it's not done, which is unfortunate given the 1.0 release on paper. There are some things which are still being worked on, (and some of those just came out in the recent patch). Things like Marriage, the Merfolk, side bits of story and quests. The game doesn't feel unfinished, but there are components that will def add value that are known and being developed still. Second, it is not perfectly optimized. The game hitches here and there, there are minor rendering slowdowns and slightly laggy bits. You can play through these, but it is a minor nuisance.The good: This is truly a modern farm sim in a lot of ways. A huge cast of interesting characters, a very progressive, ecological storyline, a big world to explore, it seems like a lot of items, complexity, and crafting at hand. Everything is gorgeous. The music is a delight, the slow unfurl of the story that engages you in this very immediate islander take on climate change is especially welcome. I want to know more about all these characters, and what representation at hand. Truly a gift from the developers to so intricately weave together what feels like a very alive community.The animations of SO MANY little things are spectacular. People's houses feel lived in, they feel personal, and unique. Everyone has a kind of voice in the world, and it shows.If you liked Stardew for how it massively advanced the genre, I firmly believe Coral Island will be the next major step forward. It's just on the way there, not quite at it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: It is very much still in early access, that is obvious. However, let's just say I've been nonstop playing for 3 days straight now. Is it very similar to Stardew Valley? _childDocuments_.review: Its the little things that keep me playing.While there is very little content, as of when I'm writing this review, I must say there is more work placed into this game than I had initially anticipated for an early access. Let me start by saying that this game is by no means complete, its very bare bones. HOWEVER, it's when I find myself very put off from lack of content that I see the most amazing work that was put in. Example 1: RainI was sitting for a good few minutes while it was raining in game completely mesmerised by the texturing of the rain movement against hard surfaces, be it leaves on a palm tree or the damn roof! The attention to detail to rain surface physics were mind blowing with how life-like it looked when it hit anything solid.Example 2: Placed FlooringNo, seriously, I mean it. The flooring you can place in your farm house. I'm not talkign about how nice it looks aesthetically. (TBH I couldn't care less half the time) That being said, ANGLED IMAGING! Literally the visualisation of these tiles is from an angle and will change based on how deep into your house you walk, allowing for a truly beautiful three-dimensional effect that I absolutely adore.Example 3: Character PersonalitiesI play ALOT of farming sims, to the point where its harder to name what I haven't played. Many of the characters within those can feel very washed up, phoned in, fake, or generally generic. I'm unbelievably shocked and ecstatic about how diverse the personalities of the islanders are. The first villager I actually spoke to was Leah and immediately put off by her attitude, then came Bree who I couldn't really tell if she was being nice or just channelling some sassy southern charm. Yet meeting Yuri and Zarah I was floored by HOW different everyone was and how it spanned all the villagers. All in all this game feels like the perfect marriage of Stardew Valley and Story of Seasons (Real Harvest Moon) and a smidge of AC. You can completely see all the love, support and effort that when into it while playing even with limited content. I definitely look forward to more updates and its official release! Thank you guys for all the hard work and keep going!!Also the signs switch from open to close, like i said, Its the little things.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a great time playing this game, but I've decided to shelve it for now and check it out again next year to see how it's coming along. Despite being labeled version 1.0, it still feels like it's in early access. So, as much as I want to, I can't really recommend Coral Island in its current state. I noticed that it tends to stutter quite a bit, which can be frustrating. The dialogue is good, but it can get a bit repetitive after a while. The biggest bummer was that the romantic conversations with NPCs don't feel much different from regular ones. I wish they'd acknowledge the player more or flirt a bit. Some of the animations, like waving and horse riding, for example, look a little stiff and could use some polish. The festivals are fun for the most part, but some of the mini-games, like the pet race and pumpkin smashing, could be better. There's also a handful of bugs that I've come across that others have also mentioned. Overall, it's a fun and relaxing game. I put in a generous amount of time and can honestly keep going, but I'd feel like I'd be doing the game a disservice by not playing it when it's fully fleshed out. Sadly, it just isn't there right now. I'm hoping that Stairway continues to take note of community feedback and work on making the game even better.

Foraging, growing crops, having farm animals, fishing, bug catching, as well as mining. As you get past all the normal farming mechanics in the game you will quickly learn that there is so much more to this game than a lot of the other farming sims that have graced us in the last few months including a story with giants and goddesses as well as a diving mechanic where you clean up the ocean. The dating mechanic and NPCs are really fleshed out as well which is great.Listen cozy gamers, I hear you when you say that you are so sick of every single farming sim being compared to stardew valley but genuinely, this is the absolute closest thing to a 3D stardew valley that you are going to find.

_childDocuments_.review: Though there may be good things about this game it is missing certain basic quality of life features combined with a stamina system that is overbearing, and a main line quest that so far appears to be a collect-a-thon that overall hurts this game to the point I cannot recommend it at this time.  The only reason why I am still playing it, is because I am a diehard Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Stardew Valley, and Sun Haven fan so I can handle games that are not quite as good (My profile avatar is from HM: ANB).So a few of the quality of life features that are missing: - No stamina use when tools do nothing.  If you accidentally water the same crop twice well count that extra stamina gone, or if you miss aim your pickaxe in the mine... well sorry you just wasted stamina. - Smart tool aiming.  Do not let tools target squares they cannot interact with.  In the mines my pickaxe loves to aim at the tiles next to the rocks I am trying to smash, which results in missing that pairs poorly with the previous missing quality of life feature.  To see a good example of smart tool aiming Sun Haven has this mastered. - Queued actions.  When I am hoeing or watering and click on the next tile before the previous action is finished, be smart enough to know to actually perform that action. - Hold to perform continuous actions.  Clicking on 100+ crops to harvest or water them is bad.  In other farming games they are smart enough to know that with the basic tools since they cannot be charged if the player holds down the action key let them do a continuous action so they don't kill their finger clicking on every single crop or tile.Stamina system: - It takes a base of 20 stamina to catch a fish and it takes 20 stamina to catch bugs.  Why is bug catching so stamina intensive?  Fishing makes sense but bug catching does not considering a miss swipe only costs 1 stamina. - You start out with 450 stamina which translates out to 150 actions (this does get better, but in early game first impressions matter).  Might sound like a lot, but every watering counts as an action.  So if you have a nice 10x10 field with 4 scarecrows that is 96 actions every day to water your crops in early game leaving only 162 stamina.  Might sound like a lot, but a trip into the mines will deplete that very fast. - Other activities outside the farm drain stamina fast resulting in you being left with the only thing you can do is foraging.  This in turn causes a huge chunk of the game to become gated in early game.  For example lets say I want to start raising some chickens, I need bronze ingots to make the coop.  Which means I need to do mining, but I have no stamina to do mining (and the ore spawn rate on the first floors is terrible, on one run I found no ore on floors 5, 6, and 7).Main plot line:So early game I am presented with two main goals: 1) Fetch a bunch of items for this quest, and 2) Fetch a bunch of different items for this quest.  I did not mind Stardew Valley bundles, but this game cranked it up to a level that it is off putting to me considering how a number of said items involve activities which drain stamina extremely fast and thus make them tedious to collect.  I am low on stamina and see a bug I might need, do I really want to waste 20 stamina on a bug I might not end up needing?  Meanwhile the town folk so far have not really shown any effort on their part for contributing to save their town that they supposedly treasure.  I am the new guy, why am I doing all the hard work to save their town/island?

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to be said about this game that is positive.  So first here's the caveats:While it's clearly still being improved upon. It feels like it's 1.0 release was pushed more by the publisher than the developers. The developers clearly have a lot of love for the game. I wish that they were given more time to the full release but understand that ROI and bottom line for publishers can make time constraints hard to balance against best laid plans and all. Over all the game is charming, and refreshing. It has some story-lines that really hit close to home and I recommend checking out the Reddit a bit if you'd like to get a better feel for the game in it's current state. You can adjust the in game speed time and there's a ton of fun aspects to the game that feel refreshing. I really enjoy what the under water area could be. It's not fully fleshed out so I wouldn't buy this for the mermaids just yet.This game feels like a more updated version of Stardew Valley and it even pays homage to the creator of stardew valley. That said, it does enough to differentiate itself from others in the genre. The sheer number of datables is really fun, when I rarely have more than one that falls into my type. This game has 6 which is really fun to me. Areas I wish it could improve upon: The interior decorating. Give players better ways to interact with horsesOffer a bike as an optionShow wheelchair users in the game and create a more accessible feel to the town. Obviously these are really odd things that I don't think are needed to make the game amazing. They just feel like they could offer more dimension to a game that already has a lot of unique aspects to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Some highlights:- You lose crops to crows before you're even allowed to craft scarecrows.- You get shorted cash when selling whole stacks of produce at once.-You face a pretty hefty in-game punishment for needing to use an unstuck option because the map is buggy.- Or you plant a five-day crop on day 1 and it isn't ready on day 6 for some reason. Not individual plants like I missed watering them, but the whole crop. I water first thing every day except on rainy days, it's habit from similar games. There was a rain day on day 3 or 4, so did the game not register the rain? I'm guessing so because the crops were ready on day 7. Very frustrating because that failed an item request errand.I like a lot of parts of this game, but a lot of other parts feel janky and rough. Like tool use, you can't change tools until some period of time after use, it doesn't even seem tied to the use animation. So many times I have whacked a rock and tried to swap to my axe to whack a log only to waste energy by still having the pick equipped. Same with watering. You can't chain crop watering, and instead you have to wait for the animation to finish each time. There does seem to be a very narrow sweet spot where you can activate toward the end of the animation to quickly start again, but it's inconsistent to hit so watering by hand is annoying which is bad considering it's such a big part of the early game. And why are we still using a watering can in 2024? Where's my garden hose like in SunnySide?Clearing trash is similarly annoying because it seems hard to reliably hit more than two or three nodes at once. With proper positioning and aim, you can hit like five or six, but I can't seem to manage it all that often and frequently find myself going after single nodes which wastes a lot of energy and time. This portion makes me think that maybe the game was designed for controller use  with keyboard and mouse getting just a basic implementation to cover that base. Furthering that feel is that advancing dialogue requires different mouse buttons depending on the type of dialogue, as well as a few other things where the controls don't feel intuitive compared to all the other games like this I've played. Like inventory management. You're severely limited in how much you can carry starting out and can't drop anything on the ground to clear space to make a chest, you have to destroy a stack of whatever. Then, even with a chest placed, you can't pick up a stack to move it with either left or right mouse, both buttons kick the stack to the chest . To rearrange your inventory while you're accessing a chest, you have to kick the item/stack to the chest, then pick it up from there to place where you want. So annoying. Just make it where you Shift+Click to kick the whole stack and let left mouse  pick the stack up like in pretty much every other game with an inventory to manage.The diving portion is a cool concept, but the animation bothers me. You're wearing a small SCUBA-like setup, and yet you ponderously bound across the seafloor like you're wearing an archaic diving rig with the full bronze helmet and heavy suit. I get that they don't want to have to code in three-dimensional movement like you're swimming, that's fine, but make the animation more like what you'd expect for someone swimming along coral reefs and such. It really breaks any sense of immersion to simply be walking along the sea floor. And here's a design idea for you, remove collision from the trash piles and such to give the player a better sense of depth for being underwater.Also, I think that the energy management is unnecessary for a few reasons. It's a complaint I've had about a lot of games like this, because I don't see the need to have two activity limits to manage, day cycle for time and energy for actions. It's a chill single player experience, not anything competitive. Get rid of one.  But also, food that you can make early on requires nearly three times as much energy to get the materials as what you get out of eating it, while food that you can purchase is just too expensive with too little energy gain to be useful. It's like you're not even supposed to bother with energy recovery, just go to bed at eleven in the morning.Lastly, this game could really benefit from modding support via Steam Workshop. It's one thing to have a vision or design goal, but ultimately a game's merits are determined by who plays it and how they want to play it., it's pretty decent and fun for the most part  and beyond that overt clone vibe, it has a lot of nice positives. I'm aggravated due to a lot of the above being piled up all at once because I just started a new game twice and wasted over a dozen hours of gameplay, so I'll revisit this review once I've gotten further in the game and try to add some more detailed positive notes to balance out the negatives.Edit: Scratch that, just in the twenty or so minutes of returning to the game after posting the review, I came back to add four more things that really feel like they shouldn't be in a game that is supposedly out of Early Access. I'm not recommending this game at this time, I'll revisit later after more updates have rolled out.Re-edit: Added another bug that shouldn't be in a full release title; you don't get paid the full sum when selling an entire stack of something at once. You have to manually sell each item in the stack one at a time to ensure you get paid in full. I first noticed this because I glanced at my wallet and chuckled because I was 2 dollars shy of having 1337. Sold a stack of 28 potatoes which sell for 75 each so I was expecting 2100 back for a total 3435 only to end up with 3335. When you sell a stack, it pops up the sale as the correct amount, but that isn't added in full to your wallet.Re-re-edit: There's this handy looking "I'm Stuck" button on the pause screen, which is a nice touch considering the  and all that. Never tried it out until just now when I actually got stuck behind one of the buildings in the forest . When you click the "I'm Stuck" button, I would have assumed it simply ported you back to your farm and that was that. Maybe they would be clever and have it log your x,y coordinates so they can try to find what you got stuck on. Nope. It gives a warning that if you use it, you'll be ported back to the farm, have your character's stamina for the day completely drained, automatically end the day, and then slap you with a stamina penalty for the following day.So... they're going to punish you for finding an issue with their map and having to use a 'cheat' to get out of it."But it's to keep people from abusing it!" Then why give it? Or put a time limit on using it. Besides, it's a single player game, there's no such thing as cheating. If I want infinite ammo in my sp game, or infinite stamina, or health, or free crafting, or be able to zip around the map really fast that's not an issue with the player, that's an issue with whatever aspect of the game is boring and not wanting to deal with it. Your map is buggy, thanks for the unstuck option but remove the punishment for needing it, it's not cheating.I'm at the character limit, but there's so much more to say about this  game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only mostly through year one, but here goes.I try to avoid comparisons to Stardew Valley, especially in the farming sim/RPG genre. Usually those comparisons end up being the basic staples of the genre and they don't allow room for the game to stand on its own.That said, comparisons to Stardew Valley are unavoidable when it comes to this game. At its heart, from a gameplay perspective, it feels like someone took one part Animal Crossing New Horizons and four parts Stardew Valley and stuck it in a blender. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but the spectre of its predecessor looms large.THAT SAID. This game is still unique enough to stand on its own. Not to spoil anything, but the mysticism and fantastical elements are MUCH more explicit and involved than in SDV. There are more characters, but because there's no friendship decay it doesn't feel overwhelming. There's more to explore, more mechanics, more characters, and honestly out of all the farming sims I've seen and played this one is pretty solid and unique.I've only played since 1.1, since I usually avoid EA games and I'm not involved in the fandom or community surrounding this game. So this perspective is from someone who came in blind to the finished (?) product. I'd love to see more- romanceable giants, maybe, or being allowed to romance Antonio. _childDocuments_.review: In short I would recommend this game for those who like cozy games and don't mind one that can be a little more difficult. Longer explanation: Obviously this kind of game lends itself to "inclusion" of people that can be otherwise excluded from life and things in general. It does a good job of including all kinds of people and age ranges. The game is a cross between Animal Crossing and The Sims games. More detailed and difficult than than Animal Crossing; but in some ways not as detailed as the Sims. Not quite a fair comparison to The Sims since the The Sims is not a farming game. That being said there is a lot of detail in this game and I found the "Halloween" activity to be very enjoyable and you can tell the makers put a lot of love into the details at the activity. The game still has some bugs. For example: I did have an odd thing happened where I was locked in the craft menu and I could do anything so I had to restart the game which meant I lost all that I had done within that day. Which brings me to my biggest complaint is that you can't save the game whenever you want. The game is saved when your character goes to sleep. So I have gone to sleep at times to make sure I don't loose my progress if something significant happened that day which meant I also lost a full day of stuff I could have done. Have played for over 30 hours so far and I have really enjoyed the game; particularly the romance mechanic since it is fun to see if you can get a character to become your significant other. There is a good portion of the map that is "fogged" out. If the fogged out area represents the full map that gets revealed as you play than the full map is huge. Also besides the bugs there is room for improvement for example the NPC only reveal a few things that that like and just keep repeating what they like rather than revealing other things they like as you talk to them. You have to do a lot of talking with them before you even scratch the surface of what they like so it becomes a guessing game and there is no way to ask them what they like either. But besides any negatives I have mentioned I would buy the game again (if I had too); because I have enjoyed it that much. oh one more thing the game does not hold your hand and tell you how things work; but thankfully there is info on the internet.

_childDocuments_.review: While the art style is fantastic and the atmosphere is very pleasant, there's several things about this game that just feels...off, to me. I first noticed it when the intro cutscene played and it was an exact beat for beat replica of the stardew intro:-Player leaves big city and moves to a small rural community-Greeted by town mayor-Mayor takes you to your new cabin-Cabin is being fixed up by local carpenter(s) -They do a bad job so you have to upgrade the house-The farmland is overgrown and you're tasked with fixing it-Mayor gives you tools and seedsNext thing I noticed was the player moves incredibly slow for how big the map is. Idk if you can move faster later on but my god is it a chore to move around the islandNext is that the game is uncomfortably quiet. You get small jingles (that dont loop) when inside interiors but walking around the island it is dead quiet. No background music, hardly any ambience, just the sound of your footsteps. My pros:* You can make a lot of Artisan products * There's a lot of insects, fish, and forageable stuff* Cute aesthetics and a lot of customisation to play with! You have indoor and outdoor decor.* Animals are very cute* Mini games and events!* I'm 150 hours in and there's still so many things to learn and farm!* Mermaids! How often do you see them in farming games?Cons:* Consistent crashes when I customise furniture in certain buildings. (I do understand that the game is still developing and will have future updates.)* Combat and mining: It isn't as engaging, the cave systems may be randomised but can get boring after a while. * Pets: Can't have more than one and you don't really get rewarded for building a relationship with them. Coral Island is a stunning game with lots of hours of replayability. I'm going to put more hours into it!

_childDocuments_.review: After no-lifing this game for 22 hours, here are my impressions as a long-time farming sim player. I'll separate it into the good and the bad.The good:- First of all, the game runs really well so far. Loading screens are pretty short, fps is perfect on max graphics on my computer, and I haven't experienced any crashes/significant bugs as of yet.- The ambience + graphics + music in the game are really nice. There's a lot of care and detail put into the environments, and I really enjoy the art direction and style. The soundtrack isn't groundbreaking, but it's very relaxing and suits the game a lot. I've really enjoyed all the little touches they added to make the town feel more alive (seeing dogs playing in the fountains, cats walking on roofs, the lil frog and lizard dudes chillin around the island, and so on). The water also looks very nice, which is a big plus for a game set on an island.-The core gameplay loop is very enjoyable. Farming is usual for a farming sim (main things I appreciate are how the qol is pretty good. I never end up targeting the wrong square or struggling to place my sprinklers in the right formation, and watering the plants is surprisingly painless considering how much I normally hate doing it lol). Fishing is decent; I think the minigame is a little too easy, but it's still pretty relaxing. Diving is pretty basic, but I find it really relaxing, which is in big part due to how nice the environment looks. For the most part, it's pretty standard for a farming sim, but in a good way.-I really like how varied the townspeople are. It feels like I always get new dialogue when I talk to them, the portraits for the characters look nice, and I like all of them. Being able to talk to the animals is also really cute (and their portraits are REALLY CUTE). The cast of the game is pretty expansive, which means that if you're the type of person that likes to max out friendship for everyone, I imagine it can get pretty overwhelming, but  since I didn't feel pressured to do so I personally found it nice how there's so many characters. I like how you can see them just doing stuff around town, like yoga sessions or beach volleyball and so on. I can't speak much on heart events as of yet, since I got a little too addicted to the farming/diving aspect of the game so I've been slacking on my gift giving.-I already said this technically, but the game is REALLY pretty. The lighting is nice, textures are nice, and especially the aesthetic and art design. I love the way the whole game looks. -QOL is nice. It's easier to place buildings in this game than in stardew, and while I haven't gotten too much into decorating my farm and everything, it feels a lot easier to place fences/floor tiles/etc.-Combat is basic but feels nice. there are only two types of monsters in the mines so far (though I assume they'll add more) and afaik you can only use a sword as of now, but it feels pretty decent, though basic.The bad:- Standard early access jankiness. Runs the range of barns/coops being kind of awkward to enter once you upgrade them, bc you have to stand in a very particular square that is actually a little far from the door. I've noticed that sometimes I lose the ability to scroll through my item hotbar for a bit, though I'm not sure if that's maybe an actual feature that I just don't know the keybind for. There's nothing that has been incredibly bothersome, but there's definitely room for improvement in these aspects.- Mining is rather tedious. Compared to stardew (just using this bc I imagine most people interested in this game have played that too), the mines are a lot bigger, which means more rocks, but at the same time there's less ore/gem nodes/etc? So it means you spend a LOT of time just hitting boring rocks to get to the next floor, without getting much ore for your efforts. The game doesn't really require huge amounts of ore, so it's not that the resource is too scarce compared to how much you need, but it just feels unsatisfying in terms of effort/reward. You can craft explosives to make it easier, but since there's so little ore per floor, it kind of feels counterproductive. You really have to hit so many rocks to get to the next floor sometimes. This is my main gripe with the game so far, since mining is required to craft a lot of items/get upgrades.- Obviously, unfinished content. I don't /really/ consider this bad, because obviously the game is in early access, but it is something to keep in mind for playing it right now. There are some unfinished textures sprinkled around the world (mostly as you get further into the mines/ocean), skill trees aren't finished, cows and chickens are the only available barn animals, social events are unfinished in some cases. This will obviously not be an issue once the full game releases, but if you're looking to drop a lot of time on the game right now, you'll run out of content in certain aspects since it's still being worked on.Overall, I think this game is really, really promising. I'm normally pretty wary about early access games, but I've been having incredible amounts of fun playing this, even given the unfinished content. The game isn't groundbreaking or anything, but it does what it's meant to do really well (which is being a comfy, relaxing farming/life sim). I love it so far, and I'd 100% recommend it to anyone who's interested in trying it out. My biggest issue with the game is honestly that it's so fun I'm sad that I'll have to wait for the completed release!

_childDocuments_.review: It's just Stardew Valley.Coral Island's a farm simulation game that's still in development as I write this. Your character moves to a tropical island where they start running a farm, and get involved in the lives of the depressed locals as a soulless corporation tries to buy up the island.Just like in Stardew Valley.You go into caves in the woods near your house to fight monsters, and dig up metal to upgrade your tools, or geodes that you take to the local blacksmith to break open and reveal treasures.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's an empty museum it's up to you to refill by finding jewels and ancient artifacts.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's a supernatural helper who'll open new areas or unlock extra features after you give them all the things in certain groups of items they ask you to find.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's a festival where you can get free friendship points with everybody in town if you add something really tasty to the potluck soup.Just like in Stardew Valley.The highest upgrade for your tools is made with a magic purple metal.Just like in Stardew Valley.Swinging farm tools uses up energy, but swinging swords mysteriously doesn't.Just like in Stardew Valley.The general store's closed on Wednesday.Just like in Stardew Valley.Basically, it's Stardew Valley with better art, and a few areas where they go one step farther. Like besides fishing, there's also a bug-catching feature. Or like how SV talked about mermaids living near the beach, this game lets you go scuba diving and actually meet them.But me, I've already played the hell out of Stardew Valley. I'm not super excited by a game that obviously took all its cues from a game I've already played the hell out of.If you liked Stardew Valley, but wished there was a bit more content, or a few more romance options, this is the perfect game for you! It does what I'm sure it set out to do, and it does do it pretty well. This is a good farm/life sim game with a lot of things to check out.But if you were satisfied with the game this is based on and already sunk hundreds of hours into that, like I was, Coral Island's just more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. as a stardew enjoyer, it is so enjoyable and fun and expands on a lot of the things I would look for in a game like this like no other does! one of my favorite additions is from the newest update, where you can ask NPCs to hang out and do different activities around the town (which is so so cute with the romanceable NPCS of course!) the feature has a lot more detail than I expected-- you can pick from a dozen different locations that offer a interesting array of things, from spa days at the salon to picnics, yoga, fishing at the lake, visiting the museum or volunteering, playing volleyball, shell hunting at the beach, getting tacos at the food truck, and so much more. it's seriously one of the best features, trust me. another one of my favorite features is the artstyle, and how everyone wears different outfits for each season that you can see in their portraits and in their profiles in the relationships tab (where you can cycle through each outfit and expressions!) everyone has different expressions, and their own dialogues, interests, and hang out spots around town. god, it's so cute. everything I ever wanted from SDV and more.there's a lot to do, from mining, fishing, ranching, farming, and my favorite-- diving and cleaning up the ocean. it's borderline addicting. I'm excited about the  section, as someone who loves  it's sooo cute and fun.some of the only downsides to the game sofar have been: special shoutout for wakuu, alice, and eva, my favorite npcs. astronomer who dyes his hair a different color for every season, and has a chicken graphic that sticks out from his shirt pocket? a sweet girl that wears cozy outfits and loves the summer, with a twin sister? and I buy bread from Sam's everyday, just for Eva (it's the thought that counts!)glad I backed this game all those years ago and am delighted with every new update that comes out. worth the buy at this point, new and old purchases, for sure! if you've been on the fence about this game because of early access and updates, definitely grab it. or, on sale if you're really doubtful. you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: While still in very very early development, there's plenty of things to do, plot to explore, characters to meet and, crucially for these kinds of games, ways to customise your farm layout, aesthetic and character outfits. What's even better is the distinct new flavour of sim this is, with plenty of southeast asian influences and specifically Indonesian input. From the big overarching themes of environmentalism and wildlife conservation, to little creepy folkloric ghosts that may turn up on dark windy nights to snatch a few valuables from under your nose. It's new, creative, and the gameplay is reasonably smooth for such an early release game. Already enjoying myself immensely, after decades of playing harvest Moon, Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley and even action sims such as Elder Scrolls - if you like any of these, chances are you'll love Coral Island. A plus is the small and dedicated developer, a trend I am absolutely loving in the Indie gaming world. Definitely keeping an eye out not just for this game, but for anything else they might come out with in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now I cannot recommended this game, because I find it to be quite deceitful to advertise this game as full release as it is clearly still in early access. Here are a few examples. The first two points might be a design choice but I don't understand why you go into full release when these "teething troubles" still exist.- Inventory controls have not been thought through yet. you click on an item and it goes directly into the open chest. you click on an item in the chest and you're able to place it where you want in your inventory. But you cannot swap it with an item already in your inventory. you have to put it on an empty slot. Also you cannot split stacks. If you want to grab half of the trash from your 999 trash stack, you have to press a button 500 times or pres and hold it for a minute or two.- hitting an enemy three consecutive times makes you stagger them which means they get pushed a few meters away from you and stops them from attacking for a moment. Weirdly, the pushing back also lets them glitch through obstacles which you then have to circumvent to use the staggering to attack them- flickering textures on the edge of your screen as well as flickering shadows in general- filling a machine with resources does not work with click and hold. you always have to click 20 times to fill up the recycling machine for example.- when your energy gets low, the colors in the game desaturate and your character starts to move more slowly. There's a button in the game menu to turn that off. Sadly that button has no effect.- highly variable loading times. I have installed on an SSD and entering the same building can sometimes take 2 seconds to load, sometimes 15- you can own a pet but as of now my pet has never left the house and does exactly nothing but sitting in its bed from dawn till dusk.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this but it's hard to recommend a game that came out of early access nearly a year ago and isn't complete despite being on version 1.1 and asking for $30. There were some things I enjoyed, hence the 70 hours, but they were mostly mindless, repetitive activities like mining or cleaning the ocean that were easy to mentally check out from and spend hours doing. At some point, I realized  I was just playing it to scratch the farm sim itch. The characters feel hollow. Many heart events don't even involve the player and a lot of them are straight out of other media, like bits from Friends. It goes beyond homage and inspiration, and instead just directly copies these well-known scenes. It reads like the writers didn't have ideas (were there professional writers involved with this game?). Honestly, almost everything feels kind of hollow. So many things feel like they're in the game because that's what farm sims are supposed to have, not because it was meaningful for this game.I should note that there ARE some good points here. The game is gorgeous and I love the tropical setting. The character appearances are cute. It's great to see aspects of cultures that you don't often see incorporated into games! When the developers split away from their "inspirations" and make unique choices, that's when the game shines. But that doesn't happen often, and it almost makes me more disappointed with the whole thing. Someone involved at some point clearly had a creative vision and I wish that was harnessed more. But considering this game received over $1.5 million in backing in 2021, multiple promised rewards still aren't or will never be available, and the game still isn't complete, I really can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Worth the price for what's in the game already, and there's plenty more coming down the road. Multiplayer is not yet implemented.Coral Island is a farming life sim in the vein of Stardew Valley and its predecessors, with some inspiration from Animal Crossing. The game goes for a Pacific island theme with an emphasis on environmental/ecological concerns. Having spent some time in early access, 1.0 has arrived, and I think it's worth a buy.Before I get into the good/neutral/bad, I want to touch on some of the criticisms I've seen leveled at the game as a farming sim. Many have pointed out the heavy similarities between the core features of Coral Island and Stardew Valley, oftentimes with accusations of stealing ideas from the game. Those folks clearly have no knowledge of the history of video games and their evolution. Every game in a given genre takes ideas from those that came before and iterates or puts a twist on it. In some genres, many features stay almost the same through the years. Stardew Valley would not exist without Harvest Moon, and Coral Island would not be the game it is without Stardew Valley.The Good- The farming and ranching aspects are well done and in line with my expectations for the genre- The characters are complex people with their own histories and ongoing stories- The town rank system is a nice way to show the progression and ongoing improvement of the town- I like the resource split of the mines and the diving sections- Great variety of ranch animals, crops, and PETS!- Like any good farming sim, there's no need to rush- Lots of great decorative options to gussy up your farm- Everyone is insanely attractiveThe Neutral- There's some QOL things that I think are missing, such as holding down a button to continually plant seeds. Right now, you have to click for every single one until you get improved sprinklers.- No Multiplayer yet.- In one of the festivals, there's what looks like a cockfighting ring. That's not what the animals ultimately compete in, but it's kind of questionable and poorly explained.- Having come from early access with a chunk of change to start out with, there's some sequence breaking with the progression that the game didn't know how to handle.- On that same note, I really flew through the overall progression of the mines and diving sections with such a strong head start. I'm worried I'll hit a wall.- None of the fun little TV shows seem to have more than one episode.The BadMy first point here is a gripe I have with development. The devs have declared 1.0 to be feature complete as they envisioned it without the extras that were funded on Kickstarter. While I'm not a fan of that way of looking at things, it's clear that there are some things that are NOT feature complete. When I see devs in the Discord mention that they're still working on heart events and that there's a plan to re-do a storyline or expand on certain sections, that to me does not come across as 1.0. It feels shady and I'm not thrilled that this is the route they've taken.- Lack of accessibility features. Many features rely on repetitive clicking.- Mining and combat both kind of suck. Combat especially is difficult to level up.- Like Stardew, fishing also isn't that great.Happy to update this review down the line or if there are any features folks are curious about.

_childDocuments_.review: I've sunk countless hours into farming sim games of all kinds, beginning all the way back with GBA Harvest Moon series, an experience that I can say with pretty high certainty is shared among fellow Indonesians who are also into farming sims (this game's developers included). For most Indonesians, HM is *the* reference point when talking about farming sims, much more so than Stardew Valley or any other later iteration of the genre. It's not even close; *all* Indonesian news and reviews of Coral Island that I have seen unanimously compared the game to HM series instead of SDV. Thus, when I read English reviews saying that the game is mostly an SDV copy, it's actually pretty funny because SDV itself was intentionally made as an HM clone with more content and an improved gameplay experience. The same can be said of Coral Island, and I'm not complaining.Most of the base game mechanics in Coral Island are shared with HM and SDV, but there are lots of additional content even in the current early access state. You may farm, mine, fish, scavenge items, raise animals, make offerings, donate to museums, celebrate festivals, all of the things you can also do in many similar games. However, it also has a unique environmentalist flair with the ocean trash collection and recycling mechanics, as well as extensive arrays of plants, animals, and items to farm/raise/fish/catch (though some will not be available until future updates). Not to mention the diverse NPCs to interact and develop relationships with.Art style-wise, it's not particularly groundbreaking, but the mixture of 3D models and 2D illustrations in this fits perfectly. I like that the game doesn't go for chibi-like aesthetics and gives a more realistic proportion (though still cartoonish) to the 3D models. The landscapes of the land and the ocean are done beautifully, and I really love the shiny, wet rendering of the town during rainy days. The music can be better but at least it's comfortable enough to listen to.For all its similarities with other farming sims, Coral Island is still a charming game with its own personality. Do give it a chance if you love farming sims in general, or have been wanting to play one but don't quite like HM/SOS and SDV aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY:Plays like a 3D, heavily modded Stardew Valley. Exactly like Stardew Valley. I supported this game through kickstarter. i did not know it was going to be an exact copy of STARDEW VALLEY. The main plot is the same (big corporation comes into to ruin the natural beauty) except tweaked to fit the location.I've only seen one festival but it was exactly the same as Stardew Valley (luau with a potluck soup)Edit: I have played another festival and it was very original and I commend the developers for their creativity. The secondary plot is the same; you donate items to bundles to unlock new areas and restore the community. The mining system operates the same way, the NPC gifting and hearts system works the same. The house upgrades operate the same wayThere's a small ape that sells you stuff in an abandoned house in the woods, just like in Stardew Valley, and hes named "Concerned Monkey"I know a lot of people say "oh all farming sims are like that" yes. i understand that. however, that does not mean that every farming sim is a copy of the last popular one that came out.There is a difference between being inspired by a game and copying a game.Stardew Valley did not copy Harvest Moon, it was inspired by it. Coral Island has copied from Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing; plot-for-plot, mechanic-for-mechanicWhen I back a project for $45 I expect it to not cheaply plagiarize from a game I have already sunk 1.5k hours into. This game has the potential to be great. I like it's diverse cast of characters, and the diving aspect is grand. However the obvious copying has made me incredibly disappointed in this game so far.##########################################################################COMPUTER DEMAND;I don't know anything about computers. At all. However, I do know that this game should not eat up that much memory.I can't have any other application open while playing this game. Discord? NO. Steam? NO. Google so I can refer to the wiki? ABSOLUTELY NOT. This is the only game I have ever encountered this kind of memory demand with. I had this computer built so I could play games like ARK: Survival Evolved on max graphicsThis little farming sim should not break my computer the way it does##########################################################################As I continue to play the game and as i gets updated I will put more information here and/or correct my original opinion. Edit #1. I've played a few more of the festivals and it was something new, and I very much enjoyed it. A lot of people say that all farming games are like this. Yeah the vibes are similar, but as i stated before, when I spend $45 on a game I expect it to have a unique and interesting plot. This does not, so I'm very disappointed in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what Harvest Moon wishes it could be. Also, I really appreciate how most areas and paths are connected in some way so there are very few dead ends. Characters: There are a ton of NPCs (over 60 if I remember correctly) and about 20 of them are marriage candidates (although marriage and higher heart events arent implemented yet). The emotive character art makes the NPCs feel more engaging and the dialogue is very expansive. For example, I've talked to Scott and Theo almost every day for 3 seasons and I really don't think I've seen them say the same lines twice. There are a few NPCs that are newer additions and don't have as much dialogue (Mark, Wakuu, etc) but I'm sure by 1.0 they will be as fleshed out as the rest. name: Crusader Kings III
detailed_description: Chapter III available now! Starter Edition About the Game Your legacy awaits. Choose your noble house and lead your dynasty to greatness in a Middle Ages epic that spans generations. War is but one of many tools to establish your reign, as real strategy requires expert diplomatic skill, mastery of your realm, and true cunning . Crusader Kings III continues the popular series made by Paradox Development Studio, featuring the widely acclaimed marriage of immersive grand strategy and deep, dramatic medieval roleplaying. Take command of your house and expand your dynasty through a meticulously researched Middle Ages. Begin in 867 or 1066 and claim lands, titles, and vassals to secure a realm worthy of your royal blood. Your death is only a footnote as your lineage continues with new playable heirs, either planned… or not. Discover a sprawling simulated world teeming with peasants and knights, courtiers, spies, knaves and jesters, and secret love affairs. An extensive cast of historical characters can be romanced, betrayed, executed, or subtly influenced. Explore a vast medieval map stretching from the snowswept Nordic lands to the Horn of Africa, and the British Isles in the west to the exotic riches of Burma in the east. Claim, conquer, and rule thousands of unique counties, duchies, kingdoms, and empires. Each character is larger than life, with traits and lifestyle choices determining their actions and schemes. Prompt fear and dread as you rule with an iron fist, or inspire your subjects with magnanimous deeds. Genetics can be passed along to your children, be it the gift of genius or crippling stupidity. Groom your heir with the appropriate guardians or educate them yourself. If found wanting, marry them off or despatch them through other means. Customize your ruler and noble house, from appearance to attributes, and create a monarch worthy of all their inherited virtues and vices. Govern an ever-evolving realm and grant titles to whom you see fit - or usurp your liege to claim their crown as your own. Be wary of rivals, from restless serfs to revengeful concubines. The shadows stir frequently, and danger lurks around every darkened corner. Recruit agents and other unsavory elements to undermine, blackmail, or murder those who stand in your path. Or be inspired by the bard and ballad, and seduce your way to power and influence. Blood will flow. Assemble men-at-arms units and powerful knights. Manage your battlefield tactics and armies. Raid and plunder nearby lands or hire mercenaries and Holy Orders for your major conflicts. Be a pious king to invite the religious powers to your side, or design your own faith as you battle between everlasting fame or eternal damnation. Bring novel innovations to your culture and construct mighty castles and bastions to increase the wealth, prestige, and security of your realm. The paths to follow are limitless: experience thousands of dynamic events and life-altering decisions tailored to each and every conceivable situation and character. There are countless ways of securing and keeping your place in the history books.

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit,  I was very excited for Crusader Kings III.  I was sitting at my PC, waiting to let it download.  Over the top with joy.  My expectations were high, and for the most part it delivered.I have played near a thousand hours on CKII between my two Steam accounts.  I own every DLC for both CK2, and EU4.  I play them religiously, and they are my main go to games, CK2 winning most of that go to.CKIII has done a lot I really wanted to be done in CK2, I like the map system, how baronies are their own little "province", I love the Character Portraits (though I do wish there was a "Family Portrait" mode so I could share with friends, I look the secrets and hooks (always hated how you only ever got one chance to reveal a bastard), and I love how more focused this version of Crusader Kings is on intrigue and diplomacy; while war is always there if you need it.That is not to say it is perfect (it for sure beats CK2 base game), for example I really like the artifacts system a lot, I wish the popular feature of renaming your grandchildren was in this game (was a late addition to CK2, but one of my most used tools), and most importantly to me, map modes.  Perhaps I have missed them, but I want to see my vassal map mode, and while I can when I click on a vassal, it goes away if I click off their portrait.  CKIII will for sure have some DLC coming that will add in a lot of the missing features, and while it is not my favourite policy, I do accept it.  What other games can you play for 8+ years and still have a blast playing like CK2?  What other games can you sink 1000 hours in and still be learning new things?  Sure it is expensive, but I feel it is worth it, especially with the amount of sales Paradox has.

_childDocuments_.review: Typical flaws a paradox game has. Unfinished game design. Dead mechanics. Stupid AI, this time they really surpassed themselves. Deleting mechanics, just because they can't handle them and people abused them. Unrealistic reaction of AI to events. For exanple I had a extreme stable empire, the moment my Leader died a girl became king and instantly my whole empire attacked me (even though there are many female leaders of katholic countries). In CK2 you could at least save-scum and select any other character in this save, but this is no longer possible, you can choose only one of 3 very narrow relatives.This game can be super unpredictable as by far not everything is explained. This leads to frustrating moments. ah and yeah the "encyclopedia", really good stuff, just that it isn't.The battle-system is more like EU4, which is good and bad. Its more unpredictable than eu4, but at least kinda explained, even though it doesn't make any sense in many regards. For example if I have debt, my army fights worse. Why? 300 gold of debt, if you have an income of 50 per month is nothing at all. Debt mechanic in general is very obscure and not explained in the game, what happens if you are in debt.My Problem at the moment with the game is, that it is very casual and easy actually, far too easy in my view, if there weren't stupid unpredictable things that destroy your save. Like the whole empire collapsing because a girls is king. There should be possibilities to stabilize your empire for longer and conquering shouldn't be so easy. I mean with some clicks and tricks you can conquer complete kingsdoms. So in 150 years or so you control half of europe and then? You must watchout that your heir is not a girl (unless you make your own religion), give gifts to your vassals and continue to snack one kingdom after the other. You can do some things to "leave your mark in the world", but then? The most interesting part in my view is to make the "ultimate dynasty" with only characters that have very good traits.And yeah the hardest difficulty is "normal". At least they are honest.Anything else about this game is actually very good to be honest.But prepare for the DLC army.

_childDocuments_.review: Grand strategy games can get a bit sprawl-y, a bit "too much to do,", and this game is no exception. Paradox did a good job on Stellaris in sort-of forcing you to not micromanage absolutely everything, and enjoy the storytelling. The systems are similar here, but feel less effective. The worst part of this game is whatever the endgame is.Combat is mostly shallow and unsatisfying. Anyone familiar with Paradox games understands this. It's mostly "who has the bigger numbers, unless you're a Militarist," with some exceptions of course.Having said all that: this is about as good as this genre gets. Not a lot of new ground broken (though this game looks and feels several degrees better than its predecessor, the UI is sublime), but it's great for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Tough to exaggerate how fun the game is conceptually. Despite my lack of familiarity with the tutorial leader (some Irish Petty King) the game quickly enmeshed me in the drama of a loveless marriage with only one surviving son. In an effort to repair my marriage I sent said son back to my wife (his mom) as a Ward (after his previous Guardian, (a brother I think, had died in one of my ill-advised wars), which seemingly fixed our marriage, as she warmed up to the king and decided they were soulmates, eventually resulting in another pregnancy. Then, in the same month, her Ward/son died of typhus and she died in childbirth. I barely managed to get another heir up and running before the Petty King (now ruling most of Ireland) died, leaving a chaotic mess with a bunch of vassals that hated me and a son more disposed to diplomacy than warfare. No idea what's next for this "tutorial" dynasty but the strength of the games' systems and delightful/horrifying storytelling that flows from its systems seems highly replayable. The complimentary side serving of fascinating historical insights is just the cherry on top. The abundance of stats, attributes, focus/dynasty trees and strategic decisions gives it all depth and a field of infinite choices.
