_childDocuments_.review: This game is missing it's Aragaminess which is the only way I can describe what the first game had. Don't get me wrong you can certainly have fun in this game with or without a friend but with the repeating missions and areas that artificially increase your play time it just wasn't what I was looking for. Aragami 2 definitely leaned more heavily into the fast paced action side of stealth action and in turn (for me) has become a glorified game of leap frog.:1. Double jump (either behind or in front cause they can't see you either way)2. Dash on top of them (because they all have an affinity to disregard anything above there forehead)3. Air assassinate (Animation is the same as ground animation so no time loss)4. Repeat step 1-3 of Operation leap frog onto next target5. If spotted or out of stamina, hide and wait to commence operation again

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say that I absolutely love the first game and sadly this game throws out everything that made the first game special. I still really enjoy this game and it is a very fun experience but don't expect it to be anything like the original. Honestly my biggest complaint is that Aragami 2 ignores much of the lore established in the first game. Shadows no longer matter, you being an aragami is not even special since there is an entire community of them, and you now have your raven abilities without having your bird. With that being said it sucks that the devs ignored so much from the original.So why did I end up giving this game a recommendation? It's honestly because the game is still solid and enjoyable. It has a much larger storyline and it is still just as satisfying finding creative ways to slice every enemy apart without being seen. I do hope to see this series continue but hopefully they go back to hiding in the Shadows and discourage being detected.

_childDocuments_.review: For this game coming out literally yesterday, It is a very clean and polished experience. My buddy and I are about 5 hours in. This includes, playing the levels and also searching for collectibles and blueprints hidden away in tough to find areas and achieving Ghost (never being detected) and Demon (killing every hostile on the map). So far we haven't gotten too much of the story as the missions are not exactly tied into the whole big plot right now. They feel a bit more like filler missions to increase your xp and level. Hopefully we get into a bit more of the story between the difference of awakend and normal Aragami.The gameplay is vastly different from the first game, no longer having to manage and use shadows to get around. Its' about a stamina bar now. In the first game you get caught you HAVE to get back into stealth in order to kill an enemy, but in this game it has more of a souls-esque combat system with attacks, parries, and dodges. You no longer have to stay in a shadow to be able to teleport, the stamina bar shows whether or not you can shadow leap to ledges. It is a very different game than the first, but I'm glad they came back to the idea surrounding the Aragami themselves. Very fun and funny experience so far. Here's hoping the game finishes strong and identifies itself from the first!

_childDocuments_.review: Over-ambition has been, and will unfortunately continue to be the end of many.It's abundantly clear that Lince Works gave Aragami 2 everything they had, and then some; however, the height of their aspirations soared far over the stars. Such a distance proved far too hefty, as we would come to discover over two years ago.This is far from a bad game. There are some aspects of it that I find myself truly fond of, such as its very free movement system, whereas there are many others that feel incomplete, clunky, or forgotten, with the main story being the most obvious example. Even so, these comparatively janky segments of the game are rarely intrusive, nor worth making a fuss over if you're simply looking for a by-the-books stealth experience. It's easy to ascertain Lince Works intent when looking closely upon these half-baked parts of the game, and see where they were coming from.Having finally completed everything both Aragami titles have to offer in convincing fashion, it's hard not to feel pity for the recently defunct developer. Making a product with a quality that ranges from great to meh doesn't earn the creators such a saddening fate, in my opinion.Hopefully the many talented individuals who helped make this game, and its predecessor a reality are able to lend their aforementioned skills elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 200 hours in Aragami 1 and would consider myself a fan. I am not confident that Aragami 2 will entertain me as much. The following list might give you an idea why this is much likely will be the case. Because Steam asks me if I reccomend the game and not whether I like it I give it a thumbs down for now . This may or may not change in the following days and weeks.- it lacks what made the first game unique (shadow jump, shadow leaping, strategy focused gameplay)- the combat (imho sucks): when you are detected youre much better off running away for 4 seconds and come back to kill in stealthy manner again instead of having a (sometimes) long, tedious and dangerous fight. - the camera autolocks when entering combat which jeopardizes youre intended movement and direction - skills+tools are exclusively accessible on the wheel (no shortkeys even on pc) - every skill has a quite long cooldown which imo is a downgrade from the first game (especially for the abillity whistle cooldown just doesnt make sense)- the game lacks the atmosphere of Aragami 1 (graphics and music dont create the sense of melancholy or mystery)- as in the first game there are plenty of bugs and glitches to be found. Looking at how many bugs aragami 1 still has wont make me bet that the ones of A2 will be taken care of anytime soon.- no workshop missions anymore - no remapping controls (even on pc)- you can now jump and dash (the free movement overall feels quite good)- killing still feels impactful and satisfying - the killing animations are much faster than in A1 - Character costumization (but unnecessarily expensive imo, why dont you reward the player for collecting metals in missions instead?)- multiplayer up to 3 people - Graphics (There clearly went more work into that part than in the first game but I think the style doesnt work as well as it did in A1.)- Music (I love the soundtrack of the first game and TwoFeathers are involved again in the sequel which is great. But no real bangers for me so far.)- diversification via skilltree and runes has yet to convince me

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 nails all of the things that matter to me and suffers from a lack of polish in areas that don't matter to me.  I think it's a great game that any fan of this dying (dead?) genre should experience, just unfortunately not at $35.  It's been on sale for 50% off every seasonal Steam sale so pick it up when the next one rolls around. -Precise and fluid movement mechanics-Visually impressive animations-Strong balance between stealth and combat mechanics-Demanding but balanced enemy perception-Diverse items, tools, and skills -Resource management-Thoughtful and interesting level design that incentivizes situational awareness and exploration-Encourages a variety of playstyles-Increased rewards for better player performance-Good/great soundtrack-Decent story, interesting characters-Character customization-Multiplayer-Unpolished story execution or pacing issues-Lack of facial animations for dialogue-Some grind-Occasional bugs that appear when pushing your playstyle to its limitsAragami 2 nails all of the things I find really important, provides most of the things I like, and does suffer from a lack of polish in areas that I can absolutely tolerate.  If you agree with the above answers and questions then you should absolutely go ahead and buy it.  If you're not sure, wait for a sale, and if you disagree then it's probably not for you.In regards to some other reviews I wanted to clear some things up and provide my own opinions. -The story is not bad.  It is creative, it's certainly interesting enough, and if you don't skip through dialogue and cutscenes it does make sense.  There are some issues with pacing, but missions are 10-20 minutes maximum depending on your playstyle and it's probably best played over a few weeks.  I personally really enjoyed the themes, ideas, and emotions conveyed by the characters, even if was simply presented.-There was a big update a while ago that added multiple difficulty settings and fixed many bugs.  The game starts out very easy and progressively gets harder.  Playing on hard difficulty increases XP and gold rewards compared to normal so you'll actually find yourself acquiring new items and skills faster and building a diverse toolkit.  I don't think I would've enjoyed the game as much on normal.-I never had a single crash, gamebreaking bug, or outrageously annoying bug.  It takes some time to learn what kinds of windows you have with enemy detection rate and perception, but playing conservatively you will never feel cheated.-I didn't find the maps repetitive.  Yes, there are 7 or 8 maps that get re-used for 50 missions, but at the beginning you are confined to small areas, and as you play later missions you are taken to new areas,  By the end the scale of the maps is fairly gigantic.  I personally liked this approach because gaining some familiarity with the environment is important for stealth games and there is much less backtracking than an entirely open world game.  It combines a sandbox feeling with a linear level design approach which I think is really cool.  I think it's better to think of the maps in terms of biomes rather than copy-pasted assets, because the latter is absolutely not the case.One final note: LinceWorks is no more, so there will likely never be a sequel.  The multiplayer still works perfectly fine, but you won't be finding public lobbies to play with randos.

No. Is the game worth the price? No.This game doesn't feel like it has been playtested at all, there are so many Bugs if its randomly glitching trough the floor after vaulting over something or trying to vault while carrying someone and endlessly vaulting in the air.The Cinematics are Boring and seem cheaply animated. The Plot feels dragged out and it feels like they put more effort in the cosmetics then the actual important part of the game.This game also doesnt really have anything to do with the Aragami like we know it from The first Aragami. The whole concept of Light and shadow has been seemingly scrapped and it has become a purely sneaking game with some more Abillities. This game had great potential but it has become a Filler filled, buggy game with the most bland plot and cinematics.This game isnt worth the current Price at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay! The game is TOTALLY different from the first game (for all those that want to have same experience - don't get it).Now: The game reminds me of stealth souls game. Not bad, but to my mind too easy - AI is way too simple - if they see you and you hide - they just run around and then come back to their posts as if nothing happened - not cool. Skills...those teleport jumps - OP! Very easy to evade enemies and detection. As a whole - I love the game, but still would love to see 3rd game a little bit like the first...at least there the shadows and light mechanics were cool and limiting...now bad stuff - BUGS!!! Developers, Please! Add some unstuck button! I was jumping around the area and got stuck on some pedestal...couldn't move or do anything (was in like falling animation)...almost wanted to restart the game, gladly, my friend called one of the remaining guards - he threw bomb at me and this kicked me off that pedestal (I have screenshot, can share). Now, my friend also had a bug where he lifted a knocked out body to hide it, but the body assumed the carrying position, but didn't get on his shoulder - it was just stuck at the place where it was, only levitating in the 'carried position', but my friend was stuck in the carrying state - he could't throw away the 'air' (no body in hands just position as if he holds the knocked out guard)...also frustrating, because we had to restart to get a good rating for that mission. _childDocuments_.review: This game is not the first one. NOT EVEN CLOSE!In the first Aragami, if you were seen, you generally died. You had all kinds of ways to keep from being seen, but if you were, that was often it. Game over but the shouting. It was  a very hard core stealth experience with a massive learning curve and for those of us who enjoy skulking in the shadows, it was epic!This game is different. This sequel's art style is similar, but not quite the same. Lore wise, it has very little to do with the first game. (No spoilers here) You can stealth through levels and leave nothing but the occasional unconscious guard in your wake. Or you can draw your sword and cut a bloody swath through the horde. I TRULY do not recommend trying that at low levels, fair warning!!!This game is different, but from what I have seen, it is fun. I play as a true stealth aficionado. If I am seen or have to kill anyone but my target, I consider that a failed mission. I have yet to be able to play through without even knocking any enemies out, but I think it can be done.I am not done with the campaign yet and I will probably update this review after I finish, but for now, the ONLY problem I have with this game is technical. There are screen tearing issues, guards who teleport, pathing issues both enemy and character, and a few other interesting things here and there.  That said? If you truly want to play as a shadow essence ninja, this game will give it to you. Not perfect, but darned good for any of us who dream of being ninjas.Haven't tried co-op yet. Sort of looking forward to that, sort of not. In my experience, the Internet hates us all equally.(VERY frustrated edit after several more hours of playing) Okay, this game is not hard even for pure stealth runs WHEN IT WORKS. When it doesn't work, it is impossible. Stealth is sort of working, sort of not. Enemies all the way across the map hear you when you kill an enemy, but enemies right beside you do not. Corner attacks where you grab an enemy just as they pass a corner, work about 1/2 the time. Sometimes they see you (and chase you down and kill you!) when you are invisible, sometimes not. Sometimes Whisper acts as if it isn't upgraded and pulls everyone in the area, sometimes it works fine. If it wasn't so blasted random, it wouldn't be NEARLY as frustrating. It can be fun, but ONLY when it works.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I need to say, that I love stealth games. So much so that I play all these games with maximum stealthiness - no kills, no detections, no knocking enemies out.I think this is a decent game but except for the last few missions which felt interesting and meaningful everything before that were just lazy filler missions. So let me summarize my gameplay critics quickly: (Behind the hyphen is an explanation)1. The abilities are far too overpowered.2. The missions are as said mostly lazy and extremely short - I think the average playtime for most missions was about 8 minutes.3. The enemy detect invisibility. - Sometimes they detect you while being invisible and not by running into you but just randomly.4. Enemy sight is inconsistent - Sometimes they can see you above them sometimes you are completely invisible just by being an a small houses roof5. The enemy AI too often gets stuck - This is especially noticeable in "An simple mission". Not a single try without at least 1 enemy getting stuck and watching a rock for eternity. 6. Stealth kill mechanics are inconsistent - Sometimes when the indicator is visible your character still performs a normal attack instead of the stealth kill.7. Enemies/Players clip through terrain - To me as a player this happend only a few times but enemies fall through the floor or clip into rocks all the time8. Hard landings are inconsistent - Fall from 20m - no Problem soft landing <> drop one floor - hard landingOther than gameplay issues the voice acting is mediocre at best and seems to be always a single word in japanese or the start of a sentence. I did not care at the beginning but it really annoyed me later on.And last but not least the characters are honestly unlikeable and have very little depth. The story on the whole is slightly engaging and at least the last few chapters were enjoyable.So as a complete rating:Graphics: 5/10Gameplay 3/10Story 6/10Audio 4/10If you like the stealth genre maybe - otherwise I would strongly discourage buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ayoo i think it's about time for Aragami 3. But Bring back the targeted shadow teleport from the first game, i miss it a lot here. Like damn, way to spoil the fun.But yeah with a modern engine and tech the sequel would be awesome.Now as for the game: I do prefer the structure of the first game, except it being short. Mission type of style here doesn't really speak to me at all and the game feels overly and artificially stretched out, like there could've easily been less missions, maybe like combine a bunch of stuff in an area that you have to go to, because with the certain amount of skill you can go through a mission in less than 3 minutes, and going back and forth to the same place for the 10th time in a span of an hour isn't that much fun. So, better structure would be great. Maybe a combination of the first and the second games. That said, i feel like if sequel ever gonna come to pass, the combination of Aragami 1 and 2 is what it should be. More focused like 1, good movement and combat like 2, more polished and fluid of course. I absolutely love the aesthetic. Masks really give it charm, reminds me a bit of Absolver.The story is... There. I definitely prefer the first one in that regard.Voice acting, if you can call it that, reminds me of old bootleg pirate anime dubs, like ouch.Soundtrack slaps. Very viby.7/10 on a discount, definitely worth picking up if you like ninja stealth games with some mystic shabang going on.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dishonored or Mark of the Ninja or maybe Assassins Creed you will like this game, it can't quite keep up but if you've been thirsting for something since SC: Blacklist, this is it.It's a third person, ninja stealth game with the usual mechanics, but less "powers" than you're used to from either of the above but better movement, with optional secrets hidden in the levels to unlock consumable tools and visuals amor and dyes, very similar in aethetics to Dauntless.You have a rating system at the end of missions that shows you time, hostiles killed, alive and knocked out, if you've been spotted or killed, you can only die twice and the mission is over, unfortunately these "medals" have 0 practical use or impact and the ratings in general are VERY generous, you do get more EXP based on rating tho.The only cons are a couple indie bugs to be expected, but the re-use of levels. The game maybe has 6 or so relatively big levels and missions take place in differently sized parts of them. As much as I like the game, that gets kinda boring quick, same with the same 3 enemies, only many hours in do you see 1 new kind.There has been serious budgeting in the story department but it gets the message across. I feel like the game has been hamstrung by a lack of budget, because of whats there is good, but there should just be more. And when my biggest complaint is that there should be more, then that must be a compliment.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of this one at all sadly. Its a shame since I recently played the first game earlier this year and its DLC and I thought it was a fun indie Dishonored-style game. This one sadly misses the mark by a lot.To start with the positives, the movement is improved as your character feels much better to control. Also you can knock out enemies and not just be forced to kill them which is great for a passive run. I also like that you can select classic mode as a difficulty which is more akin to the first game where you can't really be spotted by guards as its a one hit kill if they catch you.That's sadly it for my positives. This game while not a live service has the stink of that genre all over it, from the terribly designed Destiny like UI with that stupid mouse cursor like interface (thats always terrible to use with a controller), the home base where you accept missions, has that MMO like feeling with the way you interact with NPCs and just the very multiplayer focus of this game. While the first game had co-op it was done in a fun drop in, drop out sort of way which is my preferred style. This game just has that more live service multiplayer feel and I don't think it served this title that is a mostly stealth game. They also added in combat so you can take on enemies directly but I didn't really like the feel of this at all and like I said classic mode makes this mute anyway.Otherwise they introduce cosmetics in this game rather then just having the skins you unlock after completing challenges like in the first game. The cosmetics just look awful imo and don't make sense in the context of the game. Much of them are these very bulky looking armours which I'm just like why would I wear that if I'm supposed to be a ninja assassin? The game's artstyle is also a bit of a departure from the first game which was made on unity like this one, but it had that cool water color, cell shaded artstyle that still looks very visually striking today. In this game it just looks like a generic unity engine game, with some of the artstyle retained, but characters just look unfinished and rough looking especially your main character. Its like if the first title was a cool looking PS2 game, this is an early, ugly looking PS3 game where they didn't know how to take advantage of the hardware properly.The story also just fell flat for me and it plays into the Destiny style presentation that I touched on earlier. It just doesn't work for me. I bought this game to play in co-op with my buddy as him and I both love stealth games, but even that wasn't enough to save this one for me. It's a shame the devs had to close their doors as they could have made some great future games, but the direction they chose for this title is just disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a different game from its predecessor.Evaluated on its own merits, it feels unpolished and repetitive at times. The heavy asset reuse may get to some, but it grows on you by the end, when all that level knowledge comes in handy evading harder enemies.The combat is... definitely only suited to specific situations. After coming to peace with the fact that the combat is not a general-purpose tool, and instead an ability which helps you silence a single enemy that has spotted you, I began to even enjoy it like the minigame it is. The movement is immensely satisfying and yet to get old. I dislike the hub world, as it really doesn't add any value to the game as a whole, and serves as little more than a place to keep all the dialogue, customization and consumable menus.While my review may sound negative, Aragami 2 has so perfectly nailed down the core gameplay that I can overlook those flaws, and have a good time doing it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Aragami 2 is game worth playing, especially with your friends.Now, here's a more in depth review:PROS:   - Improved mechanics. The character movement is super responsive and fluid. It's a lot of fun to flip and teleport all around the map while stabbing everything in sight. Combat is actually a viable approach this time around since you can parry and defend.   - Customization! Now you can swap out armor pieces and color them individually, allowing for a more unique Aragami.   - Improved multiplayer. I think multiplayer is practically a must for this game. It's implemented way better in this game than the first, with limited respawns.   - Even more fun powers to play with. They balanced the broken ones and added several more that are super fun to use.   - Worlds have a decent enough level of complexity.CONS:   - All the art direction from the first game is gone. I loved how stylized the first game was with it's animation and characters. This game throws it out for a much more generic Unreal Engine experience.   - The narrative is bad to the point of being completely forgettable. Remember that super engaging story from the first game with real characters? Gone. All of the new characters are bland, conveying only the most pedestrian of emotions. Big baddie doesn't even show up for most of the game. Feels disorganized and weak.   - They reuse the maps ALOT. Most missions will take place in the same handful of places, reusing them four to five times. Far too much padding.   - The experience grind is a nightmare. For how much padding they have in the game, you really should get powers faster. In conclusion, the game is still fun but has many flaws. Definitely worth a play with your pals.

The cloned guard is only real to non host players.Picking up bodies can softlock your game by making you get stuck in a loop of redoing the pick up animation.  Sometimes this makes the body invisible.Long range Fireball guys try to swat flies in an visual attack loopTens to upwards of 100+ people floating in the sky.  A few are T-posing.  Some are walking.  Some are dead.T-Posing guards slide at you while only moving their head, tracking you perfectlyT-Posing guards try to roleplay as an owl and snap their necks 180 degreesT-Posing guards attack you without drawing their sword through their sheer psychic willpower and mightAll unarmed civilians do a draw weapon animation with an invisible sword when they discover you that should be exclusive to guards before running away (this one is not multiplayer exclusive)People have stinky green auras around them (maybe a future mechanic I shouldn't know about yet in chapter one)Clipping through walls into buildings that aren't meant to have an inside, and getting stuck inside of them for 20 minutes until you manage to clip back outClipping through the floor and falling for 10 seconds before being warped 2 minutes into the pastClipping through the floor in the main lobby and seeing the underworldWhen secondary players load into a level they will see all enemy health bars for a brief momentSeeing copies of other players after a restart in the position they were as the game restarted (this one can stack so you can see multiple clones of a player)Cloning guards until there are so many in a lobby it becomes physically impossible to complete, but they're only real to some playersSometimes when a sniper shoots a fireball just as they die, the fireball's VFX staysThrowing corpses through walls. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty buggy right now in multiplayer, although it's been only a week since release. By itself a good game, however if you are looking for the classic Aragami experience this isn't for you. The iconic light-shadow mechanic isn't present anymore, enemies can be defeated in open combat without too much difficulty, and in general you have to play way less strategetly and it's less difficult. I don't think it lives up to it's name, and currently isn't a worthy successor of the title. They added out of place civilians to the game, that aren't easily distinguishable from enemies, and you can't kill them, but they are VERY distracting, since they can "discover" you (which doesn't count as discovered for the ghost objective though). Also, pressing escape doesn't pause the game even if you are playing in singleplayer. I might change this review to recommended in case they add different difficulty settings with one of them that you only recover essence in the shadow as in classic aragami, and if they bring back classic shadowleap (the new mechanic is ♥♥♥♥), and an option to remove civilians.As a note on gaming on Linux: The base game and all the mechanics work great with Proton, which is very cool, however static images like the titlescreen and cut-scenes won't load. I presume they chose a Image format that isn't natively supported on Ubuntu derived distros. So for the full experience you have to play on Windows for now.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with mixed execution, and one I highly recommend doing with a friend or two. Otherwise... Eh?I played Aragami 1, and I like their straight forward approach to stealth. Unfortunately, this doesn't scale very well with their enemy types. The AI and enemies are, to be frank, too dumb. This sequel also provided an option for open combat, letting you get into a sword fight with the enemies. Doing so is dumb though. The combat system is too simplified for any kind of depth, it gets quite bad with 2 or more enemies, and it straight up fails in multiplayer. But variety is the spice of life. If you want to go combat, perhaps different and better weapons might help? Stronger metal armor to weather blows and really get into the thick of it? NOPE. Everything is cosmetic, and thus pretty pointless. Colors are there, but you are hanging out in the dark most of the time, so they are pretty meh.I mean, seriously, the CONFLAGRATION BLADE doesn't IGNITE. I'VE KILLED ENEMIES WITH FLAMING SWORDS, WHY ISNT MY SWORD FLAMING?! Overall, recommended with friends. Otherwise, don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great,The complaint about it being not Aragami is understandable.The problem with Aragami 2 is that, it used "Aragami" franchise,It's like expecting Tenchu (Aragami 1), but getting Shinobido (Aragami 2).Where Tenchu is more of a stealth with puzzle solving approach, Shinobido stealth approach is by giving the player more freedom (Especially in movement, controls, and utilities) at the cost of puzzle-like stealth gameplay.Perhaps if it comes under different title, the complain would not be there.Anyway, combat is smooth, the Map is less linear (Compared to Aragami 1), Movement and control are fluid, stealth is great, and hard mode could be a bit even more harder.Overall a great stealth game.I have some nitpick with the camera being too shaky at indoors or tight corners situation, and how the color is reduced when stamina is low.But is minor issue.

_childDocuments_.review: I got gifted this game for PS5 shortly after buying it but couldn't refund it. Nonetheless I played it to completion, so disregard to tiny playtime lolAs a kid I was an avid fan of the Sly Cooper games. If you're not familiar, they're a quadrilogy of stealth-action 3D platformers themed as a comic noir type story. They're incredibly fun games and I sincerely recommend them, especially if you liked this game.Anyhow that leads me to my main point. I've long been on a crusade of sorts to find a game that would invoke that same action-stealth-platforming hybrid that seemingly no other game besides Sly has ever pulled off. Playing this game was like the moment in Ratatouille where the food critic gets a flashback to eating his mother's cooking as a child. It's like a smartly crafted hybrid of both Sly Cooper and a little bit of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, with just the tiniest sprinkle of Hitman thrown in for good measure.My only strong critiques are that the controls overall are a tad bit clunky (especially the combat, but from certain perspectives that could be argued as actually quite good game design), the environments are slightly samey, and there's no New Game Plus to encourage a full playthrough with all the cool abilities you unlock during the course of the game.Conclusion: Aragami 2 is one of my favorite games I've ever played. I'm in the middle of my second playthrough and having a blast just like I did the first time. Worth every penny you pay, worth every second you spend with it.Rest easy, Lince Works. I hope the extraordinary talent you once had has found steady employment elsewhere, they deserve the world after this masterpiece

It's not bad, it's just much more restrictive compared to the original. No idea why they tried fixing what worked perfectly already. The enemy AI has not been improved at all. _childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful game by itself, but not as a follow up to Aragami.Don't get me wrong, the game looks amazing compared to the first. And the gameplay (when it works) is rather smooth and satisfying. I know the game just released so take everything I'm going to say with a grain of salt. But I do believe there are three things that could fix this as a sequel to Aragami, not just being a standalone title.The online stability is shaky but given it's week one. I don't expect much quite yet. That's one issue that can be easily resolved and knowing the devs, will probably get fixed rather quickly.The combat feels like I'm playing For Honor or Dark Souls. I don't feel the same rush I did with Aragami where I could truly use being a ninja to my advantage. I feel more like a Samurai than a Ninja. In the previous installment, you had a rather generous amount of base game options to assassinate someone. In this, if I'm not on top of the enemy, I'm coin-flipping if I'm going to kill them or get thrown into detection and combat. It's nowhere near rewarding as planning out your kill and timing it against the surrounding enemies.While I heavily enjoy the new movement mechanics. They are insanely good and I love the momentum you can use to just traverse the map with ease (assuming you don't just break your ankles because that's new). But the stamina is insanely low from the start. The comparison I use for this is the shadow meter in Aragami. With the first installment, you were able to teleport from spot to spot based on how well you actually used the shadows and how much you kept yourself from being seen. In this, when you teleport, you've now lost 50% of your stamina. And that's just base game. Base game Aragami 1 allowed atleast four consecutive teleports assuming you stayed in shadow.Overall, this game makes me wanna play Aragami 1 more than play Aragami 2. I have high hopes that either one, the devs make changes to reflect the masterpiece that was Aragami 1 or two, the community mods this game in ways that will look to improve upon the experience. But I couldn't get past 75 minutes before these took a mental toll on my playthrough. I will more than likely redo / edit my review and outlook on this game, assuming the game gets the love and attention that the community gave Aragami 1.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid indie game in my book! It's probably a hot take, but I actually enjoyed the changes made for Aragami 2. Ranging from gameplay to (some) lore, it was nice to see the devs play around with this world & if there's ever an Aragami 3 - I do hope some elements carry over & maybe even mix in with the first!Going into the mechanics, as I stated it was a fun approach. Mixing up my skills & runes based on how I felt like completing a mission really helped break up some of the repetitiveness of levels, especially since I would often go back to grab any collectibles I missed, secure an S rank, or fill out one of the 3 (or, i suppose now with Classic mode, 4) badges. I do think the demon/combat "class" could have been worked on some more, as this is a game that penalizes you for being discovered & you can't really get to that corner unless you're seen from the start of the mission. For how the stealth factor was handled, I feel as if it wasn't as harsh a change as some make it out to be; I found it more fun to experiment how I'd get around a certain area as compared to one, though I will admit - I missed being able to just jump into nearby shadows. However, it wasn't such an issue that it ruined my playthrough.NPC wise, I thought the little community the MC ended up in was really enjoyable! I found myself talking to them after every mission to see if there was anything new, and while there wasn't most times, it still felt nice to go around and say hi when I could. If there is any DLC for this game, I would love to see more dialogue! Especially for Danjuro. Honestly just give me a DLC focusing on him. Also a pink dye, please. <3Aragami 2 isn't perfect; the bugs (while being worked on!) did make story & current 100% completion progress a bit tedious, as I said earlier - the levels can get a little repetitive, and there were just some parts of the story that didn't land as well as the initial conflict you're faced with at the start of the game. But in the end, I still found it enjoyable to play through & these issues never got in the way of that. If you're looking for a quick game to casually play or just want to add something different to your library, I'd personally recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Aragami 1 and I want to say off the bat that this game should've been called "Aragami: ___" instead of being marketed as a sequel—because it isn't. That aside, I truly think this game is phenomenal and once you get the hang of it definitely an easier stealth game, but what truly makes this game shine is the movement—there is so much fun and fluidity in being able to shadow leap to ledges and in air and the combinations you can pull off with that move set. Regarding Aragami 1's essential mechanic of staying in the shadows/teleporting between them being somewhat absent, the Classic Mode definitely scratches the itch (although you can't place shadows like in the first game, so you're limited to the dark places already on the map (there are a lot, and it honestly works great), and does change up gameplay  to make it different from how Aragami 2 was designed. I wish Lince Works didn't go under after this project because it's apparent that they really liked the concepts they were going for and with more and more refinement could've reached a near-perfect product. I really enjoyed this game despite the few design choices which aren't the best, and also have to commend the devs for doing things like Classic Mode and increasing the level cap post-launch due to player feedback. Highly recommend playing this game, it's a fun take on the stealth genre with a lot of enjoyable gameplay mechanics and abilities, but it's not Aragami 1, or a sequel to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hear me out. It's not bad. It's no Aragami 1 mind you, but it's not bad if you separate this game from the first one.The addition of the "classic mode" saved this game for me. Before the addition of this mode the game was honestly not very enjoyable and really was lackluster in its delivery. I only play in Classic, therefore my review will revolve around this game mode specifically.I feel as though this game is more of an "introductory" stealth game, which when it is compared to its predecessor. It's rather hand-holdy and is much more forgiving than the first game and gives more power to the player (which following the first feels very out of place). Certain mechanics are now missing such as light harming you, and shadows are only used for re-gen of powers making them less of an importance and more of a bonus additive. However, with the addition of the classic mode, teleporting to shadows becomes the only way to utilize your teleport over terrain (minus to rooftop sides and building ledges) making the game feel more like the first in this aspect. It definitely brought more of the original feel of the game back for me when this option was available.Combat in this game is poorly optimized and very janky. They attempt to teach you in the beginning how to do it correctly, but throughout the game it ends up being a very glitchy one sided experience often resulting in your death due to glitchy mechanics and weird button inputs. Classic mode once again resolved this issue for me due to the fact that combat is still available but is severely punished with the implementation of the OG Aragami mechanic of "one shot one kill". Meaning that you do have the option to fight should you need to, but one hit will kill you and force you to start over (and you will get hit due to the poor fighting mechanics). Therefore in classic mode, stealth becomes all the more imperative due to it being more of a punishment than the ability to actually kill your attacker in a 1v1 fight.The levels do get a bit on the redundant side, especially since the first game had you going to different places throughout the game. Personally, this wasn't really a big con for me, I didn't really mid it all that much. Would some more level diversity been a little better? Yeah, was it a deal breaker for me? Not really. I also really didn't mind the hub world either. I really liked the music in this area so I wasn't really upset or bothered about it being a thing. The one thing I really was upset about was the story itself. I would have loved a continuation from the first game into this one. I was really looking forward to playing Aragami again and learning more about the character that I became attached to in the first game, however, the story-line in this game is legitimately all over the place and has nothing to do with what was established in the first game about the Aragami. That was a bit on the confusing side to me, as suddenly the entire lore was changed from what we had learned in the first game. We're no longer playing the first guy, but some other guy who's now an Aragami because he's cursed. While the story isn't "bad" per say it was a huge derailment from the established line of story from the first game which honestly left me feeling some sort of way. This story-line almost felt too "Naruto-y" to me which gave it that cliche Sasuke angst feel. This ultimately made the story really hard to connect to and had me tuning out half of what was going on throughout the story-line because it just felt so discombobulated and far removed from the first story-line. Did I hate it? No. Did it keep my attention? Not really. Did I still play the game? Yes.All in all, it's not bad but not amazing either. Do I still play it to satisfy a certain fast paced stealth itch? You bet. Is it as good as the first one? No. Is it worth $34.99....not really. I'd say if you're curious, go get the first game. Play it through with a friend and have a great time. Then come to this game when it's on sale. Personally I'd say this game is probably worth about $15 as it does have some love an care obviously put into it and it's not a hot dumpster fire disaster, but I'd not really pay over $20 for it. TLDR: Good game, not as good as the first. Janky combat. Classic Mode made game better. Wait for game to go on sale before playing.   6.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Lot of people says that the first game was better because Aragami 2 changed and it's not like the first game. Well in my opinion the second game is better than the first. _childDocuments_.review: I'd like to preface this review by saying I am a huge Tenchu fan. In particular Tenchu: Stealth Assassin's, and Tenchu: Wrath of Heaven. Tenchu is the game series that got me into the stealth genre, which opened the door for games like MGS, Splinter Cell, Dishonored, etc.   Over the course of the past few decades we've had games like Ninja Gaiden which brought a more combat and magic oriented focus over the stealth approach. While this is a popular gaming style it did not scratch the itch for stealth that the previously mentioned Tenchu games delivered. Mark of the Ninja brought it's own flavor and style of stealth into the side scrolling 2D and was an excellent title, but it lacked the open level design that only 3 dimensional games can offer.   When the first Aragami released it granted players a unique way of navigating the 3D maps. Using the shadows to leap from one shadow area to the next, both horizontally and vertically. There was no jumping in the original game. Combat was also shunned in favor of a more pure stealth approach offering players ways of both assassinating or ghosting levels without killing or being spotted.   Enter Aragami 2. The biggest deviation from the original game was the necessity of having to use the shadows to navigate, that is no longer the case. Instead, in Aragami 2 there is a dedicated jump button in conjunction with Shadow Leap (think grappling hook from the Tenchu games) that allows players to jump and dash around the games environment, regardless of whether there is a shadow present or not.    The combat has also drastically improved, whereas in the original Aragami combat was a death sentence. In Aragami 2 the game offers a more robust combat experience by comparison. Parrying, light attacks, heavy attacks, along with specific tools and powers to help augment the player if they want to engage in combat rather than having to flee. It is still far from having great combat encounters though, but at least the option is there for players that want to actively fight rather than escape when the occasion arises.  The game offers character customization in a variety of ways too. From armor sets that can be mixed and matched to various swords.  They even have an assortment of dyes to color your character with as well. The game provides runes which can be purchased via the blacksmith vendor in Kakurega Village (which is like your home area in between missions). These allow to further customize your character by augmenting your stats like stealth, armor, stamina, attack, etc. There is also a variety of tools and potions at your disposal before each mission that you can purchase and stock up on.  There are a total of 50+ missions in Aragami 2, however maps are revisited repeatedly which can get repetitive by the end of the game. The mission objectives do get tougher though as the game progresses into it's later stages, challenging the player not to be detected and to not kill anyone. This is obtainable by the abilities you gain as you level through the ability tree. There is a good selection of abilities to add to your growing array of skills to allow you to approach mission objectives in the best way that suits you.  Overall the story was cool. Nothing mind blowing but I enjoy this type of setting and way of story telling for this particular type of game. I had a lot of fun playing Aragami 2 and it brought back a lot of fond memories of playing the older Tenchu games while also simultaneously forging new ones for this game.   I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a ninja stealth game that is trying to "scratch that itch" of older Tenchu titles. In summary, the best way I could describe Aragami 2 is like Tenchu with shadow powers. Not to take anything away from this game. I think the developers did an outstanding job with the atmosphere and the music too is spot on. I am currently working on finishing up collectibles and maybe even try my hand at the hard difficulty.   That reminds me, the devs have even added a "classic" mode, which allows the player to play Aragami 2 similarly to the original game. Sticking to the shadows and shadow leaping via the shadows. It just goes to show that the developers have listened to player feedback and incorporated a feature that the fans asked for. I think that is noteworthy & worth mentioning in this day and age when a lot of requests fall on deaf ears.   In any event, it's been a fun ride and I hope to see an Aragami 3 in the works down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... Different from the first game, which in and of itself isn't a negative. But it's not what I was looking for. I'm unsure whether or not I can call any of my gripes "critiques" since they aren't necessarily bad from an objective viewpoint. I dunno, I just couldn't bring myself to play more of it. The game just feels  in a way I can't explain. In other words, this isn't a review, just a rambling text justifying to nobody in particular why I don't like the game.-Shadow dash is now context sensitive, i.e it only works when teleporting to ledges and overhangs. A design decision, since the player has added mobility in other ways. Still a bit weird, since the whole shadow teleportation juju is the bread and butter of the last game. It's kinda like a fourth installment of the dishonored franchise not having a blink/far reach move. You could say that there's a forward dash move, but the control you have over it it quite limited.-Shadows aren't nearly as impactful to gameplay. I'm not saying that it's a bad thing that a sequel does things differently, but once again, it is a core mechanic being altered. It didn't feel much like shadows were vital to my survival as it should be. Especially now that your energy isn't tied to it anymore, being instead influenced by your stamina bar.- I didn't play this game too much, but it was a weird choice to make the game so bright. So much for the quiet, somber mood of the predecessor.-Double jumping and sprinting feels nice, but you need to start every sprint by dashing, which takes half of your entire stamina bar.-Combat is a simple dodge/parry affair. Not terrible, though quite dull. I don't care for it since it further deemphasizes stealth. Aragami was a pure stealth game, since the odds were heavily stacked against you when spotted. This could have worked, if I found it fun enough to bother engaging in the combat.- I can't speak for the missions since I didn't play the game for too long, That being said, there's now a limited amount of times you are allowed to fail a mission, and there is no "reload from checkpoint" thing. In other words, if you're a stealth-purist such as myself, I reckon you'll have fun with the "restart mission" button. Either that, or they cranked down the difficulty far enough that it wouldn't matter. -It is VERY worrying that the mission that I did play felt like a procedurally generated level in a live-service game. Something more akin to what you'd find in Warframe. The tutorial and first mission felt quite dull, not being nearly as gripping as any of the missions in the first game, including the tutorial. -Skills are level based. Interesting, but the "Fastest Way to Farm XP" guide I saw before starting the game set off some alarm bells. Whether or not this is an issue remains to be seen. The game seems more geared towards the multiplayer side of things with how the mission selection and rewards are displayed, and I'm not sure how to feel about that. I'd bet good money that you'll have to replay missions for meager rewards, or maybe even play rehashed maps with new objectives. The fact that the first mission only used HALF of the map hints at this.-Games tend to get harder, but damn this felt like taking candy from a baby that has suffered rapid onset crib death. Giving enemies a wide berth is easy peasy since several spinal discs have been removed from their necks, preventing them from looking up. A severe vitamin a deficiency would also explain their apparent blindness. I only got spotted when I decided to shank the main bloke in a camp to see how they would react. Otherwise, circumventing the enemies is a cakewalk.-The levels and mission structure feels... Wrong, somehow. Like they were made for several different purposes so that a randomly generated objective could be applied after the fact. Akin to the tilesets in Warframe, albeit nowhere as memorable. I can't explain it. It's like a sixth sense has developed after years of playing games. Like I am CONVINCED that they'll rehash maps with new objectives later. And ho-boy. If the absence of the "Restart Checkpoint" button along with the resource rewards is any indication, this game probably goes for shorter, less interesting missions than the first game.-Honestly it may just have been that the mission select screen coupled with the simplistic mission screamed "Anthem", "Godfall" and "The Division".-Additionally, there's just some form of accursed ethereal jank that I wasn't present in the first Aragami.Am I being too harsh?Maybe.I just can't bring myself to like Aragami 2 nor recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a stealth game fan I will go a bit in depth with this soTL;DR This is a very beefy and quite enjoyable 3rd person sneaking game, that improves upon the original in almost every aspect and I highly recommend to fans of the genre (especially Tenchu and Shinobido bros)That being said its a bit of a rocky game. The Unity assets are nice but result to the game not having much visual identity. Especially after ditching the previous more Okami themed aesthetic. If you pierce through this facade and some rough animations(hello there air assassinations) a fun sneaker lies within.Level design is fun and kurai's new mobility is fitting to this aspect. When you get on with the flow of the stage and the powers it turns in a breakneck speed stealth puzzle that is challenging enough and never overstays its welcome. The tempo is great and it reminds me of Tenchu and Shinobido where situations are diffused quickly and have an arcady feel to them. Sound is great and Emi Evans singing is always a welcome feature in any game lets be honest. The death cries are repetitive and in a beefy game like this it can be a bit of a mind numbing affair. That being said, if you grew up with (guess what) Tenchu you are propably immune to this aspect.Story like the first one is non existent and an excuse to slit throats and sneak, nothing more there. Overall this is easy to recommend, to any fan of the genre. Immersion is a thumbs down, especially with the new art style. So if you are looking for a deep immersive dive to feudal Japan this aint it chief. But if youre up for some sweet feeling stealthing and chaos this a big yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh, I've waited for so long just to get disappointed-Let's start with some positive points:1. I like the new combat mechanism, it's actually fun and more interactive!2. The graphics are not quite better, but the resolution is definitely higher.3. The first cut scene mentions one event of the main story in Agarami 1 --> so saying that there are no relations to the first part is not exactly correct.Now the negative ones:1. The health and stamina bar literally look like they were copied and pasted out of an online RPG game which is set in the 18th century (same goes for the enemies).2. And even though the first cut scene slightly mentions the first story, it still is something completely new and could be sold as a different game... 3. In comparison to Aragami 1 this game has become an open World RPG with quests which follow a basic storyline. So basically a game like Horizon Zero Dawn, The Witcher, etc. 4. In addition to the completely new storyline, there has also been an entire switch with the characters who play an important role.5. A lot of designs in the game look copied and pasted and not like the original Aragami style... )):=> Conclusion: It just makes me so damn sad, that I've spent 20 Euros for well not really what I wanted... and it makes me sad that this game could've been so much better. But out of whatever reason, the developers didn't care about Aragami 1 at all and didn't feel the need to continue that story in the "second part". It just doesn't feel like you're playing Aragami. It feels like a bad rip off that you're playing because your mom or dad didn't want to pay for the real game.So yeah, I'm really sorry, but I simply can't recommend this- it pains me to write this....

_childDocuments_.review: I don't regret my purchase, per se, but this does not feel like an Aragami game. It feels like a generic ninja-themed hide-n-stabby with a lot of issues:-The combat is nonsensical. You can be stabbing a guy three times in a row and then suddenly he kills you, but of course you couldn't dodge or parry because hitting him twice drained ALL of your energy.-The mission rewards make very little sense. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on classic mode with my wife. Extraordinarily fun which is what counts.A very nice break from Sekiro. Similar combat but nowhere near as difficult. They weren't a big deal. The game fixes most shadow leap glitches on its own.Other reviews also complain about the lack of new maps. It would have been nice if there were more maps, however returning to the same maps with different objectives and at different locations gives enough variety when playing with a friend. _childDocuments_.review: After having played the game for a bit (3 hours as of writing), I'd say it's a decent game.Some reason, the graphics seemed a little much for my graphics card (AMD 6900XT) which was confusing for me because triple-A title games are rather smooth. It seemed to be loading a lot of assets that weren't even on screen when looking around. At least that's my assumption as when I pointed the camera straight down, my frames would shoot back up to 100+ and remain constant. Might be a mis-configuration on my part though, always a possibility. Speaking of graphics configuration, this game doesn't really give all that much granularity in graphics configuration. Not that it's really a bad thing (some games have way too many options, causing most players to just ignore the graphics section entirely), but I wasn't able to tweak the game to run  smooth enough for my liking without going into my driver settings. Again, might just be my setup. Must have been my configuration as the next day, I played for a bit longer and haven't noticed the inconsistency. Please disregard the above paragraph!The story, from what I've played so far, seemed a bit "meh". The first game got me pulled in within the first few minutes, especially with giving enough mystery to be interesting but not too much that I have more questions than answers. This one, on the other hand, seemed to take more of the idea of "Okay, so we got this really cool ninja guy, but he finds a community and helps them out a lot." While it fits in many sorts of games (i.e. Assassin's Creed III, Black Flag, etc.), I just don't feel like it fits in an Aragami game, especially considering the first game where the player is a lone wolf, and the game is designed around that entire idea. Just didn't sit right with me; but again, just my opinion here.Okay, this is just me nit-picking, but I feel my immersion instantly broken when I see characters moving around unnaturally. Walking up stairs in a linear path (feet not connecting on the steps) as well as motions not matching up with solid objects (hands moving through sword hilts and other various items hanging off the body), they just kinda take the magic out of the game a bit for me.Okay, so the first Aragami game I absolutely loved because of its rather unique mechanics of jumping between shadows and refilling energy with the darkness. And with the story behind the protagonist's power (revealed at the end of the game -- no spoilers) went and provided a rather interesting twist. On top of this, the game itself was a rather unforgiving; it was a challenging stealth game that had a  emphasis on stealth over everything else.This one, however, seems to focus a little more on mobility, aggression, and combat with an underlying idea of stealth in the background. Of course, I'm not far enough into the game (yet) to figure out where the shadow powers come from, but I already feel like it's just gone in the wrong direction by having a whole community of shadow people -- I guess this goes back to the story section a little, but having these shadow people be lone wolves is really what  these characters feel a lot more real and brings a whole lot more life to the story.Either way, I feel like the game itself has lost quite a bit of its glamour when it comes to actual mechanics, as it feels a lot more like something you'd find in Assassin's Creed, but slightly clunkier, less refined mechanics (as compared to, say, Odyssey -- not to say Odyssey was had clunkiness either, just relatively  jank from what I've experienced).As for the ledge-teleporting, I wouldn't mind it so much if I could explicitly select which ledge I want to jump to. Having the game auto-select which ledge I was able to jump to got me caught more times than I'd light to admit, which was especially frustrating when I was going for a zero-kill, pure stealth run. And it wouldn't have been all that frustrating if during those runs, there were checkpoints. I couldn't tell you how many times I replayed a single level just to  on the zero-kill run and go on a total-annihilation run (which, by the way, was much more successful in the end) because I got so frustrated at the pacifist methods I'd take, just to be caught by something so small and have to restart. All this to say: .I haven't tested the multiplayer aspect of this game as I don't have any friends who are into stealth games and I don't really like playing in public lobbies either. Not sure how it all works, but I'm sure that if there were issues, the devs probably fixed it / are working on patches for it.This was mentioned a bit here and there in other reviews, but I just wanted to also mention it myself. The lighting in this game is  to get right as it helps set the entire tone of the game. The first Aragami game was set at night time throughout the entire thing (I believe the entire game was supposed to take place in one night). Sure, it got a little boring, seeing the same old tones of "Oh, this is moonlight! Oh this is shaded moonlight! Oh, this is a fire, this is a light..." etc. However, that inherently brought a more somber, serious tone to the game and added to the ambiance immensely. Aragami 2, however, seems to bring a lot more orange, yellow, and green tones throughout the game. Sure, it makes things a little easier on the eyes for the player, but at the same time, it seems just way too bright to put the player in a place where a literal shadow demon spirit ninja thing is slicing up soldiers right after a five PM supper. Doesn't make too much sense to me, and I noticed that I wasn't really as immersed into the game, the mechanics, and everything -- thus taking me out of the story and not really enjoying the game as much as I did the first one. That being said, the music itself was really good, I absolutely enjoyed listening to it as I was creeping around rooms and open spaces.Oh, that's another thing. The mechanics that were in the first game allowed you to create shadows and teleport to them as a means to kind-of hop, skip, and jump between one place to another. This game doesn't. It not only made me feel like the area was bigger, but also made me feel like most of the ground was just lava, and that I can't walk anywhere.Just to reiterate, I don't think this is a  game. I actually think it's a rather decent game by itself, if it were separated from the Aragami name entirely. Keep the character, Kuzai looks cool asf. Also, keep the music, I absolutely love the tone it sets. But the game, honestly, doesn't feel like it should be called Aragami, especially if it needs to live up to the legacy of the first game.I put a thumbs down on this review only because there's no three-star option. I cannot really recommend this game over the first one for people who were looking for a similar stealth experience that the first one provided. However, if you're a fan of Warframe, Assassin's Creed, and maybe heard of the first Aragami game (or played it and thought it was too challenging), I'd say this is a rather decent game. It's not as challenging, but it definitely is demanding... and it's just about as frustrating as Ghostrunner, except it's slower-paced (depending on your style) and more tactical.I like the game and see myself playing it fully through -- at the very least to get my money's worth. However, if there's going to be an Aragami 3 that's just more of this, I think I'll pass.Thanks for reading, hope this review helped in some way.

_childDocuments_.review: I have since completed the game and rewritten my entire review.The review assumes you've played through Aragami 1.There are extremely minor spoilers in the story and pacing section. They are not hidden.Aragami 2 is a step away from the mechanics of the first game, bringing it more in-line with traditional stealth games. While I myself was fine with the change, if you played Aragami 1 for it's 'Stay In The Shadows' gameplay mechanic, Aragami 2 has done away with it completely in favour of a more streamlined stamina bar that regenerates anywhere.Movement is probably the best change that Aragami 2 changed. Verticality is much more accessible, movement is fast and gets you from Point A to Point B. The Blink has been replaced with Shadow Leap which only works on ledges/specific jump-points instead of being able to be aimed directly. It works for the most part, occasionally sending you to a wrong point when there are multiple points tightly packed.EDIT: So the shadow leap seems pretty inspired by Sekiro's Shinobi Grapple [], I only found this out now since I recently bought Sekiro. The circle fills in depending on how close you are to the grapple point and when filled, can be leaped to. Level design is considerably different. Aragami 1 was linear; you would go from Point A to Point B in a streamlined fashion whilst occasionally looping around an area to do multiple objectives before proceeding []. Aragami 2 instead has a handful of much bigger maps that are sectioned off for specific missions, and can be played more open-endedly, approaching the objectives from any angle you choose. The maps are very well detailed and are a visual treat, not to mention just exploring them is fun. As there only a handful of maps, the game repeats them a few times. To that end, you actually have a hub world to reside in now, where you can upgrade your skills, items, change your colours, talk to citizens.....and that's kinda it. Not too much to do at the hub-world other than progress the plot or to buy things. Not to say it's useless, though. Just doesn't have too much to justify hanging out in it [].Multiplayer is clearly more risky than Singeplayer in terms of both bugs and gameplay. Multiplayer is where a lot more funky bugs show up, and not to mention desync issues. Gameplay wise, it's another person that can make a mistake during stealth. Though it's still lots of fun, and I don't regret any time spent just laughing at the bugs with friends in call.The graphics are a step up, but I'm conflicted about comparing it to Aragami 1. Aragami 1's graphics felt like they were designed with the art director in mind, and the characters blend nicely into the setting. Aragami 2's Aragami[s] can all look very out of place [], because it feels like the Aragami and the art direction don't mix well. While it isn't an issue, it's noticeable.Briefly touching on character customisation, a step foward, but a small step at the same time. Aragami 2 features customisation of the Aragami's Head, Chest, Legs and Sword, but firstly, are locked until rather late-game, and secondly require you to find the damn blueprint first. For what it is, though, the all look stunning, as impractical as some may be [] for the setting. Also, rather annoyingly, the Toggle Light feature from the first game is absent.Combat isn't 'Press Left Mouse' anymore! I mean, it still is, but now there's actual substance. In Aragami 1, when you were spotted, it was basically over; enemies would rush to you in droves, they'd parry your attack and then instantly kill you. Now, you have a proper healthbar and combat system, meaning even if the enemy/enemies attack you, you can still emerge victorious. You can now parry the enemy's attacks for a window, but in general the fights can last a while. It's still not incredibly well in your favour to go about rampaging enemies head-on, but now you actually stand a fighting chance.Difficulty is fine. Only problem is that enemies can't seem to look up or down and their AI bugs out sometimes. Note that enemies do indeed look up if they're already locked onto you. Run/Defend, choice is yours. Bugs are everywhere, but they are being fixed, with some minor exceptions here and there. It was horrible at launch, though! Have a lot of pictures- I digress. Bugs thankfully don't really affect the gameplay as much as it used to, but don't hold your breath.The big downside of this game is the pacing of content and story. There are a total of 51 missions in Aragami 2, and the issue is about 1/3 of those are repeated missions. The story takes forever to actually pick up and 'The Big Bad' is only revealed late-game. While the reveal being that late doesn't pose much of an issue, the real problem is that there's almost little to no buildup to it! With regards to content, there's a lot of cool ideas that also suffer from being more mid-late-game problems. The game teases a fair few concepts here and there, like unblockable attacks and specific mission parameters, but the latter is used so infrequently it almost feels like an afterthought. As a side note, the only mention of Aragami 1 I could find was in the legacy attire, though seeing as the game takes place 100 years after Aragami 1, it doesn't really bug me.Characters do really feel a bit shallow. I did find difficulty in being properly invested in the characters and story. Almost none of them are properly likeable and memorable. The voice acting can't be commented on because it's not  voice acting, just mumbles here and there that sound vaguely like Japanese. Some words are intelligible, but as it's all intentional, I can't fault it.Music and sound design? Absolutely stellar. The hub-world theme is great, and I admit that I have a few tracks saved on my phone for playing. The sounds are clear and identifiable; it lets you know when you've been spotted and plays a stinger whenever you kill/KO someone. The sword SFX is a tad serviceable, but it conveys what it needs to i.e sword go swing. I do really like this game and it's art. But the story is slow, some missions are genuinely tedious, and it could definitely use a bit more QoL improvements for certain things. I'll still recommend the game, but just be prepared for a little annoyance here and there. Game's fine enough.
