_childDocuments_.review: Seriously disappointed with the sequel as i loved the first one and was excited when they announced sequel for this game.The gameplay is quite repetitive with no new variety the missions are basically assassinate  a person, get supplies, steal some stuff etc and it will get boring after sometime. The combat is horrible, its like Sekiro except it's nowhere near it. Its clunky unsatisfying and its also filled with bugs. Unlike its predecessor Aragami 2 doesn't have its core feature which was to stay in the shadow, you can just go move freely even without staying in the shadow. The AI are really predictable and unchallenging at times. The pros are basically the visuals are better than the first one, the stealth kills are quick and satisfying, and also thank the devs for the  jump ability, Also the armor sets are pretty cool not gonna lieOverall the sequel to this amazing game is below expectations thanks to its repetitive missions, the clunky combat and the bland story. It has some game breaking bugs (they might've fixed it by now), the core component of the game which made it special is gone and made it uninteresting. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good stealth action game, not gonna lie. A lot of improvements from the first part, a lot more skills to level up, customisation, free movement and more ways to kill enemies. Definitely worth a try, especially if you have a coop partner.Small update about the game.65 houts in, I've got all the achievements, finished all missions in both "hard" and "classic" modes, got all possible medals, have done pretty much everything the game has to offer. I think I have few more cosmetics and colors to buy, but I have no desire to play the game because there is pretty much nothing more to do. I've seen the message from the devs that this is it, the game is in it's final state so there will be no more content, especially the endgame one.Now for the multiplayer.I might pick the game up once I'll have a friend to play it with or convince any of my relatives to play it, but that's another story.Even though there is a multiplayer menu in the game, it makes me think it was designed in all possible ways to prevent you from playing it. All the servers are always sorted by regions and not in a normal way, but in the way that shows one region at a time. As for me, I live on a "border" between two regions - EU and Turkey, so I have to cycle through those to find myself a partner to play. Cycling through regions comes with a few seconds lag, in which the game tries to update a lobby list for that region, but the next problem is pretty dumb - regions aren't sorted by their location on the world map, so even though EU and Turkey are close together IRL, they're on the opposite sides of region list inside the game, so you have EU - US East - US West - few more regions - Turkey - Australia - few more regions - Japan - EU again, so I have to sit and manually scroll through those with few seconds of delay each time just to see that nobody is playing in needed region. Not that big of a deal, but just an annoying little thing you have to overcome each time you want to play multiplayer.Also, this game was made with third-party-programms usage in mind (for example discord or some chat messengers), because the only way you can communicate with other player (besides actions like attacking, crouching and jumping) is through pings, that can't express anything more than general direction, which is not enough at all. You can't explain to a random partner which kind of approach you are doing (no kills at all or killing everyone, no detections or it doesn't matter to you), which leads either to a lot of restarts or frustration with thoughts that you'll have to play the same mission one more time because your partner can't understand the task.Here are some examples on what am I talking about:1. I've played most of the missions before playing in coop, but was replaying those in order to get all the medals. My random coop partner started killing every enemy immediately, and I understood that my no kills medal was screwed, so had to complete few missions with him (because I've wanted to play some coop to see how fun it is) and redo all of those missions with no kills.2. Opposite example, now I had to kill everyone without being seen, but another random guy was stunning enemies and hiding them in bushes. I've decided to go further into the level and kill everyone just to return and finish his job later on, but he kept being detected and dying, even though each mission has 1 extra life, he ruined the same mission 6 times for me (didn't want to kick him because coop is quite a rare experience and I've played hours before someone joined to me).In conclusion, coop is one hell of a mess that requires discord on background, which is sad because I generally don't like talking to random people in coop games and prefer to play without voicechat.Those are just a few details for anyone who is concerned about such things, but overall the game is pretty good and worth it's money.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the review comments that I've read so far there are two camps.1. People wanted a direct gameplay sequel to Aragami 1or2. People who played Aragami 1 really wanted a spiritual successor to the Tenchu seriesThose who are in camp 1 will certainly disappointed.I'm not disappointed. To be clear...that means I'm in camp 2.Aragami 2 still has many bugs and the levels may not be as open as my favorite ninja game of all time, Tenchu 1, but Aragami 2 certainly does scratch that *Tenchu itch. I'm the type of person who would play the soundtrack to Tenchu 1 while playing Sekiro and now I'm that same person, but playing the soundtrack to Tenchu 1 while playing Aragami 2.While the combat is certainly more QTE (quick-time-event) than I would like, it is less brutally difficult as Sekiro...and for someone who just wants to come home from work and pretend to be a ninja for a few hours, that's good with me.My hope is that the developers continue to sculpt this game into what it could be for those who are in Camp 2. The movement flow feels pretty svelte and I love moving from a double jump to a dash to a teleport. However, The teleport system is still a little buggy and there are some roofs that you can't teleport on while there are others you can. While I wait for the next update, I'm very happy with what is on offer here.Cheers and thanks Devs!P.S.Please Devs, create a Steam Workshop where we can create our own levels. I really want to play the ninth level from Tenchu 1 using this game's mechanics and engine.*If you find yourself to have a Tenchu itch please consult a doctor as soon as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a-lot different compared to Aragami 1. The Graphics style has changed from a beautiful unique Cell-shading to a (In my opinion, still nice) standard indie style. Hiding in the shadows still looks very cool. They removed the "shadow blot" from the first game which allowed you to teleport freely anywhere to make your own path, they also removed the "Yurei/Pacifict" and "Kami/Lethal" reward skins for whatever reason and replaced them with a standard "You did this!" at the end results screen. Your shadow abilities no longer need to regenerate in the shadows because that system has been removed by a standard stamina bar that works in Light and darkness. Powers are also on a cool down and can be used an infinite amount of time. The difficulty has decreased with the amount of movement you have now, enemies are somewhat blind unless you stand in-front of them or just generally be careless. Which you will later on in the game when you unlock more of the stronger abilities. The A.I is very easily exploitable as-well, you can be seen killing someone and if you are fast enough hide yourself and the body and the A.I will forget about you without any penalty to your overall results.The new combat system is similar but overall a dollar store copy of Dark Souls. In short It's not good. Parrying enemies attacks feels really good and rewarding and enemies can also parry players who spam attack buttons. You can also parry projectiles.Heavy attacks are very useless as they made the animation very flashy but very slow, It's mostly designed to take on enemies who group up on you but with how long the animation takes they'll either hit you before the animation finishes or kill you. But other than that you basically just wail on these dudes until their own stamina/guard breaks and you can either kill or knock them out.Customisation is greatly appreciated compared to Aragami 1. However alot of the customisation is found closer to the end of the game which is a real shame since you'll be stuck with the same outfits and dyes for a very long time. Also the outfits and dyes are very expensive so look around for all the gold in each mission.There's no penalty for killing everyone except one optional side mission that tasks you to NOT kill everyone you see and remain unseen

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to have to rate an Aragami sequel negatively. For starters this isn't an Aragami game. It's called Aragami, you play as an Aragami, but this isn't Aragami. They basically gutted what made Aragami unique. I'm a big fan of the first one and could look past some of it's quirks as it was Lince's first game. I was hoping to see some major improvements in terms of game play, animation, and the addition of cut content from the previous game such as multiple endings depending on play style. In that 5 year gap however it seems like things never really progressed such as animations and the core game play got worse.     The whole concept of light vs shadow is completely obliterated from both a story and game play perspective. You no longer have the cape which served as a unique display similar to denote your power. It lessened the need for a UI and made the game more immersive. It refilled in the shadows and depleted in the light or when using powers. Instead it is replaced by generic stamina bar that refills regardless of the situation. Light has no effect on it at all anymore just making light something to avoid because it makes you easier to see just like literally every other stealth game on the market.    This concept has been so completely butchered that even the shadow village is just filled to the brim with lanterns and they aren't even some special kind of laterns with a blue flame or something to make it more shadowy or something. Just a whole bunch of normal lanterns that would have drained Aragami's power completely in the previous game. This also extends to missions as well where the sun is literally still in the sky in some levels something well established in the previous game would completely  wipe out Aragami. It's actually astonishing how it isn't intentional when they go this far to entirely go against every established concept of the previous game.     Next is the graphics. I'll keep this one relatively short. They certainly look nice, but I wouldn't call them an improvement. For a game so centered around shadows, cel-shading was a a perfect style to go with. The last game's graphics fit a lot better. The one thing the new game did improve upon was the character faces. If they kept the cell shading and just went with higher poly-counts and more detailed character models/environments that would've been perfect.     The animations were a true travesty. After 5 years I was hoping for some improvements, but it really is hard to tell the difference between the 2 games. The cutscenes have terrible model clipping, the sword fights are clunky when knocking out from above, there is no special animation, your character just lands and performs the normal knockout animation.     The movement system changes are easily the worst things to be changed alongside the light vs shadow elements. You no longer have the same freedom of movement you had in the first game which is incredibly odd when they seem to be encouraging more freedom in terms of the story, approach to enemies, and level design. You no longer have the freedom of the shadow leap. It is exclusively relegated to ledge climbing now. Instead you have a short dash which you cannot see or control the distance. This has lead to a bunch of times where there are 2 patches of tall grass far apart and I will dash from one to the other and fall short right in front of an enemy. In the previous game this wasn't an issue as you knew the exact range of your dash and even if it wasn't close enough, you knew that and could work with that information.     The grass patches were an interesting concept lost with the core game play of Aragami. In the previous game bushes served a similar purpose and refilled your shadow essence, but were more sparse. If they kept the core gameplay, then the grass could act similar to bushes, but wouldn't refill your essence giving you temporary cover, but limiting you on your ways out if you were low on essence going in.     The knock-out system is again a mixed bag. In the previous game pacifist runs were more challenging and the ending even prodded you to play a pacifist run. It wasn't really a necessity in the first game, but with how limited you are in terms of movement in 2 it is a requirement as you are no longer able to slink by many enemies.     The combat system was completely not needed. I play stealth games to be stealthy. Not play a "stealth is optional for this mission" type of game. Whenever I was spotted in Aragami 2 I would just find myself restarting anyways because the game actively punishes you for engaging in any kind of combat by lowering your rank at the end of levels. The few times I did get spotted and just decided to try and fight, it never resulted in a duel as other enemies in the area would get alerted to and immediately run over making it 2,3, or 4 on 1 fights. It's a completely and utterly pointless system. In Aragami getting spotted was usually an immediate death sentence, but with enough skill you could warp behind the enemy and kill  the enemy before  he could raise an alarm. That skill reward system is just gone now.I really wish this game was just a buggy mess because that would mean that it would be patched down the line, but Aragami 2 is so fundamentally flawed to the core that no amount of patches can turn this into a proper Aragami sequel. If you are new to Aragami and are thinking about getting into the series, just buy Aragami 1.For being 5 years older it has:-better and more stylized graphics-much more unique and enjoyable game play to set it apart from other games of this genre-it's biggest flaw is the cutscene animations, but Aragami 2 did nothing much to improve on this anyways.All that and you save $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to the (what I would call) indie marvel Aragami of 2016, this game is more of its predecessor in all the wrong areas.Child of 5 hellish development years, Aragami 2 presents itself with a more complex combat system, streamlined levels and a new realistic aesthetic.When in the first instalment of the series you could be insta killed when discovered, now you have to painfully play what is in reality a minigame of timings, to get out of the situation, because gone is your ability to kill enemies instantly that would have otherwise allowed you to cover the mistake.The levels even if larger they are only used for one half during a mission, leaving the other part empty and lifeless, breaking the immersion.And even if the graphic someone could tell has improved, it is now harder to discern enemies from scenery and when they tried their best to reintroduce a "classic" mode, it is clear the old main-mechanic concerning shadows does not work anymore due to the less-sylized look.Yeah, because now you no longer have a shadow-fueled meter to use your abilities, they have been downgraded to simple cooldowns that are slower if you are near a light-source.Overall it is clear from my review that I didn't like the game, it is way less fun, and it is obviously the result of a troubled development brought to the team by an overly-ambitious scope. Nevertheless, I am sad that this game ultimately killed the studio.Have a nice day

Bad sides:- ... but often bug out- The fighting mechanic is often total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥- u hit someone, u get stuck, u die, or you try to kill an enemy and get killed yourself, because ALL OF THE ENEMIES CALL ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ON YOUR LAST HIT, CAUSE WHY NOT, it will always be 2 attacks at the end of their stamina, from which, one is guaranteed to inflict damage on you.- THE AMOUNT OF BUGS ACTUALLY RIVALS CYBERPUNK 2077 and here's a quick list acumulated in about 5 hours of playtime- some times killing an enemie will make you unable to move until you dash; in multiplayer enemies can become resistant to ALL damage from you, and your friend will have to kill that enemy instead; your sword can LITERALLY DISAPPEAR from your hand (you attack, but inflict no damage); the AI can  magically decide, that they are just gonna walk into eachother, a wall, or you, sometimes ruining your stelth run, or swarming you with 5 more enemies; in multiplayer, the loading screen can glitch, making one player's screen black, and not doing anything but that, resulting in a mandatory restart of the game (and likelly a lobby restart as well)- The shadows have gotten a huge downgrade, only useful for hiding  from enemies- The blood feels sometimes too cartoon-ish- No dubbing- NO RAGDOLLSIn conclusion, It's a good game, that needs some fixes, which are possible to make (add more frames to animations, repair bugs and combat). _childDocuments_.review: One of the incredibly rare games that I will keep coming back to. Having played through and beaten it 3 times now with three different play-styles and 100%'d both the achievements and collectibles, I don't think I could recommend this game enough and it saddens me to think the studio that made this went under.If you're in the mood for one of the few stealth games that doesn't punish or chastise you for killing people in the video game, and especially if you're in the mood for a ninja themed game that isn't ball-crushingly hard, Aragami 2 is pure, clean, fun.The only negative things I have to say about this game are:1. The way the mission rewards work. You get XP and Gold for equipment you may want the most when you complete a mission for the first time. After that, subsequent play-throughs of the same mission on the same Difficulty reward you with HALF the XP and Gold. This -REALLY- incentivizes you to not only do it perfectly the first time but to play on the max difficulty for the max reward. Granted you absolutely do NOT have to Min-Max your rewards like that to get everything in the game and I understand it's to prevent grinding for things early. I don't ever really use my gear anyway so it gathers dust 9/10ths of the time.2. Inconsistent enemy detection. Enemies in this game can both see and hear you. If you knock out or kill somebody too close, they WILL hear it, turn around, and now you have to either immediately deal with them or suffer a "Player Detected" penalty. Sometimes though, this seems wildly inconsistent depending on the action that results in the kill/knock out. Killing someone from inside tall grass is apparently quieter than if you'd just snuck up behind them and killed them that way. I could understand how falling assassinations/knock-outs would be louder though. Something I do love about this game is the timer is rather lenient for how long you have to deal with them before it penalizes you. My only other gripe with this is if you -KILL- somebody it should not count against you UNLESS multiple people find you. Dead men tell no tales, usually.The other problem, and I do understand some enemies have better perceptions than others (Like the dreaded ranged enemies that can spot you practically from across the map) is that their perception seems wildly inconsistent. Sometimes guards are practically blind. Sometimes guards have super hearing. On some maps some guards are stuck looking up which makes most of your ninja ♥♥♥♥ impossible 'cause they'll just spot you anyway unless you're invisible. 60% of the time it works EVERY TIME. The game by far and large is great but once the AI starts breaking down or gaining telepathy and just seeing you when they rightly absolutely should not? Infuriating.3. And finally, this game can get buggy at times. Particularly toward the end. The AI behaving erratically on one mission. Teleporting off into the void only to be teleported back where you where. Enemies spotting you in tall grass which just shouldn't happen, that's literally the point of it. I have seen an enemy try to climb a ledge onto a water fountain, get deleted from this life, and count as a kill. Again, the game works beautifully 80-90% of the time but once it starts to fail it's like a cascading effect that can make the game infuriatingly unplayable.A lot of these are minor gripes that don't effect the game most of the time but when they do it is noticeable.I 'S' ranked all the missions save for 1 or 2 missions I 'A' ranked furiously just to come back almost immediately after and 'S' rank them out of spite. The next two play-throughs I 'S' ranked every single mission in a row. Granted with many restarts but it restarts almost instantly and the only thing stopping you is your frustration versus your patience. This game is -NOT- hard in my experience.Just remember, shinobi... Patience is a virtue.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is not like its predecessor at all. The gameplay is changed in almost every possible way, which also explains most of the negative reviews.However, in my opinion it was a change for the better. Aragami 1 is amazing, but it is very limited in terms of movement (no jumping, slow paced) and customisation. These two aspects alone make Aragami 2 a much deeper experience (also adding to the replayability) where you can switch between different playstyles all while personalising your Aragami. Aragami 2 also has a lot more missions, while Aragami 1 could be completed in under 10 hours. However, the sequel is reusing a lot of the same maps, you are just playing different parts of the same map each time. Overall I don't think that's a problem either, you'll always get maps or parts of maps that you haven't seen before and the maps that you played before are great to experiment with your new skills.

_childDocuments_.review: In Aragami 1 you had an intimate relationship with the darkness. It hid you, it recharged your essence. You were eagerly looking out for the next patch of shadow to teleport to, or a safe spot to create a shadow in. Aragami 1 is a pure stealth game, failure is quick, death is swift, running away requires reflexes and an escape plan.This game is very different from the first one - no longer a pure stealth title, and should be much more bearable to dip into for non-purists. It feels like Tenchu, but with dumbed down Sekiro combat.Couple of points from my thoughts if you want to consider:Every stealth fan will enjoy this game, but stealth purists will probably not enjoy it to the maximum. The biggest difference compared to the first game is pace. Aragami 1 is slow and unforgiving, while Aragami 2 is directly opposite.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit, but I cannot recommend it based on its price, even on sale. Everything it does right can be found better in other games.I really enjoyed the first game for its gameplay and aesthetic, but had issues with a lackluster story. Here's how the sequel compares.The gameplay is still very fun, although it feels like they've put less focus on the character blending into shadow, which was practically the identity of the original game. They've also shoehorned in a combat system, which I largely avoided. I praised the original game for dense environments that fit the stealth mechanics, however this game ramps up in difficulty by making levels longer/larger. This is far less fun, as a single attempt of a level can be over an hour long.A notable appeal of the original Aragami was the cell-shaded stylisation, which suited the player character's ability to disappear into shadows. The sequel has abandoned that unique artstyle, losing a big part of what made the franchise stand out.I didn't care for the story in the original game, and couldn't get into the new story either. Aragami 2 introduced a hub world to fit the new multiplayer gameplay. Along with it brought plenty of running around to NPCs, just to be talked at until the next level becomes accessible.

_childDocuments_.review: AI is incredibly busted sometimes, and some of the games mechanics don't always work they way they are supposed to. This game needs a lot of bug fixes and updates before it is fully playable.The game also takes wayyyyy too long to actually level up your character. After 10 hours of gameplay, I have a total of 2 abilites. Just 2. And this game doesn't even let you fully upgrade your character. It tries to be something it isn't by making you have a limited number of skill points and having to make "builds". Despite the game only having a handful of skills to choose from to begin with. Also, it doesn't even have a matchmaking system. So, if you didn't bring your own friends, it is a strictly single player game. This game also seems to have a hard time deciding what ledges you can actually grab. A large portion of the game is being able to quickly ascend large buildings to get away and plan your next attack. But sometimes a roof is too slanted and your character can't grab onto the ledge, or in some cases, you CAN grab the ledge. But in those cases, you often get stuck and can't pull yourself up.Overall, the gameplay can be pretty fun sometimes. Slicing through enemies and disappearing around corners, or knocking out gaurds and hiding their bodies in a safe spot so they aren't spotted. But all too often the game falls apart and doesn't let you do what you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the first Aragami be warned: this is a VERY different kind of game. Still fun, but different. Whereas the first was relatively restrained and had much slower-paced gameplay, Aragami 2 goes absolutely tennis balls to the walls in terms of giving you the ultimate ninja power fantasy: teleport all over the place, assault enemies from any angle, summon shadows to distract or kill your enemies, *become completely invisible* (which I always feel is cheating in a stealth game) - you're a ninja in the Naruto sense of the term, AKA 'YER A WIZARD HARRY'.Despite being nominally a 'stealth' game, there are very few sections where you're forced to be stealthy: your basic movement abilities are so ridiculous (jump, double jump, dash, mid-air dash, teleport to ledge) and the levels so open that you can usually bypass enemies completely - or else get the drop on them with no chance for them to retaliate. You can limit your power usage and play oldschool cover-to-cover stealth if you really want to, but it seems to me like the devs wanted Aragami 2 to feel more like a sandbox than a stealth game - and you certainly do get a lot of freedom with all your unlockable powers and ninja tools.Aragami 2 takes a very different approach to level design than its predecessor. Rather than a linear sequence of different levels, 2 has a dozen or so more open levels that you keep revisiting in different missions - which is fine because the levels have different start points, objective areas, enemy positions and routes depending on the mission, such that playing different missions in the same level still feels fresh - although after a while you will start to notice the same kinds of mission cropping up again and again. Still, the level design is good: each level has its own distinct theme that affects the challenges you'll face there, there are lots of little hidden nooks for you to explore (usually with some kind of reward for finding them) and you are often rewarded for creative pathfinding (hint: always consider the vertical option). If you push your movement abilities to their limit you can cover some insane distances, so play around and see what you can do. If you find yourself thinking 'Can I reach that ledge from here?', the answer is usually yes.The game has multiplayer and customisable avatars if you're into that kind of thing, and I can certainly see how this might be fun to mess around in with a couple of friends, executing perfectly planned simultaneous strikes or (far more likely) running around in a blind panic causing chaos wherever you go. But I haven't done any of that, so I can't comment on it - same goes for the somewhat Sekiro-ish combat. Call me a stick in the mud if you like, but Aragami is a stealth game and that's how I'mma play it.Like the first Aragami it has a slightly janky charm to it: it's fun and achieves what it sets out to do, despite not being the most polished product. I've encountered a few small bugs, like vaulting over a wall while carrying someone puts you in a drifting repeated vaulting animation until you press the drop button, which is probably not intended behaviour but certainly gave me a good laugh. Then of course there's the weird decision to use a Simlish equivalent of Japanese as the language spoken by the characters in the game, despite many of the names being Japanese and, well, it being a ninja game set in a faux Sengoku era fantasy world. If you're gonna go weeb, why not go FULL weeb in true Ghost of Tsushima fashion? I guess the devs didn't have enough money to hire a full time Japanese translator, or just wanted to focus on the gameplay? Not that it really matters, since the writing isn't the strong point of the game anyway. The devs gave me a full set of magical teleporting wizard ninja powers to abuse and that's exactly what I'm going to do. I hope you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Game removed all of the fun parts from the first game and added a bunch of bugs and a weak fight system. Will admit the aesthetics are reasonably pleasing but lacks the darkness of the original which is kinda core to the gameedit: Having played some more from when I wrote the review and having gotten used to the movement a bit, there are a few mechanics that I prefer in the new one such as, aerial kills are now a lot more satisfying as you must jump before the option to kill comes up. however, I don't really understand the direction of the game, the idea as far as I am aware is we are a shadow creation, and yet we are working to make a living, what kind of shadow creature needs grain? and unlike the first game shadows seem to have very little to do with the game apart from making it harder to see you, ie. no shadow teleportation etc.I am also not a particularly big fan of the two lives business - either make it you only have one life to beat the mission or you have checkpoints like the original, but that is a minor detail.Also NEVER jump while carrying an enemy as you may float off into the distance and have to reset the whole level by quitting or having a coop teammate lose on purpose to restart.I would say this could be considered a good game in its own right if it had not been labelled as a successor to the first game as it makes little sense to do so given the difference is like night and day.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2, a sequel of the first game Aragami. My overall experience is great with this game but somehow I think it lacks in content. But we'll get to those later, for now let's talk about stories and stuffs.The story sets in hundreds of years after the first game, with only a little bit of connection between them. The general characteristics of an Aragami has been rewritten, losing some characteristics from the first game. But that's no issue, since everything can change after time passes. The overall story is nice, with a little twist here and there and there are also some wrenching moments as well. So yeah, for me I felt like the main story is pretty good.The game truly allow us to build our own character, whether it's appearance or ability we are able to customise them to our hearts content. Whether is head-on attacks or stealth based the game got you covered. This make the game much easier than the first, but much more fun too so I guess it's worth the trade-off. I liked this game more than the first as it provides more freedom than the first (aerial movement, dashes, chain-kill and etc).Now onto the lacks in content part, I felt like they could've release more story contents, like how they did it for the first game. In case if you don't know, the first game has a DLC campaign which brings out new story prior to the events. I mean why don't they do it here? Why not release a DLC with a story prior or after the events? I always liked DLCs like these which introduce new maps, new characters, new storylines and let the players know what happens after the main story. Since we received other updates on difficulty and several stuff like classic mode, I felt like my comments before sounds a bit greedy. But you know what? I don't care, I want more and if they release stuff like those I will happily buy it. Overall, the game is good. Like real good, but I wish we have more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though i did have a fun time with this game during Co-op sessions, i can't recommend this to anybody.The Combat feels like it's in early alpha stages at best and is easily broken if you play co-op.Missions just consist of listening in on guards talking, rescuing someone, grabbing intel or taking out a target. This gets boring real fast as the game has you play several areas many times over, all of which are kinda just okay levels.This leads me to one of the biggest disappointments, the skill tree. The skills are lackluster at best and just feel like a ploy to get you level up as much as possible. Also, Stamina is lost while wondering around the Hub area of the game which is really annoying, especially considering how far apart everything is.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game -- but definitely more fun for co-op. And it's no sequel to Aragami 1.There's less strategy, less "puzzles", less thinking in general -- it's sekiro combat, metal gear solid style stealth ("!"), and a lot of fetch-questing. The story is worse (Aragami 1 had a weird, quirky story line that I actually enjoyed -- this was a little boring in comparison), and parrying as a non-host is impossible in co-op.However, the maps are larger, speed runs are more fun (trying to find the best path to do everything, and to get the "no-kill/never-seen" or "kill everyone" without triggering too much combat), collectibles are enjoyable to find, and there's enough (though repetitive) content to grind through to sink over 20 hours in.I think it deserves the mixed review, but I enjoyed it and recommend it. 3 player co-op is also pretty cool though I never tried it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I understand people disliking the shift from Purist Stealth to Stealth-action, I welcome the broadening approach to the missions (Though I tend to play it as purist as possible, leaving enemies undisturbed or unconscious.) Where some see formulaic mission design and re-use of assets, I see the potential for content expansion. In another year or so I may need to update this review, for better or ill.UPDATE: Lince Works have now added Classic Mode, restoring many of the mechanics and much of the mood of the first game for those who took issue with the changes at launch. So for those of you who skipped this one due to the changes made, please do give it a shot now! Got no excuse to skip this quality experience.

_childDocuments_.review: For a sequel, this might as well be a standalone game. It deviates a lot from the original, but not in a bad way. The movement is much more quick compared to the more methodical and patient playstyle of the original. The only common link between the two games is the fact both games are about the aragami, but even then, the second game basically threw out all the established lore from the first game out the window. Gameplay is mostly smooth, there are a few bugs currently like vaulting over objects and going through walls/ceilings, other weird clipping, etc. but most of- if not all- of these bugs will hopefully be fixed eventually. Theres also some areas where you cant climb up a ledge even though you should be able to, but there are very few of those kinds of areas, so I dont even remember where they are honestly. Biggest change between the original is the replacement of essence with stamina, and not being able to teleport between shadows, but most skills from the original have pretty much returned, aside from shinen (or maybe theres a bomb-like item unlocked later in the game, idk yet) and banmoku. Other skills like kurosuna and the kunai have become items instead, with limited uses per level but no cooldown, meanwhile the shadow creature kill has become an ability that is on cooldown instead of being a second, riskier kill option like in the first game. Good change imo, as the shadow kill was very low-risk most of the time because of the patrol routes of the guards. However, the new alternative 'kill' option is to knock the enemy out. I'm assuming the intention is if you choose to play pacifist, but knocking an enemy out is basically the same as killing, so thats boring and makes going pacifist feel the same as playing the game normally but pressing E to knock the enemy out instead of Lclick to kill.Only interesting use for knocking an enemy out as opposed to killing is to counter priests. They detect if an enemy that they're connected to is killed, but not if theyre knocked out. I'd say thats an interesting and smart use, but the priests are usually placed somewhere where they're alone, or only one enemy is patrolling, so they dont have the chance to send a guard nearby towards the enemy you just killed, and they themselves can't leave their post. Im hoping a mobile version of the priest with a sword will be introduced later in the game that'll track you down, but I've no clue.The game is unnecessarily long though. There are 14(?) or so maps which are very large, but you return to these maps over and over again for new objectives and missions, with enemies having new patrol routes. Due to the map's large size though, you're restricted to specific parts of the map, so its not as repetitive as you'd think, but its still fairly tedious at times. I would complain more but the movement and combat is pretty satisfying and solid, that its not a complete chore to do the levels.Finally, the animations are a bit janky at times, like, the aragami stabbing and the guard reacting sometimes dont sync up, usually the guard lags behind after the aragami stabs him, and also Lady Miyoshi's hair. The hair at the front of her head clips into her face, especially during the cutscene you meet her, because that just makes her look goofy as ♥♥♥♥, but then on the other hand, the hair on the back of her head is stiff and doesnt have the same flowing physics as the hair on the front of her face. Her whole model looks stupid, but luckily I barely have to see her so thats good. Overall great game 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, first off: I LOVED this game. There is so much you can do and a bunch of cool powers that have been added in. (Momentum was my favorite. _childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a pretty good stealth game, that's about all I can say about it. Be warned it is a significant deviation from the first. It much more closely relates to the likes of Shadow of Mordor or Assassins Creed. In fact, I would consider Aragami 2 not a sequel but rather another game entirely, set in the same world. Lore wise, they are likely a significantly apart in time.I'd recommend picking this up on a sale.It does have nice additions from the first, such as more robust character customization and more options for how to build your character skill and stat-wise. The game is roughly twice as  long as the first, ignoring collectibles/replaying missions. The new movement system and combat is rather fun to master.However, there are a fair amount of downsides, like bugs and lack of music (What is there is beautiful though). My greatest complaint, other then deviating from the first so much, is that missions repeat the same level and enemy layouts (But with different mission starting points), which is a huge downgrade from the first which had better and more carefully crafted levels. This causes the story to take a hit as well, as lore is mostly covered in-between levels rather then in the moment.Overall, the game is a fine stealth game. You will be disappointed if you go in expecting an experience more like the first Aragami.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game that I would say is a challenge and gets me looking to where I should be going for taking a stealth route, but I am thankful that there is a combat system where you can fight back instead of running and hiding, but i could still do the run and hide tactic to get the hostiles to search for me till they give up. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a major departure from the original that might have upset a large number of fans of the original but definitely felt amazing to play for me. It's faster, snappier, it features a combat system that allows you to recover against a single enemy while struggling against many, making it somewhat of a perfect feature to implement to a stealth action game. In fact, some of the most fun I've had in this game wasn't just planning and perfectly executing a plan, it's the times that I mess up and end up getting chased by a small horde of enemies. I end up having to use all my abilities and tools to my advantage which is simply great game design.My gripes are mainly that the original had level structures that allow for traversal itself to become a puzzle which added to the challenge of stealth. Finding out where to go and how to get there was part of the fun of the original. It's something that doesn't appear nearly as much in this game which takes more of a far cry style of planning then attacking a settlement approach.As for other things, I'm really not a fan of hearing fake japanese in a very japanese inspired game. Whenever you hear someone speak, it just sounds like a japanese version of simlish. Some words sound right and then it's followed up with jibberish.I'm not too fond of the way the game handles ledge teleporting sometimes. It's great most of the time cause it works most of the time. It's very fun running and jumping then saving yourself by teleporting to a ledge, but the game never properly conveys when you can't teleport to a ledge so sometimes you take that risk and end up falling for it.As for minor gripes, the customisation sucks. Dyes have four colours and one of them, you can't choose cause it's the default colour. Much prefer a colour wheel. And the amount of customisation that I've gotten so far isn't that numerable.Overall: I love this game. It's a pure encapsulation of the phrase "Diamond in the rough". And I was sad to hear that the studio isn't gonna be able to make anymore games. I hope this gets the cult classic status it deserves. Aragami 1 and 2 both deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought my friend and I a copy of this game as we both loved the first game and this sequel is a massive improvement. I do have some negative feedback and hope that the devs may see it and fix the issues. Aragami 2 has three player co-op unlike the first which was only two player and has an immense amount of detail and upgrades/gear. The stealth is really fun, although I loved the "Shadow System" in the first, I do really enjoy the knockout and kill with the shadow dashing and shadow leaping. I feel as though this game was heavily inspired by the decent and original Tenchu games which is one of the key reasons I got into and love stealth games. The combat system although it may not be, it feels like it tried to be like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. That's not a bad thing though as it has been pulled off well and enjoyable when I want to mess around instead of playing seriously and being a sneaky boy. I highly recommend this to stealth fans and fans of games like Sekiro, Tenchu, Splinter Cell and Metal Gear. It has a lot of replay value thus far as just under four hours I am only on mission 8 (Collectable hunting, getting all three awards and S rank) and seems to be many more missions ahead. Okay. So I hope this gets read or passed on and maybe these are known issues, bugs or connection errors. Also, a few ideas are noted.- Mission boundaries break in CO-OP mode for the client so they can reach out of bound areas and collect statues for areas further on in the game. - The De-sync issues with CO-OP can make the game very hard. Client can't attack, use items, gets detected across the map or through walls even though crouched or standing still and the combat is near-on impossible as a client. - Game lobby in CO-OP breaks and soft-locks if you jump in the water behind the quest board in the village as a mission is about to start and you infinitely get stuck teleporting back from land to air and can't move nor does the mission start. - Some enemies don't spawn on screen at a certain range or camera angle (if it's tilted to the right etc) or until you get closer to them. Encountered this as the host of a two player CO-OP game on numerous occasions (i.e: Mission 2, 3, 5 and 7 specifically for me). - Add a description whether or not the armour and gear pieces such as headgear, torso, legs and sword have an effect on armour rating, stealth, damage and noise. - Add a keybinding for the cover system. Not everyone likes sticky cover (if that's what people still call it).- Add a keybinding for individual powers. Personally and my friend thinks the same, it isn't the best for some people to have a "next" and "previous". I would love to be able to tap "1" and equip my Kunai's then press "3" to equip the Amnesia needles etc. - Add additional knockout take-down animations. I personally love and prefer to do non-lethal runs but it is tiring seeing the same animation every time. Maybe a variation, an aerial knockout looks different to a sneak from behind. Thank you anyhow. Great job thus far and I am enjoying the game. Appreciate the love put into this and hope we see some future DLC. Edit: Playing on Beta version which is more stable than the live version. Patch 1.0.27899.0 Beta.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on Jan. 4th and as such many of the bugs stated in other reviews have since been fixed. There are still bugs, but it's usually nothing game breaking. The biggest issue is that contextual actions will sometimes not work correctly, or stealth hitboxes will not line up correctly. Meaning, you sometimes sneak right up behind someone and press 'assassinate' but instead your character does a normal sword swing which will allow the enemy to detect you and reveal you everyone around, very annoying, but not the end of the world. If you take things slow, these issues dont usually happen. Aside from the technical side of things, the game is very fun. I got roughly 30 hours of normal gameplay out of it, but that may be reduced to 20 hours if you really rush through each mission. At max, you may get around 40-45 hours out of it if you do every optional challenge for every mission, although you don't get anything for doing so. The stealth, abilities, combat, customization, and rpg elements are all fantastic and well done. The movement system in particular makes for a very fluid and fast-paced experience should you want it to be. The entire game can be played in co-op with up to 3 players total, and overall it reminds me a lot of the WolfPack co-op mode in Assassin's Creed 4 Black Flag. Communication is key to not getting spotted, or you can just run in, katanas out with your friends and basically play what equates to a multiplayer Sekiro with lighter combat mechanics. The story....is eh, but not really a big focus over the gameplay, you even get an achievement for skipping any cutscene you skip first. Overall, pretty damn good game. Lot's of flexibility with light replayability and a good time with friends. If you're a fan of older assassin's creed titles or just looking for something to tide you over after playing Sekiro, then I'd say this is great bang for your buck. I hope Lince Works releases additional content for this game. I could see free or paid dlc taking this game very far. As it stands, there is little to do in-game after finishing it, but there could certainly be any number of additions that give players something to do. Maybe a stealth pvp mode, or randomly generated dungeons, with new enemy variety, and possibly more bosses. All to unlock more cosmetics, runes, or items to broaden your abilities.

I'll often find myself completely disregarding the objectives because I'm too busy being a sneekibreeki mother**cker.Some of the takedowns are a bit wonky, some of the cutscenes and the like are stiff...  But this is good work from a studio that has put out...  What, two games to date?  And they're a big improvement over the original Aragami's cutscenes and animations.  I'm honestly excited to see this keep going.Also, ignore those that say that this game throws out the old one's lore.  There wasn't much lore to begin with.  The majority of their complaints comes from headcanons.  What we KNEW was that we were created using forbidden magicks and a curse, and are now on a mission to save Ms. McGuffin. _childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is nothing like Aragami 1. Other than a similar main character design and some teleporting mechanics, just about everything else is different.The original Aragami was tough. Every kill you made had to be methodical, and you only had small windows to do so. Guards actually paid attention to their surroundings. It was stealth only, or die. The shadow mechanic also made it enjoyable; stick to the shadows and avoid bright lights, lest you lose your teleporting powers. And the better you got at the game, the quicker and more precise you could teleport around the map, making you feel like a real ninja.And abilities while powerful, were limited to 3 uses each time. You could not simply abuse them because they wouldn't recharge automatically.On top of that, the world in Aragami felt vibrant, and the story actually at least made some sense.In Aragami 2 however, everything that made the original great is now gone. You can no longer perform long range teleports (unless it's to a rooftop or cliff). Shadow is now automatically recharged via a generic stamina bar. Abilities also simply refresh on a timer. No longer do you need to care whether you're standing in the light or dark. As a matter of fact, you can simply crouch and walk around because the guards are all short sighted. You can have guards literally staring in your direction and you can kill a guard in full view and not alert them, so long as there's some distance between you and them. You can also abuse teleporting to rooftops without ever having to worry about finding ways to recharge your stamina, since the shadow gauge is no longer a thing.Oh and if you get caught by a guard? Who cares? Just button mash him to death with your sword since they die in 3 hits (you don't even need to parry because they attack so slow and are straight up just weaker than you), or teleport up to a nearby rooftop since your stamina recharges so quickly. The best part? You can engage in direct combat with a guard, and you won't even attract the attention of other nearby guards unless they have a direct line of sight on you; they're all hard of hearing.And say you choose to teleport away, the guard chasing you won't even alert other guards to your presence. Instead, they just mindlessly run about trying to look for you, before giving up and returning to their original posts as if nothing ever happened. No heightened alert, nothing. Oh we had an assassin in our midst? Oh well nevermind, out of sight out of mind. And if that didn't make things easy enough, you can now carry bodies and hide them in bushes that just so happen to be everywhere! You no longer have to worry about where you kill any of your targets at all! But oh wait, there's more to make the game even easier! You can now very conveniently look through walls to see guards whenever you like, at absolutely no cost whatsoever!Also, goodbye air and teleport assassinations. It's hilarious that the tutorial describes air assassinations as being a thing, when it's really just you jumping, landing, and then performing a regular kill on land. Seriously, aren't stealth games supposed to be at least somewhat challenging? Aragami 2 even hilariously gives you potions to heal yourself, and I never once found any need to use them in the 4 missions that I played. What is this watered down crap?And while I do like that you can jump and even double jump and consider it an improvement to the original game, it doesn't really add any real variation to missions, albeit making it more convenient to get over short ledges.I played 4 missions and despite them having "different" objectives, they're pretty much the same at its core. There are no differences between assassinating a target, marking barrels, or collecting items since you employ the exact same approach for all of them. It's just a matter of killing guards with dumb AI, and roaming around a map that feels lifeless. And yes, Aragami 1 was also about assassinating many targets. But you know what made that experience exciting? The level design! There were many scenarios in the original in which multiple guards were stationed in a way where they had clear view of one another, which meant that you had to find ways to pick them off one by one, or use cool abilities to kill multiples of them in one go.In Aragami 2 however? The guards appear to be stationed pretty much randomly with little to no thought behind their placement. Some guards just stand still and stare into places where you wouldn't even need to traverse. Virtually no finesse or planning is required to pick off enemies at all.No, Aragami 2 does not have improved graphics; it just uses very typical 3D looking models as opposed to the old cel-shading graphics, which while isn't horrible, isn't at all to my liking. Something about it just feels off and cheap, like as if this were a parody rendered game seen on Family Guy.- To pick up items, close tooltips, or upgrade abilities, you gotta tediously hold down the interact button. Most games learned their lesson and got rid of this crap; eg Assassins Creed.- Cosmetics aren't earned via achievements like in Aragami 1, but are bought using otherwise mostly pointless currency that are randomly scattered around maps.If you've never played the original Aragami, I suppose Aragami 2 isn't a bad game. If you're a fan of the original however, this game is a massive disappointment. Perhaps Lince Works felt the original's difficulty prevented other players from enjoying it, but to make Aragami 2 this pathetically dull and watered down is a total crying shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, brutal, and hilarious. Hilarious with friends, anyway. Highly recommended, especially if you have a friend or two tag along with you. Just beware: the swordfighting is not as easy as the gameplay trailers make it look! You have to get really good at parrying, or else you'll get slaughtered. Best to stick to stealth kills/knockouts for your first few hours of the game, if not your entire time playing.Edit: Finished the game co-op. In conclusion: Story meh, gameplay great with some bugs here and there. When I say some, I mean some that are frequent, while there are many that are rare. The game does reuse a lot of environments for later missions, but they mix up the objectives, enemy placements, and enemy types to where it's not shameless at all. There are tons of powers, with my favorite being Shadow Kill. It made me say SHADOW KILL out loud to my friends whenever I used it. Is it worth the price? Co-op, absolutely. Single player....mmmmmmmmaybe. You might want to wait for a price drop if you won't be playing with anyone else, and trust me you'll want to play with friends not randoms. Stealth games with randoms sounds like hell.With lots of character customization, powers, mobility, and co-op potential, this game is an easy 8/10 or higher for me. One thing I would improve aside from getting rid of certain bugs and glitches is the swordfighting. It's a little clunky especially in co-op. For some reason I always had issues with hit detection during sword fighting during co-op, to where my strikes would just pass thru enemies, dealing little to no damage, while they deal full damage to me. Another thing I'd change is how detection works in co-op. For some reason, if one of your pals gets seen, you are also seen, in the sense that you can't stealth kill someone from behind while they're fighting/chasing one of your friends. Why not? We're ninjas. We use distractions, even those such as a person leading enemies into a trap to be backstabbed. You could do this in Splinter Cell Conviction but not in this game unfortunately. Co-op: Full price. Single player: Maybe wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays worse than a typical day 1 release. Every single mission is riddled with bugs that break immersion and cause frustration. Enemies just walk into you while you are invisible or in shadow or foliage, they don't need to even indicate they have seen you... they just walk up and kill you. When you try and stealth kill enemies, its a 50/50 chance the game will actually let you subdue/ kill them or let you use your abilities. Map design looks great, with really nice textures but the sudden walls that appear to block off the inaccessible regions can be very jarring at times, and with no way to map your journey, direction or locate objectives (which only appear in shadow vision at very close range) make it easy to get lost, repeating the same steps over and over again, especially if attempting a full stealth run. Due especially to the last point, it feels like the game encourages you to fail in order to memorise the map and objective locations. This is fine for the first few missions but when every mission relies on this tactic, it isnt great. Being unable to tell the exact location of party members when playing in co-op also makes it extremely challenging to coordinate, even if in voice chat or the same room. Overpriced for the sheer number of bugs and frustration.Update 2022Still game-breaking bugs. Still terrible. Classic mode also has a bug that disables WASD sometimes too. Dont buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ill give some pros/cons and comparisons bewteen the gamesPros: -New combat system where when youre caught its more of a battle you have to fight instead of getting knocked back and killed instantly.-Versatility in kills can range between knock outs and killing out right, but can now be done from a jump teleport and depending on height is how loud the kill/ko is, quite fun to play with-New AI is pretty cool, theyre now able to jump over and off fences to chase you down and check out noises. do note the can jump up and down back and forth so tricking the AI is barely a thing anymore,Cons:-Brand new movement is strange, no more teleporting shadow to shadow to avoid detection, its now a shadow roll like 2 feet then your visible and sprinting after the roll. hard to get used to after playing the first game-Teleportation itself is a hassle now, it seems like the only thing you get to teleport too is ledges that your usually seen doing-Detection is incredibly fast for a stealth game, they will spot you and start attacking you within 1.5 seconds and without an instant teleport into safety its just about impossible to avoid detection when youre first caught out-Combat AI/Targeting Combat is really not fun or intresting, you kinda just take on one at a time while fliping back and forth between enemys to see which one is winding up the longest attack known to man.-Graphics look like theyre pulled straight out of unity engine. They abandoned the first games semi-ink style to replace it with what looks kinda like rough plastic action figures-Stamina is one of the worst things they added, just about everything takes stamina, Teleporting, running, rolling, combat in entirety and if you get caught up in a fight and lose all your stamina get ready for the biggest whirlwind of your life because the enemies will straight up combo 2/3 of your hp while your character sits there like he has Carl Wheezers asthma -THERES FALL DAMAGE-Stealth kills/KO Animations are almost the exact same no matter what, where, or who youre doing them toComparatively: This game shares almost 0% of what the first game was, where as the first game you would want to find out a way to get rid of everyone in a very fast strategic method as in this game you kinda just throw youself into combact and murder everyone by parrying. Stamina has taken place of shadow usage and will regain no matter if your in the light or hidden in shadow but runs out faster than you would ever expect of a combat systemGame is still fun with friends, but thats usually the case with any multiplayer gameTL;DR: Its a fun game so far, but you shouldnt play this because you loved the first one, you are sadly mistaken if you think this will be anything like it. It kinda feels like your just a Warrior with teleportation

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the first game, I was very excited to run through the campaign with my friend as we did before.This game was such a disappointment. It lost every single ounce of the charm that the first game had. The first game was simple, unique, engaging, and, while lacking in the depth of its narrative, it shone through because it strove to be a clean, fun game about bouncing between shadows and executing stealth kills.This game was none of that. It was ENTIRELY too long--it overstayed its welcome at least twofold. The worst part about its length is that it was so artificial. You run through the same levels over and over until you're sick of playing the game. The combat system was entirely unnecessary, and such a tragic mistake on the part of the developers--in multiplayer, only the host as any chance of actually successfully parrying attacks, or, even more disappointing, even knowing what the hell is going on in the first place. The person joining the host can just swing at an engaged enemy over and over again to no avail, and then suddenly get killed by a swing that you never had a chance to block (not that you even could with how poor the desync/net code was). The narrative felt so forced and it was impossible to find any way to feel attached to any of the characters because they were so bland. The first game's lack of a real narrative didn't act as a detraction from the games value, but some how everything they included in the second game only drew away from what was supposed to have been a fun, engaging experience.This is a classic example of developers biting off more than they can chew. It tried to do everything except build upon the foundation that made the first game great, and none of the other things it tried to do came together in any cohesive way that left a good taste in my mouth. It pains me to ♥♥♥♥ on this game, because I really really enjoyed the first one, but the developers made far too many mistakes with the sequel. I really hate how much I didn't enjoy this unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically and visually superior to the predecessor, but as with a sequel that is expected.I am not too good of a writer, so I wouldn't be able to tell if the story is any better or anything.But if you played Aragami 1, you'll likely enjoy Aragami 2 since it is everything you've come to know but recognizably superior. Plus, it is co-op. Who doesn't love a good co-op game? My favorite addition over the previous game is that there are guards that refuse to leave their posts, so you have to play AROUND them if you intend on sneaking everywhere. I like this game; I do, but this game is not fun enough to play 51 missions of; I am on 25 and barely able to finish because I am getting bored stiff. It makes me wonder, "Who wants to play for another 25 missions?" This is one of very few games that I have to muster the energy to open because there is no fun in playing it. Even with tranquilizer needles, sonic grenades, mesmerize, wraith, and dark flame, there are simply too many guards late into the game. It has gotten to a point that fighting them head-on is no longer desirable, and the joy that can be garnered from this game is not worth it and is hard to support. I began to realize the reason the game is designed like this is because it was meant to be played cooperatively, but if you desire some assistance, they essentially have to have beaten the game before because otherwise you are forced to play catch up. Honestly, with the shenanigans you get up to as an Aragami, it makes sense that whoever is in charge just said, "♥♥♥♥ it, put guards everywhere." Hard to recommend a game so painfully boring. I wanted to complete this game to give it a fair trial but maybe another time.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, gameplay.Why is there fall damage in this fast paced action-stealth game?Why do every cutscene have characters clipping either with other characters, or themselves?Why are there obvious seams in the geometry, and also in characters that appear in cutscenes? Why is there a piece of equipment, that changes the main character's skin tone from undead to not-dead?Why are there stairs when guards who investigate suspicious activity will climb cliffs to arrive at their destination?Why is the difficulty of the game only escalated when it introduces a tier of enemy that can spot you across the map?Why does the game break the pacing with very long cutscenes that either do not continue the plot, or give some sort of context for the player's actions?Why are there 3 defence items when 1 would do and the second and third upgrades are both 'more aoe'?Why is almost every interaction labelled 'eavesdrop' or 'observe' even when you are actually talking, investigating, or writing?Why are there mandatory stealth missions in this 3-player co-op game?Why are the mandatory stealth missions in this stealth game so late in the game?Why do you have the ability to take people down non-lethally when taking them down lethally is more effective and leaving them alive is a risk to yourself?Why is non-lethal takedowns and option in a game where you are instructed, and indeed forced to, kill to complete the mission?Why is there one mission where after a long and arduous battle you are instructed to jump down a pit; and if you fail  to grab a ledge you instantly die from fall damage? See earlier question about fall damage.These questions I have no answers for. I hope when the developers was reviewing if their design decisions were conductive to fun gameplay they had sufficient answers to these questions.Secondly, some constructive criticism of the story:Stories usually have a beginning, a middle, and an end. Each part creating the conditions required for starting the next. For example: Your family has a magic sword that is the only way to defeat the bad guy, the bad guy shows up and hides the sword and does bad things that give you a motivation to defeat the bad guy. You find the sword, and by having the sword the bad guy targets you for more bad things. The story concludes with defeating the bad guy. That's a very simple story. Aragami 2's story is not that concise, yet has even less substance.Story threads that could have been cut include the child being returned to the mother leading into the mother exiling herself leading into the mother coming back to eat the soul(?) of the child and then the child having a nap. The story thread where the clan elder is dishonoured by being bad at his job, despite it not being his fault that things went awry, attempting to kill himself, failing, and then acting as if nothing had happened. The part where they return 1\10th of the souls back to the aragami, realising it is not the 10\10ths they need, and then abandoning the plan altogether rather than repeating it 9 more times. The story thread where you are tasked to track down a powerful artist(?) whom you then imprison and continue to do nothing with. None of these story threads advance the plot, or resolve some other plot element. All of them are superfluous as none of them lead anywhere.A generally good writing tip is also to make it so that your characters do not have amnesia. Characters with amensia might seem like a great idea to suddenly reveal sweeping plot changes, but are in fact counter-productive to your story. If a character knew exactly what they had to do but simply could not remember until some random point in the future; that means every action taken up until that point was a waste of effort; they could simply have waited until the character remembered and saved themselves a lot of effort. It is also generally a good idea to employ the writing technique known as 'setup and payoff', the less said the better. Presenting a character and then telling the player that they are in fact a big deal explicitly by stating it in the text, moments before the character does something tremendous, is simply bad writing. It is more bad than doing the same, and then discarding the characters because they never mattered in the first place. This game is guilty of both.In short, do not write a story if you do not master the basic storytelling techniques you might find at a highschool level. I recommend in future to read a primer, or watching any movie, or reading any book, ahead of time to give some inspiration for structure. Also, making the final boss Darth Maul is a bad idea. If this was supposed to be funny, the intent was not clear; though the reaction certainly was. In short I would recommend to be mindful of "cause and effect" when writing.TL;DR-This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I was of mixed opinion about Aragami 2.There were a significant number of changes from the original game, such as the addition of jumping and a lot more verticality.There were also a number of bugs that never got fixed, such as using the 'whisper' ability on an enemy (to call them towards you) and having them walk THROUGH the cover that you were sheltering behind, thus detecting you without the ability to assassinate or knock them out like normal. As a result, you have combat, you have a player detection, and you get a lower score. Annoying.I also encountered a glitch in one level where all of the enemy were moving in circles almost on the spot, making it near impossible to take them out without cheesing abilities, and waiting a minute for the cooldown to expire, then doing it again. It made that level frustrating too.Aragami 2 also has a MUCH lengthier campaign, consisting of about 8 maps that are reused about 5 times each with very slight differences (ie. opening up a previously blocked segment, and closing off a previously open one). And it was here that I found the most frustration. Given there are about 52 missions in the game, by the end of it I just wanted it to be over cause I knew the levels back to front.  I also had no desire to replay the game or any of the missions to collect all of the collectibles - simply because I had seen the levels so much that I was sick of them. It'd probably be more fun playing coop with people, but playing Solo it just became repetitive, with the only difference between levels really being the placement of enemy, and the enemy types.That said, the story was pretty cool. I'm actually disappointed the Devs have closed, and we won't see a sequel to this. Because while there was little linking Aragami 1 and 2, the ending to 2 definitely opened up future game options, and left me wanting more.Overall, I would definitely recommend it, especially when it's on sale. Despite all of the issues I've listed above, it's still a really good entry into this genre of game even against titles from "AAA" developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been dying for more stealth games (for a long time ;-;) but I don't think this is worth the price tag. It does improve on the 1st Aragami in some ways but regresses in others. I'll list some pros & cons after a few hours of playtime:+movement feels significantly better +character customization is awesome +rune system looks promising+city hub is a neat area+good music+different skills/passives/items to unlock & use +assassination animations look bad-ass (excluding the "aerial" ones)+needed more stealth games in general, hopefully more developers will follow suit-very linear levels: lots of closed off buildings, invisible walls, no sewer system, no breakable doors, cant swim around, etc. Basically every level is just a few buildings/pathways -shadow leap isn't dynamic & will ONLY go where the developers want -combat system is horrible: no aerial combos, no custom combos, stamina drains WAY too fast, enemies are too easy 1v1, combat is too basic/bare-bones. I do appreciate the attempt though.-buggy and inconsistent -certain enemies (the dudes with the robes) straight-up can't be interacted with at all. You can't knock them out, kill them, anything-enemy ai is stupid: Their cone of vision is laughably bad, they return to their posts WAY too quickly after finding a dead body or you, they only have 1 patrol route, certain enemies don't even move -lost the diegetic ui from the orginal aragami -no custom keybindings -art style isn't as distinctive as the 1st game-NPCs in the hub barely say/do anything-Bloodsmoke is inconsistent, sometimes it would cloak me, other times it wouldn't & I'd get hit/killed -shadow vision should've been a duration based ability instead of being limitless -boring mission objectivesIt's obviously trying to be Tenchu (which isn't necessarily a bad thing) but the problem is that Its missing lots of things that made Tenchu great/interesting. I don't recommend it. Atleast not for 30$. Might be decent if you catch it on sale for low 20s or something.

_childDocuments_.review: (Review Mid Game (Chap 4), spoilerless)TL:DR ***All*** the polish went into the gameplay. Freedom of movement lets you yeet yourself around the map while knocking people out. Why is parrying so unforgiving? If you're looking for a planed, high-difficulty, sneaky backstabs only where you skulk around in the dark like the Original Aragami, you might be a little disappointed, but if your open to new ideas, this game takes the Aragami foruma and lets you fly with it.The game doesn't show its best cards immediately, the story is unclear and confusing and the combat tutorial just highlights how clunky it is (and you can’t change controls anywhere?). However, it's obvious the time and effort went into polishing the movement and stealth gameplay to high hell rather than giving the story the attention, and the sword fighting is clearly a “In case of emergencies.”', and you're not meant to run into a 1v20 sword fight. Gameplay this thing is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ goldmine for 1 main reason: Freedom of movement. The only ability downgrade we got from OG Aragami is that we can now only teleport to ledges rather than everywhere we want. However, we now have a double jump and a dash, and the importance of shadows has been reduced. Why is this a good thing? Insane movement techs combined with the fact you can knock someone out at any time, in any direction, as long as they're not on full alert, is very very fun. Dash into a jump to soar through the sky and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BODY some poor dude across the courtyard, teleport to a ledge and smash a dudes skull on the fence, and double jump then dash to get vertical height with your distance to get back to the roof unseen. The game is as fast and flows as quickly as you want it to and it excells at making you feel powerful without being unbalanced. The final note is the note of the “♥♥♥♥♥♥ cascade” where being caught by 1 guard causes all of Japan to know your exact position and tuned it a little too far to the other side of the scale. Guards are blind, dumb and basically never call reinforcements further than 20 meters away. In exchange if you do get caught, they can chase you down basically as fast as you can run unless you're good with teleporting. Treat them more as the game's puzzle pieces than actual guards. Good game. Bring up to 2 friends. Extra tidbits:• Don't look out of bounds too hard. Especially in the capital. • Don't throw important people into black end-of-map voids, they are unrecoverable. • Do throw people off cliffs because it's funny.

_childDocuments_.review: Different sense of pace to the original.  The introduction of a more general purpose stamina bar that covers shadow moves and ledge grabs and the change from 'painting' shadows to create handholds in the original to a narrower ledge grab system take time to get used to, but once you adapt to them they create interesting flexibility as you work your way through areas.  You can also hang from ledges now as a means to avoid detection or get a kill.Aragami 1 has a slower pace with tight AI patterns and not a lot of way to divert enemies while remaining undetected- challenging but rewarding in one way.  Aragami 2 has adjusted this in a few interesting ways with a more open skill tree and then thrown more enemies into more openly designed levels so you can slowly peel armies apart into dark areas and take them out quietly.A combat system that I'm not so fond of has given you an opportunity to fight back if detected, but what's nice is even after you're seen you get a brief moment to either take individual enemies out or use a move that incapacitates them long enough to do so, like throwing an amnesia needle at them or Mesmerize them.  You have to react quickly to pull this off, the game doesn't afford you a slowdown to react aside from bringing up the skill wheel, and even then it's over pretty quick.I'm a little over 20 hours into the game, in Chapter 3, have been playing through each level for pacifist/no detect medals and then immediately playing them over with a kill/no detect mindset instead.  One thing worth noting if you're playing is that the level rank system seems a lot more concerned with detection than with consistency, so if you're going for stealth S rank you don't have to knock out every enemy, completing the objective sight unseen is enough.  That's why when you pause the game you'll see an indicator of how many enemies you've killed, for the Oni medal (kill everyone), but no such indicator for how many enemies you've knocked out.Generally- highly recommended.  I have yet to try co op play yet but I hope to do so in the future, because the levels seem friendly to carving out areas for multiple players without stepping on toes.  In singleplayer this gets a solid endorsement, which if I had stopped at the prologue level I might not have felt as solid about.  If you like the first Aragami, give it some time and adjust to its sense of pacing.  It's different in a way that, having played this far in, I'm a lot more confident is a benefit to the game.
