_childDocuments_.review: I'm really torn on this game. On the one hand, hit detection is spotty, I fell through the map numerous times, enemies are inconsistent on if they will or won't see you, maps are reused to an excessive degree, and everything just has a general feel of being rushed and unpolished. On the other, once you get past the initial jankiness of it all, the movement feels really good, late game abilities are satisfying to use, exploration gets easier and more rewarding, and everything starts being really fun. This unfortunately took 20 hours to get to that point, but it's worth it. There is a ton of wasted potential, and it feels nothing like the first game. It really needed more time in development to iron out some annoying hit detection errors and polish up animations and whatnot. Despite all that, there are great ideas you can see working, and fun mechanics that are cool to use. Overall had more fun than not, there's just a lot of frustration to be had before you can get to the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is best enjoyed in its co-operative mode, though I had a lot of fun playing this game on my own. Disappointingly, missions become somewhat repetitive, but this issue is more or less remedied by gradual introduction of new enemy types, more consumables and higher-tier perks. Two very satisfying aspects of this game are fluid player movement and takedowns: knocking down an enemy produces very satisfying graphical and sound effects. It simply feels *good*. In addition, the charming, cartoony villages and Japanese-esque music make for a fantastic world. Then again, the sets quickly become old. As for the story, it was moving and elaborate, yet poorly explained. The music is great, though. Overall, a 5/10 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a dissappointment for sure. I feel like the attempt to create an interesting co-op stealth game was a good one, because when playing co-op the flaws are not very apparent. However, if you play this solo, bad design decisions start to seep through the cracks pretty quick: by mission 9 or 10 you're annoyed and further on it just becomes a slog to play. Pretty much every system in the game is flawed in some way: classic mode is a fun addition, but the game is not built around it, so it's kinda clunky and uninspired; the ability tree looks cool and some of them are very fun to use, but they do not become available until midgame and there is a huge cooldown on most (the first ability, Whisper, has a ~20 second cooldown); some levels are big and beatiful, but if you make aaaany mistake towards the end of the mission, there's no checkpoint you can go back to, no savegame, you are forced to restart the whole level or live with the low mission rating.One big point is the combat system, the game's advertisement says "ENTER INTO COMBAT AS A TACTICAL DECISION Become the master of a skill based combat with high risk and high reward." But as any other stealth game, you get punished if you get spotted and there is no reward for killing enemies outside of stealth, so "mastering" this 3-button single-combat system is completely pointless, when you can one-shot any enemy in the game from stealth - running away and hiding is always better, always.There's a lot more i could say about the story, the ingame cutscenes, the social hub with all the npcs, but to summarize - if you are a fan of stealth games, only buy this on sale, and if you want a game to play co-op, this can be a fun one for a couple of nights.

_childDocuments_.review: The Aragami series holds a dear place to my heart as it is one of the very first games my partner &I ever played together. We were ecstatic when we saw Aragami 2 was out & purchased it without hesitation. I've played the game for a total of a few hours now & there are definitely some pros & cons in this game.This game doesn't follow the story of the first Aragami game & I'm OK with that because it felt like the first Aragami game's story was told & not much more could be built up on it. However, I'm not sure what it is about this story, but I am significantly less invested in the story than I was in the first game. I'm honestly more excited about the action/gameplay than I am the story. Some of the things I love about this game is there is a little more character customization. In the original Aragami, the only thing you could change was your mask & the color of your outfit; that was it. In this game, you can choose from different masks, tops, bottoms, & swords. However, even though all of these pieces are merely aesthetic, the game still requires you to rack up gold in order to make some of them. If they were all cheap, it wouldn't be a big deal, but I don't feel I should need to rack up 3500 gold just so I can purchase black dye when blue, yellow, & green dyes are around 300 gold each.There are a lot of glitches in this game & I REALLY hope the devs fix them. There's a glitch where I will fall through ceilings after pulling myself up onto a rooftop. My partner & I have seen issues where one of us will have duplicate NPCs & they will actually attack & kill you even when the other person can't see them. The NPCs area also really buggy; sometimes insta-kill won't pop up even when you're above them & it causes us to become detected because the game apparently never sensed we were in the right position to perform an aerial kill. One big gripe I have about this game is the inability to map controls to specific keys/buttons. I tried playing this game on mouse/keyboard & it was god awful, but it wouldn't have been if we just had the ability to map the keys for ourselves. This forces me to play the game with a controller, which is fine, but is not as smooth as mouse & keyboard. I also do not like the controls when hanging on walls/rooftops. You either have to press a button to drop down or pull yourself up; there is no ability to just jump away from the ledge & the jump button is mapped to the pull yourself up button, so if you wanted to attempt to jump, you couldn't anyway. That might sound minor, but when you play the game, the ability to simply jump away from a walk in a NINJA STEALTH GAME would be really beneficial to the gameplay, but instead it makes it a little bit more difficult to play. Ultimately, I live for the action & that's what I have fun with in this game. I don't think this game is bad by any means, but I think there is significant room for improvement. I would really love to recommend this game, but in it's current state, I really cannot recommend it at full price. I would wait for it to go on sale in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable. A complete and utter disappointment.I greatly enjoy playing the original Aragami, having clocked up around 50 hours, mostly in co-op with a friend. It’s a gem. To me, that game is defined by its great stealth mechanics and the absence of combat. If you’re spotted by an enemy, you’re usually as good as dead. Sneaking, teleporting, luring and quietly assassinating enemies is such great fun, especially with a friend.But Aragami 2 is none of this. The original’s focus on stealth has been shifted to clumsy combat mechanics. Teleporting – the soul of the first game – has been relegated to only moving to ledges. Even your basic movement controls are frustrating. The mouse sensitivity cannot be set high enough and bizarrely, the camera is now (sometimes?) independent of your facing direction. Want to step off a ledge? Well, now you’re auto-dangling from it. Want to quickly run from an enemy? Well, the camera is locked to the enemy. Another enemy is attacking you? Well, you’re still locked to the first enemy. Want to stealth-kill an enemy from above? Well, you missed… or something… who knows, but now you’re dead.I wanted to play Aragami 2 in co-op with my friend, but to our confusion, the co-op option was greyed out. We both tried different fixes, sitting through the unskippable opening cinematic three times, before losing patience. Finally, we realised that co-op isn’t available during the tutorial level. So, we put on our grinding hats and got through the tutorial as quickly as possible, joined co-op for the level hub, but then discovered co-op isn’t available for the first mission. We gave up and played the original Aragami (and had a great time).The graphics are appalling, somehow poorer than the original game. The graphic-design itself is bad – look at the game’s waterfalls for a laughable example. But the thing that makes this game unplayable is a camera distortion (which cannot be disabled). As you move and look around the world, it appears and though the depth-of-field, field-of-view, and a wide-angle distortion shift and change willynilly. It does a great job of inducing motion sickness. I simply cannot play this game without feeling sick.All I wanted from Aragami 2 was a game that built on the first: new levels, enemies, abilities, enhanced multiplayer co-op, and maybe as a cherry on top, modern graphics. If I could have imported my original character, I would have been thrilled. Play the original game with a friend. Don’t touch this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is barely a positive recommendation as I found it pretty fun at times, but annoyingly painful to play at other times. It is not  2. This game feels very different losing what made Aragami great and adding only mediocre new game mechanics. Yes, jumping, vaulting, dashing mid air, and hanging from walls are welcome additions, but the completely new combat is not super polished. Fighting one enemy is perfectly fine, but add multiple and the jarring camera movements and limited gameplay makes it annoying. The removal of gaining power from the shadows and dashing to shadows was the worst mistake they made. Hard mode makes it annoyingly hard to escape if you are caught. Its almost impossible to simply just run away as the enemies teleport directly on to you and one hit you every time. When you add on the annoying auto lock with the combat system, its extremely annoying and clunky feeling. And only on certain maps is it physically possible to escape due to the possible shadow leaps. Speaking of maps, the repetition of the same maps is so lazy and makes each level blend together making every mission feel the same. I also think the crouched moving animation is weirdly bad. If you are looking for a decent stealth ninja game with a variety of fun abilities, then yes, buy Aragami 2 when its on sale. _childDocuments_.review: (Summary at the bottom as well as my score for the game.)Aragami 2 feels so pointless, the first game had a pretty definitive conclusion, and this one seems to exist to cash in on and take advantage of the people who loved the first game like myself. The story is there, kind of the only thing I can say about it since I really didn't care about anything that happened in the story and only begrudgingly progressed through it because of how much I enjoyed the first game. The characters aren't memorable, even after just now finishing the game, I couldn't tell you any of their names or anything they did beyond assigning me missions. However, the most disappointing aspect of the game is the game play loop.There are 51 missions in Aragami 2. That may seem like a lot of potential for variety; however, this game seemingly took the Wolfenstein Young Blood approach to level design. You go to the same areas constantly, fighting the same enemies with the same spawn placements with the same music for the overwhelming majority of the game, and much like Young Blood, it's tedious and boring. This gets repetitive almost immediately, I think I got 2 hours into the game before it became unbearable and it took me almost 11 hours to beat this game. I started on Normal, but the AI is incredibly finicky on Normal and will spot you almost immediately, and besides Aragami 1, I don't usually play stealth games, so I found the experience to be a bit more tolerable on Easy. Doesn't help that the AI cheats and can often times spot you through walls, while hiding in grass, and even when you're invisible.There's only a handful of different mission types as well (Kill x amount of thing, eliminate this target, carry thing to teleporter, 3 missions where you auto fail if you get caught OR kill something, find random item, and listen to people talking to name a few, probably missed 1 or 2 others). It feels like the game was rushed since even late into the game, think it's missions 46 and 50 both take place in the exact same area, both require you to find 7 of the exact same item which is in the exact same place in both missions, only difference is that mission 50 also has you kill 4 Necromancers (and not to mention half of the last 10 missions in the game have the objective to kill Necromancers). You fight the same exact enemies the entire game as well, until mission 40 where undead versions of the same enemies appear. The only major difference is that they'll spot you much quicker, kill you in like 2 or 3 hits, but they don't notice dead bodies, so you can just power through them if you got a lot of stealth upgrades in the skill tree. As you progress you'll get new enemy types, but everything dies in 1 hit if you stealth kill them, and they all have a similar movement pattern, so even with 3 or 4 different enemy types, it only feels like there's 2 in the game. Ground troops or archer/look outs. Even being spotted doesn't feel punishing. In Aragami 1, if you get spotted, or if a body is found, the enemy that spots you and/or the body, they'll alert the other guards and every enemy in the map will be fully alert and hunting you down. In Aragami 2, since the maps are so huge, you can litter bodies everywhere, and even if a guard notices, they won't alert other enemies, they'll just be more alert for a couple of moments.There's also a hub world where you can upgrade skills at the Dojo via skill tree and there's an armory that let's you "craft" (you just buy stuff, but the game calls it crafting) items, armor, and runes. While the skill tree is fine, the armory is a bit on the useless side since only a handful of items are worth taking, the armor is just cosmetic, and the runes are underwhelming to the point where I didn't use them at all during my play through of the game and it went fairly smoothly.The game play is different than the first, it's like a poorman's Sekiro Shadows Die Twice. The new melee combat system just doesn't feel good to use, and fighting more than 1 enemy at a time isn't worth the hassle. You're better off playing this game like it's Aragami 1, but because M1 melee attacks now, if you turn off V-Sync, the assassinations barely work. It'll flash across the screen constantly, or often times not show up at all even if you're walking behind an enemy that doesn't notice you and it lead to my first half of the play through being really frustrating because I'd get caught due to instances that weren't my fault. The movement in the game does feel pretty good, especially later in the game when you get different upgrades that let you move with even more stamina and stealth, but the decent movement doesn't save this game from feeling stale because it's way too long. There's no reason there should be 51 missions, even half of that would be too much. Additionally, since the maps are so big now, there's these obnoxious invisible walls that completely break the immersion that the first game nailed. Aragami 2 is so unpolished! You'd think that since this game is made on Unity (like the first game) the developers would have an idea how the engine works since Lince Works had no problem nailing Aragami 1, but it's laughable how many visual bugs and glitches you'll find in this game. Anytime there's a cutscene with a character that has hair, their hair will clip through their face and clothes constantly. If the character has a weapon, it'll constantly go through them as well; even long clothes just constantly clip through characters. It looks really bad and breaks the immersion even further since the levels you play in the game hardly feel like they exist in an actual place as well.Ultimately, I'd give Aragmi 2 a 4/10.While the movement can be fun at times  the tedious repeating levels and mission objectives absolutely slaughter what could've been a fantastic game. Unfortunately, I feel that I have to not recommend this game. 35 dollars is way too expensive, and even with the on sale price going down to 17.49, I'd highly recommend using your money to get Aragami 1 if you want to play a game in this style. With a default price of 20 and currently on sale for 4, Aragami 1 offers a much more well rounded experience. Better story, better level design, better stealth, and better game play. Best thing I can say after finishing Aragami 2 is good riddance.

_childDocuments_.review: 1/10 DO NOT BUY.  Go play the first one, or replay it if you're looking for a sequel.It saddens me to give this a low score, but it's well deserved.  Aragami 1 was a game I absolutely loved.  Each map felt carefully crafted, and the missions were all uniquely flavored.  Gameplay unveiled story, abilities, and enemies in a way that progressed difficulty at a pace that made sense and tied in to the plot.Aragami 2 is an uninspired cash grab by a developer trying to squeeze as much money as they can out of an existing IP and assets.  The game has ~10 maps that they've jammed 50+ missions into, and by missions I mean 3 missions all copy pasted.  Go to Map A and find this item, go to Map A and kill this person, go to Map A and rescue this person but this time we've blocked off half the map!  Rinse repeat with Map B.It feels like when you're in school trying to get a few more pages into our essay, so you go back and make words longer and add sentences that don't add anything to the essay other than words.  The game is peppered with tedious, unimaginative missions that repeat over and over.  At one point, they even straight up name 5 missions in a row "Family 1-5".  And I haven't even gotten to the glitchiness of the gameplay.  Movement and controls are clunky, things get shifted around magically as you slap button prompts, and at one point the animation of putting a body down teleported me into the nearby building.I'm going to stop my criticism here because honestly, it's not worth your or my time to continue any longer.  There are plenty of other co-op games that deserve your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a Stealth-oriented action game & a decent sequel that took the risk of changing it's overall formula from it's predecessor. You control a special type of ninja warrior with the ability to "resurrect" & you aid a village afflicted by a supernatural curse that makes it's hosts to slowly lose their personalities , memories and eventually their faces. So you try to find a way to lift this curse while defending the village from invaders & the shadow army.  Kakurega Village will be your HUB/Home base , from which you'll take quests from it's inhabitants, craft/buy weapons, outfits & consumables, unlock characters, abilities & runes that enhance them & completing tasks/ from the billboard to further progress the story. All these gave me strong Monster Hunter world vibes in terms of how you organize your char and their stuff before embarking on missions.  Gameplay wise, you can either conceal in the shadows and find tactical approaches to reach your given tasks, one hit killing or knocking out the enemies & hiding their bodies to not alert caution, or you can go the traditional Rambo wayand comforting em face to face. Combat in that aspect, feels like your typical light soulslike , with a few attack sequences , guarding / parrying & dodging while managing your stamina bar.  Special skills come to play as well , with either enshrouding darkness to reduce vision in a area, enhancing your weapons,teleport kills, creating shadow decoys and much more. In comparison to the 1st one, this one feels better in some aspects and worse in others.Movement feels heavier in a good sense, instead of teleporting in between shadows you gotta decide more tactically how to approach to remain unnoticed, the combat feels a bit better overall and imo this feels more like Tenchu than the previous one. Lastly , i encountered a few bugs , such as throwing bodies and them ignoring walls or terrain, a few off-sliding animations during execution cinematics but nothing deal breaking so far. It's not a breath taking or amazing experience , but it's an enjoyable one, especially if you're into Stealth adventures and Ninja's.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the original Aragami 1 and was expecting/wanting something similar (or anything like the original), ABSOLUTELY DO NOT BUY! NOT FOR YOU! Aragami 2 plays more like an arcade quick-kill speedrun then a stealth game (classic mode sucks). It's an okay game in it's own right, but nothing like the original. Should not have marketed this as a sequel, will no longer be buying any future games or DLC.This is one of those games where I wish steam had a middle-ground option. Honestly, buy it when there's a large sale.  -❌ Frustrating at worse, tolerable at best. (Why are we shoving combat in a supposed stealth series??)-🆗  It's okay. Kinda boring. Lacks variety and laughably easy. -✅ Fun. Nothing like the original. -🆗 Looks better, not great. I prefer Aragami 1's cell-shaded style.-❌ It seems like there was barely any thought put into it. -❌ An unborn child could play this with their eyes closed. -❌  What story? It's just plot-holes??-👍 Encountered no bugs when I came back to give it a second chance.-👍  Functional, with new changes.             -Could not test bugs for co-op. -❌  You will find yourself replaying the same few maps over, and over, and over again for the next 20-40 hours :)  BLOATING AND PADDED PLAY TIME The game is severely bloated, with only 9 maps and over 20+ missions- you will be forced to replay the same map over, and over, and over again. During replays some changes are made, but none of them are substantial enough to make it worthwhile. The most you'll find is the addition of more guards, or another section of the map (that you've already played) opens up. I'm not particularly against more content, my problem with the bloat is the repetitiveness of it. Level design is very lackluster which  further bogs down the game. Guards are seemingly placed at random barley watching each other, patrol routes that  don't cover anything substantial, and very uninspired map designs that do not take into account the player's incredibly flexible movement system. The ability to run in, kill everyone in "stealth" with no detection is easier then ever. You can clearly tell that quantity over quality was the main design philosophy here.  Played a little bit, didn't like. Feels like a half-assed attempt at replicating the original game's clever use of light/shadow mechanics. The most classic mode does is nerf you slightly (the game is so easy that it basically doesn't matter), and give you an extra teleport as if you needed another one on top of your 5 million OTHER movement techniques. It really feels like the dev's don't understand what made the original game as loved as it was. Tacking on a poorly replicated movement system from the first game won't work. One, the replicated system is half-assed in Aragmi 2, and two Aragami 2 was not made to handle Aragami 1 mechanics. In Aragami 1, the core mechanics of shadow/light were baked into the level/map design. Aragami 2 maps, were not made with those core mechanics in mind. All it does is make 'classic mode' look like some half-assed attempt at appeasing fans of the original Aragami 1. Honestly, Classic mode was unnecessary, and a waste of resources. Tacking on stuff from Aragami 1 won't work unless you commit to it fully. Just pick one thing and stick with it. Don't try to pander to both because in the end you'll just end up disappointing everyone. ❌I only have this to say: It's clunky, awkward, and frustrating. Just, no. Stop. 🆗Again, not much to say here. It's okay. Due to the repetitiveness, and lackluster level design it gets really boring. ❌I like the village and the music that plays in it. However I think it's a bit large, it poses the same problem as MHW Astera: too big, and annoying to traverse.Outside of the home base, the maps are fairly boring. Nothing super special going on here, pretty standard ninja, fuedal-Japan inspired setting. The lack of variety really hurts, since the main campaign will have you replaying the same few maps for the rest of the game. I played the entire game only doing ghost runs (100% kill, 0 detection), and it was still easy. Raising guard detection rates and fields of view will help with difficult but only for a little bit. I don't think tweaking some numbers is going to help with difficulty all that much.The biggest problem is guard AI is stupidly stupid, and unbelievable easy to abuse. The most you have to do here is find an enemy, make sure no one is watching him (which is basically 90% of the time), kill them, coin-flip if you should hide the body, and then move on. Not to mention guard placement is absolutely awful. They barely watch each other's backs at all. ❌Skip it, save yourself the headache. Plot-holes, and plot-contrivances out the wazoo. Terrible voice-acting. Animations/Cut scenes still leave much to be desired. Very boring dialogue, uncompelling one-dimensional characters I hesitate to even call characters, and the single most generic morally-grey three act story I've seen in a long time.  🆗I suspect this game's graphics won't age very well if you're buying this later down the line. -✅Hiding bodies is no longer a skill -✅Sound plays a little bit of a larger role in stealth runs -✅One new enemy type. -✅Co-op mode is now 3 player -✅ Playstyle choice, Stealth kill + no kill -❌There are only four enemy types in the game (technically 5, but not really). Not a huge demerit in a stealth game, but with a game as bloated & repetitive as this- it really brings the game down. -❌Would like to reiterate, why is there a half-assed combat system in a stealth game?-❌Too easy on any stealth run (ghost, spirit, demon). -❌SPOILER FOR LAST MISSION:  -❌When playing co-op, difficulty and guard-count is not increased to account for multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a very big fan of the original Aragami and completed it multiple times. I even speedran it in under 10 minutes. Consequently I (and the friend I played with in Aragami 1 COOP) were pretty hyped when we saw there should be a Sequel. Both of us immidiately preordered the game as we were hoping for a more refined Aragami, with a immersive story, cool stealth and nice new abilities. When the game finally feleased we immidiately started playing and were shocked. The game has next to nothing in common with its predecessor. The Shadow teleport which defined the first game is gone, replaced by a boring sprint and ledgegrap. The 1 vs 1 fighting is very lacking and feels kind of clunky. Moreover it has no real purpose as you are basically dead when you come to fight in a 1vs1. The COmbat could have been very good in boss fights which could have brought the aragami franchise to a new level, but guess what there are nearly no bossfight. The Abilities in this game feel boring as they are your standard stealth game abilities. The next really bad point is the story. There is no story or atleast not a story that you are really a part of. After each mission some characters tell you some information, but that is just boring as you see nothing of that exact story in the game itself. In Addition to that the level structure of the game is very lacking. Remember the unique levels in Aragami 1. They are gone, in this game you are constantly revisiting the same maps with some new tasks (like destroy 5 barrels). This makes the game feel very repetitive, boring and uninspired. I am honestly very dissapointed. The game is not completely bad, but lacks the identity of an aragami game.If you like Aragami I would not recommend buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: 🏯 First of all, the top reviews aren't updated and people are too harsh on this indie (still one of the best ninja stealth games that you can now play with friends!) The style has changed, but the design & atmosphere are still fascinating. The plot remained small, smooth and appropriate to the setting, but the gameplay was stretched (this is where more isn't better). Many missions are quite monotonous, as they are designed for co-op (locations are repeated, and there aren't enough bosses for variety). But the only real problem (since the classic gameplay was returned as an additional difficulty) is the “Unity clumsiness”, which creates minor bugs that can sometimes ruin half-hour missions that you wanted to get through undetected or without killing anyone. Various secrets help unlock more customization items, the arsenal is gradually expanding so there's plenty of replay value. The game isn't even close to bad, but yes, the first one was perceived better.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was a challenging, fun, and unique stealth game that I thoroughly enjoyed playing and replaying. This is everything that the first game was not. I played through the prologue and the first mission and I kept thinking to myself, "This feels nothing like Aragami." There's no hook to the story that made me invested--in fact, it just left me confused and irritated. The stealth mechanics are severely dumbed down, the levels felt linear, and the ability to engage in open combat was not a welcome one. Probably the one good thing was the ability to do non-lethal takedowns, though I kinda feel like that made getting a Spirit walkthrough too easy. This is nowhere near the challenge, nor the fun, nor the heart of the first game. In fact, I'd say that this is a sequel in-name-only, because not only does it not feel at all like the first game, it doesn't feel related to it, either. Don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this game is not the exact same as first game, but releasing the exact same game but with upgraded graphics is lazy and boring.Aragami 1 was a slow-paced and more or less tactical stealth game with a pretty annoying coop with barely any respawns Aragami 2 however, is has a much more casual, fast-paced gameplay, with parkour and freedom of movement, where being busted no longer meaning game over, instead allowing you to correct your mistakes and fight off an enemy that you've alerted, which also allows a fun, engaging, challenging non-stealth playstyle. The game still has great challenge and depth to it, it's still very challenging to try and be 100% stealthy+pacifist/demon. Level design is great, levels are big and barely restrict any movement, yet no level has those weird empty spots with nothing in them, instead they're filled with collectibles, enemies or objectives.Want to also say about the games perfomance, the game at launch has stable fps, next to no bugs that I've encoutered, doesn't force an online connection 24/7, with a fair price, which is rare for modern games to have.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost have no words for this review, as I think everything shown has already been said.But anyhow..Aragami 2 does not feel like a sequel. I have to get that out of the way. It's a total different approach. Almost like a reboot really. While Aragami 1 was mostly stealth focused, and got you in absolute great trouble if spotted (hell, my adrenaline was rising when I heard that horn go over..), Aragami 2 basically is the definition of stabbing someone infront of an enemy, saying "nothing to see here" and dumping the body in some tall grass or off a cliff. The stealth isn't a big focus anymore. Sure, it's recommended, and the combat is only really there so you have a way of defending yourself if you manage to screw up the stealth (Unpopular opinion: I...Actually kinda liked the combat. It's so janky making it funny but the camera movements and the quick decision to kill or knock out on the end is actually quite epic.), but stealth is really nerfed compared to the first game.I did have fun with the game though. Running around the levels, killing enemies while blood spurts everywhere and dropping bodies or throwing them off cliffs feels nice and great. But..Well..The best I can put it as is that it does not feel like an Aragami game. So if you are a fan of the first game and see this game called Aragami 2, and you probably going "Oh more Aragami?! HELL YEAH!", then don't expect much. The reaction you SHOULD be giving to enjoy this game is "Oh another game from the same devs? Seems quite nice!" because really..There's just so much different here compared to the first game but it CAN actually be quite fun (DESPITE THE REPEATING MISSIONS, I ALMOST FORGOT ABOUT THAT. THE MISSIONS ARE QUITE REPETITIVE BUT THEY DON'T GET TOO MUCH IN THE WAY IF YOU ARE A CASUAL PLAYER LIKE ME. I JUST PLAY FOR THE FUN ANYWAYS TO ENJOY THE REST). I just can only recommend it if you don't mind everything I just said..It's still a pretty fun game for me, despite feeling like an entirely different game. I suggest playing the tutorial and the first mission first (and maybe the second one too if you have the time for it), because that's kinda what you will be expecting for the rest of the game. Sort of. Just with different levels. If you don't like it then refund it. Don't waste more time. That's the best advice I can give.-------------------------EDIT: Ok so there's a new update, introducing Classic mode, which is much more closer to Aragami 1. I suppose it's a good decision but it's really a "too little, too late" situation. I mean I guess it's okay, I played it for a bit. I just want them to add the shadow paths as well and the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 takes the concept of Ninja stealth to the next level of Ninja stealth. That didn't sounded right was it?What i want to say is that this game is the underdog of indie games right now imo, the game looked down on due to the amount of bugs and graphic issues which i kinda agree. If you are really looking for the best stealth experience, i cannot word it enough of how much i recommend Aragami 2 as the best choice of both financial budget, PC game budget and... budget?The game is pretty easy to learn and master but sometimes there are moments that DOES make you think that this part was poorly made, but then you realiz how much accurate the stealth really is.Pros: -Fast-paced stealth and the reaction time you need just like a ninja, you have every tool of a true ninja to approach the enemies in various of different ways that you cannot imagine.-Three different playstyles with each having it's own talent and rune build which i find pretty impressive-Crossplay which is not something many games add these days.-Creative customize options and the return of [REDACTED] attire.-Lore weak but yet really touching story and sometimes actually makes you wanna drop tears.-Three player Co-Op is out of question, it's the best experience i ever had for a Ninja stealth game with a multiplayer. The game is extremely fun with friends, i cannot describe the perfection.-Intelligent and really challenging enemies, they actually act as a human and not a pure dumbass, and some enemies have different abilities and make your experience really challenging, by the way, did you know that they can climb walls?-Ninja, just Ninja. the way you can travel through the map or design your character is extremely creative.-The game is extremely long and offers ours of playtime, with the gameplay and the beautiful environment, this game never gets old since you also have to revisit the locations several times. Cons:-Bug fest, but it will be fixed soo.-Unachievable Medals because of problems with... coding?-Some location extra closes the doors to secrets so you actually have to load the right level in that location for the door to unlock.-Items get extremely expensive at one point. -NPC's mouths wont move when talking during cutscene.In short, I recommend Aragami 2 to every stealth fan, it may not be as good as games like Batman Arkham series, but sometimes it just offers something that i never saw in any other stealth game, which is what is making the game so unique that i will come back to the game once i finished it for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for Aragami 2, especially after enjoying the first game, but unfortunately, it falls short on multiple fronts. The stealth mechanics, which were the core strength of the original, feel clunky and unreliable. Enemy AI is inconsistent, often swinging from comically oblivious to unrealistically perceptive without any logical progression. The story is forgettable and lacks the engaging narrative that drew me in before. Character development is almost non-existent, making it hard to care about the protagonist or their mission. Additionally, the graphics, while slightly improved, still look dated compared to current standards, and the level design feels repetitive and uninspired.Multiplayer mode, which could have been a redeeming feature, is plagued by connectivity issues and lag, making it more frustrating than fun. Overall, Aragami 2 is a step back from its predecessor and fails to deliver a satisfying stealth action experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying currently i have about 7 hours in the game by the time i write this review, which means i have a neat grasp of the game and i will judge the game both as its own game and as a sequel to the first Aragami.As its own game, this is a fantastic stealth game where movement is smooth, there's a wide variety of gadgets that can be used for different playstyles and how you approach things, a clean HUD and UI, customization where you can make your character look like an assassin or a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bare chested monkey, and animations that are clean and quick.As a sequel to Aragami, its a bit complicated. The devs certainly have improved some things like how movement makes you feel like a ninja instead of a slow snail that needs teleportation to catch up to enemies while sneaking. The game has also added combat that is "passable", its certainly not the best but that's the point, as its supposed to be a last resort option instead of immediately giving you a game over in the first game. Customization has also improved by separating armor sets into four pieces (Headgear, Chestgear, Pants, Katana). The level design and AI has also changed due to the movement changing and how the dev's aim for bigger maps instead of linear levels like in the first game.Now here's the bad part about it being a sequel to Aragami, some stuff HAS indeed improved, but at what cost? Aragami 2 stripping away its identity as a sequel to Aragami. The shadow teleportation mechanic in the first game has been removed and has been replaced with a more simpler teleportation where you can teleport to ledges and you can roll to become shadow. Now some people say that this is a bad thing while i'm pretty fine with it, as the shadow teleportation wouldn't work due to the fact that movement has vastly improved over the first game and how shadows are less important in the second game. Speaking of shadows, you heard me right, shadows are widely less important in here, that shadow essence bar? removed for a stamina bar. Although i would put a reason being how lore wise that you're not the same Aragami as you were in the first game and blah blah blah, i would guarantee that you give ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about lore, but the actual reason was again, due to the movement being overhauled. Lince Works didn't have the skill and manpower at the time to create a movement system so they made the shadow teleportation in the first game so there's more movement with the use of the ability.I can go on and on but its better if i make a checklist of the pros and cons of the gamePros/Things that i liked about the game:-Movement has been overhauled-Animations are quicker than the first game-The game has RPG elements such as a skill tree that doesn't allow you to unlock every skill so to make co-op more interesting, and runic charms that you can imbue onto armor sets that give buffs and nerfs-Customization is waaay better than the first game-The game is longer than the first game-Clean HUD and UI-The soundtrack in the game is a banger-Banmoku has been removed for "Shadow vision", which is basically Eagle vision from AC-Maps are bigger and better and mixed in with the movement, will make traversing through it a breeze-Kurosu (the bird in the first game) is removed and now you can just use shadow vision to highlight where you're supposed to go, what your objective is, and where enemies are-How abilities are used is different from the first game as now there's a cooldown instead of running out of abilities-Consumables exist as you can heal yourself, throw shurikens to damage enemies during combat, smokescreen the area around you to blind enemies and cloak yourself, and more-A hub area-More enemy varieties-AI can now navigate through the maps so its harder for you to escape-An option to kill or to knock people out for genocide and pacifist runs-Enemies are woken up when they're asleep so to give an actual reason to knock people out instead of immediately killing peopleCons/Things that i didn't like about the game:-The story is "there", it certainly exists but not even a decent story to keep you engaged-They removed things from the first Aragami for better or for worse-There are too many levels (50) and too little maps (10), it will get repetitive-Shadows are less important as the only use for them is to make your character glow in the dark (like in the first game) and making enemies spot you slower when you are in shadow-Combat is dull but its a necessary dull as combat isn't the point-No checkpoints as the bigger map size would be difficult to implement it, no quicksaves too. BUT you get two lives in each mission so you have one more chance to press onward before you have to start over from scratch-Medals return from the first game but aren't as important and harder to get as there's more enemies and armor sets are gained from blueprints instead of medals-AI and enemies are sometimes questionable, sometimes there's enemies who wont leave their post, which is more realistic but gets annoying as you cant lure them in, and sometimes civilians (enemies who you cant kill/run away to alert real enemies) will just continuously run into wallsAnd a third section: Things that i didn't like about the game BUT will be fixed in later patches/dev's have acknowledged them and will be rolled in the next patch:-You cant stop the game when pausing it-Co-Op has issues such as delays, lag, etc, but its only the first week so no wonder theres a bunch of bugs-Bugs, you are likely to encounter one or two but its not as bad as most triple A games at this point, and its nothing game breaking like soft locking or crashing the game, just some minor ones-You can't remap controlsIn SummaryYou will not find a worthy successor to Aragami here, but you will find an awesome stealth game made by passionate devs who wanted to make a great ninja game. It can be summed up that Aragami 2 is the "true" Aragami experience as this was the game that they wanted to make and that they would have made when they were making Aragami 1 if they had the power to actually make it.As its own stealth game, i would rate it an 8/10As a sequel to Aragami, i would rate it a 7/10I'd buy it if it was under $20 bucks, i got it for $10, so its definitely worth the money. And all i'm gonna say, don't listen to the people that have below 1 hour in the game and complaining about the smallest things in the game and giving it a negative review. Listen to the ones that actually have feedback about the game and an actual reason that they cant recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not Tenchu... but I'll take it. And I like it!I wasn't a fan of the original Aragami. I like this sort of 'ninja simulator'. I like that if i get seen i can choose to fight or run. That is why I also liked those Tenchu games. Im really disappointing that many who look at this game seem to believe that this is just another stealth game. I fail to identify another single game that resembles this is so much as people seem to suggest. All the parts combined make it IMO only truly resemble Tenchu Z. From the way you can go over mission maps again with different goals, to the feudal era inspired setting. I can name as many contrasts to the myriad games that others are comparing this to. The stealth genre is wide and varied. If we judge, say, 1st person shooters by the same standard literally all those wildly hailed games appear to be clones of one and other, but we dont judge them so harshly. Why do we do so here?Its not without flaws. Controls can get a little wonky, sure sometimes; but gameplay is overall tight. One of my complaints is that i think its overall too bright, even with brightness set low. At some point we begin to nitpick. Overall this is filling a very specific gaming style which, honest to goodness, has been missing for decades. Its an enjoyable experience to boot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a major improvement over the previous game. It’s less stiff, has more fluidity in every aspect, and is genuinely more fun to play. But that doesn’t make it worthwhile in any way. It took me 13 hours to beat the story which consists of the exact same missions copy pasted onto the same 10 maps. A game like this shouldn’t have 50 missions given how they are recycled multiple times on each map with unnecessary lengths if played as intended. Because for a game that is all about stealth, it seems to do everything to discourage it. It’s simply smarter and faster to just rush each mission and ignoring stealth entirely. In retrospect, it was a huge mistake to rely on stealth constantly. The only reason I did so was due to the horrendous combat system this game has.Maybe the only reason to avoid direct confrontations. But then again, you don’t even need to do that. Simply running away will do just fine. My biggest grudge with the game aside from the stretched content is the lack of information you’re provided in every mission. There is no marker unless you’re close enough to your objective. In later missions that take place in vastly open maps, I would be running around aimlessly, trying to figure out where to go. They didn’t even bother giving an ounce of a hint to guide you. But who needs directions, am I right? Simply stating “Go to area” is all you need in a game that is about carefully moving around. Thanks for making these tedious missions even longer by letting me search a needle in a haystack.What else is there to say? A majority of the upgrades are absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and don’t benefit you whatsoever. The equipment system could have been interesting if the buffs actually made a difference. 10% added or subtracted from your stats won’t do ♥♥♥♥ all. Even accumulating them, I hardly felt a difference. Currency was also the last thing this game needed, but I suppose the item system does provide some room for experimentation. How fitting that I would remember to mention the story at the very end of the review, right where it belongs because just like my memory of it, it is completely forgettable. I eventually couldn’t take reading all this garbage dialogue anymore and simply skipped through everything because my level of tolerance had been tested too far at that point. There is only so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I’m willing to put up with until I lose interest. Not that I had any to begin with because this story belongs in a burning dumpster, right next to Frozen 2. I’m not sure what these developers were thinking when making this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but I’m glad they went bankrupt, deservingly so.

_childDocuments_.review: First off what made the first game special was the story and personality of the characters. And even if the stealth was sometimes clunky it was still far better than what this sequal has to offer! This game is clunky and troublesome to move around in at times, and I have it stuttering sometimes, especially in combat with the a.i. Which is pretty much a death sentence once you have three enemies on you because you can't run away due to the automatic lock on. Don't buy this game if you loved the first one. From my perspective I think Lince tried too hard to make the game about gameplay and failed at it due to the unity engine, and then forgot about the story which was solid in the first.Edit: If you are reading this after some time and see that I have more than five hours on it the reason for it is that I am still hoping that 1; it'll get better the further I progress and 2; I unfortunately see playing this game and completing it as a challenge due to all the B.S. mechanics.Edit 2: I now have over 30 hours playing this game and after completing the main story I still have no idea as to what the heck the ending was. (No spoilers though) I generally am pretty good at following a story even if I take breaks from a game, but this time I have absolutely no clue as to why the heck the ending was the way it was. And because of that said ending felt hollow for me. My original take on the combat is still generally the same I think I just got less frustrated with fighting as I got good. At the end, just like in the first game, I'm now able to go from stealth teleport kill to stealth teleport kill and so on fairly easily. Multiplayer experience was not the best, however I am willing to concede that it could very well be my internet connection rather than the game itself being bad. Like most casual games that have VOIP no one uses it or seems to hear me. Other than that doing missions with strangers is different so thats nice.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------------------------------Missed potential but appreciated what I gotPick it up on a sale, It's lacking the substance for full price.Achievement Hunting Difficulty:  Easy as balls, just be thorough and try a couple skills in your playthrough--------------------------------------------------------------------Aragami 2 gives you the choice to play as violently as you wish and does it's best to make combat based players viable. You'll quickly find however that playing a vengeful spirit isn't as efficient or as fun it would seem.Why spend the extra 10 - 20 minutes making sure everyone is dead on one of the larger maps so that when you win you get an arbitrary performance rating and the same XP that an efficient pacifist run would offer in less time?Now if you were to tell me that my playstyle had plot rammifications, NOOOOWWWW we're talking.Suddenly going through the effort to be a Ghost or a Demon is significant.You'd think the political parties you thwart would take countermeasures against the literal one mofo ruining their fun but no. They're content with regular guard routes and static observe posts.In fact, some missions require you to do a genocide run - making the illusion of player agency even more superfluous.Now when I say they "Do their best to make combat playstyles viable" I refer to the Essence System. Basically a buff that detracts from another skill. You can make yourself dish out more damage at the expense of stealth but in all honesty, you can break their LOS and just instant kill a guy and suddenly you realise you dont even need to touch this system beyond getting the achievement to apply one.I could pick from a few nails but I'll close this coffin with this:Returning to an old map with new areas unlocked and filling them with vague instructions and dumb objectives is what really hammered the tedium in for me."Aragami, I need you to make the journey to the capital city of some bastards messin' with our ♥♥♥♥ so you can cut the rope on 12 regular alarms, then travel back home so we can send you to another familiar place because we realised we needed to collect something from there - but hey the black wall of denying exploration has been lifted in an area so there is 25% more map for you to explore"I mean c'mon whats goin' on?------------------------------------------------------------------Sure. There is a thrill in navigating maps & moots efficiently, Unlocking cooler cosmetics tickles my brain & parrying anything gives me the false impression I would be just as good at it in Sekiro.I think with the introduction of some smaller details to flesh out the core systems and this would have been gold:- Throw in some spicy acrobatics when jumping/ long jumping. - Perhaps other weapons beyond swords exist in the Aragami world - What if the final boss .- What if the AI reacted to your typical strategies? EG:  "Oh, you use Darkflame to knock us out alot" - insert counter-measure.I very much am thankful that Lince Games is pushing through with expanding the Aragami franchise. I only wish that what we got in this sequel had more substance. I realise it's easy to ask for more without acknowledging the true scale of a task But I also believe every creative sets out to the do their best work, and Lince can do better.I wonder how Lince Games will use the lessons learned in making Aragami 1 & 2 in their next work

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked some of the changes made: the movement feels more fluid, there are more traversal options, combat is pretty fun and rewarding, and the option of lethal or non-lethal takedowns is a welcome change. The aesthetics are still on point for the setting, and the soundtrack is fitting and adds to the atmosphere. I don't mind the leveling system or that skills have a cooldown now and are no longer limited per se. Crafting and dying apparel is nice as it allows you to better customize your look (you can mix and match from different sets, and you have a helmet, upper body, lower body and sword slots). The hub area is a decent addition, as it offers a brief respite and allows you to interact with certain NPCs. Also, shadows and light are no longer as crucial as in the first entry in the series, which may rub some of the fans of the original the wrong way, but for me, it's not really an issue. Haven't noticed many bugs (fell through the map at one point and had to restart the mission, but otherwise nothing that game-breaking).The biggest problem with the story is that it's incredibly long, and it overstays its welcome. There are a few levels that get reused multiple times with the exact same layout and enemy positioning. Most of the quests in the main story are just fetch quests and are dull/uninspired; they could've been omitted or just be optional content to farm gold or find blueprints. Maybe playing co-op would alleviate some of the repetition and boredom, but the game is still flawed, and the campaign should've been much shorter (similar to the first game).Can't really recommend this one, as it feels like an exercise in frustration most of the time, and completing all missions/finishing the story is a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings it to the point when one thinks of "quantity over quality". Technically, the game is really good. The mechanics work, and while it may seem now more generic than the first Aragami game, I think a lot has improved and gives much more freedom to the player how to advance and what playstyle to pursue. Also, this gives a lot of replay values to the missions. That brings us to the elephant in the room: the missions. Most of them, apart from very few, are just mindlessly set on ever repeating maps. Go here, go there, grab that item, kill a target, save/kidnap a target... It gets repeated over and over again with almost no storytelling at all. This happens mainly in the hub area. I can see why they did this: the devs wanted to bolster the multiplayer part, and the way to do this, when not everyone wants to follow the story or skip cutscenes, is to do missions without any story to them. But it is just so boring to play through them. Even with changing maps, it feels like the same routine over and over again. Nothing really to discover, it just feels so bland. So instead of having over 50 missions that are totally forgettable, I would have preferred a dozen very well designed. Well, if you have nothing else to do and just want to throw some time away, you can just play a mission every evening (no save function inside a mission!), maybe you have some fun. But certainly this went into the wrong direction for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow feels like a downgrade visually and mechanically from the original.The original's shadow mechanics created this interesting gameplay loop where you could use shadows created by the environment or yourself for advanced mobility and setups, but this game feels like a disassociation from that in favor of promoting co-op and more aggressive gameplay.While not inherently a bad thing, the fact that the original game started off as this almost stealth-exclusive experience that gave you a very basic idea of what could otherwise be evolved into something greater, this "sequel" decides to do nothing innovative other than reformulating the entire concept into something worse than its original.Animations and textures are mediocre (even on high settings, as far as I could tell) and the story is so shoehorned into your face that it's difficult to appreciate anything the game is actually trying to say. There are so many 5 minute long cutscenes in the first 30 minutes that it feels like I'm watching an extremely mediocre movie moreso than playing a game.Just play the original Aragami. It's not perfect, but it's better than this.

That is because it doesn't follow the path left  by his predecessor. the dev team decided to completly rework the gameplay for a more dynamic version. If I can understand the desire to not stay on well known gameplay mecanisms, it looses in the process the first game's  idendity. To be more precise what annoy me is the lost of:  -the very good and warm graphics  of game 1-the well designed  lore,  and characters of game 1-the vital aspect  of shadows in game 1 which greatly force the player to be wary of lighting. and it add somes very debatable mecanism as such :- combat mecanism completly inspired by sekiro which  is very punishing. My problem with it is the fact the game discourage you greatly to go berserk and fight enemy. we may  appreciate the new combat system, but I would have prefered an improvement on  others aspects of the game.-The fact IA is VERY impredictible with their detection. Sometimes guards are blind and deaf and other time they instant detect you when you are invisible or when you kill a mobs outside their normal range detection ( like they are outside a building and detect you while you are at the first floor and far from windows )  -It have so much bug than its become artistic.-the game is  very  easy and , more problematic,  without  difficulty settings : that is a very problematic issue for players looking for a challenging experience.- A lore completly inexistant and inconsistant. Sometime, you can play some hours without any cutscene and at some point, you will encouter 3 cutscene very close to each other.  The story itself is badly narrated. its not clear and the fact cutscene are rare and the story is greatly explained by subtitles outside cutscene is not very immersive. i spend some time  resisting the urge to just skip some subtitle.Another issue is the fact your caractere sometime speak ( very few line I must admit) and sometime he become mute ( you can see the classic '...' during cutscene. maybe the dev team had some budget issue ? still its very annoying and break any attempt to immerse the player. Moreover, during cutscene, when someone speak , his lips doesn't move. at the same time, characters, still during cutscenes,  seem very static and not dynamic at all ( specialy during the encounter with the antagonist when your character is pushed back by you don't know what) and some cutscenes are a real mess at the point you don't understand what is going on.....- the maps ! that is very boring. You will play on the same 6-7 maps  but fragmented. At the beginning, you will have access to a tiny part of the maps but as the game go on, you will access more part of each maps.the fact you play on the same maps during the entire game is , for me very dissapointing, i would have prefered to play on differents smallers maps   than returning on the sames maps again and again and again.- Finally the fact some quest are clearly here to fill the game and add nothing. for example at some point you will have to kill some specific foes somewhere on the map and you will have to do the same quest 3 or 4 time before continuing the main quest..... this is boring, lazy and add nothing so it is very disappointing.-the fact somes skills does not work as the lure. Aragami 2 looses a lot and add some debatable mecanism. before finishing, i will just mention the good point which is the insane  movment which is very enjoyable ( even with the huge nerf on shadow leap wich is  understandable after the change on mobility) and the improved customisation which is always enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: A shame the studio closed down, it had potential but there were frequent bugs, mostly due to collision being mostly a suggestion.Fell down out of the map often, sometimes when teleporting to a ledge or beam it instead catapults you across the map...Seemingly randomly you stand up after a teleport, had to restart quite often due to this going for no detection runs.The story was drawn out way longer than it needed, could have combined some of the shorter missions or just cut some of them out, 51 missions was a bit too long to the point it got annoying near the end.Did all missions no kills and all kills, at least one of them undetected and with classic controls (so teleport worked the same as Aragami 1, enjoyed this more than the original move set of 2)Had some problems on one of the longest missions, mostly due to the teleport standing up problem and the hardest type of enemy can detect you out of your ability range. so took several tries to get it done and was frustrating near the end as it often failed at no fault of my own, collision bugs, detection when they shouldn't as if a wall didn't exist sometimes.But overall was fun if a bit longer than it should have been, would have Gladly looked forward to Aragami 3 but again as the studio closed down that won't happen nor will the bugs get squished but it's playable and no game breaking bugs.Playtime inflated as i left it on now and then, can only play short bursts (due to health reasons) so often didn't bother closing it down until i tried again.Probably doable for most people in around 20h if going for all 4 medals on every mission (All killed, no killed, ghost and classic mode)

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a lazy crashgab, which only exist due the success of the first title. While most people complained about the combat, which I think is fine, that is not the issue here:This game has 10 playable areas. Some of them are okay, some of them are awful. They reused the same areas dozens of times which leads to repetition. Also have I mentioned there are no checkpoints in missions? Meaning if you die 20 minutes in a mission, you have to do all of that again. Another thing is, there is no continuity in the plot, which leads me to the next point:The first games story was linear you went from area to area, while the story progresses. It wasn't complex but it worked.In this game most of the story progress happens in the village, meaning most of the missions have no connection to the story, which makes them feel like filler-missions to make the game longer.This game has 51 missions, which sounds a lot, but you only have 4 different tasks in different variations:Knowing that, you could cut out 45 out of the 51 missions and the story would stay the same.Most of the bugs where fixed post launch but there are still a lot of them in the game, which get especially noticable in the late game missions, where the game starts to get really hard.Some of the bugs I've encountered are:While I bought the 2nd game close to release because I really liked the first one, especially the DLC, which was great, I won't do that for the 3rd title, if they ever release one to see if they learned out of their mistakes.I guess at least you can buy the armor and sword of the Main Character of Aragami 1.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine for what it is. Very nice customization (it isn't skyrim or some RPG level of customization but you have armor sets and weapons. The new skill tree is good, allow you new gameplay variety (you can even go into combat now if you want or when you fk up your stealth. It is kinda like sekiro but more clunky). _childDocuments_.review: A good sequel, all things considered. Not as purist as the first installment and sometimes even feels like an early access game =/ Good load times, though.Rather unlike the first game, this one allows for combat. The combat is very much like Sekiro - decrease the enemy's stamina with parries, then kill them (or knowck them out if you wish to)However, just like the first game, you can stealth and kill unaware enemies with one attack. The new shadow leap allows you to climb ledges and traverse rooftops and does not consume energy/stamina, so your mobility is better.Plenty of abilities to unlock eventually but no safe ranged option initially.The art style and music are quite pleasing.. Also, some things that should be possible (one button stealth klills from ledges and such) are not in the game either, but they .I hoped for a straight evolution of the stealth game but this will have to do, considering the genre draught.If you're unwilling to buy the game right now, you might want to at least keep an eye on it. Aragami 2 has potential to become even better in a few patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing Aragami back in 2016. i loved the story and had so much fun both playing it solo and with my friend. Now Aragami has returned better than ever AND I ADORE THE CUSTOMIZATION. At the time of this review there are some small bugs and glitches, but don't let that scare you off. this game has a good story line and plenty of customization. your missions are done in a few different levels with different layouts to do your stealthy killing(or knocking out :D), but if you prefer the "not so stealthy approach" then go for it!Customization in the game has been done in a way that i personally like a lot, your armor is divided into 4 pieces (that can be earned and found throughout the game) but these are purely cosmetic and give no benefits other than looking awesome, the 4 pieces are as following- Mask- chest-piece- pants/leg-piece- swordIt is possible to dye your armor as well, each dye needs to be purchased once and can then be applied to all cosmetic pieces.Compared to the first game you now don't rely on the shadows to regenerate your abilities (no more constant sneaking, such a blessing) and your stamina is shown under a health bar. this is a big change compared to the first game in which a cape was used to show your energy and you had no option to attack enemies out in the open as a tactical approach because you would die instantly.There are plenty of maps in the game. Going through the story, you won't notice it that easily but you eventually repeat the same maps over and over. At the moment this is no problem for me, but i have a feeling that endgame this might have people not enjoy the game as much as they are right now. Then again, this is simply a small thing i noticed but honestly do not mind. I'm used to these kind of things because I've played a lot of RPG's in my life.Multiplayer is a little bit wonky if i say so myself and needs some work, crossplay is an option but for that to work you need to use a specific workaround if you are in different regions (EU/US), if you are in the same region you can easily join through the public lobby system on both console to steam and vice versa. The multiplayer system is simple, you can create a public or private lobby or join a public lobby through the in-game  tab, joining private lobbies is done by receiving an inviteAt the time of this review, rebinding your hotkeys is not possible, this was at the beginning of the game the first thing I wanted to do, but after getting used to the layout anyways, i paid it no mind. This is a small "ease of access" thing that most games have, however .The workaround is only available if you play with 3 people at once and is done as follows: we have player A(EU steam), player B(US steam) and player C(US XBOX).If player B hosts, player A joins via the steam invite sent by player B. Player C can join via public lobby menu

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is fairly different from its predecessor. It's faster-paced and uses a replayable mission system with varying difficulty. I also started with Aragami 1, and I see these two games in the same way I see Dishonored 1 & 2: each is different, each has strengths the other lacks. If you're going into this as an Aragami 1 player, keep that in mind.They also more recently added a "classic mode"  that tries to mirror the original game, which you can use at any time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth noting that while Aragami 2 improves on the visual style, music and feel of the original, it is not entirely the same style of game. Aragami 1 was very much built around the teleporting through shadows mechanic. Whereas Aragami 2 is more like, what if the early Tenchu games without the clunky controls and mobility. That's the feel I get while playing the game, zipping through the levels like a shadow of death ready to perform my mission.I understand some people have concerns. The reused levels on the one hand, might seem repetitive to some, for me I like the way you come back to the same location, with different guard layouts and different areas of the map to infiltrate.Some say the fluid movement makes the game too easy. I think that may be true if your goal is simply to finish a given level. I still find it challenging going for some of the triple playstyle elements, especially the unseen aspects.Some have complained about the unattackable civilians who exist solely to raise the alarm. Whilst they did confuse me the first time I met one, this is not an unknown concept in the genre and is an interesting obstacle that can't be dealt with in the usual, stabby manner.I haven't tried the co-op yet but I know the slower pace of Aragami 1 was sometimes frustrating in co-op, especially simply waiting to recharge or waiting patiently for guard patterns so you could breach an area on  a no-kills run. The improved mobility feels like it would really benefit the co-op experience and I'm eager to try it.There are some minor bugs. Nothing too drastic for me. Fell through the world once and there's a vaulting bug that's been addressed and marked for patching but these kind of things are expected for an indie project.Ultimately, I sat down to play this at 6pm last night "for an hour or two" and finished up around 1am. So, yeah, beyond all those concerns I still had an absolute blast. I still think there's some room for improvement for an Aragami 3 to really encapsulate the full modern Tenchu experience but this is yet another giant leap forward. In a market still oddly devoid of such games, Aragami will continue to be king.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a sequel to Aragami if you didn’t read the number 2 right there. It takes place like 100 years after the events of the first game or so I’ve read somewhere. After playing through the game, I realized that you don’t really need to have played the first game to understand this one. The only thing you’ll miss out on are some references to the first game, but nothing major.The gameplay is like any other stealth game. You do objectives while sneaking past enemies, while being able to knock out the enemies or outright kill them. In this new game, the developers decided to add a mechanic where you can now fight your enemies in combat, rather than simply die immediately like in the first game. The combat is ♥♥♥♥ though, and you can usually win if you just spam left click and time a right click somewhere in that. There’s also no merit to combat, except for one mission that involves you fighting a boss-type enemy in combat. In fact, there’s not much merit to other things too.For example, let’s say I had an enemy blocking my path. It’d be best if that enemy just didn’t exist at all. So now, you have 2 options: kill or knockout. Whichever one you pick doesn’t really matter in the long-scheme of things. If you knock out the enemy and someone finds the body, they just wake the person up and stay alarmed for a bit. If you kill the enemy and someone finds the body, they warn others and get alarmed even more. But, none of that matters if you just hide the body well enough. The only other thing you can consider is style points when killing enemies, but unless you’re recording a video for YouTube then who the ♥♥♥♥ would even be watching your “stylish executions” that you’re proud of??Mission objectives are basic, and tedious. There’s 51 missions, and a lot of them are the exact same ♥♥♥♥. Here’s how it works:You have different areas in which you can have missions, with each different mission involving different parts of different areas. One mission may have 1/3 of area A while another mission has only the other 2/3 of area A. The issue is that there are not 51 areas, there’s like around 10 at best. This means you’re running through the same areas, doing more or less the same objectives. Again, the objectives are simple, and it gets pretty tedious.At first, I found the reusing of areas good, because it allows you to go about areas with prior knowledge of the areas and, with being able to unlock skills and such, allow you to go about areas in different ways. At first, I liked it. Then I reached probably mission 20 before really being tired of this. The game is a slog in the middle, and the story doesn’t clutch up at all. Speaking of which, story time!The story I cannot even put to words, because I don’t understand ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about what happened. The start of the game was confusing; I literally had no idea what was happening at all because the game just threw at me these names that I was just supposed to know? Of course it’s not THAT bad, I ended up learning who the hell were these people that I had to care about. The story does have its twists and turns, but it fails to be engaging in any sort of way. In contrast, the story in the first game, Aragami, was a lot more engaging. The first game cut down on the amount of characters you needed to care about, told the story in a linear fashion, and featured cutscenes that really solidified the whole experience. Aragami 2 has none of that I’m afraid. I have no attachment to any of these characters; I could care less if the home base were to get raided by the enemy. Oh, the first game’s protagonist had a voice actor, and the second game does not. While good in a roleplaying sense, this isn’t a roleplaying game, and so it suffers because we’re playing a voiceless character that doesn’t really seem to have much emotion at all. In other words, you play a boring kind of guy. Ok, I would be lying to say that the story was bad. It’s not; it’s just ok. There isn’t anything I could really praise about the story, but it doesn’t make it bad. It really is just ok.I’ve mentioned enough about what I don’t like about the game. However, there’s some good stuff too.I mentioned it previously but you can unlock skills. The skills are entertaining, with some really useful and others ok. You have active skills which are the fun ones, and passive skills that are mostly basic but some of them are interesting. My favorite active skill is one where you can blow out torches, knocking out any enemies that are nearby them. It’s a simple yet incredibly useful skill, that I managed to not go on a mission without using them (bit of an exaggeration). Another cool skill is one called Shadow Kill, where you can just kill someone from afar with a pretty badass animation. Handy? Yeah, it gets the job done and can be effective in also hiding the body, as the body just poofs away pretty much. Cool as ♥♥♥♥? Hell yeah.To get skills, you need to level up. The max level is 30, and you aren’t able to get all the skills with 30 skill points. Thankfully, you can reset your skill points so you can get rid of skills that you absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ despise and switch on over to the cool ones like Shadow Kill.As a last note, there is multiplayer. The multiplayer I haven’t personally tried, because I have no friends who’d bother playing a stealth game with me. From what I’ve heard, the multiplayer works alright, but I would recommend playing with friends rather than randoms. Naturally, you’re more than welcome to play with randoms. I just think it’d be a ♥♥♥♥ ton of fun with friends.There’s also bugs, but it’s been a while since I’ve finished the game so some of them may have been patched. Most bugs are game ruining so beware.Overall, game aight. 7/10

name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles
detailed_description: Immerse yourself in a dramatic yet charming and witty world of evidence-gathering, deduction and courtroom battles with this double-pack of the adventures of rookie lawyer Ryunosuke. Set in late 19th century Japan and England, each title features five murder-mystery episodes filled with all the drama, laughs, twists, and “turnabouts” you’ve come to expect from the legally labyrinthine legacy of Ace Attorney. Join Ryunosuke Naruhodo, ancestor of series mainstay Phoenix Wright, as he attempts to uncover the secrets behind an international criminal conspiracy and solve a hauntingly baffling cold case, while tackling a series of tricky trials along the way. Dozens of hours of attorney action awaits you! In the course of each case, you’ll speak to witnesses, examine evidence and clues, and attempt to deduce the dastardly intent behind the crime before proceeding to the courtroom. In court, you will hear testimonies, cross-examine witnesses, and present evidence. And of course, it wouldn’t be an Ace Attorney game if you couldn’t shout “OBJECTION!” when you know you’ve got the facts and evidence needed to contradict the prosecution’s claims and prove your client’s innocence. The game includes a convenient assistance feature in case you hit a dead end in your investigation, so even if this is your first Ace Attorney game, you can get into your amateur sleuthing adventures with ease! Will you be able to crack these clever cases? The game is afoot! NOTE: This game can be played with English audio or with Japanese audio and English subtitles.
