_childDocuments_.review: After finally beating the duology, 100%, I decided to edit my review. But if you just want to know if you should buy this or not, then my answer is this: if you're a fan of Ace Attorney, then you definitely should, as I'm sure you'll love it. If you're new to Ace Attorney, I feel like you shouldn't because then you won't be able to appreciate everything that TGAAC does for the franchise, but on the other hand I've seen people that have gotten into the franchise with this one, so it's not like it's the worst entry point for the series either.I'll start by saying that this, as a duology, is one of the best entries in the series in many ways - visual, story, characters, etc. - however, I would also rather review each game separately, as I do feel that'd be a fairer approach to each of them. I'll also try avoiding spoilers, but do read at your own risk if you haven't finished the game.For starters, Adventures was by far my favorite of the two. Of very particular note is the fact that, either for better or worse (personally, for better), Adventures was bold enough to actively break many established molds of the franchise. While I understand that the cases being composed only of one-day investigation and one-day trial could be detrimental, I feel like writing the trials with this format in mind really helped the pacing of the game greatly. And, in fact, I also like the fact that there's an entire 'case' that doesn't even have a trial section at all! As I said, a break from the mold. The pacing is good enough that I do feel like no case overstayed its welcome, and the finale of case 5 really makes you feel like you earned hearing the "Great Pursuit" at last.Resolve, on the other hand, for better or worse (personally, for worse), goes back to the series's roots in more than one way, and while I understand that the budget for Resolve was significantly lower than Adventures, sadly I will formulate my next points without that fact in mind. For starters, we're back to every case having a trial section, which makes sense - that's what people play Ace Attorney for - and definitely not something I raise an objection to, however... every single case is forced into the formula of two days of investigation and two days of trial. For better or worse, this means that some cases either drag on for unnecessarily long (case 2) or are simply too short for their own good (case 3), which really helps to killing the pacing of the game. On the topic of the pacing, rumors circulate around that the Great Ace Attorney was meant to be a trilogy, and in fact some people have said that's not true, it was always meant to be a duology - and at first even just a single game - but that'll make my next point even worse for the game: the pacing of the "grand overarching mystery" (trying to avoid spoilers but you know what I'm talking about if you played it already) is totally butchered by the simple fact it gets introduced late into case 3 and by early into case 5 you've already resolved it, not to mention how short case 4 already is by itself. And case 5... well, stop reading from now if you don't want to risk spoilers, but... I totally hated case 5's conclusion. The main villain basically just blatantly and shamelessly confesses to everything as soon as Ryunosuke vaguely hints at him being a villain, and that really sucks because it makes 'defeating him' feel rather shallow, especially with one of the best breakdowns and tracks (Resolve 2017) being wasted on Sholmes's 'checkmate strategy' sequence.In short, I prefer Adventures over Resolve because it has a much better pacing compared to its sequel, Resolve, but they both come in the same package regardless and both games are already good anyways, so this duology is definitely worth playing for avid Ace Attorney fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a big fan of the Ace Attorney since I was a high school student. The plot, the tricks used, and the connections I built with the characters have always intrigued me. Upon finishing this game, I do want to say the game itself is interesting, but there is something lacking as compared with the older version of Ace, making it a good game, rather than a classic staple. I am not a English native speaker. While I understand most of the script in the game, some of the language used in the game seem challenging to understand (especially with slang/accent). I don't want to read every script out loud to understand, however, I won't be able to fully understand the meaning without doing that. Not sure whether native speakers will have similar problem though..Another issue I have with the game is that I feel the length is a little bit too long and the connections among different chapters are weak. I kept forgetting the plot from previous chapters and had to kept reminding myself. One plus I love in this game is they add the feature of auto solving the case (story mode). There are some puzzles that are very challenging to solve and that feature can help you get over those puzzles.

Thats laudable, not laughable.No one has the right to deride another for such choices.~Baron Van ZieksGreat Story, characters, soundtrack, plenty of Interactivity, very attached to each of the characters, and memorable.When the Journey ends, you'll be desperate and wanting more of their adventure.Like me, reminiscing the adventure that i've had, with listening to the amazing OSTs.Salute to CAPCOM and the team behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: Someone was wrongfully accused and as a lawyer it's your job to uncover the truth. At the core of this is a visual novel with a lot of gameplay elements. But be warned, It's not a passive experience far from it, you will be actively presenting evidence, focusing on topics, identifying inconsistencies in certain statements and more. You will have to put your thinking hat on and will have to be in the right mental energy when playing this. The writing and story is very easy to get into. But don't expect too much character development, most of the time you spend time on the case at hand and rarely will you have interactions outside of them. I think this was by design in order to focus on the courtroom drama. The writing often takes an interesting and absurd turn of events unfolding as the investigation continues. The main characters are likable and sometimes we get bits of humor, it helps not to take things too seriously. Overall it is well written and keeps you guessing on what could happen next.The music and artwork are simply excellent. Some of the negatives are: a lot of coincidences in the plot, verbose writing like the story sometimes repeats itself with clues or deduction already established.Now this is a big game, well actually you get the 2 games for a total of 75+ hours. There is a lot of reading with no voice over and that did put me off at first but I got used to it. Personally, I found it exciting and unpredictable. I never played the other Ace Attorney games and I’d definitely recommend this one for anybody wanting to read and play something interesting.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview:So i have just finished The first of the two games in the chronicle, 50 hours played id say its already money well spent! (I believe i bought on sale for  12-13 GBP)An introduction to the mechanics is necessary for new players and is definitely a must have in the first episode of the game (it has 5 episodes in the first game), having played Phoenix Wright: ace attorney i found it slightly hand-holdy but for new players to the ace attorney games this won't even notice this as the mechanics and gameplay are unique to most other games. Besides the first episode is by far the shortest and mainly sets up the narrative for the rest of the game whilst still being a compelling story in and of itself.After this 'tutorial episode' The game truly spreads its proverbial wings, In terms of difficulty and Rich and captivating story, Similar to reading a book you simply cant put down you find yourself compelled to continue the investigations and trials in order to satisfy your thirst for the next story beat. 100% of the time its worth it! Great story and unique diverse characters you, don't immediately, learn to love.Gameplay:Unique to the series, however Quite basicAlthough the gameplay is basic, Point and click adventure- esque meaning examine rooms and catalogued evidence for clues or questioning witnesses, thats all the gameplay has to be! The real satisfaction is using all this information and putting pieces together in your head of how events went down or at least how it could possibly have went down. and uncovering the story which you undoubtedly get invested in (at least i did).Story:The game's greatest asset!The story is linear, whilst this does hold some problems ill list at the bottom in the good/bad points , Meaning no matter what you do the story will play out the same.. This may sound like a negative point but on the contrary. I love Choices matter, Tell-tale like games such as 'the walking dead 'or a 'wolf among us' these stories are great but not as quite as refined as they can be. This is where linear storytelling shines, the writes only have to focus on one storyline and because of that.. the twists and turns are more fleshed out and also the ways in which the twists are revealed are more satisfying as they're usually down to a discrepancy in evidence or witness testimony that you yourself have pointed out. Even though its linear and progresses only if you present the right argument and evidence once you are immersed in the story and acting as a lawyer/detective you truly believe that your choices matter... even though they dont.Difficulty:Not Difficult but still a fun amount of puzzle solving. now personally i did not find the game hard per say and believe i only failed one trial throughout the remaining episodes(upon which you can simply retry from a similar position in the trial or from the beginning of the trial).Throughout a trial you have 5 lives, giving the wrong evidence for your current theory will result in a life lost, once no lives are left you must restart the trial which is definitively more of a nuisance than it is necessarily difficult as most of the time you just have to re-watch a few boxes of dialogue before you try amend your mistake.This all sounds like a hassle but if you follow the dialogue and examine evidence thoroughly it actually ends up being the perfect level of difficulty, assuming you don't get stuck and present every piece of evidence one by one in hopes of striking lucky.Good:- Great stories and characters all intertwined with one another- satisfying payoffs for solves in the form of story progress- very relaxing game for when BR's or Competitive games are too much- 50 Hours of story and im only halfway through! Cheaper than a book and its interactive, No brainer!- Addictive! i think these 50h playtime are only over the course of a week!Bad:-Although i love the stylized graphics i cant exactly say they're groundbreaking.-Somewhat slow start-A game probably not everyone would enjoy however for those who are interested in detective stories its actually a great find.- Failure in a trial isn't actually detrimental.. just downright annoying.- No Japanese voice acting for majority of text (not sure if English is fully voice acted.)Outro:Whilst i realise this game may not be for everyone i implore you if you are even somewhat curious or have the slightest appeal... Try it! underneath its basic aesthetics is a surprisingly satisfying gameloop and story.  Especially on sale! Thumbs up if you found this helpful :)

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished the game on Android devices a few weeks ago, I highly recommend this game now. The story is great and in-game mechanism is very interesting. The 'turning around' elements are now more structural and embedded within the whole story in a rather subtle and symbolic way. It's no longer the forced 'turn around' as in Ace Attorney 1, 2, 3. It's also great to see how the game discuss the themes of ethnic racism and internationalism in that fictional yet realistic early 1900s. It's inspiring and sometimes consoling to read between lines about how in the game the Brits and the Japanese find common grounds as human beings.That said, lacking any Eastern Asian language (e.g. CJK) is rather disappointing. I understand that it's Japanese students studying in the UK, so they ofc speak English. Still, it's a pity that young people in Eastern Asia countries, especially those that still lack a just legal system, cannot play and experience the story in a language that connects more with them. I wish one day Capcom would supplement this release with proper Eastern Asian languages.Also, it's 2021 and still there's no high definition texture. It's a shame, really.对中文或日文用户来说，可以购买此游戏，然后自己找国内汉化组过去的汉化版本在电脑上玩。此版故事和机制都很不错。然而可惜没有中文或日文等语言，使我等东亚学生不得以更亲近的语言游玩并感同身受。其他评价可阅读以上英文不想（主要是不想再写一遍）。

_childDocuments_.review: This game improved a lot on what Ace Attorney is about. The story and the characters were so well written that I had actually believe I was in London during the Victorian Era and that these people (Susato, Herlock, Iris, Kazuma) were actually my friends. It was such a bizarre experience that I would love to relieve again. I recommend that you should never play this game with music turned off or listening to other music while playing, simply because the soundtracks are a bunch of masterpieces, not a single song in the entire OST is bad and it fitted well with the time period. Naruhodo's objection theme is a must hear because of how epic it is. More gameplay mechanics were introduced to make the game less of a visual novel and more focused on the gameplay aspect of discovering the truth, since the legendary Herlock Sholmes is guiding us along the way after all.The game featured the most awesome main protagonist, Ryunosuke Naruhodo, who is literally Phoenix Wright's ancestor. Along with Susato Mikotoba being the best legal assistant in any Ace Attorney ever, not to mention his wonderful best friend Kazuma Asogi who is very similar to Miles Edgeworth. And the most badass prosecutor Barok van Zieks, a legend amongst the court. And of course Herlock Sholmes, the most funniest and enjoyable character in the game. Overall, everything is great about this game and there's no denying why it is called "The 'Great' Ace Attorney Chronicles". Wonderful story, lots of play time, great music, an amazing casts of characters. Such a charming game that I will never forget along side the Ace Attorney Trilogy. ∞/10!
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: After playing both games and the side content to the end, I can say that this is probably the best ace attorney game out there. After playing the phoenix wright trilogy, AJ, and DD, this game has plot writing that overtakes all of those. The murder mysteries aren't as insane and crazy as the original trilogy, but all the good of this game from Herlock Sholmes to the character development of Barok Von Zieks, this game is absolutely f*cking fantastic. The game's story ends with the second game so there's no need to continue Ryunosuke's story, but I wouldn't mind if we got more...
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like the culmination of everything the AA devs have learned over the years. The story, the characters, the music and the cases are all absolutely brilliant being among the best in the entire series. I have played all the Ace Attorney games and in my honest opinion these games are among the best, rivaling and in some ways winning over the original trilogy. Although this collection contains both GAA1 and GAA2 they really should be considered one long game as the over arching narrative spans both adventures. Its a slow burn at first as the game takes time to establish the setting and plot but once it starts going the you wont be able to stop until the end. I would highly recommend this game not only to Ace Attorney fans but to anyone who wants a good and fun adventure to go on!
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've played just about every published Ace Attorney game, and I have to say that the Great Ace Attorney games are among the best in the entire franchise. The music is beautiful and moving; perfectly matched to the scenes and adding a great deal to the game. The characters are unforgettable, and their writing is the best I've seen from the ace Attorney games. There are no wasted or one-dimensional characters; character arcs have beautiful nuance and great emotional payoffs. The story line is one of the most complex ones I've seen from Ace Attorney, owing to the fact that it's spread over two games and given the time it needs to develop. This game is even friendly to newcomers to the series, as it exists within its own self-contained world, so there's no need to have played any other games or even know anything about Ace Attorney to enjoy this game. I cannot recommend this game highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Personally my favorite installment of the series. It has been quite enjoyable to play. Below are some things to consider for your purchase though:PROS:>Amazing and funny story>Fun new mechanics and dialogues with charming individuals>Enticing cases that will have you on your feet from start to finish>Beautifully orchestrated musicCONS:>Some visual/input glitches may occur (save often if you haven't gotten used to it by now my fellow AA fans)>(I don't have much else to say, it's really good)BUYER BEWARE:Due to the time period of which the games take place, do not let it surprise you if you find sexist or xenophobic content within. It is to make the environment more true to the time period of which it is simulating and adds some interesting aspects to the story which you will experience during gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: So, here we are again in the courtroom. I'm a big fan of the Ace Attorney series (I've played all the games, including AAI2), and was anxiously waiting for this one to be released as well. Overall, I'm very happy with the game. And in summary, this is pretty simple: if you like Ace Attorney, you'll like this game. If you don't, this won't change your mind. If you've never tried it, I would recommend playing the Ace Attorney Triology first, and coming back here after that.Let's now dissect this a bit more for anyone interested.Let me start with what I didn't like so much, just to get it out of the way:- The pacing. There are two games in this collection, and I gotta be honest, the first one is pretty... slow. I started getting actually really tired in 3 of those cases. This happened due to many things, but especially because, different from most Ace Attorney games, the investigations and trials are one huge block; most of the time in other AA games, you switch back and forth, but during Adventures, I don't think that happened even once, and I really don't think that worked. The second game (Resolve) was a great improvement in this aspect.- [English] Some of the voice acting is... not fantastic. Ryunosuke's "Objection!" felt super weak, unfortunately. "Hold it!" and "Yes!" were pretty good, but "Objection!" is the main one for hype and emotion and it left a lot to be desired. In general, I really liked Barok van Zieks' and Kazuma's VA, but other than those two... yeah, sorry.- The second game clearly had lower budget and did not have any "anime" animations like the first one, which was a shame.Now, let's go through the good stuff:- The localization. God, I love it. It's superbly well done. This is a thing Ace Attorney has generally done great in the past, but this might be the best one. I loved how the written dialogue expressed different accents. How you could tell if they were speaking Japanese or English based on how they address each other in text ("Susato-san" vs "Ms. Susato"). Just... everything about it, honestly. Give whoever worked on this a raise, please.- The cases. As I mentioned before, the pacing of the first game could be much better, but the cases themselves are great. Just what you would expect from this series.- The characters. I love all of them (again, as expected of an Ace Attorney game). Ryunosuke is great, Susaso is great, Gina is great, Gregson is great, Iris is great, everyone is just great. Special shout-out to van Zieks and Sholmes. Van Zieks is one of the best prosecutors and characters we've had yet for sure, his development from the start all throughout to the last chapter is incredible to see; and Sholmes is just legitimately the funniest character in any AA game ever, while also still being true to his original counterpart. - The soundtrack. Do I even need to say it, how this is just as expected from the series? Yeah, it's fantastic.- Resolve. As I mentioned before, the first half of this experience (Adventures) wasn't that great on its own in my opinion (don't get me wrong, it's still really good, but it wouldn't be Top5 in the series for me), but the second half, Resolve, more than makes up for it. It's just incredible, and the build-up is completely worth it. In conclusion, Chronicles gives you everything you would expect. There should be no disappointments here: if you know what you're getting into, you'll enjoy it. Just don't stop playing in the first game; as mentioned, the second is way better. All you need is...  to see it through.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my favourite of all the Ace Attorney games. In terms of the story and setting, it is indisputably my favourite. Right from the very first tutorial chapter, the game is already introducing many of its important themes and topics. International politics and corruption getting in the way of justice. Legal systems racing to keep up with the explosion of science and technology in the early 20th century. The imperialism of Victorian-era Britain exerting its influence upon Meiji-era Japan. The undercurrent of racism that permeates the colonialist mindset. And yet, despite all of these big ideas, the story of this game is first and foremost character-driven. All of the main and supporting characters are wonderfully fleshed out and believable, and their relationships change and grow across the two games in this collection. Unlike the mainline Ace Attorney games, the first Great Ace Attorney game ends in a cliffhanger and which is continued in the second game, so you should think of this collection as one 10-chapter game rather than two 5-chapter games, and the additional length really gives the story room to grow and develop over time.

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney is a spin-off of the Ace Attorney series, a visual novel with the theme of being a lawyer. This is a great entry if you haven't played Ace Attorney. Most of the time you are investigating, collecting evidence, and piecing the puzzle together like a detective. There are no multiple outcomes, just one correct answer. So, you'll be tested if you can piece the story with the evidence you have. It's not an accurate lawyer sim and you are here just for the puzzle & story beat.This game takes place at the end of the 19th century and the dawn of the 20th century. I may be biased because I recently read some Sherlock Holmes and Arsene Lupin novels, but I can not overstate how amazing the setting is. By being limited to the technology of that era, the cases and story progression are engaging. There are no fingerprints, DNA readings, channelling, and so on. Most of the time you are trying to persuade the jury that your theory is sound and correct. They will have a hard time because the truth is outrageously insane, it's your job to make them believe.Compared to the Ace Attorney Trilogy, these are easy puzzles. I have fewer problems in court cases and things piece together easily. Because of that, some characters can be really dumb when you already know what is going on. It definitely takes its time until the 2nd game (Resolve) where difficulty finally ramps up. Initially, things are slow and some story plots are left hanging. However, the cases in these games are building up to the grand finale in the Resolve. When it finishes, it REALLY finishes. This is by far my favourite conclusion of an Ace Attorney game, which is funny because you need to play 2 games to finally conclude. The production quality of this game is high. Each character has their own soundtrack theme (absolute bangers), and characters animate and pose like they are hand-drawn.Honestly, I'm very happy that I was able to experience this game. When the Shu Takumi (game director) wants to cook, he REALLY can cook. Just like Ghost Trick. This is 100% recommended by me, you just need a little bit of patience to enjoy the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: Its finally here and I finally had the time to finish both of these new entries in the Ace Attorney series. So how good are these games and are they worth the huge amount of time to play through them? Its always so incredibly hard to write a review about a story driven series like Ace Attorney. Trying not to spoil anything while still explaining what makes the story good or bad is always a challenge. To cut myself short its great, its much more slower paced compared to the original trilogy. But the overall story is fantastic, the quality came in waves for me, some trails felt really slow and a bit tedious while some others felt like they just fly by in a flash and made me want to play the next part as soon as possible. Even the slower parts of the story feel like they feed into the better parts of the story. The best way to describe the story of this game is as a puzzle, you might sometimes get stuck on a certain part of a puzzle, but once you surpass that roadblock so many new options and interesting new elements open up.One thing that is especially interesting to see is how they incorporate the 19th century as a setting, so much love and attention was put into trying to portray some of these incredible sights and bringing over those cultures to an audience that maybe doesn't truly grasp every detail of that time period, I know I at least didn't know a lot of these cool details about the 19th century.The last thing I wanna compliment the story on is tackling the incredibly difficult and deep subjects that are present in this game. Racism, Justice, Classism, Misogyny, Poverty. Some of these were talked about before in the ace attorney series, but the way they presented some of those subjects like Justice felt completely different in this game. The thing that immediately caught my attention is how simple a lot of trails felt, even the more complicated ones, I think its due to in part that a lot of these trails feel more realistic as well as the game being a lot more lenient with giving you tips. In the previous games you could sometimes get stuck on certain parts of the investigation or trails because the devs wanted you to do something in a very specific way, I almost never had that feeling while playing this game, I sometimes even felt like the devs were supporting me a bit too much. Overall I wasn't super satisfied with this and I wish the devs would not only have challenged the players more but generally just tried playing around more with what is possible with the medium, There are so many incredibly difficult choices you have to make in the game, but often in the end the game will somehow find a way to bring you back to the games intended path, which feels like a real shame. I really would have liked to see more control given to the player or to see them being punished for some mistakes more readily.Two last things I wanna note about gameplay is that the first out of the 2 games puts a self imposed rule of making trails only last 1 day, which means trails don't get split up at all and this can make trails and investigations feel like they drag on for a while or like they should have ended a while ago. The second thing I wanna mention is the jury, the jury is a new aspect of the trails. But they feel like they don't add a lot to it, it feels like they often are a way to force the trails to artificially continue, it can sometimes be fun, but those fun times felt like an exception to the rule. Those are mainly nitpicks as the main bulk of the gameplay still feels unchanged and still feels great, but it was something I noticed and felt important to also inform people about. Huge props to Capcom, translations are always a hard subject for any visual novel fan. But I think almost anyone can agree that they knocked it out of the park here. Trying to incorporate all these old terms and the different accents into the translation really shows the level of attention they put into it all. The translation constantly sparked my curiousity into learning more about old british proverbs and language. Its immensely interesting to dive deep into it all and push myself to learn as much as possible about all the words being used. One thing that also comes with this bundle besides the wonderful translation, is the equally fantastic port, I pretty much had a flawless experience from start to finish. The port even comes with a lot of features that I really felt missing in the original Ace Attorney trilogy collection, the options are a lot more robust, there is a history option to catch up on text and best of all, they added DEVELOPER COMMENTARY AS WELL AS ADDITIONAL ARTWORK AND MUSIC. Thank the lord for that. The world of Ace Attorney is so wonderful, and a huge part of that is thanks to the hard working developers. Hearing their voice and how they brought this world to live was something I am extremely thankful for.The only addition I really missed here was more text options. You can't really set text speed for example which is a huge shame for a game this long, I wanna take in the incredible animations and facial expressions without skipping through it, but the original speed for the text felt painfully slow at times. I saved the best for last. Ever since the first chapter this was the #1 thing I couldn't wait to talk about in my review. My god have they gone above and beyond with the presentation in this game. The music is mindbogglingly good, Every part of it felt memorable, and just when everything feels a bit repetitive they add a whole bunch of new and equally as amazing songs. Locations feel super distinct and spark a ton of curiosity, every chapter I couldn't wait to see and hear more about the world. The character designs feel a bit more down to earth compared to some of the previous designs, but they still look great and often convey a lot of incredibly interesting themes in fun ways. The addition of cut scenes and voice acting is something I really appreciated and I wish they would have done more in the game with, it added so much to a lot of scenes. The whole presentation is truly fantastic and bring this insanely interesting setting of the 19th century Britain/Japan to live in a modern but faithful way. So what did I think of the game? Well my dear reader, I think that if you read the review that answer should be quite elementary. Its just fantastic and I love it, its equally as good as some of the best parts of the original trilogy. Its a great entry point for newer players because you don't need any knowledge of any game before playing this and the story in these 2 games are self contained. Its maybe a slower and easier experience compared to what im used to in Ace Attorney (The original 3 took me around 80 hours while these 2 games on their own took me 100), but that does not take away from the feeling you get when the game gets to one of its many good parts, so much love and attention was put into these games, and the high points in this game really were incredible to witness. A big recommend to anyone who is a fan of Ace Attorney or wants to get into the series. And a big recommend to anyone who enjoys visual novels overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played nearly every game in this long-running series, I am happy to declare Great Ace Attorney the best of them all. The characters are dynamic, entertaining, and have engaging motivations; from case one, the game treats you to difficult but fair logic puzzles and deduction, without many of the grasping-at-straws moments in other games of the series. The trial segments are near perfect, the music still top notch, and the 3D models are also done well, proving to be quite expressive. The biggest improvement are the investigation phases - no time is wasted on lengthy and repetitive mechanics (like the magatama in the original series) or by throwing every single piece of evidence at every character (95% of the time presenting will be obvious). The Great Deduction segments are interactive and swifter than the alternatives in other games. With main plot threads running through every single case, even what a different AA game would call "acceptable filler" could contain a clue for a vital revelation, and only one case in the set of 10 left me slightly annoyed at the resolution (not necessarily the plot details, but how the game asked the evidence to be presented). But, caveats. This is still Ace Attorney. While the game can be perfectly serious, there will still be silliness/hijinks, and there will be one-off witnesses who are caricatures. However, it is a perfect refinement of the series formula, and I expect it to stay that way for some time. It's only natural we didn't get this game on its original release, eh Old Capcom? I'm not bitter.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Although technically a prequel, GAA feels deserves the title of spiritual successor more than the games after AA4. It has all the charms of the original trilogy, but – through modern technology – has the benefit of smoother 3D models against a beautifully designed backdrop. Writing is also tighter, and thematically coherent throughout the game. Although it sounds corny, I truly believe that the setting is a character of its own. The story is all the more richer for it. The new mechanics (i.e. Logic and Reasoning Spectacular) are also a welcome addition to the gameplay. For long-time fans of the series such as myself, GAA is not to be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional AA game. Yes, game, because despite the 2 titles in this collection they're better understood as two halves of the same game. A great conclusion buoyed by the usual highs of the AA franchise: exceptional writing, criminal cases that border on the insane and strong characters. The setting and scenario really strengthens the game and the casual period-accurate racism gives the game a lot of flavor. The game is structured in a way that the finale, seeded from the very beginning, builds to one of the best in the series, likely since AA3's legendary slow-motion final objection.That having been said, there are some drawbacks. Because of the way the game is paced and structured, there is very little comparative payoff for cornering someone, at least in the first half of the game's cases. You don't get the usual AA satisfaction of seeing someone melt down on the witness stand until quite late in the game; this is all for plot reasons, but it also makes the first half of the game less satisfying. The game also takes way too long to get going. The prologue case is fine, but once the intrepid rookie lawyer decides to actually travel to Britain and the course of the game's plot is set in motion, the game spends way too long introducing its characters, setting up its mysteries and new mechanics. Of this the most egregious is the Sholmes 'Course Correction' mechanic; the sequences are both way too simple in practice and take too long to play out, leading to them generally feeling like unnecessary padding.But what are you reading this for? If you're an AA fan, you already know this is a must-play. Newcomers to the franchise, I suggest looking to complete the earlier games in the series before you tackle this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't recommend this more if I tried, I went through these two games more quickly than Barok van Zieks could slam his leg on the table. Great setting, very memorable characters and soundtrack, and a lot of new gameplay elements that were so much fun to go through. The two games feel very well connected and bring up very interesting points about the judicial system in its setting, as well as cultural aspects. I'd also like to praise the writing and the pacing of the story and character development (and there is a lot of development, trust me), the story combines a good mixture of comic relief and more serious and intense moments, much like what we were already used to in previous Ace Attorney games. Having played nearly every Ace Attorney game, I can say with certainty that these two games are my favorite in the entire series (yes, even more than the original trilogy), and I hope we can have more like this in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the Phoenix Wright series, and this one did not disappoint!A special hats off to the translators for the first case - one of the big challenges of the series has been how to translate the many pun based character names, and I thought they did an especially great job with the Japanese characters in game one.If you're a fan of turn-of-the-century Meiji period/Victorian period history, the concept is a brilliant merging of real history (Japan's program sending citizens abroad to learn about science, law, and medicine; treaties requiring Japan & China to only trial European citizens in European managed courts; historical figures like Natsume Soseki) with the Sherlock Holmes mythos.I cannot stop fanning out about this game. Just go and play it!

_childDocuments_.review: So I love the Ace Attorney series but my goodness do I have some things to say about this particular game:First off, I’m still on the first game. The pacing is INCREDIBLY SLOW. I purchased this game back in March of 2022, excited to try a new Ace Attorney game. And I still haven’t completed it. Before purchasing, I did read the reviews, which all mentioned in some way or the other how slow the game’s pacing was. BOY WAS I STUPID TO THINK THEY WERE EXAGGERATING. So, speaking of the pacing, like everyone has said on here, all of the characters including the main character himself, act clueless beyond belief. There are just so many obvious points when examining things and they for whatever reason act shocked beyond repair when uncovering something new. Not only this, but pretty much all sentences of dialogue are extended unnecessarily, even though there is clearly a way to shorten it so that players aren’t steadily losing interest as they read. I don’t think I need to provide examples because I’ve seen a few on the reviews here. I’m actually stunned by how much of the dialogue in this game opts to stretch out for seemingly as long as possible before getting to the point, it’s baffling and totally starts to bore me and clearly others on here too. Another thing: the Dance of Deduction featuring Herlock Sholmes is a cute and charming little addition. Seeing Ryunosuke and Sholmes working together to make those correct deductions is really cool and satisfying. However! One thing that I’ve noticed with this feature is that it is childishly easy. All you really have to do is look closely at certain objects or people for clues, examine that newly found clue, and then present it. These clues are hidden but extremely easy to find which made me feel like a little kid playing this game. Whenever Ryunosuke and Susato are glossing over certain objects, there might be a new clue sitting on one of the objects, and they go on to comment whatever they need to comment on the object before vwalla! A long pause and one of them goes “hmm, wait! There’s something here!” “Oh my! Mr. Naruhodo you’re right!” Or something to that effect. It’s just not really worth the dramatic reactions these two give when new clues are discovered during this process. Don’t get me wrong, it’s a new and refreshing concept, but I wish it had been more challenging. Yet another thing: when first playing through this game, you are not allowed to skip through dialogue with a right click of your mouse or however else you usually skip dialogue in Ace Attorney. The game, like many others have agreeably mentioned, forces you to follow its slow and prolonged pace. The only thing you can really do is turn on the auto-play option so that when characters are talking amongst themselves you don’t have to press a thing, but it’ll still play out slowly. Oh, and speaking of playing out slowly, the animations that play while dialogue is being displayed can be ridiculously slow. Like, it adds to the slowness of the game it’s actually frustrating. Ahem, take for example van Zieks. Boy were his animations during trials so prolonged and slow! You can’t skip animations either, so it truly adds to the snail pace of the game.Oh look, another thing: The amount of times a scene has played out in which three or more characters take turns sharing the “……..” dialogue is insane. Like my goodness I know it’s a moment of silence or uncertainty but it just feels SO UNNECESSARY. And I know there’s more to come!I want to also say that it hurts me to make a review like this on an Ace Attorney game, but this is something that has blown my mind with how slow and nearly uninteresting most of the first game has been so far. I’ve really been trying to be patient with this game, but I’ve come to the conclusion that I’m not patient enough! Yes, I will finish this game for completion’s sake, and because I want to know what happens, but yikes will that take me a good 15-20 more hours! The interaction between Ryunosuke and Susato is quite bland and uninteresting. This makes investigations even more punishing and boring for me. The way they comment on everything just isn’t as interesting, entertaining, or engaging like the way Phoenix and Maya or even Phoenix and Pearls interacted. Even Edgeworth and Kay were interesting together and made investigations much more fun. There’s almost no personality in these two when they talk to each other. I don’t know a better way to word it. It’s just not fun.The soundtracks are nothing memorable, in my opinion. I don’t mean this in a rude way, but my gosh is the music so dull! It honestly blends in too much with the background while playing the game. I mean, take a look at the Ace Attorney Trilogy. I LOVE the fact that so many characters had their own music! Like for example, “Happy People” would play with cheery characters like Lotta Hart and Desirée DeLite. Or when the music would change depending on whatever was happening in the game, the mood, and even wherever you went! This game doesn’t do that, making the music very bland in comparison. And the overall audio for the game is so low it’s not even funny. I turn my gaming laptop all the way up to 100 and it sounds extremely weak. I even went to settings in game to turn up the music to max volume. Everything from sound effects to music sounds so soft and muffled. Not loud or crisp and clear. It honestly sounded like I was playing a game on my 3DS, but even quieter than that! Here’s to hoping the new Apollo Justice game isn’t going to be that quiet!All in all, these are my frustrations and thoughts on the game. Was it worth the $40? Not for me it wasn’t. I’m not saying it was horrible, but it did disappoint me more than I’d like to say. The animation is great, most characters aren’t very memorable aside from Ryunosuke, Susato, and Sholmes. I’m really pushing myself to be patient with this game. I want to see it through to the end! But, it’s still painful to play through because of the pace, and honestly it feels like even Ryunosuke and Susato themselves don’t have much personality. But maybe I’m saying that too early. I just don’t feel that powerful duo spark I felt with Phoenix and Maya. All I can say is, I would not recommend this game to someone who is new to the AA series and wants to get into it. Go to the AA Trilogy for that. It’s such a gift. However! If you are someone who has played the trilogy and possibly all the other games, and you are looking for more, then maybe you won’t mind giving this a shot! I don’t know. I’ve played AA up until Dual Destinies and nothing past that. I was seeking something different and found this game. It didn’t really blow my mind the way the trilogy did. But, I am grateful for it regardless. Just wish I’d waited for a sale before buying :)So far, playing this game has felt like more of a chore than playing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Phoenix Wright games, but this is not a game. I had jury duty recently and it was more fun than this game. I say that without the slightest hint of exaggeration. And my first case took almost as long as the real-life case I sat through. The game has some good elements, but it's like the developer said the runtime was short and ordered them to make it longer, so they padded everything with tons of boring dialogue. The story and cases are actually good, but they're padded under so much meaningless blathering. You spend 30 seconds playing, and then you can set the game down for ten minutes as the characters talk and talk and talk without saying anything. The main character bumbles around not getting to his point and then the prosecutor says he doesn't understand and the judge adds that he too does not understand and the witness chimes in that they also don't understand and so the main character stammers and doesn't make his point and then his friend talks to him and encourages him to keep going so he does and then the prosecutor says he doesn't see how my point is relevant to the case and the judge says he also doesn't see the relevance and the witness says they too don't see the relevance and so you explain it and then your friend explains exactly what you explained but with even more words and then the judge is shocked and the prosecutor is shocked and the witness is shocked and the entire courtroom murmurs and then everyone is silent and you repeat what you just said but in much more detail, rehashing the same facts over and over then the witness laughs and then you wonder what the witness is up to and (about 10-15 minutes have gone by) they explain away the point you just made and prosecutor says your case is hopeless and the judge agrees and you spend a minute or two panicking and it looks like it's all over but as a player you know it's not because you're already three moves ahead of the story so you're just waiting for them to let you make another decision but they will not. Finally, the judge asks if you have any more evidence to present before wrapping up this case, and after another moment of panic and a couple more motivational speeches you say that, yes you do have more to say, and the judge, prosecutor, and defense all argue for a few minutes about whether the defense should be allowed to waste the court's time with this pointless endeavor and finally you're allowed to spend another 30 seconds selecting the next piece of evidence to present.And then the entire thing repeats itself. Not a different series of events. Not a similar series of events. THE EXACT SAME THING HAPPENS AGAIN. They'll use slightly different words, but the story repeats itself, beat for beat, after every thing you say and every piece of evidence you present. This is not a detective game. This is barely a game. If anything it's an idle game where you just sit there and wait for enough time to pass so you can make another tiny amount of progress. There are good character moments, fun plot points, good character moments, and interesting mysteries, but they're buried under hour after hour of useless drivel, drivel that was boring the first time and maddening the fifth time they go through the same storyline beats with slightly different wording. If you don't like games that are mostly reading, don't buy this game. If you do like games that are mostly reading, buy a game with better writing, like one of the other games in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Key success factors for a game like this: 1. the writing, pacing, dialogue 2. the clues, riddles and mysteries 3) the user interface, mechanics of interacting and taking actions.The game falls flat on all of these measures.The dialogue is incredibly drawn out, with very many irrelevant and meaningless statements. This is not "lore" or interesting background talk - characters are cardboard cutouts and almost all statements are meaningless, trite, irrelevant and boring. "Rynosuke, you need to speak up!" "Let your voice be heard" "Do not be nervous" "Tell the judge what's on your mind" "Just speak plainly" "Express yourself" "Speak without hesitation".  It feels like someone decided that the game's key success factor was rather the number of lines and how long it takes to get through it - so they ordered some poor underling to just put a LOT of effort into dragging out, reformulating, repeating, extending, even the most miniscule thought.The clues are either completely trivial or completely obscure. There's no happy medium of reasoning or deduction, like in original Ace Attorney episode 1. Some stretch credulity, like they are forced - someone thought up a logical plot point, but it's just not fully coherent, yet it's still hammered in without anyone challenging it. Mechanics are cumbersome and obtuse. It's easy to trigger a repeat of 20 lines that add nothing useful, per the above. Overall, it's a tedious disappointment. There is a small bit of value if you are a fan of this type of game. I was a fan of Ace Attorney 1, but feel my money is wasted.The first 2 hours should give you a correct impression of what the rest of the game is like. If you like them, you will like the rest, and vica versa.(Hours played is incorrect.)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, whilst I would normally write down a detailed review for this game, I would largely be repeating what I said in my review of the Phoenix Wright trilogy. So let me just give the short condensed version and then add on whatever extra stuff I wanna say.Great story with compelling mysteries, good characters and dialogue, excellent art, involves using your brain a lot and being attentive to small details, and it's fun regardless of whether you take it seriously or laugh at some of the ridiculousness. Now to move on to the stuff unique to this game that I want to say.Having these two games bundled together just makes so much sense. They kinda end up feeling like one long game rather than two separate games because you kinda need to play both, both to understand everything and to get the proper closure on everything. This game is especially long compared to other entries in the franchise, and whilst I don't think it ever felt drawn-out because there were a lot more mechanics at play, some people may find it tiring (though I personally usually didn't). You have a brand new cast with brand new rivalries and relationships. It's very refreshing.The story in this game is phenomenal with the final few chapters being the peak of the series' writing. The only problem is the build-up for it all. The entire first 5 chapters are all build-up, with small tidbits of payoff within, only to find more intrigue and mystery. And honestly, that is asking a lot from the player as 5 entire chapters of build-up and suspense can feel taxing as  test your patience.But oh man.The latter 5 chapters are incredible, and it's really here that Ace Attorney Chronicles managed to become my favourite Ace Attorney game . The payoff was well worth it in this amazing journey. Also, Sholmes is best boy.

_childDocuments_.review: I was delighted to finally have a chance to play this game and I feel as though it was definitely worth the wait. I tried my best to get into the game without making too many comparisons to any of the other Ace Attorney games ( especially with my preference for earlier games up to Layton vs Attorney). I was also really happy to learn that Chronicles consisted of two games. It took me around 87 hours to complete ( I was pretty thorough ) and these are my take aways:PROS: - Great story. I found myself coming up with all kinds of theories about things as I played along. Some of the cases from the end of the first game and the entirety of the second game really had me guessing about things. - Great characters. I found myself enjoying all characters and not finding any that grated on my nerves at all.- The second game has mutli day trials / investigation, which felt true to AA games.- Any unanswered questions you have after playing game 1 are answered throughout game 2.- Quite catchy music.- Sholmes and Iris.- Susato is a lovely assistant.CONS:- Cases in the first game are a little too easy to solve.- Cases in the first game only have 1 day investigation and 1 day trials, resulting in hours long of trials at a time. That isn't a format that really worked for me.- While characters are endearing and some are quite memorable (Sholmes), there still felt something a bit lacking. I didn't feel the affection I did for some of the side characters in older games.- While the music was good, it's not too memorable.- The jury summation system was not something I personally enjoyed too much.- I did not see anyone truly go crazy on the stand after a guilty verdict in the over-the-top fashion that makes me chuckle, past the very first case. That made me sad.All that said,  I truly enjoyed the game and marathoned it over 11 days and I would love to play any future installments. I would highly recommend it to any Ace Attorney fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor - or, rather, prequel - to the iconic Ace Attorney series. With a steampunk Victorian setting, it represents a lot of firsts for the franchise, including being the entry that finally convinced the localizers to entirely stop pretending the Phoenix Wright is from California. Honestly, though, the whole 'period piece' setup is a bit of a bait-and-switch - at first, it seems to promise a move away from all the forensic and technical evidence you have to contend with in the more modern games, since you're now operating in a time before DNA-testing, surveillance-cameras and Luminol, at a time when fingerprint identification is still considered a revolutionary new technology used in only a small number of court-systems... not including the British or Japanese one that you get to wrestle with. So, a greater focus on witness-statements and more primitive-yet-ingenious trickery.Buuuuuut then the game introduces you to Steampunk Sher... ahem, HERLOCK SHOLMES, and his Dr. Watson stand-in, who together proceed to invent Steampunk DNA Testing, Steampunk Luminol, Steampunk Surveillance Cameras, and so on. Not that it stops there, even, since they're soon busting out stuff that qualifies as sci-fi even TODAY, which cannot help but feel somewhat ludicrous. But then, this isn't a series that's ever taken itself overly seriously, despite the dead-serious subject matter it often works with - murder, betrayal, emotional trauma and so on.Still, the game DOES have some new entertainments to offer, such as joining Herlock Sholmes in a 'dance of deduction', or going toe-to-toe with the British Jury-System of the time. Certainly a worthwhile outing for any old fan of the Ace Attorney series - and also a treat for any 'Wrightworth'-shippers, I'd imagine, considering how very  the ancestors of Phoenix Wright and Miles Edgeworth are shown to be. Why, just in the second case of the first game, we see them sharing a cabin for a loooooong sea-journey, and get strong hints that Steampunk Phoenix Wright is in the closet... or at least the wardrobe!

_childDocuments_.review: Ace Attorney is my favorite game series, but these games are extremely slow and boring, and the characters lack the charm that usual AA characters have. While any other AA game I would be excited to play through them as fast as possible, for these ones I have dropped them multiple times struggling to push myself to make it further. The atmosphere is pretty unique, with the setting being entirely different from the other AA games, and it tells more one coherent story while in the other games this is often more of a side thing compared to the individual mysteries. It makes it feel more like an actual VN where you make your way through a long story, including the incredibly slow pace that makes a lot of VNs a pain to read through. This story and atmosphere is probably what appeals to a lot of people, because I know a lot are positive about these games. But it loses all the appeal of the other AA games, which is the mix of murder mystery and comedy, an endearing and entertaining cast of characters from the main characters to the side characters, the excitement of its fast-paced plot twists that you slowly uncover, and the fun in tearing through the witnesses' lies. The very slow pace and more story focus loses all this appeal that the other games have. If the individual characters and mysteries were more compelling instead and the pace was more in line with other AA games, this would have been a more solid entry. There are AA games that do this while creating a very solid overarching story as well so there's not really an excuse for failing at that.I can't speak about the quality of the overall story as I haven't been able to push myself to make my way through it yet even after trying 3 times. Maybe one day I'll be able to finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: (This Review is intended for The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles: Adventures part only)After some good and bad in the Ace Attorney franchises, Capcom finally took a really interesting yet innovative direction in this franchise after the new trilogy mixed reception (esp. Apollo Justice & Dual Destinies), This game really defines what is an "Ace Attorney" game after allFor starters, this is and Adventure & Visual Novel with Courtroom Drama as a main theme. All of the main cases in the Adventures game are written really good for a new-gen Ace Attorney game (the 3rd and 5th case for me is the greatest case in this game)Some of the new Mechanics such as Dance Of Deduction, Summation Examination, and Multiple Witness (for multiple witness, it first implemented in Phoenix Wright vs Professor Layton crossover game) are implemented really well that it helps our main character doing their investigations/trials and serves more than just a gimmick feature.Characterization pretty much a solid one, althought it could be better for certain witnesses.For Now, it a must buy for anyone who loves Ace Attorney series

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles consists of two games that tell a single story over 10 cases. If you ask almost any Ace Attorney fan, they'd say this is the peak Ace Attorney experience. While I don’t entirely agree, I will say it’s a REALLY good game. The story is compelling, but the pacing is painfully slow.The first case is particularly frustrating. It’s ridiculous—they try to introduce all the main Japanese characters and set up a mystery that doesn’t pay off until the latter part of the second game. At the same time, it tries to balance a wacky Ace Attorney vibe with a more serious tone, all while stretching on for 4 hours in the courtroom without any investigation. So, you have to commit 4 hours to a game you haven’t even formed an opinion on yet and don’t fully understand the mechanics of. It’s absurd.But that’s not all—the game piles on mysteries that won’t be resolved until the second game. The first game needs closure, but the ongoing story is only really continued in cases 3 and 5, which isn’t enough to tell a big story. As a result, case 5 drags on for 10 hours. The second game, however, improves significantly after the first case, and you really start to appreciate the storytelling and characters. You begin to understand the atmosphere, the humor (though the original trilogy is funnier), the tight overarching plot, the insanely good soundtrack (probably the best in the franchise, in my opinion), and the incredibly likable characters. This game made me sympathize with a character who was complicit with a serial killer, which is a bit unsettling but a testament to the quality of the writing.But none of that even matters—this game has Herlock Sholmes, and he’s the most epic thing on the planet. I recommend this game to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a case where I really wish Steam had a "mixed" review option; because this game has potential - it's just a slog to get through.As someone who bought this game immediately after finishing the original Ace Attorney Trilogy, I was honestly expecting the same thing as that game. What I got was like trying to wade through cobwebs in Minecraft with soul sand underneath and the effects of the Turtle Master potion applied - slow as hell.In the original Ace Attorney, the "tutorial" case, the "First Turnabout", was about 40 minutes long. Here, the first case, the "Adventure of the Great Departure", which was just an intro to the trial portions of the game for those unfamiliar with the Ace Attorney series, was . They could have easily condensed this down; but everyone in this game talks like I put the original lines from the Ace Attorney Trilogy, and asked ChatGPT to make them more verbose and wordy. Like, for example, something as simple as "that's a ladder" turns into "that's a climbing device known here as a 'ladder.'"Although, I will state, it nails down the Ace Attorney formula very well despite it being a mess to get through; the music is actually really good; and they definitely nailed down the 3D models in this game compared to Dual Destinies or Spirit of Justice.That being said, I would still recommend this game to Ace Attorney fans or visual novel enjoyers, just not to someone who has a fairly short attention span (like me) or expect the game to be quick and snappy like the original Ace Attorney Trilogy.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played each ace attorney game in it's entirety (some more than once), I have a pretty good idea of what makes each game unique and enjoyable.  The Great Ace Attorney series has (in my opinion) the best continuity out of any set of ace attorney games.  All noticeable loose ends are nicely tied up by the end of the second game and despite being able to predict some of the game's twists and turns, each case continued to grip my attention. The gameplay was wonderful and though I did hope that another gameplay mechanic would be added in the second game, I can see why they elected not to and respect that decision.  These two games may not require knowledge of any other game in the franchise but it's still wonderful to see references to older games scattered throughout each case.  I would highly recommend these games (especially the second) and I truly believe they lie within my top 3-5 ace attorney games of all time. Capcom please make more, it has been so long and I am so very desperate for content, especially content like this.PS: I may or may not be a little bit biased since I have such an attachment to this series but biases aside, I still think the game was great, at least a 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the Ace Attorney Trilogy I am incredibly disappointed. This was one of the most boring and infuriating games I have ever played. Text moves incredibly slowly in an already filler heavy game. And worst of all, none of the cases are interesting. Maybe I've been spoiled by Danganronpa's incredible mysteries, but nothing here requires an ounce of thought. None of the "twists" make me feel shocked or engaged. The second to last episode, which takes place around 16 hours into the first game, has the same twist as the second chapter of Danganronpa. _childDocuments_.review: Wholeheartedly recommended for people who> Don't mind doing a lot of reading/like visual novels, and are interested in experiencing a grand adventure of an underdog lawyer> Like catching liars in their lies and proving people wrong by rubbing evidence in their faces> Have played / are familiar with at least 1 Ace Attorney game already> Are interested in seeing the creators play around with the setting (the-end-of-19th century Japan and Britain) or the character of Sherlock Holmes and some of his stories (or, you know, Herlock Sholmes - thank the licensing laws for this one)> Don't mind spending something like 80+ hours to play through both gamesIf at least some of these check out for you, then there is a near 100% chance you will have a great time with these games!The visual presentation of TGAA is outstanding for the visual novel genre - from the character designs to the environments and animations. The music is incredibly varied in themes, and *will* make you hum some of the tracks after you're done playing. The plot, that spans throughout the 2 games, is incredibly intricate. The cases you go though are all connected in some capacity, and the intrigue of various plot lines that you discover along the way comes to a quite cathartic resolution by the end. All the major characters are very well-written at best, entertaining at worst. It's a very strong cast, but the side characters are also a treat, with some of them bringing lots of light-hearted comedy to the table, some being irritating but in a way that makes is all the more satisfying to bring them down, some being very fun to hate, and some bringing out genuine sympathy, loathing or pity. All in all, there is a diverse range of personalities and stories.Cons that I can foresee making the experience of playing these games less-than-great:> The first 2 cases' pacing might be a tad slow. Mentally prepare for that, if such things worry you, get through those cases, and have fun with the rest, because the story picks up big time.> If you're someone who gets really irritated by being 'ahead of the plot' the game play may frustrate you sometimes. Just like in any other Ace Attorney game, you *have* to follow a certain order of presenting evidence/discovering plot details, so you may end up in a situation where you figure out where things are headed before the main characters do. Again, *if* you are bothered by something like that, these games may irritate you at times.TGAAC is a very lovingly crafted collection, where the creators tried to make something really compelling and unique. And I think there is nothing quite like these games, so I very much recommend them.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game thinking it would just be like the previous trilogy, but it ended being a completely different experience. The game is still goofy, but still grounded. Real-world racism and xenophobia are also present in this game, which I wasn't actually expecting either.I felt like the story was lacking a bit towards the end. Felt like we missed out on any building up of a certain character's malfeasance. And the very end felt rushed, despite how long the trial and investigatory segments were. Really odd.Anyway, my primary complaint is the Sherlock Holmes character. I didn't like him and dreaded every segment he was present in. It made me care very little for some aspects of the story. I just felt like he weighed down what was otherwise a fantastic game with a super interesting narrative and underlying mystery.Still loved it, though!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game near it's English release in 2021 and loved what I played, but after playing Case 2 of the 1st game I put the game on hold cause I wanted to finish this series with my brother after he joined my half way through Case 2. I never got around to asking him to join me playing this game for whatever reason and I put this game off for almost 2 years. I realized I was putting The Great Ace Attorney off because it's the second to last Ace Attorney game in the series I haven't finished, the other being Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright, and I didn't want to live in a post-Ace Attorney world. TGAA 2 (2017) is currently the last Ace Attorney game made as of this date with the last mainline game coming out in 2016.After listening the TGAA soundtrack the other day, I'd finally decided to finish up the rest of these two games. IDK if there will be anymore Ace Attorney games in the future, if The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles are the series final entries, then they are without doubt a worthy end point for this franchise. The character writing and narrative are some the best this series has ever produced and Ryunosukes's character development makes him my favorite protagonist in the series. My man can go from being a goober to an absolute savage in the courtroom and produces some banger quotes that go HARD. Thank you so much Ace Attorney!!! You're are one of my favorite game series since I first watched a let's play of the first game in 2016 and thank you Shu Takumi and everyone else at Capcom for creating this wonderful franchise!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I kind of liked the game. But as time went on, I was more and more disappointed.The animations and stuff are so slow that without speedhacking it with cheat engine I wasn't willing to play it. Speedhacking however breaks the movie parts of the game.The cases are not very complex. And they fade in comparison to ace attorney trilogy. There are only 9 of them too, so lower playtime is to be expected.Except for the main ones, the characters in the game are mostly unlikable. Ace attorney was always notorious for absurd characters, but this is just cringy.The story is nearly identical to AA trilogy, just with worse narrative and some character swaps. In the AA trilogy you had corrupt chief investigator who'd use people under him as minions to do his bidding through extortion. This is completely identical here, just replace chief investigator with someone else. And you have other things common with the AA trilogy. Cases closed through forged evidence or cases connected to another case that happened 10 years ago to name a few.At the beginning I was willing to recommend the game. But after finishing it I just can't. It's average... and looks more like an attempt to milk cash out of the AA franchise than an attempt to make a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a masterpiece! Definitely one of the best and most unique entries in the AA franchise.The sheer amount of care and love that went into the treatment of the story (including localization) is nothing short of amazing. Felt like a real glimpse into 19th century London with a lot of actual historical tie ins weaved into the story.I think this is the first time ever that the total 10 cases from both games are interlinked with one another that built up bit by bit, twist after twist until an epic grand finale.If anyone played the 5th AA game, Dual Destinies, I think TGAA showcased a much better version of 'the dark age of the law' than the former. I mean sure themes like foul play has been brought up many times in previous titles, but TGAA's handling of it stood out for me. This game is actually darker than I thought it was.The soundtrack is one of the best things about the game. Not only that it fits with the period piece, but I feel like this is one that comes close or is equal to the first game's iconic soundtrack, if not better that is. Of course, what is Ace Attorney without its zany cast. Its pleasing to say that a lot of them grow on you. My personal favourite being the racist rival prosecutor, Barok van Zieks. Finally, I guess I have to add that is was the best AA game that made full use of their 3D models. Since I played it on PC this time, I have to say the game was aesthetically gorgeous. It hits all the right notes and looks great!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: -Fantastic setting. Meiji Era of Japan + Victorian England all in one, with some steampunk stylings thrown in for good measure. -Excellent characters. Main character is relatedly anxious and makes plenty of goofs, but isn't an idiot and shows impressive resolve in a pinch. Rest of the cast- from major to minor characters- are also pretty well characterized and a good time. -Engaging story. "I laughed, I cried, it moved me Bob"- Larry the Cucumber, Veggietales. And in seriousness, probably one of the better game stories I've played: I immediately wanted to go back and re-experience it after ALREADY playing it for 50 hours. -Stupendous soundtrack. Don't know how to describe it- maybe classical music refinement meets over-the-top anime stylings?- but it's absolutely killer. One of the best VGM soundtracks I've listened to, no joke,. Cons:- Lotsa reading. Most action you're gonna see here is dancing and suplexes. - Even if you DO like reading, you might find the pacing slow at times. Good writing helps to make up for it, but it can still feel a bit long in the tooth. -Wish there was more of it. It felt like there was enough story here that they could've easily added some filler cases to make the Great Ace Attorney Chronicles into a trilogy, if they had had the opportunity. Alas though, probably woulda made this fantastic game even harder to localize with all that extra text, so I'll cope with the excellent cases we have here :) Overall:Highly recommended. If it even looks remotely interesting to you, I'd definitely encourage a buy. I feel fairly confident you'll have a good time :)

_childDocuments_.review: Very high praise from me. Possibly the best Ace Attorney game in the whole series. I hate to spoil it for you, so I won't say much. You may not get as great puzzles and gameplay as like, Ghost Trick, JFA, or T&T. But they're still there and it's still really fun. I'm saying I didn't struggle much with this game, but I did struggle a few times, and it was fun during all of it. Story is amazing too. Don't wanna say much. If you're not into period pieces, then I guess avoid it. But I think the story could win anyone over.Localization is great. I regret not playing this sooner, but also I think I played this at just the right time in my life. I was waiting on the Scarlet Study mod that swapped the character names. But I decided to just... accept that the names won't be the same transliterated ones in Scarlet Study. Is the official localization better than Scarlet Study's? I wouldn't judge it like that. They both have merits. Official has such an amazing period appropriate lexicon (it's good to open wikitionary and write any words you don't understand). Scarlet Study is a bit simpler and easier for an ESL to read. Both convey meaning and emotions efficiently. Regardless, I'm recommending the Steam version here, and since the Scarlet Study script isn't available for the steam release as of now, I recommend this official version for you.You'll also want the Admiral Curtiss mod to unlock framerate. A few animations are stuck at a lower framerate, but it's easy to accept that I feel. I just couldn't play the game at 30 FPS. It gave me a headache.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been an avid fan of the Ace Attorney series ever since I played the first game on the Nintendo DS several years ago. The characters and stories in each iteration have never failed to be short of amazing, and this addition continues to hold to that.When I found out both of The Great Ace Attorney games were finally going to be released in the US, I was beside myself with joy. Having played both games all the way through now, I can say with certainty I was not disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: I have played every game in the Ace Attorney series. After Dual Destinies and Spirit of justice, I was dismayed at the stark decline in quality of the series and not hopeful for it's future, despite it being among my favorite video game series. As it turns out, a change of setting and the return of the legendary original series director Shu Takumi is exactly what the series needed. These games do a fantastic job of telling a complete and expertly-woven story with fantastic characters while also providing the thought-provoking and exciting gameplay and witty, intelligent dialogue the series is known for. I never thought any Ace Attorney game could surpass the prowess of the original, but upon completion it is clear to me that The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is the best game in the series. I was initially worried that, with how complicated and interconnected of a story it weaves in the first 9 cases, the game would not be able to wrap everything up in a satisfying conclusion in the final case, but I was proven wrong in a spectacular manner, and the game's final chapter feels like not only the culmination of the story of Ryunosuke Naruhodo and all the people he meets on his long journey, but also the culmination of a 20-year-old franchise that has innovated and defined it's own genre of puzzle-solving visual novel. As far as specific mechanics go, this game introduces many brand new ideas to the court system and the investigation segments alike, such as the jury examinations, witness pursuit (though I feel that this particular mechanic is a bit underused), and the incredibly fun and vibrant Great Deductions. It is very refreshing after the cluttered and obligatory mechanics of the most recent preceding Ace Attorney games. Also to help combat the staleness that had begun to plague the series, this game has a completely new cast of characters and constantly builds and expands its immersive setting. There are a slew of historical references and references to The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes that keep the world interesting far beyond the surface level.Overall, if you enjoy Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy, this game is basically a must-have. It feels like the magnum opus of the Ace Attorney series, in which the developers and writers have finally perfected the core gameplay/formula while simultaneously defying every expectation a long-time fan would have going into it. I'm not sure what's in store for the future of this series, but The Great Ace Attorney will be very difficult to live up to. It's a once-in-a-lifetime kind of game and a fantastic ride from start to finish, and I implore anyone who may be interested to try it for themselves.
