_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a prequel spin-off to the Ace Attorney games, with this steam release combining both “Adventures” and “Resolve.” While not the first game to not feature the most well-know character, Phoenix Wright, it is the first time we step away from that time period and instead go back to a time where Japan is getting use to western technology (and culture) England is going through an industrial revolution.Enter Ryunosuke Naruhodo, whose through events, friends and resolve, becomes an “Ace Attorney” in his own right.To say that Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a return to form would be a disservice to early games as even the “weakest” titles in the Ace Attorney franchise are still good visual novels in their own right. But this is without a doubt, the best Ace Attorney game since Trials and Tribulations. Now technically this is cheating since this steam release combines “Adventures” and “Resolve.” But the complete package is so great, you might as well consider it one game.The presentation is amazing. The expressions of characters has been raised to a whole new level and it’s just so much fun to see them; from Ryunosuke’s wild-eyed terror, Susato’s look of disappointment to Gregson’s stress-eating of his seemingly bottomless cup of fish and chips. In or out of the court, important to minor, each character doesn’t just feel like a stand in, but important to the scene, if not the story.The UI is solid, though it can be a bit jarring If you come to this game from the DS and 3DS and not seeing prompts like “Court Record” and “Present” on the screen, it can take some adjusting to as instead you have to get use to using keyboard (or controller) to press, open evidence screen, present evidence and etc. Also, you can’t get rid of key prompts at the bottom right of the screen, so if you’re hoping to capture some in-game screenshots clean, you’re gonna have to wait for opportunities where it’s not displayed or get a bit creative.When it comes to the places you visit in Great Ace Attorney Chronicles locations has a postcard-feel to them. The painting-like quality to the locations may not wow players but it doesn’t distract either and is visually interesting enough to not be “just another location” but feel very important and noteworthy.Adding to the presentation is the music, which is amazing. It’s not as instantly bombastic as past games in the series but has a better build up, with an excellent crescendo and climax feel to it.When it comes to gameplay, long time veterans of The Ace Attorney franchise will feel right at home, with some added mechanics and some great Quality of Life here, such as saving and resuming from almost any spot (which may encourage save-scumming but also you’re not forced into playing for long stretches just to get to a safe point to save,) pointing out what you’ve searched in investigations, making it handy to keep track of what you already seen, a way to fast-forward the story (though the game doesn’t point this out).For those who just want to enjoy the story, there is a “reader” mode for those. It could probably being considered a divisive inclusion but the game is at heart a visual novel and there are those who will just enjoy the story of such a visual novel and not worry about gameplay mechanics or wrong choices.And what a story the Adventures and Resolve bring. It’s a slow going at first but this just makes the stakes feel even more higher as you complete case by case. It gives time for the characters to become more fully fleshed out, to warm up to them (Herlock Sholmes being a great example) and see their evolution, their motives and personalities bloom is a joy to watch alongside Great Ace Attorney Chronicles insane, well-crafted and well executed plot.Another stroke of genius that Great Ace Attorney Chronicles does is being great at keeping up suspense. This is due to the fact the game won’t instantly let you know you’ve made the right choice at times and will play out scenes that will put your heart in your mouth! (it helps the track usually proceeding it is a banger) as well as using pacing to a masterclass level. And while the Adventures and Resolve do fall on tropes established by the series (and visual novels in general to be fair,) the execution is so well done that even if you predict what’s going to (eventually) happen, you don’t feel cheated. The risk to split the story into two games was a huge gamble but the superb work pays off excellently. And to top it all off is the fact you don’t need to have played any any of the previous games in the Ace Attorney franchise to come is just another feather in its cap.Is there bad points? Well this being an Ace Attorney entry there is the usual slightly contrived elements to it that the Ace Attorney games like to throw up in climatic cases, the final cases can feel long and Resolve, does suffer from having to recap certain information or mechanics that the player and characters should already be familiar with, as if it expected a few people to start here and If you’re achievement hunting, be aware that some of them, like the series itself, requires a bit of outside the box thinking and are semi-missable (the fact you can replay cases avoids it being permanent and will even tell you where you need to check)But these are VERY nitpicky issues. The fact that Capcom have released Resolve and Adventures together as one game, at a fantastic price, is a huge blessing. Quite frankly, The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a game as great, maybe even better, than Trials and Tribulations and is one that any Visual Novel fan, whether you are hardcore, new to the genre or picky, needs to play. It's simply that damn great.

_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: * Non spoiler bitI've played most of the Ace Attorney games throughout the years (except AAI2, PWvsPL and AA6) and I must say, out of them all these two games as a whole are the best out of the whole series. Seriously, this divergence was what the series needed. The story is phenomenal, the fact that all cases are connected and slowly build into a one giant story and that story culminating into one giant epic climax where you feel so triumphant and accomplished after this long journey. The characters are all very well written, interesting and memorable, you actually feel emotionally attached to them at the end of the game. The gameplay is such a breath of fresh air, gone are pointless gimmicks, say hello to great deductions to spice up the investigations, multiple witnesses on the witness stand to pursue and the jurist system to pit jurors arguments againts each other. The soundtrack is easily the best OST as a whole in the series, nothing comes close to it. There is only a handful of songs from the other games that can be compared ("Wanting to find the Truth" for example). For any Ace Attorney fan this is a mustplay and for any puzzle solving/thinking game enthusiast a game worth trying. The only downside is that I got a bit burned out at the begging of the second game so I had to take some breaks from it because some parts are a bit longer but otherwise it was a blast.If I overlook that one small problem I mentioned, this game is an easy 10/10.*Big Spoilers bit

_childDocuments_.review: Over the last few weeks I finished the "Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy" and liked it so much, that I bought this game immediately after I noticed that it was on sale. After around 15 hours of playtime I can confidently say that "The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles" are better than its predecessors in all aspects.While this game (or these two games to be exact) offer similar gameplay than the previous ones, there a bunch of new game mechanics being introduced which make the overall experience more enjoyable in my opinion. For example, the interrogation of multiple wittnesses at once and the possibility to switch your attention to any one of them at any given time, investigating and interacting with 3D objects similar to the bonus episode of the first Phoenix Wright game, interrogating the jury in hopes of changing their verdict, etc.Overall, if you liked the first few games I think it's highly likely that you will also enjoy these two games. For me, "The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles" are a great addition to the franchise and also my favorite games of it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game in 15 years that truly matches the original trilogy in quality. It has everything that makes Ace Attorney great. Character development, mind-blowing twists, and high stakes...wrapped around quirky characters and witty dialogue. It's a contender for best game in the entire Ace Attorney franchise. There aren't even any filler cases this time: what ends up seeming like filler comes around by the end to be entirely significant. It's a bit of a slow burn, especially in the first half, and its plot involves high-level political corruption that might be hard to wrap your head around at first, but by the end, it becomes a rollercoaster ride of twists and turns that makes it all worth it.My only complaint is the soundtrack. It's not bad, and there are a few nice tunes, but the vast majority of it blends together in an unmemorable mess of classical stuff. It just kind of disappears in the background and you hardly notice it. Disappointing compared to every other game in the series, which usually has a killer OST.

_childDocuments_.review: The best games since the original trilogy, and the most ambitious out of all of them by a long shot. The approach to the themes and their handling of this story is so unique and grounded that it has a firm identity outside of the mainline series, but the ideas themselves clearly tie the two together. Something small I really appreciated: over the last couple mainline games (which became very grating to me in Spirit of Justice, a disappointing game) the bombast of breakdowns reached extreme, overly-long heights. In comparison, this game (after the first case, which is Doing Something With It, I Swear) looks downright subtle with its breakdowns. Shout out also to the third case of the second part for not only breaking the bad-third-case curse that plagues so many Ace Attorney games but being one of the best cases over all in the entire series. I have so much good will for this game that I don't even particularly care that the ending systematically burns the entire thing down. All the ideas of imperialism are tossed out the window for a neat, clean resolution about how everything's essentially fine and there's nothing too severe to worry about, which can be (and is) very disappointing. But the stuff leading up to this self-sabotage is so good that it's worth playing through all the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Two hours with this was enough to tell me it is not enjoyable or worth the expense of its purchase. It is repetitive, juvenile and simplistic - so much so that it insults the intelligence of the player. Even granting the factors (e.g. cultural and linguistic differences) that go with a foreign origin, the game fails to suspend disbelief long enough to arouse any sympathy or connection to its wooden, stilted, silly characters. Perhaps it would have some utility in teaching elementary school pupils the rudiments of logical thought and rational argument. Apart from that, the only audience I can imagine finding it appealing would be pre-teen anime fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the first two cases of The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures, I sadly cannot recommend this game to anybody. The graphics and music are drastically improved to the point where I was extremely impressed with the overall presentation of the game. The music engages you more than any other game in the Ace Attorney series. I also quite enjoyed the new mechanics of this game. The first being where the player can make deductions in real time alongside Herlock Sholmes. I believe this to fit in well with the Ace Attorney franchise, it adds something new to the game that previous titles didn't have, and overall I thought it was a lot more fun than some of the gimmicks of the other games. I also enjoyed having multiple people on the stand at once. Although minor, this seems like a good way to add something more to the court sections that, again, other games don't have.However, this is about where the positives end. The cases themselves feel much more drawn out than the previous games and the logic seems lackluster at best.  The first two cases also seem to mimic the first two cases of the original games.  The humor of the game doesn't seem as funny as the game hopes it is, some characters seem extremely smart at some points and completely oblivious at others, and after the third or fourth time where a "groundbreaking discovery" was found in a case, especially when some happened mere minutes after the others, the overall impacts of these discoveries were lost. I didn't feel as though I was delving into this exciting world full of court drama where anything could happen and at any moment my world could be turned upside down. I felt as though I was in an actual court, waiting for all the information I already knew to be repeated time and time again. Plot twists aren't as fun when they come back to back to back.All in all, I believe that if you want to play an Ace Attorney game, this is definitely a decent way to scratch that itch and to delve into more cases with a similar gameplay style as previous games. However, if you want a game with a compelling story then I believe that The Great Ace Attorney series leaves much to be desired.Also, I saw some players and people online stating that the second case of this game isn't great and that The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures is more fun during/after the third case. Although that might be true, if the game doesn't start to get good until ~40% of the game is done, then it isn't that much of a good game. I also have not played any of The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve, so I cannot comment on that.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a big fan of the Ace Attorney series and this release on Steam was something I've been looking forward to for the longest time!! _childDocuments_.review: This is hand down the worst games of the entire series, 43 hours in and I'm desperately struggling to push my self though the 2nd game.The entire reason this thing even exists is to tell a ridiculous intricate story of grand scale touching every second and interwoven to the point of being a constant bombardment of ridiculous storytelling that hideously over focuses on a small cast of characters being constantly reused.Investigating is virtually non existent and few things can be looked at or you are forbidden from looking at until the correct time the story wants to explain it to you, shomes exists only to force the games logic down your throat with a new tedious minigame of change this word thats wrong.Trials which should be the hi-light of the series have become a complete mess, new mechanics are messily added to try and act as fun new features but do nothing but drag the story forward. The jury system is only there as a scripted event to force you to play its new minigame as part of its heavy handed forcing the story to continue by having them explain issue to you instead of working anything out for yourself.Honestly a few characters are charming, but the constant handholding and deus ex machina prevented me from feeling like I was working anything out for myself, I have no time to get to know characters if they are in this constant super mega grand plot every second. This game might be great if you want some massive grand story told to you but this thing is terrible as a game.I strongly recommend you play every other game in the wright series and never touch this one at all, its clear why this was a spinoff set in a completely alternative time to distance itself. Before this spirit of justice was the weakest of the series for me but that game at least had me feel like I was mostly investigating and solving things myself still.

_childDocuments_.review: 99.9% text and the rest interaction. The whole story is drowned in just wading thru endless dialogues. I have replayed the others many times, but doubt I will even get thru half of this one. Pity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but I feel this game(s) definitely deserve it.The stories told over the course of both games are in my opinion the best in the series, often ending on a more somber and realistic notes than in other installments. All storylines are resolved by the end of the second game, culminating in the grand finale, that's on par with "Rise from the Ashes" or "Farewell, My Turnabout". The music is the best in the series so far, fitting to every character, every location, and of course every part of the trial.The cases were very well written, often making pretty solid twists and playing with players' expectations. I could't really find any "weak" cases, I thoroughly enjoyed all of them.My only issues with the game were that sometimes during the trial you have to present an item that fits your narrative, but doesn't actually prove anything, so you'd probably just miss it. Also the game may occasionaly crash (but autosave mitigates it well, and it wasn't a major problem).Overall I believe it's one of the greatest (IF not the greatest!) games of the series, which makes it even more infuriating that this gem remains so underrated. From what I've heard this duology was supposed to be a trilogy, but because the first part wasn't very popular in Japan they've scrapped that idea, and waited 4 years (or 6 if we count from the first game) with English localisation for both games. Which was a crime more heinous than the ones in games.

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a fantastic breath of fresh air for the series that manages to stay true to its roots while also bringing in new and exciting elements. The first game, The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures, is admittedly a slow burn compared to other Ace Attorney games. A majority of the first game is slow, but thorough with introducing characters and plot elements while also exploring the new setting. Many players may find themselves frustrated with the slow pacing. However, this is a deliberate attempt to thoroughly set up the plot and characters. If I had to describe it, it wouldn't be inaccurate to say that "Adventures walked, so that Resolve could soar." That isn't to say that the Adventures is a bad game. It is a fantastic entry to the series in its own right with endearing characters, a brand new setting, a fantastic soundtrack, and solid cases. Its only major downside is the fact that it is clearly written with a sequel in mind, which is not an issue for the Chronicles remaster, as The Great Ace Attorney: Resolve, is packaged with the Adventures.The Great Ace Attorney: Resolve, thankfully, does not disappoint. It is packed to the brim with amazing cases and rewards players of Adventures by giving them what they were teased with in the first game. Although many elements are re-used from the first game, they are masterfully mixed with brand new content in order to keep the game distinct from its predecessor while building upon it. The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a fantastic duology, and a wonderful entry into the AA franchise. It is both familiar and fresh, calling back to its roots while also adopting a new coat of paint to make an identity for itself through unique character designs, an engrossing plot, and an amazing soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't sure that I would like this game because it takes place in another time period and features another set of characters. Now I can say with certainty that this is my favoutire game from "Ace Attorney" series. Characters are great. Cases are interesting. Music is awesome. The final chapter, "The Resolve of Ryunosuke Naruhodo", somehow made me cry more than "Bridge to the Turnabout" from "Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Trials and Tribulations".100/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I can admit I was waiting for this with only mild hype. I was fairly "meh" about every Ace Attorney game after the original trilogy (which I've probably replayed a half dozen times). The nonsense forensics, emotion bars, locks, etc. Everything to take away from the bread and butter deduction, story and characters. And boy can I ever say I never expected to love this as much as I ended up loving it. I admit a couple of chapters may have been a tad slower, or didn't quite fit into the larger plot, but the way they made bits of each episode relevant to the central plot really was unexpected. The dance of deduction is one of the coolest things they added to the franchise, and the London setting along with the Sherlock Holmes spin-off stories (A huge fan of Holmes, read all of the original books), I had no idea what I was in for. The jury was a bit hit or miss, it sort of just felt like an extended cross-examination. If perhaps there was a more direct just pinning statements, without all the pressing, it would have effected the pacing less.This is like everything I wished the series would become, back when I first played the original trilogy all those years ago. I'm so happy the series had such an amazing return to form, and I really hope they find a way to continue it. I've had plenty of Phoenix's story, I'm more than happy to see where Ryunosuke goes next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty standard Ace Attorney game, but then a standard Ace Attorney game is still an 8/10 at minimum.Very good, very fun, very dramatic, great writing, fantastic cast of enjoyable characters, memorable music, lots of twists that you can predict and twists that you would never have expected. Also as a resident of Britland I can confirm that they completely nailed how consistently racist we are.10/10 alone for Herlock Sholmes' surprised falling over animation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Ace Attorney series, and especially if you're a fan of the original trilogy, then Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is more than well worth the price. It's the pinnacle of the series, with the best cast, score, story, Herlock Sholmes, and so much more to just enjoy once you're past the two introduction cases.It's been a long while since I've felt this way about a story, but it reignited my passion for the series and for stories like this in general after so long - it's just that good. Shu Takumi and his team really haven't lost their touch.

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest disappointment with this game is, after finally finishing it, learning that Capcom doesn't appear to have any plans for a sequel. GAAC has the same appealing story and writing found in the Ace Attorney mainline games, but with an even more appealing setting and supporting cast. The Victorian era allows for a tiny bit of steampunk "magic", but otherwise forces the investigation and logic to be reasonably grounded, with fewer plot twists dependent on deus ex machina solutions.On the other hand, GAAC is perfect to get into even if you've never played an Ace Attorney game.At around 40-50 hours total, the 10 GAAC chapters will definitely feel long at times, but all of the gameplay mechanics are at their most polished, so at least that time is spent reading the fun dialogue and interesting plotting. I'm glad I experienced the two games as a single package -- if there's one major complaint I'd make, it's that the first game is heavily tuned toward setting up the mystery and climax of the second game, so you're not wrong if you feel like it's a slog in some parts, with mysteries that feel relatively low stakes. Thankfully the setting and new characters are more than enough to keep your interest.By comparison, the second game is a real barn burner. It does feature the same Grand-Conspiracy-in-the-Justice-System seen in the other AA games, but there's enough twists and tweaks for long time series players that keep it interesting even if you can see some of the major twists a mile away.If you've liked any of the AA games then GAAC is a no-brainer to play. If you're interested in visual novel-type games in general, then GAAC is a great entry point into the Ace Attorney series

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game simply because of how amazing the first Great Ace Attorney was. I had played it with a fan translation, and was amazed at how good of a game it was despite it being such a late installment in the series. It introduced so many new things that made it feel so fresh. The cases were great, the characters were hilarious, and the prospect of a direct sequel/part 2 got me quite excited.So, as for Resolve, it was everything I hoped it would be. The story runs so deep. Every case is connected to the final showdown in some way. I found myself looking back at cases not only from Resolve, but from Adventures as well, to connect the dots. There were so many twists and turns, and I love it. It had me second-guessing so many times, which is great for an Ace Attorney game. The predictability of other installments in the series was not nearly as present here. I found there to be quite a few challenging parts, which was quite refreshing. The final case was absolutely spectacular, with so many shocking revelations. I really felt that the final case was possibly the best case in the entire series. If not, it is at least Top 3. It was expertly put together and I do not think I could have enjoyed it any more.I do not want to say too much to spoil the game, so I will leave it at that. If you are looking for a fresh installment to the Ace Attorney series, especially in the area of theme, I would absolutely recommend this game. Both Adventures and Resolve are excellent games and are some of the best. I hope that there may be another installment to this particular series. I would love to see van Zieks, Holmes, Iris, and Gina again.Oh, and Drebber's animations had me laughing so hard.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is afoot! and so is my learned friend    One of the best games I have played in a while. This is my second Ace Attorney game played (after the trilogies) and while the trilogies are my all-time favourite so far just for the sheer nostalgia and special place in my heart, this game was battling to be my favourite. ( I am currently finished with the first game and onto the second) Gameplay-wise, this does top the trilogies. It was marvelously interactive, I found the "Dance of Deduction" to be one of the most fun I've ever had playing an Ace attorney game. it made me feel like I am doing something rather than pressing A and RB occasionally while the character did all the thinking for me. I LOVE going back into the evidence and spinning it around, and it not pointing out what I have to do to find it.     However, I also like that it's a little easier to understand. It is by no means simple! but I have to look up what to do less, which I appreciate. The story is easier to follow with many plot twists, though they don't seem unreasonable. But, by far my favourite aspect is the CHARACTERS! Susato is such a lovable helper, Herlock is probably my favourite (I just love his effortless likeability) and Naruhodo is a great main character! He can't compare with Phoenix, but at the same time, it's different. He's cute and cool in his regards. I love the scenery, and the dialogue is amazing! I play it in English, they portray the accents well. I also play it in the Japanese dialogue, and they do great there! The graphics are phenomenal and the idle animations are so cute. I LOVE the jury minigame, and the pursue mechanic is also so nice. I do miss the pysche-locks, the lumisol, and other mechanics of the trilogy but gameplay-wise, this game blows it out of the park! Anyways, 10/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: slow start, but once you get onto Resolve you're in for one of the best Ace Attorney games.plot: very very good. 1-2 and 1-4 are a little below average but every other case is very good, even for ace attorney standards. the ending to the first game feels a little unsatisfying at first but everything is explained in Resolve, so don't worry! plot twists are amazing, the mystery behind each murder is very well written. i'll hold back from writing any more on this before i spoil anything because it's best experienced going in blind!characters: the best cast in the series. you'll fall in love with the detectives, prosecutor, assistant, protagonist, defendants and culprits. even the judge, jury and random suspects have great characterisation. if you play games for the characters this is for you.music: great! fully orchestrated, sounds "epic". not the chiptune sort of style you might be used to from the Trilogy but the composers handled the new style very well.setting: i really love the setting. it feels exactly like my perception of what victorian england should feel like.animation: the best in the series. there are only a few cutscenes but they're good. the characters' animations however are amazing, i really hope they put this sort of detail into ace attorney 7! animations alone will make you fall in love with certain characters ;)investigation game-play: the weak part of the game imo. can be slow - the pacing isn't great. if you're patient and like reading/character interactions then you might not mind it. there are no psyche-locks/logic but it's okay. the "move" screen gives you hints for where to go if you're stuck.game-play: pretty great.sometimes multiple witnesses take the stand at once, and the jury system is cool (at first, but i feel it had more potential and eventually felt overused). evidence presentation and pressing are entertaining and fair. the difficulty is pretty high for the series (definitely harder than AA1/danganronpa/investigations) but i liked that. would still be fine for beginners if you're up for a challenge, though! _childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is the first international release of two previously Japan-exclusive Ace Attorney prequels helmed by series creator Shu Takumi. These games are on a fundamental level quite familiar to fans of the series in terms of both gameplay and narrative and aesthetic tropes, but the setting is now primarily Victorian London. They also prominently feature characters and names from the classic Sherlock Holmes stories, but as some aspects of those stories are still under copyright in the United States, these games remained Japan-exclusive until 2021 and arrived internationally with some tweaks to circumvent those legal issues. It's a shame that they took so long to get here, though, since these are both very excellent games and among the best in their series, and all the better thanks the remastered visuals and excellent localization. The two games are effectively two halves of a larger story, with heavily overlapping casts of characters and identical gameplay. Many of these characters fall into familiar Ace Attorney archetypes, but most of those put their own spins on their predecessors that help them stand out, and that's to say nothing of highly entertaining "original" characters like Herlock, Gina, and Soseki. This game also introduces several mechanics that build upon the series' existing gameplay and feel like they're worth transplanting to the mainline series. The biggest highlights of these are the Dance of Deduction segments that help break up the traditional point-and-click system of investigation segments by incorporating the deductive elements of the courtroom segments, even if they're usually stretched out excessively long. The new jury system and the changes to the cross-examination system, both within the courtroom trial segments, are also very welcome.The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures serves as an introduction to this new version of Ace Attorney, but it's definitely the shakier of the two. The first two cases are tutorials of the courtroom and investigation gameplay respectively, and only the final trial manages to have a proper Ace Attorney-style victory without asterisks. On the other hand, this contributes to the protagonist's character arc that ultimately satisfies, and the odd-numbered cases are all highlights. Particularly, the pacing of the first case does a great job at building up to the protagonist's first declaration of "Objection!" Still, Adventures ultimately leaves large number of dangling plot threads to be resolved (no pun intended) in the sequel.The Great Ace Attorney 2: Resolve fires on all cylinders even in comparison to Adventures. The game is consistently excellent from start to finish, with the opening case being the weakest only in comparison. Besides having played the first game being more or less necessary, this game's most questionable choice is the odd chronology of the game. The first case focuses on a different protagonist than the rest of either game, the second is a flashback to an unseen case set immediately after the first game's fourth case, and the fourth and fifth "cases" are actually one single case spread across two chapters. Still, it executes all of this superbly, with even the "filler" cases being up there among the series' best. That's to say nothing of how this entry manages to tie together nearly every dangling plot thread left from the first game in an extremely satisfying way, culminating in a spectacular climax.The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is an easy recommendation to just about anyone with an inkling of an interest in Ace Attorney, be they completely new to the series, fans who fondly remember the Phoenix Wright Trilogy, or even fans burned by the more recent mainline games. I eagerly await to see what Capcom has next in store for the Ace Attorney series.

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a duology of The Great Ace Attorney Adventures originally released in 2015 and The Great Ace Attorney Resolve originally released in 2017. It is a spin-off to the mainline series featuring Ryunosuke Naruhodo, ancestor of Ryuichi Naruhodo or better known in the west as Phoenix Wright. If you're new to the Ace Attorney Series this is a great place to start. The episodes of the game all connect into an overarching story; each case you solve gives you a piece of the puzzle and builds up towards the final episode. The final episode is stellar and makes the journey through the previous episodes worthwhile despite some of the episodes being rather slow to get through. The antagonist of the whole story is pretty predictable but the journey getting there and the why was fun to experience. The game portrays Britain at the height of its power really well and gives a lot of characterisation of the relationship between Britain and Japan. There is a lot of text to read through so be prepared. All of the main recurring characters are well portrayed and memorable. Just like the other Ace Attorney games there's plenty of quirky and fun characters to enjoy.Ryunosuke Naruhodo is a nervous rookie of law but grows through the episodes where he has doubts about what his goal should be when he defends his clients, whether he should believe in them, do whats right for them or seek the truth.Herlock Sholmes the great detective is active in the game with his logic and reasoning spectacular and although he may act weird and dumb at times he's actually far smarter than he leads on making him a reliable ally in times of need. Kazuma Asogi is a Japanese student of law given a mission by the Japanese Government with the goal of changing the climate of law and justice in his home country. He is Ryunosuke's best friend.Susato is a reliable judicial assistant that is able to give Ryunosuke the push and support he needs when he feels like there is no way forward, her father plays an important role and she at times questions what her father really knows causing her to choose her own path.Barok Van Zieks is the main prosecutor you face against and he is often able to force Ryunosuke into a corner right from the outset, making the accused seem like the true culprit. He has an interconnected history with the overarching story of the game. The game follows the formula of Investigation sections and courtroom sections. In the investigative sections you examine objects and characters to find evidence or information relating towards the case and build up weapons to use for the courtroom sections. In between these investigative sections are Sholmes' Logic and Reasoning Spectacular where you will have to correct Sholmes deductions to make sense of the situation at the given time. Using the powers of observation, you can correct and deduce additional information which is one of Ryunosuke's strong points.During the courtroom sections you cross examine witness testimonies and present evidence to show inconsistencies in their testimony, this game unlike previous entries features multiple witnesses at the stand, so you are able to confer and compare their testimonies on the spot with each other. This is a pretty cool way to include more characters at once rather than sitting through just 1 person at a time. At times when you are backed into a corner by the prosecution the Jury gives their vote and you subsequently have to do a Summation Examination, very similar to a cross examination and pit their statements together to overturn their decision and keep the trial going. By the end of each case you are given a small hint as to what the overall story is about and there's never a large gap between cases creating a good sense continuity while playing.While there is a ton of text to read and go through, these gameplay sections were never too difficult to figure out and it only got really difficult, understandably towards the end. Each episode could vary between a 5hr-12hr each, so best to take your time going through this one.The 3D models and environments were great and it was always easy to identify any evidence or objects of interest. Each character has their quirky movements such as Ryunosuke's bullet sweat, Susato takedown, Sholmes cap flick and Van Zieks destroying of expensive wine. The environments represented how Britain looks fairly well though it leaves out quite a few major landmarks we know of today.Soundtrack is great, many enjoyable themes and its easy to recognise each characters theme when they get their moments. There's a very clear leitmotif especially in Kazuma's theme that invokes a sense of courage to pave the way forward. The pursuit theme is pretty fun and gives you a heroic feel when you figure out the inconsistency. Investigation theme is pretty sick too, really makes you feel like you're a great detective yourself looking for clues. The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a solid entry into the series giving a full complete story, leaving no mystery unsolved and paving the way for the future. There could very well a sequel in the future if they wanted to make one. This game is definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, awful PC port...Ever since the original release of Dai Gyakuten Saiban, I've been dreaming of having a chance to play, what can arguably be considered some of the best Ace Attorney games in the franchise. Now finally... 6 years after the original release of Dai Gyakuten Saiban and 4 years after the release of Dai Gyakuten Saiban 2, I finally got to play them... Words cant describe how happy and satisfied I feel having been able to enjoy these games by myself.-The PC port has some issues-Let's begin with the elephant in the room... Now, it's pretty clear that these are just the mobile versions of both games ported to PC. Even though playable, it's quite clear that these games were not designed to be played on a PC. Exit game... Where is it??? Seriously, not having an option to exit the game in the main menu was already a pretty bad sign. The only way to exit the game is through the options, which honestly isn't where an average gamer would look for it. Exit game is typically located in the main menu, this is honestly something that should be fixed as soon as possible in my opinion.It's very easy to see how muddy the textures look and how models clip through each other on higher resolutions. Anti-aliasing needs some serious improvements and the game needs more options for the players to finetune the game for their computers, there are only 4 customisable options in the game: Resolution, Windowed/Borderless, AntiAliasing On/Off and V-Sync On/Off.  That's right, the graphics are not customisable, you're not able to tune the frame-rate... Just very barebones settings in general.The frame-rate is locked to 30 by the way, this includes all the main menu animations and this frame cap is there seemingly for no reason whatsoever. And before you say that it's normal to be locked at 30fps, I have to disagree since even the Nintendo Switch version runs  at 60fps. Luckily there is an amazing mod to fix the frame-rate alongside some other issues:  And the audio... God, how did Capcom mess this up so bad? Luckily there is also an amazing mod to fix the soundtrack:  I do use both of these mods myself, but I have to say that these issues shouldn't have been there to begin with. If you don't want to deal with all this garbage, I would honestly recommend buying the Nintendo Switch version instead if you already own the console. And please Capcom, for the love of god... Fix the PC version ASAP, I honestly expected better from a 39,99€ game.-Localisation: The Good-Episode 1 The Great Departure is the way Ace Attorney games should be localised. Just the fact that you allowed us to play this game with the Japanese dub instead of the English dub was already a huge step in the right direction. Honestly, that is the way I would love to enjoy the mainline entries in this franchise, give us the option to play the games with the original dub, original character names and Japanese elements.I know I may just be beating a dead horse here by mentioning Ace Attorney Investigations 2, but honestly, I would love to play both Investigations 1 and 2 with a similar localisation seen in Episode 1 The Great Departure. Hell, I would love to play every game in the franchise with that kind of a localisation. Perhaps something worth attempting in a future entry?-Localisation: The Bad-Now... I have to express that I am disappointed about some characters having their names changed. Now just to be clear, I am not referring to Herlock Sholmes here. I am referring to characters that didn't really have any copyright issue behind their change of name such as: 'Mitrov Stroganov' being renamed to 'Bif Strogenov' , 'Benjamin Dobinbough' being renamed to 'Albert Harebrayne' and most disappointing of all... 'Haori Murasame' being renamed to 'Rei Membami'Some of the changes were completely understandable, but honestly there were a lot of names that should not have been altered to begin with, unfortunately the localisation team went too far with the changes... Again.-Herlock Sholmes-I know that some people have an issue with the fact that Sherlock Holmes was renamed to Herlock Sholmes and Watson into Wilson. However, this happens to be the only way we're able to enjoy these games in the west. It's not Capcom's fault that Sherlock Holmes has such awful copyright issues. If you want to complain to someone about this, complain to Conan Doyle Estate, since Capcom really didn't have a choice here.-DGS1-An absolute master piece, I loved every moment of it. I honestly don't really have bad things to mention about this one. Perhaps my only complaint would be the lack of a task list during the investigation sections of the game. The characters were fun and unique, all culprits had solid motivations that even made you somewhat sympathetic of their fate.-DGS2-I have to say that, DGS2 had a lot to live up to as a sequel to DGS1 and it is clear to see that it was aiming to be even more ambitious than it's predecessor. However, there were a few downsides to the scale of the game. For example, the lack of animated cutscenes was somewhat disappointing as they really contributed to the overall feel of the first game. However, the pros really outweigh the cons in this sequel. It had a significantly better story overall, having more twists and being darker than its prequel. It introduced plenty of new characters and expanded the soundtrack. -Conclusion-Whether you're new to the franchise or a long time fan of the Ace Attorney games, this is something you absolutely have to play and enjoy for yourself as this is one of a kind masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: A must-have for fans, but not the place to start.GAA is a game that takes the series to new heights in mystery and suspense. The puzzles are tough but rewarding, the characters are memorable, and the writing is superb. In particular, this game challenges many of the cliches and tropes the series has built up and puts new spins on them. This occasionally lapses into a more annoying satire, but rarely. For newbies, I would not recommend starting here, as I think many of the twists and jokes would fall flat for someone not familiar with the background behind them. It's still fun, but perhaps play the original trilogy first.In addition, this is not as comedic a game if that's what draws you to AA. The suspense is excellent, but the characters are much more rarely given time to just hang out and play off each other. Not a bad change, but a notable difference.

_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've played (and been in love with) every Ace Attorney game since their DS days. The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is no exception to this love and (so far) has massively exceeded my expectations! Despite being excited the translation/localization of the game finally came about, I was a little hesitant going into a game with an *entirely* new cast of characters (even Apollo Justice and Edgeworth Investigations had familiar faces). I am so glad I played anyway..!! All of the new mechanics, like the Dance of Deduction and wooing members of the jury, are new and fun additions to the classic visual-novel style gameplay. The animations look crisp and are fun/entertaining, and there are even more of the usual "punny" characters the Ace Attorney series is known for.On that note, I've noticed a ton of little animations/easter-eggs in during what would otherwise be a stationary scene! Little movements or ways characters look/act that are not pointed out or ever shined a spotlight on, and just go on in the background .. It's all quite endearing!I've only *really* just started, but I'm already looking forward to continuing my journey with Ryunosuke (and very hopeful for future Ace Attorney Chronicles)!

_childDocuments_.review: These games are damn good. A detective/lawyer story with colourful characters, interesting plot threads and puzzling mysteries. Ace attorney games never fail to disappoint. _childDocuments_.review: is the complete duology made from the two games  and , both visual novels developed and published by CAPCOM.It follows the adventures of Ryuuichi Naruhodo's (Phoenix Wright's) ancestor, Ryunosuke Naruhodo, as he, by a weird twist of fate, ends up becoming a practising defence lawyer in the late 19th century London.My favourite character from this game is (yes, he's based on a real person). Because of this, all subheaders in this review will be four-word alliterations. (I've tried to underline the most significant word for the subheader. Don't be too hard on me, I tried my best.)I'll also be referring to "the original trilogy" in this review, by which I mean the Phoenix Wright games.I'll not speak much on the story, but one thing right of the bat: Every case ties into the overarching plot. There are no "filler" cases like in the original trilogy. Yes, even the tutorial cases have some significance.In typical Ace Attorney fashion, many cases are ridiculously convoluted but the momentum of the courtroom drama tends to make you forget about it, which is good of course. They're not meant to hold under heavy scrutiny, they're roller coaster rides that you go on for the thrill.This game respects its setting though. Most of the time. For example:In one case, a friend of Ryunosuke's develops a chemical compound that makes blood change color depending on "whose it is". My initial response was "surely a 19th century court won't accept that as evidence", and it didn't! Coming from the final case of the original trilogy, this surprised me in a good way.As previously mentioned, this is a visual novel. Most of this game is spent reading. There are a few things in place to spice it up however.This game is divided into 10 episodes (5 each for GAA and GAA2), and with the exception of 3 episodes, they have the same structure: one or more investigation phases and one or more trial phases.In the investigation phase you talk to people and investigate the crime scene to build your case for the trial phase. While this part may seem free-roam, it's actually pretty heavily on rails, and the game will not move on to the trial without you having all the evidence you need (thank goodness).To break up the investigation phase this game has the Logic and Reasoning Spectacular (also known as the Dance of Deduction) minigame where Ryunosuke helps the character Herlock Sholmes figure out some sort of truth using the environment and evidence. This is a fun visual spectacle if nothing else.In the trial phase you listen to formal witness testimony and point out contradictions in their statements using evidence. You can press their statements to reveal new information or alter their testimony.Unlike earlier Ace Attorney entries, multiple witnesses can be in the stand at the same time. Another witness may react to the currently speaking witness' statement, which you can then pursue to gather even more information.Also new to this entry is the Summation Examination game, in which you try to convince the jury (who have all voted your client guilty) why they should allow the trial to continue. This involves selecting two different jurors and pitting them against each other for some reason, usually because their statements contradict.The original Ace Attorney trilogy comprised of the first visual novels I ever read. I've since read a lot of different ones, and I've realised that Ace Attorney can be quite inconvenient to maneuver at times.I'll go over a few good and bad things:Even with "skip read text" on, the text goes by so slow. The reason for this is because Ace Attorney games alter text speed and pauses to give an impression of how the speaker is saying their lines. It's not worth it. There is also no skip button, a feature found in even the oldest visual novels out there.This is at its worst during Herlock Sholmes' deductions, which take FOREVER to get through. They first have you read through his deduction, then you have to go through them AGAIN to correct his mistakes.This game's soundtrack is stellar. It uses significantly more classic instruments compared to the original trilogy's more electronic soundtrack, which is fitting considering the game's setting.I'm particularily partial to the Cross-Examination theme, which I consider the best in the series. Compare the  version, which is played during most witness testimony to the  version, which is usually played during the final critical testimony you have to work with.There are many more good ones, but I'll put  as my last example. It really reminds me of a puzzle.Steam Achievements for this title are tied to in-game "accolades". Some are gotten by just playing, for others you need to do certain things during your playthrough. The window of opportunity for some of there are as short as one dialog box, and if you miss one you have to either reload a save or start the episode all over again. Because of the aformentioned lack of skip mode, this is beyond tedious and I'll never see myself doing it. Use a guide if you desperately want all accolades in one go.There are a few surprises thrown in, which are more likely to get you if you're an old fan.There's for example a moment where you have to , even though you have  that you can do so. You instead have to realise you have to do it based on other factors. This was great! I personally wished you had to use the new courtroom mechanics more, and in even more unorthodox ways. It may have sounded like a lot of negatives, but this is a really good visual novel aside from the things I've mentioned. It clearly respects itself and its characters more than, say, Spirit of Justice. It's also a step in the right direction for the future of Ace Attorney (if there is still a future that is).I love Phoenix, Edgeworth and Maya as much as the next guy, but this visual novel is a prime example of what this series needed: new characters and new stories.If you've never read a visual novel before this is a  entry point to the medium. It has more gameplay than normal visual novels, so you'll be eased into the experience! You'll also not miss the normal visual novel conveniences like skip mode and the text scrolling issue I've mentioned.For returning fans I say: This game is for you. It's new, it's fresh, and it's Ace Attorney.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge props to the madmen at Capcom for localizing these two fantastic games. These games are definitely quite unique from the rest of the series, in both setting and atmosphere. You'll be spending hours and hours listening to Victorian orchestral music and staring at the depressing streets of London. This game will really give you an idea of why there's the usual depression, and then there's the BRITISH type of depression. It's a whole different beast. It also has some very interesting cases, with one of my favorites being the closed-roomed murder mystery inside a moving horse carriage. The writing quality, the mind-bending mysteries, and the "soul" of the series, which are the zany and creative characters, are still intact despite the change in setting. The second game, especially, has some of the coolest and most entertaining witnesses out of the entire franchise (Drebber and Shamspeare). Playing these games made me realize that it's been 20 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ years since the first game came out. It's been a long journey, and I'm glad that these games have been a big part of my life for so many years. Buy this collection and god save the queen.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we start let me disclose that the number of hours in my steam account is not true to the experience I have with this game. I played it before, sailing the seven seas, and bought it immediately upon completion, because I felt like a criminal not paying for something like THIS.So, Ace Attorney huh? I’ve seen something about it but I still don’t get what all the raving is about. Isn’t it a joky visual novel about lawyers that scream really loud and hit their desks when they are mad ? Well, yeah, it’s about that, but that would not do it justice.Ace Attorney is a half visual novel half adventure game series about being a lawyer. These games have a lot of humor but that does not impede them from developing some of the most hard hitting emotional drama you will ever see in a story game. The series has a tradition with excellent characterization and it counts with some of the best characters i’ve had the pleasure of meeting, period. The mystery is good, the relationships are solid, the humor is hilarious and the twists unexpected, cruel swings of fate that could change everything, from a character’s motivation to the significance of previous events. Gameplay wise, you will investigate like you would in any classic adventure game, but then you will participate in the famed court trial sections, the heart and soul of the series.These sections are “narrative puzzles” and they will test your understanding of the mystery at hand and facilitate some groundbreaking revelations about the plot that you as a player are uncovering. And that is the gist of it. The series has seen some innovations and upgrades along the years, but nothing has broken this formula yet.So why do I think then, that this is one of the best games i’ve ever played and probably the best entry in the entire Ace Attorney Series ?The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles does not break the mold. It has a lot of original ideas, but most of what you do, see, and are told here, you can find it somewhere else in the series.But, it does something the rest of the series does not: ALL OF IT, AT ONCE, HANDLED WITH SUCH CARE AND PERFECTION.That is why I consider TGAA the magnum opus of Sho Takumi. It’s threading familiar ground, but with absolute passion and almost 20 years of expertise. The main difference between TGAA and the rest of the series, is surprisingly, not the time it is set in, but it’s narrative structure. Past entries are sequels to one another, but they don’t benefit that much from it. Yes, you get character progression and development that lasts for 3 entries during the original trilogy, but the events of each game affect mainly themselves. And surprise surprise, the best moments in the original trilogy happen at the end where narrative elements from all the rest of the games come to the picture again in one last case that is as complex as it is emotionally satisfying.Well, TGAA does exactly that… with every single case.TGAAC contains both TGAA1 and TGAA2, and that is a good thing, because TGAA2 is not the sequel to TGAA1, its PART 2 OF THE STORY. Both games need each other and are incomplete without each other. TGAAC is a 50 hour narrative experience where every single event, character, motivation, secret and past event is relevant and necessary to the narrative. Let that sink in. 50 hours where everything matters. That is something that i’ve only experienced a handful of times. Yes, JRPGs last that many hours… because you are grinding, fighting and leveling. Ace Attorney is 100% story the whole way through. And the best thing is that THEY ACTUALLY PULLED THIS OFF. THEY MANAGED TO HANDLE 50 HOURS OF NARRATIVE AND MAKE IT MAKE SENSE EVERY STEP OF THE WAY. I cannot even BEGIN to describe the awe I felt when I finished this masterpiece. There I was, with my heart in my hands, one tear crossing my cheek, having beaten the last case, and when I thought it was over they gave me 1 more hour of characters just… being characters. Saying goodbye to each other. Being nice to each other. Making life decisions. The story is so good and it knows it so well that is has the massive balls to ask you for 1 more hour of your time to spend with its characters and my answer is YES, GLADLY, AND THANK YOU.Again, TGAA is not groundbreaking for what it does, but for how well it does. If it ain’t broke don’t fix it, but that is not an excuse for being lazy and this entry, more than ever, has a lot to prove. And it does just that, by also iterating and improving on the formula.It might take a little long to implement those changes (3 whole cases from the first game as a complete introduction) but it ends up paying off in the end, when part 2 pulls off a case 3 that feels like a case 5 from other games.And along the way you will find a lot of “firsts” for the series.A difficult and long case 1. A case 2 100% dedicated to investigating that feels like an old school adventure game. A case 3 where they get the actual crime scene into the trial… in an extremely original way that i won’t spoil.They also managed to spice up the actual gameplay, not just the setting and pace. You can cross examine multiple people at once now. You can make statements clash in certain segments instead of just press/present evidence. You can fully examine every piece of evidence, which sometimes refreshes the info you have for that piece on the court record.All of these are good changes and make the experience less monotonous.On a personal note, I think TGAA has some of the most likeable characters in the series and I want to adopt, befriend, or marry a LOT of them. Everyone is at their peak here,Relatable but talented protagonist, incredible mentor figure, bubbly but layered and amazing assistant, top tier backstory having prosecutor, and an ABSOLUTE UNIT of a final villain.♥♥♥♥ ,now I’m just fanboying.Buy this. If you are a fan, if you want to try the series and don’t know where to start, or just cause you like Sherlock Holmes and mystery. Whatever the reason. This is a 10/10 story.

_childDocuments_.review: Dare I say the Great Ace Attorney Chronicles surpasses the original Ace Attorney series? Amazing story, so many different intertwining threads so carefully woven into an intriguing and intricate story. Truly a masterpiece visual novel with perfectly harmonizing story, music, characters, mystery, humour, wit, sound effects and animations that sets a new standard.The good: Everything.The bad: Nothing to complain of other than the fact that it's a very long game and might not be fast paced enough for some folks.The ugly: Game is only partially voiced.PS. _childDocuments_.review: TGAAC is another great entry into the Ace Attorney series. I've played all 6 main games, the 2 investigations spinoff and the crossover with Professor Layton and this entry ranks probably in the top 3 (Below T&T and Dual Destinies).The game follows Ryosuke Naruhodo mostly in Court with the main gameplay coming from listening to testimony and pointing out contradictions. (For QoL turn on skip for unread dialog since there is no voiced dialog for the most part to make text appear faster)This is the first entry that doesn't reuse any recurring characters from the main games so the overarching story takes place within the 10 cases. If you are not invested into the series this is a great place to start, the other one being the original trilogy (AA, JFA ,T&T). If you are acquainted with the other games then you probably know what to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: A revolutionizing tale of an upcoming lawyer and his journey to the city of London. This game does a fantastic job of putting you in the shoes of the main character, Ryunosuke Naruhodo, as you explore different environments, interact with many zany and compelling characters while solving mysteries and pointing out the true culprit in classic Ace Attorney fashion. Not to mention the updated graphics, amazing soundtrack and Sherlock Holmes-inspired storylines that really make it feel like a Victorian Era Mystery game. If you're a fan of the genre, the franchise or just want to try out a game with an interesting story and fun characters, then I recommend giving this a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: What a truly marvelous game and experience it was.I waited until I finished both before I would leave a review and 63 hours later here we are!So the pretense, as a huge Ace Attorney fan I was excited for more in the series and at first had skepticism on whether or not this would live up to my expectations of it being great so I tempered them. I won't make this an extremely long review but will point out what I did enjoy and didn't enjoy. The music, the story, and the setting was such a beautiful package for this duology. I do agree with people's sentiment that the first game by itself unfortunately doesn't hold much water and it's alright at best do to the overall story just ending abruptly and feeling like you never really got a chance to understand everything at play.The bright side though, is that the second game is a masterpiece of it's own. Essentially the first game more or less sets up the story to be explored and resolved in the second game. It's a long journey that feels exhausting to the point of wanting to just give up and drop the game after the first one but the payoff is worth it. Luckily this game sells as a package with both the first and second game so you can experience both of them but I must advise to really push through to the second game and it's slow start to get to what I and I believe some other fans would concur as one of the best games in the entire series. If I would to compare to Original Ace Attorney Trilogy, I would say I prefer the Great Ace Attorney Chronicles over the Trilogy just because I am slightly biased the setting of Britain, detectives etc but also because as a whole package Chronicles really nails it on the head. With Trilogy I felt it was easy to enjoy certain aspects of some things while disliking others but it was always hard to say as a whole the game felt like a masterpiece of sorts. With Chronicles, it felt like they took everything they learned from Trilogy and made it that much better. The entire package from the music to the setting, characters etc were all just wonderful and made for a great experience that I will always remember. I do hope one day we get a third installment in this chronicle as it truly deserves one. Overall If you're a fan of Ace Attorney in general, or maybe detective stories/investigations I recommend you give this game a shot even if you're not a big fan of visual novels. I personally don't care for many myself but felt glued to this game, and previous experience of the Original Trilogy is not needed to understand or play this game.Thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Yes!I've played through all the Ace Attourney ports on the app store, and am a big fan of the series. I love these games, and I've been looking forward to chronicles finally coming to european players. The Ace Attourney series is a mix between visual novel and detective game. It's memorable for its goofy characters, slapstick humor, and story arcs that span several cases.I think this game takes everything I enjoy with the series and puts it neatly into one package. I think it's the most polished and consistent attourney game I've played. I especially like the care that was put into the music, I think it makes a big difference. And the characters are done so well! They are memorable, lovable, and goofy - to the point where they almost seem to form the substance of the game.What usally dissapoints me with these games is that the intended audience is someone who has never played ace attourney, and so every game starts off frustratingly easy. This game had a difficulty curve that progressed into the second game, which I appreciated.Some moments felt very tedious in the game, like the deduction acts - although visually fun, I thought they were a little tedious and simple. The testimony has a gimmick that could have made interesting gameplay, if it didn't hit the player over the head with it with a big alert. The cases were good, but ultimately, It's not Ace Attourney to me unless you're stumped sometimes and get the hammer and verbal abuse and such and such, and I didn't get that feeling until the second game.Otherwise, I can't find too much in this game that's objectionableI hope you get this game and that you like it as much as I didSee you in court~~
_childDocuments_.name: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the Ace Attorney series, I was quite interested and excited in this series now that it was being localized. Though I would technically "recommend" this collection, that comes with a huge heaping tablespoon of salt as well.I'm not going to sugarcoat it; the first game in this collection/story is BORING. Like, really boring, and super slow. All of the characters feel incredibly one-dimensional. Dialogue is tedious and drawn out to a mind-numbing degree. Many characters (especially Herlock Sholmes) are just idiotic way beyond the degree that would be entertaining. The Herlock Sholmes deduction "minigames" are incredibly slow and repetitive, make the character look even more incompetent, and more often than not just waste the player's time due to how pointlessly easy they are. Despite sporting slow and tedious dialogue, the game ironically also has a serious issue with pacing and rushing through key moments of the story; the few investigations that the story does have are crammed into a single day, which leads to awkward overly detailed investigations of places with seemingly no relevance to the issue at hand. Since trials also only last a single day, every important story beat is crammed back to back which leads up to a feeling that the game will pause for a brief reprieve only for the entire case to just conclude abruptly. The first game has a couple of interesting moments, but it really does get drowned out by the 30+ hours of tedium and the overall insipidness of the story.The second game in the collection (and the conclusion to this duology) however, is AMAZING. The individual cases are much faster paced and exciting - with much more complex characters and its' stories interwoven together to make a really satisfying final picture. A large number of the cases in the second game would honestly rank among my favorite Ace Attorney cases of all time - they're that good. Ideally, I'd just recommend skipping the first game to enjoy the second game, however...In reality, the biggest problem with this series is that the first game does nothing but set up the metaphorical dominoes of the story (a slow and tedious process), while the second game spends the entire time knocking those dominoes down; this is why it's so exciting and memorable. Basically, the first game crawls so that the second game can sprint. Unfortunately, the second game is going to lose all of it's impact without seeing the first half of the story.Personally, I think the second game's merits vastly outweigh the issues of the first game. Keep in mind though, that means trudging through 30+ long and boring hours before you can get to the 30 great and exciting hours. If that kind of commitment seems excessive, I'd recommend passing on the whole collection. Otherwise, I'd still highly recommend it - especially to existing Ace Attorney fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, The Great Ace Attorney. This duology of games with it's endearing cast of characters and very gripping story has sold me fully. As a longer-time fan of the Ace Attorney franchise I had heard mixed opinions on this game and was hesitant to try it out - but to me The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is well worth the price. Getting the obvious out of the way first: Yes, TGAA has trouble with its pacing, especially the first game. The first two cases are extremely slow paced, which for a visual novel can be detrimental as engagement will suffer for it. While it does pick up from there, the rest of the first game and a lot of the second game still have a pacing issue, most notable in the filler cases. It is very noticable that this was initially meant to be a single game, which was too lengthy and thus split into two. The first game in the duology got the short end of the stick in terms of engaging cases and story, sadly. There's little to say in its defence here - this was an avoidable issue and can definitely turn people away from the game.Another point of warning is that the game deals with some heavy topics in the racism/sexism that Ryunosuke and Susato often encounter in their time in England. While I personally think it good that the game does not shy away from addressing these issues and instead have the Japanese law duo fight and overcome these prejudices, it can understandably be a turnoff for some. Luckily, though, The Great Ace Attorney also does a lot of things right. To begin with: the characters. The main cast consisting of Ryunosuke, Susato and Herlock Sholmes are all very different in character and mesh pretty well together. Ryunosuke's general unknowingness stands in sharp contrast to Susato, who is well-versed in general knowledge. And Sholmes' character is wholly chaotic in the best way. He's almost always entertaining in some form, whether that is through his curious methods of deducing or his general inability to act like a normal person, whenever he's on screen it usually brings me great amusement. And that's just the main three; many of the rest of the cast also have a lot to love. Ranging from the intimidating Barok van Zieks and Lord Stronghart to the adorable Iris Wilson - there's only a few of the recurring characters who I didn't feel at least something positive for. The interactions of them with the main cast and with each other add a lot to the worldbuilding. None of the recurring cast feels like they were there just because a character was required for the story. The story itself is the most important part of a visual novel, and these games deliver. The story, importantly, feels cohesive despite its pacing issues. The games have a lot of dark undertones and the story takes itself really seriously. For a genre where the story is heavily important, that's good! A main reason for me to keep wanting to play this game for long sessions is to see where the story would go from there. To me it was not a predictable storyline and when the story concluded and all was revealed - everything makes sense. The twist reveals are logical, the motives line up and the conclusion is very satisfying. The climax is honestly my favourite part of the duology and it left a very strong impact. Though I must say that I love every single bit from the third case of the second game all the way until the very end: these to me are some of the strongest cases the series has to offer. Another point in favor is the soundtrack. This games music shines the most in its character themes, whether that's Susato's soothing song, Sholmes' almost-serious detective theme, Barok's intimidating theme that really sells his accordingly intimidating character or Iris' whimsical vibe with its upbeat tones that fit her cheerful nature to a tee; when a character has their own theme it is without exception a great exposition of their character. The court and area themes do not disappoint either, the moderato/allegro cross-examination themes keep these sections engaging while the suspense themes rise the tension as they should. And that's not even having mentioned the Dance of Deduction themes - wonderful pieces of music only adding to why I love that mechanic so much.Speaking of which: this game adds a few mechanics onto the standard Ace Attorney formula. Already having mentioned the Dance of Deduction, I'll start with that: these are short sections that break up the investigation segments with a logic minigame of sorts. In these sections, Ryunosuke and Susato try to make sense of whatever ridiculous nonsense Sholmes has cooked up this time in order to reveal new information. They are generally pretty simple but they serve their purpose well and the charming animations help sell this mechanic. The second and third mechanics take place during the court sections. One is to have multiple witnesses at once, where they can react to each other's statements which reveals new information. The other makes use of the jury system, where Ryunosuke has to convince the jury of his client's innocence by finding contradictions in their reasoning. These mechanics serve to add a little extra depth to the court sections, which for me is appreciated. It makes you feel like you're actually making progress whenever one of these shows up, helpful because of the general lenghtiness of the court sections. In conclusion, this game to me is definitely worth the investment. The second Great Ace Attorney game is my favorite game ever made, though I tried to be as objective as possible writing this review. This duology is not perfect, but if you're okay with playing a slower-paced game I 100% recommend it. One of the franchises highs, for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles is a fantastic duology and albeit flawed a brilliant experience to play through.I played the first game all the way back in summer 2021 and finally got around to playing the sequel in March of 2023: And while my memory was a bit hazy, I cannot stress enough that the characters are so memorable that picking up 1.5 years later was no issue. As soon as someone came on screen I immediately remembered them, and that just is peak character writing to me.Things to consider:The biggest issue that I have with especially the first game is the excruciating slow pace. And the issue to me doesn't necessarily lie in the slow storytelling, it's more that the game often gives you clues so early that you figure out what's going on before most of the characters can. While that eliminates the tedium of the mainline games where I remember often being stumped, not knowing how to continue, GAA takes it a bit too much into the easy direction. GAA feels much more like a courtroom drama and less like detective games, which means you pretty much always know the culprit from the get-go and instead of piecing together what happened it's much more like: "alright, we know the destination, but how do we get there and out of the current conundrum".As soon as I understood that I had a much better experience, leaned back for the ride, and enjoyed everything the game was throwing at me.Especially the second game goes hard. It culminates in a grand finale that to my satisfaction was able to tie up literally every single loose end. It doesn't leave any question unanswered and gives all the characters closure. I haven't felt that good about finishing a story in a while.One other thing that stood out to me was the brilliant localisation. The team that translated these games went above and beyond. I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys visual novels or the mainline series. The second game for sure has catapulted itself into my top favourite entries of the franchise, and I will remember the characters of the duology fondly.
