_childDocuments_.review: It would be tempting for me to say that if "White Shadows" was any more inspired by Playdead, it would possibly be named "Inside 2: Electric Boogaloo". But for all the similarities there, "White Shadows" has also many differences - some of them very big - from Playdead's games. Because if Playdead ultimately puts play above everything else, "Shadows" cares very much about its story, mood and emotions. It's a game that leaves little to our imaginations, and very much wants us to know what's going on, even if gradually. Which is not a bad idea: it may be good to see developers at Monokel - in its inaugural game - trying to do their own thing. But when this takes a toll on gameplay, that's when I have my issues.For starters, let's give credit where credit is due: "White Shadows" is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. I know I say that a lot in my reviews, but this one delivered one of the most visually arresting and immersive experiences I've ever had in this medium. It's truly a game to marvel, a black-and-white looker that will give you plenty to look at. Not only that, but the sound mixing is also spectacular, with moments of radio cacophony, distant sounds and pitch-perfect usage of classical music, such as "Ride of the Valkyries", "The Blue Danube", "Flight of the Bumblebee" and "Dies Irae". It's a game to play either with big loudspeakers, or with headphones.But I guess this is part of the problem: it's too much about visuals and the lore they transmit, and not so much about gameplay. As I played it, I quickly realised this is not firstly a puzzle game. There is a fair share of problems to be solved along the journey, and a lot of platforming to be had, yes. But the game may feel at times like a walking simulator, with no secret paths (that I know of), and with some tedious situations that are so... well, tedious.It mostly rejects Playdead's penchant for teaching players what to do by punishing them, albeit it does have one of two situations that play out like that. That was my major issue with "Limbo" and "Inside", and it's nice to see that "White Shadows" doesn't lean much into that direction. But it can be very slow paced sometimes, with moments when control is taken from us and drag on for way too long - again, in an attempt to woo us with its visuals, with its visual storytelling. While it indeed is a truly "cinematic" game, not everyone will enjoy it, and this should have been advertised better.Characters don't talk (one sings however), but there's a ton of signs telling us what this world is, how it came to be, how it works. Even the chapters are announced in signs across the world. I hope this is not a major spoiler, but at a moment there's even this boring play meant to tell us what happened, and who our protagonist is. At two moments, the game got interrupted by an unskippable commercial break for a product within that universe. That's right: commercial breaks in my game. The same commercial, by the way. Avoiding commercials is the only reason I pay money for YouTube Premium, and now I'm stuck with two. Being upfront about lore is not much of an issue itself; it's how it's too much at front and centre.One issue I had with the game at first is that its visuals can be misleading. The game is so visually loaded that, sometimes, I confused visual elements with platforms. For instance, there's this train section that ends with this giant mechanic wolf swallowing the wagons. That felt threatening to me, so I felt it was time to abandon ship. I thought there was a platform in the environment I should jump at, and I kept on missing it. As it turned out, it was... nothing. Just a thing in the environment, and I was supposed to be indeed swallowed by the wolf thing.  The game is not what I would call original, for all its ambition. Again, it's beautifully made, and you can see a lot of time and love was poured on it. But we've already seen several things present in it, like "BioShock", "Brazil",  "Animal Farm", "Schindler's List" and "The Matrix". The game starts with this warning that we're about to see some heavy stuff, and we should be prepared, but I didn't find the game to be so disturbing. It's not like you're going to see hard rated-M stuff, but there were moments that did make me feel part of the developers were vegan.The game also introduces some gameplay variation. To break from the routine of moving, interacting and platforming, there are moments that are genuinely amazing, such as the train ride, or humiliating, like the circus. There's this moment near the end that I will not spoil, but that makes the game substantially more interesting.All in all, I do observe the issues of this output. It's a dystopian drama that is also a game, not the other way around. But all things considered, I just cannot dislike it. It's engrossing, it's fair, it doesn't overstay its welcome (it's about 3 hours long in a first playthrough) and it accomplished in bringing me emotions. Not big emotions, but enough to make me impressed. It's a game that must be played in its own terms, and while it's rough around the edges, it can also be very rewarding.I would say there's a great game in "White Shadows", and you just need to have the patience to find it. It was a huge first step for Monokel; let's hope that, for their sophomore game, they'll improve over it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little torn on this one - White Shadows offers up a beautifully imaginative world, with emotive art direction and some incredible camera work. I hate to not recommend this game, as clearly a lot of work went into it but it unfortunately falls short in almost every other aspect:NO HDR!!! - Although the lighting has been artistically designed well, it has not been implemented (technically) very well at all. The game doesn't have HDR capabilities, which for a black and white story focused entirely on light and dark seems like a massive missed opportunity. The lack of HDR leaves the game feeling horribly washed out and I spent the whole time panicking that I was burning my screen in with all the unnecessary bright grey backgrounds. The light sources in the game disgustingly bleed into the surrounding areas, it's not pleasant at all.Story - nothing new or interesting - without spoiling it, it's all very surface level, well trodden ground, and even at that it's not fully fleshed out. The ending left me whelmed af. A lot of the environment flourishes are just lazy character and story beats literally spelled out for you. Platforming/Puzzle solving - again, nothing new or interesting. Some of the puzzles that could have had emotional heft were squandered, and if you're going to be a Limbo clone you'd think they'd want to put there own spin on some of the platforming, but they didn't.Performance - it runs respectably, but the player character and NPC's often jitter about for no reason.I feel like the developers genuinely tried to make a unique, fun experience here. _childDocuments_.review: For the first game of the developer, this is a good effort.Sadly, there were a couple of issues that really hampered my enjoyment to the point where I actually quit in chapter 5, probably close towards the ending. It was actually a funny situation: I had to stop playing to do some personal life stuff, right when I was in the middle of finally figuring out how to fly (because the game does not tell you its controls, at least not in-game..), so the game was paused mid-flight. When I came back half an hour later, I clicked the button instinctively to , but the cursor was actually on . As if the universe wanted to tell me something here... After cursing my impatience, I restarted the game, only to find out that the checkpoint system put me 10 minutes before the flight scene into one of the worst chase/run away sequences in the game where you have to jump-run away (not run, that's too slow, continuously jumping is the key), but take care not to fall into some holes. Of course I fell into those holes. Twice. And then I quit for good. It just wasn't worth it.As a German, I recognized the German-ness of the game immediately. Can we have our own LIMBO? Yes, we can, just not nearly as good. Can we have a spooky dystopian story? Yes, we can, just with a silly premise and a lot of "cleverly hidden" social commentary (because in Germany everything needs to be a commentary on real-life social struggles) that we will beat you over the head with continuously with the same message. Can we have 2D platformer gameplay? Yes, we can, just with floaty jumps, some imprecise collision detection and some painful checkpoints. Oh, and your controller won't work natively, so it's just using Steam controller mapping to keyboard controls, which may or may not be part of the control issues. And the worst of all? Instead of its own sound track, let's raid the classics and use songs where the copyright has expired decades ago. It's all so German, I wouldn't be surprised to hear that this game got an official sponsorship from some German Ministry of Awful Decisions because of its thrilling social commentary.Okay, enough ranting. It's probably not half as bad as I my description makes it seem, I am just frustrated that the game for me squandered its excellent premise and a couple of really novel ideas with an overall "safe and pedestrian" execution. I may have demanded too much from it. I just lost interest less than 2 hours of actual gameplay in and probably close to the ending. And because I paid 15 € for it a year or so ago. If you try it, do so when it is on 80% or more sale, as you only get abour 2-3 hours of gameplay out of it even if you like it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: White Shadows is the debut title of German developer Monokel. It is a cinematic platformer very much in the vein of INSIDE and especially LIMBO. It draws many elements from it's contemporaries, and is fairly short, but it's unique and striking sense of style, and thoughtful, well paced narrative make it a fascinating must play for fans of it's genre.In terms of gameplay, it's very simple and similar to most modern cinematic platformers. You run, jump, and interact with the world to solve puzzles and avoid hazards with simple controls. The physics are weighty, and help sell the physicality of the player character while still having a sense of control in the way the best cinematic platformers do. If there is one minor nitpick to the controls, it's that the ledge climbing can feel a smidge stiff. However it never gets in the way. To veterans of the genre the game may seem a tad easy, and the puzzles simple, but the sheer sense of STYLE makes up for it.The audio-visual aspect of the game is a treat. The visuals are all rendered in black and white, but it stands out by playing with light and shadow. The animation and character design are all very well done, with the player character's animation having small touches that add a bit more characterization that expected. Special mention has to go to the camera work. For a 2D platformer, it uses it's 3D environment well. The camera swings about with scene changes, zooms in and out and adds real depth to the world. However, all of that praise pales in comparison to the sound design. The world of White Shadows is a world of machines, vehicles, neon lights and electric dynamos. And it sounds gorgeous. From the patter of little feet against metal panels to the roar and squeal of trains zooming by, the soundscape is richly layered with industrial noise. There almost never seems to be a moment of silence in this world, yet the sound effects never become a painful cacophony. In fact, at several points, the sounds of industry seem to become a part of the soundtrack, like a great and terrible rhythm to an eternal machine. The soundtrack itself is mostly made up of classical pieces such as Blue Danube and Ride of the Valkyries, however the songs themselves fit the Metropolis-like silent film aesthetic of the game perfectly, and with the clatter of gears forming a percussive backing, it all feels engrossing.The narrative also deserves special mention. This section will remain spoiler free, at least to the best of my ability. Compared to most games like it, White Shadows has a much more straightforward narrative that only dips into surrealism right when it needs to. The world is a great underground city, with twisting pipes and grinding metal. The player will see the workings of this world with each new chapter, learning it's function and understanding the mega-structure they are in, but it isn't until later that a real goal beyond "survive and move forward" becomes clear. Partway through the game there is an exposition sequence that actually explains much of the world, which is somewhat unexpected, but it comes at just the right point to feel surprisingly cathartic, as it also gives the player a final concrete goal. It also hit's some occasionally heartfelt and bittersweet moments. It then ends up veering into the strange and unusual at the end, and still leaves much unexplained, but in this case leaving much up to interpretation is better than trying to answer every possible question.If there is one thing that will turn some away, it's the length. White Shadows is a short game, clocking in at around 2 to 2.5 hours. For some, this will be a deal breaker. However, I think it's short length is actually one of it's strengths. It works as a brisk, tightly paced experience that never gets mired in itself. There's no one gameplay mechanic or puzzle element that feels overused, and by the time any section get's stale, it switches gears to something new. It's short length also feels fitting for the narrative, which never feels bloated or confused. It's a great example of "All Killer, No Filler". And I am going to be watching the developer, Monokel for their next project.(This is the first steam review I've written in years, so pardon if it's long winded and full of formatting mistakes and strange wording.)

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag, but ultimately a very lovely little game.When I first saw this advertised years ago, it felt like a hanger-on to the sub-genre of "children in danger in a dark place" sidescrollers like Limbo, Inside, and Little Nightmares, and while it does owe a lot to those games, this does have its own particular flavor to it that makes it stand out.The depth of the backgrounds and variety of what is done in the world is unique and starkly beautiful at times, with the black and white giving a suitable noir meets Kafka decor to everything. The inspirations -- from Orwell to Kubrick to Bioshock -- are all present, and would have been better toned down into something wholly original instead of directly referenced, but do not greatly detract from the experience.The gorgeously realized visuals in a world of chiaroscuro contrast marry well with the classical music, though it did become tiresome hearing the same pieces I've heard used dozens of times in other works (though the use of Blue Danube during one sequence with mechanical arms got an amused laugh out of me). The platforming was simple and the puzzles also easy to figure out, with only one or two sections frustrating me due to timing issues.A demerit is its length, at under 3 hours, $20 is a hefty price to pay, and I feel it would have gotten more love at a more manageable $12 when it was released. Maybe look for a sale, or hell, just buy it to support indie devs so they can do more projects, as this one fell through the cracks when it was released.The ending....just kind of is? I was hoping for something more grand and evocative, but it seems like it just stops and leaves you very unfulfilled. There are a lot of themes in the game about scapegoating and oppression that marinate well with the overall aesthetic of dark and light contrasting, but I feel like it never fully realizes these efforts and instead gives you a sense of incompleteness.Nonetheless, this is absolutely worth your time and a playthrough, there are some really interesting and unique ideas and executions here, but they don't quite reach the heights of the games they aspire to be.

_childDocuments_.review: As you've no doubt realized this game is thoroughly in debt to Limbo, Inside, Little Nightmares etc. It has less puizzle solving and platforming and a pretty short play time (finished in well under 3 hours). That being said what it lacks in depth of gameplay it makes up for with great story and presentation. 8/10 would walk through the pretty world again.

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice accomplishment for a first game, and I might go a little further still. This was quite impressive, Yes, this might be a little derivative for those who know their literary history, but in these times the positive approximation might be that these themes are in dire need of a little homage for new generations, which might be less inclined to pick up the classics.Loved the visuals, and the puzzles were quite easy, but sometimes I just like a game to unfold itself and let me focus on the art and the effed-up themes on display. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard to find words to describe this game, i would say that it's as good as Limbo, as brutal as Little Nightmares, with an incredibly beautiful mix of suggestive graphics and music that feels old like a classic movie, and new at the same time. _childDocuments_.review: I played this as I was streaming to a friend and I kept praising this game for its eccentricity and surprising depth and parallels to our own world. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Overall the game was pretty alright. (I'll do my best not to put spoilers in)Is it worth buying at full price? Depends on what you look for in a game. If you are looking for harder puzzles, this is probably not it. However, if you are looking for a well thought out dystopian story then you're in for a treat. (It has much darker themes than I originally thought it would have so proceed with caution.) Disturbing in the best way :DThe graphics of the game were fitting though sometimes its hard to see your character with everything that's going on. I played with Ultra graphics on a 1920x1080 resolution. It made everything much clearer compared to the default starting settings. I play on a laptop and there were no frame issues with the settings being on "Ultra".The game has no "how to play" prompts during the start; If you've played platformers before, its pretty standard and easy to figure out - there is also a way to check on the Settings tab if you'd prefer. Most of the game is shown through actions, with very little dialogue. The dialogue that is provided comes in the form of advertisements and videos.The game itself is pretty short- at a casual pace including snack breaks it took a little over 3hours. Easy to finish in once sitting. While i was playing i didn't encounter any bugs and the game ran very smoothly, the only issue i did have was in the middle of Chapter 3 where i had to redo it. I made a blunder and died on a jump to a chained hook, when I was respawned i couldn't run at full speed because of the chicks swarming. I tried to get rid of them in different ways but i gave up and just restarted the chapter. (If you end up buying the game you'll see what what part i'm talking about.)-----Final thoughts,  In MY PERSONAL OPINION this game is enjoyable but "meh". I usually buy platformers for the puzzles and the ones White Shadow created were mostly straightforward (which is not a bad thing) with little difficulty.OBJECTIVELY, its well produced. It certainly goes above and beyond what it promises in terms of atmosphere and story.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I would have recommended this for fans of Limbo/Inside/Little Nightmares but there was a bug that stopped me from advancing. The last checkpoint was ages to go and I didn't want to play the same part again (it was the slowest part with least interaction) so I didn't finish the game. I watched the rest from YouTube.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: For such a short game, I don't regret any of the money I spent on it. $20 is a bit steep for 2 hours, but the game really does make up for it. It tells so much without a single line of dialog. When it does directly outline things, it does so in a very gut punching way.The story is strange and almost dream like as we move through a setting of a strict ethno-class based society. It does fall a little short in that it mainly shows the consequences of racism and xenophobia where as the people perpetuating it really do more so feel like part of the background with a few rare exceptions. There are a few moments (mainly when a phone is used) that leaves the lack of voice acting particularly noticeable.However, as it stands, as divorced from our own reality as this world might be, the imagery and sound design are spot on enough that I really wish they actually showed more of the world and the consequences of the Wolves' leadership. It feels like we got such a thin slice of this world and the ending leaves the probability of a sequel to be very slim.Expect to spend about 2.5 hours on this. More if you want to try and get 100% completion and, to be honest, this is the kind of game that's worth showing off to friends over a voice call.

_childDocuments_.review: White Shadows is a cinematic experience which can be easily recommended. The wonderful art direction, cinematography and sound design come together to create cohesive and visually stunning journey. So even though it doesn't emerge from the shadows of Limbo or Inside, White Shadows certainly comes to the light ... (7.5/10)

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm a fan of puzzle platformers, I'm not someone who feels that one should necessarily emulate other popular examples of the genre. Any complaints I make aren't about whether the game deviates from expectations but on things that affect the game's enjoyment.This game had all the ingredients to be something special. It had an interesting setting and aesthetic.  I was wiling to overlook that parts went beyond mere nods to Animal Farm. In the end, though, it's potential exceeded its results.  First, the game ran slowly. In areas where timing was essential I bottomed out the graphical settings to have a workable if muddied game. This is a real shame as the designs were certainly one of the highlights for me. It was occasionally buggy, including one checkpoint where I kept restoring midfall. I felt too much of the game (especially after chapter 3) was more an extended guided tour than a game with actions.  The exposition dump in the latter half needed more show less tell. Finally the plot itself -- and this may be something that I'm blindly missing -- seemed to have the trappings of deeper meaning without presenting anything beyond that which was already obvious in Animal Farm. I don't mind if a story is open-ended with multiple interpretations, but I'm struggling with one that makes sense from start to finish.I wish the makers of this game the best of luck, and if they make another game I will look it over; though I may decide whether to buy it based on others who play it before me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not much of a puzzle plattformer player, but I really enjoyed White Shadows. It's a short(ish) game, even though it took me 4+ hours to finish it. The scenery/world is beautifully dystophian, dark and detailed. The classical music fits the gameplay perfectly. I was also really impressed by the few changes of perspective during the game. The game deals with/reflects on real-life issues. So playing White Shadows was sometimes emotional and made me uncomfortable, worried, excited and sad at times. I look forward to more releases from Monokel.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: White Shadows isn't a perfect game but the developers deserve credit for the thoughtful work they put into this. I guess if you were to make a musical analogy, you might say that "Black and Blue" and "Tattoo You" by the Rolling Stones aren't classic masterpieces like "Beggar's Banquet" or "Exile on Main Street" but they still qualify as being quite good overall. The puzzles in White Shadows aren't too innovative--I can't think of anything here in terms of puzzles that I haven't already seen before in one game or another--but where it really excels is in the world building. This is simply a darkly fascinating, deeply layered world that looks almost like stop motion animation. There's a definite, exquisite sense of cinematography in this game. The old fashioned, classical soundtrack perfectly compliments the action and the story here. Speaking of the story, it's well done throughout--George Orwell's "Animal Farm" is an obvious influence--but I feel that it falters in the final chapter...the ending feels too abrupt and vague. It's feels almost as if they ran out of time and money and didn't provide the game with a well fleshed out ending to the story. Like I said initially, the game isn't perfect but it is a truly interesting piece of art and it's still well worth your time. The developers tried hard with this and deserve credit. Hopefully they do another project that's even better than this! 8 out of 10 stars. One of the ten best games I've played this year,

_childDocuments_.review: Step out of the cuckoo clock and into this monochromatic nightmare of twisting cables and bright signs of propaganda illuminating the world below. ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL.This game is an absolute treat. It is visually stunning with dynamic camera movements making the game feel more like a cinematic experience. I don't want to say a lot because one needs to simply experience this game and I highly recommend you do. Stop often. Look at everything and most of all, just enjoy this game. It isn't long, spanning only a couple of hours, but I am grateful I got even that long.Monokel came out with an absolute masterpiece for their first game, great job to all involved.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals totally sucked me into wanting to play this game. The theme of the game is for sure something we have seen before and Monokels take was beautifully done. The choice to make the game monochrome really helped bring out the stunning visual backdrops the game has and the parts of the game that had background music were such a perfect fit.Gameplay is pretty straightforward and very similar to games like Limbo, Little Nightmares and Inside to name a few. Things do open up as the game progresses with Ravengirl evolving along with the story.I very much look forward to what Monokel come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILERS) White shadows is great at conveying references to animal farm and the many abuses under a communist/fascist regime. Having a similar social hierarchy with the wolves being in charge like the corrupt pigs, the rats being like the guard dogs, the pigs as the common ignorant people, and with the birds being an analogy to the persecuted Jews under Hitler's leadership. Game-play wise, it was lacking, with the ending being anti-climatic. It felt more like a movie than an actual interactive puzzle game.  A show and tell approach may have been what the developers wanted, but I just wanted another Limbo experience!
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I thought this game was very good. A little rough around the edges, but i also understand that this was probably a very ambitious first game for this company.This game is very visually pleasing and interesting, although for what it holds visually, it lacks in gameplay. The movement is a bit clunky at times and the character feels a little bit floaty. There was no bugs to be found other than occasional stutters and objects clipping through each other during cutscenes. The game is a puzzle game, but also not really. Puzzles were not hard and could be solved with little effort, and dramatic scenes didn't feel tense. They were more leisurely which is why I am glad this game is short. The story was good and interesting, but also felt a little out of place or not cohesive. As a game is visual and atmospheric, it is supposed to be immersive. One thing that very much ruined that was the audio. Either repetitive, not really existing, or taking away or not adding much. The classical music is a good touch but did not fit in a lot of the scenes.Overall good game, I recommend it to anyone interested in these kind of games. Although the price is a little bit expensive for how short the game is, but i do not regret buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the setting and the dark creativity. The way the soundtrack goes along with the game is nice.Criticism: A lot of waiting. Certain scenes are super long for no reason and I understand this kind of thing can add suspense, but half the time it just felt like it could be moving a bit faster. The ending felt rushed, but that's only my opinion. Besides that, a very interesting game.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Visually impressive, soundtrack amazing, puzzles are mellow, story a bit heavy handed at times but it gets the point across. Plays more like Limbo than Little Nightmares, mostly walking around taking in the beautiful scenery than being thrown into any major peril. Ending  Could be good setup for a sequel or expansion but overall felt a bit lacking.I recommend it for my fellow platformer noobs, but wait for a VERY heavy sale, it is WAY too short to be $20.Impressive first game by the devs! Just would have liked to see more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game with a very dark atmosphere and gorgeous visuals!!!While it is a side-scroller with puzzles here and there, it is still a great story told mostly through the impressive visuals.I highly recommend that you experience it for yourself and not simply watch someone play through, since there are points where you feel your choices via gameplay that you can't get by simply watching.For a first game from an unknown studio this is a terrific piece of, dare I say, art!Do yourself a favor and grab a copy, you won't regret it ;)

name: Paradise Killer
detailed_description: Buzz About the Game An island outside of reality. A rogue human civilization hoping to resurrect dead alien gods. A murder behind locked doors. Paradise is an island that regenerates every few millennia. The psychic power that the alien worshipers within release into the universe is meant to feed and eventually resurrect their fallen deities. But this force also attracts undesired interest from demons, who eventually corrupt each island — until a new alternate reality is birthed by the Council. The system isn’t perfect, but it will be one day — on Perfect 25, the next island-to-be. But on the eve of rebirth, the Council is murdered and Paradise is killed. In the aftermath, the “investigation freak” Lady Love Dies is summoned from exile to find the culprit. This is the crime to end all crimes. What are the facts? What are the truths? Are they the same? Return to Paradise Island in this updated and enhanced version of Paradise Killer, featuring new music and new mysterious beings, additional quests and rewards, extra Starlight skins, and more collectibles to find, plus performance improvements, a HUDless mode and Steam achievements. A free update for all players, available now. Featuring DX12 support, ray tracing* (DX12 only), advanced upscaling (NVidia DLSS and AMD SR), and a host of other visual and performance updates, Paradise Island looks more stunning than ever! You are tasked with finding the killer and building an airtight case against them. Take your case to trial and argue your interpretation of the evidence. Only when someone is successfully convicted can the crime be considered solved and Paradise be saved. The “truth” is that there are many possible killers, and many ways to build a case. Even if you make a convincing case for prosecution and get someone convicted, is the mystery really solved? Paradise is an island set in an alternate future history filled with cryptic lore and even more mysteries. Examine bizarre relics to learn more about this world’s surreal history. You choose who to accuse, and build a case to support conviction. Everyone on Paradise has a secret to hide and something to gain. Old friends become new suspects, forcing you to choose between the evidence, the greater good and your own beliefs. There are many possible murderers, but who you pick will define your own personal truth. Let your personal computer and electronic assistant Starlight be your guide through another dance of an investigation. Collect evidence, record testimony and interpret the facts to form your own truth. Solve hieroglyph puzzles on ancient nightmare computers to discover new areas of the island, find concealed evidence and reveal terrifying secrets. Paradise Killer has a suite of accessibility options that allow you to tailor the game to suit your needs. *Raytracing requires a compatible NVidia RTX GPU, DirectX 12 and Windows 10 Build 1809. To play with Raytracing, please launch the game in DirectX 12 mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do games that have the vaporwave aesthetic, since they tend to be too chaotic to have a coherent story or plot, but to my surprise the vaporwave definitely fits in with the amazing narrative and history the game weaves. Paradise Killer was definitely a worthy purchase. I had so much fun exploring the game world, I could parkour everywhere and anywhere I could think to go, and the world felt open to me like no other game could even though the game world is pretty small. The graphics were *amazing*. Reflective surfaces reflected without any lag and the game world was overall breathtakingly beautiful. Exploring and going back and forth between characters never felt like a chore.With the plot the game made me feel very smart following up on leads. I overall love the ambiguity the game has with its narrative and the mystery that unfolds with it. I have been yearning for a game that weaves the truth as it goes, a game that doesn't have a 'canon' so to speak. I know I have heard people complaining about the ambiguity of it, but I absolutely love the game for it and its ingenuity.A big plus is that all the characters are either hot or aesthetically pleasing. Yes, even Shinji.So my thoughts in a summary: 10/10, wouldn't play again since I don't think this game has a lot of replayability (which honestly isn't a bad thing), but definitely would lose my memory and experience it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game. Aesthetics and music are on point, and I love the dedication to the vaporwave 80s style. The worldbuilding is weird and I love it.As others have said, the final trial is a bit less involved than I'd like, but it still at least felt a bit satisfying to see it all laid out after I collected all the evidence.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it, love everything so much but unfortunately not much to say that has not been said thousands of times in this review section. This game allows you to fully live in this world that is oh so different then our own without shattering the illusion with hours exposition, and just teases at the long and complex history that has left me begging for more. _childDocuments_.review: Among the best presentation of anything I've ever played. The game looks spectacular, and the music is especially phenomenal. Fascinating characters and world combined with said presentation work together to make Paradise Killer a joy to play through. My only real complaint aside from minor nitpicks is that, due to the game's open world nature, it is entirely possible to stumble upon game changing evidence far earlier than what was seemingly intended. _childDocuments_.review: I like it, it's weird. I've only played just under 3 hours of it, but I like it's style.Wow, you sure gotta like a lot of pink to play this game!It's completely weird and odd ball, and it's got it's own kind of charm and world. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece.  I do suffer from motion sickness while playing but this game is beautiful and has such a compelling story that, despite that, I can't stop playing.  The world is very open and meant to be explored to the fullest.  There's a dog you can pet.  There's ghosts you can appease to help them move on to the afterlife.  The world is full of lore and it's all so interesting and compelling to read about.  I have already told my friends all about this game and some took the step and also bought it.  To those who needed extra convincing, I needed only to show some screenshots of non-spoiler character interactions and that sold them. I need more people to play this so I can freak out about it with them!!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game on gamepass, but I loved it so damn much that I rebought it on steam just to review it. I don't think the story is particularly amazing. It's good, and has plenty of twists and turns, but it's not a game changer. However, the aesthetic, the music, the world, the lore... Those things are ALL game changers. This game is CRIMINALLY underrated. My favorite aspect by far is the world and the lore. It's so rich, like every inch of this game is teeming with such creativity, love, and artistic flourish. The game's characters are fine, they are deep enough to not hold the world design and lore back. It's still enjoyable to learn about the characters inner workings, their secrets, and interpersonal relations. I think Love Dies is one of the more compelling characters and I wish there was more about her. But the STAR of the show is the world. Cthulu-vaporwave, with just absolutely incredible lore. The island sequences, the syndicate, the "real world", the citizen's place in it all, it's hard not to spoil with how many cool things there are. I do wish they explored it more, because much of it is told through knick-knacks you find around the world. I love the item descriptions, they evoke such strong emotion... but I wish more of that was through mechanics of the game itself. Don't get this game for the story, or the characters. Get this game to VIBE. It just has such a strong aesthetic, while I want to spend more time there. I want to vacation there. But I don't ever want to live in Paradise. And that, in-and-of itself makes the world so very compelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review after finishing the Story. It took me about 14 hours to finish this game, although I must admit, that I was exploring the whole island and collecting collectibles that crossed me. I would say you can finish the main story of this game in about 7-10 hours, depending of how thorough you are searching for evidence. When first starting this game I was a bit confused about the whole idea of a syndicate trying to create the perfect island and how each island ended in mass slaughtering of citizens. Well there's a whole religious theme in this game, but nonetheless the further one plays the more you are curious about why the next sequence "Perfect 25" was overshadowed by murdering the whole syndicate council. Whosdunnit? You are called as the investigator from exile to find out who did it, interrogate the remaining people on the island (a few have already been moved to the next island), crack computer puzzles (which are fairly easy tbh) and find evidence for the murder of the council. At any point of the game you can go to the judge who called upon you to start the trial where you need to provide evidence. I must say I have not tried starting the trial right away (wouldnt make alot of sense for an investigator right?) but I was collecting every bit of information that I could find. There's a grand scheme in the murder of the council, it actually was surprisingly twisted, and I enjoyed playing this game alot. I actually enjoyed the vaporwave style of the game, the soundtrack is awesome and there's a little demon (Shinji) who I actually appreciated to much, I tried to get any conversation I could with him (he's roaming the free world in a few locations).I should mention there are about 3 or 4 side quests in this game from ghosts and a dog, but they were "nice to have" to me. They didn't add anything to the main plot nor did they feel like they rewarded you enough to finish them. They are probably added so the island does not feel too empty in some areas, which is fine by me. Can you bring justice to the murdered council? Can you help bring perfection to the next island "Perfect 25"? It is for you to find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game could be considered a pseudo-visual novel but there's so much more to it than that. It's a blend of many different things, so do yourself a favor and give it a shot.Man, if either one of vaporwave, its sub-genres, investigation, collecting stuff or just chilling on a tropical paradise could be considered more or less your thing, this game was made for you, let me tell you. It's unbelievably stylish, simply brimming with character. Takes a few minutes to get into, bit janky around the edges, but it's absolutely worth it. The music is bloody banging, and the more you explore the island the more enthralling it gets. The characters are pretty well written and the world is simply breath-taking.Additional notes:- A few parts of the game will be particularly hilarious if you speak Romanian- Shinji would absolutely have the pass irl- First time I thought an Unreal game was made in Unity
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The vaporwave whodunit - that's the perfect way to describe this game. Amazing music, fun style and interesting story. What else could you want? Maybe multiple ways to solve a mystery? Or a way to  anyone you want? Maybe some cute dog or a funny demon? Cause this game has it all.I had fun time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The best detective game I've ever played.Thrilling plot, weird and captivating universe and a great cunning female protagonist. It made me really nervous going to the trials. Moving through the island feels great after a couple hours.Maybe a little bit hand-guided, but feels incredibly pleasant to unravel the whole truth clue by clue.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An actual investigation game that lets you actually go around, gather clues and draw your own conclusions, eventually presenting them to form the truth you want to show. The plot is quite interesting and it has plenty of twists to make it all full of proper discovery. The music is damn fine and provides a great backdrop.The fast travel system actually using your limited blood crystals is very much unappreciated. If there was some renewable currency to use at this.... one might feel better. Also, NOTHING tells you that the foot baths are worth the cost. Some things are downright unintiuitive and you will need to throw yourself at them to get somewhere. Sometimes you might feel like you hit a brick wall when there is in fact more to see. The lore is downright bizarre at first, making one feel like they have been lost in a world that makes very little sense.Also, as a native Romanian, Akiko REALLY bothers me. I tend to kill my sound whenever she is talking simply because her randomly chosen swears shoved in dialogue feel like an insult. Also, her repertoire is so limited it gets jarring after a bit, especially since most of the time it does not make sense. But I can't afford to stop ALL the blurbs of speech from the others.Overall, flawed.... but GOOD.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: No danger or death, just investigation on an aesthetically beautiful and relaxing environment. It's a very relaxing game where exploration and willingness to explore and is important. Much of the island is empty but there's a reason for that and left behind are the keepsakes, mementos, and clues to the residence. You discover all that as you try to uncover a who committed a mass murder. I like really like this game's style and music, although there is little direction and having character get miffed you asked them about something on a whim can be annoying. Still I recommend it as a "before bed" game to unwind and relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Nani the hell?- All, and I mean all, of the characters are unique feeling and have a different chemistry with Lady LD as well as clear motives and even family trees and backgrounds that they are tied too. Very well written cast considering there is a lot of them- The actual case is unique and even though its more of a VN when it comes to investigation the investigating is pretty fun. Finding the clues and using them all in a big flashy trial at the end is a great format.- Oh God the OST is amazing, literally just wall to wall bangers.- The island has this weird vapourwave inspired look about it and I know that's gonna make some people roll their eyes but I honestly think this is one of the best applications I've ever seen this "aesthetic" used.- The dialogue is pretty funny at times especially when interacting with Doom Jazz and the vending machines.- I know its minor but I love the names in this game. Dr. Doom Jazz, Crimson Acid, Sam Daybreak. Idk I think they all sound cool.- Thank Christ there's a fast travel because the island is big and kind of daunting when you're released into it to explore and solve the case.- Did I mention the amazing OST?The Bad:- As mentioned before its not really an investigation game. More like a spot the evidence and have it explained to you game. I don't think this is a negative per se but don't come in expecting Ace Attorney or something.- The Nightmare Computer stuff is basically a waste of time. The same puzzle about 20 times.- One of the main pieces of evidence is literally in a hole in a mountain. Which is weirdly placed and the only case of bad game design.- This is a game which should have voice acting because the 4 lines every character has get repetitive very quickly (NERONICITO!)... except for Nani the hell of course.Massive thumbs up recommendation ignore the losers who say its not hard enough. Focus on the story and the pleasantly floaty platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like many others, I went into this game thinking it would be similar to Phoenix Wright or Danganronpa. However, these games are not similar at all. That's not a negative for the game itself I just thought I would bring it up since a lot of the other reviews are wrong when they compare those games with this one.For the game itself, it does have a lot of good things going for it. The art is beautiful, the music is fantastic, and the writing is stellar. The characters are very interesting but I wish I could talk to them more. I guess that just means I liked them but wanted to know more about them.The negatives are far more glaring. The game advertises itself on its open world which at first is really cool to see and you want to explore it all. However, when you actually start exploring you realize just how overwhelming the size of the island is. This is probably in part to the terrible map you're given that makes it super hard to navigate especially in the housing area. The game also hamfists this awful traversal gameplay into it. The geometry of the island is really bad and it's hard to know if you can climb a rock or not. This is a problem since the characters you need to talk to are so far spread out around the island that you have to constantly traverse the environment in order to talk to them. There's a lot of running back and forth between characters whether it's waiting to hang out with them again or to get one piece of evidence from one character and then running across the map to talk to another on what you just learned just to have to run back to that first character. It all felt more like a checklist rather than wanting to go talk to a character at a specific moment when I got a specific piece of evidence. I also got really sick of the blood gem popup every time I picked one up. Yeah it's a cool aesthetic for the splash screen and audio but after the 50th time seeing it I'm sick of it.Another issue is the detective gameplay. I mentioned not being like Phoenix Wright isn't a negative for this game but there is quite literally no detective working going on in this game. You're given a checklist of questions to ask characters depending on the other clues you have obtained and sometimes you can choose 1 of 2 responses to characters which I'm pretty sure don't actually make a difference other than what they reply with. This all leads into the trial which is really cool to see everything come together into one big event, but it takes literally no brain effort to do it. You're just given the choice on which character you want to prosecute for each crime and then just go through all the evidence one by one that you already obtained. There is no deductive reasoning in the trial. There's also no post-trial dialogue that changes depending on your actions in the trial. I understand the point of the trial is supposed to make up your own truth on what you believed happened so it's open to interpretation, but I was upset when the characters alive after the trial didn't have anything special to say about what had happened, especially if you end up deciding to kill one of their friends.I would recommend this game to people who just want a VN with a cool aesthetic, world building, and characters. If you're here for gameplay in an open world or big brain detective work and trial you've come to the wrong place.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: There's really nothing else like this. A detective game that essentially engages in no hand-holding. Beyond markers reminding you that you have new questions for the other characters, the game is perfectly willing to let you miss evidence that is absolutely material to the investigation. The structure of the trial at the end supports the open-ended nature of the investigation mechanics - you're free to accuse anyone of any of the committed crimes. The final sequence of the game is a bit less reactive than one might like, but the number of permutations that the trial can potentially take probably precluded characters reacting to some of the more informed choices the player can make about who to accuse. More games like this, please.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very on the fence with the game, but the mechanics ultimately tip the balance away from recommending it. Working out the mystery is fun to do on paper, or in your head, but the conclusion of all that work is a simple checklist from a judge to determine whether you've picked up enough collectables. There's no understanding check and no need for you to have been paying attention. If you walked everywhere and clicked everything, you will crack the case, even if you didn't read a shred of dialogue.And that's not really a murder investigation game. It's a collectable hunting game.A few red herrings (there aren't any) and a better ending sequence that tested the player's understanding of the case and allowed you to prosecute the trials would have totally made this experience. Instead, I just look back on it as a something I'll soon forget about, and wouldn't have gotten into had I known it for what it was.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it and it's pretty much just MYST without nonstop puzzles and instead collectables nonstop. The vaporwave setting is neat, but the whole crazy island-chain-immortal god lore is pretty much overhanded and overly complicated.Dialog is written well, but the game feels like a chore moving around the island. You get double jumps and speed dashs to unlock which help a tiny bit, but it's still feels like a slog.Ending, regardless if you get everything correct or not, feels very rushed and bland.Can't recommend it, which is weird because I normally love mystery games and have been listening to future funk for like ten years now. Way too much fluff lore with mumbo-jumbo that can be ignored for the most part. Puzzles that far too easy.It's pretty much a meh visual novel with Assassins Creed style collecting. Take it for what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a wonderful detective game in an interesting world. This game does an amazing job of making you feel like there are secrets around every corner, and makes you want to scour the map for every last one to make sure that you have your story straight through the twists and turns it takes you on.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to like this game, let alone love it. I found the graphics ugly, the character names silly and the initial plot hook bizarre. I am so, so glad I tried this out. The weird setting, the over the top characters, the insane world building all comes together in one solid neon vibe that just WORKS. I loved the free rein you are given to explore the island and discover a huge, complicated mess of characters and motives and history in a darkly funny and disturbing world. It's not really detective work, you're just finding the pieces of info and the game neatly packages it up for you. You're not performing logic leaps like in obra dinn or the golden idol, you are sifting through multiple and conflicting pieces of evidence and deciding which is true. It's this exploration that got me hooked, those moments of wonder and discovery that you can only experience once. Despite the complete difference in tone my experience playing Paradise Killer reminded me most of playing Outer Wilds. Outer Wilds was more awe and reflection though, Paradise Killer definately earned a few wtf.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer was a real surprise. I've been looking for a Detective Open World game for a long time and have found one of the most interesting games in recent years. The goal is to solve a murder and you can search the entire island at your own pace for clues, ask the residents of the island about the murder and slowly uncover an increasingly complex and much deeper story than what you initially suspected. At first it was a little difficult to find one's way into the world because it is very crazy and complex (alien gods ala lovecraft) but over time I understood and learned more and more how the world works. The soundtrack is an absolute killer, you can find various collectebels in the world which in turn enlarge the soundtrack. The island is mostly beautifully designed, but there are also a few corners that don't look so nice. My only real problem is that the way you move through the world has sometimes been a bit stiff.But still this game was one of the biggest surprises so far this year. Anyone looking for an excellent detective game with a brilliant story and good sountrack is at the right place here.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Mystery as a whole is extremely compelling. A supernatural murder where events could not possibly happen if they were confined to our own world had me interested from the start. Usually something of this caliber would be difficult to pull off since you can pull anything out of thin air and make it feel cheap. They avoided this by setting up all the players prior and ensured that you understood the capabilities of every being involved. I was engrossed for the first couple of hours. However...As a Mystery GAME, it's nothing more than moving through a large Hub getting from one NPC to the next and occasionally finding points of interest on the way. You are hardly piecing clues together, as the player character is doing this for you. Evidence does not need to be presented, just collected and the game will inform you of where you need to go next. Normally this would be okay if they left things up for interpretation and let things escalate during the Trial sequence where you put everything together and reveal a big conspiracy. "But that's exactly what happens!" you may say if you have played the game before, but all i did was click on the text prompts and let the character i was controlling do all the deducing for me. You merely have to accuse the right person and the game will take care of the rest for you. You cannot be wrong at any point other than the initial accusations during the trial, which are usually spelled out for you by the game if you found any amount of clues while investigating.Navigating around the map is tedious, it's exciting when you find clues initially but given the size of the map it becomes cumbersome rather quickly. Whilst fast travel exists, it's difficult to tell where you're actually going unless you really study the map and even so it still requires you to go through several time consuming menus. Platforming around the hub is awful even with all of the upgrades you can get as there's no way to alter your trajectory once you leave the ground. There are collectables scattered throughout the hub, but it is more tedious to collect these objects than it is enjoyable for the previously stated reasons. I appreciate how open the map is and how you can tackle the game in any order you wish, but I ultimately did not like its execution and would have preferred something more condensed.It actually pains me to not recommend this. It's oozing with style and I thoroughly enjoyed the setting and the characters. Although I enjoyed my time with it initially, that Paradise was killed rather quickly and that feeling was replaced with a general apathy (haha i put the title of the game in my review). If you enjoy walking simulators and want just a story I could see myself recommending this, but as a game about "Gathering Evidence and Interrogating suspects" I would give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and mystery! It takes some time to get into, the lore is a little different, but after about an hour you'll be locked in. There is a trial component to the game, but it's not like Danganronpa or Ace Attorney where you'll figure it out during the trial. You'll need to have it figured out before you head into the trial, which means you can accuse the wrong people. It's not quite on the same rails as other detective games, so execute justice how you see fit!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Great!Might have casually binged this game. Beautifully fabricated story, and a great ending. Would love to see a sequel with more real choices about how the game ends based on your investigation, and a little more mechanical nuance would be great. The concept and lore behind everything was fascinating. Overall, Definitely worth playing.Great music, funky art with clear artistic choices made that made it feel really unique, and lots of things to explore. Really interesting and riveting stuff! Compelling characters and some really exciting moments and twists. Really loved the additional range of accessibility features, that was a blessing after nearly being bed ridden after playing some other first person games that surprised me how nauseous I got. I would suggest adding an option related to strobing lights as well devs!Also enjoyed the use of voice lines. The game doesn't have a full voice over, and definitely reuses voice lines in non-directly matching lines, but I think it was done much better than a lot of games that do this. It's immersive but not distracting.The character motives felt reasonable for the environment, which I think can be tricky to nail in wild settings like this, so it was cool, and again, if this gets expanded upon, I'm really excited to see how the writing pans out!The game ran smoothly minus like specific issues I could count on one hand, and it had personally a perfect balance of graphics. Enough to make it stunning, pretty, and impactful, but simple enough that I didn't get distracted. Could definitely see more graphical variety adding to replay value, but for what it is, and what I paid, I really feel like I got exactly what I wanted out of it. That can be a lot to ask too lol.Downsides include some playthrough that ends up being somewhat linear in the long run with somewhat minimal margin for error if you just spend enough time which is a little different from what I expected at the beginning of the game and from the "open exploration" vibe. It had some buggy ladders (oh my god I probably spent a good 1-2% of my playthrough stuck trying to get to the top of a couple difficult ladders where I would just fall immediately back down) and a few spots you can just get stuck (which the 'respawn' seems to be a solution for). Also, limited character model variety in terms of representation* and in terms of character motion and expressiveness. It's a little odd that considering the massive effort that went into assets and lore for this game, that they didn't add a few more poses for character art or another character or two. I was also really hoping that more of the items that you can find hidden around the world would be of some consequence, but still fun to check them out.*spoiler:
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting setting and aesthetic.  The writing is solid.  As you play the game, the mystery unfolds pleasantly and I'll admit to being very surprised about what was going on at least a couple of times.  The Trial phase was not as involved as I was expecting but I guess I appreciate that things didn't get dragged out at the end when you've got all the evidence laid out in the open.I don't want to say that the game was too easy but I got every piece of evidence in the game without any issues (that's a lie, there was one puzzle that absolutely stumped me) and without ever feeling pressured.  Maybe an option for a time limit?  I dunno.Character audio interjections were very distracting.  I probably should have turned those down.  Kudos for the option.This game has NES Castlevania jumps and boy do they suck.  Do yourself a favor and treat yourself to the foot spas ASAP for some movement upgrades that aren't necessarily mandatory but are huge quality of life improvements.  Lastly, I felt nauseous almost the entire time I was playing and I don't really understand why.  I'm going to blame Shinji, but it probably isn't his fault.Lastly, but for realsies, A++ design on Crimson Acid.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Thought an open world detective game sounded a bit wonky but the atmosphere and character design was more than compelling enough to get me to give it a try. Game definitely takes a bit of getting used to when finding one's way around the island and trying to find hidden clues, but the overall mystery as presented is done very well, with lots of misleading clues that could cause you to misplace suspicions if your investigation is not as thorough as possible. Overall, well worth giving a look if you're into either the vibe or the mystery, and if you're into both, then it just might be one of the better games you pick up this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 9 hours in a row, and personally it was rather grating.The story feels a bit flat- Predictable, and the outcome is based purely on the player's investigative choices and skill. It feels as though, even though there is an outcome, it has no real standing on the plot or outcome- This game could certainly could have used a set of endings for each decision you made.The music does not fit the general 'vibe' of an Investigative game, making the game feel more like a grating sandbox, and while there is an 'in-world' reason for this, it would be much more preferred if the music gave off a vibe fitting the situation or game aesthetic.- Felt weird walking into a bloody room with really peppy pop/punk music playing.I understand the game is a sandbox game, and 'walking' and 'enjoying the environment' is a part of that, but for those who are purely invested in the story, punishing them by making the Fast Travel system cost currency is rather irritating at best.Which reminds me of the map system, which was vague- I would have preferred a detailed map I could have read directions on to a general location map.It feels like most of the content in this game is back and forth walking (teleporting if you explore enough), and your character being unable to ask someone about evidence relating to them unless you have a direct lead connecting them to that said evidence; also collecting random collectables. So, in all.Pros:- Good worldbuilding (The lore pickups and the backstory is great, the story itself is not.)- Good art style and voice acting.- Will give them props for some of their accessibility options.Cons:- Nondynamic storytelling that makes your choices feel rather moot, could have been more mixed.- Music does not fit genre, and can be repetitive and grating.- Fast travel shouldn't cost money, even if your game is about sandbox and exploration.- Bad UI, Map certainly could have been more intuitive.- Minigame quickly became repetitive, as did dialogue, talking, and walking.All in all, I can see WHY people would like this game- Don't get me wrong, it's a decent game, but it's not my cup of tea; but I also don't think it deserves all the hype it has and has been getting.If you decide to get this, do so with a grain of salt, or at least take into consideration that this game is an EXPLORATION SANDBOX game first, and everything else is mostly sidelined to that.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding work of worldbuilding that leverages the best of games as a storytelling medium. Though with some glaring flaws, such as the sparse world and large amounts of backtracking, the characters and deductive process really pulled me in.Don't spoil your own experience, stop reading reviews and get this full price. Can't wait to see the next work from Kaizen Games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy games like the Ace Attorney or the Danganronpa trilogies, then I highly recommend giving Paradise Killer a shot. From the beginning, you are thrown into a giant crime scene and left on your own to investigate and uncover the culprit. I enjoy how the game doesn't hold your hand and give you an easy trail to follow, and the way your collected evidence is organized makes it that much easier to keep track of everything. The game also has custom pacing in which you can end the investigating phase at any point and move on towards the end game. This allows for players to take in as much or as little as they want. I really appreciate not having time pass/being rushed towards a conclusion because you certainly need the time to reason through your evidence and notes.As for how the game looks and sounds? It's incredible. The aesthetic of the map really helps build the world around it and makes for just a really cool looking game. The soundtrack is just top-notch.  I'd say at least 2 of my in-game hours are from me just running around and jammin' out to those sweet, sweet tunes.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite have the words to describe Paradise Killer. It's a strange game, making me nostalgic though I'm not quite sure what for. The vast majority of the game is focused on exploring Island Sequence 24, the powerful Syndicate's attempt at creating Paradise, searching for clues to unravel the truth behind a murder. This is a slow process, but that's very much as intended - there's a lot to find, a lot to discover and a lot to piece together before you're able to present the truth and bring down justice.I don't want to get too deep into discussing the setting or particular characters here - IMO those are best discovered through play. I'd like instead to focus on the gameplay side. (Though brief shout out to our MC Lady Love Dies - badass of the highest order)Island Sequence 24 is an Open World - you can explore it freely, find whatever clues you can, and present the truth to the Judge whenever you feel its ready - while some events happen in sequence relative to each other, there's no firm plot for the majority of the game. This is extremely liberating and exciting - it's a classic setup for immersive gameplay and can lead in theory to some great, unique moments when you find a key discovery early. I was able to slip into a secret passage earlier than the game seemingly anticipated, and it was exhilarating to sneak along to the other side and find several key clues to pursue new angles on the crime.Further, I can't undersell the sheer enjoyment to be found in just exploring Island Sequence 24. The worldbuilding, combined with the environmental design, makes for one of the most memorable settings for a game I've seen in a long time. My first act in the game, after Judge had provided me with my briefing, was to pick a direction and keep walking. This place was as new to Lady Love Dies as it was to me - it really felt like I was in her shoes, learning what the Syndicate had been up to with her.However, I'm not entirely sold on this open world approach.The problem is that, while you can  go and report at any time, there's nothing really pushing you to risk an early accusation. Indeed the game discourages this; while it's not fully comprehensive, there is a quest log for your investigation that will alert you to potential leads. With no firm ticking clock, and a list of potential leads, the player is encouraged to be slow and methodical, to gather everything before trial. This can get really tedious, as the island is heavily stocked with collectables of various sorts, a large majority of which are simply currency. This is the sort of game intended to drive completionists mad. But  more fatal is the fact that this approach will leave you with very little need to actually think through your final answer. Once you reach the trial, if you took the time to gather all the evidence, almost everything is eminently clear. Only one point remains ambiguous, and that ambiguity is ultimately a moot point. It made the story ultimately de-escalate right at what felt like it was intended as the climax. It felt like this should've been a moment akin to Danganronpa or Ace Attorney at its best, with me in agony alongside Lady Love Dies about if the Judge will accept my findings. And instead... it was slow, laboured and the most distant I felt from the characters - I was that sure in my conclusions.I  recommend this game on grounds of aesthetic, story and for anyone interested in a fun new take on mystery games as a genre. But the investigative gameplay means I have to give a caveat to mystery fans - only go for this if you're okay knowing what went down before the climax. And not feeling too smart for working it out. (That said... this deserves awards so if you're in season for Steam Awards, get to nominating!)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like nothing I've ever played before. There are some elements of other games in here, but nothing quite describes this game well without expressing it is a Vaporwave Detective game. Every minute of my time playing the game I was just in awe of the world's unique design elements and the world building given by the artifacts and characters relaying information. The music is exactly what you'd expect with Vaporwave themes. A lot of comfortable jazzy 80's sounding music and you have the ability to create your own playlist of the music in game, which more games should allow that.The characters are mostly text based speaking, but do have some audio lines, though they aren't anything really to talk about. They sound unique and frankly I wish there were more of them, so I didn't hear the same 5/6 lines repeated over my playthrough. It doesn't necessarily detract from the experience, but I feel like they could've had at least more responses especially considering how dynamic the conversations can become based on what evidence you are speaking to them about. The characters are also vibrant and they each stand out against each other, so you never feel confused as to who you are talking about or to, even though they have some interesting names to say the least. They are 2D images in a 3D environment but somehow the aesthetic works really well for me. There are only so many characters to interact with and in game they mention the names of other ones who are not on the island anymore. I really wish this game had a random selection of the list of 18 characters, and offered multiple stories based on which characters were available in your story thereby giving it an immense amount of replay-ability. 90% of the collectibles you will find in this game are the currency used in the game Blood Crystals. There are littered everywhere, and I mean EVERYWHERE. You can unlock new movement abilities and a useful skill to help see where all collectibles are for a few seconds, but it has infinite uses. If you collect every single Blood Crystal you can use all of them needed for the entire game and have a surplus of 55. So do not feel afraid to use the fast travel system even though I rarely did. The other collectibles are Artifacts which give some interesting lore and information about the world you are in, but for the most part they did absolutely nothing. I would love it if there were more NPC's like the citizens looking for more of the items or asking questions regarding the in game lore to make it worthwhile having collected them all. There is no minimap and to be honest the in game map is not very useful minus the times you need to fast travel, since the names are fairly informative of where you want to go. At times I wished for some further mapping, but realistically there are so many unique landscapes and design elements that the more you walk around and explore, the better you'll feel about knowing your surroundings. Plus early on in the game, they give you the ability to hold a button to see the location of all major characters to talk to, which will come in handy. I should also mention that there is a respawn function in the game in case you get stuck or lost, it'll move you to a recent save station nearby. However, there are locations, since you can freely explore every inch of the island, where you can get stuck and the respawn function may not work. I only had this issue once, but it really reminded me that this game DOES NOT AUTOSAVE. Due to you having the ability to go anywhere and speak to anyone, the game asks you to save manually. Thankfully there are tons, and I mean tons, of save stations which also work as the fast travel locations. Overall, I loved this game from start to finish. I was streaming this game to a few friends of mine over the course of my playthrough and the details and exactly what happened on that day were so intriguing. The game makes a point early on, I believe before you even start the game if I recall correctly, that you are not given definitive answers. You are given pieces of a puzzle that fits together by deducing logically reasoning. You can prove the truth by your answers, you just need to be firm in your decision. At any time you can choose to end the game by going to Trial, but I urge everyone playing this to fully explore the island and learn every last detail you can. There are some things left to be desired, mainly the game offers nothing more than a single experience especially if you get the story correct, but that doesn't mean this game is bad. If you are a fan of detective games/novels and want to immerse yourself in one of the most bizarre worlds I've ever been put into, I highly recommend this game. You are doing yourself a disservice if you don't allow these developers to show you what a wild story they have in play for you.  8/10 Worth every penny I spent.

_childDocuments_.review: interesting character/story, unfortunately you spend 99% of the time running around in circles for hours. The exploration is not interesting because it is not challenging. You don't observe a situation and make deductions based on the actual environmental detail. Rather, you click on and collect neatly packaged "clues" that show up as glowing squares. The game becomes more an exercise of patience to walk along every square inch to find all of the clues. Further, the collected clues simply open up additional dialogue options. There is not much thought needed to complete the game, up until the very last scene where you finally can put the pieces together.To provide a counter example: In The Outer Wilds every clue gives you knowledge about how the world works. The player then has to use this understanding to figure out what to do next. The freedom of 3D exploration benefits this game as it is impossible to simply brute force your way. The player must actively engage with the clues and knowledge in order to progress. whereas in Paradise Killers, you can more or less ignore everything, and simply treat the game as one big fetch quest for the first few hours to collect all the clues and run back and forth between characters, before getting to the actually interesting part of piecing together the story.Unfortunately environments in Paradise Killers are not interesting to explore, and don't contribute to the investigation. There are few details in the actual 3D environment that area relevant. Many clues within single screen snapshots anyway, like in the Pheonix Wright games. In that series, clue collection can also be more or less brute forced collected by simply clicking on everything. However, you are limited to just a few screens, and it is fairly streamlined process to collect all the information you need. Paradise Killer feels like playing Phoenix Wright if every scene change required half an hour of walking to the next location, and another half an hour looking in every nook to make sure you didn't miss anything. Even moving between characters takes a very long time. Overall, I felt like there was potentially an interesting story to tell, but it just got bogged down by wasting the players time with hours and hours of tedious busy work slowing the actual story progression to a snails pace.

I have lukewarm feelings about the ending, while I liked the open-endedness and available ending choices, they didn't feel as impactful as I would have liked. It would have been nice to see the consequences of the choices you make, even if just in text form.Why I still recommend it: It's worth a play purely for the worldbuilding, storytelling, humour and aesthetics.Adorable Shinji and his quirky, thoughtful and at times deranged commentary is the best part of the game.
