_childDocuments_.review: I can't get enough of games that have mystery solving not just in their story, but also gameplay.Very reminiscent of Danganronpa.The world, the style and the soundtrack are amazing.The only bad things about the game, in my opinion, are a somewhat weak ending, and how much you have to walk from point A to B and back, searching for hidden items on a huge island.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration-heavy detective adventure that takes place in a bizarre world. Very odd, very cool.Exiled lead investigator of a disbanded Psycho-crimes unit is called upon to solve a gruesome mystery of mass homicide in paradise. Old friends that may have turned foes, old foes that may have turned even more bitter, and demons that may have turned… no, those just stayed what they are – all making things a lot more complex and, maybe, a bit nostalgic.  There’s only one god, but he is still weak, and the rest of the pyramids stand empty waiting for powerful inhabitants. The island is dying, but the new paradise is already built and brought to life. Someone is meticulously planning kidnapping of a fresh bunch of humans from real world – residents of the island aren’t going to service themselves, of course. And there is murderer on the loose – everything falls into place for an investigator Lady Love Dies to have a grand old time. Was any of that clear? Or was it “what the hell did I just read” moment? If it’s a second option - it’s quite alright. To explain original, multi-layered and quite peculiar universe of “Paradise Killer” would be a daunting task and, in some way, a disservice to the player, as discovering all the oddities and complexities is part of the fun. This is a game with a heavy narrative element (in a Danganronpa-ish sort of manner), and Lady Love Dies would be moving investigation forward as well as exploring through loads of dialogue , much of which will contain tons of info about the brand new (to the player) world. Considering this fact, the narration is done well and flows relatively smoothly, not counting almost total confusion about surroundings and works of the society in the first quarter of the game. Occasional necessary info dump and quirky character flight of fancy included, “Paradise Killer” has a solid writing element going, maybe not to be thoroughly questioned, but enough to intrigue a player, leading straight into a rather addictive gameplay.Gameplay that is, unusually for adventure games, is built on heavy exploration of the surroundings. As a lead investigator, not only does a player get to explore extensive and colorful areas of the strange island tracking clues but also traverse this world vertically - from the sewers up to the highest towers - finding secrets, blood crystals (currency of the island), all kinds of collectibles and quick words of wisdom from one particularly vulgar demon. The exploration can be done at player’s own pace and can be as thorough or as limited as one desires. Same could be said about the mystery at the center of the game. While search for “who and how”  doesn’t provide for any kind of deductive freedom and is being logged by Lady Love Dies in a fashion that doesn’t require much input from the player, how much is being discovered, brought to trial, and used there ( and in what way exactly) is entirely up to the player. It is possible to go to trial without discovering major plot twists and end up with a wrong conclusion. It is also possible to understand what happened quite clearly and yet put everyone through a grinder just because Lady LD felt like it that morning. This combination of free exploration and carefully doled out by the game mystery makes “Paradise Killer” all about the journey rather than destination. The ending might seem slightly anticlimactic, but the process of getting there, especially if the player’s into exploring, is fun and quite addictive.The graphic element is as peculiar as the rest of the game but will seem familiar to all the Dangaronpa players as yet another, at least a little inspired by that game, element. Strange and colorful cardboard cut-out character models with no animation stand out in the surrounding 3D heavily detailed and very complex world. While said characters are drawn with a big imagination and gusto, it’s the “world” that takes the prime spot as the main visual element. Everything from eerie, opulent temple full of sacrificial blood to strange futuristic factory and agriculture set-ups to diverse neighborhoods and then some - are highly creative, intriguing and rather breathtaking examples open for exploration. All this vivid variety full of thoughtful details and colors can be viewed under the clear, sunny sky or during romantic, deep sunset that slowly descents into dusk, as it’s possible to see the passage of time while investigating murder (it has no bearing on the investigation itself and seem to simply add to the mood and atmosphere).What else adds majorly to the mood and atmosphere? Music does. What a wonderful, part romantic part relaxing techno jazz mash-up “Paradise Killer” has going on! Something to notice from the very beginning and continue to marvel at throughout this rather lengthy game. Tracks changing based on the area of the city, becoming bit more bluesy and soothing next to calmer areas, and bit more dynamic when getting closer to dangerous zones. In general though, the jazzy, smooth vibe permeates the entire game and makes the exploration absolutely wholesome. There’s also some VO here – every character has a number of lines they repeat during the dialogue (hello again, Danganronpa) and whatever is present is done well, but ultimately, it’s just a softer, less noticeable support to a great soundtrack that dominates the game.“Paradise Killer” is an oddity. It’s a detective game based on exploration and finding clues, where detection itself is curated by the game, but exploration is 100% given to a player. It’s has wholly unique universe and lore, intriguing story and fantastic soundscape. Hours put into this game tracking perpetrator and finding secrets can end up being seriously addictive and fun. Sort of a game that might not be for everybody but that most adventure players would enjoy, if that makes any sense. Most of all though, despite gruesome happenings, the game is quite relaxing and strangely light-hearted. There’s nothing like looking at blood and gore during pink sunset listening to soft jazz and planning your next sexual encounter, and “Paradise Killer” is here to give everyone this opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What happens if you mix Big Danganronpa Energy with an aesthetic that’s two parts vaporwave and one-part occult esoterica, sprinkle in enough collectables to make Mario Odyssey blush and serve it all up in a glass of janky-but-surprisingly-endearing first person platforming?You get my surprise favorite game of 2020 so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game more than I thought I would. The art style was warm and upbeat which distracted from the serious tone of solving a mass murder. Story elements were reminiscent of a cross between death loop and the myst series. It's relatively short but in this case that could be a pro because it doesn't wear out it's welcome. Even hunting down the collectibles for evidence isn't that bad once you unlock meditate. The biggest con is that the in-game puzzles can be pretty basic and repetitive. Overall I'd give it a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: How would you like to solve a mystery wherein the answer is whatever you ultimately guess, played out with you as the only actor trudging about in a dead world inhabited by cardboard cutout characters and littered with randomly-scattered collectibles?When I read that the game, despite sporting the "Investigation" tag, isn't really a mystery game and leans more towards collect-a-thon, I was almost put off, but decided to give it a try anyway since it had such positive reception and looked like it might still be interesting.  The game certainly has a style to it, but it's not one that really appeals to me - the dialog is in that frenetic casual style that seems to be getting more and more popular in games, and the characters do that thing where they occasionally spew a soundbite that doesn't necessarily fit well with the current written line.  Visually it's all sharp contrasts and wild colours, with the character sprites dressed up in their best cosplay outfits, but graphically it's quite unimpressive other than the pretty nice draw distance (which is good enough to let you see the entire city from a high-up vantage point, which is cool).The gameplay seems to be mostly walking-simulator with a bit of frustrating jumping-puzzle tossed in - movement, especially jumping, is far from fluid, so I can't imagine enjoying the platforming aspect in this game.  Some of the collectibles are stashed away in cupboards or placed as part of the aforementioned platforming challenges, but for the majority of them, it seems as though they might've all been tossed in a sack and then upended to fall haphazardly about the environment, for all the thought that went into their placement.  The collection of these items - which, when claimed, treat you to a disjointed snippet of lore which the developers obviously hope you find intriguing - seems to make up the meat of the game.The story seems alright and is enough to inspire curiosity, though, at least for me, this was dampened by the knowledge that there is apparently no true solution to the mystery - according to what I've read, at least, the game is designed so that things will play out to completion regardless of what evidence you present and who you accuse.  The characters and their backstories are original, at least, and you have a bit of (ultimately meaningless?) choice in the dialog trees, but I didn't find myself very excited to learn more.  Regardless, I might've put in a bit more time and progressed a little further...But, then the soundbite "Nani the hell?" was uttered, so I headed off to leave a negative review as required.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game to be enthralling! The plot and mystery solving was a great deal of fun! The art work and music go together so wonderfully and finding new tapes was great. However, this game is not without its flaws. It's throws a lot at you when you start which I felt to be overwhelming. I found the island tedious to get around if you ran out of blood crystals and places like H.K's workplace, Camelina's, the counsel building, and the shrine not only hard to find but very difficult to find an entrance to. There were random places I would fall and have to respawn to get of which I found immensely annoying like pier at the Doc's place, I'd fall into the water and be respawned. Don't let this list of cons keep you from playing this game though, I really did enjoy playing it even though it frustrated me at times. It was a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game alot, i recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the finding information aspect of Outer Wilds and Return of the Obra Dinn, and also to any fans of Danganronpa because it had heavy comparisons in the story and vibe of the game. Although there is no replay value because it is hard to enjoy it a second time when you know the outcomes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting setting and the best detective game I ever played, with the player free to explore the entire island at your own pace. Interesting point is that you can start the final trial whenever you want, and the game just gives you a result depending on the evidence you have and who you choose to accuse, without grading you on your outcome being "right". It's up to you whether you are satisfied with what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this game checks several boxes of things I don't generally enjoy (Cthulu, Neon, Collectathon), I'm extremely satisfied with how it all came together. I didn't particularly come in with an expectation that I would actually like it, and I really really liked it. If you're on the fence, I strongly recommend taking a chance on it. The mystery element is EXTREMELY good.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I fail to find much to enjoy in Paradise Killer. The world is highly abstract and seems to operate on lots of moon logic, which feels at odds with its murder mystery setting; Right from the setup I had a bunch of questions about what exactly happened, and the story didn't provide a coherent explanation. Instead, it unleashes you onto this barren open world full of meaningless collectibles, where you have to slog your way around questioning people. Questioning them involves tedious menuing through dozens of options where the characters often just insult each other and nothing gets resolved. I found the dialogue presentation poor, with character sprites being way too small and awkwardly positioned on screen, loads of punctuation errors, and obnoxious regular choices that don't add to the conversation. Also, the characters constantly interject with canned voice lines that kept pulling me out of the writing. You might say having some voice lines is better than no voice lines, but this feels like a clear showcase of the problems with a halfway implementation.And that's about all I have to say. I love detective games, and I love visual novels, and yet this just did not do it for me on any level.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Every now and then I enjoy a game so much I feel indebted to return to it's store page and write a full review for it. Paradise Killer is such a game.I won't bother to explain the plot since it's so psychedelic and weird that grasping it fully in a paragraph or two is too hard to accomplish. Although it's lore is a bit odd (the whole game is a bit odd honestly) it's still very well written. It drips a strange sort of pop-funk, synthwave nectar that's intoxicatingly sweet. The art style and game's presentation is too good for this world. Good enough that they had to make another realty just to contain it. Music is very nice- only annoying thing is that music in the game is played from these large megaphones spread throughout the map so sometimes the music fades in and out as you're exploring. The entire presentation seems so Warhol-ish pop colorful jazz that even Lovecraft Cthulhu elements prevalent in the lore come off as more "space bop" "lo fi beats to relax/study to" than the actual horrors they are. For example the one demon in the game seems more of a pot head miscreant than he seems like an actual threat.Game is straight forward but not simple. You're tasked with solving a murder and all the characters on the island are suspects. Most of the game revolves around dialogue and interrogating suspects to glean different testimonies and accounts as to what happened during the murder. Gradually as you go along you rub out lies from truth and are left with one of the most ambitious crimes in all of human history: The killing of paradise itself. You can take your evidence and go to trial at any time but, obviously, the truth lies in the details and to get the full experience you naturally want to track down every lead you have to their conclusions before going to trial. Once you do start the trial, there's no going back. (unless you have a save then there is going back haha lol)There are a few complaints though. The map is huge and, although it doesn't look like it, extremely detailed. Every inch of it can be explored. However sometimes it gets a little  big. Towards the end of the game you start scrounging around the same empty areas you've been to dozens of times, searching for that one hidden secret. It's no big deal for people who just wanna play and go but for people who really love the game and want the full completionist ending, sometimes it can get tedious at the latter end of the game as you scour the entire island over and over for physical evidence. Not to even mention all the relics and lore items that are not immensely key to the plot, as well as the game's currency of blood crystals- which is also unlocked through exploration and is needed for several key items such as Starlight upgrades, double jump, and ability to see all the items on the map, etcetera.As a last and final complaint- the ending somewhat seems flat. There's a final trial but there's not much theatrics or conclusion at the end. I can't tell if that's because there's different kind of endings and I just happened to get the mundane one but I doubt it.At the end of the day though it was still quite a ride, and provided (in a full playthrough) at least 15 hours of good enjoyment for those who like a great mystery, great music, great art and great writing. It's a 9/10 and when i completed the game it left me aching for some sort of sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best-realised detective fantasies ever made, gorgeously presented with a very good cast of characters and an excellently conceived central mystery. It's not a perfect game, but these things aren't flaws! They're, uh, idiosyncrasies. It is almost aggressively quirky in a way that works for me about as often as it doesn't, and I think quite a few members of the cast are one-note, but it's a pleasant note so it works.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game, but only barely. Before I go into a full review, I want to give some tips that would have made this a more positive experience had I known ahead of time. Just a heads up, this is more of a collect-a-thon, than it is a detective game. If you intend to play: here are some spoiler-free pointers to give you a more positive experience.Anyways, on to the full review. Paradise Killer was a wildly mixed bag for me. I really wanted to love this game, but there are so many flaws in the nitty gritty that I was exhausted with the game in the final hours. But just to be clear: I will be closely watching this studio to see what they come up with next, because I think their next game will be great.- Music, without a shadow of a doubt. If the music weren't so great, I honestly might not have recommended this game due to everything else.- Aesthetic. Just look at the screenshots, its a really cool looking game.- Character Designs. Very unique characters that I will very much remember.- The playable world. It seems really overwhelming and huge at first, but as you play it starts to get more and more intimate, and by the end you really feel like you know it like the back of your hand. Very unique space, that I will have fond memories of. (Smaller things that I feel a mod or patch could fix):- Clunky Platforming. Your character cannot step over the tiniest bump, so you have to jump. The problem is that you cannot change direction once you are in the air. I think the overall clunkiness could have been fixed by allowing me to move forward just a little bit while jumping. In its current state however, if you wanna get over a 2 inch bump, you have to back up, get a running start and then jump. It sounds minor, but given 80% of the gameplay is just running around, these moments really add up.- Collectible pop-ups. For every single "Blood Crystal"/(currency) pick-up, a pop-up covers the entire screen, and you have to wait about a second before you can close it. You'll probably collect near 100 of these, so the constant interruption gets really annoying after a while.- Lack of being able to call someone. You get a phone call from one of the suspects early on in the game, confirming that phones exist in this universe. I really wish that I could call suspects, but maybe limit it to only one conversation. It just pads the game out when you find a "new break in the case", and thus you now have to go visit all 10 suspects and ask them about it, only for 8/10 of them to just say "IDK". I understand that witnesses are going to not know the answer or lie sometimes, but good lord it just adds so much pointless traversal, fast travel, and wasted time on the player's behalf. This alone could have trimmed at least an hour or two off of the playtime.- Fast Travel gets annoying. I appreciated the "in-universe" explanation for fast-travel at first, but I'll admit I got tired of the little dialogue/"scene" after the first dozen times. I wouldn't mind as much if the dialogue changed at all, but given how much you have to fast travel in this game, it eventually just got old and I mashed through it. - I wish Shinji's dialogue referenced your current location more often. Out of the 30-40 times I spoke with Shinji, only twice did he ever mention where we were physically. Otherwise it just felt like he was reading through a static list of vague observations.- I feel the lore was a bit over-written. They throw far too much in your face at first. And with how exotic all of the names for things are, it was just lore overload. I think the world is cool, but there's just too much that is explained that has absolutely nothing to do with what is going on. Some of the collectibles are just wildly uninteresting, and I really didn't care about the text that came with 80% of them.- The voice acting. I get that the game might not have had the budget to do full voice acting, but it does have some. Each character has half a dozen short lines that they repeat far too often. Usually while you are trying to read something that is not even close to what they said. It just gets really annoying after a while. Special shout out to the Grand Marshal's really poor voice acting in particular though. She was insufferable.- World devoid of life. Due to an investigation going on, I can understand everyone being "locked in their homes", but some characters were just hanging out outside. I wish there was a little more life on the island, because honestly it felt like I was just running through an empty world like a level designer would or something during development. The 2D PNGs representing the suspects in the world also did not help with this. - Also, the bar cutscenes didn't really do much for me.- You also don't really need to use your intuition much in this game. If you collect 80% of the evidence, your character kinda just deduces everything for you in the end without you having to think much.All in all, a very memorable game - albeit it one littered with clunky gameplay, and some frustrations that add up. I think the team will likely take feedback for PK into account, and make a pretty great 2nd game. I will be listening to the music for the foreseeable future, and picturing this cool world in my head.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant weird game. Go play it.I spent the first hour or so wandering around trying to figure out what the hell was going on. Islands? Gods? Relics? What is this bizarre place, why does all the text look like it came from a poorly translated PS2 game, WHY CAN'T I SAVE ANYWHERE? And then the genius of it just sorta... clicks.You're an investigator. Crime beckons. When all is done, only justice remains. What are the facts, and what is your truth?
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute hidden gem of a game with splendid atmosphere and gripping story.You're THE investigator, brought back to help shine the light of Justice on the crime to end all crimes. Do what you do best and snoop around the empty, dying island - reconnect with old friends, some the same, some unrecognisably changed. The gameplay consists of making your way around a liminal, odd island that's equal parts beautiful and eerie to collect hundreds of collectables, clues, upgrades and currency to make your investigation easier. Visit  suspects and improve your relationship to prod for details - it has been 3 million days after all, even your closest friends might need a bit to warm back up. Your sojourn on Dying 24 will in the constant company of a minor, harmless charmer of the demon that goes my Shinji. He always has insightful and fun input for Lady Love Dies, and is certainly one of the few things worth something in this twisted crucible of sin. Once you're satisfied with your investigating, you can begin the Trials! The cases you handle will depend on what you've uncovered and the people you  accuse, some might spill their gust knowing their lives are over, but they might still drag somebody else with them. How will you handle Justice? What are your facts, and can you weave them into a satisfying Truth? Will you follow the easy path out, or condemn only those you deem truly worthy of death? Or, perhaps, will you follow the rules and ensure anybody and everybody with but the most tenuous connection the the crimes you investigated are Justly punished? It is all in your hands,  Investigator!Enjoy this vaporwave inspired, liminal, lovely little experience chock full of pretty sights and boppin' tunes while you uncover conspiracies spanning decades - or just collect everything like a person-shaped crow and try to get in the pants of your sexier old friends, who can choose?
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most Grasshopper games not made by Grasshopper that I've played. Interesting, kind of messed up, world to explore with fun characters and nice music. Cool mystery that lets you find all the pieces yourself and has you judge yourself on whether you reached a satisfying conclusion without handing it to you. Cool game. Recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I dare to say that Paradise Killer revolutionizes murder mystery games. Being able to make your own deductions while investigating the open world environment, interviewing suspicious individuals and trying to come up with your own theories you must later prove to be right. Additionally, the world building is fully unique from anything I've ever seen. Only thing missing is a sequel, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What?! You never heard about most bizzare first person adventure game? You never heard about murder mystery involving gods, demonology and immortal people on artificial tropical paradise? Don't worry me neither until a week ago on this roller coaster.Now, now let's chill. This is cleverly written open world detective VN game that gives you WHOLE CONTROL over the course of story and charms you with it's beauty. It's your choice how will you start and end investigations. You have all influence on the story and it's hell of a twisted story so take care. Presented with artistic locations and insanity spiced with perfect music jams. Hours fly by when you spend time with different characters also antagonists and you just see more and more of this island. Part of the fun is exploring even if it all is confusing. Even though you run like headless chicken for most time talking to people observing days and nights in paradise, it is a good time once you know how to appreciate it.Once you get a grisp on this island madness it's P-E-R-F-E-C-T. And it's sort of a charm that you will remember for a long while. Go back for more until there is nothing left. Do I dare to say that Paradise Killer is designed as 10/10? Yes, because I still want to see other islands give me my perfect 25 th and let me "Stay Forever".
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The best visual novel I experienced. I played it immediately after Obra Dinn and the contrast in the aesthetics was super refreshing. The setting is completely surreal but despite this the world building is extremely well-done, so this crazy universe quickly starts to make sense for us.The good:+ The JoJo-esque colorful aesthetics+ The jazzy tracks+ Exploring the island freely+ Gradually piecing together your case file like a real inspector and understanding what happened feels very satisfying+ The freedom to accuse who you wantThe bad:- While everything plot-relevant is consistent with the universe, the optional collectibles, on the other hand, bring pieces of lore that feel completely random. I get that they're more about setting up an atmosphere than actual world building, but I feel like it harms all the aforementioned work that has been done to have a consistent universe.- The constant ringing of the phones used to save the game gets annoying fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game will probably be for you if you're a fan of first-person adventure/exploration games and other lightly directed narrative experiences, and you like games with a strong audiovisual aesthetic.I think it can be hard to get used to, but the fact that this game doesn't tell you whether you 'won' or 'got the right person' makes it uniquely rewarding and (if you're the right kind of person IMO) gives you a drive to learn as much as you can so you can come to the right decisions since it's your responsibility and your responsibility alone. It also gave me unique privileges in how I decided to pursue the trial which I won't go into much here because I don't want to spoil much, but it made me feel like I actually did something more than pick from a series of endings.I love the music, the little bits of flavour text dotted throughout the world, side characters you meet, and so on, it all contributes to the tone really well without feeling annoying or over-indulgent (the fact that they are typically just collectibles helps too - you can often choose whether you want to see them or when you want to.) You can feel a lot of genuine enthusiasm for the different aesthetic strands of influences in the game and I love that. Unlike a lot of other games with fantasy settings, it doesn't put it's lore on a pedestal, it recognises that it's in service of the story. It's nice to read a little one-sentence vignette about a god that makes the world feel more colourful and like a place, instead of trying to make you feel like you're decoding some sort of ultimate truth about the game world.If there's one thing I wish the game did better was explain to you how the trials worked, because I was confused as to how the normal gameplay of talking and gathering evidence would mechanically tie into the process of putting on a trial and how conversations in the trial would work. It was only until I tested the process of trials and went to the point of no return did I understand how the trial process worked.I'm also the kind of person who gets really motion sick at very specific 3D first-person games and this was unfortunately one of them, which was a real shame because I really wanted to be able to just hang out and soak in the lovely surreal environment but I couldn't really do that :(.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I always love a good mystery/whodunnit, so I was intrigued by this game. It combines a really vibey aesthetic and soundtrack, incredibly unique worldbuilding and eccentric characters to build an experience I still think about. It's really fun going around and unravelling the story, so if you like detective games it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So, up front, recommending this with a catch. I really enjoyed what it brought to the table, but it isn't quite what it advertises.It WILL give you a great setting, a clash of styles that I've taken to calling "Cthulhu vaporwave." Miami beach condos within view of walled-off sites of demonic destruction and temples of marble and gold where immortals make blood sacrifices to alien gods. The main draw of the game is to wander the island, bob your head to the future funk soundtrack, and enjoy the strange characters and stranger locations.It WON'T give you a deep investigative experience. Paradise Killer is much closer to a walking simulator than a game where you would actually need to solve mysteries. You can dig up information for your investigation for at least a dozen hours, but the reward is mostly the journey itself. You can end the search and begin the trial as soon as you have enough evidence to point a finger at anyone. The end result is of little consequence, and the trial itself is probably the least interesting part of the game even though it puts some finishing touches on what you found before then, but the journey is, in my opinion, enthralling.The other aspects of the game that you are better off knowing beforehand are regarding the collectibles. Blood crystals are the currency used for any exchanges:Secrets, purchased from a particular character, which can aid in your investigation.Drinks from vending machines, which are purely for lore if you want to know more.Foot baths, which, for whatever reason, give you powerups which make navigation significantly easier: one gives you the ability to see hidden objects, the other lets you double-jump. Neither of which you need, but are helpful.Drinks, purchased from another character, to allow you to have chats with them.And the fast travel system, both unlocking nodes as well as using them to travel between them. This is the part of the game that I think just flat-out sucks, since it encourages you to not use the conveniences you've earned, but since I finished the game with 40 crystals in my pocket and I'm sure I missed a few, I think you can be fairly liberal in your use of them to go to areas that you know will have new developments.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an... odd game. Its unique visual style will be immediately obvious, from the plastic looking 3D world to the 2D sprites for characters, and you may not love it right away. But trust me, it will grow on you. Another thing that will be immediately obvious is the odd controls. When you jump it's straight up and down, you can't move while in the air (ok, fair, that's realistic). Running feels very floaty, and jumping while running feels like you remain in the air for far too long, making the platforming aspect of the exploration difficult... at first... but there ARE upgrades you can find which make the movement much better so don't drop it just because it feels weird.The story is as unique and interesting as the visual style, the mystery kept me guessing until I was just about done, and the final resolution is both satisfying and complex.It's possible this game just clicks perfectly with me, but I feel like it's an experience anyone could benefit from. Give it a little time to get its hooks into you and you'll find that you've lost four hours to it without even realizing.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'M LITERALLY BEGGING YOU TO PLAY THIS GAME!! I have never made a review so enthusiastic but this game it legitimately amazing. The only slightly disappointing part is the epilogue, but the entire reason is because only you can decide if you made the right choices in the end, the characters won't weigh in on it for you. There's so much lore and so many details and characters are all amazing and exploring is so much fun, oh my god you have to play this game I hope there's a sequel, I loved it so much I seriously couldn't put it down.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The mystery keeps you on your toes until the end. really solid game for such a small studio. Now there are some minor points that knock a few points off this game for me:I personally find the Island to be WAY TOO BIG. Can't say I'm a fan of running around so much.Also most of the collectibles are absolutely useless, unless you're into meaningless lore. The blood stones on the other hand you pretty much NEED to collect if you stumble across them cause they fuel fast travel and you will fast travel, A LOT, unless you enjoy wasting your own time. While playing, you keep darting around between these characters, learning new information. You don't wanna walk the same, sometimes very convoluted path to reach the character you need 20 times or more. Also the distorted sound the collectibles make when you're near them is so annoying I felt like I wanted to pick them up just to get rid of the noise. Even though these might sound like a lot of negative criticisms, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. I'm looking forward to their future projects
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: "I'll grab a drink 'cos it's gonna take a while, To get a taste for the lie behind the smile"Straight-forward "detective", item collection game. But where this game really shines is the story & atmosphere! The characters and lore of this world are so deep and rich, you can't help but get absorbed. And the vaporwave synth soundtrack is amazing. It ties together the pop-like graphics of this beautiful, superficial environment with the hidden darkness of a brutal dystopia.It really is a shame that this game isn't more popular and widely known. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's an open-world Phoenix Wright with an art and world that Suda 51 would have made, but it actually makes sense.In Phoenix Wright, if you don't prove the Counselor was at the scene of a murder 10+ times, then he gets off scot free. In Paradise killer, so long as you have *enough* to prove beyond a reasonable doubt, it's fine.In Suda 51 games, the madman just jam packs all kinds of things for aesthetics and just ignores the rest of it. Meanwhile with Paradise Killer, *everything* is explained or at least there's an allusion that there's an inherent reason why. How does this person's car manage to get into weird places? Well, it just happens to *look* like a car but is really an advanced piece of machinery more akin to a spaceship.So it basically has the best of both of these, and fixes the problems that were often endemic to this. Best of all is, as a mystery game, *there's a genuine mystery to it.* The more you explore, the obvious solutions you find start to get turned on their heads and you find yourself with several plausible explanations, and it's on you to find what would be the most plausible, mostly by trying to investigate or discount certain theories.But, due to the open-world nature of the game, there are some new problems that the game introduces. In Phoenix Wright, sometimes you'll have severe pixel hunting issues. Here, you have *extremely* out of the way non-organic means of gathering pieces of evidence. This isn't inconsequential stuff either,
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: annoying visuals (graphics are straight from 2007), absolutely dead world, tones of texts (which isn't a bad thing by itself but not in this case), blunt characters, (they are even represented as a cardboard dummies), ducking load of objects to collect, but 95% of them has 0 relations to the world or story, idk... tried to love this game, but it absolutely didn't do that to me
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is what you you would get if Kojima made a Phoenix Wright game and dipped it in pure liquid Anime.The story has you investigating the murder of immortals. That is, in a world where strangely named immortals (Lady Love Dies, Dr. Doom Jazz, etc) regularly sacrifice mankind to their very real gods.By interest and/or strange fascination, the story will keep a firm grip as the game progresses.Which is good, because the gameplay mostly involves walking around and collecting things.The main gameplay is fairly boring. Most of the time you will be walking around the island collecting clues, money (blood crystals), and other collectibles.Occasionally, you will talk to NPCs which can reveal parts of the fascinating story and do some good world building, but usually are not very interesting, require you to have found the right clues, or need you to have talked to other NPCs about specific topics.TLDR: Not perfect, but interesting game.Get it on sale, if possible. Play it for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5 / 5.0Paradise killer is a first-person open world investigation game that revolves around solving a murder mystery. The game has a lot of character and style and it's undoubtedly influenced by the works of Suda 51/Grasshoper Manufacture in several aspects such as character designs, visual art direction, quirky stories/dialogues, and even audio effects. The world/island is very fun to explore and features collectibles and different places to explore and gather clues for your investigation. Interestingly enough, you can go to the final trial as soon/late as you want. The idea is to gather as many clues as possible to hone down on what characters are suspects and finally guilty but ultimately there is no right or wrong ending in terms on who's at fault; it all depends on your personal judgment and interpretation of how the case went based on the testimonials and clues you gathered. Overall, I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of Suda 51 works and are looking for a unique investigation/detective game thanks to its setting and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Played this mostly on Switch, but man this game is oozing with style and charm. Memorable characters, and an interesting story. I'm not quite finished with it, but I am intrigued by how so many people seem to have different motives, and it's up to you to decide which leads you want to pursue, and what you believe is the truth.Quite mysterious. I'm being somewhat vague, because it really is something worth experiencing without too much before knowledge.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game over 3 or so sessions and I absolutely adored it! The setting and lore, with it's aliens as gods and demons, weird alternate realities and magic/technology balance, gripped me right away, I wanted to know more. The music is absolutely great, especially if you love synthwave bops, it helped to give the island so much more character, especially in locations where the radio didn't work. Piecing together the mystery and everything that had happened on the island while interacting with the colourful and creatively designed characters was a fun ride and I enjoyed every second of it. The art in this game was also stunning - props to the character designer!I feel myself wanting more - I want more lore, to play around more and interact with the setting more; an open world mystery rpg style game in this setting, perhaps on Perfect 25, would honestly rock my world.The only thing I feel that let the game down was the finality of the end trial. I felt a little caught in some of the options and wanted to be able to save some characters from their fate because of their level of involvement.  Would also love to see achievements added to Steam, as I think I got everything but can't be certain.If you like detective games, synth/vaporwave, a mad mix of sci-fi and fantasy and fun characters I would highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A crazy, open world, detective game in a style that's best described as "a threesome between Danganronpa, Jojo and Phoenix Wright" Outstanding aesthetics and art direction. Great, inspired soundtrack. An open world mistery free for you to unravel at the pacing you want, disclosing itself as you chill out, free roam in the smartly crafted Paradise Island or talk to the interesting and quirky suspects and witnesses you'll meet. There's Lovecraftian horror to be found here, too (as you are investigating the murder of the heads of a cult - which you are a part of - whose goal is to bring back to life ancient dead gods from outer space), but beware: it's Lovecraftian horror completely revamped by the modern Vaporwave sensitivity affirmed today. Summarizing, last, but no least: this game is great and, more important thing, has reshaped the rules of detective games adapting them to an open world map, devoid of the usually hand driven narrative of this type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. My only lament is the lack of commas. Oh, the lack of commas! It has a flavor of Mario Odyssey in that everything is fun to climb and explore and you're likely to discover a strange collectible reward along the way. I don't remember if Mario Odyssey had fountains of blood.The writing, aside from the comma desert, is a delight. Hang on, I wrote this one down: "Blades that glimmer in the moonlight when held aloft the top of a conquered pyramid of sin are highly valued." First of all, after about 10 hours, that garbage starts to make in-game sense, and second, much of it is clever. That sentence there made me laugh out loud, because in this world, that is an accurate reflection of the ridiculous, immoral value system. Even though the open world means you'll stumble on clues in an order that is not predetermined, the nature and history of the world, the relationships between the characters, and the plot of the story unfolded gracefully. The highly technical, dreamy synthwave environment offers the player a handful of useful digital tools to enhance exploring and traversing, and these tools are not ignored by the narrative. I turned on the option to have each clue entered individually into the notebook, finding it easier to keep track of the many different stories being told if I immediately reread a one or two line summary of the new information. The notebook, Starlight, was a great menu tool after I acclimated. The map which you can see in the menu is mostly garbage, but the world is not difficult to traverse, except the darkness can get intense at times and the flashlight is fairly poor.It's a weird, subversive narrative that asks a little more of the player than the average game, and I appreciate how well this suits the mystery framing. I am not quite done with the story, but I already feel a deep satisfaction at the approach taken to discussing problems of class and power. I don't feel a sweeping finale is necessary for the game to have made its point about investing too much power and too many resources in a few egos.The music is what drew me to the game, randomly surfing game soundtracks from 2020, and I could not be happier. I had never heard of this game, but after about six tracks I jumped onto Steam. This is going to live in my memory as one of the best story-driven games I have ever played, and the successful blend of open world and traditional mystery investigation is really fun to play. I'm already talking it up to everyone I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mystery story dripping with atmosphere and aesthetic. I really enjoyed my time on Paradise 24. I like how open the island is, how free you are to explore and chat with the people on the island. I really like the cost for fast travel, it was great design decision so that, early on, you want to walk everywhere and by mid-game/late-game, you have enough currency to do as much travelling as you want. And the music is great, I enjoyed listening to the OST after my time with the game was done.The island is nicely detailed, but some places are sparsely populated and feel like they could have had some additional detail or items to look for. There are a lot of collectibles, which didn't mind since the game makes it pretty easy to track them down if you want. I thought the whiskey bottle interludes were pointless, they take you out of the game, and they could have been cut. One thing I did find odd was that the game world is static, characters do not move, and there is no penalty for just disclosing incriminating evidence to someone or by saying the wrong thing is a dialogue to someone. They will all hang out with you, even if they hate you. By the mid game, you'll be finding single pieces of evidence about someone and then immediately just going to them to ask them about it, to tie up loose ends, and they will still talk to you.It's hard to really talk about the mystery, I did find it had a satisfying conclusion, as well as a few good "Oh snap" moments along the way. Despite the game's marketing talking about "finding your truth" there is enough evidence to firmly discover the correct answer to the mystery. Two big flaws are a lack of probable suspects in some cases to really test your ability to reason and/or have the correct evidence. And that you don't need to apply the evidence is a logical way, you basically just dump it all and the game fits it together for you. I think a few more characters on the island could have helped obfuscate things a  bit more, as well as requiring the player to make a few more leaps in logic in fitting the pieces together. Finally, I do not agree with how the game handles the epilogue, I feel like they should have made the player own their choices during the trial and had a few different epilogues to handle some variation. We need more good detective games, bring on Paradise 25!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good.First hour was learning the premise of the game, it's mechanics and controls, and then you're thrown into investigating a mass murder. After that, I spent another 8 hours interrogating each suspect, and every character is really cool, except for Yuri and Akiko. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The city was cool. Getting around with Blood shards and stuff was quite annoying however, and it could've shaved down an hour or two of game play if you just had to unlock fast travel points instead of unlocking them and then paying to fast travel. The movement in this game is also kind of eh. Trying to jump over stuff was a pain sometimes, even with the double jump upgrade. The dark zone and Second Seal room were also very atmospheric and gave me a bit of anxiety going through them.The trial was satisfying. It didn't feel like I wasted my time majority of the evidence I presented. Although, it felt very simple to get the right verdicts if you spent the same amount of time as I did. The most interesting part of the trial was choosing which suspect is responsible for each case file, which I enjoyed even though there were at most three people to choose from.This game has mad potential, and if it got a DLC or expansion that involves the 25th Island, I would play it in a heartbeat.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for Vaporwave lovers!  Aesthetic is there, imagery, palette, retro-wave music etc.  Cast of characters is odd, and mostly compelling.  Pace is your own so it's a nice exploration game.Few gripes to be aware of:Some of the abilities to unlock that would be helpful early on, you have to find on your own and have the money to buy them when you find them.  The abilities could just be baked into the game, and it makes navigating easier.One of the abilities you have to turn on every 30 seconds for it to be meaningful if looking to find every secret.Quick travel shouldn't have a cost to use.  It makes players weary of using even though you will have plenty of currency to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating game lay, you actually get to feel like a detective as youre mainly left to make your own conclusions. The world is huge and beautiful which also also includescollectibles to hunt down throughout the game. Most riddles are fun to solve, besides the nightmare computers which I found very boring. Luckily they dont take long to get past. The one thing that really disappointed me though is the implementation of the final trials which felt mostly like dialogue to click through. I wasnt really doing anything any more and there was no way to fail. So, for me, Paradise Killer was 22.5 hours of mystery solving with a somewhat anticlimactic ending. Still, the characters (esp. Shingi) and the ingenious conspiracy story make up for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Its an open ended and open world investigation game where you pick up clues and testimonies and then come up with what you think happened at any point in your investigation. It's not as complex as other games similar to it but it's a good time nonetheless and has superb polish, visuals, and sound design.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I came into paradise killers with somewhat low expectations after picking it up in the humble bundle and giving it a go on whim, as visual novel type games aren't usually my thing. To say I was blown away would be a criminal understatement.It was a totally unique and refreshing experience that had me enthralled all the way through. It's been years since since I have played a game so captivated by the story and setting. Not only is the utterly bizarre world of paradise killer fascinating to explore and learn about, but the intertwined story of murder and conspiracy is gripping all the way through. The ending was great and it truly felt as if I had solved the case through exploration and detective work rather than being led there.The Visual style and soundtrack also leave nothing to be desired, both being exceptional in their own right. Add that on and I'm struggling to find faults with this masterpiece< and it makes me seriously excited to see what is next from Kaizen Game Works.I cannot recommend this incredible game enough, pick it up and give it a chance and I promise you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem. I never considered a combination of Lovecraftian and Vaporwave but this game makes it work. _childDocuments_.review: the vaporwave aesthetic is p good there's a lot of good music to collect the world is very pretty the puzzles aren't very hard as u can brute force all of them as they are simple switch puzzles and the starlight puzzles are almost all the same so you'll probably try a few times on your first attempt and remember the patterns for the rest of the locksthe trial tho is a little too brutal, some characters had no real reason to be judged that harshly due to their contribution being so minuscule 2 characters are written in such a way that you know they are guilty and i think it's a bit sad mostly for the most involved of the 2 as their reasoning in partaking was completely understandable and their finale judgment too harsh, which i think kinda ruins the mystery. i was hoping for a big plot twist for that chara but it never really came overhaul its a good game with an amazing world with great vibes that you're free to explore, most characters are interesting and i'd recommend giving it a go if you like the vaporwave aesthetic and or like murder mysteries
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer isn't perfect: some of the traversal and exploration becomes a little tedious towards the end (especially with the almost useless map you're given - you can't even zoom it in!), and at least one item requires an arbitrary trigger before you can collect it [despite the protagonist knowing what the item is before that trigger happens]. One or two mechanics are opaque before you try them [and you should try anything that costs money - there's more than enough to unlock everything], and the Trial system at the end felt like it could be more fleshed out......but these are mostly minor issues. On the positive side, Paradise Killer has a fantastic setting - well realised and internally consistent, whilst also being self-confident enough to be directly "weird" and cosmic horror in the "right" way [no lazy dependence on goo and tentacles - more unsettling weirdness beneath the surface of things, and manipulation and "blessing" of unknowable entities]. The central mystery has all of the twists -and banal evil - you'd want from a locked-room murder mystery [although it's short, perhaps, one final twist], and mostly holds together because of the host of larger-than-life characters. (although, it isn't a spoiler to say that, as in most murder mysteries, no-one comes out of things looking perfect - everyone has some kind of secret).And, of course, the music and visual presentation is excellent. Most importantly, Paradise Killer knows it doesn't need to stick around longer than necessary: I finished [and I think, got all the possible evidence] in about 20 hours, and that's as long as the game needs. More games should know not to stick around too long, and this should be rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: this is what indie games are all about. its experimental, it prioritises art direction over blind realism, and it isn't interested in wasting your time (yeah there's some backtracking to get all the testimonies, but that's what fast travels for). its not without problems, the platforming is a little stiff (but not strictly necessary) and some of the evidence is a little too well hidden (that's what meditation's for) but its heavily outweighed by all the positives. do yourself a favour and pick this game up if it looks or sounds even remotely interesting, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of those detective games where you feel like doing actual detective work. In this game you are given a case near the start, which you to solve in the island to complete the game. If you are confident enough with your investigation, you can also start the trial anytime and finish the game. If not then can keep collecting every evidence after following all the leads which will give you almost full story of the murder case.Exploring the island was pretty much fun, and movement was fluid. Conversations are well designed and explains much of the things happening well. Though, single line repeating dialogues feel annoying, as 99% of time the random dialogues doesn't mean anything close to real dialogue in text.The ending was kind of satisfying. Though going with flow I couldn't punish everyone I wanted to, so, it could have been designed better.Overall, the games feels very unique and gives a great detective experience. Recommended. 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a little weird. It's a detective game about talking to suspects and uncovering secrets, sure, but it's also a 3D platformer collectathon with an unlockable double-jump and air-dash. It also takes place in a slightly bonkers setting that will take a while to fully understand, but I ultimately found very compelling. On top of all that, I think the sexy goat lady wants to sleep with me? I thought I was a respectable lady, but now I'm not so sure... What I'm trying to say is, you've got to meet the game on its level. I got a lot out of it and by the end was fully hooked by the mystery, characters, and aesthetics. But, know what you're getting yourself in for, I can imagine a lot of people bouncing off of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A cool combination of a murder mystery visual novel and an explorey, first-person platformer, set in a psychedelic, glamorous, otherworldly paradise gone wrong. Feels like an avant-garde itch.io game on TONS of steroids, in the best possible way.My only criticism is that the game is badly in need of a map; there's one in-game but it looks like a joke that was drawn in MS Paint (which doesn't match the rest of the game at all), and I was perpetually lost and trying to find places I'd already been multiple times. This is alleviated somewhat by a feature that shows you the direction and distance of the characters, but doesn't help when trying to solve puzzles or navigate to a specific area or building.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting a short, little indie game that I might open once or twice and then forget about it. I was wrong. There is clearly a ton of passion behind the game, and so much more content than I expected, especially for the price, and I'm probably not even halfway through. The game doesn't have AAA visuals, but has a surprisingly complex and compelling story that I cannot get enough of. The gameplay is hard to describe, but feels almost like a mixture of just about everything, and it works. I've been trapped at home with flickering power due to the recent storms in Texas, and honestly, all I've thought about was this game. It's easily one of my favorites now, and certainly enough for me to write my first game review, ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the gameplay, the graphics and how it plays, however it feels like theirs too many useless collectables and the game completely flops the ending, well "ending".Their is no canon ending, its just whatever you decide at the end, with no validation that you got anything right. This is even emphasised with the Achievement "Accelerated Justice: Speedrun the game and complete it in under 10 minutes".I think you should try out this game if you are interested however, you shouldn't expect a satisfying ending unlike games such as Phoenix Wright or Danganronpa series.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game, kept a notepad with me and by the end it became a journal that looked like ramblings of some cultist fanatic. overwhelming at first but everything slowly falls into place.At times it can feel repetitive and I walked away to do something else but the mystery slowly seeped in, distracting me from whatever I was doing; I couldn't stop thinking about the case! These times where I wasn't playing the game were arguably the most immersive and it was at these times where I came to some groundbreaking theories that would bring me running back to the computer to follow the leads.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I love it!In terms of mechanics, this game isn't great: mostly you ask each NPC every dialogue option and you pick up every object you can (in case it's useful). However, in terms of mood, setting, worldbuilding, distinctive looks, dark humour, this game is fantastic. The story is pretty good, there were plenty of twists and nobody is above suspicion until the end.I rarely ever return to a game, but I think I'll probably replay this in a few years. I would heartily recommend it to anyone who is happy to play a game more for the experience and as a piece of media than as a challenge or for the mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute vibe. + The art is excellent+ The UI is so stylish+ Music is excellent, very Japanese/vapourwave aesthetic and just chill as hell+ The collectables, I 100%d everything. It's that addictive because it all ties in to:+ The lore of the island. The openness is fantastic in this, it's kinda like Return to Obra Dinn in its investigative options but I wasn't hooked like this with Obra Dinn. It's just so fun and mysterious and conspiratorial and yeah just LOTS to uncover and learn about your initial crime then the inhabitants then the island and history itself. _childDocuments_.review: Idk. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: not for everyone, and thats ok. Journey before destination, and what a journey this was. While there is a "truth" to be found on the island about the events that took place the night before, what really matters is what you can prove. I spent about 8 hours collecting all the evidence and piecing together what happened on this vaporwave [paradise/hellscape] and another hour or so deciding my truth. Was Justice served? Was Truth extolled? Did I condemn any Innocents, or spare any Guilty parties? How gray can black and white get? And while after collecting everything and piecing it all together the trial was much less of a "gotcha" moment type of deal than, say, Phoenix Wright, having to conclude Sequence 24 with the trial felt right. And theres definitely something about a group of objectively evil cultists playing at Justice in their own private heaven that really strikes you, even if the investigation phase felt like the better part of the game to me.At the end of the day, If you think you'll like it from the trailers and the basic premise, you probably will, and if not, that's fine. Aesthetic, music, plot all excel if you vibe with them. I loved it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's like someone made a non-linear Danganronpa game and threw in some collectathon elements + vaporwave and cosmic space-gods. Enjoyed the game most of the time and would gladly recommend it to anyone interested in playing a detective. Also a really good value for money since I invested about 20 hours in it. Definitely worth the time.That being said, there are some issues. The world is big and it takes a lot of time to navigate from one place to another, especially in the almost maze-like city. There is a fast-travel system, but it costs in-game money and I found it inconvenient altogether cause you can only travel to specific points on the map. This wouldn't be a problem, but there is a lot of back-and-forth running in the game, because every time you get a new clue, you get new dialogue options with one or multiple suspects. This is especially irritating when you discover a major alibi-breaking evidence and want to corner someone with it, travel across the map, and then all they have to say is something like "So what?". And that's it.Another weird and somewhat annoying design choice has to do with doors. There are a few special rooms in the game that you can access by opening a pink door in the game world. For some reason though, some of these doors are placed in locations that make absolutely no sense. For example, a random office door on the side of a building above a thousand mile abyss, accessible only by hugging the wall on a narrow ledge. I stumbled upon a lot of these by mere accident, not because I actually noticed them and decided to investigate.The final thing that bugged me a little was that I was kinda confused about how the endgame trial would actually play out once I reached that point in the game. Because of this, I wanted to exhaust every dialogue option and gather everything from the world just be sure I had everything I needed, cause I had no idea what I was expected to do in the trial. This kind of uncertainty felt a bit counterproductive to the "free-form" investigation the game wanted me to conduct.+ Interesting concept+ Soundtrack+ World building+ A E S T H E T I C S- Constant back and forth running- Poor fast travel system- Weird placement of some doors and evidence which you might or might not stumble upon by accident.- Unclear endgame requirements.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Unique artstyle, gorgeous soundtrack, interesting premise, and solid writing. While some of the text could have used editing (mostly with misplaced or omitted punctuation), the overall narrative flow is barely affected. The characters feel distinct from one another, and the story is engaging. The actual gameplay is somewhat sparse, only having a few puzzles and platforming sections, but it's easy to forget when you get absorbed into the story.This is one of the most unique experiences I've ever had with a video game. I struggled to describe it to my friends, as I struggle to do so here, but I can easily find the words to recommend this game.It's a beautifully illustrated investigation with an amazing soundtrack to accompany you on your interrogations of the interesting and unique citizens of Island 24. The story is riveting (though a bit confusing at first), and nothing is as it seems. Your investigations will show you how little of what you see can be trusted.I found the philosophical undertones engaging as the game grappled with deep universal questions such as "What purpose do we serve? How do we find meaning? Do you need to go to the bathroom in an eternal paradise?"Yes, this game even has a sense of humor.I highly recommend this game. It's relatively short (~15 hours for me, and I completed essentially everything) and incredibly engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Is it great? No.Is it good? Maybe?Is it bad? No.Paradise killer has a great soundtrack that melts into the background. The voice acting and characters are pretty bad, and the "mystery" is more exploration than figuring out a killer (like Phoenix Wright of Daganronpa).In all, I found the game more tedious than fun, although I did play to the end--so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game lives rent free in a my head far after I beat it, which only took me around 10 hours. Having never played any other games in this genre, I wasn't sure I would like it. I really  like it it turns out. Others have covered game play (lots of fun too) way more in depth, but the entire cosmological horror, utopia vs dystopia, and caste of humans that  on top of the bright colors and chill vaporwave are such a juxtaposition.  The music is really great!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like the lovechild of a visual novel and murder mystery RPG, and I found the puzzles to be just the right level of challenge for me. The visuals are stunning and the world is huge and bursting with stuff to do. For the first hour or so, I was really confused with the lore and wacky character names and I got lost finding my way around because it’s that huge! Once you familiarise yourself with it though, that’s where it gets less tedious and more fun. Likes:I enjoyed the mixture of 2D art against the open world concept, it felt really fresh.The hacking challenges were fun for me, would have been better if it got harder as we processed.Shinji is adorable and I look forward to hunting him down.Even the seemingly insignificant interaction contributed greatly to helping you advance. Lady LD is bisexual? Yes please! The collectibles made running around so much more enjoyable, kinda upset that there’s no achievements.I liked the trials, finally presenting my evidences and they aren’t able to refute any of if, very gleeful since you’ll already know whodunit once you gather the evidences. If there's one thing I could change, I'd add the option to Dislikes:The map could be improved — you’re unable to see where the characters are at and before you memorised the area, you just have to pray that you remember the way back; was confusing at first since the open exploration area was big. Would be better if the background changes with each unlocked safe points so it’s easier to tell where exactly it is. Some of the mini challenges required more effort in return for some blood points — I felt disappointed that I did all that for nothing! The unsorted evidence  was a great help but eventually it encouraged you to be lazy as they dish out helpful questions to aid your hunt and you can just turn your brain off.All in all, if you like a stunning open world murder mystery with easy-medium difficulty, this is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly, this is one of the best murder mystery games out there. The general aesthetic is.... special, as you can see from the screenshots, and I was a little doubtful going in, but it's grown on me a lot. Every single person had distinctive and complex character development, the world building is immense and very original, and the case itself is really complicated but holds really well together once you've found all the evidence. I always felt very engaged in solving the mystery, even if the infodump at the beginning could be a little overwhelming at first.A few minor pitfalls: Something about the movement made me slightly seasick at times. Also, some of the most crucial pieces of evidence can only be found by randomly stumbling around the island, and I don't recommend starting the trial until all leads have been cleared and all evidence is collected, as every single piece counts.Finally, going back and forth between different people can get tiring near the end once you've explored everything else, I recommend using fast travel liberally. Still, strong recommend from me, this was a very creative and memorable experience

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored the aesthetic of this game.  As soon as I entered, I knew the vibes were just my style.  I was however a little disappointed in the overall gameplay, in particular the trial.  I enjoy games like Danganronpa where you investigate and then put together your case for the trial, but here it almost felt like my input wasn't needed, and the outcome was pretty much the same regardless of what I said. Slowing the camera down was helpful but didn't entirely eliminate the issue.  So just a heads up.So overall I would recommend based on the vibes and characters, but there's a few drawbacks as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a captivating first person adventure mystery wherein the player, as investigator Lady Love Dies, a long time exile from the Syndicate, must discover the facts of the murder of the ruling Council, interviewing suspects, inspecting crime scenes and searching for clues in a somewhat familiar yet alien world. The world has its own mythos, religious belief and system (involving mass kidnapping and murder), but it doesn't take long for a new player to be brought up to speed regarding the happenings in this world. Nor does it feel awkward to build on the relationship that Lady Love Dies has with the suspects on the island (since after all, she was their friend before she was exiled a thousand years ago). There are some tools to help you investigate, although getting jumping abilities from footbaths and unlocking computer systems by buying soft drinks from vending machines might be rather stretchy even for a traditional point and click adventure game. However, the charm of the narrative, as well as the multiple layers and complex relationships between characters and their motivations means that there is plenty to investigate and keep one occupied. It is likely this game will be good for perhaps a couple of playthroughs, if at least only to see other potential trial results. While the graphics are relatively bare, the color scheme is attractive, save for the harshness of the prison island, and while the two dimensional cut outs made to represent the suspects looks like it came from a pixel game twenty five years ago, it is functional, and the art work used for character portraits and illustrations is adequate. Sound is excellent, with a slightly incongruous pop beat as you investigate demons and murder, but it works. The limited speaking dialogue serves to move the story along, even if you still have to read the actual dialogue boxes to understand the plot. Gameplay is serviceable, and proves that the old adventure game format of the past can be replaced by a first person view. Don't expect a lot of inventory puzzles, though - although there are a few, they are not complicated nor do they even require you to open your inventory! The emphasis is really in the data gathering, especially interviews and crime scene investigations. While it is a short game overall, I did find it very enjoyable and look forward to playing similar games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a good game, albeit one with some deep flaws and that has some difficulty establishing its own identity. It's a crime VN/platformer that's heavily inspired by Suda51's "Kill the Past" trilogy with vaporwave stuff slapped on top of it.The idea is that it's a completely open-world, non-linear detective game. The only thing set in stone is that there's going to be a trial at the end. The game more or less throws you into a world that doesn't make sense and asks you to make sense of it: the gist is that the world is an alternate reality that relies on the mass sacrifice of people kidnapped from the real world to exist. Here's my main problem with this game. Because of its open-world, non-linear format, it is entirely possible that you will stumble upon the solution to more or less all of the mysteries on the island before you actually finish even unlocking the crime scene. There's a single room that basically answers all of the questions, and I managed to find it after a few hours of wandering around - I fell off a platform with an NPC on it and as soon as I examined it I had basically sequence broken the game.The one good thing is that even finding the magic evidence room won't get you everything you need to truly finish the game, but at the same time answering all the questions involves a lot of boring stuff like spending time with every single NPC outside of just interrogating them, and none of the NPCs were really interesting enough that I felt like doing that.Another problem I have is that the game doesn't really adapt based on what order you find things in. As an example, one of the sidequests you get early on involves finding a missing person. I found that person's dead body just by wandering around before finding anything else related to them (as their house is very out of the way), but nothing in the game seemed to acknowledge that I found the body: every dialog I could initiate about it acted like I hadn't found anything. Going with that, it also suffers a bit from the same problem the Ace Attorney games have, where you know exactly what happened but the game won't let you say it.I'd say if you're going to play this game, stick strictly to doing what the game's "notes" screen tells you to do so you don't wind up sequence breaking the entire thing. That might be kind of hard, given that the game doesn't really have a map and some locations can be kind of hard to find unless you know where you're going already: I think if they added a map it would definitely help with that. It's definitely not a bad game, but it could use some work.
