_childDocuments_.review: My relationship with this game is complicated.On one hand, much of the game feels cobbled together, with parts of it seeming to be very nicely polished and yet others mysteriously held over from a time when I presume the game was much earlier in development. It's hard to pinpoint exactly which parts of the game were calculated sacrifices and which were developmental oversights. For instance there is a flashlight icon with the keybinding to toggle it on and off glued to the bottom right corner of the screen and yet I have absolutely no idea in what situation it would serve you to have a flashlight. There is a day and night cycle and yet the concept of time in the game is extraneous. The free roaming and platforming aspects of the game seem to provide no real value to the core gameplay experience (which like many games in the mystery genre is essentially a virtual novel with light evidence collecting mechanics) because the majority of the scattered puzzles in the game serve only to provide you with currency rather than to provide opportunities to freely gather evidence and examine crime scenes. The currency itself after a few hours into the game loses much of its function, changing from a means to gain upgrades to your personal computer and to buy information, to merely a means of fast travelling through stations you've already paid once for to unlock travel to and from.The game does not take itself too seriously, though. It is filled to the brim with vague, platitudinous language and stream-of-conscious-like snippets in item descriptions that reference all of the cliches of film noir, but do little to inform the player of anything except that the world you are exploring is apparently as mysterious as the murder you are trying to solve. There is a bizarre and seemingly irrelevant preoccupation with describing various liquors and beverages. The contrast between how cliche everything is and the ominous, cold and grotesque nature of the world makes the game both charming and horrifying at the same time.  And yet it is surprisingly easy for the player to accept the horrifying nature of the world and get on with their job.That said, the world is barren and empty. The game calls attention to this as often as it can with dialogue referencing the end of the world, which after awhile feels less like a well-utilized plot device and more of a convenient explanation for the lack of content. The characters feel like they did not get the patience and attention they deserved as nearly all interaction with them is either through interrogation or idle banter that focuses too much on telling and not enough on showing. Like everyone understands that it's their job to provide a history of the world to the player and that they only have a 20 hour game to do it in.I realize all of this sounds like I'm describing a very deeply flawed game. And part of the reason is because that is exactly what I am doing. To me, it is less of what an open world mystery game should be, but a demonstration on what they COULD be, and that dynamic and the understanding of how few people were involved in its development are inspiring to me.That and the music slaps.

_childDocuments_.review: Does 10 hours of reading a tumblr-flavoured visual novel while exploring a lovecraftian vaporwave open-world to solve a mysterious murder with your own wits sound like fun?I mean, probably not. Sitting down to read isn't most people's idea of a fun videogame, especially when, because this is a murder mystery that you genuinely have to use your brain to solve, you need to be reading closely in search little nuances.But if that *does* sound like any fun, you should really try Paradise Killer. It scratches that information game itch that keeps flaring up for me since playing games like Outer Wilds and Obra Dinn, and it's the best-written narrative game I've played in a long time. I ran through my entire 11 hour playthrough in two sittings because I was so hooked on its mysteries and its characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review with the comment that there are major spoilers. Do not read the spoiler text if you do not want this shown to you. Normally I would not reveal such critical information, but it is necessary for me to explain the glaring flaw in a title that I otherwise felt was unique and fun.  is a game that puts you into the role of Lady Love Dies to investigate who murdered the council on Paradise Island 24. You must travel around the world in the first person and speak to the different individuals, all of whom are suspects, to try and ascertain whether the accused party committed the crime or whether there are other factors at play. The colorful world of  is somewhere between cyberpunk and some sort of wild religiosity. The characters are all rendered in static 2D images, the world itself is devoid of anyone aside from the suspects (this is explained), and aside from the collectibles scattered about, it largely involves you traveling an island that looks like some sort of weird Dali fever dream. So, while colorful, it is somewhat bland, especially as you have to platform on narrow ledges and find yourself jumping up buildings and rockfaces trying to get to the blood gems, the world’s currency, and myriad other collectables. The music is 80s synth. It is not terrible, is suitable for the game world, and overall unobtrusive. The voice acting is limited to phrases and partial statements from conversations. Characters have dynamic accents, representing the various cultures from which the people hailed before they arrived on the island. You travel around the island, speak to residents, build up a relationship by “hanging out”, and generally try to find testimony from the people and clues from the environment. In terms of any detective game out there, you spend time collecting evidence, revisiting people to build up trust to unlock more dialogue options, and solve a few puzzles. Once you have accrued enough information (all stored in your handy computer), you can then go to the Judge to begin the trial. The more frustrating parts of the game are collecting the blood gems, necessary for fast travel, buying information from one contact, unlocking new abilities, and a key plot point. These are scattered about the world and can be tedious to platform to. You will spend a lot of time collecting these and other items to interact on the island, especially if you are a completionist. •	Interesting lore and story•	Unlocking new options and learning more about each character is fun•	For the most part, exploring the island is fun and Shinji is an interesting diversion•	In many ways unique for having a female protag who is not “svelte” and being a really         basic, clean game world that is fun to explore•	A lot of retracing of steps to fully unlock all clues•	The platforming can be annoying, especially when you need to get to ledges and must         fall from a higher point to reach a lower ledge, which requires precision gauging with the         physics•	The conclusion with the “true” ending•	The puzzles generally have no clues and are “try until you succeed”Now, the major problem that I had with the ending:While I genuinely enjoyed  and found it to be a fun diversion after my college studies were done for the day, the ending was so horrible that I find myself not being able to recommend it. Maybe the publisher should go back and realize the dynamic they created through the revelation of the “correct” ending and consider the underlying message that it sends.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a wonderful time with this indie gem, it's definitely a little rough around the edges but it's absolutely worth your time and money if you're even remotely a fan of murder mystery games.Paradise Killer exists at the cross-section of Danganronpa and something more open ended like Disco Elysium, with a simple collectathon tagged on for good measure. What makes it unique in the genre is that the game actually expects you to do the investigating, figure out what happened and come up with conclusions yourself - no part of this process is particularly complex in this game but doing all of it on your own time and thinking things through with your own human brain is actually super satisfying. Coming into the trial knowing exactly what happened, who did what and the whole sequence of events is a great feeling.Finally, it's what I always wanted, a game that lets you feel like Poirot calling in all the suspects at the end of the story and telling them exactly how it is! All of this doesn't even touch on the crazy, intriguing setting, surprisingly in-depth and compelling world-building or great sound track. Great little game, I'm looking forward to checking out whatever the developer comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is what you get if you crossed the tone and stylings of Suda 51’s games, Ace Attorney, a bit of a collectathon platformer, and a whole bunch of dead mall style vaporwave. I first played the demo back during Ludo Narra Con months back and it intrigued me and I’m happy to see that it ended up being one of the best detective games I’ve played alongside the likes of Sherlock Holmes: Crimes and Punishments, Her Story, and Obra Dinn. Paradise Killer does its own unique style of detective game, with a strong focus on exploration as you travel around the 24th Paradise to find clues that helps you solve the case. The game guides you a bit on potential leads to follow so you have an idea how much you still need to do but it does not hold your hand at all when it comes to interpreting all your collected evidence to figure out whodunnit. You also interrogate suspects, but it’s less like say, Ace Attorney and Contradiction, where you have to trap them in their lies, but more of showing them evidence or asking them about their or other characters’ alibis and motives to glean more information. You also interact them to build rapport so they can eventually open up to you with more clues. You will have to do some exploring if you want to get currency to help solve the case but I honestly felt it entertaining to do, though you don’t need to go too crazy, I had a large surplus of blood crystals for most of the game. You also can get two upgrades that aid you with this, a double jump and a secret radar that makes this easier. There’s also sidequests to do and just random minutiae to collect that adds to the game’s world-building of the setting. Said setting is a real interesting one too, a world of decadent zealot blood cultists sacrificing the downtrodden underclass like livestock to try and make a “perfect paradise” for their insane cosmic horror gods; the anti-capitalist allegory isn’t hard to get. The vaporwave aesthetic really genuinely helps to build the satire and allegory of the game too, as it utilizes the satirical edge of the genre that mocks consumer culture exemplified in the 80’s mall; exploring Paradise 24 even feels like exploring a dead mall because most of its denizens have packed up to leave to the 25th instance of Paradise, “Perfect 25.” The character writing is solid too as you have to deal with a bunch of oddball suspects in your quest for the truth. The soundtrack, mainly compromised of vaporwave, is also great, being peak chill.You can actually go right to the trial at any time and can do so immediately once you’re let loose, though obviously you aren’t gonna get the full picture at all. But when you do really put the work into it it’s a really great climax that feels rewarding when you successfully pieced everything together and you can pretty much do that where there is barely any loose ends. One problem though is that because the game goes with the mentality that there is no “right solution” even though there clearly is a correct path to your investigation that ties everything together it makes the denouement of the game super weak. The characters have nothing to really comment about the results of the trial and the game doesn’t really take what you did into account much in said denouement. The protag, Lady Love Dies, especially feels completely removed from the ramifications of the trial that can happen and you’re just straight up railroaded into having her just move to Perfect 25 even though you can play as her someone that despises the Paradise Elite for her unjust exile and their corrupt society and is only solving the case out of obligation/love of investigating. She also has nothing to say about you potentially executing people she considers old friends which is pretty glaring. This railroading also rather ruins the themes of the story a bit too because it feels like the writers kind of just threw their hands in the air and said “Hey maybe the 25th instance of this dystopia designed by insane capitalist blood priests won’t be completely awful too?!” The weirdest thing is in this post-trial section is that you can just randomly gun down or exile people which just feels tacked on and undermines the importance of the trial and all the work you put into it.  Despite all this it doesn’t truly ruin the game, it’s just a disappointment how much the game peters out in its denouement because of everything before it being so strong.Ultimately though Paradise Killer is a fantastic and stylish detective game that belongs aside the greats and is one of my favorite games of this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Very unusual and interesting, but not without flaws. It's indie, so don't expect high production value in all areas. If I had to define its main genre, it would be "3D platformer" (in 1st person), but you may like this even if, like me, you don't care much about this kind of game. Here are my comments divided in topics: by far the best the game has to offer. The lore, the characters (and their names), the worldbuilding, it's all very good, weird and unique. The plot itself is not brilliant, but this universe is fantastic and I hope we get to revisit it (in Perfect 25 or in a previous or future island sequence), even if it's in a totally different gaming genre.  Initially I was really bothered (since "Deadly Premonition" I wasn't so put off by a game's graphics), but they grew on me after a while. It gets better when you disable the night/day cycle, because the game looks worse at night _ also, it makes more sense, because the action happens on a single day after the crime. Reminded me a bit of the original "Myst"; it has a retro feel and it's more quirky than beautiful.  Not the most optimized game. I had to turn off reflections to make it run smoothly. Played the DX12 version.  Good overall. Voice acting is very sparse, but not bad. The lauded soundtrack is OK, especially when the  (which only happens during the ).  Not really great as a detective or courtroom game ("L.A. Noire", "Sherlock Holmes: Crimes & Punishments" and "Aviary Attorney" are better in those regards). You just collect evidence and make interviews (and for the most part dialogue choices don't matter). When you are ready to wrap up, there are trials and , even if they . Besides, afterwards you can , even without . Most of the game consists of exploration of the small, but intricate open world _ this is , though, since it's highly interactive and demands 3D platforming abilities if you're going to be thorough.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it when a game comes out of nowhere and blows you away with how unique it is.An open world murder mystery in a world which is something like if Charles Stross' The Laundry Files were set in a neon-lit drugs&alcohol fueled 80s LA beach. You play as Lady Love Dies, official investigator for the Syndicate, which is the fancy name for the corporation/cult of blood-magic wielding immortals who have created a pocket universe. In this dimension they have created their perfect little beach paradise and also incidentally worship dangerous inter-dimensional alien gods. Someone has killed all the members of the ruling council of the Syndicate, and everything points to the perpetrator being a demon-possessed Citizen named Henry. Henry is one of the many enslaved normal human beings who have been kidnapped from earth do menial and dangerous jobs in "paradise", and also to be sacrified to the gods, so Henry certainly has a motive.The case looks a little bit too open&shut and the suspect a little too convenient though for the being called Justice, and Lady Love Dies is allowed to return from exile so she can walk around the island and find clues, interview suspects and gradually uncover the truth. Gameplay is split between first person 3D open world point&click adventuring with some light platforming, and visual-novel style dialogues as you interview Dr Doom Jazz, Crimson Acid, Witness-to-the-End and the other Syndicate members who still remain in paradise. The gameplay is fine, but it is the soundtrack and unique setting that sets this game apart. If you liked Obra Dinn I think there is a fair chance you will like this too. Don't miss it.

The demo turned me off initially with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-y writing (mostly from Shinji) and character designs that felt like they were trying too hard BUT once i settled into the groove of the game, all that was in the rear-view. _childDocuments_.review: Such an odd world. I love it for all its quirks and color. I’m just not convinced that I love the game. It’s a whodunnit, set on an island paradise where man has transcended his limitations, and is now constructing a series of island resorts in search of a perfect paradise. It’s a pure adventure game, with character and dialogue and conflicting motivations. But it’s also staged in a rather big world, where you traverse where you want, when you want -- horizontally and vertically. It’s a weird combination. And not necessarily one where the one genre complements the other. But it is what it is, I guess. It’s one of the few games I’ve played that has tasked me with both parkouring around, gathering relevant and irrelevant collectibles like a platformer -- whilst also unralveing a murder plot in a tighly scripted narrative by interviewing inhabitants and witnesses.There’s a lot to process at the outset, but it does reside a bit into the background as soon as you encounter the colorful cast of characters and start to converse. The story is actually very fun, with loads of twists and turns -- and some unexpected genre bending to go with it. It’s unique, to say the least.Carefully recommended, if you think you like this sort of thing. Whatever it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Five stars for this one, a good old thorough, rational investigation of a murder mystery, with a satisfying conclusion. Rewards logic, reason, and attention to detail. _childDocuments_.review: TRUTH OR FACTThis was a weird game. Basically an exploration game in an open world, where the whole world is basically a huge crime scene. Part open-world, part visual-novel.You interact with characters, all full of colors and with JoJo poses, putting pieces by pieces how the whole world works, what is the reality of the people living here. Space demons, gods, possessions, secrets, space... Most of the rules of the real world doesn't work here, sorry. It's a paradise, not a perfect one, it's the 24th version, the one preceding the perfect 25th. Nothing make sense at first. Will you be able to differentiate facts from your truth? You, who has been put into exile 3 million years ago, for being manipulated by a god? It's not as easy as it seems. Lady Love Dies, may you reach the moon.JUSTICE HAS BEEN SERVED

_childDocuments_.review: It is not exactly a Dangan Ronpa game, but it is probably the closest to it you can find on Steam.From beginning to end the game has a vibe that remind me of the late 80s, mixing in map design of the late 90s. It feels big and small at the same time. The same can be said about the lore, which is quite unlike anything I've ever read before.The biggest difference to DR is that there is only one trial and you have an open world to explore. It's your choice who to talk to and what part of the island to explore first. You might find out something over 10h later than a different player has, just because going somewhere else.You also get movement upgrades (TAKE EVERY 5 BLOOD CRYSTAL BATHS AS SOON AS YOU FIND THEM), which makes it a real joy to explore.The only small downsides I encountered are minor spelling errors, the voice lines being very limited and it's weird you have to use blood crystals for fast travel. I did end up with around 30 blood crystals left over at the end though, after having unlocked everything and did a bit of fast traveling in the last ~6h out of 20h it took me to finish.A very minor tip/spoiler for something that cost me a good two hours of running around aimlessly; You can actually just walk through the fourth seal. This was never said or indicated clearly, so I didn't even try it at first.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I beat the game, got all the acheivements and my review still stands. The only things I would (and wish I could) change about Paradise Killer are its many typos and grammatical mistakes.***Original Review:I am really liking this game and wish I could call it perfect, since it's very close, at least as far as indie games go. While it doesn't have amazing AAA graphics or high-action gameplay, it does what it aims to do extremely well. I'm near the end at this point and have found most of the collectibles, so I'd be surprised if I encounter anything new that drastically changes my mind about the game's quality. If I do, I'll update my review.As for what I like, I would say almost everything about this game is enjoyable. The story and lore are extremely wild and intriguing, like an 80s detective movie with alien gods/demons and corrupt immortal politicians. The bizarre, hypersexualized aesthetic also makes for a unique experience. An like many other reviewer's have said, this game really does make you feel like a detective. There is a lot to take in and it can be a bit overwhelming at first, especially since you can go pretty much anywhere right at the start. However, as you piece together the evidence and get to know the characters, things start to fall into place. The thing that has been bothering me most is the spelling and grammar mistakes. While most of them are not too obstructive, others make it difficult to understand (and sometimes even contradict) the character's intentions. For instance, at one point, Lydia says "now" when she meant to say "no," which reverses the meaning of her sentence. In another instance, Crimson says "it" instead of "is" but for some reasons adds a different "is" in the wrong place. The most common mistake by far is the lack of commas before characters' names and question phrases. For example, a character might say, "Are you an idiot freak?" when they meant to say, "Are you an idiot, freak?" Or, they might say, "It is great isn't it?" instead of, "It is great, isn't it?" Most of the time, it's easy enough to understand what the character is trying to say, but sometimes it's confusing. The amount mistakes like this (there are a lot of them) makes it seem like the developers didn't really care enough to address read through the script before publishing the game, which is a bit disheartening, since this game is basically a visual novel. Part of me wishes I was capable of making a mod to fix these textual mistakes, or that I could persuade the developers to hire me as an editor. While minor in the grand scheme of things, this game does involve a lot of reading. Encountering so many textual mistakes makes the writing seem amateurish, which may turn some people off to what is otherwise an incredibly engrossing and detailed story. In sum, I would say you should definitely play this game if a detective game with a bizarre, supernatural story and deep lore sounds interesting to you, as this game does all these things well. However, I hope the developers will consider releasing an update that fixes the many spelling/grammar mistakes, so their story (which they obvious put a lot of effort into crafting) can really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on recommendation, and I loved 90% of what this game did.  Unfortunately, the 10% I didn't was that it *completely* collapsed at the end, in a way that is difficult to articulate without spoilers.  Half of it is that there is a single piece of pre-trial evidence you can find which totally, unambiguously blows apart the game's central mystery and goes from zero to literal confession within the span of 30 seconds, so for all the game's talk about distinguishing facts from truth, the facts end up having a super clear truth which removes a huge amount of the moral dilemma it was building toward.  The other half is that, having spent all game pushing the thesis statement "Is paradise worth saving?" at you, there is no way to follow up on it whatsoever.  You never get to see the outcome of your choices (aside from everyone you convict of any crime getting the immediate death penalty); there is apparently no difference whatsoever to the structure and trajectory of the next island, whether you murder the entire main cast or find a single scapegoat.  More crucially, there is absolutely no acknowledgement when you have enough evidence to convict someone and then deliberately refuse to present it.  I replayed the final trial, and was SO looking forward to the catharsis of saving [redacted] and then talking with them later to say I knew exactly what they had done.  But there is no way to even bring the topic up in post-trial conversation, just an option to supplementarily kill (or exile) anyone you thought was guilty but couldn't prove it in court.  (And nobody even reacts to that!  It just happens and it's done.)This would have been a fantastic game if there had been any denouement whatsoever -- or, failing that, if the linchpin evidence had been treated with even a fraction of the care and thought of the rest of the game.  As it is, this is a weak recommend on the strength of its worldbuilding and atmosphere, with a warning that it will likely leave you unsatisfied, despite the good parts of it sticking in your head.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool little game, you walk around in a big 3D world interacting with odd characters and collecting items and its a big murder mystery you have to solve. Very nice music and art and stuff, gameplay is simple but it works. Lot of things to do and collectables to get. Has a small amount of voice acting but what is in there is pretty decent. The setting and the world and all the lore is very interesting and I would like to see more of it. Runs pretty well, didn't really notice any bugs, didn't have any crashes. Ran at a good 100-144fps most of the time. If I had any critiques its probably that its a bit straightforward and as long as you go around and do everything you more or less don't have to worry too much about solving things. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing open world murder mystery with an unique style and great, interesting characters.Two things stood out that make this game special:1. The open world fits perfectly into the gameplay of a detective. There's no "clue" counter to know if you found everything. No big icons for each and every clue or place to investigate. Compared to most other open world games, there's an actual reason to having an open world, aside from saving on loading screens and padding game length.2. The style and craziness of the world and characters actually comes together as a coherent world. _childDocuments_.review: I really don’t like calling things pretentious. I avoid it if at all possible, because I think claiming something doesn’t have the depth or meaning it purports to requires a level of understanding that most people (myself included) don’t reach with their media. I’d rather not say a game fails to express its intended meaning unless it’s really, truly, painfully obvious that it missed the mark. I bring this up because I’ve heard Paradise Killer criticized for being pretentious, and I don’t think that could be any further from the truth. The characters and concepts are about as far out there as you can get without becoming wholly experimental, but the gonzo themes are only setting you up for the brilliant, poignant ending. You might not be expecting it, even when the game tells you exactly what it’s going to be.Lady Love Dies is known as the “investigation freak”, or at least she was, until she was exiled from Paradise. Paradise is an island, managed by the all-powerful Council, that is unmade and remade over and over again in the hopes of forming a perfect society that will revive a host of ancient, alien gods. This reality manipulation can have nasty side effects, like demon infestations that have to be purged by remaking the island. However, the Council seems to have gotten it right with their next iteration of the island, which they’re in the process of relocating to when they are all quite suddenly murdered. This unthinkable event is enough to summon Lady Love Dies from her exile, and put her on the grisly case.If you think that’s weird, it only gets weirder once you’re in the game. You’re going to interview suspects like the cyber-enhanced Doctor Doom Jazz and the goat-headed Crimson Acid. You’re going to learn about gods that whisper dead secrets into mortal ears. You’re going to buy sodas from Dead Nebula machines, and scour cabinets and trash cans for blood crystals. And you’re going to do all this in a wide-open city that looks like some kind of insane vaporwave FPS mod, meeting up with 2D characters that transition you to pre-rendered scenes from a Windows 95 screensaver to question them about an impossible murder. It’s a lot to take in, thematically and aesthetically, and honestly this might be what makes Paradise Killer work so well.The moment you load into the game, you’re dropped into Lady Love Dies’ palace of exile, a white-marble affair accented with lush gardens and golden skulls. The plot is blasted at you by your talking computer, you’re taken down to the gates of the island on a road to nowhere, and then you’re given the full scope of your task from the Judge, a being of pure logic fused to the island through mechanical and spiritual means. Opening the game with the full gamut of the game’s weirdness honestly makes it a lot easier to accept as status quo, and helps put the player’s mind where it needs to be to comprehend the events that unfold. The plot is a complicated one, with dozens of players and elements to keep track of, and they cross in ways that would make no sense in our world, but perfect sense in the world of the Syndicate and Perfect 24.At the heart of Paradise Killer is a murder mystery, and everything you do on the island is to the end of uncovering the facts of the case. But doing that requires running around the island, exploring the deserted neighborhoods, industrial centers, shrines, cliffs, and more. This is accomplished in first-person, and is honestly some of the most fun I’ve had scrambling about a location. The wild architecture is certainly a big plus, but there’s an element of first-person platforming to it that controls exceptionally well and makes finding secrets and collectibles that much more gratifying. Perfect 24 is just a fun place to hang out, and I never got tired making laps around the island to find new things or follow up on leads.As for the mystery itself, there’s a ton to unravel and every character has something to contribute to the unraveling. You will indeed need to make several laps of the island, to ask about new evidence you uncover or refute a claim a character made earlier on. A few locations require some puzzling to get into, nothing overly complex but it does add to an overall sense of progression. There’s one revelation that came out of absolute nowhere for me, perhaps because of how I came across it, but that’s forgivable in part for the incredibly open nature of the game. Even with all the time I spent uncovering secrets and making connections, I’m still not sure I got the full picture, but fortunately that’s not necessary for the ending.I do want to mention one thing about the ending, without getting into spoilers, because it’s perhaps the most brilliant part of the game and also the most misunderstood. Early on in the game, while you’re getting your bearings and coming to grips with the bizarre setting, the Judge explains your investigation in detail. They say something about how this will all wrap up that’s meant to be taken literally, and I get the feeling some folks didn’t pick up on that. Because of this, the conclusion you get once you close your case might not be the definitive answer to the mystery you’re looking for. All I can tell you is that that’s the point, and to heed the words of the Judge both at the beginning and the end of the game.Even if the mystery angle doesn’t hit as hard for you as it did for me, Paradise Killer is absolutely a game worth experiencing. A lot of indie games go hard on unique aesthetics and themes, but this is one of the rare ones that really makes it work from start to finish. The vaporwave look, the wild architecture, the almost nonsensical characters, and the surprisingly deep lore all combine to make a world that’s utterly implausible and yet still feels real in its own way. I greatly enjoyed my time scouring the island and collecting clues, and I was incredibly impressed with how it all wrapped up. I hope it’s the same for you, because it can be one hell of a trip.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: This game is weird…really weird.  I feel the world design is questionable at best.  I’m very confused with the decisions they made in the actual construction.  I feel they clearly did not have the budget to create a 3D world, it’s sloppy and ugly looking.  The proportions of the buildings…also don’t feel right…the doors and houses all feel too small/slim.  The fact the characters you meet are 2d sprites is equally confusing…I just don’t understand these design decisions other then ways to face the realities that they didn’t have the money or development team to create an actual world.  Honestly, this game probably should be a visual novel…but that would make the open world detective nature of this game impossible and that’s one of its best qualities.  So I don’t really know what the best solution would have been.  I think ultimately they should have tried an isometric open world like Disco Elysium…however, if Outer Wilds managed to create a beautiful 3D world with the slim staff they had, I don’t know why this team couldn’t have as well.   They could have also just made it more like an adventure game like Laura Bow, I would have preferred that to this hideous 3d created world.So it’s strange, because I really don’t like the look of this world as it feels so junky...but except for that I would say everything else in this game is incredible.  So if you can get past what the world looks like, this game is a must play for anyone who likes adventure/detective games.   Very few detective games actually require you to actually look for clues and use deductive reasoning to search for those clues.  This game excels at it.  A lot of clues are hidden, but there are all logical reasons for the clues to be where they are.  You have to actually explore the crime scenes and you are always rewarded for that exploration.  It was shocking to me when I realized how well the clues/exploration was handled. While I think the world design is as ugly as sin, the art direction is fantastic.  The character designs are outstanding.  They are all just super wild and really lock in how just utter crazy this world is.  It’s hard to even pick my favorite design, they are all so wonderful.  I might have to go with Crimson Acid aka Goat Head Woman…or maybe Sam aka Skeleton man, honestly they are all so good.  They bring the world to life.  The game has a strong 80’s vibe with a great synth soundtrack and these character designs are all very bright/neon and vibrant.  It fits so well together.It’s a strange direction to take…the plot of the game deals with elder gods (Lovecraft Gods) that have created their own “paradise” on another planet.  Normally anything involving Cosmic Horror is dark, creepy, and foreboding.  This is literally the opposite, it’s all bright neon and synthwave.   If you had told me this was your plan, I would have called you the dumbest person on the planet, but it works and it works so perfectly.  The story is certainly still dark, it deals with a cult of elder god worshipers that kidnap and ritually sacrifice other humans from Earth in order to fuel the power of the elder gods.  Your character, Lady Love Dies, is culpable in all of this.  She’s a very likeable character, but she is still a senior member of a cult that is involved in the outright kidnapping, murder, for the purposes of worshipping elder gods that are also not real nice gods…they want to enslave/destroy humanity.  So a very strange setting for the game, but it all works.  As far as for the actual murder mystery that this game requires you to solve, I will say it’s fantastic.  It’s one of the strongest murder mysteries written for video games.  Where Disco Elysium’s story pretends to be a murder mystery it has no actual clues or deduction work…this game actually does and it’s done very well.  I’m not going to go into spoilers, but I will just say, everything works, all the clues work, the deductions you can make from those clues all work.  This really is a detective game and one of the best ones ever made.  You have to actually talk to suspects and interrogate them to gather evidence and no one is spelling things out for you, you have to put all these clues together for the grand finale where you have to decide who the murder is and why.  My issues with the game are more that it’s simply too short.  Realistically it’s about 10 hours…that simply isn’t enough.  Their also needed to be more characters so you have more suspects.  I feel the ultimate solution was quite easy.   I wanted much more time with these characters.  I think the game should involve a lot more interaction with them, a lot more character development, and also far more gathering of evidence and a lot more evidence in general.  All characters should at least have motive and evidence related to them, but by the end really the solution comes down to mainly 3 people.  The game starts after the murder occurs…I think that was a mistake.  It should take place prior so you have time to get to know these characters beforehand.  This almost feels in many ways like an alpha/beta of the idea for a much more involved murder mystery game.  Hopefully, that is the case and we haven’t seen the last of Lady Love Dies, because this game is fantastic and I need more!  I just hope next time the case is much more involved and they massively rethink that hideous 3D world design.  Due to the length I would say this has to be bought on sale #Worth $10.  Still this is a must play for anyone who likes adventure/detective games as it’s literally one of the best by far.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of very few games (and probably not only games) that manages to create a convincing atmosphere of total madness. Or being high. If you've ever read Philip K.♥♥♥♥ and felt the terror creeping out of the pages and mixing with your own reality, you'll know what I mean. Except that madness in Paradise Killer is not grim and punishing. It's bright and colorful, and the game universe is very consistent with almost zero inner contradictions. You started playing and don't understand a thing? Nevermind, just play along! In an hour you'll know enough about gods, demons, vending machines and reality folding drives. Technically, this game is a wild mix of metroidvania, 3D platformer, and visual novel. It rewards you for exploring the world, though you're not obliged to do so. What's nice, there's always more than one way to get what you want, be that an item on a rooftop or a piece of evidence. You can always find your way around, if you don't feel like following the "default" path. Under its somewhat silly appearance, this game hides a solid captivating plot, a detective story with alibis and evidence, lies and truths. Everyone has their agency. Everyone can be found guilty. They can, however, be framed. They can both be guilty AND be framed at the same time. It's up to you to decide who's to blame in the end.And the music will keep playing out in your head long long long after you close the game. Even if you normally don't listen to the music like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Not everything is as it seems in paradise.This game took over my life for a couple of days. Seriously though, this was the perfect game for an achievement junky like myself. Along with all the collectibles, there are so many aspects that make Paradise Killer an extremely unique game to devour. It has a cast of memorable characters, a stylish vaporwave aesthetic, captivating lore, and a web of mysteries that just seem to spiral into more mysteries the more you delve into it. The world and map admittedly took some time getting used to, however I came to appreciate it the more time I spent on it. If there is ever a chance for a second game, little icons that show the location of key characters on the map would be helpful. I didn't really mind the parkour, as it only got tricky getting a few specific collectibles. Overall, I really enjoyed this game and hope to see more of Lady Love Dies in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: An open-world, murder-mystery, vaporwave detective game that might even be better than Return of the Obra Dinn as far as the detective/investigation genre of video games are concerned. The main character is great, the music is fantastic, the environment is vibrant, there's plenty of mystery to uncover. The only downside was that it took me a little bit to get used to the setting of this game, but once I did, everything clicked and it was really enjoyable to fully explore. Also, I really appreciate that there was an in-game mechanism to hunt down all the collectables on the island, forgoing the need for external guides.Definitely pick this up if you like being a detective, or are super into the vaporwave aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an okay game with great soundtrack and visual style, fresh setting and well-written characters. I've completed it and for the most part had a decent time.So why "Do not recommend"?Because it positions itself as a detective game and in that regard it's pretty awful. It doesn't "feel like real detective work in a way few games do" (quote GameSpot), neither does it "set a new standard for investigative gameplay" (quote PC Gamer). There is absolutely no detective work, no deductive reasoning or investigating, required from you. All you have to do to uncover the truth is: a) run around the island collecting the clues scattered throughout and b) exhaust all dialogue options with characters that just stand around and not interact with the world or story in any way. Some of the dialogue is locked behind the pointless relationship system, but ultimately, if you talk to everyone enough times, you are guaranteed to find all there is to know. And I mean, there is no reason not to - no time limit or missable content, just run around till you get everything (or get bored). All the clues you find are connected to relevant case files and suspects automatically, so no involvement needed here either. There are also a couple of "puzzles", but they are really nothing to write home about: just looking for key items and minimal trial-and-error tinkering.And then there is the final trial. Don't expect anything intense and full of dramatic twists like Phoenix Wright or Danganronpa. There are several crimes to solve, for each one you just choose who you want to accuse and dump all relevant evidence and testimonies on Judge, who, for the most part, never questions you. If you found all the clues (see above), there shouldn't be any problems with that, and even if you make a mistake, it ultimately doesn't matter, which brings me to the worst part of the game (and the reason i'm writing this review): the ending.Not to spoil to much, I'll just say that the game has an open ending, which doesn't change (as far as I've seen) whether you find all the clues or not. Moreover, for some of the crimes there are two equally possible culprits, and the game rolls with whoever you choose. I think that was the intention (it says something like "your facts have become truth"), but I really didn't like it. All in all, the ending felt really underwhelming.So, unfortunately, despite the good music and unusual setting, I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What are the facts? What is the truth? Are they the same?In Paradise Killer, you take on the role of a detective solving a murder in a fantasy world, full of weird and charismatic characters and lore.This is mainly an exploration game. You'll spend most of your time walking around the island, talking to people and collecting items as you go. There are a lot of things to unlock, and the game rewards you for looking into all corners. This ties in with the movement, which while being limited presents a fun challenge, and there are a couple optional movement upgrades you can unlock that make it a lot more dynamic and fun. The game presents some tricky platforming but it's pretty easy in general, although learning to move from location to location around the island is a fun challenge on its own.The dialogue is very linear but well written. Don't expect to have to think a lot or to make tough choices. If you gather all the relevant evidence, you only need to pinpoint the culprit(s), and the game will do the reasoning for you. That didn't make it any less fun though, as you'll end up figuring it out as you go, and the final trial is more of a cutscene/climax. Or you can go ham and make false accusations ;)Oh, and the music goes really hard. It's an 80s style soundtrack that doesn't get in the way of thinking but gives you funky beats that'll get stuck in your head. Really good for setting the atmosphere.Overall, 8.5/10. A bit hard to get into, and has some rough edges; but its charm, uniqueness and writing more than makes up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games in the murder mystery genre, that keeps player autonomy and choice at the forefront of its game design and story at all times. Extremely satisfying and rewards you for your efforts as a player. Also delivered one of the most exciting and gripping finales of a game of this kind. If you enjoy the murder mystery genre or exploration and dialogue-focused narratives, you would be doing yourself a disservice passing this one up. Find your Truth, and save Paradise!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, got sucked right in. The world is immersive, the characters are interesting, and the story has depth. It's really a collect 'em up, that unfolds the narrative as you go about your way, I would say it's kinda a mashup between Pathologic 2 and The Other Wilds (probably with a bit of Danganronpa thrown in at the end - though I haven't played that yet). Music is top notch synthwave affair too. The only thing I would say is that I didn't find it particularly difficult, but it was very satisfying. Highly Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The review says I played ~5h of gameplay but I have actually played for about 15h. I didn't have internet access for a couple of days and those gameplay hours were not registered somehow.Anyway, Paradise Killer was one hell of a ride. The best thing I can say about it is that there's nothing like this game out there. It masterfully blends a lot of different gameplay elements and concepts and creates a very risky package that works surprisingly well.First off, I must say I had a lot of fun exploring the island and it never felt bloated with nonsense content just for the sake of throwing content into it; every collectible feels like a reward for your time invested in its world and I really appreciate that design decission. The character movement, albeit a bit clunky sometimes, is very comfortable and once you've unlocked every upgrade it breathes a lot of verticality into the formula like few other open-world games do.This matches surprisingly well with the main investigation topic of the game. Uncovering the island's secrets never gets old and there's always some new bit of information you can add to your court record if you take your time to properly talk to every character involved and explore every area thoroughly. This gives the progression of the game a certain degree of non-linearity (even with the plot being solid and closed) that differentiates Paradise Killer from other games such as the Phoenix Wright saga, where everything is much more linear and straight-forward. You really feel like an investigator following leads and uncovering buried secrets.Story-wise, the themes used for PK's lore are a very unique choice. Mixing religion with cosmic horror while reimagining the western concept of Paradise and afterlife and tapping into some of the biggest modern alien conspiracies was definitely a very risky move, but the creators managed to pull it off somehow. The artistic and sound design choices are also on point and help a lot in that regard, as the Vice City-esque island filled with vaporwave music gives the world this distinctive flair of fabricated reality that boosts the game's thematic choices.Paradise Killer is a game that rewards the invested player who really take their time to delve deep into it, and that's exactly how I would recommend playing: embracing it as the creators' did with their ideas. This was a very pleasant surprise and its weirdness can't be a better match for year 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So I've 100%'d this game twice--on both Xbox and PC. Not counting the speedruns, I've played this game to completion three times. I love this game. But before I get into what I love about it first I kinda have to be mean to it.First, the platforming is like, abysmal. It's a mix of places often feeling far too small for Love Dies to properly navigate, and the jump/dash physics seem to be actively working against you half the time. Finding footing after climbing up a ladder is somehow a Herculean task. I like to move through games quickly but often found myself walking instead of sprinting because everything felt too narrow to safely race across.The voice acting is also...a real mixed bag. I don't feel comfortable calling everyone in here a bad voice actor because I don't think I've heard them in anything else, but the voice acting ranges from "poor" to "doing the best with what they're given". That second one is very specific in its wording. The voice acting would probably come across better if a lot of the lines weren't written so awkwardly--special mentions to LD's "Nani the hell?" and the Architect's "Craft is its own reward".Okay those are my complaints out of the way. Now onto the things I find charmingly wonky. Like still kinda bad but it's in a silly little way that I think adds to what makes the game special. The character sprites are all drawn like they wanted to give everyone dynamic poses instead of having them stand around like Danganronpa characters but they went way overboard and I love it. The repetition of things like Starlight's "Blood crystal obtained"/"Key item obtained"/etc will probably grate some players but I found it charming. There's also the fact that the devs are definitely weebs and it feels silly but again, its charmingly wonky to find a shoehorned manga reference.Finally, onto the real good stuff. Atmosphere, vibes, music, and world. When I hear the concept "immortal beings trying to resurrect genocidal gods by kidnapping humans and turning them into slaves" I do not think of a vaporwave-themed island paradise setting but they really managed to make it work and it in fact adds to the horror of what these people are doing. By dressing everything up in bright colors with funky music blasting over the speakers while you pick up mementos detailing how much the Citizens suffered and resorted to violence, it really helps the investment you have in solving the crime, knowing that the Syndicate is full of terrible people and yet another one of its Citizens is being exploited for their gain. The presence of the ghosts adds to this feel as well.The characters, even if several of them are kinda of caricatures, all have reasonable depth and history with one another. Some are stronger than others, but they all, in their own way, help support the narrative of how evil the Syndicate is, even with some of the more likeable ones.The mystery, while not groundbreaking and kinda predictable, at least makes full use of the bizarre mythology they've created, so even if I saw something coming it was still very entertaining to watch unfold.  That aside, watching the convictions unfold after trekking around for 10 odd hours can feel really satisfying. If you've gathered enough evidence to make the trial feel worthwhile, that is. Small complaint--the trials are really brief. Even with all possible evidence collected, some of them are over very quickly and it feels like we don't have time to truly ruminate.The unique and bizarre world the devs have created for this game should be commended. I love the small reference to things in the past that are kinda dropped causally, a history we don't know too much about but adds to the flavor of the worldbuilding, like timelines shenanigans and a demonic siege and LD's deception. The game's ending leaves further exploration of the Syndicate and their mission open, whether that be through a sequel exploring Perfect 25 or maybe a prequel about a past island sequence. I hope this isn't the last we see of the Syndicate.tldr; good worldbuilding, great vibe and design, fun characters, bad platforming, wonky sprites, nothing groundbreaking in terms of the mystery but well worth your time if you wanna sink yourself into an entirely new world for a short period, if you don't mind picking up like 500 collectible items.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting well written sandbox murder mystery with mysteries inside mysteries, in an even more interesting Vaporwave inspired setting involving syndicate and council members living in a pocket dimension called Paradise Island. The island is regenerated after mistakes/tragedies with the coming 25th said to be perfect. Each with abducted enslaved citizens to serve as fuel to resurrect ancient genocidal gods, run by a council that has lived for thousands of years and other chosen who have started to grow bored of their lives, the way things are run, or their place in the island's hierarchy. When the council is discovered to be murdered by what is assumed to be a demon an investigator is called back after over 3,000,000 days of exile to discover the truth.The look, setting, writing, music, and being rewarded for looking into things and exploring are the strong parts of the game. The actual investigating and case connections are basically done for you when you find new information by exploring the environment or questioning characters. You can't actually get your questioning wrong and even the trial at the end only involves accusing the people that make sense based on the evidence you discovered (you can easily miss things or start the trial early) and clicking every choice to present all of your findings to the judge. The actual running around back and forth, looking for currency in addition to collectibles and evidence to pay for upgrades or fast travel, and platforming to reach those collectibles also ends up being a fairly mediocre part of the game. Though the actual lore based items you find can be interesting and give a clearer picture of the game's unique setting.Not everyone will be satisfied with the ending as the trial doesn't have the tense, shocking, back and forth moments of games like Phoenix Wright or Donganronpa, you don't have to piece much together like in Return of the Obra Dinn, and it isn't in the game's or your character's job's scope to solve or influence the problems with the setting's society or to delve deeper into real world/gods/demons talked about in the lore. As one of the characters already living on the new island you never get to see says in a brief vision, "Solving a crime doesn't mean that the world is fixed." But it does tell a good story in a world that is both unique with a rarely used art style, and searching the island to uncover more of the facts about the case and the island's citizens is different but very satisfying experience.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: This game had an interesting story that made me want to play through the game and play until the end. You solve multiple crimes and see those responsible punished. This game has no replay value and is extremely linear in its nature. I completed it in less than 10 hours and that was getting every piece of information possible. I ran around for awhile to see if there was anything else I could do/collect or if I was missing anything and there was nothing. You may want to go through the story again, I won't feel inclined to for at least a few years.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the story/world, just weird and crazy enough to keep me interested most of the time.  I didn't like the spiral staircase climbing and there's a fair amout of it. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic investigative game. Gameplay mostly involves scanning areas for clues and interviewing the cast of unnecessarily sexy characters, but the mystery is compelling with a ton of twists and revelations. The vaporwave aesthetic is top-notch as well (The main theme being stuck in my head inspired me to write this review). The setting is also totally bonkers and I found I was playing as much to find out more about the Syndicate and their islands as I was to solve the murder.Minor complaints would be that movement is a bit clunky, as is the fast travel system. Unlockable movement upgrades help a lot, but there is still quite a bit of backtracking accross the island. Luckily exploration is rewarded with money or "relic" items that give you little backstory snippets, as well as the occasional clue in a well hidden area.The ending trial is pretty interesting in that you can choose who to accuse of each part of the crime, and what evidence to present. You might decide that some of the guilty parties don't deserve death, or you could frame someone you don't like. I highly enjoyed my time with this game and it left me wanting more. If you're at all interested in investigative games give this a shot, there's nothing else quite like it out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game from start to finish. It's impossible to describe but I'll try.It's a detective game! A few things it does excellently:- It's an open world. You can explore the entire island, and nowhere is gated at first. There are a few locations that you can't get into immediately but 95% of the whole island can just be wandered into after a 10-minute intro sequence. This is AMAZING.- It also means evidence and characters can be encountered in any order. The game just... handles this. It's fine. And it adds to that feeling of flexibility and freedom. - Sometimes evidence is an object that's been dropped, or left somewhere. This means that you can't necessarily just do what you're told and assume you'll get all the evidence. A few times I had to go off the beaten track, wondering "hm, since I know this fact, I wonder if there is some key evidence hiding away over here?" Sometimes there wasn't. Often there WAS, which was a great feeling.- You can start the trial, in which you expose the conspiracy, at any time. You can accuse anyone. - Oh, and the crime is really clever too!This all means that, while you'll probably not take advantage of all of this freedom (you won't accuse someone for whom you have no evidence, for example) the fact you CAN makes the whole game feel so much more earned. YOU wandered into an area based on a hunch, found some evidence, and are now using it to accuse person D of committing a murder? You earned that.And I haven't even talked about the setting! It's a gorgeous, grotesque mix of a Miami hot pink "I left my rhinestone sunglasses in the fuchsia penthouse" aesthetic, and glitchy cosmic-horror satanism. The story and worldbuilding are absurd and SO out there. Each character fits seamlessly into this bizarre and tragic world. I find the setting completely irresistible, and I desperately want a sequel so I can see more of it.Oh and the music? IT BANGS.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A collectathon game with detective elements, not the other way around.I expected it to be more like Ace Attorney or Danganronpa in terms of the general process, but in the end your choices don't really matter much outside of pointing out suspects at the very end, which are heavily telegraphed in most cases. It's basically a visual novel that's even less interactive than the games mentioned.Controls are pretty damn bad, honestly. Not only does your character barely have air control when jumping, the dashing move you unlock doesn't change your character's flight trajectory after using it, leading to a good amount of frustration when trying to get those pesky relics and clues somewhere high up.The premise of the game and the case itself are pretty good, but it had  much "fictional" stuff thrown in, for my taste at least: . At some point I just stopped trying to unravel the story myself and basically thought "Whatever, we'll see what devs came up with this time, no need to think about reasons/causes much since new stuff gets made up so fast.". Obviously this wasn't the case with Ace Attorney/Danganronpa games, they were pretty grounded in reality while still having mythical stuff there and there, it was fun to figure stuff out.7/10, had fun clearing the entire map even with annoying controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the coolest games I've ever played. Its world is vibrant, strange, obtuse, and over-the-top. I was addicted. It's a sort of a collect-a-thon/visual novel/walking simulator type game, so if you like those kinds of games check it out! The March 2022 update adds a handful of new collectables to the game, and a new side quest. It was a great excuse to pick it back up and get some achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy Paradise Killer, but it had a huge problem with its scale.  It was trying to be so much more than it really is.  At its core, Paradise Killer is a visual novel that allows you to undercover all the different plots of each character, and decide the outcome at a trial.  But getting there has to be the most painful thing imaginable.First person Platformer: Scale issue: There's too many odd jumps, missed falling, and hard to see jumping in this game.  I don't like playing platform games in 3rd person.  The amount of odd jumping, falling, and using the special powerups just to get minor items in the weirdest of places was extremely tedious and painstaking.  I did a lot before the i found the powerups, because I'm insane.    This really didn't add very much to the gameplay, other than to make the game longer.  Exploration: The scale problem here is that the map is pretty wide east to west and north to south, but it's just as expansive Bottom to Top.  Why do I need to scale a 10 floor apartment building where the majority of the floors are nothing?  I had to use the motion sickness assist, because it was way too much.  To get from one side of the island to the other was crazy... it's easy to get lost and turned around.  Some sections were impossible to find the entry point (I'm looking at you Marshall Barracks) because the save point wasn't in the section you expected it to be.  There was no reason to have this huge of an exploration area, other than to just make the game longer.Blood Crystal Currency: The problem of scale with the Blood Crystals as currency, is that you're always afraid you're going to run out.  At the end of the game you're swimming in them, but early on you have no clue if you're going to have issues.  It discourages the use of Fast Travel, which should not cost any currency at all! You shouldn't be punished for moving about the island quickly at the end game, but yet I'm running from the Isolation Cell to the Yacht because I only have 10 crystals.Nightmare Puzzles:  Why even bother?  This would be something I would just have edited out of the game.  You got the Cosmos upgrade, great... now you can access these terminals.  The making of the symbols in the Nightmare puzzles was overly simple.  The interface was super clunky.  You could easily shift to the wrong spaces on the controller, so it did nothing but anger me every time I had to do one.Visual Novel: The scale of the visual novel was probably correct.  It would have been nice if this was set up more like Ace Attorney where I could go to different areas, do a little investigation, and interrogate the character there.  It would have flowed much better.  Instead, I had to keep zipping back and forth to people to do the hang outs.  The Hang Outs felt very added on, and just there to make the game longer.  Would have been nice to fast travel back and forth to people, and just burned the blood crystals, but the timer prevented you from doing that.  Another system causing conflict with the system.The sub-screen: I really wish the interface and the sub screen were better organized.  The case notes were really helpful in knowing what to do next, and the file organizations actually did organize the information well.  I thought that was well done.  But the controller would sometimes his the evidence to clear out the "!" mark and then you wouldn't be able to scroll back up to someone else's testimony forcing you to back out of the record, and then go back into it.  Which leads me to:Collectibles:  Why? This was such a tedious exercise.  I haven't gotten 1... and I mean 1... of the red crests to finish that one puzzle.  My level of caring is so low after the crazy amounts of work I did to find all the others.  When I see that "6.4% of players" have all the Island Sequence Memories, I'm left wondering if it really was worth it. It feels like a lot of the achievements just aren't worth the effort.The ending: Satisfying?  Meh.  I think the most satisfying thing is knowing that it's over.All in all, I really think Paradise Killer would have been better if it was more linear.  There's too many conflicting things to do, when the core of the game is the world building visual novel. Take away the blood crystals, excessive exploration, and collection tasks, it would have been a nice compact and tight game.  It just needs heavy editing to remove a lot of the bad pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun experience that's not really like any other game I've played before. The characters, setting and lore are all interesting and contain a depth that makes them exciting to learn about over the course of the game. The premise of the murder you work to solve is compelling, and the way the game approaches constructing the truth and enacting justice at the end is innovative and allows a shocking amount of room for player input. Paradise Killer is one of the best experiences I've had with a game in a while, and my only complaint is that I wish there was more. [EDIT: They just released a huge free update with more!!] The pacing is up to you, as the world is wide open for the entirety of the game, but the mystery moves along at a pace as you learn more that, even if you take your sweet time, doesn't make any of it feel slow. I highly recommend this game to anyone who's interested in the concept, even if this genre isn't usually what they go for. Paradise Killer is a fantastic experience, and I'm really looking forward to seeing what Kaizen Game Works does next after playing it.

Secondly, the resolution of the mystery is a bit disappointing, since it breaks one of the Knox Rules of Mystery, but the ride trying to figure it out is still a blast, even if my theories were proven wrong.Lady Love Dies is the investigator the world needs.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bizarre game to be sure, but one I thoroughly enjoyed. Went in completely blind (other than the premise of being an investigator solving a murder) and came out pleasantly surprised.It's a perfect weekend killer - I managed to find all the collectibles, find all of the evidence, and reach the end in about 10 hours flat. I'd say the other hour of my play-through was probably just the game running in the background. Characters and setting are interesting, and while the less said about the plot the better, it has enough "angles" to keep you interested for the duration of your play-through.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a very good whodunit. It's magical for more, other reasons, though.I feel like this game may have been conceived during a conversation between friends watching some sort of cheesy movie or playing a grimdark occult game. "Why are cultists always so grimdark? Why do they have to wear black, hooded robes and cover everything in skulls and ♥♥♥♥? Why would they be so ominous about everything, when summoning horrors from beyond the void is what they actually want? Wouldn't they celebrate it instead?""What would they be into instead?""What is everybody into right now? Synthwave. Vaporwave. Some kinda neon, candy-coated vision of the eighties."And, well, here you go. Purple, opalescent sculptures of things humanity was never meant to see. Gilded, white stone terraces overlooking shimmering tropical waters, studded with pyramids meant for untold horrors. Unremarkable canal-side condominiums with beach views, full of --Well, no spoilers.I caught myself sitting here multiple times, staring at my screen, trying to imagine what the setting would have looked like if the things under discussion were being portrayed the way they're usually, stereotypically portrayed in a story. It broke my brain. Paradise Island is a vision.The music is still on loop in my head three days after finishing it. I want a sequel, but I'm not sure how that could ever work. Maybe the devs will find a way. I wouldn't put it past them. They managed to make candy-coated cosmic horror work beautifully, layered on top of what would already have been a very good detective mystery.Looking forward to seeing what they do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a wonderful, wacky detective game of the likes I've never played. The game is two games in one. The bigger part of the game is a first-person walking sim where you wander around a VR dayglo vaporwave island picking up random collectables that add to the lore and occasionally provide evidence in the cases you are investigating. The smaller part of the game is an Ace Attorney-style visual novel that triggers when you enter into dialog with the characters or start the final trial.The walking sim section is the better game. The vaporwave aesthetic is perfect, and it's a delight to wander the buildings and the beaches listening to the relaxing synthpop soundtrack. There are no jumping puzzles, no timed puzzles, no enemies, so you can investigate at your own pace. You feel like a real detective, checking out different locations, hacking locks and scouring the scene for clues. The world is aggressively weird at first, but as you persevere with the lore you start to get a feel for this strange island and its culture.The VN section is a bit less successful. The dialog itself is well-written, and although the characters exist in a bizarre, alien world, they feel believable in that context. Uncovering their motives is a lot of fun, as is flirting and engaging in casual banter... But by the end it feels like there is little emotional weight behind any of the relationships, because the light-hearted tone of the dialog doesn't change even when you uncover clear evidence of guilt. Then at the trial you can choose to accuse and convict anyone you like, which results in summary executions that none of the surviving characters react to either. I understand the technical reason - if the developers had set up a more linear storyline with scripted emotional beats, then it would undermine the open world/free roam investigative concept - but it's still a bit of a let-down.All that said, if you like walking sims or detective games, Paradise Killer is worth buying. It has a strong aesthetic, the world is deep, the characters feel believable (at least during the early/mid-game) and it is a ton of fun investigating the crimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most stylistically confident and unique adventure games of late. It is immensely fun to explore the island at your own pace and untangle not only the crime itself but the imaginative and weird world building and it's many mysteries. Add to that fleshed-out characters, nice music and a world that's at the same time comfy and deeply unsettling and you get a vivid, memorable experience. A great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of my absolute favourites -- this was so unique in terms of storyline. I loved the mix in gameplay, between point-and-click for dialogues and choices combined with just enough movement to keep it low production budget while enjoyable at the same time. A perfect combination of enough side-quests with in-game achievements for a lazy day, as well as plot that keeps you guessing! Love the characters too!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game that I didn't know I wanted to play until I did. I'm not big on detective stuff or puzzle games typically but I loved every aspect of this story from beginning to end. I was enthralled enough that I binged the entire game in one sitting, which is saying something because this isn't a really short game like I was expecting it to be. I've never played the ace attorney games but from what I can tell, if you're a fan of them and you like vaporwave/cyberpunk design then this game is a must-have. Totally worth the money and I'd recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an open world mystery game that borrows inspiration from Suda51's works and writing style. Because it's an open world game, the mystery, combined with visual novel elements seen in games like Ace Attorney or Dangan Ronpa, is presented in a way I have not seen in any game before. Unlike other visual novel based mysteries, the game emphasizes a freedom of choice in both movement, discovery, and pursuit of the truth by allowing players to use the facts of the case to their choosing. The facts of the mystery are the same each time, but there's room for subjectivity on the player's part.While the plot is in some ways standard mystery fare, I would say the real star of the game is the world and lore itself. The island is a gorgeous, well-designed environment with an obvious vaporwave aesthetic along with an incredible and well-considered soundtrack that's worth owning on its own. The island is enjoyable to explore and observing the different districts and how they function in this computer built society is interesting. The setting is a high concept, esoteric sci-fi involving a cult-based society that struggles to create a utopia while battling off demons and insurrection. While there are a ton of collectibles covering the island that deliver random lore tidbits, talking to other characters and finding out about the world through osmosis while playing as someone who's been away for years is plenty to understand the world you're living in.The execution of the mystery can be very subjective, but I do think if you go into this imagining something purely like Dangan Ronpa or other mystery thriller VNs, you'll do yourself a disservice. This game is not purely its mystery, but also the universe it has created for itself and if you're sold on that aspect and its aesthetic, this game is WELL worth your time. It's an absolute delight to wander around in and the amount of universe given to the player is not too little or too much to be satisfying. Definitely a game that took me by surprise and stands out to me among all the games I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I wanted in an investigation type game.It takes a bit, and not every character is going to cooperate with you, but that helps make it oh-so satisfying to finish.Paradise itself has quite a lot to offer, mainly in its collectables which, while its not much, does add to some worldbuilding.The main puzzles itself are nice and simple, Which is nice to help keep the pace going.I'd say its worth it at full price, and a good amount of replays.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Ace Attorney/Danganronpa, you might *not* enjoy this. Despite a lot of comparisons being drawn between PK and those series, I see that as a bit of a stretch. While PK is a murder investigation game with plenty of dialogue and evidence, the similarities fall apart there. The trial does not involve punching holes through witness testimony, you don't get to know if you made errors in judgement, and there is only one grand trial for everything (albeit with multiple parts). If those are the similarities you were looking for in PK, I recommend doing a little bit of research into this game before deciding whether you want to play it.Personally, I never felt the "click" while playing this game that I did with many other mystery/detective games that I love (Ace Attorney, Danganronpa, Return of the Obra Dinn, Nancy Drew, Her Story, Shenmue, Zero Escape). However, PK was a confidently executed, fresh take on the genre and I'm excited to see what may follow after it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very interesting Myst-like game where you explore a giant interesting island with  of nooks and crannies to amazing music. The goal is to figure out the clues to a murder, but as long as you're talking to characters the game automatically compiles notes, and if you still can't figure it out you can pay for clues.  For the asking price you can't find a better adventure-esque game.   Easy 9/10 from me. Also, a lot of people are complaining about the ending.  It's not bad at all, and frankly I find fitting for a murder mystery such as this.
