_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a decent deductive game that has arguably too many collectibles (even with the in-game searching upgrade) that ultimately detract from the game for me. Instead of investigating, my completionist tendencies took over, leading all of my interest away from the mystery. Upon gathering all evidence and having all the conversations, the actual presentation of your deductions is lackluster and ultimately has no impact in some ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game reignited my passion for video games and got me excited for what we'll be able to do with the medium with enough time, creativity, and talent.Immediately you are thrown into the world of Paradise KIller, and it seems like everything has been crafted in-world and has been there all along, from the branding on song packaging, to each and every character and their connections in the world.Characters are well-crafted both writing and design-wise, with a nice blend of Jodorowsky extravagance and Jojo's bizzare Adventure-ness permeating through their designs, while maintaining a feeling of uniqueness.The music is phenomenal; it is a drive through the city outskirts under a digital hot pink sunset orchestrated, and matches the tone of Paradise Killer perfectly, from the low-key synth's accompanied by cruising, distorted electric guitar ballads, to electronic organ solo's, creating a modern interpretation of 80's synth and euro pop with it's own unique personality.Minor gameplay element spoilers below:All in all, the game is a solid 9/10 for me, in that it provides something new, fresh, and exciting, and implements it's ideas, themes, and story in a well-crafted game with a few minor hiccups. It's current reviews and relative success is a testament to the clear time, effort, and love the developers poured into this game, and I can't wait to see more from them.But why are you reading this? Who am I to tell you what the truth is? Do you want facts or truth?It's time to breathe life back into paradise.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This a great mystery game, but it's emphasis is mostly on the Exploration and Investigation side. It's very fun and very satisfying to piece the story together. But where this game REALLY stands out is the worldbuilding and setting. Not only is the world uniquely done, but all of the unique aspects are important to the story and not just there for flavor. Great soundtrack, great aesthetics, great story. If you're looking for a fun mystery game with a fresh take, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: -Music is really nice on its own and also fits the game’s vibe perfectly-The story is intriguing, keeps you want to move forward all the way till the end-A seemingly well-thought-out world was built to encase the game and similarly various and interesting characters inhabit it-Massive amounts of accessibility settings-While the base controls feel off, you can rebind almost everything, or just get used to it being slightly flawed-I find the visual representation of the protagonist doesn’t fit with either their character nor their voice actress-while not ugly per say, graphics certainly could be way better-failure to commit (ie. giving a character a personality of swearing a lot, but not actually having “♥♥♥♥” in the sentence, but rather f**k – why not just decide one way or another and commit? Or the case of the phallos demon actually not showing their wood or the case of voice overs below)-partial voice acting takes away both the pleasure of listening to a nice dub and at the same time the immersion of reading conversation and imagining whatever voice you’d like for each participant-around the 10th or so hour, running back and forth between characters for just 1 line updates becomes a bit jarring-surprisingly no steam achievements, if you’re into thoseWhile the Paradise Killer experience starts out rough on the back of weird sounding sentences and a rough control scheme, I’d say it takes an hour tops to get used to both of these. As you get into the game and start finding out more and more of the worlds and the events that took place, .For more detail on the above points and a look at gameplay, please join me as I elaborate on my thoughts in this video:.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a detective game in a rather open world (well, island, but there's a lot to explore) in which your goal is not to deduce the facts but to create a truth from the facts you find. And since this isn't a mathematical equation, that's slightly more complicated than you may believe.To create your truth, you will need to learn a very important lesson - you gain nothing by catching people on a lie, so don't make a big deal out of it if you do. Your truth will need to be assembled from the moments in which they were  lying to you, and you need to learn to spot those moments, otherwise you'll never be able to put the pieces together.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What a friggin journey. Except for one rather important clue, which seemed a bit too obscure and almost impossible to find without help, this is a very well constructed mystery narrative. Interesting characters, very intriguing lore and a beautiful, nostalgia-driven 80's vibe, mixed with occultism and cosmic horror, this game delivers a memorable experience within a manageable time frame. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game was absolutely amazing. While I did have a few gripes with the game it didn't take away from the over-all experience that it lends itself to.Positives: The game is absolutely gorgeous. I'm not sure if it is inspired by Danganronpa but if it is it shows brilliantly in the artwork, from the 3d landscapes that are absolutely stunning in their colors as well as how they are over-all designed mixed with the 2d artwork of the complex and creative characters. The story was also quite creative. It left me guessing in quite a few places, and ultimately it was a fine game of being absolutely certain on the guilt of one half, and everything falling into place by time the trial happened. It was fantastic. I also found the world building amazing, from the characters themselves making me fall in love with them to the general lore of the world such as the various gods that existed to the entire system that the paradises function in, and by the end of the game I was still hungry to learn more about the world and revisit this setting again, even if it wasn't necessarily with the characters I grew to like.Mixed: Theres only one thing that I truly dislike about the game, and only one thing I feel mixed about. Their minor nitpicks, but it would be unfair not to list them. I loved the world building, the way the world was introduced to you, and the implications the lore had in the grand scheme of things, but at the same time it made me feel like I was drowning in information. As it stands, I wouldn't have it any other way and I wouldn't want the sequel to change in its world building, but as I have seen somewhere else it feels like your playing a sequel or reading the second novel of a series. Your given a lot of information your expected to know, and never really explained this information bluntly. Your left to pick up pieces and interpret the lore as you go. Its not terrible, and I quite enjoyed it, but at the same time I almost would be hard pressed to say I don't know much about this world in general. I want to know more about it.Negatives: The one negative I have is about one of the final parts of the game. At one part of the game I had pretty much talked to everyone, 'befriended' everyone, and thought I had gathered all the evidence. I'm fairly certain I hadn't, as I did find that I was missing one piece of evidence at the end of the game, but at that point I was convinced I had figured everything out. I would have started the trial without a key piece of evidence that completely exposes the main killer. I found it by complete accident. It didn't ruin the game, but I was starting to have problems by that point and wish the location of this last critical piece of evidence was better hinted at, or in a better location.Over-all: It was fantastic. It had problems, but they were so minor that it didn't subtract from the game itself in the slightest. I hope they continue this world in some fashion. Thank you for the fantastic experience, and I couldn't recommend more even if I tried!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: What I thought I was getting was a Phoenix Wright game that was just one big case, and it's up to you to know when the mystery is solved and you're ready to move on from the investigation phase to the trial phase.  What I actually got was a game with no incorrect dialogue options, and summaries of everything you learn.  That makes it so as long as you follow the leads in your notebook and look for the two(?) pieces of evidence in the world, you can't possibly fail to put the mystery together.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about this game from the vaporwave aesthetic to the music and dialogue. It reminds me of when I explored games on the N64 as a child, finding ways to platform around to gather items. At the same time Paradise Killer has a Phoenix Wright feel to it with gathering evidence and pressing for testimony, and depending on your approach, you can form your own narrative. The game's simplicity works in its favor and has a lasting impression after completion.I really liked the world, its characters and overall story that I really hope the team decides to make a sequel. I haven't binge-played a game like this in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting mix of Danganronpa/Visual Novel/Open-world exploration with a heavy dose of vaporwave aesthetic sprinkled all over it.The gameplay is all about building up evidence/statement/alibis/alibi-breakers surrounding several aspects of the Big Murder Case the protagonist gets called out of exile to solve, all for a final trial showdown after you feel you collected enough evidence on your Starlight laptop and have a good idea of who did what.   If I had to give it a numerical score it would be around  so I do end up recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I disliked the massive amount of walking back-and-forth between the characters to interrogate them, but I loved the adventurous aspect of this game. The game world is strange, beautiful and a joy to explore. Even after 10 hours I came across a part of the map that I'd completely missed somehow. Great soundtrack, it was a really relaxing time and just what I needed.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, so sad I finished it! I may even play it again. Lots of fun investigating a complicated murder. I really appreciated there being no pressure to complete the investigation cuz I can't take no mo pressure right now and just wanna putz around and pick up blood crystals sometimes. But when I was ready, I finished the game by engaging in the trials.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion is kinda mixed, in some ways I was dissapointed, in other ways I was positively surprised.The main dissapointment is this game is not the detectice/ace attorney game I was half expecting. I was kinda looking forward to the moment I'd have to dig through the evidence record for that one critical fact, but that moment never came. But on the other hand, the atmosphere and characters made this just an actually enjoyable world to walk around in. And when the investigation was nearing its end, I was wistfully walking through areas I knew I wouldn't see anymore. The combination of characters, music, and for lack of a better word "vaporwave aesthetic" made the ~11 hours actually fly by though, so thumbs up
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing investigative experience. You'll need a few hours in order to completely understand the story that unfolded and is unfolding before you but after that, is a boundary-free, completely surreal experience.The investigation is entertaining and rewarding, and the vaporwave atmosphere simply amazing (the OST does a wonderful job). I just wished for a more nuanced final trial - if you gather enough clues, there's no real failure chance. I wished there were more games like this! I fell in love with every part of the story and the island.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, low stress, exploration murder mystery game full of great lore and creepy surreal cosmic cults.  If you enjoy poking at corners and finding ways up and over obstacles for the hell of it, you will love this game.  The music is amazing and so is the whole aesthetic.I spent most of my early play just exploring places rather than talking to NPCs and it added to the slow buildup of "What is wrong with this place?!? WHAT IS EVEN GOING ON?" a bit more entertaining, but by no means is it the only way to play it.If there is anything I'm sad about, it's that I wanted more lore/secrets/easter eggs to find.  I give this game 5 out of 5, totally fun and worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The game was generally well organized and relatively fun, but the ending was not worth the time spent investigating. I was hoping for almost a "danganrompa" like experience, but the investigation was the meat of the game, not the trial. The lore and writing were very well done; no complaints with anything but the structure of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with it, but I also don't plan on playing it any time soon. I consider it basically a walking sim, running around the cool environments and enjoying the music. The trial at the end was also fun, as depending on the evidence you found, you could incriminate anyone or even everyone. Most of the talking to people during the main game was tedious and annoying though. The plot and characters are definitely overrated, this is some simple shallow stuff essentially.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining open-world visual novel that has the player running around solving a conspiracy, speaking to suspects and collecting evidence in any order that they choose.I hesitate to call this a great detective game however, as the player's computer companion automates most of the brain work. The endgame trial is a pretty big letdown as well, as the player will "achieve victory" regardless of who they accuse and the evidence they present.Still, I had a great time with Paradise Killer. Catchy tunes and memorable characters. I would recommend it to others who are looking for a fun mystery that doesn't take itself too seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly this one didn't do it for me. Being a huge Fan of Ace Attorney and Danganronpa i was very excited when I saw that one at the PC Gamer Show in 2020. So be warned I am gonna draw some comparisons to those games in this review. If you don't think that's fair you should probably read a different review.Anyway the first impression of the game was very nice for me. It had an interesting cast, the worldbuilding is interesting and something completely unique and the overall aesthetic is completely unmatched. However what kills it for me is the lack of a red threat throughout the story. It really does feel like an Ace Attorney or Danganronpa game but you are playing all 4-6 cases single game would have at the same time! You see, those games get often critisiced for being too linear, but that means you unravel the mysteries the way they were meant to be unraveled, one after the other. Paradise Killer gives you complete freedom in how to solve the case but that ends up with overwhelming you with details and new loose ends that I straight up kept forgetting what I am even investigating in the first place. Pair that with the fact that every single topic in the game is a dialouge option for each and every character on the Island. As you can imagine many times all a character can say about a very specific topic is "Sorry I don't know anything about that, you should ask XYZ about that!". This wouldn't be a problem if the games map wouldn't mark these as new dialouge everytime they unlock. So you might end up traveling across half the map and walk down paths you have already walked through five times to reach a character with "new dialouge options" just for them to tell you to get lost because why would they know what the Islands barkeeper had for breakfast at the morning of the murder (Exaggaration, i  don't think that was a plotpoint in the game). In ace attorney and Dangarnonpa you get like 3-5 Dialouge dialouge options for a character and those actually make sense asking. Sure not all of those are revealing critical plot points but at least they offer more than just "IDK LOL".At the end of it all, maybe it actually is me and not the game. Maybe some people will enjoy it for the exact reasons why I hated it. But after i realized that I just didn't care anymore because it felt like I spent 8 hours getting nowhere, I just kinda stopped. This was sadly not the cool "whodunit" I expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A slightly offputting start leads to a really fun and unusual murder mystery with an imaginative cast of characters and world, including some great worldbuilding and lore. Interesting that there was no true "canon" ending, rather the player is left to use the evidence and facts at their disposal to craft the truth narrative. Well worth playing, runs well on Steam Deck and will blast your eyes out of your head on an OLED in HDR.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is the Vaporwave, Lovecraftian, Ace Attorney-like game that I never knew I wanted.Hunting for both evidence and collectibles feels great as you explore the winding pathways of the 24th Paradise. The story is a complex web of intrigue woven around an interesting world of demons, gods, and the Syndicate Cult.The game offers a lot of freedom. Right off the bat, its up to you to decide when to start the trail whenever you fell confortable.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Half of the game I played offline, so the hours shown don't match what I actually played (about 15~16hrs).Seriously, it's been such a great experience. Bought it during the Steam Sales just before it was given to me on July 2021's Humble Bundle and have no regrets about not returning it.The exploration is pretty well done, although you have to move back and forth between characters every time you discover anything and fast travel has a limited currency paywall, so you decide you don't need to fast travel as everything is relatively close (may take 2-3 minutes in the endgame when you know everything, which is when you really have to move that much) and it can be bothersome at the end.You have trails about where to go and what to do at all times, so you'll never feel stuck. Some clues can only be obtained through increasing your relationship levels with others, so I would really encourage it.The trials can be accessed at any point you feel you have enough clues to pinpoint the crime to somebody, which is great. You can do whatever you want at any point, and have many places to explore so feel free to move around the island to uncover another piece of truth.I've been thinking about the game nonstop these days that I've been playing it, what really happened and who was involved in the crime. It really has been a great experience, and I would recommend it to anyone that has an interest in detective-like games. It is really fun too if what you are looking for is a collectathon. And the mixture of both is just glorious.Have fun in Paradise!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly not sure how I feel about this game. On the one hand, it is a pretty good mystery game with a very unique flavor and world to it that makes me want to always be learning more about it. On the other though, the gameplay mechanics themselves are tedious and the ending felt like I was intentionally fed two solutions on purpose for the sole purpose of making me unsure as to which was the right one. I spent some time painstakingly trying to figure out which was the correct answer and it turned out to not matter as much as I thought, which I found to be a bit of a let down. It could have been though that I was super tired from staying up late because I couldn't stop playing and my brain didn't fully understand. The gameplay was also quite tedious as it was a lot of running around somewhat aimlessly over a space that was simply too large.There were also quite a few core mechanics that were never explained and I wish I had known right out of the gate. Like hey you should go get a foot bath because that allows you to see any pickup items around you. Or hey you should go to all of the Syndicate symbols because those are the computer terminals to progress the main plot. Or hey, don't worry about fast travel costs, just get the foot bath so you can see pickup items and then you will never run out of blood crystals. I would have done like 50% less wandering aimlessly around if I had known this stuff to be honest.Overall though, I would play a Paradise Killer 2 with a cleaner ending and less tedious gameplay mechanics and would recommend this game for detective fans who want something genuinely unique and interesting.Also, the final version of the main song that plays throughout the game absolutely slaps.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a unique experience that I continue to think about. I wish I could see more of its characters and setting. You grow attached to (most) of the characters even some of the ones who are a bit rough around the edges. I went back to try the Ray Tracing options and honestly it did noticeably enhance the experience quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The vibes!  Great soundtrack, a fun mystery to solve filled with interesting characters, just enough optional collectibles to make exploration rewarding.  The colorful vaporwave aesthetics and extremely disturbing cosmic horror elements make for a really unique atmosphere that I could not get enough of.  Big recommendation here.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent! This game was part of my humblebundle monthly subscription, and it did NOT disappoint! I was stoked to be playing a story game with such interesting characters, but I was overwhelmed with nostalgia at the mechanics and look of the game. It felt very much like playing bunny tracks online maps of Unreal Tournament back in the day. Lastly, I would recommend this game to anyone interesting in stories with Lovecraftian lore!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I would caution people by saying that it IS ultimately a 10-15 hour walking simulator, so the easily bored might not enjoy it. On the other hand, if you are a fan of fantastic atmosphere and world building, and dont mind a bunch of reading, its a great game.Additionally, the exploration aspect is fantastic, and players who love discovering stuff and traversing first person open worlds will really enjoying how jam-packed the huge open world is with cool easter eggs.The city-pop inspired soundtrack is also top notch. (and available on spotify!!)All in all, a fantastic game for those who don't mind a more calm and cozy game over a action or shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetics speak for themselves: pop-vaporwave, bureaucratic pagan mysticism, and a lot of blood. The vaporwave deployment of archaeological visual motifs (cuneiform, pyramids, etc.) runs the risk of being corny and Orientalist at times, but the setting of  relates to "the real world" in such a way to be cohesive and interesting. and  are absolutely touchstones, among others, both for the character design as well as the core gameplay elements. That being said, there are some bold choices that make  unique:Overall,  wants you to engage with its geography and narrative atmosphere, and it expects you to be responsible for that. That means getting lost, picking up Blood Crystals (the currency), and collecting countless "meaningless" items, each containing a couple sentences of flavor text. Sure it may feel offensive to have to pay tokens for fast travel and other things, but the game gives you audio clues to find them, so just explore, and don't be scared of running out.The game doesn't strive for a singular climactic moment during the trial -- you accuse someone and exhaust the dialogue the game calculates from your evidence and choices. This is a breath of fresh air coming from the linearity of other investigation games whose endings are bogged down by riddles and monologues.  lets me make discoveries and deductions on my own, and doesn't make me perform them in the game. All that is expedited so  can do what other investigation games don't, which is to provide a world worth investigating alongside the crime.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 If you love detective style games where you have to go around and solve the murder, you're going to love this one. The artstyle is fine, the music is alright. The voices got a little irritating after a while so I just turned it off. The movement is basic, if a bit too floaty.But the NPCs are very fleshed out and have great emotions and feelings, the story is great, and the clues all come together at the end very nicely, which is important for a detective game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a compelling mystery with some fun characters. However, I felt like it was such a rough game overall. Getting around the island is a bit of a slog, and the environmental collectables and relics felt like a way to bloat out the map and the game. I realise that there are reasons for there to be so few people on the island, but it felt very artificially empty. Plus some areas of the map can just be so difficult and annoying to get through, like the residential areas.I really liked the unique format, especially with the entire game basically just being about solving one case. But I'd really only give the game a 6/10; its good, but it could have been a much more fun, smoother ride. Great setup and setting for a murder mystery, though - the story itself would easily be an 8/10, but the game around it disappointed me a little.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer isn’t a perfect game but it’s a very good time if you enjoy detective games, visual novels, and open world exploration. It’s not a typical combination but I think Danganronpa fans in particular will find it up their alley. The game sets you loose very quickly with only a tiny bit of background on your character, Lady Love Dies, and the murder mystery you need to solve. In some ways, it feels like you’re starting a series on the second entry, but it’s all just a design choice. Your character knows more than you, but eventually you piece most of the backstory together as you go and it feels quite rewarding. You’re very much free to do as you please, and the gameplay loop consists of traversing the island, picking up currency and collectibles, and sometimes key items and clues. You’ll talk to suspects to reveal new information, and then use that information to drag new clues out of the other suspects. If you look at this negatively, it means you’re spending a lot of time just walking back and forth from one suspect to another, again and again. But as you do this, you’ll start getting a much better feel for the island’s layout, the clues and mysteries will get more intriguing, and you’ll unlock abilities to make it easier to get around the island and find those precious collectibles.The game culminates in a grand trial where you present your evidence and declare who you think the guilty parties are. While not as in depth as an Ace Attorney trial by any means, it’s still an exciting and satisfying way to end the story. There’s still much left unexplained and unexplored about the world and characters (who are mostly all insane cultists living in an artificial realm when viewed from an outside perspective)- I would certainly bite if a sequel or prequel ever appeared. The visuals and overall vaporwave aesthetic are fantastic, and the game has recently added ray tracing support and other enhancements, including achievements. It’s a great time to jump in if you haven’t experienced the game yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: this game was great, the mystery was compelling the exploration never got tedious, the one thing I had an issue with was how momentum was affected while jumping, no matter what inputs the player did, they had 0 air control. overall I highly recommend this game for anyone with an interested in detective visual novel games, or people who enjoy exploring open worlds for secrets
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I like to wait a little time after playing a game to give it a proper review. It allows me to have some perspective on it and not go with my initial impulsive thoughts. The sound design, story and aesthetics in this game are killer. It's a special game indeed where I remember the audio so sharply and fondly in my mind. It is not without its flaws. The endless walking (noted by most reviewers as an annoying feature), the slightly dodgy map and the frustrating fast travel system could all be improved. It says something that I began to see this quirks as being charming as I continued to play the game. I accepted them as I accepted some of the buggier aspects of games I loved in childhood. I reflected on the virtues of the imperfect game, a game where its charm shines so particularly despite and because of its quirks.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer has the best of all worlds. Cosmic horror, excellent (and hot) character designs, demons, a plethora of world building including through collecting a mountain of items (something I personally enjoyed hunting down thoroughly), a killer soundtrack, diversity in its characters, queer representation, and was so infectiously delightful to play that I was thinking about playing it even when I wasn't doing so.In fact, it's a game that benefits breaks. I would be ruminating on the mystery unfolding while I made coffee in the morning, or while showering, and suddenly have an epiphany about something. Recall a place I should go back to and check, or make mental notes on what to do next. I was constantly rewarded for it as well, discovering the next piece of information, even if I didn't know where it fit in yet with everything else, was so gratifying.Every character in this is interesting in one way or another, but even besides that as a draw, the entire aesthetic and environment is endlessly satisfying. The game design and sound design has been thought out with such care that just punching the buttons to a vending machine, or hearing the familiar cackle meaning Shinji is nearby, is deeply satisfactory because of this. Everything from using Starlight and mousing over options, to the screen while the game saves, it all neatly fits into the universe built and makes it delightful.The impressive amount of lore behind everything from the gods to the inhabitants of the island made exploring all the more interesting, because not only was everything gorgeous, but there was meaning behind it. The statues, the monoliths, all of it was so pretty that I almost never used the fast travel. I was happy to just run around the island and take it all in, and because of that I grew so familiar with the huge map that it felt like home. There is just so much to discover, and I relished every moment of doing so. I already miss playing this game, and I will be hoping that there's more to come. Or some merch would be excellent. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what this was going in to it, and all I'd really seen was the cover and some screenshots, so I actually expected it to be an FPS. While there might not be much shooting involved, it certainly wasn't dull. Exploring the island is quite satisfying in itself. Being a lover of open world RPG's I love exploring in every nook and cranny to find stuff. That alone made it quite enjoyable, but then adding in a murder mystery and a few puzzles was a good touch to really tie it all together. Nothing too crazy, and thankfully not super long. Given all the text dialogue, had it gone on much longer, I think interest would have died off slowly. All in all, a very interesting, non realistic world to discover, and worth a look!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Overrated IMO. Not much deduction  for a detective game. Positives: Tells a story where the you and everyone else is still complicit in a heinous and absurd system.Open world system is pretty neat. I think more detective games should incorporate this.The writers put a lot of heart and effort in crafting characters.Negatives:Basically no deduction at all. The ending and some gross looking textures leave a little bit more to be desired, but overall a super fun game that I beat in less than 24 hours after buying because I was so engaged.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where you investigate an increasingly complex mass murder as an immortal who was locked away for roughly 8,000 years. This is a game where you run around a beautifully constructed island dense with things to find, puzzles to solve, and mysteries to uncover. This is a game where the vibes and aesthetics and music all come together to be excellent. It manages to blend a funky vaporwave-ish beachtown with ancient dread gods and the repeated enslavement & mass sacrifice of mortals. I had a very good time with Paradise Killer. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A great game to play in the final weeks of summer. Island 24 is dying and Perfect 25 is coming; will it really be perfect? Would we even know perfection if we saw it? Was paradise really worth saving? Was it really saved at all?I think this game would be better classified as an open-world walking simulator/visual novel. The "investigation" really consists mostly of exploring the island and picking up collectibles. Some are relevant to the story, many are not, and there's usually no way to tell the difference. So if you want a true detective game, this probably won't be it, but if you're happy with just exploring a vaporwave paradise island with elements of cosmic horror and some really great music, this is definitely for you. It did get a little frustrating trying to get all the collectibles by the end, but overall I had a great time with it. The music, aesthetic, and overall themes were more than enough to keep me engaged the whole time and a little sad when it ended.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It is weird. It is not a standard game, but if you are after a narrative detective game that rewards exploration this is for you. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a vaporwave acid trip unlike anything I've ever experienced. Its an open-world detective game that doesn't hold your hand for a second. It lets you wander around this incredible setting to find or miss clues as you go and then you decide when you've figured it all out and take it to trial. The accusations and conclusions are your own.The setting itself is wild and deeply thought-out, with graphics that are as strange, beautiful, horrifying, and cool as the world they're portraying. Plus, a dope soundtrack.There should be no hesitancy in picking up and playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best mystery games I've played recently.  The game's setting is fearlessly original, and by far the highlight of the game.  The writing is very good throughout, and the plot is well-constructed.  On the other hand, some of the exploration parts were a bit tedious, and I feel like I could've gotten stuck a few times if I hadn't gotten lucky.  Still, this was an enjoyable experience, and at ~20 hours it's the perfect length.  Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an open world visual novel, the visual novel aspect of this game is good, but the open world aspect, not so much. A game with a good story that is unfortunately undone by it's  monotonous open world traversal and gameplay loop. The environments look fun and are vibey, but really lack detail and storytelling. The world design and environment sorts of break down in to a monotonous maze in which you are constantly battling against it's verticality and winding passageways to get to a character or a piece of evidence. The game world is filled with meaningless collectibles that don't really incentivize exploration. However, Paradise Killer's lore is exceptional. One of the most unique settings that I've ever seen in the video game medium. A trans-dimensional religious cult called the Syndicate utilizes humans from alternate realities to assist in the re-summoning of dead gods. Syndicate members are high society and live forever, toiling at their endless attempts to summon the gods. Demon's endlessly assault the syndicate corrupting their efforts which requires them to recreate their reality (island) to start the process anew. Each iteration of the island is an attempt at creating a perfect incorruptible environment. It's really cool stuff. The game also has a really great city pop soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but in the case of Paradise Killer I'll make an exception because it's one of the most unique and interesting games I've ever played. The world is completely insane and yet feels cohesive and lived in, with characters as believable as they are memorable. The murder mystery gameplay manages to be simple without being boring, and there's a massive amount of collectable artefacts and currency to encourage you to explore the map. It helps if you're as much of a sucker for some top tier vaporwave aesthetic as I am...This has quickly risen to being one of my favourite games of all time, and I really hope we see a Paradise Killer 2 at some point!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Some games are just made for you.So, when I first read about Kaizen Game Works’  – a murder mystery on a weird tropical island – I figured it would be exactly my kind of paradise. Glitzy and cool and dangerous, with plenty neon. It was, and maybe that would’ve been enough. But to my immense pleasure it turned out to be oh so much more.Describing the game isn’t easy; it’s such a singular experience. Playing it, I kept thinking of an episode of Michael Mann’s 1980s cop show, , where one of the characters, Trudy, encountered a UFO. That episode is not much liked, and for good reason. It’s a bit of a far cry from the drug cartels and corrupt yuppies Crockett and Tubbs spent their time fighting. Sometimes genre-blending just doesn’t work. Yet in a weird way,  inadvertently asks where that UFO came from and what it wanted with Trudy - answering it in the wildest way possible.If she  been whisked away, Trudy would have found herself on a metaphysical island with a population of human slaves governed by immortal aliens who are trying to bring their ancient gods back to life. Trudy wouldn’t have liked that and eventually would have been sacrificed in a blood ritual as the next island came into being. Because these islands keep failing, right. Failing miserably to achieve their eschatological ends. So, they get rebooted. Perfectionism’s a ♥♥♥♥♥.The world of  is bizarre. Overwhelmingly so. It’s loaded with lore – a dreaded word and, in the wrong hands, easily the real paradise killer. But in a masterstroke of storytelling,  makes that absurdity the point. Even though you’re reading a ton of text and reaching for esoteric details, it’s conveyed as part of the  of the place.That place, the island, is deserted, save the depraved Syndicate who govern it, and the cruelty of its existence is as bright as its false sun. Its overloaded history has produced a cadre of mad, evil, scheming immortals, whose conspiracies warrant the arrival of Lady Love Dies – the “investigation freak”. Someone has murdered the island’s council, and no one’s moving on until she learns whodunit.The open-world island is massive and gorgeous. With its aesthetic beauty and eccentric characters, it’s something totally unique. I couldn’t get enough of being there, even though there’s a relative parsity of stuff to  do. Mostly you’ll be looking for clues, finding collectables, and speaking with suspects. It’s in the latter that  comes brilliantly to life.Whether it’s the flirty playfulness of Doctor Doom Jazz or the cool condescension of Carmelina Silence,  suspects are perfect whodunit material. Lady Love Dies has been out of action for a while – an unfortunate exile involving a demon – so some of these people are new, but others are old friends. What they all are is guilty of , and diagnosing that guilt is your job. Every conversation sharpens your understanding of the crime, leading to fresh clues and surprising confessions.The web of intrigue is complex, and unravelling it is properly electrifying. When you feel like you’ve put all the pieces in place, it’s up to you who to accuse. For my part, I felt I’d achieved a real sense of catharsis, and yet I was sure I’d missed some minute clue that allowed one of the lesser culprits to wriggle free. Sure because as much as that island was something of a dream, it was an evil dream, and absolutely everyone in it a monster. In that context, guilt is a strange and heightened phenomenon......but I guess some things never die.* I went the whole review without mentioning the ECSTATICALLY GOOD soundtrack. For shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's "fine".The game is basically a walking simulator collectathon for 8 hours while you go talk to people and collect evidence. I'm sure there's an audience for that type of game, but I'm not it.The trial felt underwhelming. I was expecting a Danganronpa/Phoenix Wright style trial where you need to select proper evidence/rebuttals, but you basically just pick a person and show the evidence to convict them. No real deduction is needed.Following the evidence and piecing together the story was pretty fun, but there's at least a 2-3 hour time investment of mundane searching before you get to that point.There's a good game in here, but I don't think the time investment is worth the payoff.But you can abuse physics to wavedash to move stupidly fast once you get a certain upgrade, which made grinding a bit more bearable. The "fast travel" ironically takes too long and is a waste of time imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, it's kind of like one huge open world chapter of an Ace Attorney game but in an alternate reality. The art of all the characters is really striking, the music is good, the alternate world babylon is really fun. I was actually pretty surprised with how big the island was and how much there was to explore. I liked to come back and chat with most of the characters over and over and see all their reactions. The trial at the end was a lot of fun--I thought it was going to be more serious, like an Ace Attorney trial (you know, no mistakes) but it was really refreshing to see that there was some flexibility to have different outcomes. The achievements for this game were really fun to get as well. With some games its such a drag to collect 100% of the game objects or whatever, but I really didn't want this game to end. Maybe there will be more crimes to investigate on Perfect 25?
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent! My one piece of advice if you pick this up: The foot baths are worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, definitely recommend. I stayed up way too late several times playing it. 8.5/10The character design is so fresh and 3-dimensional - I loved interrogating them. Really outstanding art direction and OST too. I had a great time digging into this story layer by layer. I was also really pleased to see so many accessibility options built into the game.I was disappointed by the ending and the final twist, which seemed inconsistent/sudden. The handling was also a little awkward on PC - seems like it's designed more intuitively for a controller. Overall, worth the time and money. It was aesthetic and it was fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: your enjoyment of this game will likely hinge on how much you like the open world setting. It's a world with a few puzzles, lots of collectables, and no combat, and you are encouraged to look through every single nook and cranny first before using fast travel (you need blood crystals to unlock and use fast travel, and they're scattered throughout the map). There's also no compass to tell you your exact position on the map and where you're going; you're left to try to figure out for yourself where you need to go/what you need to do next. I personally love the open world setting but if what I described might be a problem you might have more fun just sticking with the Ace Attorney games.  With all that said, I cannot recommend Paradise Killer enough. The mystery is intriguing, the investigation is full of twists and turns, the ensemble cast is fantastic, and the whole aesthetic of the game is just absolutely gorgeous. Without spoiling too much, while the game does imply that there is a 'correct' route, you ultimately decide how the game ends and what defines 'justice', especially as you gather more evidence and build your relationships with the suspects. It's a game that will make you question your choices, and if you're into games that make you think and stay under your skin for awhile, you've come to the right place. Go play Paradise Killer now!

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a one-of-a-kind murder mystery game that is set in an almost-utopian, synthetic world. I have mixed feelings with some parts of the game, but I truly enjoyed the experience as a whole. It can definitely be a hit or miss for some, so here's reasons why this game is or isn't for you.Plus: 1. Amazing charactersI mean, come on, when have you played a murder mystery where the suspects readily show off their abs to the detective? The art style and character designs are all so amusing, and their voice acting complements them perfectly. If you ever wonder what fashion is like in a concrete, synthesised parallel universe, then this game manifests that concept into reality with their quirky characters.2. Lore is very interestingAside from investigating a murder, you also get to explore the island as the investigator and get to collect stuff/ talk to people. There's apparently a lot to learn about the Paradise Island, which delves into the existence of supernatural beings and how the island started. While some parts of the lore uses abstract language and it might be confusing to understand at first, it all makes more sense the longer you play the game and you learn to connect the dots yourself. Understanding the lore is actually important to solving the case as well.3. Very Unique but consistent theme (and music that I can vibe to all night)The theme of Paradise Killer is Vaporwave, which is a subgenre of electronic music/visual arts + retrofuturism. This is the only game (to my knowledge) that uses this theme and implements it so well. Just from looking at the character art, I already knew I'll be in for a special ride. The flamboyant character design, GUI, music, and somewhat abstract story-telling ties in to the theme of Vaporwave itself, and I love how the devs took such an unconventional approach in a murder-mystery game. Also, the music is an easy 11/10 for me. I might be biased because of my love of vaporwave and therefore I'm more forgiving of the games' imperfections (which is written below), but even so, this game is so memorable even after I completed it.4. Deep Story that is well-explainedWith a murder involving an entire island, this game does a good job in explaining to the players the suspects' motives and classifying the evidence in an orderly manner. For a relatively complex plot, it was quite easy to understand what's going on because the evidence management system in this game is implemented really well. Evidence is sorted based on who has ties with it, and the motives for every character seemed sensible. I really hate murder mysteries where the motive is weak or unintentionally creates a plot hole, but this game is consistent in their narrative.Minus:1. Limited Logical GameplayLet's get this straight. This game is a murder mystery game, but NOT a detective game. (although you play as an investigator) Don't expect it to be like Danganronpa or Ace Attorney where you make logical deductions, because the game already does that for you. Your job is basically collecting evidence and see what the protagonist says about it. This makes the final trial less interesting, as based on the evidence that are already explained to you, you don't get to figure anything out yourself.2. Walk-and-Collect SimulatorWhile there is a fair share of talking with the wonderful band of characters, the majority of the time you'll spend in this game is travelling around the island to collect stuff. There's literally so many collectibles that it becomes a chore to get them all. Of course, you can skip the extra collectibles, but there's always a dreaded feeling of where and what you might've missed while collecting evidence. Sure, exploring the Paradise Island is fun, and the level design is great, but it does get a bit draggy after a while. This is the number one reason why this game is not for you, especially if you're looking for more "gameplay".3. Overly-simple and uninteresting PuzzlesTo address point no. 2, I think it would help if there are puzzles that could make the game more than just a walking simulator, which this game does have. However, the puzzles are very simple and doesn't feel creative. It mostly involves matching a bunch of symbols and pressing random buttons. The parkour places are also lacking in this game even though movement is its primary gameplay. Even a place (avoiding to name it to avoid spoilers) which I expect to be the center of attention is fairly lacklustre in its level design.4. Inconsequential ActionsThe journey through Paradise Island is a refreshing and memorable one, but your actions don't seem to matter in the end. Of course, you get to decide who ends up being the blackened, but there are no ending branches after the epilogue. You could literally accuse other people in another playthrough and it still shows the same credit rolls before blacking out, as if nothing changed in the future. I think this is a weakness of this game's narrative, but one quote they do emphasise frequently in this game is how "facts and truth are not the same". Maybe this is a deliberate choice to make the player  think whether they've missed anything from their investigation. Regardless, I have mixed feelings about this.5. (Personal Preference) Lack of full voice actingThis is more of an "I wish" scenario rather than a drawback of the game. The voice actors of this game really portray the characters well, the only problem is that they only say snippets of the characters lines. For example, they'll just say a few phrases that are iconic to them rather than the whole text. I understand that not all games have or can have full voice acting, but it's such a shame that this game doesn't because the voice actors are wonderful. They could at least implement it in the trial and I'd be happy with it. I'm looking forward to the devs' next project, and if they have full voice acting to go with their characters, I think that'd be awesome.TL:DR This game is more of a walking collector simulator than a detective-logic-puzzle game. But if you like vaporwave theme/music and you're in it for the story not gameplay, buy it. Otherwise browse other games or wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; Detective Conan on LSD feat. David Lynch - The Walking SimulatorThis is a rather unique game, with its combination of deep world building, weird and quirky characters, the neon-bright tropical island setting and its zealous themes and architecture. In it's core it's a detective game where you, "the investigation freak", explore an island and all its nooks and crannies, as well as talking to the various inhabitants, to find clues that help you solve various crimes linked to the mass-murder of the island's council.First of all, there's a lot to explore, from hidden rooms to artefacts, vending machines and even secret characters. Oddly enough, the devs did not enable achievements it seems, even though this game is something of a collectathon, with a ton of hidden objects scattered throughout the world. Most of them serve as currency, which after a bit of exploring you should have enough of to buy anything you can, so don't feel like you have to save up, while the rest is used for world building (although some are gameplay-relevant as well).Speaking of which, this game does a great job of creating a really unique and seemingly deep world, that has a rich past, it's own rules and traditions and confidently radiates a certain vibe. More games should be this brave and venture away from the boringly over-used themes of Greek mythology, Middle Ages, angsty teen dramas etc. and just build their own world. Kaizen surely succeeded in that and it makes the game feel fresh and interesting.It might be important to also note that there is no combat in this game, it really is just a walking simulator with parkour elements and dialogue. There are sometimes choice options in the dialogue but they seem to be more flavour than actually affecting anything. Technically, there are also puzzles thrown into the mix, but they feel more like an alibi and are easily the weakest part of the game. They are neither difficult nor engaging. Some are crucial to entering closed off areas and finding the most important clues. Others only have currency rewards, which I found a little disappointing. The strength definitely lies in the plot and the odd characters and in the satisfying process of unveiling the truth behind all the secrets. Although, in reality, it's just about finding the clues and then everything is just kind of presented to you. It's not a game where you have to use logic to find loopholes in someone's alibi or come up with a story yourself. Whenever a clue has not been concluded yet, it means you haven't found an item, a location or spoken to a person enough. Despite that, it is still a lot of fun to roam the island, simply because it's so quirky and otherworldly and invites you to have a look around, jump on rooftops and parkour your way around. And the characters have their own personalities, accents and stories to tell. Some even give you further clues after you speak to them enough in private.The most fulfilling part of the game is however the trial at the end. Serving justice is exactly what you will want after the roughly 10-14 hour island marathon.If you like somewhat weird games with a slow pace, an inventive and intriguing plot, fresh ideas and themes, funky music and the certain pizzazz that other games often lack, then you will enjoy this one. It may not be a masterpiece but it should really be praised for how brave and unique it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it after buying it a couple days ago. If you're a fan of the Phoenix Wright or Danganronpa series, this game is for you. It's more in the same vein as the latter, but a 'lite' version. Paradise Killer definitely leans more into the exploration and story elements, as opposed to the puzzle elements in PW and Danganronpa games. Now that I think about it, the game is really an open world visual novel.The islands environment, is beautifully done. There's a significant vertical element which means there's a fair amount of exploring to do even though the area is relatively small. The game features an overall bright, detailed, kinda anime-ish Vaporwave aesthetic that permeates both visually and musically. That's something that drew me in initially. There's also a lot of what seems to be Babylonian mythological influence. I thought that was neat since that's not a mythos that we see in games very much.The story drops you "in media res." Which can be a little overwhelming initially. You're told that there's been a mass murder and you have to investigate. And that's it; very little direction, outside some leads/hints. Nearly all areas are open from the get-go. As you progress, side cases come up that obviously tie into the main murder case. Like Professor Layton games, all will be solved by the end.I thought the characters (main suspects) were interesting, if not a little shallow and cliched. Though as I made progress, constantly going around talking to the characters, bits and pieces of their background were revealed, which made me want to know more about them and this world they're in. Speaking of constantly going around, that is one of the downsides: this game is a bit of a walking simulator. Many times I found myself going from one side of the island to the other and back again by foot. However, there is a fast-travel system. You have to pay with in-game currency, but it's cheap and the currency plentiful. Still, I'd suggest getting about by foot until you've checked out all the areas.All-in-all, I enjoyed Paradise Killer. The whodunit story and exploration kept me interested, enough that I played like 12hrs straight so I could finish it during the weekend. If you're a fan of any of the games I mentioned in this review, I'd definitely recommend Paradise Killer.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this because I like mystery-solving games and the way it was advertised (you can accuse anyone at any point in the game) intrigued me. I wasn't initially very impressed, though. The characters and world seemed overly weird and quirky, and first-person viewpoint made me queasy, and gameplay mostly seemed to involve running around and picking up random items that didn't seem to be very useful. I frequently got lost and wasn't really sure what I was doing.After some fiddling with the display settings to reduce the queasiness, I started to enjoy exploring the island and figuring out its secrets. Checking the Discussion forums also helped - some of the game's most helpful features are only accessible if you do things that you might be unwilling to do because they cost Blood Crystals, a finite resource you collect as you explore the island. Yes, there are only so many Blood Crystals, and you could paint yourself into a corner if you use "fast travel" too often (it costs one Blood Crystal to activate a fast travel point and one Blood Crystal to fast travel), but seemingly useless things like  are very much worth spending Blood Crystals on. I bought every item on the island that I could find, paid for every available service and scrap of information, used fast travel a handful of times, and still ended the game with about 50 Blood Crystals (with a few probably still on balconies, because I eventually decided those were too much of a pain to get).A few hours of exploration later, and the world and mystery itself hooked me. Every time I thought I'd been everywhere, I discovered new hidden areas that provided me with more evidence and potential areas of investigation (and more Blood Crystals). I had to laugh, because this was a murder mystery and it took me somewhere between 13-16 hours to finally reach the crime scene. I'd previously found two other places I'd thought were the crime scene, due to all the blood, but it turns out that these characters live in a world that is really fond of bloodshed. (Speaking of bloodshed: although certain areas of the map have a very sinister feel to them, there's no way for you to die in this game. Falling into deep blue water will send you to a nearby Save spot, but that's it. Jump off buildings all you want - sometimes that's the easiest way to get from one place to another.)The trial aspect didn't work at all the way I would have expected, based on what I'd initially heard about the game. True, you can accuse anyone at any time, but you have to have the necessary evidence in order for your accusation to stick, and it's not like the evidence, crimes, and suspects change every time you play. The main thing is that, the longer you play and the more you explore, the more likely you are to uncover all layers of what occurred on the island.I'm pretty sure I've collected all the evidence it's possible to collect, so I conducted my first trial. Although I didn't think the results were necessarily false, I wasn't satisfied with how things turned out (the only punishment is execution - I'd have preferred a couple people to have been exiled instead, if they really had to be punished), so I'll probably replay the trial another time or two to see if I can get a more satisfying and less upsetting ending. Overall, I highly recommend this, but be aware that it takes a while to really become good, and I imagine the first areas you're drawn to explore will affect your initial impressions a lot. (Personally, I first ended up at K. HX's place, where I debated whether it was safe to jump off a cliff, did so, and was then worried that I'd never figure out how to get off the beach and back to somewhere more interesting again.}
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: In considering what to write for this review, fresh off the back of completing the game to what I would consider to be "best ending", I find it difficult to nail down my exact feelings about the game. Not to say that I don't like it; quite the opposite, I found that I really really loved this game finishing the trials of the game and finding the truth was bitter sweet.I'll gloss over the plot a bit. You are an investigator, a crime has occurred, it is up to you to find the truth. Things pretty quickly start to unravel as you discover that not everything is as it would seem. A detective drama at heart, but what Paradise Killer does best is world building. The basic premise revolves around the main characters all being part of a syndicate to revive their dead gods. And from there, the lore of the world that is born forth sucked me in almost instantly. Learning about the gods, the little "Paradise" that the Syndicate has been building for several millennia, it gave the world an unexpected depth. I found myself gladly reading every scrap of lore I could find to glean new insights into the world of Paradise Killer.Graphically, the game isn't going to be taxing on most low-mid range PCs, so anyone with even basic on-board graphics and no graphics card can jump in and enjoy it. The story of Paradise Killer takes place on a massive island that is "Paradise" and is a fully free-roaming 3D world. I found myself spending hours just running around the island finding many of the various collectibles in the world or searching for new leads in the investigation.I wanted to separate this line to make a point. While exploring, you will be treated to an incredibly good soundtrack. And you will find more songs as you explore, adding to the excellent tunes that you can listen to while seeking out clues or trying to track down lore about the world itself.The game is not incredibly long but can be padded out depending on how quickly you want to close the case or are able to find evidence. Lady Love Dies' personal computer will track the evidence and leads you have found, organized into "Notes" for leads and "Cases" for evidence and clues that are sorted. The notes section was helpful to me when trying to find some of the crucial evidence I was missing, but I did end up having to look up a couple of clue locations because the notes were either too vague or I was looking in the wrong place. As an example, one of the notes will tell you to search a particular building "from top to bottom" for clues. And when they say that, they mean literally, including evidence at the very bottom and the very top of the building. If you want to find the "true" ending and gather all the evidence, careful examination and exploration are key, otherwise you will find that you still have some loose ends to tie up at the very end.All-in-all, Paradise Killer is probably going to be one of the top 5 games I played this year. With a tight 8-10 hours of play (if you just want to solve the case and not 100% the collectibles), the story and world do not become stale before the case has been solved and kept me riveted, even once I was fairly sure I knew the truth of the crimes. And honestly, my friends can't get me to shut up about it so that's a 10/10 in my book!

_childDocuments_.review: Great vapourwave murder mystery game whose characters and setting sucked me in, and didn't let me out until I had literally 100%'d it. Then it refused to leave my head for days. It trusts the player to come up with their own conclusions, and execute justice accordingly. All the while runs an insightful commentary on politics, classism, scapegoating and justice. Each character is beautifully-designed, extremely memorable and has their own fleshed-out motives and beliefs. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.One of the best investigation games I've seen, the freedom it gives really made me feel like I was investigating, trying to piece together what was happening etc.One interesting thing (trying hard not to spoil) is that while I  there is a definite truth as to what happened and I think I figured it out, the game never tells you whether you did a good job or not. It just lets you find all the clues and make your own truth. Do you think you figured it out? Are there parts you're not sure about?Moreover you are free to do what you want with the clues. Maybe you find out that a character you really liked committed a crime. Maybe you can forgot to mention it, or find a way to pin it on someone else. Someone else you dislike but you're pretty sure is innocent. Maybe you commit to pure justice and kill your friends and spare your enemies. No matter what you choose the game won't tell you anything, you're the only one judging whether you did good or not.And finally there is the vibe. The game could have worked in a more boring setting, but there is something about that island, with the unique art style, with that music, that will make you really feel like you've been there. It will stay with you for a while.Really, really strong recommend, and thanks to the team for a genuinely amazing experience
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best detective game I've ever played. It has a delightfully unhinged plot and aesthetic but at its core it is a true exercise in fact gathering and deduction.As a big fan of the genre, there's relatively few games that actually pull off a satisfying conclusion once you've gathered your facts (what Jon Ingold called the "sudoku problem"). Paradise Killer on the other hand has a wonderfully dramatic and interesting finale, complete with new surprises and entertaining options in the epilogue. Even when I had all the facts, I still had to think hard about my decisions during the trials and put in a bit of planning to get everything laid out successfully. It really made all the work put in gathering evidence and exploring every nook and cranny of the island feel worth it, even though that process itself was plenty fun, with lots of interesting lore to find, characters to interview, and mysteries to solve. Great soundtrack too.As with all the best detective stories, the facts are there for you to find if you can, but in the end you decide the truth. For better or worse. Fantastic experience, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- A very pretty game with a good soundtrack that will hook you for about 6 hours, then you realize you're bored and the story is a few red herrings, a few misdirects, and a bunch of deus ex machina.   If you want a walking sim through a repetitive and bland world, this game has you covered. The general way to play this game is:  start game, have no idea what you're doing, run around the island to unlock all the fast travel points you can, writing down which ones are closest to the main NPCs, get the few ghost side quests as you pick up enough blood crystals to buy drinks, the 3 “footbath” upgrades, and get the 3 new types of symbols to open the doors (worship, cosmos, and pyramids).  Once you have done enough collectible collecting to get those upgrades (or for the lazy use cheat engine and cut off hours of wasted time hunting for blood crystals), then for all intents and purposes, this game is just walking between NPCs asking the same questions and getting the same variants of the answer “Did you ask the other NPC?” or “Here's a half truth, a lie, and the other guy is lying to you” (or for crimson paying a few blood crystals to get evidence for the final case). This will go on as you finish getting all the fast travel points, use the investigative mode to pick up phones, jump off mountains (no fall damage), and going through the doors using the computers and the picture matching mini-game. Depending on the speed you find a few key items (or look at a achievement guide to find out what main puzzles and actions correlate with the items that lead to plot twists), the mystery behind the murder and the 4 “gates” that lead to the scene of the murder are rather lackluster. I will say that this game at least had me consider whether or not I should “prosecute” certain characters at the end, after all attempted murder or setting up a murder isn't the same as actually being the person holding the knife to kill someone or being the one ordering someone to hold the knife, so the game has that going for it. It doesn't make anything more interesting in the long term, but it did give me a few minutes of considering before I started the final trial. Finally, I'd point out that this game has little to no replay-ability. Once you've gotten a rough idea of what actually occurred, all the little details you go hunting for are to flesh out how to prove things, and unless your looking for achievements, there is little enjoyment to reading bland flavor text about how “Genmaicha tea is the best and everyone who thinks otherwise is lying or hasn't tried it”. Trying to make the double jump or air dash physics work is an exercise in frustration, and the thought of starting from even my pretrial safety save doesn't motivate me to finish hunting down all the collectibles. I'm sure this game had some highlights for me over the 9 or 10 hours I sank into it beyond the “I kind of want to know what the heck happened”, it's just a shame I can't remember them.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot understand the amount of positive reviews this game is getting. The story is bland, Paradise Killer just dumps fanfiction level exposition about demons, gods and whatnot on you. It's full of nonsensical character names and absurd lore to a point where the whole thing doesn't really make any sense and comes off as uninteresting. It simply lacks substance, charm and execution to pull this kind of thing off.Another big problem is that the world is just empty, artificially inflated with copy pasted assets and models to a point where  it's simply boring and looks uglier than it would otherwise. There's hardly anything to find in the dull streets and paths around the island - no npcs, no interesting places, nothing - just bits of lore and in-game currency pick ups. The currency that you apparently need for unlocking some clues/tools and fast traveling, which again just feels like another trick to artificially inflate the play time. Whoever decided that fast traveling in a game like this should cost currency should probably consider a career path other than game design.Honestly the first 40 minutes were so bland that I can't be bothered to see if theres anything more under the crust.The only good things I find about it are the artwork and music. They're stylish and catchy, too bad they cant carry the game on their own.Paradise Killer tries so hard to immitate Danganronpa but falls flat on its face in every aspect. Spare yourself the disappointment and play something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, stylish, unique and ruthlessly thorough murder mystery. Highly recommend for fans of detective games that don't hold your hand, quirky Japanese games in the style of Suda51 & SWERY, and people who grew up playing early 2000s anime influenced Newgrounds games. One of the best games of 2020. If you felt like other detective games like LA Noire held your hand too much this game is absolutely for you, Paradise Killer throws you into a large map and tells you to solve the case. You can start the trials at any time, even from the beginning. The rest of the island has already got a suspect with damning evidence against him, and if you want you can leave it at that and never get to the bottom of the murder. The investigation has a ton of different threads to follow while you explore the island. The fast travelling system is mechanically one of the best I've seen in a game, since it's an investment that takes fairly limited currency from the player and acts as an incentive and then reward for exploring thoroughly enough. Once you've finally put the pieces together you're treated to a satisfying Ace Attorney esque trial at the end that rewards the hours you've likely spent exploring and connecting the dots. Paradise Killer hits a decent balance where you're able to think about the case for yourself and receive input from the protagonist.The writing is generally pretty good, there's an option to 'hang out' with each character that essentially involves having a conversation with them that I didn't really feel mattered much. The more your bond increases the more likely they are to give you hints on the case or point you in the direction of another suspect. However, it's a little jarring since some characters will treat you with just as much as scorn as when you first meet yet your bond with them is apparently at it's maximum. I feel more could have been done with the questioning system in general. Every character is just fleshed out enough to be engaging but after a while some of them can become rather one note. There's an enormous amount of world building that can get pretty obscure, and while it does lend a sense of mystery to the island but it can be difficult to get an complete idea of what's going on if you're not willing to read every item description.  The mystery itself is the best part of the writing, you start off with a seemingly open and shut case that quickly turns into a tangled web you have to make sense of. The protagonist, Lady Love Dies, isn't incredibly nuanced but fits perfectly for the game she's in. Just as the game encourages the player to leave no stone unturned, Love Dies is equally as fixated on the investigative process - no clue is too small or too tangential for her, no off hand comment so trivial that it can't be used against a suspect. Most of the suspects despise her and she has a  reputation as an investigation freak to the rest of the island. Some criticisms: The game really can grate after a few hours when you can't find any fresh leads and things can turn into a collect-a-thon for a while, and the constant menu pop ups for picking up any item really start to annoy. It's one thing for relics since they're all different, but I don't understand why every time I pick up a Blood Crystal (the games currency) Paradise Killer has me mash my left mouse button to close the same pop up menu. There's even a slight delay just to make sure the pacing comes to a screeching halt. I've been collecting these for the past hour and they already make a distinctive noise and there's a counter in the HUD anyway, so why did the devs feel I still wouldn't get it? Also, the game does that JRPG thing for dialogue where it isn't fully voiced other than a handful of stock lines that play every other sentence, to give you an idea of the character's personality and mood. It's fine in limited amounts but it can get really distracting, especially since it sometimes doesn't even really line up with the discussion that's being had and tells me basically nothing.  Also, while I like how detailed the game is, I hate when the HUD tells me I have new questions for a suspect that end up being a 'Did you see X suspect on the night of the murder' and their answer is essentially 'no', this is a fairly large map where fast travel has a cost, you really can't afford to waste a players time like that. I know I mentioned the questioning system could use more fleshing out, but in this regard it should probably be more streamlined.
