_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So is this a good experience? Yes it is. You get to experience a sensible murder mystery story with amazing music and a good art style. But is this a 10/10, or even an 8/10? hell no.So there are two phases of the game: An exploration phase that will take 95% of the gameplay, and a trial, for the last 5%. In the exploration phase you CANNOT DO ANYTHING WRONG. There's zero tension: Wander around, search for items (plain old click on things, and do some very easy puzzles), until your list of things to do drops to zero. It's good, in some sense, that you always know what else is there to investigate, but since you cannot make any mistakes. It's a matter of clicking through everything. Your only choice that matters is whether you want to go to trial with all the evidence, or not.The music is excellent, the graphics are pretty, but the exploration mechanics? Ugh. It's all wandering around in first person, finding things to interact with... and some are not exactly in easy to find corners. "pixel hunting" in old 2d adventures was never a good mechanic. Looking for larger targets, but in a 3d environment, is just a chore. The island is large-ish: too large for how much investigation will happen. And many sections are just repetitive: Welcome to residential area: Here are 15 houses! and some tall buildings, that you climb via external stairs! I don't know about you, but climbing rectangular stairs, over and over again, is going to make me dizzy: There might me some FOV issues or something, because even as a very seasoned shooter player, the camera + all the stairs just made me want to stop multiple times.And on top of this, some sections require some jumping around, and the jumping mechanics are NOT good. The game eases things over time by adding double jumps, but this ain't Metroid Prime. There was little fun in there, just frustration. If this wasn't enough, the game is full of random collectibles that add little, other than being mandatory to move forward with a decent ending: Want to open this door? OK, you need an upgrade that costs collectibles. Want to fast travel? Congrats, you pay in collectibles to unlock the fast travel location, and then every time you use it!We get to talk to suspects. but it's a lot like a japanese visual novel from the 90s: Just do all the clicking on all the things until there's no more talk options left. You might be able to pick option A or B, but they appear to be all false choices that don't affect the plot.Now, fortunately the actual mechanics of the mystery are quite good: We learn the relationships among characters, how things could have happened, and get all necessary evidence. All and all, that setup is quite good. Overall, about as good a mystery of one of the best cases in Danganrompa: Possibly a bit better.But then we get to the trial. If you've waited until no clues are left open, you have all the information you could ever want. The mystery is divided into multiple claims, and you get to decide who is accused. There's little fun back and forth or anything: Once you decide who you accuse, you get to just present all your evidence, in any order, and wait for a veredict. So the only sensible choice was whether to accuse the right person, fail miserably, or maybe choose to let someone off the hook.So I get to still recommend it because it's a great story, with good art and music. But this is so not the complete package that it could have been. For all the descriptions in the game developer's game of "story interacting", the game is lacking in actual interaction with the story. Getting anything wrong is really hard: the only way to fail is to decide "meh, I want to end the game now, who cares about not having all the information?"Dear developers, your writer is quite good, whoever made the music deserves a medal, but please, invest in gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice murder mystery game that combines exploration and character interaction to solve the case. I very much enjoyed the unique setting and characters along with the chill OST. It reminded me a lot of Danganronpa with how the 2D sprites existed in 3D, along with the visual novel style gameplay. I found the game easy due to the main task being collecting evidence and testimony, but there were certain puzzles that were unintuitive and required a walkthrough.One thing is that I did feel like the collection aspect made it hard to enjoy actually playing due to several reasons. First, I had to collect in order to use fast travel, making it a necessity (until I used Cheat Engine to max out my crystals). Next, it made finding actually important items harder due to the sheer amount of crystals and useless relics. Meditation didn't even differentiate between any of the collectibles, making it completely useless. Finally, forcing me to wait or click through a screen for every single action like picking up a crystal, taking fast travel, or riding an elevator made the whole experience feel really tedious.

Without spoilers, there's not a lot that is expanded on - which I would have loved - but if you enjoy lovecraft, or SCP, or just a messed up timeline, you'll love it.I don't see much replay value, but it's 10 hours I'm extremely happy with.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to cut to the chase - this game is a perfect example of a developer having a clear vision: aesthetic is on point, (vaporwave ftw) the characters are colorful (both literally and figuratively), the mystery is compelling... and there is a lot of subtext here, everything from social commentary to Lovecraftian horror.Overall- had a blast playing it! _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Many investigation games (i.e. Danganronpa, Phoenix Wright) are essentially long cutscenes interrupted by the occasional crime scene and trials that follow the "use evidence A to refute statement B" formula. While I enjoy that type of game, Paradise Killer sets itself apart in a peculiar way. It has an open world in which it is up to you to find secrets and hidden evidence and to some extent, decide the truth for yourself. There is much less emphasis on trial procedure and finding the "correct" answer, and more focus on using the information you find to unravel a conspiracy. Pros:- Great story and world building- Exploration is enjoyable, there are always collectibles and/or evidence around the corner- A breath of fresh air in the investigation genre- Fantastic visual style and soundtrack- Diverse and interesting cast of characters, with many things to hide- Riveting plot twists- The player has much more freedom compared to similar games, including how justice is carried outCons:- The currency system is poorly implemented. Fast travel and some information have costs, so you feel constrained to walking everywhere for a good chunk of your playthrough. Thankfully you can get around the island somewhat quickly on foot- Certain objects around the world that seem meaningless are very important for progression, which can leave you glancing over them and becoming lost in the process. These also cost currency, which further demotivates you from interacting with them- There is a TON of backtracking. You will need to revisit characters essentially every time you obtain new information, and reuse objects once you acquire certain upgrades or key items- Hacking puzzles were a bit repetitiveOverall, I had a great experience with Paradise Killer. Unveiling the secrets the island and its inhabitants hold was thrilling, and I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a good mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The story is garbage, characters are as flat as their sprites, map is far too large and empty w/ fast travel gated by a currency, first person controls are not good, "investigating" means "find things you can press the collect button on scattered throughout the giant world", the writing is unbelievably snarky and self-assured for being so bad (though I suppose that contributes to its badness).I should have refunded before 2 hours, but decided to give it a chance - which I now regret.[EDIT]: After talking it through with some friends (we all played through this at the same time), I think you might have a better time than I did if you're already bought into paranormal-type stories (ghosts/spirits/demons/cosmic horror/etc w/o a grounding in reality). I am not into those things myself and that in combination with the mediocrity of everything else led to the whole experience falling flat to me. If you like that kind of stuff this might have a pull for you, but for me there was nothing to pull me through w/ the 3D portion of the game lacking in the "game" department.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm just gonna come right out and say it; I love friggin this game! One might even say I am bordering the line of obsession, and honestly, I can't say I disagree. Honestly I could write an essay about how amazing I think this game is and all the things that make it so, but you probably don't wan't to read all of that. I haven't finished the game yet, I honestly doubt I'm close to done, and I'll probably play through it a number of times and continuously realize I actually knew nothing last play through.  - For starters, it kind of reminds me Danganronpa, like if the entire game was the period between discovering a body to the class trial, but better, because it doesn't hold your hand. I haven't actually reached the trial stage yet, because there is just  much in this game, and I love that. You could start the trial at any point, regardless of whether or not you have all the facts. I love the thinking I know something, then coming back to something I found like, 10 hours ago, and realizing that it is  important to the story then I thought it would be.   - There is a lot of back and forth once you start connecting the dots, and while I like it, it might be a little to repetitive for some people.   - I kind of struggle using the little in-game computer,I just feel like it could be better with how it categorizes things.  - That map is pretty big, but there are things you can access to make traversing it quicker, although I recommend taking your time and looking around. There's lots to see   - Definitely repayable   Honestly I could write so much more but I'm scared of accidentally spoiling something. It's a great game, 13/10, do yourself a favor and play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An open-world murder mystery game with a vaporwave aesthetic. You play as Lady Love Dies, an investigator brought out of her 3 million day-long exile to solve the crime to end all crimes: the murder of the island's Council. At first, the case seems pretty straightforward: a Citizen named Henry, who was possess by a demon 10 years ago and has been imprisoned ever since, broke out of his confinement and killed the entire Council. But as you explore the island, speak to its immortal inhabitants, and uncover clues, you soon realize that everything is not what it seems. Is Henry really the murderer? Or is he just a scapegoat?- Vaporwave aesthetic- Fast running speed and movement upgrades (double jump & dash) allow you to explore the entire island relatively quickly- Fast travel mechanic helps with the tedium of traveling around the island- AR and meditation mechanics help you find collectibles- Freedom to choose your own ending--you don't have to arrive at one solution to finish the game- Crimson Acid is a total MILF- First-person view can be nauseating when traversing certain regions- If you hate vaporwave you'll get tired of the background music- Conversations with characters don't have any real consequences--if you say the wrong thing and piss someone off, they'll still talk to you afterwards and give you the information you need
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Game 138 of my backlog.Spoiler freeNote: This is a Visual novel. There aren't a lot of choices to make realistically. Only looking for evidence and then watching it play out in the actual trial. I'm let down by that fact. You will not be proving or disproving anything. Only collecting, and hoping you collected enough+ Open world Phoenix Wright-esque investigation style gameplay+ Collectibles and upgrades+ Interesting Lore+ There is a decently good story to discover+ You can start the trial at any time+/- Would've loved to see a little more voice acting in there- Trial itself is a huge letdown. You get an mild option of choice simply by picking a candidate but then there is no proving or disproving anything beyond that. It just plays out. - Fast travel option is slow and tiresome. Bad implementation.- Constant backtracking, and not in a fun way, to collect all evidence, usually by talking to 2 people on opposite ends of the island, over and over again.- Dull Hang-Out mechanic.It starts fun, but ultimately I think it falls short. I feel like this is where Octopath Traveler 1 makes a nice comparison. Tons of great ideas not fully expressed very well. There is almost a golden gem of a game here that falls just short of being phenomenal if only there were some small changes in a few spots (disregarding my Voice Acting comment).
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game, particularly if you get it on sale, is 100% worth your time and money. In today's modern age of gaming, there are hundreds, maybe thousands of worthless and mediocre titles that demand your money in exchange for contrived, painful tropes and game-play all stolen from each other that provide nothing of substance. This is not one of those titles. While Paradise Killer does not excel in terms of its gameplay mechanics or replayability, it is absolutely stunning in terms of its visual presentation, characters and worldbuilding. It's quirky, charming, and will surprise you again and again as the plot unfolds. If you can put up with some tedious collect-a-thon stuff and bizarre exposition, you are sure to enjoy this.1) The game-play is a bit grating, comprising mostly of "find this, find that, go here, interrogate this person, solve this puzzle, etc." HOWEVER, the mystery underpinning the game is more than enough to compensate. No one mystery is spoon-fed to you or given away entirely in a single session. Out of the 14 hours I put in, I didn't determine the full shape of the mystery until about hour 12.2) The environment is just... wow. Certainly for being a smaller game, you can tell the team put a ton of love and effort into every area of the map. It feels like Vaporwave incarnate, and you will be living for every inch of it.3) The characters, my God, the characters. They're all so charming and quirky, and you get to know their ambitions, dreams, background, secrets, all of it. Some of them are more flat than others, for sure, but in general you will enjoy speaking with them at every turn.4) Without spoiling anything, the game really puts you in the driver's seat in terms of how fast or slow you go through the game. You never feel rushed, but you do always feel intrinsically motivated to learn more and comb every inch of the map. Highly appreciable, given the maddening obsession AAA studies have with map markers and "golden-path" design. The moment to moment gameplay definitely feels limited in that your dialogue choices are pre-defined, but you really get the feeling that you are determining the emotions that come into play. At no point did ANY character say ANYTHING incompatible with the conversation choices I made; it all just flowed organically, flawlessly, 100% of the time due to the way the game structures revelations.Finally, the game runs like a dream, even on max settings and ray-tracing on. No crashes, maybe 2 bugs the whole time, pitch-perfect soundtrack. I got this game for like $12 and feel like I robbed Kaizen Game Studios. Please buy this game, I beg of you. Your future self will thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: If this game interests you even slightly, go play it instead of spoiling yourself! The story that unfolds as you uncover the truths of the island is spectacular with a few twists and turns in it. The world is incredible and you, the player, get to uncover that mystery as well. There's plenty of worldbuilding and almost nothing is wasted in the experience. I do wish the game had full voice acting, as the few lines there are get quite annoying. Thankfully there is a feature to turn down the frequency and even disable them entirely, which I did pretty shortly into the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful gem of a game.  It's an investigative mystery game I'd say most compares to Phoenix Wright games or Danganronpa, in that the structure of the game has an investigative segment followed by a trial.  Unlike those games, this game is primarily about the investigation, which takes up >95% of the gameplay, and that there is one big case and one trial, rather than a series of cases.You are an immortal detective called into action to investigate a murder mystery on an island.  The setting of this game is the real selling point as it is so bizarre its formulation must have had assistance from mind altering drugs.  In the first five minutes of the game you escape your 3 million day exile, talk to a four armed fox demon who is perpetually flipping you two middle fingers and has a giant smiley face over his crotch, and then walk off a cliff since it's the fastest way to get where you're going. (But remember you're immortal so you're fine)  By the end of the game this will not even register on the weirdness meter.The investigation is quality stuff.  You can question everyone involved, pore over crime scenes, search for evidence, hack computers for records, and so on.  You get ability unlocks that allow you into more secretive areas to find more clues.  The island you're exploring is fairly big but not TOO big that you can't remember where everything is.  Just about a perfect size.  The story has lots of twists and turns that recast previous evidence in new light and turns your conclusions on their head.Unfortunately the game does have many issues.  The fast travel system is one of them.  There are save point phones scattered everywhere around the island, of which you have to first find them and then pay money to unlock them as a fast travel point.  Cool so far.  But then you have to pay money AGAIN to actually fast travel anywhere, and money is FINITE in the game.  Not cool at all.  Another thing is that the map is just saturated with useless collectables that do little or nothing.  Maybe 1 in 30 pickups will actually be related to the investigation and the rest just pointless fluff, although their descriptions are consistently bizarre.  I was expecting this was there as achievement fodder...but the game doesn't even have achievements.While you can press suspects for evidence, conversing with the other characters rarely leads to investigative leads or real evidence.  Pretty much everyone blames everyone else and denies anything you accuse them of.  Laughably you can shove damning evidence in their face and they still just deny it and say it's fake news.  "I was in bed.""Well I have a witness that saw you outside at the time.""They're lying.  You're lying.""Now I have your cell phone data that shows you weren't home at the time.""The data is wrong.  You're wrong.  I was in bed."You don't even really show evidence as it is, you just pick questioning threads that automatically update based on your current accrued knowledge.  This game could have learned a bit more from Phoenix Wright and put a lot more effort in the conversations as part of the investigative gameplay.But the main problem comes in the ending trial.  The game allows you to essentially end the game at any point and proceed to trial, so you can decide when you think you have enough evidence and proceed to the accusations.  Now this should be the climax of the game, but if you're expecting a Phoenix Wright style showdown where you bust witness testimony by countering their claims....you're not going to get much satisfaction.  The game will sort of twist reality to accept whatever conclusions you have drawn, even though with enough investigation you can absolutely know exactly what happened and who did what.   Even after getting a "perfect" ending they still hand wave "Well hopefully that was the truth" at you as if we'll never really know what happened (even after people confess)  So you gotta extract your own satisfaction from the proceedings.Weaknesses aside, the game is absolutely worth playing!  It's engaging most of the way through and novel enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very, surreal, in a positive way. I had a bit of trouble grasping the dialogue at first, but very quickly grew interested in the story. You spend your time exploring these vaporwave landscapes, investigating whodunit.There's no combat, the game is entirely exploring the island, collecting doodads, and talking to the few residents still hanging around. You're essentially wandering a ghost town, which at times gave me a really unsettling feeling, despite the funky jams playing over the radio.I had a couple frustrations while playing, but nothing substantial. Pretty solid game, imo.I got this game on sale, 75% off, and felt it was more than worth that price. Really neat game that I hadn't heard about until the "Sorry We're Closed" social media account posted about the bundle with the two games. Glad they did!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: this game was absolutely amazing. it was an adventure that i'm sad has come to an end. the story, the tiny details, the music, everything about this game was a blast. there is really no other game like this out there. at first i was a bit skeptical to play this game, but once I really got into it i was HOOKED. worth every penny spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. I really wish there was a new game plus that had items hidden in different locations so I could replay again and not know where everything is already.Paradise Killer has a AAA level game aesthetic done by what appears to be a handful of people. It's a game where, after a few minutes adjusting to the in-game world (it's a bit abstract) you just kind of "fit" into it and forget you are playing a game.There's a lot of great music and the color scheme and overall design make you feel like you're playing inside the cover of a 1980s Trapper-Keeper. The controls are tight, and the character designs are creative and amazing.I recommend playing this in small chunks because once it's over you're going to wish it wasn't.  I have seen a lot of folks compare this to Danganronpa, and It's a very fair comparison. The way this game feels better to me is that, after you've completed the adventure portion, there is a trial and where as you only have one correct decision in Danganronpa games, this game is more open to letting you follow what you feel is the evidence trail.I'm not much on doing reviews but I had to review this game. I can't recommend this enough. PS Devs if you're reading this: Please consider a New Game + or some game content DLC soon!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't really played many investigative type games, so my perspective may be a bit different than other reviews.  I saw some gameplay on youtube for this game and was just intrigued by its weirdness.  And man is this game bizarre...like wtf bizarre, but in a good way.  The setting, characters, and story are all unique and very interesting (IMO).  I can try to nitpick some small things about mechanics or game flow, but honestly it doesn't outweigh the good.  If this game has caught your eye for whatever reason, just give it a try.  I'm really glad I did on a whim and I'm getting a very different and refreshing experience from my usual game diet.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and very unique crime solving game with open world, interesting characters, vapourwave aesthetic, and always having something to do. Basically you're expected to explore the island's every corner while looking for various things such as memories, relics, evidences etc. But I don't think especially evidence materials are random or disorganized, they are all placed within a logic throughout the island, so much that even if you don't explore properly and just go to places that are related to crime, I'm pretty sure you can still get what's going on.I usually don't like finding scattered stuff across the map but in Paradise Killer, it was really fun to explore so I just got everything except all the blood crystals I think and I wasn't even trying. I was just trying to find everything that was related and conveniently placed other things were also there, helping me gather them.Over all I enjoyed the game, I think it was unique and refreshing. From world building to finding the people responsible for everything was very fun. I definitely recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just say it.  I am in love with .So many elements are done so well, and the whole comes together so beautifully.With all that I have gone through over these 15 hours, I wouldn't have changed a thing.  This is one of those experiences that carves out a place in your heart and makes you not want it to end - though the length is actually perfect too.  They knew the story they wanted to tell and took the right time to tell it without dragging things out and without skipping over anything.Above all,  fills me with , triggering feelings of longing for my real world past through masterful evocation of its own fictional one.  The setting taught me so much about itself that, as I played, I already felt nostalgic for earlier islands, the times of innocence I never saw, the old friendships with the whole cast; and now that it is over I'm nostalgic for Island Sequence 24 and the adventure I had there.  I'll miss the living and the dead, even those I never met; I'll miss the help of the trusty Starlight computer sidekick; and I'll miss myself as Lady Love Dies.  She does some damn good detective work.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best way to review this is "this is an amazing investigation and exploration game, attached to a very mediocre collectathon". If you're ok spending hours collecting pointless things, or ignoring them ,then this is VERY good. Honestly there's just too many thing things every 2 feet to pick up but the actual talking and investigating is so good its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% completion Paradise Killer is part visual novel murder mystery, part first person platformer, and part collectathon. The vaporwave aesthetic is well-earned by the game's critical tension with the titular paradise. That tension permeates the entire narrative, as characters both benefit and suffer in their self-imposed immortality. The mystery is enjoyable to uncover, with lots of dramatic moments if the player chooses to chase down every line of inquiry. The characters are memorable and nuanced, with complicated overlapping motives and skillsets. Unlike similar titles, there isn't a specific hard truth to uncover; rather, the player can present evidence that they feel is more incriminating in order to weave a compelling narrative of the crimes. This did make the ending slightly unsatisfying, as all the crimes have multiple plausible culprits.I also found island navigation to be a bit irritating at times. The map is useless, and the overall design is a bit mazelike. That said, it is a small enough space that this issue fades into the background as you progress. First person platforming certainly adds a retro vibe, but this implementation is not a significant improvement over its very dated predecessors. With all the upgrades unlocked I did end up enjoying jumping around the island, but there were quite a few moments of frustration mixed in there as well.Overall the imaginative world, consistent vibe, and exemplary writing made this a unique and compelling experience. I can forgive a few shortcomings when they come from a place of artistic experimentation, and the result is a game with a tremendous amount of heart and personality.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, the world is completely nonsensical, but you start to get it within 30 minutes, and then an hour later you'll pretty much understand everything important.For most of this gameplay, it's a collectathon where you jump around a huge and cool island getting clues and collectibles, talk to people for more clues, and upgrade your tools along the way. Then there's a great trial. This has one of the best game stories I've seen in years.Since this is something you'll want to know, you should just buy everything you can (except fast travel points if you don't care about the bonuses). If you get all the money in the game and don't spend on travelling, you'll have 50 left, which is a huge amount.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't sure what to expect when I started this one.  There's a strong Japanese aesthetic running through the whole thing, and there's a weird almost 80's vibe to the color scheme and music.  You play a detective with free reign to explore an island and uncover as much evidence as you want before starting the final trial.  You could run straight to the end if you so choose, but won't have much to support your case.  In addition, there are a TON of hidden items to find, and getting them all is a challenge even with what little help the game provides. It reminded me a lot of the later Far Cry games where you collect for the sake of collecting.  All the characters are bizarre and interesting and the investigation just keeps throwing revelations at you that, thankfully, the game keeps track of for you.  The final case isn't nearly as difficult as I was anticipating given all the evidence you've collected, which I really appreciated, but I kind of wish I got some kind of final grade for my effort.  This is definitely a game if you want something more low-key that you can take your time with and enjoy the exploration.  You don't fight, kill anything, and you can't die, so all the pressure comes from being able to find what you are looking for, and they don't make it easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer has forced me to think about a world where everyone is superbly attractive and shop at an H&M catering to fashion designers. When the palm trees sway in the ocean breeze on island 24, the wood groans a detached sigh about the malaise of paradise. The farms are flanked by perfect pyramids beckoning the farmer to dream of life off of the land they were abducted to. Island 24 is a beautiful thing. Vast apartment blocks tower over intimate parks with gilding generously applied to everything. It's a space made to worship, and when walking through the comically long hallways, it's hard not to feel blessed by a sweet curse.It's residents, or what remains of them, feel perfect too in a sad way. They long for things outside their station, promises unspoken, denied by birth, by love, by circumstance. Love Dies, the detective freak, was conned a long time ago and forced to exile. The crime to end all crimes has happened, and without the intervention of Love Dies, the involved may find the things they seek. But to call their pursuit justice, that is not the truth, and a detective has to find truth. You will be treated to a lush soundtrack, spaces contort in uncomfortable ways, but I found a lot of comfort in navigating the weird vistas of 24. I can only dream of what "Perfect 25" might look like. In this game too, I wonder what might happen if more people were involved. At the core is a game about walking, talking, and collecting. Objects are placed with a steady deliberation, but the logic can be unreadable much to the games credit. Would more time and effort make Paradise Killer better? Would inventory systems, multiplayer, high scores, rich animated figures really benefit this composition?Paradise Killer kept accidentally directing my attention to what this thing could be, and it was distracting from the thing that it is. If not for the demonic invasion, could people be happy on 24, paradise that it might be. I found myself in their longing, but for what comes next. I do not know if there is such a thing as a better Paradise Killer, but I do know that Paradise Killer is inspiring enough a product to bring interested eyes to the future of this team. Characters swirl in layers upon each other, the efforts of Love Dies often bring discomfort as more truth becomes known. Worth putting the time in, and worth sinking the dollar in for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 4 years after finishing this game when it first released, I'm surprised I never wrote a review for it. So I might as well, because I wholeheartedly love and recommend Paradise Killer.When I first played it, and when I thought I had gathered every single piece of information, there was something that didn't add up. A piece of information that didn't fit in with the rest. It wasn't complete. I passed it off as unimportant, thinking that maybe I misunderstood the description, that I got the order of events wrong, that I made a mistake and that it was unimportant. So I ignored it, finished the game, and called it a day. But even after finishing, that bugging feeling of this little detail missing something persisted. And so to my surprise, when I looked at the Wiki for this game years later to remind myself of the lore, there was a name I didn't recognize. A character to whom I could not identify a face. If you told me the names of every character with a sprite in this game, I could most likely give a vague description of their appearance now. But not this character. And when I looked at where they could be found, I returned to the game. And it was then that all the puzzle pieces suddenly fell into place. Everything suddenly added up. Suddenly, everything made sense.This satisfactory feeling of slowly coming closer to the truth, of discovering the chain of events and the actions of the parties involved, is a one time experience akin to Outer Wilds. It's a bold comparison, but I truly felt the same emotion when finishing both of these games. If you need a reason to play this game, then it's that the story and lore are absolutely beautiful and sure to grab your attention. If you need multiple reasons, then the gameplay, music, art, general vibe, dialouge, puzzles, character personalities and world design should be more than enough. My only critique, which is honestly just nitpicking, is that I wish the final trial had its very own music, because there is a time and a place to listen to Breeze With U, and it's not when a character is begging for their life.I may be 4 years late, but I do hope this game gets vastly more attention the same way other games have.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! The world building, mythology, and gameplay all come together for a great experience. My time above does not reflect actual playtime.The Story: Undying Gods have created an alternate reality where they have set up "islands" for thousands of Citizens (aka sacrifices). These CItizens are ruled by the Immortal Syndicate, privileged humans who have been given Blessings and special treatment to maintain the islands. Demons psychically and physically plague the islands, causing madness and corruption. As the Investigator Lady Love Dies, you must investigate  why the Syndicate were wiped out in a mass murder. You've been in isolation for years, so you have learn what happened on the island, leading up to the murders. Why isn't there an anime in the works???The Style: OMG the style in this game!! Fabulous character designs, over the top personalities, and excellent voice acting on top of it all. And the music is so jazzy and fun- perfect for running around the island. Soundtrack was an insta-buy for me.Gameplay: You can't die, which is super nice. You can jump off high buildings and land safely with no problem. If you go in the ocean you just respawn at the nearest save spot. You run around the island as Lady Love Dies after given your mission by the Judge. There are a dozen people to talk to on the island, all that remains of the Syndicate, and the people guilty of the mass murder. But which one? You have 2 options when you talk to someone: Investigate and Hang Out. Investigating you can ask questions and pick up clues and evidence. Hang Out, you can become friends with everyone on the island and receive special gifts and vital clues to the investigation.There are computer you have to hack but it's super easy. This game would be ok for young teens and up who will understand the story. There's just one character (Henry) who drops the F bomb and he does it A LOT. There's also a lot of blood at the crime scene which might be disturbing to some people. There's no rape or sexual assault, but you can have sexy times (off screen) with a couple of characters.Here are some tips for gameplay that I wish I'd known from the very beginning:1) Pick up all the Blood Crystals, they are scattered everywhere. Use them to buy info from Carmelina, soda cans from vending machines (at least 10), and to use the foot baths (there are 3 total). Don't hesitate about doing this at all, you won't use up all of your blood crystals and it's vital to the story.2) Hang Out with everyone BEFORE Investigating. If you make them happy you'll get what you want, sometimes very important clues. 3) The more clues and evidence you have, the better the end trial will be. Investigate everyone until there are no more '!' left on the map.4) Use CTRL to locate suspects, ghosts, crime scenes, and computers to hack5) Use left SHIFT to sprint6) Go to the top of EVERY building and check behind EVERYTHING. Some items are difficult to get unless you use all 3 foot baths.7) Talk to Shinji the demon, he says some funny ♥♥♥♥.Similar game would be Curse of the Obra Dinn in terms of investigation techniques and finding evidence.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a weird looking game that isn't actually that weird once you get dug into it. Oh the character designs are a bit odd and there is that blue rectangle headed naked fox demon following you around but honestly at its core PK is just a kind of exploration/collectathon/detective game. You spend most your time going from place to place, hunting down leads, talking to people for testimonies, and occasionally finding new things off the beaten path. While not an overly long game if your just concerned with the trial aspect, there are enough collectables to keep you occupied for much much longer.   The game is not without its flaws, unfortunately explaining those flaws would require spoilers. Still even with them I would recommend the game to anyone looking to do some mystery solving without having the game hold your hand, because this game does not hold your hand very much at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard to compare PK to any other games as it is definitely a unique take on many genres. I still don't really grasp the story and the lore but it is rewarding to tease out. The 2D art is gorgeous! I love the character designs. Even though there is only brief character interactions (so far) the characters stand out and are memorable. The 3D world is less great, but it is serviceable and it fits with the concept of manufactured island.I heartily recommend you check out this gameI have the following gripes, but they are not deal-breakers!-Limited voice lines for each character that does not follow the conversation. They repeat very often especially if you click-through dialogue-Your questioning of a character does not always take into account what you have already learnt from elsewhere-I am not a fan of the Fast-Travel costing moneyThe biggest issue for me however is the First-Person exploration. The environments are super interesting and nice, but climbing all over the show for crystals is a bit annoying, especially when it relies on platfroming in first person.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The characters were surreal, the dialogue was entertaining, the art was great. I loved that the elements of the detective case while dealing with otherworldly settings can suspects maintained consistency that makes for a great detective story. I was able to draw my own conclusions and guide the end result as I saw fit and it was satisfying.Small note to the developers, if you are going to insert certain small annoyances like blinking for 5 seconds every time you want to reveal items, maybe allow the player to eventually get rid of that annoyance buy participating in the game somehow. for instance a final reward for collecting certain items or the like.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to write this review considering how excited I was to finally play Paradise Killer, but god was this game an absolute miss. I've had it on my wishlist forever and figured the steam sale would be a good place to pick it up! And I am so glad I waited until it was on sale because I cannot recommend buying this game at full price to anyone. There's a long list of problems I had with the story and gameplay mechanics, so I'll start with what I really enjoyed. The art for the characters and the music. Beautiful. The character sprites were so good, to the point where it made me like characters that otherwise I would think literally nothing of with how bland the writing for them is. The music was perfect for the feeling of the island/world that was being conveyed, and discovering new tracks was one of the few collectibles I actually enjoyed completing. The dialogue with the . One of the few gameplay mechanics I did like were the decryption puzzles, which there were much fewer of than I had anticipated. I wish there were more things I could compliment the game for, but unfortunately I can't.Starting off the list of cons: the story. It's bad. I don't know if I can even critique the story, because it felt like there wasn't even one there while playing. Without including spoilers, essentially your job is to figure out who murdered the elites of this island by investigating and interrogating suspects. Except it's not, because your job is in fact going up to suspects who you have just found incriminating evidence linking to them and getting a resounding "No... that wasn't me. I didn't do that." Now, you would think, 'Oh, obviously the trial is going to be more in depth with you linking these pieces of evidence. Surely there is a reason why this PROVEN piece of evidence isn't getting me any further talking with them.' And you would be so very wrong. The trial is one of the most disappointing parts of this game in my opinion. It's less deduction and more common sense Who Did This Crime, the conclusion of which is generally led to by a single piece of evidence found. Even without the way this was set up, the story is completely unfulfilling. Character hangouts felt very bland or down right intolerable, specifically Yuri's. I don't know what Shinji's interactions were meant to convey but I felt literally nothing reading them. Even the overarching story of your backstory and the islands themselves felt just... empty. The entire game feels like some cool character designs were created and they tried to shove them into an unfinished story and world. I wasn't expecting a lot from the story, but I also wasn't expecting to be left feeling absolutely nothing about the characters when I completed the game. Moving onto the actual gameplay mechanics, this is where most of the big issues lie. To preface, I love collectibles in games. Love completing side quests. This game has a lot of one of the two. A Lot. Of collectibles. And it weighs the game down an immense amount. I'd say about 80% of this game is bouncing around with the god awful physics and drowning while you slide down a mountain trying to pick up a Blood Crystal. That was my experience in a nutshell. Trying to get evidence for the murders that happened? No, it's just a crystal. And then another. And another. I understand they're the currency for fast traveling and such, but god is it annoying to try to collect evidence for the case only to find out there's nothing more and only a plethora of these crystals leftover. And to my knowledge, collecting these does literally nothing aside from purchasing items or info. Don't worry though, they aren't the only thing filled throughout this island to make it seem like there's more to do! There is so much junk to sift through, just random items with the most bland flavor text I've read in a game like this to date. The collectibles revolving around the lore just feel like weird world-building without the actual effort of doing it. Most of the stuff about the gods or the way the world works was just left up to the player to interpret, which I don't generally mind, but with a story as convoluted as this it's almost necessary. The few side quests that were available were actually good, I liked being able to go search for things residents asked for, as it gave more reason to explore the world and also gave me the most understanding of how the society worked. This would be great if there were more than like, 5 of these throughout the entire game. I feel like a lot of the issues with general storytelling about the world itself could've been solved with more of these citizen interactions, so it's just frustrating how little they were incorporated. Some issues I had that were less of an issue and more of a nuisance were the voice line loops and the map ui. I ran into multiple situations where the same voice line would play back to back, no tone change, nothing, just the same line repeated. It wasn't a huge issue but it just felt strange? Regarding the map, I didn't use it very much in my playthrough, usually only in the portions where I fast traveled, and I didn't even start using that until closer to the end of the game because I still wasn't familiar enough to remember each suspects location on this big open world map. This is where a better ui for the map would've helped immensely, at least just with the faces of people next to their closest warp point.TLDR; Do not buy this game if you're looking for a fully fleshed out story, or any sense of reasonable exploration. The game tries to bring up bigger issues of right and wrong, morality, the exploitation of the working class (i assumed), and falls completely flat. There is a murder. Is it a mystery? Not really, besides one single aspect of it. Pick up the game while it's on sale if you think you'll be able to get more enjoyment out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Man I love paradise killer - the mystery isn't super in depth in and of itself, neither is this game a standard detective or puzzle game if that's what you're interested in. It's a collectathon platformer, based in truly one of the most interesting and creative sci-fi/fantasy worlds I've seen in games. Every location is just oozing style and vibes and the amount of stuff to explore and find is excellent.It's quite wordy so if that's not your thing this won't be for you, although also if you just want words it also won't be for you. The platforming is a little jank, but only imo in ways that enhance your ability to get to each nook and cranny of the game world and the story doesn't quiiiiiiiiiiiite stick the landing, but not in a way that massively impacted my enjoyment of the game.Overall highly recommend it, if it seems like it's your thing it will be.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games I have played. The soundtrack offers great vibes and I've been listening to it almost every night this summer. The world has plenty of collectibles to find, if you're into that sort of thing. The story and setting is definitely out there. I saw a review that described this game as an eldritch vaporware murder mystery, and I think that sums it up nicely. Think of it as a fusion of a Florida beach town, late 80's/early 90's a e s t h t i c, Satan worship, a classic murder mystery, and a diverse cast of stand out characters. A good buy for the price. Support indie devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game's environment and lore are so unique and amazing. It could be a little hard to get into at first but it pays out.The game world reminds me of playing counter strike: source's prison escape maps in the old days. You can go anywhere you want in a massive map as long as you utilize movement techniques (just like in source engine). The developer rewards you for exploring. it's a world that closely resembles reality but is simultaneously bizarre, isolated, and full of secrets. Of course unlike those full-on liminal space cs:s maps, this game is vibrant, lively, and has a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game overall. Music was great, characters were good, and the actual murder mystery investigation was fun. Sometimes the collectible stuff was fun. Unfortunately the biggest mark against the game is the moment-to-moment platforming.Platforming in first-person is a pain and with floaty physics like these it's even worse. Blood crystals also become more work than they pay off to be, especially when you can find a blood crystal next to things that require them often enough. It's not worthwhile to collect more than 20 at a time.Otherwise would recommend for those murder mystery and trial simulation fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Not exactly what it says on the tin, but a fun, stylish piece nonetheless.Paradise Killer is an investigation-lite game. I'd call it more of a investigation-themed exploration game/collectathon. While yes, you're playing as a lovely Lady Love, an investigator, you're not really... investigating the crimes. You're just collecting evidence scattered around the island, like in Dangronpa's investigation phase (you'll hear that comparison a lot in this review) and you can honestly forget about them until it's the time for the trial. It goes something like this: talk to a suspect, they point you to a place to check out, you start walking in that direction and immediatly get sidetracked by hundreds of collectibles to be found in this world.And what a world to explore it is. Absolutely peak aesthetics, brave colours, memorable landmarks, inspired by vapourwave, brutalism, small, japanese towns, ancient, egyptian monuments and a dash of futurism and yet, it works perfectly together. Not to mention the entire lore and the worldbuilding the game has. A completly unique blend that was fascinating to learn about. What's up with these Gods? Wait, there are demons possessing people? Why's there air conditioning literally everywhere?The world is also inhabited by a colourful cast of characters (you, know like in Danganronpa), who each have their own clear goals, motivations, agendas. Who's working with who? Who's gonna gain something from the confustion and who wants to lead you astray? Also, the game has two cute dogs (you can pet them) and a possessed fish yearning for knowledge.While you're exploring the island, you'll be jamming to some killer (pun intended) soundtrack, jazzy, funky, etheral, a perfect fit to the visuals. Paradise Killer is oozing with style, especially the stylized UI elements, that really set the tone of the game. Everything's slick, flashy, bright, yet somehow tainted by some hidden force working in the shadows. You'll get it, when you realise why the hacking terminals are called "Nightmare Computers".Okay, the game seems pretty good, what's the catch?Well, while the mystery is really cool and complex, and you can find out everything about everyone, the game kinda... fizzles out at the end, when the time for the trial comes. It's just a very simple text-based scene, where you don't really do anything, except point your finger at the guilty, like you're going with the motions. I was hoping for something like, you guessed it, Dangaronpa trials, where you're more of an active participant. That would make it more memorable I think. What's more, is that the trial actually... doesn't really matter? No matter who you charge as a titular killer, the result's all the same, which is a huge shame. Why not at least put a "where are they now" kinda thing to show you how your choices affected the world, so you had an incentive to play the scheming game The Syndicate loves so much. Overall, Paradise Killer is more of a journey than a destination kind of deal. It's a beautiful, memorable journey, don't get me wrong. It's just a shame that it couldn't stick the landing. Otherwise, we would have gotten pretty close to perfection.JUSTICE HAS BEEN SERVED
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING!In practice a collect-athon/platformer/explorer game in an incredibly creative surrealist vapor-wave pocket dimension setting.The story has you discovering secrets and clues to solve a murder mystery among a bunch of astral-super-villains who are on the run from demonic invasions and the god-hunters of the real world who seek to stop them from resurrecting and worshiping dead lovecraftian gods from beyond the stars. Also the music slaps
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It has a very wacky setup and setting but it is ultimately a murder mystery solving game and I really like those type of games. To be fair the setting and general wackiness of the game sort of grew on me as I played anyway.The basic premise is that you play a character called Lady Love Dies who has been exiled for 3 million days, but is then recalled to investigate the murder of the rulers of an island. And yes that is your characters actual name and yes I meant days and not years.To investigate the crime you will scour the island for clues and question a number of suspects to determine if they were or weren't involved. When you decide to finish your investigation you then move onto a trial where you will accuse the suspects you believe are guilty and present your evidence to convince the judge.As I said I did really enjoy this game and was hooked from early on. Exploring the island for clues and evidence is fun. There's also other collectibles to find, mainly crystals which are a form of currency which you'll use to fast travel, unlock fast travel points and abilities as well as buying information from one of the suspects. The other main form of collectables are relics which serve no purpose other than to serve as a bit of lore flavour.All your evidence gets collected on a laptop device and is nicely sorted by case and suspect which will aid in your investigation and guide you in determining what to look for next.So if a game that has investigating a murder as it's main focus sounds appealing then definitely give this game a try. As someone who likes investigation games, I can easily recommend it. It might not be to everyones taste but it certainly was to mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled, this is not a detective game. You will have to do no logical deductions to play through the game. It's more a 3D platformer collectathon wrapped in a detective story (in a bonkers world).(By the way, don't worry about wasting your blood crystals, there are more than enough on the island.)It has some weird game design decisions, but in the end it's more than the sum of its parts. And I mostly enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to continue running around world and finding hidden objects. This is not what I signed up for. It's tedious. When over 90% of the "gameplay" is just running forward and trying to find something to click on, it's not good. At. All. The style, design, lore and art of the game is appealing, but can't really carry this game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of detective-style games and so I was really happy to discover that Paradise Killer existed a few weeks ago.  It's not a perfect game but if you like murder mysteries set in a non-traditional environment then by all means, please try it. The scenery and layout is beautiful, as are the character "sprites" The music fits the game well - there's also a variety of tracks.The sleuthing makes sense - everything is logical and you can deduce stuff before you find certain pieces of evidence. I didn't mind the voice acting, but during the conversations they seemed a bit too repetitive and arbitrary. Thankfully you can turn it off in the settings.Whilst I liked the characters it was hard to feel invested... everything seemed a little too disjointed. Maybe a bit more history at the start could rectify this but it may just be the setting, whilst beautiful, didn't gel with the investigation.It's not exactly a con but I think achievements would have made it a little more enjoyable for me, especially since I spent a lot of time bouncing around picking up random little objects. So in short, fun game, I'd give it a 6.5/10. Thanks for coming to my TED talk.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing games with a unique visual style and you're not against climbing every single house and/or hill, you'll dig it. The characters have their own charm, even though some of them might be a bit bland. It has investigations and even a court trial, although it's MOSTLY focused on gathering evidence and "interrogating" suspects, so don't expect Danganronpa levels of court trials.In short, if you loved investigation phases of Danganronpa then you would love it too.P.S. When love dies, truth remains.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic take on a classic "Who Dunn it" story. The games rich world is imaginative and full of secrets to discover, complimented by an enjoyable collect-a-thon gameplay loop, leading you to naturally discover evidence, all while accompanied by the games City Pop soundtrack and vaporwave aesthetic.The games story keeps you hooked as you discover evidence and talk to the fun cast of potential killers.What I loved about the game, is it never directly tells you who the killer is, instead allowing the player to come up with their own theories and really become an actual detective. One players take on how the "Crime to end all crimes" played out, could be wildly different from another's.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: "19th Island Sequence - When you sat with me and looked at the moon."I re-wrote and deleted the review 3 times by now. I can't really put it in words, but this game is an . I can't really recommend it to everyone, and I don't think it's a game that absolutely everyone should play. It took me 10 hours to 100% the game, and at its current price-per-hour point you're looking at what should feel like a nice restaurant 3-course meal, and what you end up with is a dinner at a Michelin-star restaurant where the main chef is using goat blood and demonic murmurs to spice the food, the servers look like they're on acid and they smell of whiskey, and the other patrons are loving it. So in what case would this game be a good purchase for you? Should you be able to look past minor inconveniences and don't mind an indie feel to a game, you end up with what I can only describe as a "I wish I could play this for the first time again" type of experience. Paradise Killer is very unique in a lot of ways, and I struggle to piece together a Frankenstein of similar games that can fill all of its parts - and this is is what alienates the game from the mainstream gaming audience. What you should know is that the game is an Open World Mystery, but it doesn't stop at that. The trailers also don't do justice to the game's movement, which once mastered will leave you zooming from location to location, progressing plot points and collecting bits and pieces of the world being spoon-fed through collectables and dialogue. And what a world it is! If you made it this far in the review and like what you're reading, I warmly suggest stopping and getting the game. There's more I'd love to tell you, but the experience of going in blind and reading the reviews later will do you proper justice. Is the game perfect? No. Should you play it? Maybe. Overwhelmingly positive worthy? Yup. And finally, best girl? Crimson.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into open world exploration and *murder/mystery investigation - GET THIS GAME, this has been a wild ride!Don't use guides, just let this bizzare, colorful and eerie world suck you in. Truly is one of the more entertaining games I got to play in 2023.Main Points:- The voice acting, in my opinion, did more bad than good (repetitive sentences, unrelated to the actual text) so I turned it off and everything was perfect.- Talk to everybody, multiple times, you will receive new information. Even if you're past 5 hours of game play and not sure who the killer is - GOOD! Keep playing, exploring, collecting evidence and questioning everybody.- The names can be confusing, but you get used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This bizarre vaporware-ish Danganronpa-inspired adventure/visual novel game turned out to be my second most favorite game of 2020.If there's one word that can describe Paradise Killer, it would be "stylish". The contrast between flat, simplified "external" elements like HUD, UI, menus, even the architectures, and the baroque fantastical visual design of characters and locations give Paradise Killer a chaotic vibration, just like how the intricate writing manifested its complex lore. Nothing comes off as gimmicky as the narrative is tightly directed. The dialogue is just as slick and distinctive as its character design. I also personally find very few of narrative pieces in this game to be filler, and even with its bizarre atmosphere, everything is constrained and developed within its internal logic. Nothing becomes too wacky, too ridiculous, too out there to believe. It's like a fever dream of a literature architect obsessed with magical realism, but the crazy part is, the realism here nails down the magical elements, unlike most of the notable works in this genre.The game's main mechanics are split into two parts - the conversations that's tied to investigation, and the exploration that actually functions like a collect-a-thon. You don't actually find too many evidences in the world, the majority of items you collect includes recording, tidbits related to lore and various artifacts that speak about the mystical history of Island 25. It is very unconventional in some senses, as the open world is on the same scale as Kamurocho found in Yakuza games, but the level of freedom is much higher with different verticality and hidden items in places you don't expect. It legit feels like a first person platformer at times due to the lack of invisible walls, which makes the open world incredibly satisfied to explore.And then there's the disco-fueled soundtrack that merged synthwave, vaporware and electronic. For a game that deals with pretty unpleasant themes, the music is uplifting and is just as colorful as the visual style. Half of the game's title is "PARADISE", after all.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Just fantastic all around.-The good-The world is downright beautiful, the music is catchy and soothing.All the characters are unique, and the story interesting.You can take your time and try to figure out the mystery or go around collecting the many items.The world is verbose and raises so many questions.-The Bad-The map is terrible.-The mixed-The game doesn't hold your hand on anything.Some things it should like the 3 powerup stations.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great detective game at its core that rewards those who are thorough and methodical in their search for clues. It can take a while for the puzzle pieces to fit together, but once it does it's a satisfying feeling to see the picture. My only complaint would be that much of the text in the game is presented on a bright white background, which can strain the eyes. It would be better if the background was darker. The art and music in the game are cool. Especially the art/design.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's literally just random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nonsense and pressing E on items that talk about nothing until you trip on the item that tells you exactly what's happening. The most basic stuff gets screwed up like finding a corpse and it still listing them as MIA in your computer. Does the dumb 5% of dialog is voice acted approach too where just totally random stuff is fully voiced midway through a conversation- not important lines even just random stuff. The whole game is pretty lol random so I guess it's just being consistent.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Franz Kafka and Danganronpa had dirty filthy sex and made a weird lil existential nihilist, anti-establishment/classist baby and dressed it in funky 80s vaporwave style and soundtrack. Its best mate at daycare is GTA Vice City (but mostly because they both like palm trees and funky shirts) and it hangs out a lot with its auntie SMT Persona (because they both like weird ♥♥♥♥, dark mysteries, and murder). No way you wouldn't love that kid. You'd love it but also end up with some kind of postmodern existential dread and you'll feel SOME kinda way about the government but be like you know what? THANK you, weird baby. I love that you're bringing these things up in such a chill way. PLAY THIS GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So, this isn't really a detective game, It's an open world exploration collectathon in which you find clues, chat with npcs and present those clues to them. That might be weird to say, but the deductions made aren't explicitly required for the player to make, unlike in Obra Dinn or Outer Wilds for example. This isn't a bad thing, Paradise Killer is very good exploration game, and it has a lot of elements that would benefit a true detective game that many games I consider detective games lack, it tracks your progress really well, It lets you know what you may have overlooked and the mystery is fun to unravel on your own despite not being prompted to do so.To elaborate, let's take Sherlock Holmes: Crimes and Punishments and Danganronpa as examples of 2 elements Paradise Killer emulates but does not reach.In Crimes and Punishments and Paradise Killer you collect evidence by exploring the world, however, in Crimes and Punishments it's on the player to put that evidence together to form a connection with their deduction board mechanic. Paradise Killer makes those deductions for you.Danganronpa and Paradise Killer feature trial sections where you present evidence to find out who's guilty of a crime, in Danganronpa you have to find contradictions in various statements and prove them to be untrue using what you know; doing this wrong fails the trial, Paradise Killer simply requires you to choose who you believe committed a crime and throw all the evidence at them at once without having to parse through statements or select the correct evidence.None of this is to say Paradise Killer should have perfectly emulated the above games, I think it does a great job at being an exploration game but the detective part of it might as well be an on rails visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cool, well realized world oozing with personality for you to explore. A freeform mystery game where you can solve the crime at your own pace, following the leads you want.Only minor annoyance is that the voice barks are a bit overused and almost seem like they're going for an intentionally-badly-acted style, but you can turn them off.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly slaps. It's all about exploring the island to collect as many clues and pieces of evidence as possible. The puzzles are fun, and although they're somewhat repetitive, never get stale. The story is probably the best part of the game. I found myself totally wrapped up in the narrative and desperate to unravel this conspiracy. There's a lot of moving parts, and finding each piece of the puzzle to put together is incredibly rewarding. The exploration mechanics (ie jumping around and navigating the island) can be a bit wonky at times, but I never found that it hindered my experience. Overall, it's a really special game. I would definitely recommend to anyone that likes narrative-driven experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Murder mystery with hot people.An aesthetically pleasing game with a narrative that at the very least makes sense and filled with a ton of character. When it comes to a game where you play as an investigator you can't really ask for much more. Though I will say the early game progression is a little bit awkward, often getting blocked due to not having certain upgrades and having little indication on how to get said upgrades until you go to certain locations on the map. That aside I think this games great, Exploring is rewarded and following up on strings of inquiry will bare fruit quite often.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most distinct games I played lately. The world and the characters are really interesting and memorable, as is the story. The player is free to progress and try to figure at the mystery at their own pace. Exploring the world is rewarding and it didn't get boring even after searching every corner of it. The length of the game is perfect too. Not too long to overstay its welcome, neither too short to feel rushed. The character designs were all really notable and probably the highlight of the game for me. The music, even though it isn't my type, felt perfect for the world. Really liked the, not so subtle, social commentary too.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: PARADISE KILLERis a game that dove confidently into an absolute bonkers premise and had me fully invested by the end, if not halfway through. Enjoy yourself as you gallivant about a surprisingly detailed island, listening to snappy 80s style funk songs, interviewing ludicrously-named characters and collecting evidence, y'know, detective stuff.It ain't perfect, but there are some really novel game design choices. Well-written, sympathetic characters despite the outlandish tone.Recommend avoid reading too much and just enjoy the investigation for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A great time. After 11 hours I feel I've found all the important clues while also completing most of the side missions, but to collect everything would likely take another few hours at least. The characters were all very fun and interesting to talk to, and the open-ended nature of the mystery made each discovery and conclusion drawn feel like my own. The soundtrack and style are both intoxicating and I'd love for there to be more games in a similar style. There were a few flaws, though. Making fast travel cost a limited in game resource ensured I rarely used it and now at the end I have a bunch of blood gems I don't need stockpiled. Also, the voice lines get repetitive really fast, as each character only has a handful of voice lines that they repeat each time you speak to them.The last flaw, however, is more of a compliment; I really wanted more. I wish I could have more time interacting with all the cool characters in this really unique world. Thus, I'm really excited for whatever Kaizen Game Works puts out next, because if it's even half as good as this I'm sure I'll enjoy it.tl,dr; Buy this game if you want a cosmic horror murder mystery set in a neon-tinted nostalgia ridden vapor-wave island, and I'm sure you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game.  I liked the world building and the open world exploring.  I really enjoyed it wasn't just a visual novel(A reason I actually put it off for so long) and that the writing really brought you into the world.  The aesthetic is also really neat if you like that almost 90s style geocities website kind of stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get into it.  It's more like a visual novel. Dialogue-heavy.  It becomes a chore to click through pages of info-dump dialogue until you have control over your character again.  I immediately lost track of all the meaningless alien names being thrown around without any context.Lacking in engaging gameplay from the start.  (After spending 10 minutes adjusting the settings to reduce eye strain and volume levels) You run around a very basic first-person 3D environment picking up items like meaningless tokens.  Every time you look at a flagged area of interest, a jarring banner flashes up on the screen.  The very first NPC you meet has incredibly annoying voice.  The rest of the voice acting overlaying the dialogue is jarring short canned responses that don't match the text.Shortly after speaking to the judge, I would have saved and returned to play another day, but the game still hadn't indicated how to find the save points.  I gave up and exited without saving.  Not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This culty vaporwave murder mystery is a very unique game experience. You've got platforming for collectables being put against one of the most convoluted murder mystery plots made. All the characters are stylish and constantly pose, and the jumping physics suck. If you execute the taxi-driver you can't fast travel at the end. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Delicious character designs and a banger ost with the feelings of playing one of those old 90's demo/exploration showcases. Comes with a free story and a beautifully bizarre world.Don't actually expect a detective game due to being able to brute force most of the story line without consequence, but figuring out the pieces of the puzzle yourself without doing so feels pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Island, a world outside reality. There’s been a murder that only "investigation freak" Lady Love Dies can solve. Gather evidence and interrogate suspects in this open world adventure. You can accuse anyone, but you’ll have to prove your case in trial to convict. It’s up to you to decide who’s guilty.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

detailed_description: Welcome to LYNX, the solar system’s leader in spaceship salvaging! We offer you the privilege of helping turn humanity’s past into its future by salvaging ships in zero-g. Each one is a puzzle, and how you solve it is up to you! Carve your way in, salvage everything, and maximize your profit. Our cutting-edge LYNX tech helps you do the job. Slice metal with the laser cutter and use the grapple tool to move salvage with ease. Earn upgrades, such as demo charges, sensors, and safety gear. Careful where you point those tools! Hazards include explosive decompression, fuel, electricity, and radiation. Your life is protected by our EverWork™ technology, but our profits aren’t. Your LYNX adventure starts now! Account balance owing is: 1,252,594,441.92 Credits Start paying that debt! Good luck, shipbreaker!
