_childDocuments_.review: I waited until a bit to write this to have clearer thoughts. Frankly, this game made me some of the saltiest I have ever been due to sheer game mechanics. I was SUPER excited about this game, I could hardly wait until download day and announced it all over how I was looking forward to playing!! It was gorgeous, gave windwaker vibes, and seemed like something that would give me hours of enjoyment...Please note, I played using a controller.What it does right:-Graphics: They are gorgeous. The art style is absolutely winderwaker-ish and it was what drew me to the game in the first place. In this regard, it does NOT disappoint.-Music: I love the concept of the animals having unique sounds, especially when a few types run around together and make a sort of song. It's also cool to hear them and start recognizing what they are by the sounds. The sailing music is gorgeous (though it is a bit repetitive after a bit)-Story: I did NOT finish this game (will get into that later) but the story up until this point (i was past chpt 3) was for the most part very emotional. It was definitely an interesting concept.. but they just sort of throw you into the fray without much explanation.-Sailing: It is like a lot of sailing in games. It does feel like you are against the wind a LOT but that is nothing tacking doesn't solve (allowing rowing w/ sail would fix). The water and just sailing around freely was as advertised. I spent a lot of time just excited to be running around with pretty music in the gorgeous waves. It gets even better as you upgrade ships.The disappointments:-Combat: It's a bit awkward. I played through and just found so many awkward weird things happening. It didn't feel polished. It got very monotonous after a while just kill, harvest, kill, harvest. Things rag doll or freeze in animations periodically. I either used my bow or just stab/doged-The bugs: This game is not being released as alpha or beta. That being said, there were a lot of bugs in this game for the price. It felt like they didn't bother letting people playtest it. Example: one of the tigers on the island was stuck in the jump down animation and glided around not animated. Periodic ragdolls, stuff disappearing, etc. They have been fixing things per the updates apparently. It takes time, but I am talking a bit too many for it being advertised as a finished game. They JUST fixed some of these things end of September.-"Survival": The survival mechanics in this are ridiculous. Definitely a huge make or break. I feel like 80% of this game is me struggling to keep her fed. One moment I have tons of food, the next it is all rotten and I am starving. There is no in between with this. It added nothing to my experience having to struggle with this. Did I mention I was in STORY MODE?! It doesn't keep you fed long and it rots super quick even in storage. What is the point here? (they have allegedly adjusted this though I have not experienced it)-You snooze you lose: If you do the 'real' game mode, death means you lose EVERYTHING and start completely over. Die in story mode, lose everything except your inventory.... so you still lose. Have your boat hardcore upgraded and lots of high tier stuff you were saving to upgrade something?... too bad. It again adds nothing to the game but frustration and forcing people to replay and regather things adding unnecessary grind. It felt lazy...  instead of giving us actual content, the gameplay puts all bets into you dying and having to grind back to where you were more than a few times. If you do respawn in story mode, it doesn't mean you can get all the stuff back you had, resources are so limited you probably can't rebuild your boat to even a fraction of where it was. (They apparently updated this end of September but I'm so burnt out on this game I probably wont try again until a while from now)-Music: I had to keep clicking in and out of the game to a music player for stream so that they weren't listening to just nothingness for large extents of time. If you are on an island, you will have a LOT of time in a musical black hole. It really is a pity because what music there is, is extremely high quality and wonderful to listen to.-Scarcity: I thought the scarcity stuff was interesting but you can't have crazy material requirements for recipes AND make everything hard to find/limited. Pick one or the other because this aspect was NOT balanced. There was a point I had to sail around EVERYWHERE just to try to find grass... spending more than 30 minutes doing so. Same with things breaking... if weapons are going to break that fast, then don't make materials that scarce or give a way to repair them.-As far as the eye can see...?: It talks about procedurally generated islands and such but really it doesn't add much at all. The islands may 'generate different' but that difference only means shapes of them and location for the most part. It's the same stuff. Sure, each new chapter gives you some new animals/biomes/items but that is very short lived excitement.-Storage: The storage situation was a constant issue. Many types of items and the talked about 'scarcity'; yet there is a constant need for lots of mats for recipes including things like campfires you have to constantly refuel... the storage is NOT good. It gets better later on in the game once you upgrade containers but there is a lot of inventory management that again does not fit well with the scarcity of resource concept. (They allegedly fixed this but again I am reviewing what I played and cannot comment on that fix)-So much wasted: No autosave... forget to save and lose potentially hours of progress.My Final Thoughts: This game had so much potential. It promised a lot of things but it seems to not be sure of it's own identity as a game. There needs to be more beyond adding a few more material and animal types each level. They talked about how things generate but it felt so cookie cutter each time I finished the 'level'. After the 3rd, I was sort of bored... I knew I would resource grind some more, try to upgrade some stuff,  kill things, try not to starve, activate alters....that's about it. Why should I feel for this protagonist? What is my emotional connection to her and her quest?...  I don't know many people who want to have a feed/respawn simulator. It just needs... more, even side quests on each level that help us understand our character and what is going on better or SOMETHING. I see her fall into water at the beginning and then?.... It really lacks in giving us a compelling reason to have any sort of connection or care of what is going on.... the story reveal at each chapter is just not cutting it, you can't bank everything on it which is exactly what they did. About my saltiness and stating I had not experienced the update? Frankly, I rage quit mid stream. I died a second time from hunger, lost my boat and all my stuff and I was done. D.O.N.E. I had pushed through the insane hunger/spoil rates, I sailed through the repetitiveness, I fought my way through the landscape of bugs and uncertainty... until I couldn't do it anymore. Having nothing and knowing even decimating the entire map strip mining it of everything would not get me close to what I had back and that I would not be able to get my ship back to even half of what it was due to the material requirements... It was a hard NO for me and I quit and never opened it again.  (this was back at the end of August)If you have no issue with dark souls; maybe, just maybe you will be alright with this level of grind/repeat. Beyond that, I expect a LOT more for $30 in terms of story/quest and content. Wait for it to be on sale if you truly want to try it. I streamed every second of my elation and frustration and it is painful to rewatch but when I feel maybe I should give this a try again, I do it to remind myself... save yourself the agony until they change A LOT of things.

_childDocuments_.review: A genuine slog to get through, Windbound is trying to be too many things at once, and isn’t good at any of them.Let me just say firstly, the music is lovely, and the art style is also great. The story is your typical indie, ambiguous nonsense but its fine overall, everything on the surface, conveys a rather tranquil experience (this is ruined by the gameplay, but we’ll get to that) And performance was mostly fine for me, with everything maxed, it isn’t an intensive game though.Survival mechanics that add nothing to the game, and just serve to annoy. Kara is hungry  the time, and it really gets repetitive having to constantly keep her hunger bar in check. Crafting is fine mostly, but it is nothing special or new, its just  in that regard.Frustrating sailing mechanics that never feel tight enough to be enjoyable. Constantly sailing against the wind to get to the next island is just not fun, at all.Combat is meh, very basic and enemies are annoying to fight, this is compounded by a roguelike death system of all things  that is just unfair and doesn’t give any incentive to play again, have fun going right back to the beginning of the game and losing hours of progress because of a loose combat system.The game is also rather short. I saw a comment left by the publisher that stated that the game has over 40 hours of content,, I’m sorry. The main story takes 7-8 hours, at a push, and that was with me really taking my time. I’m sure you can stretch the game out for a few more hours if you really wanted to get stuck in with the crafting (not sure why you would want to though) but 40 hours?

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wanted to enjoy this game. I really did. But for the most part, it looks like I'll be echoing some of the previous reviews. I got this game after all the DLC had been released, keep that in mind.PROS:- Beautiful artstyle, I've always enjoyed somewhat simplified cel-shaded environments- Crafting and gathering is satisfying and often relaxing- Battling creatures is interesting, each having their own patterns of movement and attacking. Learning them all eventually and defeating them that way was satisfying- While the OST is nothing to write home about, the adaptive music in this game is very well put together. I really liked the different instruments playing depending on what kind of creature is nearby.CONS:- The game has a pretty steep learning curve. You'll have to respect every bit of available resource, cuz they WILL be important in one way or another, like the food items for example.- While I did just say gathering and crafting was nice and all, along with traversing the map, its novelty quickly wears off and becomes tedious once you add the Forsaken and the Loathing mechanic to the mix. Speaking of...- The Forsaken have little reason to be there. Sure, it ties in with the lore, but their Loathing mechanic, which lowers your max HP until you cure it with a potion, along with other obstacles in their area are a pain to deal with. Fighting them one at a time is no problem for me, but because of how much of a regular occurrance they become, it sort of conflicts with the other more relaxing elements.- Despite the implied importance of items and the relatively large number of different item types, inventory management is a pain. Even when I tried my best to get the next best bag to expand said inventory, there were still many occasions where I had to seriously consider even taking a single certain ingredient with me until I find use for it later. Once you do drop the ingredient however, you've already traveled to a new chapter, where there's a very high chance you won't find any places where you could get more of that item.- For some things like Alchemy, you'll need a lot of different ingredients for a lot of different potions. And by the time I actually got a Cauldron, most of the important ingredients that WOULD'VE been useful are now stuck in another chapter, left on the ground because I needed space.- The crafting system in general is pretty robust as well, some items requiring a fair amount of resources. I went through most of the game in this slow pace of stopping at every island to soak in all the good materials because I thought I wasn't gathering enough. 16 hours as of writing this, and I managed to get SOFTLOCKED on the final chapter, because i got killed by a Terrorlurk, and the base of my wooden hull boat just despawned, leaving only the hull guard, the sail, and my chest with my extra items in it. This was the final straw, and I ended up watching a gameplay video on Youtube instead.If you wanna experience it yourself and want to train your analytical eye (like I did for a possible video), then I say go for it, but with this 3rd DLC out, I don't recommend buying it just to have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember No Man's Sky at launch? That's what this game is with amount of content.Windbound is described as being an open world survival game, I think a better description would be a survival-roguelite with physics based sailing exploration. I think a lot of the reason behind the negative reviews for this game are a miscommunication on what this game is.The game flow is very very similar to No Man's Sky 1.0 as you go to procedurally generated islands within a small area of ocean at a time. There's usually 4-5 islands within each of these "Chapters", the islands themselves are pretty dull and are just a place to gather resources for your boat. Dying causes you to lose any progress made within a Chapter including your boat which you gather resources to improve and craft. The combat system is not exactly the most clean and polished. There is a targeting system but no targeting indicator, which means you might not know if you are actually locked onto an enemy or not. Some hits with spears and bows don't seem to register, which can be frustrating when death means you lose your boat.Sailing is okay but there's no easy way to switch between paddling and sailing. If you want to switch from sailing mode to paddling mode you need to open your crafting menu and deconstruct your sail from your boat. Overall this game isn't terrible, with a few patches I think it could be a great game. I'd personally be happy if I was able to assign my own key binds in a future update, and some form of targeting indicator was added for combat. I'd also like to see this base of this game expanded, maybe separate game mode where you explore an infinite ocean with infinite islands and see how long you can last before you die.Edit: After playing the game for a few more hours I decided to add some things to this review that I think would make the game more enjoyable overall.

_childDocuments_.review: This is first and foremost a survival, sailing, and crafting game. If you're thinking of getting this game based on aesthetics or comparisons to other games, make sure you are clear on what to expect. Those who come thinking this is an extensive open world BotW-like fantasy RPG will be disappointed, and I think this, plus some early release bugs (that seem to be mostly resolved) are largely what account for the early negative reviews. I really enjoyed my time with this game and think others will too if entering with the right expectations. This was my first ever survival-type game, and I'm so glad it was this one. Ultimately the gameplay loop is small, but it can be very relaxing, especially as you gain resources and confidence - sail, explore an island, hunt and gather, craft, and repeat. This is broken up with some light questing in Story mode (find some towers, complete any tasks to unlock them, find the final tower, perform a sailing challenge), but as a game about a sole character lost in the Forbidden islands, there aren't really other characters or side quests as such.  While grinding to avoid starvation and gather supplies for upgrades felt difficult and at times repetitive early on, it really does build a sense of accomplishment and engagement when you reach a point of abundance. The crafting system is deep enough to spur on a desire for discovery, and building up Kara's boat, weapons, potions, and other resources becomes a satisfying loop as you progress. The graphics are beautiful, the music is amazing, and overall the controls felt good. There are some nice little details in the environments, as well as the movements and sounds Kara will make, that helped keep me immersed. I enjoyed discovering all the different biomes as I progressed - they were often very cinematic and gorgeous, although there's not a ton of overall variety (the procedural generation of the islands mainly has to do with island shape and resources). Still, I was finding new biomes and creatures right up to the 5th and final chapter of the story-mode gameplay. Additional treasures and bonuses are regularly found on small islands scattered around the map, encouraging exploration. Sailing is surprisingly nuanced, and while it will certainly lead to some early game frustration (especially when traveling against the wind), it become increasingly enjoyable as you upgrade your boat and learn to master the controls (tip: by Chapter 3, make sure you find the resources needed to build some figureheads on your boat - the Gloomharrow figurehead allows you to apply occasional bursts of speed that make sailing against the wind or outrunning sharks a non-issue). There are a lot of environment variables both on land and in the sea - storms, fog, coral reefs, hidden rock outcroppings, sharks, little crobsters that will chew away at your boat; night/day cycles in which animals sleep (making it easier to catch them by surprise when hunting),  sunsets and moon rises, rain, and more. Combat is a bit limited (dodge, attack, dodge works for most enemies) but further updates are apparently coming in 2021, including a significant combat overhaul, and so far the devs have shown themselves to be really responsive to community requests, ideas, and bug reports. I only encountered a few minor bugs during my play time (killed animals disappearing when momentarily out of sight; creatures occasionally glitching when caught on an environmental factor; one time an accessory disappeared from my boat when loading a save) but I can see from the updates that a lot of progress has been made, and more is coming, and I experienced nothing close to gamebreaking issues in my time. Overall, the story is perhaps a bit thin (and told wordlessly, leaving a fair bit of room for interpretation until the end), but by the end of Chapter 5, I'd built enough investment in Kara's journey that the ending still had emotional resonance for me. The different gameplay modes are  great: survival mode turns the game into a roguelike, where all progress and collectables are lost on death except what's held. Story mode is generous in letting you keep everything you have so you can focus on narrative progress, and can even be abused (by collecting resources, crafting, dying, and then collecting again from new procedurally generated islands) if desired, to over-level your character before proceeding. There's also a free sailing mode that allows you to just enjoy the flow without worrying about progress, and a New Game+ that allows you to continue with your profile in Endless mode (no cap on levels) after finishing all 5 current story chapters of the game. Having 3 different save slots for profiles is nice as well. There's even a really cute Photo mode that can be used at any point in the game to capture gorgeous images of Kara in motion. Each story chapter features a "crossing" at the end, a sailing challenge that I admit was my least favorite part of the game, as they grow repetitive after the first few times. Otherwise, I took my time, and found the play experience very relaxing between bouts of intensity - dealing with a shark attack in the middle of a storm; fighting off an unexpected animal attack; etc. I really hope more people give this game a chance. It's clearly been created with care by a thoughtful team who continue to show it love post-release. Had it been first released as an early access title, I think a lot of the complaints you'll find in the comments would not exist - and as it is, many of them have been addressed at this point. If you want to try a sailing and survival game that isn't constantly fraught  and is mostly concentrated around a small but varied gameplay loop, this is a great title.

_childDocuments_.review: Allright folks, if there was a "maybe" category of review that's what I'd put down but in the mean time I cannot recommend the game at this time. For now lets Look at the good, bad, and ugly.The Good1. Graphics are phenomenal. Love this cell shaded style that is very similar to Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild. It is very very clear the devs went in with a clear idea of the style and feel of the game and each asset is well crafted.2. The story is interesting enough, having you piece it together through alot of context clues and little blurbs of text.3. The sound track is really good, if a bit repetitive.The Bad1. The "survivalist" mode boasts a mighty challenge of you needing to live through all 5 chapters of play. Die and you get sent back to the beginning with only you're "held" inventory. While you can cheese the "held " inventory, its real easy to get turned off because you died in a stupid way and now have to restart the whole thing.2. Critter variety is fairly low, meaning you over come the same type of challenges over and over again.  The predator critters also tend to get cheesed a lot after you get your hands on any type of bow.3. Repetition gets really extreme. Each chapter is "find the three maguffins" and then a sea race portion that only gets progressively more obnoxious rather than challenging. its a bit disappointing considering that they've built a world with interesting lore, but haven't done anything to incorporate it into being good progression.The Ugly1. Length- WHY IS THIS GAME SO SHORT AND $30!!! You get 5 chapters to go through for a story play-thru and if don't stop to do any crafting outside of making a canoe or small boat and food you can easily beat it in maybe 4-5 hours.  It is a absolute travesty that the game has a lack of content to this degree for this price point as it doesn't meet the "dollar/hr" test.2. Bugs- Hoooo boy. Game shows lots of graphical polish but there are bugs abound in this one. From creatures doing their best sputnik impression when ya kill them, to some very very questionable map generation (hi i spent 3 hours looking for a tower that decided to spawn MILES away from any other solid landmass) But biggest offender is that the boat physics is BORKED to all get out. From rubber banding, to randomly taking a nose dive into the water  (despite being back heavy). This makes it very frustrating to sail the seas which is a big selling point of the game.3. Master of none- So they had some very cool ideas and concepts that they iterated off of games like breath of the wild and Raft, but it feels like they couldn't commit to anythin. The combat system is loose and is VERY frustrating as their combat lock does not jump between targets (you have to click out and click back in to lock on to a new target). The ship building mechanic is very, very touchy often times making it hard to put things where you want them. (Also if you put a sail on your boat you can no longer paddle manually which is VERY useful for getting into islands with extremely tight inlets) The stamina mechanic is obtrusive and annoying making your character (Who is very clearly some form of islander) Damn near incapable of swimming for more than 3-7 seconds. on a map that is 97% water.   They touch on so many interesting and potentially awesome concepts but it just seems like they aren't baked all the way through.Overall- Would not buy at full price. wait for a sale and go in expecting a survival-lite story game that has alot of limitations and issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a bit of a rework for combat before I'd consider keeping it/buying it again. Spear weapons stab only into the ground to cripple only the ankles of whatever you're fighting, slingshots and bows deal damage that is negligible to anything other than squirrels, and recovery time for any movement during combat is sloth-like.The crafting and sailing is intriguing at first, but it's limitations reveal themselves quite early in Chapter 1. It is extremely frustrating to see elements in the wild in Chapter 1 that you have no reasonable way to obtain without extreme dedication and effort:In order to make a shovel, a default recipe, used for digging in the dirt you find on the island you start on, requires a rhino's horn plate. These rhino creatures can be found in Chapter 1, but travel in pairs and deal a stun with every hit they land. They're as fast as you and take off a quarter of you max health every hit. So with your plastic knife, sharpened stick, or sling, you have to either be dedicated to playing this game, or a no armor DS3 god. This difficulty is not much easier when dropped to the "easy" difficulty.Getting dunked on by bugged enemy AI is just not the "relaxing rafting survival sim" that all material i've seen about this game has made it seem

_childDocuments_.review: An AMAZING game, if you want a beautiful relaxed-ish, survival, crafting, building, exploration, hunting, fighting game.I have been playing games since 1982 and have played a lot! I only write reviews when I feel a game is really something special (not often) or it has been unfairly reviewed by other people (both in this case).You basically have a mobile base (your boat) and move from one island to another (each with its own ecosystem/biome) exploring, in order to progress onward through a magical portal to the next island archipelago. And so you sail in between islands, which creates a nice change and different dynamic in between exploring islands. And the sailing mechanics and physics are super. It can sometimes be exhilarating when the wind is at your back; sometimes stressful when there is a storm; and sometimes relaxing when the wind is against you; like actual sailing really! Graphics, animation and art style are all incredibly beautiful. One of those games where you just stop for a while and gaze around… Music is also great. Story is mysterious and wonderful. Altogether it creates a really enthralling mystical atmosphere. There are some different game modes too if you want the experience to be more demanding and less relaxing.Only three small problems: (1) you cannot rebind keys but there are plenty of external software options that can sort that out and its worth the small effort; (2) it is very addictive; (3) it will end at some point and you will feel disappointed it is over, but that is just like life really… (I hope the devs make some dlc or a Windbound ‘Too’ and that I am lucky enough to be reborn into its world when this one ends ;)A bargain at full asking price! I stumbled across it only by chance (thanks to Steam’s terrible algorithms…) and am very lucky to have done so. It is a work of art and deserves to be honoured as such.[Non-essential footnote: as for the bad reviews; it’s the reviewers that have problems; not the game. If you read them carefully, you can see how superficial, petty and unfair they are. There are no substantial criticisms in the bad reviews. Bad fighting mechanics!? I had no problem with them, and for a game that isn’t really about combat (and it makes up only a small part of the game) I think the mechanics are actually very good. You obviously just don’t have the skills to deal with it. Buy Tekken 7 or some other braindead fighting game and not this game… Sailing is slow and you check your mobile phone!? It is called relaxing! Have you ever sailed before?! Don’t buy a game with sailing in it… It isn’t actually that slow; sometimes it is fast; you just have the attention span of a fruit fly because you are oversaturated with sensory input from rampant capitalism…and your parents have not raised you properly to know any better…  My overall recommendation: get your hands out of your trousers and yourself out of your bedroom, spoiled kids, and try to create something that is even a fraction as good as this game, and then your insignificant existences might have been worth something… rather than disrespecting things you don’t understand… (sorry… did I go too far? I am a little perturbed by the unjust reviews that might put others off from experiencing this great game. But unfair reviewers, you might just now know how it feels to have to deal with overly harsh and completely unnecessary criticism).]

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at other reviews, I think people are being a little unkind on this game.  My guess is the frustration comes because the game is a bit mis-sold. I was genuinely expecting a lot 'more' game, the crafting system is pretty good but again with a tiny bit of planning it's very little work to have an abundance of resources.  My other minor criticism is completing chapter 1 gives you an opportunity to become completely OP for the rest of the game.  (I won't mention anything specific as I don't wish to put in spoilers).There is fun to be had out of this game, it's pretty relaxing, the audio reasonably good (although the sailing music quickly gets repetitive as you do have to sail a lot). _childDocuments_.review: A fun and interesting game with a lot of potential, marred and held back by massive bugs, glitches, and poor optimisation. tl;dr Fun game riddled with bugs and glitches. Hard pass unless on a steep sale. Game needs a LOT more polish to be worth full asking price.Pros:Unique and interesting story/loreCellshade art (if you're into that)Really nice OSTBuilding your own boat is entertainingCombat is simple, yet punishingRogue-like that's not too punishing (and can be gamed if you plan ahead after a few runs)Still getting updatesCons:You fight the camera more than the beasts you huntNo option to rebind your keysThe physics engine only works when it wants to when sailing (I've come to complete dead-stops sailing WITH the wind on a stable boat)AI is easy to cheese and sometimes outright doesn't workObjects spawn inside other objectsOverabundant corrupted islandsHit boxes are janky as hellThe game CHUGS when you make a boat bigger than a handful of hullsYou CAN get soft-locked with RNG if tools break (have had a shovel break and needed to get to the next chapter and the mob needed for crafting did not spawn anywhere on the map)And a laundry list of other small bugs and issues that escape me as of writing this review.I've had really high highs, laughing at seeing a mob helpless roll down a slope, and other hilarious and hair raising moments near death with no food or potions fighting to find the next few scraps to proceed to the next map. And really low lows. As I mentioned in the cons, I've come to complete dead stops while sailing with the wind which makes absolutely no sense. The camera snaps off to some other point of focus mid-combat more often than is acceptable with combat as punishing as it is. More noticable in more tight areas with objects that obscure/force move the camera (boulders, large trees, piles of goop, ect.).If this game gets any updates that fixes the massive list of issues that it currently has, I'd happily change my recommendation. Until then, I cannot in good faith recommend this game. There's a lot of fun to be had in Windbound if you can look past the issues it has, you can find yourself a diamond in the rough. Hopefully the devs keep up with the updates and make what's currently a lump of coal into the diamond it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: This is tough, I was really looking forward to Windbound.The combat is messy; nothing really feel like it connects properly, plus for melee you have a dodge button and a single attack button. That's it. Encounters became quickly boring, especially as the lock-on feature doesn't really stay trained on enemies if they move around you. I'm not asking for a full-fledged combat system with masses of combos, but it feels uninspiring enough to discourage me from engaging in fighting anything. The only goal to kill anything is to obtain resource, but manages to remove any element of fun in the process.The aspect that I thought would redeem this title is the sailing, but I was completely wrong. You're constantly battling against the wind to an extent that if the breeze is moving the other way, you simply don't move at all. While that sounds logical, from a gameplay standpoint it is terrible. You don't have the option to row against the wind once you've invested in sails, so you're forced to go wherever the wind takes you. While this may appeal to some, it doesn't appeal to me when I'm trying to get to a specific island and my only option is to simply just wait until the wind changes.Also, Kara is hungry literally all the time. I've always found hunger to be a hit and miss mechanic in most survival games; if it adds nothing to the experience, then there is little reason for it to be present. Hunger feels like it was just tacked on as an additional forced gameloop in the game, I can't think of a single positive reason about why it was added.As far as positives go, the game looks and plays really well. I was able to get upwards of 170fps at 1440p on an RTX2080 and 3800x, which feels almost unheard of for launch titles these days. The sound and music is also gorgeous, so my heart goes out to whoever did the sound design and OST.Either way, this game could be a lot better with a few but crucial tweaks. The combat needs some extra polish and the games main travel system needs a little more thought behind it.If anyone feels the need to get angry at me for leaving a negative review with only 1 hour play time, it was enough time to for me to figure out that the game was just going to be annoying and tedious for the next several. Also, I've seen people post positive reviews with 0.1 hours playtime, so I guess it swings in roundabouts.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, so I do not usually like survival games but this is an exception I am very VERY glad I made! It's not perfect and they are some little issues the game has but most of this is either very small texture issues or just jumping to a ledge and not landing it. The last one is definitely something games have been suffering with for years at this point so... yeah.Anyway! The game is, in my opinion, really good! It nails the feeling of being alone and in a world that wants to kill you at every moment it can get and that's why I love it so much! Well one of the reasons anyway. There are moments where this game is utterly serene and incredibly relaxing and other moments where you will be fighting for your life against a huge shark who flips your boat over and can even destroy it!Pros:- The music is STUNNING! I am not even joking here, the music in this game is excellent!- The art style is really nice in my opinion!- The enemy types are varied and can genuinely scare the crap out of you if you are not paying attention.- The combat is simple but extremely rewarding when mastered!- The crafting interface and overall HUD of the game is very nicely laid out and finding things/understanding it is easy as can be.- The game runs very very well on my PC. Yes my PC is very overpowered but it's nice nevertheless.- The character model of the playable character is really nicely done. No over exaggerated proportions or silly stuff like that.- You can find different armour and clothing in the world and doing so is unique in it's own right.- The story is nice. Simple but nice.Cons:- I can see some people getting frustrated with this game. If you can't stand Survival in any form, you are likely not this games target audience.- It can be brutally hard. Like if you go into a fight even slightly unprepared, the bosses in this game especially will mop the floor with you.- This is very much a personal taste and I don't personally care about it but the lack of voice acting may put players off and if you are a slow reader and want to understand the story, you may need to give this some thought.Overall: An excellent game that took me hours to get into and enjoy and when I did, it is an excellent little game! I'm honestly surprised and also not at the reviews the game has gotten so far. It really is a slow burn but when you get to the meat of it, you will likely see why people enjoy this game! It will definitely be the gaming version of a cult classic in the future in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: is a hugely ambitious game that is pretty difficult to recommend. The developers attempted an , and they came pretty close to realising that goal. The game has a lot of praiseworthy aspects—the sailing mechanics, ship building, music and art direction are all top notch. But those qualities are held back by clunky and repetitive combat, made even worse by the heavy-handed punishments for death the game employs. The result is a game that can be super relaxing one minute as you sail around on your ship, and then massively frustrating the next as you get stunlocked and ragdolled across an island to your death.Despite all this, I'd still tentatively recommend Windbound—especially if you have a soft spot for sailing in video games—with the caveat that it is best played on the Adventure difficulty. The Survival and Endless gamemodes can be masochistically punishing.

_childDocuments_.review: I already played this game on Epic Games, so my playtime on Steam doesn't reflect my actual time with it. The main reason I decided to buy it on steam was to support the developers, and to give it a positive review, since I was genuinely surprised at how mixed the reviews here are.Personally, I found the game really fun all around. The combat is pretty basic, but engaging and challenging enough to allow for a satisfying progression curve and give you an incentive to get better tools. The heart and main selling point of this game really is the sailing. Genuinely, this is the first game where I actually had fun just traveling from one island to the next. It is a bit difficult to wrap your head around at first, and personally I had to look up a guide to help me understand this mechanic (it is explained in-game and honestly not particularly complicated, I guess the explanation just didn't click with me), but once I figured out how to zoom from one corner of the map to the other regardless of the wind's direction, I had tons of fun just traveling from island to island and discovering new biomes, enemies and materials.Essentially, I believe this game will be fun for anyone who likes the basic game-loop of the survival genre, doesn't hate stamina-based action-combat and is willing to invest the 5-10 minutes necessary to learn how the sailing works. From what I can tell, most negative reviews come from people who only find one of these aspects appealing and thus aren't able to enjoy the full experience as it was intended. That is of course a fair reason to dislike a game, but it's also not the game's fault.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Verdict:TL;DR : " This game has an ocean full of opportunities, but the depth of a shallow puddle. "- me 2020I have to give the game credit for it’s incredible visuals, the artstyle is very pleasing and gives you that classic cell shaded windwaker feel. I only saw one or two minor graphical errors. The music is also beautifully fitting for a calming and relaxing voyage albeit a small soundtrack that will quickly take you back to the same tunes. Controlling and upgrading your ship feels pretty good. I honestly don't understand all the complaints about wind direction or sailing. Sure once you get a bigger ship the wind hinders you significantly more, but if you are tightening and loosening the sail as well as zig-zagging while sailing against the wind you can still get significant bursts of speed. I have not once been forced to a stand-still or unable to move / sail into the wind like some reviews mention.Though after playing for a couple of hours I can’t help but be left with the feeling of “Is that it?” As I said earlier, this game has a lot of opportunity but it feels like everything implemented in the game is rather shallow. Melee combat has a single attack button and can feel clunky. Ranged combat is nothing intuitive. The potential for exploration is there as the map is beautiful and fun to explore initially, but once you have seen the area once, it’s going to be the same when you restart. It has a “rogue-like” permadeath restart when you die kind of mode yet has minimal procedural generation and lacks meaningful aspects of change to make any playthrough feel unique. The “survival” aspect of the game is just “eat when you see this bar get low” no shelter creation, no need for hydration, no need for rest, no need for management of temperature / keeping dry, no weight / inventory management aside from organizing your stacks of items to decide what you would lose upon death and what you would keep on your next playthrough.All in all, I have to say this game is an enjoyable experience for me and I love everything this game is setting out to be but at the same time leaves me wanting so much more. To a point that I just can't really feel satisfied with the content it does provide. I feel like they didn’t go in depth enough for many of the core mechanics of the game. Not enough variation in exploration or world generation to satisfy as an exploration game. Not enough character development, progression or customization to be an RPG. Not deep enough combat to find any enjoyment in the combat system past overcoming that new creature the first few times which can only happen a few times due to the limited wildlife roster; combat lacks capability of discovering combos, abilities or experimenting with different approaches to encounters (Take BotW for example. Despite having a combat system consisting of a single melee attack button there is still an incredible amount of depth and creativity available in how you approach every combat situation through a mix of ranged attacks, combat utility tools, etc) Not enough management of needs to satisfy as a survival game. Not enough crafting freedom to satisfy as a sandbox. It feels as if this game is early access, and if it was I would say it has an incredible foundation and a mass of untapped potential. Though, if this is truly everything the game has to offer I just can’t completely recommend it because there isn’t much depth throughout the game and I feel like many aspects of it should’ve been expanded upon. Although, it has some positive aspects and can still be an enjoyable experience if you're just looking for a relaxed simple sailing & survival lite game. I have to admit it was much less than I expected to get from it and left me feeling disappointed that they didn't do more with this ocean of opportunity available to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, at first it looked beautiful, but the longer I played, the more flaws I noticed.Graphic-wise it is really nice. The story and setting needs some addition. You drop right into the game, without proper introduction or tutorial. But as you progress you get some tutorials. Unfortunately over and over again. Each time you encounter the same scenario, you get the same tutorial...The balancing is quite special...the food is just for the chapter, theres no way you can spare something for later on. Materials for building quite the same, you unlock recipes with items required which you get 1-2 chapters later.But there are flowers all over the place. Too much to carry or even store them. The storage-system is unbalanced as well. Its easier (and gives you more spaces) to craft bags and racks than storage crates...At last, there are some bugs/glitches as well. Bugs more annoying, glitches likely to be in your favor. If you want to carry additional tools with you because the current one is close to breaking? Too bad, with the current one the new breaks as well. You want to finish a level because you farmed and killed the entire map? Well, too bad, you can't unlock the final island of the chapter because you are missing something? Wanna know what? Go and take a look yourself, the game won't tell you.But in return you can use some glitches. If you deal enough damage, all mobs run away and you can follow and harass them all around. And certainly the halloween-items help you out. The weapon deals enough damage on range with no ammunition needed and well, this item doesn't break.Over all the game is quite good, but has definitely issues. The balancing needs a rework for sure, the guidance troughout the chapters at least some additions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful looking game, but ultimately the controls and some poor game play decisions by the dev just ruin what could have been so much better and mean it's time for me to stop playing mid-way through.Devs if you're listening:- Let the mouse control movement of the player when not on a boat.- Trying to replicate the actual wind physics of a sailboat sounds good on paper, but ruins the casual nature of the game.- Add more resources to the game, and provide a mode where tools don't break.- Don't reset my save game if i die. and then force me to reconquer the three towers. That's very, very, very unfun. I really can't wrap my head around this. Especially since your player controls are so poor that I find I'm dying due to issues outside of my control.- Don't show me items in the first few levels that I am unable to obtain (eg. underwater seashell fragments in level 1). Again, that's just frustrating. And it's not like I can go back to retrieve them, since the levels are procedural.- the sharks are very, very, overpowered. - the boats are too fragile.Honestly, I think if there was a little bit more time dedicated to gameplay balance, this would have been a really neat entry into the Zelda/casual adventure genre

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game. I recently finished, it is a masterpiece. A rough and deeply flawed gem, but a gem none-the-less. If you are interested in getting this game, let me give you some tips:(FAIR WARING: this game is buggy at times, but I've encountered nothing that can't be fixed by reloading)1. Don't give up until you get to chapter 3. It is clunky starting out, but like Pathologic 2 or Rain World, it has a lot to offer the determined player. 2. The bamboo raft goes *on* your existing canoe. Once it is on there you get to start expanding your ship and the game starts picking up pace. 3. Wood/sticks don't seem to grow back - your canoe needs to have a bonfire on it first and foremost to save wood for more important things (like ammo/spears).4.EXPLORE! There are secrets and goodies all over the place. 5. The sailing is very realistic. Large waves and strong wind can capsize you. A still sea and the wind against you can leave you dead in the water. Try to understand what the game wants of you.6. Food is plentiful if you know where to look. Mushooms on trees and berry bushes regrow. Take advantage.7. Melee is for losers (CORRECTION: *was* for losers. The new combat tweaks and skills make melee viable against a number of enemies). Get a bow as soon as possible and just pepper whatever gets in your way. If you use slings, I hate you and you deserve all the suffering you experience in life.8. Save often.9. The Broom is your best friend. Fishing, Silkmaws. Razorbubs. Any small enemy is almost instantly dispatched by the broom.10. You're going to die, embrace it. Learn what materials you need to hang onto for your next run. If you are looking for a demanding survival adventure game, this is the game for you. Take it slow and you'll be just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game at its current stage. Saw the trailer and got really interested, really loved the idea of island-hopping and survival. The visuals, environment and soundtrack were spectacular; it has that strange and peaceful vibe to it. However, that's the only benefit I could find. The survival mechanics were really basic, the same could be said about its combat, it doesn't bring anything new to the table. The hunger system is really annoying, especially early on in the game. Like what the previous review said, Kara gets hungry way too often. The wind is another downside to this game, thought realistic and somewhat cool, it quickly becomes a chore. It would be of great benefit if we could swap between the oar and the sail seamlessly. The wind also makes larger ships practically impossible to move if you're going against the wind, it's realistic but not fun. However, the biggest issue I have with this game is the lack of content. For a $25 game I would expect more at launch, after playing for an hour, I've felt that I've explored most of what the game has to offer. Yes, I could build a giant boat but it's not really true gameplay as it's more of a grind; I guess some people might like it? This does not include bugs, such as V-SYNC affecting mouse sensitivity, lack of guidance/tutorial and annoying gameplay mechanics. Also, not to mention that you can't change your keybindsIn the end, I do not recommend this game at its current state and price point. It's a promising game but I would wait for a sale or at least a few months.Overall Rating: 4/10, maybe a 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: i got this after all of the DLC came out, and only started playing it then; the same way that you will likely play it. Right from the outset the game does have a steep learning curve and is fairly unforgiving. The beauty of the game and the potential of it's tranquillity that were part of the original hype around the game have given way to survival, limited crafting and  challenging enemies. This got worse with the release of the third DLC and the introduction of the Loathing and Forsaken. There is not ability to turn these off, and they appear about a third of the way in. I felt they ruin the game by needlessly adding a further class of enemy thats very challenging to beat. Replayability is limited, and after completing it once i don't want to go back. Some of the control mechanics are too clumsy and poorly implemented resulting in the wrong action at the wrong time - often a fatal problem. It looks like the developer changed course early on, totally changing the direction of the game and in doing so compromised the concept. If you're coming blind to it you might accept that and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: That game has a lot of potential, but at the moment I cannot recommend it.This could be a nice game, with a distinctive BotW feel, but it feels unfinished right now.Visuals are good, but not great. Music is relaxing. Movement is a bit sluggish, even on the boat. Combat is disappointing.Exploration doesn't feel rewarding at all. You just run around, burning stamina (that implies eating) to find nothing: rocks, grass, a few "sea shards" (the game currency), and that's it most of the time.The crafting part is boring and requires materials you cannot get quite early: you need to kill huge beasts with tons of HP that can 2shot you, with the best weapon you can craft: a spear made from a twig. Weapons break very fast, and you constantly need to hunt to prevent starvation.I know it's a survival game, but cmon, this isn't supposed to be that boring.Added the fact that you start back at the very beginning everytime you die, it's a really frustrating game.The worst part of it is the controls, which are split between two camera modes: one for running, jumping etc., and the other one for aiming, dodging, fighting. That means you cannot dodge an attack you detect late, and you cannot jump over a rock while fighting.Btw, couldn't find the keyboard remapping option, so I played with my Xbox controller. I feel it would be a bit easier to deal with the weird control scheme with a correct mapping.I'll try again later if I see some interesting patch notes.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but I felt I had to try to do something to correct the baffling number of negative reviews this game has received. Steam shouldn't even allow reviews from players who play less than 10 hours, because they just do not know what they're talking about. I'm about 20 hours in now and just beginning to wrap my head around how good this game really is. Yeah, it's hard. You actually have to exercise an abundance of caution if you don't want to die, and yes you will die. You are meant to die in fact. The mechanics that all the negative reviewers whine about are deliberate and are what make the game as good as it is. You gotta git gud with the combat mechanics, which takes time. You gotta learn what stuff really is the best to bring with you when you die. You have to learn some sailing mechanics or you're going to drown. Sometimes you gotta zig and zag into the wind to make progress, just like actual sailing. You are going to starve to death until you gain experience with hunting and gathering. The slow mastery of the games difficult mechanics IS the game. Played this for an hour and didn't like it? Your loss, move on. But don't think for one second that you have any understanding of what this game really is, because in 25 years of gaming this is absolutely one I'll take the time to recommend. It's a unique gem of a rogue-like survival crafter, not without its minor issues, but well worth your dollar, especially on sale. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I must say I'm a bit confused at how vehement the negative reviews of the game are. You would think this game killed their parents or something with how angry some of the reviews can get.I've had enough time in the game to experience all the mechanics, from gathering and inventory management, to sailing, to combat, and the various other mechanics. I have thoroughly enjoyed Windbound so far. The story is pretty solid, the art is gorgeous to look at, exploration is fun, and the core gameplay loop is pretty solid. I've never felt like I spent too much time in any particular Chapter/World/Whatever you want to call each set of islands. I've also not run into the problems that the other reviews so prominently feature.Windbound is a good game. It does a good job of explaining to you what you're supposed to be doing, if you're paying attention. I went in expecting a steep learning curve, like one of the reviews put it, and that never actually happened. The in-game tutorials are non-intrusive and do a good job of explaining the game's mechanics. They continue to show up until you've gotten the point of it. My only gripe early on was inventory management, but it quickly becomes easier as you craft bigger baskets and bags. Before that, it was tough to manage my resources, with me dropping things and leaving them behind (but even then, not really). Even then, inventory management only really became a problem for me in the World 2 (or Chapter 2, or whatever it's called), and it was also solved in World 2. Once I got a Bamboo basket to put on my boat, my worries were solved. It slowly crept up again in World 3 with the addition of the forest islands, but once again, it was solved in World 3 with the addition of silk and bigger bags. The only "scarce" resources (as in, they don't respawn when harvested) are things like Sticks, Thick Grass, Clay, and Bamboo, but the game supplies you with enough of it. That being said, I've never felt like I've been starved on resources - especially not any of the critical resources like Thick Grass, Sticks, Palm Fronds, Bamboo, etc. Most appear frequently enough that you'll have a good amount to spare.I think the only mechanic that isn't really well explained is boat crafting. I knew it was possible to expand my boat, but it didn't really teach me that. I learned  to do it when I was standing on my boat while in the boat crafting menu, because the boat parts just kind of snapped to the rest of the boat. I can picture some players running through the game with only a single hull, which has room for a basket and a sail, and that might be where some of the problem arises with things like inventory management.The combat isn't the best combat I've experienced, but it is also by no means bad. While it can be a little buggy sometimes, I've never come away from a combat encounter with a bad taste in my mouth. I have a couple of minor gripes about how the system works, particularly with regards to targeting, but it's also nowhere near as bad as one of the reviews puts it. The ability to "target nothing" is by design. I've also never had trouble with enemies getting the jump on me or sneaking up on me because there are very clear audio cues that tell you you've been spotted/are in combat. (Yes, this is in direct response to one of the reviews that angrily calls the combat trash because of what amount to personal problems and skill issue).If you're really worried that you won't enjoy it, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is lovely, and I liked the boat construction and sailing. But that's about it for the pros. I would refund if I could, but y'know, Steam.I knew going into this game that it did not have housing/building like many survival games do, but I still hoped that it would offer a little bit more Valheim-esque exploration. It really doesn't.Each "chapter" or map, you have a small circular playable sea region and some islands are scattered within it. You must gather materials to make your boat and weapons, acquire food to survive, and then make it to towers on certain islands to activate them in order to progress to the next chapter... another circular ocean with islands (of increasing difficulty, such as the corrupted islands).Point being that there really isn't true exploration with a sense of mystery... you can't ever get lost at sea, even if there are storms and fog slightly inhibiting vision, because the map will show your location. You can just reorient yourself back onto your intended trajectory to the next unexplored area to clear those islands. It begins to become repetitive and unexciting.The game has two "difficulties," which I'll simply state are... -- Lose everything (including entire boat), except for a few "Held" item slots in inventory. Too hard, causes frustrating repetitive grind. Death resets all Chapter progress, back to chapter 1 in the very beginning. Extremely punishing. -- Don't lose anything, keeps boat, inventory, and only returns you to the respawn start of your current chapter, not all the way back to Chapter 1 (reminder, Chapters are the circular ocean maps, so redoing all of those means resailing out to find each island with a tower on it, activating it, and then finding the "portal" island to exit to the next. Multiple times, for example if you died in Chapter 4. So in Survivalist mode, that's a long way to go for... whoops, one death.)Adventure mode is simply too easy. If you find yourself low on food, hungry, or needing more boat mats because the islands didn't give you enough... just kill yourself. You'll respawn with everything, full health/hunger, and the map is regenerated (so you do have to re-explore everything), but more mats so no scarcity. That's too easily abused.They missed the mark in balancing and finding a middle-ground between those two difficulties. Something challenging, but not relying on repetition or frustratingly having to do it perfect without ever dying once.The game also has an Endless Mode (but only uses the harsh Survivalist ruleset, not Adventure), and New Game+ after beating the game (which can be Adventure, but New Game+ is essentially just replaying the already repetitive story campaign). Not like Endless mode, which the only info I can find from the devs states:They don't state whether that means (for example) a Chapter 6 gets procedurally generated, meaning new random content for more replayability. I assume, haven't gotten to it myself, and likely don't intend to. But again, it only plays with Survivalist mode which is too frustrating, and Adventure mode would be too easy.Lastly and perhaps most importantly...  It's clunky. The controls are weird, and you cannot fluidly and easily go between shooting the bow and then meleeing. You have to Cancel out of using the bow, then hit Target Lock for melee, before you can ever actually attack (or dodge), which costs you precious time.In a game where one death loses a ton of time and effort, you want to choose the most efficient and successful tactic. The bow is useless aside from hunting for food, and one enemy type in the game who needs to be kited (Tremorlurks) and you don't even see those often until late-game. Most other dangerous enemies (like Forsaken) will dodge every single bow shot.There are several melee moves such as Lunge, and counterattacks after Dodging or Parrying which play a new animation... but I honestly found little use for any of those. Lunge was fun and occasionally used when at range as a gapcloser. Mostly, I just Dodged and then did a regular spear attack, because dodging is king when you don't want to get hit at all. Parrying does not parry everything, and if you mess it up, you're getting hit. It's better to remove all potential risk and just dodge everything, then stab them after.TLDR They did not create fun, fluid responsive combat. And the harshness of (Survivalist) gameplay means you're compelled to find the safest way to handle situations, not necessarily the most fun and engaging.Oh, and there's an aimbot of an unkillable shark that guards areas in a certain circular radius, and will beeline for you if you try to sail through that region... charging your boat and doing significant damage to it. You cannot damage or kill this shark, your only options are to circumnavigate around its area (combat music plays and ends when you go past the border, so you know) or if you have the wind behind you, you might be able to outrun it and dodge if it tries to charge in. If the wind is remotely against you, you better not even try to go that way.Again, another poor decision of a mechanic. I like the potential challenge, excitement and intensity of the idea. But I was in two stages when I first discovered the sharks (and there can be multiple blocking certain spots per map):1, when I was a newbie and accidentally sailed in my first time, looked around like WTF at the sudden boss music, then got knocked sky-high as my bamboo boat was shredded and everything totaled. Not entertained.2, once I had figured out that the music started/ended and could tell the shark was essentially guarding circles on the map, and could avoid those until I had (both a fast enough boat and the right wind angle) to make a run for what it was guarding... which unfortunately is usually a tiny island with Sea Shards, which eventually become useless once you have enough and have bought all of the Blessings (buffs of a sort) with them. Eventually I just began avoiding the shark areas, not worth.Much like how the xenomorph in Alien is rarely seen, a good enemy needs to retain mystery, unseen, you don't always know where it is. This is why sharks are scary (for example, in the game Stranded Deep, little dun-dun-dun musical cues if one was lurking around at any random moment, rather than it being a circle the player can easily figure out and just be annoyed by an essential roadblock that can completely wreck your boat.)I understand it's likely a challenge the player needs to overcome before reaching those tiny reward islands (which as I said, aren't that rewarding), but they could've done with toning down the boat damage when the game is already so punishing.TLDR. I bought because I saw a ton of  in this game. I would refund if I could, because it fails to deliver that potential in so many ways, and has little replayability. My hours played in this are not out of enjoyment, so much as forcing myself to try to squeeze out my money's worth since 2 hours wasn't enough to realize all of this initially... which is something Steam's refund policy refuses to understand.Lastly, . For this little amount of content and playable runtime, it should be half this price. For $30, right now you can get  from Ubisoft, which is a gorgeously textured AAA game with raytracing and an entire Grand Theft auto-esque interactive city, story, voice acting, clothing/customization, weapons and varied combat... obviously that comparison is unfair to an indie, but don't try to price like this, then.

_childDocuments_.review: I had some fun with Windbound but the content is just not there.I played this with the "expansions" and I still thought content was poor and the systems and mechanics were rudimentary at best.The combat is fine, its actually pretty snappy and responsive but it all boils down to dodge and hit over and over again. There is a very clear META that means trying to implement anything other than this tactic will be sub-par. This system is not broken but it wildly repetitive. There is groundwork here for a good combat system, its just a pity they didn't make one.Similar to the combat; sailing is a fun system that (mostly) works but is very poorly implemented. There are sections that require you to traverse narrow gaps between rocks at relatively high speed while the main "exploration" section of the game itself encourages building bigger ships to accommodate more equipment and storage; these 2 systems are at odds with each other. Making a great boat seemed (at first) like an enjoyable endgame goal but the physics punishes you for going too fast. At high speed the slightest wave will flip you over breaking the fast paced flow of transportation you were hoping to get from building a top tier boat. The boat I finished the game with was very simple with low quality materials, cant be too fast, cant be too big. On the steam page for Windbound (in the about this game section) There is an animated gif at the top of the page depicting a boat with 3 sections and a red sail. That boat would flip over so easily if you try to go fast, making it essentially useless... If you were going to go slow and monitor your speed so you don't flip over... Why bother making the red sail in the first place? This entire system could have been much more fun.This is really it... Windbound is not a bad game... Its just the shell of a good one. There are only really those 2 things to do in Windbound; explore and fight and as I have explained, both systems have serious faults.I really want to love Windbound but I just cant recommend this to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Gave this a shot as i loved the setting, look, and gameplay. Was ultimately disappointed with the lack of proper keymapping, ever prevalent storage issues (apart from unintuitive, it's simply a plague for most games of this type), and the base combat, which is disheartening because mostly everything else is fine, but unfortunately combat is forced quite often. There are a lot of opportunities for deeper combat mechanics like throwing your spears for massive damage with having to retrieve it be a fair trade off, or stuns and knockbacks by damage type / element, etc... you know, start from the base before working up to new skills, abilities, and upgrades. As it is, it's far too clumsy to be a combat oriented game, and unfortunately that is what it's become with the DLC. Exploration takes a backseat and makes it unappealing to visit every island when at a point in the game, nearly every island forces combat on you.Over all, i give it an okay as i found some fun in it after 16 hrs, but i can't really recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt a little barebones at launch but it's definitely in a much better state now.The devs are still updating it with new content and abilities that keep the gameplay fresh and the exploration exciting. It did take me some time to get a firm grip on all the mechanics but once it all clicked I was in for a ride.What particularly stands out to me is the beautiful environment design and the changing biomes of the islands, including some interesting (even if not too perfectly scripted) enemies, ressources to find and things to craft and - even though I usually hate survival mechanics - playing it on Storyteller Mode never had me feel like I was being punished just for playing the game (read: trying to keep my character alive).The hunger/stamina system feels manageable and there are quite a few game modes now that help you get into the flow of the game without resetting your progress or punishing you too hard in case you get lost or in over your head.It may take a while to really get into this game but if you take the time to stay aboard you will be rewarded with a great adventure and many things to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful and exciting but has many flaws and bugs that outweigh it.    Windbound has a steep learning curve with a somewhat robust crafting system, forcing you to go island hopping for materials and shrines that will allow you to go into the next chapter.    However, some craftings require combat, and that is where the game falls apart.    Hits that should contact hitboxes are often not counted and vice-versa.    The player will constantly get stuck on geometry while targeting.    The targeting will not work half the time and will not even allow you to change targets without exiting and reentering it.    The camera does not help.    When you target, the camera will sometimes get stuck to the ground.    I think this was a design choice to make it look more cinematic, but it is a hindrance.    The camera is an issue when sailing also.    The camera is so close to the boat that you constantly have to move it to see what's ahead, forcing your boat to turn in directions unless you counter the camera.  Other things don't make sense, like the character being so weak that they cannot swim for more than a few seconds.  Some boats can go so fast and flip over, launching your player through the map and strand you in open storm water, drowning you.  Enimines you kill will sometimes bounce off the ground into the sky and never be seen again without drops or rewards.  Enimines will respawn on you right after you kill them while cooking at a fire and can kill you in one hit.  The boat suddenly stops in open waters while sailing, sometimes causing damage or allowing things to attack you.  You can craft decks that allow for pontoon boats, but the deck only enables you to place a cooking fire or storage on it when it has plenty of space for more.  There are so many inane choices and bugs that I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Windbound is not a bad game but it could use a lot of improvement. I have read some reviews stating that it tries to be a lot of genres at once and fails to do so. I don't agree, I think most of the things fit together quite nicely, the problem is that pretty much every part is underdeveloped and implemented in most simplistic way. Let's review each component individually:If you are looking for a good and immersive story you won't find it in Windbound. The story and player goals are very weak in this game. There are 5 chapters, in each chapter you have exactly the same goal - find 3 keys and go through portal. After each chapter you will get kind of ambiguous lore. This can make the game feel very repetitive, especially if you are playing "Survivalist" mode which makes you start over on Chapter 1 when you die.The whole survival system can be described in one word "eat". To elaborate, you have only 2 resources to manage - Health and Stamina. Over time your character gets hungry which reduces your maximum stamina. Eating food restores both max stamina and lost health and that's it.Exploration can be fun but is also very predictable. In the game you encounter several types of islands and each type has its own unique enemies to fight and resources to gather. Each chapter will offer you one new type of island. The problem is after you have visited a certain type of island you have seen all that it has to offer. And when in following chapters you see the island type you have already visited, even from far away you already know what monsters you will encounter and what resources you will find. I would suggest to mix it up a little maybe even randomize the islands so that the player won't immediately know what to expect and will actually experience exploring them.Combat is also too simple. You have 3 types of weapons - Sling, bow and spear (And technically knife). Melee combat is a joke you only have 1 jab attack and that's it, no light/heavy attack variations, no movesets nothing... Also its quite easy I didn't even have to use ranged weapons at all. Each monster has a huge tell when they are going to attack. All you have to do is wait for the tell, dodge and then attack rinse and repeat. Huge room for improvement here.I think crafting was the best part of this game. Crafting new items, upgrading your gear and especially building boats was really satisfying and I was always looking forward to unlocking new recipes. I don't have any complaints here.Also well done. Fighting with wind and trying to navigate through waves, trying not to collide with stones etc. was pretty challenging and fun. Also when you upgrade your boat and it becomes sturdier and faster it feels really satisfactory.The game is very short and fairly easy. I was playing on hardest difficulty and I think I died only twice early on and once I got the gist of combat I beat it in one go. As you can see it took me only 10 hours to beat the whole game. The game also offers you the easier mode where you don't lose any loot and you don't have to start form chapter 1 when you die, which will allow you to beat the game even faster. Also since the chapter goals are repetitive and as I said in  section the islands become very predictable, I think that the rougelike mechanic where you have to start over on death doesn't really fit this game, since it has no replayability value.In conclusion the game could use a lot of improvement, but by no means is it a bad game. I had fun playing it and would definitely recommend it. Just don't go in expecting it to be more than it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I would stay away from this game for now. its a good game or it could be with a few tweaks. 3/10, I would wait until the game gets a few more content drops and bug fixes.The worlds (chapters) are bare and there isn't much you can do. the first world i got was ok, 4 main islands and 3 tiny "treasure islands". it was pretty cool discovering slightly different islands. I spent a good 3 hours in chapter 1 before I discovered everything there and moved on.The middle realm is neat, spending your points to buy gear and upgrades is cool.Chapter 2. I got a couple new islands and a couple new enemies, new materials to craft better items. Again I spent about 2 hours here before i discovered all the islands and "treasures". Time to move forward.Chapter 3. This is where the game got stupid and hard. The islands I got were all spectral islands, you get these ghost type enemies that hit kind of hard but are weak. 1v1 is easy, but you can get quickly overwhelmed by 2 or more enemies.At this point in the game, the potions would come in real handy BUT you need crude metal to make the cauldron and there are no islands here with crude metal. at least i couldnt find any or get to any if there are some and the reason is the sailing sucks, sometimes its smooth and fluid but most of the time its like you're a student driver in a tv show or movie, you go forward and jerk the brakes, go forward and stop, forward and stop. Something worth adding is the wind ALWAYS seems to know where you need to go and blows from that direction, again, it wouldnt be that bad but the sailing is far from good. To make it worse, theres sharks here that travel way faster than your canoe and can pretty much one shot you and will knock you off your canoe. you cant escape them and have no choice but to try avoid them which is kind of hard with the sailing mechanics. The BIGGEST problem with this game is that it sends you into worlds severely under equipped and seems like it expects you to find the things you need to survive in that world IN THAT WORLD. You should find these things or "lesser" items in the world before: example! In chapter 2, give us everything to make slightly better weapons, canoe defenses and a few minor potions that will help us in chapter 3.Populate these worlds more with more islands, more enemies, more materials and new recipes per chapter. I'm only 8 hours into the game and i feel like the game is good and has potential but needs a few tweaks and bug fixes to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pleasant experience for those who allow a game to be it's own thing. Even though it's quite short (I finished it after 14 hours of play, and I'm someone who savours and indulges in a game), the length is indicative of good scoping. One will quickly realise that it is quality over quantity. Resources well used, a project well planned and executed. Some people say the combat feels clunky - This is false - It's all about how well you can aim a spear. To me, the combat was fluid and strategic. It's not about button mashing, but about timing. Some say the survival aspect is too "annoying" - Not so. It's about eating berries out in the field, and keeping the meat inside the campfire to prevent it from spoiling. It's not a chore at all if you "eat from the land" directly.  I think it's those ARK people who are used to storing cooked meat in 15 fridges stacked on top of each other who feel challenged by the nomadic life-style. Ranged weapons are the meta in this game. Melee is quite under-powered, especially for it being a rogue-like. I highly recommend this game because the experience, atmosphere and immersion are very pleasant and fun. I am going to do a second play through, simply because I rushed through the first 2 chapters, and realised there was a lot more things to discover than I thought. This game is to be played casually. It's like letting a bubble gum sit in your mouth, as you savour the taste, instead of chewing out the taste.
