_childDocuments_.review: This game can best be described as Zelda and Raft making a baby. The game mechanics make for great casual play or a frustrating and then rewarding all or nothing challenge. The world is relaxing to play in. The game presents a small open world for each chapter. The player ultimately decides what to do with the limited resources. Ocean changes every moment you are playing and at time is hazardous enough to capsize all but the largest ship. Game is exploration based and each death in a chapter regenerates the island world somewhat or at least there is plenty to explore. So far I have made it to chapter 3 the first two chapters seem to be there for establishing how to play and building a supply of resources.GREAT GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: the game itself is an interesting concept and the battle mechanics are pretty nice a little different from the norm but still good sailing however ruins the game a feature needs to be implicated so you can sail against the wind like the ability to switch between paddling and sailing because it is impossible to sail against the wind ( as it should be) however that shouldnt be able to stop you from progressing to where you want to go
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know what all these negative reviews were about.  If you like exploration, Minecraft, Windwaker, Breath of the Wild and learning the story through playing rather than having the whole story fed to you all at one time in a cutscene.  This is the game for you!  I enjoyed it but due to all the negative reviews, I waited to buy it once it was 50% off.  I am now writing this review after hitting 5.8 hours straight according to Steam and I'm completely satisfied!  Don't let bad reviews keep you away from this gem.  Great art, great music, the AI isn't stupid either, very well put together game.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Was a bit unsure to buy it at first because of a few bad reviews, but then i noticed the bad reviews were given mostly by people who played 2-3 hours.I got off on a fairly bad impression at first because it only shows me the max resolution of 1920x1080 and i have a 4K ultra wide screen so that was a bit of a bummer, but not that big a deal.The progression is a bit slow at first but you can pick up the pace pretty fast after Chapter 3, i also recommend screwing around because there are many random treasure maps and hidden skill upgrades and stuff that makes grinding way easier.All in all it's a very fun and relaxing game, big thumbs up for a well done survival game!
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Over all the game is pretty and runs smooth, as expected for a single player game. This game has some good points, but also many points that i found that need some work or rethinking on its mechanics. Pros-The game play its self is smooth and relaxing, the crafting system is pretty straight forward.  Animals/creatures have an AOE music sound to them, i found that rather unique and enjoyable. The sailing system is more realistic, but once you get the hang of it you will find ways of sailing against the wind. The boat building system is pretty straight forward and rather forgiving if you make an error. The graphics remind me a lot of worlds adrift.The things that could use some work--I have found the rag-dolling your character tends to do has some glitches, she takes a long time to get up and can be prone to getting stun locked. This is especially the case when getting attacked at sea, my character rag-dolled all over my deck for like 2 min while the shark went to down on my boat.-Items degrade WAY too fast, even the item you make to prevent degrading degrades really fast. I found my self constantly farming to keep my tools and weapons going. paired with having to farm for food non stop because my character is always hungry. Some rethinking on the "realism" needs to be done, tools do not degrade that fast nor do people get hungry that fast. re-balancing this will be a huge QOL change.-Game modes seem off to me.  Its either easy mode or all in and fully restarting on death, no in-between. You can not go back to previous areas, so if your tools break and you do not have extra materials on hand to make another you may be SOL.  If you get attacked at sea and loose everything during adventure mode 3-4 chapters in, your likely stuck there and will have to start a whole new game. This is a ♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic and will likely have people quitting the game over it.-Adding a few things to the game and calling it a "DLC" is a joke, its a minor content patch in the least and makes me wondering if the dev's are half-assing it or are just lazy.Over all the game is not bad, it does have its issues and quirks but that is common with every game.  I would not pay full price for it in its current state, but its not a bad title to pick up if its 50% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Well, at first it looked beautiful, but the longer I played, the more flaws I noticed.Graphic-wise it is really nice. The story and setting needs some addition. You drop right into the game, without proper introduction or tutorial. But as you progress you get some tutorials. Unfortunately over and over again. Each time you encounter the same scenario, you get the same tutorial...The balancing is quite special...the food is just for the chapter, theres no way you can spare something for later on. Materials for building quite the same, you unlock recipes with items required which you get 1-2 chapters later.But there are flowers all over the place. Too much to carry or even store them. The storage-system is unbalanced as well. Its easier (and gives you more spaces) to craft bags and racks than storage crates...At last, there are some bugs/glitches as well. Bugs more annoying, glitches likely to be in your favor. If you want to carry additional tools with you because the current one is close to breaking? Too bad, with the current one the new breaks as well. You want to finish a level because you farmed and killed the entire map? Well, too bad, you can't unlock the final island of the chapter because you are missing something? Wanna know what? Go and take a look yourself, the game won't tell you.But in return you can use some glitches. If you deal enough damage, all mobs run away and you can follow and harass them all around. And certainly the halloween-items help you out. The weapon deals enough damage on range with no ammunition needed and well, this item doesn't break.Over all the game is quite good, but has definitely issues. The balancing needs a rework for sure, the guidance troughout the chapters at least some additions.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad.. but not good. Traveling (sailing) is painfully slow and the wind mechanics are janky at best. Resources are scarce.. and islands are small, so you will spend a lot of time slowly traveling to another island. During the "story" you will often have to retrace your steps to get a key (token) from another island.Combat targeting is utter garbage. Switching between ranged to melee will kill you and make you throw your keyboard.It is somewhat fun to unlock new crafting options and build up your boat (raft).. but grinding materials quickly becomes a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Story...There is not much of the story so to speak, just objectives that repeat and bits of text that I didn't bother to read. I feel that the story could be improved to offer more diverse objectives that would make the player feel they are doing something different.Multiplayer...I feel this game would benefit from multiplayer or 2-4 player co-op to make it feel less empty out there on the ocean.Crafting...I feel crafting could be improved to allow more things to be make like maybe steel hulls and surfaces, walls and roofs, tool tiers, more food types and different styles of hulls.Graphics...Graphics are great and have a real comfy feel to it. I can honestly say I have found no issues with themOverall I would say the game needs a lot for the money they are charging for it and a few little bugs need to be fixed but I do enjoy the game a lot and will most likely continue to play the game if I want to sail on a boat I made
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I liked exploring the different islands, although it was a bit repetitious. The islands were about the same through the different chapters. It changed a bit and got a little harder to kill the enemies. It had a nice story and the graphics were clean and crisp. I am glad there was a map and after the first two chapters I could kinda guess where the islands would be laid out.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I  loved the game, this has the best water simulation i have experienced, the issue I have with the game is that the character in the game is going hungry with a seal full of fish,  I think the focus should be on getting water instead of food and how come there is no fishing???? I even with all this I give the game 4 starts out of 5
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Play for 2 hours. Loved every moment of it...then I died. I was on chapter 2, and found 2 of the 3 shrines. Excellent I thought...then I died...and had to start the chapter from scratch. Logged off for the night. I'll see if I have the gumption to load back in knowing that is a thing going forward. Excited to see what is out there, and saw on the patch notes that is a thing they will be working on.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: ----- Mixed Review! -----Pro'sGives me a lot of Windwaker/BOTW vibesEnemies are interesting and have all different attacking patterns.Recipes are different, not what you might expect and funThe more you go a long in the game, The more rewards you recieveGraphical this game looks amazing! Building your boat, Just go completely ham! Think of something crazy and build it!Music and story - very nice, story might confuse some.ConsWater Physics - Go over a big wave and hit the water to hard? Instant stopIsland surrounded by lots of rocks - Denies you to build bigger boats, since otherwise they dont fitNo open world - World is small, you respawn in a new world everytime you finish a chapter and you have limited supplies everytime.Repetitive - Find 3 towers & loot, find big island, finish chapter that's itCoral - The most annoying blockade in the world. If you dont have enough speed you might get stuck on them. This means you have to dismantle part of your ship.The Wind - The main source of movement is one of the biggest flaws in the game. It is random, it barely works. Sometimes you get stuck on nothing or bounce off the waves without any reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Pro's Lovely graphicsInteresting storylinechallenging but fun crafting systemSailing and upgrading your boat to your own shape/design is cool!!Music and abience great to help with awareness of enemiesInteresting enemies and neutrals and good AI behavioursConsA bit glitchy when you jump / grab doesn't always hang on to ledges or climb themIf you stay on an island hunted enemies/prey will respawn but they don't always have resources when you hunt them so if you're preparing to journey or just enjoying living on an island this forces you to move on which is sad. Overall I enjoyed this game and would be interested in further developments. After the main story is completed I would love to continue exploring sailing and crafting please or have a sandbox option in addition to the story option :)
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very fun experience. People say it only has a single attack button, but so do some zelda games they compare it to. It has different weapons that have different mechanics. There is a struggle bus for if you play survival. Be prepared to start over a lot unless you select story mode(I suggest this for first play through). I will play this game for probably 10-15 hours maybe 20 if I try to 100% well worth the price they are asking.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Except for some fun little bugs that make enemies fly or get stuck, this game is a really detailed, polished and fun experience. The game mechanics include influences of Wind Waker and Breath of the Wild and although there aren't any big bosses, I have had some intense fights with certain creatures in later chaptures.The sailing mechanic needs some training on the player's side and sometimes also here the physics cause some funny animations. All in all, this is a game that appeals to all gamer types and has a lot to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good but miss the mark in some parts. Gathering resources and sailing are quite fun. Combat is kinda there and good enough for this style of game but could be improved a little. This game really needs something like an endless mode because I would love to have unlimited islands to go and visit not just the 5 sets we get. Overall good game with tons of potential that just missed a few marks. I really hope they make a second game and fix the few issues of gameplay they have
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't convinced but after the first hour I got into a mad gameplay loop where I understood the mechanics better and started to survive quite well.Struggling with the interface and inventory management however as it is quite clunky (might be purposeful).Really good fun. Do not expect this to be a typical adventure game. You lose progress when you die but not all is lost as you keep some items and blessings.If this game had an open world story mode with similar gameplay mechanics that would kick so much ass.Current impressions are positive with minor balancing and usability tweaks required. Support aussie devs!!Edit: after spending a ton more time in the game I have been enjoying myself, I've yet to dive into the patches but what I've seen looks to be positive and an improvement of overall systems! New modes! Etc
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I love the physics-based sailing. The survival aspects are less interesting. Once you get the hang of keeping yourself fed, it's fun to just sail around in the waves. As many others have pointed out, to sail into the wind, you need to "close haul" and tack back and forth.The devs should consider adding a sandbox mode with no survival mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, do yourself a favour and play storyteller mode. Still has the survival mechanics and a much more balanced gameplay experience than the standard mode. Game is nice if a bit short and a bit confusing. I got it for full price and while there is no replay value in the story itself there is plenty in how you build your boat. Now, sailing. Sailing can feel really nice but also can be very annoying when the wind is against you. I would say really wait for a price drop. At £25 it's a bit much but £15 or less  would be ideal.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Knockoff-Brand Zelda Windwaker Light Version....  Worth to go through once, but no replay or challenge.  ProTips: 1, dismantle your boat after landing on the final island of each stage and take the materials into the next act.  2. Crossings need only the grass canoe - nothing else. 3. build fires on your boat so you take them with you and not have to keep building fires whenever you want to cook meat. 4. You can gather all the materials in game...yet still pass the end with a simple grass boat and no weapons needed.  So toil at your own misery.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun and would definitely recommend this game. The graphics are gorgeous and I love the use adaptive music. It also had a lot of cool creature design and biome diversity, this along with the procedurally generated islands made exploring exciting!If you're looking for a beautiful, story-driven survival experience this game is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I do not post many reviews, but with this one I had to. This game is released but really has a lot of bugs. The one that was a game breaker for me was after saving the game and coming back to play it the mobs no longer dropped any loot. This makes it impossible to move on in the game. Unfortunately I have played for over 2 hours, so I can not request a refund. I would definitely ask for one. I would not recommend this game at this time until they fix this and many other bugs. I can not understand how you release a game with this bad of a bug in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: So i was really looking forward to this game and for the most part its not a bad game but here are some random thoughtsit does have a lot of issues, ive seen it best described as this game doesnt know what it wants to be and thats accurate,it has survival, story, crafting, combat and exploration elements but none of them are done particularly well.The RNG generation of islands can be pretty ass as well, sometimes a map will completely lack resources you require to upgrade.Dying in this game is ASS as well, and incredibly frustrating and not in a good way, you lose so much time and resources and it doesn't really feel like you need to lose anything, theres no gameplay element to justify this its just as an inconvenience.It has bugs and glitches with animals joining the Nordic space program when you kill them, when i sail fast i always dip under water and come flying back up onto the water lol, none of the bugs are game breaking but just annoying.Sailing is VERY tedious at times, i get that sailing into the wind should push you back and cool good job, but im not playing sail simulator 2020 (or maybe i am) but i want to just go, Legend of Zelda Windwaker had great sailing because you could change the wind to suit you and the sailing was peaceful, this game makes you wrangle with it and not in a way i enjoyedFinding islands in your play area sucks, you cant see them from anywhere and once youve sailed around the inside of the map you have to travel a stupid distance to try find more islands which is such a waste of timeI have encountered a storm at sea ONCE, and it was honestly one of the best parts of this game, the big swells and rain and lightening was so cool and funoverall i did enjoy this game, there are a lot of little annoying things but it is fun. I would love it if they just make a proper big open world sailing game and built on the crafting aspect, i think all the gameplay elements and story is too shallow and it hurts the experience BUT it feels so close to being a great game with a fun idea
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be SO good, it has the potential for it but right now it has more issues than its worth. The design and music are what pulled me into it but the execution and what they wanted this to be was done poorly. There's magic? cool. Monsters? Neat. Visuals? Awesome.Story? What's Story? What's happening and why am I doing this? What's the point of this weird Wanna be Survival-adventure-Monster hunter game?I would love the story if it wasn't for A. Your combat sucks. B. What happens when you die and how it sets you back and all but forces you to start over, that really kills the mood of the game when you force someone who's ALMOST finished the chapter but accidentally falls to their death or a monster pops up out of NOWHERE and kills you. That's not fun. C. You can speed run it in less then a few hours, there's no reason to actually Build/Explore anything.D. It was fun, Until it wasn't. It's a repetitive slog of the same thing with some story sprinkled in. It really is trying too hard to be too many things at once and because of that it's not fun to play, it's boring and annoying. (Spoilers)Story mode: You Die you lose everything that's not in your inventory. Boat, bags, wepons, etc. Gone.If it's not with you it's gone. Have to start over from scratch. if this is supposed to be their enjoy "the story mode", it feels more like the devs are saying "Na screw you, now start ALL over with nothing besides what's in your very limited inventory!"Survival mode: Never got to it because Story mode felt like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and awesome job making a world fun to explore, absolutely fun to play and as you learn it gets easier and more interesting.  For the negatives, while it is fun, the bugs are pretty bad at times.  Skyrocketing enemies after they die is only funny once or twice, especially when it happens like 20 times in 10 hours of gameplay, also I beat the game in 14 hours playing at a Snails pace of just exploring every chapter and dieing a few times.  Do not play on story mode unless you want to beat it really quickly.  Once you get a bow everything is easy to kill, like extremely.  If you are good enough to do it from a distance (not even really that far) you will confuse enemies and they will not even aggro onto you.  Combat is clunky at best and for a game that bases everything on exploration, there really isn't much to explore.  Also if you beat the game there is no replay value like unlocked content, harder difficulties, even a freeplay mode would have been awesome.  I would still rate it a 8/10 because its just fun and great when it works, but at 30 bucks I expect more chapters or options or something...
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, i wish it was longer, i really like the fact that you get to keep your blessings you earned, when you die. It lets you start with a bow or spear etc. which lightens the blow of when you die. i found myself dying on purpose in act 5 so that i could start over with the small amount of equipment it lets you keep when u die. giving a huge advantage. i played through the game 4 times and the 2 biggest complaints i have are when you go too fast and your bow goes underwater. and the fact that i cant actually make it to the portal at the end, I've tried nearly 20x.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Would it be possible to just get a survival mode? The story was repetitive but fun. I liked the idea of getting better and stronger boats but the resources just were not there. I wanted to be Moana damnit. If there was a pure survival mode with resources and islands scaling as time went on to not make the beginning such a challenge then it would make for a fun experience. The story was over for me in just under 6 hours of a single gameplay. Not worth the price as it stands currently. And again I fall into the mixed category here. I like a lot about the game but there is still plenty that needs work. Until some patches it will have be be a no.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, it's a decent game. I'd say it has it's charms. The combat is pretty decent with every weapon having a place to be used in. The different elements to the game make a ton of it's recourses worth gathering, while some you'd only really gather when you absolutely need them. The combat is surpirsing fluid and isn't jard to get a grasp of. It's targeting system is very useful in many situations. My biggest problems with the game were the fact that you could not change your keybinds. While i opens your inventory, it's also the only key used on that side of the keyboard. Also the targeting button is middle mouse button. Not being able to change those was quite annoying as I tend to always customize keys. The inventory key is actually annoying to me because of how often you end up going into your inventory to craft. Is that the end of the world? Nah. For it's 30 dollar price tag it does pretty well overall. I'd give it a 7/10 as it's world is quite beautiful and the music is great. The combat is solid and every weapon has a time and place for use. I do think there is room for improvement with the game but I don't feel like the game is unplayable. It's rather enjoyable. I do recommend the game but I can understand why someone would dislike it. A lot of the game is sailing and surviving. The story elements are kind of lacking and the overall lore so far is pretty bare minimum. Only between chapters are there any actual story telling. Would have liked for more scattered lore among the islands themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style and music. Everything else is just really not that enjoyable. The crafting and combat are very mediocre and something I'd expect from an early access title at best. The sailing mechanic felt like it really had so much potential but once I switched from oar to sails it just all goes downhill from there. Can't recommend for $30 for a game missing so much polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game is interesting. a COUPLE PROBLEMS AT THE MOMENT THO... sometimes when I kill something the corpse goes flying off into the distance never to be seen again. Also, I tend to get stuck on things after climbing up onto them. Such as the tip of the boat... which I was trying to push, not climb.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad overall. Not quite yet done with the story, but unless things change after story completion, there's no replay value.I came here for crafting, sailing, and fishing. I got sailing. Fishing, even spear fishing, is not really a thing until you get the creature hide from chapter 3 that helps with stealth.Material resource nodes don't respawn, but food resource nodes and mobs do. This makes it necessary to move from one chapter to the next, once you've exhausted the available material resources.I want more fishing, and material resource node respawns.Would recommend once through to get your sailing bug squashed, but, like I said, unless something changes after story completion, starting over from scratch and necessarily having to push through chapters to continue sailing but not fishing just isn't going to happen for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you, 5 Lives Studios for the game and to Deep Silver for publishing it, I've completed the game and it only took me 11 hours. It was fun to play but I felt like I wanted more things to craft so hopefully it will come with a future patch one day to this game. Sadly after game is ended and I press on continue I end back to the final chapter end again, I thought I was able to continue outside that place, it's why I rushed the story. Oh well, thank you for a really great game and It was beautiful, <3. I recommend this game to everyone!, and CYA.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Windbound because it looked like a cute survival game. I don't really feel like its worth 30 dollars though. It's short, and very repetitive once you complete the first chapter, you've experienced the whole game and then it's just more of the same, but with a few added resources and creatures.  I liked it but I wish there was more, but I did get enjoyment out of it for about 2 days. I'd recommend it, but I'd suggest people wait for it to be on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a good 7 hours now and this game is great! I can't believe I almost let the "mixed reviews" stop me from playing this game. I was absolutely sold off the trailer and I've only encountered ONE bug ONE time since playing. It's a great time. One enemy moved a little funny for a second and then everything was back to normal.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: had no issues with the game until i reached chapter 2.   Got stuck at the loading screen for 10 mins and had to reset the game.  Tried to load it again and same thing happened.  The third time it actually loaded but my inventory was gone.  Attempted to restart a new game and, imagine my surprise, stuck at a loading screen...again.  All this happened around the 2.3 hour mark.  So I've requested a refund but seeing as it shows me at 3 hrs of playtime its not likely.  Aside form the technical issues its a pretty well built game, no major glitches other than what i had happen to me.  Mouse controls are very sluggish even at max settings and combat system could use a bit of an upgrade to make it more fluid.  Had a hard time staying interested  but i think that's because I expected more of a survival type game and this is not what I would call "survival" game. This is a storyline based game with a direct path from start to finish from what I have seen.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is too lacking in basic features and the gameplay loop is banal. You can't remap keys, nor see what the keys are. This coupled with some bugs that occur while in the menus, leaves you with an ever-present frustration with basic crafting and inventory management. The symbols for resources are also too simplified and many look the same. Progression feels all right, but also I felt like I was being level gated. I had more resources than I needed while in the first area. This would not be a problem unless the storage options were less obtuse. Storage seems to be designed to add more level gating and stretch out the loop without hiding it. I was honestly excited to find more options for combat so early on. Meaning in the first and second areas you can upgrade your weapons if you're willing to fight the creatures around you. The inventory frustrates this progression as well. I found no easy or apparent way to quickly swap weapon and ammo. Time does kinda slow down when you are trying at least. I think much of my frustration with this also comes from the character control to feel sluggish and not precise. Almost like I was playing an online game on a poor connection. I hit my breaking point with the game specifically because of these issues. I finally found the creature you need to kill to get the axe to harvest wood. I had max stamina, Tempest bow (damage over time electric effect), with metal arrows. This thing was teleporting as it's ability, but if I had my bow drawn while I was waiting for it to appear, it seemingly would cancel my bow draw when it reappeared. In my frustration and new experience with this animal, being the only animal who would teleport like this that I had seen so far, I died. I was playing the Story mode, which is I guess the Easy Mode, but I still "washed up" on a previous island with only my inventory. I think I could reload my save, but I didn't care to try. The lack of explanation or clarifying this result was insult to injury. I've played 1500 hours of Worlds Adrift, which was way more buggy and I lost ships and progress all the time to other players in pvp, but honestly this ♥♥♥♥ just irked me. It has promise, but it's trying to be too survival based, with annoying barriers to stretch out the content.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: In short: i really like this game. I did hope for more but its ok for such a small developer. Sadly you cant deactivate the hunger because i want to enjoy the game more (playing more slowly) but with the CONSTANT threat to eat (she is like a 300pound strongman who wants to eat all the time!) it isnt as enjoyable as it could be. I think you should experience the game for your own. Give it a chance if you like Botw, Windwaker or even Moana.
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: Are you want an epic and beautiful experience with lived in world and charming characters with amazing soundtrack and close to 100 hour content then go play Breath Of The Wild, Windboudn want to be a Zelda game (?) and its not far, if in the future more content coming would be a nice survival game but so far  the story is short and told in pictures, (XD) its a nice touch but short, and the survival element not keeping you going forward after the story and became repetitive and boring , need more depth and more options like a main island witch you go back and have a cabin where you craft then head out for the adventure and collecting stuff with the random instances generated on the fly it would be way different then what it is now i give a thumbs up because i can feel the developers soul and heart in the game , and the core concept is nice, from now on we just need an evolution
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: i've been craving a game like this for a while. the art style really appealed to me because i loved botw and wind waker, and the idea of having such an open area to explore was exciting. i've read through some of the reviews and i've noticed a lot of them complain about things like combat and the inability to change your keybinds. to me, this game isn't something super hardcore but more of a "chill and relax" kind of exploration game. the combat is simple enough for it to be entertaining (to me, at least). as for the keybinds, like i said - it's a simple game. it's not like there's a plethora of keybinds in the first place, so it isn't really a HUGE deal, but i guess i can see why people are so angry about it.the only things i'd really like to see added to the game are obviously more chapters so it's longer, but maybe an armor crafting system or an xp system added in. there are so many resources on these islands that COULD be used to craft armor, so why not be able to? plus, who doesn't like cosmetics :) i suggest the xp system so we could maybe feel more rewarded for killing the bigger monsters on the islands, maybe have a chance at a rare weapon or something like that?i think for the kind of thing i was looking for, this game is great. not perfect, obviously, but i definitely not worthy of all the negative reviews of the angry people
_childDocuments_.name: Windbound

_childDocuments_.review: great game. if you play story mode it will feel a little short. having to start over from the very beginning if you die in survival mode can feel like a cheap shot the first time, but after playing story mode it makes the game seem longer and more challenging. the story is a little odd but still enjoyable. overall if you are out of things to play i would def recommend this game. but if you still have some AAA titles sitting on the shelf waiting then i would wishlist this for when you run out of other games to clear.

_childDocuments_.review: WAIT FOR A SALE!! _childDocuments_.review: I'm one of the people that hated in BotW having weapons break so quickly.  But that's offset by just a wonderful adventure, good story, and puzzles/dungeons.  My spear broke before killing one of the first large animals in this game.  Very small inventory to start with.  Which when you do upgrade you lose if you die.  Which I did, in a really strange glitch.  I'd save often, at least until the clean up the bugs.Add to that I had to paddle long distance between islands just to get enough supplies.  Took me 2 islands to get enough fronds for my added inventory space.  And honestly I lost any excitement for the next island...as they just felt like generic island 1, meet generic island 2.  And honestly the goal of any good game should be trying to capture your excitement early.Top that off with a fairly fast reduction in stam/food meter.Then I actually looked up to see if it gets better.  Saw people that had great things to say about the game.  But unfortunately they also chimed in with the repetitive nature of game play of find 3 items and move to next chapter.  Islands feeling very similar.  And also constantly grinding to keep crafting your gear over and over, with one even saying it's not really worth exploring since your food/stam depletes so often.  Now I really don't have any desire to go back and play, have too many other games I need to get to instead.Make sure you know what you're getting into, thankfully there is a refund process, that I have rarely used, but have to on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Zelda Breath of the Wild 1.5,This is Raft if it was actually any interesting,This is Rust without a toxic playerbase,This is Ark if it was any good,This is Outward if it wasnt as much of a disappointment,This is Terraria a journeys "♥♥♥♥ it we are into rougelites now",This is probably what MInecraft should have been during the aquatic update,I saw an ad on youtube about this game about half a year ago and obsessed over it since, i played it on release and was really satisfied.Like coming home and taking of your socks you have been working in for 9 hours.Only its the anticipation for a game that could fill a void inside you ever since you finished all those other good games.Yeah, its a little rough around the edges, combat is a tiny bit stiff with the one second delay for when you can move again after attacking, and expanding your boat was kinda confusing, but in the end its the windwaker for the grownups, with a dash of sit-back-relax-and-take-in-the-scenery.Do i recommend it?Absoluetly.Its creative, artistic, relaxing with the dash of "OH ♥♥♥♥" sprincled in there, its rewarding and epic. Keep at it 5 Lives Studios.

_childDocuments_.review: Some stuff definitely still needs work. The combat system is rough, the respawn timer is unpredictable, and the game crashes whenever I exit it (I have to force quit every time). I'm running a top of the line gaming computer designed for VR, so I know it isn't a hardware issue.That said, the game is fun and engaging. Some stuff is repetitive, but that's kind of the point. It starts to scale up the further you go into the game and gets progressively harder with each chapter. The death mechanic is great in storyteller mode, but I'd avoid playing the normal game mode until you get more confident in your ability to keep going (you start back at the beginning of the game with only held items). Inventory management is what you'd expect from a game like this. The one thing I'd also say is that you don't always get recipes for the items you're holding...so you don't know the significance of some of the items until much later.

_childDocuments_.review: Embark on a personal journey and discover the history of the idyllic forbidden islands; each holding the key to a mystery and unexpected revelations. Head towards the horizon, advancing across the islands, each with their own wildlife, landscapes and challenges to face. Scavenge the island's untamed terrain for resources that you can use to craft a full range of tools and weapons to hunt wildlife and upgrade your boat. You must set sail when resources become scarce. Your boat is your key companion on this journey, carefully craft your own custom sailing vessel to take on the treacherous waters, traversing from one island to the next.

name: Eternal Hope
detailed_description: A story of love and hope 'Perhaps you’d be willing to go to the end of the world for your beloved, but would you go beyond it?' In Eternal Hope you'll follow the story of Ti'bi, a lonely boy who has lost the love of his life. You’ll embark with him on a highly unusual journey – one that might bring the soul of his cherished girlfriend back from the Shadow World, a purgatory-like realm. But visiting this new world will not be easy. There will be dangers to overcome and many mysteries to unearth before you can continue your passage. Granted the ability to shift between dimensions by the Keeper of Souls, this power will enable Ti’bi to travel, solve puzzles and meet otherworldly beings that live among the shadows. Travel with Ti’bi into the great beyond on this journey as you unravel ancient secrets not meant for the eyes of the living. Eternal Hope Features Embark on a journey to a dark, magical world full of mysteries! Travel across mystic forests, hidden caves, ancient cities to make your way up the mountains to the Temple of Souls. Use special powers to shift between worlds and change the environment in which you play. Solve puzzles with a little help! Use the environments and creatures of the Shadow World to help overcome the obstacles before you. Friend or foe? Meet unique creatures and find more about the species that dwell in the Shadow World. A beautiful and original soundtrack that will immerse you in Ti’bi’s emotional tale. Traverse evocative landscapes that help to tell a unique story. See the world through Ti'bi's eyes as you unravel mysteries about yourself and a long-lost civilization.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Hope~~~~~~~~~~~Eternal Hope; an emotional, story-rich platformer about a boy named Ti’bi who embarks on a journey to find his beloved’s soul. Ti’bi spends most of his life alone and lonely. He has always wished to meet someone.  Someone special, someone he could relate to.  Ti’bi spends most of his days roaming around, alone with his thoughts and desires. Until one blissful day when he hears someone singing alone by the hilltop. He rushes to see who it was and finds the love of his life; the very person he has always dreamt of.  Upon approach, they fall for each other and go on to spend countless hours in each other’s company, talking about everything and nothing. But as fate dictates, nothing lasts forever.  One moment, Ti’bi woke up to find himself alone; his love was not anywhere to be seen. He felt that something was wrong and went on a desperate search, hoping to reach his love in time. Passing through obstacles, he reaches the very hilltop where they met, and heard his beloved’s plea for help.  Ti’bi rushes to save her but is too late. The thunder cracks and hits the ground. The ground breaks apart, taking his beloved with it. Ti’bi was helpless; all he could do was stand and witness the horror as his beloved fell to her demise. Heartbroken and distressed, he mourns the loss of his beloved. Ti’bi tries to move forward, and encounters a tall shadowy figure; the Soul Collector of this realm. The mysterious figure tells Ti’bi that on that fateful day, his beloved’s poor soul was scattered around the world. The Soul Collector loses his strength and makes a deal with Ti’bi; if Ti’bi helps him collect the scattered soul of his beloved and of those whose souls need to be collected, the Soul Collector will revive his belovedThe tall, shadowy figure also gifted Ti’bi with abilities that will help him throughout his journey. Agreeing to this unbelievable deal, Ti’bi embarks on a desperate journey to find his beloved’s scattered soul. Gameplay: Eternal Hope brings some time-tested platformer game machines to the table, using arrow keys to move, jump, and climb down, and E to interact with items and obstacles scattered around the world. Where the game really shines is with the abilities that were given to Ti’bi by the Soul Collector. These abilities are unique and work really well throughout the game, complementing the already amazing story perfectly. The first ability: by pressing W, Ti’bi will interact with the Shadow World. With a limited amount of time gained with this ability, Ti’bi will be able to see things outside of his mortal vision, interacting with beings from the Shadow World and using them as platforms, etc. The second ability:  by pressing Q, Ti’bi will be able to glide. Using this ability, Ti’bi will be able to reach some difficult spots throughout the game.   Progression: the game progresses through chapters, with each chapter unveiling more about the journey of Ti’bi and the story surrounding his journey. Each chapter brings its own unique sets of puzzles and obstacles, which keeps the game fresh and holds your attention.  Although there’s nothing to complain about in regards to the gameplay itself, there are a few minor annoyances, including the fact that the foliage around the world sometimes makes things hard to see. Checkpoints are another minor annoyance. As you fail and the game takes you back to the checkpoint, it’s always two or three steps away from where you fail.  I imagine that most will ignore this as a minor setback, but it bothered me.Visuals: a well-designed world with amazing Cinematics. Beautiful art style with a character that brings extra flair to an already amazing story. The only downside with the visuals is its foliage, which, in places, disrupts the view and the beauty of those scenarios. Sound effects:  beautiful, calming sound effects that complement the game’s relaxing music.  The music does not disrupt the gameplay, and the background effects are well suited for each scenario. I found the controls a bit sluggish and by changing the controls it might help. Nah, the game does not allow you to change the key binds. Although the game is not dialogue-heavy, I must say that the number of dialogues/conversations the game features are well written and appropriate for each scenario. Puzzles: quite simple and minimalistic puzzles play out very well during the game. There are minor hiccups here and there, but nothing that you can’t overcome. The abilities given to you by the Soul Collector play an important role throughout the game, including solving these puzzles. Positives: + Rich story+ Decent Sound effects+ Beautiful landscape+ Unique and well-designed abilities + Well-made puzzles + Solid base gameplay + Well-placed and designed obstacles+ Well-scripted dialogues  Negatives: - Can’t change key binds - Foliage disrupts the view at placesAn emotionally driven story that leaves you breathless and amazed.  9/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: It was a good first P.C. game for a mobile game company, however there were a few things that were a bit frustrating to me:- No ability to bind controls- There weren't a lot of Waypoints- Way too many achievements in the main story line. It felt like everything I did I got an achievement for.- Achievements were bugged as well, making it difficult for some people to achieve them- The orb had some hitbox problems for me, where I had to be in the exact right spot to get it, although my friends never had this issue.However the story and the puzzles were great, and I feel like this game is a good showcase for what this team is capable of in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and I mentally gave it so many chances, but its just so unpolished and sluggish.The storytelling is almost child-like, but with some surprise "horror" parts. It feels like the cutscenes are telling the story and you're just playing a few levels in between - The game and story somehow feels very disconnected.Things like "Press A to skip" and its really X that you need to press, just make the game feel super unpolished and when you later hit a glitched log that won't break, its just another unpolished feature to fill you up with annoyance. Also the fact that you sometimes can fall two times your own height without damage and others barely your own height and die on the spot - Its just frustrating!But all this is nothing compared to the controls. I've died too many #!%! times without reason because the controls either didn't respond at all or were super sluggish - Its almost like you're playing in slowmotion which is super infuriating.Sadly this game is a prime example of pulling inspiration from other games, taking all the good parts and putting them into one game without any finish or thought. It has all the right things, but its just not using them right - Especially considering the pricetag.The only good thing about this game are the masked creatures, whom I absolutely adore, but even those aren't worth the sluggish 1-2 hours gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: is decent, but that's about the strongest word I'd use to describe it. The best part of the game is its visual design as well as some of the music; it looks very pretty and sounds nice.When it comes to the gameplay, it's a mixed bag. The main loop is 2D platforming and solving puzzles very similar to , with some of them being instant-death and trial-by-error. Most of it is pushing objects to climb higher or phasing the environment in-and-out to make different things appear. A noticeable downside during the entire game is its controls. You move pretty slowly, and the way some of the jumping works doesn't feel fluid.Later in the game you get into some puzzles with enemies and eventually a boss where you must move as quickly as you can; making a mistake means you restart a section. In my opinion, those sections were not as interesting and were a bit more frustrating as well. The boss in particular required a lot of standing still and waiting as well, which I'm not a fan of in general. Probably a fifth of my game time was dying and restarting sections.The game has a pretty simple story which suddenly tries to fan out into something more complex in the latter half; but I don't think it nailed the landing, and the game is pretty short overall which makes the latter half seem even more rushed.All in all, there's not much deeper to go into here. I think the game was OK; I wouldn't say it's bad by any means. But the developers definitely need more practice. Polish the gameplay, make things move more fluidly without throwing the player into too many chase or stop-and-go sections, and, if you want a story, try to build it from the beginning instead of throwing pieces in later on.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game - it's very pretty, and I enjoy emotional platformers. But I just could not figure out the logic of the world - eg sometimes. you have to step on the boards and let them float you up while the water pours in; other times, you have to wait for the water to fill before stepping on the boards or you'll drown. _childDocuments_.review: I came across this game after a friend posted a screenshot.  The art style immediately grabbed me.  I wasted no time picking it up for myself and streaming it.  What a gem.  If you are a fan of Limbo, this game is a must play.  It's a less difficult and prettier version of Limbo.  The checkpoints are extremely generous, so if you die, it's not rage inducing.  The sale price is an absolute steal, but I'm happy having paid near full price.  I only encountered one glitch that was easily resolved by reloading the checkpoint.  I played with a controller and had no movement or control issues at all.  Everything was fluid and responsive.  I enjoyed the game so much I went back and got all of the achievements.  I can't recommend this game highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever ventured into the intriguing, silhouette-filled worlds of games like LIMBO or INSIDE, then Eternal Hope deserves a spot on your radar. This 2D side-scroller is a charming platforming adventure that delivers more than you might expect.Eternal Hope begins with a poignant setup: a young boy named Ti’bi is on a quest to save the love of his life in a post-apocalyptic land. After a tragic accident claims her life, Ti’bi's mourning is disrupted by a mysterious entity known as the keeper of souls. The keeper offers a deal: if Ti’bi collects the shattered fragments of his beloved's soul scattered throughout this desolate world and brings them to the keeper's temple, she can be revived. The stage is set for a heartfelt journey.The gameplay in Eternal Hope is simple yet effective. Whether you're using a keyboard or a joystick, Ti’bi's movements are easy to master. The controls mainly involve running, jumping, and interacting with your surroundings. Your primary objective is to navigate the world, solving puzzles that block your path to collecting the soul fragments.As you progress through the game, an interesting mechanic emerges. Ti’bi gains the ability to enter the "land of shadows," effectively granting him access to a second plane of existence. This power allows him to manipulate the environment, removing or adding elements that change the landscape. This dual-dimension gameplay adds an intriguing layer to the puzzles and keeps the gameplay fresh.Visually, Eternal Hope shines. The game presents a captivating world filled with beautifully designed environments. The interactive layer is mostly in silhouette, which beautifully contrasts with soft, colorful backgrounds. When Ti’bi shifts into the land of shadows, the palette takes on faded, washed-out hues to emphasize the realm of death. Occasional cutscenes, resembling illustrations from a children's picture book, convey key emotional moments in the story.However, where Eternal Hope truly excels is its soundtrack. The game's music creates a fitting atmosphere for each scene, transitioning seamlessly from calm melodies while exploring to frenetic strings during intense encounters.Though the game features enemies, it doesn't rely heavily on reflexes. Instead, it emphasizes observation and problem-solving. You might die, but these moments serve as learning experiences. You'll discover how to deal with certain obstacles by carefully observing your surroundings, adding an element of strategy to the gameplay.On the downside, I encountered a few technical issues, like a tutorial bug and some puzzles breaking. Fortunately, these were minor and didn't significantly impact my experience.Overall, Eternal Hope doesn't bring groundbreaking innovation to the puzzle-platformer genre, but it's a well-crafted adventure that's thoroughly enjoyable. It's a bittersweet journey that, despite its occasional challenges, offers a beautiful and captivating experience. If you're on the lookout for a short yet memorable gaming adventure, give Eternal Hope a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty short puzzle platformer that's fairly derivative of previous games, it's nothing you havn't seen before both in plot, theme and mechanics. It's the usual push and pull boxes, pull levers, horrific deaths... if you played Limbo, this is pretty much exactly that but with a minor twist on the artstyle. The controls are a bit jank and definitly not as good as it should be, but not quite as bad as some other make it out to be IMO, for the most part it works perfectly fine, the generous checkpoints make it so that you never have to replay too much if you die. If you care about 100% the game it does have tons of checkpoints you can restart at any time from, pretty much after each main obstacle, so you can always go back and pick up the colectables you didn't find the first time. Always nice when devs does that. Picked it up at a pretty deep sale but it was worth it for a handful of €. I would probably not recomend it for full price, but on a sale? Sure. Ending is definitly sequelbaiting, let's see if that ever happens.

_childDocuments_.review: At first this may look like another Limbo clone, but Eternal Hope have enough elements to hold an identity of its own. The game has good ambience, a nice flow, responsive controls and good puzzle variety, with cool mechanics to solve them.The difficulty is average, some puzzles may take a few attemps but nothing to get stuck on. As for the game length, it's somewhat short (2~3 hours). You may need a second playthrough to find all collectibles.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Hope

_childDocuments_.review: When I opened Eternal Hope for the first time it was clear that this puzzle platformer game drew inspiration from indie classics like Inside and Limbo, though Eternal Hope presents more of a colorful premise rather than a gloomier one that those before mentioned provided. The little pop of color is most welcome in the background of the silhouettes of the characters and creatures, making it a pretty game graphically.You follow the story of Ti'bi, a boy who embarks on a journey to restore his beloved's soul and having hope that they will be reunited once more. He gets granted a mask and with it, the ability to shift between dimensions, by the Keeper of Souls, this power will enable Ti’bi to travel, solve puzzles and meet otherworldly beings that live among the shadows.The gameplay is rather simple, but is very well thought out with the different abilities, making it interesting and fun to play through. These abilities are unique and work really well throughout the game, complementing the already amazing story perfectly. Sometimes the puzzles get a little frustrating, but dying isn't a problem as there is a checkpoint system. In the end though, the puzzles were pretty simple and didn't take too much thought process to complete and get through.I believe the game shines mostly from it's sound design, the sound effects and soundtrack being very well done and it complimenting each part of the game really well. I felt completely immersed within the game because of this soundtrack, and it was absolutely fantastic.All in all, definitely a game that I would recommend to any puzzle platformer lovers and those who enjoy a tragic story. It's a little on the shorter side so I don't think 10€ is a good price, so maybe waiting for a sale is the best option.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Hope

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really hesitant negative review. Really makes me wish neutral reviews were a thing.Art style is beautiful, the story seems ngaging enough, but the gameplay falls really short. Puzzles are simple, short and feel forced sometimes. Some of the jumps were quite mean too.This game feels like it was the studio's first real attempt at a game, which looking at Doublehit's page, seems to be true.I would still recommend it, but don't go in expecting a supremly polished experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternal Hope

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Hope is a grim and sad 2D platformer in the Limbo type. I have nothing to say about the graphics and art style, you have seen it all before. This one is probably more colorful.Also, there is nothing new to tell you about the gameplay. Puzzles which don't forgive your mistakes. One wrong move and you kick the bucket. Enemies are merciless too and kill your character with one hit.At the start of the story, a strange creature talks our nameless character into a dangerous journey. It is very persuasive, and the stakes are high, which means you have no right to refuse it. And you don't do it.This review is more about the story. It is melancholic and touching theme about sacrifice. You should be prepared, because it can catch you off guard.  I would call it a philosophical fable for adults about our life.I recommend it to play if you prefer short time platformers, Limbo-like gameplay or if you are in search of a good story.P.s. You can find all my short reviews .

_childDocuments_.review: Got a review code for this game a few days ago and had no idea what to expect. I saw the art-style and thought I was in for another Hollow-Knight/Ori Metriovania type game. Surprisingly, Eternal Hope is just a simple 2-D puzzle game. One that's more in tune with PlayDead's: Limbo or Inside. And I thought that type of gameplay fit perfect for the story and mechanics in Eternal Hope. Everything about the game is very simple. You move in four directions: Up, down, left, right. You can jump, and you have a few unique abilities. The most memorable being an ability that lets you access another realm, opening up puzzles that might have been hidden otherwise if you had the ability turned off. What makes the power exciting is that it runs on a time limit. So if you're standing on a monster that can only be seen in this "shadow realm," then you have to make a move before your ability depletes and the monster disappears. Just like everything else, it's a simple concept that gets stretched really far, and at times even had me scratching my head at how to progress in the game. As for negatives, I actually experienced a few major bugs in the game. This can be seen on my livestream, but there was a moment where I would try to move past the checkpoint, and every time I took a few steps forward the game would freeze. I tried reloading my checkpoint, but the problem persisted until I rebooted the game. I also don't think the controls feel as responsive as they could. Overall, Eternal Hope is a really short but good time. If you're looking for a challenging puzzle game with a nice story and world, I would definitely recommend checking it out! My only complaints are the bugs I experienced and how the controls felt overall!

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Hope is a 2D puzzle platform game, you play as a young lonely boy called Ti'bi, you have lost the love of your life, a girl called Hope, who seemingly dies during a storm after she is stuck under a fallen tree and then falls to her death, and you are about to undertake a journey that will hopefully bring back your girlfriend. While grieving for Hope, The Keeper of Souls appears and he tells you that his job is to collect souls, but he has become weak, and Hope's soul has shattered into fragments, you then make what I assume is a deal with the devil and agree to help him by collecting various souls and fragments, which in turn will give him his strength back, and in return he will bring Hope back into the land of the living.The Keeper of Souls gives you some powers, and you now have the ability to briefly swap into the land of the shadow realm for 10 seconds at a time. You can do this to pass areas un-passable in the real world, to use harmless creatures to help you get to hard-to-reach places, or to solve a puzzles.There are no enemies to fight as such, just running from boulders, or escaping from situations.If you have played Limbo or Inside then this game will feel very familiar.The GoodBeautiful graphics, enjoyable story-line, and great soundtrack.The BadThe controls are just not sharp enough, I played using a Xbox Controller, and really this game should be geared towards people using game-pads, but most of the mistakes i made while playing were due to the controls, and then if you do die because of a missed jump, you then have to wait what seems like forever for it to reload to try again. Now realistically this loading time is no more than 10 seconds, but in 2021 this feels like an eternity, especially when you have a feeling that your failure in the game was not really your fault. Of course as you play you will get used to the lack of sharpness and adjust, but it really is something that can and should be fixed. The game is also a little short, and you will finish it within a few hours.OverallDespite my gripes over the controls, I really did enjoy the game, it is beautiful to play, and the story is lovely.I score Eternal Hope and strong 8/10Review originally published on

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly wins out for its graphics, creating compelling atmosphere and chilling visuals using very simply artwork. The puzzles are okay, some challenge but never very tough, and the use of the real and spirit worlds, and switching between, was pleasant and well-utilised.However, the challenge often didn't come from puzzles so much as from extremely strict timing of controls, leading to some sections where, even having figured out the puzzle, I would have to run the same sequence a dozen times before I could get just the right split-second timing, or manage to hold on to a second of rock without slipping the fraction to high or low that would get me killed. While the silhouette graphics are elegant and attractive, they are not conducive to some of the things that the game wants to do with depth and perspective.Spoilers for plot/endgame in the paragraphs below.The basis of the story - rescuing a loved one from the underworld - is a classic that has been done many times, to greater or lesser extremes of success. This did not feel, to me, like one of the greater successes. The obnoxious and heavy-handed "female" signs on the love interest - a flower in her long, ponytailed hair - just felt unnecessary. The female character got no backstory as to how she survived or how she met the male character, and there is no indication of why they fell in love - simply that they were a male character and a female character who spent time together. How did she survive to this point? Was she a refugee? A feral child like the male character is almost implied to be (though this is never actually followed through with or explored)? And at the end of the game, the male character dies - leaving the female character in exactly the same position of heartbreak he once occupied, only now with the guilt of feeling like the cause of his death! She has no backstory, is fridged for the main plot, and is left alone at the end. She has neither voice nor agency throughout the entire game - something which might feel less gendered if there hadn't been so much effort to put them into gendered boxes at the beginning of the game.Secondly, there is the matter of the antagonist. While I guessed the plot twist about the guide about halfway through, it was moderately well done. However, the game hints at a sympathetic backstory - the destruction of another world? A prison realm? - but neither follows through nor makes it clear that we are supposed to condemn the antagonist anyway. Are they supposed to be a tragic figure, or are they a monster trying to make excuses? It's never made clear, and not in a thought-provoking or morally complex way - in a lazy one, which makes it feel like the devs simply didn't care to follow through on the plot of the story they have created.I really wanted to like this game. I found the puzzles moderately engaging, and the appearance stunning. But I just couldn't get past the shallowness of the plot, the forced feeling of the relationship between the characters, and the unsettling last feeling that I wasn't sure whether I was playing the hero or the villain of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic puzzle-platforming.Technically well done; nothing original.If you like the genre, you should like this.It contains rope-swinging, gliding, access to a superposed world, all elements that I personally do enjoy.The story is nothing to write home about: a sappy little drama in which no emotion is ever earned. Still, at least it's competently told and makes your progression sensical.The two real issues are the severe lack of checkpoints (you'll have to redo too much too often) and the complete lack of chapter selection, a feature that is common to pretty much every game Eternal Hope tries to emulate. Very odd.I managed to overcome my repulsion to forced repetition, which is highly unusual from me. It shows that I actually enjoyed the puzzles and the overall gameplay. I'm not going to replay the entire thing to look for a few missing secrets, though. Post-game disappointment there; I had noted a couple of suspicious spots to be revisited later.

_childDocuments_.review: Received in the Yogscast Jingle Jam bundle.I really wanted to like this game, because it looks and sounds very cute, and for its puzzle elements. Unfortunately, movement and controls are far too sluggish, and cliff edges are not where they appear to be. I was constantly falling to my death on accident. The checkpoints are also inconsistent in where they save or how much progress in a section you lose. And they love rolling boulders at you that are difficult to avoid thanks to the sluggish controls. The time limit on the shadow realm also felt way too short. I don't mind having it because it kind of makes sense in context of the story, but it could use a few more seconds or at least a way to extend the time by finding power-ups or something along the way.The combination of the sluggish movement and dying too often are huge time sinks that just ruined the experience for me. I don't really understand why there are so many puzzle/walking sim games that don't let you move around at a reasonable speed. Usually I can push through it, especially if they at least have a sprint (though even that is usually still too sluggish), but only if I'm not constantly dying and losing progress.

Other times the controls aren't playing nice, like once I spent 5 minutes before solving a puzzle because normally dragging an item is a very simple affair so when it didn't work I assumed I couldn't, but this one puzzle the object took longer. And that's not counting how terribly unpolished the controls for the platforming is. But the most common problem is the game is far too dark. I don't mean narratively, I mean it's incredibly hard to see the various elements. It doesn't help that often the game is way too stingy with checkpoints, forcing you to complete several puzzles in order to have another go at the present one. It's trial and error, but not in a fun way and with all the rest it's not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎵🎵If you’re on this store page, chances are you are familiar with the Angry Video Game Nerd (AVGN). For those of you who aren’t, I can provide a quick summary but it’s probably best if you check out his  In short, AVGN is a persona who dedicates his life to playing and describing how bad some video games are (typically older ones). As the name suggests, he is best known for his anger and very liberal use of profanity.  (AVGND) is the embodiment of the AVGN series. Everything you’ve come to expect, such as his infamous potty mouth and extreme depictions of violence, alongside bucketloads of AVGN references, is incorporated in this pixelated adventure. Despite constantly being referred to as a “sh***y game” (by the Nerd himself), I quite enjoyed my playthrough.AVGND is essentially a parody of terrible games that continuously criticises itself for also being a terrible game. Despite this, AVGND is actually a good blend of challenging and fun (at least on normal difficulty). Since this is a play on terrible games, it only makes sense that the developers intentionally designed many segments to be unfair and/or trap the player. Funnily enough, this never pushed me to the point of frustration since the game is quite fair (I know this is contradictory but bear with me). Movement is reliable and familiar (feels like playing MegaMan), checkpoints are evenly spaced out, there is minimal RNG (except for boss fights), and respawns are infinite and quick. With a little patience you will know what to expect, allowing you to progress through the levels. Additionally, both games control in the same way, which makes for a smooth transition between AVGN I and II. Level design is surprisingly diverse. Each level (AVGN I) or zone (AVGN II) has a specific visual style, background music, gimmicks, and enemy types. For example, in AVGN I there is a level based on old erotic games - I don’t imagine I need to specify what the enemies are here. There is also a zone based on the TMNT NES game, complete with the awful electric seaweed and the  mini gap. Better graphics, map design, difficulty settings, etc - rest assured that everything stated on the store page is delivered. Since I have played AVGN I before, I could tell there were significant improvements in graphics and playability, which made the experience as a whole more enjoyable (AKA less rage-inducing). This deluxe version also comes with four additional levels (of which one is a boss fight) that can be accessed once you beat both I and II. Additionally, since all games (I, II and bonus) are built on the same game engine, the experience is quite streamlined. You can really feel that this is the definitive version of the AVGN games.Nevertheless, the core game is still practically the same. Although I can only speak for AVGN I, I don’t imagine AVGN II has changed much either in this version. If you haven’t played either AVGN game, I would recommend picking up the deluxe version. If you’ve already played both, it doesn’t make much sense to buy this version since it is hardly different from the originals (unless you feel like financially supporting the Nerd). Assuming you don’t get stuck and die a lot, most levels/zones should not take more than 15 minutes to complete. Altogether, my casual playthrough of AVGN I, II & bonus levels (on normal difficulty) only took about 4 hours. More content is included in the form of hidden characters/secrets and four collectable video game cassettes per level but once you’ve collected them all, there isn’t much left to do. If you’re really hungry for more AVGN, you can always attempt to complete every level without dying or increase the base difficulty.Dialogue is caked with insults and profanity, turd references are plentiful and enemies explode into gory messes when they die. This is exactly what we have come to expect from the AVGN series and the developers definitely managed to capture it here.  Honestly, I had completely forgotten how vulgar AVGN is. My teen self would have had the time of his life with this game but at this point in my life I don’t care for it much. Regardless, a very faithful representation of AVGN.Yep, that’s right, you can fire as quickly as you can button mash. This is especially broken if you have a controller with a turbo function - I imagine it would just look like a stream of white squares extending across the screen. Evading is still necessary but it feels cheap to cheese through boss fights mostly by mashing; generally speaking, they did not take more than 3 attempts to beat. Perhaps this was designed this way to make boss fights more viable at harder difficulties. There is limited time to read the dialogue as it proceeds automatically. This usually isn’t a problem but I find that the time allocated here is very short, forcing me to quickly gobble down the words on the screen. The writing isn’t Shakespearian but I would have liked to read it properly regardless. I’m not sure why the dialogue progression isn’t gated by the player’s input. Although it may seem that I have outgrown my appreciation for the vulgar, I actually quite enjoyed playing AVGND. Besides being a nice shot of nostalgia, this game is more fun than it is frustrating (at least on normal difficulty), especially when compared to AVGN I. Just bear in mind this deluxe version is essentially a remaster of the two previous games.To simplify things, I made this flowchart to help you decide whether you should get this game or not:

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of AVGN, I found these games to be a great supplement to the series. There are plenty of references and the same charm of the AVGN. Though this may turn off many who do not watch it, I do think that on its own this game holds up very well.	The part that stuck out to me the most was the gameplay. It is very satisfying. I found that movement was tight as a platformer, the game was generally fair, the level design was well done, and the gameplay was fun the entire time to the point where I 100%ed the game pretty much all in the same week. I do feel though that many people will find that this game is unbelievably punishing. When my brother played the original version he ended up throwing in the towel just because of how damn hard it was. This game on the other hand has far more difficulty options and that was perhaps this versions greatest advantage, it allows this game to be played by far more people, and on the easy difficulty will be far easier to beat while still maintaining a large portion of the challenge that the game has in its level design.	Graphically the game has a style that I appreciate, I am a sucker for pixel graphics and this game does it well. It is very colorful, backgrounds are very detailed, enemies have a great variety, and the UI and menu design is fitting. I have always disliked the gross-out stuff that the AVGN does and some of that is reflected in the game and its visuals, but honestly, that is my only gripe and I do not think that that is a real criticism since that is very much just a personal thing.	The controls are great, I had zero issues. Everything felt tight and I liked how the menus and games control.	I did not think I would say this, but I thought the soundtrack was fire. I really enjoyed it to the point I have gone out of my way to listen to some of it. The other sounds in the game are really good as well.	Lastly, this game vaguely has a story, and it is serviceable. It sucks that it is pretty minimal, but not surprising given that it is emulating older games. I don’t really have any praise for it beyond that it has the standard Nerd humor.I think this is a fantastic game. It is exactly what it should be; an old-style platformer, with AVGN humor, good graphics and music, and overall plays well. I am not a huge fan of platformers but this is definitely a good one and I found that I ate this game up and had a great time playing it. I do think that some may find this game a little lackluster for the price. I got under 12 hours out of it and it goes for 15, so I think it would be wiser to wait for a sale to get your best bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: CHECK OUT MY VIDEO REVIEW AT THE BOTTOM AS WELL!I give details on the difference between the versions and go over each level.I received a review copy of this game a while ago and cannot get enough of it. This is more than just a compilation of the first two games. It's a complete overhaul of the first, a tweaking of the second, and a brand new third for the grand finale!Refitting the first game into the engine the second used, we get a lot of improved graphics. The colors really pop! Also no more "Continue/Quit" screens! When you die, you immediately reform at the checkpoint! So you don't loose any momentum! At least one boss has been replaced but I'll leave that for you to find out (Or you can watch my video). Also the Cameos/Collectibles are intact (Although the Cameos are now Future Nerd appearances) PLUS you can now find the NERD letters like you would in II. And best of all, the difficulty has been curved for the better! 3/4 of the death blocks have been replaced with spikey balls! It can still be a pain but not as infuriating.Most of the changes in the second game are cosmetic. A few characters/bosses were reworked to make it more self contained (meaning it's no longer a movie tie in) any Cameos are nixed, and at least one level has been overhauled for the better! This was a great fine tuning of a great game.Lastly there's the new chapter! A four level (three plus one boss battle) gauntlet that's equal to the Wiley Tower levels of Mega Man the Wiley Wars! It is a gauntlet of some pretty challenge levels! And a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane final boss as well to wrap things up!Now for the more technical details.Graphics: Like I said they're gorgeous! For a retro game this is one of the bests!Controls: Perfect! Never had much of a problem either with M&KB or a controller! No delays or anything.Difficulty: You can select your difficulty now and they really show! You can also receive all the achievements on Easy mode alone. Pick the difficulty you wish for whatever challenge you want! It's rather balanced.So yeah I'd give this game a 9 out of 10! It is a great game, a terrific remaster! If you love the first two, this one improves on them and then some! Get it now!

Collecting the cartridges, extra characters, and special nerd gear just made for a more memorable adventure, I highly recommend you give this game a purchase on a good discount.
